text:
We stumbled upon this while passing through St. Petersburg. We loved it. The entire menu is vegan and it's basically a Chinese/Vietnamese fusion menu with completely vegan options.  I ordered the Portobello Noodle (which was great) and my wife ordered the Ginger Soy Protein (which was also really good). For appetizers, we also ordered the Kale Potato Soup and the Wonton Soup (both were decent - nothing special). 

When you first walk in, the place looks a little hole-in-the-wall-ish...and isn't the most well kept of places...but the food delivers in a deliciously satisfying way. I would highly recommend this to all vegans alike... and even those carnivores who are looking for healthier alternatives than your typical neighborhood Chinese joint.

The prices are reasonable (most entrees are around $9-$10) and the service staff is friendly (a little inexperienced, but friendly still).

text:
Toma is your best option in Santa Barbara for upscale Italian/New American fare. In a town crowded with beautiful restaurants featuring high price tags and sometimes disappointing food, Toma is miles above the rest. 

It's an excellent place to celebrate a special occasion or have a nice meal while vacationing. Tucked back facing the waterfront, Toma is a very small, intimate restaurant that is elegant without feeling pretentious. It's away from the crowds - a perfect escape from State Street and the Wharf. 

I favor their pasta dishes, which use the freshest ingredients available and are generously portioned. My favorite dish at Toma (and perhaps in Santa Barbara as a whole) is their gnocchi. This features delightfully fresh, sweet rock shrimp, tender gnocchi, and a garlic-tomato sauce. It is consistently delicious. 

Consider reservations to avoid disappointment.
name: Alex

text:
I was feeling a little homesick and was craving dim sum. I used to go Sunday mornings with the family in DC. I was elated to find that there were dim sum places in Tucson! Luckily, they served it on weekends only! 

I arrived with my husband and obviously any person knows you don't go for customer service. The decor needed some minor improvements but we were seated quickly around noon-ish. 

I will have to say since it is not primarily dim sum, the nostalgia of the a la carte experience where you get to pick and choose items they push in the carts and stamp your card is a little disappointing. For one, I couldn't gauge how much food I wanted and ended up ordering too much, but leftovers is never a really bad thing now, is it?

As for the food, it satisfied my craving and cured my homesickness. We ordered Har Gow, Sui Mai, turnip cake, pork spare ribs, bbq pork, shrimp ball, taro cake and some other stuff that I can't recall. I will say it's not the best I had, but it tasted like what it was suppose to taste like. I want to say it was somewhat bland. 

We did order sushi: salmon and yellowtail. Being that the establishment is focused on sushi, I will have to say their fish to rice ratio is not very proportional. Too excessive to be honest. The quality was decent, but I would go to a different place if I wanted sushi. 

Overall, will I eat here again? Probably if I am craving dim sum again.

text:
Vernick Fish is offishally open and you should try to seas a reservation asap, but also be ready to shell out some money to get the full experience! On a scale of 1-5 I give it a 4.5.

The restaurant interior is beautiful, very sofishticated (unlike all the fish puns you're about to endure). It's a shame much of the place faces a parking garage. Full disclosure: we were lucky enough to come during soft opening when food was half off for Comcast employees. Some of the staff seemed to flounder a bit at times but overall service was good and I'm sure it will be better once they get their sea legs!

True to it's name, the menu is heavy on seafood, but there are some non-fish options as well. In addition to the raw bar (oysters, shrimp etc), there is a decent selection of tartares, and crudos, and then some small and large plates and vegetable sides. Definitely recommend sharing dishes. A vegetarian would probably feel like a (hungry) fish out of water here- not too many options. The sourdough and seaweed butter was also a lovely accompaniment and they didn't judge us when we asked for more butter.

First they reeled us in with some oysters (with lots of accoutrements), then we loved the spicy tuna tartare (which we didn't find overly spicy) and the scallop tartare, which both came with waffled chips and were a decent portion size. For raw things, we got the torched kingfish and the sea bream with spicy melon and prosciutto. Aside from fintastic presentation both were very delicious (and came with 4 pieces each.) Would also highly recommend the scallop with dashi and truffle (even though it's a splurge for $24 for ONE scallop) the presentation is beautiful with the shell and ceremonious pouring of the dashi over it. The ricotta tuna corn njuda gnocchi and squid pad thai were also great and more regular sized shareable portions.

For the large plates we opted for the bronzino with tomatillo and avocado salsa,  the tilefish which was cooked perfectly and came with summer squash and pesto, and splurged on the dover sole- a fish that comes with it's own side table where it is filetted in front of you and then smothered in delicious sauce. Everything was delicious but I'm not sure if could justify the $115 price tag on the dover sole without the discount. As someone who enjoys deboning a fish and eating as much as I can of it (tail, cheek etc.) the table-side filleting doesn't have as much appeal (although maybe just for the spectacle and experience of other tables staring- you'll feel like a reel big fish). We may have been the first table to actually ask for the head back... 

Towards the tail end of the meal we somehow managed to find room for dessert despite being stuffed to the gills and they were nice enough to bring out the key lime pie with a candle in it for our friends birthday. The "Vietnamese" tart with bubble tea balls between layers was also delicious!

If you drink like a fish- there is a full bar and bottle options- we opted for sparkling rosé because we'd had a few cocktails at JG sky before (recommend doing that too!)

Would love to come back for lunch (would be great for a business lunch) and looking forward to coming back for dinner- great place for a special occasion!  As the delicious fish we devoured might say, I'm hooked.
name: Melissa

text:
For me, Smiley's is that "if I lived nearby, I'd be 300lbs" sort of place!

Fair warning, the food is so great here, if you show up an hour or so before closing, some menu items are often sold out.

That said, all of the sandwiches or platters?  Smiley's food is truly EPIC!

You can easily feed 4 and STUFF them on just $16-$20.

Their "Tony Montana" version of a non-traditional STUFFED Cuban should now really be declared a St. Pete original?  Long-pressed until crunchy, and with a mountain of meat.  This sandwich alone has made me make 3 visits here so far.

And that special sauce?  Soo GREAT!  Make sure to ask for it on the side if you have to travel a bit to make it home with a Smiley's sub, like I always do.

Note:  There is very little parking and it's mainly a take-out joint, with no real inside dining.

I hesitate to promote this place and suggest you visit, as you will likely be the guy that arrived JUST before me, and now their "plato de la casa" is all sold out!

(Finally:  Yes, I also realize this place is almost a clone of another long-standing joint with a very, very similar menu.  I am a big fan of both!  I'll let others battle out those details...)

text:
I keep coming back here and trying more food, and it's all just fantastic. They're primarily corn-based here, with plenty of vegetarian and even some legitimately good vegan options. There are various specialty platters, but I think their titular papusas are the best thing they offer. I don't know that I've had better beans in New Orleans than what they stuff these things with, and they are very clearly freshly cooked. They've mostly got cheese, but the vegan one has a dash of garlic along with the beans and it excites the tastebuds too. Platters come with a salad, a couple of pieces of fried plantain, beans, and some weird but presumably healthy fermented cabbage.

You do have to put up with some stuff to get to that food though; it is a small place, and for some reason I can never get good cell service inside. They're cash only (ATM inside), and it costs a fair amount for being a little place with not a lot going for it other than deliciousness. And when I say the food is fresh, you will be waiting a while for it to be cooked (which is why the cell service matters), with interactions with staff in the meantime ranging from friendly to pushy.

That being said, if you can handle the wait, the resulting meal is totally worth it.

Got my order, added a raw apple chai cookie, went home, and dug into one of the tastiest meals I've had in a long time.  Tons of noodles, sliced radishes, green onions, salad greens, etc along with a warm sliced chicken breast, and the dressing is FANTASTIC. I know it's sesame something-or-other and I'm practically licking the little cups. Each time I've gone back I think I'm going to try something new but nope. The soba noodles win out. Oh, and the chai cookie is tasty too, a nice treat the next morning with coffee. I highly recommend Great Full Gardens. There's something for everyone's tastes, and the staff is friendly.

text:
We had lunch at Madina this weekend as a part of our quest to have food from every country, something that's taken us to all sorts of interesting establishments across Indianapolis and across the country. Never before had I seen a Guinean restaurant...we've had Ghanaian, but other than that our West African experiences have been limited.

The overall verdict with Madina is that it's one of those places you go only for the food and not for the experience. Might be good for takeout, heard they also do catering. The place was dead when we were there, looked closed when we drove up to it. Except for one guy who came up and got takeout, we were the only customers in the restaurant the whole time, and it was verrrrrrry quiet. Like awkward quiet...no music, no other customers chatting, just silence. They have a front room with a couple tables by the register and a buffet (which they apparently don't use anymore) and a much larger back room with a bunch of tables. For whatever reason, we were seated in the back room in the middle of the empty room instead of just in the front, but we were glad they turned the lights on for us because it was kinda dark when we went in..LOL. 

Waitress explained to us what dishes they had available at the moment, but we didn't really catch everything she was saying. My mom and I both went for the chicken yassa. Didn't look like the same chicken I saw in the Yelp photos but nonetheless was very tasty. Feels like it has been marinating and stewing for quite awhile, seasoned with onions, peppers, olives, and bay leaves. I had couscous as my side and it is a HUGE plate, way more than you need, so expect to take home leftovers. They'd do well to add a little oil or parsley or at least something to the couscous to add flavor, but if that's not the traditional way I get it. Not complaining because I love couscous. My mom got rice and it the portion size for it was almost ridiculously large, but once again not complaining, makes for more meals later.

My dad had a lamb kebab. Probably not as traditional Guinean food, but we really wanted to try the plantains and that seemed like the best shot at getting them. The kebab was pretty good, but don't expect it to be anything crazy, it's just straight up lamb, no sauce or anything--they did bring some sort of green hot sauce to the table, and it was SUPER spicy, like too much to handle for my mom and I. The plantains were very well-cooked, just sweet enough, the right consistency, etc. Definitely recommend.

A second waitress came who was a bit more conversational, answered some questions, asked us how we found out about them and told us how they'd been doing and all that. Although it wasn't perfect, the food here was good, especially the chicken yassa, so I really hope they do well here. It's kind of off the beaten path, in a random strip mall on the westside that I can't see many people just stumbling across. Nice people and good food should hopefully bring them enough customers that they stay in business.
name: Sam

The sweet potato noodles just glistened in the container.  They appeared to be silky and were​ just that as you eat them.  
The meal came with two veggies​: I selected the roasted sweet potato and the parmesan broccoli.​    The sweet potatoes were just the right size and had that familiar sweet taste.  The broccoli was a bit too salty for me.
The meal also came with two proteins​: ​BBQchicken​e​, and grilled citrus chicken.  One of the chickens they had burnt​t which left a terrible taste in your mouth.
I also purchased a portion of salsa which had like a vinaigrette​ on it.
I ended up getting two sauces which were favorable.  Holy kale and creamy white ginger.  
Well, I am glad I purchased the larger of the two entrees offered.   Now I have enough for another meal.

text:
Oof- this was my second time at Kei Sushi. My first experience at this restaurant was not so great, so I wanted to make sure I tried again before I left a review. Unfortunately, my return experience was consistent with that of my first. 

I came with a friend on a Sunday to satiate our long-ongoing sushi craving. 

Both times that I visited Kei Sushi, there were not very many people at the restaurant. We were greeted and seated quickly. We did AYCE sushi, and this restaurant is unique because there are no forms. Instead, the waiters/waitresses come by to take down your order. This led to a lot of forgotten appetizers (I had to order multiple miso soups on such a gloomy day!) and delays. The first time, we didn't get dessert due to the change in waiter and lack of communication. Both times, we also had to wait for a very long time to receive our check and our waters were not refilled.

While the decor and ambiance is grand and inviting, the service turned me away from returning in the future. 

Now, for the food! I was personally excited to visit Kei due to the numerous vegetarian options. However, the majority of the food does not taste fresh. Be prepared for a tremendous amount of chewing! The seaweed that the sushi was wrapped in was too chewy. The edamame was stale, and undercooked but covered with heaps of salt. The veggie rolls contained too much rice, and the rice did not taste fresh either. Kei Sushi's redeeming savior was the delicious, rich miso soup. It contains mushrooms and soft tofu, and I ordered several of them. 

We were brought dessert this time. The mochi costs extra, so we chose a green tea ice cream. It had a weird aftertaste, almost like ice cream with freezer burn. Long story short, the service and poor quality of food (and consistently so) have discouraged us from returning.
name: Raghavi

text:
From the moment you walk in until the moment you walk out, this place feels as though you've stepped out of US and straight into some corner Istanbul restaurant.

The place has phenomenally authentic decor. No efficient AC though, so be warned. The walls are adorned with rugs and ceiling with murals.

We've ordered hummus and Iskender.

Hummus is one of the best I've had. A bit gritty, plenty of tahini flavor, their Spanish paprika smokiness pops throughout the dish. It comes with pita slices which are baked to order and oh so flaky and chewy... pure heaven. Be prepared for entree leftovers.

Iskender was phenomenal as well. The meat is high quality, tender, perfectly seasoned and doused with bread and sauce. Two HUGE dollops of yogurt on each side compliment it perfectly. Oh and the portions are easily enough for two meals. 

Place appears family owned. Everyone is pleasant. Our service was slow the first time around, but the second time we came to visit it was much better. Still, everyone was nice and efficient once they got to us. 

Highly recommended.
name: Paul

text: Perfect date night restaurant: romantic, cozy, authentic Italian. Ordered the caesar salad, penne vodka and lasagna, and homemade tiramisu. To die for. So tasty. Excellent service, perfect ambiance. Will definitely come again.

text:
We decided to come here as it had recently opened and had all sorts of great reviews. Since it was Saturday night around 7 it was pretty busy but we didn't wait more than 10-15 minutes which I thought wasn't bad for a Saturday night. As we were seated, and given a few minutes to look over the menu, the selection of food was very straight forward and mostly things you'd expect to find at a bar or pub. They have a large selection of pizza options, as well as your typical assortment of seafood (fish, clam, scallops) and chips, other seafood options as you'd expect from a Halifax themed restaurant, and what they call an "OG Halifax Donair". 

We decided to get the Garlic Fingers to start, as well as a large OG Halifax Donair, and a Clam Po' Boy for myself. If you were thinking about getting a pizza as an entree I would strongly advise against the garlic fingers because the garlic fingers is a cheesy mozzarella pizza with garlic butter, served with donair sauce as a dip. The donair sauce is very sweet, and at first feels strange to pair with the garlic cheese bread, but the more you eat it the more it seems to work.
The Clam Po' Boy was a bit dry and more tart than I expected. It's not something I would personally get again, but it wasn't a bad sandwich by any means, it just didn't wow me. The donair on the other hand was one of the best donairs I've had in a long time, the meat was flavourful, the sauce worked perfectly in harmony with all the other ingredients, and it was just a solid donair. 

The service was very friendly and often checked in on us despite it being so busy. My only other comment would be that this place was a bit on the louder side, from the music, to all the people wanting to have conversations over the loud music, it just isn't a great environment if you're looking to have a conversation on a first date or something like that, but if you're looking for a fun place to get some good pub Halifax style pub food and some drinks, this is the spot to hit up.

text: My friends wanted to try it for our lunch date, and I'm non-celiac GF so I thought, why not? The place was super cute, very fountain square atmosphere. I felt like there were plenty of gluten free options, and it was affordable, which is hard to find. They even had an option to sub out a GF bun on their sandwiches which was a nice surprise. I tried the chicken tacos, which are labeled as GF on the menu. When they came out they were on flour tortillas. Now, the menu does say corn or flour, but I guess I just assumed since it's labeled as GF that the default would be corn. Of course I should have clarified and asked, but maybe the server should have asked which kind I wanted as well. Just kind of tricky, but it was fine. I asked her for some corn tortillas to just be brought out and she did so with no trouble. I dumped my tacos into the corn tortillas and they were still delicious. The habanero pineapple topping was amazing! Obviously, if you're more sensitive to gluten, you couldn't have done what I did, so clarify that what you're ordering is indeed GF. All in all it was good and I would go back.

text: Let's begin this way... made a reservation for 2 for the 15th of February 3 weeks in advance. No big deal, used the open table app thru the website.  All good.  A couple of days later, we ask our friends to join us, we go thru the website again and change our reservation. Just to be sure, we called right away after changing the reservation... they assured us they got it, reservation changed to party of 4..EVEN GOT A CONFIRMATION EMAIL that night (and the day before our actual dinner for that matter)... fast forward to 15 of February, we meet our other 2 in the party of 4, we find them in the vestibule of the restaurant if you can call it that... THEY ONLY HAVE MY NAME FOR A PARTY OF 2... oh what the hell? But somehow the lady working the hostess desk keeps TELLING me how we tried to change it and it's not our (my) fault... we wait like idiots standing there in front of everyone eating... there's really not a waiting area, it's pretty much a show up at your reservation time and be seated type of place... we get seated a half hr after our thrice confirmed reservation time and the hostess assured me again, it's not our fault for trying to change our reservation... NO SHIT LADY!! how about a comped appetizer or something?? anyhow,  as for the food and ambiance,  it was very good. I had the gnocchi flavored with beets and pan seared chicken,  EXCELLENT... the starter salad is very good but small. Everything is ala cart...  wife had pasta with a little oil and cheese... that sucked... I forget what the other 2 with us had, but I remember them saying they  enjoyed it.  Creme brulee was awesome as well as lava cake.  This isnt your typical Italian spaghetti and meatball type place.  Regional fare with local ingredients.   I recommend,  but their reservation system SUCKS BALLS!
name: Tim

text:
The lunch special was great. I had the TB Turkey minus the bacon, pressed. It was delicious and had cheese and maybe arugula as well. I also had the steak fries and, they were good. My co-worker got his with the sweet potato fries. They were excellent. 

The lunch special also comes with a soft drink. 

I highly recommend. Will definitely be back to try more things!
name: Jac

text: Price felt a touch high for what it was. The music was louder than it needed to be. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. For the price I expected more than this. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait.
name: User

text: Best buffalo wings in town and most of the waitresses and bartenders staff are very friendly and helpful... I definitely recommend dropping by and checking out the atmosphere.
name: Kevin

text: I'm typically not a 5 star guy, but this experience was pretty darn perfect. Sunday Jazz Brunch at Cafe Sbisa. The place was really busy, but it didn't feel like it.  We had reservations. Were seated immediately and  the service was professional , informative, and fun. Thank you CeCe and Angelique! Crab cake benedict was delicious, and the oyster Po Boy was well presented and tasty. Cajun slaw with blue cheese crumbles served on the Po Boy was an unexpected treat. Jazz combo was really good. The experience was so delightful we are considering going back for dinner while we are in town.
name: Roger

text:
There's always an insane line here and honestly, the chicken isn't worth it. The spice levels are incredible inconsistent depending on the day. Additionally, I find the chicken to be more greasy here than other Hot Chicken places in Nashville. The pimento mac n cheese is either loved or hated. I prefer a more traditional mac n cheese.

All that being said, if I were comparing this to hot chicken places outside of Nashville, it would be ranked higher... there's just too many better options close by.
name: Alex

text:
Jamar was awesome he toasted oysters with my husband. Will definitely be back..
Place was clean friendly,food was FANTASTIC 
Will be back for Breakfast tomorrow
name: Mary

text: The worst bartender service I've seen in a long time. It has a tiny bar and the two beauties behind the bar were more concerned with their gossip than filling glasses. Bottom line is it's the only place in south Philly and they know it.
name: Blues

text: The owner and management staff are Terrible...The doorman is a Real Cutie, but everyone else can Kick Rocks on a Hot Sunny Day in Open Toe Sandals. The blatant disrespect from the owner was very on called for, he tried his best to ruin our night but the devil was a Lie...Anyway in conclusion we will never go back. Now, I might drive by to see the doorman but that's it.
name: Layla Ann

text: The staff was pleasant, however, the chicken in my salad tasted like it was three days old and reheated three times.
name: Mike

text: First time ordering from here and I honestly wasn't sure what to expect. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly.
name: User

text: We went to the boiling house this past Saturday for lunch and it was PHENOMENAL! Loved the seasoning on everything! We ordered the seafood lover. I highly recommend everyone to visit this restaurant!
name: Lorraine

text: Herbsaint used to be one of our favorite restaurants to visit when we were in New Orleans. We enjoyed several excellent meals there over the years.  Sadly, the quality of the food and service has diminished significantly. The Sicilian beef appetizer was a standout, but the rest of the food was sub-par.
name: Rusty

text: We came here for an impromptu birthday dinner and our group of 5 was extremely pleased. We came about 45 mins before they were supposed to close, but unlike recent restaurants lately, we felt SO welcome and not rushed at all, which truly was one of the best best parts: the service. As mentioned, our server treated us as if we were her first table of the night, not the last, and didn't make us feel like we needed to rush out. On top of that, the food was absolutely delicious. I had the scallops on a bed of for risotto and it did not disappoint. The scallops were huge and I left feeling extremely satisfied. The sunset Martini was delicious as well. I was a little disappointed they didn't provide a complimentary birthday dessert, as it was a little pricier of a spot. It would've been a cherry on top of they maybe offered some kind of birthday or celebratory offerings for occasions like that. Aside from that, all was great.
name: Erica

text: Great brunch place. I ordered the Ela burger and my husband ordered the Biscuits and gravy. Our server warned us that the burger is a reddish color because of the preservatives and not because it is undercooked. I appreciated the pre-emptive warning and the burger was delicious. My husband really liked his biscuits and gravy. We also ordered three samplings for the cheese plate and it was absolutely delicious. For our first round of drinks we both had the Seelbach and it was incredible. We then made the mistake of ordering a second round but went with the drink that had scotch, absinthe, lime, lemon and egg white. I forget the name and I swear I have had it there before and it was very good. This time it was absolutely awful and borderline undrinkable. We should have said something so that is in us but it was probably top 5 worst cocktails I've ever had. I don't know what happened but the drink was not balanced and honestly downright disgusting this time around. Again, its on us- we should have said something and next time if it happens we will but it was definitely enough to kill the vibe just a bit.
name: Laura

text: You had a crazy Saturday night and you literally feel like you've been hit by a bus Sunday morning. Where are you going in fishtown to nurse that hangover? Don't go to a boujee, hipster place where you'll be the only one that looks like a cretin. Come here! The wait was only 10 minutes and every thing is reasonably priced. It's also BYO if you need a little hair of the dog.
name: Sam

text: Had a reservation for a group of 14 getting together.  Although the table was prepped no one was allowed to be seated before the noon reservation.  It was awkward to stand in front of the host station just inside the doors.  Two wonderful servers were assigned to us and they took orders for beverages and food quite timely.  Some in our party received meals as ordered.  Some were not served until others were almost finished.  One gluten free order was served with a roll!  The kitchen obviously has a problem.  We know large groups can be a challenge and we won't meet there again.  Since some enjoyed their meals, I would be willing to try it again if the party was 4 or fewer.
name: Roberta

text: Went with family on a Sunday and it was louder than I expected. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. For the price I expected more than this.
name: User

text: Fine for mall food !  Prices are high but it's a place to be seen.  Food and cocktails are to be expected.
name: Anthony

text: I love the tofu pad Thai here. The tofu is always made with a crunchy outside and soft inside. The level of spice I request is always perfect and my meals are always tasty. The staff is always pleasant and willing to serve. Parking is a bit tight, so if you don't find parking in front of the restaurant, there is a line of parking spaces across the street.
name: Iritte

text: This place is a gem in Philadelphia and frequented by all the locals.  Whether you want cookies, special brownies, small specialty cakes (including the papal one), or especially cannoli (piped fresh) this is your place.  My wife and I had the cannoli with a delicious filling and a perfect shell.  They are very busy so I recommend to order over the phone or grab a number when you step in the door.
name: Brad

text: It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. The music was louder than it needed to be. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. Glad we tried it. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. It looked better online than it did in person. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. The whole meal felt kind of uneven.
name: User

text: This place never disappoints! The prosciutto and Brie sandwich is my go to every time. George was awesome and gave us excellent service with a smile!
name: Christina

text: Desk Clerk at Country Inn & Suites recommend this place. Said we would like it. She wasn't kidding .! It was wonderful! Great homemade food. Doesn't look like much from the outside but boy is it good. Great food very affordable. Busy place.
name: Ellen

text: Fair for the price but not great. Go to other fine restaurants instead. Food was okay but over cooked and bland. Salad bar was nice but it didn't make up for the rest of the dinner.
name: Phil

text:
Please try this place. I don't normally review after the first visit, but it is Monday and I am still thinking about dinner last Friday. 
FOOD:
--Jalapeno cornbread (each table gets that day's version) - crumbly and spicy.
--Spinach-artichoke dip, creamy and hot, served with crispy, crunchy, thick rounds of bread.
--Smoked Duck Leg Quarter - duck was tender; crawfish dressing moist with a nice kick, going well with the sautéed spinach. (I get duck whenever it is on a menu since it is not the usual for restaurants in this price range, a treat!)
--Pork Porterhouse - pork cooked perfectly to medium as requested; again the crawfish dressing, with veggies (this night, sautéed zucchini, caramelized onions)
--Lagniappe Burger - a beast of three meats and cheddar cheese, set off by caramelized onions, lettuce and tomato and what initially looks like not enough of the Chef Sam's Famous Sauce (but it is just right - it is like a barbecue sauce, sweet and spicy).  French fries mealy, crispy and yummy.
With the exception of the Lagniappe Burger, the portions initially looked rather small, but that is as compared to other "Friday night" restaurants that serve platesful of easy food - the quality and execution here are exceptional.
AMBIENCE: like O'Briens was, a nice hum of conversation but always able to hear those at your table.
SERVICE: friendly, knowledgeable, timely.  The timing between appetizers and entrees took a little while, but I have that down to the preparation going into the dishes.  This isn't line cooking like chain restaurants, but chefs who are using their skills to create meals you won't soon forget.
WB-owned, deserves the love, needs our support.  Hopefully you'll have the same experience.
name: Amy

text: Food was good, service was better and beer was ... as described.  No hidden surprises here.  This is a solid restaurant/bar.  It's large so it's good for parties.  They have a good kids menu with the average price of $6.  The kids meal was plenty for kids that don't eat much but a kid that has a hearty appetite should order off of the adult menu.
name: Lisa

text: This was my first time here and the service can't be beat.  Tyler was awesome and the food was pretty good as well.  Oddly enough at this hot chicken spot, I had catfish.  It was pretty good as well as the greens.  I could have done without the mac and cheese but once I said I didn't like it, they quickly replaced it with mashed potatoes.
name: Keli

text: Hands-down best sushi in all of Montgomery County. Easily could rival most spots in Philly. Extremely fresh fish and the overall quality of all of their ingredients is spectacular. FYI it's BYOB but they have another location in Montgomeryville which is also very good that has a bar
name: Bilbo

text: They have very good lunch bento boxes. I always get beef teriyaki with crunchy rolls. My daughter loves the salmon nigiri and shrimp nigiri. The customer service is also good.
name: Vieda

text:
If you love Mexican but don't want to schlep to Philly for authentic eats and atmosphere, then don't delay--check out Mad Mex.  

Went there for lunch.  Combos are plentiful (enough for leftovers) and reasonably priced.  I had a burrito and salad combo . Delicious!

Megan, our server, was super duper, too.  

I will definitely return.
name: Maryanne

text:
We were really happy to find good vegetarian food in the area. There are plenty of veggie options. 

The place looks very bare bones though. We sat outside where people were smoking, which was really annoying but there is very little space inside. So unless they impose a no smoking policy for customers, nothing much you can do about it. For a place that's almost like a takeaway bar, food is quite pricey here but at least it tasted good.
name: Lali

text: Came with my sister during lunch rush, the service was great and the food all came out fast. Very friendly staff. For all you can eat, not bad at all. Would recommend.
name: Hang

text: Best Chinese food in the Treasure Valley. Hands down. Been going here since they opened up and I love it. Service is always great and the food is always made correct
name: Paul

text: Came here with my family tonight. Very clean and casual dining with outdoor seating as well. Reasonable prices, Generous portions, and the Friendly staff provided excellent service. Our waitress Mary was awesome. There were so many options on the menu so we were so indecisive. Mary was patient with us, attentive and great with My children. Would definitely recommend.
name: Tineisha

text: I am just so upset. My family and I come for happy our, sat at a table, ordered off the happy hour menu, and then receive the bill with all of our happy hour items at full price! I want to clarify our server was good as was our food. The manager comes by and tells us that we didn't sit in the "correct" section for happy hour since we got a table, to which I told him that there were happy hour menus on the table. Why put a happy hour menu on a table that isn't in the right section for happy hour?? Super misleading. And then he tells us that we should have told our server we were ordering off the happy hour menu first, and he refused to give us any kind of consolation. We only ordered items off the happy hour menu, and ended up paying $30 more than we expected because of this ridiculous and misleading policy or whatever you want to call this. He was just unsympathetic to our situation. The host even walked over to us afterward and apologized to us because he overheard and knew we got screwed over. This was incredibly upsetting and I'm just appalled with how this was handled.
name: Wanda

text: Got takeout from here twice now so I feel like I can say a little more. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The staff seemed tired but still polite. I can see why people like it, even if I wasn't fully sold. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text:
Worst experience ever today!  Coming here for years. Sitting here for over 45 mins and still no food and my son is starving. Not even busy, so that definitely isn't an excuse. Usually love coming here, but this is just unbelievable. I had to ask to get our food to go, since we have things to do.

And of course they couldn't even do that. And no sorry from a manager, just the server
name: Ed

text: Went for Happy hour. Unlimited fresh chips were awesome! The drinks and meal fair were equally good. The atmosphere is frat party. It was difficult to have a conversation. If you can get past that, its a keeper
name: Alex

text:
Pleasantly surprised by this place. A little pricy for the portion size but the flavors are there. Authentic, clean, and friendly staff. We were in the area and decided to try. We ordered the Fried Okra appetizer, Chicken Vindaloo, and Shrimp Korma and two orders of Garlic Nan...paid $63 plus tip. 

My 2yr old who hadn't had her nap yet managed to break a plate but she turned on the water works because she was sad and managed to puppy eye her way into two desserts. They graciously gave us rice pudding and a mango yogurt drink. 

The Okra Appetizer was crunchy with red onion and tomato. Great flavors and a unique dish. The Chicken Vindaloo starts at a good spicy level for kids... we got a half level above that and were happy. The Shrimp Korma was not on the menu but they accepted our trade from the chicken Korma for Shrimp and it was the perfect compliment to a spicy dish. It has a great dipping sauce for the Nan. The Mango yogurt drink reminded me of a Rita's mango misto (if you know what that is) and was delicious. The Rice Pudding was reminiscent of arose en lenche or a loose rice pudding with shaved almonds. Also good. A light sweetness. If I was a sweets girl I would have finished it. Very happy with my meal. My only complaint is the price. Lived in Hawaii and paid less for larger portions of the same dishes. Best Indian I've had was in Hawaii at Cafe Maharani... go if you are in the area... so I measure every other restaurant against them. This place is a solid 4 stars. If they found a way to add garlic and cheese stuffed Nan to the menu they might get an extra half star from me.
name: Mel

text: We stopped in for a quick breakfast on our last day in town. Phenomenal meal at a more than reasonable price. The service was some of the best I have ever experienced. Jonathan was exceptional.
name: Samir

text: Really enjoyed Taco Bar. This was my first time there. I got 2 tacos and street corn. The street corn was delicious! I never had street corn that was on the cob before. The tacos are pretty basic, just topped with onions and cilantro. However, they do a have a hot sauce bar with 4 different sauces and a good variety of meats to choose from. I got a steak taco and marinated pork taco. The marinated pork taco was my favorite. Good prices too....got lunch for less then $9.
name: Jimmy

text: 1st time there and it was amazing!  Festivals and plantanes for appetizers and then jerk chicken and curried chicken. Can't wait To go Back and try something different like the curry goat
name: Rick

text:
Tried this place tonight..
My wife passed it several times a week and was interested 

The drink menu is far more extensive than the food and well it seems like they are more interested in selling drinks than food

The drinks were good of course it helps to like tequila 

I tried the coconut shrimp tacos. They were very good but extremely small. I ordered two should have ordered four

The queso and chips were very tasty 

Biggest problem is parking very limited and the air conditioner was on freeze do the food got cold very quickly 

Some interesting techno playing on the sound system 

You can opt to sit outside on the neck or on tables out front ... in All honesty it wAs more pleasant than the freezing inside air conditioning 

I guess they are getting it together... seems like a popular place
name: Alex

text: Found this place when searching for restaurants by the Amelie arena before Tampa game. LOVED it!!  Not big but staff was friendly and recommended special which was amazing. Thin crust and not alot of cheese or sauce so ingredients are key, which I love. Best pizza I've had since Italy!  Will be back!
name: Cathy

text: Flew in Philly and was staying downtown.  Went for a walk and was looking for a place to eat.  Stumbled upon this gem.  I had the pesto pasta, with a side of foccia bread.  Excellent.  Just hit the spot.  Prices were good, just a great serving of pasta.
name: Dave

text: Stopped by after work because I was nearby and hungry. Food was fresh and service was quick. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. Anyway, pretty smooth experience from start to finish. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait.
name: User

text: One of my favorite places to visit in Tucson. Dropped by a week ago Friday with a couple of friends. Sat at the bar for a few beers, some appetizers and small plates. Restaurant was buzzing and the servers were in great form. Great food, and owner bought us a round of drinks and took time to discuss the menu, etc. Highly recommended!
name: Mark

text: Believe the hype. This place is good, really good. I had the damn hot (habanero based) and the hot. Delish! It's not that typical vinegary hot sauce, but it's a flavor that is well seasoned and not just hot.
name: Kemi

text: Our family had the Thanksgiving menu. The food and service was outstanding. We definitely will be back. Would love to see a Christmas Eve menu.
name: Nancy

text: Garcia's hotdog stand is pure heart. Over the past few years the line has been growing at 16th & Emerson.  I mean how many times have you came across a man & his hotdog stand on yelp??? Enough said! It's just amazing.
name: Jalin

text: The soup was better than the sandwich, which I wasn't expecting. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which prob says everything.. For a busy night they handled it okay. I left full, which at least counts for something. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really.
name: User

text: Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. By the time the food came out I was already annoyed. Probably not coming back. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish.
name: User

text: This was a delivery order on a night when I really did not want to cook. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Price felt a touch high for what it was. No big complaints, just a nice meal. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Would return. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish.
name: User

text: Food was amazing but the wait was 25 to 40 min. All of our dishes we were very good and very filling. My one complaint is my endless toast was not endless- our waiter never asked if I wanted more. Really cute vibe and even though there was a wait it's around a lot of shops you can browse while waiting
name: Emily

text: Awesome pizza, but the people at the counter need to work on their customer service skills! It's always very awkward going in pick up pizza. They seem to be only concerned about you paying for your food and forgetting about being friendly and service oriented with customers.
name: Mary

text: Needed a freaky fast meal before our ticket time at the Arch. They did it, fed us freaky fast and it was delicious!  We made it back to Gateway Arch National Park in time. Thanks Jimmy John's for always being freaky fast and  yummy !
name: Marie

text: Worth the drive from Sparks. Fresh burgers made to order. Garlic fries are perfect. Service was friendly. They serve beer for the drinkers. Burger me also has different options, from French dips to chicken and different sides.  Some games to play  and TVs with sports on.
name: J

text: We had a fun night out, did the 97X Shindig, saw Two Feet. Had drinks and played pool at a bar. Saw this restaurant was open until midnight so we walked the half mile to get there. Not only were they not open at 11:20, it was apparent they had cleaned up and shut down sometime ago. If you are not open until the stated time advertised, change your advertisement! Would not recommend this place for that alone.
name: Cassie

text: I always believe it when places say they are "the best (insert cuisine here) in (insert city)". Matoi Sushi has this claim permanently printed on all their signage and I have no reason to question it! I thought this sushi was very fresh and tasty, though not cheap. They also have some nice Korean dishes (+1 for seafood pancake) and housemade dumplings. I got the lunch special #2 and enjoyed it.
name: Jennifer

text:
This is the place to go for authentic tacos and delicious paletas in St Charles.  They have ice cream and popsicles in so many flavors! Super fun place to bring a kid or grab a quick bite to eat. Staff is friendly and knowledgeable. Its the same people as Tradicional 636/ El Pueblito so you know its gonna be good. 
Get the Al Pastor taco and a lime popsicle for the perfect treat
name: Jordan

text: Claire, Joe, and Al are the best! Claire and Joe are attentive and knowledgeable. They give the best suggestions and are almost like family. Food can be inconsistent but other than that I always have a great time. Al the best floor manager. Took care of us when we had issues with the food. Amazing. And  adorable. GO HERE!
name: Brook

text: Have been going here for over 30 years and even with owner changes usually still within the family, it's still been good. That is not the case anymore. We've tried it a few times since the newest owners and have been disappointed every time. Last time was the straw that broke the camels back. Ordered 2 calzones and a pizza turnover with sausage. The calzones did not have the sauce in the box and were sitting in a pool of grease. How that's possible I'll never know since calzones are baked! The pizza turnover didn't not have any sausage in it although we paid $2 extra for it. So i called and the girl on the phone immediately gave me attitude saying the calzones don't come with sauce, well they have for the past 30 years but whatever so i tell her about the grease and the turnover issues and she nastily tells me to hang on. Seriously why? For free food or a future discount? Thanks but i don't want it. Go elsewhere and do yourself a favor.
name: Denise

text: Delicious food. Had the Shrimp and Grits. House appetizers like the Tapenade are also excellent. Great beer selection. Ybor Premium, Gold Klub, and All I Wanted Was A Pilsner were great, and my favorite was the Tombstone. Really friendly service and a fun, attractive atmosphere. See if they'll give you a tour!
name: Steve

text: Black garlic ramen was really good. Great flavor. Pork was tasty and had good mouth feel. The only minor complaint would be for the bowl to come out hotter but that's a personal preference and I am sure it's plenty hot for most people.
name: Ro

text:
A pizza place in the style of a subway or q'doba. But quality pizza that you'd expect from a true pizzeria with wood fired pizzas. So the first thing to know from that is that you're not getting a huge XXL pizza to share with your friends. You're each probably getting your own individual pizza and maybe having a few slices leftover (or if you're me, none because I shared with my toddler).

The best part of this concept is that they're making it in front of you and they'll ask you if you want more cheese for example (and the answer to that question is always yes by the way). I have not ventured away from cheese as this is my favorite (and my toddler's too). But it's pretty darn good. The sauce has a bit of a kick to it so be prepared for that. Not crazy spicy, but enough that you know it's there.
The crust is typical of a hand tossed wood fired pizza, you can ask for the extra dough to give it a bit more crust, but I found that I didn't prefer it that way (despite my penchant for deep dish pizza). 

Now, my favorite part. The blackberry lemonade. I would buy this from them in jugs if they sold it. Perfect combination of lemon and blackberry with just the right amount of sweetness. Did I mention I'd buy a jug of if? Or two. Or three. Hey, MOD! Get on that!
name: Shannon

text: LOVED this spot! Great to get some work done on a Saturday afternoon. Looking forward to coming back and trying more of the menu!
name: Sam

text:
This is my new favorite place for Chinese and Thai. 
The prices are great, the food is the best I've eaten. I will no longer wait 2 hours to pickup at my old go-to place that's right in my neighborhood.
name: Anne

text:
we went again this summer to Burger study... it just confirms the previous five stars rating I gave. The prime burger is fantastic. And I got confirmation that the kids food was excellent, including the Mac and cheese.
Service still also very good.
name: Yann

text: Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Food was fresh and service was quick. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Would return. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. For the price I expected more than this.
name: User

text: Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Wouldn't really choose this place again. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent.
name: User

text: The food came out fast, which was good because we were starving. So yeah, the food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. So yeah, the experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. text: I don't understand how this place only has 3 stars, so if you are reading this please give them a chance. My husband and I stumbled onto this place while vacationing in the area. After checking out the other choices food-wise we decided this menu looked the best. We came on a busy Saturday and waited in line for maybe 5 minutes and maybe 5-8 additional minutes for our food. My husband and I both ordered The Dixie Chick sandwich and shared a side of fries. We also ordered beers which are only 5 bucks which I feel like is competitive for this area. The reviews on this post comment how small the chicken was - I beg to differ. Our chicken was bigger than our bun by a large amount and was extremely delicious. It was well seasoned and moist - tasted so fresh. I got the fried chicken and it was the perfect amount of crunch and moist. The pimento sauce was just delicious and the pretzel bun did not disappoint. Ignore the negative reviews and give this place a chance. The only complaint I would have is the ketchup was out and they were too busy to change it when we needed it - but this happens ANYWHERE and EVERYWHERE if you think about it. 10/10 would recommend!
name: Jessica

text:
This place is AMAZING!!!! I am in love with everything about Samuarai Blue and I pray that one day they venture out to the South Florida/Ft. Lauderdale region. I would proabably declare bankruptcy if that ever were to happen because I'd spend every night here LOL.
 
I stumbled onto this spot by pure chance, as me and my boyfriend were vacationing in Tampa and craving sushi. I found Samurai Blue and we decided to come on a whim as it seemed new.  I am so lucky I did, because this is a pure gem. We loved it here so much, we came here both nights of our short Tampa vacation. And when we venture to Tampa again, we will make it an absolute point to come here.
 
We walked in and I was immediately drawn to the open floor concept and the immaculately clean floors. Me and my boyfriend sat at the sushi bar and we decided to try an appetizer; I eyed the blue crab rangoon and wow. They were delicious, not overloaded with too much crab, as that can ruin it, and not too fried that it takes away the flavor of the crab. We ordered the Mango sake, which I have never had before, and it was amazing. It was not your typical hot sake, which I enjoyed, as sometimes the warm sake can bother my throat a little. But the one thing about the Mango sake was that it left a weird aftertaste in my mouth. For sushi we got 2 rolls, the Tokyo Rock and Roll and the Spontaneous Combustion Roll. The Tokyo Rock and Roll is an imitation of your Dragon Roll however there is Grilled Eel on top; This roll was OUTRAGEOUS. I suggest this is a roll you must try if you come here. The Spontaneous Combustion Roll was OK - I do not like hot fish in my sushi, so I was not crazy for it. For dessert we got the brownie with ice cream - it was not the best but it did the trick.
 
When we came the next night, we wanted to try a little bit more, so we ordered a lot of rolls. For appetizer we got the Dim Sim Shumai. Think Pork dim sum, and this is it. It was awesome. We ordered the strawberry sake, which was SO GOOD. If you are going to order a cold sake bottle, definitely try the strawberry. It is not too sweet and does not leave an aftertaste like the Mango. We ordered so many rolls the second time around. See pictures in this review. When we ate each of the rolls we could tell that each roll was made fresh and the ingredients popped. I am not an adventurous sushi eater, but the Hamachi Fresh Roll was pretty good. I am not a fan of the cilantro, but the jalapenos was the perfect touch.
 
This is one of those spots that I assure you will not regret coming to. The service is great and not to mention that the sushi here is definitely going to be the better of the sushi you will have in this area. I will absolutely be coming back here next time I am in Tampa.
name: Christina

text: They brag that they have the best clam chowder in Saint Pete Beach . . . well we agree!  The chowder is chock full of clams and flavor. The salmon was grilled nicely, huge chunks of lump crab meat over a perfectly cooked bed of asparagus and smothered in a scrumptious lobster cream sauce. Yummy!

text:
My husband and I decided to try habit burger for lunch today. His work is close by and they had received free char-burger with cheese coupons so we were excited to get to try these burgers for FREE! When we showed up today around 11:30 there was a line out to the door and every table was taken.  The two girls at the cash register were friendly and fast and the line moved fairly quickly. There was no issue with us using our free Charburger coupon. We also added a drink, fries, and onion rings. When you place your order they give you a buzzer instead of a number that goes off when your order is ready. Once our order was taken and we filled up our drinks people had started to leave so we were able to find a table. The wait for our meal was under 10 minutes.
 I like to think of myself as a cheeseburger connoisseur and these cheeseburgers do not disappoint... They are awesome! We didn't modify our burgers we just order them the way they came and they do not need anything else added to them they are perfect just the way they are. As for the fries they were just OK. But the onion rings were fantastic!! The next time I go I would just get the Char Burger with cheese and onion rings and skip the fries. 
They do have a email club that I signed up for and will be excited to receive coupons and other specials from them.

text: So I'm not the type to complain about restaurants, but when I do it's when the service is just shit. The restaurant today, dinner time is very empty. Probably 10 people MAX are here. text:

The only let down was the dessert. They had cut fruits as well as some Indian fare. The Rasmalai and Kheer were good, not amazing. However I would stay away from the gulab jamun which was too dense and the jalebi which was too hard and crispy throughout.
Anyway I'll go back for the food for sure and hope to try some more dishes on their menu on a different day.

My boyfriend liked his veggie benedict and his mom liked her veggie omelet. They had a good amount of vegetarian options for breakfast. We all got take home boxes cause we only ate half.

text:
I am obsessed with Sukhothai. I tell everyone it's my favorite restaurant in New Orleans. It just really hit the spot every time with that delicious combo of salty and savory and umami. I think their dishes are really consistent and excellent. All the curries are fabulous, I love the drunken fried rice, the Tom kha soup, there's something about the curry noodles that is just magical, And pretty much everything else I've tried there is great. The chicken satay is so tender and delicious! The vegan eggplant lover is beyond. I could go on forever.

They also have a lot of fun drink specials! Every day of the week has something different. I think Thursday is half-price bottles of wine, and Sunday is five dollar cocktails. And they have a quite a big cocktail menu!

I go here all the time for takeout or to dine in. The seated service can be a little weird sometimes. Everyone seems nice and well-meaning but sometimes it ends up being kind of slow. Well worth it for the amazing food though.

If you like Thai food, I definitely think Sukhothai has the best in New Orleans, and some of the best I've ever had.
