text: a great old school bar.  a bit dark, a bit crowded, a bit old school....just the kind of place that Sam Spade would hang out at.
name: Craig

text: Extremely rude staff.  Went in to pick up a to-go order and the man at the register didn't say a word, didn't look up, nothing.  The waitresses walked by and rolled their eyes at me.  Don't know if it was the color of my skin but it sure felt that way.  Then finally when I asked about the order they simply pointed to a shelf behind me without a word.  Horrible way to treat a patron of your business.
name: Geoff

text: The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. The wait felt longer than it should have. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Probably not coming back. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..
name: User

text: Besides the fact that this place is veteran owned, everything I've tried has been delicious.  Do not skip the mac & cheese - you'll regret it for eternity.
name: Carlos

text: I love coming home back to the city because I always go to Cajuns to get some crawfish and a hot sausage poboy! Nothing compares. I was so sad to leave because I knew I wasn't going to be able to find food like this in Dallas. The first time I came was on Saturday around lunch time. And we got 6 pounds of crawfish with 2 big shots. Then later on that day we got 2 more pounds of crawfish lol. Yeah, we had been craving some good crawfish so we had to double back. And finally, right before we left to come back to Dallas we got hot sausage poboys, 2 more big shots, and a box of mama noodles. Yes, you can say it was a pretty good experience. I'm just counting the days I can come back home and get some again.
name: Alesia

text: Amazing new restaurant from the creators of Philadelphia's Parc. I hesitate to say it's better than Parc but it might be just that; waitstaff was attentive, food service was speedy and portion sizes larger. The food service was so fast in fact that if you want a drawn out leisurely meal (as we did) order your appetizers and eat before you order the entrees. We sat in a small room on the second floor that was quieter than the rest of the restaurant with some of the most comfortable chairs I've used at a restaurant to date. 10 out of 10 for food, service, atmosphere and presentation. Dessert is also a must, the French opera cake was not too sweet and the perfect end to a great meal.
name: Emma

text: Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. The wait felt longer than it should have. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Wouldn't really choose this place again. Not bad for a quick meal. It looked better online than it did in person. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Food was fresh and service was quick.
name: User

text: Great food choices ....fresh fruit & veggies was perfect...good service...reasonably priced
name: Bernadette

text: Amazing service! The people that work here are great and do everything they can to take care of their customers. The food, unfortunately is mediocre at best and the pricing is ridiculous for what you get. I didn't take pictures of the food but it looked nothing like the pictures I did see on Yelp before ordering. Maybe we went on a bad night?  Again, the wait staff was great!
name: Scott

text: World class food, and polite service. Speedy delivery. The inventors of the strombili sure do still make them taste amazing. The milkshakes are very well done too. There's often a lot of police eating there and sometimes tour buses from out of town. Very highly recommended.
name: James

text: Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. So yeah, they mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. not sure I'd order the same thing again. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent.
name: User

text: The food was good and the service was easygoing. Food was fresh and service was quick. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. A very pleasant experience. Would probably stop in again if nearby. The food was good and the service was easygoing.
name: User

text: This place was just ok. We had sushi's rolls and clams to start. Clams were just ok sushi was decent but who can screw up a California roll. Lamb was very good! We had the salmon special and it came out very dry. The Mac and cheese of awful! Do NOT order it. The service was the best part of the meal. Pass this is one by not good at all for the $$$
name: Richard

text:
Ordered a burger, fries and a shake.  I visited in on a quiet evening.  

Price was a little higher than other fast food places,  but not too bad.  I was pleasantly surprised by the service; It only took six minutes for my food to arrive.

The burger was typical, but pretty good for a fast food place.  The fries were average at best, and the oreo shake was nice. 

The only negative was that I ordered my burger without mayo, and they put it on anyway. Everything would have been great if they hadn't screwed that up.
name: James

text: This was our first time visiting this place.   We were greeted from the back of the restaurant straight ghetto.  The place looks like someone home.  Someone's old car seat in front of the entrance and a printer and obsolete computer near the bar area.  There were so many flies around our food once it was served.   Very disturbing experience.   Someone should go back to restaurant hotel management school and re-train on proper greeting of customers,food preparation etiquette to ensure your following Dinning out best practices.  By the way the food was ok but they ran out of collard greens, potato salad and yams and it was only 2:30 pm in the afternoon.   My advice... Try a different place to get soul food with better service!
name: Nille

text:
Pretty good lunch spot, have to say. The portions are outrageously huge and very tasty. Always order the smaller portion because it's basically an xl portion (for example, we got a calzone and it was the size of half of a pizza). The subs were pretty tasty but kind of set up like a taco. 

Don't forget you need to order at the counter. They won't take your order at the table!
name: Kelsey

text: Wow. I'm sitting inside this place at 420PM on a Tuesday and it's absolutely disgusting. First review on yelp. I had to make one. I paid 10 dollars for a bowl that looked like a bowl of rice and 4 slivers of chicken on it. There is a trash picker upper sitting on the floor where the tables are and has trash overfilling. The sauces are a complete reck. Management needs to get ahold of this place. What a joke. Love pollo tropical but I won't be coming to this one again.
name: Derek

text: Best Italian in Boise...by far. Service is always good, and the food is consistently outstanding.
name: Marty

text: Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. Wouldn't really choose this place again. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Food was fresh and service was quick. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text: Stopped by for an early lunch on a whim.  Got the lamb pita.  It was one of the tastiest sandwiches I have ever consumed.  Long line but it moved fast.  Staff was very friendly.  It's a Solomonov place so your going to try it regardless of what yelp says but here you are right for doing so.  Can't wait to try more.
name: Dan

text:
Decided to come here after hearing all the hype about this place and quiet honestly it didn't reach my expectations. Don't get me wrong, it isn't bad chicken at all - it is quite good, it just isn't anything necessarily special. Long story short, I live on the west side and I don't think I'd be making a trip anytime soon to go here. 
Again, it is good! Just nothing special about it at all.
It is pretty inexpensive which is nice but it is also VERY small (space wise and table size) so if you're coming with more than one person and planning to sit in you'll probably be out of luck. 
I got the onion lover and the boy got the garlic and soy. The macaroni salad was good, again nothing spectacular but I will say the corn fritter was to die for, it was super addictive.

Over all if you want the best Korean fried chicken in e-town I'd highly suggest ITdog over any other fried chicken place.
name: Nicole

text: The bacon cheese burger was absolutely awful!  The meat was old tasting and the fries were horrible and cooked in old oil!  Need to change your fryer oil more often!!  Not quality food at this diner!! Will not be back to this location again!!
name: Kristyn

text:
I am obsessed with ramen! It is one of my favorite dishes. This particular restaurant doesn't offer half bowls only full bowls at about $14. I ordered the spicy miso, I also ordered the chicken bites. The broth itself was a little lemony in my opinion, the noodles were flatter than what I was expected. The portion is really large for the money. I didnt finish.

The chicken bites were very tender and good with the sauce they provide with it. A tad pricy though, $6 for basically nuggets.
name: Kami

text: Came here for a quick lunch and snack. This place is situated on University, which can get quite busy. We chose to sit outside, in the beautiful patio area. The weather was amazing, and there was plenty of shade. I ended up ordering the babaganoush, which is in my opinion overall a better choice than hummus. I was not disappointed. The flavors were on point, with a nice smokiness and some solid pita. The edges of the pita were a bit tough, but overall it was great. My friend got fries and shawarma, which he enjoyed. He also felt the baba ganoush was excellent, and he is actually more familiar with these flavors than I am. Got some to go later in the week as well. Will definitely come back!
name: Kathy

text: Amazing food. Some of the best Mediterranean food in Tucson and definitely the best place in the food court. Wish they weren't in a mall!! So so good.
name: Amalek

text: Didn't know what to expect and was pleasantly surprised. We got the meal in a bag....tons of shrimp, mussels and fish. Very tasty, albeit kind of messy, the name of the restaurant is spot on. We'll be back, I'd like to try some of the other "bag" offerings.
name: Dave

text: I love this place! It has such a great vibe. The staff is so nice and this past weekend we got to eat outside for the first time which was amazing. I love that it is BYOB. The Chicken Parm is next level and I loved the Gnocchi my husband had as well. If you want to support an awesome neighborhood family restaurant, this is the place to go!
name: Danielle

text: Found Beach Shanty Cafe while waiting for our room to be ready.  It was around 2:30, so we had the place to ourselves.  It's very small, but it was clean and decorated beautifully.  I ordered the Philly Cheesesteak.  It was pretty good, the bread was fresh, but I would've liked for the meat to have had a little more flavor, and the cheese was a little sparse.  My husband ordered the patty melt.  He loved it.  I tried it and like it a lot, it was cheesy and the sauce was so rich.  The service was very good; the waitress checked on us often.  The restroom was just okay, not great but not awful.  We would go back and try other items.
name: Lanissa

text: This place has changed ownership, it is now Sentinel Peak and it is good. Some of the same great staff and a couple great new ones. The cooks are amazing and the food rocks. This place is owned by firefighters. Great drinks as well. They smoke a lot of there  meats , even the wings. It's all good. I've tried most of the menu. If you can finish the nachos my hats is off to you.
name: Jim

text: Super good food and the owners are sweet people also. At the risk of of ruining a good thing and not getting a table anymore this is a fantastic place and recommend it highly. The baklava is amazing!
name: Robert

text:
There is a lot to like about Flat 12.  They have a wide variety of beers to choose from.  They have a large patio with plenty of spots to sit in sun or shade.  They share a space with Hoagies & Hops, so you can get really good sandwiches without having to bring it with you or wait for a delivery.  There are lots of televisions to catch the latest games/events too.  Basically, it has about all you would want for a relaxing location to sip a beer and enjoy being with friends.

I won't say it is my favorite brewery, but I definitely enjoy coming here.  Like a lot of places, parking is somewhat limited to street parking.  

Note:  Dorman is one way northbound, so head east on New York St to get here.

Review #984
name: Ken

text: Had the spicy salmon roll and the Fantastic roll! Absolutely phenomenal, both of them! I highly suggest the (very affordable) Sauvignon Blanc to pair!
name: Seth

text: Okay the food was delicious but they are so slow. To stay this is a more upscale restaurant they do not move very fast. We made a reservation and still waited to be seated. They took forever to take our order and even longer to bring everything out. Our waiter was very polite but the kitchen is just so slow man. I wouldn't go if you are a person that gets hangry.
name: Eboni

text: Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. For the price I expected more than this. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..
name: User

text: This is my favorite place for lunch or to stop by for a dinner takeout order. Food is always fabulous with a good variety of appealing and healthy menu options. Can't say enough good things about this restaurant. All 3 locations are equally appealing.
name: Christina

text: My husband and I ate here this past Saturday for the first time. We sat on the patio, which is really nice and has a large amount of tables and a bar. Our server was very friendly but she was stretched too thin because there weren't enough servers for the patio area. Drinks and food took a while to arrive. We ordered the seafood sampler for our appetizer and it was delicious! Our entrees were just ok. My husband got the lasagna and I had a crabcake sandwich with fries. My sandwich came out about 15 minutes after the lasagna. We were ready to go by the time it arrived. The lasagna was piping hot but lacked flavor. We may try again but next time we'll eat inside.
name: K.

text: The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. The staff seemed tired but still polite. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Will be back. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Food was fresh and service was quick. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..
name: User

text: The photos made it look a little better than it actually was. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text: I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. For the price I expected more than this. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait.
name: User

text: I had heard good things about the Zionsville Rosie's so I was looking forward to going to the Carmel location.  My friend and I ordered omelettes.  What we were served was not an omelette.  They cooked the eggs and then put the ingredients on top and folded it.  The eggs were overcooked and tasteless.  The entire concoction was dry and it was a challenge to try to get a bite of egg with some of the add-ins as it wasn't cooked together like an omelette should be.  My friend ordered avocado on hers and cold avocado was sliced and placed on top of her omelette.  The potatoes had been sitting around for awhile and the biscuit was just okay.  The service was spotty at best.  Very disappointing.
name: Rebecca

text: When I booked my reservation for Dickie Brennan's I knew I was going to one of the best steakhouses in New Orleans. I was not disappointed. The service was top notch and the food was as well. Was a little weird having 3 servers, but they eventually melded into one excellent team. My family and I split BBQ Shrimp and Bone Marrow Escargot for appetizers and both were very good. Had to fight my son for the shrimp. Steaks were all cooked perfect, even my Porterhouse. The sides were all good, but the Miriliton poached in butter with a beet sauce stole the show! Will definitely take friends and family here again.
name: Doug

text:
My whole family went to Peddlers Village last night!  All 15 of us were there!  I asked my family prior, if we should make reservations, they said no that's ok I'm sure they have food trucks for such a busy season.
Myself being in retail for 30 years, understand how busy it is during the holidays.  However, when we went to Hart's bar at that point, there was 6 of us.
We stood in line, several people behind us, the place was packed!
We were slowing trying to get in cuz there was SO MANY PEOPLE, that I was holding the door open so was the girl in front of me! 
This man came out of no where and screamed" You can't leave that door open! In or out!"  I said "I understand, but there's a line to get in" He yelled back" Doesn't Matter in or OUT!"   I said to my family, "Let's go! That guy is a d*#k!!  I told them we will NEVER go there EVER!! 
To the man that yelled at me, granted I should've made reservations, but that's not the point!! You were VERY RUDE!! And by the way my brother, who was there in the back of the line, heard what you said to me, and he could buy that bar very easily!! But instead he had choice words and wanted to do more than that, because that "joker" was rude to his sister , but he was also rude to a woman!
name: Lisa

text:
Who wouldn't want a winery that is within walking distance to your house? Well your in luck, senoras and señores Nashville Urban Winery is your answer! 

The atmosphere is cool and chill. They have a few areas that felt really urban. 

Their "indecisive white blend" is amazing! Make sure you order it. You will thank your palate for it! 

Also I HIGHLY recommend their Italian meatballs. It is DELICIOUS!! You will never look at another meatball the same. 

Make sure to stop by their shop to pick up a few canned wine, you can bring them to concerts, picnic, family gatherings and boring company conferences or retreats you will thank yourself for it!
name: Horton

text: Horrible service. What a waste of time going there. It was dead and yet still took over an hour to make one egg sandwich and then another 15 minutes to ask for the check. And during this whole time, we never once saw our bartender. We had to ask the kitchen staff for our check.
name: Molly

text: Good place excellent food the customer service is 10, they are very welcoming and friendly staff
name: Belkis

text:
Basically what you would expect from a large touristy mass-beer hosted place. 
Cool that it's across from the stadium and in a bar-hall type place that projects lots of games and events. 

Expect mediocre food, expensive drinks, and a touristy atmosphere. If that's what you like, this is your place! If you're generally a little more crafty and more of a foodie, I'd keep looking.
name: Sally

text: Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Nice little spot, decent portions too. No big complaints, just a nice meal. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. For the price I expected more than this.
name: User

text: My cousin told me that she wanted to go to this restaurant for the longest time. After I got off work we walked over and it was BUSY & smelled good. Any time a food place is busy and smells good that is a good sign to me. Our wait was about 20 minutes, which it did not feel like it.  It was our first time going so we asked what was best on the menu for 1st timers. We both enjoyed our meal and the shrimp tempura is absolutely amazing! Very affordable and tasty food. text:
I'm going to preface this post by first saying that I am not a beer expert in any way--I actually prefer wine over beer. However, the selection here is nice and diverse and they had a good number of lighter beers, which I liked! Also, my friend and I split the loaded potato pizza, and I was pleasantly surprised at how good it was (I'm originally from NYC so I have a high pizza standard)! The crust was so perfect--super crunchy, thin, tons of flavor. I will definitely be coming back for the other pizzas! 

The decor is very simple and understated but also trendy and modern. The space is also really big--there's a back room that I didn't even get to see. They also offer 3 sizes of beer, which is also a nice perk for those of us who don't like to drink high volumes of it. 

A few drawbacks: walking towards it, it is extremely bright and you can literally see everything because it's all windows. I would say maybe dim the lights a little just so it's not so blinding. Also, they opened all the windows halfway through the night which made it SO cold. They said it was because it was getting warm for the workers and they also wanted to keep the glasses cold because they just came out of the dishwasher? I just thought it was unnecessary and made all the customers put their jackets on, which isn't fun. Overall though, a good experience, and I look forward to coming back (just keep the windows closed in winter)!

We approached the cashier desk as we were waiting to be seated and it didn't take long for the host to recognize some new customers and seat us. The host was very friendly and amiable. She sat us and took our drink orders. We ordered just water to start. That was our mistake. We didn't realize they serve TAP water. Not filtered tap water but straight tap water. I don't want to seem crazy for making this a bigger deal than it is, but I don't drink tap water anywhere just because of water contamination and how bad it's become all over the country. So bottle water or filtered water is all we and our families drink. That would have to be the only downfall about this place. That and maybe just making their waitresses seem more welcoming to guests and not just a potential tip. The food was great though. I ordered the #1 breakfast special and it filled me up perfectly. Decent price and good food, just don't order the water until they start serving filtered water or you're  comfortable with exposing yourself to potentially dangerous bacteria.
name: Freddy

text:
The great... the food. There is really something for everyone on the menu, vegans, keto, norms. Everyone and it's really tasty.

The good... the space is lovely and the tables are well spaced. The staff is attentive and helpful.

The oh dear... on a weekend the wait is ridiculous and then they end up in the weeds. The worst was when a dish was put on our table and then they attempted to take it away since it belonged to another order, but I had touched it. Oops. Also the same time that I didn't actually receive the correct entree but honestly by that time since it was something I would eat, I just did and said thank you.

I will definitely stop in on a random weekday. I no longer attempt Saturday or Sunday visits... maybe if I tried after 2pm? Also I've been in when a large party inside was so very loud that I could not hear my friend on the other side of the table. So it can get noisy. As for accessibility I *think* there's a ramp that takes you into the back of the building to access the restaurant. I have not attempted but it's a new build so there HAS to be an accommodation.
name: Jen

text:
Rainy day food at its best! We stopped in before tackling Reading Terminal Market, and that silly mistake led to an awesome ramen experience. Who goes to a restaurant before scoping out the market? Feel free to judge us on that alone, but we were not disappointed. I liked the chicken better than the pork, but that pork bun was on point. Our server was helpful and attentive. 

I saw a review that said no cards, maybe that is for a certain dollar amount. We paid with a card and no one asked us to change methods. 

Loved it, and it was exactly the right meal at the right time. The lunch special is a good deal too.
name: Katie

text:
This was the first meal I had in New Orleans during my weekend trip and it set the tone perfectly for the food adventures to come. I've always loved New Orleans style cooking but damn, the people here just blow my mind. Don't think I'll ever eat Cajun anywhere else again. 

Came for brunch. Parking sucks, but that's not unique to Atchafalaya. We ordered: grapefruit Bellini, shrimp and grits, chicken & biscuits, duck hash, and the étouffée omelet. We had "an hour" wait but was more like 20 mins. 

Everything was delicious, but things could've been better. Duck hash barely had duck, the étouffée omelet fell a little flat in flavor, the chicken and biscuits were divine (biscuits are the PERFECT amount of sweetness and fluff), and the shrimp and grits were above average, though I've had better. I would say omelet and chicken and biscuits were the better two dishes, but over all still an amazing meal!

Qualms: the price is a little steep compared to some nearby places, and the place is a little tiny. If you're cool with that then this would probably be the perfect place to come for a bougier but unarguably delicious meal.
name: Pandy

text: Would probably stop in again if nearby. Nice little spot, decent portions too. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Not bad for a quick meal. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Food was fresh and service was quick. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent.
name: User

text: The fries were probably the best part of the meal, honestly. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. Kind of landed in the middle for me. text:

text: We ate here about two months ago and thought it was great.  We just came back last Sunday, boy were we disappointed.  The girl who served us was clueless.  We asked her about a bottle of wine and she said "well pick one."  When she brought our pasta and pizza she slammed it on the bar top.  She made us feel like we were a bother.  The pizza was bland, we had a margarrita.  It had no flavor unlike the pizza (a margarrita) we had the last time.  The pasta was good, the sausage and mushrooms.  The service sucked and we will never go back.   We will never recommend this place do it's service.

After eating only a few bites, we both felt sick for the rest of the day. I had the pimento mac n cheese, and he had the bacon cheddar chicken burger. My mac n cheese was far from creamy and good, and his chicken was dry. The only food we enjoyed was the chips and queso. I like fast service, but this service was "too fast", we ordered and it came out only a few minutes later like it was already prepared hours before and just heated up. I would give it one star, but I am giving it 2 stars because the staff was 5 stars, they were one of the nicest staff I have ever met at a restaurant. I may have to give it another try, but my first experience was a no go.

text: To start my wife and I had the Persian lemon and cucumber cayenne gin and tonic. Both were delicious and deserving of the $9 price tag. Not too often does a restaurant admit a mistake AND take action. Hedge Row gets 5 stars for taste as well as most importantly customer service.

text:

the price i don't mind paying for a good steak it was $25.99 on promo. the server was nice.

text:
It is so sad to read from the news that Imperial Inn is closing as of today, 1/27/2019 after 45 years serving diners in the Philly area. We started coming to the restaurant in early 80s. My children grew up in learning dim sum in this restaurant. The entire staff was like a second family. We brought our friends and colleagues to this place. My American colleagues learned how to order dim sum and authentic Chinese dishes. This is an institution, second to none!

When we visit the Philly Chinatown in our next trip, we will terribly miss this place, its staff, and its authentic Chinese dishes!
name: Pauline

text: We love going to Blue Box Pizza, it's such a neat fun place! Staff is friendly and the food and drinks are great. My daughter loves their cheese pizza and I love their achiote pulled pork burrito (SO GOOD and spicy). Their margaritas are good. While you wait for you order, you can play some video games or draw whatever on their big white board.
name: Angelica

text: Met an old friend at Dolce Vita last night at his recommendation.  What a hidden jewel!  When's the last time you dined at an Italian restaurant where everything prepared is fresh and from scratch. I had the Chicken Marsala with penne pasta topped with marinara sauce. The penne pasta melted in my mouth and was cooked to perfection, not too soggy, but aldante.  My friend Steve had the Carbonara. Most Carbonara dishes are prepared in a heavy cream sauce but this one was not.  It was a lighter sauce but still with a superb bacon flavor.  The Ceasars dressing on my salad to begin was from scratch and flavourful. The tiramasou was the best I've had, dense in consistency and creamy in taste.  Portions were generous, service attentive and atmosphere was like dining at a good friend's home.  If you've never tried Dolce Vita you won't be disappointed.  It will become a new favorite as it has for me!
name: Mark

text: I usually come here for company functions, as it's near my job, but the food is absolutely amazing! The atmosphere is homey and intimate and the staff are friendly and so warm!

text: Nice river View good service great food Great valet service could you recommend anyone for a nice night.

text:
A great experience, different in many regards, but really good.  I imagined something like Zaytinya in Washington DC.  Loud, kind of modern, in a sprawling space. 

Well, I did know Zahav is in the one time Copper Penny bar, which wasn't huge. Zahav is loud, with happy diners, and a really wide mix of music blaring from new hip hop to 80s Joe Jackson and beyond.  The decor is country/homey/wooden. 

We were there on a Saturday before Christmas and seated promptly for our reservations at 7:30. Decided on the $48 pp tasting menu and the $36 pp wine flight. For the dinner, get choice of hummus (best I have had) with laffa and 3 small plates and dessert each. We shared and it was actually too much. Especially since we were comped a small plate of chicken shishkebob and a dessert. The halloumie cheese is gout inducingly good. 

Zahav is rich in flavors and overall decadent. The experience is great and differs from Zaytinya immensely.
name: Shaun

text:
This review is for brunch only: 

Located a few minutes drive from the French Quarter, Elizabeth's is definitely a neighborhood joint loved by (I'm assuming) both locals and tourists. The only thing I have to complain about this place is the wait. We came for brunch - It is extremely popular and waiting for a table under the scorching sun is not fun. Hide under the trees after you put your name down on the list! Also, food took 30 minutes+ to arrive after ordering. 

Food is good and simple - nothing to complain about at all. We ordered the Banana's Foster French Toast and the Shrimp & Grits! The food was really good, but not worth the long wait in my opinion. I would recommend it, but I think it's only worth trying it once for the fun ambiance and interesting decor. The Eggs Florentine looked good though, I would try that next time! Or, go for lunch (weekday) or dinner; the menu looks way more appetizing than the brunch one.
name: Alex

text:
Wavered between a 3 and a 4 star. The food was pretty good. I came on a weekend morning to grab some food and do some work. They have free wifi and a couple of outlets. The staff were friendly, especially early on a weekend. 

I got the Papayay bowl with an addition of spirulina and protein. The bowl looks small but it's definitely a lot of food! The bowl tasted good, but not amazing. There also weren't bananas on my bowl as advertised on the menu. Also, spirulina usually has a pretty strong taste, but I couldn't taste it at all in my bowl. Either they didn't add very much or forgot it? Since it's all blended, you can't really tell. Overall, it was a little disappointing but not bad tasting. I might go again and try something else, but only if I'm in the area or feeling particular about the food there.

text: It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. It was crowded but still moved along. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer..

text:
This hot breakfast/brunch/lunch spot is the epitome of a great value + tasty food combo.  I ordered the West Coast Omelette which had avocado, bacon, onion, and tomato.  It normally comes with feta, but I swapped for cheddar.  It was perfectly portioned with the side ingredients!  It came with hash browns and pancakes (your choice between a few things).  More than enough for a meal; in fact I had it the next day for breakfast, too!  Service was great as well.  We went on Christmas Eve and there wasn't a wait.  I've heard it can be quite busy on Sundays (and probably Saturdays), so be mindful of how long you have to eat and your party size.  

There were kids menus and coloring books to keep the kiddos busy while the big kids chat.  We barely had enough room for all the plates, but we all left with full, happy bellies.  

Looking forward to another trip during my next Indy visit!

text:
So Obama's been here. Automatic five stars. Just kidding (not really), but these po'boys are no joke. 

We came here less than an hour before closing on Saturday night and the place was still popping. We decided to order to go.

I split a large golden fried shrimp and a large Italian meatball with marinara and omg. I could barely finish half of a half. The large po'boys are huge (that's what she said?)! The fried shrimp really hit the spot and the meatball po'boy was savory and delicious (or maybe because I've been on a marinara sauce craze for the past 18 months?). It reminds me of a typical meatball sub... but for some reason, it was just better. But if you're looking for a more traditional po'boy, go with the fried shrimp. They give you so much protein (shrimp, meatball, whatever!) that you just can't be mad at that. 

We also picked up a couple desserts - the bread pudding and the rum cake. Both were UGH SO GOOD. Rich and decadent was the bread pudding; moist and rummy was the rum cake. I got the last piece of rum cake and we ordered the last slice of bread pudding, if I can remember correctly - it was just our luck!

There's a great outdoor patio for some communal seating and fun. Join in if you're willing to bask in the NOLA heat and humidity. 

Overall, a SOLID po'boy joint! Visit - even Obama did!
name: Tiff

I stopped by this bakery for breakfast and I had high expectations because I always see people eating on the patio on my way to work.
I ordered a build your own breakfast sandwich with egg, cheese, bacon, cheese, and spinach. The biscuit was hard, crumbled as I tried to eat the sandwich instead of absorbing the moisture. I expected it to be fluffy, buttery, and soft but it didn't meet any of those expectations.
The toppings were not flavorful at all and the egg tasted like it was thawed and microwaved. I asked for bacon and honestly, I'm not sure if they gave me sausage by mistake or it was a faux bacon but it definitely wasn't something I recognized.
All in all, the best part of this experience was the customer service and the homemade jam that they gave me for the biscuit. Even though my breakfast sandwich was an epic fail, I could be convincing try this place again for lunch or for one of their pastries since they are probably better known for their baked goods!
name: Tasha

text:
3.28.19 First time eating here, and we loved it! 

We all decided to meet after work for their Happy Hour. As we were about to enter the restaurant, I noticed a posting on their door saying "Prime Rib Night Every Thursday". It was a three-course dinner all for just $19.95. It just so happened that evening we chose to dine in was also a Thursday! 

We started off by ordering the Artisan Cheese Board, American Kobe Beef Meatballs, and the Italian Polenta Cakes. The Artisan Cheese Board was served with Cambozola Cheese, Fontina, White Cheddar, along with honey, pear, and assorted crackers. The American Kobe Beef Meatballs was served in a bowl of Mission Figs Demi Sauce mixed with a Humboldt fog Fondue, micro mint and crostini. Lastly, their Polenta Cakes were crusted with crispy parmesan, served in a Pomodoro Sauce with dollops of Mascarpone Cream, sprinkled with Italian Parsley. Having a cheese board is always a fun way to dine, and everything was absolutely delicious. When it came time for dinner, I was dead set on ordering their Prime Rib Special. As advertised, it was a three-course dinner, starting off with either a soup or salad, the prime rib, and lastly, vanilla bean ice cream. I opted for their soup, which was a hearty and tasty Chicken Posole Soup. Their prime rib was tender, juicy and served with steamed vegetables and a baked potato. I just kept thinking to myself that all of this was just $20! The ice cream was simple and a sweet way to end our dinner service. 

Service was notably on point throughout from beginning to end. Our waters were always filled and finished plates were promptly cleared. 

For being our first time dining at Napa Sonoma Grocery Company, we were all very much impressed. The atmosphere was casual and welcoming with such exceptional service. Their food was tasty and we left no survivors. Being so close to home, you can count on us visiting more often!
name: Cory

text: My sisters wedding reception was held on Sunday 3/19. I initially booked with Devin. I had about 5 items that were "up in the air," so when she sent me an email and informed me it was her last day I was initially concerned. However, Jessica made it an effortless transition. From the moment our event was turned over to her she made me feel like I was the only event she was working on. I worked in the hospitality industry prior to being a SAHM (spent a few years in the catering sales industry actually) so I know the ins and the outs. I didn't tell Jessica that and she still took care of me like I was VIP, despite the fact that our event was just a very small one. She called me on my cell phone to not only personally introduce herself but also to go over the BEO and answer any questions I had. There were a lot of intricate details to our little event but Jessica made sure it went without a hitch. The moment we stepped on property, the level of service we experienced was top notch. My husband travels often and stays at fabulous hotels and has dined with several Michelin-star chefs and he was extremely impressed with the level of service and the quality of food. We truly felt like we were the only event they were working on, when in fact there were two large weddings on property. Jessica was extremely thoughtful and upgraded our space from a partial view to a 180 ocean view and away from both weddings. I ruined the my sisters small cake I brought with me upon arrival on property. Juan came to introduce himself, rearranged the room according to the decor I was setting, saw the disastrous cake and went above and beyond his call of duty. He had the pastry chef not only fix it but made it look like a brand new cake with floral decor and detailing. The pastry chef Savannah was gracious enough to fix the cake for us and brought it up with an introduction. As I mentioned previously, I have worked in the hospitality for years and to say I was beyond impressed with Jessica, Juan, Savannah, Oscar, Jaime and Audrey is an understatement. They truly made us feel welcomed and so very special. We certainly could not have pictured a more perfect reception and ending to a very memorable weekend. Thank you and your fabulous catering/banquet team for an unforgettable experience and we look forward to staying with you again!
name: Julie

text:
Came here Saturday afternoon around 1:30pm. They had a buffet that looked fairly good so we opted for the buffet. The hot food looked pretty good and was very tasty. The enchiladas were okay - just hamburger rolled with corn tortilla and a little sauce poorer over the top. But the really bad thing was the cold section was empty. No salsa, no pico, no sour cream, no cheese and only a few tomatoes. So you could get your taco fillings but no toppings for it at all. Really disappointing :(. I will never return for the buffet. I really wanted chips and salsa but they don't bring it to the table when you order the buffet and since there was no salsa at the buffet no chips and salsa for me. 
And I understand the buffet was over at 2 but when you're purchasing something you expect to get what you paid for. 
I am not one to say anything while in the restaurant because I don't like to cause an issue. Just one of those things where I learned not to do the buffet.  I suggest looking it over and know what you see is what you will get. There is no restocking it.

The brisket came on a cutting board with tortillas, white onions, bbq sauce and pickles. I think this is the best brisket I have ever had. We went with friends who used to live in California and she said that the food was as good as she'd get there, so that's a pretty strong endorsement. It's not a place you go for the ambiance, but the food and service are consistent good and we go with the family nearly every week. The kids love the place too!

text: Great food, service and ambiance. Try the fish tacos they were excellent. Very interesting and eclectic food menu and drinks, especially the bacon! The staff is very welcoming and upbeat and they did not rush us out. Great for groups of friends who want to talk and celebrate. I would recommend Keen to any foodie! I'll be back...

text: We Checked this spot out through a yelp find. We didn't know it was all Vegan so when we placed our order we were expecting chicken and beef. The waiter wanted us to be surprised but we wished we would have known so we could have ordered differently. If we would have known we would have ordered items without "meat". Definitely a unique restaurant for those who are vegans and plant based! The staff was really nice and Joe, the owner is a really nice guy. I would highly recommend this restaurant to those with dietary restrictions such as gluten or vegans ! So many options on the menu and it is homemade ! The dessert menu was good as well !

text:
This is amazing Vietnamese food from a Mall Food Court, who knew?  I go all the time from the King of Prussia area, drive right by their location in the KOP Mall and go up to Montgomery Mall. It is worth the drive as the food is that much better. 
The guy that works the counter remembers me now and pretty much knows my order. Hahahaha. The broth of the Pho is super complex and tasty and tons of meat and other things in the beef Pho. There is also some Thai chili paste on your plate. This stuff is legit spicy. Only a little and your soup is totally spiced up. Whoa!  My favorite Pho place in Philadelphia. Keep it up guys!

text: Tried this spot for lunch during a work break. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. I'd maybe go back, but I'd order differently next time. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.

text:
When visiting this restaurant make sure to check that the food preparers are wearing gloves. In my personal experience the food preparers were not wearing gloves while handling my food. Who ever is in charge must be oblivious to this because I've also witnessed the manager on duty "bump" my order off the screen before my meal was ready because the fries were taking too long. text: I want to love goldie.  I went a few times and the first few I liked it but recently it seems they added cilantro to their cucumber mix so I have stopped going.  What I do love there are their tahini milkshakes - so good as well as the tahini sauce and the falafels. They do have a 'bag of balls' to go which is just the falaffel. Maybe it would be good to get that and bring it across the street to dizengoff?

text:
Another Tucson local gem loved by my wife's sisters (locals)!

They come here often and we followed their lead.  It's similar to Punch Pizza in the Minneapolis area, but a bit more upscale and they also offer pasta and homemade soups.  They also do table service if you desire.

We placed our orders.  One sister and hubby split a Caesar salad and a lasagna pie, another sister and hubby split a Margarita pie with prosciutto, we had a Suprema Pizza substituting the normal red onions and Crimini mushrooms with Kalamata Olives and artichoke hearts.  Our very attentive server Alan took excellent care of us.  

The house red and Pinot Grigio house wines were very good, as was the Butter Chardonnay.  There are a number of other red and white wines as well as beer and soft drink options.  Salad lovers will find a dozen choices and can add chicken or salmon, if desired.

They also have locations in the Phoenix, Scottsdale, Mesa and Gilbert areas too.
name: Todd

text: Great tasting pizza, just disappointed by the delivery. Delivery guy knocked on the door and asked for payment. Once I handed him the payment his demeanor instantly changed. He then opened both the boxes acting as if he was inspecting them and then removed the 2 ranch sauces, stating that I did not pay for them...What!!? My jaw was left on the ground in disbelief!  He sped away in his obnoxiously loud Honda Civic
name: Max

text:
Excellent food!

First of all, this place has HAPPY HOUR ALL DAY, everyday which includes $3.50 house wine, margs, selected beers, and well drinks. I had the $3.50 house wine - you can't beat that deal!

This restaurant has a very relaxed, casual vibe to it which you don't often get at a seafood spot. They have peanuts at the front that you can grab yourself and I loved the chalkboard menu. They have a variety of fresh fish everyday that is very reasonably priced. Each fish comes with two sides (veggies and rice but I think you can substitute). 

My brother tried the Barramundi fish and a cup of chowder (which they are famous for). I started with a side salad and had the Ultimate Combo which included a salmon filet, shrimp skewer, and a crab cake. All of it was delicious. I particularly loved the crab cake. Note, the portions are huge here!

We had great service (the manager came over to check on us which is always nice) and we were extremely impressed with the value and quality of the seafood. 

I'll definitely be back next time I'm in Tampa!
name: Lele

text: No big complaints, just a nice meal. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. No big complaints, just a nice meal.
name: User

text: This isn't your typical review because I've never actually set foot in this restaurant. My mom gave me leftovers she had from here, a fish taco, at her hotel. 60 seconds in the microwave made me appreciate the spice profile and the well cooked texture. Not every places food aged well, even if it's less than a day, so I feel like this deserves some credit to the chef.
name: Dominik

text:
We came here on a Saturday night before heading into Philly.  I absolutely love good Poke and was looking forward to my meal.  Having spent two weeks on the Big Island and two weeks in Oahu, I have had my fair share of island poke.  
The set up is similar to most poke shops in Philly.  You select your base, choose two scoops of protein (you can opt for one or three) and then choose toppings, sauce and crunch.  The owners were genuinely nice people who took the time to discuss their new poke shop with us.  Super friendly and welcoming.  
The shop has only been open since December so there is a lot of room for enhancement using customer suggestions and trying new items.  The portions were generous and they allowed us to sample items.  I prefer my poke marinated in the sauce rather then having it squirted onto it as I order.   There were some items that were not currently available (Garlic edamame and furikake to name two) but perhaps could be in the future.   It would have been been nice to have additional sauce selections also.   I did ask for the spicy mayo which another reviewer mentioned was kept in the fridge.   Good addition to my poke bowl.  

The owners seemed open to suggestions and we wish them the best in their new business endeavor.
name: Lori

text:
The few people giving low ball review scores here should probably have their taste buds checked or maybe try brushing their teeth more often. Regardless, they're definitely off their rockers and have no clue what they're talking about. 

Eric and his family are some of the nicest people I've met and the food is delicious. The sauce can definitely be heavy, but if you prefer less sauce, ask for less. It's literally as simple as that. To those saying the chicken has no flavor, I just don't get it. I usually need a ton of salt to be satisfied, but with both the blackened and regular chicken, whatever is on it is great (I do prefer the blackened chicken). 

Anyone thinking they're going to get handmade pasta at $10-12:/dish is smoking rocks. Anyone thinking they're entitled to free bread when the dishes all cost around $10-12 and have freshly made sauce is smoking rocks. This business is family owned, it's not a major corporation. It seems that the people bashing this guy are just cheap af and are making statements they definitely can't back up. Not to mention that one of the bad reviewers gave Sopapilla's a 5 star rating (comical lol) and another gave a McDonald's a 5 star rating (even more comical).

Do yourself a favor and listen to the 95% or so reviews that say this place is awesome. The majority is definitely not wrong here.
name: Travis

text:
Thought I would try a new "pineapple" beer with dinner last night. The beer arrived and after taking a few sips I wasn't a fan. The server came by and asked what I thought, I shared.She insisted on replacing it with another beer and I told her it wasn't necessary, I was happy to pay for the drink. Not two minutes later the manager arrived at my table to inform me that he would take the beer off my tab as long as I promised that next time I ordered a beer I would get a  taster so that I didn't waste their beer. I told him (again) I was happy to pay for it, but he poked me in the arm and said "no, next time get a taster-this is a limited edition beer and we don't want to waste any of the beer, we only have one barrel left"

I'm confused. I ordered something, was willing to pay for ieven though I didn't like it, but instead I was given a lecture by a condescending manager about how I'm wasting precious beer? text:
1/2.  Dined on 1/27/18 
My boyfriend brought me here for my birthday and had been planning to do so because he swore it was the best place in Philly to go after a good experience with a friend, so he was very excited to share it with me for the occasion. I was excited to try somewhere new and trusted his experience. 
To say we were disappointed is a severe understatement. 
We were seated after a short wait although we had a reservation, no one offered to take our coats which I had observed to be abnormal, but I am actually glad because I was under a vent and had to put my coat back on by the time the meal came.  It took a while for us to be greeted and once we were there was no real welcome or guidance from the server, no recommendation just mentioned a salad that was an add on and then she was off.  Waters were filled eventually and then she came back...  I ordered a cocktail, sans egg whites due to an allergy, asked her if it would still taste good and she said she'd check with the bartender, then the drink was dropped off...and it actually tasted like what I imagine a cocktail made of the kitchen cleaners under my sink would taste like, if that was going to be the case I would have passed but no one checked on it after it was delivered anyway so I attempted to drink it, hoping it would taste better with time, nope not really. After some time another random sever came to take our order, again told him of the allergy since he asked which was slightly confusing that now we had two servers. They were absolutely understaffed or disorganized or inexperienced because the service was really lacking to even average establishment expectations. We ordered two toast an entree and a small plate.  The toast came out after some tiny little soups, no bread though which were on other people's. The one toast had delicious kumquats on it and that was probably my favorite thing I ate all night, the other toast was the pumpkin butter and it really wasn't anything special.  Then after a decent wait in a very loud crowed room making it hard to really chit chat our food came out after I watched them replate it on the expo line. I had the small plate lamb, it seemed to be cooked okay,not warm though,  and the chimichurri complimented it well but the "whipped potatoes" were more like weak potato soup, runny and tasteless. It was a sub par dish for a "nicer restaurant". My boyfriend ordered the venison which came out cold, tasted like beef jerky and was over seasoned, and the veggies it came with were beyond over cooked.  Not a single sever checked on us during our meal so we couldn't even voice our concerns.  So we ate because we were hungry and trying to make the best of it. After a period of empty plates they were cleared and desserts were offered.  As I already noticed with the dinner menu the menu is a little different then online which left me with only one choice thanks to my allergy.  The spec sorbet..."Myer lemon"...should have have been titled "frozen pine sol" it was so gross, and tiny, giving two soup spoon was a joke and I am 99% sure the thin waffle cookie that was served with it had eggs in it because it was brought by someone who wasn't even our sever and those cookies normally have eggs in them (when you have allergies you get good at learning what to avoid...or else) so that could be very unsafe...or it would have been nice to be reassured that it was egg free like most places do...you know C.Y.A. And to top off the disappointment there wasn't even a candle on the dessert dish and my boyfriend told them it was a bday celebration....while the table behind us received sparkling wine on the house for their occasion (I know this because I saw it arrive and basically heard their entire conversation, not sure if it was because of the cramped conditions or their over the top loudness or a combo) .  Then some other random dropped the checked and ran the card.  No consistency.  It was unsettling, we never felt like a priority or even like our table mattered other than an order to get out and a table to turn and burn.  I worked in the restaurant business for almost a decade of my life  before I started my career in health care and I hate leaving bad reviews but I also know when an experience is terribly wrong and I am usually very lenient because I know things happen behind the scenes and shifts can be brutal  but this was sloppy and a disappointment after all the hype and high expectations.
name: Gina

text:
Michael Solomonov team has done it again. Man oh man, is K'Far worth the visit. Zahav is by far our favorite restaurant, so we had to try K'Far out ASAP. Located right near Rittenhouse, the location is perfect. Yelp reviews suggested a long line, but we only waited for ~10 minutes before placing our order at the counter, so not bad at all (easier than waiting 3 months for a Zahav res)! We arrived ~11:30ish on Labor Day, so it was a little crowded, and they had run out of a few items, so just keep that in mind if visiting later in the day. 

For eats, we both got the grilled cheese on the Jersualem bagel (my BF wanted the egg and cheese, but had run out). This was a great spin on a classic grilled cheese - with kashkaval cheese instead of American, roasted tomato, and za'atar, we were definitely vibing with the Israeli flavors. We attempted to order the pistachio sticky buns and chocolate babka, but unfortunately, they were both out. Instead, we chose the tehina chocolate chip cookie and the chocolate rugelach (which they wound up giving complimentary). The cookie was delightful, very dense with just a hint of the tehina flavor to cut the sweetness a tad. The rugelach were surprisingly delicious as well - often, I find this pastry dry, but K'Far's take was incredibly moist and chock-ful of chocolate flavor, so definitely proving me wrong! Lastly, I tried the Yemenite latte and my BF had the cappuccino. I'm not usually one to order "fancy" drinks, but I am SO glad I did - this latte was devine, so creamy and delicious with unique flavors of cardamon, cinnamon, and ginger. The cappuccino was tasty too, but would 100% recommend the Yemenite latte :) 

To top off our great experience, Michael Solomonov himself was actually serving and delivering food to tables! We had to do a double take to make sure it was actually him, but indeed was. He delivered our food, so we got to snag a pic with him and chat for a few. A very humble and kind dude, and so cool that he gets to hang at K'Far by day and Zahav by night. K'Far did not disappoint, and we are so excited to try the Solomonov team's other upcoming endeavors. And I'm already looking forward to another K'Far visit for that latte and some of their other pastries :)
name: Rebecca

text:
Had dinner with friends while in Tampa. We went to this location as they recommended. There were seven of us (4 adults, three kids). 

Service here is slow, so be prepared to wait for food. What I wasn't prepared for was to wait for drinks and the bill and to go boxes etc. 

We orders 2 fried rice, Ramen, soup, beef and spicy pork bulkigi. The food was delicious and worth the wait. The beef was tender and a little sweet. The spicy pork was also tender and had good heat without sending anyone to the ER. The fried rice is enough for two people. Our kids could have easily split the dish. The rice was great also, very good flavor without having to add soy sauce or other seasoning. We, of course, got all the fixings to go with it. The onion salad mixed with the beef bulgoki is excellent. 

I wanted to rate this restaurant higher, but sub par service limits me to three stars. If you aren't in a hurry I would highly recommend. If you are in a hurry, maybe pick another destination.

text:
We went on a Monday afternoon and it was not busy at all, both in the arcade and restaurant side. I did the dine and play deal that gave me a choice of an entree and a $20 power play card that gave me 100 credits. Each game cost about 6.6 and up. The most expensive games are the ones from the App Store like angry birds which was 9.9 credits. 

When you get to the restaurant area, you just pick a seat and a server will come to you. I got the caveman combo and it was pretty good. The ribs had a hoisin Asian taste to it. The sliders were just plain. But the totchos are the best, crispy and cheesy with loads of bacon bits. Service was great. 

Parking is $10 and it is located on the 6th Floor. There were two games that were broken but you just have to call someone over and they will give you credits to play any game you want. Tickets are stored onto your play card so do not lose it. I recommended downloading the app so you can store your play card's information. Just in case, you have to lose it and that you can keep track of your credits and tickets. Credits do expire after a 45 day time period but tickets do not. I would definitely come again on an off day like this.

text:
Constructive criticism review coming here.

My wife and I wanted to give this 5 stars since we live down the street. A few hang ups stopped us unfortunately, but none of which couldn't be fixed! 

Our waitress Tristen was fantastic. She knew the menu very well and was able to recommend the best options based on our preferences. The food itself had innovative flavor profiles and was prepared well. My wife had the barbacoa taco and the grouper taco, and I had the mongolian wok bowl. Everything tasted great, however the portion sizes seemed small for the price. I, unfortunately, left hungry after the wok bowl (5'8 170lbs guy here). Ordered three tacos to go for lunch tomorrow will update tomorrow after nom nomming them :)

Similarly, the appetizer (duck fig and brie dumplings) came with only 3 dumplings at $10 and the filling was minimal and we could not detect any brie. 

The drinks were perhaps the most disappointing. We came on Wednesday night for the $2 off drink special, so we tried several. We tried the just in thyme old fashioned, the marble rye, the five island mojito, the salt aire margarita and the honey margarita.  All were very promising as they had unique flavor profiles, but the common theme was that the alcohol was undetectable across all 5 drinks and sweetness was the prevalent feature. The drinks all had excellent presentation and looked fantastic with great garnishes!

After getting 5 drinks, the waitress mentioned the "orbs" at the bar, which are not advertised on the menu. We would have liked to try them, but were not aware of them until several drinks in. There is a seasonal feature, that should be called out either on the menu or on a specials page so that patrons are aware of the option. 

The decor and ambiance was festive and fun, we loved the little touches such as the salt and pepper shakers shaped like beverage shakers, the neon signs and the music. 

To sum up we feel the portion sizes on the bowls should be a bit larger, the tacos should be about .50 cents cheaper for their size, and the drinks just a bit boozier. Cheers!

Excited to see how this place evolves!
name: Ryan

text:
Although this location has changed from the original renovated corner store location opened as New Orleans was recovering from Hurricane Katrina, Ruby Slipper continues to deliver innovative Cajun inspired breakfast foods with Southern warmth. The Ruby Slipper reference translates to the Spirit of New Orleans in post-Katrina recovery, in that "there's no place like home." 

In the spirit of Urban renewal, this location is also housed in a historically renovated building. Built in 1951, it was a carpenters union hall that had been empty post-Katrina. The renovation features permeable paving to help improve storm water drainage (and is much easier than the limited parking for the original location). You can sit outside on the patio or let the kids play games on the lawn as you wait for your breakfast.   

Too many delicious choices, but over the years....

Love the Eggs-traordinary benedicts. Usually go with The Peacemaker which is a mix and match of any two. Favorite is the Smoked Salmon   
Bennie with the caper and dill hollandaise, but the Corned Beef Bennie is great as well. The Chicken St. Charles is like a twist on Chicken and Waffles. 

Their French Toasts are so delicious. Our last one was stuffed with cheesecake. Who doesn't love dessert for breakfast? You can also get a "flight" of pancakes which is a perfect option for someone who can't decide what to choose. 

For omelets, our favorite is the hot-smoked salmon topped with dill hollandaise and flash fried capers. Tip--if you make omelets at home, take their "recipe" and use goat cheese. It is sooo good! 

Kudos also to Ruby Slipper for giving back to the community and feeding the families affected by the current shutdown...and don't forget to sign in on YELP for a special lagniappe.

text: Me and my bf are down in NOLA for my birthday. We chose Willie Mae's being hype beasts off Yelp reviews. There was a line outside but it soon died down when we were inside so I guess we just came at a wrong time. I ordered the catfish with candied yams and mac and cheese. My boyfriend ordered chicken with Mac and cheese and candied yams. They didn't have any candied yams ready so on top of our 30 minute wait outside we waited an additional 20 for candied yams. Our waitress was so sweet and explained the wait for the yams to us. The food was... ok. My mom is from Mississippi so I'm not a tourist when it comes to that and my expectation for it is very high. This did not meet the expectation. My boyfriend loved it but he's Haitian so he's more into creole food. The mac and cheese was VERY bland. Like no salt whatsoever. The candied yams were good and both of our meals came with peas. I haven't had peas in years but that's not a plus. I would of preferred string beans if they're gonna throw something green on the plate. My catfish was ok but I like my catfish from my local soul food place better. Our meal came out to 43$ and some change.... too much money for too little food. I could have gotten two meals for half this price with more food back home. (And free and better tasting from my momma) The meals come with ONE side. Never in my life have I heard a soul food place give ONE side with your entree. The extra side was 5.00 a piece for both of us. To sum this up.. would I eat here again... nah.

text:
Wow! This place was really, really cool. Didn't realize there's a post-apocalyptic-themed restaurant here in Philly! At first glance, you'd thought it was a chain. After some digging, it's actually not, and it's special just to the City of Brotherly Love!

First thing's first, going to talk about stuff besides the food. It's easy to get to. It's right off the highway, in Fishtown, next to The Fillmore (a music venue), and right across from SugarHouse, the casino. Parking's eh; pretty much street or finding a close by lot. As soon as you walk in, it won't take you long to realize the post-apocalypse theme. I actually came without knowing, and realized early as soon as I saw the weird chairs and leather/bullet-casing outfits on display. It was pretty cool! The wait was a little annoying, but luckily we made a reservation literally on the way there from Fishtown proper and was able to be seated within 10 minutes. Some people walking in had to wait for 30. There was a bar area that was poppin' (with pretty good Hip Hop music as well), but maybe because it was St. Patrick's day. Service was great! And finally, an interesting part of this restaurant is that it also has a VR lounge. Sadly I didn't try it, but will do so next time and update my review. They also serve cigars if that is something you like.

As for the food, price is decent. There are your typical burgers, small plates (that is not take small), and appetizers. However, there is a "Survivor Menu," which has food items that go with the post-apocalyptic theme. Items on this menu are primarily meat, or whatever you can cook on on a super hot stone (which sizzles as you place your food on it). The experience of ordering from this menu is pretty much a main reason why most people come here. I had the burger (see picture), which I was able to cook the way I wanted, and it was very, very, very good. I looked over to a table next to ours, and saw someone cooking flank steaks with butter all over it (it was mouth-watering). Portions were great. Finally, they have a drink menu and a very good draft selection as well. Tad bit pricey

Pros: Experience, VR, cooking food on a stone, good for groups
Cons: Price, wait at times
Recommendation: Definitely would come again, and with a group!
name: Patrick

But sadly, they had NOT one appetizer that didn't contain fish, I can't eat fish :(.  Anyway, the salad and bread before dinner was delicious! We each ordered the bacon wrapped filet, medium. I could tell before I even cut my steak that it was very much a medium rare, border-lining on rare. They threw it back on the grill, but had they been better trained, they wouldn't have had to. The steak was also very bland and not seasoned at all. Will a good amount of salt added, it was ok. It definitely wasn't the super delicious steak I was hoping for and my baked potato was super dry, even after drowning it in butter. So half the meal was amazing, and half was meh. The one thing I would go back for?? The turtle cheese cake. It was the most delicious turtle cheesecake I've ever eaten, and I'm not a skinny girl!! LOL. The service was also amazing, the staff get an A+, the food a C at best. All in all it wasn't horrible but definitely was not a $100 meal. We will go elsewhere next time in town.

text:
Unfortunately I was very underwhelmed by Rocco's. I've heard some good reviews and was eager to try it out when I was back visiting on the east coast, so I went in for happy hour on a weeknight to sit outside and enjoy the beautiful weather on the patio. 

This spot is dog friendly outside which is a plus. When we got there, there were many open seats, as it was early on a weeknight during happy hour (probably right around 5pm), and the hostess ignored us for a good 5 minutes and we watched as she stood at a table talking to a group while we stood around waiting to be seated. Only after being seated when our server came up to us, did we find out that the side of the bar we were sitting, happy hour was not offered. I could walk to the outside bar in about 5 steps but where I sat, no happy hour. You have to be on the opposite side of the bar or at the bar directly to get the happy hour. That makes no sense to me whatsoever as the whole point of going to a restaurant during happy hour is to get happy hour prices! 

Our server was friendly, nothing to report about him, but you can tell that most of the wait staff is young and definitely does not receive much training as a lot of server 101 stuff wasn't happening-orders not correct, no bread brought out right away or water, taking orders took a long time, bringing food took a long time, plates taken away before we were done, etc. I'm hopeful that if the management gives the team some better training a lot of these basics will improve. 

Food wise, also underwhelming. The tuna appetizer which to me does much better stacked was all smushed together in a bowl and heavily dressed which took away from the tuna itself, and the salad we ordered was also overly dressed leaving the soggy.

Then after paying our bill, we thought we'd get one drink at the happy hour prices at the bar, and it took an extremely long time to get drinks and the bar was not overly crowded by any means.

Not my favorite spot in town. Hopefully a lot of this is just because the restaurant is still relatively new and they can fine tune it and improve.
name: Jacqueline

text: I love when a restaurant pays attention to the details. Stopped by for lunch. Ordered the Blackened fish sandwich which was served with potato salad and coleslaw. There are so many restaurants that put old lemons in their ice tea and on their entree plates so I can really appreciate that someone is paying attention here. Even the lettuce tomato and onion were perfectly fresh. Seems easy enough but again, so many restaurants don't pay attention to the details. This restaurant was also very clean. The staff worked as a team and every one was friendly. It seemed as though the staff took pride in their restaurant which is very rare to find. There were so many items on the menu that sounded so good like the Grouper cheeks and blue crab claws in garlic butter that I'm looking forward to going back. text:
Honestly, I debated between three and four stars. The food was phenomenal but the spotty service left me wishing for more. It wasn't too bad of an experience, though, so I'm giving them the benefit of the doubt. Four stars it is.

Half-price bottles on Sunday to go along with my brunch? Yes please! Good thing we thought ahead and made a reservation for our group of seven because otherwise we would've been waiting forever.

The food is incredible. I had two crepes, one savory and one sweet, and I was able to load 'em up with as many fillings and toppings as I wanted. Other items available were omelettes and classic scrambles with hash browns, eggs and sausages. When giving your custom order, such as with a crepe or omelette, you fill out a half-sheet and circle all the ingredients you want added. This took us a second to understand how to order and what the prices were since no one explained it to us for a while, not even asking if this was our first time here.

There were long periods of time between when we saw our waitress. We had lots of questions, from asking for a wine list to getting a real menu with prices and not just the half-sheets. It felt like we were bothering her with our questions, and she all but ran away as soon as she answered one question per visit. 

The food is where this place really excels, and I hope the service staff can catch up soon. I'll likely be back for the crepes, pretty chocolates and the Britney and Beyonce playlist that graced our Sunday morning.

text:
Hands down a very professional establishment from the hostess greeting to the two gentlemen working the oysters at the oyster bar.
I pop in one evening to a packed house, and the hostess assured me it would not be long to sit at the oyster bar.  I waited maybe 15 minutes in the bar where the bartender made me a "Brian" special.  It was a non-alcohol drink made with cucumber and mint.  The drink was refreshing and lasted me the whole evening. 
I ordered Oysters, Lamb Skewers and the Chocolate Flan cake for desert. The waiter was courteous knowledgeable, friendly and eager to please.  The 1st serving of oysters were served on a king size bed of ice chips with vinaigrette and cocktail sauce in a beautiful, artistic deep pan.  I requested horseradish and was promptly served.  The horseradish was perfect the way horseradish was meant to be served with Oysters.
The lamb was ground with the perfect mix of spices along with a testy white sauce.  The chocolate flan was on a crispy cookie covered in a chocolate shell with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.  The vanilla was wonderful and aromatic and perfectly balanced with drizzled caramel.
I cant wait to be back.

They never apologized for messing up and didn't even try to expedite her order and she had to wait another 20 minutes for her salad. We then wanted drink recommendations and were curious what another customer was drinking and asked her if she could ask the bartender what it was. text:
Came here for the first time tonight. My parents just got to town and they love seafood so this was the place. Nice, modern atmosphere. I definitely enjoyed the aesthetic. 

Charles was our server and Bryce was the server assistant; they provided great service. We came in relatively late on a Sunday night but they made sure we did not feel rushed even though we were trying to get in and out and not keep the staff there all night. They were attentive without being overbearing, which I love. You can tell Charles has a lot of experience. His anticipation of our needs was excellent. 

We started with the calamari fries. My dad devoured them. Cooked perfectly and the sriracha ketchup was a nice complement. We also had the burrata salad - simple and delicious. The arugula pesto was very bright. We had the stone crab, as well. Thankfully they do some pre-cracking before it gets to the table because those babies are thick. It was served with a few sauces but the mustard sauce was bomb! If it is stone crab season, don't miss them! 

Entrees were grilled grouper, seared scallops and lobster mac and cheese. All three were cooked wonderfully but we only took a few bites as we were mostly full by entree time. There was no hope for dessert. 

We plan to come back next Sunday for brunch!
name: Ana
