text: This is the second time that I have been here and I have not been disappointed! The first time I came here I have the vegetarian Cuban which was wonderful because I love a good pressed Cuban sandwich but it's hard to find a vegetarian option. The reason why we came here today was because we were excited to learn every Sunday in October is Goth Brunch. We came in a little bit later so we didn't see the DJ's full set but she definitely did not disappoint with wonderful goth classic songs mixed with modern goth songs. The specials were all Halloween based from the drinks to the food. We decided on a vegetarian burrito and it was delicious. Originally it is a vegan burrito with no cheese but we added the cheese. The bartender forgot to add the cheese but then offered us queso instead, and it was an amazing idea because that was one of the best vegetarian burritos I've ever had in my entire life. We appreciated not only the delicious food but the bartender offering the option because it was not only really considerate of her but absolutely so good! I was very happy to have come here today. All the bartenders dressed in a very fun, spooky style clothing which made us feel really comfortable walking in and feeling comfortable in our own skin, dressed gothy to the max! I honestly wish Orlando had an option like this because this is very unique and definitely was a main reason why we even traveled into Tampa today instead of going straight home from St Pete. Considering I've only been here twice I would absolutely put this on the list of a place I would return to again in the future. There are so many options for vegans and vegetarians not to mention a full Liquor Bar and a very friendly staff.

text:
Came here yesterday for a late lunch expecting it to be mobbed for St. Patties Day celebrations, but we walked in to an empty restaurant. There was ample seating at the bar, but we asked to be seated at a table. 

Our waiter came over with 2 cups and a jug of water. His name was Tony. He was pleasant and courteous. Initially, I had placed my order with lunch in mind because I didn't know brunch was served until 3pm. We placed our order around 2:30 and Tony came back giving us unfortunate news that we had to choose items from the brunch menu since lunch didn't start until 3:00. Besides that hiccup, I have nothing negative to say about this place. 

To start, we ordered the hummus. It was roasted red pepper hummus, feta cheese, Kalamata olives, red peppers and cucumber slices with warm pita to accompany it all. I've never ordered hummus at a restaurant before but I must say this was some killer hummus and the vegetables along side of it were crisp, fresh and a perfect addition to the plate! 

I ordered the veggie burger. A MUST TRY. So many interesting flavors on this one, but I loved it. It was juicy and cooked properly. The bacon was supposedly made from sweet potato. The aioli added a kick to it. It came with a side of fries. The inside of the bun was slightly burned but didn't tasted burnt when I bit into the burger. 

Again, Tony was really helpful and checked on us various times. He brought out a box for my leftovers and asked us if we needed anything else before we got our check. For two people, it was around $55. We each got beers so that's what racked up our bill. Delicious food and great service. I'll be back to try the lunch/dinner items!
name: Lisa

text:
On the morning of our check-in date...After comparing prices on different "comparing websites," I ended up booking our reservation via Trivago- which compared to everyone else, ended up being $6 cheaper. (Every dollar counts when you're trying to save money.) One night, one kingbed, in the West Tower came out to be $39 plus all the rando resort fees, but either way this was the best value. 

Upon check in, Gail got us set up with our reservation at the front desk. She was super friendly and provided great customer service. Our room was located in the West Tower, which seemed to be the more "updated" Tower with more modern fixtures and amenities. The room was decent in size, the toilet flushed, the shower had hot water, only bad thing was that the bed was SUPER uncomfortable. No pillow top here, baby. 

Once we got settled, we found the closest bar which led us to Jade Bar. Buzz, our bartender was cool. We shot the shit for a bit then found ourselves at the card tables. Cool thing is that they have $5 blackjack tables, everywhere- heck yeahhhhh! The hubby opted for the craps table. They have a ton of TVs, so we were able to watch the Warriors Game while having a good time on the card tables. My girl, Ivory hooked me up with a few blackjacks and I found my self walking away with an extra $100 after playing for almost 45 minutes. *Thumbs Up! 

For dinner, we ate at the hotel buffet Cravings- where we redeemed our BOGO promotion. Can't beat $19.99 for unlimited food for two! Lucky for us it was barbecue night on Wednesday nights. The buffet is open for dinner 4:30p-8p, so plan ahead. Pretty good food, for a buffet. 

All in all we had a decent stay. The hotel is on the older side, so expect that it will attract an older crowd. *wink. 

P.s. The room was a bit dusty, so the hubby and I woke up with super bad allergies and must have sneezed at least 20x.

text:
The portions are just right, miso broth with udon noodles (I requested udon instead of ramen) was absolutely flavorful, though a bit too salty which is not surprising as it is miso. The egg is only half an egg (always wish they'd just give the entire egg) but it was cooked well, the yoke was soft, and there was a good amount of vegetables which always makes the dishes feel healthier.

I ordered the chasu pork and this was done right in flavor and texture.  It was not dry, it pulled apart nicely and the fat interspersed between fibers of muscle gave it a nice spring to each bite.  

I would come here again, but might ask them to dilute the miso broth just a bit more.

text:
One of my most memorable meals in NOLA, and that's saying something. We went after our visit to the WWII museum.

I came for le pig mac - it was a thing of beauty. The meat is pork (obvi) so the flavor was much different than a big mac but elevated. The layers and toppings were just right, and it was actually big. The duck pastrami sliders were like mini grilled cheeses, nicely buttered and toasted but dainty - they were tasty but could have used a little more meat. The mac and cheese was perfectly cooked and had just the right amount of cheese. It was fun choosing a unique soda.

We also bought jars of house made pickled veggies and satsuma jelly to bring home. In addition we got the charcuterie plate to go (various meats and pickled things with flatbread) - we ate it for breakfast in bed in our hotel the next morning!

text: Came here for brunch with my husband on a Sunday. The host was very polite and we were seated immediately. The waitress was very attentive and sweet. I got the eggs Benedict and my husband got the philly special. The eggs Benedict was cooked perfectly ! And we got the jalapeño cornbread, yummmm. Great experience, will be returning!

text:
I went to New Orleans a little while back with some friends, and we decided on Pat O'Brien's for our first dinner in the city. I have to say, this dinner really lived up to the hype, and set the tone for all the yummy food we were going to experience that weekend! 

First off, this was a Saturday night, so we had a bit of an expected wait (so worth it). Once seated, we noticed the beautiful ambience. This restaurant definitely exudes New Orleans style and flavor.  

On to the food! First, we split some deep fried gator bites! I love trying new foods, and this was my first time trying gator! I have to say that I did like it! To me, the flavorand the texture were similar to a blend of chicken, frog, and fish, if that makes sense, lol. But I did like it. As far as main course goes, I went with some famed crawfish etouffee, with a cup of gumbo on the side! Honestly...this meal was insane! Lol. Every bite was bursting with spice and flavor! I daydream about this crawfish etouffee and gumbo pretty often back home here in CA, lol! I definitely wouldn't mind coming back here for a meal the next time I'm in the N.O., ya heard me?!?

text: I am not even sure of where to start with how phenomenal the food is here! I guess I will start by saying I was visiting New Orleans for work training and this place was recommended to try. Since it was only a 4-min walk from my hotel, I figured "why not?". From the moment I walked in, the bar staff was very friendly and told me to try one of their signature cocktails as I browsed the drink menu (which I did). Another patron was brought his food and it looked so good I asked anout it. He let me know it was the bbq oysters, bbq crab claws, and gator balls (not sure if that was the accurate name, but that's what they looked like). I decided to step out of my comfort zone and try the bbq oysters. I like raw oysters and never liked cooked one, but why not try something different. OMG, the oysters were the BEST I've ever had in my life. So much so, I went back the next day as well so I could have them again before I left New Orleans. On my second night there, another patron had a ahi tuna dish that looked amazing. That will be what I tey on my next visit. And there will definitely be another visit (but for vacation and not work). It's a mustbtey place and it's located on Bourbon Street so you can take a walk to enjoy the festivities (which seems to be something every single day). Enjoy!!

Then we order relatively quickly which was nice, I was thinking that first experience was a fluke... until our waitress came back 15 mins later and said there was a mix up and she never put our orders in but she would "as soon as she could". What???? As soon as you can? It seemed obvious she just forgot to do it. When she finally did put our orders in she forgot to put in some wedges we ordered. We got those w/ the wrong cheese on top... text:
We brought our 3 kids (ages 5, 4 and 2) and our teenage niece to Brothers Burger Joint. As soon as we walked in we were greeted by the staff. They quickly went to work pushing tables together for our sizable family. Almost immediately they brought out kids menus and crayons for the littles, and made pleasant attempts to engage with the kiddos. This was a great distraction while my husband and I took a minute to get settled. We began with ordering drinks and of course the needs for cups with lids and straws were acknowledged and met. When you go out to eat with young children, it's the little details like this that make dining manageable. We ordered our food, and it came out in a very reasonable amount of time (the kids were playing tic tac toe and tackling the word search while we waited. I forgot to bring toys and such, so the crayons and paper were a great distraction!). The food came out hot and delicious. During our meal, as staff members made their rounds, they checked in on us as we juggled cutting our kids food, administering ketchup, and attempted to keep our 2 year old from dropping his beverage every 8 seconds). I have to include in this review that our 4 year old dropped a tomato on the floor, and as soon as we were about to tell her "no, don't eat that!", one of the staff members jumped in and politely suggested to her that she hand it to him, and my strong-willed 4 year old actually gave the tomato to him! He was ON IT!) Anyways, once the kids realized they loved the food, I ACTUALLY GOT TO EAT! I usually don't get to eat much when we go out with the family because I am always busy trying to keep kids calm, quiet, and fed, but the food here was good enough for them to eat and eat and eat! Oh my goodness, the burger with the blue cheese and balsamic reduction and sauteed onion, it was amazeballs! (That's what I had) The chicken tenders were loved by the kids, and the fries were a hit for everyone. 

Brothers Burger Joint is delicious, and very family friendly! I am so glad we decided to try it out today, and we will definitely be back!
name: Rachel

text:
I like eating in the neighborhood. I like supporting small family businesses. It's important and vital to our community. I've been here a few times and to their other location more than once. I waited to review. We called at 6:45 for a table for three on a Friday and got in 10 minutes later. Everyone was nice, the valet was amazing. Service was good. Multiple people stopped by to place, refill or clear. 
Food was good. I noticed the age of the crowd, older to say the least. It was a plus 65 crowd. The restaurant needs updating. The ole school murals of Italian scenes and grapes can go. I'd recommend they take their old world recipes and skills and place them in a updated modern surroundings. 
The red sauce was deep and rich. Pasta was hot and spicy. Meatballs were the best. Veal was ok. Chicken was done well. My only complaint is the surroundings. Clayton's a cosmopolitan area with more and more young people moving in. They need to look forward not backward. The thought of stopping in for a cocktail at the bar would most likely result in you running into your grandparents. 
Things change. Customers change. You need to flip those tables a few times more, hope for a wait at the bar, or want to fight the crowd to get a drink.  That's not the case. I'll return. I always return. It's those meatballs and spaghetti that keeps me coming back.
name: Rick

text: After my last review shortly after their opening, I said the service was lacking because the food came out so slowly. Jason, one of the owners remembered us and graciously responded that he agreed with the review and and asked that we give them another chance. I'm thrilled that we did. The food is delicious. Guacamole is perfect as is the creole queso. The mezcal drinks are smoky and fabulous and if driving wasn't an issue I would have had more. Fish, shrimp and cauliflower tacos are excellent. But do not miss the deeply rich chocolate chili ice cream. Could eat that til they ran out. Amanda was lovely. Strongly recommend this restaurant.
name: Bill

text:
When we first visited the Ice Centre, we know there is a restaurant going to be open in the Centre. It take them a year for this restaurant to be open. When we know about the news for opening this month, we decided to stop by and check. I also invite couple of Yelp friends to join us. 

Judging the price of the menu, it is about 10% more than regular restaurant. However we were no regrets that because the food measured up with the price we paid. It still has some bump to iron out, our waitress is still don't know which beer is happy hours. They offer happy hours item from 4 pm to 7 pm Monday to Friday. The app is 25% off from the pregame section. The draft beer is $2 off. 

We started with Ybor egg roll. It has mojo pork, ham and salami wrap together. Who can resist it. I also get the tuna bowl. It seared blacken Ahi tuna over rice and Asian slaw. It has the honey soy ginger sauce. It was quite good. Lastly we have the Top Shelf wings. This is must have item. It is about $0.20 more than normal outside restaurant wing place. However, it worth the money. This wing is marinated in mojo sauce, then grill over the open flame and top with the house sauce. It was delicious. 

Overall is good experience. The place has TV. But who actually watched it when you can see live hockey from the high school competition. Love the game, love the food.

Constant turnover in the wait staff results in unreliable service. Waiters disappear for 10 minutes or longer. For the first time last weekend, a manager asked us about our meal. I should have taken the opportunity to ask about service, but was ready to leave by then. Be quick on making selections and it won't be a bad experience.

text:

Small store front, staff very friendly. There is usually a wait, probably because the place isn't that big but also because the food is slammin'. Grits are creamy and smooth with lots of flavor. The shrimp are seasoned very well with a great sauce and light bread. The portion is perfect. 

The shrimp and grits are ranked among top 2 BEST shrimp and grits I'VE had in the country. I'm a big shrimp and grits person. I've had a lot in my day and I dream about these! The banana fosters french toast is also good but the staples here is the SHRIMP AND GRITS. 

The food comes out fast and try the home made juices. Very good. I visited N'awlins for the first time this month on a 3 day trip and came here twice. 

You must try it. You wont be disappointed.
