text:
I wish could give zero stars. The whole experience was disappointing.  Just zero class, zero attention to detail, zero responsibility, and zero "do the right thing".

I planned a private party to celebrate my daughter's college graduation.  Twenty family member traveled over 1500 miles to join the celebration.  I had worked for about 3 months with the catering manager picking out the right room, food and wine.  The event cost over $2500, and all I can say is the service was lousy, and the food mediocre (except the undercooked fish which was gross). I emailed the private party manager during the event every time something else happened, and spoke to him two days later.  I detailed the issues, and he was oh so apologetic. He talked to his Director and "generously" offered me a $100 gift card for a future dinner at the restaurant. Future dinner? Hmmmm, no thank you. Just ridiculous.  Problems:
1).  The Wine Cellar is actually two rooms, not one.  Our family, who wanted to be all together, had to decided whether to split up into two rooms or get crammed into one room.  We chose cram.
2).  The Wine Cellar is downstairs with zero accessibility for folks with mobility issues.  A couple of our elderly family members could not make it down the stairs.
3).  The printed menu had numerous misspellings: "Marlyand Crab Cakes" and "Rack of Lamp".  Ever heard of spell checker, or how about a simple read through of the $2500 menu?
4). I had discussed with the manager that we would like to offer beer and wine by the glass and asked to offer wine that was $12/ glass or less.  How was this handled?  The waiter handed out the full wine and drink menu and then announced that everyone needed to stay under $12/ glass.  Classy, right?
5).  5-6 of us ordered the bass.  It was significantly undercooked/ raw on the inside (the center had that translucent jellylike quality), we called the waitstaff back in and let them know it was inedible.  Then a head waiter came in and said "Oh, that is how we cook it, but if you want it cooked more, we can do that."  Uh, yes, we would like our food cooked so as to avoid illness. 
6). Dessert trio, is three thimble sized desserts that are essentially tasteless except for sugar.
7). After I had had enough, I asked to speak to the manager in private to express my concerns.  After every thing I said, he fed me the party line "I'll pass along your concerns". After hearing the standard response about 10 times I gave up...like talking to a robot. 
Take your private party to another venue that actually cares about quality and customer service.
name: Sally

text: Best sushi in New Orleans. Come here for a night of fun music, great food and good vibes. Expect a wait on the weekends as they only take reservations for 10 or more. Rent out the back room for a party, or sit at the sushi bar for a faster experience. The fish couldn't be fresher and the food is overall delicious!
name: Olivia

text: A nice experience overall. I was a bit surprised that we weren't permitted to sit at the bar and have a beverage while we waited for a table. Once we were seated, our server was pleasant and informative. They have a nice variety of foods to choose from. The meat and cheese board was very good! I had the asparagus pasta. It had been WAY over salted but I basic the flavors were good. The manager very politely apologized for the salt issue and removed the pasta from my bill and offered an alternate selection. It wasn't a perfect dining night but, I would definitely be willing to try again!!
name: Ann

text:
This was our first time, to this location and we had mixed feelings. The atmosphere was good and similar to other locations, and being at the dinner rush - the restaurant part, was loud. When presented with the menu, I was shocked with the lack of selection for entree's. You pretty much much get steaks done in about 6 different ways, chicken served in 4 different options and then 1 order of salmon.
The food took, what seemed forever, and when it finally arrived, the quality of the meals, was to  what I expected. I had the salmon, the Mrs just wanted nachos and our little one, chicken fingers. 
Salmon was good and presentation was great. The nachos were as expected, however, upon getting the bill - I was floored to learn that the plate of nachos were over $20!! For what? A regular sized plate and all we did was add beef?! I've had nachos at a pub, by my house and they were, by far cheaper and more worth the price. And the chicken fingers, well ...... its chicken fingers. The only negative thing I can say, is that our server didnt ask if the child wanted ketchup, since most kids I know refer THAT over ranch dressing.
We decided to stick around longer and have dessert. Why not, since the child got ice cream, we ordered the Toffee Pudding. Again ....... FOREVER to get our desserts. I can guess it took almost 18min from ordering the dessert, to when it hit the table. I can actually say this, because we managed to watch, just over half an episode, of our child's fav cartoon show! Of a 30min episode, there was 12 min, remaining of the episode.

So, I can only give this location 3 of 5 stars because of the time it took to get our orders. The quality of the food and the restaurant is the same as other locations, so it's a "Meh", if I'm in a rush to head back to this location.
name: John

text: Get the fried chicken!  So good!  My meal included: salad, split pea soup, main course of giant plate of fried chicken and pie.  There was probably a side of something but the giant portion of fried chicken was out of this world.  The restaurant is a house converted into a dining area.  The woman that took care of us treated everyone like they were family.  It was a pleasure to dine there.  It's been a while but I still crave that fried chicken!
name: Melanie

text: A friend and I ate here this past Friday.  I had Gravy and biscuits and hash browns. The hash browns came out 15 minutes before the biscuits and gravy.  It took asking 5 times to get it. The hash browns were not even edible. Can you say awful? The biscuits and gravy were fair. The cost was over $12 for a terrible meal. They did the right thing and comped mine.  My friend had pot roast that he said was only fair. If you want hash browns, stop at Waffle House. This was my first and last visit to Metro Diner.
name: Edward

text: Came here for a photoshoot.... The scenery is not that great but I was still excited. For the photos. The photographer wanted $50 which i thought was ridiculous... Still don't have the photos...
name: Kyle

text:
This one of the largest D&B's I've ever been to. Rightfully so...located right in New Orleans around shopping and tourists. It has SO many games and a huge bar area. Parking is in the garage and is expensive so be prepared...about $10.  

The food was actually delicious and not expected for a place like this. I got the Grilled Fire Salmon with mashed potatoes instead of rice and green beans $16. It was so good I didn't take a pic before I demolished it! Also got a strawberry watermelon margarita. It was way too sweet for me. 

Sarah was our waitress and was nice but seemed new. Our food order didn't come out till hours later and the manager had to come out several times. Also, had to comp a meal for hair in the dish. Our party was super disappointed after leaving about 11:30pm and arriving at 8pm. The manager should have comp'd the entire party's check, that would have been appropriate considering the chaos but he didn't. Just an apology. I wouldn't return to this location...seems too much for them to handle.
name: Tiffany

text: I was ravenous when we came so I ordered 3 tacos. Pork was definitely the best one I got. Steak was good. The duck was different than what I expected but an interesting mix of flavors, I think mainly because of the goat cheese. Overall great experience. We came at a busy time so we didn't mind waiting at the roof top bar. Margaritas were good too!
name: Sammy

text: Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. You can tell they care about customer experience here. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent.
name: User

text: The medium flavor was pretty hot! I can't even imagine what the hot and what the cluck is like. Definitely a staple in Nashville U will have to try. Skip the line and order online instead and then just come and pick up your food or eat there.
name: Simret

text: This is one of those places where I can see other people loving it more than I did. So yeah, the tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than i pictured from the photos. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. Anyway, my pasta was decent and not overcooked, which i appreciated because that happens a lot. not sure I'd order the same thing again.
name: User

text: I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Would probably stop in again if nearby. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Food was fresh and service was quick. The leftovers held up okay the next day..
name: User

text:
Great brunch location in center city. The place is pretty busy, but I was able to easily make a reservation for two the night before for prime brunching hours. You can also try your luck, as there is a lot of seating, but be wary. 

The ambiance is great - mood lighting, more antique furniture, and a bubbly vibe all around. Our service was also great - our waiter checked in on us and kept our water glasses filled. 

Foodwise, my friend and I both got the Biscuits and Gravy. It was delicious! Cheese on ham, eggs, and home fries, doused in their delicious bacon gravy. I absolutely enjoyed every bite of it. And the price was pretty fair for the amount and quality of food that we got. 

The only downside is that seating is a little too close to each other. You kind of feel on top of people next to you. Also, some table yelled that there was a rat, but no one really saw it. I'm not convinced that there was one, but thought I'd mention it. 

All in all, I'd probably come back here for brunch again. It's a great spot for anything from hangouts to dates. Definitely a great place!
name: Will

text: I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Food was fresh and service was quick. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. A very pleasant experience. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price..
name: User

text: Awesome happy hour!  The guys are the bat are super nice.  Don't be worried if you are seated in the lounge area, the servers do an excellent job taking care of you.  The food is great and the drinks are on point!
name: MP

text: Food was all very good. Service was pretty good. Nice setting and ambiance. The only issue was the price. For a party of four, we ordered (2) appetizers, (4) entrees, (2) desserts, and (5) beers. $188 before tip. Seems like this place should be rated $$$ on Yelp, not $$. If you've got the budget, Waltz is worth a visit.
name: Evan

text:
Thanks to Yelp for letting me know about this place. Coffee/lattes here are pretty strong (and I'm a daily coffee drinker). Gotta love that caffeine! Ordered an iced latte with coconut syrup. My drink had the perfect amount of caffeine and flavor. 

Their food items looks pretty dang delicious too. Definitely would recommend coming here for a quick, casual lunch.
name: Cynthia

text:
We wanted to treat our family to a special evening out. In the past we have only had happy hour drinks and appetizers. This was our first dinner there together. Our grown kids and their partners were impressed with the ambiance and character of the space. Our meals were served hot and were delicious. From the appetizers, main courses, to dessert it was all perfect. Our two servers were excellent and attentive to our needs. 
After we finished they opened one of the patio doors so we could stroll through the outside area a bit. It was a colder evening, but still so enjoyable. When we came back, they were waiting right there to allow us back in to exit through the restaurant. Overall, Rat's gave us the special evening we had hoped for.
name: Iris

text:
My husband and I came here for our one year wedding anniversary. It's one of the few nice places in Tampa my husband hadn't been to. 

We were greeted promptly and taken to our table that had a lovely card and rose petals on it. Our server, Lucia, took great care of us the entire time. The food came out promptly and was delicious!!!! 

One of the managers came over to check on us and wish us a happy anniversary. What a great touch. To top it off we were each served a bananas foster. I'm not a banana fan but I ate the entire thing. 

We can't wait to come back!
name: Amanda

text: Recently stopped in for dinner with friends and loved it! Very cool place, love the look and the feel. Very impressive craft beer list and a huge bourbon and whiskey selection, if that's your thing. We started with the truffle tots, which were incredible! So crispy and flavorful. I went with the Morning Glory burger and it was melt in your mouth delicious. A little messy but for a gourmet burger, I would expect nothing less. I went with a side salad instead of fries since we had the tots as an appetizer. My wife had the fries, of course I stole one, and it was awesome. I had fry envy. After seeing the menu online, we were super excited for the booze milkshakes. I had the Brimley and was licking the bowl clean it was so good. Many beers and good times were had. If you're going on a Friday or Saturday night, you had best make a reservation. They are very busy on the weekends, as any great place should be. The owners and operators are great and we will certainly be going back.
name: Mike

text: Parking was annoying and I was already in a bad mood by the time I got inside. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. There were a couple things I liked and a couple things I probably wouldn't get again. Food was fresh and service was quick. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything..
name: User

text: Any visit to the Whitpain Tavern is a treat.  My wife and I go every Friday night.  We have tried many things on the menu and haven't been disappointed yet.  Beer is reasonable and the staff is second to none.  Try the garlic bbq wings.  Amazing!  Definitely a must.
name: Michael

text:
This place is so cool. It was a spare of the moment decision and a  great one! The ambiance is very welcoming and chill. We we're greeted punctually with a smile. The pizza is delicious as well. I noticed great beer and wine specials throughout the week. It's a must visit!

Cheers
name: Daniel

text: For the price I expected a little more care. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. The staff seemed tired but still polite. There were a couple things I liked and a couple things I prob wouldn't get again. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Ordered a few things and liked most of it.
name: User

text: Ordered delivery from Bo Fung and I was sorely dissatisfied. I ordered General Tso chicken and lo mein and both were inedible. The Chicken tasted like chicken nuggets and they were soft and mushy. To make the dish worse, the chicken was soaking in some kind of sweat and sour sauce. The lo mien was so greasy it was sliding off my fork when I tried to take a bite. The taste was a mix of salt and grease with no actual flavor. Do yourself a favor and  order from somewhere else!
name: Hannah

text: My girlfriend and I have both come to the conclusion that Vegan Commissary is honestly the best, AND affordable vegan cuisine in the city. We are constantly on the hunt for plant based food in the city and we've tried almost every option imaginable. These guys truly stand out. SOO delicious and creative. Also happen to be some of the nicest people we've come across. Their new layout is designed to where you walk into a front room with already prepared food in a refrigerator. They have fresh made to order sandwhiches to choose from as well. I believe their "main hustle" is catering but their fresh made sandwiches are our go to options. Everything we've tried is awesome. Fresh squeezed juices, muffins, cookies, kombucha...I'm telling you it's the best. Give them a try you will not be disappointed.
name: Im

text: Great drinks at the bar. I love the frozen Paloma but the service is consistently rude. Also I came in for a drink a good 25 minutes before they close and the bar tender ignore me until I asked for a drink and he told me they were closed.
name: Oliver

text: The setting is lovely. The service is excellent. The food is delicious. The manager and the chef are charming. We eat there fairly regularly (even though we have 1700 other options available to us). We strongly recommend reservations. We recommend the Shrimp and Grits, the salmon entree, and whatever else they have on their seasonal menu. We've eaten it all at one time or the other. La Petite Amelie on the corner is sensational, too. Be assured, if you are nice to people, they will be nice to you. Bring your manners.
name: G L F

text: The food was good I just felt that the customer service side of things could be improved.
name: Belen

text:
Came in for a dinner tonight. Granted I didn't have a reservation, my experience was terrible. First face was the hostess who took 2 minutes to actually realize I was there. They were sassy and came off rude when telling me there were no seats. I started a timer and saw a few tables open to see if they would be filled by the time I left. I was there for 55 minutes and they ended up being empty the whole time. I got directed to the tables near the bar and realized fast that it was a mistake. Having to go to the bar to order is not what I want when spending $10 for a meatball appetizer that comes out at the same time as the entrees. The bar tender treated us like we didn't matter, even when my date spilled a water on herself no help to even get a napkin until we asked even though he saw it spill. I have to say that id rather go to McDonald's where I would get better service and more consistency. Please do better.   

FYI: Put less Pepe in the cacio e Pepe
name: Jacob

text: Nesting in the hippest part of town, right across from the magnificent Henry B Plant museum, OE is a one stop shop for all kinds of needs from coffee, dinning, studying, to event hosting, etc. The restaurant has a nice clean and industrial aesthetic to it. They serve simple American dishes like salad and sandwiches. We came for lunch and ordered fried brussels sprouts, seasonal chopped salad, club sandwich, and some coffee. The food came out quite quickly since it was lunch and with much larger portions than we had anticipated since we're from Miami and used to the tiny portions there. Everything tasted great, nothing extraordinary, just good old nicely seasoned and prepared food. Service was also very warm and attentive. A must stop when you're in town.
name: Tam

text: Cute cafe in an old Victorian house. Good food, good coffee, good service. I got the huevos rancheros, my gf made an omelet. Both were very good, and quite filling. I intend to go back!
name: Steven

text: Best margs in town! Lots of great flavors and choices! The food is amazing too! Try the nachos and sonoran dogs!
name: Jon

text: First time ordering from here and I honestly wasn't sure what to expect. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. Food was fresh and service was quick. A very pleasant experience. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean.
name: User

text: The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable.
name: User

text: Just went there for the first (but definitely not the last) time. The place was packed but we were seated as soon as seats became available.  The staff hustled the entire time we were there.   Service was great, everyone was friendly and quite funny.  My husband and I both got a roast beef po boy.  They were delicious!   Glad we only live across the river so we can come back here soon.  Trust me, skip those places on bourbon (except GW Fins) and go here.  You won't be disappointed.
name: Bonnie

text: Stayed overnight for the game and had a beautiful king room at the inn with great views went to the bar for happy hour and the service and scotch/beer selection was all excellent. The Hppy hour food was meh, thus the missing star:( the guy next to me at the bar had a dinner entree he seemed to very much enjoy though. But the entrees were a bit pricey so didn't go that far. Over all great experience. Thank you for the personal service:)
name: Misty

text: I have stopped in Alice bakery a few times over the past months and every time I do am very happy with the results. I have stopped for lunch and breakfast. I have also stopped just to pick up baked goods and they are all very delicious, my favorite being the butter cake. There is plenty of street parking and it is easily accessible. They also have tables set up outside if you prefer that. The shop is very clean and well kept. There is a pleasant order from all of the baked goods. The staff is very friendly and professional. They have open face croissants for breakfast and they are falling off of the plate they are so big and they are very delicious
name: Lorence

text: What an AMAZING customer service! Hands down the best Italian restaurant & food we have EVER had. This is coming from a city family who have been exposed to many Italian culture & food. So very VERY pleased.
name: Marjory

text: Ehn. Underwhelming - Service was not attentive for a slow retardant night. The corkage fee is higher than the sister Resturant in Chesterfield. Also, my husband's dish wasn't very good (Cannelloni). Babbo's is sooo much better. Ironic - given it's the same owner.
name: Jen

text: Bk , its just BK. Except now they Dellllliiiivvver. Bam. I used to dream of that day. Oh yeah and #originalchickensandwhich
name: Vanessa

text: Excellent Mediterranean food in a cozy Doylestown location close to everything.  The food is incredible; the owner is terrific, engaging, and so positive; and the service is excellent.  Tip - the mega appetizer platter is superb!  We go on a regular basis.
name: Paul

text: Great neighborhood place.  You don't have to go to South Philly for a great Italian meal. Food is excellent and fresh.  Great service and atmosphere.  Prices are very reasonable plus it's BYOB. Only bad point is parking can sometimes be a pain, but worth it.
name: John

text: This place is a diamond in the ruff. My only complaint is the wait but it is so worth it! I had the breakfast bowl with grits and avocado twice now on it was so savory and perfectly seasoned! Love the atmosphere! Short walk from our BnB! Highly recommend this lovely place! Best would be to order and do other stuff, but be ready to eat it all!!
name: Sam

text: This was a delivery order on a night when I really did not want to cook. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. I wouldn't write it off, but I also wouldn't hype it up.
name: User

text:
Los Arroyos is a nice more upmarket Mexican restaurant. They have a wide range of delicious meals on their menu. We ordered chips, guac and salsa to share. Their chips are homemade and the perfect thin and crispy style. The salsas and guac are on point. I ordered the tacos al pastor for my main. Holy moly. I ate every last bite, it was so good-- right down to the rice and beans. Everything was full of flavor. We paired our meals with the Arroyos Margaritas-- they are a must. 

Parking is limited in back but there is also nearby street parking. They have a lovely outdoor patio and plenty of indoor seating. The service was nice and friendly.
name: Annelyse

text: I needed a quick lunch before heading to the airport after staying in the area. I had one of the best cheeseburgers I have had in a long time and even the salad in the burger was fresh. This was o key topped my the friendly service of Tina S! Thank you Tina :) I will be back here next time I am in the area. Great views and a real nice breeze.
name: Paul

text: The photos made it look a little better than it actually was. So yeah, the food was good and the service was easygoing. For a busy night they handled it okay. It looked better online than it did in person. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. idk I'd try something else next time. No big complaints, just a nice meal. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Ordered a few things and liked most of it.
name: User

text: Burger was ok (even though it wasn't what I ordered). Most employees seemed unhappy. When burger was delivered I thought it might have been someone else's because it was not what I ordered. Response was "nope this is for your number", sets the tray down and walks off.
name: Tanner

text: Delicious food that will not disappoint! We had the deviled eggs as an app and the hot chicken pizza to share. It was amazing!! Seriously amazing!!! One of the top 3 pizzas I have ever had! Try it!
name: Olivia

text: Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. Pretty happy with it overall. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish.
name: User

text: Tasty and quality meals. Love the concept and their foods. You won't be disappointed.
name: P.

text: So, all I can say is: don't let looks deceive you! I actually like the fact that only 21+ can enter, and seating is limited, but the food legitimately is fresh and delicious. I started to order the shrimp creole, but our bartender (we sat at the bar) felt the étouffée was better -- and her suggestion was on point! Now, didn't try the creole shrimp to compare, but the étouffée was wonderful, so I'm glad I listened. If you're visiting NOLA and want some authentic food that isn't terribly expensive -- highly recommend.
name: Julie

text:
My daughter and I were curious about this place because we heard such good things about it.  The inside is gorgeous.  Lots of seating options.  Our first visit was fun and the servers were prompt and friendly.  Food was outstanding. We went  there tonight and again we were not disappointed.  They have an extensive menu, reasonably priced.  I know we will be going back. 

JWK
name: Jacqueline

text:
My Dad wanted to go somewhere different for Father's Day... so we landed here.  The initial draw was how cute it looked from the pictures and not too many tables which meant to me it was not loud and noisy.  So we came and had what I would rate as an okay meal.  We came at around 3:30, which was ideal as it was not too busy.  The place is absolutely adorable inside, super clean with lots of what appeared to be Polish decor.

I immediately ordered a Polish beer they had on draft (they also had a nice selection of bottled Polish beer), and it was very tasty.  We ordered various things -- my Dad ordered the beet soup and 8 piece Pierogi dinner (beef); my Mom and I had the Pierogi dinners with mushroom and Sauerktaut and the Hubs had the classic Rueben.  All of our responses to the taste of the food was "it's okay".  I felt as though there was no real presentation going on with Pierogi dinners -- just dumplings put on a plate, nothing more nothing less.  I did absolutely love the vegetable salad that came with my husbands sandwich though.  Was an okay experience, and it was fun to try something different.

I will call out the Apple cake as being wonderful --  we ordered two pieces, I barely got a bite of the one I was splitting with my 89 year old Mom who literally inhaled it.
name: Betsy

text: If you want to eat breakfast in an enchanted garden with fairies that look a lot like birds, then you must go to Sweet Sage.  The large outdoor dining area is dog friendly and the food is pretty good.  You can order from the menu or enjoy the breakfast buffet, featuring breakfast staples like sausage, bacon, eggs, hash browns, oatmeal, fruit, etc.  One of our favorite places whenever we're in Clearwater.
name: Indera

text:
My husband and I visit Banh Mi Boys at least twice a month. This is, hands down, the best banh mi spot ever. DO NOT LET THE LOCATION DETER YOU, IT IS AMAZING! They have a large menu, and everything I've had is great. 

We regularly order the grilled pork spring rolls as an appetizer. Always get the grilled one, it's way better than the other ones. My other favorite menu item is the bang bang shrimp banh mi. It's so delicious. Sweet and salty, with huge shrimp. It sounds silly, but I especially love the way they slice their vegetables (cucumber, carrots, and daikon). It's unique and just has a different, fun texture. 

The employees are so awesome and friendly. We usually go during their lunch rush. It's usually one or two people running the register and food out, and they are killing it every time. 

The spot is kind of small, with very limited seating indoors. We try to aim for days that are nice outside, so it doesn't feel dreadful sitting on the patio. Even with the big fan out there, if it's Louisiana hot, it miserable. The parking lot can be a pain sometimes too since they share it with the gas station.
name: AC

text: Wow!!!! What an amazing renovation!!! Looks brand new!!The interior is beautiful! Rooms and furniture updated! Super friendly and accommodating staff!!! The beds were very comfortable! This hotel will shuttle you to the airport and allow you to leave your vehicle there for a amall fee AAAAAAAND pick you up when you return to nashville airport!!!
name: Dianna

text: Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Nice little spot, decent portions too. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. The food was good and the service was easygoing.
name: User

text: This place is awesome! Great mixture of light fare with coffee and fresh pressed juices to go. My only negative is the wait on weekends when tourists come to town. Keep up the great work!
name: Britt

text: Mai Lee is amazing! I am a huge fan of the #16 (Bun Dau Hu Rau Cai), and my fiancé gets the pho with medium rare beef. The food and service never disappoints. It's one of my favorite spots in STL!
name: Courtney

text: Meh. Ordered the tonkotsu ramen. Broth doesn't have the depth of flavor you'd expect from bone broth simmers for days. Just sort of bland. The tako balls are the best thing we ordered. If you need ramen far away from the city there's not a lot of options. But definitely just so so.
name: Xiaomang

text: I am a regular and want to compliment Jenna the daily bartender. She is always nice to everyone and I notice she has a lot of people that come to GT because of her. She is an example of providing excellent customer service!
name: Bill

text:
If it hadn't been for the sweet waitress, the sangria and the deviled egg flight, I would have liked to give this place less than one star. 
In a nutshell, every dish was served cold. Most of it under-seasoned and simply bland. And dry... Sahara desert dry... There are heaps of the less expensive items on the plate (grits, potatoes, cornbread), in sharp contrast to the diminutive nature of the more expensive items (salmon, asparagus). 
I actually apologized to my foodie for bringing them here. Some assorted details:
The deviled egg flight was fabulous. Each egg filled and garnished in a different way. Pleasing to the eye and the palate. $10 a bit steep for  5 half eggs, but it's Carmel, so it's expected. 
The cornbread. Huge portion of it... 4 big squares... this at least had some flavor, but also on the dry end of things. A bit of butter and bit of Pimiento cheese accompanies this cornbread appetizer. 
The fried green tomato and black-eyed pea fritters. For $11 you get three slices of tomato and 4 little fritters. The dips are great, the fried green tomatoes also quite tasty. The black-eyed pea fritters not so much. After biting into one, you find the center has the consistency of re-fried beans, but cold and tasteless.  I wish they would just sell the tomatoes in a separate dish, because I will not ever eat those fritters again. 
So let's discuss the main dishes. Grits, cheesy grits... I was so looking forward to those... what I got was a mountain of some substance that clearly had corn in it, but was more the consistency of... darn I can't even think of anything that I would willingly eat with that consistency... It was a huge lump of cold, dry, hard tasteless something with bits of corn showing. There were some black beans on my plate also and they were cold but tasty, so I do recommend those. I also had two pieces of fried banana on my plate and they were delicious. Wish I had more of those. My friend who had also ordered the same dish did not receive any bananas. The salmon seemed tiny on the mountain of grits. Nice grill marks though... a little too much actually as those were seared halfway through the salmon and tasted simply burned. Welcome to cold hard unseasoned burned salmon. The chili lime butter did nothing to combat the situation as the grits soaked it up like a sponge in record time. My friend's salmon was in the same condition as mine. 
All my guest that had ordered dishes with asparagus received 4 extra skinny half stalks of it. That in itself would be ok, but it looks ridiculous when you lay that across 5 pounds of grits or mashed potatoes that are on the plate. 
Unfortunately the meatloaf didn't fare any better than the salmon, but there was a more generous portion of it on the plate... unfortunately... nobody really wanted more of it. It's a giant cube of meatloaf, which apparently has to have one or more sides that are completely burned. and of course it kept with the theme of cold, dry and bland. The slow roasted pork... per my guest... evoked memories of her childhood's school cafeteria... cold, dry, bland... 
The mashed potatoes were deemed to be ok by some of my guests. 

In my opinion this is great if you want to hang out on the patio on a nice night, sip some drinks and share some apps. Otherwise... NO

text:
We went to this Mel's for the last time today.

We ordered the Sunrise Sandwich, and specifically asked for the bacon to be crispy/well-done.  

5 minutes after calling in the order, we walked in the door.  The waitress told me the food just came up...wow, that was fast.  They must have had bacon ready to go, right? Wrong.

The waitress went to get our food from the window where the cook had placed it.  As she grabbed the container, we over heard her ask the cook, 'Is the bacon well done?' We couldn't hear the response but I assumed it was a yes since she immediately brought the order over to us.

My husband looked inside the bag to see our sandwich.  He pulled it out and showed me the raw ends of bacon sticking out the sides of the sandwich, obviously, not well done.

We showed the waitress and she laughed because she had seen this also.  She told us that is why she asked him, but when he didn't own up to not making the bacon well done she just let it go.  She asked if we wanted to send the food back, fearing retribution for complaining, (which is why I think she also didn't press the issue) we decided to deal with it and I remade the sandwich when we got home.

It only gets better from there, since we had a long drive home, I ordered a coffee to-go.  The coffee isn't delicious, but it's cheap and convenient since we are already getting breakfast.  When I had about a half cup left in the bottom of my cup, while driving, I took a big swig....of coffee grinds. So Gross.

The waitresses are always really nice here, they seem to all be happy and genuinely friendly.  It's too bad the chefs can't get it right consistently.

We have eaten the breakfast sandwich from here many times.  Mostly it has been good, if you don't count the time my over-hard eggs were literally raw, I mean the white part was still gooey, and again, we were on the road when I discovered this. Super Gross!

So that was the last time here. We will still go to the BoomTown Mel's because, when it's good, the Sunrise Sandwich is delicious!!

text:
Date: 2-3-18
Time: 0945 & 1400

Very good food, in a beautiful space comes at a price. 

Armature Works - Heights Public Market: is the very recently opened 22,000 ft. food hall concept that brings together some of Tampa's most influential eateries into a single open concept dining experience. You will see many staples of the Tampa food scene: Ichicoro, Ava, Inside the Box, Cru, O Cocina to name a few, all under the same roof and vying for your monies. 

-The Space: While the space is most definitely still under construction (mostly outside) it's the quintessential of trendy/hipster. There is a lot of brick, woods and exposed filament lightning. I am not saying that I don't like it...just making it known. The space is massive and when we first arrived at 0945, with few guests, it looked as though seating would not be an issue. This changed as we returned later in the day. The outside, when completed, should offer a great view onto the water. 

-Inside the box: This spot is a meat market/Sammy spot. As we walked by my eye was drawn to the beautifully decadent porchetta that was ready for take home preparation. Then...my gaze went to the menu to see they had a "Roast Porchetta" Sammy, I was instantly transported back to Toronto and Porchetta & Co, the best bite of the trip. The expectations were through the roof, but it was a must order for me. It was quickly prepared and came with a side of pickles. It...was...delightful!!! So rich and fatty from the pork, with some great texture from the cracklings and then balanced excellently with the balsamic kale to cut the richness. All on a beautifully toasted pepper roll that had the perfect amount of give and crunch. It was an amazing experience and one I was happy to share with my wife. PS: The side of pickles was also a great palate cleanser and tasty accoutrement.  Price: $12.59 

-Butcher & Barbeque (BnB): The next stop on this foodventure was the local BBQ spot. We noticed that they had our favourite, burnt ends and had to give it a go. We got the B-Ends with two sauces and a side of spiced watermelon. The BBQ was out of the kitchen in short order and we took a few to try and find seating, but located some in our favourite space adjacent to the soon to be opened Astro ice cream. While the B-Ends had a great fatty/smoky taste, the char was lacking. As for the sauces, the signature sauce was the definition of forgettable...waits...did we get that one? The "Texas Heat" had a good balance of heat and twang to make it a go to sauce for us. The plate came with a side of Hawaiian rolls and pickled veg (onions, pickles & okra) that were very tasty and a great side for such a rich dish. The spiced watermelon was good, but nothing to get worked up about. Get some more char/crisp on those ends and we will be talking! Overall quite tasty and the takeaway looked legit. Price: $16.50

The little touches really elevated the dining experience: The self-serve water station, the vintage inspired hand wash apparatus and the well-appointed washrooms were a welcome addition. 

I am looking forward to getting back to this place...if you could not tell (I did go twice in the same day) and try some ramen and that astro ice cream. 

Get some friends...get some credit cards and get down here to sample some of the hotness that is the Tamp Bay food scene all under one roof. 

The 4 star is only because of the price tag that comes with the yumminess that I outlined above. 

I miss you already...
name: Christopher

text:

text: eDESIa is truly a hidden gem in Nashville, both from a culinary and service perspective, and deserves to be one of the go-to restaurant hotspots in our city.  My wife & I ordered the fried gnocchi, eggplant parmesan, & risotto, and everything was nothing less than spectacular and insanely delicious.  Let go of any preconceived notions or skepticism you may have about the concept (a mashup of Italian & Indian flavors and cuisines) - this was one of the best meals we've had in quite some time.  On top of that, the service is top-notch - our server Regan was so warm, generous, and knowledgeable, and the owner treated us to an incredible tiramisu at the end of our dinner, completely on the house.  The kindness of the staff at eDESIa alone makes it worth coming here, and simultaneously, the food is simply superb.  A winning combination all around.

text:
I never thought I'd see the day where I would say "restaurant provided too much delicious food and wine," but I suppose there's a first time for everything. My husband and I had previously gone for happy hour and loved the food and the cocktails, so on our latest Philly visit we decided to throw caution to the wind and do the 12 course tasting. That might explain the food coma, especially since it seems like some others have had issues with small portions for their a la carte menu. It was most definitely NOT an issue for us, and we are both pretty big eaters/wine drinkers. In fact, the wait staff actually cheered us for making it to the dessert round, so either they sensed we were struggling or it wasn't the first time that they had guests about to pop at the dinner table.

That said, the food was awesome, and it was a truly sad moment to have to finally admit defeat midway through the last dessert. The menu changes with the season so certain things may not always be on the menu, but we especially loved the Iberico ham, the ricotta gnudi (a fierce contender to a similar dish at Vetri nearby), and the lamb crepinette. The wine selection introduced us to some new flavors and textures we would not have otherwise gotten to experience, and it was definitely super generous on the pours.

Special shout-out to Jennifer at the hostess stand for being very friendly and accommodating while sorting out the reservation and taking care of us once we made it there.

text:
My husband and I went to dinner on a Saturday night. Wanted him to try Spasso as my last experience there was a positive one..Food, service, wait...it was all great!
It was a very busy night this time although there was no wait and we were seated right away. 
We ordered within 10-15 min. I ordered a Cabrese salad, which technically isn't on the menu but the waiter said he could do it, that was nice..
I waited and waited... we ate the bread, all of it!
the table beside us who came in around 15 min after us.. had their cooked appetizer and THEN a salad. The table outside, (I could see from my seat) had every app brought out and cleared away.. and I STILL did not have my Cabrese.. (it's JUST tomatoes and Mozzarella cheese). The waiter came over and took the empty roll basket and said I'll get you more rolls, your salad should be out soon.. huh? It's TOMATOES!! I was looking for him to re-enter the room to tell him, never mind on the salad. 
Around 5 min after that.. so we are at about 20-25 min now for the salad. It came!  I took it as I decided, nope.. not getting upset.. still waiting for the bread too.. had to grab a bus boy for our basket back. 
Around 5 min after salad, dinner came..
Now.. dinner was DELICIOUS.. and I know the place was very busy, but to wait that amount of time for a Cabrese salad and watch others eating COOKED apps..was annoying..
I was hopeful it wasn't on the check.. but..it's ok.
I ate I'll pay for it.
Food was worth it.
Service definitely tried our patience and was far beyond being understanding.

text:
OK, see previous my "review" for general info, i.e. hours and URLs. 

On our night, there was a special event going on, so it was quite busy, and thus a bit on the loud side. A couple of things might have helped this. More soft stuff on the walls, there's nothing, just pictures of Dewey (the dog). Open the windows, but it was hot and humid. 

I'll break this down quick:

Moscow Mule: Tasty, but not served in a copper mug. Glass was pretty big, so maybe I got more? 

Menu seems to be in an experimental stage, so yours may be different. 

Appetizer: Calamari - Very good!

Thuy's burger: Very good! 

My Fish and chips: Fish was mahi-mahi. I'd give it a good. It was served with a couple of sauces, all tasty, but not malt vinegar. I guess I could have asked, but the sauces were tasty enough I didn't bother. Chips were generous, but the same fries served with the burger. 

I was super curious about the banh mi, but unless it was a grouper banh mi, just couldn't see going that route. 

Although busy, service was very attentive, so kudos for that! 

Bottom Line: I regret that we did not check out the roof-top bar. My Mom has been up, and she says it's very nice.

name: Donna

text: Great barbecue. I recommend the pull pork. I am an older man, so I have had a lot of good barbecue, and this is probably the best in St. Louis.
name: Derrick

text:
We had chicken wings with a side salad. Both were very good. Wings were large and well cooked but not overdone. The side salad was fresh and big. 
We also had a gyro pita salad. Very large and delicious. 
We definitely go back and try the other choices
name: K

text: Came into In Riva with the wife for a coffee on a Friday afternoon. Super disappointed with the filter coffee we were served (@ $3 a cup). Cold and undrinkable. Definitely go elsewhere.
name: Anthony

text:
Back again this year and still a great place for the local favorite ~grouper and of course, those $3 margaritas. 

Still enjoying the vibe here and wait staff is friendly and attentive. Our server Josh was phenomenal!!  Attentive, friendly, and just so darn nice!!  We will be back a couple more times I'm sure before we head back north!
name: Barbara

text: Last night we ate dinner at Finch & Fork before the final film at the Santa Barbara Film Festival.  The atmosphere was great, our server top notch and the brussel sprouts appetizer was superb.  Two of us ordered the entree of the evening for Saturday, which was Lasagna Bolognese.  While the presentation was nice in a small cast iron dish, there was so much cheese on it that it was work to find noodles and sauce.  Therefore it was really rich, I could only eat around 1/3rd of it.  I expected so much more of a fine restaurant like Finch & Fork.
name: Amy

text: We come for the enchiladas especial every time and it is the best we have ever had! The most amazing thing is that the head of the bar knows our order the moment we walk in? We aren't here every week or month, but he immediately knows us! This is the perfect example of what a neighborhood restaurant is all about!!
name: Cindy

text: I was in New Orleans Louisiana for Mardi Gras with my family for Birthday celebrations. We were told by a person that lives in New Orleans to try Mothers. The line was long. I thought this is a good sign. We finally got in, I ordered the chicken since it said it takes 30 minutes I knew it would be hot and good. after pre paying for my food we had to find a table. The floor was disgusting. I got my food within 5 minutes. The chicken was cold, my gumbo was watered down..... no flavor! the rolls were cold and hard . I could thrown it up against the wall and put a hole in the wall. Not only was I disappointed my family was in disbelief. I paid 20.00 for a meal that wasn't fit to feed the Homeless. Whatever you do Never go to Mothers! it is Terrible!!!!
name: Debra

text: Ford's has great atmosphere, especially for a larger group,  and the giant tower of onion rings is aptly named. I didn't care for the lobster mac & cheese - the noodles were dry because all the cheese sauce collected at the bottom. By the time it arrived, stirring it up didn't bring everything back together. However, the menu has lots of options and I'd like to visit and try some other things.
name: Christina

text:
A friend was in from out of town, and her flight home was super early--so we were looking for a place to grab breakfast that opened early. Cafe La Maude fit the bill, and it had been on my list of places to try for a while.

I'm now kicking myself for not eating there sooner.

I cannot adequately describe how good the food is. Their Green Shakshuka is . . . well, I could happily bathe in the broth. Every bite tasted just a little different. Every bite was delicious. The breaded feta . . . the sweet potatoes . . . the fried cauliflower. Geez, just writing about it makes me want to head over there right now for another order. 

Yes, it's pricey. It's definitely not a place I could afford for breakfast every weekend (although at a lower price point I would probably be there every other day). It's worth a regular splurge, though. Definitely.
name: Mick

text: Food took forever but ended up being better than I expected. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. It was crowded but still moved along. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. No big complaints, just a nice meal.
name: User

text:
I came back to the northeast to revisit one of my once favorite sushi places. I used to come ALL the time for fresh sushi and the happy sushi chef who always was attentive and professional. This... wow, it's really gone completely downhill. 
Sushi should not be dull colored or served room temperature. Cooked food should not be luke warm. The waiter should not only be able to answer questions about the ingredients of the food being served, but also should check to see if the ONLY table in the restaurant needs beverages refilled. If there are complains being exchanged, someone should approach the customer to ask what is wrong, not blatantly ignore it. 
The place is disorganized, sloppy, the sushi was done messily and, to be quite honest, seemingly not up to health standard, let alone any other standard. A complete disgrace to what this place once was. 
NEVER GO HERE. I literally threw up in the bathroom and my stomach is still in knots. Just awful.
name: Erin

text: Best restaurant I've been to Tampa so far! The door was definitely hard to find (it's around the back by the pool). But once we got in, everything was incredible. From the staff to the ambiance, and the food. We had a private booth just for the 2 of us which was pretty cool. We had 2 signature cocktails, the monkey bread, and the burrata. All would highly recommend.
name: Kimberly

text:
This restaurant exceeded our expectations, and if we lived nearby, we would make many return trips. We happened to be in town for a concert and were looking for a light bite and a few drinks after the show.

We were greeted with a smile by the host and seated immediately. Our waitress was also super friendly and mentioned that the kitchen had just closed, but would make us whatever we wanted.  I got the grilled octopus (absolutely killer!) and my wife got a plate of arancini (also incredible!).

Cocktails were diverse and well made.

All in all a hidden gem for sure!
name: Blair

text: OMG THIS PLACE SUCKS!! The only bar in town where it's named by the alleged owner. Arrogant? Well ya the staff is. The bar tender spits a big luggy on floor when my wife wants a drink,,,,,REALLY ?? What a douche'
name: Dave

text: Food is delicious. Never a bad meal. Service is good and staff is friendly. Can't find Mexican food this good in a Tampa.
name: Brad

text: Awesome food, awesome service. The manager the night we were there was amazing! He was playing host, food runner, waiter and bus boy.
name: Tara

text: Very yummy food. The servers were friendly. I came here twice for breakfast while on our trip. I ordered different plates and was really happy with them both.
name: Nirelle

text: The food could use some improvement. Although our waiter was really nice and helpful.
name: Carissa

text: Always a great visit.  We tried a different place (crannies) and commented on how much we wish we had gone to Frenchys.  Price is good, quick service, the perfect beach meal place.
name: Jim

text:
One world market has the best sushi in Indianapolis. You might not get the ambiance of ukiyo, but One World's rolls are way more bang for you buck, and the quality is amazing. It is all counter service, as it is also a grocery store, but the service is very quick and they have amazing take quick to go roll and bowl options. Also, in their a la cartel area, you can buy small portions of sashimi so that you could try a few different things and pick the amount of each you want. 

Everyone has to try a onigiri! They are so good a great options for a quick lunch on the go.
name: Brittany

text: The owner was extremely friendly and helpful. She helped navigate us through the menu. Conversation was great and the food even better. Everything we tried was extremely tasty and we plan on going again. Coffee, hush puppies and gator are a must try.
name: Alexis

text: I enjoyed the mezcal shots with Fanta! That was a pretty good start to my evening. The food choices are delicious, especially the steak sandwich. It's a bit on the pricier side but I had a really good time here.
name: Melica

text: I was excited to find a new coffee shop close to work. A friend and I stopped in for a quick chat, coffee, and breakfast. My experience was very underwhelming despite some great reviews. The menu is extensive but that's about it. The service was honestly among the worst I have experienced in a local business in ANY city I have visited. The barista seemed bothered by having to serve us. We waited over 15 minutes for scrambled eggs. She didn't even bother to call out that our coffee was ready. What's the point of giving us a number and having a tip line if they aren't full service. None of the staff seemed happy to be here or smiled...
name: Chris

text:
Happy Hour review only:

What a beautiful collection of white and brown liquors stacked to design on the back shelves of the bar.  

The "well" liquor for martinis blew, so I went with top shelf, which at any other place would have been $14-$16, this went for $8.25 at happy hour.  I HOPE it wasn't a mistaken charge. ;)  The beers, my follow up to my martini so I wouldn't get totally trashed and make an ass out of myself, especially since I am "single" again, were a few bucks off from stated normal prices during said Happy Hour.  The beer selection was OK, not large by any stretch, but I found two IPAs for my taste...good enough...in a nice cold glass poured by EXCELLENT bar-servers.

OK, I got a minor buzz on, time for food.  Happy hour menu was very reasonable.
   --Fired up shrimp, 5 stars
   --Steak tacos, 4 stars
   --Crispy ribs, sooo tender and crispy coating, 5 stars
   --Crispy cauliflower, not my fave, had better, 2 stars

The bar scene was eclectic, no losers, nice looking middle aged women for conversation with me and my buddy, not that I will EVER date again...I'm done with women. ;)
name: Brian

text: Breakfast here was DELICIOUS! We got the blueberry pancakes and a biscuit sandwich with tomato jam, bacon, eggs, and cheddar cheese.  The pancakes were we seriously the best pancakes I've ever had!  The coffee was strong and delicious.  Our service was wonderful and the restaurant was really cozy!
name: Katie

text: Parking was annoying and I was already in a bad mood by the time I got inside. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. There were a couple things I liked and a couple things I probably wouldn't get again.
name: User

text: I've been to Ainsworth twice, and both experiences were bad. The first time I went with a group of friends, and our waitress rushed us at every point of our meal, although there was almost no one else there. The second time I went to Ainsworth, our waiter was clearly intoxicated, and very inappropriate. He pushed alcohol on our group (all students), got our orders wrong, and set down our drinks at a different table before bringing them to us. I am disappointed that we still paid for our meals even after telling a manager about our terrible experience. Our food was decent, but I would recommend most other restaurants in Nashville over the Ainsworth.

text: Been here multiple times since my best friend lives in walking distance. Never had a bad meal. Prices are reasonable and service is always good. Been here for both breakfast and lunch/dinner and both have been great. Small menu but I feel that's better for quality any way
name: Cassie

text: We chose to go to Feast to celebrate our anniversary and were so disappointed that we left to eat somewhere else. We got seated and sat there for 15 mins and no one other than the person pouring us water even acknowledged we were there. Waiters were constantly circling us talking to the tables next to us or just standing at the bar observing until someone needed them. And still no one brought us a menu or spoke to us. When we left an older gentlemen said "Have a good evening" and I told him we were leaving because no one had been to our table and he said "Can I offer you a drink to calm you down?". I'm just so shocked and disappointed that a nice establishment would treat us like that.

text:
This one is better one of the 3 Sweet Tomatoes located in Tampa. A bit more cleaner and better service is the difference. Other two I visited were not that comfortably clean and as well serviced as this one.

Buffet with options of Salad, Soup, Pizza, Garlic breads, cupcakes and ice creams. Drinks is extra so decide upfront if you want to drink.

Try the craft salads they keep mixing fresh. Those Were interesting.

Don't forget to show Yelp offer at the beginning before billing so you get whole 15% off on the food.
name: K

text: Ordered takeout because I didn't feel like cooking and it held up okay. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. It was decent, just a little uneven. The food was good and the service was easygoing.
name: User

text: We have been coming here every week, since, we moved here over 2 months ago.  They have a very large menu~ for brunch @ 7 a.m.  to closing for lunch & dinner.  Music every night, Thursday @ 6 p.m. Trivia night!  Happy hour until 6 P.M.   You can  call ahead seating....  & take a chance!!  as, it jammed packed.   Love this place!   Came here before, when my daughter lived here for 17 years!  (She now lives in CA!)

text: Place was awesome!!! Drinks were strong, with a laid back atmosphere!! We could people watch outside, charge our phones and relax while we waited to go to the airport! Great waitress!! Limited menu but the food was worth it!!
name: Lindsay

text: We came into this bar during the afternoon on Friday, June 22nd, to listen to music and have a drink.  It wasn't extremely busy.  I had to use the restroom downstairs and there was only one restroom each for the women and men.  While I was in the restroom, some mean and/or drunk person was yelling at the restroom to get out because they had to use it.  So I hurried out and accidentally left my expensive Maui Jim sunglasses sitting on a stand/cabinet.  Immediately after, I realized I forgot them and turned around to go back to get them and they were gone.  I went to each bar downstairs and asked the bartenders if anyone turned them in and of course, they didn't.  The bartenders weren't very friendly and didn't seem to care.  So someone decided not to be honest and steal them and keep the sunglasses for themselves.  Very disappointed with some people these days. Very dishonest.   The point is--why does such a large bar/restaurant only have one restroom each with this many people that come through.  This is unacceptable and very poor planning on the part of the builder/management.  If we ever come back to Nashville, I'm not sure I would go to this bar again.  There are much better choices down there to go to.  I did send an e-mail through your website that same day to see if anyone turned them in but I didn't hear back from them until June 25th.  I like Dierks Bentley's music but not a fan of his bar/restaurant.
name: Lola

text: Everything is always delicious! For a pretty good price you can keep craming your face full
name: Pete

text: As a fellow South African I've been dying to try out and support Barbara's but we keep on forgetting that they are closed on Saturdays (when we typically are in the Franklin area) but with todays gloomy weather I was longing back home and for my Ouma's/Nana's Sunday lunch cooking and finally remembered that I haven't tried Barbara's! So glad we went today. I have NOTHING bad to say. Absolutely stunning and yummy southern home cooking! Probably the best fried chicken and okra I've tried in the South/Tennessee. Worth a try! Nothing better than South African Tannies cooking!! You'll see much more of me!

text: The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Food was fresh and service was quick. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Ordered a few things and liked most of it.

text: The hot pot is extremely worthy. I like their meat and vegetable! Hope everyone want to eat Chinese food can choose here! You will not regret for choosing here!

text: Got there today at 1145am today, looking forward to great meal and service, instead, I got 1/2 of it, great meal! The service experience begin at the counter, waited a few minutes, then a new line open...the manager, instead of calling for next in line, he proceeded to take someone just came in the door...the cashier that was helping me, was good and cordial, but disappeared, and never gave me a receipt, nor offer me one? text: It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.

Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus..

text:

text:
Stopped by here for brunch on a Thursday around 11 a.m. and waited about 30 mins. The hostess will take your cell phone number and text you when your table is ready if you want to explore The Gulch while you wait (the famous wings mural is only a block or two away). They also were nice enough to hold our suitcases for us while we ate as we were waiting to check in to our house.

The food was good and came out quickly for the entire restaurant being full. But the waitress seemed a little confused at every touch point - brought me a hot coffee instead of iced, had another waitress bring us orange juice when she already dropped it at our table. But overall she was very friendly and happy to help when we let her know of our issues. 

Super cute decor and all of the breads are made in-house. The biscuits are a must get!

text: Went to JM's on a cold, snowy Saturday morning and the place was PACKED.  The hostess indicated a 45-minute wait, so we saddled up to the bar.  Service was fantastic and the food was absolutely delicious.  Large portions and very, very good.  We will absolutely be back.

text: It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. If you're more of an Olive Garden type and thrive off counting the exact number of shrimp, then Annabella's may be a bit out of your league. Hey, a lid for every pot, right?

text:
DISCLAIMER: I am 21 years old so I probably enjoy this place way more than college graduates do. 

The Boot is by no means a nice bar. It's filled with underage college students, us fraternity brothers, and sometimes even highschoolers who will tell you they go to Tulane (until you ask them what dorm and they get completely bamboozled). Do I care? Not at all - this scene is what makes The Boot, well, The Boot!

Music:
The music here is top-notch. From throwbacks to current hits, the music never gets old. 

Let's take a trip down memory lane so I can explain my reasoning for the solid 4 star review. Some of my favorite memories here at the Boot are during the most exciting times of the school year: Syllabus Week, Wet Bid Night, Mardi Gras, Tequila Sunrise, tailgates, etc. Syllabus Week, for those reading this who are unfamiliar, is the first week of every semester where us college kids get absolutely obliterated for a week straight. Why? Well, no one is ready to get back into the swing of things schoolwise quite yet so we drown our sorrows in watered down, triple vodka sours. On game days The Boot comes in clutch. Tired of Natty Lights at the tailgate? Walk less than two blocks to The Boot for a John Daly (which are awesome here). Hungry and want to get drunk? Cop a slice of Boot Pizza, pair it with a tequila lemonade and you got yourself a drunk 5 star meal! 

The memories here are truly endless. I probably have a picture at this bar with every ex-girlfriend of mine (does that say something? Crap). Getting into fights for absolutely no reason. Eating cheese fries at 2:00 AM while your friend pulls trig by the garbages behind The Boot Store. Man, these were (and still are!) some good times. 

Although I have been thrown out of the Boot (think Jazz being tossed out  by Uncle Phil in the Fresh Prince of Bel Air) before, been served watered down drinks, and made decisions that have "L" written all over them, The Boot holds a special place in my heart. Mardi Gras, here I come!
name: William

text: Friend and I booked a Double Tree location downtown. Service was terrible. From beginning to end. Final straw was the knock on our door at 2 am from valet demanding our keys; we didn't valet. text:
Blue Box Pizza is a great new addition to the Delmar Loop, though it is much like Doughocracy...but with an upgrade! Pizzas are ordered with the same formula as with the place's previous tenant. You get all kinds of choices. Not only do they have pizza, they have sandwiches, fried foods and burritos you can customize. 

While you wait, or after you eat, they have retro video game stations at the place. I played some old school Atari after eating my pie! As long as you give them your debit card (also show them your ID), you get the controls to any video game system of your choice. They do have the Classic NES, Classic Super NES and Atari 2600 systems. Also available are charging stations. How cool is that?

I had the traditional pizza, with the original crust, sauce, mozzarella, with sausage, onions and black olives. The dough tasted great, like it was also sort of sweetened. It tasted perfect to me - after all, I chose everything! Lol. They have fountain soda, but they don't have the "remix" machine that Doughocracy had. That's okay, as you get a lot for your money no matter what here. 

I will definitely come back and try some of the other menu items. Some time in the future I'd like to have pepper jack cheese and tuna on my pizza (don't ask me why...)! If you're strolling along Delmar Loop, be sure to stop in here. It will all be worth it!
name: Jason

text: I have grown to like the store  When it first opened I gave it 1 star. The meat department is usually pretty good & the bagels are great!  Had to upgrade my review! Hope they keep it up!

text:
I'm a military brat and was born and raised on German rye breads. Trust me if I tell you that I have tried dozens upon dozens of rye breads in the US that purport to be 'European Style' only to be disappointed and let down each time.
Until Barrio Bread opened its doors.
These are, without a doubt, the best loaves of bread on this side of the Atlantic Ocean.
European rye breads are very complex, both in taste and texture, but you have managed to perfect the recipe and bake loaves to die for.
To top that off, they freeze and reheat magnificently, so that after you take them out of the oven they taste like you just walked out of the bakery with them.
Hats off to all of you at Barrio Bread, you have enriched my life with your mastery as well as the good folks of Tucson. Thank you.
name: Mike

text: We've eaten here before. It was a good enough experience to warrant a second visit but I think we're done. It is a very attractive and warm setting, but that's where the pleasantries end. Our busboy brought by our waters when we sat down and then a long time later, it turns out our busboy was our waiter. He simply didn't have the personality for hospitality. He didn't notice empty drink glasses, never came by to inquire how things were, when I ordered a second drink after calling after him as he continued to ignore our table, it didn't come until we inquired where it was - and we had both finished our entrees. When he brought the drink he said the bar was 'backed up' but it was clear the drink sat back there for a long time. I asked for a 'tall' drink - more soda than liquor and, of course, it came in a short glass. Anyway, the duck wings - which were really drumettes, were tasty, crispy and the best part of the meal. When the entrees finally came, my partner got the $22+ scallop entree which looked to me the size of an appetizer or a lunch entree. Four small scallops. I got the crispy duck ramen. The duck confitte was good - not at all crispy but at this point we were glad we just got the food, BUT, cardinal sin!!! the broth wasn't there. It was a bowl of a duck leg and ramen. While it came with the requisite large soup ladle, there simply wasn't any broth except at the bottom of the 1/2 lb. of ramen. Most ramen places prize their food on the quality of their beloved broth. I wouldn't know - there was none. The table next to us complained about something and a female manager tended to them to their satisfaction - we were hoping she'd turn to us and ask us about our experience. No such luck - she was gone in a  flash. This place has serious problems, especially when you consider our two meals with two drinks and one shared appetizer came to $94. Last weekend we had a spectacular lunch at Ocean Prime in Tampa where we each got lobster bisque and a wonderful seafood salad and it was $86. Absolutely no comparison.
name: Walt

text:
To be honest, I'm surprised that there are bad reviews of China King.  I've had their food at least six times now, and only found one offering to be less than great.  

So far I've had: crab rangoon, steamed dumplings, spring rolls, Kung Pao chicken, deluxe Lo Mein, General Tso's chicken, Szechaun style pork, sweet and sour chicken, pepper steak, and Moo Shu Pork.  The only disappointment among the list were the spring rolls.  They weren't as light & crispy as expected, and I'd probably skip them in the future.  

But, everything else has been sensational.  I've ordered in-store for carryout/take home once, had food delivered all other times.  Food was hot and fresh each time it was delivered, and within the quoted timeframe.  All the food is flavorful, fresh, and hot.  It's far and away the best Chinese (or Americanized/New York style Chinese) that I've found in the Largo area.  The Lo Mein, Moo Shu pork, and General Tso's chicken have been repeat orders, as well as the crab rangoon and steamed dumplings.  

Aside from excellent food, the people who run the business are attentive to detail.  Request extra hoisin sauce for the Moo Shu pork?  Check.  Asked for medium spicy General Tso's?  Check.  Hot mustard packets thrown in?  Check.  They haven't missed a beat with any special requests.  

Note that the sweet and sour chicken is just fried tempura chicken with sauce, but no vegetables.  And even dishes marked "hot" or "spicy" are very tame.  But as noted, they will add heat if you ask.  

All in all China King is a top-notch eatery in Largo.  They've earned my repeat business and I look forward to the next order.  The only problem is, as a single person, what do I order and what do I skip?  it's all great, so that's a nice problem to have....
name: Brian

text:
I want to share about my family's experience we had at the King Of Prussia, PA Red Lobster on 10/31/18. Unfortunately, we had a very disappointing experience. 

1. I had called and reserved call ahead seating for 6:20pm. My husband, our auntie, and myself arrived and had to wait about 10 minutes to be seated even though we had call ahead seating and there were clearly places available. (It wasn't a very busy night.)

2. Our waitress took a very long time to come to us and take our drink orders. (Probably about 20 minutes.) When she finally did take our drink orders, she took several more minutes getting back to us and got 2 of the drinks incorrect.

3. We ordered an appetizer, and it took so long to get to us, we asked if we could cancel the appetizer. Our waitress told us it was being prepared at that time, so we couldn't cancel it. It took at least another 15 minutes from then to get our appetizer.

4. We weren't asked about placing our entree orders until being at the restaurant for an hour.

5. When we went to order, we all ordered what we wanted. Three of us ordered salmon. We later found out the restaurant was out of salmon. Our waitress convinced my father and mother in law and our auntie that the swordfish was a good substitute. Then, 10 minutes later, we found out the restaurant was out of swordfish too! Tilapia was then recommended. But, it's not the same taste at all, and not what anyone wanted.

6. I had really wanted a burger and had found it on the Red Lobster website as a menu option: https://www.redlobster.com/search-results?indexCatalogue=default&searchQuery=Wood%20Grilled%20Cheeseburger*&wordsMode=AllWords The waitress looked at me like I was crazy and said she would ask the cook. 10 minutes later, when she came back, I had to ask about the burger to find out if it was available. It wasn't. I'm disappointed it was listed at all if it wasn't available.

7. Our entrees took a long time to get to us. We had been at the restaurant for two hours when we had finally gotten our food, eaten, and were leaving. 

8. It seemed like our waitress was only half trying and really didn't care about serving us well. It was a really frustrating experience and left my husband and I not wanting to return again.

I sent this message to Red Lobster corporate, and they have yet to respond. It seems like they really don't care about giving good service.
name: Katelyn

text:
On the riverfront. This place might upgrade itself to a three with a little extra effort. We were seated promptly without reservations, but service was *extremely* slow, inexplicably so since it was really not that busy. OK spot for a quick bite to eat IF it was "quick". 

We had a very pleasant waitress take our orders (when one finally came to our table) but two others served us (one who brought drinks and one who brought food). No check-backs, no refills. Food was good, but portions small (for the prices). TIP for management: get your staff better organized and add a little more of that tasty gumbo to the bowl.

text: I wanted to love this place. It's a cool spot and the menu looks great! But...I didn't . Neither did my wife. We ordered the O.G pizza and meatballs. The meatballs were very good but a little pricey for three meatballs. Sauce was tasty and the meatballs had a nice herbal taste to the them. We also ordered a bottle of wine. Three choices only. White blend, Rose or Cabernet Sauvignon. All of them are available by the glass as well. I would ha w like to see more varietals offered. The white was decent and around $40. The O,G. pizza description sounded great:Italian sausage, Calabrian Chile's, arugula and smoked  mozzarella. We didn't taste the sausage or smoked mozzarella at all. Almost none on the pie. LOTS of Calabrian Chiles and arugula with long tough stems. Visually the pizza looked great. The crust had nice char on it. The texture was unfortunately dry and tough. Disappointed. The service is friendly although our pizza took about 25 minutes even though there was only a couple tables seated besides us. The courtyard seating is nice and it backs up to the Lark Restaurant. The meatballs were a 4 plus and the pizza was a 3 star pie. I probably would try Paxton's or other place the next time I am in Santa Barbara.
