text:
This place was awesome! I've heard so many good things that I needed to try it out myself. 

Came here on the rainy Sunday afternoon around 2pm. The restaurant was completely empty and remained that way the entire time we were there :( 

Our waitress was super kind and helpful. We ordered the Vegan Crepes with bananas and blueberries and the Banana Bread (gluten-free) french toast. 

It took around 15-20ish minutes for our food to be made. A little long considering we were the only people in the restaurant, but we didn't mind. My brother enjoyed a matcha tea with almond milk. 

The portions were great for each dish only being $9-10. We loved the crepes. They were light, fluffy and sweet. They even had almond milk Redi-Whip on top. The banana bread french toast was even better though! The homemade banana bread was fresh and flavorful. We loved the entire dish. It was $22 for both dishes and my brother's hot drink, not bad at all! I hope to come back soon!

text:
Sindoore is very close to the airport, so anyone who is staying in a hotel or in Nashville for one night--this is your place to try! The restaurant is on the smaller side but it is cozy inside and decorated nicely (with a Bollywood flair of course). 

I was passing through this area and decided to get some food to-go. I ordered the Bangin' Baingan ($12) for my entree, which is roasted eggplant cooked with peas, tomatoes, onions, ginger and garlic. As with many other Indian dishes, this was very flavorful and had a soft texture almost like a dip. The main dishes come with jasmine rice but I wanted to try their pulao, which is flavored basmati rice with peas and golden raisins ($6). I really enjoyed this rice. I got a side of Dahi ki Chutney ($2), which are grated cucumbers in a homemade yogurt with chopped mint leaves. One of my friends always eats this over the rice, and it goes so well together as kind of a palate cleanser. I also had to have their original style naan bread ($2) which was two huge pieces of naan. 

My eyes were bigger than my stomach since I had over half of the food I ordered uneaten. However, all of it was delicious. I liked dipping the naan in the eggplant dish and eating the chutney and rice together. The combinations of all the food was so good. 

The staff was nice, the food was packaged up well for my to-go order, the prices were reasonable and everything was tasty. I will keep Sindoore in mind for my future Indian food cravings!
name: Maddie

text: The actual Whiskey Cake was amazing with its warm caramel and candied pecans. Mixed drinks were delicious, although not very strong. The food was okay, I ordered the tomato basil soup with the adult Mac and cheese. Everyone liked my dish the best, but I noticed that none of the food was hot, more of a lukewarm (hurry up and eat it) temperature. Our waitress lacked personality and we wanted to order more drinks but it was taking too long to place an order and then wait for the drink to be made. It would've been nice to have someone explain the menu and guide us to recommended whiskeys- 300 is difficult to choose from. We came here for a birthday celebration during the week when it was slow. I have mixed feelings about this place because I love the decor and it has a lot of potential. Just a few kinks to work out and this place will be successful. Love the homegrown aspect, just needs to be built up and showcased more with love and attention to customers, especially when the price is this upscale. Might give it another try someday.

text:
This was easily my favorite place that I ate in New Orleans. After hearing all of the acclaim (it's been recognized as one of the best restaurants in America, and written about by Bon Appetit), I knew that I had to try it out. Honestly - this was the best seafood I've ever had in my life. I enjoyed some shrimp bisque and a Louisiana shrimp roll, and they were absolutely amazing. I can't even imagine eating better shrimp in my life. It's that good.

Not to mention - I tried my first oyster here! I was so nervous to eat an oyster - I thought I would hate it! However, I was proven wrong, because they were delicious! 

Not to mention - this place is so reasonably priced. The most expensive entree on the menu is around $27. Can you believe it? However, you DEFINITELY need a reservation. 

Even the atmosphere in this restaurant is perfect. It's very intimate and friendly. If you are ever in the NOLA area, you HAVE to stop by this place. You will not regret it.
name: Janelle

text: First time ordering a takeout tonight.  Ordered pork fried rice, a Chicken vegetable stir fry, and crab rangoon.  Ordered the pork with 0 heat and the chicken with 2 heat.    Found that all the food was delicious, glad I only ordered a 2 heat on the stir fry.  They go up to a 5 on the heat so I can't imagine how hot that could be.  Definitely thought the quantities were generous on the food and it was all very flavorful.  Definitely will go back and try some of the other items on the menu.  Found place has been cleaned up from the previous owners.  Would not hesitate on eating in.  Staff was very pleasant.

text: Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Nice little spot, decent portions too. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Food was good and came out fast. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really.

text: Southern cooking & hipster fusion. Husk is a creative and delicious blend of traditional southern cooking with locally sourced and hipster overtones. The cocktails are surprisingly complex and excellent. The plates are outstanding. Be sure to enjoy the vegetables - an unexpected treat. The restaurant is located a short walk from downtown, but you feel like you're nowhere near the crowd. The staff is attentive. I will return.

text:
Not much to say.
Yes the Sandwiches are pretty much the best around.
But the service was very slow.
I waited 20 minutes + for 3 Amighetti specials. 
Bummed that The Hill location is closed.

text: I got an iced coffee & an almond croissant. It is clean, and has a pleasant staff. I will be back!

text: Long story short: boyfriend got a number one with only ketchup and mustard, and his had everything on it. I got the four for four.... and I didn't get the nuggets or the sauce. Oh, and our fries were already lukewarm when we were pulling out of the drive of the Wendy's and did the normal "oh I'll just have one before we get home." Didn't go back because we were already home and it was late. Majorly upset I didn't get the FOUR for four, only 3 (and it was missing the BEST PART). Don't mean to sound like a "Karen," but I'll be speaking to someone higher up, because I really wanted my nuggets and most places won't give them to you unless you have your full order with you and I'm not going back at 12am. :(  Hope I get my nugs. Seeing the other reviews, I'd definitely say to go to the one not too far away from this one. Maybe they have a better history of getting orders right?

text:
Nahhh not the Mexican food joint of my life. 
Came here for lunch and the service was super slow. Ordered the steak fajitas for lunch and they clearly forgot my order. It arrived after everybody at my table had already eaten their food. The house guacamole was good. Glad we ordered it or I'd have been starving. When my food did arrive the steak was way over cooked and tasted like napkins...flavorless. I wouldn't come back unless someone else was paying and all I ordered was guacamole and a $2.99 marg!

text: Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. The wait felt longer than it should have. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Wouldn't really choose this place again. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean.
name: User

text:
If you like dancing and Vietnamese noodle soup come to this spot. You might run into the Weeknd.

This is a good example of what a "supper club" is.. supper during the day, club at night. XO is centrally located on 103rd street downtown just outside of City Centre mall and about a block away from Roger Place. 

The menu is very extensive and lends itself to a premium Vietnamese restaurant. This place isn't dirty. They have granite counter tops and pleather chairs. Mother fuckin' pleather chairs in an Asian restaurant. I mean, I think this is a place where the producers of "Crazy Rich Asians" would choose to film a stupid dinner or lunch scene. 

In addition to the furniture, you pay a premium to eat here. A bowl of loaded pho is $15 before tax and tip. But it's decent soup, not the best but it's full and rich of flavour. I don't know if you guys want me to talk more about the food, it's just regular Vietnamese food. 

The problem is, there's not a lot of competition around the area so if you have a hankering for some Asian persuasion, come here. But pick your times correctly so that you don't get Hennessy spilled in your soup. 4/5.
name: Tony

text: Honestly I think I ordered the wrong thing. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. Ordered a few things and liked most of it.
name: User

text: The food was good and the service was easygoing. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus..
name: User

text: Great pizza and just right amount of sauce and cheese and delicious fresh ingredients-- only exception is the crust and dough is crispy and good but not like the original DeLorenzo's in robbinsville-  it has that perfect chewy/ crispy crust - but overall very nice and good pizza and very nice and good service

text:
Food-5
Ambience-5
Service-5

I went here for happy hour, but I can't really speak for the main attraction, the tacos, because I just had an appetizer and drinks. My friends did order tacos, and looked like they really enjoyed it. Our waitress was really nice and helped answer any questions that we had about the menu. We sat outside, and it was a nice setting to catch up with the girls. I had frozen margaritas and took one to go; they were excellent and had me feeling just right! I also shared some delicious queso with two friends, but I would recommend sharing it with only two people because it's not extremely large. Overall, great experience!

text: My Dad and I visited this restaurant in September.  The Po-Boy was one of the best I have had in NOLA.  We also ordered the fried pickles as an appetizer...surprisingly this appetizer seems to have been made for 4+ people since the portion was so huge.  The staff were friendly as well.

text: Great food, great people, great atmosphere. If I could give it 100 stars I would!! I feel at home here!!! Cannot say enough great things about this place!!! Love this place!! Must try if you want great Mexican food, also they have vegan options
name: Franco

text: They had live music the Sat morning I took my 4 year old. Great food and atmosphere (cozy and busy but still nice). Delish croissant sandwich, fresh squeezed OJ.
name: Alicia

text:
Good luck finding parking.  The food though is delicious.  Wednesday at 5:30 approximately 25 min wait. Dinner salad was average tasting. We ordered Chicken spedini and seafood ravioli.  The spedini was good the side white pasta was extremely thick.

The seafood ravioli was phenomenal.  I savored every bite and the sauce was soaked up with bread. It was so good more bread was ordered to sop up all the sauce.
name: Steve

text: I did two tours while I was in New Orleans this past week and they were both phenomenal. The first was the ghost and vampire tour, guided by Lee. He did an absolutely fantastic job showing us around and getting us into the spooky mood. We enjoyed it so much, we booked the cemetery tour two days later. That tour was also a ton of fun and gave us a great education on the history and culture of New Orleans. I would definitely recommend this tour group to others visiting New Orleans and will definitely be doing the Garden tour next time I'm in the city!
name: Rachel

text: Honestly I think I ordered the wrong thing. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. The music was louder than it needed to be. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. I can see why people like it, even if I wasn't fully sold. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything..
name: User

text: One of my new favorite sushi places of all time. The atmosphere was amazing and the food was great. The staff was very nice and very attentive and the pricing for the food was a great deal, considering the average price of sushi in the stl area.
name: Tina

text: Staying at a hotel down the street and needed something to be able to bring back. Food was great and the service was amazing. Everyone was super friendly. Only reason it was not a 5 Star was it took much longer than I thought to get my food.
name: Tj

text: We went for lunch. Taylor was our server, he was very nice and gave us great service. I got the build your own burger. It was absolutely melt in your mouth delicious. My husband have the buffalo chicken sandwich that was yummy also. We will definitely go back!!
name: Leigh

text:
Came in search of our go to Chinese food place. It was pretty quiet for a Sunday night. It was clean and service was pretty quick. We ordered shrimp and rice combo with egg drop soup and spring roll, steak and pad Thai noodles combo with egg roll and wonton soup and Korean BBQ combo with egg roll and wanton soup.
 
The shrimp and rice was  pretty good, not spectacular but not bad. Would have liked some yum yum sauce but did not see any. The spring roll was good and not greasy. The egg drop soup was also good. Our daughter liked the steak and pad Thai noodles, her favorite was the wonton soup. The egg roll were also very good and not greasy. The Korean BBQ was very spicy and not to our liking. We wished for more veggies. 

Dinner overall was good but would try a few different menu items next time but would stick with the soup and egg rolls. The price for three was about 50$ and we came home with leftovers. If we are in the area we would stop by again but not sure it is our go to place.
name: T

text: Oh Milktooth. Just like about everyone else in Indy, this is one of my favorite spots- especially for brunch. With the ever changing menu, the freshest ingredients, the cozy and funky atmosphere, and the knowledgeable and pleasant staff you honestly cannot go wrong. If you want the best of the best don't sleep on this place!
name: Liz

text: It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Food was fresh and service was quick. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Nice little spot, decent portions too. It looked better online than it did in person. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..
name: User

text:
Hands down, the best Chinese food my family has found in Reno. Palais De Jade is a little off the beaten path for the average out-of-towner, but definitely worth the effort. 

Located in a strip mall a few miles of the interstate, this place is a medium sized restaurant. Once inside you'll find a nice sized bar, plenty of booth style seating with dark wood and white tablecloths. There is a back room with the large tables for bigger groups.

We were greeted with an extensive menu with all the usual dishes. Everything we ordered was wonderful. The hot and sour soup was loaded with goodies and had a wonderfully rich stock, that seemed to have layer after layer of flavor. The house chow mien, house fried rice, Mongolian beef and kung pao chicken were so flavorful and full of crisp fresh veggies, and huge portions of meat. The only dish not to hit it out of the park was the beef and mushrooms. Still good, just lacking a little flavor compared to other dishes.

The staff was very friendly and attentive, keeping glasses full, dishes bussed and making sure we were enjoying ourselves. Portions are average as were the prices. I certainly wish we lived closer, Palais De Jade would be a regular on the rotation!
name: Brent

text: The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. The music was louder than it needed to be. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. The whole meal felt kind of uneven.
name: User

text: Ended up here pretty late, maybe around 9:30, because everything else nearby had a wait. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it.
name: User

text:
Lost stars this visit. Pizza was not up to their usual. Not enough cheese and crust was kinda soggy. Order was to go and picked up quickly, like last time.  Don't know exactly what happened this visit but we will try them again and see what happens next time because we really like their pizza. I think i'll skip the order ahead and I'll order when I get there and be able to take it home right out of the oven.


Great pizza. Found this place from a Yelp event. Pizza served at the event was a tasty treat. So we decided to try their store. Pizza is full of toppings and cheesy. Crust is soft but crispy and just enough dough. Not too thick, not too thin. We ordered the chicken Alfredo with spinach. It was yummy. Enough sauce and plenty of chicken. We also had a Backyard. Again, it was excellent. Enough sauce and plenty of pepperoni, sausage, onion, and mushrooms. Crust cooked to perfection. Staff are friendly and helpful. We will return to sample other menu items.

text: Dude the food is garbage.  Frozen oysters, frozen shrimp, frozen grouper.  Shame...with easy access to seafood it should be easy to make good food and get good reviews!  Like the atmosphere, but can't eat that crap.

text: One of my favorite restaurants in the city. The food is consistently great and reasonably priced for what you get. The staff are extremely professional and take great care of the patrons. Will be back many more times in the future!

text:
Grabbed a quick lunch yesterday. The subs were good, fresh, the bread a bit chewy but also fresh. This place filled up super fast, yet the food came out super fast.

Much better than those chain stores. Worth another trip.  Will return again.

text: On vacation for a wedding in Safety Harbor we were looking for a decent affordable breakfast. Athens didn't disappoint. We ate here everyday except 1x as we were headed out early and didn't have time for breakfast. Eggs cooked perfectly, coffee was hot, bacon was crispy. They butter the toast for you so if that's not something you like let them know. For 4 people to eat our bill was $30. Can't beat that!

Arturo and Linda

text:
Everyone told me to go to Hattie B's but I know Prince's is the originator so I ignored them and went straight to Prince's.

Prices were very reasonable and the place was very clean (including the bathrooms). You don't bus your own table and when you leave, they swoop in and clean up right away. It's in a strip mall so there's plenty of parking.  They also sell beer. 

Do I recommend you come here? Yes. Often. 

I've not had Hattie's but I can't imagine it's better than this.

text:
Diamond Street Bar & Grill is definitely a hidden gem.  It's a small, unassuming restaurant on a side street near the convention center.  We were in town for just a day and staying at a nearby hotel.  I checked Yelp for creole restaurants nearby and this was one of the top recommendations, along with another place called Galliano Restaurant.  I asked the hotel front desk and they said they'd never heard of Diamond Street but that Galliano was the place to go.  We stopped there first, looked at the menu, and neither one of my sons wanted to order anything.  We left and walked a couple of blocks to Diamond St.  When we walked up it looked a little sketchy, but we said we would give it a try.  I'm so glad we did!  Here's the order and rating (1-5 scale)

Mozzarella sticks w/marinara - 3.5
Swamp fries - 4.5
Buffalo shrimp & fries - 4.5
Fried shrimp po boy - 4
Ribeye steak - 4
Overall value - 5

I couldn't believe the pricing.  Each po boy is only $10, and a huge ribeye steak was only $15!!!  Everything was good.  The cheese sticks were pretty standard; good but not great. The swamp fries are super cheesy and have an amazing meat & gravy combo that takes them over the top. Buffalo shrimp was pretty close perfect; flavorful, spicy, juicy, and fresh.  Po boy was really good but would have liked to have a little more shrimp on such a huge loaf of bread. Ribeye was juicy and flavorful.  My only issue is that we ordered it medium rare and they brought it out closer to medium well.  We didn't send it back because it was still good, so my son just went with it.  

If you're in New Orleans and looking for a place to get a great meal at a great place, Diamond Street Bar & Grill is your place!
name: Mychael

text:
I went in for lunch on a Monday. We ordered from the lunch menu. We went with a soft shell crab sandwich, catfish po boy, and two kid lunches (hamburger and spaghetti).

The soft shell sandwich is decent. Not the best crab, but not the worst. It is a little unwieldy in sandwich form, so you end up eating it with a fork. The remoulade sauce on it is quite tasty and original. The fries that came with it were marginal. The catfish po boy was huge. It had a ton of catfish on it. The catfish had a slightly muddy taste to it. The po boy came with gumbo. The crab sandwich did not. Not sure why it came with one but not the other, but the gumbo was very good ~ probably the best part of any of the meals. 

The service was sound. No complaints there. But this is the thing. The bill with tip came out to $70. For two sandwiches and two kid meals. This ain't New York City, y'all. It's Marrero, Louisiana. Charging nine dollars for a kid meal, for example, is way out of line. The food here is good, but it's not seventy dollar sandwich lunch good. So, if you've led a charmed life and money is no object, go and enjoy. But if you're a budget hawk like I am, there are hundreds of po boy joints all around south Louisiana that have similar to superior options at a quarter of the price.
name: David

text: The music was louder than it needed to be. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. Will be back. Not bad for a quick meal. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. It looked better online than it did in person.
name: User

text:
I am updating this review today. Since the last time I have been here maybe 25 times. Consistently good! Also a notable improvement with the employees. Keep up the good work!
KEEP THE FRENCHIE!!!!
name: Greg

text: Nice environment but my food had no flavor unfortunately. The alcapurrias appetizer is was the only thing we ordered that was good.
name: Lynette

text:
A must visit in the French Quarter! 

This place looks like an unassuming little establishment from the street but is huge inside and has seating on 2 floors. It has a ton of charm and character inside as well. The location is clean and very well maintained. We visited on a Saturday evening as a party of 6 and there was a small wait, but nowhere near as bad as many other places. The line did spill out into the street from time to time, but it also moved pretty quick.

The staff here is top-notch. Everyone we came in contact with was cheerful and welcoming. The bar made some very good drinks for a number of people in our party. Our waiter took the rest of our drink and appetizer orders and was able to answer all of our questions about the menu.

We ordered a wide variety of food and everything was absolutely amazing! The gator tail bites were very tender and flavorful with a sauce that had a bit of kick to it. The cajun fries had a delicious sauce that was like nothing we had tasted before Their gumbo was rich and savory. BBQ ribs were some of the best were ever had in a restaurant. I tried the shrimp fettuccine alfredo and it was the best I can remember having anywhere! The sauce was rich, buttery and creamy with definite parmesan flavor.

For desert, we ordered the banana foster ice cream cake with strawberries. It was amazing as well!

This is a DONT MISS experience!
name: Jay

text:
I love everything about this place everything was A1 from the service to every piece of food I ordered, my friend and I drove from Baltimore for a dinner date we never heard of the place we found it on google and we had to check It out..long story short I have a reservation to go right back in a week the owner even called me today about my experience I've ate many places never that much gratitude Continue to flourish Kevin
Ashley
name: EMmy

text:
BEST WINGS.  Smokey and Healthy(meaty) No joke. 
Also they have a ton of TVs 
-cheers!
name: Evan

text:
So tasty and what a beautiful historic building and restaurant. I loved the bar area and Oyster Bar with the freshest oysters.
The food was incredible and so was their home made 'Remoulade' for their seafood dishes.
Absolute MUST for your visit. I will be back
name: Rudy

text:
Have you tried their eggs Benedict? Have you? Let me tell you, it's probably the best eggs benedict in town! It's that good. The eggs are perfectly cooked the hollandaise is perfection. It's so delicious! It's rare to go to a place where everything is perfect and delicious. Let me tell you, Two Chicks does it right!!
And their pancakes are as AMAZING as everything else on their menu. Now I am not a huge pancake fan, but these pancakes are the bees knees. They serve it with this delicious whipped butter and the best syrup. 
If you haven't been, I highly reccomend trying them out and if you have to wait go check out Dragonfly across the way while you wait!!
name: Shanel

text:
A very unassuming Mexican Restaurant that requires you to order your food and pay before. Then you collect a number on a tall stand so that the server can find you at your table when your order is ready. There wasn't a very long line today, but I believe that was because it was a week day. 

We ordered Fajita and Quesadillas which were both wonderful. The food was fresh and plentiful.
name: Andrew

text: I was so so so excited to come here and I was let down so so so hard. This place has such a great vibe with coolers lined up with craft beer along with original and modern decor. Unfortunately, none of that can help the fact that the chicken's flavor was god awful. They highly brag about their pretzel crusted chicken, but they forgot to leave out that doesn't compensate for the potent flavor that instantly hits you when you take a bite. Even the 75 cent honey mustard couldn't save it. I'll give it an extra star because the fries were somewhat decent. Such a shame for such a beautifully decorated place. Give it a try for yourself and let me know if you felt the same. See you all at Popeyes down the street.
name: Morgan

text: Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. Will be back. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price..
name: User

text:
My last couple visits the place has been dead, and I'm not sure why. We've come in for dinner a few times, and maybe Jason's is more of a lunch spot? I've always been acknowledged as soon as I come in and made to feel appreciated by the staff. 

I've tried a few sandwiches, and they've been tasty, but I usually go for a salad bar and soup, specifically the broccoli cheese. I'm sure that creamy and cheesy cup of goodness is terrible for you, but it is so tasty. The salad bar is always fresh. They offer a huge variety, so I think anyone could find something they like here. I love the black currant iced tea. And you get free ice cream; I don't hate it!
name: Ashley

text:
Wow! Best seafood Boil I have had so far. Cooked just right to perfection. You can tell that All ingredients were fresh and man it was good. The fish has the texture of crab or lobster dipped in that sauce. If you are ever in Clearwater beach, come here just for the seafood boil, for $24, it's a steal (maybe in compared to where I am from -California) And try the mussels, also very big and humongous! 
Ask for Emilia, fun lady, she recommended our dish and service was very good. 
Will come back if ever in town again.
name: Tom

text:
Visited with my husband after exploring University of Pennsylvania. If you go, plan a large chunk of time, this is definitely not a quick spot.  

The had a large bar with lots of good selections and seemed to be a great place where people were meeting up with friends. It's on the smaller side, so you may be rubbing elbows with a neighbor. 

My husband has the shrimp BLT, and it was amazing!  I had the chicken sandwich, and it was good, but not as good as the shrimp BLT.
name: Ashley

text: The food is a bot pricey, but other than that this place is great after 10. However, I will say they have my favorite jalepeno poppers. The happy hour seems to satisfy me and my friends for some late night drinking. And the atmosphere seems to be a very laid back one with some high volume music and chatter in the background. If you are looking for late night drinks come check it out!
name: Jason

text: Had brunch here over the weekend and it was kind of a mixed bag. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Would return. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Not bad for a quick meal.
name: User

text: Tried it again. Service was friendly, attentive and fast like last time, much more so in fact! I enjoyed the peaceful atmosphere. The food once again was somewhat bland. I got the dry egg noodles and it looked just like the photo, which greatly impressed me! However like last time the ingredients taste like they are cook separately then put together, rather than creating an overall, single taste profile. It was also a bit too salty. I got the lunch special but still felt like the price was only average for Thai food. Because this place is so close to my house, I may try again someday, but I still prefer other Thai places.
name: Gabby

text: Delicious food but not sure it was worth the price point.  The service was exceptional. We're not big dessert eaters so the fixed menu doesn't work as well for us.
name: Carlos

text: Meh. Boring food. Inattentive service. Very strange owner/chef that did nothing on a busy night, other than go from table to table, handing out free dessert cards, asking for yelp reviews. He seem to be more concerned with how his hat was perched atop his head, then how the food and service were. Odd.
name: Rayelle

text: Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. The food was good and the service was easygoing. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. For the price I expected more than this.
name: User

text: The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. Worth checking out. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. They were out of one thing I originally wanted..
name: User

text: I have been here multiple times and the food is awesome. At times it seems to be a little loud, however it is a family restaurant.
name: Bradley

text: Our steaks were perfect! The Fleming potatoes were great! The house salad and desserts were delicious too. Our server Sebastian took great care of us we will be back for sure.
name: Rose

text: Ordered take out super late. Got our order perfect, made 3 pizzas in like 20 mins. They killed it, owner was super nice!
name: Jonathan

text: Our first food stop in Nashville was the Frothy Monkey (which I kept calling the Flying Monkey). It was full inside so we sat outside and enjoyed the sunshine, although it wasn't quite warm enough yet. My favorite part of the experience was learning how friendly Nashvillians are by being chased after when I tried to bus my own table. Despite being in Tennessee, I ordered the California breakfast since we were going to be eating more soon (Five Daughters Bakery is nearby and delicious) and my friend had the Julie with a latte. I would definitely come back for the charming rustic ambiance and try more items and cocktails (!) on the menu
name: Sarah

text: Adorable place, great customer service, the desserts are delicious, I especially love the chocolates. I am not a fan of their macaroons but to each their own
name: Carolina

text: Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. The menu wasnt huge, which I usually prefer.. Honestly, the wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. Anyway, really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The staff seemed tired but still polite. Also, ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. not sure I'd order the same thing again. Would prob stop in again if nearby.
name: User

text: 5 star all the way!!  Great and friendly staff, Key West like atmosphere and to die for food!!  Local brews only $5.  Please trust me and get the drunken shrimp.... they are made with bourbon and we used the sauce combined with their house habanero sauce on EVERYTHING (broccoli, coleslaw, fish etc)  It's kicks all up a notch!!  I will certainly come back here whenever I find myself out this way.  And they have a resident black crown night heron "chuck"!  Such a sweet friendly bird!!
name: Jules

text: Visiting near here on business and tried this restaurant for dinner based on the reviews. Excellent food and service. Extensive menu - Japanese, Thai, Asian fusion. I had the seafood delight and it was very good. If I lived locally I would definitely return.
name: Chuck

text: The name doesn't make sense for this place at ALL!!! The decor is modem and upscale, if I hear a name like stompin barley I would expect to walk into a sort of country dive bar/ restaurant type place. So I do love the atmosphere inside. I felt like they could have more midweek drink specials on wine or whatever. Friendly staff!  Didn't eat yet... but will try soon.
name: Erika

text: Just waited 24 minutes in the drive through for a bowl of soup, drove all the way back to work to find a half full bowl of water. Never again!
name: Melissa

text: Wow, this place does not disappoint. it all starts with a cute little plate of nachos which were delicious. Then I got enchiladas de mole - i took home half because it was such a huge portion but they were delicious! My friend got a really well made veggie burrito. The veggies were cooked nicely but not so soggy that the entire burrito was a drippy mess like at some places. It came with a fresh side salad with avocado. As if we weren't full enough they capped off our meal with complimentary peaches. So yummy! Definitely can't wait to eat here again - at $25 total for the two of us before tip you can't beat it!
name: Jaime

text: Great views and cocktails. Cheese board was amazing too. Such a fun new place to enjoy Tampa.
name: Nancy

text:
The view is beautiful, however, if you visit be prepared to wait!  I was told the wait would only be 30 minutes but it turned in to 75 minutes -- for a table for 1!  Unacceptable. 

The burger was subpar as the bacon was chewy. I ordered a Pina Colada and it was so weak.  In hopes that dessert would save the evening I ordered the Beach Brownie Blowout. The presentation was awesome but the brownie itself was not fresh. 

If you're looking for an amazing view, this is the place. If you're looking for good food and drink think again!
name: Michael L

text: A large coffee is $2.05 here everywhere else its $1.08. This is ridiculous! I'm not coming back to the Macdonalds on Oddie & Sullivan.
name: Robin

text: Ended up here pretty late, maybe around 9:30, because everything else nearby had a wait. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. Food was fresh and service was quick.
name: User

text: I've only had the churro's so far, and I loved them! They were so good that they made me go back 3 weeks in a row for more. I kinda needed to take a break to contain myself from the tastiness of them before I gave myself a sugar problem haha. If the other things they have there are as good as the churros, then it'll be a real treat trying the rest of their stock
name: Jonathan

text: Food is decent but service is horrible.  Run by a bunch of younger kids that have a bad attitude.  Would not recommend unless you enjoy sub par service and being talked does to.
name: Kory

text: Came here for lunch on a Sunday afternoon sat outside basking in the sun and ordered a beer and a burger. They were both so delicious! I ordered the shoestring fries and they were really small but I ate them all anyway! Next time I'll try the medallions. Beautiful on the inside I really liked the outside seating-server never forgot about us. Can't wait for spring :)
name: Rachel

text: Despite the bad reviews this place had , we decided to give it a try   It was a sat night I will admit but they were not that busy ... I rarely leave bad reviews , this will be short . We arrived , were explained the menu / floor dining system , we decide to go to the 4th floor .. sat for well over 15 minutes no one ever came , so we left , this is review is only based on the first 29 minuets of my arrival , unfortunately I cannot tell you about the food etc... maybe one day I will give them another try but for now 2 stars is the most I could give ..
name: Slex

text: It was...fine. I was expecting a lot more given the reviews. The waiter was great but the food was not worth the price. Maybe this is a summer place and is better with the patio? I found it really weird there were no 7pm reservations available and the restaurant was empty when we got there at 7:20 for our 7:30. We had a nice bottle of wine for $35 which was the only good thing about the dinner.
name: Jill

text: Very nice dining environment and great food!!! Love this place and definitely recommend it!!!
name: Melody

text:
We wanted to try this place, based upon YELP ratings. We were not disappointed. The food was great (pretty much what one might expect from a buffet- the "hibachi" was a Korean-style bar-b-que), the service was top notch, the price well within normal limits.
This place does like jalapeno peppers! We suggest you take small portions originally to check for the heat level.
The place was clean, the restrooms well kept. The building was a little hard to find (it's on the western edge of the Metropolis, and is accessible from Highway 40.)
The only "suggestion" to the company? Your overhead music did not help the dining experience. Yeah, we know, the ambiance should reflect Asian culture. However, Asian techno music was way overwhelming. This restaurant (lunchtime!) is not a Rave party. Could you please have music more focused to dining, not dancing?
name: Thomas

text: Had brunch here over the weekend and it was kind of a mixed bag. For a busy night they handled it okay. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. There were a couple things I liked and a couple things I probably wouldn't get again. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed.
name: User

text:
Amazing!!! I will say it was such a great experience. We ordered the Mexican frittata, so yummy. Enjoyed a mimosa with freshly squeezed OJ. 

If you love good quality service and food. This is the place to go! Great on a Saturday with little to no wait.
name: Brianna

text: Good vegan food was scarce during the holidays but I came out to Breads on Oak three times! Everything was delicious and the bakers and other employees obviously take their work and craft very seriously. Vegans rejoice!
name: Karen

text: Visited due to the Yelp reviews. The food was good the chicken and waffles were delicious. Great customer service. Nice family owned establishment.
name: Contia

text:
This place has supposedly been St louis' best Thai food restaurant for years. I would disagree with that opinion. I haven't been able to check out many other Thai options in St. Louis, but I have definitely been to better Thai places before. 

What we ordered: I got vegetable tempura and it was good. It came with a nice selection of veggies and two sauces. My boyfriend ordered the green curry, which I really liked and I am picky with curry. He chose a medium spice, which was the perfect amount for me- not too spicy, but still had some heat. 

The service was average. The environment was average. 
I will still be looking for a delicious Thai place in STL
name: Midori

text: Honestly probably the best pizza I've ever had from a restaurant of this type. It's not your authentic hole in the wall New York pizza, but the crust is cooked so well and the sauce is delicious. No complaints
name: Andrew

text: The one star is for the flavor. Went for lunch buffet, the service was poor, the variety of food was ok but not much chicken or meat in the sauce. Chicken was raw.
name: Rawan

text: This place is amazing. Delicious teas with edible flowers, all vegan and gluten free macaroons and ice cream (and you can't tell they're vegan and gluten free!) so delicious, I would eat here every day if I lived in NOLA. The ice cream is hand rolled with toppings insane. Such a treat!! Definitely a must if you're looking for a delicious dessert.
name: Lauryn

text:
WOW!  What a great find!  A very nice Italian style BYOB in the heart of West Mt Airy.  Great hearty dishes, excellent service and a very cozy - almost cramped atmosphere.

The only reasons it is not 5 stars is that the antipasta was just OK.  We will be back.
name: Paul

text:
We stopped in on Sunday during brunch.  They offer bottomless mimosas and bottomless bloody Mary's.  Draw back is you have to go up to bar to serve yourself.  Area is very small and gets cramped when busy which makes it not so fun. 

Hubby and daughter had shrimp and grits.  They did not enjoy them at all.  

Daughter's fiance had the fried buffalo chicken sandwich with fries.  He enjoyed his meal. 

I had the buffet.  Food was tasty but not replenished often enough.
name: K

text: Discussing floors, food containers mostly empty, food old, service slow, too much $$$$....never again.
name: Mike

text: The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. They were out of one thing I originally wanted..
name: User

text: Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Food was good and came out fast. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Food was fresh and service was quick. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Not bad for a quick meal. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine..
name: User

text:
Al's BBQ is a pleasantly simple restaurant with a cozy and friendly atmosphere. The folks who work there are pleasant and Al himself is often there when I stop for lunch. It's a down-home family-feel kinda place -- nothing fancy in a good way.

The BBQ style is definitely Florida grown with a hint of the Carolina's. The pork is the star here with the pulled pork sandwich being my go to lunch. Their lunch special is a good deal. And the sweet tea is southern style with a lot of sweetness and I like it that way. Ask for half and half if you prefer moderately sweet. 

One area I haven't been too thrilled with are the sides. The baked beans were rather bland for my taste. And the mac and cheese (only available Friday) reminded me of a mediocre picnic mac n cheese with the cheesy sauce sort of dried up or congealed.
name: Mike

text: If there's a way to make a better burger and fries I can't imagine how it would be possible. Cool environment and the folks seemed genuinely happy. Friendly but not overbearing service.
name: Kevin

text: Seared salmon is literally my favorite thing ever!!! So freakin delicious.  It is truly wonderful; you must try it if you are a salmon lover!  The salads have ginger dressing, which has become a rarity these days in STL for some reason as most have switched to like a weird spicy mayo dressing.  This place is a gem and is my favorite sushi place in town for aforementioned dishes.
name: Bethany

text:
The food wasn't bad, but every other request we made was not followed.
-we requested an appetizer be brought with the entrees, since one of us was not as hungry. The appetizer was brought with the other appetizer
-we requested no scallions or chives (dietary restriction), the cauliflower came drenched in chives (the chives were also not mentioned on the menu)
-we requested a substitute with our dessert, this did not take place, but they did fix it when we pointed this out.

All in all the food was fine but not amazing. Would not be back.
name: June

text: Reading some of these complaints now feels a little overblown. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Maybe expectations are just off for some people. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would..
name: User

text: No big complaints, just a nice meal. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. You can tell they care about customer experience here. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. Would absolutely visit again. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Ordered a few things and liked most of it.
name: User

text:
Tried the bbq pork and Mac and cheese and the brisket burnt ends sandwich and my goodness!!! We walked in once we realized that eating at Cochon would not work out. We walked across the street and saw this large saloon type place but were intrigued by the menu. 

Hats off to the bartender/host/waiter/busboy. He was on point taking care of the large crowds that came in after us to watch Monday night football. Mixed crowd of locals and convention attendees. It was great and highly recommend it if you are hungry for some bbq and don't want to wait too long or spend a fortune.
name: Gissel

text:
It has been years since we've dined at the Iron Skillet. I was so pleased afterwards that I look forward to returning soon. It was decided we would celebrate my sister-in-laws birthday here with several of the family. So we made reservations for 6:00 p.m. on a Saturday night. Arriving promptly as a complete party we were seated right on time by a extremely, friendly hostess/server.

The table had been prepared prior to our arrival. White tablecloths, fresh flowers, candles, antique glassware in a cozy dining room. Water glasses were filled, bowls of cottage cheese and beets were already on the tables with biscuits and apple butter following quickly.

We had 2 servers for our table of 10 with assistance from the Manager and what appeared to be a runner. Our drink orders were taken immediately and arrived in less than 10 minutes including beers and wines. Our beverages were NEVER empty unless they were told specifically to pass.

All entrees are served with choice of creamy onion soup or chilled tomato juice and a individual side salad. Once the entrees were ordered the soup or juice arrived followed by the salads. 

All side dishes are served family style. We received multiple bowls of green beans, whole kernel corn, mashed potatoes and gravy with baskets of biscuits and rolls. By the time our entrees arrived, we had polished off the cottage cheese, pickled beets, pickles, our individual appetizer with most of the bread and apple butter. Of course, refills were offered and brought within minutes.

Our entrees were as diverse as the menu. Four of the10 folks selected fried chicken (both dark and light meat) and all RAVED how perfect it was prepared, lightly fried, golden brown with a wonderful crust. Even with everyone having all the Fried Chicken they could possibly eat, we took home 2 large to-go containers. The portions here are large and I can say no one will leave hungry.

The Grilled Salmon was the fish of the day. The presentation was attractive with a lightly grilled, flaky piece of salmon. It disappeared rather quickly and I was told it was delicious.

My husband ordered the 12 oz. Black Angus Steak prepared medium rare. I was totally surprised how much he enjoyed the steak. It was tough to pull off but he struggled to eat every bite. 

Our nephew couldn't decide so he selected the Combination Plate. Perfect for those who want a variety with choice of light or dark meat fried chicken, 3 large shrimp and a 4 oz. beef tenderloin. He thoroughly enjoy the variety of entrees. He couldn't finish all so he had a nice carryout for the following days lunch.  

My sister-in-law #4 ordered the Fried Shrimp dinner. The shrimp were large and lightly breaded, fried and served with tartar sauce and a side of Iron Skillets own hot sauce. She was very pleased with her selection.

I ordered the Baked Tilipa served with tartar sauce and  topped with a lemon butter and sliced almonds. The piece of Tilipa was the length of the plate. I had devoured the side dishes and salads so I ended up taking the majority of the Tilipa home.

After the left over entrees and side dishes were boxed and plates removed, a large basket with hot towels arrived. What a perfect touch after the fried chicken and biscuits with apple butter.

Now you would think after consuming this amount of food we'd pass on dessert. Nope! Everyone was looking forward to the ice cream sundaes. My husband and I had to pass. You have a selection of sherbert or 4 or 5 types of ice cream. When the ice cream was delivered it was accompanied by sundae toppings to build your own personal sundae. Of course, several had coffee to finish off a perfect experience.

If you've never been before I highly recommend. Perfect service, delicious food, large portions in a very cozy, comfortable atmosphere.
name: Wanda

text: What a great place for a romantic dinner. This was one of the best and favorite meals that we enjoyed in NOLA.
name: Chris

text: I thought that this was a very good atmosphere ... my style of interior, music, etc. I tried the lasagna which was mediocre at best, I tried the deviled eggs and fish tacos Anna Bananas Foster's cake all of which were delicious,... I'll give them the benefit of the doubt on the slip up with the lasagna I really like this place
name: Bert

text: Nice unassuming sandwich/salad/bakery/breakfast & lunch spot in Fenton Industrial Park. If not for Yelp I would not have known it existed! The small storefront disguises the large interior space with spacious dining rooms. Order at the counter and in a few short minutes your food arrives at your table hot and fresh. BLT and Fried chicken club were both good sandwiches with generous portions. Sides are pretty standard - a bag of chips, potato salad or very small side salads. Too full to try dessert but several choices looked delicious. Only open daytime hours M-F, but a nice affordable lunch stop.
name: Lolo

text: The food was good and the service was easygoing. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Worth checking out. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Would probably stop in again if nearby.
name: User

text: Worst service ever. Called twice here tried to order take out. The girl taking the cal could not understand me. Rather than getting someone else who understands. She just hung up instead. Price is a little more than usual places and service is terrible. Would recommend
name: Xiaolu

text: I love the cheesecake factory. It is one of my favorite restaurants because is has a great selection of food, drinks and desserts. This cheesecake was really nice because the staff was extra nice from the hostess to the waiter. The food was prepared to perfection and the restaurant was clean. I recommend it to anyone looking for a good meal on any occasion.
name: Deshaun

text: My favorite apple tart in Ardmore! Beautiful, delicious, and flaky! Ambiance is nice, clean, and good to work or chat
name: J

text:
By far our favorite place we've dined at since arriving to New Orleans! The food was amazing & the service was phenomenal! 10/10 experience and we might just come back for a second night in a row!
BEST BREAD PUDDING! Alllllll the food had so much flavor. The creole seafood gumbo has been the best gumbo we've had by far!
Busy on weekends so make reservations!
name: Jazz

text:
Today was only my second time visiting Ms. Winnie's since it's a little far from my Job, and I walked out of there thinking the same thing as last time. "Why don't I come here more often for lunch?" Once again, I left highly satisfied! As someone of Caribbean descent, and a South Florida native, the most difficult part about living in the Philly Burbs now is accessibility to Caribbean food and Culture. Now I know where to come when I'm feeling homesick! 

I ordered the Jerk Pork sandwich and a side of sweet plantains for lunch. The pork was well seasoned and cooked through. The slaw on top gave it a nice crunchy contrast and the Mango Chutney was as authentic as it gets. And of course, it was paired perfectly with the traditional Hard Dough bread. If anything cold have topped it off, it would have been an ice cold DG Kola Champagne or Cream Soda and a side of Festival. 

As with my first visit, I couldn't have left without 2 Chicken Patties to go. Mainly because my wife would kill me if I didn't bring her back a patty. As someone who doesn't eat beef, you don't understand how happy it makes us when Jamaican establishments carry Chicken patties. Too often do we run into that issue, so we highly appreciate it! What is uncommon is how fresh the patties are! It's always nice to receive patties that weren't sitting under a heat lamp for hours. 

Overall my experience was outstanding and I can't wait to go back! Big up to the Ms. Winnie's crew!
name: Andy

text:
To premise this review, the food was definitely 5 STAR but our service was -1 STAR so it averaged to a 2 STAR review. I made a reservation and we showed up five minutes early. The desk host was pleasant and told us our table was not ready so we should wait in the bar area. We waited in the bar and each got a glass of water as we were a little dehydrated from the heat of the mid summer day. A few minutes later we were approached by the hostess who took us to probably the worst table in the restaurant. We sat without complaining but to be honest, we were sat in a hallway with our table being the only one there in front of the entrance to the bathroom and a staircase leading to the second floor. Yes we people watched everyone fixing their zippers as the exited the bathroom.
Our server Daniel K arrived at our table and he seemed less than thrilled to be working. He started pushing the wine and when we declined he left and sent the water boy to remove the glasses. When he returned there was still a bad vibe and we considered walking out and going somewhere else being that at this point we had lost the enjoyment of this dining experience. Daniel then asked if our party of 5 was celebrating anything special and we happily told him it was our 32 wedding anniversary and we had brought our adult kids to dine with us and that we were here on vacation. Not sure why he asked because he could have cared less and didn't even ask if we wanted any celebration dessert at the end of our meal. 
In between the appetizers and the non existent dessert we did order food. We knew the portions were quite large and being from out of town, we didn't want leftovers so we ordered a salad, a 16 oz. steak with 3 added prawns, a chicken entree and a side vegetable for the table. I know that there were really only 2 entrees but we did end up with leftovers at the end. 
The food is served with a beautiful presentation. (MUST SEE MY PICS)
The Burrata w/Compressed Watermelon, Pistachio, Arugula was a great combination of sweet and salty and had plenty of texture from all of the ingredients. The NY strip we chose was wet aged, 16 oz cooked medium rare and we added 3 grilled gulf prawns that were served head on. The steak was a bit over seasoned with salt but it was tender and juicy. If Daniel would have been a descent server he would have had it kitchen sliced for table sharing as he was told that we would be sharing everything. Anyways, the Roasted Katharos Chicken in a Molé sauce with Avocado, Chayote Squash and radish for decoration was simply beautiful. A true kitchen creation with two whole large boneless chicken breasts resting on top of a creamy risotto. It was very rich and filling. The Street Corn, Cornbread, Chili, Cultured Cow's Milk side dish was probably the most interesting thing we ordered. It had the crunchy fried Peruvian corn on what seemed like a chili and cornbread stew with radishes, carrot tops and sprouts. That was a meal in itself for the portion size and richness. Once again, the food was outstanding and I have eaten at some pretty terrific places to compare it to. For me, to recommend and return to a restaurant, it has to be at least 4 stars and this was not it! Sorry, but there are other wonderful places in the Downtown Nashville area that gets higher marks.

text: One of the best "General Hotel Restaurants". Many great restaurants are located in hotels that are owned and operated by excellent restaurateurs and/or chefs.  But far fewer are the restaurants that are part of the hotel itself and usually just a place of convenience for guests to grab a bite that could be considered really good.  Well, this just happens to be one that is great.  From the first greeting to the wine selection, every detail of our dining experience was impressive.  After 4 of us shared an order of crispy Brussels sprouts, we ordered salt grilled wagyu culotte  (braised short ribs), gumbo, the fountain lounge burger and a fried goat cheese salad as our meal.  Then we split the flourless chocolate cake for dessert.  Everything was delicious and our server was incredibly knowledgeable and made great suggestions from the wine list.  We were one of only two tables being served, which prompted a well deserved conversation trying to figure out why this place isn't packed every night of the week.

text:
Great time on a Saturday at noon with carts. 

I hate waiting. I called about 11:45 a.m. on a Saturday to see if they were on a wait. We'd come before when it was packed and I didn't want to be stopped when I wanted to get my chow on. The woman on the phone said no wait so we hurried on in. When we got there, it was only moderately full. This is my favorite amount of people, not too many that I feel rushed, but not too few that make me question if this place is going to go out of business. 

When the first cart came around I panicked. I thought it would take forever to try the second so I got a ton of dishes, some I probably wouldn't have gotten. Don't be like me, know that the second card will be around shortly. Yes, there are only two carts so there is a limited dim sum menu, but you can order off the regular menu too, which is what we did. 

I always get something salt and pepper, usually the salt and pepper calamari. As always, it was delicious. I love the seasoning - it even has a kick to it. 

We always get egg tarts to end the meal. They are delicate and flakey. 

There were tons of parking spots open when we went. We will keep going on Saturday since there are less people there! Staff told me that there are more dishes on the Sunday carts, but I rather have less dishes and no wait.
name: Christina

text:

Ordered Alambre mixto with barbacoa and carnitas; meat was so flavorful I was talking about it hours later- hints of cinnamon, fresh cilantro, bacon, bell peppers/onions w/ a pleasant char, & spicy tomatillo salsa. I love complexity & this dish delivered a truly rich & satisfying flavor profile.

Tried shrimp tacos, tamale- also very good just cleaner, simpler flavors. Condiments, chips, rice/beans all high-quality. BYOB. FREE margaritas won't knock your socks off, but add your favorite alcohol and u got a win!

Good portions, reasonable prices, fair charges for extras. The atmosphere is simple, but the tasty, authentic food & friendly staff make up for any shortcomings. Can't wait to return.

text: Magerks has a great menu with all your bar faves! Outdoor heated seating and lots of TVs keep the mood fun and entertaining. Large selection of taps and attentive wait staff.
name: Aloise

text: In short, the food was excellent. We ordered Salt and Pepper squid, Papaya Salad with Shrimps and House Special Vermicelli. The fried squid was crispy outside and tender inside, lightly seasoned so we can enjoy the taste of squid, natural umami. Papaya salad was fresh. Adding a little bit of fish sauce which comes with the salad brought it to the next level. I read a couple of reviews on lack of taste. Just like Japanese food, they focus on the natural flavor of the ingredient. Next time, we will try Country style Beef Cubes. I heard that it is very nice. This restaurant is a definitely nice addition to Mainline.

text:
What a treat to be able to try this new Italian restaurant at the mall. 
For starters, you're not going to believe you are even at the mall as the atmosphere is fresh, lively and it feels like an outdoor sidewalk cafe! 
Then, their happy hour is nearly never ending because they do a happy hour after work and another happy hour starting at 8pm. This is a true happy hour with 1/2 off appetizers, and drink specials.
Speaking of appetizers, let me give you some recommendations: 
- calamari - theirs is fresh, and taste like it! You can tell it is not frozen as it melts in your mouth
- spinach and artichoke dip is divine and comes with fried Naan points (whoever thought to take the amazing Naan bread and turn it into fried toast points is a genius!)
And if you want stellar service, you need to see Kayla as she is friendly, full of energy, and ready to impress you with her hospitality.
I truly think this is a restaurant that will be here for the long term and it is worthy of your visit.
name: Tina

text: Believe the hype. Worth every part of 5 stars. Tostachos to start are fantastic. The sofrito pork, bbq pork sliders, and twister dinners were outstanding. The staff was super friendly throughout. Looking forward to our next time here.

text:
Typically I stay away from restaurants where I can't pronounce the menu items, but we got a gift card for our wedding, and decided to check it out. We made a reservation the night before, and were promptly seated when we arrived. 
It's a smaller restaurant with a very romantic vibe, and the seats by the window have a nice view of the river. 

We started out our meal with bacon wrapped dates, which were out of this world! 
For dinner my husband got the hanger steak and I got the filet mignon. The filet mignon was amazing. It practically melted in your mouth. 

The only reason I didn't give 5 stars is the service was really slow. When we arrived only about half the restaurant was full, and there were so many servers I swear every table had their own. 
However, when we did see a waiter or waitress they were really nice.
name: Steffini

text: By far the best breakfast value in the french quarter. Service was top shelf and the breakfast food was delicious. We had no line for breakfast.

text:
A fantastic Pho place in the western suburbs.  

If you live in West Chester, Downingtown, Exton or Coatesville you owe it to yourself to check this place out.  The restaurant is brightly lit and casual as one would expect for a Pho place.  The Pho has been consistently delicious and I've stopped going to the pho place in West Chester downtown once I found this place.

The portions are always just right, and they put various fresh fruits in their water pitchers to infuse it with a little bit of extra freshness and sweetness that I've never seen before at a casual ethnic cuisine.  This is definitely something that puts Pho Now above their peers.  The beef broth has been flavorful without being overly salty or greasy and all their fresh wrapped summers rolls are not dried out on the outside.  

If you are craving a nice bowl of hot Pho in the area, you can't beat Pho Now.
name: Bo

text:
Let me start off by saying that I have been to MANY Cracker Barrel locations and not once have I had a bad experience like I did in this particular one. I went on a Sunday, which I understand can be one of the busiest days of the week. I've worked as a waitress/host before so I absolutely am not one to complain easily about them. 
Unfortunately this experience was just so terrible and unpleasant that I am left with no other option. 
My fiancé and I were seated quickly and politely by the hostess. We waited about 10 mins for our waiter to come take our drinks & he quickly got us our drinks. He then began taking our order and we waited about 20 minutes to get our food, which I thought was okay considering it's a Sunday. He brought our food and then proceeded to ask us if we needed anything else. We replied, "yes, we need some Mayo & Tabasco sauce as well as a refill on our drinks" (mind you I waited 20 mins for food, so we finished our drinks while waiting) he said he'd bring them right out and we waited. Believe me, the food looked AMAZING , but it would've been better if we could have enjoyed it while it was still warm. We patiently waited for our waiter to come back with what we requested. 20 MORE MINUTES. He comes to our table (without our condiments nor drinks) & proceeds to ask the DUMBEST question. "Do you need to-go-boxes?"
I was most absolutely outraged. We waiting patiently, thinking he must be busy. We sat and watched as he brought other clients their food and drinks. 
I will most definitely not come back to this location nor do I recommend this to anyone in the area. I'd rather drive to a whole different city in TN, if it means getting GOOD SERVICE. Unbelievable.
name: Nanis

text:
I came here with 3 other people and our expectations were pretty high after reading all the amazing reviews on Yelp. Farm Burger is located off Charlotte Avenue in West Nashville and there is a parking lot around back. The space is modern and trendy. 

I got the #1 Farm Burger which is a grassfed beef burger with aged vermont white cheddar, caramelized onions & farm burger sauce. I added bacon ($2 extra). We also got the half housemade panko crusted onion rings and half hand-cut fries with smoked paprika mayo. Their paprika mayo is amazing! The onion rings were interesting and had kind of a mustardy flavor but they were good. I think what made the burger enjoyable was all the flavors on top of the burger, not the burger itself. 

Pros: 
-Burgers have great toppings and their sauces are great. I like that the burgers are grassfed as well and the ingredients are fresh
-They have a play area for kids
-Restrooms were clean

Cons: 
-We ordered our burgers after our friends but got them before they did. Their order wasn't anything complicated but it was strange that they had to wait 5-10 minutes longer for their order
-The windows were open and there were no fans or air conditioning so we were all incredibly hot and uncomfortable 

Overall, I like their concept but we were so uncomfortable because of the heat in here it was just so hard to enjoy this experience, thus the 3 star rating. If they fix this I'm willing to come back and bump them up a star!

text:
It was Christmas afternoon, this is the only restaurant that's open in the whole town, we pretty much had no choice, my mom and I had some food in the car on the way there, so we ordered one plate to share, we asked for hot water, the cashier answered me with two fingers "2 hot water?", but ended brought us only one cup without any explanation. While eating, my mom wanted something hot to warm up the body, so I ordered another Tofu Ramen, I then asked for another cup of hot water, but being rejected for the reason of not having enough cup, and I needed to bring the cup to the cashier if I wanted more hot water (I wondered what I am paying the 15% tip for?) when I brought the cup to the cashier, I saw another exactly same cup sitting right next to the water kettle, I asked the cashier why not give us that cup, he answered "that's not what you think." So I wondered what's exactly what I saw???
When he brought the hot water (with the cup I brought over) back to the table, I decided to ask him if it's because we only ordered one plate? He said no, and he further claimed he didn't not charge me for the hot water which is actually not free. 
And came the tofu ramen made with instant noodles you can get from the super market....
All the above ruined our Christmas Day.

text:
Crispy Bird was quite disappointing to this homesick Southerner. We went in the first week of opening so I'll give them some credit that they might work out the kinks. However, I'm not optimistic about the menu. Service and atmosphere were excellent so that's why I'm giving it a second star, but the food itself was quite subpar especially for this price point.

I'm not just a Southerner, I'm from the Deep South. Fried chicken pulses through my veins. James Beard awardee Ashley Christensen's Beasley's Chicken+Honey in Raleigh, NC sets my standard for "fancy fried chicken." So I admittedly set a high bar to clear. $5 Popeyes, late night Church's, and gas station chicken are at a price point where I won't blame it if it's a bit too greasy or not on point. However, our meal for two was quite expensive and it let us down. 

We walked in and the place was packed...to be expected with a new opening. The interior was Nordic chic, with lots of wood and simple lines. The wait staff was helpful and friendly as they took down our names. We waited for about 20 minutes and were seated at a very tiny table right next to the full-length window. I juggled my coat through the meal as my left side froze next to the window.

The waiter was very friendly and gave us an excellent overview of the restaurant concept and menu. We ordered the chicken skins (they were sold out already), maple brown butter biscuits (tasty, recommended, but dense, not fluffy southern style), and two orders of fried chicken. We got one light meat and one leg+thigh. We also ordered the mac and cheese.

The meat was both over-cooked and under-seasoned. We crunched, and crunched, and sat in silence, trying to figure out how the chef spent "months" perfecting the recipe. It was served with a strangely tart coleslaw (really just limp shredded cabbage with some Granny Smith apple) and pickles. The mac and cheese was just straight up burnt. It came out on the plate half blackened, and not in a good way. I'm honestly surprised the waiter served it to us because it was visibly black on top. We ate it, hoping it was just some flavor-boosting browning, but it wasn't. It was just burnt. 

I didn't expect this to be my grandmother's fried chicken. I'm willing to give new flavor combinations and new side ideas a try, and I'm willing to pay a premium for things like quality bird and seasonings. However, this just totally fell short on basic execution. Food was burned and overcooked. We won't be going back unless the menu is overhauled. At this price, I'll take my date to Livery instead.
name: Susan

text:
Everytime I drive up to Santa Barbara, my first stop is to Brophy Bros. Seafood is my favorite food and theirs is always fresh. I usually get the fried shrimp or fried clams, clam chowder and sop it all up with the fresh bread they offer. The prices are reasonable, in the $15 dollar range.

There's usually a wait however it's located right on the marina, so there's a wonderful view in the meantime. I have never waited longer than 20 minutes. There's indoor and outdoor seating plus self seating at the bar. The noise level is high however you tune it out after a while. My waiter/waitress have always been friendly and attentive. 

My issue is with my last experience. I came in this past labor day Monday and was seated facing the kitchen. While I was eating, I noticed one of the cooks (wearing a black hat with a red oval and white center) pointing at me and saying something to another cook (wearing a black hat that said "Devour"). The cook with the Devour hat turned around and stared at me and they continued to talk. I was there approximately 30 minutes and they continued to stare at me to the point I was uncomfortable, irritated and was unable to finish my food. The cook with the oval logo on his hat kept walking behind the wall and coming out starting at me with a mean look. The cook with the Devour hat would paused, eat something and stare. I ended up paying and leaving and going elsewhere to eat. 

Although I love the food here, I more than likely won't return. I'll find another seafood restaurant where I'm comfortable eating.

text: Yes, almost everything we ordered was good. I was disappointed in the Lobster Ravioli, as I wasn't expecting the sauce with it (very disappointed and not what you'd expect).
