text:
I used to think the food was good but the staff has some severe issues.  If you're looking for a fake friendly smile and a staff that curses under their breath when you or your family place an order that may mildly inconvenience them this is your place. The WORST service aside I've been able to look past the "I'd rather be anywhere than here" attitude of the staff until recently.  At 10:30 on a thursday, a woman emerged from the closed store to start trouble with me and 3 city officials.  She claimed despite the fact I lived nearby I was not allowed to stand where I was and I needed to "move along".  When asked she said it was the law.  When my colleague who works in the law enforcement agency said it wasn't she claimed to be "above the law in Doylestown." 

All four of us stood there dumbfounded -- we let her know we had been patrons there for months, spending upwards of 100 a week.  She claimed she did not care, she was the owner, and it was her right WHEN CLOSED to demand others to move along as she saw fit.  

A police officer, a court advisor, a prominent carpenter, and a google employee stood there dumbfounded.  This woman (Helen, who claims to know my mother but lets just say that's impossible) could not answer why she was leaving the building hours after it closed nor why she was aggressively attacking us.  Despite treating her with respect she had nothing but anger and hate from a level I could not believe.  All of this recorded on video due to the fact the woman had repeatedly threatened us (the police and lawyers of the township) with the police.

Don't bring your kids, loved ones, or anyone else nearby.  This woman obviously has unresolved issues and is not afraid to take them out on paying customers even after the building closes.  

Try not to have your poker games at residences anywhere nearby or she may take offense to it.  

I've listed my number in a message to this business in an effort for all five of us whom were wronged to have a word with the REAL owner.  

TLDR; The food is great but the staff I've encountered ignorant, uneducated, aggressive, and will NOT direct you to the owner when you have an issue with them.  Save yourself the headache and get your average BBQ elsewhere.
name: Matthew

text: So I walk in there's and there's three people at the bar. I set down and the bartenders on the other side of the bar I sat there for a few minutes and two guys came in and she came over and served them beers got them menus. The bartender then proceeds to check on a table and get their checks and bring them up and ring them up right in front of me at the cash register. I thought maybe she say something then. Nope takes the change back over to the table comes back stops at the two guys on the other side of me asking if they want another beer (one stool between me and them). Turned around and walked across in front of me and proceeded to go back and check her phone.  I should have known when there's only a dozen or so cars in the parking lot at 6 o'clock in Indy that this place was definitely hit and miss. Needless to say I'm heading out to the next restaurant and won't be back.
name: Tim

text: The flavor and uniqueness of the dishes were great. Wonderful actually. The service was so awful that I will never go back. No Chardonnay by the glass. The bottle was $87. We ordered our appetizers, and then we were pressured to order our entrees at the same time, and that's just not how we do things in my family. It was 7:30 on a Wednesday. The server made a snide comment that it was only 7:3o and that we had all the time in the world to make up our minds for our entree. We had. We just didn't want food piling up on our table before we were ready to eat it. The first entrees we ordered were not available. We were informed of this about 19 minutes after we placed our order. We all had second choices, so it wasn't a problem, and we all ordered our second choice options. When the entrees came out, only 2 arrived. I had to get up from the table to tell someone we were missing an entree... a few minutes later someone came to our table to say that they only had one order left of the item my dad and I both ordered. Why didn't someone inform us of this before our entrees arrived? So... my dad and I shared our entree and ordered some more Brussels sprouts so he wouldn't leave hungry. Our server informed us that they comped the food that never arrived as well as a glass of wine and the additional order of Brussels sprouts. THEY COMPED THE FOOD THAT DIDNT ARRIVE??? This is bullshit. The food tastes great if they have it in stock... apparently nobody knows what they have or do not have until your other entrees are delivered and one is missing. Unprofessional. Lame. Too stuck up to compensate for their inadequate business model. It's places like this that perpetuate the stereo type of my generation feeling entitled while absolutely failing at the business they are trying to run. My dad is now home eating crackers and cheese because his dinner never showed up. Thanks for the glass of wine and the veggies, jerks. The things we were able to eat were delicious, otherwise this would be a one star review. I will never recommend this place or spend my money here ever again. What a frogging waste. Even with the incredible flavor, this place isn't worth 2 stars.
name: Wendy

text: The food is so good for the price. I came on steak night. The steak was only $6.99 and perfect size. The press drink was really good and 2 is all you need for the night. The goat cheese balls were surprisingly delicious. I bought the chocolate mousse cake with ice cream, but couldn't wait to take the picture. The ice cream is home made and so good. This place is definitely perfect for a first date.
name: Shar

text: With not many people there, it took 20 minutes to get 4 crispy ground beef taco's and the grease made up about 10% of the meal. Maybe strain the meat a little, sure some fat gives it flavor but when it runs out each time you pick up the taco, that's too much. It was better in the past, not sure what changed.
name: Butch

text:
Wonderful, welcoming, warm service -awesome menu spread and remarkably delicious vegan food! Great coffee 

Clean, white, bright open space.
name: Kara

text:
Good food and service.  Came here last night for restaurant week.  Recommend the ensalada verde (tapas), salmon (main course), and churros con chocolate (dessert). 
Ensalada verde was a great combination of brussel sprouts, kale and dressing.  This was a lot better tasting than the other salad we got, the Ensalada de kale, which didn't taste good with the beets and goat cheese.  
The salmon was great tasting, three medium pieces of salmon on a bed of spinach and chickpeas slathered in lemon cream sauce.  The sauce is what made this dish great.  The other main dish we got was the seared ahi tuna, this was ok, kind of forgettable, not recommend. 
We got 3 desserts, the churros was the best, 2nd best was the flan. The worst dessert was the cremoso de chocolate because of the olive oil, I thought the oil took away from the chocolate taste. 
Service was friendly and fast.
Kinda pricey, this is why I'm giving 4 stars and not five.  The salmon alone cost $21, although listed under "larger plates" it's appetizer size in my opinion.  We had no problem parking on a Thur night around 7pm, also no wait when we came it, but it got busy soon after.
name: Tony

text: It sucks worst biscuits I ever had and extremely pricey for the poor quality of food I will never go back.
name: Mauro

text: Cane here for breakfast before school. Dined in. They had us in and out very quickly which I'm very appreciative for. The restaurant is so clean and quiet too. You don't have workers socializing. Instead they are focused and serving the customers. Great job. Enjoy coming here.
name: Brigitte

text: Really surprised at the low rated reviews. Service in the dinning area can be slow...agreed. But the food has ALWAYS been good. I prefer to eat at the bar...always great service. Best margaritas...period.
name: Glen

text: Y'all, this place is legit. And this is coming from an Austinite-where tacos are life. Our waitress Shelby was upbeat and gave great recommendations for a quick bite prior to heading back to the Lone Star State. We had the a la carte crunchy shell taco with ground beef and the shredded chipotle chicken in addition to the shrimp tacos. We were shocked at how AMAZING the tacos were. I mean, you never hear about the taco scene in NOLA but seriously this is a must try. The cheese dip was on point and the house margaritas were smooth and refreshing. Thank you Shelby for the water to-go for our trip back and thank you for the friendly greeting, the great recommendations, and a perfect goodbye to New Orleans!!
name: Mckenzie

text: I love this place. Either location. That is all. BEST Bloody Mary in town. I've had everything here from simple eggs/bacon, to some of the more creative selections, and all have been perfect. Just be forewarned - the wait can stink!
name: Angela

text:
Although I ordered a Vito on a wheat roll, it was served on the sliced wheat bread. Nonetheless, the sandwich was good. 

The real gripe is that there were roughly five employees standing around doing nothing, no line, no one waiting in front of us and it still took five minutes for them to make the sandwich. 

Freaky fast? I'm afraid not.
name: Patrick

text: New favorite restaurant in Philadelphia. I believe their menu is updated frequently, so there's constantly great new items. We ordered 6 plates to share between two people and the total was around $70 each. Get the jack- so good, a great start to the meal. We ordered the blackened cauliflower TWICE. Once for an appetizer, and once for dessert. Make a reservation at least two months in advance if you want to eat at a normal time and not 930pm.

text: Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Definitely coming back. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. No big complaints, just a nice meal. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced.

The food is amazing along with getting an eegee! The prices are reasonable but understand that it may not be the best fast food place to go. The new update has made the place a lot more welcoming and bright! 

The people are very slow and sometime are hard to work with. The managers are always uptight when you try to talk to them about something that you feel is wrong. Drive though is very fast though. It gets very busy on weekends since it's a very popular place.

text: The whole meal felt kind of uneven. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. Wouldn't really choose this place again. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. No big complaints, just a nice meal.

text: Savory food ( I've only eaten here a couple of times,  I really enjoy it.) their 'country benedict' is really tasty!  I sit out side. under an umbrella, in a modest front patio, with wood, brick and colorful planters -- and just enjoy the food and the quaint, relaxed atmosphere here.

text: This place is okay. The chicken tikka masala is good! I would highly recommend that! Their Naan is also solid. Sadly their potato vindaloo is bad! You can tell they boiled potatoes and put them into a sauce. That is not how dishes like this are made.

text:
This was a second choice for us since the first restaurant had horrible service and the menu seemed lacking (we didn't know about this place yet). That being said, it should have been the first choice the whole time!
Service was prompt, attentive, and helpful from walking in the door. Thank you Ryan for continuing that in your great table side help as well. 
The food was fantastic. The Bloody Mary mix was hands down some of the best I've ever had. 
I even remarked on neighboring tables food choices about how good everything looked and smelled. 
Go here. Don't let yourself down.
name: Kristina

text: Visited here on a Friday evening and our group of 3 got seated quickly. Our waiter was friendly and I ordered Rockefeller oysters, as well as the fish poboy. The oysters were large and some of the best I've had. The poboy was also pretty good as well. My only issue is that they don't give separate checks so we had to pay our one check with 3 separate credit cards and the waiter mixed up two of the cards so the two other parties in my group got charged for one another's order. Most restaurants in America are able to give separate checks and this would have prevented the hassle of a mix up this night.

text: First time ordering from here and I honestly wasn't sure what to expect. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. For a busy night they handled it okay. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait.

text: Good food. Good atmosphere. Great service.  Reasonable prices.  Menu looks like there are many great things to choose. Will try something new the next time as well.  First time customer.  Will definitely be back.

text:
Mr. Jerry was waiting on us. Initially we thought this location had oyster bar. He was excellent waiting on us, excellent conversation and great laughs.  The food was amazing! Crawfish dip, NOLA bbq shrimp, crawfish, and oyster platter! Yummo!! Everything was Great! Thank you!! 
The atmosphere was awesome! All the staff was fun and engaging. Coming from Atlanta and craving seafood, this spot helped with my craving!! I will be back again!! Thank you for a great experience. My Big Momma  and Aunt TT enjoyed it as well!! Thank you!!

I had the Pork Chops. Two because usually they are fairly small and I will eat two. Not today. These were thick cut and one was all I could eat. Looking forward to eating the other one at home.

text: What the heck happened to Harrah's? This use to be one of the best hotel & casino in Reno. We got married and decided to do a a quick "honeymoon" weekend in Reno. We usually stay at the Peppermill but we had just gotten a puppy and needed to bring him with us because he was too young to board. I saw that Harrahs had petstay rooms so we booked our weekend there. The whole floor smelled like a kennel. It was horrible. We went to Walmart to buy fabreeze and a scented candle for our room it was so bad. The pet relief area is a little square sand box with booze bottles, trash, and cigarette buds surrounding it. I was afraid to even have my puppy go near it. Our puppy is only 3 lbs and a small breed so he could wiggle under some of the furniture in the room. When he lost his ball under the tv cabinet we were horrified by what we saw under there, piles of garbage. Not just dust bunnies or a random Scooby snack but straight up trash. We didn't see it until we were about to check out or we would have ran out of there and stayed somewhere else. I showed the pictures to the front desk when we checked out. The agent said it was his first week there and that they had contracted out the room cleaning. I realize not everyone is a responsible pet owner so you wouldn't want carpet or nice furnishings but it should be at least clean and not have piles of trash in it. I grew up in Reno and I'm sure old man Harrah is rolling in his grave for what has happened to his legacy. It's such a shame. On a brighter note, the Steakhouse is still wonderful with great food and great service. I give the steakhouse 4 stars and the hotel casino a fat ZERO but the lowest yelp will allow is a 1.

text:
Menu Recommendation:
Bun Bo Hue

Food:
Within my first sip of the broth, I already knew the Bun Bo Hue was going to be amazing. I could tell there was definitely a lot of time put into the broth by the depth of its flavor. The noodles had the right bounce to them and the meat was nice and tender. They definitely do not slack on the meat, so prepare for heaps of juicy bites of beef. The only problem I had with this bowl was that the pig knuckle wasn't as soft as I'd like it to be and the plate of vegetables was lacking banana flower, an essential ingredient to Bun Bo Hue.

Location + Service:
The storefront doesn't look like much from the outside--in fact, it comes off as a hole in the wall type place. But once you enter the little bistro and hear the Vina house bumping in the background, you're immediately transported back into the little side restaurants in Vietnam. With a little shrine in the background to greet you at the front door, this restaurant will give you the true experience of a traditional family-run Vietnamese restaurant. Service is what I typically expect from a Vietnamese run establishment

Tips:
Ask for spice on the side so that you can adjust the heat. Additionally, if you're feeling adventurous, you can dip your meats in fish sauce (I believe this is a south Vietnamese style of eating where we like to dip everything into sauces).
name: Daniel

text:
This 3 star review is based on the ATTITUDE towards EXCHANGING chicken for beans that I encountered today. The food itself is delicious and if we had ordered our usual order of pinto beans and coleslaw, which we pile high with all the fresh goodies, I'd have to rate this place 5 stars. 

I joined the rewards club and received a free entree so we had to buy one to get the free one. They don't offer a vegetarian version so we ordered a chicken tostada asking to EXCHANGE THE CHICKEN FOR BEANS which I requested be put on TOP of the salad...the order taker said he'd let them know. 

There were no beans (and no chicken) on top so I asked for them. The counter woman tried to convince me they were on the bottom. I had asked for black beans on top because it comes with pinto on the bottom. I wanted both to be sure I got BOTH PORTIONS. Rather than just giving me some beans, she asked the woman in back if she put both on the bottom and was told no. So she dishes up about 3 tablespoons of beans...less than a quarter cup, and handed it to me. 

I asked for more because it's REPLACING THE CHICKEN. She INSISTED that she gave me the amount that is considered a "serving" on the BOTTOM of the tostada. I'm sure if I'd asked for a manager I could have gotten a more fair portion of beans but you know...most people won't ask for the manager. So I decided to just walk away and share this experience. 

It probably isn't the counter woman's fault. This "stingy thing" problem probably comes from Managment or the owner. So it's up to the owner to explain to these employees that when someone wants to EXCHANGE beans for chicken they should receive a fair amount of beans. And that if they want the beans on TOP...where the chicken goes...it's ok to put the beans on top. 

I hope this review encourages vegetarians to stand up for themselves at this location when they want to eat beans rather than chicken!  And I hope the manager will fix this!  I love their chicken here but my husband prefers beans!  

Great food...a little attitude adjustment and this could be 5 stars!  

If you find this review useful, please VOTE!
name: Danada

text:
We were so excited to eat here for Mothers' Day as the reviews were good, but unfortunately our experience was not the greatest.  There were four in our party and me and my mother were seated first.  While we were waiting we ordered drinks and appetizers.  The remaining two people of our party came about 15m later, then ordered drinks and appetizers.  15m later our guests' appetizers arrived, then we had to remind the servers that we were still waiting for ours.  They were delivered to our table shortly thereafter.
We all ordered our entrees, but the wait was extremely long to receive our food.  The manager and waiter kept coming back to apologize regarding the delay and we were told multiple times that our food was being plated. While we were waiting, other guests were getting food though they arrived after us.    When our food finally did arrive is was lukewarm and we surmised that it was not getting plated, but sitting somewhere getting cold.  
Since the wait was so long and the fact that the bill exceeded ~$250.00 (for two), that they would have served our food and provide service with higher standards.  My mother and I took our food home and heated it to the proper temperature the next day which was so much better than what was served at the restaurant.
The amount of the check did not justify the quality of food nor the service we received.  I will go back to the Hard Rock but will never EVER eat at this establishment again.  BIG DISAPPOINTMENT.
Oh I and forgot to add, that we received a free glass of wine for our troubles - thumbs down.  I'm giving one star for the wine and for the yummy appetizers.

I asked about 20 minutes in if there was any way that we could be moved inside as it was clearing slightly and a delightful young woman said absolutely and assisted us. We were able to slightly enjoy our time but between the lukewarm pork and the hot smoked salmon that had a slight funk it is absolutely not worth the $27/person for normal brunch let alone the $48/person for Mother's Day brunch. Don't be lured in like I was by the rating go somewhere else nearby there are many fantastic choices!
The only way this place will work is if you're starving or drunk!

Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Not bad for a quick meal. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..

text: My first tip is to wear no slip shoes.  Floor was super slippery.  We watched as our table was cleaned off for us and the busboy wiped the crumbs from the table to our chairs.  Silverware, menus and just about everything was dirty.   Trying not to make a scene We continued to order our food.  APP ARE OUT!  Everything came out nice and hot .   Just blah in my opinion.  I ordered the NY Strip with a side of 2 scallops ($9).   Steak comes out with no seasoning.   The scallops are already cooking and the steak hasn't started.  The waitress begins to cook everything, I thought that I was supposed to do that?   So I say I will do it.  The scallops are over done ( Ramsey would be pissed ) and the steak still hasn't had any salt and pepper yet.  The side of asparagus was in a plate, Im not sure if they were supposed to be done when they came out but they needed to be on the rock too.  Everything was bland and although I have yet to see the check, I already know, I got robbed!   This place is awful and I will certainly never be back.  Too many fails to list.  Save your $$$$.  I don't want to spoil the night like dinner with the Goldbergs ( if yo ever saw that episode), but I don't want to pay for this crap!

text: This was a delivery order on a night when I really did not want to cook. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. There were a couple things I liked and a couple things I probably wouldn't get again.

This place has excellent food and service.  I had 
looked long and hard for a place to get caldo de res in Indy and finally found it here as a special on Wednesday's.  It is a rich beef and vegetable soup that I learned to love while living in Arizona.  Everything I have tried has been good.

text:
Went after they had been open for a couple days. Arrived at 11:30AM and the drive through had cars lined up around the building, at least a dozen cars. We went inside and we're about 8th place waiting to order from 2 registers open. (PDQ only has 2 registers) It took about 8-10 minutes to get to the register to place our order for 2. They took one of our names and said they would call us when our order was ready for us to come pick up. We waited about 5-7 minutes before they called our name, so basically about 15 minutes from arrival to receiving our food. 
Pros. Chicken sandwich and tenders were very good, but I wouldn't say excellent. Tots were average, like you get anywhere. Sauces were the only thing better than average, sauces and selection were great. 
Cons, Even with the VERY busy crowd inside and outside, the fries were surprisingly bad, medium warm, limp and oily, like you would expect from a slow business that had fries sitting around waiting for customers. 
The worst part was the cashier taking our money and distributing change and handing us our drink cups while holding them from the lip of the cups. GROSS! Even if it wasn't Extreme Flu Season like it is right now which makes it worse, that is  Unacceptably Unsanitary. While waiting for our food I spoke with Alex the Manager in hopes that they would address this issue. I never mentioned the fries because they were undoubtedly cooking high volumes and I assume this is just the way they serve them, maybe appealing to others. Not us. Would we return,  we're not sure. Would we recommend to others, probably not. Chik-Fil-A has more than 2 registers open at peak times and we've never waited that long to order or receive food with even more customers ahead of us. Chik-Fil-A delivers our orders to our table and they give you a filled drink as soon as you place your order, unlike PDQ giving you empty cups so we could go wait in yet another line to fill our own drinks from 1 single dispenser for every customer in the restaurant. Last but not least the Chik-Fil-A  comparison between the two is No comparison at all, PDQ food quality and customer experience is considerably less.
name: Rob

text: Awesome service! Shout out to Joseph! The chicken was juicy and tasted good. I prefer the floured chicken over the breadcrumb crust like they do here but it was still good. The fries are yummy. The Mac was OK. Don't expect anything too crazy good in that respect. And it was very reasonably priced, so I left happy and very full!

Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Would probably stop in again if nearby.

text:
Lure is my absolute favorite restaurant in Santa Barbara. I've never had a bad meal, and the staff is always on point. Oscar is my favorite bartender, and he always has a smile and friendly greeting whenever I come in. Whenever anyone asks who has the best Happy Hour in town, I don't hesitate to send them over. 

I do have one minor annoyane, which has nothing to do with the service, but more so with the pet policy. A friend and I stopped in for lunch 2 weeks ago. I usually sit at the bar, but since my friend was pregnant, we wanted to enjoy the fresh air outside, so we chose the patio. There was a group seated 2 tables over from ours. One lady in the bunch had a dog in her lap, and it growled at everyone walking past. The people seated next to them moved over towards our table. The dog did not appear to be a service animal.

I personally do not care for animals in bars and restaurants. I understand people in SB are attached to their dogs, but other customers shouldn't be made to feel uncomfortable, or have their dining experience interrupted by someone else's pet. I really wish the management would take this into consideration. 

I'll continue to support the restaurant, but perhaps stick to the indoor seating. Otherwise, great job, Lure!!!
name: Phoenix

text: One of our favorite restaurants and bars in Brandon and Tampa. The owners are incredibly friendly, the staff is great and the food is the best part. Always a new item in the menu and the fries are out of this world!

text: Good food, great service. Our waitress, Jess M, was awesome!!!! Authentic NOLA food. Try the Bloody Mary!

text:
Generally, I default to poke if there's a poke option with a 6 mile radius. But for once, on a late lunch break, I boldly broke my poke pattern and went with the Thai option at Auction House.

You guys. The unicorn noodles are light, delicious, and perfect for this time of year. I had them with tofu and mushroom--highly recommend.

I'm already planning my next trip to Long Chim and calculating exactly how soon is too soon to go back and order the exact same thing.

text:
There aren't many options for German food in Tampa so by default Schiller's German Delicatessen gets four stars. The food is delicious, the German owners are super friendly, and everything in the deli is very fairly priced considering the items are imported from Europe. The building is dated and is in desperate need of renovations, but I can overlook this since the deli is family owned. I would suggest calling your sandwich order ahead because the service is a little slow.

I always order the bratwurst lunch platter or the bratwurst reuben sandwich and the German potato salad. The grilled bratwurst and tangy sauerkraut are excellent and my toddler can inhale more brats than it seems humanly possible. I want the recipe for the warm German potato salad with crumbled bacon!!!

Side note: if ordering to-go, check your order before leaving. On three separate occasions they have forgotten to add my potato salad to the bag.
name: Michelle

text: Love this place! The pork and beef dishes were fantastic! Can't wait to go back.  They are always kind, and quick to get my order made.
name: Shaun

text:
I am always up for trying out new places to eat. Watervue opened recently and of course we had to come since the menu looked quite intriguing. Our reservations were set for 6:30 on a Saturday night. When we got there, they were pretty backed up on reservation time. 
Our table wasn't quite ready, but it was fine with us since we had noticed there were two spots open at the bar. 
We both ordered drinks, a beer and one of their specialty cocktails. As far as the food, we started off with the Smoked Fish Dip, Flash Fried Calamari, and Cracker Crusted Oyster Sliders. I was not impressed with the dip. To me, it lacked flavor. The Calamari was pretty good, and since I'm not a fan of oysters, I can't really be fair and comment on it. Although, the carrot slaw that came with it on the side was really good! 
For our main course, we had their Market Fish which at that time was Alaskan Halibut...nice creamy sauce with truffles and potatoes. Yum! 
If you are wanting to try this place out, go for it. It's worth a shot.
name: Nicole

text: People are being a little dramatic in these comments honestly. Food was fresh and service was quick. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. The service is fantastic, the pizza is delicious, and the beer selection is always a great variety. This is an excellent meeting place between Dickson & Nashville. We bring new friends here with us every time we go. I have had the best service from Silas - ask for his section. All my single girlfriends go wild over him too - it's adorable. text:
We went here because there are only 2 ice cream places on state street. Upon entering we were told they had no gelato today even though  the place is called Scooped ice cream and gelato. They had very small variety of ice cream and sign said sorbet, so I asked what flavors they had and told me they were also out of sorbet. I settled on mint chocolate oreo which was overpowered by the mint completely, not a good combo of flavors.  My husband got butter pecan which had basically no pecans and tasted like plain vanilla. Also, 2 scoops cost the price of a gallon of ice cream at a grocery store.

My reply to business owner's reply: Your employee told us there was no sorbet, nor did we see it. I have excellent review to competitor because they had 8 flavors of gelato and you had none. I recommend using your time more wisely by using negative feedback to improve your product.

The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. The music was louder than it needed to be. Pretty happy with it overall.

text:
This is one of my favorite pizza places in Nashville. 

These are long style instead of round so you can get a slim 10" (good for one person) or a husky 16" (good for two people). You can build your own and there is no crazy charges for as many toppings as you want so you can go crazy. 

They send it through a conveyor oven so it comes out hot and fresh. It's a crispy thin crust. 

The best thing is their sauces. They have an array of sauces you can add to your pizza. Let me recommend the Balsamic Molasses or the Garlicky Garden Butter. It's the perfect addition to the pizza.
name: Elizabeth

text: I wanted to love this place.  With much anticipation, our party of 6 adults arrived for a midweek dinner.  We started with cocktails and a perfect selection of cheeses.  So far, so good.  Actually, my cocktail (the graduate) was quite delicious.  However, another guest's glass of pinot noir was less appealing.  (Having lived in Italy for 5 years, his taste buds have been spoiled perhaps.)  We ordered a mini mushroom pizza for the table which was a favorite.  Then the entrees...sea bass, rib steak, duck - all received praised.  The lamb, unfortunately, was my choice and I just couldn't eat it.  The chef may have spilled the salt shaker and the dish was uneatable.  (The others commented that their dishes were salty, but they didn't mind enough to complain.)  I couldn't get past the salt, so I sent it back and reluctantly ordered a different dish.  We had the green beans and cucumbers for the table, which would have been enough for me, but I agreed to another entree.  I would not be charged for my lamb - no kidding - but they had no trouble charging for the steak which was almost twice as much as my lamb. Poor business move - this left a very bad taste in my mouth - and consequently a less than glowing review.  We were offered one complementary dessert along with the desserts we ordered.  Big deal.  Bottom line...our party spent $600 for dinner, drinks, and dessert.  I would happily pay that if the food had been mouth-watering delicious.  I can't say it was.  I wanted to love it, but I didn't. I'm disappointed and can't say I'd try the Philadelphia location again.
name: Terry

text: Best in the DT area. We eat here 2-3 times a month...  they do a great job with allergies and other food issues. Great tobthat they source locally for a lot of items.

text: I had dinner at Harry & Izzy's a month or so ago, sorry for the delay, life you know. Anyway, I didn't have a great experience. However I think they had an off night. I hate to give three stars, because I think they could easily earn 5 on a regular basis. Let me explain... I met an old colleague for dinner to catch up. He is an Indy native and recommended the shrimp cocktail. It was absolutely as described and the cocktail sauce was tangy with hot chunks of horseradish that clear your nostrils. I highly recommend trying the shrimp cocktail, but beware, the horseradish is legit. We both ordered steaks and I also ordered the Brussel sprouts. The Brussel sprouts were awesome, the steak was not. My ribeye was tough and over cooked. I mentioned it and they were very nice. However the next steak they brought out was raw, not medium rare. I finally asked for a filet and they brought me a passable steak. The staff was amazing and tried very hard to get my order right.  So take my three stars as an off night. I will try them again and expect it will be a good experience.

text:
Just to clear it up, three stars mean 'O.K.'
I've had a lot of burgers in my life. In and Out and Fat burger and even Febo burger in Denmark or Real Kobe burgers in Japan. 
I love burgers and Five Guys is right up there as a great burger! The service is always exceptional and it's always good. 
The problem I have is why a burger fries and a coke costs twenty dollars. 
This is not a burger at a Michelin star hotel on the beach with a sunset and table service. It's a burger joint. 

Even though it's a good one and I'm not a cheap ass, I just don't see why it's $2.50 for a medium drink. 5-6 dollars for fries or ten bucks for a burger.
 
I disliked writing this but it just seems expensive for what it is.

text: I have to preface this by saying, other reviewers are right. If you want to eat early, make sure you reserve your dough ahead of time and also show up early. So the next night we made sure to reserve dough. We showed up by 6 and were told it was about an hour wait or so. We ended up just waiting because the place is BYOB and decided we could just tap into our drinks. A few drinks later and we were seated. We had four things of dough reserved so we got to try a good bit of everything, given the menu is on the smaller side. Everything was delicious, I loved the pizza. My favorite by far was the Rosso Verde. If you like red peppers and arugula, you need to try this pizza because it was amazing. The crust was thin and perfectly cooked. Before I finished it, I knew I would need to return to this place!

text: I'm seeing double!  Only because I couldn't stop eating this near perfect and daring ensemble of a Large Villa Rina Pizza!  Spectacular price for quality pizza toppings and fresh dough.  EVERYTHING was ample.  My pictures should be clear enough of my Heaven and Happiness.  I could continue this admiration, but I do have a couple of suggestions. While boldly the thickness of a Greek Style pan pizza, it should've been cooked just another 5 minutes with a bit of oil underneath at a high heat to create crispiness.   It is definitely not a NY thin crust (Thank God!).  I read a previous review of too salty.  Apparently, they listened.  I had pepperoni and sausage and I believed it needed a bit more push with seasoning and salt.  The sauce,  a bit bland, either go robust or add a pinch of sugar with some flash of heat (if you're using homemade sauce). The topping and cheese was delicious regardless.  It certainly was not shortcutted or chintzy.   I am way beyond satisfied and if they can master those suggestions,  then I declare this Tampa's Most desirable pizza and family treat.  A large pizza, in this case, the slices could be sliced again on each and could feed a family of 5.  Great job, Pizza Rina!
name: David

text:
Took some time for me to try PDQ, growing up on Chick Fil A. Been to this location and the Clearwater one. Typical fast food ambiance, but I do like the TV screens and the open layout. Bathrooms are kept clean and I see staff doing they're best to clean up trays left behind that previous customers don't bring up to the trash bin. Staff is friendly, welcoming, and energetic. 

Favorite is the Buffy Bleu sandwich. Spicy chicken with bleu cheese. Totchos (tater tot nachos) are another fave. Bacon on top helps. They have decent salads and rice bowels. Haven't been able to try the shakes, dessert drinks, but I see plenty of people order them. Speaking of drinks, soda fountain machine on the inside...the one with all the different types of coke is always a fun novelty. 

This time I had the pimento sandwich. Totchos like usual. Sandwich was kinda cold. 

Still like the place. Nice to have something different then Chick Fil A. They have drive thru and have done Uber eats with a another location before (food can get soggy with delivery).

Let me say first that the fish and the employees are great.  Those are the only things that are good about this business.

My view of how this sort of place should be run is colored by ahi poke and the place downtown, poke zone.  In these restaurants, the experience is great.  It's a social experience.  You get to chat and point to things, it's fun.

At Hoki Poki, you order on a confusing tablet.

At other poke restaurants, masago and crab are free.

At Hoki Poki, both cost extra.

At other poke restaurants, they have about 3 people running the entire place.  Why does this place need so many employees?

Portion size was small.  The container was too small for a salad to be eaten from.

text:
I was very excited to try this place. I was surprised to go to lunch on Friday and find the place empty, because the food was so good this place should be jampacked from the moment the doors swing open till they roll you out onto the sidewalk at night! 
I was waiting for my friend so decided to try their pupusa. I've had them before but never quite as good. These were bigger,  fresh masa clouds with an incredibly generous filling. My friend arrived just as it was being delivered to the table, and it was large enough for us to share. Then we were provided with a gratis basket of chips and salsa, lightly sprinkled with cheese and a little bean sauce. I'm trying to watch the carbs so I only had two chips but they were absolute perfection. Not greasy or over salted, Which is what I usually find at restaurants. My mate had enchiladas while  I had Pollo Azado, mostly because I was trying to do a healthy option and stay away from the fried Salvadoran appetizer combo, which was super tempting. 
For a healthy grilled chicken, it was very flavorful, and enough to feel someone with a good appetite. I ended up taking a doggy bag home. Having enjoyed lunch, I will definitely return. In fact, based on the pupusas alone, that may be sooner rather than later, and considering how light, without being greasy the chips & pupusas were, I don't think it'll be too long before I tell that Combo Salvadoreno to "get in my belly!" 

Also top notch service. Our waitress who I believe is the owner, couldn't have been nicer or more charming. This is such a great addition to the neighborhood and perfect for when you want to go out to eat but you don't want the hassle of having to go far, dress up or spend a lot!  
It ticks all my boxes, and as far as I'm concerned you don't get much better than this !

text:
Coopers Hawk is one of the best places to grab a drink or meal with family and friends. Located on boyscout across the street from International Plaza, the winery has a tasting room as well as proper dining space. 

The tasting room is fun! You can try 8 wines for $7 or their lux line tasting is $12. The lux is usually worth it! You can try sparing through whites to reds. The list changes monthly and there are discounts if you buy a bottle or join their club. Their food is good but a little on the pricey side for a restaurant that isn't particularly fancy. Most entrees are $25-40. The Brussels salad with salmon is a winner($18). Our steak was overdone so they gave us a free dessert which was nice. The wine list is extensive and affordable which is also great. The tempranillo($8) was delicious. 

Definitely make a reservation as dinner is quite busy! They also have a space  you can book for private events.

text: They say that wine gets better with age, but I was never much of a wine guy.  Good thing Flat 12 is nearby!  This brewery has seriously gotten better with age. Who doesn't enjoy THAT blast from the past?  The craft beer scene in Indiana has blown up in the last few years, but if you haven't been yet (or in a while), check out Flat 12 again.

text:
I grew up in a Texas border town and grew up traveling to Mexico pretty frequently. This place was very underwhelming. The rice was over cooked and seemed as if it had been reheated 5 times over. The refried beans were a weird purple-ish color. The ground beef is the strangest I've ever seen -- it's almost as if it's thrown in the blender and so mushy. My fiancé had the fish tacos, which were also very flavorless and bland. We are pretty sure that's what made him very sick when we got home. I'm all for supporting small, local restaurants but they REALLY have to step their game up if they want to call themselves a Mexican restaurant because this is not a good nor accurate representation of what Mexican food should be.

The chicken salad with cinnamon dressing was to die for--never take this off the menu please!!  As well as the Birra tacos, Mercado quesadilla, Campecheno....10 stars.

text:
This place is such a mess.

The woman at the front acted inconvenienced when we asked her to double check our reservation when we were told we only had 2 rooms and not 3. Spent 20 or 30 minutes trying to figure it out only to find out 2 rooms she finally found for us weren't ready.

We then decided to look around and half my party ended up getting stuck in an elevator for almost 30 minutes. The door slammed shut behind me as I walked out and bounced from how hard it hit. Luckily no one's limb or anything was in the way or it honestly would have been cut off. Management took 30 minutes to get help and part of the reason was "because we don't know where in the elevator shaft they are." even after we told them multiple times the elevator never moved... The door was just shut. They also never asked us what they could do to help or if anyone was injured. They just basically let us out of the trapped elevator and said peace. As a Manger, I'd get fired if I treated my clients like that.

Finally after 4 hours of wandering because our rooms weren't ready, we go up to the front to find out.. Surprise... They still aren't. Alex at the front is the only employee I met today who genuinely seemed interested in customer service so A++++ for her!! She got us rooms quick and though they weren't next to each other like our reservation was supposed to be, we seriously just wanted to get in our rooms so it was fine.

This is all within 4 hours of getting here. Hopefully the next 4 days are better but we'll see.
name: Kellyann

text: So disappointed in Barrio Sandwich. It's located in the space across the courtyard from the ticket office for Tucson Theatre Company. You order at the counter and they bring it to you. Half sandwich $8.00. I was going to order one, and Frank another, so we could compare bread and taste. We couldn't order Frank's sandwich choice without mayo and seed mustard! Really. text:
What a great neighborhood haunt!  I had read about 58hundred in one of the local throw away's and wanted to try it based upon the reviewers recommendations.  We just wanted appetizers so we tried the smokey roasted beets. I LOVE roasted beets but must admit these didn't tickle my fancy.  We tried the hash brown potatoes with an egg on top, LOVED them. text: Cute and trendy pastry shop. I got the opera cake, the chocolate pillow and the creme brulee. I took one star off because they don't have to-go dishes. You can buy the creme brulee ($8) and the dish ($6), but I didn't want to spend $14 on one dessert. They boxed up my creme brulee in parchment paper so I had a slightly tough time eating it. text:
A nearly 50-year-old location, this Friendly's held the banner high. 

My dad and I stopped here at the end of a long day of bicycling on the Delaware towpath and had a great meal. 

Our enthusiastic server (Eric) was quick with suggestions and we tried the lobster quesadilla - which, no lie, was just about fantastic. 

Service was also quick but with a few pauses we'll say. All good though, as it was an enjoyable spot: kept our drinks full, the place was very clean, all kept up nicely, and again, the food was solid... so some waiting was no problem. 

We went ahead and got Sundaes like kids and although I forgot to take pictures of the lobster quesadillas I remembered the ice cream. 

When Eric brought the sundaes, he proudly announced "I made them myself and hope you love them". 

Feel good moment +++!

text: Amazing! Delicious! We ordered the Brie as an appetizer which was amazing especially with the pizza crust to dip in! I got the create your own pizza which was so filling but worth every bite! Other than being a little pricey and crowded I give it a 10/10!

text: Jason's Toridasu just opened on City Line underneath the Madison building of Presidential City. The restaurant itself is very clean and tidy. In addition, they have an awesome lunch special... from the time they open each day until 3:30PM they have 10.00 roll + salad + miso soup. This is an awesome deal considering it is a 9 piece roll, a large salad and soup. Most sushi places charge for spicy mayo, but this is complimentary at Jason's. When I go to Jason's I usually get either a Spicy Salmon or Philadelphia roll. They also could alter and make rolls on the spot, which is nice. I don't think this sushi is as good as some of the sushi restaurants I've been too, but I would give it 4 stars for the lunch special price, the nice staff and the convenience factor. The downside is that this place wouldn't be my first choice as a sit down dinner location.

text:
A must!
went for here for restaurant week date. the restaurant decor seem very cozy and comfy. 
we started out with 2 drinks - Old Fashion and french 75. one was whiskey other one was gin. both good and strong favors. 
Appetizers - Œuf du Pêcheur Fisherman's style poached egg, toast, mussels, tarragon cream - I have to admit this dish is my favorite appetizer course. It all works well. The mussels cook to perfection while the runny poach egg soaks the bread with the tarragon cream. each component balances one another and it was delicious.
 Must get! Escargots à la Bourguignonne Six Burgundy snails, garlic herb butter, croutons - Delicious snails with garlic herbs. After I devour the escargot I used the garlic herb butter sauce and put it on side bread. Delicious...trust me
 Terrine de Foie Gras Vanilla-scented foie gras pâté, red wine-poached pear, walnuts, endive - im not a big fan of Foie Gras but this dish was rich and delicate. Pear help out with the favor. Rillons aux Panais et Poire Pork belly confit, roasted pear and parsnip puree, sherry vinegar jus, watercress 
Pork Belly was out of this world. Tender, moist, delicious pork belly with the smooth puree. I was a big fan of this. entrees & side - Gratin de Pâtes Façon Peggy Macaroni and cheese - cheesy goodness. 
Magret de Canard aux Navets et aux Pommes I really loved this dish. The Duck was cooked perfectly. Wish I could have a whole duck and just eat this all day. Its just that good.
 Lapin Rôti à la Moutarde first time trying rabbit. wasn't as bad as I thought it would be. It was a bit salty but good. 
Taglietelle wish it was buttery and oiled a bit. Dessert - Mille Feuille aux Framboises Delicious and worth getting Gâteau Mousse au Chocolat when you think about this cake. You would think it would be rich and heavy. It was actually very light and smooth.

text:
Brand new to Midtown, Rue Bourbon is a New Orleans-inspired bar and grill featuring live music, plenty of seating, and room to dance, with free billiards and darts. The decor is fun and certainly evokes a sense of the Big Easy, though étouffée and filé gumbo will have to found elsewhere. The bar bites menu is produced in an exceptionally cozy kitchen.

At the top of the cocktail menu is a sazerac ($10), typically made with rye whiskey, sugar, bitters, and a hint of absinthe. Our server/bartender asked if I'd like, "well or top shelf bourbon." I politely read their menu description of a rocks glass washed with absinthe, filled with rye and a "sweet and spicy house mix." Looking confused, she replied, "Ok, rye then." Thankfully, what I received was actually not a bad example--served "up"--though a little on the sparse side, with no hint of the promised spice.

Onto another pair of classics, a mint julep ($10) and Pimms cup ($11). The julep was pretty strong--with lots of mint and ice--and copper mule mug substituted for silver julep cup. Pimm's #1 is a gin-based liqueur with spice and citrus notes, this example of its famous cocktail properly mixed with soda, fruit, and cucumber over ice in a highball glass. Overall best amongst the trio.

An order of cajun swamp fries ($14) was described as being piled high with cajun shrimp and house remoulade. There was certainly a pile of crispy seasoned fries drizzled in spicy sauce, topped with a pile of "kickin'" vaguely vinegary, bland coleslaw, escorted by five (5) fried prawns. This was followed by a basket of gator bites ($15), boneless chunks of marinated alligator meat--deep-fried in seasoned cornmeal batter--served with cups of remoulade and slaw. Oh my goodness, those beautiful swamp monster bites were a treat. I was pleasantly surprised by how moist and tender they were compared to some previous encounters. Definitely the best I've had in ages.

The muffuletta cold cuts sandwich--so named for its round, low-profile Italian bread--hails from New Orleans' Central Grocery. Rue Bourbon uses the jarred original olive salad (proudly on display), with sliced provolone, capicola, sopressata, pepperoni, and mozzarella, served with choice of fries, slaw, or Zapp's Louisiana kettle chips ($13). The bread was a little dry and could have used a bit more of the olive mix, though not overall a bad rendition.
 
Next, three "po' boy sliders": shrimp ($14), chicken ($10), and andouille ($10), available with the same choice of sides. There's nothing better than a big ol' crusty French roll po' boy stuffed with goodies, so I'm puzzled how a halved 6" sandwich on forgettable cornmeal-finished soft roll equates as either po' boy or slider. The bread was grilled, so there's that. There were a couple shrimp per side, and the cajun sausage was very good. The most stuffed was chicken, though the meat itself was a bit dry and lacked seasoning. The dressing of tomato, slaw, onion and remoulade or aioli (depending) helped all three.

Perhaps our most anticipated item, beignet made with Cafe du Monde packaged mix ($6 for 3). Served hot-- dusted with plenty of confectioners sugar--at first seemed to be just the thing. But, unlike the expected light and airy doughnut cousin, these were on the tough and chewy side. Perhaps the oil wasn't hot enough, or the dough kneaded a bit too much. Either way, sadly not the beignet of my dreams.

text:

Everything was super fresh and really good. They even make their own corn tortillas.

The cocktails include more than the standard Mexican fare, although their house margarita was on point with a bit of smokiness. I worried the Blue Eyez cocktail would be too sweet - as so many of these types of drinks are - but alas, it seems they know what they're doing. All in all, excited to have a place that feels a bit more adult but still FUN. Welcome to BR!

text: My wife and I went here for appetizers and lunch. We were seated immediately and the waiter came over within 2 minutes (good right?) Well that's where it stoped. We ordered our appetizer and lunch at the same time so we wouldn't be there for too long. We got the bang bang shrimp for the app and soup and salad for lunch. It took 20 minutes for them to bring it out the bang bang shrimp which were delicious, but to long of a wait. Then we sat there for another 20 minutes waiting on soup and salad. We gave up and left before we got our lunch. 40 minutes for soup and salad
name: Frank

text:
Owner: Don Rizzo told our group to leave his restaurant and go someplace...he said "I don't need your business".
Our group of 9 retired AB employees made a reservation for 11:30 on 12/11 for our Christmas Luncheon. I was the 1st to arrive at 11:15 and was told that I couldn't be seated until our entire group arrived. At 11:25 we had 4 of our 9 and was this time told by the owner that they have a sign at the door that states groups of 6 or more won't be seated until all members are present.
I said we could go to another restaurant and be seated, but we would wait for the 5 minutes for our reservation even though our table was sitting vacant. The owner said no need because he was cancelling our reservation and told us to leave because he didn't need our business.
Our group...now 8 strong went across the street to Rich & Charlie's where we were treated with more respect and had a wonderful lunch with no wait and had excellent service from our waiter Mike.
Please remember that even though Rizzo's has excellent food...the owner - Don Rizzo doesn't need your business.
name: Dave

text: It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Food was fresh and service was quick. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait.
name: User

text: Very tasty vegan options. I had the Thai Tofu and vegan pate. Outside seating only so just be prepared
name: Fern

text: This was my first time ordering a catering order from them. Everything was on time and complete. One things that Panera does well is constancy with their food. Everyone loved their sandwiches and online ordering makes everything easier. Why I didn't give them 5 stars is because I asked for some cream cheese because I wasn't able to place it through my online order. While trying to explain this the lady was really short with me. I wanted to walk her through my process so that they could maybe fix this issue but she didn't really want to hear anything and just said call next time. When I ended up getting to the event, the creamcheese that she gave me was already used half way. Im not sure if they don't check but it was just dissapointeg to get an already used tub of cream cheese after you spend over 200$ in catering.

text:
This is a legit dive bar in a strip mall that seems like it would probably be a good venue to watch sports.  The drinks were fairly priced and the service was efficient.  The only negative issue for me, but one that kills it for me, is that this place is super smoke filled and 100% of all the patrons in this joint were hitting the cancer sticks like they were never getting to shove another one in their mouth.  Also on offer during my visit were some really hilariously awful karaoke performances going on; as chain smokers often have raspy crackling voices from all the years of turning their mouths, throats and lungs into a pieces of dehydrated shriveled meat like a ham hung in a smokehouse what else could you expect?  The space of time I was able to handle being in this joint was one beer and then the clothes I was wearing reeked of smoke for a week after until I got back home and could wash them.  

One day if the practice of smoking finally dies off maybe I might return but likely the last kooky suicidal smoke inhalers will be lingering on in here for a few decades more.  So all you smokers have firmly established a strong home base in this establishment to fully enjoy exclusively to yourselves.
name: Shannon

text:
Stopped by for a mid Saturday lunch and restaurant was busy, but we were seated promptly for lunch at the bar. 

Staff was very friendly and attentive. 

Rolls were fresh and delicious! Highly recommend the Scorpion and for nigiri, the Cajun salmon! Appetizers were good, however, the muscles were pretty plain but that was our only disappointment.
name: Tessa

text: Fantastic service, even for takeout, even though they were super busy. Nice atmosphere. Will definitely be back to dine in!
name: Walker

text:
I would definitely recommend reading the reviews before coming to this establishment. While I didn't have an extremely long wait to order, or receive my food... the food did not exceed my expectations. I ordered the shrimp entree, which came with 7 pieces of shrimp and about a cup of seafood rice (including crabmeat and pieces of shrimp). My order total including tax was $16.28. 

The reason why the Main Course received only 3 stars, was due to the small portion size for an $16 meal. Also noting the food was not hot at all, more around room temperature. For those who don't like spicy food, I was caution the shrimp in the shrimp entree. 

In terms of the customer service, the individual taking the order wasn't extremely polite but manageable. 

Overall I would not recommend this establishment, but okay for a 1st time try.
name: Alyssa

text: I've gone to The Row for lunch and dinner, and I must say to get the best experience, I'd recommend going in the night for the live music. The dishes are very Southern with classics like grits, fried pickles, and deviled eggs. The prices are a little inflated, like buying 6 pieces of eggs for $8. There are almost no vegetarian options since they mix meat in even with veggies like braised greens (if you're vegetarian, make sure to ask the waiter about the dishes). However, the meat dishes are very flavorful, though oily. Overall, the food is on the heavier side both health wise and price wise.
name: Jenny

text: Fabulous meal. Falafel, hummus, mixed grill of various kebabs and Mendi chicken- all were great. Rice was outstanding. Good service as we sat on the floor in a booth.

text: I'm not sure if this restaurant is under new ownership but the service and the quality of the food is significantly lower than previous occasions when I've visited. text:

text:
Back again since last time.  Still stellar, still the same cool and friendly people.  Still the same phenomenal food (oooooo and I asked for the rest of our olives to go since we had to go to get to the Paul Simon concert and they gave us *extra* olives!!!!!  Bonus!!!!!)

These really are such cool people.  We had a schedule tonight, which was unfortunate.  You should really go when you have time to hang out and shoot the shit and really *think* about what you want to eat.  This is because their menu changes based on what's available locally and what's in season.

Two things for dinner :
1). Make a reservation unless you're a regular and show up early
2). If you only have an hour or hour and a half to spend before you leave, let them know and they will accommodate you.  When I tell you that these folks take their food seriously, I mean it.

The food is crazy good and crazy fresh.  The folks who run it make you feel like you're eating in their personal dining room.  You'll like them so much, you'll want them to sit down with you and eat!  (I'm not joking here, my friend said said he wished we could've spent 3 hours here)

Having said all that yes the filet was still good, yes the scallops were still good, yes the wine was off the charts good, yes the hummus and olives were good, yes we wanted to try the gumbo and pot stickers but our stomachs weren't big enough and we were on a schedule yadda yadda yadda...

text:
When we first arrived here we thought it was just a supermarket but there are actually seating on the side for ppl to dine in. Most of the ppl came here for take outs. The server was really friendly!

I got pork taco, pork with pineapple taco and beef tongue taco. I also added the lettuce and cream cheese on my tacos. I thought it was not worth it since it didn't enhanced the taco flavors in any way. The beef tongue is not good cuz it was a little chewy. Pineapple one was fun to taste but the pork one was my favorite. My friend likes her beef taco the best out of her tacos too. So I guess the original is the best. My brother got a burrito and it came with fries. The fries was the best part of the meals. It was so crispy!! My other friend got the fajita with steak. The steak looks pretty dry and the yellow rice was okay. 

Overall, the price was friendly for the food that they served. I would just recommend the pork and steak tacos. It is a place suitable for quick bite and nothing too fancy.

text:
We spent one night at the motel, a Thursday overnight to Friday. Check in time was 3 p.m. but we got there a few minutes before 3 o'clock.  We were able to check in though. Pleasant friendly clerk checked us in, went over all the policies with us, asked us if we wanted an upstairs or downstairs room, gave us our complimentary tickets for breakfast the following morning, and drink specials for happy hour (5 to 10 p.m.) in the bar.  We chose a downstairs room since we didn't want to do stairs. Both had patios outside of the rooms, the upstairs were more enclosed than the downstairs ones were.

The room was very nice and roomy.  Clean.  Not too noisy at all.  My biggest complaints are about the room, otherwise would have given it a 5 star rating. The 2 complaints are the shower head was really high up, was not effective for us in showering, and the shower curtain didn't quite reach to the bottom so water did splash on the floor. The other complaint was the lights for the bathroom with the toilet and shower as well as the lights for the sink area of the bathroom were set on timers (efficient I get it to save electricity and resources) but we are used to leaving one of the lights on at night for maneuvering around the room. Waking up to a pitch black room was a bit disorienting and caused me when trying to go to use the bathroom walk to the opposite side of the room. Thankfully hubby woke up and turned his flashlight on in his phone so I could see I was going in the wrong way. Leaving any of the other lamps on would have caused too much bright light for sleeping. This has happened to us in another motel in the Tucson area so I'm thinking we need to pack a nightlight from home so we can plug it in just to be on the safe side.  Otherwise, the room was fine.

The complimentary breakfast was at the restaurant part of the motel.  We were greeted by several waitresses when we walked in.  You sit yourself.  The waitress brought over the menu for the complimentary breakfast. There were a variety of items on the menu.  You could upgrade for an additional charge if you wanted something more. We both got the 2 egg special which came with either bacon or sausage, home fries or hash browns, toast or baby cakes. I got the baby cakes. Just the right size of pancakes. Food came out quickly and tasted good.  Note, its a complimentary breakfast but gratuity is not included so tip the waitress (or waiter).

We got 2 for 1 coupons for happy hour.  We got there about 8:30 p.m.  Ordered a glass of wine and hubby got a greyhound.  Total were $6 for both.  It was karaoke night so it was fun to see others singing.  

Nice experience and if we are down in Tucson again, would consider staying there.  The motel is about 5 minutes from downtown Tucson.
name: Betty

text:
I love Oceana and make it a must every time I travel to NOLA. 
For apps I ordered the oysters which were very good and flavorful. My friend got the bbq shrimp which I tried as well and the sauce was delicious. 
I ordered a blackened catfish po boy and my friend got the fried shrimp. Mine was good and everything but the fried shrimp one looked better, and that's what I would get next time!
They also make a good hurricane with dry ice or some other sort of smoke effect. Very fun!
Oceana is a good spot for solid food and drinks.

text:
Ordered online through GrubHub after a 6 hour drive to Philly today. I ordered at 7:23, and it was delivered 10 mins earlier than estimated at 7:42. The driver was very friendly and helpful. He remembered to give us plastic tableware (though the restaurant also remembered, it was buried under deliciousness). 
I had the steak kabob with grilled veggies and a Greek side salad. My friend had the same sides with the Mediterranean chicken. The steak was perfectly medium rare and very flavorful. The delicious grilled veggies were a lovely mix of peppers, broccoli, onions, carrots, mushrooms, and tomatoes. I received dressing for my salad and an Italian Verde sauce for my kebobs. So delicious!

text: I've been here two times and everytime it gets better and better. The food is incredible, the service is great. All the seafood options and it's fresh quality make it one of the best places in the French Quarter. I haven't had a meal yet that disappointed me. Great place to go to taste true New Orleans Food.

text:
Absolutely delicious. I'm currently 8 mos pregnant and was looking for a healthy place to grab dinner because I'm too tired to cook but also didn't want fast food. Found this place so close to home. Small and cozy like interior and a nice outdoor patio with heating (that's where I sat).
I ordered the homemade bread with honey and olive oil to start. For my main course I had the most delicious pesto penne pasta. There were nuts and olives in the pasta but obvi you can get it without them. I drank Chia Tea with rice milk. For desert I had the freshly made cinnamon roll. I had to get it to go because it's huge. I also ended up ordering a cáptese sandwich with tomota soup to go for later. I would highly recommend this place and I will be returning. There are also vegan dishes. Very excited to try other dishes.
name: Asia

text: We arrived here around noon on a Monday, asked to sit at the bar (no bartender around yet), and they obliged. Ordered a couple beers and perused the menu. On the bartender (that finally showed up) recommendation we ordered the chargrilled oysters and they were fantastic. Honestly we didn't even want to use crystal hot sauce or lemon or anything on them...they were SO GOOD. Come here and eat these, you won't be disappointed. The reason for three stars is that the service was mediocre. We heard a male server whining as people came in for lunch "why are people coming in on a Monday!" Okay. You're a server. Shouldn't you want customers? For heaven's sake. Several of the staff were just lackadaisical (for lack of a better word). It was just odd and not very welcoming. The one bartender with a beard/goatee was awesome and the only person who was really friendly. I'd go back for those oysters though.
name: Marianne

text:
I was really excited to eat at Royal House, but with each review I read I became more and more nervous that I sat down and spent my time here. What really made this trip disappointing is that my experience started to match some of the negative reviews I read. 

First we order the Crab Claws. We initially came here for fried shrimp and other seafood. When the dish came out I was shocked and appalled any manager or restaurant would let such a measly dish leave the kitchen. The taste was good, but there were only 6 claws in the dish with a very small portion of meat, not worth the expensive price it was sold for! 

After we finished, we kept thinking , "What does this mean for the rest of our dishes." Our nerves were high. 

Our oysters came out with our shrimp platters, so that was a little frustrating. The oysters weren't great, they weren't as hot and buttery as expected (Acme Oyster House has the best so far) 

Now on to this shrimp platter. Definitely good in terms of breading (it was light enough to taste the shrimp) but I had so many shrimp the size of my nail-beds, which is completely unacceptable for $19!!! You will be pleased with the overall amount of shrimp; Some were a decent size but the others were embryos so I didn't know how to feel and was confused. Needless to say, the shrimp were the highlight of my experience, a plus? 

Nice try Royal House, I won't be returning. 

Btw our waiter was GREAT! Very attentive and timely.
name: Talia

text:
Love love love this gem. I don't know where to begin. Lets see, starting from the outside, I have to say that one major bonus in my opinion is that there is actual parking lot parking available street side and a gravel parking lot behind it. So, I have never, not found a place to park that isn't a block away. They have a great patio for nice weather days and also for special events they put large tents up outside on the patio area. 
   I have been to this place for various events. Great concerts held here (check website) and there is a decent sized dance floor. Depending on the event, they have amazing food prepared by Paulie and the fabulous staff. 
   We held a celebration of life here for my sister. The moment we sat down and talked to Paulie about what we had in mind, I knew he understood what we wanted and he did not disappoint at all.Decorations,food,drink, music, video, all done very well and very professional.  A tough day for our family was made so much easier, knowing it was all being handled for us. 
    Our family has also held a wedding reception here!! Again, Paulie got the Brides vision and did not disappoint. The entire staff helps out in making these events great. We feel like we are now among friends when we go to ORH. If you are curious, then get there and check them out.

You get to pick your own flavored salsa to go along with it. They do give you a small bowl of chips with salsa. Additional chips and salsa are 4 dollars.

text:
My girlfriend is obsessed with this place. OBSESSED. we seriously go at least twice a month... I know you're probably like that's not that much; BUT we live downtown and this is in Southport. Listen, it's 25 minutes and we drive past several amazing restaurants but she insists and I'm just along for the ride. 

The food is amazing, I won't lie. I always get the chicken and steak and the ball and chain orders the scallops. Everything has always been cooked perfectly... I give props to the grill, but the chefs do entertain while they cook. 

Service is kind of rude/short but I don't think they mean to be... just efficient. They are quick to turn their tables. You don't really get to sit around after your meal... they literally start cleaning the table around you until you get up. 

The restaurant needs some updating. It's pretty old and several of the chairs and booths show wear and tear on them. 

Look, I know my review sounds like this place is mediocre but the food is amazing. They could literally just serve me outside and I would still give them 4 stars. I refuse to let my girlfriend know this, but I do like going here... it's worth the 25 minute drive. 

CHEERS!

text:
We've been meaning to try this place for a while and finally made it out on a Thursday night! It was pretty busy when we arrived and the hostess cleaned off tables to get us seated. Service left a lot to be desired -- but we kind of just assumed we hit it at a really busy time. It took forever to get the food even though there weren't many tables full by the time we got it. 

I totally appreciate the local sourcing of meat and creativity of the burgers. I had the Avocado one and my husband had the Franklin (but added bacon to it). The burgers were really good -- juicy and hot! The fries were awful. We had such high hopes too with the fresh hand cut description. They were cold and very greasy. Typically a sign the oil isn't hot enough, and they weren't cooked long enough. 

We did really appreciate that both of our beers were half off when we got the check (ladies night happy hour all night on Thursdays), and we will likely give it another shot and hope it was just an "off" night as far as the fries and service. The burgers were worth trying the place again and the vibe is nice. Also, it's great to have a spot other than fast food chains open late in Franklin!

But I couldn't overlook the fact that all 3 meats were over cooked and not very flavorful like typical ramen is. I struggled to finish most of it. Price is average for a ramen joint but there are definitely better places in the area for what you get. 

I've also tried the bubble teas which I don't think are worth the $6 for most price tag. text:
I have stayed here twice for multi-day trips to Edmonton. Sounds trivial but this hotel has very slow elevators & a lack of elevators (you end up spending a lot of time waiting for the elevator or being in the elevator, and the stairs take you outside, not to the lobby). The first time I stayed here one elevator was out of service and it was a disaster. They also charged our credit card for Mini Bar items we didn't use on my first trip! 

Both times I have stayed here my room has been across from the elevator and have been woken up in the early morning by other guests heading downstairs as walls are far from sound proof (you can hear everything that goes on in the hallway, even the elevator changing floors). Bathrooms do not have fans. Mattress in the room on my second visit was very hard and uncomfortable to sleep on. There is also no underground parking.

However, funky decor, good gym, clean rooms, great location, and tasty free continental breakfast. While they have done their best, the reality is that this is an old building and at best a three star hotel. As it was noisy again on my second stay (and the elevator issue & hard mattress was annoying) I am not sure if at worth the $$$$/ night and I will look into other options next time I'm in Edmonton.

text:
I'd never been here before but had heard great things. Went there for lunch this past week and wonder what the deal is...I realize this is a lot of complaining but (a) it's the owners, not the staff, who are at fault and (b) the last item earns me the right to b***h...

1. You stand in line to order your food at a counter. While you're trying to decide what to order, a giant TV shows the menu but only for 25% of the time.
2. You're asked to tip when you place your order, which is backwards. I don't understand why tipping is even appropriate when you have to go up to place your order, you get your own drink and utensils, and you go up again to get your food. There is no "service" whatsoever.
3. When you order, you get a number. There were 12 orders ahead of mine once I paid. It then took 47 minutes to make a simple fried fish sandwich. Long wait times are a common complaint, so it shows the owners don't know what they're doing, like they run the whole kitchen with one Fry-Daddy. Two people walked out without getting their food.
4. The frying oil hadn't been changed recently. Simple fried white fish should not come out brown.
5. And finally - 14 hours after eating at Caplinger's - having eaten canned soup and pbj for dinner the night before, nothing that morning, and cereal for dinner - I got food poisoning.
