text:
If you haven't experienced a Brazilian Steakhouse you should! In the past few weeks I have been able to eat at 2 Brazilian steakhouses - 1. in Canmore (forget the name) and the other here in Edmonton at Pampa's on Ellerslie. The experience is amazing and everyone should give it a try.

Pampa's on Ellerslie is relatively a new restaurant. It is easy to find, lots of parking and has a great feeling when you enter the restaurant. It is an open concept but it looks like there is two semi-private rooms for group functions.

We were attended to right away by the hostess and were seated near the wonderful and large salad bar. You can also see where they are cooking the meat etc.

Our waiter came and explained the process to us. Simply put, you have access to the salad bar and other options like buns, soup, stew, lasagna etc. Once you fill your plate you return to your table when serves with meat on a stick/pole come to your table and ask if you would like a piece of meat. There is lots of variety of cuts, roasts and choices of meat. To help with the pace you have a green card on one side and red on the other which signals the server if you are wanting for them to continue to bring meat. I would say there is about 11-12 choices to choose from. The servers generally serve medium rare to medium cooked meat, but by request you can order a different temperature to your liking.

While eating from the salad bar and beginning to eat some of the meat in they brought to us, we noticed that it was quite noisy with the sound from the customers bouncing off the concrete walls and floors. If you are out for a sociable night this may not be of concern, but for those wanting a quiet dinner this is something to make note of.

In my critique,

I found the selection of meat being served tonight quite dry and tough. I did try some other temperatures but I was unhappy with the meat that they were serving. 

Service was fantastic with the servers coming by regularly and having the manager check in on us. However, when we asked for the bill it took about a 1/2 hour for it to arrive. This was concerning to us as we mentioned to the server that we wanted to leave as soon as possible as we were planning to be somewhere else at a certain time. 

Be prepared for a costly bill - experiences cost money. For four of us with 4 cocktails our bill was just over $250. Cocktails average around 12 dollars, beer around 8 though they do have some great drink specials that were on for 6 dollars.

In ending,

I think this place is good and would be a great place to have an experience. The food was ok for me, I would have liked to see some juicer cuts but it could have been a bad night. I would go again if it were a group function, but for 2-4 of us I would have to pass.
name: John

text: Terrific atmosphere and vibe. Excellent food and service. Beach-sophisticated interior. Pretty. Super staff.
name: Mary Ann

text: I had high hopes for this place. I'll give them a break because it does look like they were understaffed so that does attribute to the slow service. One thing I hate is when I order an appetizer and it comes with the entree it completely defeats the purpose of the appetizer. I ordered a Gyro melt since I've never had one before. The meat was cooked pretty well but I wasn't a fan of the  Tzaiki sauce. The fries were decent seemed like they were a little over cooked though. Ironically the best part of the meal was the wings. I may try them again and get something different but I wasn't to impressed with this place.

text:
Can there exist too much of a good thing?   Say hello to the Cheesy Todd, which is a combination of the American peoples favorite foods: bacon, cheese, hamburger meat, the typical fix-ins & all served between a fried greasy goodness bun composed of mac & cheese.  Totally delicious but left with a feeling glutonous guilt.  Fun to experience, i guess, but nothing i could order a 2nd time in good conscience.

text: The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Nice little spot, decent portions too. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. They were out of one thing I originally wanted..

text: For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. Worth checking out. It looked better online than it did in person. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable.
name: User

text: Service was nice, kitchen was just moving kind of slow. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Food was fresh and service was quick.

They stick to classic burgers and fare at an extremely reasonable price. I'd go as far to say that it is as good as In-N-Out! Two full meals and drinks for two people and we had an amazing dinner for under $15! Can't wait for our next visit to this new burger joint.

text: Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. It was crowded but still moved along. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. Glad we tried it. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Would probably stop in again if nearby. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text: Finally got the opportunity to pop into one of the most highly regarded beer bars in the country, the Avenue Pub, on a beautiful Monday afternoon in New Orleans. On a previous visit a year ago I had called and been given inaccurate information regarding kids being able to sit at the outdoor front tables, and because I had my daughter with me at that point wasn't able to get in and enjoy the place. No such issues this time, as it was just the grownups for an early afternoon lunch. It was a gorgeous afternoon as we settled under a tent in the back beer garden and began to examine the impressive and sizable beer list. The place is in the final two for an online contest for "Best Beer Bar in the United States" with Monk's in Philadelphia, which is high competition. My brother enjoyed several classic Old Fashioned's, and the rest of the party worked our way through the outstanding brews. Great local stuff, super rare stuff, very varied in style. A must for a craft beer fan. We started with two orders of fries, the To Die Fries served with creamy béchamel, and the Dumptruck fries, which featured the béchamel with lemongrass and flavorful pulled pork. Both shareable choices were dominated by our party. I went with the classic and recommended Pub Burger, a 7oz local Artisanal Beef pattie perfectly prepared, with Arugula, Tomato, Onions, Pickles, Garlic Aioli on a Bakery Challah bun. I had cheddar cheese and candied bacon on it, and it was perfect. Juicy, flavorful, what a great burger. The service was great, and our bartender was awesome all day. When we wanted a comparable recommendation after liking this beer or that she did a good job, and didn't just steer us towards the most expensive or the stuff they were trying to get rid of. The reputation of this place amongst the craft beer set is serious, but seriously well earned and well deserved. The upstairs bar features entirely different options, and I would be intrigued by a return visit as well. Awesome time!
name: Ian

For example, order a burger Togo and if there are old fries in the pan, the chef will drop them in the fryer again to heat them. Nice attentive ppl work here.

text:
I've been going to Cantwell's M&D since the '80s. Unfortunately, the quality of the food has declined significantly while the prices have skyrocketed.  I've been dissatisfied with Cantwell's prices vs portions for a while, but today convinced me to avoid Cantwell's in the future.  

Today a friend and I went to Cantwell's to grab a couple of sandwiches to go.  I chose "the special," which was a Tri-tip sandwich on a roll for $9.50.  What I got was a sandwich with lettuce, tomato, onion, cheese, mayo, and a single slice of tri-tip that was 3mm - 5mm thick--not several slices of layered tri-tip, but a single slice.  My friend ordered the club sandwich, which was made without any bacon.  Yeah, you read that right, an untoasted club sandwich with no bacon. So, two pathetic sandwiches, one bag of chips, and one beverage ended up costing around $23.  That's not going to happen again, not to me anyway.

I have no complaints about the staff, they are friendly and helpful, and I doubt they have any discretion when it comes to the portions of ingredients that they can add to the sandwiches.
name: Tswrench

text:
This place is DELICIOUS!

My husband and I came out to the mid-West for Thanksgiving and found this place after our flight into Indianapolis. We just wanted a solid burger with some fresh veggies and a clean, nice atmosphere. Burger Theory really delivered!

We were greeted very warmly and seated immediately. Alison was a great waitress, making sure we had everything we needed without hovering (A+). Our food quickly came out hot, 100% to order, and fantastic. I had the Lone Star (GF w/ a lettuce wrap), 6'10" husband had the BT Boss and we split fries and onion rings. Everything was well done and tasted really yummy! We were really bummed when we didn't have time to visit again on our flight out.

Told my parents/siblings about it. Whenever I'm in Indianapolis, THIS is where I'm coming to eat!

text: I so wanted this to place to be a win but the food was lackluster and barely warm. Save your money.

text:
Typical Asian buffet. Not many hot dishes or desserts to choose from, sushi was okay. The sauce they added to some dishes were either too salty or tasted Americanized. This place takes reservations for large parties (we had a part of 12), which made getting a row of tables to ourselves easier.

Liked their unique shabu shabu (hot pot) station, which I've never seen in a buffet setting before. The dish I tried from the hot pot station was bland, may have had some spiciness to it but that was about it. The system they have in place for this station was a bit confusing at first because you have to hand them one of the Jenga blocks from your table (with your table number), but it was easy to figure out after. Plus they bring it straight to your table once it's cooked.

Thought the food was bland, but there were a couple of things that I usually don't see in an Asian buffet restaurant that made it more interesting.
name: Nancy

text:
First off I have to say I love love love this place. I have been here a number of times over the years in the service and quality of food have always been excellent.

The location of this place makes it perfect for watching that sunsets coming down on the golf of Mexico.

Tonight we had a large group and we had to wait for a while which was completely understandable. We are sitting upstairs a little ways away from the outside but we could clearly see the sunset. 

As the food came out most of the family felt that it was just simply OK and that it was not outstanding. I ordered a shrimp Po boy that came out and I guess I should've realized that the shrimp would be fried and that the bread would be super enormous . However i was a little disappointed that the flavor did not pull through on the entire dish.

I ended up eating all of the shrimp and the coleslaw and never touched the bread.
This is a really cool spot to stop and have a quick meal and a cocktail. If you're around Clearwater I highly recommend stopping at the original crabby's. It is well worth the money. If you're looking for high-quality food however I recommend stopping somewhere else.
name: David

text:
My son and I stopped by the Founding Farmers First Bake Cafe & Creamery for a quick breakfast before heading to an appointment at CHOP.  I ordered an iced coffee and bagel with cream cheese and he ordered a donut and milk. 

The three year old was tickled pink that his milk came in a travel coffee cup, the same as my coffee.  I did find it odd that my iced coffee came in a hot cup versus a cold cup with a straw, but not the end of the world. 

The chocolate covered donut was not good.  I hate to say it that way, but the taste was completely off.  It was doughy and somewhat flavorless.  

My bagel did not arrive until my son was well over half done with this bagel, it took quite a bit of time, especially since there appeared to be more employees in than customers.  Not the best scenario when you are in a mild hurry and your toddler is not patient once the good is gone. 

The bagel itself was okay, but there was barely any cream cheese on it.  I don't like a ton of cream cheese (I hate places that slop it on), but this had hardly any!  

On the flip side, my iced coffee was delicious, I would order that again if I happened to be there, but I wouldn't go out of my way to grab breakfast there again.
name: Erin

text:
I had previously seen this establishment before and when asked to join another couple, my girlfriend and I jumped at the chance. To say I was disappointed would be an understatement. From the very beginning it took 10 minutes before anyone said a word to us. We had chosen our drinks and what we wanted to eat by the time our server, a short female who's name was never told to us, came and asked us if we wanted any drinks. Before any of us could answer she asked if we'd like waters, of which we all replied yes, and then bolted off.

That was the tone setter. The following hour would be filled with her rude attitude mixed with a feeling that she wanted us to hurry throughout our meal. When we finally ordered our food she started to take off before I had to stop her and say we wanted an appetizer. We ordered Calimari and some type of roll with Caviar on it. She brought our drinks, never recommended anything to us, never suggested what was good, and never smiled the entire time. We were a bother to her.

When the Calimari was ready, she literally dropped the plate off and ran off. I had no idea what was on our table. The Calimari was thick/clumpy/a lot of bread, which could be your style but I would never know because we didn't know what it was until we tasted it with a mystery sauce that was never described to us. My girlfriend has a mango and cantaloupe allergy, the color of the sauce scared her from trying it.

The server then brought two dishes with a 5 minute gap in between. The ladies with us felt uncomfortable eating without us getting our food so we all just sat around looking at two plates without any awareness of what was going on. Communication was sorely lacking from this individual. The manager that night knows exactly who we are by the way, we spoke to him several times that evening, including telling him how bad that server was.

The dish that was supposed to be for my girlfriend was a kimchi fried rice dish. there wasn't even a hint of kimchi in the dish and when asked about it the waitress got extremely defensive. It was off putting. Finally, when we were done with our meal, my friend wanted to try the Miso Creme' Brulee. We had seen the chef prepare it with the torch behind the Sushi counter and it looked very appealing. We never got that chance. She did a walk by drop off of the check and went to the kitchen. I personally don't get many chances to go out, let alone to a place that seemed more upscale than most. I spent $113 on poor service and very good food outside of the kimchi fried rice. In total we spent over $225 and may never return.

text:
Read the history of Ted's Montana Grill on their website and they will mention Ted Turner as the co-founder of TMG. Is it THE Ted Turner? Just something to think about. 

And of course, celebrities have opened countless restaurants and establishments (Kenny Rogers Roasters, Tim Horton's, etc.) and they can be hit or miss. 

So my wife and I had the afternoon free of kids, so we tried out Ted's. I thought it better to try it without the kids because steakhouse bills can add up and the kids may end up eating very little of what we order. In fact, Ted's does have a very reasonably priced kid's menu ($6-$14) with everything from chicken fingers to miniature steaks. They also give complimentary pickles. The server was honest and said some people love them and some people hate them. We're Korean and it tasted like Korean pickles, so we asked for more! 

As for the steak, my wife ordered a salad with steak on top. I ordered the NY strip. I asked for it between medium rare and medium. It came out in between medium and medium well. We were on a tight schedule (needed to make it to a movie), so I didn't send it back. The taste was excellent (I added bacon garlic butter) and the kale salad and fries/onion rings side were a nice complement to the steak. We ordered in house made lemonade (and the provide free refills). The total bill was around $50, which was pretty reasonable.
name: David

text:

The service was fast, efficient and friendly. I have absolutely no complaints; my waitress was wonderful and kept the coffee warmed up and the water topped off. 

I ended up docking two stars because they are cash only. Absolutely no excuse in 2019 to run a cash only business unless you're trying to hide something. There is, of course, an ATM. text:
So I was in a car accident on April 2nd of this year. My mom had a sudden blackout while driving and hit a parked car. Our car was totaled.
The EMT's were amazing and I cannot thank them enough for their kindness and warm smiles. Helped calm me down a lot given the circumstances.

Now then, neither me nor my mom were in immediate medical danger. I called the ambulance for her, as I was afraid she had a concussion. I had lightly sprained my right ankle and my right elbow had a small scrape on it.

Apparently, according to this hospital that means I need X-Rays on BOTH MY ELBOW AND ANKLE!! I insisted they ONLY X-Ray my ankle, as I knew my elbow was not broken. But they did it anyway.

I was given UNNECESSARY RADIATION!! I joke about it with people and say "Hey, maybe I'll get superpowers!" but that's just a facade to hide the fear that they may have permanently damaged my body in some way. 

My right ankle still hurts if I move it the wrong way though.
I was not given my X-Ray images after the fact. I was scared mostly for my mom as my mom was in worse condition and they did not offer her any means of doing dialysis and if they did, she would be stuck doing clinical dialysis rather than home dialysis. HER KIDNEY FUNCTION IS AT 3% NOW!! I wanted to go to St. Vincents hospital in Caramel not Methodist but Methodist was closer and I did not want to inconvenience the nice EMT's. 

They seemed shocked when I refused tylenol or ibuprofen for my ankle. Like it wasn't even that badly sprained! Why would I need it? 
My mom was several hours late for her second dialysis session that day and her kidney function was at 5% before the accident. 

I just wanted them to make sure she did not have a concussion, do a couple of scans and let us go. The nurses varied from caring to apathetic. 

I have not received any sort of counseling after the accident.
name: Lauren

text:
Absolutely terrible. 

The floors were dirty, counter tops and menus were sticky and other surfaces were dusty. 

First they served my father Diet Coke instead of Regular Coke. The server got the soda from another machine and it was still Diet and not Regular. He said they must've ran out.

My brother ordered the Sampler and the Salad Bar. He was told they had Chicken and Rice soup, but they did not. His Sampler looked like old, stale, frozen stuff.. none of which looked edible. The Sampler was supposed to include jalapeño poppers, but it did not, instead they gave him two chicken nuggets. They never said they were out, they just gave him those instead and served it that way. 

I tried to keep things safe by getting the 2 hot dogs and fries. The fries were okay, albeit there was a small portion, but the hot dogs tasted kinda odd, almost sour. I only ate one and left the other. 

When checking out, they charged us the full salad bar price for my brother when it was supposed to be half off with a meal. But seeing as he returned the meal for it being disgusting, they upped the price of the salad back to full price. He didn't even get soup with it because they didn't have the soup they told him they had when ordering. 

Avoid this place, it was a huge waste of money.

text:
Philadelphia tomato pie in Delaware? You bet! Searched for "tomato pie" as I was leaving Middletown DE and saw many good reviews for Tony's. Ordered the square tomato pie and WOW! Really, really good. The crust is crispy on bottom with well done edges. The sauce is closer in flavor to pizza sauce than the Philly bakery sauces, which are thicker, richer and a bit sweeter. This is not to   knock Tony's sauce,  as I found it to be a delicious take on my favorite pie and am already looking forward to having it again. The top was covered with loads of minced garlic. Just fantastic. I would guess their pizzas are great. 
I mentioned that I found them on Yelp, and was given a free cannoli. Super freakin' good! The owner told me they're made fresh everyday without all the sugars others use. My wife and I shared it on the way back to Jersey and nearly turned back for another. Very friendly owner. Locals filled the place on the Saturday we visited.

The kimchi stew that costs about 14 dollars is the biggest ripoff I've ever seen. I would never recommend it. It had some kimchi (not even the right type for stews), a few pieces of tofu, and almost no pork at all. 

Based on the bibimbop alone I would say 3-4 stars (def better places out there in the city). The stew definitely makes me give them a solid 2. Price wise for the food, I would say it's a bit too pricey for the content and flavors you get.

text: This place is amazing! The service is great. The owner is very nice and makes time to talk to customers. The food is delicious. I love the onigiri and the Mt Fuji Don is on point as well. The seaweed salad is light and very good for before or after your onigiri or even the Raman. The Raman is nice in flavor a rich broth taste great as well. Thank you guys I can't wait to go back.
name: Richard

text: We live in Chicago - the city, so happily have an abundance of wonderful sushi. BaiKu did not disappoint. We loved it and have eaten here every time we are in St. Louis. The specials are unique and always a scrumptious delight. The space is comfortable and chic.
name: Maria

text: Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, tho the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. Worth checking out. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish.
name: User

text: Had brunch here over the weekend and it was kind of a mixed bag. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. Food was fresh and service was quick. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Overall, a strong experience. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really.
name: User

text: I would give it 5 stars--the grits, eggs, greens, peanut salad with salsa was one of the best breakfasts I've ever had. But my husband's sausage muffin was equally atrocious (he said he could have made it better or gotten something equal at McDonalds). So if you go here, go for the adventurous food, and you won't be disappointed. Kitschy decor is not my taste, but probably fun for some.
name: Selena

text: I love the fajitas at verde. This is our Friday night family dinner place. Great models on tap. Fast service and yummy guacamole.
name: Candace

text: Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. By the time the food came out I was already annoyed. No big complaints, just a nice meal. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. They were out of one thing I originally wanted..
name: User

text: Really strong heavy roasted coffee, delicious breakfast (eggs over avocado dish with pico and pancakess), fast service even during a 20 minute wait!
name: Dr. Jason

text: Best huevos rancheros I have had. Staff is very attentive and nice. My husband had one of the skillet dishes and really and blueberry pancakes and like them as well. The only reason I didn't give it five stars was because my hash browns and chorizo were mediocre at best.
name: Leigh

text:
Stopped in for lunch, had a great meal. In a strip mall near the Towne Square shopping center, they had private rooms as well as the normal eating area. We found a lunch special that was amazing - soup, salad, a combination of sushi and sashimi, as well as something OTHER than a traditional california roll (eel avocado roll).

Our nephew from Florida had a similar special, but his roll was a dynamite roll with spicy salmon.

They also had no problems substituting whitefish for ebi given my wife has a shrimp allergy.

Although we didn't have any dinner items, the lunch impressed us enough to ask for a take out menu which we are looking at to decide what to get when we go back!
name: Dan

text: I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. It was crowded but still moved along. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. The staff seemed tired but still polite. Definitely coming back. Food was fresh and service was quick. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly.
name: User

text:
Came in for lunch on a Tuesday and were basically the only guests in the restaurant.  The space was really cool, and the service was good.  We had:
- Complimentary biscuits (4/5) - Soft, moist biscuits served with two really delicious butters.
- Melon and coconut soup (4/5) - Really light and refreshing.
- Hot fire chicken (4/5) - Really juicy chicken with an extremely flavorful sauce that was hot enough to make you feel it, but not so hot as to cover up the other flavors.  Very tasty.
- Curried goat (3/5) - Only had a few bites off my girlfriend's plate.  Felt like maybe this dish was under salted for us on this day.  There seemed to be lots of flavors that were hiding under the surface that just didn't pop out without the salt.
name: Simon

text:
To be honest I wanted to like this place because it's one of the few places we've found in this area that doesn't have pounding music. However the experience was not great. It took 45 minutes for oyster appetizers to be brought out. When they were finally brought out, half the trays had no sauces. We had to ask for crackers twice.No drink refills were offered despite empty glasses for more than an hour. Our server disappeared for long stretches of time.

Honestly this was incredibly disappointing. When you serve food at this particular price point, there ought to be better service. It should not take two hours for the food to come out. We should not go more than an hour waiting for a drink refill.

When we got our food, it came in three sessions. My crab cake was room temperature. We'd been waiting for two hours at that point. Paid the server cash and didn't get my change.
name: Morgan

text: We were so excited to come here for Sunday brunch and we left super underwhelmed. I'm a huge fan of their other restaurants and Barbuzzo is always a fav, but it wasn't the case here. For starters, I ordered the Mangolada and it tasted like a watered down mango seltzer. Did they forget the alcohol and mango puree? The "warm" pecan roll was room temp and nothing special. The korean bacon was a lazy attempt...literally just bacon with gochuchang on top. And not to mention two slices of bacon for $6.The chilaquiles were underwhelming and bland. Maybe we were there on an off day but we won't be returning any time soon.
name: Mel

text:
4/5 for the baked goods, 3/5 for ambiance

I was in Nashville, and was hoping for an amazing breakfast kolache before a long day of walking around. Honestly, the best thing on the menu that day was the brisket biscuit which is a biscuit sandwich with brisket, cheese, and some other stuff. It was so great and only $1. 

The other baked goods were okay as well. The cinnamon bun is HUGE, and the kolache's are good as well. The cherry one is a little artificial tasting because of the topping, but the bread part itself was good. 

The coffee was good, but on the pricy side. Would come back but not to eat there- defiantly to take home and eat.
name: Giselle

text: You are in Reno and this is the best sushi you can get. Fish tastes fresh although I wish they have more sophisticated rolls. We come here often and the wait, when there is one, isn't too bad. Mountain and Samurai rolls are amazing and you can't go wrong with your favorite nigiri.
name: Flavia

text: Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Food was fresh and service was quick. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Not bad for a quick meal. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. For the price I expected more than this.
name: User

text: King's Wok!  First, they're open on Mondays which is handy while many restaurants close shop.  This place may lack ambience, but who cares -- the food is excellent.  I ordered Kung Pow Chicken for myself and Sesame Chicken for my mother, who proclaimed, without prompting, "this is the best Sesame Chicken I've ever had," which says a lot coming from a world-traveled woman in her 80's.  We also ordered their egg rolls and chicken potstickers; everything was delicious.  Oh, and when I was in the restaurant ordering our food to go, a customer was talking about how much she and her co-workers love one of their broccoli dishes -- so I am clearly not alone with my big thumb up for this establishment.  If you have a hankering for Chinese food, give King Wok a try!  You won't regret it!
name: Steve

text:
Will be back to try more cause we tried the Browned Butter Gnocchi & lost our appetite.  It was greasy & drowning in flavorless butter believe it or not.  No hint of sage or anything described.  

Our bartender was ok, not too helpful just agreeable as though she never tried the menu before.  That's fine just be honest.  We saw the table side Bananas Flambe or Fosters & she said we don't usually do that, but if you go to the Palace Cafe they do it.  Ok.  So we did.

Ambience nice & opened, but dark lighting.
name: Poco

text: Diner food. Not pricy. Clean pleasant. Plenty of options. Better than a drive thru or fast food. No complaints.
name: Julie

text: Yelp lies! This place opens at 4! Just sayin. Fix that Yelp! Good spot though! Great pizza! Great wine/drinks/beer selection.
name: LaLaLa Lynda

text: Grease is beyond amazing. That brown sauce is think and over ladled on every dish. You will die of heart attack eating here too much. Service is gruff too.
name: J

text:
We came here for lunch on a Thursday.

Tip: make a reservation because it fills up fast.

The restaurant is a gorgeous old house turned restaurant in the heart of the historic garden district. There is a dress code so no shorts, jeans, or sandals.

The restaurant has several rooms spread out over two floors to dine in. Ask to sit upstairs in the tree room. It has floor to ceiling windows with views of the surrounding oak trees.

The lunch menu had a la carte options as well as three course menus. I had the eat fit NOLA three course menu which included butternut squash, grilled pompadour, and strawberry shortcake. I enjoyed every bite.

The lunch menu also includes a selection of 25 cent martinis. There is a limit of three per customer.

If you are celebrating a special occasion let the reservation line know. It was my mother and I's birthdays and we were greeted with balloons at our table, a dessert presentation with candles, and chefs hats.

You must try this classic New Orleans restaurant.
name: Becky

text: Terrible customer service. Food is hit or miss depending on if the owner is present at the time.
name: Steve

text: I enjoyed my first time at Kona Grill. I went for a birthday party with about 35 guest. They were able to accommodate seating for everyone. All of our food came out at the same time and was hot. I had a Kona Mai Tai to drink which was delicious. I ordered a dish with flank steak that was really good. I will definitely go back
name: Octavia

text:
Given my own budget, Hedge Row will probably always live in the realm of the occasional cocktail and the cheaper lunch menu. But even in that limitation, man oh man was I impressed. 

First of all, they have the sickest jams raining down over you while you eat and drink. From 90's hip-hop to down tempo international lounge music to some remixes and covers I'd never heard before, everything seemed curated to perfection. I rarely find the soundtrack of a restaurant much augmentation to the experience, but it was definitely true here.

Second, the mixologists are incredible. I have literally never used the word mixologist to describe a person who makes me a cocktail, by the way. But even with what seemed to be a somewhat shallow selection of liquors, they know how to improvise and keep it delicious. I came in on a cold and dreary afternoon groggy as anything, and not ready to down anything too boozy despite that being my usual taste. The barkeep improvised a coffee-based cocktail that I would love to replace my actual morning coffee. It was the tastiest, yet most understated and balanced coffee cocktail I've had, and they are really transparent with the process for folks interested in learning.

I just can't wait to actually be in the space on the patio on a warm day. It's tempting enough after an afternoon sample that I'll be back for dinner soon.
name: Ronak

text: I really enjoyed my visit at Mauhaus! I recommend booking ahead especially on the weekend because it can get very crowded in the afternoon! I feel like there were a lot of people at one time so it's hard to spend quality time with the cats. Many of the cats are not super friendly so they may run away and avoid being petted. Some people may find this boring because they would not be able to play and interact with the cats. You pay $10 per person for an hour inside with the cats plus one drink included so I think it's pretty reasonable. Their drinks were pretty good! Vietnamese iced coffee tasted very authentic. I met some wonderful cats today but so sad that I can't adopt any due to my living situation. I would come back again if I ever need a cat fix. 4 stars because it was too crowded on a Saturday!
name: Giang

text: Is it possible to ask customers for more tip? I really am unhappy about their behavior!
name: Linh

text:
Why 4 stars? Because they have freaking ice cream flights.

   ---   ---   ---

I was planning out a lunch nearby and noticed the amazing reviews at Micki's, so I added it to the itinerary for showing a couple of locals around the area. I had already stalked the menu online and knew that my decision on which flavor to go with would be extremely tough. The girl behind the counter offered for me to sample anything that looked interesting, but the problem was that they ALL looked interesting. And you don't want to be the guy who asks for 18 samples.

But then she uttered a sentence that nearly changed my life: "we have ice cream flights." 


Ice. Cream. Flights.

Hello, every owner of an ice cream shop in the free world. This is Brett. I've probably been to your business. I have a suggestion for you: offer ice cream flights. You'll make millions.

Sincerely,

A guy that's lactose intolerant but suffers through for the greater good.

Seriously... every ice cream shop needs to do this from now on. I enjoyed  Salted Caramel, Mango, Coconut, Bubble Gum and Cookies & Cream. My favorites were probably the cookies & cream and coconut. The salted caramel was pretty mild but the others were all tasty.

Next time I'm in the area craving sweets, I'm definitely coming back to Micki's.
name: Brett

text: Delicious muffins, breakfast sandwiches, smoothies.  Have not had a bad meal or drink from here.  Staff is wonderful- very friendly.   The seating fills up fast during prime time but other than that this place is great!
name: Katie

text:
This our second visit in the last two weeks-a good sign from us.  The food here is very good-higher quality than most AYCE places.  

They don't skimp on the rolls here-they are pretty big and the sticky rice is nice and moist.  There is a wide variety of appetizers and soups to get you started.  Dinner offers sashimi and other items not available at lunch.

The service is consistently good and the prices are reasonable.

Like the Terminator, I'll be back.
name: Jerry

text: Food took forever but ended up being better than I expected. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. I wouldn't write it off, but I also wouldn't hype it up. For the price I expected more than this.
name: User

text: I don't know what changed here but the last couple times I've came in.. the wait time has been insaaaane.  And all I'm getting is a classic combo.  Nothing special.    Less than two people ahead of me.    I used to love this quick stop on the way home... but now i think I'll drive a bit further
name: Audra

text:
After my typical indecisiveness, I settled on my gut based on the yelp reviews. The burlesque show made me skeptical of the food aspect but be assured; the food is  FIRE!  

First off, they had the nba playoffs on, so yes they have a TV. They have exceptional bourbon and craft drinks. The bartenders were outstanding personalities. Also very knowledgeable about bourbon. AJ and Brian were friendly and perfect guides for your culinary and cocktail journey. 

I ordered the rack of lamb and it was possibly the best I have had. The bartender told me they marinate it in a pomegranate glaze and then serve it with a sauce that you want to bathe in. I don't eat mashed potatoes often but these were served with Brussels and both were a perfect compliment. I ate the meat off the bone. 

I'm tired and happy so I'm going to bed. You should eat here and then feel the same.
name: Matthew

text: Seriously the chicken is wayyyyy better than bonchon! The chicken is so tender and juicy, also they have more options for the sauces. Really recommended!
name: Aurelia

text: Ordered the tall boy burger and received an ordinary burger.  The waitress asked if we wanted catchup or hot sauce which we asked for both.  I had to stop her 5 min later to request them. Then asked about which burger I received because no avocado was on basic. Which I asked the waitress to have them make it deconstructed or whatever because I'm gluten intolerant and eat no bun. She said they'd put the stuff to the side, so I know I ordered correctly and she said she heard basic.  Offered to recook, no thanks.  The burger was flavorless needed seasoning terribly bad, so did the tallboy tots.  The tots come with season salt on them, the red dye gives it away as a flavor.  The booth seat was saggy, the music blaring, the Arnold Palmer I ordered was lime juice with Icetea,,, fail!  Creativity and menu I give them a thumbs up, execution not so much.  Cleanliness things looked good, tables cleared and cleaned promptly. Silver was heavy sturdy stuff. Glasses nice and clean.  Plating was done well. Atmosphere needed a tune-up or turn down really.  Price was a bit much for what I got. I'm willing to spend the bucks on a non-fast food lunch but it needs to be higher caliber.  Not sure how I feel about a round 2.
name: Dean

text: Had an A-ok spur of the moment dinner at Dao's. Service was fast and friendly. Had some pho and a beef bell pepper dish along with some shrimp spring rolls. Probably won't be in my normal rotation, maybe again someday if I'm in a hurry for take out.
name: Paige

text:
10 large pretzels for $7
Small rivets box (nibblers) for $4

You can't beat the price, flavor and softness anywhere else. I visit the Philly Pretzel Factory every time I'm in PA. I've never had a bad batch, sometimes a bit too salty, but nothing that I can't rub off. Their spicy brown mustard and cheese dip are the way to go for dipping sauces. 

The next day, if you even have leftovers, you can reheat them in the microwave for 15-20 seconds to bring back the softness. 

I LOVE LOVE LOVE these soft pretzels.
name: Susan

text:
I ate at this restaurant today on the advice of a friend. 
It was fabulous. Water was served in halved recycled wine bottles. Nice touch. We shared several dishes. Flat bread pizza..just the right amount of seasoning and crunch.  The wood fired wings-I've never had better. Oversized, smoked and seasoned perfectly.  The dipping sauce was a bit too hot for my taste.
I didn't eat my burger because I was getting full.  But I had it later at home. Yummy.  And I like mine medium rare.  Lots of places it has to be cooked just a little pink or well done.  The side was truffled potatoes.  They were boiled small potatoes with a seasoned cream sauce drizzled on them. Way better than frozen French fries.
We had creme brulee for dessert.  It was caramelized just right with pistachio pieces and a ton of whipped cream. I want to say the staff was friendly and attentive. I was full; but have you ever been to a place that really satisfies?  This is it.
I only give it a 5 star because I can't give it any more!  Kudos..I'll be back for sure!
name: Karen

text: We appreciate the remodeling and felt right at home. There's a TV in every direction which we thought was a good idea. Our food was delicious as in the past!
name: Nancy

text:
Growler USA brings craft beer to you. With an extensive beer list, you can try multiple brews in your favorite style. It is amazing how different a beer can taste. The beer list has Untapped ratings to help narrow your selection. Our server was very knowledgeable about the options and steered us to several new finds. I thought it would be useful if there were bartender recommended flights to direct the selection process. (Yes, you can get overwhelmed in the selection process.) After finding a favorite, you can take more home in a growler for repeat enjoyment.

If you are out for the evening, Growler USA offers a full upscale bar menu, mostly burgers and sandwiches. Their version of a reuben was tasty. I wish there was more variety in the sides: tater totes and french fries.
name: Hart

text:
This is a great place to go on a Friday night when you want something yummy and filling! My go to meal is brown stew chicken. I always call in my order because they can get very busy. The longest I've waited was 25 mins. 

The food always tastes fresh and the workers are nice. 

The restaurant has sitting but not a lot, if you're looking to have a private conversation it can be loud and tight.
name: Jessica

text: Had brunch here over the weekend and it was kind of a mixed bag. It was crowded but still moved along. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated bc we didn't have a reservation. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Not sure though.
name: User

text: Food was fresh and service was quick. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Price felt a touch high for what it was. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didnt have a reservation. Will be back. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. The food was good and the service was easygoing.
name: User

text: It's been a while since i order from this place, so thought i would give it a try.  Ordered a sicilian pizza rustica - there crust is still one of the best however thicker than others.  Skimpy on the pepperoni - perhaps each of the 16 slices had one thin slice of pepperoni, the pie was bland in taste and barely had any sauce on it so was on the dry side.  Called and spoke with the man who made the pie, asked him where the sauce was and he said of you wanted extra sauce?  I said no i simply wanted sauce that should be on it lol....he said he put sauce on it - I said certainly not enough for the thickness of the crust.  So I guess if you order a sicilian pie, tell them to put enough sauce on it!  But again the taste was bland and while there were other toppings, the certainly skimp on the pepperoni - other toppings were roasted peppers sliced black olives and some green onion, chopped tomato.
name: robert

text: We drive 30 minutes for this delicious food! Dim Sum on Sunday is THE BEST IN TOWN! Running in Friday night for dins and it is soooo good!  The owners are AWESOME!
name: Niki

text: The cashier was friendly and helpful and the service was snappy. We got burgers with green chiles and cheese, onion rings and seasoned fries. All were delicious! I expect nothing less from Blake's.
name: Chelsea

text: Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. By the time the food came out I was already annoyed. Just not for me. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. For the price I expected more than this.
name: User

text: Had a late large filling meal with family for a weeknight birthday celebration . First time here , big booth, bear decor , big hearty comfort food meals. Had the pot roast very tender as the yelp reviews guided me. Others had small tri tip which was big ! The taco salad biggest I've ever seen papa beAr ate the whole thing! Baby bear had chocolate pancakes & milk. As seen on yelp signed up for bear club got free coffee & bearclaw! McKenzie our server was great very patient. Mike the manager very personable , Stephanie nice too! Thank you bear diner family we had fun & took home enough for meals tomorrow.
name: John

text: I like these guys quite a lot ! They're always nice and I'm a big fan of the Buffalo Shrimp Pizza. Their 2 Slice and a Drink for $7 is awesome if you're a fan of toppings ! Think about it, you could either get a slices of cheese or a Slice of Buffalo and Taco Pizza. If you want to explore toppings this deal is for you !
name: Lorenzo

text: The alligator dumplings with sauce were excellent. All the dishes had distinct flavors that really popped. Next door at The Butcher, they make a pastrami sandwich that really stands out. This is one of my favorite restaurants in the city.
name: Edward

text: Rude seating hostess, slow service, however huge menu with lots of options.  Would only recommend if you are not in a hurry and have lots of mouths to feed at a reasonable price.
name: Kinsey

text: A solid neighborhood Ethiopian restaurant. The vegetarian platter had all the basics (yellow lentils, red lentils, cabbage, greens, a little salad) all of which was not mind blowing but good. Our favorite parts were the sides of tofu (delicious!) and eggplant (also delicious! But more oily). We als tried the special full (Fava bean mush-like Dip) which interestingly seemed mostly like refried beans (perhaps to those who have never had them before) the paradise smoothie was ok - tasted mostly like strawberry.  The injera was good.
name: Sonali

text: This was one of my favorite breakfast places for starters....We came in for a late breakfast. The restaurant was semi busy but the server took a while to come over. We ordered an omelet and a hash brown dish and a pancake.  Both came out cold. My hash brown dish was a veggie style with minimum cheese and veggies. We were very disappointed in both dishes. Even the pancake was flakey and non fluffy. Just as I was saying I won't return the GM Marquita came over and spoke with us. I will say she is an asset to City Diner she handled our concern with a high level of professionalism. This did not include comping our check which I didn't expect (so this is not why I'm writing this review). After speaking to her I will be returning to City Diner one last time to try it! Thank you Marquita!
name: Rashelle

text: The food is fresh and good. The place needs to be freshen up a little bit, especially the bathroom. But overall, we enjoy the food and the service.
name: Han

text: I came here the past weekend on Saturday on MLK weekend. This was my second lunch (lol), so we did not order a lot. The waitlist was long when I came (around 1:30), but we were seated within minutes because our seating preference was outside. We ordered the uni plate ($21.50), clam chowder bowl, fried oysters, and oyster Rockefeller. The uni was meh to me. It lacked the oceany sweet taste it usually has. The lime made it taste bitter and the dark soy sauce tasting sauce it came with did not compliment it at all. For 21.50, you only get half an uni and six scallops. To me, the pieces were kind of small and overall not that worth it, but presentation looks good! Their clam chowder was eh as well too. It had nice flavor and wasn't too thick, but it was bland and needed more salt. I also wish it came with bread. The oyster rockefellers were good, the flavor was nice. The real star in our meal were the fried oysters. I was presently surprised by how big they were! They were super fat and still had the nice oceany oyster flavor in them! They were fried a bit too much, but they were lovely. For the price, it was the most worth it item that we got. Came with 6 and was around $14 I believe. Overall, my experience here wasn't bad and I would come back to try their pastas because they seem like a good deal and good. Till next time.
name: amy

text: Uuugh first time in Mt. Holly and this place had really good reviews so decided to check it out. We were seated and then ignored for a solid ten minutes before I asked hostess if someone could take our drink order. Our waitress came over and she was friendly enough....and apologetic. We ordered our drinks and our food. After waiting a longtime for our food - my medium burger with sweet potato fries came out very much later well done with regular fries. Even if it were done properly the patty of meat was disappointingly small considering it cost $13.  I said that I would eat it anyway as we were going to the theatre and I didn't want to waste food or wait another 15 minutes for my burger while I watched my friends eat their food. The waitress was apologetic and told us that she took it off the bill. Upon getting the check at the end of the meal it was marked as "staff meal" with a 50% discount. I don't know why you would say you are taking it off the bill and then discount it 50%.  I loved the two drinks that I got and I think imbibing them allowed me to have a pleasant time despite a disappointing burger.
name: Gwendolyn

text: We love chargrilled oysters! This place definitely has the best in NOLA .  Don't miss out on getting these!
name: Melissa

text:
My boyfriend and I attempted to go to ms. Tootsies. When we arrived no one was at the hostess station outside so we went inside. When we arrived inside we walked to the back where we thought there was mother hostess station. The bartender yells over to us " y'all want a table " we reply yes and she walks back
Outside puts our name on the list , and we wait. Moments later another hostess comes out and immediately starts talking to a young man who just came outside after eating and they start to exchange numbers and ask about calling one another later and about instagram etc... this is all while people are waiting to
Be seated. She then says oh it's a 30 minute wait , meanwhile we have been waiting for 20. Needless to say we did not eat there. This Resturant is a Philadelphia stable but it has awful customer service and I will never ever eat her or attempt to ever again. What a awful experience.
name: Chrissy

text: Excellent service for grocery pick up. Meat and produce are always fresh. And employees are happy and helpful.
name: Marcie

text: The service here is inexplicably slow. I like the location and their food is fine but waited for 20 minutes for 2 to-go bagels on a day when it wasn't particularly crowded. If I'd known it would take so long I would've skipped it. Don't come here if you're in a hurry.
name: Liz

text:
I'm in love with this place. I love knowing that anything I choose will be delicious. I love the limited choices because I'm so indecisive. This was my favorite dining experience in a long time. Our sweet waitress brought some hummus and olives to the table. It was tasty. Clam chowder- broth base, lots of clams, excellent flavor. Spicy mussels...this was my favorite.  The spicy broth and tender mussels were a party in my mouth. You just keep wanting more. Beautiful crusty bread to dip in the broth...I was seriously in heaven. Poached oysters...never tried such a dish. The oysters were soft, almost melting in your mouth. They were very good, resting in a curry, coconut milk sauce with fresh cilantro. The flavor is unique and yummy. Last came the fish dishes. We had the grouper and the marlin. Both were delicious. The grouper had a tasty black pepper seasoning on it. It was accompanied by a little salad concoction with cucumber and carrot in a delicious viniagrette. Some vegetables were also on the plate..a creative mix of a grain, plus paper thin zucchini and other yummy tidbits. 
The presentation and creativity is wonderful...everything was top notch. The service was excellent. By the time we left, we felt like we knew everyone. Our waitress called us by name...just so impressed with everything. Chef Frank, will you marry me?  See you again soon!

text:

text: I've been going here for a long time - it was a favorite spot in graduate school. I have to say, of all the things on the menu, my favorites are the tomato soup, a build your own sandwich and their amazing Mac and cheese. On the latter, I always add jalapeños in and it's SO worth it. It's baked with the little crumbles on top and just the perfect portion. The salads are fresh and made to order right in front of you and they have just about every topping you could think of or want. They also have one of the modern soda machines with tons of flavors but the real treat is their lemonade, which is fresh! Service is always friendly and helpful and they will help you out with to go boxes if you can't finish your giant salad. Lastly, I highly recommend getting a brownie. They are fresh baked, soft, and absolutely delicious. I always take one to go. The only thing I will say is that your meal can get into the pricey side if you're adding a lot of toppings or want a soup and a create your own sandwich so keep that in mind if you're on a budget.

He got everything in my order right and then when I picked it up he showed me everything was there which was reassuring. It's small but he asked if I wanted utensils which not a lot of people do, so that make an impact on me. The food was great for the price and the crab puffs are my favorite! The amount of fortune cookies for the amount of food seemed a little excessive but we'll save those for a later date haha!

text:
Came here on a Monday night and the place was sparingly occupied. We ordered A LOT of food, so much that it would be better to rate each dish separately.

Roti Canai: Although it's one of their highly recommended dishes, I found the dish rather disappointing. The Roti itself was a litte too doughy and thick for my liking. I was expecting something a little crispier and more buttery. The chicken curry that came with the roti was also too salty and heavy (2/5)

Roti Telmur: A variation from the Roti Canai, this dish also consisted of roti but was stuffed with egg and red onion. I liked this dish a little more than the Roti Canai because of it's slightly more complex than the Roti Canai. The curry was the same as the one that came with the Roti Canai. Again, the Roti could have been crispier and more buttery (3/5)

Mee Siam: Thin rice noodles stir-fried with peanut, egg, chicken, fried tofu, and sweet tamarind. The flavor came together rather well, despite it being slightly too sweet. The fried tofu was a good addition, offering a change in texture that balances out other creamier components (3.5/5)

Beef and Chicken Satay: Well-cooked beef and chicken skewered with wooden sticks on a bed of cucumbers and red onions. The peanut sauce was very balanced, creamy, nutty, and overall very flavorful (4/5)

Tang Tang Belakan: Morning glory stir-fry with sambal (shrimp paste). The morning glory was overcookef and the sambal was overpowering; nothing outstanding (2.5/5)

Short Ribs: Deep fried Marinated/Pickled short ribs. The sourness of the marinate really came through and threw me off a little. I also think it would have been better to use a smaller cut of rib, something with smaller bones and more meat to make the meat standout more and easier to eat (2.5/5)

Bean Sprouts: Bean sprouts stir-fried with soy sauce. Again, nothing spectacular. Somewhat oily and salty. This dish may have been more interesting as a cold appetizer(?) and with a little more sweetness.

Oyster Omlette: There was a fair amount of oyster dispersed throughout the omlette. The dish was again salty; the sweet chilli sauce was a necessity to balance the omlette. Fluffy and soft, the dish was decent (3/5)

Coconut Jumbo Shrimp: Deep-fried battered jumbo shrimp on a bed of fried coconut shaving and rice noodles. I didn't know what to expect of this dish and was taken back by how massive it was; although it was mainly because the shrimps were thickly coated with batter. The batter casing was somewhat crispy, but full of oil. The whole dish had too many oily components, in my opinion, and could have been tied together better with something fresh or a sauce. The sweetness of the coconut did help with the flavor of the dish (4/5)

Overall, the place offers a wide range of South East Asian food. However, the taste of the dishes do vary greatly. On the other hand, the staffs were attentive and helpful. For me, the place was not horrible but average and doesn't standout in terms of their execution of the food.
name: Ploy

text:
Some friends and I decided last minute to grab breakfast together on a Saturday morning. We called breakfast places in the area to see if they could accommodate 6 of us around 11:30, and Turning Point ensured they could. So that basically made our decision for us.

When we were there on that Saturday morning, it was oddly not busy. We didn't even need our reservation. We were sat quickly, however after that the service was much slower. Our waitress gave us more time after we didn't know what we were ordering when she first stopped by. But she gave us almost too much time, leaving us antsy and a little confused as to when she would come back. 

Our food came out in a normal amount of time though. Usually I am not a breakfast sandwich girl but for some reason it was calling my name that morning. I got the Classic Pork Roll Sammy with a side salad. The presentation is pretty poor but I thought my food was decent. The salad dressing was not evenly mixed but that was something I could take care of. I was pleased with my decision to get the salad over the potatoes as the side because my friend's potatoes didn't look crispy or seasoned. My dish was pretty inexpensive too.

The waitress was kind to split up out checks at the end and did not rush us out. I was satisfied with my breakfast but I also believe there may be more unique options for brunch on the mainline.

text:

For me, the Seafood Ceviche, although good, was a little disappointing as was the unusual Deep Fried Duck Leg which, served on a hot dog roll, seemed to be ground meat mixed with spices inside some kind of casing.

text:
The Basics: Sacred Pepper is a restaurant located in North Tampa. The restaurant has a beautiful interior with big, comfortable cushioned seats and modern decor. There is a large bar and a large seating area with many tables. Reservations can be made online and there is plenty of parking. Sacred Pepper has a big menu with a wide array of items to choose from. Thoroughly enjoyed my meal here! 

Things I like: I enjoyed every part of my meal. We started with the Sacred Meatballs, which included three large meatballs and two pieces of bread. A great appetizer to start off with. I then ordered the Veal Milanese which I truly enjoyed. It tasted very fresh and was delicious. I finished my meal with the Creme Brulee Bread Pudding, which I would highly suggest! The ice cream with it was homemade and the bread pudding was great. 

Things I didn't like: The service was a bit too fast and I wish we had some more time between courses. We felt a bit rushed. Also, I thought the Bellini Bliss cocktail was a tad too sweet for my taste. Other than that, loved my time here! 

Overall, Sacred Pepper is a great addition to the food scene in North Tampa! A great place to stop in for a good meal in a beautiful atmosphere!
name: Lauren

text:
Stopped here for the Jazz Brunch, one thing to note is that there are only three things on the Jazz Brunch menu (breakfast may be different but for the Jazz Brunch it is minimal). 

Service - Amazing! 

However, I ordered the Crab Cake Benedict. It was very good but unfortunately had a lot of pieces of the shell in it. Although I can understand having some pieces, this was to the point that each bite was crunchy...

When I sent it back the waitress handled it with a great attitude and offered to get me a new plate of it. I did however ask if that would be from the same "batch" as my first one. She went and asked in the back and came to tell me it would be from the same one. I declined a new plate, unfortunately, because I don't know how it could have been any better. I am a little concerned about the fact that they were perfectly fine continuing to serve the cakes after getting this feedback? 

Overall, I was very disappointed to have this experience because the atmosphere was gorgeous and the waitresses that we had were phenomenal. Unfortunately, you can have all these things and if your food is sub par people will not come back. And I don't recommend that you go there to begin with because of this.

text: Bought the new mini cheesesteak bites, and they were raw inside. Actually stretchy, raw, not fully cooked, pretzel dough. I threw them out because I didn't feel like risking food poisoning. Not really planning on going back anytime soon.

text:
Good grief people.  What is the hype about???  As I am writing this review, I am thinking that 2 stars might be too generous.  Let's start at the beginning.

We had reservations for four people at 8:15pm on a Friday night.  We got there, it's busy.  We were given one of those light-up buzzer things like what they give you at a TGI Fridays.  There are much more discreet ways of letting people know their table is ready.  We were just at Nashville Biscuit House (divey restaurant) and even they had the texting technology.  Anyways, we took our light up buzzer thing and got a drink at the bar.

While we waited for our table, my friend and I made a stop in the restroom.  Out of toilet paper.  Obviously nobody is checking the status of the restrooms while it is busy.  Gross.

We were finally seated and then we waited.  And waited.  And waited.  Our server was nowhere to be found.  Turns out, he had a big table next to us that got all of his attention.  That's nice.  I will say that our server was a very nice person who was able to answer all of our questions about the menu.  But that's about it.  He was one of the least attentive servers I have had in recent memory.  

Our food (appetizers and entrees) took forever to come out.

Our table ordered the smoked oysters and the biscuits as a starter.  The oysters were good--fatty, rich and briny.  The crispy pig ear on top was really good.

I ordered the trout.  The menu says that the entrees come with mashed potatoes.  The server did not say that the mashed potatoes come in one little bowl for the table.   They were very creamy and buttery but not hot enough for me.  If you are going to serve mashed potatoes, they can't be room temperature.  My trout was okay--really salted down the middle of the fish and the two sides had zero flavor.  Strange.  I asked for salt and pepper (not on the table which is annoying to me) and was given The Look for asking.  

My fiance ordered the fried chicken and said it was not that good--lacking flavor were his words.  My friend ordered the beer can chicken and said that her chicken was really good.  Her boyfriend ordered the Mixed Grill which he let us try.  The venison really did not have any seasoning.  I had been thinking about getting the venison and was glad I had not ordered it.

We topped of the meal with a Boozy Brownie which three of us shared.  It was your basic brownie with a scoop of ice cream on top.  I did not think it was anything special.

Overall, I was just not impressed.  Oh and I forgot to add that while we were waiting and waiting and waiting, a group of four was seated next to us.  No joke--they had food on their table almost immediately.  They were obviously VIPs of some sort to the restaurant because their service was way better than ours.  

That's fine.  We will take our money and spend it elsewhere.
name: Angela

text:

text:
I've had more good experiences than off situations at the various to Coras. I do recommend that it's always good to arrive earlier than you think you should to get a table, especially if you're more than 2 or are wanting a booth over a table. As it's been mentioned, the waiting area is a bit of a difficult space to stand but it's been awhile since I've had to wait outside due to a longer line up. There was even someone today (5 people after me on the list) and I was glad to see everyone make space for the wheelchair to make it to the front of the line and inside of the restaurant vs force them to wait outside (yay for good human beings today!).

No matter how busy and crazy the front end is, my group of 4 or more always gets well taken care of. Be it with one or more servers (sometimes we choose earlier or later times in hopes that we'll get seated quicker so that means shift changes too). Yes, the restaurant is loud but it does absorb enough that it's not too intense having a mixture of families with little ones and larger groups. Even with a larger group, food arrives in a decent time. Sometimes you do need to remind them of items that you ordered to come with the meal but I see that more often when multiple people are trying to help a table (so I totally get that happening and always gets quickly fixed). 

Every once in awhile I try their featured blended drinks but usually the orange juice is my option. I would not recommend the coffee if you're part of the elite coffee drinkers. However, if you're looking for a jolt of caffeine, it works. Today the three of my brunch friends all seemed to enjoy their coffee (and had refills) with enough cream and sugar added. 

Fruit is a hit and but some fruit items are a miss (mostly due to my preference). Today the kiwis were harder than I would prefer to eat (that made me sad) and I ended up giving them along with the cantaloupe and honeymoon (that is always over dominant on the plate) to a friend that enjoys them much more than I do. I'm aware asking for specific fruit (so less of a mixture) can lead to extra cost. So I usually offer my less liked fruit to others at my table and everyone wins. 

Depending on the waitress, when I order my potatoes with my standard favourite Sunshine panini- crepe awesomeness, I get asked if I want to replace the fruit with potatoes (fair choice to not get charged more), some offer half fruit (which is my preference as I do like fruit but really depends on the day if there's an extra charge to that option) or like today, I ended up with a full side of fruit and a full side of potatoes. My bad for not double checking on that before she rushed away to enter our table's order. So I happily consumed my extra potatoes with my hollandaise sauce (yes that's an extra to that dish) and pushed that stomach limit but it was worth it. Summary, when knowing that inconsistency happens (not just between restaurants but at the same location too) just be aware to ask if there's extra charges. Or go in knowing you'll most likely have extra charges if you do like I did today and didn't clarify what I was asking for when I was ordering. That being said, I think it's reasonable to add an extra fee if you're adding more to the meal.

Everyone was happy with their meals and the amount of food is always more than a fair size. Nice plus that there's more than enough surrounding parking options due to other restaurants and businesses, so it allows us to meet in a reasonable location for our larger group gatherings.
name: Laura

text:

I went basic for my first time, mostly because thinking when hangry is hard. Their Anna Wintour My Way pizza is a build your own. I just kept it simple with tomato garlic sauce and skim cheese. My pizza actually had a rise tonite, most GF and cauliflower pizzas are thin crust with no rise. This one was soft, perfectly cooked and oh so flavorful! 

I am so glad I stumbled upon this place. Best GF pizza I've had in a very long time. I'm sad I live like 10 states away, but if I am back in Tampa again, this is a must! And yes, it's a bit pricey but the size is enough for two people and all GF is more expensive, that's the reality!

text:
This was my first visit to Chili Szechuan since its relocation from Baltimore Avenue in West Philly.  It is certainly larger than before, and its booths and dark tones, more cozy than before. It has always offered authentic Szechuan spicy cuisine from Chongqing, China, but now it even adds the reality of many restaurants especially in the northern climes, of being chilly temperature-wise in winter.  We appreciated the cultural use of cold weather and wore our coats during the meal in honor of the reminiscent freeze in the house. Brrrr....

The food was as good as before. Spicy Lamb Chops, Szechuan Chili Sauce Fish Fillets, Eggplant in Garlic Sauce and Crispy Shrimp - Sweet & Sour, were our choices. They were all good to great, although our waiter admitted that even on the non-Americanized menu, they cut the heat for a western customer. So, even though we were mostly Chinese at the table, we all suffered through reduced burn and numbness. Next time, we will insist on the full monty fire treatment. We can all handle it!

The dishes arrived as prepared by the kitchen, and not all at once. Thus, the spicy lamb chops made the first impression of the night. They were excellent; with enough cumin and pepper to heat the tongue and gums, but not anesthetize them. Fun finger food.  Next came the eggplant in garlic sauce.  It, too, was a strong contender, with plenty of Chinese nightshade and a thick, rich dark amber coat. It could have been hotter, as the innate sweetness of the veggie dominated the other flavors, and needed more competition from Szechuan chilies. The shrimp was delivered next.  It was good, with 10 jumbos in an orange glaze. However, it was far more sweet than sour, and suffered most from Americanization syndrome. It really needed a blast from the smelter to bring out its hidden attributes. Finally, the Szechuan chili sauce fish fillets arrived in a deep dish to accommodate the soupy red hot bath it cooked in.  This dish was excellent and packed the most punch.  Tender pieces of boneless flounder is a beautiful orange/red conglomerated hot liquid.  Finally, a little numbness!

We passed on their dessert options, as they were not Chinese, and all came from an outside vendor.  The hot tea was from a non-descript bag, rather than loose pack.  Not so good. 

Overall, Chili Szechuan was a worthwhile trip on a cold winter night, yet it would do itself a favor by fixing the heating equipment, not making assumptions about "round eyes," and upgrading their tea choices. While these are mostly secondary considerations, they do detract from the experience.  As such, it really can't compare holistically to Han Dynasty or the other Hot Houses in Philly, where those details mean something.
