text:
I found this spot who had some interesting sushi rolls. So, we went over to check it out. With the wall facing the street being all windows, the inside was flooded with natural light. They had a quite large sushi and bar counter in the middle, with seating all around it. They also had small two-person booth seating on the side as well. Very clean decor, I am glad they didn't put up any kind of cheap or fake Asian "artworks" on the wall.

We ordered an appetizer and side dish to go with our sushi rolls. We chose Creamy Rock Shrimp, Lobster Fried Rice, Sindy Roll and Old City Roll. All in all, they were all very tasty, high quality and we enjoyed them very much. Yes, everything was perfect until we ordered some desserts... 

Since they didn't have a dessert menu, we ordered Tree Cake and Green Tea Cheesecake based on the description of the dessert that our waitress gave us. 

This so-called Tree Cake...I call it "rip-off" cake. Our waitress described it as a cake made with almond, egg and butter. When it came out, I was shocked what it really was... If you are familiar with a common and popular sweets in Japan, one of them is called Baumkuchen which is actually a German layered cake. They can be purchased from most bakeries and stores, and not so pricey unless you go to some fancy boutique to get it. The cake we were presented with, in my opinion, was store-bought, and sliced as thinly as possible. For $10, you can buy an entire cake!!! Very disappointing... And on top of that, it was dry (with these thin slices being cut off from the cake, I wonder how long it has been since the cake was first purchased?). And if that is not enough, we were given spoons to eat this...why? I don't know...

Our waitress was very friendly and polite, and we were well taken care of. Everything we had, other than the Tree Cake was great. High quality and tasty, a bit on pricey side, but that comes with the quality. I wish if we made a different choice with the dessert. But then, you live and you learn. If you go there, avoid the tree cake!
name: June

text: This place is beyond amazing!! We came in on a whim and were pleasantly surprised!!! The gentleman behind the counter was so nice and explained how to work the menu which was so easy. You pick everything you want, from the meat to the cheese, toppings, sauce, everything!!! They had a wide variety of different meats. Chicken as well as vegan!! I got the normal chuck and for someone that doesn't eat many burgers anymore!! This thing was huge and juicy and had amazing flavor. I got cooper cheese on mine and it went so well with the burger perfectly melted and the special sauce is to die for!!! I love how they have shredded lettuce too not a huge rib of lettuce!!! We also got the hand cut fries with the BBQ cherry sauce that they make in store!!! All I have to say is I licked the container!!! It was amazing!!! Don't waste any time!!! You have to check this place out!!! The staff is so friendly and the place is so cute! We will be going back again! It was so good I forgot to take pictures to post!!!

text: I love this restaurant. The food is absolutely delicious. Hospitable, very warm welcome every time I visit! If you're in the south jersey area  this is thee premier place to go for authentic Caribbean food! Take it from a tough critic! The owner and staff are always professional. Their food oozes flavor! And they're always generous with the portion size..   ---- Gary M.

text: D'Floret is my favorite restaurant, hands down. The food is absolutely phenomenal. Denis is a genius. The flavors and textures in his food are incredible. Being able to see him prepare all of the food fresh and right in front of you is a wonderful experience. I love that it's a small and intimate restaurant. Estella runs the front of house and she is an exceptional hostess. She welcomes everyone with a warm smile, and all of the staff feel like they are a part of the family. They are accommodating and welcoming, and the food is second to none. I will continue to come here for years to come. My small children agree that this is their favorite restaurant as well. It is the perfect place to come with friends on a double date, to go with your family for a special celebration, or just to go with your significant other for a meal that will blow you away consistently every time. I cannot recommend it highly enough!

text: Went with family on a Sunday and it was louder than I expected. Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Food was fresh and service was quick. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. A very pleasant experience. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. For the price I expected more than this.

Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..

text: This was a great place for...one of the most welcoming bartenders (Collin) we have had on New Orleans. The bar was very laid back and the food was good.
name: Tony

text:
I've gone to Alibaba's more than a handful of times throughout the years and always enjoyed it. I always defended this place when I heard people giving it flack, but no, no sir. Not anymore. 

My last time going there I took my friend who had never been there before. I'm not a picky eater and I am generally very forgiving and easy to please. I can honestly say this was THE WORST MEAL I HAVE EVER PAID FOR. No kidding, this place would make a great candidate for an episode of Kitchen Nightmares. 

When we got there, the first thing I noticed was that the place was completely empty--no one else was eating there. To add to that feeling of emptiness, there was no music playing. You could literally hear a pin drop. This would later magnify the awkwardness of my friend and I listening to each other trying to choke down our food. 

When we got in, a young man at the front told us that our server would soon be coming. When he finally did come out from the back, which was over ten minutes later, he seemed standoffish. I wouldn't say "rude", but he didn't seem very engaged whatsoever. 

We ordered an appetizer to share; I ordered a lamb gyro with fries, and my friend ordered some kind of lamb entree with a side of rice. 

After waiting in the empty restaurant for over 30 minutes, during which time our "waiter" was arguing with someone on the phone, we finally received our food. I noticed they had not given me fries and instead gave us both the "Saffron Rice". I didn't want to raise a big stink about it, so I just kept the rice. Our waiter told us the rice was kind of "spicy". This rice was more plain than cooked brown rice, but completely bland and not as good. It tasted like it came from a box. No veggies, no seasonings. There was no saffron to speak of. 

I took one bite of the appetizer, which supposedly was made with lamb, and almost threw up. It tasted literally like butthole, or like ground beef that had gone bad.

While my gyro was certainly large, the majority of it was lettuce and crusty pita bread (not naan). The pita bread was so stale I couldn't fold it into the form of a sandwich, so I had to eat it open face style--more like a tostada. The lamb meat itself was only a few pieces, which were charred black on the outside and leathery on the inside. It was so tough and over-cooked, it almost hurt my teeth to eat it. It was similar the texture of jerky and didn't remind me of anything like gyro meat. I began wondering if I had even been served what I ordered. 

I didn't try my friend's entree, but I can tell you it didn't look good. The meat was lamb, but was orange and looked more like chicken. My friend tends to be a fast eater and usually scarfs things down pretty quickly. He picked at that thing over the course dinner like a five-year-old mashes the food his mom made in hopes making it appear smaller, so as to make it more believable when he says "I ate". By the end of the meal I realized he had hardly eaten any of it. I already felt bad, but the worst was yet to come. 

We had already been finished eating and stacked our plates at the end of the table and were waiting for our waiter to come by to bring our check when a woman walks in, goes into the back of the restaurant, and begins yelling at our waiter. I approach the young man at the front to ask for the check, he says the waiter has to give it to us, so we continue listen to the two of them arguing for another 15 minutes. At this point I am theorizing that all the employees have quit or have been let go, and the only people working there are the owner, the lady who walked in (likely his wife), and the man in front (likely their son).

The lady finally comes out from the back and is holding the check with our waiter's writing on it. She says "let me go over this with you to make sure it is correct. I do not trust him." The check actually was correct (though the food was not) and we go to the counter to pay. As she's punching in the numbers, our waiter comes out, snatches the check from her hands, and tries to push her out of the way to enter the numbers himself. She yells at him, grabs the check back, he leaves. She repeats: "I do not trust him" and goes over the contents of our check, again. 

In all, we had been there for nearly two hours and paid $55 dollars for gross food. I recognize these are first world problems, but I felt very uneasy leaving on many levels. It was pretty disturbing. I was worried that we got swindled, wondering how many other people might have been swindled in the past, and terrified of the possibility that we might have food poisoning from that butthole meat. 

Alibaba's, I am very upset with you. I remember when your food was fresh and generous and the atmosphere was lively and charming. Perhaps there is a divorce underway that is causing you to become desperate? Just a bad day? I don't know, but cutting corners will not serve you, and I will not let it go unpunished. Get your shit together.
name: Trevor

text: Came here today for birthday brunch with my girls! I heard good things about Two Chicks and it did not disappoint although I would not recommend 11:00 on Sunday to arrive It was exactly the 45 minute wait they gave us At our table we had a chorizo omelette, bacon and eggs and the 2 choice Benedict which in this case was caprese and veggie. All of the food was very good. 4 stars is due to the food not being really hot when it arrived at the table which seemed odd as busy as it was.  Both of my friends had toast and it wasn't warm enough to melt the delicious strawberry butter. The Benedict's were lukewarmish. And, across the board, everything needed salt. None of us are saltaholics but it seemed salt or seasoning wasn't present. A nice dose of salt later and all was well. The restaurant is really cute, the coffee was very good and our server was prompt and friendly. I suppose we could have complained but having been a server for years in the past unless it's inedible it's not my style. We will be back but next time we will get our famines out of bed and come earlier or later
name: Suzie

text: The decor is very nice. The restaurant was very loud, difficult to have a conversation. Really wanted to like this place, unfortunately the service was very slow, lacked professionalism and the food was less than average. I hope they can improve in both the front and back of the house. It was a Saturday evening and several empty tables. It was a very expensive and disappointing dining experience!
name: Colleen

text: Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Not bad for a quick meal. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait.
name: User

text: What a GREAT place to eat. Fits into the Hipster trend going on with restaurants now, but that can't detract from the delicious pizza and appetizers. I would highly recommend.
name: Fred

text:
Sure the bagels are pretty good, but coming from CA/NY, I won't say it's particularly special. When you factor in the price ($5 for a bagel with cream cheese.....or even just $3 for one or the other), then it's really not worth it. And then when you consider how long you've spent waiting through the line, it's hard to leave not feeling a little ripped off for how much you've paid and how much time you've spent waiting for a "pretty good" bagel. 

I got the everything bagel with the rosemary garlic cream cheese. Still tasty, but they put a lot of cream cheese on even when we asked for it "light." I came in with a larger group, so we tried everything from the standalone bagels to multiple cream cheeses (bacon jalapeno's pretty good), to breakfast bagels and sweet potato mash. Lots of options is great, but I'd argue this place is a little too pricey for what is really is!
name: Cindy

text:
So yummy! Authentic and delicious food!!
There is a liquor store in the same shopping center so you can buy a bottle of wine as they do not sell alcohol. :)
name: Veronica

text:
The service was good and the food was okay, but my first time coming here I got FOOD POISONING from something that I ate during lunch yesterday afternoon. I can narrow it down to a few meals... the mango with white bread for desert (the yogurt tasted warm and like it was starting to spoil), the rice pudding, or the chicken tikka Marsala (which tasted like vodka sauce with chicken cubes).

Anyways, I got home, started prepping my meals for the week, suddenly got really nauseous. Ended up violently throwing up in my bathroom for about 4 hours and had to take the next day off from work. Still recovering from this place. I will have to report this incident. Man, I had high hopes for this place based on the reviews.
name: Edward

text: My friends and I decided to visit after we saw the churro ice cream pictures on Instagram. It's a really cute place and I love the vibes/decor/etc! My only concern was the churros itself lol. The waitress brought them out within 10 ish minutes, and then we spent maybe like 5 mins taking pics for insta cuz they looked cute or whateva. Now idk if they weren't made right or we waited too long to eat them buttttt the churros were crunchy. I tried to break a piece of the churro and the entire thing crumbled into a million pieces :////// The only soft part of the churro was the part that was sitting in the ice cream. As far as taste though, the tres leches was def the best flavor, but man I really wish the churros were softer. Oh well.

text: Great drinks, great bar specials, great service, great location! Walking distance to our hotel was a bonus. We will be back!

text: I've been here about 4-5 times now and the first time was the best but it's been downhill from there. They need to stop giving away freebies and up the quality of their food. The flavors are pretty good here but the texture of the chicken is too weird for me as it's too tough. It seems like they swapped the chicken they use since the first visit. This is really close to my house but I think I'll make the drive to Chengs.

It was easy to pick up a piece, meaning the crust was crispy enough to hold up the ingredients. This will be our new go-to place for pizza.

text:
A cool spot with good food. I have never had any issues with it and the staff are friendly and cheerful. Usually I grab a couple of chicken tacos and I'm good but this time I got the enchilada plate and my friend got some beef tacos. The enchilada plate exceeded my expectations. You get two nice sized enchiladas, with beans and rice...the refried beans are great! 

The dining area is spacious and there is also outdoor seating but it stays pretty busy. As far as parking you will have to find metered parking on the side streets.

I only wished they offered chicken tacos in the hard shell as I prefer hard shell but all well...

text: Cute little spot in West Philly with outdoor seating and open windows--perfect for the summer months! Came here for brunch with a friend because it's right by my church, and we both ordered the chicken and waffles. I literally licked the plate (or wooden board, rather) clean. Delicious and refreshingly different from your typical chicken and waffles with its mediterranean spice kick. Have yet to try anything else on the menu, but will definitely be back! Docking 1 star simply because it's a BIT overpriced.
name: Grace

text: Ended up here pretty late, maybe around 9:30, because everything else nearby had a wait. Honestly, the wait wasn't awful, just longer than i expected for the time of day.. Idk, my friend liked their dish more than i liked mine.. Honestly, ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. So yeah, the fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table.
name: User

text: Yikes...This store is frightening! Looks almost abandoned...when you walk in you are greeted by tables/displays with very sparse amounts of produce. I only came here to buy fresh herbs and vegetables but there were mutliple items with mold on them such as galangal and chiles. Very unappetizing. From the looks of it, I just can't trust the produce as the owners don't mind selling bad food. This whole place needs an overhaul.
name: Stephanie

text: it tasted fresh, just not especially memorable. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated bc that happens a lot. The music was louder than it needed to be. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. I'd maybe go back, but I'd order differently next time. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text: We have been back several times since our last review. They are doing much better at management and service. The employees were very friendly and helpful. The ladies that work here actually act like they want to be here rather then the young men from the past. The food was served hot and fresh. A nice restaurant for a quick dinner.
name: Lucye

text: Came here for the first time St. Patty's day weekend. After a long day and night of walking and partying, we were hungry for some good authentic Chinese food. Everything around us was closed, but luckily, this place was still open at 2am in the heart of Chinatown. A 20 minute walk from our hotel, but it was soooooo worth it! The fried rice was AHHH-MAZING and shrimp eggrolls were crispy and HOT!! The best decision as far as food choice for the day by far! The food was so good I had to go for a second time while I was in town this past Sunday and it did not disappoint!! The place is very small and crowded, so I wouldn't suggest dining in, but it is perfect for takeout. I will definitely be back!
name: Audrey

text: This place is alright. It's essentially a coffee house that also serves lunch salads. I've eaten here a few times and walked away more often. The issues are first that this place is small, like really small. There are a few outside tables but unless the weather is nice you only have a few seats inside. Second, the food is ok but not worth the hassle of trying to get it, mostly salads and cold sandwiches for lunch, limited break fast. And finally they open late, the hours say 730 but that's an estimation it seems. There's a Starbucks up the block that does a vibrant breakfast biz and it seems that there's a crowd and that an extra hour or so would be well worth it but they don't want to put the work in I guess. It's not a bad place overall but there's better lunch options all up and down the street and they are so small and limited you aren't missing anything for breakfast
name: Rich

text:
what a great find !!!
after recently relocating to a different apartment in reno, my wife and i were starving after a long day of moving.  yelp to the rescue!! i yelped the closest pizza joint to me and low and behold less than a 5 minute drive is this hidden gem !!!!
small parking lot as you arrive. coming from chicago, i always have to admit i am very picky about my pizza. 
we ordered the special of a large 2 topping pizza, a pound of medium wings, and a 2 liter of pop for 25 bucks !!! what a steal!!! to make this place even better... when i walked in for my pickup,,, the inside was mostly hockey stuff!!! ( boooo pittsburgh penguins stuff) but i was totally amazed that the tvs had all the NHL playoffs on !!!! this is a great surprise! i may have found our go to spot for the playoffs.   heck i could walk there !!  all the workers were friendly, and the pizza was great !! we had pepperoni and onion pie and the pound of wings, and these wings were up there with my favorites!!! so glad we tried this place. the pizza was fantastic.   i can see us dining in here with a couple brews and watching some hockey!  great find !

text: The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. You can tell they care about customer experience here. Would return. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.
name: User

text:
Simply put, excellent in all areas! big statement but one of the top three mexican of its style in all tucson in my opinion!! 

WORTH THE DRIVE!

Cute and comfortable inside (except for really hot days , no real cooling system) with warm and friendly service! 

Cant wait to visit again!

Wish they would open one in central tucson!

text: Had another excellent meal with friends at Mizza. The Pizza was terrific and there Bruschetta is always fantastic. I love people watching sitting outside off of State Street.
name: Carl

text: I really hate to give a semi bad review but it's wayyyyy to expensive for a veggie combo platter! Iv been to a bunch of Ethiopian restaurants and often the max is $15 for a veggie combo, it's like $25 here? Make the portion smaller and please keep it under 20$ and I will go here ALL THE TIME. Like multiple times a week. If it remains over $20, I'm sorry but I simply won't go. It's way too pricey, and I'm ok with paying a little extra but not $30 (I tip too)

text:
First of all the food was delicious and the location perfect since we were staying at the Noelle. The experience was pretty lackluster as the coffee refill took over 10 minutes and we had to call someone over. 

The manager came by to ask how things were, but obviously didn't care. He barely waited for a reply while walking away. I could tell his sports jacket was new as the vent stitch was still in tact. Lol. Did anyone in the kitchen notice that the sandwich was cut wrong? I couldn't match the sides so I had to eat it open face. The bread was tasty but could have used a steak knife. This is a pricey place - please plus up the service and let us feel it was worth it.

text: It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Not bad for a quick meal. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. The food was good and the service was easygoing. The leftovers held up okay the next day..

text: Cute little place. I had the BLT and my husband had French toast. Both were yummy. Good coffee to. Service was exceptional

text: Stopped here for lunch....got the catfish nuggets and fried okra....also tried the fried mahi sandwich and mac n cheese side. Fish tasted fresh...nice light breading, tasty.... location is clean and the people are very friendly...woul definitely come back and try the shrmp.
name: E

text:
Of course, everyone loves the king cakes... my quick analysis is that they are good, uniquely flavored with more of a whipped cream type icing and served on a soft brioche, but it's just not as fantastic to me as everyone says. 

My five stars come from the other items in the bakers... the meat pies, chicken or pork, are both spectacular. Easily the best I've ever had. The chicken is dark meat, tender and juicy and marinated in traditional Vietnamese spices. The pastry dough is just right, perfectly flaked. 

I also love the fresh baked bread... it is absolutely delicious by itself, or even better, used to dip in BBQ shrimp and other rich sauces. 

And I haven't even tried the pho or Vietnamese sandwiches... I'll get there. 

BOTTOM LINE: Forget about the king cakes, go for the meat pies!
name: Matt

text:
Great People. Great service. Awesome food! Would highly recommend to anyone. 
We live the atmosphere, the building looks relatively new. The artwork on the walls is great, I would let that dude tattoo my body. 
The food was better than any Indiana seafood I've ever had. 
The servers great, attentive, and timely.

text:
I was glad to find a local bagel place that served the style of bagels they have.  I always liked the City East in Memphis and was looking for something similar here.  This is going to do for now.  The bagel tasted fresh and was at least as good as City East, but they didn't have a banana nut flavor, at least not that day. Still, they serve very good bagels at a good price if you order six or a dozen ($6 for six; $9 for baker's dozen).  I haven't tried their coffee or their breakfast menu as of this writing.

However, the person working there didn't seem to know the prices off hand, and it took a bit of questioning to get my answers.  They also didn't accept Apple Pay.  Still, I will probably want to pick up more bagels from them soon.
name: David

text: You can tell they care about customer experience here. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. Would return. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..

text: Great service and food was portioned generously.  Enjoyed my salad and the gyro meat was as tender as I've ever had it.  Great DDD spot that still produces.

text: This place was awesome!!!  Especially Harrison's positive attitude. and not to mention his extremely hygienic look will always make me come back here. He is the best at scooping my ice cream! 10/10 would recommend to a friend.

text: This is a charming new addition the the St. Louis Hill neighborhood and can stand shoulder to shoulder with the heavy hitters like classic Italian Gittos and tapas-centric Guido's. The Steak Modiga Flatbread is a perfect starter to excite your palate and pair with their Cucumber Martini.   The medium-rare filet had a perfect warm, pink center and i topped it with a Signature wine reduction butter melted over top to finish it and pair exactly with a HIP Cabernet (from The Sagemoor Farms Vineyard in the Columbia Valley, WA and supplied by Bommarito Wines). A great date, meet up, or celebration locale without the dark visage of most upper crust Hill restaurants.

The hashbrowns were probably what I enjoyed the most, a little greasy but still very good. I recommend this place if you are looking for easy diner, comfort food.

text:
So I like soup and I like Asian food, but can you believe I've never had ramen before? I've been wanting to try it for awhile, but I'm not an adventurous eater and I guess it just looks so ..unique to me.

Anyways, how did I end up here?  We live in Chicago and I told my fiancé that I wanted to try ramen after walking by some underground ramen spot with a massive line in Chicago's west loop.  I mean come on, it had to be superb considering how many people wanted to eat it in a basement setting.  

Anyways, we were in Philly visiting family and this place came up as one of the best ramens.  So we made a reservation at 8:45 on Friday night (they're like booked solid!).  The restaurant and area reminded me of Chicago's wicker park neighborhood , home of the hipsters.  It was pretty small but comfy, and very ....grunge?  Our waiter was excellent and we each got a bowl of ramen super quick! 

I had the regular miso one considering I hate spicy, while my fiancé got something similar but spicy.  Portions were large! In my ramen was some pork belly, green stuff, and an egg. I'll be honest, I was a bit hesitant about eating the egg but it was all good! The broth was salty which a tiny kick to it.  I mean it wasn't my favorite thing in the world but it was good enough where I'll definitely be eating ramen more!
name: Karolina

text: Great food with a creative version of many classics... The ambiance is excellent, roof deck and patio, plus a great historic flavor bar with live music on the weekends... I highly recommend!

text:
Every time I eat at one of these restaurants that are tucked away in a nondescript office plaza, I feel like I'm getting away with something. Like I found the pot of gold at the end of the rainbow. This place is no different.  

I had this joint bookmarked for about 7 or 8 months before I finally got around to trying it the other day, and for the most part it was as good as most of the reviews stated. Sure, I saw that a few people were disgruntled with the ambiance or the lackluster appearance of the plaza, but I don't give a shit about  any of that because I was here for one reason and one reason alone--to eat. 

$6 quesadilla and some loaded fries did the trick. 

The quesadilla was good, but I wanna focus on the fries and how good they were. First, it's a meal in itself. In fact, if I had it to do all over again, I'd order the loaded fries, add a meat condiment and be done with it. They come covered in real melted cheese sauce, not processed liquid crap from an industrial pump. On the side, they include some mysterious yet magical white dipping sauce. Don't dip though, just pour that shit all over the fries. Trust me. 

Bartender was great and the food came out quick. Whoever was in the kitchen was rockin out to some Metallica and I could just imagine him busting out the air guitar while slinging chicken, peppers and onions across the grill while whispering to himself, "Fugg yeah quesadillas... fugg yeahhhhhh."
name: Mark

text: Imagine it is a rainy March evening, you have walked about 10 blocks from your home, open the door, and immediately feel warm and relaxed. Fireplace on, Hawthornes provides you with a place to just kick back, eat some delicious food and just chill for a bit in this more-modern-looking pub. We were starving after our walk in a downpour, and everything on the menu looked good. It was a Thursday, so the special was $8 mussles. The featured mussles were Dijon herb, garlic, and Yards Philly Pale Ale blend, which sounded amazing, and were SOOO GOOD. Would definitely order them again. We also ordered fried cauliflower. I guess I have been more used to a 'baked/fried' cauliflower elsewhere so I was surprised to see battered and fried. They were good, but not what I expected. We got the garlic hot sauce, so when you ate the sauce with it, it was kind of like eating vegan chicken wings. I ordered the pork chop and it also was extremely delicious. The brussels sprouts with it were tasty and the potatoes were good but could have been better had they been more crispy. I didn't eat all of it and had the rest leftover for lunch, and it was still very good. We finished off with chocolate cake which was a solid good, nothing amazing. I was a little disappointed with the dessert menu as it only had like three things and all sounded fairly basic. But I think they change around what they have for dessert, so maybe there is more variety and interesting desserts. Overall we left full and happy, and definitely willing to come back again. Looking forward to trying brunch!
name: Caitlin

text:
I like Just Salad and had a great experience at one of their other locations. This location is only okay. 

I ordered a salad with mixed greens, chickpeas, apples, roasted sweet potatoes, edamame, sesame tofu with an agave dijon dressing. I've had this combination before and loved it. But this time it was pretty gross for some reason. I didn't like the taste of the sweet potatoes and the dressing tasted funky.

The woman who helped me didn't know much about the food either. I asked if the focaccia bread that came with my salad was vegan and she had no idea. I don't think I'll be returning.

text:
Stopped here for lunch. Will stop here again. Pleasant atmosphere. Good customer service. Lite music playing. Clean. Now then food : OMG!!

I'm eating healthy right now and this menu was awesome. I opted for the Roll Sod healthy roll. It was fantastic. Sticky vermicelli roll stuffed with lettuce , cucumber and shrimp. Beautiful presentation and served with a light peanut dipping sauce. I added some dry Chilli for a little heat and wow, what an amazing bite. (Be careful - that shit is hot )

I then ordered the Tom Yum Goong. Tasty and a little hint of spice. Fresh vegetables and very savory tomato broth. Just perfect. 

  This place is a gem hidden in a strip mall. Go find it.

We really wanted to like this place, and we tried but, the food was so disappointing that I don't think we'll ever be back.

One star for the drinks, tasty and refreshing, albeit inconsistent (maybe different bartenders, I don't know)

The staff were nice and friendly.

The food, underwhelming. For an appetizer we went with the crispy spare ribs which included a piece of corn bread and slaw. The rib was pre-cooked and warmed just before serving, and the corn bread was cold. I use the term "warmed" loosely, it was a bit over room temperature and no hint of crispy came to mind.

For the main course we ordered the chef's special - unfortunately there was nothing special about it. Grilled shrimp over rice pilaf, and somehow the shrimp were over cooked but still just over room temperature, and the pilaf was meh.

We elected to pass on the desserts, fearing much of the same meh.

The ambiance is pretty neat, lighting was modern and again, the staff were nice but nice doesn't mean good food. I'd be willing to try again but the wife said "no thank you."
name: Seneca

text: We checked in on Yelp to not haveto wait in line when we got here we were seated right away! (Yay Yelp app) loved our server , super sweet. Got the cheesey bread it came out fast and was nice and hot, and cheesy. My boyfriend got the chicken parmesan, its a huge portion and I got the stuffed riga tony. It was delicious!
name: Alba

text: Great food friendly staff. When they're busy it may take a little longer to get your food but that's because it's a small operation. I recommend the honey jerk wings.
name: Von

text:
The sandwiches are pita based. I tried the egg sandwich as well as chicken schnitzel. Both are well seasoned with spices with fresh veggies including chopped cucumber to give a crunch. The chicken schnitzel isn't breaded, tender and not dry.

The salatim has very strong spice.

Hummus is really smooth, highly recommended
name: Retna

text: Shows some promise. Beers are good, but there are serious deficiencies in very basic things. Serious enough to make me write a review. For example, while a beer may be advertised at 7 dollars on the menu, pay in cash and you may well find yourself having paid 8. Why? Apparently, unlike most bars, here tax is not included in the listed price, and they "Don't do coin change." I really don't care much about a dollar, but the principle of a deceptive practice like this is enough to keep me from coming back. I'll probably go back if other people do, but structuring something like this shows poor attention to detail. Again, I'm hopeful it's something they're able to work out.
name: Leo

text: This was a delivery order on a night when I really did not want to cook. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Would probably stop in again if nearby.
name: User

text: Loved this restaurant! In town visiting and decided to try this out. My boyfriend and I loved it. The ladies working in there were extremely friendly and warm, true southern hospitality! And the food was pretty good! My favorite was the fried chicken, smothered cabbage, Salisbury steak, and gumbo/rice. Will be back when in town!
name: Alexis

text:
Came for breakfast on a Saturday morning. The restaurant is pretty spacious and has a good relaxing atmosphere. Our server Sean was great. 

My girlfriend had the avocado toast and I had the breakfast sandwich and a cappuccino. The large cappuccino is very large. Both meals were great with no complaints. They have a great menu of coffees, teas and smoothies.
name: Shane

text:
This place was umm...underwhelming to say that least. I ordered 2 sushi rolls and they were very average. The seafood didn't seem very fresh. My fiancé ordered the hibachi and it was not very good. Everything was just below average yet not completely horrible. The customer service just meh. Extremely slow service. Won't be returning. 

Back to Umai Umai we go...our only sushi place that never disappoints! (It's just a far drive for us)
name: Keisha

text: My experience was awesome! Great food at Great prices! Katie was the manager on at the time and she was very personable and very attentive.  She gave me great recommendations being that I was clueless as to what I wanted to eat. She was very patient and informative going over the different food/drink options. The restaurant has a nice ambiance and is very clean which of course is always a huge plus! They also have an awesome Happy Hour Food/Drink menu! Definitely a great place to get together with friends and or family. I will definitely be back!!
name: Carolina

text: I'm going to keep it simple and say that this place is absolutely amazing. Delicious food and great genuine customer service. Do yourself a favor and give it a try.
name: Danelle

text:
Must stop when in the area. Lamb meatballs are incredible!!!
Pizza is cooked perfectly with tons of flavor !!

Well done
name: David

text: The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Worth checking out. They were out of one thing I originally wanted..
name: User

text: Had a really good dinner here. I had the NY Strip steak which was done perfectly and my wife had the Swordfish steak which she said was very good. The Baby iceberg salad was great too. Our waiter was very friendly and attentive, had good recommendations and knew the menu items very well.  Al in all a great dinner, will definitely go back again.
name: Max

text: Wow!  What a fancy location.  We loved our waiter, she was so funny and nice.  Food as usual is amazing.  I ate too many piping hot Brazilian cheesy bread balls.  For first-timers-- this is a buffet, definitely go hungry.  Also, don't fill up on the salad bar.  Make sure you are patient with the meats-- don't go big early and fill up on e.g., ribs.  If you want a specific type of meat that has not come around, make sure you ask your waiter.  The sirloin server came to us three times, but we never saw the chicken server or sausage server...we had to ask our waiter for them to come over.  Filet server was also not widely visible.  Maybe they limit serving the more "expensive" meats.  The desserts were incredible...we were stuffed before then but still manage to lick our plates clean.  We got the tres leches cake and the chocolate mousse cake.  I think it is hard for the servers to see the green/red cards for some tables, so make sure to make them visible if you are GREEN.
name: Shoshanna

text: Had brunch here over the weekend and it was kind of a mixed bag. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. Price felt a touch high for what it was. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. I can see why people like it, even if I wasn't fully sold.
name: User

text:
Usually amazing, love the ice cream here. However, tonight was a disappointment. The chocolate ice cream machine was apparently being cleaned(in the middle of a shift?!).. they did not inform us upon ordering. I pull up for 5 orders for my family, 3 being chocolate and they hand them to me ... completely white/vanilla. The girls never said a word, I handed them back and asked to remake as there was no hint of chocolate. They were nice enough to try, but it was just vanilla ice cream. 
I wish they'd told me before I ordered $15 worth of ice cream. Drove away but nobody in my family will eat them, me included. Into the trash they fix Would have appreciated a refund without the ice cream. Wasted $$
name: Jill

text: Dessert saved this a little. Price felt a touch high for what it was. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. I left full, which at least counts for something. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer..
name: User

text:
I got off work late and wanted to celebrate a little victory, and decided on the Biltmore for its lovely ambiance (especially their decorations in winters)!

We got the seat in front of the fireplace (yay) and checked out their menu. I was grateful that there was a legend for what was vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free (although the labeling was hard to read). There seemed to be only one vegan option (the olives), but upon asking the nice server, he was able to verify that other things could be made vegan.

I got the veggie burger (made vegan) with the truffle fries (veganized by removing the parmesan). Delicious! I would probably get regular fries next time, because I found these were really oily (yes, there's truffle oil on them, but there was a lot and I've had truffle fries that weren't this oily).

My partner had the tuna empanadas and thought they were okay. He loved his cocktail (I think the one with cacao bitters?), which I found really sweet. 

There were A LOT OF OLIVES. They were tasty, but we brought them home and are still eating them a couple of days after!

All in all a delightful time. Service was excelent, the food was tasty, the ambiance was romantic, the decor was festive.
name: Ivan

text:
The food is actually pretty good.  The salsa is bland but if you ask for the spicy and mix in a little of it then it is pretty good.  I was SHOCKED that they charged for extra salsa with your chips.  What kind of Mexican restaurant does this?  I would not return simply for that reason.  And we weren't told of the charge until we got the check. 

Updated: returned a few days ago and they no longer charge for extra salsa.  Food was good and beer is cold and cheap.  I would go back.
name: Zach

text: Let me start by saying its late and I've never been so thwarted from eating a burrito. Late this evening my husband and I went to grab 3 seven layer burritos with NO CHEESE & NO SOUR CREAM. We have an allergy to meat and dairy and cautious when ordering out. We explained this while ordering. It happens, we aren't all perfect. The ordering experience was an entirely other issue I'd rather not even elaborate on at this time. Lets just say it's Taco Bell, I wasn't expecting customer service like Chick fil a. However, we get the burritos and I can't see cheese or sour cream, but its dark and I cannot see that well (I'm as blind as fetty wop navigating through a dark room). I get home and open the burritos and there is a white creamy substance on all the burritos. I drive back to Taco Bell and see the same individuals before. I calmly explained I have an allergy. Let's just say explaining this offended the taco maker or taco chef if you will. She was quick to tell me its the guacamole and that she made it right. I asked why the guacamole was white? She said it has dairy in it. Hmmm, did I not say we have a allergy to dairy?! I was dumbfounded! What ingredient in the guacamole makes it white? She proceeded to tell me the guacamole is just white and that's just the way they make it. I simply said so the guacamole is white just because avocados are green?! Is there milk or sour cream in the guacamole? None of these questions could be answered. I look up the ingredients on the Taco Bell website in the drive-through. There is NOTHING in the ingredients to make it white. I asked her one thing before my refund, "So, if I eat this my throat will not swell up and I won't be headed to the ER tonight, because the white sauce is avocado"? She slammed the door on my face (Jesus told me not to overreact it had been a rough day) and I waited for her to create a new receipt (she lost mine) and short me $2. Shame on me for thinking I could simply order 3 burritos with NO CHEESE or SOUR CREAM because of a food allergy......and thank goodness for figuring out Taco Bell is making magical guacamole with white avocados!!!
name: Kimberly

text: Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Will be back. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. No big complaints, just a nice meal. They were out of one thing I originally wanted..
name: User

text: Honestly, McDonalds is preferable to this stank hole. Staff is rude, slow and has the personality of dirty underpants. I want to buy this place so I can tear it down and personally drop the employees off at the unemployment office. THEY DONT EVEN HAVE TO TAKE YOUR ORDER AND THEY STILL CAN NOT GET IT RIGHT. This is honestly unreal. And the food is hot garbage...only it's not hot.
name: Jen

text: It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Worth checking out. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Food was good and came out fast. They were out of one thing I originally wanted..
name: User

text: The food is great. The staff is friendly and attentive(especially Olivia). Also, you can't go wrong with the vast beer selection!
name: Joe

text: My friends and I are 21/22. We came to New Orleans for a fun weekend get away. The bouncer told our one friend he had a fake ID. When we called the manger over he said the bouncer said he must have seen something funny.. he was no help and our friend who is 21 then was unable to enter the bar. This was so unfair because we had multiple friends from the same state with the same ID. The Manger was unhelpful and clearly did not care about our business. This bar is not even that cool don't even bother.
name: Allie

text: The service is terrible. The server was making faces and very impatient. She seemed aggravated because we were a party of six. She had to bring many drinks and food to our table. The food was pretty good but the chicken tenders were bland and dry. You guys need to get it right!!!!
name: Kelly

text: One of the best Thai restaurants that I have ever been to!  The Pad Thai was unbelievable- full of great tastes. And for dessert, order the White Elephant. You will not be disappointed.  The owner has served me twice, and both times he is so friendly that i enjoyed giving him a good tip. He truly cares about his customers' experience unlike most restaurant owners who care about the bottom line.
name: Tony

text: The food is still good as always. However they need to fix the air conditioning. We were there s few nights ago and the humidity inside was as bad as outside. It's hot and muggy inside the restaurant. Not pleasant and does not make you want to stay.
name: Kyle

text: This place seems like it serves good beer. Unfortunately I wouldn't know because the bouncer told me they don't let anyone with luggage/backpacks in. I found it strange because almost every restaurant/bar in the immediate area welcomes people attending conventions who, inevitably, carry luggage/backpacks. When I asked if there was someone I could ask to verify this I was told the managers didn't want to be bothered by this. Well, that's all I needed to know. So a word to the wise, if you're here for a convention and you have any sort of "luggage" on you, look for somewhere else to have a beer.
name: Eddie

text: Ate there today for the first time.  Although it was between lunch and dinner time I went for the breakfast.  I have to say everything was cooked just right.  Eggs over easy were perfect as were the American fries and bacon.  The 1/2 order  of biscuits and gravy hit the spot.  Christie, the server/cook was great.  I'll def be going back.
name: Richard

text:
Date:4-8-18
Time:1230 

Brief: If you happen to be in the area...it's the best Thai around. 

My better half and I moved into the area about a year half ago and one of our first missions was to locate the best local Thai, tacos and pizza joints in close proximity. The Thai options were slim (this being the only one)...so we were hoping for the best and we were not disappointed. 

We have been to this spot many times over the last 1.5 yrs and we recommend it anyone in the area. The menu is large, the presentation is above average and most importantly the offerings are tasty!

Yum Beef Salad $11.95: This is my go to dish and one that I find myself ordering anywhere it's offered. The portion size is on the larger size for this dish and the ingredients are text book (sliced beef, tomato, cucumber, bell pepper and onion) all tossed with a varying spice level fish/lime sauce that is delicious. My only critique is that all the veggies are large cuts which makes it harder to eat and distracts from the presentation. Also, I think the dish could use more cilantro to brighten it up a bit. 

Panang Curry w/chicken $13.95: Great Curry for those coconut lovers out there. The balance of sweet, savory and spice make this dish a pleasure to dine on. It's served in a bowl with a good portion of white rice as an accompaniment. 

My wife and I eat plenty of Thai and to have a local spot that serves up quality Thai that is both consistent and tasty is a real treat.
name: Christopher

text: I was overall disappointed with my visit. I ordered the gumbo with a side of red beans and rice and both dishes looked the same as well as my order was wrong twice. You have to pay over $3 for a small bag of potato chips with sandwiches - they can't even bother to make their own. The gumbo was terrible and took more than an hour to get. Unless you come here for a lunch sandwich it's not worth it. Cheaper but not recommended, go to subway.
name: Kara

text:
Not a fan of the new happy hour menu. Food is mediocre at best. Service is inconsistent from visit to visit..,perhaps management should encourage the staff to focus on guests and not talking with each other.
The only reason to go here is the beautiful patio. 

The management team should head over to Bottega Michelangelo and pick up some pointers on service.
name: Kelly

text: Would not go back. Bad service and somehow worse food. Both vegetarian meals were inedible - lack of spice, flavor, really any thing except tomato. Friends who got the etouffee had undercooked rice. Appetizers were okay but everything else was painful to eat.
name: Bhavna

text:
I have pretty low standards for fast food spots. One of those standards is somebody should be available to take my order. Another is that the staff shouldn't be back in the kitchen arguing about their jobs while customers wait for anyone to come out. Finally, once someone comes out, it is usually polite to greet a customer and apologize/explain for making them wait 15 minutes... not treat them like a nuisance.
I don't think my standards are too high, but this location couldn't be bothered to meet them. Just skip this location. You could drive to another taco bell, place your order, receive it, drive back to this location, and eat it in the same amount of time.
name: Hank

text:
Very surprised to find a Jamaican restaurant in Carmel! 

I've had the curry goat meal for dinner and curry chicken meal for lunch. Both were wonderful meals that came with a vegetable and rice. 

I've also had at the jerk wings which comes with a side of jerk sauce for dipping. I've had the Jamaican beef patty which is wonderfully seasoned meat inside of a pastry shell that is Golden colored with curry added to the dough.

There's plenty of parking as it's in a strip mall and there's interior seating and exterior seating on a enclosed patio type of space.

They have some island inspired beverages including an interesting ginger beer that is like ginger soda but it's 5% alcohol so be careful there!
name: Jordan

text: Amazing gelato, fresh ingredients, and great owners!!!! You won't be sorry!!! Highly recommend the pistachio gelato.
name: Deb

text: I seldom eat red meat, but when I do...Bern's is the best! It's not just the very high quality of meats, vegetables and ingredients, not the exceptional and vast collection of wines (over 100,000 on premises!), not even the highly trained and attentive staff that are watching every minute to assist you. No, my friends, this is more than a meal, it is an experience! Ask for the full tour and you get a glimpse behind the curtain into one of the largest and cleanest professional kitchens you will see, then down into the wine cellar with VERY old ports and rare wines. Enjoy what fine dining is supposed to be. Then after your meal, should you have a shoe horn handy and a wee bit of room in your belly, head up to the dessert room for some rich and decadent treats and aperitif. Most recently, the schedule was so full for months, yet they accommodated my wife for a early sitting due to some health issues. Above and beyond in just about every category. Can't wait until my next trip to the left coast! Mmmm!
name: RJ

text: I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh.
name: User

text: I had a great time with a local pal. From NH. Felt very relaxed and happy. Great way to distress.
name: Lynn

text: place is disgusting if you don't want waste your money don't come here ... and I found a  cockroach
name: Jennifer

text: Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Overall, a strong experience. Food took a while and didn't rlly feel worth the wait. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. It looked better online than it did in person.
name: User

text:
This was my 2nd time here. 1st time was mediocre, nothing to write about but this time around was the worst experience. 

My girl friend and I were seated. We had 3 waiters come by and had to order water with each of them because no one came back with water. That was 15-20 minutes into the service. Food service is slow but that I don't mind that because I understand sushi takes time to make. But pouring water, that takes a minute. No one refilled water, it was like trying to find Waldo to get a refill. 

We asked for several things but never got it on the initial inquiry. Throughout the night, they didn't bring anything we ordered, instead brought us a bunch of things we didn't order. We didn't have a problem till the end of the night when we order the dessert. Yet again, they came over with another item we didn't order, a vanilla ice cream. 

We didn't have a problem until a waitress comes out with a udon dish and we were like we didn't order this. She goes away and come back with an attitude and almost a decibel below yelling, scolds at us. Telling us we did order it and showed us the paper. We didn't order it but there was a mark near the item. It might have been a pen smear or maybe we unknowingly marked but we didn't have any intentions on ordering it. We tried explain to her but she didn't want to hear any of it and kept giving us attitude. It was extremely condescending with the way she was speaking at us. She then tells me that this time, it's okay, making it seems like she's doing us a favor. If it's okay then why are you making it a big deal, especially when it's the last order sheet. 

I do want to note that no where on my sheet marked a vanilla ice cream which earlier they brought over to us. So it goes to show that there's a flaw in their system but instead of refining it, they like to push the blame completely to the customer. We were patient with the entirety of this crappy service until this moment. I was so stunned at this behavior that I didn't know what to say. I'm definitely not coming back. The sushi is not good enough for me to subject myself to this.
name: Rachel Minhua

text:
We love to support local. Discovered this place from advertisement on a Radio station as it tucked in a little strip plaza on cass circle across from the pinch o Penney. Needs a bigger sign. 
I'm told it has grown since opening expanding into second store front. Staff are extremely nice. Front has large cases filled with wonderful cakes and deserts. We selected several for takeout and not disappointed. There is also a section to dine in. We have eaten there twice. Chips come out warm and salsa and sauce yummy. We were told everything is made scratch. . The Ruben sandwich is very good. I had the tacos. I was disappointed to have the cold soft shells and cheese cold.  I also tried the butterfly shrimp. They looked too perfect and reminded me of the frozen ones from Publix.  Need to go back 
It's worth a try to visit. It's very clean. Nice decorations. Clean bathroom.  Get a desert. You will not be disappointed
name: Debbie

text:
Great ramen spot! A little pricey for me personally, but the cost is definitely worth it for the quality. The meat felt like it was melting in my mouth, everyone in my group really enjoyed coming out! 

Waiter was really cool too-helped me order and I really liked what he got me to get! Original ramen with chili sauce and garlic oil, with pork belly meat!
name: Jonathan

text: Not for the faint of heart:  stopped into McDonald's for some dinner.  Order off of their 2 for 5 menu with an extra fries and soda.  Drive away and fries weren't in the bag.  Wait in a second long line to be questioned like a criminal when I say I didn't get my fries.  After everything I head home to eat and MY CHICKEN SANDWICH LITERALLY HAD A BONE IN IT.  I was so horrified I literally vomited immediately.  I will never eat at another McDonald's as long as I live.
name: Alyssa

text: If you're looking for a lunch that will be filling, tasty, and still easy on your conscience, you should stop by Elaine's. She has put so much effort into her shop and you can truly taste it. We stopped by here on a whim and it was such a great decision. There is tons of variety and what we had tasted great. It was a good stop to add to a weekend in St.Louis.
name: Mia

text:
I'll start with the positives. The shower was nice and the pool looked great (it was too cold and rainy to enjoy it). The spacious room and common areas were clean. The location was convenient and the price was ok. 

The rest was not good. The staff member at check-in was rude. Our room smelled of smoke and chemicals that I assume were meant to cover up the overpowering smoky scent. After speaking to the rude staff member about it, she found us an alternate room after making me wait in line again. The heater was either all or nothing--no real option of a reasonable temperature without constant monitoring throughout the night. The WiFi was too weak to download email or check social media--completely ineffective. The elevator was out of order so we had to drag our luggage down the stairs.
name: Jeff

text: I was immediately greeted when I walked into OEB by myself on a Tuesday morning and sat at the window bar to add some natural sunlight and people watching into my dining experience. Both of the servers working were friendly and efficient. I ordered the house coffee by Caffè Umbria ($3.25) and it was really tasty with free refills. For my meal I got the scallop and hog breakfast poutine ($20) which was plated beautifully and full of flavor. I ordered it with half potatoes half spinach (no extra charge). The flavor of the scallops and pork themselves was really lovely and the egg was fresh with a bright orange yolk. I will say that although the dish was tasty, it was a bit intense. I think it could have done with a bit less pork and hollandaise as both are pretty overpowering flavors. The hollandaise combined with egg yolk was kind of soupy and I was unable to finish the dish because it was quite soupy/strong. Perhaps next time I would ask for less hollandaise or stick with the traditional fixing of the dish (more potatoes) to soak up the liquids and flavor a bit more. I definitely like the atmosphere in here...light, bustling and clean with a slightly eclectic vibe.
name: amanda

text: Huge bowl of amazing ramen and spicy crab roll with beautiful presentation. The ginger in the ramen and pork belly  the staff were super helpful and full of recommendations. The place is small inside but has a variety of seating and it's very cozy. Will definitely be going back!
name: Jordan

text: We had lunch at Palm Pavilion today. The food and service was excellent. Our server Erika went above and beyond our expectations.  We shall return and request Erika as our server. Great view of the beach adds to the ambiance.
name: Ellen

text: Went to dinner on Jan 17th.  Great Pizza, Great IPA beer, great live music! Great Service. Met the owners and they are awesome.  Will definitely return.
name: Marilyn

text: This is a nice restaurant. Very close to El Dorado. Place is small though but their service good, and food was great. Will stop by again next time we are in town.
name: Kwee

text: Portion size looked small at first but it was actually enough. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The food was good and the service was easygoing. For a busy night they handled it okay. so yeah kind of mixed on it. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed.
name: User

text:
The breakfast menu here is impressive. Omelettes, BYO omelette, shrimp & grits, waffles, etc. We were quickly seated on a Tuesday morning when we were famished and in need of breakfast food. 

I had the red beans omelette with grits. The omelette was good but a bit on the watery side (probably due to the beans it was stuffed with). The grits needed a ton of salt but the texture was all there. My boyfriend created his own omelette which was good but his homefries were cold.

Service here is spotty. Our waitress got our drink order, then our food order, then did not stop by until we were almost done with our meal. It seemed the same with the other tables, too. Not a bad spot if you're in the Quarter and need some breakfast but don't expect top notch service.
name: Kristy

text:
Just moved to the heights and have been trying out the local dives! Food overall at every place ive tried has been outstanding so it really comes down to service.

Pretty cool place of all the ones I've tried. Comparatively a little mediocre in my opinion to the other options in the area.
Service was standard no complaints there.
name: Alexis

text: Amazing! My wife and I stopped in for a drink and a quick bite . The wings and brunch wrap were really good. The food came out quick and was cooked perfectly! We're in town for a few more days and will definitely be back!
name: Aaron

text:
Stopped in here with a buddy because he wanted me to try it for the first time.

I ordered the BARDENAY AMERICAN-STYLE KOBE SANDWICH. Basically, it's an upscale philly cheesesteak with provolone cheese and creamy horseradish on a multi-grain focaccia bread, served with a side of their rosemary au jus.

The meat was extremely flavorful and juciy, and was perfectly complimented by the soft crunchiness of the focaccia bread. I ordered an extra side of horseradish because I enjoy the extra "sting" in my nose.

My side with the sandwich was Bacon Blue Cheese Coleslaw. It was tasteful, yet extremely light for those that don't want to feel heavy or bloated after your meal.

My buddy ordered a side of there Apricot Walnut Cous Cous, which I was hesitant about at first, but surprisingly enjoyed and will probably order next time I visit Bardenay.

To top everything off, staff was EXTREMELY friendly, courteous, and attentive to food and drink requests.
name: Jerry

text: Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. It just never really recovered once things started off weird. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Maybe other people have better luck here. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus..
name: User

text:
The best Philly in pizza. Full stop. Its not even close.
Byob, you need to order the day before. Getting a table and your pizza takes time and its all a truly small price to pay for the best pizza in philly
name: Marc

text: I had the black oil ramen which was ok.  I've had worse and I've had better.  The chatsu was the best part.  I wish the broth was a bit hotter.  The outdoor seating was nice and the servers were adequate.  Not much else I can say.
name: Samir

text: Very quick and great device on a Thursday night at about 530. Tomato Caprese salad was lite and tasteful. I had the strawberry balsamic chicken salad. A lot of salad enough for two people. Great taste on the balsamic vinaigrette although too much. I would of liked the vinaigrette on the side. The salad had grapes, strawberries, blue cheese, pecans and lettuce. The party I was with had lobster ravioli, lobster bisque, crab cakes and the special sol fish. The bread was very soft and tasty. I would recommend the sol, the lobster bisque and the lobster ravioli. The carb cake was a little dry.
name: Timothy

text:
Don't know if I'd count as a regular but I tend to visit every 1-2 months for the all you can eat during lunch time. My last 2 visits were a bit disappointing. My previous visit, the fish didn't seem like its usual freshness. The salmon nigiri, which is my favorite nigiri, had a borderline fishy taste and looked as if it was getting ready to go a touch slimy. The wasabi must have been old too. Piled it on because the fish wasn't it's normal freshness but wasn't getting the flavor or "bite" from the wasabi and kinda gave up. 

I ended up trying a couple new places due to this experience but came back 5/23/19 to give them another go. The fish quality and wasabi freshness had definitely improved but I was a bit disappointed with the service this time. Took a while for my nigiri to arrive but I was ok with it as I only saw 2 behind the sushi bar and it was the tail end of the lunch rush. That changed as I sat there with an empty plate and holding my order in hand as I kept seeing my waitress walk past and disappear. Not sure how long it would have been if another waitress had not seen me and I think took pity as she cleared my empty plate and got me another drink. I ended up ordering too much since I wasn't sure how long it would take if I chose to order again. I then sat there for a good while and watched the couple next to me get roll after roll served. 

Finally got my rolls to be disappointed again. The rainbow and shrimp tempura rolls were loose and several pieces fell apart as I tried to eat them. Often a problem especially when all you can eat rules state you'll be charged for leftover rice! The philly roll had more cream cheese than I seem to recall as well. Felt like eating cream cheese chunks instead of a sushi roll. At least the check came promptly when I threw in the towel....
name: Jacob

text: Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. The service was off and the meal kinda followed that energy. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. Anyway, my pasta was decent and not overcooked, which i appreciated because that happens a lot. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent.
name: User

text:
We had a gift certificate here so we decided to take advantage of it and order tons of food to bring back to the hotel.

First of all, in the dark of winter, it was really hard to find. Look for the entrance just after the Jaguar dealership and park in the back, walking through a small courtyard. The restaurant is on the left among all the businesses.

We had a somewhat complicated order but they did everything right. All told, the meal came out to about $140 or so, but we ordered the garlic noodles (we should have ordered more, they were Da BOMB), two orders of Vietnamese fried egg rolls (surprisingly good), seafood rice (pricy and decent amount of seafood, just disappointingly dry), and several pounds of assorted mussels, jumbo shrimp, oysters. Now let me note that we three who were dining on this meal are no lightweights when it comes to an appetite and we certainly had our fill.  We opted for the special house sauce and it was deeeeeeelish - nice kick.  Lemme have some more of that!  Big messy eating and thoroughly enjoyable.

I also noted to the restaurant that we were eating this at a hotel, and they generously provided lots of napkins and extra empty containers for us to dump all our "empties" (ie shells) to keep a mess in the hotel room to a minimum.
name: Allie

text:
Even here several times and it's always amazing. 
Today was best ever!  
Fast service, absolutely amazing food and very cool environment. 
I will keep sending people here!
name: Marty

text:
The Oyster Bar

Located in downtown St. Petersburg, Florida on Central Avenue the Oyster Bar is a seafood tavern with a robust menu, craft cocktails, and an excellent brunch. Reviews on Wine Dine And Play were written in July 2016 and September 2018. The Brunch menu is a combination of either platted dishes with an oyster section or a set priced buffet at $18.00, that had a large grouping of items, making it very reasonable for that price point. You could also order a ​bottomless mimosa or Bloody Mary's for $14 or $18. Our group mainly ate from the buffet but I ordered from the menu having the shrimp n' grits dish made with slow cooked stone ground grits, mixed with pimento cheese, then topped with baby shrimp, bacon, and an Étouffée sauce. You can read the full review on Wine Dine And Play...​
name: Sean

text:
Just ate here. EVENTUALLY. Service was absolutely terrible. Lots of staff members around...all but one seemed to be on permanent slow mode. Probably close to an hour before our appetizer came out. Wrong appetizer. When we did get the correct one it was missing the topping. Probably about 1-20 later we got entrees, mine was a skillet dish  that was meant to include bacon: no bacon. Was only warm not hot - skillet itself was not hot so I doubt it was actually cooked in the skillet. 
First time - last time. Beyond a joke.
name: Nicky

text:
Came for opening night and there was quite the crowd. We had about a 30 min wait bc it's a small dining room. No good waiting area especially if it's rainy outside, and not much space at the bar to wait, only two seats there. But I was in good company so NBD.

Service was efficient & friendly, food was pretty darn good, but definitely a heavier meal. There is a go-box picnic theme, I guess. Our server mentioned you can also buy one of the picnic baskets that lines the walls? 

We ordered the Smoked Fish Collars & Face, which was not bad. A rillette of sorts, an off-putting name for my friend, but I will personally order the weirdest thing on any menu. My sister has a crab allergy, but was intrigued by the West Indies Crab taco and they subbed bluefin tuna on request, for an upcharge. We ordered the crawfish boil hot fried chicken basket, which was cooked very well but while I didn't get any crawfish boil flavor to the chicken itself, it was served with chopped carrots, celery & sausage pieces, so maybe I misinterpreted what the chicken batter was going to be seasoned with. It did come with optional Crystal Hot Sauce pulp, which were the pulpy remnants from the actual factory after the liquid was pressed to make the Crystal Hot Sauce. That was delish. 

We also ordered the BBQ'd Black Angus Beef rib. 1.5 lb sounds like it could be shared, but if so, would really be appetizer portions for 2-3ppl. It was perfectly cooked however and I wanted more.

We finished with the Campfire Cookie Dough S'mores which was presented on a tiny cast iron griddle and set en fuego. It was my favorite thing of the night. 

It was a solid meal, notable for great fried chicken, excellent rib dish and a fantastic dessert with great service. I'll be back!
name: Sarena

text: Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. It just never really recovered once things started off weird. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Wouldn't really choose this place again. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. It looked better online than it did in person. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text: Loved it! Food was delicious, staff was helpful & I totally dig the space.  We just happened to pass it on a Sat. right before it opened.  Was glad to see there was a wait by the time we left.  We overheard several people say it wasn't their 1st time.  We'll definitely be back.   Taco  salad   & 10th street burger did NOT disappoint.
name: Truen

text: The location is tough to get into but the food was on par with most TGI Friday's. We shared the loaded fries and I had the bacon cheeseburger and my daughter had the quesadilla, all was good.
name: Landis

text: The bakery I go to and recommend for every event. Delicious and beautiful. Frank really knows how to take care of his patrons. This time he really hit it out of the park. Thank you!
name: Jonathan C

text: I absolutely love this place! Great service and a really cool, cozy atmosphere. The pirogies are my favorite appetizer and I always like to switch it up for dinner. They always have different specials so I like to keep it interesting. They also have a great brunch on the weekend. Highly recommend!
name: Jane

text: Solid oysters. Went for raw and grilled. Great bartender. Beautiful facility! I'd recommend happy hour.
name: Doug

text: If I could give it a zero, I would!!  This restaurant (if you can call it that) has gone WAY DOWN. After talking to the district manager months ago, we tried it again today. Upon arrival, no one was eating in the dining area. They were all waiting on their food and looked pretty bewildered. When we got up to the counter, the young man working said it would be a wait for our food. I asked "like an hour?", he replied, "I really don't know". The worst customer service ever. Needless to say, we left. Do not eat here if you want customer service or you want to eat. Surprised they are still in business.
name: Lucye

text:
Downward spiral was our experience here.

Sunday afternoon hoping to watch some football while grabbing a bite to eat and it's not crowded. Our waiter comes over to our table and sits down with us being a bit too chummy. We order our food and he writes nothing down (seeming very confident that he's got it all). Our food arrives ... and then he realizes as he's placed a meal down at all but one person. He asks what I ordered and goes back to kitchen. Comes back with an excuse (doesn't apologize) and says it'll be out in 10 minutes. 15 minutes later he walks by and realizes I'm still not eating. Goes to check on it and comes back saying it'll be out in 3 minutes. 7 minutes go by ... everyone in my group has finished eating ... and he's just bringing it out. But not everything is on the plate. He says they ran out of baked beans. I ask where the cole slaw is. I also tell him I'd like a take out container because my family is done eating already.  He gives me a not so nice look and goes back to the kitchen.  He comes out with the cole slaw and slides it across the table, drops a takeout container on the table, and then curtly said they found some beans and are cooking them up. I call him out on the fact that he told me they were out of them and say I want them. He leaves and brings them back ... sliding them on the table without saying a word. Again no apology for the delay. Took awhile to get our check. We expected to see some sort of credit for the mistake and delay ... everything including my meal was on it.
