text: Amazing. Best italian I ever had. I went there for my birthday. I suggest the seafood fetecini Alfredo...... my personal favorite.
name: Camden

text: Went here for breakfast on weekday morning. No wait. Server great and food was all delicious. Had the breakfast sandwich with bacon and avocado. Subbed a salad and it was quite tasty and healthy. Others had oatmeal and eggs/banana pancakes. Everyone loved their meal. Only reason it wasn't five stars is that it is a bit pricey.
name: R

text: Stopped by after work because I was nearby and hungry. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. A very pleasant experience. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. The sauces helped more than I thought they would..
name: User

text: I absolutely love this place I have eaten at the original restaurant in Bisbee AZ. This place carries over the original great flavorful food and ambiance of the original restaurant. I absolutely love the chorizo rancheros. Highly recommend this place for breakfast.
name: Justin

text: I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Not bad for a quick meal. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh.
name: User

text: Loved this place! Had to find food while I was starving in Edmonton and its quite hard for me because of all my allergies but thought to give this place a try. They had food that I could eat! I couldn't believe it! Having an allergy to eggs, milk and gluten is so very hard but they made it work. Not only did they have food I could eat but it was delicious! Mouth watering and so filling oh my. Also its very reasonable price. Would definitely go again!
name: Sarah

text:
Crepe!!! My visit here was good. Order on the counter and they bring the food to you. Since I gone between meal, not many people there. It is actually pleasant and quite moments to around that time. The decoration is simple. They do have some wall unit sofa. The also have the stool high top section. Other than that, the outside sitting also available. 

They serve salty, sweet, or breakfast crepe. Some of the lunch salty crepe is interesting. Please look at their special of the day which not in the menu. It may surprise you. Happy hour start 7 pm to close. Beer and wine half off. 

I got the nutty joe. It is crepe fill with Nutella and Oreo cookies. It top with vanilla ice cream. It also come with a shot of espresso. It is good combination. I actually like the way they made their crepe. It is sweet with chewy condition.
name: Boon

text: Absolutely the worst airport food experience ever.  Ordered a salad with a scoop of tuna and recd a tuna sandwich.  Returned for a do over.  Salad comes minus tuna.  Attempt three and it seems correct.  Yes, a salad with tuna...and no dressing.  $23 including a $3.33 tip they automatically added.  Come on.
name: Fawn

text: This place is all about the signature cocktails, local brews on tap, well-seasoned southern yumminess and ambiance. The weekly bar/drink/bite specials are worth checking out - but even though those deals aren't offered on the weekend - #SmokinBettys still deserves a visit and promises a great meal, superior cocktails and tasty dishes in a great atmosphere. My advice: build your own perfectly seasoned burger with their crispy on the outside, soft and warm on the inside, fries. Try a signature cocktail - but start with the BBQ Rib appetizer!
name: Nick

text: I've been waiting for a good seafood spot to arrive on our side of town and I think it is here. We ordered appetizers that included wings( barbecue and sweet chili tai) and mozzarella sticks. The cheese sticks were basic but the wings were great!! I will definitely order them again. I got the combo that included crab legs, shrimp, potatoes, corn and added the boiled eggs. There are different sauce options ( which is much appreciated). I decided to "live" a little and try the juicy sauce which is a combination of all flavors. I really enjoyed it and will definitely be back. The only issue i had is that there aren't any kid menu options. My kids can be a bit picky and most kids won't eat adult sized portions. I think juicy Seafood is the place to be ( if they incorporate kid menu options )
name: Jessica

text: This is hands down the best Starbucks in the area. It's huge, plenty of seating, and friendly staff. Per my conversation with the manager this is the new layout coming to the entire Starbucks platform. Very spacious and a great vibe. Starbucks greatly redeemed themselves with this store I guess as a make up for the train wreck that is the Race Track store that Westchase residents have had to suffer through.
name: Gaijin

text: Food was mediocre, plus there is a "Trump Train" the runs across the top near the ceiling. A disgusting display given the current administration's treatment of women, minorities and the LGBTQ community. Will NEVER go back.
name: Kevin

text:
Pretty darn Good! I come here fairly frequently for Happy Hour, which is 10am to 6pm. (Not the WHOLE time, lol)
Today for the BBQ special, they had oxtail soup, jerk chicken, red beans and rice and a plantain/strawberry cake for $12.
The oxtail soup was beyond amazing! I tasted the plantain/strawberry cake b4 anything else and thought, "Uh, oh, it's ok". Then, I paired it with soup....oh, YUM!!! It mellowed the zing of the soup to a perfect level!
The red beans and rice were fabulous, the jerk chicken was very tasty. The soup just stole the show on this one, though, lol!
Friendly bar with an excellent spread of beers including craft- draft and bottle- and a lovely wine selection, Ermanos is a must-try kind of place.
name: Diana

text: Just dropped in get a little food and a drink. Sat at the bar had the grilled oysters and crawfish crab cakes off the starter menu. Both were outstanding but Mike the bartender really made the night. He is from Chicago and had plenty of stories. It's a small place on a busy night you may not get in but they do have upstairs seating. All the staff and even the other patrons at the bar were very friendly.
name: Jim

text: This place is a must eat if you are in Tampa, Ybor City area. It's soo good I ate there twice in 2 days. You will not find peel n eat shrimps of this size anywhere for the price!  Lots of great selections. The hush puppies are fantastic too.  Tonya was a great host and we even got to meet the owner briefly.  You simply cannot go wrong with this quiet on the corner eatery!!
name: Ryan

text: Fabulous food, great vibe, fun times. The haddock soup was to die for and they have the best burger in town. Not just bar food, expansive on entrees as well. A definite must when visiting New Hope
name: Andon

text: Reel Foods has been our go to for fish for many years.   After heading downtown, ( because google still says that's where you are and I was double checking your hours) we realized they have relocated to Vista.   So, we head over there, only to find that store is closed and they are moving again.   Tried calling---mailbox is full.   Do you plan on having a storefront in The Boise area??
name: Stacy

text:
If you have a special occasion coming up by all means go to Commanders.  They will help you keep the memory of that occasion. There is a really good chance everything will be almost perfect, especially if you are a local, a "somebody" from out of town or a regular. Don't be afraid to let the helpful folks on the reservation lines know about you.  If you are the mayor's second cousin,tell them. If you work at another restaurant, just happen to mention it.  And if you are from Michigan and it has been a life long dream of yours to eat here, sing out.  At The Palace they are vigilant and have defined levels of VIP service. 
   Which is not to say that an anonymous,timid couple on their first anniversary will have a bad experience. Chances still are that everything will be almost perfect 
   The ambiance is high class and tasteful. 
The food is tasty and, while the kitchen is allowed to be creative, the traditional Haute Creole cuisine here is unrivaled, considering the volume of business they do.
   The service is the best in the city.  In over a dozen visits here, spanning 30 years, I remember encountering one bad attitude and that was taken care of right smartly. 
   The owners run this place themselves, with a Will and a consciousness of the tradition here. There is little pretense, so go and soak it up, celebrate. It's expensive, but at Commanders they can deliver on memorable pleasure
name: Steven

text: The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Overall, a strong experience. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Food was good and came out fast.
name: User

text: Been here many times. Always great service and really good steaks. Don't bother getting the filet. Every place in town does a filet. Get the skirt and hanger. Seriously, get both! I'll be back very soon.
name: Jon

text:
Commander's place is not a restaurant. It's an experience. They make you feel like a real king. Outstanding service, perfectly tasting food and drinks. We went for brunch and enjoyed good food and live music. Band comes to your table and asks you for what you'd like to listen to. 
A must-go place if you're in NOLA
name: Chris

text: Pizza arrived cold and missing toppings(that I was charged extra for). After tip, $27 for a large pizza...expected better. I won't be ordering here again, plenty of other pizza places around here.
name: Dustin

text: Had gone to the convention center in Philadelphia for an art show and was very hungry. We went to where the crowds were going and I'm glad we did! The Waite staff were fantastic getting everyone seated and orders taken. Loved the food some of the best in Chinatown. Parking is difficult but we used the parking garage and did a lot of walking.
name: Greg

text: R2L is one of the best restaurants I've been to in Philadelphia. The view is breathtaking, especially being on the 37th floor, you see as far as the eye can see. The waiters and staff are friendly and knowledgeable of the menu items and offer great recommendations. The lobster Mac and Cheese is definitely one of the best choices to go with as a side. Also the drinks are strong and delicious.  Definitely recommend!
name: Gabby

text: They say their specialty is the "Montreal bagel." But despite the mistakenly convincing long lines out the door, I don't think there's anything too special about it. I had a pizza bagel and my friend had a toasted bagel with cream cheese spread. We went on a Saturday morning and waited a long time (at least 15-20 min for bagels, which I could toast and slather on cream cheese in less than 5 minutes?!) My friend waited much longer for his bagel and schmear which had its cream cheese spread sliding off his bagel). And for only 1/2 a pizza bagel and iced chai, it cost me a whopping $8.
name: Anna

text: Margaritas were weak (just water and sugar) and such overprice tacos that were so plain! If you are going to charge $4 for a steak taco at least make it good. Won't return but ill give them credit for the decor, it makes it a very attractive place. The service and quality of the place was just a bummer.
name: Vanni

text: I come here for brunch/lunch at least once a month! Such a friendly staff and the service is quick even if there is a long line. I try to get something new each time and still haven't been let down. My favorite is the turkey biscuits and gravy, it's the only place I've found that doesn't use pork! Yum yum yummy!
name: Jordan

text:
OMGosh, what took us so long?
I believe that any dish you order at this hole in the wall place will be good!
name: Anne

text: The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. By the time the food came out I was already annoyed. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Probably not coming back. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon.
name: User

text: First time back here in 3 yrs and I cant recommend this place anymore. Not sure if the Groupon Rush ruined this place but the food is not good anymore, not even the Margherita's are worth the trip. How can you mess up fried ice cream. If you're looking for good Mexican this isnt the place
name: Chris

text:
Upland has definitely improved over time. Thankfully the issues I had in my original post were solved with employee changeover and action from manager, Allison. Finally getting around to writing a new review I so neglected doing.

The beer is (of course) great and more varieties and seasonal  shave been added in on rotations. Definitely enjoy swinging by for the latest rotations to taste! I'm personally not a fan of sours but my sister is and swears that Upland's are some of the best she has had. Over time the menu gets changed with some frequency which I really love! Definitely forces me to try different things but a staple is always the soft pretzel and pimento spread! Luckily that stays on the menu all the time :)

Staff is a night and day difference from all prior issues and Allison runs a smooth ship and I see her around regularly! She definitely makes sure guests are happy while letting the staff do their jobs. Whether lunch or dinner every experience I've had in the last couple years at Upland has been great, even on busy weekends!
name: Alexandra

text:
BJs brewhouse. Food and beers
We liked this restaurant.  It was conveniently located.  Yes it is a basic chain restaurant, large with lots of tables but what we loved was the huge menu of food and beers. Big shout out to our server Jorge who was friendly, attentive and fun.  
Tried several beers. Piranha IPA, Blind 805, Dragoon IPA.  Didn't care for the BJ red.  Really enjoyed the spinach artichoke dip.  The Ahi salad was fresh and good.  The Deep dish pizza also good. Ribs also tasty. Wish we were hungry enough to try the Pizooki.   Overall a good experience.
name: Kimberly

text: The Bercy is hands down my favorite restaurant! Always a fantastic experience and never a disappointment. From delicious drinks (try the plastic heart) to amazing appetizers such as shrimp cocktail and yummy escargot, to wonderful dinners (best trout) and desserts, you just can't go wrong. Welcoming and attentive staff who make you feel like family. Go and treat yourself! See you there!
name: Debbie

text:
The pizza is delicious here. Never greasy as far as I've experienced. 
They make it pretty fast as well!
Dine in option with tables and booths or take out also. 
They always have different flavors of gelato as well!
name: Chris

text:
5 stars for service, 3 stars for food.

My family decided to go to Oceana for breakfast since my mother had noticed a line outside twice within a day. Everyone at the restaurant was extremely friendly & hospitable - 3 people came to check on us throughout our meal! It was also a great atmosphere; however, the food was not nearly as remarkable. Considering it was a little pricey, the food was not very flavorful and was a little boring compared to the menu descriptions. Overall, Oceana is a place with wonderful people, but average food.
name: Nikita

text: One of those meals where nothing is exactly wrong but you're not excited either. For a busy night they handled it okay. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. I wouldn't write it off, but I also wouldn't hype it up. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. The food was good and the service was easygoing.
name: User

text:
Oh Holy Lord no!

I've been Yelping for years. In that time, I don't think I ever left a "scathing" review. But this time. This time is the exception.

I walked into this cesspit of an excuse for a fast food restaurant and there were zero other customers in the place. No one in line. No one ordering. No one sitting in the many empty, dirty seats eating. Nadda.

So did someone take my order as soon as I walked in since the place was deserted. Nope. How long did it take to even get to give my order, you ask? I got there at 5:34pm and my order was taken at 5:39pm. Literally 5 minutes to take my order in an empty restaurant. Was that the end of my wait. Not even by a long shot!

I ordered a small #1 meal. That's the Whopper meal. The Burger King signature meal. Should be super easy. We'll gloss over that the clerk asked if I wanted cheese without telling me there's a 60¢ charge for cheese. Whatever. Again, with zero other customers in the store, it took them another 7 minutes to get the Whopper cooked and to me. They weren't waiting on fries. There were some drive-thru orders happening. But that was it. 7 minutes AFTER ordereing in an empty store to get me the signature burger.

You'd think that the burger would then be super fresh and made just for me. Nope. The patty was a hockey puck and there was barely any sauce. I'm glad I upgraded to the cheese or I wouldn't have been able to choke it down.

While I was waiting 7 minutes for them to cook me a Whopper, another gentleman came in. He also ordered a Whopper meal. The clerk asked what size and he was confused by the question. Rather than simply clarifying "The Whopper meal comes standard with a small fry and drink. Would you like to upgrade that to medium or large?" she starts actually raising her voice at him and just repeating the same "What size?" question.

There was no ketchup out in the restaurant. So after my 7 minute wait and getting my food set down, I had to go ask them if there was any ketchup available. She barks at me that there's none on the floor because the pump's broken and huffs while reluctantly giving me some packs.

So I'm eating my hockey puck of a burger and two African-American teens walk in. They looked 15 to me. Seemed like OK young men. They go up to the counter and ordered some food. I'm at the back of the restaurant, so I couldn't hear their order. But I sure heard when the clerk huffed and slammed a cup down with "Here's your 'water'!" The boys took their cups and went over to the drink machine to fill them and she watched them like a hawk and then barks again "The water is the BLUE button!" So we can safely add racism to the list of things this Burger King excels at.

I wouldn't eat at this location again if Burger King paid me. The story above doesn't make it clear but there were TWO different clerks running the registers. So this wasn't just one grumpy lady. And there were cooks behind the counter. Why it took me 12 minutes to order and receive a Whopper in an empty Burger King is a dang mystery. And then you compound that with bad attitude, shady upgrades, and mistreatment of other customers of all races but highlighted with some specific racism, and this is the pits.
name: Aaron

text: Have been here twice and never again! Lily Boccardi is rude. The food is blah and both times I've seen cockroaches
name: E

text: Great service great food great price.  We have been in St. Pete for 15 years and tried this for the first time last night.  Sorry to take so long to find this gem.  Also great ambiance.
name: James

text: The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. Food was fresh and service was quick. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. Pretty happy with it overall. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price..
name: User

text: I love all the food here . The crab Rangoon and Crispy Duck are so good. If you have a sweet tooth crispy banana and ice cream with a Thai ice coffee are my favorite. My wife and I go here once a month since we found it and we recommend them to everyone.
name: Steve

text: This place is amazing! We went for lunch for the first time and we were delighted! The food was great, the atmosphere was quaint and typical of a small cafe. Will definitely go there again!
name: Stephanie

text: Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. No big complaints, just a nice meal. The staff seemed tired but still polite. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. Definitely coming back. It looked better online than it did in person. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Food was fresh and service was quick. The sauces helped more than I thought they would..
name: User

text:
I've always liked this triangle shaped building.I remember going to a delicious restaurant in the 80s but it's been a coffee shop for a long time. I stopped in to grab a quick hot beverage on a chilly day. 

Service was quick and polite and my hot chocolate was tasty. Reliably good hot beverages and baked goods. Yay. 

But where this location is just a little bit better is the locale. I would love to sit at the table in the nose and read a book and feel like I'm in the prow of a ship. Seating isn't too jammed and folks were chilling and talking on this chilly morning. There is outside seating which would be lovely on a non-rainy not-cold day.
name: Jen

text: We had to wait two hours for our pizza and when it came, the order was wrong. We ordered the Cheez It pizza and it was undercooked and didn't have the pepperoni in it. When we called the store, the lady was rude, unhelpful, and hung up on us. Our delivery driver was really nice though, so I would like to point that out!
name: Loren

text:
What a cool little place! Came here late on a Saturday night and the place seemed to be emptying out. 
The servers seemed to be pretty tired but they took pretty good care of us! The hookah was good we had coals brought regularly and they gave good reccommendations on what was what.  
We also got food and it was super tasty!! Its definitely not in the best are but we had fun!
name: Madison

text: Went with family on a Sunday and it was louder than I expected. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Food was fresh and service was quick. Would return. Not bad for a quick meal. For the price I expected more than this. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything..
name: User

text: Went with family on a Sunday and it was louder than I expected. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. No big complaints, just a nice meal.
name: User

text: The pizza here is terrible now. Everything is over priced. Chuck was rude to my babies (literally threw tickets at her when she was reaching for them). Sooooo I probably won't be back.
name: Pash

text: First thing I loved about when we walked in was one of the waitresses said sit where you want. I'm a person that likes picking where I sit so that made me happy. We had a party of 4 and the big booth in the corner was free so we sat there where we would have plenty of room. I ordered the shandy cocktail which was amazing! It was so light and refreshing! And not bad for $8! My friend ordered the cocktail that had a B in the name (sorry can't remember) and she also said hers was very good. It was in a rather small glass though for $10. We shared the pretzel and the nachos with chicken. Both were good. We requested both the beer cheese and mustard on the pretzel, which they provided no problem and was tasty. The nachos had mounds of sour cream, salsa, and guacamole, which for me is like heaven. Another friend at the table ordered the fish sandwich. The waitress forgot to ring it up so she needed to remind her. She said the sandwich was okay. It tasted like a bunch of things just thrown onto a sandwich and some of the flavors didn't make sense. She wouldn't order it there again. Apps were good and service was fairly quick despite it being fairly busy. It was right next to Curtis Hixon, which is where we were going after so that was super convenient. I'd try it again for a regular meal and see!
name: Alexis

text: What a charming little restaurant! My husband and I came to Tavern on the Hill on Saturday evening for an early dinner. From the moment we walked in we felt welcome. The dining room is small, and we were seated at a nice table next to the fireplace. Our waitress was wonderful. She let us try a taste of the white Bordeaux before we committed to a bottle. The wine was delicious and price was great. For an appetizer we got the buffalo shrimp. I'm not a huge seafood person but this was delicious. Grilled shrimp with a delicious carrot and celery slaw. For dinner I had the filet and my husband had the redfish special. Both were good. Dessert was amazing - we got the key lime pie and the blueberry crumble and both were amazing. We will definitely be back!
name: Sweet

text: Nice Atmosphere and great servers very friendly however the food is just semi-OK. They don't season their food very bland. The chicken for the fajitas was overcooked with no flavor not enough grilled onions to help offset the blandness. The guacamole dip was just a bowl of smashed avocados with no seasonings.
name: Cheri

text: This is some of the BEST breakfast I've had while visiting in Philly. The Jewish Apple Pancakes were absolutely AMAZING I would eat breakfast here everyday if I could!
name: Kelly

text: Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. Will be back. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.
name: User

text: Food was delicious...wait was a little long, but definitely worth the price!!! Get the queso, it was very good. Salsa verde was great. Highly recommend!!!
name: Jason

text: If you like Cajun/Creole/New Orleans style food and are ever in (or even remotely close) to Franklin this place is a MUST!!!!! The menu changes daily but if you are a 1st timer (or if there is something you haven't sampled before)...they give you a sample plate with a couple of bites of each item to "try before you buy"!  I tried 5 of the 7 options (2 had crawfish so I skipped those)...& I liked all 5 of them A LOT!!! And I am a very picky eater! (They even have a vegetarian option every day & most days have a gluten free option.) Oh, and that innocent looking piece of the bread on the plate isn't so innocent...it is covered in butter mixed with jambalaya seasoning...they affectionately refer to it "crack bread" & it was...I had to order more!
name: Lisa

text:
Love at first site - even more so after first bite! 

I absolutely love the decor  - modern and sleek with traditional touches and warm lighting. Seating is comfortable and noise level moderate. Service was impeccable without being intrusive or overbearing. 

We started with (not pictured) crudités and green goddess dip which was goddess worthy - with a beautiful assortment of colorful seasonal vegetables and delicious savory dip. And, the perfectly crisped duck salad with butterscotch pears and a ginger dressing, which was easily shareable. 

My veal lasagne with ricotta, green kale and basil noodles with tomatoes melted in my mouth. It was heavenly and a must try! The acorn squash pomodoro with fresh burrata and tomato sauce was rich and creamy but not heavy. The Brussels sprouts were fried and but not overly (perhaps I delude myself) and finished with a soy glaze. 

For dessert we ordered the cranberry brown butter bar with organic caramel and toasted pecan ice cream. A friend sent us the "Not your neighbor's cookie plate", and it wasn't. A combination of sweet, small delights featuring salted caramel and chocolate chip cookies and other pastries covered the plate and were a nice finish to the meal, along with my freshly brewed espresso.  

I look forward to returning. Aimee Olexy and Stephen Starr are blending their special magic by Rittenhouse Square.
************************
More love at The Love. 

After a relaxing but cold+snowy day, it was love at first sip of my "Very Good Bourbon", with Jim Beam Black, Gran Classico Bitter, Iris Vermouth and Apple Cider. So smooth+soul warming. 

I quickly warmed up and relaxed, and neglected to take photos of our food. My friend and I both wanted to eat fairly light and we shared the Gnudi (the Love's spin on Gnocchi) which was tender and melt in your mouth delicious, made with with sage, Saba and toasted chestnut truffle brown butter sauce. It was so light we could almost forget we were eating pasta. 

We also had the torched broccoli in a house hot sauce. It was delicious and not particularly hot, though I have a high tolerance for heat. And, we shared the exceptional Brussel sprouts with soy balsamic. Hardly health food but not too heavy and worth every fat gram. 

I  the Love.
name: Liz

text: Decent. But nothing special. Neat atmosphere. Service was just okay. Music was good but almost too loud. I just prefer to have something I can't make at home.
name: Hannah

text: The burgers were nice, but I especially loved their Caesar salad. Service was good, consistent, and food was reasonably priced.
name: Michael

text: We went to Mango for lunch. It was pretty good. The waiter forgot to bring my sons drink so when I reminded him he brought it to us and told us it was on the house since he forgot. They plantain chips they serve are amazing as is the sauce. They can make most of the dishes gluten free. I had the Lomo Saltado which was so tasty!  My son had chicken tenders and fries. He was not a very big fan of the chicken. Over all it was very good and I recommend it.
name: Alicia

text: Ice bar is a gimmick. Sushi priced higher than other places in the area but not any higher quality. Ordered an old fashioned and they charged me $2 extra for ice (rocks) and it was just regular ice cubes.
name: Ryan

text:
Came to watch the Preds game. So much more fun to watch with a big group of Preds fan. All the tables has access to see the TV or the big screen behind the bar. Roof top was closed so unfortunately, I didn't get to check out roof top view. 
Bar menu has a big selections of beers and cocktails. Bar tender can make any special drinks on request.
Elote dip was a light tasty appetizers for sharing. 
Reservations was made online for a table. Got seated shortly when we arrived. Parking was a hassle but you can find several garage near by.
name: Diana

text: Amazing. Staff was extremely friendly right off the bat and gave us samples of the etouffee. Well, it didn't take much longer to decide after sampling because that's some of the best etouffee I've ever had in my life. We ordered the gator bites as well and they were exceptional. I'm a happy camper and will be back.
name: Kasey

text: Went down there tonight to grab some food and got talked in to the Prime Rib special they have. This was not special at all. My piece of meat was mostly fat, and was not seasoned at all. text:
Staff quickly took our order. I asked for eggs Benedict, but asked to omit the ham. They did bring my order without the meat, but also they didn't put hollandaise sauce on it. I asked the waiter to please bring it back and add hollandaise, which he did.  

My lady friend ordered crab Benedict. When I asked her opinion of her breakfast, she said "it was nasty".  There was a piece in hers that she had pulled out of her mouth which had crab leg shell. She asked for a spicy Bloody Mary, but it wasn't spicy at all, and she had to add hot sauce to it.

My male friend commented that his had browns weren't crispy whatsoever and we're more like potato mush.  He pulled out something he almost broke his tooth on which when we all examined it we determined it was a bone shard. 

My dish was pretty tasty, once they brought it back and added the hollandaise sauce. The hash browns had a nice flavor but definitely should have been a little crisper. There was also one giant hunk of hash browns within that pile on my dish that was rock-hard in a clump and I swear I almost broke a tooth when I tried to chew it before I realized it was a hard clump. 

From where I sat beside the kitchen door, in my view was a garbage can leaving up against the area where the cashier is. The floor under and around that garbage pail, and the wall behind it, looked like it hasn't seen a mop or been wiped down in literal eternity. It was revolting to have that within my line of sight as I was eating food. If they leave where I can see in that condition, I could only imagine the status of the kitchen. 

Won't be back ever, nope, that's a wrap.

text:
Average food, horrible service. This place was not busy AT ALL on a Saturday afternoon. Nevertheless, when my girlfriend, our kids, and I came in and ordered, the cook/owner shook his head at me while I was ordering, simply because it took us a while to place the order. What an asshole! Clearly he doesn't have kids, or understand that sometimes it takes a while for them to figure out what they want. Anyway, the food came out pretty quickly... the waitress that was working there was pretty quick, so I give her props.

The wrap I ordered was decent. Most of the rest of the food we ordered was average to poor quality. My girlfriend's son never got a slice of pizza that he ordered (the cook mistakenly gave it to another person who ordered after us). This wasn't really a problem, except for when it came time to pay...

When I went up to pay, the cook told me the total. There was no bill, just a number he had written on a piece of paper. I asked to see the bill, and he told me his system was down. Never mind the fact that he wrote everything down when I ordered. Apparently it was too much trouble for him to write up a bill for me. I told him that my girlfriend's son never got the slice he ordered, and to subtract that from the bill. The cook acted like I was lying. He reluctantly subtracted the cost of the slice from the bill, but he kept muttering that he was sure he had given us the slice.

The final straw came when we were leaving. We had a couple plates of the kids' food that we wanted to take to go. I asked for some styrofoam containers and a bag to put them in. The waitress helped us out with that, but she gave me a paper bag to put them in, which was too small. I asked her for a plastic bag, and the cook said, "We don't have any"... which was a lie. There was a pack of plastic bags hanging up on a hook behind him. I had had enough of this guy at this point, so I turned and left the restaurant. However, my girlfriend stayed behind and told the cook, "Sir, there are plastic bags hanging up behind you." The cook ignored my girlfriend and went back to whatever it was he was doing. Eventually the waitress came back over and gave her one.

If you ever find yourself over in this area (possibly because you're going to see a movie), and you think of eating at this restaurant, THINK AGAIN!!!
name: Chris

text: Been to Kona Grill 4 times and my 5th is most memorable in a sea of unremarkable (past 4 outings to Kona) visits.  Sadly it was such a let down, cuz the atmosphere, staff & location are pretty great but the prices and food need serious improvement. I ordered Pad Thai (Chicken), potatickers (chicken), and a side salad.  Now I would swear to you, with my hand on a bible that the potsticker were made with ground beef (NO JOKE)!  The salad looked quite appetizing, good portion size and brightly colored veggies and crumbled blue cheese. The house vinegrette was the dressing:  it was the color and texture of applesauce and tasted like what I imagine rancid oil mixed with a dirty ashtray would taste like.  Lastly, was the entree, which smelled great but my enthusiasm and dropping heart stopped there.  The noodles were under cooked, not aldente, but hard.  The chicken looked pan seared bit tasted microwaved.  There were WAY too many peanuts. Possibly the abundance of nuts was to hide the lack of bean sprouts or veggies. I think this is past my limit on chances to get it right.  I would have sent the meal back, but it was deliver by UberEats, which was the ONLY positive I could give Kona.  They chose a good, fair priced and quick to deliver delivery service. Sadly, that's where the enjoyment and this review ENDS... God luck & Happy Eats!

I have eaten here before when it was called The Lunchbox Cafe and ordered Thai food, which was good. As another review stated, the American cuisine leaves a bit to be desired. 
I ordered the BBQ Chicken wrap to go. The menu description says, chicken breast, BBQ sauce, ranch, cheddar and lettuce, and comes with fries. I was expecting grilled chicken, it was fried and very dry even covered in BBQ. There was no ranch which was highly disappointing, I love the ranch/BBQ combo and was why I ordered it in the first place. My wrap also had bacon on, which was not listed on the menu. Luckily I do love bacon, but if you didn't eat pork this would be a huge issue. The BBQ sauce was meh... To top it off my fries were very generic, like the frozen bag you buy at the grocery store. Definitely needed some seasoning or at least more salt. 
To many other great places to eat in West Chester to waste my time here. But I will say the best thing the Spicy Pig Cafe has going for it is their cheap prices.

text: I've been going here for years and the food is consistently delicious, the service is perfect and overall experience is very pleasant. We always eat like it's our last day on earth when we visit the Franklinville because their food makes us very happy. For starters, I recommend ordering the warm crusty bread for dipping in any one of their scrumptious soups. Their soups are as lovely as their fresh salads. The bread takes time to heat up so it's wise to request it when you place your first order. The wedge salad dressing is a bit heavier than what I prefer so I order the Caesar salad. It just depends on your flavor preference. Their baby back ribs (cooked in an on-premise smoker) are fall-off-the-bone, finger lickin' good. And the Maryland style jumbo lump crab cakes are expertly prepared, which is hard for this Baltimore native to find around these parts. Both are served as apps or entrees. The filet mignon and chicken marsala are both so good. I like the sweet mashed potatoes, sherries mushrooms, creamed spinach and rustic potatoes for side dishes. The apple pie (get the vanilla ice cream on top) and key lime pie are my favorite desserts. They have very good wines, too. And, the host/hostess and the servers are always so gracious. They make you feel very welcome, which matters in an era when dining often feels like a rushed and impersonal experience. Brace yourself for an exceptionally delicious experience at the Franklinville, it's worth many visits!

text:
My boyfriend and I couldn't resist checking out Akira Sushi & Hibachi's AYCE offerings! On Sundays it is dinner all day which was $25 a person. We ordered 3 rounds of sushi, but I only got one picture because I was overly excited.
* It is prepared fresh when you order. It isn't set up like a buffet where the fish is just sitting out in the open.
* We have been here before and think the service is pretty much the same. It's your typical Asian service, not the best but definitely not the worst. They were really good about refilling our drinks and taking plates out of the way.
* The kitchen dishes took significantly longer to come out than the sushi. Some places will start giving you less quantity or quality the more you order, not here!
* I had mostly the salmon sushi and it was great! The meat is fresh and sliced generously but not too big.
* For my boyfriend and I, the cost of this was the same (mostly less) than what we spend on a typical sushi meal so it was well worth it!
Good: salmon, yellowtail, tuna, eel, Rock 'n Roll, mussels, gyoza, seaweed salad, beef teriyaki, salmon teriyaki
Bad: hibachi rice (too sweet), spring roll (egg rolls, all veggies), cucumber salad (cucumber and soy sauce? But it might just be me)
Bottom line: I definitely recommend this place if you enjoy sushi.

text:
Came by myself and requested to sit outside on such a beautiful day. Server was a little slow to get to me, and when he did, he gave me the unfortunate news that the $1 oysters had run out. No biggie. I ordered the spaghetti ($10) and the halibut ($28).

The spaghetti was no ordinary marinara spaghetti and meatballs. This was something completely different with a little spice, a little citrus, a little sweetness, and a good amount of cheese. It was definitely creative and I liked the novelty of it! If I could change one thing, I would dial back a little bit on the sweetness of it. (And have more of it!)

When the halibut came out, I immediately noticed how small the size was. For an entree categorized as Medium, and a $28 pricetag, I was hoping for a little bit more. That aside, I very much appreciated the light searing done on the top of the halibut, while keeping the rest of the fish very soft and 'juicy'. I have had my share of overcooked dry fish, and this was far from it! Very well cooked! I am still thinking about how superb this fish was cooked.
The extra goodies that came with the fish (kohlrabi, mushrooms, and smoked almonds), were all really good as well. Mushrooms were really soft and flavorful, the kohlrabi was really soft and meaty on the inside, and the almonds were crunchy with a packed smokey bacon flavor. The sides also went well with the dish, and weren't just random pieces of vegetables/fungus. The only downside to the flavor of the dish was that it was a bit on the salty and oily side.

For the finale, I succumbed to getting the bread pudding ($9). This dessert was quite large in portion. I enjoyed how the base of the bread pudding came out quite warm with a scoop of cold white cream on top. Wish there were a bit more cream though.

All in all, a great meal! Highlights: very creative on the flavors for the spaghetti, fish cooked extremely nicely with great textures of crisp on the top and soft on the rest, extras were cooked really well and complemented each other, and great play on temperatures with the bread pudding. Downsides: small portion on the halibut, bit salty and oily on the fish and sides, and service was continuously slow from the start to finish.

text:
Vegetarian only, cheap, but filling, buffet-style.

I've seen the advertisement and walked by this place so many times, but truth be told, if you curb your expectations and like paneer saag, Samosa Vegetarian is your spot for just $8 pp (lunch only). Also, I hear they serve food to the homeless at night, which is just a rumor, but if true, props to the owners.

I think my favorite was paneer saag, the lentil soup and also the milk tea. I was actually quite surprised by the amount of fresh salads next to the classic indian dishes as well, and after my fourth plate of saag + spinach, I needed to unbuckle a notches on the belt and leave very full and happy. At the end of the day, all of the dishes taste homemade and authentic, and the service is quite attentive. So if you're hungry, come to Samosa!

Of note I think their samosa could use some more spices and peas.

text:
So being from NYC originally, I thought my journey to find a great sushi place had failed... we've tried restaurant after restaurant, all served dry, one too many day old sashimi with too much rice. 

... until we came across this place! I can't say that this place is to die for (sorry my sushi standards have risen since having traveled to japan!) but I have to admit that their selection in their all you can eat menu ranging from salads to fried appetizers to sashimi to sushi rolls (hand/maki and specialty both) all the way to their fried banana and green tea/red bean ice cream, you can't really go too wrong here. Their prices are awesome too, around $20 a person not including tip and tax. 

Definitely would recommend going here with a group of people so you can pick a bunch of different items on the menu and share; but do note and remember that if you order excessively and have remaining leftovers, they WILL charge you... 

I think their fried shrimp tempura and their spicy kani salad is an awesome place to start with a side of mushroom soup! Their rolls are really hit or miss depending on what you like, but majority of their rolls like any other place are tuna or salmon based w/ some eel sprinkled in. 

Great location, very clean restaurant, attentive wait staff!

Again, Don't skimp out on their dessert menu; they do have awesome ice cream! I'd probably skip the bubble tea and save room for more ice cream and fried bananas!
name: James

text:
Ariana's Pizzeria & Italian Restaurant on Levittown Parkway is a basic pizza parlor with booths and tables that seems primarily to toss and bake tomato pies and related sandwiches, calzones, wraps, etc., that can be found in most red sauce establishments. They also have a short list of dinners and entrees that looked appealing on the menu. 

We were all hungry and took the chance on the bigger (more expensive) meals, rather than the safer sandwich route. To some extent we regretted that decision. Each came with small side salad, heated torpedo rolls and butter, and a bed of pasta under the chicken offerings. Salad was fine. Bread hot and crusty, and spaghetti copious. 

Problem was that while the marsala was decent with a nice load of fresh mushrooms in a sauce closely resembling what it should be, the Ricci and Abbruzzio chicken dishes were not quite right.  The Ricci lacked much flavor despite the load of sauce and melted mozza, and a corner of the pasta was much cooler than the rest of the platter, like it had been sitting too long far from the stove. A little red and black pepper in the mix while cooking would have made a big difference. The Abbruzzio with the large bore pasta looked great, but the chicken was overcooked and tough, and the sauce flavor, AWOL.

I was overall content with my dinner, but the fact that my family ate so little of their's reflected the reviews they would write if asked. We took the leftovers home to see with we could improve them with a little doctoring. Yet, at more than $15 per dish, we were unhappy with our choices and the abilities in the kitchen. 

Teaches us to go out to eat hungry. Definitely clouded our judgment on how to attack the menu. 

2.5 STARS

text: Let me start off by saying that we host a large group dinner every year.  We typically go to a local BYO in the Rittenhouse area to keep the cost down.  Some places do large groups well, and others do not.  This year I hosted a group of 26 at Melograno for my husband's 50th birthday.  I could not complain about a single thing!  Erind, the manager, could not possibly have been more accommodating, especially since we had 2 more people than I told him.  He was the literally the best ... the best!  The food was excellent, and the service could not have been more attentive.  It was an extremely positive experience for all, especially for my husband who was celebrating his 50th!  For large groups most restaurants have a pre-fixe menu.  At Melograno, guests could order any three courses from the regular menu, and the cost was very reasonable.  The experience was so excellent that I'm sure Melograno will be a repeat for one of our next events.  I could not recommend this restaurant more highly for a large group.  Thank you, Erind and Melograno!
name: Tina

text:
Hershel's had been on my "to try" list in Reading Terminal Market for years by the time I finally checked it off last week. It suffered partly from extreme proximity to my favorite sandwich spot in the whole market, DiNic's, which has lured me in with it's intoxicating garlic & pork aroma a number of times I was considering Hershel's. Hershel's itself does very solid business, so long lines had also scared me off in the past.

I finally stopped in on a Thursday night and did what seemed like the only right first move there - ordered a corned beef Reuben. It was very good and I would definitely eat it again, but I have to say that after all of the anticipation that I had built up, it still managed to just every so slightly disappoint. 

The meat was excellent, and standing in line while it was prepared, I found myself fantasizing about pigging out not only on the corned beef brisket my sandwich was carved from, but also the pastrami and brisket ones nearby. The portion of meat is generous and makes a very filling sandwich. But for much of my meal (the Reuben came with two pickle spears that complimented it nicely) I did feel that the corned beef was so abundant that it was masking the flavors of the Russian dressing, sauerkraut, and cheese. Now a sandwich bursting with delicious meat is hardly anything to complain about, but I did order a Reuben because I wanted all aspects of its flavor profile and so there were bites where I wished I tasted some sauerkraut. 

That said, I enjoyed and was satisfied by my sandwich and expect that I will order from Hershel's again, if nothing else to sample those other meats.

text:
I was curious to try this outpost of the Midici brand formerly in King of Prussia. What a happy surprise to learn theirs is an 'artisan-style' pizza as opposed to Neopolitan, which did not disappoint, and even better than KOP.

My husband and I are gluten free by choice and we both agreed their house-made gluten-free dough is THE BEST we've had in the Philly area to-date for crisp and thin artisan pizza. My husband had the Margherita, and I had a Build Your Own white pizza - both delicious.  

The restaurant has a "nice-casual" vibe, but the ordering and dining process is more fast-casual wherein you place your order, pay, grab a number for your table, and seat yourself. There's also a self-service area and bar to get utensils, napkins, and condiments. A server takes your food to your table number. 

They have other food options besides pizza such as great salads, & pastas, as well as desserts including gelato. It's a BYOB too. We'll definitely be back soon!

text:
Decided to come down to Franklin to get some lunch and found Merridee's on the list of restaurants nearby. Very reminiscent of a welcoming Cracker Barrel-esque atmosphere met with a cafe/coffee shop in my opinion. The menu is a little overwhelming since there's so many items to choose from, but that's not a bad thing at all! Just gives me more options to try next time. 

There's tons of different baked goods like pies and bread on shelves and more pies and some cookies in the little see-through cabinets at the ordering counter. 

I went with the chicken pot pie and a slice of key lime pie to top off the country-style cooking feel. The chicken pot pie was warm and flaky and didn't taste like it was reheated or anything like you'd usually expect from a hole-in-the-wall restaurant, so I was happy about that. 

The key lime pie was the star of the meal. I LOVE key lime pie and this was some of the best I've had. I sorta regret not getting a whole one to bring back to my dorm room so that I could eat the entire thing tonight... 

But seriously, overall it was a very good experience. There's several places around the counter to order at for busy times, the cashiers are nice, service was quick.

text:
One and done...  

First, the location: You may glance at the Delaware Ave. address and think Penn's Landing, or South Philly by Ikea; but it's across from Sugar House -- a neighborhood you probably don't want to be in unless you're going to Sugar House (which I also wouldn't recommend...)  I just saw on this Yelp listing that they claim a free parking lot at 1100 N. Delaware; but this lot was signed as "permit parking only after 7pm;" so I figured it was specifically NOT Golf and Social parking.  As far as I could tell, the closest legal parking where you'd dare to leave your car was across the street in the Sugar House lot; which, unless you choose to hop a 5' fence and jaywalk, means the equivalent of about a 2-block walk to the place (in the rain, in our case.)  

Apparently (and unknown to us), there must be an entrance for the Golf around the side of the building; but without proper directional signage (and wanting to get out of the rain) we entered through the door on Delaware Ave., which required us, golf bags and all, to work our way through a crowded bar area.  As soon as they saw the golf bags, the staff was very helpful in guiding us through and to the stairs (great...) to the 2nd floor, where the golf was.

Once upstairs, I was surprised to find only 4 golf bays.  There was a bar (which looked like it's only used maybe on weekends; everything we ordered had to be brought up from downstairs), a pool table, big screen TV, and plenty of tables/chairs/couches.

The food was OK at best (I wasn't exactly expecting fine dining), and the Bud/Miller Light draft (don't recall which) I ordered was skunky; so I switched to a Yeungling draft, also skunky.  The service was as good as could be expected from one guy who had to go up and down stairs for everything.

Now the golf: The price wasn't bad - $49/hour, which is basically $49 per person; since it takes about an hour to play 18.  But this was the worst golf simulator I've ever played -- including all they way back in the 90's, when the technology was new.  Even though they use Trackman, which I think is pretty much the gold standard in the industry, it sucked.  Maybe it was an old, beat up unit, or badly calibrated (or maybe we just had a bad bay -- didn't pay close enough attention to see if the guys in the other two bays that were going were having the same problems); but between the two of us, we hit at least 20 shots that didn't register.  And probably another 40 shots where we said 'there's no way that swing would produce that result;' a few for the better, but mostly for the worse.  I understand it's not an exact science; but this was really bad.

I remember being surprised that I didn't have to pay/enter a credit card when I booked (there's even language on the booking page about still being charged if you don't cancel early enough) -- and even more so after I got there and saw how few bays there were.  But when the bill came, I figured out why they do it (at least on weeknights, maybe)...  I knew the golf was a hundred bucks; so when I glanced at the check and saw $170, I thought "There's no way we spent $70 on food and drinks..."  We didn't; we spent around $40; but there was an automatic 20% gratuity added -- including on the GOLF!!  WTF is THAT?!  I probably could have argued over that extra $20 tip on the golf (as I'm sure people often do) and got it taken off; but already knowing we were never coming back, we thought 'screw it, let the guy have it.'  The final irony was when the credit card slip asked how much ADDITIONAL gratuity I wanted to add -- but I did resist the urge to write, "Yeah - don't smoke in bed..."

Takeaway is, the staff was helpful and friendly, but everything else went from "sucks" to "Meh..."  Plenty of better places in Jersey and Delco; and you won't run the risk of coming out and finding your car up on soda crates...
name: Pat

text:
We dined here on the 4th and because we arrived early, the restaurant wasn't completely full. Our server and manager was phenomenal, given how "needy" our group of 20 was.

We ordered roughly 15 dozen of raw oysters, 4 dozen of charbroiled oysters, alligator tails, gumbo, crawfish mac and cheese, shrimp and grits, salmon salad and other shareable dishes; along with several specialty drinks. The entree itself was OK - nothing that really stood out from a flavor profile. What I did enjoy were the raw oysters. The first several dozens were cleaned and nicely shucked, and the oysters were big and plump. However, as the restaurant became more busy, the griminess and dirt on and inside the oysters were more evident and the presentation was slightly sloppy.

I would say, all in all my experience was pleasant up until we were leaving. As we were walking towards the front of the restaurant, there was a group of customer waiting to be seated right next to the hostess's desk. They made loud comments such as, "look at how many Asians there are", "why are there so many Asian". Surely, the hostess heard those comments and said nothing and did nothing. Given how diverse and inclusive New Orleans is, I'm very disappointed that this type of behavior is still tolerated/ allowed these establishments.
name: Thuy

text: Brand new, incredibly clean, amazing fresh food, such kind and friendly service!  We love this place.  Excellent for vegetarians and meat eaters alike.  I had the vegan tofu banh mi, the tofu spring rolls and the jasmine milk ice tea.  My uncle had the pork banh mi, egg rolls and iced green tea.  He said the green tea - which they brew fresh every day - was the best he's had in his life.  The sauce on the banh mi was perfect with just the right amount of kick and the jasmine milk tea was delicious.  Very affordable and has a lovely, large aquarium with living coral to keep your eyes occupied during the short wait for your food.

text:
I've eaten at Kasai two times now. One time I ordered lunch take out and the second time was for the dinner 'all you can eat'.

I'd say the lunch take out was decent. I ordered the vegetable lo mein, which naturally isn't anything too special. I ordered it to be ready at 12:00pm and they didn't actually get it to me until about 12:10pm, so that kind of stunk. Luckily I didn't need to worry about time for my lunch break.

The second time I tried this place we got the all you can eat sushi. I was impressed with the options overall, being that this is a Japanese restaurant on the East Side! Everyone was pretty friendly. The only thing I didn't like was, I can't eat raw sushi and so the cooked sushi menu felt pretty limiting and they all shared the same ingredients, except with the subtraction or addition of one or the other. I ordered wasabi on my sheet and they never brought it to me. We had to ask twice for another item. 

Overall, I was pleased and will be back here again! Hopefully the service is a little better this time.

text:

Perhaps my favorite part of the meal though, is the Stubborn Soda fountain. I can't for the life of me understand why more places don't carry this liquid gold, but I've been hunting a fix since I first encountered it months ago in another state. What a pleasant surprise to find it here. 

I will say the second time we visited, I tried the sampler and the brisket was a little fattier than the time before. My Kansas City bbq aficionado/snob husband wasn't a huge fan of the ribs. I would probably say the delicious sandwiches are the way to go.

For main course we ordered the chicken tacos and kale salad. The tacos came on a huge plate that included rice, beans, salsa, queso, chips. Tacos were smaller but loaded with excellent flavored chicken. Believe it was $13 or 14 for the plate. 

Kale salad was big and my girlfriend said it was good. 

Overall, it was a nice venue, staff seemed organized, and were very friendly. Food was above average. Was a nice play to go and have a drink/chat.

text:
We hadn't checked ahead. We won't make that mistake again we WILL make a reservation. IF we go back. This is a local popular place. We are questioning why. There were no less than 8 empty tables when we arrived. They were pushing the hightop tables. I cannot sit on a high stool due to a recent surgery which we told the hostess. She told us then it's a 1/2 hour wait. We got on the list in spite of having to stand and wait on my post surgical leg. We waited 39 minutes and checked again ( the 8 tables were still unoccupied). We were told we were next. After 5 minutes more we were seated. 
We had two excellent martinis and a lager. The bar works well and is able to quickly produce good product so they'd get more stars if I were only reviewing them. However, staff listening skills clearly needs work. We ordered the smoked salmon spread it came as ordered but the taste was meh. It needs something to jazz it up. Onions? Some other flavorings... the real trouble started with our entrees. We ordered the Ybor burger no problem there our guest enjoyed it as well as the upgraded truffle fries. We ordered two house salads they were fine. We ordered two orders of large stone crabs and got only one. When we said we ordered two we were told oh I thought you were sharing. Then she told us they were out of large crabs but could get us an order of the medium claws. We opted to make the meal into a surf and turf and ordered the kebab appetizer to share - that we got two of! The other fail was that we asked for bread with our salads and while we know she heard us because she said it'd be an additional dollar the bread never came nor was it on the bill. So what gives?  All three of us did not feel well later in the evening - since we ate different food was it poorly cleaned dish ware? Silverware? 
A couple of days later I received a text request for feedback and they hadn't even spelled my name correctly. SIGH unfortunate experience with an out of town guest. I gave them feedback and informed them as a Yelp Elite I would be posting this review. They knew I wasn't happy. If it were my business I'd have replied in some manner. I let 5 days elapse. No response. Makes me wonder if they care at all about my opinion.
name: Donna

Our knowledgeable, attentive waiter was able to recommend both wine and main courses to us. My husband and I ordered wine by the glass and both selections were very good. My daughter and I split the beet and arugula salad, which was served with a yummy beet puree; husband tried a classic caesar with real anchovies. Delicious. Our entree choices were Frutti di Mare, the Ravioli Special and Gnocci with a mild tomato sauce. All dishes were very well prepared and presented with attention to detail. The pasta was extremely fresh and obviously house-made. Sauces were delicate and seasoned perfectly. This was my second visit to Convivio. We had tried it once when it first opened and were not impressed; however, this visit has changed our minds and we look forward to trying some other dishes on the extensive menu soon. Thanks for a lovely evening!

text:
Thai food worth driving from Goleta for. Siam Elephant consistently out-performs all of the Thai diners in the Santa Barbara area. It's a tiny little restaurant at the edge of Carpinteria's downtown that offers generous portions of fragrant stir fries and curries. 

What is amazing: 
- Eggplant with thai basil 
(so much flavorful basil and vegetables in a spicy brown sauce) 
- Spicy basil leaves 
(similar to the eggplant, but with more bamboo shoots and onions) 
- Pad prik tai dam 
(peppery stir fry with mushrooms and mixed veggies) 
- Pumpkin curry 
(red coconut curry with tender chunks of steamed pumpkin and vegetables) 
- Larb kai
(super-fragrant ground chicken salad with plenty of lime juice and mint) 

Essentially, anything with "thai basil" in the description is going to be fantastic because they add plenty of fresh basil and balance the flavor with strong savory-spicy sauces.  Many other restaurants simply add a few leaves and the taste doesn't come through. 

One big plus with Siam is that if you ask for your food cooked very spicy, it will come out at least a reasonable 3/5. Say the same thing in most SB restaurants, and it simply won't have much spiciness. 

As far as things to watch out for, some other dishes can tend toward the sweet side (pad thai, curries, and the peanut sauce with the satay). If you don't like things sweet, stick with the more savory stir-fried entrees. 

I love the restaurant itself, which is small, but comfortable and inviting. The servers are kind, and the service is always surprisingly fast. I am so grateful that Siam Elephant exists - they absolutely never disappoint.
name: Alex

text:
These are the biscuits dreams are made of.

I once had a biscuit obsession. I found the recipe on the back of a baking soda? Baking powder? (shows how much I cook) box and realized I had all the ingredients. Sure, the biscuits weren't pretty and as I ran out of ingredients, such as milk, I substituted other ideas, such as water, and although they weren't the best biscuits, they were my biscuits and I loved them. These biscuits are a thousand times better. 

I'm the type of person who likes their baked goods slightly undercooked. It gives it a doughy texture. That's exactly how these biscuits taste. I tried both the Squawking Goat and a cinnamon bun biscuit (I forgot the exact name but it was in the case) and both of those biscuits were good and doughy. They slather than cinnamon bun biscuit with tons of icing, which propels it to a notch above amazing. I really enjoyed the Squawking Goat. I thought the jelly added a nice kick without being too spicy (I can't stand spice). The chicken is crispy and not greasy at all. Move out of the way chicken and waffles, the chicken and biscuit is here and it's better.

You get in line to order and then find a table. There are tons of big tables so don't be shy about sharing with people. I thought it was going to be absolutely packed since it was the second day it was open, but they have so many seats that it was still pretty easy to find one. 

Instead of getting your name, they ask you for your favorite band. I don't listen to music so I was absolutely stumped. I thought about saying The Foo Fighters, since my husband is making me go to that concert, but I was afraid by the time they called that name I'd have forgotten I said that. Even though she's not a band, I went with Taylor Swift. I panicked. It was fun hearing other people's favorite bands. I knew about 1/10. 

You can get full off of just a chicken and biscuit sandwich. I was super full since I added on the cinnamon bun biscuit. 

This is the type of place that if anyone wants to go I'll immediately say yes. Although I live pretty far, I'm already trying to figure out the next time I can return.

text: This cafe is "line up and order" style. I met 3 people there after an afternoon film at the Garneau. They have several types of chai on the menu   but I chose a pomegranate juice. I found my gluten free wrap to be heavy with yellow coloured rice.- so the proportion of curry to starch was rather thin, given that I paid over $20 for a wrap and a drink.   I traded one of my small wraps for a  palak paneer wrap- cheese and spinach. I found there was too much potato mixed in with the spinach Also, the tamarind dipping sauce that came with 3 out of four wraps was turned into a thin, pancake-syrup-like substance by too much water, sweetening (sugar) and cinnamon-way to ruin tamarind sauce. I much preferred the hot mint sauce that one of my friends got- green and spicy- sorry don't have the name. It was all quite filling, and I still had a stomach ache the next morning so I'm a bit wary of their "GF" claim. I had a taste of a friend's tandoori chicken and  I thought it was quite good- I like spicy so I might try that next time-or just stay away from wraps altogether. text:
I had a strikingly unfortunate, humiliating, and discriminatory experience with a Porta employee. I followed up with Porta management. While the general manager promptly followed up with a personal phone call, our conversation revealed that he was not equipped to handle conversations regarding discrimination. He was rude, insensitive, and also ignorant about everything I was talking about. 

I tried to enter the establishment on a Friday night. The bouncer refused my ID and verbalized that I didn't look like my picture. I am a 25 year old African American woman with natural hair. The ID I presented was a photo of me on my 21st birthday with my hair straightened --although no one (including bouncers, airport security, national guard, police officers etc.) has ever questioned my ID in the past. I presented three forms of ID, including my driver's license, credit card, and Penn Law student ID. Still the bouncer began quizzing me about my address and then my zodiac sign. I answered these questions but by his final question I was pissed and no longer has any interest in entering the establishment. He told me I wasn't allowed in because I had an attitude.

After explaining this situation to the general manager, he insisted this sort of questioning was standard. I asked "even after presenting 3 forms of ID," and he dodged the question. I explained that this "standard protocol" disproportionately and adversely affected black women, and I requested confirmation of disciplinary action and an explanation of how the establishment would make black women feel more welcome at their business. He said he didn't understand. I said I wasn't here to be his diversity advisor but insisted on hearing what the restaurant would do to make my experience more typical of their patrons. He said he didn't understand what the situation had to do with diversity. I hung up. 

I discourage anyone who cares about discrimination from supporting this business.
name: Olivia

text:
First of all, it seems very apparent that 3 of the first 4 reviews on here are not real.  Friends and family reviews might seem like a good idea, but it just comes off as phony.  But what do I know.  All I can do is be skeptical, and compare these glowing reviews from faraway visitors with my own experience.  

I'm happy that Chalaco's opened in my neighborhood.  I hope that they do well, as I wish that upon any new business, but they're just not ready for prime time.  They should have done a few dry runs before opening, to get their game tighter, instead of delivering a poor experience by opening early. 

First , the bright spots:  employees from hosts to servers to bussers were all very positive, nice people.  The people experience was pleasant, and friendly.  Definitely good for a neighborhood spot.  The chicken there is awesome and the sauces for it, which I had to ask for, had a lot of flavor.  I'd 100% return to get take out chicken.  It's phenomenal.  It's seasoned well between layers of meat, and well rubbed under the skin.  The skin was crispy and tasty.     

But, now, the reasons for the 1 star review.  It's bright in there.  The lighting is grocery store level eye searing.  Next, I was given a paper takeout menu, which they plastered around the entire neighborhood- stuck on windshields, doors, trash, flying everywhere.  That's not being a good neighbor.  Also, the printing on the menu looks terrible.  The font is strangely flattened and just looks off.  It's like they created the menu in MS paint and changed the aspect ratio.  Just strange.  Placemats were also paper- not a good look for a sit down restaurant, where rent is presumably high.  There's some not so subtle text on the wall as decor- sub-Panera level.  

Food and drink:  the pisco sour- I'll never order it again. I like alcohol, too, but this was a terrible drink.  And yes, I've had plenty of pisco sours, all over the place.  The appetizer with short rib and little mounds of mashed potato(?) showed up cold. I'm not sure if it was supposed to be served cold, but it was very mildly lukewarm. After taking 1 bite of the 3 on the plate, my server tried to take away my plate.  My arroz con mariscos just wasn't good.  The mussels were dried to all hell, and the rice was dry and lacked flavor.  The shrimp in there was solid, though, but lost in a black hole of flavor.

Service: I was promised small plates to eat on, which never came.  No sauces were served with the chicken, which again, was excellent.   And the 3 sauces were also delicious, but I had to ask for them.  My server disappeared for a while, and it was a hassle to get my check, but the excellent, friendly busser/food runner took care of it.  

All in all, a very disappointing experience.  But, I acknowledge that it was opening night, and they definitely have issues to work out.  I'll 100% go back, though, because this is a new spot in my neighborhood, and that chicken is great- but I might limit it to take out only- though it's a bit expensive for take out- $30+ for a whole chicken.  I'm open to revising this review as well, and I wouldn't usually pan a new spot right away, but I can't stand by and let the community think that this is a 5 star spot.  It most definitely is not.

Added later:  Uh oh.  Here come more fake reviews.  Maybe I won't go back.
name: Earl

text:
I like this place a lot, and I'll be back.  I don't know much about Ramen, but I was in this neighborhood at lunchtime, and I saw a lot of good reviews.  The staff is friendly, and the inside is nicely decorated and comfortable (it was not so crowded that I sat next to anyone).  The patio would be righteous for happy hour on a nice day.

I had a bowl of the red, spicy, pork Tonkotsu.  It was hot and delicious, but it was the spiciest thing I've ever had!  I love spicy, food, but it was almost too much.  Next time I'll have a milder miso.  The noodles were amazing.

Be prepared to use chopsticks, because the menu says, "spoons are for amateurs."  Ha!

It's a little pricey - after tax, it was about $12.50 for a bowl at lunchtime, but if it's excellent for Ramen, then it's probably worth it.

One small caveat - the parking lot is really tight.  If you're driving a large vehicle, I recommend parking on the street.

text:

This store doesn't have the same atmosphere as the remodeled store on Plumb, but they more than make up for it in fast and friendly service. The team members on the register are quick to greet guests and are happy to handle any special requests you might have. They all seem happy to be at work and that translates to a consistently great product.

text:
We were in town to see a movie and decided to have dinner at Anton's beforehand which we found via OpenTable. Turned out to be a great choice! The food, service and atmosphere were all quite good. 

We really enjoyed the cozy dining room with its quaint decor and old time charm. It was a really nice spot to unwind, have a drink and engage in some conservation. The noise level was absolutely perfect; not too loud, not too quiet. 

Service was attentive and swift. They got us seated promptly upon arrival and dinner was served within 20 minutes of placing our order. The food was quite good too! I got the beef filet topped with gorgonzola along with a side of fingerling potatoes and sautéed vegetables. The steak was sublime and had great flavor, easily on par with any upscale restaurant and in my opinion, surprisingly better than a steakhouse like Ruth's Chris or Morton's. Yes, that good! My wife got the grab cake and had nothing but nice things to say about it. 

Overall, we had an excellent time at Anton's and would absolutely love to go back in the near future. I really hope the modest menu is updated often because I'd love to sample more of the chef's cooking. Five stars.

text:
