Tip: if you happen to call an order in, be sure to ask what their special pizza of the day is. I did not ask and they did not tell me, so I was disappointed when I got there to pick up my pizzas because I would have loved to try the special.
name: Sara

text: Great food and margaritas. The patio is a bit small, but nice! The staff is also very polite. Will be back.
name: Brooke

text: I can't imagine why every review is not 5 starts.  Tasty fast and healthy option, multiple locations friendly staff.    Some of the best food you can find sans meat.
name: David

text: Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Anyway, solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. It looked better online than it did in person. For the price I expected more than this. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait.
name: User

text:
I really like Kona Grill! It is a great place to go for any and all occasions. The food is eclectic, fun and really tasty. Their menu items range from, for example, sushi to pastas to salads and a nice selection of appetizers. It's definitely a good place for sharing a bunch of dishes/sushi. Like I said, with the menu items being full of a lot of flavor, if you are into good food and variety you want to try not just one entree, but sample of various menu items. This really makes sense here. 

Some of my favorite menu items are the avocado egg rolls which come with some sort of cilantro dipping sauce and a small portion of pickled veggies. I get this appetizer every time I go there. One of my all time favorite salads is at this restaurant: the Kona Chopped salad. This includes the macadamia nut chicken with avocado, cheese, bacon eggs etc with honey mustard. I also really enjoy the sushi in general. It is quite large of a sushi menu for having a lot of other menu type items. Their happy hour is definitely something to try out since it gives you half off of a large portion of what they offer on the regular menu.  I believe they have a late night happy hour as well so do check about those offers too. 

The atmosphere is quite fun as well. The bar is really cool because you can enjoy sitting both inside & outside. They also have a pretty nice size outside seating area. This is a popular place, so you should consider calling ahead for a reservation if you want to sit at a table. 

The service has been pretty good overall at the bar. I don't really have anything bad to say about this place except that it is sometimes really busy, crowded and loud, but its fun and overall a great experience.
name: Dr. Danielle

text:
Food was tasty and prepared pretty fast! I had the general tso tofu and my husband had the kung pao chicken. We both had a roll each as well - soft and delicious.

The servers were friendly and the place is well lit and decorated! 

Will be back!
name: Nupur

text:
Great stuff!! Food and service was great. 
For appetizers we had avacado artichoke dip and the sweet pea and avacado toast. Both were awesome!! 
For entrees my wife had the Dashi Ramen with shrimp skewer. Said it is delicious. I had the Spring Sea Scallops and lemon risotto which was tasty, but a had tad too much salt. 
Beer was cold and tasty as well as the sparkling water. 

Great experience! Fabulous food and even better service puts this at the top of our dining list.
name: William Thomas

text: This location pretty much still feels very much like its former restaurant Houston's. The food is good along with good service. I had ordered the grilled tuna salad and it was amazing. I also drank a yummy Sazarac, my second one was not as beautiful. For dessert the Key Lime pie had a clean taste and texture and a nice size.
name: Angela

text: Fresh Handmade Beignets! You should definitely try them! Period.
name: Piotr

text: If you want a filling breakfast that tastes like your momma made it, come here. Best biscuits and eggs!
name: Cooper

text: It's an average "cantina" with a decor that is just as confusing as the fact that they are cash only. Dry pork in the al pastor and basic, overall.
name: Robin

text: Fast service for a Friday night. Food was fresh and flavorful. I could actually understand what the staff were saying compared to other local take out places. They were really nice and patient when helping decide what to eat. The food wasn't overly salty, greasy, or sweet like most Chinese food take out. I will be back. I was really satisfied.
name: Ruth Shandale

text: Great food, the tortilla soup, and burger is amazing, the rotisserie is the best I've had in years, I will be back for sure!!!!!
name: Sam

text: Always awesome service and the food is always great!!! I have eaten at every locaation and everyone is consistently great.
name: Tom

text:
Great service and probs the best burgers in town. The big names in the burger business in Philly are Rex , Royal Tavern, Whiskey Burger and Good Dog in my opinion. The burgers at Guppy's are HUGE, quality meat, almost always perfectly cooked to order and inventive! The fries are yummy as well. 

The beer menu is kind of the downfall. I think they go for the best deals from their distributor which leads to not the best beers on their list. That being said, the list is long with many options and they always have tons of local beers. 

The secret of all secrets are their daily deals. They change each day, hence them being daily deals. Stand outs are their 5 dollar burgers on Monday, 5 dollar nachos on Saturday and 2 dollar tacos on Tuesday. 

So many restaurants have failed at this location. Guppy's definitely deserves to stay!
name: Carlos

text: Literally the worst chipotle location in existence. The trash is always over flowing, staff is extremely rude, and they are always out of EVERYTHING.
name: Kate

text: Stopped here on the last night in Tucson. One of the coolest restaurants I've ever been in as far as the setup and the atmosphere.  Our server was super-attentive and when she learned it was our first visit, brought us a free appetizer of pretzels and fondue.  It could easily serve 6 people.  The ribs were very good and the beer list was solid. It's a really awesome place.  Multiple bars, lots of seating and even though the huge lot was full, there was no wait
name: Tim

text: Always visit here when I arrive to NOLA...BBQ Shrimp are absolutely hands down my favorite & super delicious and worth the price!!
name: Delores

text: Sat us down super fast, the ambiance is totally chill and inviting. Food is yummy! Try the Cajun Chicken Pasta!!! Yummy!!! Jesse Jones is the bomb, sweet and accommodating. I requested her put my friend in her own table and she made it happen with out any questions!
name: Kenneth

text:
I always enjoy my food choices from Panera Bread but I did not like the Ham , egg, and cheese breakfast sandwich.   My egg was rubbery and I did not enjoy the ham.  It was a new item so I tried it and I did not like it 
Thumbs down
name: Sheila

text: The food is very good. Nice greasy spoon. They have so many specials for breakfast. I go there sometimes and I'm never dissatisfied
name: domenique

text: I don't really get some of the harsh reviews on here. The food was good and the service was easygoing. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. My experience was honestly fine. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Food was good and came out fast. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text: One of those meals where nothing is exactly wrong but you're not excited either. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. There were a couple things I liked and a couple things I probably wouldn't get again. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Ordered a few things and liked most of it.
name: User

text: So this was my favorite Mexican restaurant. I would drive 45 minutes to get here just so I could have my favorite dish if all time. I came here tonight only to find they changed the menu and my dish is not on the menu anymore!!!  Wtf???  Why oh why do restaurants change their menus. They just lost a customer. I won't be back. Devastated!!  Seriously. Just so so sad right now.
name: Beth

text: Tourist trap. Tourist trap. Tourist trap. I guess that's expected for the Bourbon Street area. Food is bland and not at all fresh. Would not recommend.
name: Nicole

text: This is my favorite subway location. They make a mean sandwich! They're always friendly and fast! Even when your kid is making war and explosion noises in the background!
name: Kadie

text:
Wow, where I do begin? I came here for a business dinner with a group of colleagues and had an amazing experience.

My friend and I started out at the bar, where the bartender described a delectable drink- the VIP. Pineapples soaked in citrus vodka for 2 weeks! It was amazing.

For dinner we started with shrimp cocktail, the goat cheese, and the mushroom flatbread. Everything was flavorful and really delicious. My favorite was the goat cheese. It was encrusted in walnuts and dripping with honey. Sweet raspberries adorned the crust of the baked cheese.

I also had truffle macaroni and it was perfection. The sauce was creamy and rich but not too heavy. For my entree I had the flakiest, most tender salmon. It fell apart with every forkful. The asparagus was tender and was a perfect complement to the salmon. 

I can't wait to come back!
name: Karnesha

text: Excellent breakfast spot. Christine and her team are the best. Check out there new menu it's awesome.
name: John

text: This was my first time going and I was a bit skeptical but I was completely wrong. I got the Triple Cheesesteak and I even added pickles and it was amazing. The flavor from the onions wasn't overpowering at all (and I don't like onions) the bread was toasted to perfection and the steak was nice and juicy. The fried had the perfect ammount of crunch and overall was a really good spontaneous lunch.
name: Brady

text: Heard so much about this place and tried to get in for three times before I could get a sandwich. The third time, the wait was an hour long. Is it worth it? For the experience? Yes! For the taste of food? Probably not. It's just the hype. In my opinion, the sandwich tastes alright. I am giving it a four for the experience.
name: Jeff

text: This is a really great spot, very clean, nice atmosphere, good food, friendly staff. Really good for All American food as they advertise and a lot of variety. Their sandwiches are really good.
name: Anne

text: Would probably stop in again if nearby. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. No big complaints, just a nice meal. so yeah kind of mixed on it. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. The food was good and the service was easygoing.
name: User

text:
I ordered the biscuit with egg & gravy.  I had the chai latte with almond milk.  It was good.  The food was ready in 4 minutes.  When you place your order they ask what type of animal would you be? I said lion. Then they ask your first name. They used the words Lion April to acknowledge my order was ready.  

I took two bites.  I found out my egg was runny.  That wasn't discussed or on the menu. ( how the egg was prepared). Nor was I asked when I placed my order.  I returned the food.  I have an immune disorder I can't eat runny eggs.   My new plate of food was ready in 2 minutes.  No problem.   I admired that.  


The restaurant was packed.  It was difficult to find a seat.  Either you sat communal with strangers or  went outside.  We chose outside.  It was so hot outside I put ice in my latte.  Our total was $20.00. I got a box to take my food home.  I couldn't finish it.  It was worth it.  I would eat here again. The biscuits were light and fluffy.  The parking lot is not large.  You may have to drive around to find s space.

text: Sushi options come in a jumbo size! Order less than normal. Good ambiance. Servers very nice, and manager came at the table to check of everything was good. Sushi menu with a excellent variety.

text:
Good stuff. Service was too slow, or I'd be rating it five stars. 
The food was exceptional. Tried the orange salad, gumbo, jambalaya, and grilled cheese (my daughter thought it was weird, but I loved it). It was just familiar enough to feel like comfort food and just spiced up enough to offer a surprise. 
We sat outside, and it was very pleasant. 
This is not dramatic or fabulous, but a very solid place.
name: Marlo

text: Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. For a busy night they handled it okay. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. Worth checking out. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Food was fresh and service was quick.
name: User

text: Ive been here a few times. As a vegetarian, they offer some really delicious foods! I loved their mixed menu- it's not just your typical eats. I've gone here for happy hour and they've got pretty affordable snacks that are delicious. Their use of spice and flavor is awesome.
name: Justine

text: This used to be one of the better barbecue restaurants in St. Louis.  We had a very disappointing visit there recently end it will be a while before we go back again. At 5:15 they were out of their brisket.  They suggested pulled pork or pulled chicken as a substitute. The pulled pork was so dry it wasn't edible and the chicken was lackluster and flavor with very little smoke flavor. Macaroni and cheese was cold. This begs the question is there less oversight in the kitchen with multiple locations now.

text: My boyfriend said I could pick anywhere I wanted to for our date night and I chose this place! The cafe is really cute and has a nice atmosphere. They have a nice variety of food and teas. The service was friendly and was very fast. I went with the teriyaki chicken bento box and a strawberry milk tea with boba. It was delicious! Can't wait to go back there again!

text:
We enjoy the loop area and had never dined at The Peacock Diner. It was approximately 11:30 when we arrived and seated ourselves. We were greeted and drinks were ordered. We were notified that they were out of coffee and tea. That was disappointing. Not sure how a diner that serves breakfast all day runs out of a staple like coffee.  We ordered fried pickles and the olive you cracker(5) to start. Pickles were standard fried pickles, the crackers are triscuits with can spray cheese and an olive, Yum! 
The boozy shake, Human Sacrifice was delicious. The main entrees we ate were the mac n cheese, three cheese grilled cheese, the turkey melt, loop trolley burger. All come with a choice of sides. Good size portions. Mac n Cheese was good and cheesy. You are eating at a diner and you get diner food. I can see college kids after a night out, eating here frequently. Okay overall experience.
name: Deb

text: Wow - for a new restaurant open less than a month, they have their act together. We ordered different plates so we could all taste a little bit of everything. The fish, shrimp and steak were all perfect. The service was incredible. Ask for Aisha, excellent, excellent, excellent. We will definitely be back. Prices are very reasonable for what you get.
name: Richard

text:
This place does some things really well and others not so much. The biscuits, I'm not a fan. They're more like dense hamburger buns...that's a big no for me.

The "bonuts" however were very tasty served with rich blueberry mash and creamy lemon mascarpone. Get those!

Eggs were properly cooked to order, well done bacon unfortunately was limp. Cheese grits were average as were the fried potatoes. Cappuccino was great! 

Southern Benny was blah with those bready biscuits, salty southern ham slivers and sausage gravy.

There's a line out the door, but I'm not sure it's warranted. IF I go back it would only be for the bonuts, eggs and cappuccino. That would make a nice breakfast.
name: Tara

text: I was on business travel and we went to the Kingfisher.  It was excellent.  I have the boullibaise (sic).  It was extremely tasty and lot of seafood.  I highly recommend the Kingfisher.  Will be back if in the area again.
name: Guy

text:
4.5 stars 

This place would get 5 stars if it weren't for the line that is always out the door, even on weekdays! It's a fast casual set up, meaning you order first before sitting which is why the lines are long. The food is excellent though, they have hot chicken options or elevated breakfast food. I usually get the princess, it's hot chicken on a biscuit with honey on it, delicious! The bonuts are also great, fried donut balls with a compote on top with whipped cream. Their other options are also good, they have something for everyone. Whether you want a Benny, omelette or yogurt they have you covered! Just be prepared to wait a while, and if you come on the weekends don't be surprised if it's at least 45 minutes.
name: Van

text: Good happy hour, excellent beer selection that changes really frequently, nice outdoor spaces with fire pits, a good choice for a large group. The food is pretty bad though, and the atmosphere is a bit commercial.
name: Sabrina

text:
hit and miss..have been here previously and all was pretty good. Yesterday went for a Caesar salad no croutons, with tomatoes and red onions. 
The lovely young lady with the colorful hair told her co-worker to finish the salad with no croutons. He misheard and added double croutons. Ok, so he started over with a fresh salad, no problem. He then proceeded to add red peppers but no onions. He was about to pour the salad dressing onto the salad directly when I asked for it on the side just in time. I also asked him if about the red onions. He said "no red onions, but red peppers" I responded with " I didn't order red peppers" He ignored me and handed me the salad with the red peppers and no onions. This is very poor customer service and am surprised as during previous visits the employees always asked multiple times just to be sure.
Besides picking out the Red Peppers which I could not eat, I also had to pick out about 1/3 of the Romaine lettuce as it was wilted and brown. 
I hope management will take action regarding these issues.

text: Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. A very pleasant experience. Would probably stop in again if nearby. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed.
name: User

text: So my cousin from London and his New Zealand friend visits Philly so I want to wow them with Philly food scenes.. they wanted Italian and immediately I thought if cafe aroma- great food, intimate and great prices. So we had reservations  for 5. four adults plus toddler. We were welcomed with high chair and one of the restaurant managers doted on my daughter. She got her a delicious plate of speghetti with red sauce and a baby spoon- my baby inhaled the food- afterwards got her a dessert of tiramisu cookies that can dissolve in milk- great for my baby. As for us grown ups, the food and service was impeccable. I enjoyed my meal, especially the arincini and garlic knots. They can accommodate big parties and have outdoor seating. This is my go to spot for visitors. BYOB
name: Esmahan

text:
This place is damn charming. Is it the little painted tiles in the bathroom with art on them? One of the little tile-vignettes is a sign that says: "No selling cat." That's a sign you'll see all over the city (along with "Be nice or leave.") 

Despite being born in Indianapolis, I'm not usually an ignorant hick. Since just about every house in the bywater had a cat slinking around the front door I saw these "No selling cat" signs and thought:

"Huh, what do you know? People enjoy pets so much here that sidewalk cat-peddling has become a common nuisance for business owners."

Okay, that was naive. In this case, yes, I was Woody Harrelson on Cheers. It turns out that the "No selling cat" means "Do not prostitute here."

But it ain't the tiles in the bathroom that make this place charming.

It is the food.

Look around in the morning and every single plate coming out of the kitchen is some sort of piled-high masterpiece of pastry and whipped cream or local delight. The effect of "Oh, I want THAT" coming from all directions at once is dizzying.

We felt like we found one of the gems of the city, here.

Perhaps adding to the overall experience was an unexpected loss. Our first time here, I got one of the best po boys I had in the city. 

It had a hot and sweet house-made BBQ sauce that conjured magic from those fried shrimp. It was never to be seen again. After that bright shining day, the po boy never returned to the menu. Possibly making this the only "po boy-free" menu for miles around. 

But everything we tried was either very good or great. House-made sauces, desserts, everything.

Grit Fries - an awesome invention. Perfect little crispy creamy geometric forms. You want to make a grit-fort but you eat each one you pick up to stack.

Biscuits and Gravy - are great compared to other areas of the country, with fluffy biscuits and real-cream tasting gravy. But you get the sense the pancakes and waffles are their breakfast wheelhouse.

Fried Chicken - ask for the house chicken-finger dipping sauce alongside this, because it doesn't come with the sauce unless you ask. I tried this just after my "Willie Mae's Scotch House" experience. I was still reeling from that, but this stuff is better than any fried chicken you'll get outside the South.

Praline Bacon - yes, it is praline bacon. Although not crunchy, it is ambrosial, increasingly so with each candied strip. Try sharing a plate with someone and find out just how strong that relationship really is.
name: Chris

text: We really enjoyed our dinner at Columbia! We booked this place because apart from the fact that it has over 7,000 reviews, it's the oldest restaurant in Florida. The service was above and beyond and the food was delicious. We started off with the 1905 salad, one of their signature dishes. It's good and refreshing but it's nothing you can't recreate at home. The crab and lobster artichoke appetizer was delicious, as well as the paella Valenciana. The portion was big enough for 2, so definitely shareable. The white chocolate bread pudding was one of the best I've had. If you're in the Tampa area, I highly recommend this place for dinner.
name: Marcelle

text: First visit to Bob's last night. The steak was awesome. On par with Morton's and Jeff Ruby's. I had the filet mignon.  Four of us all tired different steaks except one had salmon. Everyone was pleased. Great sides and desserts too! Everyone, ages 22-54, was pleased. Service was awesome also.
name: Gina

text: A really building and atmosphere. Menu is updated daily and I had the catfish - maybe the best fish dish I've had. They are very creative with the menu and ingredients and the wait staff know their stuff. Service is not only knowledgeable but also polite. They have a solid whisky selection and made an excellent manhattan, custom with whisky of your choice. Their shrimp and grits is really good - nice appetizer to share with the table. Pecan pie with sweet cream ice cream was a tasty way to close tour the meal. This is a nice change of pace to enjoy with a date/spouse while in Nashville.
name: Jason

text: Unique atmosphere! Great happy hour. Worth a visit! Ceviche was very good as were the Brussels sprout appetizer. Sushi was yummy too!
name: Alicia

text: Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Not bad for a quick meal. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. The food was good and the service was easygoing. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. No big complaints, just a nice meal. For the price I expected more than this. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable.
name: User

text:
Solid 4 stars for Verbena. Had a decent meal a little while back.

Came early and had the restaurant to myself pretty much. Service was fine, timing of meal was good. Overall the food was tasty, not anything super interesting but there were solid flavors and use of textures on the plates. Bread service was fine (warm bread and good olive oil). For my appetizer, I had the peanut glazed pork cheeks. This was my favorite of the night, delicious pork cheeks served over rice. Very much reminded me of some Filipino dishes I grew up with - the pork was perfectly tender, the glaze was peanut/soy based, and the bites with rice were perfect. For my entree, I had the ribeye. It was cooked perfectly medium rare and topped with a chimichurri, portion was a bit small for the price. Cauliflower appeared on the plate 3 ways (pickled, puree, and roasted), but the best aspects of the plate for me were the mushrooms, truffle vinaigrette, and I think there was a layered potato cake too if I recall correctly. 

I'd come back to Verbena - one of few higher end options in Kennett, wish there were more mushrooms on the menu though
name: David

text: The only thing we enjoyed were the truffle chips. We had a party of 7 and nobody was impressed with anything. The fried chicken needed more seasoning. The quinoa patty melt was a complete bore. The fish tacos were skimpy. The pulled pork was just pork on a bun. The drinks were average and took forever to arrive. The food came out slow and one of our meals (the mac and cheese) trailed by 10 minutes. Service was incredibly slow even though the restaurant wasn't very crowded and even though drink and water refills were offered, they never arrived.
name: Lisa

text: This location has been closed. There's a new one opening on the other side of the road on Telecom Pkwy by the new RaceTrac, but it's not open yet.
name: Bryan

text: This place is really good. Love the re model of it I came in for my birthday brunch and our server was very sweet she sang happy birthday and sounded awesome. The food was reasonably priced and very flavorful. I got steak and eggs and it is really hard for me to eat eggs somewhere because they normally make my eggs wrong. THESE eggs though.... they were perfectly cooked middle runny and white cooked thoroughly (it's like magic)   Definitely will come back on my next visit to New Orleans.
name: Megan

text:
Firstly, Mokabees has the fastest WiFi of any place I've been in St Louis, it also has a great atmosphere for studying or conversations. There are electrical outlets at most inside tables and even a few outlets on the outdoor patio, so SCORE for getting the internet coffee part right Mokabees. 

As to food, Mokabees has a lot of selection with most dishes being decent to very good to my taste. As far as drinks go, You can get an above average coffee concoction here, but you may have to work on individual baristas as there is considerable variance between the 7 different baristas I've had make my orders here. 

Note: the politics are on vibrant display at Mokabees with the staff being mostly classically liberal and many clientele being far leftist genocidal maniacs. I consider this a plus because as a person with political views to the right of Attila the Hun, I enjoy discussions with unbelievers.

As long as you aren't a prima-donna requiring servers to worship you, or so insecure in your politics that you can't withstand being around others that might think differently than you, give Mokabees a try, it's my favorite coffee shop in STL
name: Joel

text: My first time here and normally Thai isn't my favorite.  I had the Beef Noodle Soup and the broth was D E L I C I O U S! The staff is very courteous, they even bow and thank you for coming. So it's the entire experience here! The parking lot was packed, but it took no time to get a seat and I was very pleased! I will be coming here again real soon!

text: Walked in no one greeted me no one seemed to care if I wanted to order any food so I left
name: Steve

text: We went to Amigo Joe's the other night to meet up with some friends. All in all it was a pretty good experience. We had drinks at the bar while we waited for our friends. The margaritas were strong and delicious. We also had some chips and salsa which were good. The bartender and hostess waiting on us were able to get us a table for 4 in the bar area when our friends got there. Amigo Joe's has Fri and Sat happy hour so we were happy to get a table in the bar area. We started with cheese dip and guacamole. I had a chimichanga. My husband had street tacos. Everything was very good. We definitely will be back!

text: 11/10 for great service... awesome staff.  Cubano (Mihami Vice) was solid and greens paired nicely.  Great/simple sandwich joint with downtown Boise vibe.

text: Very disappointed with service..1.Asked for highchair and got seated in area that didn't allow so waited 15 minutes for booster seat with an active toddler 2.Asked for soup pre meal and it arrived 5-10 minutes after main dish 3. At food delivery asked for additional utensils as we got 2 not 3 sets..after my husband ate 1/2 meal with his fingers my husband walked to bar and asked manager for a set along along with a drink refill (that had never been checked in 1st 45 minutes at table). 4. After waiting 15 minutes for check and no sign of waiter asked other server for it..luckily manager who came over to print check realized that my husband was who asked for refill and utensils so ended up comped meal..after he originally mentioned just a discounted one.  So kudos to manager but won't be back.

text: Everything we had was delicious. Loved the flavor of the house salad, and the red sauce was probably the most delicious I've ever had. The spiedini prosciutto was delicious!!!! We'll definitely be back!
name: Allie

text: Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Food was fresh and service was quick. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. Food was good and came out fast.
name: User

text:
Attention tourists. Avoid Katie's. You won't like it. 

Ok. My opening will probably not change anything, but a dude has to try. 

Katie's is a traditional New Orleans neighborhood joint that everyone and their mom has heard about. That means you are likely to encounter massive wait times and lots of people who say you guys instead of y'all. Is it good? Yes. Is it worth the wait? That's up to you. 

I've been to Katie's several times. Most of those times involved someone suggesting it, me pulling up, and me driving away saying hell no. While I am known for being incredibly patient, I really dislike waiting around unless the place is worth it. 

Luckily for me, I lucked upon Katie's right at opening a few times and didn't have to wait at all. 

The food, and service are typical New Orleans neighborhood joint. That means service is friendly and fairly prompt. The food will please locals and visitors alike. 

My most recent visit I had the redfish special. It involved grilled redfish topped with crabmeat, shrimp, and a side of some sort of veggies for around $20. I can't be certain it was actually redfish (aren't their rules against commercial fishing if redfish), but it was very good. If you've never had grilled redfish topped with shrimp and crabmeat, you're really missing out. 

Other items worth trying include their poboy, gumbo, and fries with cheese and gravy. 

I'm a fan of Katie's. I think you will be too. Just come early to avoid the long wait.
name: John L.

text: People are being a little dramatic in these comments honestly. The food was good and the service was easygoing. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. My experience was honestly fine. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced.

text: The food is always good, the portions are the right size, and the service from the owner is always great.  I was worried the meal.soze would be small.  The size is on par with what calories you should be eating.  Overall extremely happy with the weekly food service

text:
My husband and I stopped in for a bite to eat last night (8-30-19) and were disappointed by both the food and the service. While Marianna was polite she seemed lacking in customer service and the details of the contents of the menu when we inquired. 
My husband and I have both been in the food service industry and were not impressed by our serving sizes of the appetizers and the menu is overpriced for the serving size. The drinks were watered down.

The only reason I'm giving 2 stars was because of the view.

Not bad for a quick meal. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Food was fresh and service was quick. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything..
name: User

text: For a busy night they handled it okay. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. It was crowded but still moved along. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. Pretty happy with it overall. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly.
name: User

text: This place is interesting. It has 3 floors but at the time we visited only the first floor was in use. But the bar on the second floor looked like a perfect spot to have my birthday gathering. The menu was small which I LOVE! My fiancé ordered the chicken Caesar salad with the dogfish head draft. I had the chicken sliders with a glass of Rośe. My sliders were absolutely delish. Everything stayed together and there wasn't too much sauce where it was all over. My fiancé enjoyed his salad and beer. Bartender's suggestion of Rośe was great however it's just a little bitter for my liking. Was a great alternative to white Zinfandel which they didn't have. Bartender was a doll and was very attentive helping out the waitress. The waitress was a sweetheart and took great care of us. Definitely want to visit this place in the evening and see how their night life is!

text: This pizza place has a great selection of chicken meals. They prepare it fresh every morning, and it's obvious in the flavor it exerts. I experienced the Grilled chicken panini with lettuce tomatoe and bacon and it exceeded my taste expections, expecially for the price. Fresh produce and served with fries and a drink. The service was above and beyond that of a local pizzeria. If you are in a chicken mood i highly recommend this place.
name: Sir

text:
My wife and I chose to have our dinner in the self-seating bar area with bar height tables. Ambience of the outdoor seating area is great. There were a lot of people, but it never felt loud or overwhelming. Perfect blend for a nice dinner, and a place to bring your friends to watch a game on the tvs above the bar. 

I had the shrimp and sweet corn chowder, and it was great. The rest of the food was okay. It took anywhere between 30-40 mins to get our food, and my wife and I ordered a very simple dinner. Soup, baked potato, flatbread, and a side. And when we received our food, we could tell the flatbread had sit for a little bit. Dough was also kinda "gummy". And it didn't help to get a flat Coke...

But, overall, I'd come again to see if the food may come out better. The atmosphere makes it worth it.

text: If I could score Hattie B's higher than 5 I would! This is my absolute favorite restaurant in Nashville. I have gone out of my way to return every time I come into town. It's a cute atmosphere. You order at the counter and then take a number and wait for your food to be dropped off at your table. The wait time is never too long even on a busy afternoon. The sweet tea is perfect, not too sweet! The chicken is unlike anywhere else I have ever been. I highly recommend the pimento mac and cheese as a side also! I splurged and tried the peach cobbler after my meal and it was good. I would add a scoop of ice cream on top next time. If you are visiting Nashville definitely make it a priority to stop by Hattie B's!!

text: Johnson's barbecue has been around forever and once you eat you'll know immediately why. very good from top to bottom. The service is always pretty ,friendly ,very helpful and really great atmosphere. Your hit in the face with That wonderful smoked barbecue aroma that you've been waiting for all week. text:
Tonight was my first time here at Hobey's Coffee Shop. We've been to the Steakhouse in Hobey's and definitely love it there, too, but this is a totally different restaurant. Both worthy of a trip, for sure!

Anyway, we loved it so much and I was shocked that it wasn't already on Yelp when I tried to check-in. Yes, it's in Sun Valley, but not that far in... AND it is worth the drive for some amazing food you wouldn't necessarily expect.

First of all, they have a good variety of choices. We all three had totally different meals. 

My teen son had the Ultimate Burger (bacon double cheeseburger) and fries. He is a connoisseur of them and highly approved! 

Hubby got one of tonight's specials: All You Can Eat Spaghetti Dinner with Bolognese Sauce served with Garlic Bread and choice of soup or salad. He didn't need to ask for more, because the first serving was plenty.  He really enjoyed it.

I chose the Grilled Salmon with a baked potato (your choice of potato), veggies, and choice of soup or salad. I chose the soup of the day which was Pork Pazole Soup. Oh. My. Taste Buds!  I had never had this before and it was amazing!  I could easily eat a whole big bowl of this for dinner! The salmon was also grilled and seasoned to perfection. I expected something nice, but this was honestly a steakhouse quality.... for SO much less. See the pictures I took.  Even the veggies were more tasty than those at most places. They were seasoned to perfection. I am not sure if it was just this particular chef (on a Thursday night) is just THAT good or if the norm, but I was very impressed!

It's in a casino and there is smoking on the way in, but not nearly as bad as several others in the Reno/Sparks area. It's also not that long of a walk through the casino. The parking lot was well lit and not in some "scary area". I think its location is why many probably don't know about it or go there. It was easily at least half full tonight, so someone sure knows about it! I'm thinking that it is considered a local secret. Check it out for sure!
name: Stephanie

text:
I could go in for a very long review but I decided to boil it down(!) to the essentials. 

Price:  $175 for two. Shared a salad. Shared a dessert. Had one drink and one wine. 

The drink:  ordered a classic Old Fashoined.   I get carded in Costco.  The bartender is decades younger than me (he should be carded) and I am certain he has never tasted a classic Old Fashoined. No cherry. At the price I expected a luxardo cherry, of course:  classic!  

The room:  50+ seats. A third booths. High ceilings and no acoustic walls. It was so loud but it was a party. Not a dinner crowd for sure. Maybe we wandered into a hipster joint!

Dinner:  small portions. I don't expect Mandinas seafood platter but a piece of grouper ($28) the size of a small valentines envelope!  We were hungry when we got home. 

Cooking:  excellent. The ghost of Gautreanxs. Of course. I expected nothing less from Sue. She can cook!  

Dessert: let's deconstruct it. 4 raspberries probably from Costco. Good and fresh. A teaspoon dollop of whipped cream. A half teaspoon of caramel sauce. Ten crystals of kosher salt. All on top of a very small ramkin dish of nice chocolate pudding. It was promoted as shareable at $11. Not really. 

Well,  you get the picture. Driving home we listed five great New Orleans restaurants that we would give 5 stars and come home with $50 and a leftover box. 

You ask which ones:  ok:  Brigstens. Station 6 and Gabrielle's. There are others. Zasu needs to step up in this town. We take no prisoners!  Enjoy!
name: Stephen

Even then he didn't greet us or smile and didn't even say he would be right with us or if we had any questions to let him know. It was a very unpleasant beginning and start to our date night. I don't know if it's because he was the only bartender or if it was that busy, but I think he could've at the very least acknowledged us when we sat down right in front of him or told us he would be right with us. I was trying to give the situation the benefit of the doubt the whole dinner, but nothing got better because it did eventually slow down. He simply took our orders and handed us our orders. text:
Pretentious, over priced, overrated wine bar. Welcome to New Hope, where they think they're just "it". Unfortunately Nektar Wine Bar failed to hit the mark, miserably. 

At first we were seated in the back of the restaurant which is half outside. After being seated a nice enough server named Justin came over to greet my girlfriend and I. He started by saying how unique and great their menu was, and after I had already rifled through it for a few minutes by that point it simply wasn't impressive. Maybe it's special by new hopes' standards? He then started recommending flights of wine which were very pricey but something that interested me. The wine was nothing special at $40 for 3, 3oz pours. He then recommended the charcuterie board and since this part of the menu was extensive, I let Justin pick the meats and cheeses in order to pair with our wine. Big mistake. This kid made no effort to pair our wine with the food. He simply upcharged us for all the most expensive smoked and cured meats. I could've easily ordered the meats with +$1 -$4 indicators marked next to them myself bud. Such a shameful move for this kid to pull, (like I wouldn't notice) The food was all just ok. We also got truffle raviolis. A joke. Like chef Boyardee cheese ravioli with a truffle cream sauce instead of tomato sauce, righteous . Tuna tartare was ok. Came with like 4 chips to dip though, insufficient. And by far the worst, beef cheek stew or something along those lines. Recommended by Justin, it was a terribly seasoned dish. I've had nice ethnic stews before but this was just bad. Tasted like someone accidentally dropped the bottle of cinnamon into the stew and no one noticed but the customer. Eventually my girl ordered her own glass of wine for barely less than $20. None of the wine was "write home to mom", in fact it was more like worse than a $20 bottle from your local LQ but at $20 a glass. Fruit flies almost immediately flew into it causing her to not want to finish the glass of tainted wine. I told the server and he laughed and said "must've been good wine!" Real funny Justin. I wouldn't quit your day job of serving tables and upcharging unsuspecting customers anytime soon though kid. 


I've never ever in my life tipped less than 20% until this day. Congrats Justin thanks for comping my girls fruit fly wine out of your tip son. All said and done skip the goofy pretentious wine bar in new hope unless that kind of thing is up your alley. "Wonder what else goes up your alley if you frequent this spot" 

Good food is hard to come by but if you want a great culinary experience than Portland, Oregon is a must visit. At least until these underwhelming, overpriced spots can get it right and not hire a server like Justin who truly only cares about the money and a phony experience
name: Lee

text:

text:
Brunch review!

This is probably one of my favorite spots for brunch in philly for food and value. I always recommend Amada for brunch. They're brunch special includes a coffee or tea, basket of pasteries, and three dishes for $27 per person. They also also have $5 brunch cocktails. 

My fav dish on the brunch menu is the avocado toast. This is a must try! So much flavor. We also tried the seasonal berries, crab benedict tortilla francesa, patatas rosti, and chorizo. The berries were very fresh and sweeten with a touch of honey. The patatas rosti and chorizo are also very good and great shares for the table. 

The pastry basket in the beginning is also amazing. The cherry fig jam served with it was fantastic. I really enjoyed the olive oil cake in the basket. 

Staff is always friendly. The place is actually much bigger on the inside than it looks from the outside and I've never had an issue getting a reservation the same day for a Sunday brunch.

text: AMAZING TACOS. The pastors are my favorite. Juicy, fresh, flavorful, and the onions and extra sauces that they offer with tacos is a great touch. I eat here at least once a week! Prices are great and service is wonderful too!
