text:
I think there's a bit of grade inflation in the reviews for vegan restaurants.  Vegans want them to be good, they want to reward restaurateurs who offer plant-based food, and they don't want to criticize the one fancy vegan restaurant in town.  I'm not going to play that game.  Our Thursday night visit to Oliver's was quite disappointing on all dimensions.

We arrived for an 8 pm Thursday reservation, which was apparently too late for Santa Barbara.  No one was at the host stand to greet us, and several waiters walked by while we were waiting. 

I ordered a virgin juice cocktail, but they delivered me one containing gin. The waitress caught the error after a few minutes and was very apologetic.  I didn't send it back (I'm not an alcoholic and wasn't going to let a perfectly good drink go to waste), but she still billed me full alcohol price for the drink, and the virgin one she delivered later. That's a tacky way to make $7. Don't put me in the position of being the jerk customer throwing out good drinks, just comp me with a correct drink when you make a mistake like that. 

The food was pretty average, generally underseasoned and severely undersalted. We used up almost the entire bowl of Himalayan salt that was placed on the table.  Perhaps they undersalt their food because of all the hypertensive old folks living in the Santa Barbara area?

None of the dishes had the "wow" factor of dishes I've had at well-known--and frankly much, much better--vegan fine dining restaurants in LA (Silver Lake), Oakland, and Philadelphia. 

Artichoke "crab cakes": undersalted and underseasoned 

Mushroom tostada: seemed like they left it under a hot lamp too long, the tostada was not tostada, but soggy. 

Margherita flatbread: just fine, nothing to write home about. I've had a better vegan pizza at a cheap pizzeria in a dodgy neighborhood in Riverside, CA. 

Truffle potatoes: acceptably tasty, but not all that original. Is this 2005?

Apple salad: best item that we had, but no wow factor 3.5/5 

They gave us the bum's rush at the early hour of 8:55 pm, asking us to order dessert before the kitchen closed.  Busboys were shutting down the restaurant around us as we were finishing our under-sweet granola-like apple crumble dessert.  The stingy portion of vegan ice cream topped off an underwhelming dessert and an underwhelming evening.
name: Clayton

text: I've been to the Capitol Grille in Las Vegas, Miami, King of Prussia and NYC and this location remains in first place for quality meals and service. Lovely place,  get the lobster bisque- it has lobster meat almost too big for your spoon.
name: Lizz

text: Despite the poor grammar and spelling on their menus and signage, the food is pretty tasty. Love their shrimp, potatoes and corn. Cant remember what sauce I had but I think they charge you extra for that? (I could be wrong) However, it is far too expensive here. I'd rather get a garlic tray from a hole in the wall and eat it in someone's driveway because for 2 people to eat a satisfying amount, you can be out nearly $60 and it's by no means a lavish establishment. On that same note, the decor is TOO much in my opinion. I'm also not a fan of how environmentally conscious this establishment is not. Think about all the plastic that gets thrown out daily from the hot seafood trays throughout the day.
name: Heaven

text:
Classic Cheeseburger and fries with a glass bottle coke! One of the best ways to live your life. 

Dining in the shack out front or to-go, this is always a good choice!

I always want to try something else, but their burgers are just so good and grass-fed.
name: Alyssa

text: i ordered a chicken burrito and it fell apart, because of the shitty rolling job, and so i thought to myself "i might as well have gotten a damn bowl, even tho i wanted a burrito". #1stworldproblems
name: Billy

text: OMG! We used to go to the other location this family owned.. and it was amazing. Then randomly we just kinda realized the food just wasn't as good anymore. So this year (Sept) we ended up at Dian Xin after seeing a yelp review. Crazy enough, it was the family that had previously owned the other place we loved!! Insane, but an amazing find. The food here is worth the wait time, the cramped seating and even the air of busy all around this place... because their food is fire! The sizzling garlic shrimp.. that's all I have to say. This visit we had the kids with us so we couldn't dine in, regardless we did take out. So worth it. This place is worth every penny and more. Plus, the family that runs it are such great people. Can't recommend this place enough.
name: Farheen

text: Open Hands is absolutely amazing! From the moment you walk in you are greeted with the best hospitality. I came for a 2 day trip from Texas and am so grateful to have found this small family owned restaurant. It was by far some of the best food I had on my trip. My brother and I ordered the "Seafood Stuffed Fish Platter" which came with Mac n' Cheese, Sweet Peas, Hawaiian Bread, and a cake. Originally we had planned to split the platter between the two of us, but the moment we took the first bite we locked eyes and in that moment I knew; I just knew that war was upon us. It was one of the hardest fights of my life. I struggled through fending my brother away from the food while still trying to eat my own food. Now as I sit here typing this review with a black eye and unbuttoned shorts and looking at my brother sprawled out on the floor I know that: 1. I am the alpha sibling and 2. I will miss Open Hands all the way from Texas. The moral of the story is definitely stop by open hands and try their food. You will definitely not regret it!!!
name: Braulia

text: Not sure why this place has such split reviews, but my experience was mostly fine. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Not a bad stop, just not one I'm rushing to repeat.
name: User

text: Seated at table. Waiter brought water 5  minutes later. 10 minutes later still no waiter to order from. Party of 6 across from us said they ordered 15 minutes ago and still no food. We got up and left. Food is generally good but don't go on the weekend.
name: Ray

text: Props to being the first in St. Louis to serve Viet-Cajun!  Menu could be a little bigger but for what they do have they were all good.  The place was busy and the service was good.
name: Richie

text:
I was craving tzatziki so off to Effie's we went. My boyfriend and I arrived a few minutes early for our 6pm reservation on a Friday. They were happy to seat us right away. Our waiter brought an ice bucket for our wine and some fresh hot pita. The pita was amazing and started us off on a high note.

We started with the tomato and cucumber salad with added feta. The salad was a generous portion and more than enough for two. My one complaint here is that the amount of added feta was not worth $6. (The feta was very good, but minimal in portion).

After the feta, we each had a chicken souvlaki platter. The chicken was tender and well seasoned. The rice was flavorful but a little over cooked so was a little sauce. The vegetables were fine, but bland. We were treated to a compliment dessert (galaktoboureko) that was very good and very sweet.

My major complaint is that we chose to sit inside and there were a large number of flies flying around. It was less than appealing as we ate.

Even as I write my review, I am still on the fence about Effie's. BUT I am willing to give it another chance to confirm my feelings.
name: Beth

text: Love this place! Great cajun food. Not as spicy as you'd get in New Orleans but good. Good drink specials. Their Hurricanes are very tasty. The atmosphere is colorful and has some history to it. A real New Orleans feel. I really like their shrimp and cheese grits. Hubby enjoys the Jambalaya. He gets it extra spicy. Will definitely be back.
name: Connie

text: VERY BAD. Wasted $50.12 which included a 15% tip for the driver for a large pizza and 12 wings. I ordered online for home delivery 08/16/19, paid with CC.  Tracker said 19-29 minutes for delivery; it arrived in one hour.  That was not the big issue. The box was literally folded and the pizza was stuck to the box.  The driver laughed and said it was a good pizza and stated that is how he got it and the wings caused the box to collapse.  Still laughing he mentioned tip, I stated I was stupid enough to include it with payment.  I closed the door in his laughing face.  I called the store and spoke to the manager to register a complaint.  The manager offered to re-send the driver with a new pizza.  I declined, he then asked what I wanted...I stated nothing, I would Yelp his store.  Not even a sorry.  Never again!
name: Andrew

text: A true gourmet restaurant. I had the boulliabase(sp?) which was a mixture of some items you wouldn't think go together but they did. And we'll. Wife had the NY strip which was outstanding. Lobster salad was the appetizer. Really done well. Owner/manager was ever present to make sure all was to your liking. Try it
name: George

text: Slowest Wendy's ever. Drive thru is awful. Waited 15 minutes just to get to order with only 2, yes 2, cars in front of me.
name: Ariana

text: I don't really get some of the harsh reviews on here. Food was fresh and service was quick. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. The music was louder than it needed to be. My experience was honestly fine. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer..
name: User

text:
I love the amount of these seafood spots popping up! Okay so here are the facts. 

Pros
The seasoning is the best I have had at any of these style seafood spots in Indy
Huge portions
Service is great 
Quick to seat us and serve us 
Clean, fresh, comfortable atmosphere

Cons
Super packed with people tables very close
The amount of oil in our bags was a lot and it took away from the amazing seasoning
The clams I had most were only shells, no clam 
Parking is hard to get here 

Our server Ivy was awesome - best server hands down!!!
name: Lauren

text: It looked nice inside and the dish was filling and satisfying. Planning to come there again. They have complementary valet.
name: Kevin

text: The Tuesday night vegetarian buffet was fantastic and we can't wait to enjoy it regularly!!
name: Dana

text: Decided to eat a late lunch here.  Arrived a little after 1.  More parking was available than I had ever seen.  Hostess seated me right away. ....  I sat and I sat.  The hostess came back through three times, once clearing a large table.  Three other tables in the section had people seated.  They were all finishing their meals.  The waitress checked on them,  but never came to my table.  I finally just left.  Told the hostess that no one ever waited on me.  She said,  "Have a nice day."  I am not certain why they ignored my presence.  I looked around,  two of the three tables appeared to have folks over 60 at them,  so I don't think it was age discrimination.  I was the only Caucasian person in that section.  I'm a good tipper.  I leave anywhere from 25-50%,  so the waitress missed out on a decent tip,  and the restaurant missed a sale.  I had the impression that the restaurant was extremely poorly managed, that employees did not feel compelled to adhere to any performance standard,  and that this location of Logan's will probably go out of business.
name: Debra

text: The first few bites were promising and then it kind of leveled out. Anyway, nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. Also, delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. Anyway, the sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something i'm still thinking about two days later. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Anyway, the portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough.
name: User

text: today i came in to the restaurant and from start to finish i enjoyed my time. the food was ok but the service i received i think ill want to return just for that, the server kevin was so friendly, he had our entire table in good spirts, i really need enjoyed him and can't wait to see him again!
name: Rasone

text: In town for a work conference and needed a lunch spot each day that was walking distance. We chose this based off yelp reviews. It DID NOT disappoint. The owner took our large owner and was spicy and kind at the same time! We had a variety of food (turkey sandwich, roast beef sandwich, 1/2 sandwich with potato soup, and salad and spinach and artichoke soup). The portion sides are HUGE! You can share one plate with two people. Make sure to stop in for a quick lunch if your town!!!
name: Carla

text:
My know that New Orleans is known for spicy, singular cuisine reflecting its history as a melting pot of French, African and American cultures. The first evening we decided to go to Cohon restaurant and it was a right decision! 

There was a line and we had to wait about an hour but as we did not make a reservation it was a good sign. We were sited at the bar table near the stove. It was nice, warm and cosy.

We had wood-fired oesters, roasted brussels sprout salad, fried alligator with chilli garlic mayonnasie, catfish courtbouillion. All was amazing, tasty and prepared in a delicious way. I personally prefer hot brussels sprout but they were still a good choice.

In short, very good food, reasonable prices. We will definitely come back when next time in NO.
name: Piotr

text: The best fried chicken I've ever eaten. The wait staff are so courteous!!!  Worth the hour wait in line. I'm coming back again!!!!
name: Minni

text: Great place for bar semi outdoor or sidewalk dining. Great service, nachos a must. Tacos are small portion but very good, you may want to add a side or two. Great for fun, casual dining
name: Madeline

text: I ordered the steak and chicken finger combo,, when the server brought the food he had placed the order he had put on bbq chicken. I told him and he said he would bring me the fingers. When they brought them they were over fried. I had to peel the breading off just to eat them. We eat there 3 to 4 times a month. We will not go there again.
name: Lola

text: Excellent pizza and friendly family service.  Father and son owners usually here during the day.  They know how to treat their customers.   The food is excellent as well and only place in the area where you can get individual slices.   This is my go to place when in Yardley.
name: Kenneth

text: This place is super friendly and cozy. The music is super chill, the whole vibe is super chill. The floor is literally clean enough to eat off of.. Which I had to do a few times!! I just kept dropping stuff.
name: Brandon

text: Great sushi .... friendly staff .... the albacore special is so good .... clean .... I love this place we go here atleast once a week ....
name: Jessica

text: I have eaten a lot of shrimp poboys, but this has to be one of the top THREE I have ever eaten. (I am 60 years old).  It was so fresh. There was shrimp falling off, everytime I ate a bite. Loved the fries. The staff was nice and knowledgeable. I used to go to Mahoney's, but I am sold on NOLA Poboys.
name: Anita

text: One of those meals where nothing is exactly wrong but you're not excited either. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. not sure I'd order the same thing again. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean.
name: User

text:
I came here for lunch. Everyone at work talks about how great the cheese steaks and burgers are! I ordered a bacon cheeseburger- no cheese  combo. It came with fries and a soft drink. The burgers are made fresh to order and the grill is right in front of you so you can literally see them make your food. Once my burger was done it went to the prep  station where they dress your burger however you like. I think my burger has 3-4 slices of bacon on it and he broke them in half so there was a good ratio of burger to bacon on my sandwich. The buns are large so if you know you want a thick burger go for it and get 2 patties instead of one.  My fries were hot and lightly dusted ( per my request) with seasoning salt. They put 2 mini cups of ketchup in my box. I asked for extra and they gave me packets of Red Gold . If you are a ketchup snob just opt for the packets instead of what they put in your to go box. 
I will be back I want to try the loaded cheese fries
name: Felicia

text: Beautiful bday experience from start to finish! Oysters, octopus to start...artful presentations and excellent quality. My bf had the wagyu burger and I tried the scallops for main course ...both were delectable. Finished with special bday dessert they provided complimentary and we also tried the black swan dessert - so awesome! Wonderful service, ambiance, cocktails (Steve Martin and his wife were dining next to us which was a fun bonus :)...highly recommend this lovely place
name: Amber Dawn

text:
Decent neighborhood Taiwanese and Chinese food. The food's super affordable, made really quickly, and tastes great for the price. They hold back on the spice quite a bit, but it doesn't stop me from ordering their other stuff.

My go-to's the popcorn chicken. Super similar to karaage, but more garlic-y.
name: Mitch

text: Great service and staff. Quick and delicious food. Got the chicken parm platter. Great price with enough food for multiple people or meals.
name: Johnny

text:
[777]

We were in the area so we wanted to check out these Premium Outlets.

Parking was TOUGH!  They even offer a paid section where you park your car for $5. Almost like valet but no valet.

The layout of the outlets was nice with tons of outdoor space which included a grassy area for the kids to play in.

Tons of cool stores to choose from.

I'm not sure if I will be back.  It's a hike plus parking was too tough.
name: Cindy

text: I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. The music was louder than it needed to be. Parking was annoying, although that's prob more about the area than the restaurant. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Will be back. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Food was good and came out fast. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly.
name: User

text: This used to be a fun diner with good food and service. On a recent visit it became clear that things have changed. It was clear that the waitstaff, kitchen, and management were overwhelmed and the place wasn't even that busy. It just seems to be poorly run. The food quality is also terrible. I ordered a breakfast burrito that was cold and gross. Gas station burritos are of better quality than the garbage they served me.
name: Mike

text:
Best lunch I've had in a while...

Was browsing trying to kill time before a ball game and the name won me over. The tri tip sandwich was PHENOMENAL.
name: Kelsey

text: My wife and I stopped here for late lunch/ early dinner. Wow is all I can say. We tried the octopus appetizer with humans. It was amazing. The lamb chops had the best flavor and quality of meat that we have had in along time. The waitress was so pleasant and friendly. Gyro platter was great. Greek food is a passion of mine and this place lived up to our expectations. Will stop here often.
name: Jeffrey

text: Well mom and I stopped in on our way home from shopping. Mom had a great dinner mine ,not so much.  I got the "fish" and chips.  What came out to me was what at first I thought was cod. Nope as soon as I took off the half a pound of batter on every tiny portion I discovered it looked and tasted like tilapia. Which is fine except for the price I was paying I expected it to be be cod. Also the fries were very crispy on the outside and nothing on the inside. The waitress only came by once at the beginning of the meal so she didn't know of the issue, no manager to be found.  Cue to check out we told the mean lady what we had and she proceeded to argue and then admit that she would never have the fish n chips as it came in frozen except on fridays. Ridiculous why can't you hand batter fish all the other days. Are these people really not that good at cooking?  While she did take off that nasty food she never once asked us if we would like anything else and the waitress disappeared after our food came and at the same time she put the check down. Very unprofessional and very disappointing. Will not be returning to this location I'd rather go to Denny's before coming back here and that's saying something because I loathe Denny's. Have a good night a get people who want to work.
name: Angela

text: I can not believe it took me this long to try this place!  Took a phone call this morning to head out the door and Immediately try their breakfast.  They have an unexpectedly hip clean modern interior truly a great ambiance.   That was so refreshing!  Then you get in a line and order and walk away with a number.  Service was great at the register and we hardly had a wait for what clearly was not your typical meal. Picture worthy but holy s#*@ were the flavors amazing.  I had chorizo con tortilla and my daughter had Plato mixto.  Never ever have I expected so much happiness in a meal.  I can't wait to try another meal venue.
name: Ava

text: I joined my family late for lunch but ordered right before they got their food and got mine very quickly afterwards. I ordered the kids mac and cheese for little A and a clam chowder soup for myself. Little A refused to eat one bite of her mac and cheese but A and I liked it so much that we devoured it for her. I didn't try the sandwiches and salads everyone else got but everyone finished their food. This place is located in a super cute picturesque alleyway that was a bit hard to find at first but if you know it's in the alley, it's not hard to find near the end tucked next to another restaurant.
name: Brietta

text: Parking was annoying and I was already in a bad mood by the time I got inside. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. Kind of landed in the middle for me. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. For the price I expected more than this.
name: User

text: Today is probably our last visit to this restaurant. We have a large family and it seems like we are not welcome at this place. We get it in other restaurants as well because we are a large family with small children up to a 17 year old teenager. We do our best to clean our table after we eat to make it easier for the bussers and staff to clear the table and we try and leave at least a 20% tip. We also try to be as friendly, respectful and quiet as possible with our kids. Anyway, the last few times we have been to this place we have noticed a definite feeling that we are not welcome. So, even though we love your salad, pizza and beer, we will oblige and get pizza and beer elsewhere or get it to go and stay home. Anyway, I just thought maybe you should know there is at least one big family that feels this way. Maybe we are the only ones, but maybe we are not.
name: Adam

text:
My brother suggested I eat here when I get to New Orleans. Now I know why. The food is incredibly good. Come hungry.  
Bradley was the bartender that night and he suggested the special. I got grilled redfish over a cornbread-jalapeño pudding. Topped with shrimp and their sauce. I would eat here every night while in town.  Thanks Bradley.
name: Silva

text: The line was long but the service was surprisingly very fast! The pho is worth all the hype. A little slow on cleaning the table before we sat down, but still worth the drive there. Prices were also very good for such a large amount of food. Can't wait to go back.
name: Song

text:
Amazing food! 
Loved the ambiance!
Great service!
Our waitress Jessica was amazing and had tons of suggestions for our first time visit. She recommended the spicy Brazilian bowl and I'm happy I listened to her and went with that. Our chips and guac came out a little late but they put it on the house. I'll definitely be back for brunch!b
name: Steven

text: The best barbecue I have ever had !!!! Matter fact the best restaurant I've ever eaten at !!!!!
name: Michael

text: This place is consistently good - it's become a go-to spot for lunch and dinner when we we're hungry and looking for low-key casual.
name: Max

text: Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. No big complaints, just a nice meal. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. Definitely coming back. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything..
name: User

text: Great place to go for dinner with a group. We went on a Friday night and had a table on the beach patio and watched the sunset while they had a live band playing. Our server was nice and told us about the happy hour options and most popular items on the menu. The service was good as well as the food, and the atmosphere was fun. The environment and being able to watch the sunset on the beach makes Palm Pavillion worth a shot.
name: Jessica

text:
Visiting the St. Pete area and Dad always finds the best places to eat.  He had been here about a week ago and took us there for an early dinner, still the lunch menu, great prices!!   Food was beyond fabulous.  Homemade pasta cooked to perfection, veal and chicken dishes, ravioli and pasta amatriiana superb!  Started with the gorgeous shrimp scampi and can't say enough about it, sorry no pics, too good to stop and take, lol!

Must visit if in the area, small, intimate and romantic, may require a reservation for dinner.
name: Jackie

text: The food is delicious!  The presentation of the food was amazing!  We all cheered when the food was brought to us because it looked so delicious. We highly recommend this place anyone looking to have a great meal.
name: Jesse

text: Best secret hidden gem in Plymouth meeting the Sam in hibachi is my favorite meal of all time, the Decour of the ambience. The wait staff takes a little bit to get to you but other than that amazing
name: Danielle

text: The fries were probably the best part of the meal, honestly. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. This feels like a place where your order choice matters a lot.
name: User

text:
I really like this place. The staff is awesome and the food has always been delicious!!! C.C. usually takes care of us when we go. It's the kind of place where everyone knows your name.
My favorite is the philly steak hoagie. The fries, shrimp cocktail, salmon app, and the onion rings are delicious!! Everything is really fantastic!!
name: Racheal

text: Place was dirty but can't expect a ton when you go in at 1:30am. Staff was not friendly. Only thing that earned stars was that they were the best sliders I have had of the few locations I've been to around the country. Better than the White Castle in Las Vegas. Food was ready very quickly though. Would maybe go back early in the morning if I needed a little something. Open 24/7 is big plus.
name: Dave

text:
As much as I want it to be better, I have to give Tavola a solid three stars. You can't beat the atmosphere, especially when the fire pit is open, but the food just doesn't match the prices. I do love that their patio is open all year long, and almost always sit out there. I've eaten a ton of things on this menu, and just haven't been wowed by anything. Your best bet here is to sit out back and stick to beer and apps. 

Last night we came to watch the Villanova game and enjoyed everything. Our group shared nachos (devoured before I could take a picture), margarita pizza, cheeseburger pizza and rosemary garlic wings. Everything was delicious; their bar food is definitely the way to go here.

This being said, this is definitely the place to go in Delco when you want to go somewhere nicer than a dive. You'll definitely pay more, but it is worth it for a nicer atmosphere sometimes.
name: Liz

text: Great spot!  The omelet was huge, lots of bacon & chicken sausage. JP has the quiche and it was awesome: light & great flavor. Must try their house made almond milk in your coffee!
name: Steve

text: The food was great. Service was terrible. Rude waitress who was snooty and nonexistent until we had to go find her talking in the back soo we could pay our bill then she was syrupy sweet. Lame. Gumbo was good. Chicken sandwich was good. Category 5 hurricane drink nasty. Fun feeding the pigeons by our table. They were nice.
name: Andrea

text:
I am baffled by all the five star reviews. This is a fairly new place so when I read them prior to dining I had a hunch they may have been written by people somehow associated with the owners.. After trying the place for myself- I'm fairly positive.

We arrived at the BYO spot around 7pm on a weekend. It was not crowded. The ambiance is relaxing and intimate. A nice date spot. 

We were seated and offered a pitcher of margarita mix for our tequila for $16! **this is an alcohol free mix*** To clarify- that is a $16 pitcher to make 4-5 margaritas using your own alcohol which is a price higher then any food menu item. It was apparently fresh squeezed, but still- I cannot justify that price for overly sweet lime juice. To me this just completely counteracts the whole point of a BYO. Lesson learned- bring beer.

Next we had chips and guacamole. Blah. The chips were so hard, almost stale tasting. I wanted to send them back but maybe that's what they were going for. Almost cracked a tooth trying to eat them. Guacamole should have been called avocado purée because it had no other ingredients then avocado. Where's the onions, cilantro, lime, etc!? Definitely not in this guacamole. So not worth $9.

For entrees we shared a smothered brisket burrito and duck tacos. We agreed these items were both tasty- not the best out there and also not the worst. 

Overall we found this place to be overpriced for the quality of the food. I really wanted to love it but they just missed the mark. We won't be back.
name: Moira

text:
THANK YOU ARARIO!!!!!!!!! 
I have so many great things to say about this place. 
20 stars not 5!!!!!

1. This restaurant is beautiful!!! Clean and very inviting. Looks "expensive" but is very reasonably priced. The namesake is so cool and clever as well. (Ask them about it)

2. I came in asking if I could have a very personalized dish... udon noodles with doenjang-jijae (soybean paste soup) he said it was no problem and I was so thankful!!! He also made sure there was no seafood (traditionally there is seafood) for me :) included was some delicious side dishes 

3. THE FOOD !!!!!! Ok so, definitely not spicy but the flavor was so developed I cannot complain. The broth is so good and authentic, I am very impressed. Every bite is an experience. It is so savory and salty, and the beef was delicious all by itself. Super good!!! I don't remember the last time I had this soybean soup (my childhood favorite) in America and it tasted this great... I am so thankful they made this for me! Every ingredient tasted high quality. The veggies were firm and so delicious, I want to eat this every day. (Zucchini, onion, cabbage, mushroom, bean sprout) made me miss Korea so much !!!!!!! I feel like I had a complete, healthy and delicious meal! 

3. Back to great customer service, I had soup Togo and they Saran wrapped it completely with the lid on top. Seems small but show that they truly care about the customer, not to mention I came pretty close to closing time! They could've told me no about my special soup but here I am almost emotional about how good it is. Haha truly Korean style thinking of the guest. I love Arario!!! I can't go back to Korea but I can come here !!!

I need to go to this restaurant ASAP TO TRY EVERYTHING!!!!!!!
name: Brie

text: Above average food, poor service.  Servers were incredibly inattentive.  If you don't mind walking to the bar to get your own drinks it will be ok as this is the only way you can enjoy a glass of wine with dinner.  Overall I would say come if you want a decent steak and can ignore poor service.
name: Jerry

text: Ok, this place is new and still really busy. It's worth it! The original chicken salad is good enough to keep me going back,  it the more inventive takes on a classic are DELISH! So glad this place has come to our area. The staff and owners are bending over backwards to make the community feel welcomed, show them some love.
name: TyLee

text:
Wow not the best and close to the worst.  I am from California so I am a bit of a snob, not sure what these 4 ratings are coming from but wow this was pretty bad. This wasn't just me, everyone in the party pretty much said the same thing. First they have nice service so from that perspective they sure were nice.

So they give you a soup or salad. The salad was essentially like iceberg lettuce you get out of a bag. The dressings were nice. Then the pasta (which I didn't order) were reported as overcoooked and not great. The steak I ordered was thin as hell and initially way overcooked from the medium that i asked for, which they quickly replaced but this was so thin very hard to make medium rare.

So I gotta say not great at all.
name: Jeff

text:
Brooklawn Diner (now Empire Diner) is under new ownership and it has only improved! Friends and I frequent there weekly, for dinner, and we are always greeted with happy staff, the owner comes to say 'hi' if he is there and we genuinely enjoy ourselves every time. 

Looking for a reasonably priced, good food establishment, Empire is it!
name: Andrea

text: I was excited to try the seafood soondoboo. I previously worked at a Korean restaurant in Washington and was craving a bowl of it. I was expecting to eat the soup at the restaurant but they had packed it to go instead. The soup was bland and watery, I asked for an extra egg and only got one. The panchan tasted old too.
name: Nohemy

text: We enjoyed a wonderful Christmas Day buffet at this quintessential colonial destination. With Revolutionary War history mere inches from our table and the exquisite Currier and Ives atmosphere adding to the enchantment, WCI is the perfect holiday idyll. The food was expertly prepared, uniformly delicious and made a wonderful punctuation to a magical holiday morning. I look forward to visiting again soon. Very highly recommended.
name: Michael

text: Good vibes. We went for some drinks and apps. There was a live band and they were great. Really spendy though. We got the boneless wings... you got 8 little guys that came out room temp. Good flavor though. Then we got the nachos, also yummy. But the prices were just too high for the amount of food we got. I know we are outside, but the birds were out of control. There are many bars in the area that have strings set up to deter the birds.. I'd suggest this for them.
name: Katarina

text:
Part of me wants to give Italiano's five stars just so that the lovely woman who operates this classic water ice window keeps it open for many more years to come.

In our American food culture, where so much is mass produced, and homogeneous, these classic regional outposts are treasures.

And on a hot and humid summer day, after a dinner of a roast pork sandwich or cheesesteak, nothing hits the spot better than a water ice. It's Philadelphia's dessert. And if you are visiting the city, you should get one inside of you.

That said, I could do without the shocking colors and synthetic flavors. Mango, cherry, and even pineapple are produced in teeth staining hues. 

I saw some people getting the iced tea flavor. Maybe that's a sleeper. I had to go with chocolate, because that was what I always got as a kid, and it never fails to bring me back to those happiest days of childhood. This one totally hit the spot.

If you come, prepare for a line. Also on Friday, the shop was closed from about 4:30 to 6:30pm. I guess the late afternoon can be slow. And I'd rather the shop be closed for a few hours a day, if that means it can remain open for the season. 

Despite my ideological differences with Italiano's on flavors and colors, I'm so glad I was able to pay them a visit and experience this piece of south Philly.
name: Daniel

text: I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. Would return. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Food was good and came out fast. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine..
name: User

text: Great deep dish "Detroit" style pizza. I will definitely be back....
name: Darrin

text: Good place for a hangover breakfast. The wait staff were awesome. The food was delicious. You can't go wrong. The cakes, pies and pastries are delicious. There's also TV to watch your NFL games while you eat.
name: Joe

text: The food here is fantastic! Their veal parm is delicious. I also love the limoncello cake. My only complaint is about the owner/manager. She's very racist. I have friends who have worked there, and they have told me she uses racial slurs and dislikes anyone who is not white. The last time I ate there, she would not stop staring at me. If I didn't know about what she's said behind closed doors, I wouldn't have payed it any mind. It's such a shame. I would keep coming here because the food is spectacular, but I'll just take my money somewhere else.
name: Imani

text:
I followed this project since it was first rumored that John Stephenson was working on a concept in the old assembly hall. Finally made it in last night and was overwhelmed. What a beautiful space. No expense was spared.

Delicious, creative, and generous dishes. Great cocktails. Great experience. We can't wait to come back!
name: Greg

text: The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. Worth checking out. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. Food was good and came out fast. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed.
name: User

text: Absolutely a must if you visit Nashville. It's like sitting in your grandmas kitchen having breakfast. The food is great, all of it. The country ham is wonderful. The fried pork chops and gravy are my favorite. It can be a wait on the weekends if you don't get there early but there are things to see and do on the grounds and it's worth the wait.
name: Gus

text: Great Thai food; I've eaten here a couple of times. Recommend the ginger stir fry and Tom yum chicken soup is incredible. Nice outdoor seating and the owner is friendly and helpful. They have a full bar and a few beers on draft. My favorite Thai in Clearwater
name: Stephanie

text: Don't go, unless it's for the beer. And even that isn't much of a selection. Got the Macho Nachos. Ridiculous. 10$ and change for a plate of cheap corn chips with about 6 pieces of ground chicken, approximately a cup of cheese, 2 tablespoons of sour cream and 8 pieces of pickled jalapeño. Really????
name: Jean

text:
Really cute little place. They have a variety of foods to choose from. Great for breakfast, lunch or brunch. The coffee selection is mind blowing. They mix a variety of flavors together that you typically wouldn't think to do. 

I ordered the California. Almost similar to a avocado toast very good and earthy flavors.
name: Letty

text: Omg; I love this place! I like both locations, but this one has a bar. The food is amazing, the tortillas are super fresh, and the drinks are good, not overly sweet. One of my life goals is to try everything on the menu. So far, the fish tacos and the avocado breakfast burrito are my favorites. In addition to the killer food; the people who work here are great. They're always friendly, helpful, and even when the place is slammed, you never wait very long. There's even a nice (but a little small) patio. The place is sort of trendy/modern looking, and the food has a sort of modern flair. But from a quality standpoint, it's like getting tacos from the best street cart south of the border. It's the tortillas and the meat/fish cooked and seasoned to perfection! If all that isn't enough, the prices are totally reasonable.
name: Anthony

text: We were in the neighborhood and decided to stop in for dinner with a group of 8. We were seated quickly and our server was pleasant. She ensured we always had our drinks and beers full. The food was better than we expected. We started with the loaded tots and an order of chips and salsa. The tots were good and the toppings on them were generous. Their salsa was fresh and really tasty, with just the right amount of spice (not too spicy, but not flavorless and weak). I ordered the Cuban sandwich with a side of fries, and it was delicious! Really flavorful, and I think I picked up a hint of horseradish in the sandwich? Not certain on that, but either way, it was really good! My husband had a burger and fries, but wasn't too thrilled with it. Our kids had a quesadilla, and it was good; the cheese was really stretchy and the tortilla was nicely crisped. Others in our party ordered the pulled pork sandwich and salads, and they all expressed that they enjoyed their food. The atmosphere was as expected for a sports bar/family restaurant. We will be back if we're ever in the neighborhood!
name: Katrina

text: Great food...Great service ask for Jamison B. Can't miss if headed to Busch Stadium! Try a little Gekkeika Sake from the bar!
name: J

text: This restaurant is situated near the river and likely has a nice view during daylight. While thoughtfully presented and served, the food was average. For a weekday night, it was crowded, so would suggest making reservations.
name: Lou-Anne

text:
Best dang good hot dog ever!!! Who knew?
I loved the rolls that open in the top and grilled to perfection.
Everything and everyone at this location are awesome.
name: Jean

text: Made reservation of large group through Jennifer. She was very helpful and apologized nobody had responded. We are looking forward to our dinner!
name: Matias

text: You know when you find a place that you want to tell everyone about?  This is it!!! The hibiscus tacos are heavenly!  I've been dreaming of these tacos ever since my recent trip to Mexico and they were even better!  The back beans and other toppings were unbelievable!  And Carlos the owner is a gem!!  I can't wait to bring my husband here this weekend!!
name: Erin

text:
I was looking for a good Korean place and I'm glad I tried this place out. I had the Gal Bi beef plate and it was tender and fell right off the bone. With some tasty sides which were different but definitely worth trying. 
Service: The service was amazing! For it being the first time being there, they were patient with us and she helped us out in so many ways. Especially with as much as we ordered. The food came out hot and fast.
name: Rocio

text: My daughter and I like to order pizza once every couple weeks and we usually get half pepperoni half cheese because my little one only likes cheese on her pizza. We thought we tried something new and close to home so we came here. I ordered just a pizza, the pepperoni to cheese ration was off. There was too much cheese and the crust tasted like cardboard. But the prices are decent.
name: Shane

text: Great view and food is good....but absolutely horrible service. Been here about 15 times. Walked out a few times after sitting around for 20+ minutes with no service. Waitstaff stands around talking to each other so even when they are dead service is horrible. It's only 10 min from my house so I so want it to be good but it always disappoints
name: Alicia

text: Seated right away in a booth and we didn't have to wait too long for our food. The BBQ was delicious with the perfect mix of coleslaw and pickle for somebody who generally would choose such condiments. The chicken was a tad over grilled but still a delicious sandwich. Chips and simple salad on the side were generous servings.
name: S

text: I didn't do too much homework, came here and saw that they were open and there wasn't a wait. We quickly learned that on Sunday evenings, they offer take out but the back room is only open when reserved for private parties. We ordered a drink and they were able to prepare what we had wanted from the dinner menu. I had read a few reviews, and for the few mentioning the price point as well as the amount of sodium-I see where they are coming from but I honestly think if we had come on an evening we could be seated at a table, that the experience would increase the value and also that the sauce on the kung pao meal would not have as easily saturated the rice at the bottom of the container. (Yes I ate it out of the container). Aside from that the Rangoon's were out of this world and surprising, I'll be back I'm sure.
name: Berkeley

text: The food was just awful, the floors were sticky but not as sticky as the table tops. I ordered the shrimp which I am sure came out of the back of a Sysco truck. The French fries were not fully cook for anyone at the table. The Yazoo IPA was cold and satisfying... the only highlight of the meal.
name: John

text: Went to Churchville Inn last night for dinner and was extremely disappointed. The service was very slow. We were told we would be seated in 25 minutes and told the hostess that we would be at the bar. An hour later after the crowds were thinning out my husband went back and a host there said in about 5 minutes we would be seated upstairs. People that had come in before us had already been seated (there were two of us). Fifteen minutes later my husband went back and told the hostess we were leaving and she said the table was ready and gave us a table downstairs. No mention was made of the upstairs table and people were walking in and being seated right away. Obviously they forgot about us. Then the service was terrible. They kept apologizing because they had two large groups of at least twenty people. If they can't handle it why do they take them? Or bring in more help! I ordered chicken and waffles. It was supposed to be on a Belgian waffle stuffed with cheese and ham. It was thrown on a regular waffle. It was ok but not what the menu said. We won't go back. We were there two and a half hours. They need to get their act together!
name: Heidi

text: My mother and I came here for breakfast on our last day in NO.  We had previously gone a day or two before for lunch and it was outstanding. For breakfast I ordered the Chef's Special Omelet with no chili. Food came out in no time. I was surprised at what I saw, french fries built in the Omelet! It was too die for, my mother and I couldn't stop eating it. It was the best omelet I have ever had. The Grill was probably the best food we had in NO.
name: Lauryn

text: Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. Food was fresh and service was quick. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. Will be back. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. No big complaints, just a nice meal. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text: Good salads. Pizza bread good. Only accepts cash!! Not good! It's 2019 no one carries cash! AND their convenient ATM charges $3.50 to get cash. Not good
name: Lisa

text: Raquel was absolutely amazing!! Try the Nola Bites. WOW!!! Service is excellent. Manager was extremely polite. Will definitely be on my return to list!
name: John

text: Their plates are huge! Always have extra to take home! I love their Country Fried Steak and Eggs! Also, prices are fair for the big portions they give.
name: Kathleen

text: Worst McDonalds ever. Even at 10 o'clock at night, anticipate being in line for 45 minutes as you get blocked in and skipped over by five people in the next row even though their line was empty when you got there. Also, 7 times out of 10, you will get the incorrect order in a box marked as your correct item. McDonald's has been my craving for the past eight months of my pregnancy.  I have contacted the corporate office and they were about as useful as dog crap. I also filled out a review about how that issue was handled. No feedback. I try to avoid this McDonald's at all costs, but the heart wants what the heart wants.   I've attached a photo of my Diet Coke. The lady actually looked at it and was putting a lid on it and said "Diet Coke, right?" And I said yes. And she gave me this crap. Seriously?  I'd most certainly give less than one star if possible.
name: Ashley

text: We have eaten at the Lemon Tree several times and it is always a great experience. It's worth taking a chance when you order food here because they're always doing something interesting, and it always tastes great!
name: Sean

text: These donuts are made to order, so you get them hot. Flavors are interesting and amazing. The donuts also have a nice crunch that I wish more places had.
name: Jesse

text:
Milkshake is great! Fries need to be cooked more-floppy not crisp but tasty. (Better if crispy)
Cheeseburger very good.
name: Kathy

text: It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Glad we tried it. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable.
name: User

text: For the price I expected a little more care. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. It was decent, just a little uneven. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would..
name: User

text: What a fun place to hangout! The vibes of bakery bar, and the friendly staff was fantastic. The food was great-- we had the biscuits and the charcuterie with 2 different cheeses and meats. We wish there were a few more entree options for dinner time-- but would still recommend as a great place for appetizers, drinks, and/or desserts! We tried the grasshopper bombe, but would definitely go with cake next time.
name: Kristen

text: Picked this place after reading some reviews off the web. My group of 8 visited from out of town on March 10th. We were more than pleased. I arrived on time and was immediately seated in the back. Now, we as a group, were looking for real authentic Cajun style cooking, and we were not disappointed. Now Antoine's is a bit pricey compared to other options available in the French Quarter, but if you're on vacation and looking for a relax classy atmosphere compared to the craziness of the French Quarter, then I recommend stopping here. Our server, Lawrence, was awesome. Very attentive and friendly. A real good-getter.  He even recommend to us some places to visit after our brunch. Above and Beyond service! The menu is awesome. They have a lot of great Louisiana Cuisine to fancy your palate. I chose the 3 course meal with oyster, chicken, and red velvet dessert plate. Trust me, everyone was incredibly delighted when there plates came out. Our table went through 4 bottles of wine and actually, the price was each of divvied up wasn't that bad. The overall experience was awesome. You won't be disappointed with this place if you're looking for a quiet relaxing place to escape to from all the hustle and bustle of the French Quarter.
name: Josh

text: Wow!  Just amazing!  I've had St Louis, KC, Memphis and Nashville BBQ. It's easily the best!!
name: Jill

text: The hotel is nice some of the workers are friendly customer service in the afternoon was very helpful. The breakfast is off the chain and is included.  They have lots of places to Lounge it's close to everything close to the mall close to the train to the aquarium and lots of other places and things to do along Julia Street highly recommend.
name: Arsella

text:
Went here on a Friday night, 8:30 reservation for 3.
The restaurant design and atmosphere is basically the only positive thing to say about CO-OP. The bathrooms, huge lounge area in the next room, and seating area are all really nice looking.

Unfortunately the service was terrible. It took about 20 minutes to get our first drink and they did not have the Kombucha cocktail (though they still charged us for it on the bill). After sitting around for about a half hour the waiter (who was probably new) took our order. We got the Brussels sprouts and the calamari for apps. The "Crispy" Brussels were not cooked and nearly raw, the sauce was decent. The calamari isn't anything special.

For entrees the 3 of us got the Wild Striped Bass, Scallops, and Cauliflower Dukkah. The Cauliflower was definitely the best of the 3, it was hot (comes in a cast iron dish) and tasty enough, though again a bit undercooked. The Bass that I had came out barely warm - it comes on a bed of wild rice and "roasted seasonal vegetables". The vegetables were literally raw - the carrots and I believe parsnips were barely cooked, and the broccoli was more cooked but not very good. Very disappointing, and raw parsnips left a bitter taste in your mouth. The bass itself was ok, it had crispy skin but again it wasn't warm enough so it wasn't very appetizing to eat. The scallops came out cold, on a bed of spaghetti squash something or other, and the whole dish was cold. My girlfriend is much more vocal than I and she complained and they sent it back to be "warmed up" not remade...so yeah it came out again like 3 minutes later and it was lukewarm. She ate it basically because we wanted to get out of there.

When the bill came it was over $200 and like I said they charged us for the kombucha drinks which we didn't get, so we took the bill to a manager. Really the only other positive thing was the way they handled it. They reduced our bill by about 50%, took off those drinks we didn't get and brought us out a slice of cheesecake and chocolate cake, which unfortunately weren't good, but it was a nice gesture. Thanks to the manager for trying to make things right. Won't be going back for food but may go back to check out the lounge some other time.
name: Gabe

text: I hate to say it, but the donuts are mediocre at best. The first time I went, I got two donuts that were dry and seemed old. I figured it was a fluke, so I gave a solid second chance and got three different donuts this time. Again -- dry, not fresh. My absolute favorite donuts are plain glaze or sugar, so I am easy to impress. I don't need anything fancy. These don't even meet the basic expectation. I wish I didn't have to say it because this place seems like a town-establishment. It's nothing against the staff, they are sweet. The product is unremarkable and it seems like it's time to change up the baker(s) or recipe(s). Sorry, but I've never had a bad donut until today.
name: Sarah

text:
This is literally a hole in the wall and it is so worth a visit!! The food is about as fresh and authentic as you get in Chinatown and the service is fast. The menu is overwhelming with the number of options, but you really can't go wrong with anything here. 

The atmosphere is great. It's a small place, so it feels intimate and like you are in your grandma's kitchen. The crab rangoon appetizer was delicious! It was made differently than any other place I have been to, but it was obvious that it was freshly homemade. I got the crispy, fried noodles and I was not disappointed - flavorful and also fresh.

The only thing I would advise is to go earlier in the evening before the main dinner rush, because as the night went on it got fuller and fuller.
name: Olivia

text: Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. You can tell they care about customer experience here. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The food was good and the service was easygoing. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait.
name: User

text: I adore this place and everyone who works there. The food is amazing, top notch service, and the decor and ambiance is amazing. My personal recommendation is the jalapeño marg or champagne cocktail during brunch for drinks. Food wise I adore the eggs Elizabeth, county breakfast, and chicken and waffles. I am so glad this place exists.
name: Chris

text: Food took forever but ended up being better than I expected. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Anyway, the tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than i pictured from the photos. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text: One of those meals where nothing is exactly wrong but you're not excited either. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. I'd maybe go back, but I'd order differently next time. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything..
name: User

text:
What a letdown. We went in for a couple drinks and apps before the Rodrigo y Gabriela concert on 9.22. Wish we hadn't. While the majority of employees were very friendly and pleasant, our bartender was quite the opposite (James, I believe his name was). He just made no effort to act as though he cared about what we were wanting, no effort to even say a quick "Hi", and no effort to ask about our food- which was cold. 

We ordered the mac and cheese bites and they had clearly been sitting out for quite some time before being brought to us. The avocado egg rolls were great, but again it was clear they'd been sitting as well. Cold. 

I can look past all of that though. It was a busy night and I know that they're fairly new, so I understand completely. What I cannot look past was the absolutely unsanitary manner in which the bartender was working. He was touching all of the fruits for mixed drinks with his bare hands, then wiping them on his jeans after he finished mixing the drink. He was handling cash, then promptly turning around and grabbing strawberries for mixed drinks with his dirty hands. 

I watched him take in over 8 transactions and make at least 15 drinks that required a fruit of some sort and not once did I see him wash his hands (unless you consider wiping his hands on his jeans as washing). That is completely unacceptable and is bartending 101. You simply cannot do that and I would like an explanation from the manager as to why this was being allowed to happen. Why are there not small tongs that he can use instead? Why on earth are there 5-10 other people standing there watching all of this happen without speaking up?

Oh, and he gave a random drunk patron the remote for the TV which resulted in one TV being turned off and the other on something that NO ONE in the bar cared to watch. I have no idea why in a casino they are allowing random patrons to control what is being shown, but he definitely was the reason why I only had one beer instead of the 3 more I had in the casino floor. Never again.
name: Dan

text:
Not a perfect experience, but close enough for five stars. I wouldn't come here all the time, but after my first visit to celebrate my fiance's birthday, I will come more frequently. We tried coming for lunch, and the security guard at the gate told us it was closed for a private event and suggested we return for an early dinner as the sunset views on the golf course are supposedly fantastic. So we made a reservation on Open Table, which we really didn't need because at 5 p.m. it wasn't busy. No matter. We were seated promptly and got to pick any table we liked. We elected to sit outside and it was very pleasant despite the chilly weather because they had several heat lamps. The view is pretty great.

They have happy hour until 6 so we ordered some drinks and green chili fries. The fries could've been better; the green chili made them too soggy. They have good local beers on tap; I had a prickly pear wheat from Borderlands, which was $4.50. Nice, because that would normally be $8. Everyone in our four-top ordered burgers. I had a mushroom burger and also tried my fiance's cowboy (I think it was called). The cowboy burger had a lot going on, brisket on top of the burger, onion ring, and bbq sauce. The bbq sauce wasn't typical; I tasted raspberry and balsamic. It was good, but I thought the mushroom was better. The mixed green salad we ordered for the side was very good. The server brought out a free skillet cookie with ice cream for my honey's bday and sang, which was nice.

Service was excellent, and I expect that from Ritz Carlton. The place is expensive, but I think the tab was probably around $130 for four people, who ordered four full meals, drinks, and an app. Not bad. I was expecting it to cost more considering it's on the resort. I'd definitely return, especially for happy hour, and it would be a good place to bring out-of-towners.
name: Ashley

text:
My daughter and I stopped by here for a quick lunch over the weekend. We are fans of build-your-own pizza places and, after reading reviews, were happy to finally come by here. 

First off, the staff were very friendly and patient! They were also kind and helpful with each other. I told my daughter that this would be a great place for a student to work! 

Second, we were happy to see that for one price ($8.47), we can have as many of the approximately 30 toppings as we wish! I started with a pesto base and loaded up with lots of yummy veggies! They also offer "finish it" sauces, so I finished mine with a "sri-rancha sauce." 

Our favorite build-your-own pizza place in Los Angeles is more expensive but I do prefer their pizza's better crust and more unusual toppings. However, overall, we were very happy with our MOD Pizza creations and will be back.
name: Kimberly

text:
Placed an order for the Irish Dip sandwich - when the order came out, the bun was super stale and the excess au jous dipping sauce was cold, after advising the staff, they didn't seem to care...
After countless times going here for dinner and events with friends and family, we will not be back.
name: Tat

text: Went last Friday and it was my first time here. My fiancé works in Noblesville and has said nothing but great things so I had to check it out. Great atmosphere, games to play while you enjoy a drink (or two) and lots of choices as far as satisfying your appetite. We tried the calamari from the Den and it was amazing! They coat it in an Asian sauce, definitely worth trying! We will be back soon to enjoy some more vibes and spirits!
name: Micah Angelina

text: Place is amazing. Food is so original and the flavors are unreal. Highly recommend. BYO TOO!
name: Harris

text: Liiiiiiiiiiiiittttttttttttyyyyyyyyyyyy
name: Ashley

text: I have to admit that I was not excited when a group of my co-workers decided that we should go to monell's for lunch. I was however pleasantly surprised at both the quality of both the food and the service
name: Michael

text:
A solid breakfast option. Probably one of my better Florida meals... what can I say, my expectations were set low. 

If you want breakfast or brunch, you will find no shortage of options. Pancakes, fancy or stripped-down omelettes, crab cake eggs Benedict... sides of potatoes and fruit and bacon... yes, please. The menu is extensive enough to please anyone, regardless of their alliance to sweet or savory.

We got a table (on the patio) without issue. The space was a little cramped; this was more of a challenge for our server than for us, as he couldn't quite reach all of us without straining a little. The food took a little bit but it was morning-ish on a weekend, so whatever. 

Definitely worth a shot!
name: Ryn

text: We visited on a quiet Saturday night, and were immediately seated. Our server was new, so was understandably jittery, but didn't really make us feel at ease.  In any case, the food was decent - typical New Orleans fare of red beans and rice, sausage and corn bread, fried seafood and fries. The seafood was good, well seasoned and hot. The red beans were tasty, the best part of the meal. Unfortunately the corn bread was tasteless and stale, so a real let down from what we'd experienced in another restaurant. All in all a pleasant night, but not the most memorable experience. Would recommend for a quiet evening with light jazz in an intimate setting
name: Kayus

text:
I came in one morning early before work because I have been wanting to come here since it opened. I heard and seen their reviews and was interested to try it out for myself. First off, the place has a great welcoming atmosphere bringing you back to the 50s 60s. The staff were welcoming and attentive, which is a plus. They also had some great 80s music in the background which brought back some good vibes in me. I tried out their Fruit Waffle since I was a bit in a rush and did not have much time to stay in. Their fruit waffle was amazing and delicious. Fruits were fresh. I added some sausages to go along with this because I'm just weird like that. My waiter did a great job in attending me since he understood I was in a rush. 

I recommend this place to eat some good breakfast. I would definitely come back with my family to try out other great breakfast options they have.
name: Felipe

text:

text:
As a resident of Mt. Airy I had such high hopes learning that a jewish style delicatessen would be opening in our neighborhood; sadly I have been disappointed by this new establishment.  Growing up in a Jewish household I have had a lifelong love affair with all things delicatessen from local to NYC joints that serve the glory of corned beef, tongue, turkey and pastrami sandwiches piled high on luxurious rye bread.  This new place is very far from attaining this level of delicious.  
Firstly, they opened too soon.  No signage, no register (an appliance that can be procured for under $100 at any staples or rest. supply store), no phone number, cash only, unprepared staffing and an unfinished location still not complete from their construction.  
The corned beef is decent as far as meat of this style goes but far too lean to remain moist and tender; the pastrami tastes just like the corned beef with no discernable flavor difference that you expect from a peppered and well seasoned pastrami.  The "rye" bread they are offering is a sad excuse, something that resembles a square loaf of wheat and tastes nothing like true authentic rye; there is a great artisan bakery in Chestnut Hill that could source great rye if the ownership looked into them.  The portion size for a sandwich that runs around $10 on average is quite minimal and nothing that any true deli connoisseur would come to expect from a deli. Their pickles are satisfactory, at least the dill pickles.  The "pink" pickles made with beet juice, not so much. 
The second point of contention I had was with the health code standards.  The main "chef" preparing the meal was in compliance with washed hands and gloves whereas the would be owner decided to assist him in setting up bread for our sandwiches having not washed his hands or put on gloves but after touching his head and face; these are clear health code violations.  Employee open beverages held behind the counter on food prep surfaces as well; all big pitfalls to those unaware of proper health code operating standards.  
On paper this place is a great idea but not well executed and pushed to open too early.  It is unacceptable to not have any sort of register to run transactions, phone for ordering or even full scale signage or menu boards and expect to operate soundly and successfully.  
I would recommend Knishes and Dishes in Lafayette Hill, a mere 10 minutes away and with incredible meats and the Rye bread needed to compliment those offerings.  
My advice to the ownership:  take a minute, regroup, do your research, prepare yourselves and your team to be able to run this establishment properly.  
This neighborhood is spawning some great establishments as well as being the steward of some years old fantastic spots; Mt. Airy and the residents here deserve only the best, remember that.
name: Richard

text: How lucky you are if you live near this incredible Vietnamese restaurant. It has some of the best pho I have ever eaten in my life (and I've eaten pho in at least 50 restaurants in San Fran, Portland, Seattle, LA, NJ, NYC, Philly...basically everywhere I live and travel). They even serve durian fruit milkshakes which told me this place is legit and not going to be watered down and mediocre for western tastes as many establishments are....it was absolutely delicious (I haven't even seen durian on menus outside of Cali...the king of fruit in Singapore and deserving of that title). The summer roll is ok, the banh mi is delicious, but the pho, with that incredible broth and correct ratio of herbs, is the bomb. I've only been twice....two days in a row during my two day visit, and I'll be back. I grew up in Bryn Mawr and was so happy to see it is flourishing with great new restaurants like this one and the awesome Bryn Mawr Film Institute across the street. Love my hometown and proud to call it so.
name: Laila

But basically you can't go wrong with anything. Only wish is that they offered a hotter salsa, other than that, no complaints.

text: So me and my family have been coming to this place for YEARS, looking back according to my mother atleast we were ordering since before I was born. Anyways, our orders have always been pretty consistent (Shrimp and Scallops or Seafood soup with 2 orders of egg rolls for dad, an order of steamed dumplings or moo goo gai pan for mom with sometimes chicken on a stick, and an order of barbeque spare ribs or steamed dumplings, and wonton soup for myself). It's gotten to the point that most of the time when I call they tend to recognize my family's name by our order (lol) and the wife is ALWAYS very friendly and provides the best customer service I seem able to get from a Chinese Takeout. Sometimes if my parents would go out for dinner with their friends and leave me with about 20$ for my own order, but an incident also stands out where I ordered my usual but threw in a 2 liter Coca-Cola for the night for delivery. So the wife arrives and we find out that she accidentally forgot it, so she was nice enough to go back to the restaurant and came back with the original coke I ordered and a second one free as an apology. This struck me because it wasn't really a big deal (I could have skipped out on the soda) but she was still nice enough to take the time out to go back get the drink and a second one. As is likely obvious by this point, this is a place with lots of good memories for me and I absolutely love this place and would recommend it to anybody.

text:
Whew,
where shall I begin 
First of all I only wish they had an option of 10 stars because that's exactly what they deserve 

The young lady that took my order was smiling and friendly, (customer service) that's always a plus for me
The actual place is not much of a looker but it's comfortable.........
We immediately knew that we would order the seafood fries (battered fries topped with claw crab meat, 3 jumbo shrimp and a ranch old bay seasoning sauce, my husband said it was mayonnaise but I DONT eat mayo and never will soooooooo it definitely WAS NOT MAYO.
They were really good and definitely filling.
Then we ordered a whiting fish sandwich. I usually stay away from whiting fish because it's always previously frozen and you can tell because it tastes hard and nasty and that skin thing is always black and rubbery. Ewwww
But I trusted Soulfedphilly after looking at other yelp reviews and I ordered my own. Boy o boy I was pleasantly pleased to say that this had to be the BEST whiting sandwich i can remember having in a long time!!!
It was 2 big pieces of fish that was so meaty and thick and that black skin that I was talking about.....it was crunchy and GOOD
Don't think I'm being greedy but I could not leave without getting a cluster of crab legs with that sauce
When I say GOOD LORD
The lord definitely Blessed the hands that made them thangs because WOW!!!!
My whole experience was WONDERFUL 
I can't wait to return 
If you like Seafood you should definitely make this trip you will not be sorry. Trust Me 
I know Good food

text:
Went for the first time with my son, and we were tempted to order one of everything, but settled on a half rack of ribs and a Brisket Burger (From the menu: "Half pound of grilled Black Angus. Topped with smoked brisket, candied bacon chunks, red onion, and our house made cheese sauce."

I don't usually care for dry rub, but these ribs were phenomenal: fall-off-the-bone and just the right balance of  moist and dry. I dribbled a touch of their Secret Sauce on some of them because I'm accustomed to sauce, but it wasn't necessary.

The burger was the meat equivalent of a slice of Hymie's chocolate cake: decadent, but still just this side of too rich. I have to confess that I ate it too fast to be able to give much detail, but other than being closer to medium-well than medium it was the best burger I've had since I last had one at Good Dog in Philly.

The fries were a nice change from the usual freezer-to-fryer fare that's gotten way too common -- light, crisp on the outside and creamy on the inside.

We will be back, this time with my wife (who doesn't eat mammals): in addition to BBQ chicken, they have something called "The Impossible Burger" that's "Vegan Friendly," as well as a bunch of interesting-looking vegetable appetizers and sides (we're going to try the deep-fried corn on the cob next time).

Oh, and it's a BYO, so we enjoyed a couple of fine beers from Firestone: my son had a Lager, and I had a Mocha Merlin.
