text:
Wow - I can't believe this was my first time here. This is one of those places that has been on my list of places to try for a while. I pass it almost everyday but only just now stopped in. I'm so glad we did! 

The location is ideal for us as it is nestled right on MacDill in the middle of South Tampa. The parking is easy as the parking lot right in front is huge. 

The service was really awesome. Our waiter was knowledgeable and made great recommendations. My husband got the pumpkin ravioli special. It tasted like all things fall on a fork. It was the perfect balance of sweet and savory. It even had some fall spices. I had the fish special - it was incredible! The flavors were rich but not over powering. The truffle quinoa was exactly the right side dish. We both ordered off the specials menu which appears to be ever changing, but the regular dinner menu look absolutely scrumptious. I want to try at least 6 more dishes off of the regular menu!

I had the recommended Cabernet of the night which was excellent and my husband got the blackberry whiskey sour which was also delicious. The bar got backed up and ended up delaying our second round of drinks so they gave us free dessert of our choosing! I love when restaurants do that. Remedying problems for customers is really impressive and always guarantees that I will come back. 

For our free dessert we chose re espresso chocolate cookie sundae. Dear lord, it was decadent, rich, and perfect. 

Needless to say, we will be coming back and soon! I want to check out their bakery and maybe get some bread to go next time.
name: Mary Beth

text: Food was fantastic. Service was horrible. The front podium sign said please wait to be seated. There was no one around so we walked inside and were finally noticed. We were sat outside and given menus (not happy hour menus even though it was happy hour). At the time we were sat there were maybe 3 tables total being served in the restaurant. Our waiter came back , took our drink orders, and they were served promptly. Here's where the fun starts. After finishing the first round he came back and asked if we were ready for more. We ordered another round and felt now would be a good time to order food seeing as he hadn't even given the thought to ask us yet. This is the last encounter we have with our waiter for another 45 minutes to an hour. Keep in mind he has helped 2 other adjacent tables multiple times since we ordered. We did our best to blatantly stare him down just to see us but still no acknowledgement. My girlfriend and I pretty much finished our fajitas so if anything you would expect maybe a "oh how was your food?" or at the very least "would you like the check?". Nothing. No eye contact, no coming by our table, nothing. At that point we figured he's never coming by so I went up to the front podium and asked the girl for our check. Our waiter returns with check in hand and still....nothing. No apologies, just here you go . We went back up again to the podium to tell the girl the food was amazing but the service was horrible. She pretty much had her "I'll let the manager know" card fired off before I could explain why we were upset. Anyway , very long story short, order takeout if you want to try this place. Or if you want to catch up on your tan you can sit outside, order a couple drinks , and relax for 2 hours before you get asked for round 2/food.

text:
Catalina Barbeque Co. will give you your BBQ fix, and some! There is no such thing as self control with these massive plates of meaty goodness. Looking for the ultimate gains? Come here. 

FOOD:
-Jalapeño Rolls (complimentary): 2.5/5 Stars: Ours were cold...I'm not sure if they're supposed to be cold. I did enjoy them despite the cold factor. My boyfriend got a dud one that he squeezed and it exploded into a flour dust puff, which was really entertaining. Stars for the laughs at our table and the flavor. 
-Mac & Cheese Side: 4/5 Stars: So cheesy, so creamy, so macaroni-y. Yum. I could've ordered two sides of these as a meal and been satisfied. 
-Baked Potato: 4/5: Mr. Potato was huge, and came with a good amount of fun toppings to play around with for a potato creation! Butter, sour cream, bacon, cheese...what more do you really need? 
-Ribs: 4/5: I was full after 3 of these. Very meaty. They also gave us fun BBQ sauces to add to them if we wanted more sauce (which we didn't need because these were very saucy to begin with, but it was still delicious). 
-Brisket: 4.5/5: Melt in your mouth and full of flavor, just as it should be! 4.5/5 

The service was good and the food was enough for a few meals (depending on how hard you decide to go...we definitely tried)

text:
Wonderful little BYO Italian spot in the adorable, quaint town of Haddonfield. 

We hosted a truly lovely bridal shower here where we were able to bring our own centerpieces and decorations, including candles and balloons. We were able to invite our guests a fresh bread basket with house oil on each table, a refreshing, light, crunchy apple salad to start, and to select one of two entrees. We chose to offer their signature crab cakes with whipped mashed potatoes and veggies and thinly pounded chicken parm with pomodora. Both seemed to be very well liked by our guests! 

They even created a vegan meal just for me! It was the most delicious pasta primavera I've EVER had over my choice of pasta, capellini. It was filled with sautéed veggies and quite the hearty portion! Made with olive oil and no parm. Super tasty! Veg-heads, don't hesitate to ask for this! They were super helpful with dietary restrictions! Fountain beverages of our choosing as well as the wine we brought were our drinks. 

For dessert, the restaurant made a large layered cannoli cake we were able to personalize! Love that they took care of all of this leaving us, the hosts, to focus solely on other aspects of the party. A plate of mini chocolate chip cannoli were also given to each table in addition to the large slices of moist airy cake with thick creamy ricotta frosting. Coffee as well as single and double espressos were available for our party during dessert also. Espressos were on point. 

There are three separate rooms; a main dining room, and two back rooms. All decorated slightly different, but very well! The copper tin ceiling in the main room was just gorgeous! The middle room we used was bright and looked out onto the Main Street of town. It was super comfortable for our party of 25 with room for about 10-15 more! The entire place is all very cozy! 

There were two parties including ours going on at the same time, and one did not interfere with the other as there are separate entrances for each dining space! Super smart! 

Overall I was highly impressed with the precise attention to detail while planning and executing the party. The service given by our kind waiters was really fantastic! They should absolutely be commended. They checked in on the hosts often, my salad was brought without cheese without having to ask after ordering a main meal sans dairy, and they even knew to wait for the proper time after photos to cut and serve the cake, plus they packaged the leftovers as to-go slices for our guest! This was not their first rodeo! 

The food I tasted was really, really great and the $25/pp included everything I mentioned, and was well worth it in my opinion! It was such a wonderful place to host. We were left to worry about very little! What a joy! Throwing parties can be super stressful and the staff here made us feel so at ease. It was such an enjoyable, relaxing event as a host!

I would highly recommend checking this place out if you're hosting a special lunch or dinner if you live in Jersey. They did a remarkable job with everything! I would actually consider it for future dinners I host even driving the 20 minutes or so from Philly. 

I would like to come back and dine on a regular night and taste from the set or maybe even try the 3 course for $22 menu also!

We were able to park free, unmetered in PNC Bank lot just next door on a Sunday. You can do so after hours also. Other than that, bring quarters for the old school meters in town.

We generally start tipping for average service at 20% and if it is any better than average usually 25% so it pained me to tip $16 on a $106 dollar bill (15.1%) but it was still $10 more than i should have tipped. I am not leaving this to be snarky, but as a reminder don't treat 2 tops like crap and expect a good tip. Hopefully you can learn from it. Food 5 stars and Service was 1.5 stars

text:

text:
Since retiring, we have missed the roast duck noodle
soup we would get at various places near my office in San Francisco. After yelping around a bit in Reno, I am happy to say that we found a reasonable facsimile at Viet Pho. Both my wife and I stopped in to see if their duck soup stood up to the SF versions and give Viet Pho's a big thumbs up. They use a lacquered duck that has some sweetness in the skin and adds that to the broth. VP uses cabbage as the veg instead of yu choy which is a nice twist. The only critique is the traditional garnish plate of bean sprouts, lime and jalapeño was little tired and not as fresh as it could have been. The service was attentive and fast. While the decor and ambience is a bit pedestrian in this strip mall location, I don't go to these places for the ambience. Even though we just had the duck soup, the menu is extensive with many other pho soups, salads and traditional Vietnamese fare. We will be going back to check out some of the other dishes, if we can bring ourselves not to order the duck soup again and again!

text: Had an awesome chicken pasta dish that was cooked to perfection. I was on a time limit and the waitress and chef were very accommodating and a pleasure to deal with. Highly recommend the pasta dishes, salads and the great Lemon  Orso Soup.
name: Chad

text: The bar staff are awesome the view is sick af and the vibe is dope as hell. Me and my fiancé went 02/01/19 . It was pretty cool . The bar staff even snapped a picture for us.

text:
This place deserves a 10 Star. Easily one of, if not the best, meals I have had in St. Louis. We attended Farmhaus for a birthday and it did not disappoint.  The host was very generous and friendly to us while we were being seated and even came by to see how we were enjoying our meal. Our waiter was amazing. Since we celebrating we decided to splurge. We split a tasting menu and ordered a few things off the every changing menu. I don't think I can describe how everything was perfectly prepared and was tasted. 

Simply, if you have never been. Set a date and go.

text: This Chick-fil-A is located in the mall, but you'll still receive the same great service that you would at any other location! I stopped by for a quick dinner the night before Thanksgiving and the employees were so helpful and friendly. Seriously, each one of them was smiling, my food came out fast, and they were quick to get me a refill on my drink. My love for Chick-fil-A continues!

text: Ended up here pretty late, maybe around 9:30, because everything else nearby had a wait. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. So yeah, it looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Idk, not terrible, just not something i'd want again soon. Honestly, the sauces helped more than i thought they would.. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..

text: This charming sandwich shop is the perfect spot for lunch with good company. My friend and I sat ourselves and enjoyed all the photos of famous patrons who had visited. We knew what we wanted, and this place delivered! I ordered the Cuban sandwich, a tamal, and fried yucca, and my friend ordered tostones and the Obama Cuban because President Obama ate here once! I also got a coke, and we both ate until we were stuffed and had lots to take home for less than $20. Highly recommend for anyone who is an foodie and also enjoys a calm, relaxing, inviting environment. My favorite restaurant in Tampa!
name: Cody

text:
We came here for dessert after having had dinner at founding farmers. The line wasn't too bad at 8:30 PM.

The service was fast and efficient considering that they make each donut to order.  I picked the blueberry glaze with coconut flakes and salted caramel drizzle.  My husband got the powdered sugar, bacon and raspberry drizzle. 

It was soo moist and the bacon super crunchy.  The sweet and savory was such awesome combo.   They also have recommended flavor combos together.

They also make donut sandwiches and also with scoops of ice cream.  I will try this next time.  It's so rich and decadent but definitely worth a splurge.   I will definitely be back and maybe get the 1/2 dozen that seems best value.
name: Hannah

text:
Great for weekday brunch (business or social). If you are going to try anything on the breakfast menu I highly recommend the Double Stack Pancakes!

Pleasantly surprised at how good the pancakes were. Powdered sugar and butter were brilliant. We also tried their famous Holes. They are about the size of a baseball and are served in sets of three and taste like a cake donut. I like the chocolate. Friendly service and convenient location on the Monon with its own parking area. All the sandwiches looked great coming out of the kitchen too for lunch. 

All around great, I recommend the patio and coffee!
name: Jeremiah

text: Good place to grab a healthy bite of food or study. Free WiFi and good promotional offers for smoothies. Fun to sit outside on a nice day and enjoy the open doors. Good food!
name: E

text: I recently used the mobile app to order my food, normally I never have trouble at any other McDonald's but this one was the worst experience I had, more than 40 minuets waiting for my food finally had to go in. Anyway they mess my order up and did not give me all of my items I ordered. Definitely not going back any time soon.
name: Alicia

text: Ended up here pretty late, maybe around 9:30, because everything else nearby had a wait. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. I wouldn't write it off, but I also wouldn't hype it up. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The whole meal felt kind of uneven.
name: User

text:
BEWARE!
Visited this restaurant for the first time - I ordered a chili dog platter.  The woman took my money, then proceeded to pull a hot dog out of a refrigerator with her bare hands, and put it in the microwave.

I objected and asked for my money back.  The owner's wife asked what happened, and I told her.  She said, "Sir, we never touch food with our bare hands."  I told her I saw what I saw.  I was, I thought, measured and calm, but she scolded me.  "Calm down!  Calm down!"  And she threw a ten dollar bill at me and said, "I don't know how much you paid, but here, you're money is back."

I tried to explain I wasn't agitated, she wouldn't hear it.  As I left, her husband came out of the trailer and asked what happened.  I explained the situation.  He said he just arrived and didn't see what happened.  He again said "Our employees never touch our food - we have an excellent rating with the health department."  I told him I saw what I saw.

I'm not sure how long his excellent health rating will last, because next I'm going to file a complaint with our local Florida department.   

I'm so glad I saw what I saw.  If she's handling people's money, I don't need her pawing her filthy hands on my food.
name: Clifford

text: Extremely slow.  Food Sat on counter for several minutes without being called out, manager was the one that was doing it.  An employee, drive through, was counting drawer, and manager was mumbling.  Employee.said what.  Manager turned and said: I'm not talking to you.  Yikes.   Worst hardees food I have ever ate.
name: Dean

text: Haven't been to Applebee's in awhile, daughter got straight A's and got a free kids meal coupon. We enter and greeted immediately. Waited a minute for a table to be cleaned off (my daughter asked for a booth and they made sure they got us one). Seated rather quick and waited for a waitress to come. I wish I would've gotten her name but she was very friendly and was training with a gentleman named Ryan. They took drink orders then got them. Ordered appetizers (half price before five). Quesadillas are amazing, filled with meat and cheese with sour cream, pico, and salsa on the side. Took a minute to order our dinner but she was very busy between training and having so many tables (Friday night). Baby ordered cheeseburger, fries. Husband ordered the 2/$27 got me the chicken and shrimp with potatoes, steak for him with fries and grilled veggies, with two Caesar side salads. He ordered a drink from the bar and I have a strawberry lemonade. Absolutely delicious. For $50 we were so full and had leftovers to take home.

text: Rosati's Pizza in Madison, WI is our favorite pizza spot during the summer while we are back there. However, after reading the reviews on the Oro Valley location, I was skeptical. We went in on a Friday night and it was very busy. We went to the bar and were quickly served a drink and then were seated in a booth after 10 to 15 minutes. The waitress was great, our order was taken quickly and the salads and pizza arrived in very short order. And the pizza was fantastic! We had no complaints about our experience and will go back many more times. My guess is they just took a bit of time to get up and running smoothly. Highly recommended!!

text: The two men that work here are creepers! I don't like their services at all. I would give this place a 5 if they did not work here.

I kept going back and forth while eating it, which prob says everything.. The wait wasnt awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. As I was not required to sign a waiver (unless I accepted one electronically without my knowledge) I was not expecting the sheer pain and displeasure I experienced. Overlooking this, their food looks good. The interior is bright and vibrant. As I have not been defeated by a Spicy food challenge before I am giving 5 stars pending my return to try their normal menu items. Ya'll got me good.

text:
Finally an authentic Korean restaurant in Chinatown!! 

Will have to say that when hearing about Dae Bak people just talk about "that spot on top of the new plaza in Chinatown", I think you should know and call it by its name. When first arriving at Dae Bak I was confused about its menu, I thought it was too slick and modern to serve traditional Korean food. Metal chairs, slick lines, highly lit and just way too American. But then you sit and recognize IU on the water bottle that also advertises their soju and beer, the Korean dramas on the TVs and the flat metal chopsticks and spoon. A friendly face will bring you the menu and you're starving. 
 If you're  familiar with Korean dishes, you're set, the menu is pretty self explanatory and easy to navigate. If you're not, there's  PICTURES! And it's the best thing any restaurant can offer.
 We started with the kimchi Pajeon (kimchi pancake) it was pretty good, just a bit soggy once it got a bit cold, the flavors were intact, but wished it was a bit more spicy. My friend ordered the Sundubu, said it was fantastic.  I ordered the Galbitang ( beef short-rib soup) ,it was a cold late night and this was perfect for the weather. The broth was extremely flavorful and omg! The meat just fell of the bone and equally delicious. The Bamchan (side dishes) had to be my favorite part. Everything from the cold brócoli bites to the spicy tofu and scallions were just delightful. 
I really am happy to find a Korean spot with other things besides KBBQ, and also pretty aware of the demographic and how some "authentic" restaurants feel the need to numb down the flavors a bit, but please stop. The kimchi should be spicier and to be honest what good is a Korean restaurant without the right kimchi? 

I will definitely come again!
name: Leyda

text:
I spent a year down in New Orleans and this was by far one of my favorite places for grilled catfish, shrimp, and Mac and cheese!! 

Anticipate to wait on a weekend night for a bit, but get one of their specialties at the bar and enjoy mid city!

text: I'm a fan of the wonderful food, atmosphere, quality  service and creativity. This place will become known all over the Tampa Bay Area!

text: Horrible location. My husband and I went in on a Saturday afternoon. We stood at the counter with at least 3 employees walking around. Another in drive through and another making sandwiches. We stood there without being acknowleged for over 4 minutes...2 of the employees were working less than 2 feet from us. At about 4.5 minutes we finally asked if they were helping customers inside or did we need to go through the drive through? They finally helped us after another 2 minutes of waiting. I have a food allergen and made this clear upon ordering. Sandwich came with offending food on it.  I brought it back to the counter, had to wait another 3 minutes, again made it clear it was a food allergen and not a situation where you can just pick off the offending item, the sandwich needs to be remade. I watched as he took it back to the person making the sandwiches held it open, said something, and watched her try to pick off the food item...I once again had to speak up and reiterate that I need an entirely new sandwich. On top of that, both my husband and my sodas were off tasting like the tank needed changing...but at that point we were kind of done dealing with the staff at this location.

text:
Great place to grab a slice and a beer or glass of wine. Intimate setting, small establishment that delivers big taste.

Came for dinner around 7pm on a Monday. Sat ourselves and our waitress promptly came over to take our drink order. Drinks came out right away. Since they were on a new point-of-sale system, our waitress gave us a heads up that the kitchen was a bit behind. Very courteous, as I have encountered other establishments that have not been upfront before. We ordered a large pepperoni, mushroom and black olive pizza pie with a couple of house salads.

Salads came out right away and the pie was not too far behind. Our pizza was hot and fresh with a crisp crust. Even though I am biased (from New York & have had my fair share of NY style pies), this place is close if not a Very good representation of NY style pizza.

Our waitress was upbeat and friendly. Even though she was slammed with tables she always found time to check in with us and was quick with bringing out refills and later the check. 

Great experience even though there were not so perfect circumstances (new computer system to take orders). Will be back!

text: Disappointing, dissatisfying and just sad. The food was gross, dry and basically something to fill the void in my stomach. I can't even qualify this as a meal. The waitress was very nice and attentive which was nice. It's sad that they work at such a low quality place.

text:
i really like this place now. when they first opened, i was excited about the noodles but the execution of the flavors was lackluster. since then, they've gone full sichuan style and the noodle bowls are fantastic. hand pulled noodles really can't be beat!

i come here and i pretty much order the same thing: the mala stir fry bowl with hand pick noodles, enoki, fish cakes or fish balls, lotus root, tripe, and some sort of veggie. it's delicious -- flavorful and definitely spicy. 

actually, two times ago, i ordered the food extra spicy and i ended up sticking my chopsticks into the noodles half way through in defeat. Hus-Ben asked me why I did that and who died (chopsticks sticking straight up in bowls of rice or noodles look like the incense you use to pay respect to dead people). My answer: "my spice tolerance" it was definitely a wake-up call to eat more spice.

the last time i came here, i got extra spicy again and wasn't in as much pain. this place is delicious and good for my sichuan spice tolerance. i'll come here often to keep my spice tolerance in shape!

text: We should have taken the clue when the parking lot was empty at 7pm on a Friday night, but we gave it the benefit of the doubt because of the location.  Big Big mistake!!! We ordered the surf and turf, the lobster tail was ruined with some sort of awful seasoning, we ordered our steaks medium rare. Both were severely under cooked.  My husband's was sitting in a lake of blood. The waitress didn't come around until we had been there so long, we decided to just take the steaks home and leave. After 71.00 and coming home feeling sick.  We decided that the steaks were going in the garbage.  I would not recommend this place to my anyone!!!! Do your self a favor, keep on driving by.

text: This was my first time at Southwest Diner. I added my party of two to the waitlist through Yelp. When we arrived and checked in, I was told there were still several parties ahead of us. After refreshing the page 10 minutes later, Yelp indicated that we should have been seated and to see the host. Unfortunately, the hold had no record of us and hurriedly seated us at the bar. That was disappointing. I ordered a tall stack of the Buttermilk Cornmeal Pancakes. They tasted a lot like cornbread just in the shape of a pancake. They were certainly unique--in a good way--as I have never had something like this before. Nevertheless, they were very tasty, and I would totally order then again. Honestly, who wouldn't like pancakes and cornbread combined? The other items on the menu looked good, and the service here after we were seated was good. Good restaurant!
name: Richard

text: Food was amazing. Request Jessica to be your waitress. She doubles as the bartender. Our group never had so much fun and her recommendations are awesome.
name: Emily

text:
I wanted to like this place more but I wasn't impressed. It had been recommended to us to try Sonoran style Mexican food while in town, a quick google search about what Sonoran style is and assisted by yelp we ended up here. We got here around 6pm on weekday night and there was a line at the hostess stand, she quoted us a 15-20 wait min, we headed over to the bar to order a margarita while we waited and before we had even received our drink, our table was ready. Tbh though they probably should have had us wait for our table as it seems the kitchen was weeded, I think there was a lot of large parties in, we were sat outside in the cute courtyard where you can see your carne seca drying up in the sky so couldn't really see how busy the restaurant was but it took 40 minutes for our food to come out! Our waitress seemed a bit flustered by it all, and disappeared for long periods of time - I needed a refill on my margarita!! While delivering the tables food next to us she brought us out their mini chimichangas on the house due to the long wait - there were actually really nice, well the cheese one was, the beef was a little dry. For some reason the plate had 1 cheese and 3 beef on it. 

Anyway once our food finally came out, we had both ordered the combination plate #5 which came with a cheese enchilada, chile relleno and their famous carne seca with rice, refried beans and flour tortillas. I liked the tortillas, they were homemade by their appearance, pretty big too - they were good. I filled it with my carne seca but as they hadn't given us any sour cream, guac or salsa - it was dry, the meat was already dry itself and tbh after trying carne seca I'm not a fan of it, it's almost like shredded beef jerky - it's too dry to go into a tortilla. 

The chile relleno was my favourite off the dish, I really enjoyed the texture of the roasted pepper and then the cheese enchilada was good too. But nothing blew me alway. 

You also get free chips and salsa and it was a nice salsa very spicy but most of the chips were broken up into flakes. 

We also tried the house margarita and the wild berry margarita both were good, not disgustingly over sweet but the right level, a little bit more tequila would have been good though. 

Lastly I had read that chile toreados where Sonoran food but didn't see them on the menu, bacon, shrimp and chiles is one of my favourite combinations! 

Nice atmosphere, enjoyable experience, service needs some work, but the food wasn't anything to write home about.
name: Emma

text: The pot stickers were burned.  The "saute shrimp" was not sauted in anything, just boiled shrimp.  the noodles (the star of this company) were bland and well not that good.

text: We made reservations here for a Monday night for my 65th Birthday. The waitress came to the table and her first words were "What do you want to drink?" She never asked my husband what he wanted. About 10 minutes later she came back and asked me the same question!! When she finally took our dinner order she never asked what level of spice we preferred so the food was very mild. Our reservation was at 6 pm on a Monday so the restaurant wasn't very crowded yet. To top it off she never acknowledged my birthday! We will not be returning nor will my friends.

text:
I always like getting pizza tips from people that I know. 
I really enjoy it even more when their tips are actually good. 
Chevy's is a place I never heard of and it's a block away from a favorite diner of ours. 

So I was super excited to go give it a gander. We got it to go.
They do have a small amount of seating inside, but we were going out to do some errands and there's a nice park around the corner from here. What better way to enjoy pizza then eating it in a park. 

We got a large half pepperoni. There's a nice thin crispy crust, excellent sauce tang. Cheese was perfectly covered and overall was seasoned well. The pepperoni slices were even more favored over the plain. 

I will have to give the person who recommended this to me a thank you next time I see him and I will be seeing this pizza again soon.
name: Toy

text: Stop here for coffee while heading to Seattle from Tampa. Friendly staff but the food and coffee prices are outrageous. Bottle of water is $4.

text: Went for lunch with my father on a Wednesday. We were seated quickly and the staff was very attentive. My father got a bowl of chili as an appetizer which was very tasty, as they make the chili with their in-house brewed piranha pale ale. For the main course, I got the santa fe salad. This is probably one of the best salads I have had, it has the perfect amount of dressing, toppings, and chicken. My father got a buffalo chicken grilled cheese which was phenomenal, and came with ranch dipping sauce and fries on the side. I couldn't get a picture of it because he ate it too quickly. I also got their lightswitch lager, which was really nice and refreshing, but still had that biscuity lager flavor. I love BJ's and would highly recommend coming to this location.
name: Benjamin

text: Passing through town on our way to Tahoe. Chose this place based off of yelp reviews. We ordered 2 asada burritos. Bad decision. It tasted like fish!  Neither of us could eat more than 1/4 of it. There's not enough salsa in the world to make me choke this down. Yelp reviewers, you failed me.

text: Great food, and super quick! I recommend their green tea boba and number 14. Their pho is the best comfort food in avon, especially during snowy/rainy days! Their green tea boba is also great for any season (if you don't mind the cold).

text: it looked better online than it did in person. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. By the time the food came out I was already annoyed. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus..

text:
We were looking forward to trying the BBQ here after some friends recommended the Sterling Pig but were kind of disappointed. The nachos (we added pulled pork) were great, but two family members were disappointed in the French Onion soup. The pulled pork in our entrees was decently flavorful, but the ribs and brisket weren't. The sauces were only ok. Two family members were also let down by the burger and salmon offered. The mac and cheese with the platter was bland and the cornbread dry. Honestly, Mission BBQ does much better in the food department and at a cheaper price.

The servers were polite and responsive, however personally my pulled pork sandwich was cold. And while we had a party of 8, half of the meals came a full 5 minutes before the other half, and one of the servers forgot a salad. Also, our male server had extremely long and unkempt hair which was not at all restrained, and I am almost certain that is a health code violation.

The booze was ok (we had the orange beer and cider) and the atmosphere was cool but I wouldn't eat here again.

text: The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. Would probably stop in again if nearby. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.

text: I usually get a platter with pernil (pork), rice and peas, salad, and a bottle of water for $6!!! It's a generous amount of food and very filling. The food isn't consistent but it's still good. Usually the platter come with a side salad but today it came with some shaved white veggies and tomatoes instead. I'm not sure what it was but I still ate it lol.

text: This place can't be beat at $8.99 for an all-you-can-eat lunch. I went here with my mom and we were really surprised at the good quality and selection for sushi, not to mention the huge variety of hot dishes. They even had things like macaroni and cheese, french fries and pizza if you have a member of the family who doesn't like sushi or Chinese food. Everything was really fresh and tasted great. Service was good as well, we didn't have to ask for refills on our drinks, the waitress came with them automatically. We will definitely be back, this is our new favorite lunch spot!

text: Actually this experience was pretty great! I'd been avoiding Culvers as a rule because I d stopped at one once on a trip and had a terrible experience but I have to give kudos to this one. It was clean. The service was great with friendly helpful employees. Best of all the food was delicious this time. I had the roast beef and my husband had the pork sandwich. Both were very good! I had a cup of chocolate custard for dessert- very creamy!
name: Kathy

text:
This restaurant is outstanding.  The food quality is what you can only hope for when you order Chinese.  We are new in town and have ate here 3 times now.  They messed up steamed rice for fried rice on 1 dish out of 9 and was still really good.

Recommend bourbon chicken, curry chicken with onion, and fried dumplings.  The fried dumplings are crazy good and the dipping sauce is even better.
name: R

text:
Excellent flavors and attention to details! As a super foodie, I spend about an hour pouring over restaurant reviews before deciding where to go for a great meal experience. From the swift valet service to the sparkler dessert celebrating my wife's birthday, I was impressed. Now the details:
We were instantly sat on this 4th of July evening in a comfy booth where about 75% of the room was full. Our waiter, Mark, was genuinely friendly , very knowledgeable and perfectly timed each course. Both my wife and I have waited tables in upscale restaurants up north, so we know how challenging it is to give great service on a busy evening. The carpaccio appetizer was a piece of artwork with six delicate shavings of steak bursting with complex flavors. We've never had better. The crab and crawfish bisque was smooth and delightful as well. The house salads were far from ordinary with the house dressing that was pleasantly unique. My wife's scallops were perfectly tender, and after just one bite, my wife said. "We are definitely coming back here again!" My fruits of the sea pasta was a very generous portion where shrimp, mussels and lump crabmeat topped the pomodoro savory tomato sauce. We both felt a part of the family and also treasured guests. Superior Seafood staff - well done. Mark, thank you!
name: Wes

text:
Well, the name is accurate!

While our kitchen is under renovation, we are getting out almost daily to try to find reasonably-priced and good breakfast/brunch place.  We have had mediocre results, even with the 'Big Ones' (Bob Evans/Perkins, etc.).

Speggtacular impressed us in all areas!  Don't let the outside sway you from stopping in, the inside is very nice, bright, and best of all seems very clean.  I ordered the 'Speggtacular Special' (2 eggs, meat choice, home fries, 1 pancake, toast, and fruit), and was impressed by the amount of food provided, presentation, and quality.  It looked like 3 eggs, and I was really surprised by the fruit (2 cantaloupe wedges, 2 orange wedges, 2 pineapple wedges) choice and amount.   Eggs were scrambled perfect, home fries very tasty with a bit of spice.   Everything was really good, and .....wait for it.....it was at a perfect temperature.  I haven't had a breakfast in a long time where everything came out at an appropriate temperature.
Service was great (Amber S.), and it's not like we were the only people there, she was attending a few tables, and working other background work with supplies.
Overall, a great experience, highly recommended!

Returned on Sunday morning at 10:15 am.  As expected for a Sunday, there was a line-up of people.  The line moved pretty quick and service time did not suffer due to the crowd.   Still a big 5 stars!
name: Rick

text: It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. The staff seemed tired but still polite. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. For the price I expected more than this. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text: Best restaurant tacos in st. Pete! The level of fresh ingredients, from scratch food is outrageously awesome here. They even make the dough for their own tortillas! Who does that anymore?! The queso is perfection. They even put a scoop of guacamole on the middle so it's a party in your mouth. They constantly have new taco combinations to try which is a great way to try new flavors. The tacos are a good sized portion, I would say large actually. I normally get three tacos at a street vendor but here I get two and let me tell you it's more than enough food. They do not skimp on ingredients or portion servings here. My favorite is the long rider which is their ahi tuna taco. Out of this world amazing and again so fresh. I also love to get this as a bowl option because that means even more ahi tuna! The staff is so friendly and funny. They make the visit that much better. They have unique traditional sodas there so don't look for a coke or Dr Pepper. They have a couple of alcoholic drinks. Frozen marg and sangria I believe. I haven't tried them yet. They also have a variety of beer. This place has something for everyone. It ranges from breakfast tacos, fried chicken tacos, traditional (if you want to be boring), seafood and more. This is a must eat place in town. Even writing this I'm now craving capital tacos!!
name: Katie

text: We come here all the time. As a local who appreciates this place I thought I'd leave a review. The service is usually efficient and I appreciate how clean it as, as well as the relaxed ambience. Here's what I recommend from the menu: Fresh Rolls (get peanut sauce instead of the dressing they come with), Pad Thai of course, the Pad See Yew is delicious, the Curry Fried Rice is excellent, and their curries including the Massamun curry and Yellow Curry. My husband's favorite is the Drunken Noodles. I also always have to get their Thai Iced Tea of course! I think for the amount of food you get the price is very reasonable. We always have leftovers for lunch the next day!
name: Megan

text: This place is kinda dumpy as far as diner's are concerned. Went here last night after my Neice graduated college. The waitress was extremely inattentive, took forever to bring drinks out. Never offered drink refills, she simply put a dirty pitcher of water out and when we told her it was dirty she could careless. Like why bring a pit get of water out for people who had a variety of drinks on the table. Where we supposed to pour water in soda ice? I asked for napkins and she gave me wipes... that was weird, but ok girl do you. The food was weird... no distinct taste to my wings that were supposed to be carribean  mango with no hint of either....just rude service for someone who basically works on hospitality.. I guess because it was more then 6 of us she automatically gets tips so she could careless how the service was. Trashy
name: Dee

text: Went with family on a Sunday and it was louder than I expected. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. You can tell they care about customer experience here. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. Would return. text: My husband and I came here during a short trip to Nashville this week. I REALLY wanted to love this place. I've heard such amazing things about Biscuit Love and could not wait to try it. This place does not live up to the hype.  We both ordered the East Nasty, which was basically biscuits and gravy with boneless fried chicken on it. The iced coffee was not great either.  I left disappointed and I do not recommend this place.

text:
My fiance and I are here from San Diego and we've tried so many different foods, but Niravana is the best restaurants I've eaten at during my short stay here.

text: The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. text:
I WAS ON A MISSION TO FIND GOOD RAMEN IN SOUTH JERSEY, MISSION ACCOMPLISHED

It's that time of year folks... the leaves on the trees have turned and fallen, the winter coats, hoodies, leggings, scarves, pumpkin spice and UGG boots all have come out...that's right, it's ramen szn. If you're unfamiliar with my reviews or how I choose most of the places I end up going into, it goes a little something like this. Lauren gets a random craving (typically at work), Google's that specific craving, finds a couple of ideas and then checks out Yelp. Well I was jonesing ramen and Rayaki popped up first and had 4 out of 5 stars, nothing but good reviews, the menu prices were right and the pictures looked good. Boom, we got action.

Rayaki is located right next to Dolsot House, you should know that Dolsot has some of the best wings in South Jersey and you should check them out... but I digress that's not what we're here to discuss. As soon as you approach the door your greeted by a giant statue of a samurai and right there I knew it was gonna be a good meal. The inside decor is really cool, they have all sorts of different Anime on the wall paper giving off a nice hip vibe.

I was on a mission so I sat down and began checking off the menu card at my table so I could get to grubbin' asap. First up was the Rayaki Fries , these consisted of mixed chasu (Marinated pork), spicy mayo, garlic aioli, fried onions, massago, scallions....they were very good BANGING! They were essentially loaded waffle fries but man oh man I haven't had fries like these before. They were fried and seasoned to perfection and the spicy mayo and garlic aioli really set everything off.

Next up was the Gyoza and Pork Buns, both of these were really good but these chashu pork buns were so well done that I almost ordered another round but I knew I had to stay focused on the mission.

More than one Yelper mentioned how great the Black Garlic Ramen was and that was more than enough for me to pull the trigger. I ordered a bowl of that with extra noodles and yea.... the Yelpers weren't lying, this was the best Ramen I've tried and Terakawa was firmly entrenched in that position for a while. The Black Garlic Ramen consisted of Cha Shu (Marinated Pork), bamboo, kikurage mushrooms, red ginger, fish cake, scallions, black garlic oil, pork soup base, and a seasoned egg.

Man oh man it was so good that I actually forgot I was eating in public at one point and just started going in. Then I looked up and saw the girl at the table across from me giggling and regained my composure and started eating like a civil member of society again. When I discussed this on Episode 35 of the Just Grubbin Show (live every Sunday at 8 on Wildfire Radio) I mentioned that I like Ramen because its lighter and Mo responded "Ramen...looks light but it's heavy tho". This certainly applies to Rayaki because this was a HEFTY sized bowl they brought out, I actually had to tap out and ask for it to be wrapped up. You know something is excellent btw when your full and keep shoveling food down your gullet aka me before I gave myself a internal intervention at the table. I'll be back to Rayaki for sure to explore more of the menu, you can count on that.
name: Lauren

text: What a great lunch find! Under &10 and I left completely satisfied! I had the sushi lunch combo with the clear soup. I had the spicy crab and the tempura shrimp rolls- both were great but I preferred the tempura shrimp.
name: Andrea

text:
Fido is a cool local spot in Hillsboro Village which was converted from a pet shop to a cafe (hence the name Fido). I'm not sure why my feelings about Fido are lukewarm compared to everyone's rave reviews. Perhaps my feelings are my fault for ordering just a latte and a salad which were just "okay" but nothing that I would feel excited about to get again. 

Their menu does have a lot of options and they have some nice looking specialty coffee drinks. They serve breakfast all day (a bonus for me) and Fido is definitely a hip hang-out spot for both Vanderbilt and Belmont students, locals and tourists. 

Overall, a fine choice for coffee or a meal. I prefer Frothy Monkey over Fido and their vibe and menu is pretty similar.

text:
First time trying creamery ice cream at Icecycle. I tried half and half on Salted Pistachio and Macha cheesecake. It's a good combo!

text: Delicious food, lovely atmosphere and great service. Our favorite restaurant on our trip to Santa Barbara.
name: K

text:
For what ever it's worth I'm from Texas and have a pretty high standard for BBQ.  The brisket wasn't necessarily bad but it wasn't different than anything else you'll find in Santa Barbara.  This place didn't live up to my expectations whatsoever. On a separate note the sides seem to be a foodie approach on classic BBQ sides and I didn't think they were any good.  This is not a smoke house as the name would imply and I recommend traveling a ways to find some real BBQ...  

My order - brisket, potato salad and beans.

text: What a great find! So cool inside, large bar and cozy booths. I have drive by this place 100 times and never stopped but so happy I did. Food and service were amazing and Lisa is so sweet! I will be back for breakfast lunch and dinner!!

text: A delightful little ethnic restaurant in old Gretna. Cuban dishes, New Orleans Po boys and tacos are offered in a lovely little corner building, very neat and clean. We had Cuban dishes, Ropa Vieja and Asado del Puerco and a Cuban sandwich. All dishes were delicious. Staff very kind and welcoming. It was a beautiful spring day, the doors were open and lovely music was played on a phonograph.  It was a perfect meal.
name: Ida

text:
This place definitely deserves some more business. It's authentic Ethiopian (sambusa or ful anyone?) and that's DEFINITELY a good thing. This is the type of place I'd expect to find in NYC... it's thrilling to see Nashville sport that sort of variety.

I had a pure avocado smoothie, and the barista/chef recommended I squeeze fresh lime on it, which completed the flavor profile perfectly. Not too bitter, not too sweet. The actual coffee is rich and dark, as I'd expect from Ethiopian, Turkish, and other eastern beans.

Now I have another reason to visit East Nashville!
name: Eamon

text: First time in Philadelphia, we were just looking for some place that had good prices, could feed a variety of diets and had good reviews. The food was excellent and the wait staff very friendly. We ordered the chicken tenders, two burgers and a beet and greens salad. They were very accommodating for dietary restrictions. Everything was great. A wonderful little place!

text:
Really enjoy Marco's Pizza have always ordered  take out from this location. Upon pick up pizza is also fresh and hot. I usually order online to get the best deals they are having. Never ordered for delivery so cant rate or comment on that but based on my experience from picking up at this specific location I never had a
problem with my order or food. Will definitely keep being a returning customer.

text: The lasagna was a very large portion and absolutely delicious! We got everything as take out and it was definitely as good of quality as eating in. Will be back soon!!

text: What a treat! Really a welcome new offering in the otherwise bland restaurant landscape in theBroad Ripple area. Come with someone who is a little familiar with the process. It is a participatory activity and usually you pay per person to use the table for 2 hours. You can get refills of your soup ingredients for the entire 2 hour period. You can use other ingredients ordered by another on your table( if they want) - the soups were awesome and delicious! It's a fun activity!

text:
I think they have improved a little recently reading the older reviews. There's only 4 tables inside and there is no table service where a waitress takes care of you and checks on you like a regular restaurant. The person behind counter could be friendly and at least smile though. 

On scene: I walked in and and ordered a to go meal. He said it will be 5 minutes. I sat at a table and about 5 minutes later he called me to the counter saying my chicken and broccoli was ready. That's about all the customer service experienced here. 

While I waited, I got bored and took a few pictures. See photos of inside and outside parking lot. 

My chicken and broccoli was delicious. Now, the broccoli could have been a little more tender I noticed.

text: Poor service. Server not attentive.  Too loud of an atmosphere. If you plan to carry a conversation with your party forget about it. The sushi was bland. Drink menu was not offered. As soon as you sit down, the server asked what we wanted to drink before offering the drink menu. During the meal, the server asked if the one person on our table wanted a refill but failed to ask the rest of the party.
name: Emmanuel

text:
In Pinellas Park with about an hour to spare, I wasn't starving but needed a snack... and fast food didn't sound appealing. So of course I checked Yelp to see what was nearby, and Cedars Grill caught my eye with good reviews & its close proximity. After looking at an old menu photo, I decided to try them for take-out.

I ordered the hummus for $3.99, which included a bag of warm pita wedges. I thoroughly enjoyed the flavor of the hummus, and was eating it non-stop for several days. But I was really lured in when I saw Spanakopita on the menu, and at $4.99, their serving was a generous size and a good thickness. I really enjoyed the extra cheesiness & the flaky but not too greasy pastry crust. That spanakopita was so good that I was devastated the next day to find that someone at my home swiped my leftovers from the fridge! I'm definitely getting another one soon. I also tried the Falafel Plate for $5.99, but was less impressed. They were good fresh & warm, but I thought the breading was a bit thick & tough. I'm also still on the fence about the Tahini Sauce.

I hope to update this review once I try a full meal from Cedars Grill, but my first visit has me excited to return for more. My food was obviously made to order, and service was friendly.
name: Lori

text: I love this location. Yeah it's always busy, always crazy, drive they included but I still 97% of the time get my food hot, quick & with pleasantry.  I stan for chick fil a periodt
name: Corrie

text:
I took a day to decide if I really wanted to post this. After much consideration here goes....

My daughter and I went to get cheesecake and she convinced me to get real food. I don't ever have a good food experience at Cheesecake Factory but I said yes anyway. 

My daughter ordered a chicken parmesan sandwich with fries and I ordered a chicken club with salad and a glass of Merlot. I chose the glass and half. Its $13!

The Merlot arrived and it wasn't until I was a few sips in that my daughter noticed a gnat in the glass. I informed the server and she took it away. What she returned to me was a regular pour! First off gross and secondly if one of my customers found a gnat in something I served them I would return their item with the correct amount plus I would have taken it off the bill. 

Our food came after what felt like forever and my sandwich was served with fries. The chicken was rubbery and I couldn't swallow a big chunk of it. It was gross and ruined my appetite. The "salad" was mixed greens and a tomato wedge. That's not salad. 

My kid's sandwich was also very disappointing. She kept pulling out tiny pieces of bell pepper and the marinara sauce tasted like bell pepper. They either have some cross contamination going on or they need to say there are peppers in the sauce. She wouldn't have ordered the sandwich knowing there were peppers in it. I hate food waste but the sandwich was so gross we didn't take the other half home.

Our cheesecake was amazing! We took two slices home for later. The Cinnabon Cinnamon Swirl was delicious. I shared with my husband. We will get that again for sure. 

Sorry Cheesecake Factory you're back on the list of places we avoid for our meals.
name: Kristina

text: Great if you eat in the restaurant... really expensive if your  ordering in, especially for Mexican food. Great servers and the food is delicious.

text: Dinner and drinks were excellent. We had tortilla soup, mahi mahi tacos and chicken tacos. Really delicious. It's loud, so not the right place if you're looking for a quiet romantic dinner. He said that the restaurant was very busy.  I explained that all 4 entries were ordered at the same time, and asked for a manager. The manager tried to sell me the same excuse. There were quite a few open tables and after 10 min we were finally sat at one of these open tables. We ordered our drinks and our waitress was back to take our food order before we got our drinks. We had a pretzel as an appetizer and it tasted like a reheated frozen pretzel. Then my wife's entree, a flatbread, came out alone as if it were a shared dish. Finally my short rib grilled cheese came out and it was fine, but I would hardly call a sandwich with one or two slices of barely melted cheese a grilled cheese. The waitress also came over to check on our food before I even got to take a bite.
name: Tyler

text:
This Place Is Firecrackin'!

There are already many reasons to love The Grove.  The neighborhood has continued to be one of the best in The Lou, and it just got a little better with the addition of Firecracker Pizza & Beer.

After the death of Flying Saucer, many of us beerknurds have been pretty displaced.  So begins the journey for a new craft beer landing spot.  Honestly, nothing will replace the community that Saucer gave me.  However, Firecracker is very intriguing and will definitely be in heavy rotation.

So far, FPB has had the best tap wall of any contender.  With 66 rotating taps, they are not short of options.    I'm always looking for new pours, and I had no issue finding them on the wall at FPB.

However, they need an actual beer menu.  I don't like ordering beers blindly, because even a basic pour can be very pricey in the craft beer world.  The bartender acknowledged this concern and said that I could ask the price before I order.  Seriously, doing so makes me feel cheap, and I certainly don't want me bartender to think that I'm just trying to get by.  Even posting the prices on the website would be helpful, if they're trying to save paper.  

But yes, price might be an issue at FPB.  When I posted about the place on Facebook, a friend even commented about that, having never been there.  So they already have a reputation for being overpriced.  That being said, it definitely wasn't cheap.  Two beers and a regular sized pizza were nearly $30 before tip.  They do have a happy hour, so that's something to explore another time.

Nonetheless, the pizza is amazing!  I normally eat vegan, and FPB have plant-based options.  Also, they are house-made, which is pretty sweet.  However, one specialty pizza was too hard to pass up.  I tried No Sleep 'Till Brooklyn:  turkey pastrami, FPB white sauce, sauerkraut, mozzarella, swiss, thousand island dressing, and toasted caraway.  It was everything that I hoped for!  I will have to return for the vegan cheese and beef, however.

I really want to give this place five-stars, but there is certainly room for improvement.  The pizza is killer, and the beer selection is impressive.
name: Christian

text:
I've tried to get the appeal. Honestly, I have. Multiple visits, multiple dishes. I'm not impressed.

The portion sizes are not comparable to other Thai or sushi places in the area for the money. It's not that it's expensive; it's just the ratio of food to the price tag doesn't do it for me. Compared to other nearby sushi places, their rolls are consistently short a piece or two, assuming the rolls are even close to the width of other places.

Thai curry is one of my favorite dishes, especially spicy green curry with tofu. The first time I tried it here, I had a cold and was anxious for a good, spicy Thai curry to help clear the nasal passages. I had great hope, since when I asked for it spicy, they asked if I was aware of the spice levels. Having traveled extensively in Asia, I assured them I knew what spicy was. When the dish arrived, there was no heat at all. Instead, the curry was cloyingly sweet, as though they had put a significant amount of brown sugar in it. That's not what curry is supposed to taste like. I added a significant amount of red chili flakes to get the right spice. I tried the dish again on a subsequent visit, again asking for extra spicy hoping they simply didn't add the spice on the previous visit. Nope. No heat at all.

I think this place does well with snowbirds from the Midwest, and it's probably at the right spice level for them. If you know real Thai food, you'll be disappointed.

text:
Coming from the San Francisco Bay Area, the lack of decent Thai cuisine in Tampa is astonishing to me. 

We decided to stop by here for lunch because we both wanted Thai food and this place was nearby. I had a feeling the food would not be authentic based on the pictures I saw on Yelp and it turned out I was absolutely correct. 

Per the menu, I'd say this place is more Pan-Asian than Thai. They also have Chinese and Japanese dishes mixed in between the Thai offerings. Not a good sign. 

We decided to get tom yum soup, drunken noodles, and summer rolls. The tom yum soup was decent but a tad too sweet. The drunken noodles tasted terrible, worse than what a drunk person could cook. My dining companion normally likes summer rolls but he only had two bites of his order. 

I knew we weren't expecting much but I was beyond disappointed after dining here. Two stars is the best I could offer. Deff won't return.
name: Angela F.

text:
TJ Wings has always been an establishment that I've passed on numerous occasions, never stopped, and now that I have, I can't believe I waited this long to try it!

We stopped by on a Saturday before an event and were put at a random 2 seated in an odd part of the dining room.  It was like we were smack dab in the middle of it all which made it hard for people to come and go around us.  I don't recommend this table be in this position but it made do.  Our waitress was attentive at first, but once our order came it was like she disappeared.  The dining room was packed and they were short on servers so that might have been why but a stop here and there, and not just for the check, would have been nice.

I'm a boneless wing fan but decided to try the bone in ones as they were recommended and they were great.  Not your normal size for a wing, much more bigger and meatier.  My husband stuck with the boneless and enjoyed them just as much.

There was live music playing and it was great to hear tunes I hadn't heard in a long time.

Great local place, check it out!

name: Sally

text:
What would you do ?

Sunday morning 6 of us came here for brunch at 11am. The place was busy, not packed. Everyone started with mimosas while we waited on our last person. We ordered about 10 minutes later. After an hour plus three omelette dishes were served to our table. The three of us that ordered eggs benny waited another almost 10 minutes. All the food was lukewarm to cold at best.  And I have now waited about an hour and 20 minutes. Yes, I ate it. I was very hungry and didn't want to wait another hour for a new plate. The table did speak up to the server- management took 10% off food. In my case a whole $1.15. 

Serving sizes seemed good for the price. But besides food temp, only one person had potatoes cooked correctly. The request for extra hollandaise sauce was forgotten. When asked for it, it came cold too. 

I did ask the server if the manager or cook would like to talk to us, but he wasn't available. 

The server did a great job. Always checking to replace empty mimosa glasses and offering separate checks as we ordered. He was noticeably embarrassed over food delay and our disappointment. 

With other great reviews- I'm not sure I'll return. Bummer, I thought I was going to have great potential.
name: Donna

text:
I visited Broadway Brewhouse on a Sunday afternoon, so it was pretty quiet then. Service was friendly! 

Beer selection: was huge and had a great mix of local and "foreign" beers. I ordered a local IPA and a fruit beer, which tasted like a cider - minus the sweetness. 

Bushwacker: basically an alcoholic Wendy's chocolate frosty and was exactly what I expected. Disappointed that they didn't add any chocolate syrup, whipped cream, etc. to add more pizzaz to the bushwacker. Sort of expected more than just a frosty and a glass cup, since this was one of the go-to places for this drink. 

Fries: they were good - can't mess these up! 

Burger: don't get it unless you're SUPER hungry or craving a burger and nothing else is around. It wasn't awful, but I was disappointed to see that the patty looked really unfresh and was a little on the burnt side. 

Cajun sampler: this was basically a rice dish, with 2 different types of rice. Cajun rice + a gumboish cajun sauce on top & rice and beans. It was only good because I had a huge craving for carbs. 

Cleanliness: the tables and menus were sticky and the entire restaurant was generally a little on the grimy side. Also, I found it a little repulsive to see people smoking inside of the restaurant. The smell really put me off, because the place smelled like a mixture of mustyness + cleaning solution + lingering cigarette smoke. Maybe it's legal and normal to do in Nashville, but it was strange for me to experience as a Californian.
name: Serena

text: Order a Strawberry Mint Mule. Very good. But for a Friday night with reservations we waited 45 mins for are food order. I ordered jackfruit tacos and fries and my hubby order fried chicken with green and mash potatoes... he said it was more like chicken tenders covered in mash potatoes with greens on the side. Very disappointed with service. A couple seated right next to us got seated 20mins after we were seated and received their pizza before us. Won't be returning to this restaurant!

text: Food was wonderful, inexpensive and large portions!!  You can come casual or dressy. Seating area is small, so you may want to call ahead. We had the roast beef poboy and crawfish shrimp etoufee special.  We also got the fries with beef on top. Yummy!!  Plenty for my husband and I and our 4 year old twins.

text: My friend liked it more than I did. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. Idk, the staff seemed tired but still polite. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. idk I'd try something else next time. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer..
name: User

text:
With the recent ridiculous surge in Szechuan Chinese restaurants in Philadelphia to pander to the culture-seekers, one stands out among the rest as the pinnacle, and that is Jane G's. I've tried plenty - Han Dynasty, Dan Dan, Chengdu Famous, among others, and nothing matches this place in quality.

Their selection of meats/vegetarian dishes is large, with plenty of styles for each, and while I was overwhelmed at first, I was able to focus on cumin-style and am looking forward to trying the other styles. The soups and appetizers are fantastic as always, and the ambiance is plenty appropriate for a comfortable, but not fine-, dining experience.

If you're craving Sichuan food and are uncultured or don't know your way around Philadelphia, give Jane G's a try.
name: Brendon

text:
Very friendly staff. Food was definitely delicious and was full of flavor. Love the decor and the salted calamari. 

I had the beef steak that was a little spicy bit perfect with one chili pepper. My boyfriend had the shaking beef and stated it was delicious as if it had a dry run marinate with a range. He also liked the Quail and it's dipping sauce. 

Would definitely return. The only downside was no refills on fountain drinks.

text: For the price I expected a little more care. Honestly, the food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. So yeah, i kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. For the price I expected more than this. not sure I'd order the same thing again. The food was good and the service was easygoing.

text:

text: I'm in for five stars. Our service was great. Their brews are very good and that food menu, gigantic as it is, gives plenty of options that aren't over 1000 calories. I had ahi tuna poke noodles and I was very pleased. Everybody was happy and things went perfectly. This restaurant is well managed and very clean. text: My husband and I recently went vegan and we were so excited to find some restaurants that serve vegan meals. I got the califlour buffalo wrap, my husband got the black bean burger and my daughter got the califlour nuggets. She had no idea they weren't chicken nuggets!! The service was great, the restaurant was clean and inviting and the food was phenomenal. We'll be back for sure!!

text: Very clean and modern! The staff was very friendly and the food came out super quick! I had a mango margarita and beef nachos. Both very affordable and tasty. I'm excited to go back and try more items on the menu This seems like a great addition to the neighborhood!

text: first of all the table was sticky as my hoodie kept sticking to the table ??? not a good start  but service was good  food was  ok    and really over priced  for the size of the portion  i dont know how  these people  on yelp  can say this is the best chinese food in town. obviously they dont know real chinese food

text:
I am not totally opposed to the "fancy Mexican" concept. I have a place in my hometown that would fall in that category. But it is not quite to this level of offering kobe beef and lobster in their dishes. That does sound like a bit of a stretch. But hey, I'm willing to try anything. Especially that involves high grade beef and lobster.

We were seated in a private room. Which was definitely nice with our large group. Our group of 13 definitely maxed out the occupancy of this space. We started with some margaritas and queso. A whole lot more queso was ordered later. But the kurts queso with ground beef was definitely the best. The margaritas and the queso were probably the best part of the experience. The service for our large group was a little slow and definitely not easy to flag down anyone from our private space.

My friend and I couldn't decide between the kobe beef fajitas or the lobster fajitas. So we went halfsies on both. It definitely took a lot longer on our food than a normal Mexican restaurant experience. But with good company around, no one seemed to mind. The steak was nothing spectacular and was like the $9 fajitas I could get just about anywhere. The lobster was really tasty. But barely had any lobster amongst the pile of peppers and onions. With two of us splitting it, we just had enough for each of us to have one tortilla.

I didn't see the final bill. But I'm sure it was pretty high. If I had been paying for this, I probably would have a lower star rating than this. But strictly judging the dining experience without the sting of the bill, this was just A-ok.
name: Will

text:

text:
Arrived about 11:00 after church on Easter Sunday. We were the only people there, two more were seated at  the bar bar when  we left. The atmosphere was fine, we were seated quickly and our waitress was good. It was dark and a bit industrial inside. We ordered a unsweetened tea and a half and half sweet tea. The tea was served in short( in my opinion to short)  mason jars, which the waitress was good about filling. My tea was way to sweet so i switched to unsweetened(. & i usually drink coke). My husband ordered a pulled pork sandwich( it may have been the best i ever tasted), the cheesy bacon fries($6) if ordered as a separate entree, where a bit to rich and over-seasoned with something a bit spicy. His sandwich was$11 and a gd value. The slaw on the side(a gd suggestion from the waitress was very gd). I ordered the the slider appetizer($11). 
The meat was overly small, the tomato was pale, the lettuce was tired, and the bun was stale. To the point it crumpled when i took a bite. The waitress asked is everything was ok, and i told her my buns were stale. She had a fresh set of three ordered up. The meat was bigger and the bun fresher but it was still a mediocre slider. Lets face it if you open a restaurant in Carmel IN with burger in the name you better have really good burgers. Our bill was $33.00 plus tip. I did ask the size of their regular burgers is 1/4 lb and typically range from $12-$16.
name: Ann

text: Love this new coffee shop in Fountain square. Best part? They have their own parking lot! The vibe inside is very welcoming and whether you are just stopping by to grab a coffee to go, or looking for a place to get some work done or meet up with friends, Bovaconti offers it all. The staff is super friendly and all seem to really enjoy their job. They have a large bar like area to wait while they make your coffee and there is plenty of seating in the front area. If you want a seat further from the entrance and a bit more quiet, they have a back room which is perfect for that. I always get the vanilla latte with oat milk and it never disappoints. They don't really offer much for food but if you know that going into it, you should be fine. Looking forward to many more visits!
name: Steph

text: An absolute Chestnut Hill gem!  Service was excellent, but the food was phenomenal!  I had the duck--best duck I've ever had.  My wife had scallops which she raved about.  The fall harvest/pumpkin soup was a perfect October appetizer.  An outstanding wine list--we went for wine by the glass selections that didn't disappoint.  Worth a shot for your fine dining outing.
name: Mike

text:
Great menu, great food, great drinks, great staff and great service. Liberty has a warm atmosphere and add to that, a new wood-fired pizza oven. They make virtually everything because they have a full scale bakery and s Bucher shop. How do I know all this? Because their friendly manager Mika gave us a tour. Kudos goes to the chef for making gluten free pizza crust and it was excellent. Such a treat for those allergic. 
Besides the pizza, everyone on our party had a great meal. Two got the black spaghetti with squid  and calamari. The caramel boudin was mouth watering. 
Think of Liberty a great spot for dinner or small shared plates before a movie--downtown movie theater across the street.
name: Marlene

text:
Came here for my birthday breakfast and I love it! The decor is welcoming and warm. You walk in and everyone is all smiles. I didn't know what to expect because we stumbled on to this gem while running early morning errands on my birthday. Apparently, this is was a restaurant named Kimmies and had been open for some time but renamed Cup Cafe. Not sure the back story here but I can't believe I'm just now trying this place for the first time.We decided to share a short stack of buttermilk pancakes and the southern biscuits & gravy platter. Both were eggxellant choices

The pancakes were fluffy and delicious. The flavor is so good you can eat them with or without syrup. The top it with powdered sugar so if you are not a fan let them know. Personally I love it. The dish that really shined was the southern biscuits and gravy platter. 
Literally homemade biscuits!! Like real ones and you can certainly tell. Many places claim to make homemade biscuits but the size shape and texture is telling and I guess everyones definition of 'honemade' is different. The sausage gravy was delicious. Savory, salty goodness with just a touch of sweet in there. Hands down the best biscuits and gravy that I've had at a breakfast spot in Reno and Sparks. 
Eggs were perfectly cooked. Bacon was a delicious cherry wood smoked flavor. The platter is just that, a platter! It is massive, shareable and reasonably priced. To top it all off I had a delicious mimosa, fresh squeezed juice would have put me over the top but good nonetheless... a girl can dream. The service is fast, friendly and good. This place is a definite must try if you are a breakfast person.
name: Brendi

text: Amazing seafood and beautiful view on the water. Service was fabulous as well. Easy parking.
name: Doane

text: Sour Saturdays! On Saturdays, the Upland Tasting Room offers a large list of their special bottled sours to taste from...more than twenty (20) varieties (persimmon oud bruin, fruity styles, oak-aged, etc.). Otherwise, the tasting room typically has a smaller draft list, with a handful of Upland's flagship beers (Dragonfly, Champagne Velvet, etc.) and a handful "of the moment" beers. This location was recently remodeled with long, traditional bar seating and a more modernized clean style, as opposed to the more cozy, cobbled-together look from before...I guess which can be a pro or con, depending on your preference. Service was very friendly and attentive, although also very loud...in a loud f-bomb cursing sort of way. This south Broad Ripple location is tasting room only, without the delicious food menu found at other Upland locations. Street parking is pretty easy to come by or you can try the un-leveled lot across 49th street. I would definitely visit again for Sour Saturdays, in order to sample some of the best unique sour flavor combinations in the country....and it saves me a drive down to Upland's Wood Shop in Bloomington.
name: Sara

text: They offer a wide variety of food and beer, with a couple of cocktail options. The service was fast, the margarita was great, but the food was disappointing. The shrimp tacos had been mentioned in other reviews, but were not tasty at all. The fried shrimp tasted like it had been sitting out and the tortillas were chewy.

text: I haven't eaten here in many years but joined the fam last night to give it a try being that I remember not being fond of it the last time.  Still holding on to the same opinion as the service was snotty on the front line, the food just isn't good and comes out luke warm at best.
