text: Parking was annoying and I was already in a bad mood by the time I got inside. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything..
name: User

text: Stopped here on our drive to Santa Barbara. Small restaurant in a strip mall. Really clean, very friendly and competent service. Food was fresh and delicious. I had the Spanish omelette. At first glance I didn't think it was going to be anything special, but it was really delicious! They make a flavorful sauce with onion and bell peppers. We enjoyed this restaurant and will stop in again if we're in the neighborhood.
name: Cay

text: Delicious food worth the price. Drinks were great and a good price! Really enjoyed this place. Outdoor bar is awesome! Easily better than Hula Bay!
name: Juline

text: I feel like my experience here is always a little hit or miss. It being a chain restaurant, I don't have huge expectations of the good quality. But generally the food here is fresh, and well seasoned although I think the portion sizes are a little small for the pricing. The staff is always friendly and courteous and quick to take care of you in any circumstance. I really like tat they're always changing and evolving the menu, adding new options for different dietary restrictions. Overall, this is a pretty good place to get a fresh, quality steak at a lower price than a steakhouse.
name: Kelsi

text: Reading some of these complaints now feels a little overblown. The food was good and the service was easygoing. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Not saying it's the best place ever, but it was totally fine. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.
name: User

text: For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. The food was good and the service was easygoing. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Glad we tried it. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Food was fresh and service was quick. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus..
name: User

text: Just had lunch at this great place in downtown. Fantastic fun place with some great BBQ. Next time I would get the ribs, they looked delicious. Fast ordering and super fast service to the table.
name: Joe

text: Hosts and bartenders were attentive, bathrooms clean, I've had their food before and enjoyed it. Stopped by for a quick drink on the walk home, raining, just wanting a night cap. Ordered two shots of well tequila. It was $17, which is more expensive than at popular concert venues like union transfer, where I expect to pay top dollar for crap. When I walked passed sardine bar a moment later I was full of regret for not going there instead.
name: Alyson

text: First of all, this Bistro is at the back of a bar called "700 Club", may be tough to figure out where it's located. We came around 7:30pm and were bummed to see that they were out of brussel sprouts and cole slaw/ Sriracha slaw, we definitely wanted to try those items. 3 of us got the Sourhern chicken sandwiches (which were good, but served on regular hamburger buns), PBB&J wings were great, light and crispy onion rings, pizza skillet mac (was rich and creamy), piggyback fries (awesome, surprised since I don't care for Pulled pork) and the firecracker cauliflower sandwich (flimsy hamburger bun, skimpy sandwich). The food was good in general, I wish the sandwiches would have been served on better buns (previous posters showed pretzel buns). I also wish that we could have tried the items that were sold out, 7:30 seemed pretty early to run out.
name: Tara

text: My pizza was only warm in the middle, fries were cold and u know u can't reheat fries =\. I ordered a quesadilla and steak as well a salad. Salad was missing the dressing, the receipt didn't have the right dressing listed anyway. The food itself was ok, nothing to rave about
name: Tash

text: Only true authentic place on Broadway. Cheap bar food that is out of this world. Cheap beer and cool place to meet the locals!
name: John

text: Very good though very basic Sicilian food. Delicious meatballs There are more interesting places to have Italian food in Philly but this was more than acceptable.
name: Floyd

text: Service was nice, kitchen was just moving kind of slow. The staff seemed tired but still polite. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. I left full, which at least counts for something. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text: If I could give this place a zero I would. We came in on Saturday around 9:30 and there was no one at the hostess station so we sat in the bar. We just wanted a quick bite and a beer and to watch the hockey game. There was a crowd at the bar and a few other people there. I live in Kirkwood so like to support local businesses. We sat at a table and waited and waited and waited. Nothing. No one was waiting tables. There was however a very young girl (she looked like she was 12) bussing tables. I've never been in a restaurant that had no one waiting tables, no one to greet you as you walk in the door.  9:30 is not late too late to arrive at a restaurant. What a joke!   We left hardly being noticed that we were even there. Went to another local restaurant and received stellar service. I will never go to this restaurant again.
name: Valerie

text: Had the bison burger with sweet potato fries. First time here and the food was good. Had a couple beers and it was a chill environment. Calamari was one of the best I have ever had. Would definitely return for a happy hour.
name: Miguel

text: While I've never had a problem with the food, and find it to be a great, diverse menu, the service has always been a struggle. Despite always having a reservation, I've never had an experience where I didn't have to wait to be seated. One one occasion we had to ask for to-go boxes because we could no longer wait to be served.
name: Ben

text: We had dinner there last night 3/25/2019  we had a table of 10 so it took them a little time to get us set up. No problem. I ordered the Lobster Ravioli. I was pleasantly surprised how much food came out on my plate. It was without a doubt the best meal I've had in years. We had business to attend to in Trenton, we drove 50 miles and this place was recommended.  We loved it so much that we are planning a trip back down just for dinner.
name: Mark

text: Pretty good stuff! When my wife and I go hiking at Fort Harrison, we love to stop in here to pick up lunch. Solid Thai food for a pretty good price. Normally we have enough leftovers for an entire meal the next day, but not always.
name: Jt

text: Tried this spot for lunch during a work break. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. This feels like a place where your order choice matters a lot. The leftovers held up okay the next day..
name: User

text: Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. The leftovers held up okay the next day..
name: User

text: Has been a staple for our family for over 20 years. Barbecue is always delicious and hot. When I need a quick dinner, I order the family pack and it is cheaper than pizza and warms up better the next may. Tea is great! They use real sugar. If you have kids who like trains, you can see them go by through the windows, too.
name: April

text: I went here with a coworker for my birthday and the food was so good. Everything from the condiments to the main meal was finger lick worthy. I would definitely go back here. The only downside is that it takes months to get a reservation! Worth the experience and at a great location as well.
name: Anjali

text: Casual place for pizza- but best pizza in this city! We were 7 people and ordered 3 pizzas and finished them all! Cute location, comfortable seating but very casual (read: seat yourself) but great for big or small groups; great for snacks or the famished! Portions very generous, cheese very tasty!
name: Erika

text: Did someone have a sale on salt?  Virtually every dish was marred by too heavy a hand with the salt shaker.  Even the perfectly done salmon had a huge cheap glop of brown overly salty teriyaki sauce on top.  The artichoke appetizer was a salt lick.  This kind of salt behavior is bizarre for an upscale restaurant.  I'm still giving them three stars because the salmon was a perfect medium-rare, clearly grilled with expert care.  $$$$
name: David

text: They coming to my job and in south Reno!! It's so good I love the soup it's so flavorful and beefy with sweet French bread and butter it pairs great I will get extra next time!! It's the second time I've eaten at this truck and it can be a little pricey but with flavor like this the money is well spent!!
name: Keywanda

text: This place happens to be behind my house and I've never been decided to try they 3 dollar breakfast it came with eggs,grits,toast and a piece of fish gave my mom the la eggs fish and toast and she liked it the grits was rollin lol ouu wih cheese was free too
name: Nick

text: Visited Acme over the weekend as this is our to go place when visiting NOLA. Their charbroiled oysters are incredible as is the soft shell crab Poboy. They never disappoint.
name: Agustin

text: I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Food was good and came out fast. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. It looked better online than it did in person. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Ordered a few things and liked most of it.
name: User

text: First time ordering from here and I honestly wasn't sure what to expect. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. You can tell they care about customer experience here. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Overall, a strong experience.
name: User

text:
My second time enjoying excellent NY style pizza.  Great crust, sauce, cheese and toppings.  This place is a keeper.  Reasonable prices, too.

Like the Terminator, I'll be back.
name: Jerry

text:
Went for Sunday brunch to celebrate several birthdays.  My husband and I were the first there and were seated right away.  We had the largest group in the restaurant and were given prompt service by our server.  
I had the biscuits and andouille sausage gravy and my husband had the pork chop slinger.  The biscuits & gravy are a smaller plate, which is fine; very tasty.  The slinger is a big meal, with egg sides, etc.  Delicious.  They have a wonderful bloody mary bar set up;  lots of choices for garnish/snacks and several options for the base.  Great band was playing swing, NOLA jazz, etc.  They were a little bit loud, but not so much that it disrupted our conversation terribly.  All in all a really nice, fun experience.
name: Bob

text: Great service and food! We had a large group and service was quick and accurate. The food was very good and we enjoyed the live music while we dined. The music was loud enough to hear but didn't hinder our conversation. I recommend stopping by for a great meal at a cool spot!
name: Kim

text:
A nice spot to grab lunch while downtown! 

I ordered the shrimp and grits, no cheese, with fried eggs over hard. I loved the flavor of the sautéed shrimp and sausage, and thought it went really well with the grits. Overall, a good dish and I would definitely be back!
name: Irene

text: Always great and one of my favorite spots ! Grabbing a little grub before tonight's slots ! They always get it right here and I honestly can say .. never really a complaint thus far
name: Fred

text: Visited here for my first time today I would like to consider myself a biscuit connoisseur. The BLT biscuit was delicious  The MAC and cheese size was creamy and scrumptious! I definitely will be back
name: Laura

text: Excellent food for a rainy day. My tomato artichoke soup was great. The portions size were huge for all things ordered.
name: Jamie

text:
I came to Olive Garden tonight because my boyfriend and I got a $50 gift card for Christmas. The worst experience I have had at a restaurant. even walking in to the establishment was a shocker. It looks like an IHOP diner with its bright lights. Aesthetics are a definite 0 out of 10. We finally get seated and wait an extra long time to even get our drinks. The soup looks old and gross. The alcoholic drink, Milan Mai Tai was all syrup and no alcohol. Oh and the menus were completely disgusting and sticky. The entree......I ordered the sirloin with fettuccine alfredo....dry and old. The waitress' service wasn't bad BUT everything else was. I will never come to this location again....or Olive Garden in general. 

If you like Olive Garden, do NOT come to this location. (I'm City Ave)
name: Alexandra

text: Worst place I've eaten in a long time. Burger was cold. Bun was trashy. Fries were horrid. Don't eat here
name: Eric

text:
Unfortunately, I was quite disappointed in Conner's Kitchen. I really wanted to like this place, but it just did not meet my expectations.

Yes, the decor and atmosphere are quite lovely. It is cozy and welcoming. The service was also nice (a bit slow as times). But, the food just lacked in quality and flavor.

I went with a group of 5 for Sunday brunch. We started with the everything cake donuts. These were more like beignets. They were good, but tasted a lot like a ball of fried dough. I could taste a lot of grease, which wasn't appetizing. I ordered the thick cut eggs Benedict. It came with two small pieces of bacon and the English muffin was not toasted. The hollandaise was bland and had too much of an egg yolk taste. I was really expecting more flavor from this dish.

Two friends ordered the chicken enchiladas which they did enjoy. My other friend ordered the chicken and waffles. They had to remake her order as she asked for no cheese (this took them about 10 minutes too long). It was served with the most potent bourbon syrup. She could not even put it on the waffle. She asked for plain syrup, which they did have. The bourbon syrup was way too strong and unappealing to the dish.

Overall, I was just not impressed by this restaurant. Especially the brunch. I want to give it another try, but honestly there's too many other restaurant in Indy that I would choose.
name: Colleen

text: It looked better online than it did in person. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. It just never really recovered once things started off weird. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Maybe other people have better luck here. Food was fresh and service was quick. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything..
name: User

text: Whenever I travel I look for local coffee shops. I'm so glad I stumbled upon this cafe! Hands down the best coffee I've had. I got an iced cappuccino. Wow! It's a creamy latte over ice with airy foam on top! Awesome! Very bold/ rich yet smooth coffee!
name: Sarah

text: We thought the food was delicious. The service was excellent. Our thanks to Dominic, Maria,Adele and the chef and rest of your team! Thanks
name: Michael

text:
Needed a bite to eat as we walked to our next Indy destination.  Family picked this place based off YELP reviews......now I'm not a huge soup fan and it was hot as hell but as I walked into this quaint place I knew it would be ok.  

      The smell as you walk in is just.....well it's just heavenly.  I saw they had sandwiches as well so we all decided on those.  They make them fresh for you and wrap them nice which was good for our walk.  I had the Reuben (can't remember the name) and it was soooooo good......from bite one to the last bite.  Such flavor in every layer.  The rest of my group LOVED theirs as well.  

      The people working inside were friendly, and answered any questions we had.  In fact I narrowed down my choice to 2 and deferred to the guy behind the counter and he picked which I should get......WINNER!!!!!

      If you need a sandwich don't hesitate to support this small local shop.  I am sure the soup is just as good but it was just too hot out to try any.  Get ya some!
name: Scott

text: The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. It was crowded but still moved along. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. Food was fresh and service was quick.
name: User

text: Good fresh ingredients, I got an acai bowl. Staff was very polite. Give yourself some time as not the fastest service.
name: Lauren

text: Went here for my graduation dinner. Super great food. First table we had was a bit small so we asked to move. The waiter accommodated us despite having to move us all the way across the restaurant. His name was Thomas and was super nice. The hostess (i didn't get her name) was very warm and welcoming as well. Our actual waiter at the table took a minute to greet us and we were told we needed to be up by 5. I found this a little rude but I understand restaurants. Food was still outstanding and so was the service. Definitely a huge shout out to Thomas though for being so warm, welcoming and understanding!
name: Caroline

text: People are being a little dramatic in these comments honestly. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. Not saying it's the best place ever, but it was totally fine. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. No big complaints, just a nice meal.
name: User

text:
Absolute best Falafel in Philly. Try the eggplant and pickles from the pickle bar. I usually get a half falafel sandwich, which is quite filling. Remember to take cash, but in case you forget, there's an ATM inside. 

One of my favorite spots in the city for a quick and tasty lunch.
name: Radha

text: In my opinion these are the best cheesesteaks in the city.  Restaurant is clean and nice.  Get the cheese steak and the fries they are great!
name: Jeremy

text: This is one of those places where I can see other people loving it more than I did. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. So yeah, everything was tasty and the place felt clean. idk I'd try something else next time. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything..
name: User

text:
Wanted to try this place, but had to get back home, so placed a to-go order.  You know how some places just kinda toss to-go orders into the styrofoam clamshell containers? These guys don't. The food looked great. I was a little sad they used styrofoam instead of environmental friendly containers, but I know styrofoam is cheaper. Their food is very reasonably priced for the portion size. 

I ordered the appetizer sampler so I could taste most the main app items. The falafel fell flat. Wasn't bad, wasn't really tasty either. The exterior was fried crispy and the inside soft, but was just ehh. The Baba on the other hand was great. It had a perfect consistency and nice smoky flavor. The Foule was also very tasty with nice texture. Would definitely get either one again. 

I also ordered a chicken shawarma hummus plate. The chicken was moist and flavorful. Spot on. The hummus, like the falafel, fell short. It was creamy enough, but more on the bland side then I'm accustomed to. No pronounced garlic or lemon at all - I actually ended up enhancing it with some chipotle Tabasco. 

Balaclava was amazing. Flaky but full of nuts and sticky sweetness!
name: Sean

text:
New Orleans is one of the few places I've been too where literally when searching for food, just about every restaurant has 4 stars with over 2k reviews & this one is no different.

The food is literally amazing. Ive been here before when I visited & head to return again. This time around my friend & I had the Oceana famous oysters & it's delicious. The oysters are grilled with this sauce on top & it's perfection. We ordered a dozen & actually I ended up ordering another half dozen lol. For our entree I had blackened catfish with fried crawfish tails (the crawfish tails were the best) with rice & beans & creamed corn. My friend had the seafood platter & was happy with her dish as well. I've also added a pic from the last time I was here & had the Cajun jambalaya pasta which had alligator sausage, shrimp, onions w/ a creole sauce & fettuccine noodles. 

No matter what you order here, you can't go wrong. The food came out quickly & the staff was professional. If I'm NOLA this is a must go to.
name: Felicia

text: Awesome place! Had some wonderful selection of tapas. Branzino rocks. So does the oxtail dish. Price is right. Flavor is there. What more can you ask for?
name: Anita

text:
Tried Arusuvai for Lunch Today . Item selection in the weekday buffet was horrible and most of the appetizer 
Trays were empty for a while . Food was great opening week which is very typical of any Indian restaurant . I personally feel they should come with a better menu . I would think twice before going to Arusuvai.
name: Food

text: Went with family on a Sunday and it was louder than I expected. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Price felt a touch high for what it was. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price..
name: User

text: No big complaints, just a nice meal. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. Price felt a touch high for what it was. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. Pretty happy with it overall. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Would probably stop in again if nearby.
name: User

text: Couldnt believe my luck when I found some good authentic ramen in the area. Their noodles are so good and the add ins are great. Broth is flavorful. Hot the spot on a cold rainy day! Very nice staff and exceptionally clean restaurant. Will be back to try more and sample their sushi!
name: Joe

text: Ended up here pretty late, maybe around 9:30, because everything else nearby had a wait. Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Would absolutely visit again.
name: User

text: Great birthday meal here. Tried the tartar, steak with three sauces special, the catfish and the, tomato salad, ol' Fuske and the country ham biscuits. Food was insanely good; Pricey but good as was the service.  The ol' fuske is one of my all time favorite dishes I think. Almost like a southern crab risotto. I'd come again and again just for this
name: Julia

text: First time here. Noticed this new place and wanted to try it out. The food is quite food and the taste pretty authentic, especially with the skewers from the spicy pot. The staff is pretty friendly too. The space is a little small and it's more of a relaxed kind of atmosphere, but it's fine with me.
name: Caro

text:
We came here mid-day on a Saturday and it was busy but not crowded. I like the environment. And it's a really cool concept. If you have picky eaters or divided tastes in your friends/family, there are multiple options available. And for the 21+ crowd it has a bar!

I ordered from Opa Time. I got the vegetarian lover's plate and it was delicious. Good sized. I definitely had plenty to eat. And the spanikopta was absolutely amazing. The falafel was solid too. As were the dolmades. The plate didn't come with any hummus. I probably would have preferred the humus to the rice. But the rice was flavorful and good too. 

My boyfriend ordered from Dumb Fish. He's a pretty adventurous and open eater and it's rare for him to reject something as not edible. He will usually still power through something even if it is not his favorite. He tried several bites of one of their poke bowls and just couldn't eat any more. He thought it was vile. He ended up having to get something else. In the almost three years together I cannot recall another time he absolutely could not eat what he had ordered. I am a vegetarian so I did not try the poke myself to see if I concurred. He ended up getting sliders instead which he enjoyed. I tried the sweet potato fries and they were delicious!

The beer list was solid. Multiple choices including some local beers.

I would definitely come again. I'm looking forward to trying the poblano sliders and some of the Upper Crust Pizza.
name: Camille

text: You guys, level set your expectations...  this is an American Chinese chain restaurant, not an authentic experience.  It's like Chipotle is to Mexican food: tasty on its own merit, and different from whatever an authentic burrito is.  I like this restaurant for when I'm craving some orange chicken, and they have so many other options to try as well.  I MUCH prefer it over the nearby Pei Wei, because it's faster and tastes better in my opinion, and I feel like the restaurant is generally cleaner.  The portions are ample, and everyone there has always been nice to me.  It's bright (lots of windows) and a pleasant fast food experience.  My coworkers and I pop over here at least once a month, and it's been consistent for me.
name: Aubrey

text:
We just stopped in for lunch. Firstly, very happy with the decision to start a lunch service! They have a smaller lunch menu and you can also get the full dinner menu as well.

Everything we had was incredible! We started with the Shishito Peppers and some Miso Soup and had a few different Sushi Rolls. Incredible service, incredible food, will be back.
name: Nate

text:
When I came to Baby's, I was so excited because the money stated they had a veggie burger! I ordered it. Turns out it was a black bean burger, which i strongly dislike. There isn't even veggies in it so that's false advertisement. The menu should say black bean burger or they should actually service veggie patties. 

Also they were out of most milkshake flavors so that was annoying as well. 

The one good thing was the mac and cheese!
name: Cheyenne

text: Love love love this place!!  The ribs are my favorite and I really can't get past them to be able to review any of their other meat items. You also have to try the fire and ice pickles, I know it doesn't really sound like they are much of a side but they are phenomenal!!  Be prepared for the lingering burn!!  Well worth the drive to get here and a great place to relax!!
name: Melissa

text:
Great spot to listen to the blues. The bar has a great stage for music with a brick wall as a back drop. There's an upstairs that's great for listening. Nice sized tables for larger groups. There's live music every night. The cover on a Tuesday was $5.

Beer is around $7. 

Highly recommend, especially if Broadway Opera is full or before/after the Cardinals game.
name: Cheryl

text:
What an amazing experience! Their take on pizza is excellent fresh ingredients and cooked to perfection. Had a BLT pizza was surprisingly different than anything I've ever had, mayo for the sauce was excellent. The crust of the pizza has a unique fresh flavor.
Overall a great experience will be back to try the salad's next time. Staff is excellent at this location!
name: Don

text: Love love love this place!! Such a fun concept, designing your own mini donuts. Not only is it fun for the little ones (and adults!), but the donuts are delicious too. From cotton candy pop rocks to maple bacon, the unique toppings make these mini donuts one of kind. Another huge plus is that this is one of the only places I know of to get gluten free donuts! The staff is so friendly and knowledgeable and took great care to make sure my gluten free donuts were not contaminated. Their original donut with vanilla buttercream was delicious and such a treat for this gluten free girl. I also ordered a cold brew iced coffee that was perfect as well. I recently read they serve mimosas on the weekend at this location and can't wait to go back!
name: Jessica

text: This place is the only place I go to for Chinese food.  They're far above other places in the area.  The General Tso's is always perfect, the food from their Japanese menu is to die for.  Steamed gyoza is awesome, the staff are extremely friendly and food is always ready on time to go, and in a very reasonable time when dining in.  Yes, it's a Chinese place in a strip mall, but saying that does it no justice.  I hope they're around forever!
name: Edward

text:
Delighted to be the first to review this new downtown spot (note that they have other locations that are equally delightful). First off, I have to admit that I was experiencing a wee bit of city envy when I noticed Nashville has a wellness bodega...that makes grabbing healthy and nutritious eats on the fly super easy. Now that we have my jealousy out of the way, I have to admit I stumbled past this spot after grabbing a quick lunch and needing an outlet for some conference calls. Being sick on the road for work, I was desperately hunting for all the cures- be it nutritious juices or their turmeric ginger shot. (Halp!) I remembered how much I loved their other downtown location on previous visits for açaí bowls but this round I opted for the cold brew almond milk/date cinnamon combo. In addition to fresh juices, shots, smoothies and açaí bowls, they also offer a coffee bar, fresh soups and a variety of prepared eats like spring rolls or bowls on the go. 

If I lived in Nashville, I would probably spend too much money here. On the outlet/working space front, I must confess that this spot is not ideal for working (hence, it being a bodega). They do have a handful of tables on the sidewalk and a wrap around standing bar (note: no interior seats).
name: Brittany

text: Still sucks....probably will forever, just go to Hong Kong Diner all you need is a little Gas-X to be good
name: Michael

text:
1. Neither of two hostesses had any clue how the app for restaurant worked.

2. The bread plates were dirty. When we had them replaced, and they were still dirty.

3. One of the entrees was served with a hair on it.

I doubt we will be eating at this establishment again.
name: Joseph

text: Amazingly delicious food: gumbo and salmon are phenomenal. Incredibly nice staff: the owner, Alexis, waited on our group with a smile!  Definitely a must visit in NOLA!
name: Nimaako

text: We got a seat in the bar immediately, which was nice because this place is typically packed.  $5 drink night for tap beers & house margaritas.  I love a good margarita, so that's what I ordered.  It was missing something.....oh yeah, alcohol.  I couldn't taste (or feel) any tequila in it at all.  We ordered the house queso and chips.  The queso was som of the best we've had and the chips were fresh & crisp.   I ordered the carnita street taco & the Ngry jalapeño street taco.  Both were very flavorful and tiny.  I felt that these were more of an appetizer than an "entree" but they were good none the less.  My wife offered the pescado street taco.  (Basically a fish taco).  She forgot to order it with a flour tortilla and she ended up with a corn one.  Not her favorite, but she said it was still very good, but it would have been better on flour.  They have 4 table-side bbq sauces which all pack great flavor.  The atmosphere in the bar is loud, colorful and fun.  They do carry a kids menu for the dining room.
name: Shane

text: I'd rather starve. Took a few bites of the chicken curry and it had absolutely no hint of flavor, curry or otherwise.
name: A

text:
This is one of those places that you wouldn't think to go to and then when you go you're like WHY HAVEN'T I BEEN HERE SOONER??!

But for real, this place is great. I got the salmon entree and the piece of salmon you get is huge! When I initially got it I thought they gave me the wrong order because it looked like a chicken breast!

The prices here are decent too. You'll pay about $12 but you get a ton of food. With my salmon I got a nice size portion of hummus with a whole pita, veggies, and a huge serving of rice. (With entrees you get 2 sides and a choice of fries or rice).

So needless to say I will be back here on several occasions. I love finding healthy places that fill me up!

Oh and it looks super small on the outside but the inside has a decent amount of seating!
name: Megan

text: First time at this place.  Staff was friendly. I ordered chicken wings and I thought it was pretty good!  My fam had chicken tenders. All seem to like it as well. I gave it a 3 star because I didn't taste any seasoning but otherwise it was not bad. It was crispy enough.  I'd go back again
name: Melanie

text:
Your menu makes it sound like something special. Plain ham and cheese. The fig spread was on one side, two pieces of arugula. Weak manchego, white American would be the same. All in all, a poor experience. Would not come back or recommend.

Also, I order on paper with pencils that are all unsharpened. I had to dig to get one that worked. I put the order in a basket but then leave to get beverage. Then my name is called and have to go back to the sandwich person. What's that about. Why do I have to go back. Can't the sandwich person hand sandwich to cashier and I pay. Stupid concept.
name: John

text: Haven't had MOD for a few years, since we lived in Houston. We love Blaze over in Orlando and have been to a Pie Five that's alright but MOD has better pizza than both. The toppings taste really good and the crust is delicious as well.
name: Caleb

text: The atmosphere was outstanding. I was told about this place many times and I finally had a chance to check it out.  It surpassed my expectations.  The service, food, and atmosphere were on point.  Great place to go and enjoy food with family and friends.
name: Friend

text: I don't really get some of the harsh reviews on here. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus..
name: User

text: This is probably weird to say...but I swear the casino smells like stinky feet/dirty swimming pool/gassing plastic?! The drinks are stupid expensive and the casino is usually dead. Only good thing is Hash House a Go Go upstairs (and the Starbucks since I currently live across the street lol).
name: Megan

text: The first few bites were promising and then it kind of leveled out. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Nothing about the space rlly stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. text:
This place has been on my visit hit list for some time now because of the many great reviews. So why 3 stars? Sit down, take a load off, and let me enlighten you. 

On arrival the restaurant was full and we had a short wait before getting seated. There seemed to be a shortage of wait staff but they were getting the job done it appeared. We were seated and it took a few to get drink orders in, which were brought promptly. Then we waited. 

The waitress came to take our order after a moderate wait... but WAIT! We had been seated without menus and none of the three previous visits by staff brought menus either. 

Once menus were procured, our order went in quickly.  The app came out after another moderate wait....but WAIT!! We waited some time for our orders to arrive.  Long enough to get drink refills at least once, for me to finish off my pot of hot tea and start on my water.

When the meal arrived it was hot and sizzling (we both ordered variations on the crispy duck) however they didn't bring both plates at once and left us wondering how long until the other plate would arrive.  Fortunately that wasn't long.

The food itself was fresh, hot, and good, but not the best Thai I've ever had (crispy duck is my go-to rule of measure for these things). The duck was good but there were some very chewy parts that made me think they simply cooked it too long. 

Overall, while I might go back for a second try, I wouldn't expect to go for a quick bite or take any famished people with me. We arrived at 6:30p and received our main course at nearly 8pm. I understand this isn't a fast food place, but that seems long to me even for a sit down restaurant.

text:
My husband and I stumbled upon Tavern at the Point while on Mass Ave on Memorial Day.  We had no idea it was open yet and love Cunningham Restaurants.  The space is small, but has outdoor seating which helps during the busy times.  We chose to sit at the bar.  LOVE the bar seats because they are so spacious.  

There are USB outlets under the bar for charging but no hooks for your personal items.  This would have been a huge help so people don't keep hitting your purse on the chair.

The menu isn't the largest, but it provides a good array of food.  We started with the fries.  While they were good, they could have been much better.  A lot of them were more on the burnt side.  I would have much preferred them to just serve the Bru fries!  I did love the sauces it came with.  I chose the pork tacos for my entrée and my husband got the Nashville hot chicken sandwich with pimento macaroni.  The macaroni was SO good, but the chicken sandwich wasn't very spicy at all.  The pork tacos provided a good sized portion and I like that they gave you the tortillas on the side.  I got the fruit and it's a very large portion.  LOVED it. The cocktail menu looked good.  They made many Blonde Ambitions while we sat there so maybe next time I will try it.

We will probably be back, but I think I would just prefer an appetizer and drinks.  The nachos looked so good.  It's definitely on my to-do list!

text:
You would think being in Idaho you could get some tasty fries, especially at a place named Boise Fry Company.  Unfortunately, the Bown location hasn't impressed.  

I grab a quick bite here occasionally and I consistently experience the following:

1.  Fries are soft, soggy. and oily.
2.  Fries are always short (1-2 inch in length.  Too short to dip).  It's as if they use the ends or potato seconds.
3.  Their fries don't have flavor.

I think they know this, and have built in two cover-ups into their business model.  

1.  They provide a bunch of flavored salt shakers. 
2.  They provide a dozen flavored dipping sauces. 

Without fail, the first thing everyone does is cover their fries in flavored salts, and the second is they dip into the sauces.  

BFCo, you offer fries from a handful of different potatoes.  Figure out how to showcase each potatoes unique flavor on it's own.

text:
With two Niche alumni at the helm, it's hardly a surprise that Elmwood is an outstanding restaurant and a much welcome addition to the ever growing culinary scene in Maplewood. I returned this weekend after the Schlafly art festival as I had a serious craving for some quality food after all of the walking. 

I had gone in with a party of three around 8pm and although we had no reservations, they were very accommodating and seated up promptly in no more than 5 minutes it seemed. The atmosphere is very modern and perfect for everything from a nice casual dinner to a date or anniversary celebration. 

The drink and food menus were extensive and certainly had something to offer for all palates however we had decided on the malfada, lamb cruda, short rib beef jerky skewers, twice fried potatoes, sweet potato baba ganoush, and the 35 day dry aged beef ribeye for two. Although every item was amazing in its own right, I particularly recommend the malfada, sweet potato baba ganoush, and the dry aged ribeye steak. 

The malfada was extraordinary. Being an omnivore and avid fan of all meat based sauces, I was initially skeptical of the grilled vegetable bolognese that was described on the menu but after my first bite, I was a convert. How they managed to achieve the marriage of perfect al dente texture with an abundance of umami into a vegetable based sauce is pure wizardry. I tasted hints of rich shiitake  and every bite just got better. The steak was also phenomenal and easily split amongst 3 hungry meat eaters with the quality of the dry aged beef immediately noticeable which perfectly salted and cooked over live fire. Thanks for an epic evening Elmwood.

This review is for 4.5 stars.

Perfectly located next to the stadium, Mellow is a perfect pre-game or post-game spot. The food during happy hour is good at $3 off flat breads and $1 off beer or wine. Still, at $8 regular-prices flat r was, it's always a good price the beyond burger was quite good and tasted like meat. For $12 it was a terrific deal. 

As a party we had about 10 samples of beers, 2 full pints, a few flat reads, and 3 entrees. All of this was under $90. Unbelievable deal. Great beer. Mellow Fellow is one of the best in Reno and a must stop for any beer lover in the area.

When a place is that good, (well, and that close to the hotel *literally across the street*), you gotta go more than once amirite? 

Originally planned to just stop by Luke's during their infamous HH (3pm-6pm) and thennnn head to the dinner ressie. Welp, that didn't happen. The crazy fun bar side vibes had us sticking around for the long haul. 

We sat bar side on a Thursday afternoon around 5pm, to a pretty busy crowd. Lucked out on grabbing the last two seats. Proceeded to order 3 dozen raw oysters (obviously), half a dozen fried oysters, and a couple of drinks to round it out. I started with the door#three, which frankly, I wasn't crazy about. Flashbacks of my early 20s drinking cheap mixed drinks is what it tasted like IMO.

When we finally decided to cancel the dinner res, and stick around, the second round included the "ohhh snappp, gingerrrr"...and yes, you have to say it just like that. In the end, the food and drinks were delish. I definitely came back a second time before leaving for the airport. Cheap, delish HH can't be missed! text:
Adele's is exactly what Sunday brunch in Nashville should be. They've got comfort food, bbq, bacon, desserts, salads, fruit, yogurt, quiche, biscuits and gravy, you name it. My girlfriend and I visited here for a birthday brunch celebration and it was absolutely wonderful! I cannot wait to go back! This review is exclusively for their brunch service.

THE ATMOSPHERE: 
First off, Adele's is located in some prime-time downtown Nashville real estate, located near both the Gulch and Broadway so it's a perfect spot before you continue your brunch activities (we all know what they are in Nashville). The space is essentially one very large L that has concrete floors, butcher block table tops, and a mix of industrial farmhouse. They have numerous large windows that let in a ton of natural light so no matter where you sit you have a view of outside and tons of natural light.

THE FOOD:
The brunch food at Adele's is truly the star of the show (as it should be). The brunch is buffet style so you grab a plate and work your way down the line. At some restaurants, I am hesitant with the buffet because you never know how long something has sat out or how it was made, but that is NOT the case here. The food is sat literally right in front of where the cooks are working so you can see them make the food and they are constantly replacing and restocking with fresh dishes. I was born and raised in Nashville, and when I think of a good ol' southern brunch, this is exactly what Adele's delivers. Truly delicious home cooking that will fill you up for the rest of the day (for those other brunch activities, of course).

THE SERVICE:
The service here is filled with nice, friendly, and attentive staff. They always make sure your drinks are full and are more than happy to explain what is on the brunch buffet.
name: Joel

text:

You get a complimentary bread basket which had 4 types.  Creole muffin, pecan muffin, a jalapeño cheese roll and a regular dinner roll.  We shared 1 of each since we wanted to save room as well.  All the breads were yummy!  Jalapeño was my fav.  

We split a cup of the gumbo which was yummy.  Just wish they had a version with seafood but just chicken and sausage.  Good flavor though.  

We split the jambalaya with salmon plate which was wonderful!   Great tomato flavor in the jambalaya and the seasoning on the salmon was wonderful!!  Very fresh and soft salmon.  Veggies were fresh and crispy!  

I took the rest of the bread home even when I usually skip the carb!  Service was great!  Friendly and attentive!  

Definitely a must if you are there!

text: Fantastic food. I was worried that portions would be small and I'd leave hungry but that was far from being the case! We couldn't even order dessert because we were so full. We started with the smoked carrots (Phenomenal and good size) and I chose the pork (~$26) as my main while my boyfriend ordered the lamb entree (~$25). Both were out of this world. We also loved that it was BYOB and they take credit cards. Service was helpful and friendly. Overall, great experience and insanely good food.

text: I thought the atmosphere was on point. I didn't realize it was more of a tapas bar than restaurant until we got there. I was more excited for wine than I was food. And the wine didn't disappoint. I had the Axl Rose wine flight with the cheese pairing and it was awesome! Drunken goat cheese was fantastic! I had the bees sliders and they were okay, nothing to write home about. I also tried to the mashed potato tots, now those were great! But my favorite part of the meal was the dessert. text:
Sunday late morning and we needed some brunch after the pleasant experience I had at the Comfort Kitchen on Wednesday I was eager to take my husband, however they were closed on Sundays, my fault I should have checked hours. I referred to my bookmarked places, album "breakfast" and Dog and Bull was marked and only 15 mins down the road so we headed there.

They boost  a Jazz Brunch every Saturday and Sunday from 9-2 with the best Bloody Mary's in the area. We arrived around noon and it was fairly busy, I'm sure it being such a small place this place can get packed! Reservations are suggested. 

The Jazz music provided was man on a piano, the songs he played were appropriate, he was a fanatic musician and it was so loud you could enjoy your food and conversation. We couldn't see him playing but they did have a small TV that showed him playing so I thought it was nice to see it even although you weren't right there. 

The Food: the main reason I bookmarked this place is because my husband loves Chicken and Waffles so we needed a local spot. His waffle was hands down the best I ever tasted.  It was crispy on the outside, and soft in the middle, sweet and perfectly made, but the fried chicken was for sure the stand out on the whole meal. The take a whole bone in chicken breast, de-bone it and fry it! It is seriously the only way to eat fried chicken! The sourdough bread was an awesome touch, my eggs were cooked perfectly and the bloody Mary's going out looked serious! 

Why didn't I give it 5 stars, although our server was awesome, it still took a good 15 mins for her to grab our order, and the food took a decent amount of time too. Also, the decor was funky, which is cool but ceiling is lined with some kind of fabric and fabric on ceilings grosses me out. Fabric holds smells and dust and it's never a good idea to have that order your head when eating, but hey that's just me.
name: Dana

text: Change in part of the ownership has not impacted the quality and service at this amazing establishment.  Love the casual ambiance. Love that they allow you to Bring in your own bottle of wine for a nominal corkage fee.  The Gnocchi is our family favorite and probably the best around.  Try the veal Milanese,Picatta or the meatball lasagna special.

text:
I've had my eye on Enoteca Tredici for a while now. I frequent the area as this section of the Main Line has a wide array of great restaurants. I wasn't deeply impressed, but overall my experience was favorable albeit a few hiccups. 

The service I experienced was pretty poor and was by far the biggest letdown of the evening. We received our food promptly - although sporadically/staggered - but after that our server was nowhere to be seen. Towards the end of the entree my boyfriend remarked how he would have gotten wine with his meal, had we been given the opportunity. 

Ambiance is awesome. The restaurant is decorated beautifully with a lot of disparate elements that somehow work together and keep you looking around at everything. My favorite part was that is appeared as though we were eating inside a repurposed greenhouse which only took up part of the inside of the restaurant space... very unusual!

Our experience with the food was mixed. The meatballs were tender and had a great, bright tomato flavor which complimented the rich, savory meat well. The gnocchi were rather dense and the sauce they rested in was bland and watery - hardly reminiscent of a vodka sauce. 

The chicken entree was cooked well, although it was quite austere - just a piece of chicken on a plate with no garnish and nothing to compliment it. The bolognese was cooked nicely and the pasta has a good texture, but it also lacked the hearty meatiness bolognese is renowned for.

The best part was by far the flatbreads they serve (only if you ask): dunk them in all those tasty sauces! 

Overall, I was a little disappointed by Enoteca Tredici because I had hyped it up in my mind for a while before I ultimately ended up going, but at the end of the day the food was decent and the restaurant looks pretty cool, so it may be worth a visit. Definitely not cheap though, so if you're counting pennies, steer clear!

text: I have never been to Panera before, but received a gift card and decided to take my two children for lunch. When we ordered, I told the cashier we have never been there before, thinking he would explain the process or make a suggestion. No, he was too busy laughing and joking with the cashier next to him. I ordered a kids meal and then my daughter and I got a half sandwich and a cup of soup/salad. The cashier never asked me if I had a rewards card or even if I wanted one. Over $38 for one adult and two children to eat. That's insane! If I'm going to pay almost forty dollars for lunch for two kids and myself, I'm going to a sit down restaurant where they bring your drinks and food and clear your plates! The bread was so hard that our teeth hurt after from chewing. My sandwich was mostly onions, barely any cheese and three slivers of steak. My son said his mac and cheese was good and that was about the only positive comment made. Panera is overrated and I have never heard anything good about it, and now I know why.

text: I downloaded the Yelp app on my phone to specifically give this review. I have NEVER encountered such a lack of customer service. I travel every year and have stayed in countless hotels. Yet I've never witness such a disconnect from pleasing the customer. Upon arriving to the hotel my husband was met with an unprofessional desk clerk and accommodations that we hadn't reserved. We just got married and requested a king size bed but was put into a double room with absolutely no resolve. Even after my sister talked to management nothing could be done, nor was any compensation offered. Moreover, we woke up to loud noises and banging due to construction that we were not notified about. When me husband called down to the front desk we were told "sorry for not letting you know earlier but there's no compensation that can be given!" As a frequent traveler, you encounter situations that are beyond managements control. However, a business that cares about their customers compensate you for what's in their control. This hotel has no qualms about telling their customers no and not following up with any sort of compensation to ease the customers let downs. The saddest part of this stay is this hotel is situated in a prime location which is very accessible to city life.  The best part of our stay-cation was when we weren't in the hotel. We were able to walk to Redding Terminal for lunch and just experience down town. It's extremely unfortunate that I would NEVER recommend this hotel to anyone. I have never felt so underserved and ignored in a hotel before. Despite its prime location, this hotel is a -1 for me. You would also like to think that if the service is bad the rooms are amazing. The rooms are a let down as well. The rooms are  not modernized and the beds are uncomfortable. We were also told that because we have a comped reservation that we couldn't be moved to another room. We were given our stay as a wedding gift. I found that comment to be very rude and revealed that staff had no intention of even treating us like a regular customer. I hope that management figures out a better plan for training their staff and creating an environment where customers feel heard, appreciated and ultimately satisfied with their experience. I am unequivocally disappointed with mines. STAY AWAY!!!

text:
Being very picky about pasta my expectations are very low for anything I get at a neighborhood place. The chicken Parmesan entree here put my preconceived notions to shame. The plate was enormous, almost unfairly so. The chicken parm itself was above average and if I didn't have the pasta it would be the star of this review. 

But that pasta. Had to have been at least 3/4lb on the plate, but it's not the volume that's of importance. It was cooked perfectly. Still had a bite to it unlike what you're used to from a neighborhood place that doesn't have someone who cares cooking. And it was tossed with an amount of Parmesan cheese (the real stuff, not some out-of-the-can substitute) that would make an Italian blush.

So very highly recommended, and your leftovers will be enough for three days.
name: Mackenzie

text:
In Tucson for the weekend and decided to try this place out as it was recommended by some family members. I'm glad we managed to fit this place into our busy schedule because it was pretty damn good. I ordered the Chile Con Carne and I guess it's safe to say that I liked it because there was literally nothing left on the plate. The steak meat was cooked to perfection and was very tender with lots of flavor. This plate even comes with fresh tortillas, rice and beans. The rice could have used a little more flavor, but not bad.

The service is great as well. We showed up around the lunch rush and as you can imagine, this place was hopping! Even though the restaurant was busy, the server did a remarkable job of being attentive to all the tables in his section and kept his friendly demeanor along with a smile on his face. 

The decor is great and this restaurant sits on the top of a hill with a stunning view of the City of Tucson. Can't be beat! We will definitely make it back to this establishment when we return to Tucson in March! Two thumbs up for sure!

text:
Complete waste of time and money for refused service. This restaurant is apart of grubhub and claims to be open late. There is no disclaimer in their website about refused service and they are all to willing to take your money. The manager stated on the phone that he wasn't going to deliver to MacDill AFB because there was too much red tape. It didn't matter that I could call the gate and alert then that they were coming and then the process would've sped up. 

The manager then proceeded to scold me for placing the order and as every base is different I informed him in was on temporary duty here so his claim that I should have known was invalid and he refused to cancel the order and refund me and abruptly hung up in my face. I was forced to call Grubhub and alerted them of the situation. Their solution was a refund in 3 to 5 days which is utterly ridiculous and a $10 credit for my next order. 

I'm not in the habit of wasting over $45 dollars for services that were refused. It's not that they cannot deliver the restaurant refused. Rheybshouks add that disclaimer to their website. I'm not letting this go and no one should order from this terrible restaurant. Grubhub should remove them from the delivery service.

The eggs and potatoes were good but the toast was dry (no butter) and they don't bring a variety of jelly.  My husband ordered Country Fried Chicken and said it was "okay" but he wouldn't order it again.  The best thing on the table was probably the Bloody Mary which passed our test but won't be added to any "favorites list".  

The restaurant was empty aside from a few people in the bar.  Considering how slow it was the service was awful.  Our waitress was irritated when we asked for sides or refills.  At one point in time she came and asked us if we needed anything; when we responded NO she told us she was going to take a break and go sit down.  I have never had a server act so careless about their job or their service.  I definitely do NOT recommend this place for Sunday Brunch but I may have to go back and try their regular menu.

text:
Who can say no to oysters when in NOLA? Acme was on my list from the moment I knew I was heading out South so I was excited to find out that they had this location. Located in Harrah's Casino, the vibe of this location is more Las Vegas than NOLA for vibe so if you want the more authentic feel I would go to another spot. 

The line doesn't move as quickly as you would think so if you're coming with a larger group come after 8PM because the line/tables emptied out by then. 

For $20 you can get yourself 1 dozen oysters. I thought the oysters had a yummy herb butter/cheese sauce but they were on the smaller side of the scale so the 1 dozen went by really quickly. The oysters were good but I think the shrimp etouffe was the clear winner of the dishes we had here.

We had not gotten our food at this point so we were there for a good bit longer. Every time I looked in her direction she was on her phone. These are the servers always complaining about not being tipped. Well If they were as interested in their tables as they was their phone or a cigarette break I imagine they would do a little better in that department.
