text: I absolutely love this place and the concept. There's not much around like it! Their food is fresh and the prices are great. Definitely will be visiting this place often!
name: Jessica

text:
I was so impressed (in a positive way) with this place!
First, the ambiance. It is very small. I love their "U-shaped" bar. It makes sitting at the bar less lonely if you're by yourself or even a good option for couples. There aren't many tables. We were sitting at a table upstairs. 

We ordered appetizers first: dumplings in chili oil, taiwanese burger and the cucumber cold appetizer. 

Cucumber: delicious! Big chunks of cucumber soaked in a spicy but flavorful sauce. 
Dumplings: how do they even make that dough so thin? The chili oil was so good. Spicy as well. 
Taiwanese burger: it is like a bao bun. It has pork belly inside and I thought it was pretty good, despite some negative reviews I have read. The bun was warm, not too heavy... the pork belly was melting in my mouth. Very good. Would definitely order again. 

Then we moved on to ordering the main course. Tip: share!! We got one noodle dish, one meat dish and one vegetable dish for two and it was PLENTY of food. 

Chicken in garlic sauce: among their non-spicy options. Very tasty. Would order again. 
Taiwanese Zha Jiang noodles (with chicken, shrimp and pork): that was amazing! I could eat the entire bowl like.. now! 
Brussels sprouts: they have bacon so... how can you go wrong?? 

And what about how fast our food came? We were really impressed with the overall experience. 

Please note that they have reasonable priced bottles of wine, another plus!
name: Giovanna

text: Delicious!! As a vegan, I find it challenging to eat well while traveling. This ginormous poke bowl is delicious and exactly what I needed!! Super fresh!! We all need more sunshine and poke in our lives!
name: Andi

text: Cheers to the Bartenders!! SHANE is THE very best bartender I have had the pleasure of hanging out with for an evening of fun! He makes the best drinks, hustles the whole time all while making you feel like friends! Had such a great experience that it got us back for a second night in a row!! And we are so glad we did because two amazing singers, Jake & Faydra,  entertained the full house while Lindsey & Barry joined my list of great bartenders!!  You must try the Asiago Crab & Artichoke Dip and the Lava Lava Shrimp! In the sea of fun places on Broadway, this place is NOT to be passed up! We will DEFINATELY be back!
name: Amber

text:
Great Place! 
I had my husbands 70th Surprise Birthday Party there and I can't tell you enough how wonderful it was. There were 27 people in attendance, we had a private room with 3 GREAT waiters just for us. Ben, the owner and chef did a fantastic job. You had better go there hungry because they serve huge portions. I am 100 % Italian so I know my Italian food
Rosemary
name: Rosemary

text:
Pretty bad service. I got Jamaican jerk chicken, It was drier than a camels urethra. How do you even 
Dry chicken that much? The side dishes were good. My friends liked their food apparently. Drinks were kind of weak.
name: Maximillian

text: If I could give a negative star, this restaurant would take the cake (or soup). So this is the cliff-note version waited over two hours at the bar for soup. Got my Brussels sprouts which were very good. But how the hell can you screw up SOUP. All I wanted was their Ale and Onion au Gratin soup. This isn't the first time an Iron Hill Brewery screwed up my meal and made me wait! I will never go back and I consider myself a foodie, I'm sorry, but Iron Hill your service sucks and is equivalent to Trumps tan, TERRIBLE.

text: We've had great experiences before sitting in one of the red bar tables, but the service tonight was very uncomfortable with long waits for drinks, or long wait for our credit card to come back to us.  We tried to grin and bear it but the second time the one bartender handing the bar area seemed to leave for 10 to 15 minutes at a time.  This happened two times during this dinner. Food is always delicious, but that should give you an idea of how serious we are when we say will never be back.  It's a shame.  We had great experiences ove 5-7 years, but we are done.
name: Joe

text: Attended a jazz brunch in November with my friends, and this was by far one of the best experiences we've had dining in NOLA. The atmosphere is warm, welcoming and so much fun. The balloons on each table add to the happy vibes of the place and truly put you in the spirit of the city. Our waiter (I believe his name was Kevin) was promptly at our table taking our drink orders once we sat. He didn't miss a beat. He was warm, and super knowledgeable about the menu. He answered every and any question we had. We never had to ask for refills, and the food arrived swiftly. We ordered from the pre fixe brunch menu - I had the Shrimp and Tasso Henican, Cochon De Lait Benedict, and the perfect pecan pie (a la mode because why not!) we all ordered different plates so we could sample a bit of everything. Every dish was perfectly cooked, seasoned and plated to perfection. A lot of times with dishes the flavors meld together... that doesn't happen here! Every bite packs a variety of flavors that are sure to satisfy your senses. the kitchen has been the stepping stone for many talented Nola chefs - and they've left their mark on the menu. Make room for any meal here, as they aren't skimpy on the quantity. Honestly, I never expected THAT much food! We were so full by the time it was time to order dessert, but couldn't pass it up! The band was awesome and took requests - they even played Sinatra for us !! The vibes here are so uplifting and happy! It's hard to keep a warm, personal vibe in an establishment that is so large, but the Commanders Family has found the way and they sure deliver! Southern hospitality and family are at the forefront here and it's evident in the service, food and atmosphere. Commanders is definitely a must if you're in NOLA. I'll be back for sure !!! Hats off to Miss. Ella and Co. for blessing us with the phenomenon that is Commander's Palace !
name: Christina

text: Wow!! My coworker recommended this place and it definitely does not disappoint. Easily the BEST FAST FOOD PIZZA. The slices are very thick and totally makes it worth the calories. They have a card system which is a great idea! You order, they charge it to a card, then you pay after you finish eating. It's basically like a food court - lots of options from pizza, pasta, salad, hoagies to dessert and very reasonably priced.
name: Lillian

text: Best roll over I've ever had is the firework roll. We also had the Salmon bento. Wonderful!
name: Jessica

a mad costumer

text: Cafe Binh is the best Banh Mi place in South Philly. My husband and I love Vietnamese food and have had Banh mi's from all the local spots in S. Philly. This place makes the most fragrant and fresh Banh Mi's. There's always a decent amount of meat and pate on it. We love their cold cut the most!
name: Peiying

text: The first time the burger was good and juicy, second time the burger was dry and burnt, third time the onion had what seems to be 10lbs of sugar on it when they grilled it. Such a hit or miss place, I guess it's all dependent on who is cooking and heir mood, was happy with the burger their first time.

text:
The interior of Giwa is modern and clean. Ordering on the touch screen was easy -- being able to see pictures of the menu items is a nice touch, however depending on what you order it can be quite expensive. 

I had the cold bibimbap which was fully customizable. I had two proteins: spicy chicken, and beef, and then substituted kale (instead of rice). The sides that were included were also amazing.

text: Portions were generous and presentation was nice. Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. text: Ordered takeout because I didn't feel like cooking and it held up okay. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. I'd maybe go back, but I'd order differently next time. It looked better online than it did in person.

I always grab just a few usually the toasted coconut and the sugar jelly. I've had a wide variety of their donuts though. All have been fantastic! I'm a huge fan of the monster donut as well, I love buying them as gag gifts. I've heard good things about their coffee and it's a good cup of joe. I just wish there was one closer to me. I wish they would open one in Bensalem/Ne Philly. Great place!

I don't mind the wait because the muffaletta is my favorite sandwich. If you're in NOLA, definitely check this place out. text: I've been wanting to try the new Focused Health Blends, so I ordered The Trim Fit. I chose this one in particular because it's the only one without banana (though I'm sure you could ask to omit the banana from the others) and I was looking for something low-sugar. The Trim Fit is a blend of coconut water, spinach, kale, avocado, ginger, lemon, peaches, chia seeds, flax seeds, pea protein, and stevia. It's supposed to be low calorie/carb and high protein. The cashier asked if I wanted  to add unsweetened coconut shavings to it for free, and since I love coconut I said yes. Funny enough, I couldn't taste or feel the coconut at all. I got a little bit of a tingle at the back of my throat from the ginger, and the lemon flavor really came through. It ultimately tasted like a slice of lemon and poppyseed something to me - good stuff! I only wish these Focused Health Blends were offered in a size other than the 16 oz. I would've gone bigger! Can't wait to try a different one.
name: Iva

text: I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. No big complaints, just a nice meal. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. The food was good and the service was easygoing. A very pleasant experience. Not bad for a quick meal. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Food was good and came out fast. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean.

text:
This place is great.  They have smoothies, coffee, tea, takeout, and baked goods!  And the girl who waited on me was super sweet. 

I had their Wake me up smoothie with almond milk and added a banana and peanut butter powder.  It was good!!  Great size for the price.  

Though I didn't get any take out or baked goods I was definitely temped. It smelled amazing in there and their brownies looked delicious!  I'm going to have to go back.

text: I ordered a pizza (thin crust) and a salad (takeaway guilt of eating a pizza).  I ordered with the Domino's App.  It was the easiest thing I ever did.  The food was great and exact.  Jason was on time and friendly.  There is no guessing on what you ordered because you see it on the App.  It also shows you the current process your order is in and let's you know when it's out for delivery.  Can't beat it.

text: Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. It looked better online than it did in person. Nice little spot, decent portions too.
name: User

text: I don't know how their service is when you sit down but as far as takeout goes that's the worst service I've ever had food was cold I ordered a grand slam with pancakes and extra sausage I got the pancakes did not get the sausage did not get toast did not get syrup for the pancakes. Called to complain told me I had to bring it back instead of giving me a credit on my card over the phone. I will not eat at this restaurant ever again. text: We went about 10am on a Saturday, it was pretty crowded with a good amount of people waiting. They told us it would be 20 minutes. text:
Went to the Sunday Brunch (all you can eat buffet & drinks) today and had a great experience! The food was excellent and so were the unlimited drinks! Sheldon was very kind to us and very accommodating, excellent management who actually care about customers. Definitely will return and I would recommend the brunch to any and all - 10am-2pm on Sundays. There is no deal like this anywhere in IV. Thanks again Sheldon! 

Jake & Val

text: Visited 3/1/19 - While we were on the other side of town, we decided to pop into Kei Sushi. The place is nicely decorated, and we were sat at the bar promptly.  We visited during dinner hours, so we ordered accordingly.  We didn't experience any issues, but nothing about the menu was a stand-out either.  The service was fine, and so was the timing of the rolls.  Reno/Sparks has sooooo many AYCE anymore, they're either amazing, really bad or OK.  For us, our experience was just OK.  Good, not great, but not bad either.  Because it's literally the opposite side of town for us, it's not likely to be our new regular spot.

text: Don't know what all the fuss is about my wife and I were seated a bar service was fine ordered a burger which was okay at best fries looked like there were frozen and fried wife ordered the ribeye which was over cooked and would compare to a thin breakfast steak drinks were fine don't think we will be returning here.

text:
Wednesday evening 7:30pm walked over from Residence Inn (3-4 min walk).  Totally empty, was greeted warmly and invited to sit anywhere.  Outdoor seating available.

Ordered a Coke, house salad and personal sized combo (supreme style) pizza.  Salad ingredients were all fresh, pizza came out quickly and was super tasty with perfectly crispy crust.  Very nice flavor!

Very close to Courtyard Marriott and Residence Inn so great for travelers.  Great local spot.  Banter between employees was all casual and fun giving off a good vibe.  Definitely visit!

text: We stopped by after visiting Winterthur and ordered an assortment of pastries and cookies.  Everything was pretty good, but nothing special.  The employees should learn how to smile.  The prices were a little on the high side.  Next!

text: 5 star on Food & service! All 4 of us ordered a variety of dishes starting with the Golubtzy, then the Syrniki, then the meat blinchiki and finished with the Banana Nutella Blinchiki. Everything was delicious and our server was delightful.  I will highly recommend this restaurant.  It's a culinary gem in Tampa.
name: Lorena

text: This place just opened up where the old Pho Express used to be. It's owned by the sweetest Asian couple, they were super friendly. We ordered the chicken drunken noodle and the shrimp pineapple fried rice and they were both delicious! There were so many pieces of chicken and shrimp in each dish and the portion sizes were huge, you definitely get your bang for your buck here. The drunken noodle was legit spicy and had me gulping down 3 cups of water so if your spice tolerance is low, I would recommend modifying the level (they are more than willing to accommodate). Highly recommend and will be back again!
name: Bianca

text:
Every time we come here for lunch or dinner it's so good. The Won Ton soup is fantastic, as well as the rest of the food.

It's a great family owned place where you will probably eat too much and wish you have on your Thanksgiving pants.

Stop by.

UPDATE: Awesome as usual. The BBQ pork lo mein and Mongolian beef/chicken was fantastic. My wife got a cup of won ton soup, yes I had a little. It tasted so good. 

The flavors keep you wanting to eat until you can't anymore.

The food is so good and the prices are still very reasonable.
name: Mike

text: First time ordering from here and I honestly wasn't sure what to expect. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Overall, a strong experience. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.
name: User

text:
Cute new cafe in Temple Terrace, however a disappointing first visit. Our lunch visit took nearly two hours and we waited about an hour and change for our food. The server who helped us checked on us maybe every 30min and did not give an explanation of the excessive wait. This place has a lot of potential but if they want to continue to receive business they will have to figure it out...and fast. Friends of mine visited this cafe a couple of weeks ago and had the same complaints. 

As for the food. I ordered the burger and side of home fries. The burger was decent. I can't complain. The home fries were a disappointment. They were half the size of normal home fries and the portion was tiny. 

I will be interested in hearing everyone else's thoughts. Hopefully, like I said before, they get it together soon.
name: Ashley

text: Great snack. Polish Sausage with mustard / onions was delicious...and even the crinkled fries had a nice flavor/ seasoning. I'll be back.
name: Schárvín

text:
Great pizzas!  Tried the pepperoni and carbonara, both were very excellent in their own way.  Was privileged to seat at the counter right in front of the kitchen and oven and got to see them make dozens of pizzas while I dined.  Their food preparing, cooking, and serving system is very well refined, everyone working hard and on top of things, including the owner.  Be aware that if you sit here you get to see the pizzas come out of the oven and guaranteed to make you drool!
Place is not that big and is quite popular so if you are a larger party of say 6 or more it is definitely best you make reservations well ahead of time.  I hope they continue their success and eventually expand their dining area to meet the demand.
name: Ramiro

text:
I recently had one of the best steaks I've ever eaten at Brick's Restaurant in Reno, NV.   It was also one of the largest.  A 32 ounce, bone in cowboy/tomahawk ribeye served medium rare with Brick's house salad, side of freshly grilled veggies, homemade mashed potatoes, and glass of 1000 Stories Zinfandel.  I didn't think they could top it until the tiramisu showed up.....  OH Myyyyyyyyy.

THANK YOU "BRICKS" for helping us celebrate with an impromptu dinner and accommodating reservations.  You rock James! 

PS.  I brought what I didn't finish home with me for steak and eggs the next morning.
name: Michael

text:
Food was excellent but very expensive for small portions. 
Server was polite and informative but dropped the ball on the bill: he gave it to us and did not return for 20 minutes. Only when we stood up to leave did he realize we needed him to complete the transaction. 
The women at the reception desk, who also took coats, were not friendly. Cold reception. They seemed bothered to have to deal with us. 
Furthermore, if you want a reservation for four or more, you must give a credit card number and they insist on 48 hour notice and charge $25 per person if you contact them after the 48 hour deadline. Really?!  
 Too many negatives here. I like the place but won't return soon!
name: An

text: One of the top meals I've had in my life!! Amazing from start to finish, and the wait staff is attentive, friendly and on point! Worth every single penny you spend there. Only thing I wished for was more wines in the $30-50 range. Wine list is extensive, but packed with very high end options. I tasted everyone's entree at our 5 person table, and I could've licked every plate clean! Barbecue Salmon, Andouille Crusted Drum, Pork Chop, Lobster Bucatini and Wagyu Beef were our entree choices. Chicken Andouille gumbo - delicious and super dark roux - yum. The Duck Wings appetizer is a can't-miss item!! Chocolate Peanut Butter Pie for dessert - divine. They also had Free Valet Parking!
name: Rachel

text: I had lunch here today with a group of friends and I ordered the veggie quiche with hash browns.  Several variations of this quiche were listed on the sign at the entry.  Very average food.  The hash browns were just warm and I've had much better quiche elsewhere.
name: Doris

text: Great upscale setting. Service was attentive.  Food was decent but wasn't original in any form.  Good for large parties.
name: Marilyn

text: Open late, quick and friendly service, and food was amazing (tried the chicken corma and aashak). They gave us a taste of their homemade ice cream which was also great. I've been here twice and would highly recommend if you're in the area!
name: Amanda

text: I ordered the House Blend Aged Beef Burger, medium rare (without the bun, of course), and replaced the fries with cucumber salad (less the trout roe). The burger was awesome dipped in their Churchill Sauce. My wife had hers medium with the fries. She said it was cooked perfect and there was special salt on the fries. My son thinks the mac & cheese with ham hock was the best mac & cheese he's had. I had a King Henry's Kick but went straight up and no salt. If you like tequila and the smoke of mezcal, you'll love this drink. Service was excellent.
name: Greg

text:
This is no ordinary sandwich shop. Freshly baked soft but firm bread. Fun bomb sauces and garlicky dressing. Good amount of ingredients within sandwich.

I got my sub to-go and I could feel the hefty weight of the amount of ingredients.

Extra plus, it maintains its shape even when kept in fridge to be eaten later.

Lots of choices of toppings/ingredients.
name: Joyce

text:
Recommended by friends from NYC and certainly not disappointed!!  Went for happy hour yesterday (3/22). Our server, Stephen, was impeccable. Always available but never pestering. He took time to explaining the HH menu items (drinks as well as food) in detail with all suggestions, spot on. We decided to stay for dinner and this was perfect as well. Plentiful and tasteful portions!!  
Will definitely return on future trips to the area!!

text: Im gonna say, for having a drive thru they are pretty fast, went last night and had a few laughs with the girl working the drive thru because she got confused and gave me an empty cup! Haha! (From working front register so long) she was funny and you could tell she was trying. The food was great and hot I'll def be going back to that drive thru soon! Yay south meadows for having a drive thru.
name: Livi

text: Always friendly even when ordering last minute -20 min before closing time!! Portions are large and fairly priced (just add some salt). It's like a 30 min drive for me to get there which is always annoying but I've had only good experiences with this place. Try it out:) ..... I enjoy hanks hushpuppies much more but this place has way more variety in regards to fried seafood for a decent price. Love
name: Cassandra

text: Absolutely wonderful little place! Great energy! Fabulous drinks and tasty bites! The owner is one-of-a-kind! Awesome and welcoming! Just go!
name: Emry

text: Cinco de Mayo on Old Hickory Boulevard is, and has been our favorite Mexican restaurant, period. 4 generations from out family have had their food.  The folks there are courteous and helpful, and the food is the closest you're going to get to Authentic Mexican north of Uvalde, Texas.  Try their fried jalapenos - they're awesome - go on your birthday, and tell .hem, you will have memories that last a lifetime.  don't drink the water, though.......just kidding. these folks are really nice, good folks - yeah, I wish they were open until 11, but a lot of these folks work their ass off, in case you didn't know it - yeah, they've mucked up my order, but grow up and speak up - they will fix it. PS, their sweet tea is the best in the South. :-)
name: Kari

text: Nice atmosphere , but expensive 3 sandwiches with fries and 1 drink and 2 ice teas ,bill was 65.00 and wasn't anything special
name: David

text: Went with family on a Sunday and it was louder than I expected. The staff seemed tired but still polite. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. It was crowded but still moved along. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. Kind of landed in the middle for me. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.
name: User

text:
They have a lot to learn about service. The male bartender was super apathetic and seemingly annoyed by our existence...ex: when taking our brunch order he just walked up and said "Food?" In general he couldn't be bothered to interact with us, let alone do it with any hospitality. 

Lousy drinks --  the mimosas are a ripoff. We ordered a carafe, but it was 90% juice, only the neck was topped off w/ sparkling wine. We're not ordering juice here, people, we're ordering drinks! A mimosa should be mostly sparkling and topped w/ juice. I asked if he could add more but his adjustment made no difference. But here's the kicker -- when a friend of the apathetic bartender sat next to us, she was welcomed with smiles and jovial hospitality, and when she ordered a mimosa guess what she got? 90% sparkling wine, topped with juice! You know, the way they're supposed to be made.

Clearly there's no front-of-house manager to oversee and ensure good service.

Food-wise, it's meh. The forgettable $13 & $15 entrees didn't come with sides, so you gotta pay extra to have potatoes or grits or bacon w/ those eggs.

text:
This is a good restaurant for people who don't like Mexican restaurants or Mexican food. Most good Mexican restaurants are simple but warm and invitingly this place, evidently in an attempt to be hip and alternative, is outfitted more like a cafeteria:  wide open space with plain tables and chairs. Fishbowl windows. The food nods toward Mexican cuisine in form factor but that's about it. I passed on the carnitas, noting in the menu that they inexplicably contaminated it with cinnamon and orange. (?) after studying the menu for a while looking for tacos I might like (everything is "inventive"), I settled on the Carne Asada tacos. Since they apparently are incapable of preparing a taco of any kind without cabbage, I ordered the cabbage on the side. When the meal came I found two street-taco sized flour tortillas with oil on them, each lying flat with about 1-1/2 Tbsp of tough beef chopped into 1/4" cubes, and an equal amount of diced tomato and onion with some sort of oil dressing. These were accompanied by a massive pile of ordinary black beans and another big pile of rice. Since the beans and rice outweighed the tacos by about 150% I'm not sure why they named the meal after the tacos. My 7-year-old son ordered the kids cheese quesadilla which came dripping in grease (yes, it was actually dripping) and was fairly burned-- he didn't want much of it because it was so badly overlooked on the outside. My wife ordered some kind of steak bowl which she thought was okay but said it wasn't anything like Mexican food.
The server was reasonably attentive and prompt, although her interest in us was quite obviously feigned; nevertheless we tipped her well because she was doing her best.
So, if you appreciate food that has been modified for the sake of originality and are not interested in authentic Mexican food, you should probably give this place a shot. I hope you like it!
name: Pete

text:
So, I came back to Shake Shack again. This time I brought my husband along with me.

The fountain coke complimented the meal really well. (We are Coca Cola fans!) And our hotdog was just okay. I love the vibe here. I love love these burgers and fries. When we come to Nashville to visit (which is often) we'll for sure continue to stop in here.

text:
If you're looking for the best German food in the Tampa area, this is the place to go! Mr. Dunderbak's has been around for awhile and I love how they have kept their same traditions going on for all these years. The place is 100% authentically covered in German decor and I love their deli market section where they sell German sausages, European candy, and more! 

I went here for dinner recently on a Saturday, and the place was packed. People were waiting for tables but I saw that the bar was wide open and those are first come, first serve. They also serve food at the bar, so if you don't want to wait for a dining table, I suggest you just head on over to their bar. 

I ordered the "OKTOBERFEST SAUSAGE PLATTER" that comes with two sides of your choice. Loved it, and it paired so perfectly with the German beer that the bartender helped me pick out. I was full from eating all of that, but I decided that I would split a dessert with the group. We got the "HAUSMADE APPLE STRUDEL" with vanilla ice cream. It was delicious! I always enjoy eating here and I look forward to my next visit :)

text: If you're looking for good Armenian food, never tried middle eastern food, or are none of the above, you still need to go to Apricot Stone. A BYOB, very affordable, Armenian restaurant in Philly. Better than my mother's cooking? I'll never say but holy moly. Try everything on the menu. Specifically the Manti, lemajun, and khadif. Unreal experience with my friends who had never had this kind of food before. They are now hooked!

text:
Update summer 2019- after our first few times here which were great, we saw some repeating things that we would have overlooked had the service and quality of food not kept fluctuating. The last time we ate there (maybe our 6th time), my husband got a panini and it came out on soggy bread. The kitchen staff seemed blasé and two times in a row the food was not worth the asking price. Sad because my husband's dietary needs have changed and we really want to like this place but aren't intending to go back currently. 

Spring 2019: Great ambience and even better food. 
This place has been great since my husband is currently on a very restricted diet. It's fun to be able to get good vegetarian food that is flavorful and innovative. I asked them to explain one of the main dishes so I could better understand what it would be comprised of and they were helpful with suggestions. I loved the chai. 

We've been twice and had the potato salad, the scallion pancake (yum!), the jasmine rice cakes, mushroom po boy, tempeh, and more, and it's all been amazing. 

Recommend this place for meat eaters and veggies alike! Creative and classy. Two enthusiastic thumbs

text:
Culinary Dropout's food was freaking delicious! The first time I went with a friend we really enjoyed the grilled chicken sandwich and the M.A.C. Burger. Oh boy, the food was splendid, awesome we genuinely enjoyed how flavorful the burgers were and what! The fries were pretty tasty. Lip smackin'! 
However......
Our waitress seldom checked up on us, and we waited quite a while to get our tab for the meal. And even waiting for my ice tea refill was a bit of a bother. 
Alright. 
Second time, I came in and ordered the same sandwich, however with another friend. 
Funny enough, we got the same waitress! Such is fate. Service is below average, some would say it's subpar.
First thing when the food came, barely a few  minutes after we had been served; we were asked on how we were enjoying the food. Whoaaa we didn't even start yet. This time the tab came in at the right time. I asked for an ice tea refill. Maybe I should've learned from the first time we waited a hot minute for a refill. The decor, ambience, and the boisterous environment makes it so hip and fun to be at. 
I'll come back if the service is improved. Unfortunately I won't be back for a while. Sorry! This place is an unpolished jade. 

Updated review: We came back to give it another try. Considering on not coming back because of the service. It's a hit or miss with service. It truly depends on which server you get. This time we got a different server. It was excellent service. Brought our hopes up to come back again and possibly become regulars. The food, of course was not even disappointing! We love it so much! Kudos to the cooks. Much love.

text:
After a long hot morning at Lowry Park Zoo, we stopped at Taco Bus on the way to the Florida Aquarium. We decided to eat inside, where you can look over a menu as you haphazardly line up in front of a bar. There are four round tables right inside the door, and in a second room, some booths.
I ordered the Grande Twin Tacos, a carne asada and a shrimp. My husband ordered the dos tacos in carne asada and an al pastor. My mother-in-law got the burrito bowl with carne asada, and my kids each got kids quesadillas. 

My tacos were ok. Warm, not hot. The steak had good flavor, but the temperature really left something to be desired. The shrimp also had pretty good flavor, but weren't hot either. I will say that there was a pleasing amount of meat in both tacos.
Husband said he enjoyed the steak, but the pastor was bland. He said they were the perfect size to hold him over until dinner.
My mother-in-law's bowl was deceptive because it definitely like a ton of lettuce, but all the meat was on the bottom. She said was a ton of food, and delicious, but there was no way she was eating all of it alone.
Kids are kids, and sometimes they like a thing and sometimes they don't. One liked her food and the other said he didn't like the cheese, but he still finished it off.

We also ordered chips and salsa, which were pretty good. I could have eaten those all day - chips were still a bit warm, salty, with a great crunch. 

They didn't have any beer today, even though it's on the menu. Not sure what the deal was there, and the cashier just sort of shrugged and waved her hand at the cooler behind her. We got a Mexican Coke, which also wasn't very cold. Had I known there was a freestyle fountain outside, I would have gone for that instead.

Not a terrible lunch, but also nothing to write home about. I'd come back if I was in the area and needed something to eat quickly. There are too many other delicious options in the area to go out of my way.
name: Samantha

text:

text:
A friend was headed to my place at dinner time and Thai China Bistro was on the way, so they picked up take-out for us both. It was fine -- not terrible, but certainly not great. Just okay. 

We both ordered pad thai -- I got shrimp in mine, and she got tofu. As other reviewers have noted, the pad thai is a somewhat startling yellow. I'm not sure why it's this color. The flavor was very muted; I ended up cutting up a lime I had in the fridge to squeeze on it, and added sriracha as well as some other seasonings I had in order to give it more flavor. The noodles were on the gummy side, and tended to clump. I will say that the shrimp were well-cooked, though. 

It wasn't bad; it was just "meh". It was a purely a choice of convenience on this occasion, and I'm glad we at least tried it, but I'll probably opt for the inconvenient but tastier choice next time.

text:
SERVICE:  Left a lot to be desired. We went to Oliver's for lunch.  Only 4 tables were  occupied on the patio, lots of empty tables.  The waitress took our order and did not write down the one change we requested: No poblano peppers on the Beyond Burger.  This required waiting for the cook to prepare another one, as the hot pepper taste got all over the burger and made it inedible.   When paying $24 for an Oliver's burger, I'd like to think the waitress might pay attention, especially since the  restaurant was not busy at all.  The bus boy was more helpful than the waitress. She disappeared after the meals were served, but he helped make it right.  Of course, when it came time for a tip, she was most solicitous.  

SETTING:  The patio was beautiful and peaceful, and the bar was well-designed.  Pretty place to be.

FOOD:  The Oliver's burger, served on a pretzel bun with coconut "bacon," was delicious.  It was my friend's birthday, and they did give her an apple crumble dessert on the house, so that helped a bit.

OVERALL:  To hit it out of the park, the food, atmosphere and service all need to be excellent, especially at a high end vegan restaurant.  I'm not inclined to rush back, based on the poor service. I can go to Mesa Verde if I'm craving vegan food, and it will be 1/3 the price.

text:
To start, this place was participating in Brunch for Mutts and did donate a portion of their proceeds from our meal to STL Stray Rescue. This is why we decided to go here in the first place. We knew they were participating in this great cause and thought we'd try out a new brunch place. Sadly, we left feeling very disappointed by The entire experience.
We had reservations for 8 people + a baby at 8:45am. When we arrived the place (which is very large) was nearly empty. They sat us at a nice table in a back corner, which was perfect for us. We started by ordering coffees and my brother in law ordered their "coffee & donuts". The server seemed like he was either incredibly flustered already or was having a rough morning. We waited nearly 15 minutes to get our coffees...no donuts. 10 minutes later he came back to take our order. 3 of the people at our table are vegetarian and one is lactose intolerant, but we specifically picked this place since they had lots of veggie and dairy free options. We all order our food and my BIL asked about his donuts. The guy said the kitchen is backed up and that he'll go check (there were maybe half a dozen tables that had people...by no means full for the size of this place). We gave him the benefit of the doubt and waited. And waited. And waited some more. After 45 min they finally brought out his donuts. He said they were actually quite good. Finally after an hour (this is not an exaggeration) we asked a passing server where our food was. He ran back and started bringing it out. That's when we noticed nearly every order was incorrect. The tofu scrambles that we're ordered both came out as regular scrambles ( the waiter then said that we only said scramble so that's why...which honestly is not the case however even if that were true, it's probably not wise to blame the customer). My breakfast burrito came out cold with some half melted shredded cheese in a cup on the side (I'm not sure why, I did not ask for it on the side), and I ordered it with veggie sausage which may or may not have been what they actually made it with. I will never know. Regardless, it was not good at all. My husbands shrimp and grits omelet was ice cold and looked like it had been sitting under a heat lamp for a good amount of time. He took two bites and left it. We order loaded tots that never came. When we asked about them, the waiter pointed to the plain tots on the plate and said "there's tots right there". We explained those were just plain tots which we order as a substitute for breakfast potatoes but we're missing the loaded tots....he never brought them. 
When we decided to just be done with the meal it was 10:45...2 hours after our reservation (we did show up 10 minutes late due to a baby meltdown...so 1 hour and 50 minutes later). I was walking to the bathroom and the server stopped me and said that none of this was his fault and that he put the order in right but the kitchen messed it all up. It was an extremely uncomfortable interaction. Then the owner came over and apologized, which was nice but by that time it was after 11 and we were still hungry and had just wasted most of our morning. It would have been nice had she came over far sooner. We went to pay and they did take a few items off the bill, however it was still a waste of money considering we all went to get food elsewhere afterwards. We did not argue because we still wanted the donation to go to STL Stray Rescue. 
Honestly, it looks like these are all issues that this restaurant has been dealing with, so I really only hope that they are able to change things around so this doesn't happen to another group of customers. I personally would not chose to come back at this point in time. I'm giving it 2 stars for its participation in a good cause and for the interior...it's a very cool old building. However, those things are not enough to tempt me back in the door.
name: Emily

text:
We had a very nice stay at Loews Philadelphia over the Labor Day Weekend. 
The location is perfect, close to Reading Terminal Market, restaurants, center city, and provides easy access to the other Philly sites! I found the cost per night for a weekend stay to be more affordable than many other hotels in the city and also in the surrounding areas outside the city. 

Our room was very spacious, clean, and well equipped. I was impressed with the overall size of the bathroom and the comfortableness of the bed! I was very pleased with how quiet the hotel floor was at night, even though the hotel was full that weekend, which contributed to the relaxing atmosphere and sleep in the room. We ordered coffee service the night before for the following morning, as we often do at many places we stay. The presentation of the coffee tray was reflective of the high quality of hotel Loews exhibits. In addition to the coffee setting, glasses of ice water were part of the service and the waitperson, who delivered the coffee, was very friendly, professional and helped to start our morning off on a positive note!

The only reason I did not give the last star in the rating was due to the cost of parking. Parking at the hotel is valet only and they charge $49+ per night for guests staying at the hotel, which I find outrageous. Instead of paying this price, we used Parking Panda to locate a parking garage, one block away for only $24 per 24 hours! I don't mind walking a block or two to park if it's only going to cost half the price of the hotel. 

I do recommend the Loews Philadelphia and plan to stay here in the future!

text:
I was on a vacation visiting the beautiful State of Lousiana. In my home State of California, we have one of the most authentic Vietnamese and Chinese foods all across the nation. On top of that influence, my father owned a Chinese restaurant for 30 years. With my familiarity with Chinese and Vietnamese food, I try to be fair at every restaurant I go to. It is very rare to see a conjoined Chinese/Vietnamese restaurant together. Let see how it goes!

Environment - 6.5/10 Rate 
The environment itself was very appealing. Everything seemed very promising when I was welcomed in. Although, I immediately noticed some of the tables were unsanitary. The staffs were friendly, and I was very excited ordering from the menu! 

Boy did I lose all impressions of Asian food in the State of Louisiana. Here's my verdict:

Seafood Chow Mein - 2/10 Rate 
Chow mein is one of my favorite foods of all time. I order chow mein at every Chinese restaurant I go to.  But this dish tore me inside-out. The noodles were so dried, It was like eating dehydrated potato chips. The flavor was very bland, the ingredients such as the shrimp and the broccoli were not fresh. Also, the portion was extremely low. It reminds me of buying chips, you're really buying half a bag of chips and half a bag of air. This was just terrible. 

Sweet and Sour Shrimp - 1.5/10 Rate
The presentation and the colors of this dish looked promising. I froze as soon as I took my first bite; soggy on the outside and extremely dry on the inside. Seriously, what's with these dry ingredients? I know Lousiana gets hot and humid, but so does the food? Unreal.

Mongolian Beef - 3.5/10 Rate
Again, slightly dry. Although not as bad as the other dish. Also, why am I getting more onions and veggies than the meat? Are they trying to reserve meat? The portion is too low, you should've cut me a 50% discount since I was really consuming 50% of the portion. 

Brocolli Chicken - 4/10 Rate
Dry, dry, dry. Slightly flavored. I still ate it, I guess. 

Egg Rolls - 7/10 Rate 
With the side of the serving sauce, it was the only thing I've proudly swallow. Moderately crunchy on the outside, somewhat adequate on the inside. I will give this egg roll a quiet applause. 

Conclusion
I've never in my life had this poor quality of Chinese/Vietnamese food before. I'm not here to bombard this restaurant, just giving an honest feedback. I also don't have intentions to judge a restaurant by just eating there the first time. Maybe this day just happens to be a bad day in the kitchen for the staff. Yes, I will come back again to try a different dish. I hope for a better experience. 

-Alan
name: Alan

text: Mom and I stopped here for lunch after seeing the Chihuly exhibit across the street. Metered parking. Small, but includes outdoor seating as well. Perhaps five tables inside. At lunchtime the place was full but not crowded. We were served promptly by friendly staff. Mom ordered the white bean kale soup. ("What?!" I asked. "I like soup," she replied. Go figure.) I asked the waitress if I should choose the sandwich of the week (ribeye steak  sandwich with provolone) or #23, the chicken salad sandwich. She said the chicken salad was scrumptious, so I went with that. She was right! The sandwich is served on toasted multigrain bread. The chicken salad has chunks of tender chicken that carries a pleasant chicken taste (and you know not all chicken salad does!) The sandwich has avocado, Swiss cheese, and tomato on it as well. The combination yields a delightfully refreshing, satisfying sandwich. Mom's soup came with half a round of sourdough bread ~ a treat in its own right. The clear soup had tender white beans, carrots, and the promised oh-so-fashionable kale. Mom said it was delicious. So, if you like soup.... This little spot seems to cater to nearby offices ~ carts loaded with salads ready to go on a journey came out of the kitchen at a steady pace. This was a fun stop. We were served promptly enough so that our 2-hour meter fare allowed touring of the Chihuly exhibit (including the movie!) checking out the Morean Art  Center, and this fun lunch!

text: I had been researching a good Chinese buffet option and had read many good comments on Dong's. I convinced my family to head down to Mooresville and it is in the shopping area next to Kroger's. Is was very warm but had lots of great ingredients in it and was good during the winter. Next I surveyed the options. I went for a crab Rangoon as good as I've had at other places and tasted quite fresh which is harder on the fried items as they can get soggy or stale. I saw them rotating items while I was there. The honey bbq rib was great really enjoyable. Also the chicken on the stick was flavorful and I wanted to be hungry to eat more but focused on trying more items. My favorite was shrimp in the white sauce with vegetables. The vegetables were great in this as was the shrimp. I also got some of the mushrooms and meat don't remember what meat it was but the mushrooms in this was excellent. I got some of the green beans too. They also have ice cream and some dessert items. I picked up two of the cream puffs. I was getting pretty full at this point. The service was very attentive with removal of dishes as well. Overall a great lunch. I look forward to returning.

text:
We booked this "resort" through Hotwire. Hotwire has been hit or miss for us lately, so we were prepared to have a lesser quality room - even at a room approaching $200 for a night.

We arrived at night and the drive in past the guard house appeared nice with great attention to the landscaping. Valet parking appeared to be mandatory. 

The walk from registration to our room (429) was easily 1/4 mile on dimly lit walkways. We were greeted upon entering with a large stain on the carpet and what appeared to be white blobs of plaster embedded in the carpet. 

It's pretty clear this place hasn't been updated in decades. The counters in the bathroom came up to our mid-thighs (we're average height) and I have never seen such a low toilet. Ever.

We were both hungry, so we hiked over to the steakhouse (again along dark pathways). Upon arriving, we were told they were short staffed (on a Saturday night, definitely after any rush), and had to sit in the bar with some remarkably loud drunk people. The food was average. On the hike back to the room, we passed three people carrying a fourth person who was unconscious and snoring loudly. I am not joking about this. 

The next morning, on the hike back to valet parking, we passed lengths of toilet paper on the pathway, a rolled up sock and random trash (plastic cup, straw, paper) in the landscaping. 

Definitely not coming back and wouldn't recommend it to anyone.
name: Jim

text:
The hype around this place makes it really difficult to rate, as I've been anticipating trying the "best pizza in the country" for years. I am a self proclaimed pizza snob originally from the pizza capital of the world, so my standards might be higher than most.

We walked in a few minutes before our 7:30pm reservation on a Wednesday evening. We were asked to wait outside until our table opened up. Though it was only about 10/15 minutes, I really dislike when places do this. Please don't seat walk-ins at tables if you're not going to be able to honor reservations you already have.

We were seated at what I thought was the best spot in the house - one of the booths against the kitchen window where you could watch the chefs bring each pizza down the line. We decided on two pizzas: the standard pie with pepperoni and the special - white sauce with corn, cherry tomatoes, cheese, and a basil vinaigrette.

The special came out first. The basil vinaigrette had a little kick, which was a welcome flavor. I love cooked cherry tomatoes and theirs were perfectly popped in the oven. I was disappointed that you really couldn't taste the corn, as it's one of my favorite summer flavors and in my opinion really the whole point of getting a corn pie. Next was the pepperoni. I think this was my favorite of the two, though I wouldn't recommend it if you don't like a little grease. Between four people, we could've definitely eaten three pies, as they're pretty thin and ~16 inch rounds. 

I ended the meal with an espresso soft serve, which was extremely creamy and filled with coffee flavor. I think it was my favorite part of the meal.

Overall, the pizza is good. Is it the best pizza in Fishtown? Probably. Is it the best pizza in the country? Probably not. Is it worth the 1.5 month wait for a dinnertime reservation and $30/pie price tag? Maybe once, but definitely not twice.

I'm not saying don't go, you should try it and make your own judgement - I feel like Beddia is one of those places you need to try to say you did. I will also say that it was pretty cool to see Joe walking around like just another guy. While he's considered a local celeb to some, he clearly doesn't let that go to his head and still cares about the quality of food that bears his name.
name: Jennifer

text: Absolutely my go to seafood restaurant from now on. First if you order a bottle of wine, you actually get a free cheese plate to go with. Very rare these days! We had to try the soup of the day which was a smoked trout chowder. It was delicious! My husband got the fish and chips, which was extremely good. I got the seared scallop sliders... What can I say, cooked to perfection. After the meal you get a small relish tray. One of the best lunches I've had in Reno in a very long time. text:
Our go-to for Chinese Takenout in the Clermont/Brownsburg Area! They do have a small area with extremely dim lighting for those who want/need to dine-in.  I've always preferred calling-in & carrying-out so I cannot give many details regarding the "dine-in experience."  All-in-All, we've always received Great Food complimented with Excellent & Speedy Services!  All hot & fresh cooked-to-order in about 10 Minutes!  They also have a rather large menu with comparable prices to other Chinese Take-outs, but they've never failed to please us with "Our Usual" order.
The only small perk I wish they'd implement the couponing system that I've used at a few other Chinese Take-out, ("Spend $25 or more receive free soda, spend $45 or more receive free order of Crab Rangoons, etc.") It's a great incentive for those that have larger orders due to having larger families or haven't yet experienced Golden Dragon & they're teetering between Golden Dragon & the other nearby Chinese Takeouts that implement these incentives.  Just a thought, however, not enough incentive to deter this family from being repeat customers!

text:
I came here after work during the holidays and it wasn't too crowded. We were seated right away and waitress was super nice and had lots of recommendations. From my overall glance at the place, it seemed like a family friendly restaurant after a long day shopping or for a quick bite. 

This place had great bbq options for an affordable price and other options including burgers, seafood, and a variety of appetizers. I went for the stack a bunch of bbq options (I don't remember what it is called but there was a picture and had options for how many people to serve. I picked the option for 3 people) that had chicken wings, sausages, baby back ribs, fries, and other lean meats. I thought all of the meats were well grilled and presented on a pot that had a smoker inside. It tasted like bbq you make on the grill in the summer, which I appreciated. 

The meats, especially pork, did not have any smell to it typical of meats. Rather the taste was refreshing and the sauce was delicious. We were so happy with everything, especially the ribs, that we ordered another full rack with sides, which was only $25! The only downside is that the chicken wings were a bit salty and in general the food is well seasoned. I wish that I could order plan bread with no seasoning to even out the saltiness. Maybe they had it on the menu and I just didn't see it.

Otherwise, I left with a full belly and a happy soul. I'd recommend here for anyone looking for a meat craving on a budget but not looking to sacrifice quality and taste.

text:
Top notch BBQ place in St. Pete, right next to the Rays northside parking lot. 

Food:
I highly recommend their Burnt ends. It's like meat candy! Sweet and delicious. Beef brisket is perfectly cooked as is the pork belly. The sides are plentiful. They have great breakfast/brunch options of benedicts, omelettes and burritos, etc. with touches of their smoked meats if you're looking for that Sunday morning hangover cure. The chorizo frito pie is a unique snack with a flavorful punch. We opt for the Texas Two-Step which gives you a portion of two different meats and two sides. Two orders of the of the Texas Two-Step (4 meats) is an economical way to try a variety of options and enough for 4 light-eaters to share. Their house-made BBQ sauces are very good and I especially like the peach habanero which has a nice kick! The Monkey Bread is famous although we've never tried it but I hear great things.

Drinks:
Happy Hour is M-F 3-7pm with $3 domestics, $5 wells, $6 wine, and a selection of $5 appetizers. Off the happy hour menu, the drinks can get a bit pricey.

Inside:
The ambiance is wonderful with tasteful 'old west' style decor and seating on the main floor as well as upstairs. There are TV's and a projector screen for game days by the main bar. There is also a 2nd floor outside bar and seating area that is perfect for private events. 

Parking:
There are 4 or 5 parking spaces on site...BUT there is a HUGE 'paid' parking lot right beside the building to the west. We've never paid and never been ticketed so you might get lucky here as well.
name: Christopher

text: Went once off a Groupon and won't go back, the place is EXTREMELY SMALL and tight.  I made a reservation and it took atleast 10 minutes for someone to even come up to seat me.  People coming in the door are bumping into you trying to get by and pushing there way past because they want to be helped too.  The food was "okay" nothing I'd rave about. The waitress was pretty awesome though so with that said I might give it a second chance.

text:
I was staying at the Hyatt Regency for the Cardinals Winter Warm Up and they were located on the first floor. I was in a hurry, starving, and need to grab something quick. I stopped in at lunch and ordered the chicken strips.  The place was packed but my order was ready in about 15 minutes.

I didn't have high expectations since all I ordered was chicken strips but boy was I pleasantly surprised. They were amazing. The batter was more like what goes on an onion ring and it was delicious. The chicken was perfectly cooked. They were large and juicy. I liked them so much I went back the next day and got them for dinner.

While I was waiting for my order I was watching the food come out and everything looked really good. Nice big portions.

Just because they're a sports bar in a hotel, they are really good and you should stop by.

text:
This is not fine dining German food and it's a kitchy Oktoberfest theme, but it's a fun night out. I came here with some family and we had a great time.

The beer selection is really good and they go great with the giant pretzels. Can't stress enough how good the pretzels are. Really hit the spot.

The waiter highly recommended the Jaegerschnizel which is a breaded pork cutlet with mushroom gravy on top of noodles. It was not bad, the pork was a little dry and it would have been much better if they put the mushroom gravy on the noodles as well as on top of the entire thing. But it was decent enough. 

Now the highlight was the entertainment, a lovely woman playing the according and keyboards and just making it a fun night. There are plenty of TVs in the space so if you want to keep up with the Nashville sports, this is a great place to watch the game.  Also has a huge bar so you don't even have to grab a table. 

So if you're looking for a great meal and that's the focus of dinner, skip the Bierhaus. If you're looking for a fun evening out with friends that revolves around beer and kitchy entertainment, this will do nicely. I had a lot of fun here.
name: Walter

text: It was a nasty, cold, wet day, and it was nice to find such an inviting restaurant in the middle of a residential neighborhood. It is small inside, but there is plenty of outdoor seating if the weather cooperates. You order at the counter, and they bring you your food. They have many hot and cold coffee and tea selections, and I went with a hot chai latte. It was perfect on such a cold day. They explained that they make everything from scratch. My husband started with a cup of chicken gumbo. The broth was so tasty. I am sorry that I didn't order one. I started with the garden salad. It was mostly spring mix with a few tomatoes, carrots, and onions, but the homemade blue cheese vinaigrette was outstanding. We split the steak sandwich. It had cheese and caramelized onions on it and was pressed. It was very very tasty, but half was enough with the salad. All the sandwiches come with homemade chips that have a wonderful rosemary flavor. It is a friendly inviting place, and we will definitely be back to try more of the menu.
name: Elizabeth

text: Every time I go into this Starbucks the people are so kind. My coffee is made the way I like and if not they absolutely don't mind making it over. Love the egg bites tasty. The desserts are not made in house but are still delicious. I go back because the people are awesome the music is good and the coffee is hot.

text: We came here for our anniversary and had a wonderful time. Service was 5 stars and we got a tour of the wine room. The tofu bao was the best I've ever had. The dumplings were superb and the potstickers good. I tried most of the menu.

The proprietor, Melvin, is a humble and kind guy who clearly puts love into his creations. The bartender is a gem of a woman...I will come back when she's working on Mondays as she is a wonderful spirit. 

I will say (and only because at least one other reviewer mentioned it) the girl on expo seems uninterested in the whole endeavor. No communication or eye contact. 

The space is great-dark and comfortable. I will return.

text:
Mr Ed's is a nice, cozy place to get some oysters! It's a kind of small restaurant but two of us were able to walk in and get seated pretty much right away and left not long after coming. 

We went with a 1/2 dozen charbroiled oysters and a 1/2 dozen of the mix of bienville and Rockefeller oysters. My biggest regret in coming here is that we did not order more oysters. I'm pretty sure we devoured those 12 oysters in 5 minutes or less. We were hungry and they were quite delicious! I had never had a bienville style oyster and I'm glad I tried it because the taste was on point. Of course, the left over juice was great and rich and I very much enjoyed using the bread to sop it all up. It's an added plus that it's not just regular bread. I think they put some cheese and other green seasonings on top of it--too good! The other two oyster styles we tried were also very good.
name: Shelby

text:
I can't believe I haven't reviewed Kounter Kulture before now. It's probably because I'm subliminally hoping that it stays a small, little spot in South City that just has a small cult following because when I saw it's amazing, that doesn't give it justice. Locally-sourced ingredients, everything made fresh with a rotating menu, friendly people, large portions . . . I could go on and on and on. 

My most recent visit was to pick up dinner Friday night. My husband and I usually only get Kounter Kulture when the kids are elsewhere because they can be finicky. I decided to take a chance this weekend. I ordered a menagerie of things because we tend to share food and eat off each other's plates. We had steamed pork buns, the brisket, poached shrimp, tomato salad and the Korean noodles. 

The first thing my daughter asked when we got back in the car was if she could dig in on the way home. I made her wait until we got to the house. I unpacked the food and found an extra cod bun had been included. Well that was gone before I got the rest of the food out of the bag. My girl inhaled it. She was in to everything we ordered and wants to go back.  For me, the food was spot on. The flavor melded well and it had just enough spiciness. 

Kounter Kulture is top notch. Go! and go back! and go back again. And don't miss the breakfast at Tower Grove Farmer's Market.
name: Suzanne

text: I stopped by here from St. Louis to Columbus, OH. I got a BLT and a water. The sandwich was made of cheap meat and lettuce that wouldn't be in a dive bar. The pizza bread that my colleague had was oily, but they did get his drinks right. The server was very friendly, so she was the only bright spot of this place. I doubt that I'll be back.
name: Randy

text:
We had somewhat of a strange experience as we were distracted by the manager working the expo line who kept eating from EVERY single pasta dish that was coming out.  He was a larger bearded guy wearing a baseball cap, and I kid you not, not a single pasta dish was served during the hour my husband and I were there that hadn't been eaten from by this guy.  We sat at the bar, so we had a very clear view of the expo line the entire time.  I'm not exaggerating when I say this guy probably had consumed the equivalent of three to four large pasta bowls by the time we left.

My husband and I have worked in the restaurant and hospitality industry for a number of combined years, so I get trying new dishes and giving feedback and whatnot, but I find this problematic for a number of reasons:
1) Do you not trust the food your chefs are making? We saw him taste the exact same dishes probably 10 to 12 times each.
2) The customers are paying for this food, not you! This guy was even eating from the take out orders!
3) It seems to me that this guy thinks people won't notice a bite or two missing from their pasta dishes.  Would you do the same thing to the pizzas everyone was ordering...?

Also, the expo manager kept calling for food runners ("hands!"), when he could've run the hot food himself instead of standing there and eating pasta...

Food was good, but having this strange experience leaves me on the fence about coming back.
name: Liz

text:
I went here tonight with my friends, and we were not impressed at all. There were 8 of us, but the place was hardly busy (I now understand why). Both the service and food were below average. 

To begin, our waitress seemed very overwhelmed (although it seemed we were her only table). When ordering, she continuously ask us to repeat our orders and did not know the drink or food menu names. We had to explicitly state what was in some of the items for her to understand our orders. She also took all of our IDs for drinks, and we did not receive them back for about 10 minutes. We were concerned there was some issue... Finally, she told US that she could do separate checks, and then told us she did not know what each person ordered and again seemed confused of how she was going to split the bill after we told her our orders. We decided to pay on one tab.

It terms of food, my order for just my drink was incorrect. I also wanted to order off the kids menu since I was not very hungry, and did not want to pay as much for an appetizer as I would for a full meal. I was not allowed, which I found shocking. Cheaper menu options are needed! 

Additionally, food for a party should come out at the same time, however, our dishes came out at three separate occasion, so some people felt obligated to wait and were not happy about this circumstance. On top of that, the food was only OK! My friend ordered a burrito, and only ate half of it because it was dry and not flavorful. To top the whole experience, the servers started cleaning and closing up 20 minutes before closing!!! We were told while we were sitting at our table to be careful and walk around certain areas of the main dining floor to the bathroom because they already started moping. To me, this process is unacceptable and should not be done until patrons leave the establishment and they are closed! 

For being in a college town, the "Mexican Mariachi Grill and Tequila Bar" has a lot it needs to improve upon before college students consider it a viable and worthy option.
name: John

text: We called in for a reservation and put our name on the list.  When we got there they said they weren't keeping a list and seated a couple right ahead of us.  We were told the wait was at least 30 minutes.  Won't go to the Brewer's Cabinet again!
name: Barbara

text:
Marissa is the bomb 

My son, wife, and I went out for dinner, on a Tuesday night, and it was BOGO on pizzas! Amazing! Marissa let us know after we ordered our pizza so we got another one to go! Way to keep us informed  

We ordered way too much but had a good time. Marissa made the good food a great experience. I recommend asking for her if you go. She was attentive, checked on us appropriately, and made a great dessert suggestion.

Food:
They start out with house bread with olive oil and pepper. Our appetizer was the Mozzarella Fritta which was perfectly prepared and served atop delicious tomato sauce. My son was happy.

Next we had our three entrees delivered, Chicken Parmigiana, Farmhouse Salad, and Puchillo pizza. The chicken was seasoned well, had the delicious sauce, and was liked by all. However, the spaghetti left much to be desired. Although not the center piece of the entree, the spaghetti was overcooked and should changed to another type of pasta (in my opinion). Maybe a thinner spaghetti...

The Farmhouse salad was perfect! The dressing was just the right amount. It had olives, fresh mozzarella, and everything else you could want in a salad. We had salmon on top and it was cooked just right.

Lastly, the Puchillo pizza had a good ratio of meat, cheese and veggies. The pizza was cooked just right. Additionally, the Margherita pizza we had the following night was good after we reheated it as well.

As we were winding down we decided to go for dessert. Marissa suggested we try the Lemon Mascarpone cake. We did and it was good. It was a refreshing taste of a citrus custard. We also tried the cannoli that had chocolate chips and a chocolate drizzle. Good taste and a satisfying way to end a good night. We recommend you try Bertucci's.

text:
We have looked forward to eating dinner at Antoine's for a month. We finally had that dinner this evening. It took 20 minutes after we were seated to finally place a cocktail order. Then we waited another 45 minutes before the waiter took our food order. OK so the place was busy, but that's no excuse.  Our waiter was very hard of hearing and the bus station atmosphere did not help. He had to lean very close to take the food order which had to be repeated three times before he finally got it. This in itself would have been alright except his breath was disgusting.  Then we waited  for another 30 minutes for the appetizers arrived. The Oysters Bienville were hot but small. They were topped with a glob of pasty cheese mixed with onion, white wine and pimento. It was offensive to my palate.
During time spent waiting on the entrees, a neighboring waiter asked if we could loan him the salt and pepper as one of his tables had none. Of course we did. But had to ask for their return 20 minutes later when our entrees arrived. 
 My wife reported that the onion soup was tasty and hot. I was served the Grilled Pompano which was burned. Not blackened....burned on the skin side. Photo was taken. 
To say the least our dining experience was not rewarding. If this is the best restaurant that New Orleans has to offer,  we will not be back. Sorry Antoine's... you really dropped the ball on this one.

text:
I have been told that my reviews are too wordy, yet quality and quantity are both important to me than poorly written, inconsistent, short reviews. So for the judgmental, here's some quick deets:
-They are open daily until 5 pm. (For coffee...see below for the after hours)
-They serve food and tapas that are created by Corazón Cocina and Sama Sama. 
-They are an eco-friendly and zero waste business resulting in no take-out disposable cups or boxes. You are encouraged to bring in your own mug or purchase a ceramic cup for $5 which you can trade in at a future visit or keep. Otherwise, stay for a bit.
-This location turns into a "speakeasy" called Social Lab starting at 5:30 pm. Entry is through The Mill back door with bands on some evenings.
-Parking isn't too tough on Haley Street, but keep in mind that it's usually limited to 90 minutes. Well behaved dogs are allow inside.

For those who appreciate a thorough review, read on:
After living several years in Seattle and Chicago, I consider myself a coffee snob. Sadly enough, Santa Barbara has settled for mediocre coffee beans, creations and foam art for far too long. Sorry locals but Handlebar isn't all that. Thankfully, Cajé has arrived to the forefront and has grown outside of Isla Vista for another round. I have stopped in several times and am already counting down to the next visit. 

The interior decor is fun with high speed WiFi and modern with a fair amount of seating. I absolutely love the succulent green wall! Staff is not always the most knowledgeable but very friendly nonetheless.

The coffee menu drinks tend to be a bit on the sweet side. My absolute favorite is the Burnout, but the Yemen is a close second. Each coffee creation takes so much time and care into making it with quite unique ingredients. They are always coming up with new concoctions though. Of course, you can order your average coffee beverage like a latte, americano, etc. with oat, coconut or almond milk. Plus, they make all their syrups in-house!

That's a wrap!
name: Richie

text: Very friendly and knowledgeable staff. This place is unique to the St. Louis area. The atmosphere is right on and is clean and decorated nicely. Food is authentic and can tell they have a very diverse staff that has a lot of experience with their dishes. It's a great addition to Lafayette Square and is a must if you are in the area.

text: Do not believe the Philadelphia Visitor Channel hype on this place.   You're better off at Long John Silver's. Hubby and I wanted to split an entree, and we were told that we couldn't, so we were forced to order an additional entree we didn't want.  This review has NOTHING to do with the Super 70's ambiance.  I love kitsch.

text: Wanted to rate on here even though I already spoke with a manager through the Facebook account. There was about 30 or more of us there lastnight. The birthday boy was spinning the wheel near the bar and a bartender was completely out of line and screaming about everyone being in the way of the bar. So move the shot wheel then? It was mainly all of my family there and we are very generous tippers. She was mouthing to the other bartender for a few minutes about us standing there and cussing up a storm in front of all of us.Completely unprofessional. They were also all taking shots, I'm pretty sure when your working that shouldn't be okay. At one point my brother in law walked up next to me and wanted to order something and the one bartender actually said "what do you want" in a rude voice. Who talks to a customer that way? If you don't want to work with customers you may want to reconsider the job you have and get a work from home position. I can't imagine how much they made in tips off us. Kill em with kindness.
name: Ashley

text:
My boyfriend and I wanted to try a new restaurant so we picked this one on a Sunday night at about 8:00 PM. There was only one other party besides us so the service was great.

For appetizers we got the seaweed salad and soft shell crab. There was a good amount of seaweed salad and the flavor was subtle, not too strong. I personally didn't like the breading on the soft shell crab because it was a little thick but my boyfriend liked it. Tasted greasy.

My entree was the nabeyaki udon while my boyfriend got the shogun roll and the sweet potato tempura roll. My udon noodles were still a little chewy and the broth wasn't too salty. My egg and chicken was overcooked but that was expected. I only got one piece of shrimp tempura, other restaurants I've been to I've always gotten two. My boyfriend loved his shogun roll but his sweet potato tempura roll was overcooked. He said it was way too chewy.

Overall the service was good and the flavor was there. I think all this restaurant needs to work on is their execution.

text:
Years ago, I worked for an organization that ordered Upper Crust catering on the regular, so I was excited to try out the actual location in person. It was a hit-or-miss experience, unfortunately.

THE GOOD: The food was just as great as I remember the catering to be. Because of my allergies, I was a bit limited in my choices, (and they were out of their feta and spinach quiche,) so I had a full-sized Caesar salad that was rich and filled with garlic and delicious! My partner had a bison burger that had him raving for hours afterwards. 

THE BAD: After explaining my allergies to our server, we opted to start with the brie, without fruit. When the order was up, there was fruit on the plate (he had entered the order as "no fruit, honeydew allergy"). Unfortunately, we had to send it back because I am allergic to several fruits, including many that were on the plate. The brie was quickly returned and upon questioning, we learned that the cheese, crackers, and bread had simply been replated, "but only the bottom of the cheese had touched the fruit, so it should be fine," to say nothing of the breads that had shared the plate with juicy fruits. So, I had a cracker and cheese to try it (it was tasty,) but didn't trust it in the end. So, if you have severe allergies, keep a close eye on what you're being served. 

THE MIXED: We were seated relatively quickly, but then it was over 10 minutes (at which point I stopped keeping track) before anyone came by to take our drink order. It would have been understandable if it were busy, but there was only one other table in the cafe. And five servers were lined up folding napkins behind the counter, all carefully not making eye contact with us. When we were finally helped, our server was very apologetic and helpful, even as the night went on and it got busier. 
Parking can be tricky in the area, with the cluster of one-way streets. It's best to come in from the north (heading south) and park on the one-way along the side of the building...just be wary of drivers disregarding the one-way, speeding, and backing up without looking!
name: Jenna

text:
My experience was about 6 years ago, so I would hope things have improved but I won't be going back to find out.
Yes they are a good spot to get a strong Hurricane, no argument there. On one instance though prior to moving to New Orleans, two friends and myself decided to go there for dinner so we can have a few drinks and not have to go stumbling around the Quarter looking for food afterwards.
We walked through the outdoor seating to the hostess stand. The place was about 1/3 full so we figured this would be easy. However we were informed by the hostess that there were no seats available. I noted that they were mostly empty and was again refused service.
I know that is their right to refuse service but there was no reason. We were polite, respectably dressed, and had nothing to drink as of yet. I know my personal boycott won't damage their business but there are too many great restaurants in this city to drive people away for no reason especially with so many resources for the community to share their experiences.
So definitely come and get a Hurricane in a to go cup, they are very good, but enjoy it as you walk the streets and find some place to eat that actually wants you there.
