text:
We visited Goldy's while in Boise for a family reunion. I have to say that Boise has changed a LOT since I was here last (about 15 years ago), and it has become far more cosmopolitan than I remembered. The food scene has exploded, and we ate a couple of really excellent meals there. Therefore, we had high hopes for Goldy's...

First off, be prepared to wait - like at least 30 minutes - for a table. We did wait since the hype was fairly intense. We were ultimately seated in the upstairs gallery. Cute, but when you're as tall as I am, it's a bit of a pain (especially when using the restroom). We ordered some bacon and eggs, and the chicken fried steak, plus a side of my favorite breakfast food - biscuits and gravy.

The food arrived in a timely fashion, correctly prepared (eggs over-medium and crispy hash browns) and it looked amazing. After the first couple of bites of the the steak, I had to conclude that the salt and pepper were not properly distributed through the breading. One bite would be wildly salty, the next peppery, then hardly any flavor the next time. The consistency was perfect but the taste was just not so great. The rest of the food was also just OK, with the bacon being a bit underwhelming as well (too thin and a bit bland). 

I hate to write a less-than-stellar review of a place so obviously loved and well-reviewed, and I suppose that with the buildup and buzz surrounding the restaurant (and the long wait), we were expecting a lot more. 

The service was great, as is the location and atmosphere, but the food fell a little flat for us...
name: Eric

text:
We decided to give this restaurant a second try and we were much more happy with the experience this time around. 

First of all whoever was the sushi chef (perhaps the chef wearing the the grey baseball cap on the far end of the sushi bar) who prepared our first batch of sushi, we appreciate you so very much! The attention to detail and presentation of the simplest yet most delicious pieces of mackerel nigiri definitely did not go unnoticed tonight. We tried several different fish and quail egg nigiri but we couldn't get enough of the mackerel. The rice was cooked to perfection and the fish was so fresh. 

We also had the chicken katsu dinner which is tender, deep fried, breaded chicken cutlet served with a dark brown, tangy dipping sauce, rice and pieces of orange which was a different but nice touch (most other places serve chicken or pork katsu with shredded cabbage instead of orange). The chicken was light and not greasy at all, so delicious and tasty. Also I think part of the success of this dish lies in the perfectly cooked rice. 

This place gets packed for dinner so be sure to make a reservation or prepare to wait. Also the sushi bar and high top tables by the bar are on a first come first serve basis. They allow corkage for $20 per bottle. Parking is limited but they do offer complimentary valet.
name: Carla

text:
I've been a big fan of the Y Not Indian downtown in Scotia Place for a long time and the new Whyte Ave location holds up aptly with simple but fresh curries and a much more varied menu. 

In my 5 star rating for Y Not Indian's downtown fast food iteration, I had high praise for the robust flavours on display and fresh, flaky naan. The Whyte Ave location boasts the same great flavours, same delicious naan and same great value but with the addition of a wider variety of appetizers, tandoori mains, and stuffed naans. I didn't try the incredible mushrooms or cauliflower appetizers but they're on my to-try list for sure!

As is typical for great Indian restaurants, there is a solid range of vegetarian options and traditional dishes such as the dal tarka and matar paneer are executed to perfection. 

Overall, Y Not Indian's expansion to Whyte ave expands on what makes the downtown location great and while there aren't many thing son this menu that you wouldn't see at any other Indian restaurant, there's definitely something to be said for simple and well-executed curries and some of the freshest naan you can find.

text:
A work in progress.
There's a very nice and busy vibe to the place, despite that it's only less than half open.
Construction is ongoing. When it's done, it will be a strong rival to the crosstown Armature Works.
A lot of parents seem to bring their toddlers to play on the large patch of Astro turf.
That's either ok if you're one of them, or not so ok if you're a grouchy single.
Right now, the main attraction is Fermented Reality, the beer garden in the center of it all.
The various food stalls located in shipping containers are actually not very good, at least what I've tried.
And some of them are comically overpriced. BT is selling a Vietnamese bahn mi pork sandwich for $12. These are little half pint Asian subs that usually sell for about $3 in most Viet places.
The pizza square shop is likewise mediocre. 
I've had a few coffees at the coffee shop and each time it's been stale and burnt for $2.50.
I love the deck chairs on the water where you can now actually sit , unlike at the former Channelside which had everything blocked off.
Once they get the indoor restaurants up and running, this may be a more viable place to eat.
Splitsville is already there and its food is actually great. 
Too bad the outdoor grub is so poor.

text:
Very fresh sushi and friendly staff. The seaweed salad and regular salad with ginger dressing is very good and the sushi presentation is very impressive. We got the Sushi and Sashimi for One and everything on the plate was delicious! The presentation of that platter was very impressive and made us feel like we were getting a good bang for our buck. We also ordered the Wonderful Roll and the Hartford Roll such is on their half-price menu. The Hartford roll was my absolute favorite: it's shrimp tempura inside, avocado on top, and then a nice sweet sauce drizzle. The Wonderful roll was a little different because it had cooked fish on the outside so it gave it a completely different flavor. The fish was good, but I don't think I would order it again. It had spicy tuna inside and then was wrapped with seared white tuna, salmon, and avocado on top. I would defiantly go back here if I'm in the area but I'd also like to try the Casino roll: that looks good. 
It's located in a little strip mall so the outside is nothing fancy, and the inside decor is typical and everything was nice and clean. We sat in a comfy booth so that was nice. They also have seats right where they make the sushi, so that might be fun to sit there too. They did have a bunch of people going in and out for takeout, so don't expect this to be a fancy date night, but you can BYOB if you want to have a little wine with your sushi.

text:
We stopped in thinking that a new Lucky Dill had opened up in our area but what what we found was a Lucky Dill/Legends Sports Bar hybrid restaurant.  The Lucky Dill corporation has taken over what was once the Legends Sports Bar and Grill.  There was a sign posted describing the situation (see pic).  The restaurant had a limited number of Lucky Dill items and the entire menu from Legends was still available.  The wait staff, furniture and fixtures are the same as before.  We were told that a complete transformation into more of a Lucky Dill menu would happen within about 45 days.

We ordered off of the old and new menus.  Off the old menu, we ordered 'The Legend' burger which was a bacon cheeseburger with onion rings and BBQ sauce.  Off the new menu, we ordered the Dilly Philly with mushrooms.  Both dishes came with delicious Five Guys style French fries that were great.  The sandwiches were both great, too.  The burger was cooked perfectly and the Philly Cheese steak was huge and delicious.

The wait staff was friendly and speedy.  The food was good.  I'll be interested in what the final version of this restaurant becomes.
name: Marty

text: Upon arrival Avo is fresh and airy inside with greenery on the walls and a smiling host. I was seated before my party and perused the drink menu. I ordered a Paloma which was made with fresh grapefruit juice and great tequila. Next was the cheese plate with gluten free bread. The pickled vegetables were yucky and so was the jam and the "ricotta". The "pepper jack" was the best but all the cheese tasted like hummus which was weird. I've had vegan cheese several times but never grainy like this. Then for dinner I ordered creamed chars and fingerlings with Avo mash. The wait was long for food considering most of it is raw and cold so probably already prepared. My fingerlings were an assortment of purple potatoes and yams with a fresh Avo mash that was to die for. The creamed chard was soupy and swimming in coconut chips and too much coconut cream. I took a spoon and drained the liquid to make it edible. The highlight by far was the dessert. I had the strawberry banana chzcake. It was pure fruit and an amazing crust with nuts in it. I should have just ordered the drink, potatoes and dessert.

text:
Start spreading the news. 
Come in here today.
You want to be part of it. . . . . 

Ok, it's not New York, New York, but it's pretty good and we're so happy to have a new place Downtown that serves great food and good drink in a really cool space.

Red's (of Old 395 Grill in Carson City and The Little Wal on North Virginia) have opened a new spot right next to the Greater Nevada Field in the space which formerly housed Arroyo. 

The food - the fare is similar to what they have at the Carson Restaurant with a predominance of  Bar-B-Que and Mexican dishes. For lunch today, my husband had the Double Play Pork with a Dogfsh Head 60 IPA, I had the Salad 1868. All was very good. The shredded pork and ribs were deemed tasty and tender and came with sides and a choice of sauces. My salad was a upscale version of a taco salad with very tender smoked chicken, fresh greens, grilled corn, black beans, pineapple pico, and avocado, all served in a huge tortilla shell. It was smokey, spicy, crunchy with a hit of sweet from the pineapple. We came away stuffed.

The space is definitely visual overload. The theme is a mash-up of sports and cowboy bar. The pictures, and sports banners, and pieces of wagons, farm equipment and stage coaches adorn the walls and ceiling all evoking a much earlier age. High top tables in the bar area have Tractor Seat stools. The booths have red checked oilcloth on the tables. 

Staff are friendly and Matthew, our server, was polite and professional, took our orders quickly and checked in with us to see if all was to our liking. Everyone thanked us for coming in and made the whole experience feel welcoming. We assured them we would be back. 

These downtown blues, are melting away
I'm going to a brand new place today
Red's Broken Bat is here to stay.
name: Nancy

My breakfast sandwich was delivered by a young lady not even in uniform but a T-shirt and jeans. There was a young lady with the blonde ponytail that was out changing trash out and wiping tables down when she heard me ask for a clean table.  She seem to of seen a need and was the only employee responding.  Had the restaurant been busy it would've been a little more understandable but the DIRTINESS, bad service and cold food was inexcusable.
name: Susan

text:
I'm not sure I understand what happened with our experience... I mean...the ratings are so high. The place was packed! Did it just fall prey to "Southside Syndrome", wherein Greenwood-y people think things are amazing because they don't know better?

Listen, this wasn't a one off thing.  We were a party of 9, and NO ONE liked their food.  My penne with vodka sauce was all volcanic spice and no flavor, and if you can make ME sweat, you've done something. My mother's pasta was overdone to the point of mush. My wife's fish would've had good flavor were it not smothered in foul tasting sauce. The pizza was bland and boring.  I just...I don't get it.  Is this a 5-Star restaurant for people with 2-Star taste?  I wanted to love it so much, but there's better pizza and pasta within 15 minutes of Vito's, and we will be availing ourselves of those options going forward.

Edit: The server was lovely and kept the overall rating from drowning in a vat of the awful sauce.
name: Jake

text: Very good Thai food in the heart of Santa Barbara. Very fast service and all the food came hot to the table, like should be. Not very full when we went and it was during a weekend. I guess is not as fancy place as the hipster restaurants nearby in same street but it was all we wanted, very satisfying coconut soup with seafood. Also, space was cozy and traditional Thai style.
name: Carmen

text: This was my first time trying Hendricks, I was so looking forward to it. My food was amazing, my family enjoyed their food as well. However, we all agreed that the service was very disappointing. It took us around 25 minutes before a waitress had even addressed our table. I'm hoping this was just an off day.
name: Sarah

text: This is one of our favorite spots to grab lunch.  The soup is always home made and tasty.  The hubby likes a hearty sandwich but doesn't want to be in a food coma. I love that their ice tea is made fresh Daily   The staff is always friendly and service is quick.   If you haven't stopped by please do!
name: Samantha

text:
So I went back here about two weeks ago with my gal friends. One of my friends is insanely obsessed with the band that was playing. This place is very popular and is always packed with all age ranges including  families, couples,  and friends just hanging out. Complimentary Valet parking is available.  This time we made a reservation and everything was smooth sailing from there. Our waitress was awesome. She very knowledge about the food selections and gave good detail about each. We all got different food so we could try it out. She was very attentive. The drinks were flowing. 
We started off with the Korean styled Brussels sprouts. Very yummy!!!!! 
So I had  the rainbow trout. It was sooooo good. It very light and seasoned to perfection. My friend green chili stew and was really good. Also it was a huge portion!!! My other friend had the salmon. It was also very good. I would order any of these entrees again. For dessert we got the money bread!!! Yummmy. It came with ice cream. The entire table was able to share. 
The band added some fun to the night. We got up and danced. Ran into a bunch of my co-workers who were also enjoying the night.  This is going to be one of my favorite spots.
name: Tannus

text: In Tampa area on business and found Willie's Seafood on Yelp.  Highly rated.  The ratings were right on!  I got the blackened scallops.  They were cooked to perfection.  The sides were excellent, as well.  The waitress was so very nice.  The place is very local, which is so much nicer than the chain restaurants.  Worth the drive.
name: Herb

text:
I don't even eat fried chicken. Today was different.

I didn't know what I wanted..stopped here...got Chicken & Waffles ...much better than I expected. The wings were big and thick, the Tweener sauce was perfect; slightly spicy/ slightly sweet.  Waffles we're fine, a biiiiit undercooked for me but still fine.  And the soda machine had my favorite soda; Boyland's sugar cane sodas.  Black cherry / lime pure sugar cane soda topped off a great quick meal. I'm impressed. I'll be back.
name: Schárvín

text: Perfectly cooked brisket. Friendly service. Plenty of seating. Location a few blocks from main drag is a feature not a flaw.
name: Michael

text:
Very good food but SMALL portions.  Like...really really small.   The seating is also very uncomfortable- both outdoor & indoor are cheap metal chairs.   
They've got a good thing going in the kitchen but the portions should be doubled... then I'd give 5 stars.
name: Estee

text: I get the appeal, I just don't totally share it. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. I wouldn't write it off, but I also wouldn't hype it up. Food was fresh and service was quick.
name: User

text: We ate here last night, and it was delicious! Even though the parking lot was rather dark (and for whatever reason, their sign was not lit), there were quite a few full tables. Ordered shrimp chow fun and cashew chicken, both very good (some of our "go to" dishes to compare against other Chinese restaurants. The table next to us had fried calamari and crawfish that also looked amazing. Service was good, place nice and clean, seated quickly and the food arrived without much of a wait (but was definitely freshly-made to order). I'd definitely return.
name: Candy

text:
As my first hot experience (but with people who are very experienced), I was impressed with the quality of the food and taste. The restaurant has a fun, modern aura with the Japanese style conveyer belt running through the middle, brick/wood panel walls, and small booths with individual hot-pot stoves for each person. 

I got the House Hellish Spicy Broth at the Entry Spicy level, enough spice to get your attention but not too hot that you don't enjoy the meal (for those with a low spice tolerance beware, even at the lowest level it has a kick).

As a table we split the Beef combo (comes with wagyu brisket, angus prime rib eye, and Australian Short Rib) which is a great value and very good mix, along with Udon Noodle (nothing special), Glass Noodles (they were great but suggest holding it while you cook or you'll lose them in the pot), Sweet Corn (highly recommend, we ended up getting another order), and baby bok choi (solid). 

While the food was great, Chubby Cattle could improve on their service. Our waitress was friendly and had good recommendations at the beginning of the meal, she forgot our order of Fish Balls that we asked about 3 times, and had to end up cancelling because it never came by the end of the meal! We also had to ask for water refills and sauce refills, and they were a bit slow clearing the table once we had finished a dish. Overall would recommend, 4/5.
name: Noah

text:
I have to admit a mea culpa on dining here. I normally don't feel kindly toward French cooking, but after dining here last night, I must say the dishes were excellent and worthy of the price. The service was spot on, even to them taking back a bottle of wine that looked and tasted of cork leakage.

Four of us came to a nearly full house, but our reservation was ready and we were promptly attended to by Daniel. As mentioned previously, we had to ask for a new bottle of Italian wine (Rosso di Montalcino), but the second was a nice Bordaux style, (Vino Nobile di Montapulciano).

Bread was excellent, from a "secret" baker they declined to identify. Sweet butter accompanied the fine bread. It went great with our appetizers of Escargot and the Caprise Tower salad. Both have wonderful butter or dressing to be sopped up. The Escargot were the best I have had, even beating Chandler's. Be careful though, the snails take a bit of wrestling to remove from the shells. The Caprise Tower was one of the best salads, or so said those in our party who were partial to salads.

The entrees were split, but there is a plate charge for splitting. Very reasonable to do this. Our veal picata and pork gorgonzola dishes were as fine as any dishes we have had in the Boise area. The meats were precisely cooked and the sauces were wonderful and delicate. Even those in our party who were not fond of sauces found these perfect. More bread, please.

No desserts were had this night, but certainly looked delish as other tables had them.

We will obviously return.
name: Carl

text: Went in and ordered to go, food took awhile to get out even though we were the only other two people in there but it was worth the wait! Food was delicious and it was enough to leave me feeling stuffed. The. breaded raviolis are fire!!
name: Kayla

text: The atmosphere and food are fantastic. Brett was very helpful and the chicken is so good! I had the sweet potato pancakes with the chicken and yum!!!
name: Gail

text: My husband and I Went to this restaurant for Valentine's Day. It was absolutely amazing. We were greeted as soon as we entered the restaurant. The customer service is great. They really explain to you the difference between the items on the menu. They explain the differences and what each item is and what it comes with. I definitely recommend this restaurant.
name: Jewel

text: It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. No big complaints, just a nice meal. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Would return. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon.
name: User

text: The whole meal felt kind of uneven. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Probably not coming back. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. For the price I expected more than this. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly.
name: User

text: Just had dinner here for 1st time..was amazing! Our waiter, Don and his busser Cody were wonderful and very attentive. We sat outside on the patio, since inside was a bit loud. From appetizers to dessert,  everything was top notch. I enjoyed my birthday and we will definitely be back!
name: Susan

text:
I was walking by with my dog on a hot day. After stopping outside near by this place to sit in the shade for a bit, I received neighborly concern worth noting. The cook came out on his break and saw us attempting to cool off. He asked if we needed any water and brought out a small to go container with water for my dog and a large styrofoam cup for me. 

Did I mention we weren't even customers?

This spoke volumes to me about the kind of business ran here. While these small diners are not everyones cup of tea, the character behind this restaurant will pull me back in!

Thanks Peppy for caring enough to show this stranger and his dog what some might call Hoosier hospitality!
name: Trevor

text: HORRIBLE SERVICE! We ordered through yelp online.. My husband went in to pick up our order... he was told they were out of wings and tried to call the number but the last digit was cut off on the order ticket. (Not my fault that's a system issue) We just asked for our refund for the wings ordered. Girl at counter says no bc the owners not here (that's absurd!) my husband ends up waiting inside with my son for 45 minutes for another order to make up for the shortage of wings. He asked if they can throw in an extra side for the inconvenience. She says no! she never even apologized for the inconvenience. We were loyal customers but not anymore. And all this on Father's Day!! She couldn't even go out of her way to throw in a side salad or even a drink! Anything would've been better than nothing... such a shame. Another customer there was waiting over an hour for their food bc the ordering system online messed up her order as well... this place is a mess!!
name: Angie

text: Got takeout from here twice now so I feel like I can say a little more. Anyway, nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. The staff seemed tired but still polite. Anyway, pretty smooth experience from start to finish. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. idk I'd try something else next time. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed.
name: User

text:
Yo wtf this authentic Sichuan place has no business being in a strip mall in suburban pa but I'm so glad it's here. Definitely one of the best restaurants in the area hands down. 

I just had a lamb and scallion cause that was a favorite of mine at this place we went to in college but everything looked great. Some people were eating these soups that seemed incredible. Looking forward to coming back here

text: Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. A couple small things kept adding up. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Not bad for a quick meal. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine..
name: User

text: Best crab legs I've had in my life. Great service, great food. The crab legs were cooked in the best seasoning, and were steamed to perfection. I suggest everyone eat here forever.
name: Brittany

text: I am a Chinese and I am from Sichuan( the correct spelling of Szechwan LOL) . This is so far the best Chinese restaurant in town. I have been there many times. Not only is the food great but also the service. The owner values each customer and tries to accommodate their needs. To make it even better , they just hired another Chinese Chef who is from Chongqing. He was trained as a chef in China. The food we had over the weekend made me feel I was back in China.... And today I just made an appointment with my friends to go there again on Wednesday. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone who would like to taste authentic Chinese food.
name: Karen

text:
August 25, 2016: If I could give this place zero stars, I would.  I was just there at 12:30, in other words, peak lunch time. This place always perverts the concept of "fast food." The line of cars snaked totally around the building as usual, so I went inside. They had one register open and the girl stationed there pretty much hung out in the back and only came out when she felt like it to wait on one person at a time, only to leave again for a few minutes. The floors were filthy, the trashcan behind the order counter overflowing onto the floor. Two out of three times that I come here, I'm told "Our shake machine be down." Today was no exception, and this has happened for the last five years. I even filed a report on this with McDonalds and the manager wrote back to say I was mistaken about the frequency of breakdown of the shake machine.  Today I said that this has happened the last three times I've been there, I asked why the shake machine was always down. Miss Motivated looked at me like I was stupid and I didn't think she was even going to answer me. After about five seconds, she said "I don't know." Probably the truth, to be fair. I guess they think I'm just trying to torment them. It's probably an act of God, I certainly don't need the calories. But I think if they routinely can't serve something that shows on the menu, they should probably take it off the menu. The bottom line here is: nobody cares. Certainly not the employees, not the manager, and not even corporate McDonald's. It's  certainly not what you expect from this brand. And I mean that not in a good way.
UPDATE: One week after my review. 9/1/16, "Our shake machine is down at the moment."  At the moment, right.
UPDATE. Two weeks after my review. It is 9/8/16. The shake machine is down. When I was there on 9/1 and pushed back a bit, they said, "it's going to be fixed later in the week." Since that was a Thursday, I wondered what later in the week actually meant. Probably later in the month.
Update: it is March 31, 2018. The line is going all around the building, it hasn't moved for 15 minutes, the shake machine is down, of course, again. This place is a total joke. It's 945 on Saturday night. It's now 954 and I'm still sitting in the same spot that I was. They don't care and they can't handle it. They've even closed off the second drive-through lane, but they did it by putting milk pallets Right where the speaker is where you talk. This means you can't see them until you drive into the lane around the curve and run into the mill pallets. Then you have to back all the way out of that lane and get in the other lane.
Update, it is August 1, 2019. It's nice to know that after spending a lot of money remodeling the interior of this McDonald's, the service is the same crappy slow service that it's always been. It's Thursday night, there were a total of six cars in the drive-through lane.I guess people are learning not to come to this McDonald's at all. But I just spent 25 minutes in the drive-through lane. 15 minutes waiting at the last window, for a big Mac and fries. That's it. There are six people running around in their screaming at each other at the top of their lungs and nothing is moving. Unbelievably pathetic.
name: C

text: The food was so great. The service was great until the check came--then we didn't see our waiter again. Water would've been nice! They weren't busy anymore so we weren't keeping him from having another table. Excellent cocktails. Kind of loud, but it was super busy.
name: Tammy

text: Had brunch here over the weekend and it was kind of a mixed bag. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. You can tell they care about customer experience here. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. Would return.
name: User

text:
My husband and I tried here Wednesday night for dinner with his mother. Gotta say it was so good! The food tastes fresh wA nice and hot,  the place was busy and our wait wA hardly no time 
Service was great we had zero complaints and will for sure be going back loved it

text:

However I received a large bowl of gumbo with potatoe salad and three toasts I was full off that but still had some room for chicken wings and shrimp etoufee 

Good place and food

text: No big complaints, just a nice meal. Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Would return. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Would probably stop in again if nearby. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Food was good and came out fast. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price..
name: User

text: The food at this location is very good but what you have to go through to get it is a horrible experience. The lady that answers the phone is always very very rude and when you come in after finally placing your order she is equally as rude in person. Some days I just hang up because I do not have the time or patience to deal with her.

text: Nice people watching seating outdoors. I ordered the small app nachos for my meal and they good. It was a lot of for a small size order.   I also ordered avocado fries, but they never came so I had to ask the waiter to take it off the bill.  My friend ordered the chips and salsa app. It came with 3 different salsa's. They were good, not amazing, not bad, but good.  She also ordered tacos, and I tried a bite.  NO thanks. Basic, pretty boring tacos.  They should change the name to Rocco's Nachos because those were WAY better.
name: Rebecca

text: Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. For a busy night they handled it okay. Glad we tried it. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. The food was good and the service was easygoing. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus..
name: User

text: Five of us ate there 2/16/18, arriving at 1030 so the place was busy but not crazy.  As with our previous experience in November, the food was good; but the dark haired older waitress who was rough the last time was down right rude today.  When I asked to sit outside because it was so noisy inside, she thrust the five menus in my hands and said take these I'll meet you out there, and it was all downhill from there.  She didn't listen; she barked orders; the food arrived in spurts and without knowledge of who ordered what; she reached across people to give the food or take the dishes when there was plenty of room to go around.  It was a unique experience to be treated so badly; we won't be back; ever!!!
name: Beth

text: Great food and drinks in an old west atmosphere. Lunch and dinner specials daily, can get a little busy around lunchtime due to all of the area businesses. They offer a full bar, and even have areas for private parties.
name: B

text:
I (after a bunch of research) picked this place for my birthday brunch and it was a huge let down.

1. In my reservation I requested we get a table on the balcony. When I asked again upon arriving, they told us it was booked. Fine. I instead asked for a booth in the corner. Again I was told we couldn't sit there, this time because they were expecting a party of 3 and they couldn't possibly fit anywhere else. Ok fine. We settled for the sub par table next to the stairs. Normally this wouldn't (overly) bother me except that no one was ever seated at either table in our two hours of being there. Cool thanks. 

2. In my reservation I included my birthday under the special occasion option. This was not acknowledged in the slightest. Our server said nothing. I'm not 5; I don't need a parade, but why even ask about a special occasion if nothing comes of it? 

3. Our appetizer came out wrong. Again, not a big deal, and our server apologized. But then our (eggs benedict) entrees came out cold and we were just over it. Our saving grace was the side of fries (which still weren't amazing).

Really not as great as I expected based on reviews, and I won't be back.
name: Phoenix Simone

text: Fabulous brunch spot.  We sat in the lounge chairs and had brunch.  They have bottomless mimosas.  I had a breakfast sandwich and it was great.  Our server, Brandon, was super nice and super friendly.  I'll be back.
name: Cassandra

text:
We tried Stella last night for the first time and honestly we were not impressed. This place is nothing more than an over priced hotel bar with Jose Garces name attached to it. 

We were greeted by the hostess with a smile and after a few minutes we were shoved in seating in the corner of the restaurant (I mean it's really more of a bar- what's with all the TVs??) We asked to be moved because the seating was awkward and very cold. We were told to wait in which we did, but it took them a while to come back so we grabbed a drink at the bar. 

Once we were reseated, we had Ry for our server. The menu is a bit confusing so we asked for some recommendations and we were told that it was small plates and "family style" which was a bit interesting since other people had small plates coming out for their entrees (no way did this seem family style). We decided to try the bread service with all three options of Duck liver, Roasted Eggplant and Garlic butter? The bread service was eh okay. The bread was the best part but I wouldn't consider it traditional sour dough, more like naan.
We also ordered the peekyboo crab. It was absolutely disgusting. Very watery with little crab and a bunch of oil floating on top. 

We wanted to order the fried rice,but we were told they ran out of it the night before. If they ran out on a Saturday, why could it not be made for Sunday dinner service? This really irritated my husband as he has background in this industry. At this point we weren't impressed, but we decided to try one more thing to decide if we would stay for dinner or not. Ry recommended the Rye pasta. It took a while to come out, but this was a very decadent dish (and great recommendation from the server) and probably the only really delicious thing we had. 

Since we only really enjoyed one thing so far...

We opted to walk across the street to The Salt House for dinner because we questioned whether or not to risk it. I'm happy we left because dinner at the Salt House never disappoints unlike this place. 


A few things... 
It was annoying that literally no one smiled except for the hostess. 
The vibe is super weird and we couldn't wait to leave. 
Do not go here if you're hungry or have someone in your party hard of hearing. 
Don't have high expectations just because Jose Garces name is attached to it.
name: Ashley

text: Simetimes u just have to have a milkshake ... so many flavor combinations to choose from. I usually get apple cider & marshmallow.... but last night i got banana & marshmallow....they had a selection of vintage sodas as well...

text:
The food was great and it was so cheap. They're also listed on the door dash good delivery app...

I scheduled a pick up through door dash (which isn't supposed to charge extra), but my $10.50 order would have only cost $8.40 if I'd have placed the order in store...

text:
Had the hot sour soup and salty lemonade 
The food and service was good 
The salty lemonade is like the salty lemon tea that my wife makes. Would be great if the started selling ban mi
name: Henry

text:
You must start with the Shrimp Cocktail. Has a real kick to it. Watch out for the horseradish it sure does sneak up on you. 

Next the Caesar Salad. Just like a Caesar  Salad. As expected. 

Filet Mignon with baked potato was Devine. Filet Mignon with fries the only bad thing is that the 12oz wasn't bigger. 

NY Strip was very good along with the au gratin potatoes which every bite the skillet kept filling up with more!

The grass fed flat iron steak was so juicy and tasty.

text: Avoid. Not friendly. Messes up orders badly. Service sucks. Filled out survey for free chicken. And they ran out of the chicken.  Plus ran out of the sweet tea. Just bad all around.

text:
Such a beautiful Peruvian themed addition to Old city. We specifically came here to try Pisco Sours because you don't find them easily in traditional bars or cocktail places! 

The bartender definitely knew what he was doing - he made us some delicious and incredible looking Piscos. Not only that, he also explained us what some of the foreign ingredients meant and that those were exclusively imported from Peru! Definitely check out if you are in the neighborhood.

text: Only negative thing I can say about this place was that they don't have draft beer. But, we did arrive at happy hour so domestic bottles were $1 off. This being in the area that it's in, I ordered a Cuban sandwich. I'm a huge fan of them and was hoping to get one from the area it started in. While it wasn't  what I expected, it was still very good. The other folks I was with ordered a couple of calzones which they found to be very tasty and certainly filling. The portions were on point for the price. That's a huge positive for me.

text:
One of my favorite breakfast/lunch spots! The service has always been good, & the food has always been great!My favorite breakfast items are ANY of their Eggs Benedicts; & my favorite lunch item is their Grilled Vegetable Wrap (very unique!). 
Good omelets & salads too!

text:
very friendly staff, venue is clean, and bright.    The food portions are very generous so take that into mind before you "over order".    

Price is very reasonable considering the portions, flavor, and customer service they provide.   However when the Place is "really" busy you can tell the food is already made and prepared in the back.  For example my food was beautifully served but it wasn't as hot as a "freshly cooked plate"    Still good still fresh ingredients but not (served immediately from the grill). 

I'd definitely go back and highly recommend. 

Also : It's (Cash only ). But they have an ATM inside

text: Fabulous food. Especially love the red curry. Great lunch deals too. It's our "go to" Thai place.
name: Lisa

text: Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Food was good and came out fast. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Food was good and came out fast. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent.
name: User

text: This is the most delicious Greek food I have ever had. I have actually craved it the day after eating it. The chicken schwarma is insanely good.
name: Kathrine

text:
Wow, this is really hard for me to do.
The last place that I liked a lot really got turnt out.

Fortunately this place was (out) of guacamole.
They were also out of their main special.

But they did have queso, that "I thought" was much too authentic.  For someone from Louisiana I can tell you it was "hot as hell". It ain't Piccadilly cornbread.

Went with the shrimp  quesadilla and the fish tacos.

While staring around checked out the artwork.  It genuinely fit the establishment and the neighborhood "to a t". There was even a 3-D attempt of the Claiborne overpass, with protruding mini car and all.

While waiting for the food, we had that "wobbly table", and the nice waitress noticed it right away.  She was trying to fix a wobbly table on an uneven floor-boy.  That's like placing somebody in a round room and telling them there is something in the corner.

Anyway, I was completely taken aback  with the food here.  They say "it's better to under promise and over deliver".  My gosh.  The food was beyond expectation.  I cannot really express the experience really well except to say that there is a "hot & new" place in Metairie with an hour wait out the door.
 
The fish tacos  were made from fried flounder with cabbage and spicy aioli mayo and the shrimp on the quesadillas were huge.  As a matter of fact, when I got the bill, just tore it up, and told the waitress to start over just because it was so incredible.  Ordered the same exact thing- like Deja-vu or a bad dream.  And got the fish tacos with the shrimp quesadilla, again.

This time the waitress know I had overstepped a boundary, and it was really time to "clear this table".  It was like "oh, and by the way here is a mint-pineapple popsicle made by the chef". It was a like some new type of music .  This chef might not speak English, but they definitely know the international language of food.  This chef must be from Ensenada, Oaxaca, Monterrey, or someplace far away.  They are definitely the "ruin of many a good boy".  If anybody knows how the story of "billy the kidd", with his many travels across the border and back- this place definitely has some of those mysterious characteristics.  

So wrap all of that up with a unique place in a unique neighborhood that has unique food, and  bam.
I would really risk going to this place if it was in the middle of Syria . The whole time there are to-go orders that looked as if they do catering for half the city.  And there were enough people to easily handle the demand.  Least to say that Sarita's has got it going on.  I guess "just look at the photos". All I got.!

text: The wait was longer than it should've been for a pretty normal dinner service. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. I'd maybe go back, but I'd order differently next time. For the price I expected more than this. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh.

text: Stopped here on the way to six flags for a quick breakfast. Was not disappointed. The deli coffee was great, the service was prompt and friendly. Above all our two breakfast sandwiches were delicious. Will definitely be back!

text: Portions were generous and presentation was nice. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. text: Meh, overly hyped place.  It's just a trendy place.  Food was ok but staff isn't too friendly.  I guess that's what you expect if they're busy.  Was our first time here, don't think we'll come back.

text:

text: Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Food was fresh and service was quick. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Food was fresh and service was quick.
name: User

text: I went with a friend after Bayou Bayogaloo to get a burger because it has been a while.  I have always loved the burgers and often tell people they are the best in the quarter.  Unfortunately this is not the case anymore.  We each order a burger medium rare and medium.  I received the wrong burger and it was burned beyond recognition.  My friend's order was correct but it was also burned solid black.  They put in another apologized, placed a new orders and explained that the kitchen was slammed which is understandable considering it was a busy day.  Unfortunately we both received thoroughly burned burgers even though we asked for even rarer to compensate for the previous burned burgers.  By this point we just gave up, paid our bill, and left to get something to eat elsewhere.  Hopefully they get some better kitchen staff because what we had was an absolute disgrace
name: John

text:
Good place to go for Korean fried chicken fix. We had about a 20 minute wait for the chicken to be prepared, so it was definitely hot and fresh. 

The food choices are limited: pretty much just different wing flavors, regular or sweet potato fries and pickled radish side. Ordered 10 soy garlic wings $12.99 and the boneless spicy combo $9.99 (boneless wings of your choice, fries ($1 more for sweet potato fries) and choice of Pepsi can or bottled water).  The wings were crispy, juicy and full of flavor. The fries were thin cut and crispy (likely frozen, but we still enjoyed them). Definitely needed some vegetables after this fried lunch, but it served its purpose.

Food was served on a cafeteria tray which you return to the counter to retrieve when your order is ready. The staff basically takes your order and lets you know when your food is ready.

We came in around 12:30 (they open at noon). We were the only group sitting in to eat, but there was a slow stream of people coming in mostly for the teas of which they have a good variety from which to choose. Will have to try those sometime.
name: Eva

text:
The barbeque is better than average. I usually order the rib tips which are greasy and full of flavor. 

Kinda dumpy like a good bbq joint should be. Full bar.

Service is very good and friendly. I would suggest wearing a light jacket or sweatshirt as they keep it pretty cool.
name: Kenn

text:
We recently dined at Bricco this past Tuesday for lunch. We were in the area and the reviews were very good. We took the chance, Overall it paid off. I'm a huge fan of coal fired pizza but it's not very common in the area.

We arrived and it wasn't very busy. We sat ourselves and greeted by the server. I have to be honest but the service here severely lacks! It was bad! The server wasn't personable or very much helpful at all. We ordered the small Caesar salad, spice rubbed wings and large Margherita pizza. The Caesar salad was delicious! Everything was fresh and it was a fairly larger portion. The dressing was house made and the chicken was very good. The croutons were a bit burnt. The wings were perfectly seasoned and cooked. My biggest complaint is they had zero sauces. No bleu cheese, no ranch, nothing! How? Why? Doesn't make any sense whatsoever. It really made the wings that less enjoyable. The pizza was by far the best! The crust was cooked perfectly, just the right amount of color. Everything was spot on. The perfect amount of cheese, the sauce was delicious and simple, just enough basil. It really was a solid pie!

The restaurant itself was very clean and welcoming. The food was a solid 4 stars but they lose a star for the service. I would return.
name: Bob

text:
Don't let all the white customers fool ya :P they have some tasty Indian fare though maybe not super authentic!  When we arrived at 6pm on a Wednesday, we got seated quickly but the place was pretty packed by the time we left at 7:45pm. 

We ordered everything mild, except the goat curry  which we ordered medium, since my in-laws can't handle much spice. It was their first time trying Indian food so we kept it fairly safe and ordered crowd pleasers.

text: I did phone order from the parking lot (BECAUSE IT IS HOTTTTT ). The young man who picked up the phone was so pleasant! I went in and paid for my food and the staff saw why I was hesitant to get out the car as I waddled to the front door. I went back to my car and a few minutes later, got a knock at the window! text: Food was fantastic and so was the service, once they acknowledged I was there.  I would given five stars but ....

text: We had the best experience at this spot tonight. We walked in and it was 8:39 pm. Simon greeted us immediately and the place looked a little empty. We asked him at what time the kitchen closed and he said 8:45. I work in customer service so I felt TERRIBLE staying and making the kitchen cook at the very end of the night when they were just trying to close and go home. I told them not to worry, we would come back another day. He kept asking "are you sure? Are you sure? Just come stay!" I said to him "No man, I know how it is trying to get home, please, don't worry, I wouldn't want to do that to you guys" we turned around and left. As we were walking to our cars outside, Simon walked outside and yelled across and said "come back guys, let me serve ya! Don't worry just come in, we will make something for you guys!" He was so sweet and accommodating. He gave us our menus, got us water, with that huge smile! We chose something right away and they had it ready in the next 10 minutes. It was so delicious! Perfectly cooked! He kept checking on us and even still offered us desert! We left super happy and only stayed there 30 minutes since we didn't want to take more of their time! Needless to say, we highly recommend this place! So beautiful and such sweet people, especially Simon!

text: Best Sushi in town, in my opinion! Everything is SO FRESH, the golden delicious is my personal favorite. Non sushi items are good, too. My son is a picky eater, and he asks for the chicken teriyaki bowl twice a week! Owners seem very nice, would love to see them succeed! Excellent customer service!

text:
Thank-you, Tara for a wonderful visit. You were entertaining, friendly and knowledgeable.

Not my first visit here, but am glad I stopped by. The decor is very inviting. The shop greets you on entrance and it is well organized and presented. The bar is in the center of the vast room and a living room area is beyond that to enjoy your beverage. You can see the room where the wine is made from there.

text:
Shit sandwich:
Beautiful, comfortable atmosphere to relax and enjoy the cooler temperatures of the Tucson summer evenings. 

Reheated/overpriced/mundane food. Meat was fully cooked yet still cold in center. I get it, if you've got business, make it go fast. But, when you pay $40 for lamb it should fall off the bone, not be cooked and cold in the middle.  Risotto is the cheapest dinner on the menu and understandably so. Bland and overcooked. Both shrimp and chicken added (our party ordered both) to the meal was overcooked and underwhelming. 

4 margaritas, 2 meals and a split app... $120. 

I feel as though this place will attract the most pretentious of people so, if that's you, enjoy. 

Great staff and waiters. Very polite and accommodating.
name: Raymond

text:
A definite solid 4 stars. We had the pleasure of having Harrison as our server. He was awesome and very knowledgeable of the dishes on the menu. This is exactly what you want when asking about a certain dish. He made some good suggestions and gave his honest opinion. 
We started with the Braised Spanish Octopus and Tuna Carpaccio. I HIGHLY recommend getting both. The Tuna Carpaccio may have been the best I've had so far. The Octopus wasn't over cooked like some can be and the tuna was nice and fresh. 
We each had chosen our top two dishes to decide from and asked Harrison which one he thought was the best out of the two. So here's what we ordered....the Grilled Flat Iron Steak, the Double Cut Pork Chop and a side of their Creamy Polenta (which was never brought to the table). 
The Pork Chop was HUGE...I'm not even exaggerating. First of all, in our opinion, they added way too much lettuce, which seemed more like a salad, on top of the pork chop. Keep it simple! The pork chop had a nice golden brown breading which reminded me of a Schnitzel. Yum! Me being German, I'd love a side of applesauce with that. My Flank steak was cooked to my liking, MR, and was nice and juicy with great flavor. Again, I had the lettuce on the side. We were looking forward to trying the Polenta, but it never came. In the end, after eating all that food, we were ok with that, because we were pretty full and still wanted to leave room for dessert. We were not charged for the side dish. 
We are big on Tiramisu, so of course when we saw that on their menu, there was no second guessing. This was really really good. I liked that it was different and made with white chocolate. The Tiramisu was topped with little crunchy balls that I seriously could eat an entire box of...market that as a cereal and I'd be in a diabetic coma. 
Bottom line, it is a little on the pricy side, but it's well worth it. We will definitely be back and look forward to trying the pizza and pasta next time.
name: Nicole

text: for the price I expected a little more care. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. The staff seemed tired but still polite. text:

You can get a variety of interestingly crafted burgers and both adult and regular shakes. I'm always a sucker for interesting meat, so I had to go with their bison burger, medium rare. text:
Beautiful historic building! I love the contrast of urban rustic with the elegance of chandeliers. I'm chandelier obsessed, and I always love historic spaces. So we know the space is lovely, but my experience/food is enough to deter me from returning and to give my vegetarian friends a warning. They do offer vegetarian options, but for a modern restaurant, they seemed quite inconsiderate and clueless to this lifestyle. Since it's a southern kind of eatery I thought I'd make up a southern plate of vegetarian sides so I express to our waiter Im going to create a vegetarian soul food plate. Yum! 
Clue #1 to waiter: customer may be vegetarian 
I ordered collard greens, mac and cheese, mashed potatoes, and salad.
Now eating food. Nom nom. Wait. Collard greens have meat in them, which I notice after a few bites. Ask waiter, just to confirm I'm not mistaken. Yes, it's meat. After apologies for not mentioning to me it has meat, she makes other suggestions. I don't have the menu so I go with suggestions. Collard green replacement, Brussels sprouts. Yum! 
Clue #2 to waiter: vegetarian customer doesn't want meat in collard greens so may not want meat and meat liquid that got into mac n cheese and mashed potatoes from greens. Maybe a new plate? 'Nah, she'll be fine.' I ate the sprouts.
Later that night, I'm sick. I haven't eaten meat my entire adult life, but I'm thinking 'surely those few bits in the collard wouldn't have this affect.' I checked out their online menu and sure enough, Brussels sprouts were cooked and bathed in duck fat. 
Clue #3 to waiter: vegetarian customer doesn't like meat in collard greens so maybe customer won't want a bowl of duck fat. 
Sheesh, come on! I'm sorry, but this is just ridiculous and careless. And as lovely as the space is, I will NOT be back. 

None of this would have bothered me in some small town eatery, but for a restaurant born during Indy's evolving food scene, shame on you. 

Please serve your customers more responsibly, Repeal. This means train your staff to do so. 

Do I recommend them? It is a beautiful space, and maybe they have good meat options, so of course give them a go if you desire. They're not on my recommended list necessarily but I suppose if someone asked me about a more upscale southern food place, I may mention it since some reputable Yelpers seem to think it's okay to great.
name: Amanda

text: I've been here a few times and they only had 3 or 4 good meals. The rest were  ok. The fried chicken, pretzel bites and fondue, steak tacos and cheese platter. But that's really it. text: I've lived in SB for about 6 years now & I'm not sure what took me so long to try out Mony's! Best tacos in town! Affordable & great taste. Highly recommend.

text: Nice little gem on Wells ave. I stopped by their food truck version that sits next to a house for convenient dining. Although I took mine to go. All my tacos came with hand made tortilla and that made the difference  between a regular taco and an awesome taco. I went with yummy Lengua, cabeza and a regional cochinita. All were delicious and I would recommend even in this cold weather.

text:
This spring in New Orleans has been fantastic for outdoor dining.  So when Bordeaux opened, we were excited to try it.  They have a fantastic outdoor seating area in a decent area to people watch.  The weather was perfect.  Our server Larry was an extremely nice and attentive.  From an atmosphere and service perspective, we loved it.  

So now to talk about the food.  I had the lamb shoulder.  I like lamb shoulder.  It tends to have a decent marbling and I like lamb in general.  The cut of meat was decent but the sauce was really dull.  It's hard to describe the sauce because of the absence of flavor I associate with it.  I did not think it was bad, but it was just this bland yellowish sauce.  Very little flavor.  

On the other side of the table, Shari V had the red snapper.   It was a pretty piece of fish but same problem...no flavor.  She actually salted the fish and then took some of her water lemon wedges and squeezed them onto the snapper.  This was a desperate move.  

In short, 2 stars for the food.  They seem to have decent quality ingredients.  Unfortunately, the dishes did not come together for us.  I doubt we will repeat.
name: Chris

text: Service was great, food was pretty good. I'm a bit of a wing snob since I'm from Buffalo, but the wings here were pretty decent. The pizza was good too and I like you can order by the slice. It can get pretty busy around lunch time so be patient when ordering. I would visit again. Good spot!

text: Averagely good food nothing to write home about, very nice decor and the staff was wonderful. Pricey but I would come back with friends there was a lot of pretty women there.

text:
We stopped in for a quick breakfast this morning while doing some running around.

Everyone was very friendly without being too pushy. They even brought us hot chocolate to go for free (it's rainy and cold today). All in all a great experience and will be back.

text: I absolutely love dining at Zim Zari. I'm a picky eater and not a huge fan of tacos so I was hesitant and I regret not trying it out sooner. The surf and turf taco is my favorite option. The edamame are excellent and actually taste kind of like steak due to their seasoning. They do offer complimentary chips and salsa which is always a plus. Their servers are always upbeat and the kitchen always produces your dish faster than anywhere else. I've enjoyed many of their cocktails especially their seasonal options Lexing Greer. They do offer specials daily on drinks and all day specials on Tuesday for food although this can get crowded rather quickly and I would recommend are there dining for lunch or on any other day and just paying regular place.

text:
I was blown away by the service. I have really high standards for service and hospitality and it's hard to find restaurants that hit all the service points at the right time: We were greeted within 40 seconds, given info about the restaurant and menu (because we'd never been before), food was out at a good time, server checked back on appetizers and entrees, drinks never empty, plates we didn't need were taken away, etc.

Plus the food was AMAZING! We got the risotto balls, squash soup, pappardelle, "adult" Mac and cheese, tiramisu, and cheesecake. Everything tasted fresh and sooo good. The general vibe was warm and welcome! I will return!!!

text: This is now our third trip here. The food is delicious and reasonably priced. The staff is terrific. Will definitely be returning. Our new fave Mexican restaurant!

text: This review comes on the heels of Craig LeBan's scathing one bell comments on this restaurant over the weekend. Only wish I had seen his review first. My friend and I were excited to finally visit the new, sleek Four Seasons Hotel on 19th Street. The elevator ride to the 60th floor was smooth and breathtaking. We were instantly wowed by the shiny Christmas decor and the entrance to the restaurant. We stopped at the hostess desk and asked to see a menu. Then we decided to take in the experience and said we would like to have lunch. The hostess replied that she didn't believe there were any tables, despite the fact that the restaurant was half empty. I figured you must need a reservation and commented we would come back another day. As we moved away simply to take in the view, a waiter approached us and said, "we have a table right here, if you would like." That should have been a clue. The waiter was a friendly French gentleman who briefed us on the chef's culinary accomplishments and told us of his own 40 year restaurant experience. I ordered the Parmesan crusted chicken with lemon basil cream sauce, my friend had the endive salad. We each had iced tea and shared a dessert. To be perfectly honest, I can make a better chicken cutlet and as LeBan pointed out, the sauce was overwhelmingly lemony. My friend's salad was endive and pear with a dressing. The entire time we were there, the empty tables remained empty which made us wonder about the hostess's cool greeting. We are fairly well dressed older  adults but were made to feel like we didn't measure up to deserve a table. Our simple meal with no alcohol came to $97 with tip. Is it worth it? Certainly not for the food but maybe once to experience the view!
name: Ann

text: My wife and I went to dinner here with a friend.  The inside of the restaurant had unique decor and felt pretty cozy.  For appetizers, the table had the Abita Beer-Battered Crab Beignets and the Florida Alligator Bites.  The alligator bites were good but a little salty for me.  The beignets were delicious.  For entrees, we had the Jambalaya, Andouille Crusted Wahoo, and the Grouper Meunière.  All were very good.  The wahoo was outstanding and the jambalaya was better than what I've had in New Orleans.  They had a decent craft beer selection and my wife enjoyed the wine.  I would definitely return to try other items.  Preston, our server, was very attentive and friendly.  If I had to point out an issue, it would be the parking.  The lot is kind of small and was very crowded when we went but parking is a bitch everywhere on that side of town.  That being said this place is worth checking out.  Laissez le bon temps rouler!

text:
This is now our go to Italian restaurant. This was our first trip here. We arrived around 7:30 on a busy Friday evening. We waited about 5 minutes as the hostess had a table cleared for us. 

We were seated and out waitress was at our table within three minutes for drink orders. Drink orders came out and the waitress asked if we had any questions, which we didn't, and brought bread back and took our order. 

The salads we're out quickly. The house made ranch was delicious on the mostly romaine salad. The salads did have some cheese, a red onion slice, and some wonderful garlic croutons. 

The only downside on our dinner was that the entrees did take some time to come out. Fortunately, they were well worth the wait. My wife enjoyed the Alfredo Con Scampi and I had the Chef's Sampler of Lasagna, Manicotti and Fettuccine Alfredo. 

My wife stated that the Alfredo sauce is the best that she has had from a restaurant and I'd have to agree with her. It didn't need any extra seasoning added. It was delectable on its own. The shrimp in her entree were cooked perfectly and had great flavor. The lasagna and manicotti in my dish was superb as well. The meat sauce in the lasagna again was seasoned perfectly and the ricotta mixture in both the manicotti and lasagna had a wonderful flavor and beautiful texture. 

The Italian bread was warm and tasty, served with seasoned olive oil for dipping. The bread was the perfect accoutrement for getting the last bits of sauce from the dishes. 

It is a shame that we didn't have any room left for dessert. 

I can not wait for the next evening we want to go out for Italian. That being said, I was envious of every diners plate that came out with a steak on it. They looked divine with roasted red potatoes and mixed veggies. So I guess we may be back for our next steak
name: Joseph

text: In my quest to work my way through the menu, tonight I had the Aloha Classic bowl which has beautiful fresh ahi tuna, spring mix, edamame, Persian cucumbers, furikake, sweet onion & scallions and I added a little rice. This was a very large portion and the flavors were fresh and bright. It's so healthy and I loved it. I saved some for later though because I wanted to try one of their many side dishes. It takes a lot of skill to fry something with black sesame seeds because the oil in the seeds burns quickly. Not a problem here! These tofu fries were fried to perfection while keeping the generous wand of tofu creamy and soft on the inside. Hands down the BEST tofu fries ever.  Served with unagi sauce & Poke Munch sauce for dipping, I couldn't stop eating them! Looking forward to my next bowl or burrito, but I already know I'm ordering the tofu fries again.
