text: one of those meals where nothing is exactly wrong but you're not excited either. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. The music was louder than it needed to be. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Maybe better dine-in than delivery, hard to tell. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. The whole meal felt kind of uneven.
name: User

text: Delicious food! Everything we ordered, and I mean EVERYTHING, was incredible fresh and delicious. Flavor balance was perfect. I'm beyond full, but didn't want to stop eating it was so good. Great service & friendly staff add to the experience!!!
name: Henry

text: Typically a decent experience but today was completely out of the norm. Doug (as it states on my receipt) was very rude and unprofessional. I ordered from the drive thru this morning around 9:38am. I order a 8pc combo with lemonade and a large frosted key lime beverage. I wanted to redeem my very hard to accumulate points for the large frosted item. Since my rude not so smart or patient drive thru attendant Doug couldn't figure out how to redeem the CHIC FIL A App, he became rude, and dismissive. Told me this wasn't the right item. And that he was doing us a favor for redeeming it anyway. Never going to this location again.
name: Cynthia

text: I've been going to Drago's for years and I can honestly say that I've never had a bad meal. My favorite is, of course, the charbroiled oysters, but I've had several other things and each dish has been excellent. I like to go get a dozen oysters and a few drinks and it makes for a great time.
name: Catie

text: The games were awesome.  Huge selection.  My kids had a ball- we played for over 2 hours.    The bartenders in the game bar rocked. Super nice and attentive.   Then we went to get a table and were told the wait was an hour and a half.   (At 1pm) THERE WERE TONS OF OPEN TABLES.   why do restaurants have so many tables and not enough staff on a busy day near New Years? When I asked the hostess about the open tables, she was rude and told me that there was open seating in the busy and loud bar area- where we had just spent 2 hours... wanted a quieter place for lunch.   I should have checked and out my name down earlier.   I get that.   But why have sooo much open seating and not seat people?   We ended up eating in the bar and had appetizers.   They were good, for bar food!
name: Margo

text:
All of these stars go to the server and a tiny bit to the food presentation.  I wish I could remember his name.  He was also being shadowed by a new employee and he was very very accommodating and very friendly and attentive.

My salad with grilled chicken came out and looked great.  It was huge, too!  But when I ate half of it and couldn't eat any more of it, I got a box and proceeded to put it in the box and at the bottom of the salad bowl....

....Was a BIG BLACK HAIR!  EWWWWWWWWW!  I did not take the leftover salad home.  The server did not charge me for the salad - thank goodness - and I left him a tip anyway.

Not sure I plan to come back and give it another shot.
name: Alicia

text: Great tasting pizza and really affordable prices. Their drivers are always fast and food shows up still hot.
name: Chester

text:
Food was good. I got the ribeye steak and it was cut thin with some extra fat. 
Waitress was nice and service was fast. I will go back and try something more popular for a diner like a club sandwich.
name: Jesse

text: This is my new favorite place to eat. Dropped in today. We chose to sit at the bar to catch part of the Titans game. FYI several screens around, so you won't miss a play. The bartender "Chris" was great and had several good recommendations. I went with the Avocado Burger, it was awesome! You will not leave here hungry!
name: Bruce

text:
My wife and I had a wonderful time at Bodega. She recently broke her foot and needed a little bit of extra help getting around and ordering at the counter. The staff went above and beyond to make sure she was comfortable, and brought her everything she needed even though they don't technically have full table service. They were all extremely friendly and helpful, and pointed us towards their favorite dishes and beers.

The food was also great. There is very little good BBQ on the main line, but this place definitely has it down. The wings and brisket were my personnel favorites, but the ribs were excellent too. Look forward to coming back and trying the hot chicken sandwich.

My only suggestion/complaint is that I wish they had some hot sauces!
name: Zachary

text: First time ordering from here and I honestly wasn't sure what to expect. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. The music was louder than it needed to be. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. The sauces helped more than I thought they would..
name: User

text:
I have to say after reading some negative reviews I was kind of hesitant on going here but we had tickets to the IRT and figured we would give it a shot so we parked at the mall across the street and we went ahead and made a reservation although it was not necessary on this Sunday afternoon.we sat down and from the moment we sat at our table Mikayla,our waitress,was top-notch! We have never been here before and she explained the menu thoroughly even explain how many beers they had on tap, I don't drink beer but they did have about seven different cider that you could try. I love the ace Pineapple Cider but she quickly told me that they were out so I went for my second choice Unfortunately they were also out of that so I asked what she recommended so she brought me back a pear cider and then also a wheat beer that she recommended only because it was very fruity and let me say it wasn't half bad I would actually drink it. first we placed our order for some loaded nachos and it was a pretty good-sized we could not finish them , the only thing I would say they are missing is some fresh cut jalapenos other than that they were superb ! I ordered the chicken sandwich deep fried and you had your choice of french fries but not just any french fries you can choose from garlic,sweet potato, original or even truffle.I went with the garlic with a side of ranch and they were not skimpy on the garlic and they were also very delicious. I could tell that our waitress could pick up on the fact that I was very very picky she asked if I wanted my condiments on the side as I told her I did not want any lettuce or tomato, she suggested that I put the honey mustard dressing and also the cheese spread on the side that way if they were not good then that way I could decide if I did or did not want them on my sandwich; luckily there were both delicious so I actually put them  on my sandwich.unfortunately we were both too full to try dessert but next time I think we'll start with that .
Overall we had a very pleasant experience !our waitress was top-notch I would definitely definitely request her next time and also the fact that the manager stopped by the table to make sure that everything was okay with super awesome! although this was a Sunday afternoon and it was not busy at all,it was nice to go to a restaurant and not feel rushed so I applaud them for the time that they spent with us and I will definitely, definitely be back
name: Roxanne

text: If I could give it 6 Stars I would! This has to be one of the best meals I've ever had. The servers, the ambiance and the food were exceptional. Started with the amazing hamachi dish (off the menu) and grilled avocado with avocado mousse. Had to request for extra homemade sourdough bread to scrape the sauces clean!!! Then continued to the carbonara mussels with squid ink pasta and eggplant garam masala with cauliflower.  Sooooooo amazing! Then the lamb gyros that's been marinated and slow cooked for how many hours was so tender with crispy edges in homemade pita bread. Divine! The finale was the semifredo that i can't stop thinking about: it is the best rocky road dessert I've ever had: coffee flavored with homemade caramel sauce, melty marshmallows, crunchy walnuts and cocoa nibs. I can't wait to go back to Santa Barbara and Barbareño!!!! P.S. they serve this kombucha drink on tap that was delicious (and I'm not even a kombucha drinker)!
name: Sarah

text: The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. Will be back. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Not bad for a quick meal.
name: User

text: Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Would return. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent.
name: User

text: Could be a nice store, but both store and corporate customer service is atrocious.
name: Bill

text:
I try to offer the benefit of the doubt when a dinning experience doesn't go well but I feel 2 stars is a generous as I can be here. I'll offer my reasons here. Came in for happy hour with colleagues and the place was only about a quarter full at best.  After 10-15 min, a sever came by to let us know he'd be with us shortly.  Upon returning a little while later, he was unable to explain their happy hour specials and there was no literature on the table to explain it. 

We ordered drinks based off of what he could remember and said there was a menu somewhere, he would try to find it.  10-15 min later he returned with a happy hour menu that offered no more information than what we previously had.  He handed us off to another sever.  

This server knew no more than the previous one, but had a trainee in tow. I feel very. As for her as she was trying to learn but apparently there wasn't much that was needed to be learned.  

We asked about their Tuesday $1 burger special, but again, she couldn't remember but insisted that somewhere they had the special menu.  The special menu appeared shortly after.  We all promptly ordered and waited another 55 minutes before flagging our server down.  Without any kind of apology for our wait, she explained that there was another table of 4 that had ordered a number of burgers ahead of us and that had backed up the kitchen.  I can't imagine the wait had the restaurant been actually halfway filled.  We let her know we needed to leave and to forget about the burgers.  She said they were ready and they were brought out in the next couple of minutes.  We had all ordered them medium to medium rare, but they came out very well done.  When asked, again without apology, our sever explained that it was too difficult for the kitchen to keep track of that so they just make them all well done. It's easier that way.  Two in our group didn't eat any of their burger as it was cooked to the point of being burnt and hard.  We just paid our bill and headed out.  

Other than the company, this experience was a complete bust.  I'm shocked they are still in business.  Service and food were terrible. We will not be back.
name: Alan

text: Great food and a nice beachy atmosphere. Food items seem a couple of dollars higher than you might expect, such as over $4 to add a single-size serving of from-frozen fries to a $9 burger. Hot sauces and barbeque sauces are tasty and spicy. Good deals at happy hour, which was pretty crowded and bustling when we went. We will return to try some of the other yummy-sounding menu items.
name: Tim

text: I went early this week for the 10% discount.  I talk with the "owner".  They had another vietnamese restaurant around the corner from pho 75 (my fav) on Whitaker in philly.   This is also not just a pho place.  I had seafood soup there and a chicken bahn mi to go. The soup comes with jalapenos, bean sprouts,  and limes.  I used the limes and sprouts to flavor the rich deep broth.  (Unlike pho which is light,  delicate and subtle). I also used hot sauce (huy fong - the rooster) and fish sauce.  The owner came over and suggested pepper as well.  The broth was delicious.  A couple of shrimp,  halved fish balls, and squid plus clear noodles completed the bowl. The bahn mi had a light baguette  with chicken and some pickled veggies.  A nice repast before the opera.
name: Ken

text:
Great New Spot from those that bring you Pizza Mizza.  This takes up the beautiful corner as you enter the Turtle arcade off mid State street.  Food is fresh, inventive and yet with classic favorites.  The fountain inside and decor is upbeat and yet charming.   They aim to please.  Fun for families or couples. 
High quality often locally sourced  ingredients... A great new addition to SBA!
name: Hanna

text: I was shocked that they didn't have a Brazilian Steakhouse in Tucson until now. The food was amazing and the staff was exceptional!
name: Christopher

text: Great little ice cream shop that makes all their ice cream homemade. They always offer at least one flavor of vegan ice cream and sugar free/fat free, which is great. They have amazing flavors that change constantly and their vegan ice cream is to die for! Great service and they don't mind if you try things. Best ice cream I've ever had!
name: Amber

text: Darien, thank you for having the attitude of 10 happy, helpful people combined! You truly made our experience what it was. Hot chicken lived up to its name and the Mac & Cheese was so delicious! Service was quick! Thank you again, Darien!
name: Meagan

text: Absolutely incredible ramen. Fast service and delicious. Got the veggie ramen which was the best I've had. Get a side of the garlic chili sauce, you'll thank me later.
name: A

text: Service was good. I wanted something light to eat, end up getting the grilled chicken skewers with white barbecue sauce (mayo with paprika). I also have a chocolate putting for dessert. I love put in but this particular putting was ok. It's always good to go during lunch because the volume wasn't bad at all. I know during dinner they are typically swamped.
name: Akilah

text: The best thin crust pizza I ever had.  It wasn't flimsy, it kept the cheese and topping in place.
name: Mike

text:
This was my first visit since the expansion/remodeling and Herban Market just proved its worth even more! 

The store has plenty of goods that not only taste delicious but at healthy! I've driven all the way from east Nashville to HM to buy some products because they were the only store in the area to have it. HM truly prides itself on quality of goods and chooses the best ingredients! 

In regards to the expansion, it still is a bit cramped, so be prepared for that. My visit today was for a quick midday food/coffee visit with my coworkers. It was a little confusing with ordering as we weren't sure where to go. We decided to place an order for two coffees and were given a number to put at our table. We were confused with the number and asked if they would be serving it to our table and the cashier said "well it'll probably just be set over there (pointing to the counter near the espresso machine"...so what was the point of the number?
I then ended up ordering a sandwich and put it on the same number.  

It took about 10minutes for the coffee to be done and we had to go over to pick it up. My sandwich on the other hand kept us waiting..after about 20 mins I was wondering what was up cause kitchen staff were just idle and not doing anything. I approached the cashier and she went to check on it and brought it right out. So was it just sitting back there? WhT was the point of the number at our table?

The store side is wonderful albeit being cramped, but the food side needs a little more work to perfect the transaction and serving of the orders. 

The sandwich itself was about $13 which I felt was a bit much since it didn't come with sides, regardless of quality of ingredients. I'll probably just be back for coffee and the store front. Maybe I'll find a more cost friendly food the next time I visit.
name: Stephanie

text: My 3 daughters and I had a yearly tradition to go to the Women's Exchange. This year was such a disappointment. The service has always been spotty at best but our experience last week was a new low. Our server was clear that she didn't want to wait on us and she would come around to her tables with tunnel vision. She only saw who she wanted to see. She ignored us for approx 20 min. We needed more dressing for the salads (there was barely any dressing on them) and the sandwich my daughter ordered came on the wrong bread. When we finally got her attention, she picked up the plate (with an attitude) and took it back to the kitchen. My daughter's fork was still on the plate. It was obvious all that was done was the chicken salad was scraped onto the new bread. The fork was still on the plate when she brought it back. That's not really sanitary. This is not an inexpensive place to go have lunch. It gets old being treated bad and then they expect a generous tip. I'm done with the Women's Exchange. And the shop in front- NO customer service. It's unfortunate that a place that started with such good intentions has gotten so far off track.
name: Leah

text: Was great Chicken and Collard Green.    WOW.    Nice staff, quick to get drinks. Mangament checked on us 2 different time. Good place to eat.
name: Scott

text: This was my first time eating at this restaurant. It was very good . The seafood came from the gulf of Mexico, which was a plus . It was a good amount served for the price and the juicy special sauce was really good . I would definitely go back.
name: Jay

text: The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. It just never really recovered once things started off weird. Probably not coming back. It looked better online than it did in person. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.
name: User

text: Ordered takeout because I didn't feel like cooking and it held up okay. So yeah, everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. The whole meal felt kinda uneven. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean.
name: User

text: Omg sodium overload!!! Chips were so salty i spit them out and had to throw them away. The food was also very salty it was overpowering. It wouldn't hurt to ease out on the salt considering it's very bad for you anyway
name: Tiffany

text:
2 words - CHEESE CURDS. Omg the lightest fluffiest gooey cheese curds. We almost asked for a second order they were so good but we had so much food we weren't able to handle it. The dipping sauces are both really good - garlicky ranch and sort of a smoky chipotle. 

We also got the cinnamon bun - loads of sticky sauce on the bottom and perfect amount of frosting. The sesame gochujang bacon was pretty good too. 

The drinks were tasty - I was happy to find a grapefruit mimosa which quickly went to my head (in a good way). My husbands pink lemonade was refreshing. 

For mains we got the shrimp poboy Benedict and spicy chicken biscuit sandwich with bacon. The Benedict was an interesting take - pretty sure the base was a Martin's potato roll. The shrimp had a char grilled flavor but they had tails on so it was a little hard to eat with the rest of it. Ended up eating the shrimp mostly on their own. I liked the pickled slaw on top for a bit of acid. The chicken biscuit was huge and decadent. Came with fries. I tasted a friend's lemon ricotta pancake - that whipped ricotta on top is a game changer!

Service was great and food came out fast! We had made reservations for 10am on Saturday (that's when it opens). People were already hovering outside before the doors opened.
name: Alison

text: Good food but not great.  Plastic utensils made eating a little difficult.  The staff was very friendly.  Keep in mind it is cafeteria style.  Overall happy I ate here.
name: Scott

text: Yes! These are THE tacos. Very happy with the fish tacos and the tacos al pastor, while the lengua tacos were good, but not our favorite. They know Yucatan home cooking very well. The dishes are light, enjoyable, great flavor. Huaraches are quite delicious and a bit more filling.   A nice little restaurant tucked away in the corner of Lambertville. One must stop by when visiting either Lambertville or New Hope. It can be a bit of a walk from New Hope over the bridge, but well worth it.

text: Conshy Corner Tavern has been the best bar in Conshy since Bobby Burgers. You want to have fun? You want to Dance? You want to meet a tattoo artist? You want to experience living? Go to Conshy Corner Tavern and experience life!!!!!

text:
There are lots of traditional Chinese BBQ. I just find there is a new recipe of BBQ in China. Guess what , it present here. If you want to try things never try or love BBQ. This restaurant would be your best choice. 
 Recommend About BBQ

text: In my short trip to Philadelphia , I visited this place thrice as I loved it so much . With great food ,great service and a huge collection of beer I have nothing to complain about . I ate the dan dan noodles which were delicious-the best I have ever had . So was the pepper chicken and kung pao chicken. I loved the fact that u could choose your own spice level as i love spicy food . We also had the wonton soup which was really really good  . The only thing that I did not like on the menu was the fried rice. Seemed dry . As far as the service goes , it was impeccable all 3 times-warm , smiling , observant. I would definitely visit it again the next time I am in town.
name: Damini

text: Everything about this experience was amazing. Two of us came into Under The Moon around one for Sunday brunch. They have a relationship with a local liquor store that will deliver if you forget that it's BYOB. The aesthetic of this spot is like something I've created in my own head - mismatched plates and glasses, cool rustic and personalized wares decorate shelves and surfaces, a mixture of music, ABBA and then some Spanish guitar, played overhead. The food was incredible - started with rice balls which had a great combination of flavors, partner had chicken and waffles and I had a modified version of the huevos rancheros (which was no problem for them). I am a sucker for huevos rancheros and these definitely did not disappoint. The staff (one of whom helped us I believe was an owner) were so inviting and kind. I cannot wait to come back here, I will highly recommend it to friends and family.
name: Rosie

text: My friend liked it more than I did. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. Maybe better dine-in than delivery, hard to tell. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer..
name: User

text: Anthony S was the man! Took great care of us from start to finish! The steak was truly an Argentinian experience and enjoyable from start to finish. Can't wait to go next time! Thanks Anthony!
name: James

text: worst food, worst service, worst drinks, i show up with my id and got served a non-alcoholic beverage when im a 24 year old women. They still charged me full price. never go here
name: Georgia

text: Such good food, people, ambiance. Def recommend if in Santa Barbara you need to check this place out
name: Jenna

text: I don't really get some of the harsh reviews on here. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Food was good and came out fast.
name: User

text: Marzano's is a local BYOB Italian restaurant that I am in love with!  It is five minutes from my office and 15 mins from home, doesn't get any more convenient than that.  I enjoyed the best, perfectly cooked salmon EVER!  My husband had the veal that was topped with an Arugula salad, which was also delish.  For appetizers we enjoyed perfectly fried calamari and an order of little neck clams.  The atmosphere is very nice, white table cloth nice.  They have a couple of spacious private rooms.  I was impressed enough with the food, staff and overall experience that I plan on hosting a meeting in one of their private rooms soon.
name: Karen

text:
It looks like Pat's did an overhaul of their online ordering website and in the process eliminated the 10% discount for Website orders placed!  Boo!!! Not cool at all, Pat's!  1 point penalty for that :(

This was a nice incentive for me to place online orders instead of calling them, but at least the Loyalty Points Program is still there.

However, the food is good, including the pizzas, cheesesteaks (steak or chicken), but they did away with the cheesesteak fries on their menu, which was a big favorite of mine!  Boo!!  Bring 'em back, Pat's!!!

Skip the overpriced and undersized desserts and not sure if the seafood dishes are worth trying or not.

Delivery is fast and drivers are always courteous and friendly.
name: David

text: Quality food for a reasonable price. Everything we had was amazing and flavorful. The mini dessert cups were the icing on the cake! Vegans paradise
name: Rebecca

text:
Last night was my first time here and I would like to start by saying the ambiance of this bar is elegant, beautiful and dreamy. The menu is approachable while holding a fantastic selection of vegan options (though, they were low on vegan cheeses during my time there last night). I drank the Fox Daiquiri following my servers suggestion and it was exactly what I wanted. They paired the perfect amount of creaminess to this fruit forward cocktail, I was beyond impressed with the execution. The dessert charcuterie, vegan pulled pork, hot chicken hummus, and mushroom tartine were all ethereal.

Now that I've established I was there and buying items since I love to support Nashville restaurants, service industry people, and this growing, thriving culture...let's get into service. I came on a slow night. There were two booths open with a two and four top in each. I went with three people, one of whom had come prior and said she was treated passive aggressively, but would like to give the establishment one more chance since the menu is EXCELLENT. We were offered a table or the bar, but asked for a booth since two were open. The server, replied they generally reserve those for groups of five as I'm staring at a two/four top in them. He begrudgingly gave us a booth, saying how he guesses he could since its slow, as if he's doing us favor. He didn't introduce himself, ask if we'd been there before, ask if we had questions, try to I.D. us until we thrusted our IDs at him, and all around gave us horrible energy and we honestly should have walked out after the booth scenario. He forgot one of the cheese on our charcuterie and made no effort to look in the menu in front of him and correct himself or apologize? I've dined while being black my entire life and I felt my money wasn't wanted at this establishment. When my friend went she also felt and air of pretentious aloofness, even though we were buying things and trying to enjoy our night. There was a staff member with red hair I believe, who came to our table asked how our food/experience was going. He was the saving grace to an all around bad experience. The server also failed to give me proper change? My bill was $28, I handed him $40, have gave me to fives and a one back. I don't know if it was to imply I should tip him ten?  But I had my friend break since he walked away immediately and left seven, regardless of my service being poor. As we were gathering our things/leaving tips he put a RESERVED sign on our table watching us pull out our money to tip as if checking to see if we would...which further pressed us to leave the establishment, though it seemed the other three top behind us weren't getting the same type of treatment. Yeah, maybe it was because I was wearing boots with a dress and had some paint on my skin since I was pausing from painting for eight hours to enjoy some friends and libations, but East Nashville is for artists. I really have no desire to ever come back. I've never felt so unwanted and uncomfortable in a restaurant in Nashville, and all I do is eat here. Maybe would have wanted to get another cocktail, but again, my entire group was uncomfortable to the point my sister said she "hated it" and was upset to nearly years for an hour that she spent money to be treated rude. The only other time she had felt that way was when someone was openly racist to us, with the slurs included. This establishment is the tier below that. Whoever that server was should really consider the breadth of the service industry and how we should all support each other. Being rude, isn't how you shape clientele, you shouldn't choose who gets a great experience based on your assuming who will tip or not. We were all servers, I generally tip 35% or more. It was just trash. I wanted it to be great and it was trash. Thanks.
name: Jezebel

text:
I feel like when I go to an expensive restaurant, I want to be treated like royalty and catered to.  Peterson's does that.  It's a place where folks go to spend their hard earned money and lots of it. 

I had the famous prime rib and it was fantastic!  Perfectly cooked, and inch thick and melty.  I ate on it for 3 days! Totally worth the $50+ bucks. 

The staff was attentive and polite and knowledgeable.  They use a crumb scraper, which I love. 

The only reason Peterson's doesn't get 5 stars is for the price of my Oban scotch.  $20 a shot is outrageous when the average elsewhere is $9-$12.  I was shocked. 

Great place to eat but you get bent over on liquor.
name: Sara

text: Fantastic food and beer!!  One of our favorite spots to eat in town, and we always bring visitors from out of town here.  Everyone has loved it so far!
name: Michael

text: Had the burnt ends sandwich for dinner last night, along with the fried ravioli. Not only the food was good, but the atmosphere was nice and the woman working at the bar was really cool. Definitely will be going back.
name: Koi Ling

text: Actually, really, really, REALLY love this place. The pho is always delicious and the people are always friendly. Came here one night a little too close to closing and was not met with any kind of attitude or unwillingness to be served. Very impressive customer service and always a very clean little place!
name: G

text: My friend and I came here for the guided Segway tour. Our guide was very friendly and patient in helping us with the segways. Mine seemed to have a mind of it's own towards the end and I lost control of it which was scary but he helped me through it. He was great! As for the tour, it was interesting. I was a little put off by the sugarcoating of the slavery that built that place. They tore down the actual slave cabins and built newer nicer looking ones that were "similar" to the originals. The posters inside the rebuilt slave cabin had quotes from the slaves as though they were happy to be there and life was good. It felt a little inauthentic in that way and disrespectful. We stayed afterwards for a wine tasting and to listen to the band that was playing. Overall it was a nice day.
name: Aubrey

text:
Hard to believe it's been over four years since they opened. I was there opening day.  They had staffed the place entirely with D.C. area veterans who ensured that the Sardi's method was up and running day one.  They had a few slips as they transitioned to a local staff, but they seem to have hit their stride.

Now that they are on DoorDash (with a VERY reasonable delivery fee) they are in heavy rotation for those evenings where I may have had ONE more drink than I'd feel comfortable driving after

Their food travels well.  The pork and lamb chops always arrive hot and juicy and flame kissed.  It's always worth tossing in the who chicken (no sides) for $18 as it's their signature, and no matter what else you're eating, you really WANT ant least a bite (and it's great leftover.) 

Sides are HUGE and most everything is extraordinarily fresh.  A Caesar salad comes with nice shaved Parmesan instead of a shake 
from the green can.

Their food is CONSISTENT.  I've never had a case where something wasn't right.  You DO have to deal with nearly everything being 
well-done.  It's still juicy and flavorful, but you're not going to get your lamb chops rare.  Beef might show a hint of pink, but that's it. As long as you set your expectations you'll never be disappointed.  

Good choice for keto dieters (but good luck avoiding those plantains !!)

text:
ABSOLUTELY worth the wait! 

We moved to St Pete nearly 18 months ago and were told this was THE place for Mexican. Unfortunately, each time we stopped by there was almost an hour wait.

Last night we headed​ over just before​ 5 PM​, midweek​, after spring break and go in after only a few minutes. 

Not only do they have excellent Mexican food and really strong drinks, but there are about five tables on the patio, four tables (4+ seats) inside and about six hightops across from the bar.

If you come in the front door be prepared to be sent through the kitchen to the hostess on the back patio for seating.

My husband arrived first and was offered a hightop table for two, and we jumped at the offer. You are taken through the kitchen, into the bar area. 

He ordered us two Margaritas with salt ($5.00) we got two big coupe style glasses with a delicious, VERY STRONG margaritas. 

We told the server we needed a few minutes and she offered to answer any questions. We started with ​basic Chips and Salsa ($2.95) and received​ a good portion of thick, chunky, fresh salsa and a basket of corn tortilla chips. The salsa was delicious, fresh and flavorful with a little bite.

We both went with the Wet Burrito ($8.95) with chicken they are known for and added the rice and beans to make it a platter ($2.00).

Shortly, they brought out to large, hot platters with a nice size burrito smothered in red sauce and melted cheese, a side of refried beans and rice with a small mound of shredded lettuce, diced tomato, black olive and a cup of sour cream.

Everything was well seasoned, and the burrito was moist and delicious. The biggest surprise was the incredible amount of shredded white meat chicken in the burrito. WOW!

We tried their jalapeno and cilantro sauce with these, and our server mentioned they have something​ hotter if we'd like. We both love spicy food and are no wimps, but this tiny cup of spicy hot sauce was SMOKIN.

The server was friendly and attentive, the place is loud and hectic, the wait can be long, ​but the food and the drinks are worth the wait.

If they offer you a seat at the bar TAKE IT!
name: Mark

text:

The fried alligator was pretty good, but I haven't had a bad plate of fried alligator in New Orleans yet (fingers crossed). For our entrees, we had the crawfish etouffee and the blackened redfish. I enjoyed the etouffee, but it might be a bit bland for some. I topped it off with some hot sauce and crackers which kicked it up a notch. text:
We love Vietnamese food, esp Pho.  Arriving to Reno one cold Sunday in mid May, read the reviews & headed to 999 Pho.  After spending 2-4x per week ordering number 12 (Pho Tai) 99 percent of the times, we know, we like the Pho Tai at 999 Pho.  The broth is light and has light fragrant.  Plenty of noodles and plenty of thinly sliced steaks!  Plenty of fresh vegetables too!  We only ever ordered 2 other different dishes and they were decent.  They have a popular Vietnamese dessert Che 3 color, one of my favorite Asian dessert & could not find this on any other Vietnamese Restaurant menu in Reno.  Another kudos for 999 Pho. Took it to go, got so excited, mix the Che inside the cup before I remembered that I needed to take a photo!  Do not let the photo fools you, it is very good.  The menu is extensive, but the comfort of a good bowl of Pho cannot be beat.  We are highly sensitive to MSG, never once got sick after eating Pho at 999 Pho!

After a couple meals, we started to have conversations with the owner, Phat.  A very nice Southern Vietnamese man.  We complimented the Pho & he jokingly told us to try other different dishes!  Now that Summer is officially here, we will start trying other dishes(?) not sure, living out of a hotel for a few months, nothing satisfied like a good bowl of Pho to comfort the soul.

Since we have eaten here so many times, oddly we have also always sat at table #12!

999 Pho is located inside a shopping plaza corner of Grove/Kietzke across from Lithia Reno Subaru.  The restaurant is humble, but clean.  Service is prompt & polite.  Always great to be able to talk to the owner or servers at these family owned restaurants!

We will continue to eat at 999 Pho!
name: Julianna

text:
Having been to City Tap House before, on a crowded night... I'm so happy to have been able to go back when they weren't quite as packed. Just a personal preference to get a little more personal service and boy, did they deliver! 
We went to City Tap pre-concert on a Sunday night and it was early enough that we just surrendered the reservation and ate tapas style at the bar. 
Firstly, the bartenders were amazing and graciously offered samples of every tap we were curious about. They also gave honest and accurate reviews of them. Thank you, City Tap for making sure your bartenders know your taps. Then the appetizers began. We ordered a couple and then took our time on the third one...again, the staff being awesome in continuing to check in with us. We'd already said the mussels would be our last appetizer, we were just spacing it out and enjoying the scene and drinks. 
We started with the baked brie...and what a cool flavor combination. I didn't' read the description well and missed that it had whole roasted garlic with it. So that was a wow surprise. I'd expected mostly sweet and then got a clove and just....wow. I almost didn't like it, but it was my own fault for getting a flavor I wasn't expecting. 
Next the elote 'street corn' dip.  OHMYGOSH is all I have to say.  Just ohmygosh good. Loved it!
The mussels (Abigail style) were cooked perfectly....only 1 that didn't crack open and one that was already removed from the shell.  It takes a little bit to get that timing just right and they nailed it. The bread served with them was a little dense for my tastes, but the flavor of the broth and mussels themselves was amazing!  I'm going for Loretta style next!

text:
First of all let me just say that I am from Brooklyn, New York and I know a good bagel when I taste one. This place is a disgrace and they should change their name to "Rotten Apple Bagels." Having just moved down here from New York I am pretty sick and tired of all the 4 and 5 star reviews given to restaurants purporting to be "authentic". People have NO IDEA what good food is down here and I'm just finding that out. Read some of the reviews below where people have given a great review but mention "weird smell" , "paper that separates the cheese still in my sandwich" and "service wasn't that great and they looked at me funny".  Why on earth would you give a good review when you had to experience any of the above mentioned things??? This place wouldn't last a week in New York. 

I had pre ordered and PAID for some bagles and veggie cream cheese a few days ago and went to pick it up today. As usual I entered the store and no one greeted me (fourth time), and walked up to the counter and asked for my pre order. The girl working there acted as if I was ruining her day by actually making her "work" so she grabbed my order and plopped it on the counter. text: When the Town & Country location of Katies Pizza & Pasta opened there was some confusion and my original review for the Rock Hill location got deleted. I stopped by on a Thursday for lunch recently with my father and it's still great. I ordered the lunch special with the Fried Artichoke Salad and the Fiori Arrabiatta Pasta. My dad ordered the daily pizza special which had steak, gorgonzola cheese, huckleberries, red onion, and arugula. Every component of the Fried Artichoke salad is delicious! I absolutely love the pistachios and the creamy goat cheese! I would eat this again and again and honestly I have! When our entrees came out I was shocked at how tiny the Fiori Arrabiatta was. It was a mini bowl and there wasn't even 1 cup of pasta in it. I would completely expect a lunch portion to be smaller than a dinner portion and it had a good flavor but this was ridiculously tiny. The pizza was phenomenal. I would not have thought to put the huckleberries on a pizza but it was great. It was savory from the steak, pungent from the gorgonzola, sweet from the huckleberries, peppery from the arugula, etc. The service was friendly and speedy. It was a hot day and a little warm in there but not out of control. I'm sure we'll be back but I'd think twice about ordering the lunch special again. When you spend $50 on lunch you don't want to feel like you didn't eat anything!

text:
I don't often visit chains, but when I do, I like to have standbys that don't let me down. We just needed somewhere quick and tasty before an event on the NW side of town. The margarita selection is amazing, and every time my husband gets something different. You can't go wrong with the Presidente Margarita. It comes with a small glass, but then you get the shaker to pour yourself more as you go. I'd argue it gets watered down more that way, but honestly, just drink it faster. ;) The strawberry Presidente that my husband got was good too - not too sweet like some flavored margaritas can be. 

I got the margarita grilled chicken off their "Guiltless Grill" menu (something I have always liked). The chicken was juicy, and I love their black beans! They're always seasoned well, and I don't think I've had better anywhere else. My husband got the spicy shrimp tacos, but they were skimpy on the fillings. I'd rather tacos be overflowing rather than not full enough. Still, he was happy with the taste and quality. 

The pricing is great compared to what we spend other places so as far as I'm concerned, this Chili's has held up to what I expect.

text:
One of the curses of growing up in the South is now that I live in the Southwestern United States, I really, really miss good, down home, soul food. Since I was in Nashville, I decided to look up good places to eat and Arnold's popped up. It was about a 20 minute walk from my downtown hotel so I set off on foot for a hearty lunch. After a sketchy piece of walking under a creepy underpass filled with a menagerie of shady characters, I arrived to a line that was literally stretched out the door. I knew right then that I had found the perfect lunch spot!

The clientele was an eclectic mix of business men, urban teens, senior citizens, and the like. You can't really pin down the typical customer here, which is a testament to how great the food is: everybody and their mother loves it. 

Arnold's is cafeteria style and ordering is pretty straightforward. They'll serve you whatever they decide on the day you visit, and the serving line changes daily. You tell the non-nonsense folks what you want, and they pile your plate high. I love the sassiness of the servers. They weren't exactly rude, but don't come here if you need to be coddled as they just assume you know what you are doing. I didn't, and the large woman behind the counter didn't have time for that, lol. 

I opted for the daily roast beef special with green beans (my favorite veggie), collard greens (my second favorite veggie), and macaroni and cheese that was prepared just like my grandmama used to make it: baked in a dish with eggs and loaded with sharp cheddar cheese. I added on an unsweet iced tea (free refills and so delicious) and a homemade roll which was a tasty biscuit / roll hybrid. The grease on the roll was amazing, just covered in butter. 

The tables are all communal, so you WILL be sitting with strangers. It's the South so make the best of it and chat right along with them. This is not an ideal place if you're shy. Thank goodness I was raised in the South because I can talk nonstop with the best of 'em. 

I licked my plate clean (see photos) and the food was excellent. Just plain old comfort food at reasonable prices. Most everything was a little on the salty side, as most authentic soul food is. But this is a fantastic place if you are craving Southern food or if you've never really had authentic Southern food and are curious to try it. 

Loved this place!

text:
Visiting my sister and decided to order takeout from this restaurant. After calling and placing an order of pad Thai, orange chicken, yellow curry, and maifunn, we were told it would take 25 minutes. Therefore we arrived 25 minutes after placing the order, and we had to wait another 20 minutes to get our food. When we walked in there was a really strange vibe. First, we saw zero host or servers. There was no apology upfront or any explanation about the take out delay except "we are busy."
One thing I can say is the take-out package was nicely presented. Everything was wrapped up really tight. Nothing leaked or spilled. The portions are very good sized, but we were very disappointed in all of the food. The orange chicken was over cooked, we actually gave the dog the pad Thai (over cooked chicken and zero peanut flavor), little flavor in both the curry and maifunn.
The customer service was less than grand. We even asked how long it would take if we added a couple eggrolls to our order, and she told us 25 minutes. Everything was 15 or 25 minutes. I don't know if there was a language barrier, but it was just an all-around unpleasant experience. 
I would be willing to try out this place one more time. It has to be better than 1 Star.
name: Jaime

text:
I am a regular customer at the sunflower cafe, but last night I was treated so poorly, I don't know if I will ever go back. Last night was Friday 6/21/19  the Cafe was open until 10pm. I got there around 8 to meet a friend. They started packing everything up extremely early. Granted there was a storm last night. I was drinking hot tea, and I asked for more hot water. They had already put the urn away and the shift leader flat out told me no. She was very rude. I'm sure it wouldn't have taken a lot of effort to get 1 cup of hot water. It was before 9 o'clock. 

At 9:30 my friend and I were eating with full plates of food, and the same shift leader came up to us and asked if she could take our plates. Full plates of food!! I told her I was still working. She said, well we are closing in a half hour, and we want to get out of here as soon as possible. She was so hostile with us. I felt so uncomfortable, I packed my food up and left. Meanwhile there was another couple at a table, who got there after us, and she did not talk to them at all. My friend and I were the only two people of color sitting down that night, I honestly wonder if that was a factor. 

I have been working in the service industry full time for the past year. Never in my life have I asked a customer to leave during normal business hours. I could understand if we were lingering past 10pm, but rushing us a half hour before close? That was incredibly rude. We spent over $50 and tipped generously. It's very disappointing to be treated so poorly and being in such an unfriendly an unaccommodating space. If she would have politely told us that they were closing early due to the storm, we would have kindly left. But instead we were basically kicked out through hostility and passive aggression. 

I am very upset because I do really enjoy the food. I am a longtime vegan, and I really love supporting vegan businesses. But I've never had such an upsetting dining experience!!! The other staff members were very kind and helpful. The woman who prepared our food was very knowledgeable. And a woman with purple hair was especially kind. It was mainly the shift manager who was so rude and aggressive and ruined the night. By the time we left, the brunt of the storm was over. So there was really no reason for such anxiety. I've never had such poor service, especially at a counter service restaurant!! I hate to say it, but I'm going to have to take my business elsewhere. For anyone still reading this, the food is good, the prices are reasonable, but the service is aforementioned. I was really looking forward to opening of the bakehouse, but now I don't know if I can support.
