text:
I've been putting off this review because every time I go, I have something else to rave about. My girlfriend (who is Filipina) and I first heard about Maemax, we immediately changed the lunch plans we had and drove 20 minutes out of our way to LaVergne to check it out. 

Maemax is about 60% market, 40% restaurant. The inside is clean and bright, and the friendly owners and workers greet you when you come in. The market side has everything from snacks to sauces to a small selection of produce to frozen meats and seafood. They also have fresh breads, delivered weekly from a bakery in Seattle and house-made goodies. The snacks (my favorite section) are right next to the restaurant side so you can stare longingly while you eat, but the sweet stuff is kept up high to be kid friendly! Try the Nagaraya, which is a "cracker nut" (peanuts covered in crunchy shells). I may or may not be crunching through a bag of them while I write this review...

The food is served what I refer to as cafeteria-style; most of it is pre-made and kept hot. You can see the dishes behind a glass panel and choose what you want. This style of serving works well for potentially unfamiliar foods because you can see what you're getting. A selection of bottled and canned drinks is available toward the front of the store. The owners and workers are super friendly and will happily explain all of that day's offerings to you and even recommend things you might want like. For the items served cafeteria-style, pricing is based on how many items you choose (1, 2, or 3, all served with rice). As a carbaholic, the pancit (noodles) is my absolute favorite. Nothing is terribly expensive, though, so I highly recommend trying something new; it will probably be delicious! Also ask about the lumpia (egg rolls), which are fried upon ordering in the back. All of the food I've tried has been delicious.

Although its a bit of a drive from Nashville proper, we seem to find ourselves returning here for the yummy food and the friendly owners. Whether this is your first time trying Filipino food or its an old favorite of yours, it is definitely worth the trip!
name: Kristen

text: Yum, yum! While visiting Nashville for a couple days, a friend and I checked out Whiskey Kitchen for Saturday brunch. There was just a short wait, nothing too bad. We ordered the brunch sangria the arugula salad, chimichanga and a hot chicken pizza. All were delicious! The chimichanga was perfectly crispy. The pizza was great, but not as spicy as I was expecting. That's my only complaint. Our server was attentive and friendly and the price wasn't bad for all the food we ordered. Definitely recommend!
name: Suzanne

text:
Excellent food ! My husband had the special fish and I had the plum glazed jumbo shrimp. Both dishes were amazing. The wine was 50% off, so we had a bottle of rosé for 15$. Laura, our waitress was extremely kind.
It was a great experience.
name: mylene

text: Always a lively crowd wether it be Latin night on Tuesday or The VIP lounge on a Friday night! You can always expect to find the party here at franklin manor..downtown has a winner !
name: Ray

text:
Our party of 10 stopped here for dinner around 6:30 on a Saturday a couple weekends ago. Considering the size of our party, we were seated right away. (We had called ahead; they said they don't take reservations but had a large table open, which we luckily claimed.)

Service was friendly but somewhat half-hearted...maybe our server was just tired. The food was OK. Their chips and salsa are delicious! Table-side guacamole was decent, albeit a bit chunky. I think it's a bit pricey, but the portion was generous. 

Entrees were served hot and tasted good for the most part, but just seemed boring, for lack of a better word. Everything was smothered with the same red sauce. The pepper itself in the Chile Relleno was soggy and bland. In hindsight I probably should have ordered something else.

Drinks were OK. The mango in my Mango Mojito tasted like artificial flavor (as opposed to fresh fruit purée), though it was not bad. We did not get dessert.

The experience overall was all right, just nothing special. It's your average American Tex-Mex chain that has an expansive menu for everyone, a laid-back atmosphere, and acceptable service. As long as you don't go in with high expectations, you'll enjoy your visit. Not in a rush to go back.
name: Mel

text: Stopped by this food truck during food truck Friday at idlewild Park. I was super excited because it was the mexican food with the longest line. However, when I was ready to pay, the cashier stated that they did not have change and I needed to use a credit card. Luckily, my credit card gives me alerts when a purchase is made and I noticed I was charged a 50 cent upcharge for using a credit card. When I asked the cashier, she was rude and argumentative but eventually gave me my 50 cents. Obviously this is a small amount, but it is the principle and the food was overpriced to begin with. Not to mention the food was sub-par, bland and extremely greasy. Even adding salsa did not improve the lack of flavor. I recommend one of the other trucks who have friendlier staff and more authentic, yummy mexican food.
name: Caroline

text: The food came out fast, which was good because we were starving. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. It looked better online than it did in person. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent.
name: User

text: I love this place. Honestly one of the best pizza places I've ever eaten at. Their sauce and flavors are really unique. Would definitely recommend.
name: Abdul

text: For a busy night they handled it okay. The food was good and the service was easygoing. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. Nice little spot, decent portions too. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text: Not your average Joe's did not live up to it's name. P. and I came for a late lunch and it was pretty empty likely due to the time of day. We were seated at a table far away from the bar and TVs, but it was nicely decorated and comfortable so that was fine. However it seems like in retrospect, this might be a better place for watching sports at the bar. One thing I noticed was that the table next to us had not been bussed and the leftovers of the previous diner's meal was left there for the entirety of the time we sat at our table and even when a table was seated on the other side of it. It was gross. I ordered the Tuscan chicken sandwich with a side of fries and my husband got the Mustard Chicken BLT. My sandwich was small and very bland and the fries that came with it tasted like they had been sitting under a heater all day. My husbands sandwich was also very bland, which is disappointing because the description made both sandwiches sound very flavorful and full of yummy ingredients. The food gave me a cafeteria vibe as the sandwiches seemed like they should have come in a plastic clam shell container, not a plate. To top things off, the service was extremely slow as the Eagles game was on and our waitress was distracted watching the game. Overall Not Your Average Joe's seems pretty average to below average to me.
name: Mandy

text:
Not the best pizza in the world, but far from the worst. The crust is pretty good - I'm one of those weirdos that doesn't actually eat the crust on pizza, because most of the time I find it just too bland and chewy. At Gianfranco, the crust is good enough that I eat the whole slice, if that tells you anything.

Can't say I've ever ordered a whole pie, but occasionally I pop in at lunch time and get a pretty cheap meal that fills me up. Lunch time is usually pretty busy, but the line seems to move steadily so it isn't too long of a wait. I've had a few of the flavors (chicken ranch always seems to be pretty popular with folks) but I think the tomato pie is my favorite. 

Solid lunch spot in Old City that fills you up and doesn't break the bank!
name: Emily

text: My mother got takeaway from here earlier. She got us the chimichangas and three tacos, 1 carnitas and two Al pastor. The salsa was weak, needed jalapeno and more lime juice. It was the blandest salsa I have ever had. The chimichanga was decent and not too small. The beans were bland and not mashed at all. The rice was just ok. The tacos were the best part and they are a good price. I'm hoping that they will improve, I'd really like some decent Mexican food near me.
name: Meggean

text: This place could get 5 stars. Food is very good. Meatballs were amazing. Inside it's very loud. We sat outside and they put us next to the heater. They did turn it down but it was very warm. They also have very uncomfortable chairs. Server seemed rushed.
name: Davud

text: For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. Will be back. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer..
name: User

text:
This was my first time hosting a LSU Dental mixer at Blue Crab. It was such a great experience! Ana DeCastro and Anna took such great care of us. The ambiance and service was top notch! The macaroni and cheese was to die for as well as the other hors d'oeuvres.  Thank you so much for accommodating our party and helping make it a success. I definitely will be hosting future events here.
Had another awesome event here. They always take such great care of us. Thank you Alison Asprodites for helping make this event a success!
name: Esther

text:
Pierogi!
Cabbage & Mushroom, Sourkraut, Sweet Cheese, Cherry, Blueberry, Strawberry, etc. Any pierogi you may crave. Bigots, Hunter's Stew, Cabbage Rolls, Golombki. Everything we have tried over The years is delicious homemade goodness!
name: Magda

text: Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Wouldn't really choose this place again. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Food was good and came out fast. Would probably stop in again if nearby. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean.
name: User

text: As I'd been promised by friends and other reviews, there was a line, even though it was off hours. However, the line moved quickly and was well managed. It's a noisy, energetic setting with a relatively simple menu. Even though I *hate* oysters I tried a chargrilled one and it was surprisingly good. Even better to my taste was the boom boom shrimp. Also tried the sampler which included a cup of gumbo (yum), red beans and rice (yum), grilled andouille sausage (yum), and jambalaya (which I didn't love - a little too dry and not flavorful enough for my taste). Ended up being a little pricey for what I got but satisfying for sure.
name: Duncan

text: Went here on October 5th for dinner with my wife and the experience was awful. Granted the place was busy but the service was slow and the food almost inedible. We ordered potato skins and a cajun chicken sandwich. The skins were dried out and disgusting from sitting under the heat lamp and the chicken didnt even fill up the bun and was like a piece of leather. Let the waitress no our displeasure and she had the manager take the skins off the bill and that was all. The manager couldnt wvwn show their face at the table. Will definitely never go nack to this dump.
name: Mark

text: This is a great restaurant to bring friends and family when they come from out of town because the music is always great. On the other hand, the service has always been lacking. Today I came in and Hollywood was our server and he was phenomenal.  Thanks Hollywood! Great job
name: Maria

text:
We love this place. We used to live in the area and moved a half hour away. We still come here. 
The food is fresh, tasty and the portions are generous. 
The service is fast and courteous. It's a family run business and is a prime example of what first generation legal immigrants can accomplish.
They are an asset to the community and their food is wonderful. 
We will continue to come here until we are too old to drive.
name: Ed

text: I almost skipped this place because of the ratings and that would've been unfair. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Not saying it's the best place ever, but it was totally fine. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. No big complaints, just a nice meal. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable.
name: User

text: Absolutely delicious! Such a warm and engaging staff and flavorful food. Come here for AUTHENTIC cuisine with a gorgeous atmosphere. Lots of vegetarian options, too!
name: Isabella

text:
This is such a great place to go and love the staff here!! The food is great and is priced extremely fair!! 

Usually here at least once a week and love it. The grits here are awesome as are the biscuits. It's a bit outta my way but entirely worth it!!
name: John

text: Found my new Taco Tuesday spot. $1 tacos and its not just ground beef like most places. You can get the good authentic tacos like barbacoa, chorizo, steak etc. and they do takeout. Food was extremely good. Only downside for me is a have to drive into greenwood but it was totally worth the drive.
name: Aaron

text: The soup was better than the sandwich, which I wasn't expecting. So yeah, the experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Anyway, delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. maybe I just came on an off day. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The sauces helped more than I thought they would..
name: User

text: The fries were probably the best part of the meal, honestly. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh.
name: User

text: Portion size looked small at first but it was actually enough. Anyway, not terrible, just not something i'd want again soon. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Also, we shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. Honestly, service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would..
name: User

text: Parking was annoying and I was already in a bad mood by the time I got inside. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. For the price I expected more than this. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait.
name: User

text: Best Carne Asada tacos I've had!  The Sonaran Dogs are also a must try.  Quick service, easy in and out for lunch.
name: Nathan

text: Love the atmosphere, food has been excellent every time that we have been there. Service is always on point. The main bar has plenty of room and multiple big screens to watch a game. The interior restaurant bar is more upscale looking but bartenders at all the bars seem equally able to make your favorite drinks.
name: Jeffrey

text: Stopped in for lunch today and had a side salad and half a sandwich. Everything pretty good, no complaints. Bartender friendly, everyone seemed to be having a good time. Still wish they would make their own iced tea instead of that stuff out of a soda machine dispenser. See you next time.
name: Food

text:
Ok but.. 
1. All the Meat is overly salted and crazy seasoned bleh
2. Flour tortillas are too thin
3 staff are snarky and slow 
4. Steak should be cut up in bits 
5. Burrito rice is overly seasoned

Bloatedness! No bueno.  Keep it simple and let the ingredients shine :) 

I thought SF owners started this place up??? It's not  like any taqueria I've been to in my 16yrs living in SF Proper.  

Small changes will make a huge difference
name: culinary

text: Nice atmosphere, dark with lots of wood. Negroni at bar was made perfectly. Shelby our waiter was unfriendly at first and seemed ticked off, she got warmer as time went on. Sour dough bread was really nice. The best part of the meal was lobster bisque -delicious! If we ever go back I would just order the bisque and and a salad because the rest of the meal was unremarkable. Someone screwed up our order and one person in our party had to wait for their entree to be remade while the rest of us ate. The restaurant to their credit comped her meal which they should have, but the situation did not help our overall impression of the place. A high end rum listed on their dessert menu was not available. One of the listed desserts was also not available??? Since we had early dinner reservations it is hard to believe they just ran out. Unless I am craving lobster bisque we will probably not go back.
name: Hitch

text: Have been here a few times. Meatball sub is great. Their pasta is great. Really good, well made food, for a decent price. You should definitely try this place. We want to support local folks who go the distance, to prepare fresh, good food for their customers. Highly Recommended!
name: Patti

text: Stopped by on a cold night to get hot chocolate, made it fresh right on the spot not from a container. Very rich!! Also everything at a glance looked and smelled amazing. Will have to be back to try!
name: J

text: I rarely leave reviews! I've been coming to this establishment for more than two years. Not only is it the best Japanese food and sushi but the drinks as well. Take my word for it and don't go to another sushi spot in St Pete.
name: Matthew

text: I'm a fan! I chose the masala paneer Kati roll. Paneer is cheese. There was a ton of cheese on my wrap. The kati wrap was really well done, it didn't break and wasn't chewy or tough. They made the wrap right away, there was almost no waiting and it was really cheap! I hate paying a ton for fancy Indian food because most of the time the recipes come from regions where the people who cook the recipes live on very little income. The tastes in this wrap were comparable to some of the best Indian food I've tried. I think this is a chain, if it is I haven't tried any other locations. They have seating inside and outside. It is a quick service restaurant where the employees are always behind the counter and you pick the food up from the counter. There is a case of bottled and canned drinks. The white sauce is not a garlic sauce, it tastes more like ranch, it did not fit on my sandwich, so I didn't use it. Overall I'll definitely be back when I'm craving Indian! I hope they're around for a long time!!
name: Schuyler

text:
Probably the worst reservation system known to man.  Its doesn't exist. You use Yelp and it tells you 60 min wait- when you arrive in 60 minutes you then you need to wait for and hour and a half additional.  YES.  2.5 HR WAIT.

UNACCEPTABLE.  Management needs to take actual reservations.  Restaurants in the world have done this for years. It works.  Try it!

Love to tell you about the food but I'm still waiting.  I've got 2.5 hours invested.  If they serve cardboard it will taste great right about now.
name: Mark

text:
Most authentic experience of tacos in the world
My family gives Tacodelphia 5 stars!!!!
name: Sam

text: For the price I expected a little more care. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. Kind of landed in the middle for me. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait.
name: User

text: Last week Rack City catered my company Christmas party and the food was amazing!! Alex arrived on time and brought more than enough food for the party. I waited until a week before the party to make the request and although they had a few big orders already, they were nice enough to fit me in and take the time to cook for us as well. The collared greens were the best we've ever had, ribs were amazing, pulled pork was supreme, and the BBQ sauce can not be beat! I rented the house and it was my first time in the area and ordered based on the other reviews on here. I can say that they deserve to be #1. Thank you so much Rack City! We appreciate your delicious food and delightful service!
name: Ton

text: I bought a pound of the king salmon for $12. It was delicious! Perfectly marbled and closely matches the fatty salmon ordered at sushi restaurants for $10 for 2 pieces of nigeri. This cut created enough meat for 2 full salmon rolls and 18 thick cuts of nigeri. I highly recommend this store for ALL of your raw fish needs!
name: David

text:
We needed a place close to the Kimmel Center and decided to give Fado a try for dinner.  The place itself has a nice feel with a gigantic wrap around bar almost the size of the place. There was a fairly big crowd by the time we left.

They have great selection of beer and a fairly good-sized menu.  The food, however, was not all that good.  The Avocado RLT (a play on a BLT) had little to no flavor.  The Shepherds Pie was also on the bland side.

So with 2 beers, before tip, the bill came to around $40.  Might stop in again for a drink but would definitely eat somewhere else.
name: Jim

text: This place is stupid good. I'm from Texas, and these are among the best ribs I've ever had. Very hard for a proud Texan to say. If you don't like this place there is something very wrong with you.
name: Jeremy

text: Parking was annoying and I was already in a bad mood by the time I got inside. Honestly, ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table.
name: User

text:
What a lovely Italian restaurant! I've been very impressed with the Italian scene in Philly recently, particularly around South Philly. I came here for a graduation party of four and they were able to accommodate an extra +1.

Food: Perfect portions and came SUPER fast. I wasn't very hungry so I ordered a prosciutto antipasti, which was plated very nicely and tasted delicious (good cuts and I really liked the vinaigrette, though a little heavy). My family ALL ordered the lobster spaghetti and they liked it. Everything was presented beautifully and I like how it wasn't a mountain of pasta per plate, as I find a lot of Italian places can overdo it on the portion sizes. 

Free bread: Five stars. Ugh it was so good. Fluffy and doughy, and I appreciated how they poured out olive oil with a flourish into a small condiment dish right after sliding the bread onto our table--because that is the only way bread should be consumed at an Italian place (plus salt and pepper).
name: Jenna

text:
First time review - we arrived at Hugh Baby's on a sunny Saturday afternoon to see what all the hubbub was about. Needless to say, we weren't disappointed. The restaurant itself is small, but open, if that makes sense - so it felt spacious. 

Anyway - service here is great. From the cashier who took our order (I suspect he may have been the manager since he was dressed in a button down, tie and slacks) to the wait staff who removed our tray after we were done and checked on us during our meal, everyone was friendly and attentive. 

Now - to the food. It was great!!! Fresh, served quickly, and the prices can't be beat, honestly. For a shake, two orders of fries and cheeseburgers and a soda, we spent just under $20. The fries are my new favorite. They remind me of fries I had once upon a time at City Island. The gentleman who took our order recommended the cheeseburgers, and it was good advice. They weren't too heavy, which I liked. But by the time I finished my fries and half my shake, I was good. The boo enjoyed his burger so much he seriously considered a second burger before I dragged him out, lol.

Definitely check this place out, for a good burger and a good price, and quick, friendly service.
name: Nabilah

text: So I'm having a great meal over in the corner because I didn't make a reservation.  I asked to revisit a restaurant that I had visited when they first opened about 14 years ago.  I'm from out of town it that that matters. But if your not busy don't sit those who show up in the corner. I'm a little bitter I didn't get the same respect that I got the first time around.  I won't ask my friend to being me again. But the food was great.
name: Chuck

text: Fine quality Chinese food.  The mother and son combo run the show.  The interior is outdated, old and dirty.  The food is worth it though.
name: Sam

text: Excellent food, they are always fresh and really know how to put cheese on a pizza. I've been eating here for years. Great people too. One time my debit wasn't working and they gave me the food on spot. Real good people here.
name: Jesse

text: After a rocky start, this place has become new favorite. Went for dinner on Friday. Seated promptly for 6 reservations. David , waiter, did a terrific job and the food was excellent. Paella and Jerked Chicken Pasta done just right and very good flavor. Try it you'll like it.
name: Ken

text: Food is fine but service is slow and they never have my mobile order ready on time. I'm always standing there waiting for them to make it which defeats the whole purpose. Just annoying
name: Jenna

text: Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. By the time the food came out I was already annoyed. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. For the price I expected more than this.
name: User

text: Didn't expect highly for food court but here gives me so much surprise. Ordered chatt dosa and Ahi bowl, really tasty and unique. Different from poke bowl I had at other places. Strong recommendation!
name: Yurie

text:
For this experience I am giving Sam's only a 2-star rating. In the past it has always been exceptional. Unfortunately, that was not the case last night. First off we had to park on the grass at the furthest point from the door due to the parking lot being 100% full. This surprised us being 6pm on a weeknight. 
We had reservations for 3 of us which included an 82 year old relative who we were treating to dinner for a special occasion. We stood in the doorway for 45 minutes before being seating. The bar was extremely crowded so that was not an option for our waiting period. Once we hit the 30-minute mark with no signs of a table opening up we started calling other steakhouses to see if we could get in somewhere else. 
We were finally seated in the bar area. It was extremely loud with the live entertainment. We could not carry on a conversation at our table. What an awkward situation.The food and service were excellent as always but that didn't make up for the rest of this disappointing experience. We realize it is the holiday season but perhaps they overbooked their reservations?
name: Judy

text:
Came here with my in-laws not long after I had had wisdom teeth surgery. So unfortunately, I didn't try any of the ice creams with mix-ins or anything like that. 

I did, however, try their strawberry banana smoothie and let me tell you, it was delicious. Just the right amount of strawberry and banana flavor and just what I needed for a sweet, cool treat. 

The staff was super nice and didn't even bat an eye when I asked for a spoon with my smoothie instead of a straw.
name: Marisa

text: I stopped by for lunch and it was perfect.  Started with a bowl of Hungarian Beef Cabbage soup then had a smoked turkey sandwich (lots of turkey!) on Kaiser with lettuce, tomato and mayo.  Excellent!  Everything is made fresh in-house, including a wide variety of desserts.  I'm definitely coming back!
name: Marc

text: This is a must have every time I'm in the Lou! They have THE BEST dim sum! Great for a sit down meal or carry out.
name: Stephanie

text:
I felt I owed it to this location to offer an updated review based on my most recent experience. The last time I ate at this particular location (almost a year ago) I had several complaints (see earlier review below). However, my wife and I dined here recently and everything was much better, back to my expectations of what a Red Robin should be like.
Service was super friendly and helpful.
Food was delicious--appetizer (wings on yukon chips), burgers, milkshake, bottomless fries...all really, really good!
Prices are fair for what you get and you can't beat the Royalty program (earning free burgers, free burgers on your Birthday, etc.).
Happy to view my previous experience as simply an off-night for the franchise. But...I still say you should be able to get fries when you first arrive!
name: D.

text: We waited 40 minutes for a table and it was well worth it. For a cocktail I chose the Bacon Bloody Mary and it was probably the best Bloody Mary I've ever tried. It was made with smoked vodka which complimented the bacon and tomato juice very well. We ordered the chicken and waffles, crab cake Benedict and red velvet pancakes. While everything was delicious, the red velvet pancakes set a new standard. They were extremely moist, fluffy and sweet. I will definitely be going back my next time in Philly.
name: Terry

text: We went here for the first time tonight and the food was amazingly good.  Swordfish: very good.  Red Drum: possibly the best fish I've had.  Muscles in spicy red sauce: I considered asking to take rest of the sauce home.   Even the house made deserts were a home run.   It's a little on the pricy side but worth every penny.  We'll definitely be back.
name: Jim

text: Nice space that works much better as a pub than it did as a medium to upscale restaurant. Service was decent but not great. The beer selection was good and it was served at the perfect temp. The food was below average. Burger was served with no condiments or veggies. Black & Blu burger was bun, meat, and blue cheese. Meat was pretty dry. We will try again and will update review if the experience is better.
name: Courtney

text: The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. Will be back. It looked better online than it did in person.
name: User

text: First, the parking situation is awful. Second, when I walked in I had to wait in a long line (35 minutes) for my meal. After waiting that long, I waited a ridiculous amount of time for my food to get here. Also, who else thinks it's crazy they don't bring food out to you? Rude. When i finally got my food, i was disturbed to find bugs in my salad. That is extremely insanitary and I will never come back here again. Also it is expensive. I must say, the McAlister's deli not too far down the road is a much better option than this establishment.
name: Cate

text: This place was awesome! Nice atmosphere along with great staff. The food was good, we had the el Americano and spinach/avocado egg Benedict, would recommend!!!
name: Elizabeth

text: The beer shop is average and unattended. You're required to help yourself with no offer for assistance. The deli is too narrow and offers average food. Parking is extraordinarily limited.
name: Dennis

text: The best chicken fried rice I've ever had, great portions. The wings were dynamite, double deep fried and not your BBW trash size wings these had meat for days on them. Lastly the customer service was awesome, which is hard to find in the dump hole city of philly.
name: Korey

text: The soup was better than the sandwich, which I wasn't expecting. So yeah, the portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. Honestly, ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. So yeah, we shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced.

text:
My wife and I visited Under The Moon Cafe in Bordentown for dinner.   We made 5:45 PM  reservations using Open Table, but when we arrived the hostess seemed concerned.  She asked if we used Open Table and said the reservation times weren't showing up correctly.  I'm not sure why we should be concerned about that but she seemed engrossed in the issue.   Then, when they seated us the bus-person told us we had the table until 7:00PM.   I never heard of this sort of time limit on a table and while we didn't expect to linger, this cast a negative vibe on the entire dinner.  

Our waitress was friendly but service was slow (again which was odd given the wacky time restriction on our table).

We ordered the empanadas and corn brûlée appetizers.  The empanadas were excellent and searingly hot out of the fryer.  Wear a napkin bib when cutting into these as they SHOT a beam of meaty fryer grease across the table when we cut into them.

The corn brûlée was very good.   It had the consistency of oatmeal but the corn was either frozen or canned.  It was decorated with a few roasted onions or plantains, we couldn't tell which.

For our main course, I had the Argentinian meatloaf and the wife had the filet mignon and beet salad special.   The meatloaf was massive and very tasty.   The bacon wrapper was a bit soggy and stringy but overall I would order this again.   The portion size was generous so I ended up taking half of it home.

The filet mignon salad was supposed to have slices of beef but instead we got a small, fatty slab of beef set on the side.   There was just a few bits of goat cheese in the salad but it was overall a decent salad.

The ambiance is great.   The tables, chairs, plates and flatware are all purposely mismatched and vintage.   The burlap wall covering helps mute the noise so its easy to have a conversation even when the restaurant is full.

We didn't partake in the desserts but they looked delicious.  Maybe next time.

Overall the food was very good (not excellent), the ambiance was great, and the service friendly but disorganized and the table limit thing was disappointing.   We heard the server give another couple a table limit and the guy strongly expressed his surprise and disappointment as well.

Hopefully they can address these issues and Under The Moon can flourish.

text:
A-meze-ing. 

This was the meal I didn't even know I was craving. But now that I do know about it, I'm going to be craving it a lot, or until I get it again... like, tomorrow. 

I wasn't even planning on stopping in here. I was walking from my hotel to the Locale Market down the street, but after reading "authentic middle eastern vegetarian with all natural ingredients," some supernatural power took over like a strong magnet pulling me in. 

And before I knew what happened, there I was at the bar counter browsing the menu for an overly long time before deciding what to take to go. It was hard to decide, but I felt confident with an order of Roasted Cauliflower with tahini ($8) and a Curried Vegetable Soup ($6 or $4 when added on to another item). Many other options sounded great too, but I wasn't super hungry and didn't want to over do it. 

While waiting for the order, the two staff at the bar chatted and were friendly to other patrons. I was amazed at how quickly it was ready. All packaged up and ready to go in just a few minutes. Added bonus - they sealed my soup container with extra plastic food wrap so not a drop spilled on my walk. 

It all looked awesome, stayed hot, and I couldn't wait to dive in. Woah guys, woah. It tasted even better than it looked. The cauliflower was roasted beautifully, soft but still some crunch, and so flavorful. The tahini sauce was some of the best I've ever had! Including my own recipe, not afraid to admit. And the soup. Perfection. Full of vegetables, chickpeas, potatoes, zucchini, onion, carrots, tomato - can I get that recipe, please? I could go for another bowl right now.

Is it too soon to be obsessed with this place? I will absolutely be back. I just don't know if I'll get this exact same meal or mix it up and try something else.

text:
When looking for some Thai delivery options, I came across AmeriThai and my boyfriend and I thought we'd give it a try.

Our order consisted of Crab Rangoons, Massaman Curry, and Crazy Noodles. It was delivered in an appropriate amount of time, but sadly, the packaging was a disaster! The curry and noodles were both delivered in disposable aluminum foil containers with white paper lids and were literally DRENCHED in oil and curry. It was such a mess! I don't think curries should be stored and delivered in this kind of packaging. 

As far as the food goes, I would rank it as follows: #1 Crab Rangoons, #2 Crazy Noodles, and #3 Massaman Curry. 

In my opinion, you can never really go wrong with rangoons, but these were probably some of the best I've ever had. They were fried perfectly! I loved how crispy they were. 

The Crazy Noodles came with broccoli, carrots, cabbage, onions, and mushrooms in a hot chili oil. They were good, but as I said above, drenched in oil. Way too much. 

The Massaman Curry was just alright. The vegetables in it were all fresh, but the curry was pretty flavorless. I tasted more coconut milk in it than any of the spice/seasonings. I wish it had a bit of a kick to it. Our protein of choice was pork and I did like how tender it was. 

Unfortunately, this place didn't really do it for me. Maybe their food tastes better fresh out of the kitchen than through delivery, but either way, there's other Thai restaurants I'd much rather choose than this one.

A resounding YES for Cafe Lift. My friends and I went to Cafe Lift at around 12PM on a Saturday with champagne bottles in tow for a BYO brunch. The wait was around 45 minutes and they don't take reservations, which I always find to be a huge bummer. There was also no outdoor seating...wait let me rephrase, there are tables outdoors but they do not seat outside. It was a beautiful day so this was another disappointment. However, everything else about our meal was absolutely perfect! 

I ordered the migas bowl and stone fruit French toast off of the specials menu. The migas bowls was incredible-eggs, black beans, chorizo, peppers and onions topped with queso, pico and avocado. This was probably one of the best Mexican egg based breakfasts I've ever had (I know that sounds like a specific category but a LOT of restaurants do a Mexican egg dish). The stone fruit French toast was another winner with various fruits, ricotta and a tahini syrup. It was an excellent rendition of a classic dish. The waitstaff was extremely attentive and kind. The restaurant itself is roomy and bright and a nice place for groups. Oh, and be sure to check out the nearby rail park. Definitely recommend Cafe Lift!

text:
Absolutely loved! I wasn't sure what to expect here since I had never heard of it before but it far exceeded my expectations.

We were out for a special occasion and all ordered the 4 course meal, which was complete overload. It included a cheese fondue, a salad, and entree fondue, and dessert fondue. By the end of the meal we were all groaning from being too full.

Each fondue has multiple options of flavors to choose from. You and your table have to decide on the same fondues though, since it is one pot in the middle that everyone will be sharing.

We ended up choosing the Wisconsin Trio cheese (if I remember correctly) which was served with apples, breads, and veggies. Next was an option of salad. After that was the entree where you pick three different meats to cook in the community broth. We chose the mojo cooking style. And for meats I chose shrimp, potstickers, and sausage (all highly recommend). Last and most delicious, the flaming turtle chocolate fondue. IT WAS AMAZING AND THE CANDIED PECANS WERE EVERYTHING.

Our server was great, very informative for us newbies. The restaurant wasn't that busy, which was surprising because it was national cheese fondue day! Because of this, we got a discount on our bill...woop woop.

The parking lot is shared with another restaurant and other businesses, we had to park wayyyyy far out in front of the furniture store because there were no spots near the restaurant.

Overall, incredible. It's not only great for a four course meal but if you want to just do the cheese or chocolate fondue, you can!

text:
Looking for a cute diner in the Fort Harrison area that serves breakfast all day? You've come to the right place at Cafe Audrey. With the majority of restaurants in the area being chain-style or fast food, it's refreshing to find a locally owned cafe.

Situated in one of the old train depots, the cafe offers American breakfast staples like scrambles, pancakes, and biscuits and gravy, as well as plenty of options for the lunch crowd like sandwiches, burgers, and salads.

I love that Audrey's supports a lot of locally-sources food like their bacon, coffee, and breads. Many of the menu items are made in-house too like the fluffy biscuits, tasty quiches (which change ingredients daily), and their delicious Brussels sprout slaw with apples and dried cranberries.

We tend to hit them up for breakfast, so I am partial to the cinnamon swirl pancakes!

Audrey's just recently acquired their wine and beer license too, so you can now enjoy a refreshing mimosa with your brunch or a beer with your lunch.

I love that the coffee is self-serve. Often the place gets busy quickly on weekends, so you can grab some java while you wait for a table. They rotate out a flavored coffee (my fave is the hot buttered rum flavor) every week plus their signature "Cafe Audrey" dark roast, and a rotating organic medium roast of some variety.

The staff are always friendly and helpful. We've become regulars here so they remember what my usual order is. Make sure to get a frequent diner card to earn a free meal after so many visits.

text: My family (a party of seven) went for dinner last night and it was one of the best hibachi experiences we've had in a long time! Elissa, our server, was absolutely fabulous and attentive. One of our party has a shellfish allergy (he ordered sushi as opposed to getting anything from the hibachi grill) and was well accommodated. We ordered a wide range of drinks (sake, beer, cocktails) and all were fabulous. The best part of the evening was being treated to a hibachi chef performance from Ichiban, who we found out after our meal is the head hibachi chef among all the Kobe locations--and it shows! He did all of the classic hibachi tricks, plus a few we had never seen. Everything he prepared was delicious, but I have to say I was most impressed with my simple teriyaki chicken. Ichiban cooked it low and slow on the grill (it was the last meat to be done) and by the time I tasted it, it was more than chicken. It was like some new meat meant to be better than chicken in every way. Flavorful, soft, and with a moist and delicious texture that was out of this world. As you can tell, I sincerely enjoyed it! I recommend requesting Ichiban if he is available!

text:
Down in the Tyrone area, not usually a place I venture, but it was our Geekly bi-weekly dinner.  

They have an AYCE offer for $22.99 that offers a slew of sushi, apps and hibachi alternatives that turns out to be a pretty decent offer if you like what they're serving, and our table sure as heck did. 

I'm not a sushi fan, so I stayed on the Hibachi side. I started my plate with the Edamame, Spring rolls and Tempura veg.  All were perfectly done, and I should have stopped there. That was more than enough food for me.  People all around me were talking about the New York Roll and the Miso Soup being delicious. 

My second course was 3 of the tempura shrimp. I wish I'd known that you get 2 shrimp with every order, so I ended up with 6 tempura shrimp, which was too much for me, so I panned that out to others at my table.  (You're not supposed to share, but everyone at the table was doing the AYCE, so we didn't see the problem and neither did our waiter)

The peppered tuna was ABSOLUTELY to die for. It's the best thing sushi style I've ever put in my mouth. Very steak-y, very yummmm. 

My last thing I ate was their Hibachi steak. This was perfect. The meat was not over done, it was well seasoned and perfectly tender.  Often hibachi meat is over done and dry. Not here. This I would have again and again. 

If it weren't so far away  ( and I see they have a closer location) I would go agan.

text: Have y'all ever had a person who might be 100 for 100 on Restaurant suggestions and if they were wrong you would be inclined to give them a pass immediately? I'm talking about the type of experience that would make a Vegetarian eat meat kind of experience, or at least that was the hype man's way of hyping up this Burger. Well this ain't that type of party. In fact when I see him I just might hit him in his throat for suggesting it. I am at a loss as to why any person in of all places, New Orleans, would find a need to wait in line for a Burger at Shake Shack! Ok, at best it was really just ok. The size of my Burger was less than the size of a 99 cent hamburger on most Menus. Now I know size isn't everything, ( Gigidy) but as  Randy Moss would say, "Comonmaaan". The Shake was better than the Burger to me. Change the name to, oh wait, Shake is in the name with no mention of it being a preferred Burger joint. (Y'all didn't see that coming huh)? I won't be in a rush to head back for a second chance. I'm afraid I might run into the person that suggested this spot and end up going home with a Misdemeanor Assault. I have to say though the service was excellent. If your looking for fantastic service, great Milk Shakes and mediocre Burgers, head on down to Shack Shack on Veterans Blvd in Metairie La. In fact head over to one near you because they are popping up all over the place. I predict that this is a trend like when people stood in line for an hour or so when 5 Guys hit the scene to be a Burger Bully. Now you can walk right up to the counter. The 3rd Star is for the service, in the event your wondering. Peace, with 2 fingers.

Paah, y'all!   The couple who own this delightful pie shop and eatery are relatively newly transplanted from Florida (Key West) to Boise and many of their yummy pies have a bit of "southern accent".  As in their wicked good Key Lime, butterscotch, Derby, pumpkin praline, peanut butter and banana cream pies.  Others, like blueberry crumble and apple and chocolate are perhaps less regional and every bit as delicious.

I'm a pie fanatic, my Yelp profile even lists home baked pie as one of the things I LOVE, so I was delighted to find Bridgette and Terrance McAbee's pie shop and eatery.  Eatery being the piece some folks may not know about. I didn't until I went in to find they also have savory food here too like quiche, homemade soups like butternut squash or green chile or lemon chicken orzo, creative sandwiches, shepherd's pies and chicken pot pies.

THE EATS & PRICES: If you think real pie comes from one of the grocery store bakeries or Costco, think again.  Boise Pie Company pies are the real deal using all fresh ingredients and scratch made.  I'm hard pressed to think of another retailer in the Boise area who specializes in home baked pies like these, both as whole pies and by the slice.  Prices vary based on the kind of pie, but I think they are roughly $4.00 - $4.50 / slice or about $18.00 / pie.  And a really great deal is any three slices of pie as sampler for only $11.00.

Scratch made savory eats are also so reasonably priced as in a bowl of homemade soup for only $5.00 or a special this week of cheddar chive biscuit 'sandwich' with pimiento cheese, jalapeño pineapple jam, smoked honey ham, and  arugula and served with a cup of soup for only $8.95.

THE WHOLE PIES:  feed six generously and are big enough to cut into eight pieces for more restrained eaters or to share with others sipping vino at a local winery.  (Apple pie is a good pairing with some wines.  I kid you not.  And strangers become friends eating pie and drinking wine together.)   But I'm thinking for my birthday this year, when calories don't apply, I might just eat an entire Key Lime pie all by myself.  You think I'm kidding.

THE SPACE:  is light and bright and sparkling clean with décor that is both crisp, seafoam green and vanilla white and licorice black combined walls and ceiling details, and rustic with a driftwood / barnwood look trim at the order counter.

THE DRILL: is order at the counter to wait to take out, or after ordering for eat in take a seat and they will deliver to your table.  Tthe shop has seating at both high tables and standard height tables.  

WERE I THE QUEEN:  I'd wave my scepter and bid them move to a location closer to my neighborhood in Eagle so I could pop in more often.  Then again, were that true, I'd need to start a Go Fund Me account for a larger size wardrobe.

THIS N THAT:

1) Location is a bit out of the way, next to CHF resale consignment store and LaZBoy furniture, but that has advantages too in that there is a parking lot with ample parking.

2) Accessibility is good with ADA parking in the lot and an access ramp alongside the stairs to this elevated location.  Standard height table seating available.  Ample floor space. 

3) I don't now if they have a loo, in neither visit was I in need of asking.

4) Closed Sunday and Monday.

text: My son ordered dinner for us from this restaurant through GrubHub at 10:30pm.  When he placed the order, he included the address, code to get in the door and the apartment number.  The delivery results said that the meal would be be delivered between 11:20pm and 11:40am and we were going to be back at the apartment by that time anyway.  At 11:10pm,  we received a call from the delivery driver that he was here with the food.  My son explained to him that we were not there, but that he could come in (with the code provided) and leave the food at the apartment door.  Over the course of the next 20 minutes, the driver called no less than 4 times and the instructions were repeated.  We arrived at the apartment by 11:20pm and the food was not there.  My son called GrubHub and had the driver return with the food... it was midnight before it arrived.  By the time it arrived, it was cold.  When we called GrubHub to complain, the person on the phone was amazing and she called the restaurant.  She said that they gave her a hard time stating that we gave him the wrong address and would not give a credit at all for the cold food that was initially delivered early... then delivered late.  He blamed the entire issue on us and refused to credit us at all.  I would not recommend ordering anything from them if this is the kind of service that they provide.

text:
I've never eaten Cajun food before, so my opinion is likely to carry little truck with people from Cajun country.   However, I liked the place!

We arrived around 11:30 a.m. on Sunday.  It was packed out and we had to wait for about 15 minutes to get a table.

My Jambalaya was full of flavor!  Spicy hot that made my brow quite warm.  Everyone else finished their tame breakfasts and watched me savor the last bites of my Jambalaya.  My only complaint with the Jambalaya is that they put MSG in it.  I know this from the "dry mouth" that later comes after the meal.  Shame! Shame! Shame! Cajun Kitchen Cafe!  While a small sin, why do that sort of thing when your food is so good?  I'll certainly come back for that Jambalaya and say, "No MSG" to see if that works.

Most cafes like this one have crappy coffee.  I took a taste of Sofie's coffee.  Solid!  Very solid.  I ordered a cup of my own.  You should to.  They have great coffee.

These people work very hard and do an excellent job of making good food.  I love going to a restaurant and seeing everyone hustling like a team to make everyone happy.  Want to see what a well oiled machine looks like going at full throttle?  Visit Cajun at rush hour.
name: Steve

text:
We have tried several different all-you-can-eat sushi places in Central Indiana, and I honestly have to say that this place is my favorite. I much prefer the cream cheese/deep fried/spicy sauce rolls and assorted appetizers, while the hubs, C, likes more raw fish-centric rolls and sashimi, and we were both blown away! Our daughters G (10) and E (6) are big sushi fans and they loved it all, too! 

When you go in, they'll ask if you are there for "all you can eat". Just say yes. You won't be disappointed. They'll hand you a few different laminated menus and a dry erase marker. There is a menu for appetizers/non-sushi fare, plus, separate menus for rolls featuring raw fish and rolls that are fully cooked. I tend to gravitate to the cooked rolls and the appetizers and so that's what I picked up first. At AYCE sushi places, I like to order some of the same dishes the first time so I can compare them. I went for the crab stick salad, shumai, and crab Rangoon, first. The sauces served with the shumai and crab Rangoon were the highlights of those dishes. They were like regular sauces (gyoza-type sauce and a sweet and sour chili-type sauce), but they put extra seasonings in them and it made all the difference. Next, the crab stick salad was not the normal spicy mayo drenched salad I was used to. Was it creamy? A little. Was it spicy? A bit. Did they add mango for some reason? They sure did. But it the perfect dish I didn't know I needed. It served a palette-cleansing purpose and helped my stomach prepare for the obscene amount of food I was about to eat. I actually had the crab stick salad twice in my meal - at the beginning, and in the middle when I was starting to feel full. C and the girls had some sushi pizza, fried rice, and raw fish appetizers and they all gave a thumbs up because they were still shoveling food in their mouths at this point. 

Next up were the rolls. And, honey, this is why we were here. I have an intolerance to avocado and a lot of the rolls that I wanted to try had avocado. I always worry that they'll leave the avocado in, but they were really attentive to my needs - they actually put a note on the menu to let the server know if you have any food allergies. C got a few of the raw rolls - the crazy mango roll was one of his favorites. I actually tried a bite of this one. I don't usually like raw fish (shocking!) but HOLY COW, guys. It was SO GOOD. I want to try more raw fish from sushi club, now. I mostly stuck with the cooked rolls. I loved the W 10th roll and the Stop 11 roll. So amazing. We tried so many that I can't even be sure which ones we had. There wasn't a bad one in the bunch. It was all just so wonderful and I was that my stomach could expand to fit everything I wanted to try. G mostly ate what I ate and E mostly ate what C ate. They were big fans from the start.

I especially liked that they had pictures of the rolls on the back of their menus so you could see what they looked like, instead of trying to decipher the menu - which can sometimes be slightly confusing. 

THE ONLY NEGATIVE THING I HAVE TO SAY IS THIS: I wish that their green salad have a creamy ginger dressing. It was a vinegar ginger dressing. I love vinegar. I love ginger dressing. I love green salad. I did not love this. Maybe it was because I love the creamy ginger dressing that I have had at a few other sushi places and it was just so different. Maybe it was because I wasn't expecting the vinegar taste. Maybe the dressing was bad. I don't know. 

TL;DR 
Go here. You won't be disappointed.
name: L.K.

There are even peas, carrots and corn (and not those nasty baby corns from cans that other places throw in as filler). The broth was flavorful - you really could taste the signature Star Anise that should be in Pho broth.   I will definitely be back here for more!
name: Kerry

text: I went here with my mom for an early dinner. The atmosphere was nice. There were TVs everywhere with every sporting event on. We sat by the windows. Joshua was our server and he did an excellent job. He was attentive with our drink refills and assessing our needs. Our food came out quick and everything tasted great.

text: I go all the time!!! It's worth the wait. The food is always good wether it's sushi, ramen, jfc, or Brussels! This is one of my favorite places to go (friends, family, date night). text:
This place is one of the better dim sum places i had and the prices are super reasonable. If you go with a lot of people, you can eat a lot and still end up only paying 10-15 dollars (unless you're me than... you'll pay a lot more).

The wait in this place gets nuts if you come on a Sunday which is when i like to come with friends. It is mayhem and you need to fight your way to the lady with the ticket to get you seated. 

Once you are seated; the carts start rolling. They have all the basics from shumai to chicken feet. The one thing (and yes... you need to be persistent) you must get is pineapple pork buns. Holy moly... sweet fried bun on the outside while the inside has a moist, savory pork. It took me at least 4 visits to the place and constant haggling to get it. 

If you are a fan of dim sum, this place is a great spot to go to

text: Ordered takeout from Ginger Thai. While the prices were very reasonable the pad see ew lacked any flavor so I would recommend requesting additional spice! I would be interested to try other dishes!

text: Burger 21 is our go to burger place. The wide variety of burgers is what makes them so good. Their new spud burger is the bomb. Also look for their burger of the month. One suggestion is if you order fries is to order with no salt. They have a tendency to over salt their fries. Just salt them yourself and enjoy them with one of their many yummy sauces.

text: customer service was sublime, pizza was also super good! thank you papa murphy's for the delicious pizza!

text:
We really enjoyed our Friday night meal at Bud and Marilyns. We arrived about an hour early for our 630pm rez and were eating promptly. Ample table seating to the left behind the hostess station, two bars along the right side of the building with the kitchen in the back and a small wall separating the dining from the bar area. 

We were seated at a two too that was raised slightly off the ground so our feet dangled. There was a foot rest but it wasn't the most comfortable. That was my only gripe.

Our server was knowledgeable and attentive. Unfortunately, we could not get the bucket o' chicken nor French fries. Those were lunch items. Instead of opting for the restaurant week menu we went with the traditional menu. Marilyns chicken and Nashville hot chicken Sandy's. 

My friend chicken was crisp on the outside and moist/tender on the inside. It came with two hardy biscuits, pickles and homemade hot sauce. I would order that bird again. But the Nashville Sandy's stole the show. A perfectly toasted and seasoned roll with a juicy bird in between. In hindsight, we should of ordered about ten of those. Keep in mind they are very small-about two bites each. 

They have a solid happy hour menu for food. You should definitely visit them at least once!
name: Michael

text:
We went in to order for pickup and we ended up waiting about 35 minutes for 2 poke bowls and a sashimi/sushi platter. We were upset but we figured it would be worth the wait. 
It wasn't.
We received our poke bowls with the smallest amount of tofu and fish I have ever seen. There was barely any toppings and the whole bowl was about 4/5 rice. I could barely taste the honey wasabi sauce and there wasn't much flavor to anything else. I am very disappointed that I just spent $11 on a poorly made bowl and even tipped. 
I will not be going there again.

text: It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Price felt a touch high for what it was. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. text: I was looking forward to going to Thai Place Restaurant for a couple of weeks & was finally able to go yesterday.  While the food was good, the service was not.  I had gotten there a few minutes before my friend & brought a bottle of wine.  When my friend arrived, no one came to ask if we wanted the bottle opened or if we needed anything.  I had to ask for the waitress to come over to open the bottle.  Once we placed our order, we were never asked if we needed anything or needed our water glasses filled.  We had to ask for everything multiple times.  Bad service does not equate to good food.  Please work in customer service & wait staff should not do a complete belly stretch out in the open.  It makes it seem like you do not want to be there or for customers to be there.

text:
On our last day in Boise, we stopped at the High Note for lunch. Our friends had their dog with them, so we were looking for a place that was dog-friendly. Luckily, High Note has an outdoor seating area where we were allowed to bring the dog.

Unfortunately, even though High Note does have umbrellas over each of their tables outside, the umbrellas proved to be relatively ineffective at shielding us from the heat. It didn't help that this place was absolutely packed at lunch time and they only had two employees working. We had to wait a while for our food, so if you are looking for a quick lunch in downtown Boise, this is not the place for you.

Once we finally did receive our food though, I think it was worth the wait. I ordered the Reuben sandwich with a side of salmon chowder. The corned beef was thick and salty. It was perfectly complemented by the creamy Russian dressing. The bread was nicely toasted as well. They opted for red cabbage instead of the traditional sauerkraut, but the sandwich still had plenty of flavor. The salmon chowder looked a little watery, but was surprisingly very tasty. It had plenty of salmon and chunks of potatoes. 

High Note has pretty slow service for a downtown sandwich spot (especially for a week day), but the food tastes great and is filling. If you have time for a leisurely lunch, this place is worth checking out.
name: Ravi

text: The sauce carried most of the meal. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. Kind of landed in the middle for me. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. text: The price is right, and so are the blueberry oatmeal pancakes! Pinky's is a personal and local favorite. A stable in South Tampa, it offers the usual brunch food plus incredible rotating specials, so you're sure to find something for everyone. It can get packed during the early brunch hours, but the food never disappoints. If you're showing someone the oldie-but-goodie spots around Tampa, make a stop at Pinky's! Also, they have a fun mini-gift shop/nook to peruse while you wait for your food, and their self-serve coffee station features private blends for a unique cup of caffeine. What can I say - the service, food, and experience is always on point (except one single time when I brought my family from out of town and the waitress wasn't very nice - Murphy's Law!). Other than that single instance, I've never had a bad time (and there have been a lot of times). Thanks, Pinky's!

text: So delicious!!! Hands down one of the best and LEGIT Mexican restaurants in St. Louis. I'm half Mexican and have been struggling to find good places that are authentic since I moved here & this is it! Great environment, very friendly staff (she made my boyfriend practice his Spanish), delicious Horchata & delicious handmade gorditas! The salsa is just as amazing. Will be coming back for more!!

text:
Definitely becoming one of our favorite restaurants!

We ate here around Christmas and made a reservation. We arrived early so we went to the bar and realized it was happy hour. From 5-7 they do $3 drafts and 4$ house wines, the selection is great, and the $4,5,6 apps are amazing! We were able to order a few apps before dinner at the bar, and then we went to sit at our table. The dinner was good, and we each ordered an old-fashioned with dinner. Delicious!

We went to TT this past weekend and grabbed seats at the bar for HH and we're blown away again by the pricing and quality of the apps. The crawfish mac & cheese is delicious, and we also ordered the pork empanadas, chicken sandwich and mussels. All very good. 

The staff is helpful and were quick to clear plates, and the bartenders provided really awesome recommendations for drinks, including recommending a bourbon for us for an old fashioned (jefferson). The atmosphere is casual but has really nice vibes, and it is in such a great convenient location. We will definitely be back!

text:
Me, my best friend, and my oldest son all had brunch from French Press Coffee House - Airline Hwy. Saturday afternoon before my wedding. We all had nausea. My son threw up quickly, and was okayish,  but remained queasy the rest of the day, and all day Sunday. My best friend (who was also my MoH) got viciously sick, stayed sick throughout the entire ceremony, and had to leave before the reception started. She was STILL not feeling 100% today. As for me, I was super nauseated, which I initially attributed to nerves, but I've been sick ALL night last night, and ALL day today, which makes sense for food poisoning since I absorb food much more slowly than others, due to gastric resectioning I had 4 years ago.
So basically, French Press ruined parts of our wedding and honeymoon that we'll never get back. Nevermind that the food cost nearly $50 for coffees and the sandwiches. I'm rather pissed off at the memories we didn't get thanks to this food making us ill. So yeah, be careful if you order sandwiches from this place, ESPECIALLY if you order through WaitrApp...

text: I took my bride out to a Valentine's Day lunch at this Red Lobster today. The experience started off very rough but our waitress, Cierra C. saved the day. We were greeted as we entered by a gentleman (manager?) and two younger hostesses? The gentleman informed one of the ladies to take us to table 63? She then took off in the direction of the restaurant area and looked over her shoulder and said "Follow Me." It was not what she said but the tone that she used. In 20+years in the military I have rarely heard that tone used for anything other than a DIRECT ORDER. I would have preferred that she used the word please in that directive and wish that she had slowed her pace. My wife had recent knee replacement surgery and it was a challenge for us to keep up. When we caught up with her at the booth (seemingly as far from the entrance as possible) we were once again ordered to "Sit here." I was expressing my displeasure concerning this matter when Cierra C., our waitress arrived. She asked what seemed to be the matter and I told her that I was not used to being ordered around in a restaurant and we were contemplating departing without ordering. She saved the day by asking me very calmly and professionally if she could Please take our drink order. Her manner and astuteness saved the day for Red Lobster and for us. My wife had a margarita and I had a double Chivas Regal on the rocks for drinks. My wife's tilapia tacos and my shrimp scampi were perfect for lunch. The food was very tasty, the waitress was very attentive, and our bill was correct. I was going to say something concerning the way we were seated upon our departure; however, both my wife and I went to the restrooms first. I usually am done prior to my wife and was going to use that time to speak with the manager. However, when I left the restroom, I discovered my wife had not gone to the restroom. She informed me that she just wanted out of the restaurant. Once outside, she informed me that the restroom had the very distinct smell of a dead animal. She had mentioned it to one of the hostesses who had then ran into the ladies' room with a perfumed spray. Please note that the food, drinks, and service were all very good. However, the way we were seated, and the condition of the restroom resulted in a not overly good Valentine's Day lunch. This location can and should do much better.
name: Robert

text:
You would think having an open kitchen would promote proper food handling. This evening I witnessed a young man wipe his nose with the back of his glove three times, another employee wipe his mouth with his glove and several employees pushing their glasses up with their gloves and all of them continued making Pizza's and grabbing topping without changing their gloves.

 I spoke up and told one employee you can't wipe your nose and continue making pizzas without changing your gloves. I also told the manager and she said she would take care of it but obviously the employees haven't been properly trained in food safety and she isn't watching and correcting this kind of behavior.
name: Kari

text:
Mr and Mrs Crab is a legit cajun style seafood boil restaurant. 

I judge these types of restaurants on the type of seafood offered, freshness of the seafood, quality/flavor of the sauce, and spice level.  Mr and Mrs Crab did not disappoint.  

The menu is fairly extensive and in line with what I've seen at other boil restaurants.  I like that the items are offerred in half lb vs a full pound portions.  I opted for snow crab legs and clams.  The seafood was cooked perfectly.  Shells had the right snap to them and all of my clams properly opened.  I also like that they offer to types of clams...Manilla and white clams.  The corn and potatoes were also cooked perfectly.  The sauce was the right consistency and spice level. 

The food came out quick and the service was really good!

Definitely check it out!
name: Jamie

The employees forgot multiple parts of my order and gave me rushed replacements of what they forgot. In my onion strings there were mysterious bits of material, the corn pudding was sour, and all the meat was dry, poorly cooked. text:
So this is the legendary burger joint I've been hearing about....
Great looking place, and the business was packed with people..
That's a sign of something enjoyable inside..
Plenty of burger options.. They even had a black bean burger, which I passed on... Not that I don't like them. I just wanted to see what the hype was about with their beef burger.. 
Several choices of fries and hot dogs available.. My daughter chose the hot dog.. 
The service was pretty quick, and the meals were prepared within 10 minutes.. I thought that was great, considering how many people were there ahead of me..
The burger was made very well... I chose a plain Cheeseburger with LTO.. a really good burger can be enjoyed prepared simple.. The fries, they could've kept.. Nothing special. Just bagged, frozen, crinkle cut fries that could be made at home.. My daughter's hot dog was split and griddled.. She wasn't impressed!! but she gets the 10 year old exemption...lol
Overall, I'd say that I would come back.. But just for a plain burger and lemonade (free refills).. But not to break the bank enjoying everything on the menu...
name: Tim

text: Hoagie, Cheese steak, onion rings...all excellent tasting and well prepared/packaged for carry out. The service is A1 also. Always a good feeling to spend your money somewhere you feel invest in the people side and not just a food factory.
name: Onaje

text:
So much fun! This place was awesome!
I really enjoyed the music playing and clips of Johnny throughout. 
The place was staffed with friendly people who seemed genuinely happy to be there. There is a cafe that had coffee, water, and snacks. 
The gift shop is a bit pricey but priced as expected. The merchandise was fun and definitely sure to make any Johnny cash fan happy. 
The displays were well thought out with lots of handwritten notes and articles from Johnny Cash. 
My favorite item was a velvet heart he wrote on for June Carter. I am a sucker for reading about love stories - this display will not disappoint you if that appeals to you. 
His Military gear is also displayed- there are a lot of crazy facts about Johnny Cash I never knew and you don't get from the movie. If In Nashville - go
name: Elizabeth

text:
So it's been awhile since I was here last. 
First thing was a help wanted sign on the door so I know it's going to be another crappy service.

Came in, wasn't greeted right away as the guy took a call and so we waited to be sat. Then after several minutes the guy said have a seat no need to wait. ( there should be a sign ) He said take this paper and write your order. 

Sat down write our order. Turned in the slip. They came back to us to verify our requests to omit bell peppers on the kids food choices. The man sighed as it was an inconvenience to him.

There was no cutlery on the table at all or napkins.

They brought out one plate of our 5 and the spring roll appetizer. They forgot my husbands food and so he sat without his food the whole time! He insisted we eat and we were finished by the time we saw someone to bring it to their attention. So here we sit waiting for his food and decided to walk out without it. 

The women are kind. 
I understand they are short handed.
The food is ok but not outstanding to have to deal with EXTREMELY SLOW SERVICE! Total disregard for customer service. 

The building has rain stains on the ceiling and the place could be invested into but like I said the food is good and vegan food is hard to find.

Overall I'll give 3 stars for the food. I won't be back and I won't recommend it. I've told so many people not to come here and I should have known better.
name: Tracey

text: Hidden gem!!! This is definitely one of my favorite spots in Tampa. Food is consistently fresh and packed with flavor! I've caught myself having lunch here three days in a row. My go to is the Venezuelan pita with chicken shawarma. They have different fresh soups every day and they are always amazing. Staff is super friendly and the restaurant is always spotless. If you haven't tried this place you are seriously missing out!

text: Have come here for lunch and enjoyed it.  But came for dinner on a Wednesday night and wow what a difference.   They're closed Monday and Tuesday- and it felt like the food was the leftovers from the weekend and not fresh.  The pate plate was suspect, especially the low country pate.  The duck confit pate was dry and flavorless. The short rib entree was a nasty shade of grey, it seemed microwaved and was not pleasant.  Service was spotty at best.  Maybe it was an off night based on the other reviews and the previous lunch we had which was wonderful.

text: Billy is so full of energy! If you love a good happy energetic and funny bartendress with a big infectious smile... this place is the spot for you! The drinks are amazing, prices are great but she really makes this place a gem! Thank you for making our day!!

text: The best breakfast spot in the city for sure. You definitely get the most bang for your buck! The staff & environment is very welcoming! I would pay a visit on my next trip for sure! pancakes are soooooo good!

text: Best lunch buffet and so affordable , comes with a free drink! Wished I lived in Nashville so I could come here more often . The owner was hilarious.

text: Dessert saved this a little. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. I wouldn't write it off, but I also wouldn't hype it up. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. For the price I expected more than this. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really.

text: Truffle fries are exceptional! They also have such a great burger that satisfies all cravings! Yumminess: 10/10    Instagrammability:   10/10   Ambiance: quick and casual!

text: Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. By the time the food came out I was already annoyed. Maybe other people have better luck here. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon.
name: User

text: This place was off the beaten path a bit, and once you get there, it's helpful to know that the restaurant is at the back of the 700 Club bar (there is some writing on the front door stating this, but it was smudged when we got there). My husband and I both had the catfish sandwich, and we really enjoyed it. The fish was cooked well without being too greasy, and the coleslaw on the sandwich had a nice flavor. I took off one star because I wish they had a better bun for the sandwich. It seemed like a very generic, store-bought bun, and some good bread would have really made the sandwich great. But everything else about it was good.

text: What an amazing place, been there twice and i love their food everything is so delicious, was fast enough to get on my work break, prices are ok. But food super delicious!!!

text:
Hands down! One of my favorite taco places in the city. My favorite is the fish taco and the pork.
My suggestion is to go with a friend and order all the tacos and share them. It's perfect! 
Don't forget the ranch water. It's basically a margarita with topo chico, but still yummy!
