I hear one of your line cooks say he has a problem with the order because there was shrimp in the order and he asked if the lady taking orders let me know I would have to wait for shrimp.... well I was notified for that while waiting for our food..... go back out side one of you lady's is asking us if we need any trash taken away.... yet I haven't gotten my food yet so I'm still eating my chips and Queso.... they bring us our food and everything was cold the corn tortillas weren't the slightest bit warm my tacos my shrimp was cold the fried chicken was cold ..... went back in to return our food and we were told it was that way because we came in late...... I frequently go here at least once a week..... it was not what we were expecting at all we asked for our money back and left ...... we will be back that just sucked!
name: Chris

text: Fast, friendly. I was impressed with my experience. They definitely have the prices down. The woman at the front was doing to cash registers at the same time.
name: Cassandra

text: Always open late and always has the best pizza. If you're ever craving some pizza in DTSP, this is the place to GO!
name: Norvina

text:
I love this place.

I live a couple blocks away and come here every opportunity I get. all of their menu items that i've tried have been delicious - especially their sandwich offerings. The chicken and pork bahn mi are EXCELLENT. SO flavorful and juicy. You can get a small or a large - the small is filling enough for one meal especially with a side of fries. The french fries are seasoned and nice and crispy on the outside. They are great fries.

My go-to has been the chicken cheesesteak (with everything on it). It's better than any cheesesteak I've had in this city so far. The bread used for these sandwiches is to die for. Soft, with a lightly crunchy exterior. Perfect for absorbing all the flavors of these delicious sandwiches. 

You can tell this establishment uses fresh and high quality ingredients, because it makes a huge difference in taste.

The owner is almost always there and he is almost always cooking the food himself in the back. He's a very friendly guy, serving it up with a smile.

The bubble tea is also great and there is a decent selection.

The menu prices are very reasonable as the portions are generous.

I hope this place does well, they really deserve it.
name: Steph

text:
I wanted to like this food because the atmosphere is awesome and the space is so so pretty. It's really open because it's on the second floor and the sunlight makes the outdoor plants thrive. But the food was only okay.

I got the lunch special that comes with your choice of a soup, an agua fresca, and lunch-sized tacos. I got the tortilla soup, horchata, and tacos al pastor. The soup was surprisingly rich and I was really happy there was enough salt because I run into that issue so often in tomato-based soups. There's also chicken, so be aware if you're plant-based, but it was really tender and maybe was a little overcooked. 

The horchata was a bit too sweet, but at least the flavor was there. The tacos really kind of burned me up. I didn't mind that they used a different cut of pork than what is typical with pastor, but it didn't really taste like it was marinated and most of the flavor was on top, so some bites really didn't taste like much of anything.

I suppose if you're not a taco snob accustomed to the greasy spoons of the tri-state area, it's a decent spot, but I would probably avoid the pastor tacos.
name: Jada

text:
I really hope this restaurant does well in this location. This location has had trouble keeping a business but I think these ladies have the right recipe for success. 

First, they have an SBHS lunch special that looks delicious and affordable for the high school kids. I've ALWAYS said that whatever restaurant that's gonna make it there HAS TO HAVE A a great deal for the kids. That will be their bread and butter. 

Next, this menu is incredible!! Excellent dishes, fresh and unique ingredients; it's a perfect recipe! Santa Barbara is going to love this spot. 

We thought we'd go with classic favs this first visit. A classic hamburger with fries and a meatball sammie. This meatball sammie was incredible. We LOVED the marinara. HUGE sammie!! The burger came with cheese and bacon and spicy bread and butter pickles. I normally hate bread and butter pickles but these tasted house made and we fantastic!! This was an excellent hamburger. 

Finally, THE PATIO!! Every restaurant in SB needs an amazing patio!! Why else do we live in SB?!?  

However, I knocked one star off because the trendy industrial chairs they have exclusively on the patio are SO uncomfortable if you have ANY type of junk in your trunk (like me)! I had hoped to dine on the patio but opted to walk home and eat at home because I just can not with these terrible chairs. 10 minutes and I'm done. Bossie's, if you get better patio chairs, gimme a call and we'll find our way back to order our meals and a bottle of Rosé!!

I also thought the deviled eggs in the display case, while beautifully plated, had clearly been sitting there past their prime. Maybe a refrigerated display see would help, or placing non-refrigerated items in the display case would be better.
name: Abbey

text: Literally the worst food I have had in Philadelphia. So boring, bland and tasteless! Ambience was nice and the drinks were good - they managed to get my Sangria right so giving a star for that but this place deserves 2 stars at best. Penne Alla Vodka was okay and there was a Pizza - not worth remembering - which was ridiculous! I could make a better pizza and I am not even a good cook! Zucchini fritters were super oily and tasteless - lacking even in salt. The antipasti plate was rubbish ugh! I have never had such bad Italian food in Philly. Not recommended!
name: Komal

text:
You can never predict what you're going to get from an unknown microbrew. Space looked cool upon entrance, but not impressed. It was a somewhat cooler evening in Philly, slight breeze and not humid. It was so hot and humid inside the restaurant that it made eating and drinking nearly impossible. We were also seated in the very back where there was zero air circulation. Stepping outside was refreshing. 

The beer was served warm and flat. I know that some are meant to be served at warmer temperatures, but this was not that situation. My friend ordered a second round, same beer, but the beer she received was not the same beer. 

As far as the food - I had the Old City - a deep fried hot dog wrapped in bacon. The bacon was under cooked, I had to pull that off. I did like the pretzel roll though, tasted homemade. But again, it was so hot that I couldn't finish my meal.
name: Hannah

text:
Oh what an adventure you can have at IKEA! When you first enter this ginormous store they have carts for your toddler and a check in area for your older children (height requirement noted on the wall).
The food in the little cafe is cheap and tasty. My kids love having lunch here as it is very child friendly. 
The store can be super overwhelming, especially on the weekend when it's full of people and the lines are long. But today, much like other week days we had a great time exploring room to room and playing in the children's department. Even the lines at check out were quick! 
Our favorite items to purchase here are small furniture items (big ones are too complicated for me), kitchen utensils, home decor and rugs (especially for the play room since they must be replaced frequently). Oh and don't forget to grab a delicious chocolate bar with hazelnuts!!!
name: Megan

text: This was our first time here but not our last. Everything we ordered was terrific. Even the coffee was really good. I had an omelette with bacon, sausage, onions and peppers that was outstanding. The Bellinis and mimosas we're a nice touch. I highly recommend this place for an excellent Sunday brunch.
name: Ron

text:
I had my first visit to Oggi during Yelp Restaurant Week. For some reason my expectations were not high. I think perhaps because all they do is pasta, sausage and chicken with one shellfish entree. I do not eat a lot of pasta,  rarely order chicken out and I do not eat pork.  Boy, was I surprised in every way. First, I loved the atmosphere. The restaurant is very casual in a warm comfortable way.  The lighting was just right. Not to light, not to dark.  The weather was perfect, so they had the doors open leading out to the front patio. The place was bustling with activity.  I'm  liking what I see and feel.

Our server greeted us and got us going with some red wine! Thank you and keep them coming. Placed on the table is a small antipasto plate for sharing. I ordered the pistachio crusted cutlets. Also ordered was a half chicken (their specialty prepared in several ways) and the mussels. All meals come with a salad which is simple and amazingly good. I almost went with the mussels because I love them. I made an assumption they would be mixed with pasta. I was wrong. Out walked a mound of them  and they were fabulous!! The half chicken was delicious and it was huge. My entree was one lonely tiny cutlet covered in a beautiful bright green sauce. I happened to be disappointed and had no interest in eating my meal. In fact, I only took one bite. As wonderful as our server was, he picked up my plate without a word. 

Normally do not order dessert. I split the roasted pineapple with my friend which was to die for. My other friend had the cannoli which was a hit. 

Although I did not enjoy my meal everything else was spot on and I will most certainly return. I did call the mgr/owner who was a doll. I expected nothing as I just ordered the wrong dish for me. I told her she won us over as repeat customers. She still said she wants me to have a roasted chicken on the house. I hope to raise this to 5 stars after my next visit.

Oh gang, my phone is in my purse when I'm with others. It was after dinner I even thought of pictures. Trying to get better about that.
name: Susan

text: Had a yummy meal here for a reasonable price. Shrimp Po'boy sandwich was filled with shrimp and came with a spicy pickle.....yummmmm. Also had the avocado & grapefruit salad that was refreshing and light.
name: Nat

text: Possibly the best Mexican food I've ever had. I was searching for a restaurant with my son for lunch after visiting the city museum and was incredibly impressed with the staff and the service.
name: Kelly

text:
Someone at work recommended this place to me and I ordered the 8 ounce monger. I had grilled mushrooms, grilled onions, jalapeños and pickles on it with American cheese. The burger was really tasty but lacking in mushrooms problem was and I guess I should've said something when I was there is that when she wrapped my burger the mushrooms fell out onto the plate and she didn't put it back on the burger.

The fries were seasoned nicely but to be honest they were a little limp for me.

Would definitely recommend if you're looking for a good burger that's fast
name: Jean

text: It may be hard to find at first, but you'll certainly come back again and again. One of my favorite places to visit thanks to excellent food, drinks, entertainment and service. Lots of high-quality TVs with every sports package makes this a great place to view your favorite sports matchups. I enjoy watching football on Sundays while perfecting my swing. Any weekday you will find every out of market game on for your viewing pleasure. The food is excellent and there's a variety of options for picky eaters. The equipment and facility is immaculate and a great place to hit individually or with a team. Indoor cages and pitching stalls available. Prices are very reasonable and the quick service is great. Check it out and you will be glad you did..
name: Matt

text: One of our favorite places, the happy hour specials are incredible. The food is always great and there is plenty of free parking around just a few steps away.
name: Lon

text: Parking was annoying and I was already in a bad mood by the time I got inside. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. This feels like a place where your order choice matters a lot.
name: User

text: Huge menu selection. Staff were friendly and kept our drinks filled. Food came out in a reasonable amount of time and was cooked to our liking. I have not had a bad experience here since the first week they took over from the former Ali Gators.  I will continue to come here and recommend you do the same.
name: C

text: I have never had a problem in this Wendy's location, Eric who works there as a cashier is always very nice and gets my order right every time. The food is always hot, and the wait can sometimes be a little long but hey, it happens. It's not their fault if they are packed. Lunch and dinner rushes are part of all food service. The staff is always very polite and personable and the food is great. I mean, it's Wendy's, it's not a high end restaurant so I don't get what people expect when they come here. Fast food is fast food, but this Wendy's is very good compared to other ones I have been to.
name: Dave

text: Bruchi's is a yummy addition to the local restaurant scene! Super good bread and subs - but my favorite is that chicken/walnut/cranberry salad they have - SOOOOO good! Definitely, one I crave often!
name: Julie

text: The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. It just never really recovered once things started off weird. Probably not coming back. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus..
name: User

text:
Pretty good time.  The magic breakout areas are really neat.  Housed in the basement of the Johnny Cash museum, this is a hidden dinner "theater" where the theater is magic.

The prices for dinner include a magic show which consists of a few breakout areas with live magic done table side and slight of hand close up.  These magicians do about 15 minute sessions and then move to a different area, so there's 3 or 4 magicians doing their thing at any given time. 

Following dinner, there's also a "main event" where you enter a smaller theater that seats about 40 people or so and you watch a magician do about 20-30 minutes of magic on a small stage.  No big elaborate sets or tricks are done here due to the size of the stage, but still pretty neat.  I will say the tonight's show was bad.  Felt bad for the magician .. but just felt extremely cheesy and not really done well.  He tried but the jokes and most of the tricks just weren't done well, in my (and my groups) opinion.  Apparently each of the main magicians are there for a week's engagement. 

The food is good - and expensive - but it does include the cost of the "main show" and visiting the breakout magic close up shows.  Alcohol is extra.

Cool vibe in the basement and decorated really well.  Gives you a speakeasy type of feeling.  They don't allow pictures inside but do provide a complimentary picture of your group (for each party) which was nice.  

Good for a first experience, but probably wouldn't come back here unless it was for a special event or specific request.
name: Martin

text:
This is my favorite Thai place in the city. I came here for lunch with some co-workers and it was so delicious that I begged my boyfriend to go on our next date night. This review is for the date night but seeing as how my experience was approximately the same, you could also consider it a lunch review.

We walked in without a reservation on a drizzly Thursday evening armed with a bottle of white wine and we were seated right away at a booth. It was decently busy - not empty, but not so packed that I couldn't hear myself think.

We ordered a couple appetizers - dumplings and a special egg roll. I forget what the roll was but both appetizers were served artistically with nice swirls of sauce on the plate and both tasted delicious. I ordered the shrimp Pad Thai for my meal and my boyfriend ordered some kind of chicken noodle dish that may have been the drunk Noodles but I can't actually recall. 

When our dinner arrived, we first took a ton of photos but then (after squeezing some fresh lemon on mine) we took a bite and we melted. I think we literally puddled on the floor. The Pad Thai was just as I remembered it from lunch (but a slightly larger portion) and my boyfriend was thoroughly enjoying his noodles. We tried a bit of each other's dinners and both agreed the Pad Thai was the winner but it wasn't a landslide because both were amazing. The Pad Thai just blended all of the flavors so well and that fresh hit of lemon juice brightened up the nuttiness and I thought that if I was on death row and given one last meal, this Pad Thai might be what I ask for. 

We got to a point maybe 75% of the way through our plates where we both agreed we were stuffed and should stop eating. But it was too good. We kept going. We cleaned our plates. We had no room for dessert so we finished our wine, paid our bill, and left to walk home.

I was so stuffed that my back hurt (this happens to me sometimes, not sure about anyone else) and so my walk home was spent hunched over telling myself that all I had to do was get through 15-20 minutes of this and then I could be at home and in bed. We did eventually make it home (boyfriend: "why are you walking funny?") and we immediately put pants on with elastic waistbands and just laid around moaning in our no-regrets discomfort in enjoying that meal down to the last bite.

Definitely recommend eating here, but I do advise on agreeing to some strategy with the server so they know to take your plate away when your eyes are starting to glaze over so that you don't eat yourself to death.
name: Tricia

text: Best view in the city!  Nice atmosphere. Not the biggest bar, can get a bit crowded on a busy night, but they control how many people are allowed, at least that's what it seemed like while we were waiting for the elevator. This bar is atop the Pontchatrain hotel, which is a nicely decorated boutique hotel. You enter though their lobby. The service is friendly and fast. The drinks are good. There is plenty of seating but nearly everyone gathers along the balcony to enjoy the view and the breeze. Even on an August night it was comfortable.
name: Victoria

text: The food was amazing! But unfortunately the service was extremely slow; it took at least 15 mins for our server to acknowledge us, and then another 10 mins to receive our drinks. I would've given it five stars, but again the service was slow
name: Ask

text:
We have been coming to this location since it opened about 8 years ago. It used to be our favorite family spot and we were often there once a week and the staff all knew us. I'm sad to say that the service has declined so much in the past year that we no longer visit.

One visit, three of us ordered the same protein (two kids portions and one adult) and when they came out the portions were HALF of what we were used to getting. When I commented on it the manager came to the table and before even checking in with the kitchen, she told us that they were working on portion control to correct over-serving before reluctantly going back to the kitchen to ask about it. She came back and told us that there was only one serving of tofu left so they had split it between our three orders. So instead of letting us know that they were low/out of an item and asking if we wanted something else, they just gave us a tiny amount and hoped we wouldn't notice.

On another visit, I ordered a salad that came with a pita or tortilla chips and I chose the tortilla chips. Instead they brought out pita chips and I told them that I asked for tortilla chips, not pita chips. Three minutes later, a different server brought out the same pita chips again and again I had to tell them that was not what I ordered. The tortilla chips finally came out, but when our bill was brought out we were charged for the pita chips. I let the server know, and she brought out a "corrected" bill that then charged us for the tortilla chips that come with the salad at no charge. The server let me know that the manager had directed her to put the charge on.

Those are the specific events that made things particularly bad, but it has also just declined in the state of food taking twice as long to get to the table, servers being unresponsive, and having to ask for things (like silverware) multiple times before it is finally brought to the table. It makes me sad to see a restaurant that our family had loved for years become a place where the managers focus on profit instead of the customers and are unhelpful when problems do arise.
name: Sadie

text: Tried this spot for lunch during a work break. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. Food was fresh and service was quick. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. A very pleasant experience. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer..
name: User

text: People are being a little dramatic in these comments honestly. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. Not saying it's the best place ever, but it was totally fine. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait.
name: User

text: Terrible service!! They took forever to bring our food, it was cold when it came out! They brought out our naans when we were pretty much finished with the food. The only thing I'd say was good is chicken tikka masala but everything was delayed and cold. Service is absolutely terrible. Wouldn't recommend to anyone!
name: Joban

text:
*Topgolf*
Tampa, Florida

Topgolf is a unique concept blending a sports venue arena, with a full bar, and an American style restaurant quality menu. There are Topgolf locations in thirty American States, three cities in England, and several in Australia. Canada, Mexico, and the United Arab Emirates have locations that will be opening by 2019. The venue building is on four floors, with the main level being a sports shop plus cafeteria, and the other three levels for the golf bays. You can read the full and updated review at the Wine Dine and Play blog.
name: Sean

text: We sat outside near the fire & outdoor heater. Ambiance was great, food delicious & pleasant service. Will definitely return!
name: Tara

text: First time here.  Great food and very friendly staff.  I highly recommend the Gouda monster P.O. boy.  Fried oysters bacon etc.  Big enough to split.   Everything looks great.
name: Don

text: The photos made it look a little better than it actually was. It was crowded but still moved along. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. There were a couple things I liked and a couple things I probably wouldn't get again.
name: User

text:
On a recent vacation close to St. Petersburg, I was in the market for a meal I couldn't find back home. A friend recommended Bodega where the Cuban-style fare and affordable prices won me over. 

The walk-up window is practical and charming and the ample outdoor seating allows guests to take advantage of the Florida sunshine! I experienced warm and helpful customer service in a laid back setting. 

My husband and I shared the Lechon plate (garlic and onion FTW!) and the Pollo Asado sandwich. Trust me and pay a dollar more for the plate vs. the sandwich. You don't want to miss the rice, black beans, and moduros. Everything was memorable and seriously delicious. 

I also had a chance to try one of the Sodas Frescas (flavors change daily) and enjoyed the Orange Ginger. So unique and refreshing!

All in all, I'm so impressed by Bodega's ability to serve flavorful comfort food while accommodating dietary restrictions and the health conscious.
name: Cali

text: First time ordering from here and I honestly wasn't sure what to expect. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price..
name: User

text: So good! I ordered carry out and tried the classic chicken salad as well as one with bacon and cheese in it. Definitely a great lunch spot if you're in the Creve Coeur area!
name: Michelle

text: Great beer selection but the food was mediocre. I'm a wings girl and beer girl. Those two things together can make the dopamine flow for this chick. But I wasn't impressed by the wings here. Although they were juicy the sauce choices were nothing to get excited about.  The pretzel we got was good but the beer cheese we ordered in addition was clumpy and must of sat under the heater for a extended time. When I asked the waiter about the consistency of it , he advised it depends on the beer they use that time...??? I didn't realize they change the recipe for the beer cheese all the time. Regardless, he asked if I wanted a new one and when he brought it out.  It actually was creamy  beer cheese. The way its supposed to be. The service is always great and the staff seems knowledgeable on the beer selection.   I love the outdoor seating area and they have a decent happy hour from 3-7 which is an hour before other places.  Hence the reason we normally swing in here.
name: Michele

text: Had an incredible time last night at Salt!  Service was spot on - Kelly was great!  Wine list had a great variety of options. Food was delicious. We started with the Crab Cakes and the Bread in a Skillet. Both were yummy, and the butter with the bread was to die for.  We then had the Lamb Shank and the Red Snapper entrees. The Lamb shank was perfectly cooked and the gravy was one of the best I have had. The Snapper was a special last night and was served with a lemon butter sauce and parmesan risotto. The flavors worked so well together. Overall - incredible food and perfect service. We will be back!
name: Brook

text: Great local bar. Stopped here on a bar crawl. All guests and bartenders were super nice and service was fast
name: Erin

text:
Tried this place before we started doing touristy stuff in New Orleans one day during New Year's. We parked on the street and got on the waitlist. The restaurant was located in a cute boutique shopping center with a large courtyard, and an outside patio area with a chairs for diners to sit and wait

We (a party of three) probably waited about 15 mins before we were called inside. The restaurant is nice and neat with tables everywhere to your right and in the back and a bar area to your left when you first walk in. The place was moderately packed and it looked as if the restaurant knew how to turn over tables in an efficient manner.

I ordered the Mimosa (pretty good, but it's hard to mess up a Mimosa). The menu had so much to offer, I really couldn't choose for a while. Our waiter was patient and left us with plenty of time to decide.

Finally, I picked the Supreme Omelette (which had Sausage, Bacon, Mushrooms and Onions), traded the toast for a biscuit and substituted for the City Grits. To be honest, I wasn't quite sure what the City grits was going to be, but I knew that it would come with something different to try. And I was right, as the waiter brought out a creamy bowl of grits with chives, tomato and cheese on top. I also ordered a side of Baked Bacon, because, how can you not appreciate a restaurant that bakes their bacon. 

Everything was delicious. Definity going to repeat this the next time I'm in town.
name: Janae'

text: Every time I go in I can't help feel it is a little overdone-- the prohibition era doorman/host, the lighting so low I I always see people using phone flashlights to read the menu--  but by the time I leave I've always had a good time. The gin matrix is definitely the highlight, making their wide selection accessible even to novices, and as you would hope their gin cocktails are excellent and beautifully presented. The menu is solid: not super imaginative but generally well executed.
name: Alex

text: Great Chicago style pizza! It is very filling so plan on eating a piece or two. I recommend not adding onions to the pizza, the flavor of the onions can be overwhelming.
name: Anthony

text: Very nice Italian BYOB. Parking isn't great but you can find it easily nearby. The food is wonderful and the menu is eclectic. You can't go wrong here. It's on the pricier side, even for Medford. The restaurant itself is very small, but still nice for a romantic date.
name: William

text: One of those meals where nothing is exactly wrong but you're not excited either. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. It was crowded but still moved along. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. I wouldn't write it off, but I also wouldn't hype it up. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh.
name: User

text: We are not from the area and came across this gem. Wide food selections. Waitress was very informed on the menu.  Food was served quickly.  Beware when ordering the portions are large.
name: Brandi

text: Agree with others who said that 3.5 stars was appropriate. The server was extremely nice and helpful, but a bit disorganized. The food was hit and miss. Pulled pork and ribs were good. The duck fat potatoes appetizer was underwhelming and would be better as a side dish. Interesting building with a rich history.
name: Michael

text: Just found out we had a Poke Shop here and I am so happy I did. The food is delicious and fresh. Can't wait to go back!
name: Tabby

text:
Coming here for Sunday morning breakfast after a night at the casinos is a tradition for my friends and I. We always love the food, and this particular trip we had an awesome server experience too!
Lynsey was super friendly, humorous and accommodating with our special requests and substitutions. I was able to get a super yummy low carb breakfast and her chefs were very generous with the substitutions. 
Thank you Lynsee for making it a fun morning after breakfast!
name: Aliyah

text: Excellent food! Very fresh. We had the ceviche trilogy and the Andino bowl - both were great. The owner was very friendly and helped us choose what to get. Our waitress was nice, but didn't come check on us, refill our water, or remove dirty dishes. Despite this, we'll definitely be back.
name: Caroline

text: We were in town for a convention and just looking for a low key place to chill for a while. We found this place,good selection of beers and drinks. We wanted to try the St. Louis pizza,we tried the Lou ,well it was good but I can say not worth $20 for the large. The server started out great but then when it was a shift change the service got super slow. we had new people adding to our group and they could hardly get drinks. @ people wanted to order food but the server never came back we then resorted to getting our own drinks from the bar. It was a Sunday afternoon about 3 pm and the place was not busy. I would try it again but have lower expectations.
name: Tracie

text:
What a great museum! The architecture is beautiful. Love the sculptures and fountain in front of the museums. Also, the Rocky statue and the famous Rocky stairs!! This is a popular tourist attraction stop. All the hop-on hop-off tour bus stop at this location. 

Definitely a must visit place!
name: Cassandra

text: We eat here a few times a month and are consistently pleased. The Ethiopian dry rub wings are incredible, the scallops are delish and the salmon is my personal favorite entrée. The service is the best - I can't remember his name but the tall gentleman with the ponytail is one of my favorite servers I have ever had anywhere. He is genuine and kind and extremely accommodating. A true gem!
name: Claire

text: It was great ! Great service and very organized! Although they werent iranian they knew a lot about our culture! Great job!
name: Marya

text: This charming restaurant is not as good as it used to be. The wait staff is still attentive and friendly but the food sadly has not been up to par on my last two visits. The dishes were smaller, lacked enough vegetables and sauce. The lackluster bowls will prevent me from returning for awhile.
name: sara

text: Had to find a place quick since we were very hungry and this place looked like it could satisfy both of our cravings. Inside and outside seating; initially we were inside but decided to take advantage of one last day of relative warmth and moved outside. Taylor, our server, was friendly and attentive. Food came quickly and was good. Husband really liked the pasta bolognese and I had the roasted veggie tacos- two completely different kinds of food! I appreciate that I was able to order the tacos without mushrooms; they had a nice bite but were missing something- maybe a spice or avocado, but they were good. Saw games that would be good to occupy kids so it seems like a very family friendly place. Only criticism is the music was just a little loud but hubby had a headache so this may have seemed magnified. Glad we stopped before continuing down the road.
name: Lee

text: Went here for the first time today. Staff was friendly, food was delicious, and solid selection of craft beers on tap.
name: Jesson

text: The food verity is notable. The size of the place inside is soo squeezed and no space at all. I sat in the end of the place near the management office. The food was good, the avocado and the distinguish of the food is noted. The space is for sure a big less points for that. The overpriced in milk, coffee is unjustified for sure ( 4$ for kids glass of milk ).
name: Zed

text: 10/10. The pizza was great. We had the classic pizza and added homemade meatballs. Yum! The meatballs taste like momma made 'em!  Cheese bread appetizer was delish.  Service was great. My only negative is that their ranch was bottle ranch. But no big deal, just won't get it next time. Great sweet tea.  would recommend this place to any pizza lover.
name: Kiia

text: Worst service! Ordered delivery and was told it would be an hour because the driver didn't get in for another half hour which I was fine with. Called after hour and 15 and was told they didn't have something in my order and had to go out and get it and that it would leave soon. I said to forget about that item and they could just bring the rest. That was a 40 min ago. I live about 5 min away and it still is not here. Called and was told that he had a lot of deliveries. This is ridiculous!
name: Meghan

text: This spot came upon a recommendation from a friend for brunch. We made reservations a couple weeks in advance and were seated promptly on arrival. The service was incredible and didn't have the crazy honky tonk bachelorette party vibe it could have for being so close to Broadway which is a plus! My date and I both enjoyed our meal! The spiced blackberry punching bag with bubbles was phenomenal. Would definitely go back if given the opportunity.
name: Katie

text: I enjoy the Mesa Cafe and always have. It's a great locals spot, good food and nice bar. I like to get myself a spicy bloody mary on the cold days and sit outside on the patio under a nice heater! I prefer the lunch/dinner compared to the breakfast. They have a delicious Mediterranean pasta with yummy artichoke hearts, tomatoes, olives and chicken that comes with garlic bread. (It's filling!). My favorite dinner appetizer are the avocado egg rolls that come with a chipotle dipping sauce and a spicy wasabi sauce, they're delicious! The prices here reasonable and the staff are always very friendly. I recommend that you check them out for yourself if you have never been.
name: Olivia

text: This place offers a good selection of items. Veggies, noodles, rice, soup, meats, sushi and desserts and more. Their prices vary on different days and time of day. Lunch time during the week is the best time to get a bang for your buck. Lots of seating and always clean. From my personal experience and the people I've taken here, we all agree the food is absolutely tasty! Hands down you won't be disappointed on flavor. I just don't like the way the staff acts. They are usually very pushy and in your face, always staring! It makes for an uncomfortable meal. If they learned how to behave around their customers, this place would be golden. Hence the 4stars vs. 5. Hope this is helpful. Enjoy!
name: Kennie

text: Spicey! Very Flavorable and fulfilling.  I had the special abd i need to go walk this meal off so i can sleep good tonight.  I had a tropical storm and it was very good.
name: Felice

text:
Pro's: Absolutely fresh and delicious!
Con's: they have already outgrown their space! Small and crowded at prime time.
Go back? For sure!

More...
I love potstickers! I am so accustomed to the little ones typically served in the half moon shape and although delicious, more dough than filling. That is not the case here! This potsticker was like a meatball! It was absolutely delicious. I would go back for potstickers and a cup of soup! My beef and broccoli was fresh and delicious. This place is a hit for me!
name: Deb

text: Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. The wait felt longer than it should have. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent.
name: User

text:
This restaurant looked super cute from the outside and I'd been meaning to try it for awhile. The staff was friendly and the atmosphere was nice, but that was about where the enjoyability of my trip stopped.

I ordered the cucumber lemonade because it sounded fun, and the "Maggie's Pancakes". The menu isn't the most clearly written and has the pancakes listed as:

 "1) chocolate 1) bannana 1) plain 
 It comes with apricot and strawberry jam on the side"

I was under the impression it was like an assortment stack because the way it was written, not a list of options. In any case, I ordered the chocolate ones to go, alongside the lemonade.

When I got my order, the lemonade was a blended frozen drink, which I would not have ordered had I known. What was worse than the fact that I got an entirely different product from what I had expected is that the drink just wasn't very good.

My order came with a small plastic container of fruit that seems like it had been cut or packaged at least a day in advance since the fruit was all soggy.

When I opened the pancakes I found three four or five inch plain pancakes drizzled with chocolate syrup, and two packs of Smuckers breakfast syrup. Once again, it was completely different from what I was expecting. There was no apricot or strawberry jam, and I had assumed from the way that the menu was written that the pancakes themselves would be a chocolate batter. That said, the actual pancakes themselves we're some of the best pancakes I've had before.

I probably won't go back right away, but maybe once they have time to clean up their menu I think this place could be worth eating at.
name: Simon

text:
Best pretzel bites to grace this green earth.

Fresh, hot, seasoned with perhaps butter and some spice ingredient I can't put the name to..doesn't matter!! These pretzel bites will absolutely blow you away. The cheese sauce that comes with is a nacho cheese sauce that has a nice kick to it. You may have to ask for extra sauce as the portion of sauce they give you is not that large but the serving for pretzels...o it's all so glorius. Would you believe I ordered a second order to take home as the movie was approaching the end? Yes, that is right I hit the button and said, "Server, an order of your illustrious nuggets for the road!"

Get yourself to this tavern asap....as Mel Gibson states, "Every man dies, but not every man truely lives.... until you have tried the pretzels bites at the Movie Tavern in Flourtown!"
name: Mike

text: I have been dying to try this place and I am sad to say I was very disappointed. The little guy wanted the PB&J sandwich. The women working at the counter never mentioned that the "peanut butter" was salted caramel apple butter. I ate it because the little guy wasn't buying it. I ordered a goat cheese pesto sandwich.  She said that it had tomato on it so I asked that the tomatoes be removed. I ended up with a goat cheese and balsamic vinegar sandwich.  There was no pesto on my sandwich. The wedge salad had cold bacon. The staff is nice but the menu def should be explained if you are ordering from the counter. I feel badly because I really wanted this restaurant  to a place that I would visit often. It's beautiful, it's spotless, there is so much potential but it def fell short today.
name: Kelly

text: Wow!!! The cocktails are amazing! The Moscow mules were a big hit with our group. They use the right paper straws also. The lavender champagne was light and refreshing. The beef taco pierogies were perfectly fried. The fried chicken sandwich had just the right amount of breading on it. The bison burger was cooked perfectly and accompanied by the best aioli sauce. The atmosphere was intimate (small) yet relaxing. The live jazz music was a nice touch. The service had an upscale vibe to it. This is the perfect dinner spot for a casual drink or a special dinner. This place is a solid 5 stars.
name: Christopher

text: I love other Fuzzy's locations, but this one just doesn't seem to be run like the others are. Food was not warm when it came out, and the lady who was cashier was rude and unpleasant! Hire someone who is customer service oriented and likes talking to people. The margaritas were delicious.
name: Trisha

text:
Looking to dine downtown Tampa in March on a Saturday night not easy. I got a reservation at Cask for 6:45. They weren't packed and they are outside of downtown just passed UTampa on a side street with a few other funky restaurants.  I was wondering if I made a good choice- we sat outside cause that's where the crowd was and they have TVs for lightning game that was on. Decor is cool and casual. We were greeted by Lucca our waiter he was excellent. I asked specific questions on the sauce in the special because we had a guest with dairy issues and he found out the answer. 
   They have craft beers- cocktails- wine etc. lots of choices.  We ordered the mussels app to share it was huge enough for a personal dinner and delicious. My husband and son split the tuna tartare  also very tasty. We had tacos-roasted chicken and two of the swordfish specials for dinner. Spectacular choices. The chicken was sooo juicy. The fish tacos were great and the swordfish special had shrimp and a lobster stock sauce that was awesome. It's kind of a hidden gem. We skipped dessert. No cappuccino here but that ok. Enjoy
name: Resa

text: Just stumbled across this place shopping on Main Street. The building is brightly painted orange and blue with a outside deck. There is a nice huge bar and a open kitchen on the first floor and another bar and dining room on the second floor. We decided to sit in the dinning room to watch the nfl games on the big flatscreens. There were multiple football games on at the same time. The food was decent and the drinks were priced reasonably. La Roca might be my new place to hangout in manayunk. Awesome place to watch the eagles games
name: John

text:
Do yourself a favor & stop in to this easily missed spot. Solid Mexican food menu with a great selection of tequila and mezcal. 
Outstanding for brunch. Looking forward to dinner here.
name: Adamal

text:
This place is definitely overhyped by other reviewers. We came here for brunch and left the place unimpressed, granted the service was very good. Our waitress was very sweet and even opened the side doors for us when we requested.

We ordered a shrimp platter and taste of New Orleans, a Bloody Mary and a mimosa. Total bill was $75. We definitely paid for the salt that they loaded on those food, not the taste. My tongue was tingling for a good 10 minutes because the fried shrimp was very salty. Overall, food was mediocre, service and ambiance were great.
name: Sammy

text: Terrible. They advertised "All You Can Eat Crabs", and when we got there they didn't have crabs! When I inquired why, they said something about market price being too expensive. So why advertise you have them?! And the way the guy did it, he didn't even care that we traveled from out of state to come there. It's just an "around the way" bar. Not a good experience AT ALL
name: James

text:
This place is AMAZING! Super surpassed my expectations!

My husband and I just moved back here from Arizona, and this place definitely made us remember why food tastes better in Nola! 

We ordered the 3 meat platter (chopped brisket, smoked boudin, and baked/roasted chicken, w/ potato salad and pithouse beans) an extra side of Mac n cheese, and apple cobbler.

First the savory-
WOW. Just fantastic. The smoked boudin tasted like boudin you find in Lafayette- very Smokey, a little spicy, and like you stepped in somebody's parran's house! I love it. Hands down my highlight. I did not share lol
Our kids- 4yrs old and 1 yr old- loved the chicken and the Mac n cheese. My husband enjoyed everything- I think we all did- however the brisket was a little fatty for our liking. Good, but fatty.

Second, the sweet- the apple cobbler tasted like the love child of a three way between apple pie, a glazed donut, and bread pudding. I mean, that description alone, is enough said. Period. It was amazing.

Overall, we give it a full five stars because everything was sooo good, AND, the guy who took our order had the best customer service. He was patient, and helpful- definitely a great experience with this place!
name: Erin

text:
We decided to come here for St Patty's Day this year. The past few years we've been going bar hopping in Philly or Phoenixville, but this year decided to chill out and go somewhere close and stay at one place, since we had to go to work the next day. So I picked this place as the best local
Irish bar I could think of that had everything I wanted: Irish music, bagpipers, and Irish dancers. We came on St Patty's day years ago and remember having a good time. 

It was cool that they didn't have a cover and it was free valet parking. It wasn't as packed as I thought it was going to be, but just crowded enough so we still had some room to move and breathe. I started off with a SparkAle rose beer, which was really good. I would have ordered it regardless of what kind of beer it was because it said sparkale and my nickname is sparkle. We listened to some Irish music for a little bit. I was waiting for them to play the one famous song but didn't hear it. Later we put in for a table to get food. 

Our table was all the way in the back right by the outside patios doors. I was cold every time someone opened the door and was kinda disappointed I couldn't hear the music anymore. I ordered a crab cake sandwich, which was very good for a PA crab cake. It had lump pieces of crab and not too much filler. I didn't realize it came with fries though I didn't really care for them. The cheesesteak egg rolls were really good as well. I also got a greenish blue drink which I thought was going to be like an Irish mule, but it was just an orange crush drink that they dyed green. 

By time we were done eating the band was done playing which was kind of disappointing, but I guess that's our fault for ordering food. I did see some bagpipers. Didn't see the dancers though, but maybe I missed them. 

We had a fun day here. Next time if we come back I think we'll have to either eat at home or get a table earlier though, too long of a wait for a table.
name: Lauren

text: This place was perfect for us. Positioned walking distance between our hotel and the City Museum where we spent the day. We ate every bit of our breakfast and the service was fantastic. We will be back for sure!
name: A

text: We go down to Clearwater for spring break every year, and this is our favorite place by a mile. The Catch of the Day is always super fresh and delicious. The beer is ice cold and the atmosphere is just awesome. Super laid back and it's literally on the water. The drunken shrimp is out of this world. First thing you have to try when you get there. This place is can't miss!
name: Jeff

text:
Hi Sara,

 I wanted to let you know the baby shower Saturday was a Huge Success!!  Everyone came up to me saying how nice everything was and how wonderful the food was!  And the 2 girls that hosted it, were Amazing and so accommodating and helpful!  Many had no idea you all offered such a service.  I hope it will bring in more customers in the future for your business!  I cannot Thank You enough for ALL you did for us in making it such a pleasant experience.  That is customer service at its best!  Kudos to you all!   It could not have gone any better!
name: Judy

text: Awesome from start to finish. The shrimp poo boy and gumbo we better than I expected. Our server was awesome and helpful and quick just flew in from Denver and I'd come back any time. Ooh yeah try the pecan pie it was awesome too!
name: Randy

text: Best breakfast on 4th Ave!! Such a cool place, amazing food, cool vibe, good service. Feels like fun, quirky diner with a full bar and great selection of beer. Open late too! The tots will change your life. The corn pancakes are also a big favorite of mine.
name: Bryan

text:
This place is a go to of mine when I am in Tucson. There are three things that I love about this restaurant. 1) they make their salsa FRESH at your table, and you pick the heat (and it's incredible)  2) the HUGE margaritas and 3) the verde chili Burrito (one of the best I have had).  All of the above are incredible and make the 4 star rating.  If you stick with the above you can't go wrong.  

Sadly, the few times I have ventured away from the above the choices have not been quite as good.  The shrimp tacos are alright, the Chipotle Shrimp Burrito fair, the taco salad standard.  Because of that I would give it a 3 1/2 if I could.  Luckily the three highlighted above^ are my favorites!
name: Lainie

text: Terrible service. I am usually a pretty understanding person, but this was a little ridiculous. I got two small items in the drive-through. Person taking orders was not friendly, but whatever. I get to the second window to get my food-the person handing me the food gives me a look that could kill and says not one word to me. She just stared at me creepily.
name: Ragan

text: The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. A couple small things kept adding up. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Food was good and came out fast. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.
name: User

text: Perfect evening treat! Plenty of flavors to choose from. Fairly priced. Great atmosphere, excellent service. Very accommodating for wanting to sample differant flavors. Salt caramel rocks and the key lime pie.
name: The

text: Really cute place! We came here for the first time tonight and were greeted by a group of instrumentalists playing "Joy to the World," which made it all the more magical, but TGB definitely stands its own two feet, seasonal touches notwithstanding. The inside is beautiful--well decorated & appointed, a great ambiance without being pretentious. Also liked how many other families were there! My mom, toddler son & I loved it. My mom had the fish & chips which smelled great & she gave a thumbs up. I had a salad and the Carlos fries, which were great, & I'd definitely try their cheese fries or Veggie curry next time. For my son we ordered the kids Mac and cheese, which was good, but it was made with gnocchi (this is noted on the menu, which moms around the world appreciate) so I know my pickier older daughter would not have liked it. But they had a really nice kids menu with lots of options to choose from. The service was good, & the food came out very quickly for a pretty busy place on a Saturday night. We'll definitely be back, & if you're in Wayne, this is a really cute spot with a creative menu & the goods to back it up.
name: Kaitlynn

text:

We ordered 20 pcs bone-in half and half secret spicy and original. The order took  a long time to be ready. The to go box has ventilation holes so the chicken doesn't get soggy on the way home which is a nice touch. The chicken comes with pickle radish which wasn't as potent as I like it. Chicken itself is okay. The chicken wasn't covered with sauce thoroughly and the batter was too thick for my liking. I'm not a big bonchon fan and would pick bb-q chicken over bonchon, but it's nothing to get excited about. 

The location is really convenient. Okay price. Decent food. Okay service.

They also have a bunch of sauces on the side that were also delicious. There's a lot of space & also outside seating upstairs - definitely an awesome sauce place to eat, drink, & chill with friends. text:
If you're in NOLA, you gotta try Willie Mae's. It's one of those things to put on your restaurant list for the trip. Go ahead... I'll give you a couple minutes to list it on there. No I'm serious. I know you're reading a lot of reviews and lists right now and it may be overwhelming so let me make it easy for you: write. this. place. down.

Let me just let you know if you're coming for dinner (and probably lunch too), there will be some kind of line or wait. They're smart and have a line area roped off. They don't call you in order of line or anything, but they do this because there's not that much sidewalk space and of course you want to keep it orderly. You just get in line, and they'll come out and ask you how many in your party and a name. As a party of 2, we waited around 25 minutes.

As for food, I highly recommend the fried chicken meal - it comes with 3 pieces and a side. The fried chicken is so good. The breading is thin and crispy, not thick and crunchy like some other places. If you like a nice crispy outer skin and plenty of moist meat, this is your place. I like my fried chicken smothered in the Louisiana hot sauce they put on your table and drizzled with honey. Make sure you ask for a side of honey. TRUST ME. Unless you hate savory and sweet dishes. Then don't get it. But my friend, if you've never had fried chicken with honey, you need to try it!

We got mac and cheese, green beans (comes with rice and a choice of sausage gravy or regular gravy or no gravy; we opted for no gravy), and 2 cornbread muffins + 2 rolls. Everything was tasty - the green beans were seasoned great and rice was cooked. Mac and cheese is the drier cheese kind - not the gooey, drippy, cheesy kind. I personally like the drier kind. The cornbread muffins and rolls were good too; drizzle some of that honey on both or either--you won't regret it.

I also recommend the fresh squeezed lemonade and sweet tea--better yet, ask for an Arnold Palmer - best one I've had yet! Some places have sweet tea that tastes very strongly of black tea, but this sweet tea has none of that. Mixed with lemonade, it's amazing. The only thing that sucked was my cup was NOT clean and it had a lipstick mark on it. Yikes. I asked for a new one and they gladly replaced it but... c'mon they need to be on top of that.

Again, please come here - you won't regret it. Just check the rim of your cup. ;)
name: Xiaopan

text: I have lived in Tucson for 58 years. We used to frequent Mama Louisa's when I was in elementary school- so at least 50 years ago. They had the best homemade spaghetti and fresh marinara sauce. It was consistent my whole life and we spent many birthday dinners eating homemade pasta! In the last several years, things have really changed. I keep going back hoping to get that fresh marinara that I always wanted to duplicate at home. But lately it has been thick, overly cooked, too salty and just not enjoyable. The homemade pasta was good, but I ordered Joe's special and the homemade pasta comes with it automatically. I ordered homemade pasta for my mom and it ended up a packaged fettuccini. The bread sticks were soggy. I'm not sure it we're hitting it on the wrong day and the sauce is reheated too much from the weekend or what. I may give it one more shot just to see if it's a fluke. If this is what were getting from now on, I won't be back after that.

text:
Incredible restaurant for Hotpot and BBQ. A large selection of meats and veggies, self serve, as well as an extensive sauce station to bring to your table for the hotpot and/or bbq. 

My group opted to do both for $29.99, which is for all you can eat, and even includes soft drinks, soy milk, and dessert (fruit, cakes, and a variety of ice cream flavors).

We spent over 2 hours here trying different meats and veggies and the staff was very efficient and friendly, checking on us, clearing our plates, refilling the hot pot broth, changing the bbq grill paper, and not making us feel even the least bit rushed.

The buffet area was very clean and sanitary, and all the food was fresh and great quality. Loving this place especially compared to the hotpot and bbq options in NYC!

text:
Ok. Let's get serious. Throwing bad, cold food in front of a golfer during an endless "happy hour" is fine for a "clubhouse."  But!  If you want to be a serious restaurant in New Orleans you must fix this restaurant. I have been to receptions, breakfasts and a few lunches here and it is time to set the record. 

First, I have gone here often due to its great convenience, nice views and the previous reputation of other venues in City Park. But. This is not part of the catering empire of the Park, which is legendary and great( i.e., Pavilion wedding receptions, parties at the Timkin building). 

Second,  service:  amateurs. Slow. Forgot details of orders (no rice in gumbo: did not write it down). Sloppy:  actually dropped food on the floor more than once during latest lunch!  Staff seemed confused throughout the last two lunches.

Third. Food. No stars here at all. Gumbo: red color and watery. Asked for no rice and got so much over cooked rice that when I removed it from the small cup only three spoons of gumbo were left. Thin slices of fatty sausage and ground meat in the cup: what the heck is that!!!

Cobb Salad:  four stringy strips of cold chicken on top of a small bowl of bag mixed greens. And yes, a sprinkle of chopped egg, bacon bits and average blue cheese dressing on the side. Not worth $13. No stars, no way. 

Breakfast visit:  slow service (duh). Weak coffee. Cold eggs. Slow service. But a nice morning view. 

Receptions: I have attended two. Tasteless pass arounds. Bar service for drinks inefficient and long waits. Buffet food line contained standard Costco-type small bites. They are actually better at Costco on Saturday mornings!  Easy parking but went home hungry, no wait... we did not go home. We went to Reginelli's for a pizza. So we actually did not arrive home hungry!

Overall, The Fillmore has great potential but if they want to be more than a watering hole for golfers, a major overhaul is critical. I hope it happens. There is much potential here. One star today. Maybe more in the future if things change.
name: Stephen

text:
Super delicious, nice space, and sweet waiter. Only didn't give 5 stars because it was my first time and would like to see if the service was consistent. 

My fiance was raised a vegetarian and had plenty of options. There were 5 of us and we all ordered a different beverage: cocktails, latte, smoothie and they were all good! We all ordered different breakfast items: sandwiches,  hotcakes, french toast - all delicious! I also like the option to have a side salad in place of any potato side. 

Also love that you could just run in like a grab-and-go coffeeshop and choose from their big tea selection or grab a latte or smoothie. They are connected with UberEats, too!

Parking is tricky if you're driving - all parallel, but we went in a Sunday morning for brunch, but the location under the train tracks is kind of cool.

text:
I called in an order for dinner and spoke to a friendly young man on the other end of the phone.  We ordered wings, pizzas and ziti with sausage.  The employee on the other end of the phone asked me to wait a minute so he could give me a total; then he was about to tell me, but said to hang on, there was a deal that would drop my price.  /SMILE/. I was told it would be 15 to 20 minutes, and arrived at UNO's about 15 minutes later.
     I walked in and a friendly female employee held the door open for me and greeted me.  I was asked how many were in my party, but let them know that I was just there to pick up food.  She quickly let a gentleman behind the register know that I was there.  He reached behind him and checked a few orders, found mine and told me to enjoy my meal.
     When I got to my car, I thought to double check the bags, and I was missing the ziti.  I went back inside, was greeted again by the same chipper girl, and she right away went to solve the problem.  A very nice manager stopped up at the register, asked about my order, then explained it would be less than 5 minutes...would I like a drink.  I was hesitant, but said sure.  He disappeared quickly to get me a drink, but I ran to my car to let my family know I'd be out shortly...well, kind manager sir came right to my car with the beverage in a to go cup! /SMILE/
     True to his word, my food was ready in about 4 minutes.  It was a refreshingly good visit.  Every person I came in contact with was genuinely happy to help me.
     When we got home and ate, my family was really pleased with the food.  My husband had the veggie extravaganza flat bread which he really enjoyed.  My son loved the ziti, and he's a teen who is particularly fond of finding fault!  I enjoyed my deep dish, but was stunned (as we all were), the wings were AMAZING!   Grab yourself some of their honey BBQ wings, thank me later!
name: Jill

text: I ordered delivery through GrubHub, so can't speak to the restaurant staff other than their preparation of the order, which was as expected. The food was subpar for the price. $10+ Cauliflower "steaks" were more like overly breaded chunks that lost their breading the minute you try to cut them. The sauce and celery were great, though. The cheese soup had no flavor whatsoever, and the accompanying croutons had an off flavor (fennel?) I would have sent both back had I been in the restaurant itself. We also ordered a Cajun pasta which my husband thought was quite good, but nothing worth the price.

text:
Oscar's Tavern has been here for the a long time.  Oscar's has endured every Mayor from Rizzo to Kenney,  witnessed all the 4 major sports teams win a championship and watching man walk on the moon was a fairly new concept. 
The important things about Oscar's Tavern haven't changed much,  good bar food, cold beer low prices and most of all,  a fun atmosphere. 
If you want to impress your friends by paying the tab, at Oscar's you won't go broke.  Sometimes you want to keep it simple,  so I always order a hot roast beef and provolone on a Kaiser roll with horseradish and hot peppers or a hand sliced baked ham sandwich. Accompanied with some crispy fries and a tall, 22 ounce glass of cold beer and I am momentarily sitting in "dive bar heaven." 
But dive as in good,  as in complete, dive as in an experience I hope will always be there.
name: Bruce

text:

My girlfriend had the veal sotombucca and it was very tough to where she had it sent back for a new dish. For a 27 dollar entre it should be tender. I had the gnocchi with vodka sauce and shrimp which was very good.
I had 2 glasses of soda which they charged me $2.50 per glass and the glass had a ton of ice.l felt that they should not charge for refills or at least charge less for a big glass of ice with a little bit of soda in it. I'll drink water next time.

text:
So, I moved from NY to Florida in 1982 ( almost makes me a native) and have long since quit whining about finding a decent pizza pie. The water and all that stuff.
But Chinese, I know every restaurant in China Town NYC, been to them all.
Came to Florida, and no insult to Saigon food, but every supposed Chinese restaurant or take out place....ain't Chinese. 
Then I found this little gem one day waiting for my wife shopping at Publix in the strip stores alongside Home Depot in Largo.

One taste and I was transported back to Grand and Allen St !
Savory broth, large slices of beef, fresh veggies...mouth watering.
Everything on the menu is fresh made and delicious.

Unfortunately we are moving out of the area towards Orlando, if I can't convince them to move with us, I am going to have to invest in one of those big Yetti coolers.

Love this place, and nice people to deal with.

text:
Just went to Yee-haw for the first time to listen to music! The lineups were really good- but the sound tech needs to make adjustments (a lot of kick back & the I don't think the vocalist could hear well bc he was too soft/low)

I think the design could have been better because people have to walk around the stage to get to the bathrooms and gift shop.  If you are there to see music it is disappointing having large bachelorette groups walk by (they get dropped off by the party buses).  I would say my favorite part was the outdoor area.  Giant projector tv to watch games, lawn chairs, and corn hole.  It really is set up like the ultimate back yard hang out!  The garage doors that open the bar to the outside is a nice feature and allows you to hear the music. I love seeing all the cute dogs - so definitely need to wear my "hold my beer while I pet the dog" hat next time!  They also have giant jenga and a few other games past the Prince's food truck.  I was definitely disappointed with the chicken...not sure what the hype is about but Hattie B's was fresh and tender - this just seemed like cheap fast food.  My boyfriend said the tacos were just okay and wouldn't get the again (a friend got tacos later and they were much bigger in terms of proportion but against wasn't impressed).  I would love to go on a weeknight to avoid the bachelorette parties and see if the sound system is better.  There is $5 parking right across the street from the entrance but it was really sketchy - broke down cars, scrap metal, etc so I would not park there again!

text:
Fantastic option for someone on a restricted diet.

Thanks to my breastfeeding infant, when we ate here I was soy and dairy free. Mellow Mushroom makes it easy to follow a restricted diet. If you go to their website you can choose ingredients you cannot consume (like dairy and soy) and the system will spit back everything you can eat. How cool is that?! That's how I ended up eating the most delicious vegan cheese pizza with chicken, anchovies, onions, and mushrooms.

I had so many topping options, it was amazing. Also, that vegan cheese is nothing to sneeze at. It tasted absolutely delicious. My toppings really transformed this pizza so I am curious to try just a vegan cheese pizza in the future so I can truly judge the vegan cheese. Let's just say on my pizza I couldn't tell the cheese was vegan. 

The atmosphere of this place is pretty trippy. I've never been in a Mellow Mushroom before so I didn't know what to expect. I would envision this is what a stoner's bedroom would look like - psychedelic. 

My husband and I both got a personal 10 inch pizza. I ate the whole thing and my husband ate half of his (this shocked our waitress. I blame the breastfeeding.) After eating that whole pizza, I was barely hungry for dinner and I was pretty hungry when we got there. The pizza is pretty filling!

This is my new go to for a delicious soy free/dairy free meal. If you are on a restricted diet check out their website!
name: Christina

text:
My mother, sister and I reserved a table to celebrate Mother's Day.  At $40 per person (paid for online in advance to reserve our spots), it was a bit on the pricey side for a lunch...but we thought it would be well worth it for the experience.  We were wrong.  

Prior to our reservation (and after we had paid), we received an email stating the "rules" for our Mothers Day tea. Arrive early and we had 45 minutes to eat.  Yep, for $120 lunch, we would be allotted 45 min.  Who does that?

Upon arrival, there was a long line formed outside the restaurant.  Nevermind that it was cold and raining - the doors were locked until Tina's could rush out the people in the prior hour slot.  We, along with several other unhappy customers, would have left had we not already paid. When Tina's finally opened the door (several minutes past our reservation, further cutting our allotted 45 min), we were seated and told where we could find the self-serve hot tea.  Maybe it's just me, but part of the charm of this place is choosing a fun tea flavor and having it served in a cute little tea pot.  Instead, an entire restaurant of people were maneuvering a teeny tiny restaurant (the size of a small living and dining room) and pumping hot tea out of a carafe.  Meanwhile, staff were furiously trying to move and reset tables, because they clearly didn't have enough time to do so after rushing the last round of guests along.  

After getting our own tea, we were forced to leave our tea at our table, only to stand in another long line for a buffet of salad, finger sandwiches, and scones.  By the time we returned to our table with food, our tea was cool.  With a very short time left to eat, let alone enjoy time with our Mother (given the late seating and standing in lines), we watched the next hours reservations tugging at the locked door and forming a line in the cold rain.  We are quickly and left, knowing the entire restaurant had to be bused and tables reset for the next round of guests. 

I hate to complain but the hospitality was truly awful.  It was especially upsetting to watch elderly guests trying to navigate close quarters and serve their own tea, etc.  

For the next special occasion, I hope Tina's will do better.  They crammed as many people through, capitalizing on Mother's Day, at the expense of their guests.  Forty-five minutes (or less in our case) is an unreasonable amount of time to "allow" guests to enjoy a special occasion meal. It is unreasonable to lock the doors and force guests, especially people who are on time, to stand outside on a cold and rainy day.  It is unreasonable to expect guests to self-serve/pump a random flavor of tea at a TEA ROOM. 

I've been here on a non-holiday, and had a better experience, but I won't go back.  If you're looking for good manners, hospitality, or a POT of tea, go elsewhere! And, definitely steer clear for special events that require an advance payment!!
name: Jeannine

text: I've been to many Italian restaurants, in countries the world over. Giorgio at Favoloso is an example of the hospitality that Italians are famous for. His pizza is the ultimate expression of his craft, the dough is light, airy, and crisp. The toppings are generous but are left to let the pie in all of its parts shine through. His salads are reminiscent of the Tuscan cuisine I experienced only 2 years ago. Fresh, with balanced players, working in harmony to create a delicious symphony that is a delight to the last note. His spaghetti was cooked perfectly, and his meat sauce is balanced and rich, the type of richness that leaves your tastebuds intrigued as to how something could be so balanced, and yet finish so smoothly. If you enjoy the simple complexity of Italian cuisine, Giorgio and Favoloso will teach a master class in what the cuisine and hospitality of Italians truly is. Cant wait to return!
name: David

text:
Definitely a bad experience.  Been here several times before and kind of under impressed previously but decided to come in today. Ordered and paid online thinking that would streamline things since I had an afternoon meeting. When I arrived to pick up my order, they said they didn't have a record of the order; but stated they can prepare it for me while I wait. While waiting for my order, I stepped aside and stood by the plexi-glass window that looked thru into the kitchen. Two cooks were preparing food, and while assembling a taco order, one of the cooks was wearing a glove on the right hand but no glove on his left hand. He then proceeded to eat some of the fillings as he was preparing the food.  YIKES!!! Yes, right into his mouth and then continue preparing the order and another taste of the filling.  I do realize that gloves don't always guarantee hygiene; but my gosh man, do that Sh#t on your own time in your own kitchen!! So the way I look at it,  if you're doing that nasty Sh#t where I can see you, what are you doing when I can't see. 

Other than the cash register attendant, the other employees seem unprofessional and dirty. The kitchen was dirty and looked like it needed a good dose of bleach and sandblasting.

At check out, the cash register attendant was nice and he did give me a complementary order of chips and salsa for my inconvenience. I ordered an Old School Pastor (2 tacos); which not only were the meat portions in each taco microscopic, the pork that was in there was mostly fat and gristle.  I was starving so I got one down, but couldn't eat the second one. The chips were burnt and bitter; I think they probably need to monitor and change the oil in their fryer more frequently. The tomato salsa visually looked fresh but had a bitter and rancid taste.

Visions of the one gloved cook tasting food with one of his hands didn't make my experience appetizing. Hey I get it, it's cool.. Michael Jackson wore one glove but at least he wasn't preparing food for people. 
 By the look of the operation, thinking that the kitchen staff doesn't know anything or cares about safe food handling procedures. 

In summary just wasted $10. am hungry and nauseous all at the same time. Pretty obvious the owner of the establishment hasn't set up any standards for his business, it's clear he just wants to bring in money. So that's it for me, I will not be going g back again; way too many other options out here.
name: Silvia

text: Extensive seafood menu, easy parking, and lots of seating options makes this a go to spot for us. Great food and service.
name: Dj

text: This place was hands-down amazing. I was not sure what to expect since I'm from New York City but my friend said that I got some really great reviews and I love that the menu was vegetable focused but not exactly vegetarian. It's a very high-end place but they seem to be OK with the fact that we were dressed pretty casual, or maybe didn't notice! The server was educated, informative and helpful. At first I got a cocktail with basil but I wound up not loving that so afterwards I ordered some wine. The wine was delicious. I enjoyed it with a cheese plate of three different cheeses which were really tasty and in all honesty I was kind of full after that but we had several plates coming. She had mentioned that we should order 5 to 6 but I think we would've been OK with 3 to 4. I have a special note where the radish tacos which had some delicious zucchini purée and sauces and toppings to go with it. I love that it was build your own so you could put only the ingredients that you like. I didn't particularly like the eggplant but that's because I don't like anchovies. I really enjoyed the peaches with the balsamic and prosciutto all of the prosciutto wound up getting cooked on top of the grilled peach and I wasn't too sure about that. It was not expensive to me at all by New York standards but either way I feel like it would be worth it. It is kind of in the middle of nowhere though, so keep that in mind.
name: Marisa

text: ordered twice in the past 2 weeks, asked for 2 simple things, cut the hoagie in half and cut up the long onions, i got neither, i dont think they  know how to cut up an onion, ive never had a hoagie with only 3 or 4 long onions stretched out the length of the roll,so when you take a bite they pull out and hang out of your mouth, paper thin tasteless meat
name: L

text:
I was in Tampa for two and a half days, and managed to spend several hours on two different days here at TBBC.  I'm a sucker for an outdoor bar, no matter the weather, and that's what drew me in!  They have lots of beer on tap, and it was so easy to just tuck in for 4 or 5 pints and enjoy the people watching and weather.  I didn't set out to find this place, it was just right in front of me when I hopped off the streetcar to explore.  They also have ample indoor seating.  My first visit was during the day and I didn't order any food.  I returned the next night and spent a few hours drinking and watching the hockey game on their outdoor tv's.  I decided to get food to go, and after checking Yelp and the Googles, I went with the wings (which were on DDD apparently), and the lobster mac & cheese...because wings and lobster mac scream healthy balanced meal, ammi right??  It took me about 15-20 minutes to get back to my hotel on the streetcar and the mac & cheese was still hot, but the wings weren't.  They were good, and plentiful, but didn't pack the flavor punch I was expecting.  The accompanying ranch was thick and delicious, probably homemade.  The mac & cheese was the star, with tons of cheese sauce, tender noodles, and lobster in nearly every bite, which surprised me!  I really wish I had tried the calamari, the fish & chips, or the cuban.  All looked delicious.  The staff was super friendly and attentive to boot!  All in all an awesome experience, and I will definitely be back in the future.
PS...they stop serving food an hour before they close so keep that in mind if you're planning on drinking and ordering to go!
name: Doris

text: I wanted to like this more than I actually did. Food was fresh and service was quick. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish.
