text:
Dead Bob's is a nice place to eat with friends. This isn't a fancy, schmancy restaurant. There is no air conditioning. Shorts and T-shirts are recommended, during the summer.

The host will let you know how long you have to wait for a seat. He's always busy checking on diners, serving food, and monitoring tables. The host is crazy busy when the restaurant is full, but he is nice and polite. Our waitress was also friendly.

Service: Friendly and efficient.
Margarita: Refreshing and well-balanced.
Fried Avocado: Yummy. crispy. The sauce tastes like chorizo. The Fried Avocado is so good that it does not need Sauce.
No No Bones (Szechuan): Slightly hot. Good.
The Chorizo Bob: Tasty. Super-sized portion. But, what the heck, I was in a Carnivore-mood. I was able to taste the Chorizo and did not have to season the burger with salt and pepper. 
​
Hope you get a chance to enjoy the food and drink at Dead Bob's.

Most of the oysters Rockefeller I've had are super cheesy and buttery and these were just amazing!! 

The atmosphere was great! They offer indoor and outdoor seating. We decided to sit outside and had a PHENOMENAL server. Her name was Leslie and boy did she accommodate for us with the roasted oysters as well as with our drinks! Will definitely look forward to dining here again and hopefully have her as a server!

text:
This is the 3rd or 4th time that I've visited San Carlos Grill and the first time that I'm leaving a review. 

This was quickly becoming my new fave, go to restaurant. The service has been hit and miss but typically good enough to keep me coming back. 

Tonight's service was poor enough to make me so angry that we literally got up and left. 

I understand that it's Saturday and they had a fair number of diners. As wait staff, and just customer service common sense, you don't go to the bar and make a drink while guests have been waiting for ten minutes to give their order. 

Their were three people on the floor and only one person appeared to be taking orders. Poor management or improper staffing, I don't know. Either way, with the number of Mexican restaurants in a five mile radius, they'd better make some changes. 

I like their food, and appreciate their unique twist on  their menu. 

Poor service, or truly lack of service, is my pet peeve. I hope that I'll give them another chance, but I'm still pissed off.

text: This was just okay. I had the smore's cookie, which was pretty solid if a bit too overly grainy/wheaty in texture. I also had the buffalo cauliflower appetizer and only finished about a third of it. It seemed like it was trying to be a healthier twist on the deep fried spicy cauliflower they serve at places like IndeBlue. I think they must steam or pan saute it, then cover it in a sauce that is thickened with some kind of starch. It's that thickener that really kills this dish for me - it was like hot sauce paste, and made the whole dish chalky and gummy. The hot sauce could have also benefited from some additional flavor - ginger, garlic, etc. I was surprised at how underwhelming it was given all the rave reviews.

text: My partner took me here for my birthday and we were really excited to try a good Cajun place and he had heard good things about it. The decor is reminiscent of Boston pizza but we were hoping that maybe the restaurant put the focus on the food. For a drink I ordered the Creole Bloody Mary. It came with a piece of shrimp and celery. The drink was really good. I saw a lot of compliments on the customer service on their Yelp page. Maybe we came on a bad night. The server was really nice. The food didn't take too long. But she dropped it off and didn't check on us again until we were finished. No one asked if I wanted a second drink. There were a few servers on staff but they didn't circulate much and mostly hung out at the bar chatting while our server ran around. Our food arrived and it looks delicious. I ordered the seafood jambalaya and my partner ordered a combination plate. His red beans and rice were nice and smoky. My dish looked lovely and was a generous serving but once I got through the crab legs I was disappointed to find that the rest of the dish was bland and watery.  It was filling but so boring. This was a let down as it was a special occasion.

text:
I'm not sure how anyone can truly give this restaurant anything more than 3 stars. The sushi was the better part of the meal I had ordered, and it had a very faint fishy aftertaste. The texture of my sashimi was all spongey except the tuna, probably because that moves the most and the rest of the fish get rehydrated as it just sits in the fridge. The best part was the CaliRoll because that's nearly impossible to screw up. 
I also had ordered the Udon Soup... DO NOT ORDER ANY OF THE UDON SOUP!!!****
It's not your traditional Japanese Udon soup, what I had received was a bowl of Wonton Soup Broth (cause I can taste the difference!) instead of udon soup broth, with an overload of peppers and vegetables that did not belong whatsoever. The vegetables overpowered the taste of what the soup was supposed to be and it was terrible. 
If you love wonton soup with udon style noodles, then this dish is perfect. If you're seeking Udon Soup...this is a sad imitation of what they call Udon Soup.
name: Michelle

text:
This was our first visit to The Cup Cafe. We rolled in around 10 am on a Saturday and we're faced with an hour wait. So we headed over to Target and came back an hour later. We're were seated with in a couple minutes and it appeared to die down a little bit. I ordered the Irish Benedict and my wife and kids shared a stack of pancakes, eggs, bacon and hash browns.  The Benedict had corned hash instead of ham and was pretty good. The hollandaise sauce was tangy and a bit different than your traditional hollandaise, I enjoyed it. The kids love the pancakes, eggs and hashbrowns as well. They finished mine off when they were done with theirs.

Brunch here was a good experience and so was the service. There was an 80 year old couple with a lap dog being hand fed in front of me. Something about it was a little disturbing but what can you do...

text: I fell in love with this out of the way local diner. It was built in a former post office and run by a local family this is amazing.  My husband and I both enjoyed our meals immensely but were more impressed with the service.  Lots of checking in to make sure we had everything we needed.  Refills of hot water for tea.  . I would highly recommend making a stop here if you are passing through Goleta!

text: Ordered takeout because I didn't feel like cooking and it held up okay. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. text: How in God's name does this hole have four stars??? Seriously. I have no idea. Went here after the Preds game for the most unfulfilling meal. text:
Gris-Gris, you have definitely cast a spell on me.

As soon as this spot opened and food groupies started raving about it, I knew I had to stop in. Lucky me, I happened to be working near Magazine during lunch and had an opportunity to try this spot.

It was early lunch on a Monday and we were seated upstairs on a pretty low key day. I immediately noticed the lovely decor and I fell in love with the hanging lights throughout the place. The mood was lovely with a classic feel. We ate upstairs, in the bar area, which was perfect because it wasn't crowded at all.

I had looked at the menu online, so I had an idea of what I wanted to eat. We started with the shrimp and fried green tomatoes and an order of complimentary red beans and rice, since we were here on a Monday. For my entree I got the shrimp and grits which comes with tail-off shrimp, smoked sausage, roasted red peppers and cherry tomatoes.

Red beans and rice: Delicious! This was a super generous portion, especially considering that it was free. If you're stopping in, pair this with an app and it makes a great lunch. Add a beer, if you're feeling squirrely. The beans were flavorful and there was even sausage in it. I was expecting sub-par red beans, only because they're free, but this was great!

Fried green tomatoes and shrimp: I love fried green tomatoes and this dish didn't disappoint. The tomatoes were nice and thick with a light batter and a yummy sauce. Again, I was really impressed with the portion size: the shrimp were huge and plentiful. I would order this again.

Shrimp and grits: Yum! Y'all know that I'm a huge fan of shrimp and grits, and this was one of the best versions that I've had. Creamy smooth grits topped with fat juicy shrimp, sausage and cherry tomatoes in a delectable sauce. Really, what kicks shrimp and grits up a notch? Sausage, always sausage. This was so rich I couldn't even finish all of it and I enjoyed the rest later. This is a "must" order- you won't regret it.

The staff was really friendly, and although the waiter was being pulled in different directions, our food came out quickly and he stayed on top of the drink refills. I want to go back for dinner and try the chicken and dumplings and get the full dinner experience because I feel that it's probably pretty special.

text: Food took forever but ended up being better than I expected. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. text: Chili's has gone down hill. I worked at the one in Brandon 25 years ago and we were slammed every night.  The service here sucks.  No one refills drinks or removes dirty dishes.  If you drop the check off and leave my table without taking away as many plates as you can you will get a 10% tip.  I usually tip 22%, but servers seem to expect more these days, but do less work.  The fajita meat is weird and grisly.  Everything just tastes frozen.  My Presidente margarita tasted like it was made with a powdered mix.  Chili's needs to be great again.

text: Dropped in here after reading the reviews while on business. I ended up going back 3 more times in a week! The bar had fantastic drinks. The food was super and it had a laid back vibe that worked for me after a day at work!

text:
Tyler's is just okay; no egregious issues, but also not memorable in any way. What keeps it alive and even crowded is decent happy hour prices and the fact that it's open late in an area that has very little else going on past 8:00pm. I've been here a few times with friends and service is consistently slow, even to just get a bottled beer delivered to your table. Servers seem a bit clueless as to what specials are happening and what beers are on tap. Sometimes they stand around talking to their friends, and more than once they've plopped themselves down at my table and  and expected to hang out with us rather than, you know, taking orders and serving customers... very odd.

There's a good beer selection, but it can be a little bit pricey if you don't stick to happy hour or drafts. Similarly, the food is way overpriced for what you get, and just generally isn't very good. I wouldn't be surprised if everything was frozen and microwaved to order, or else poured directly from a bag or can. If you stick to beer it can be a decent place to hang out with friends, as it is attractive and well maintained inside, but there are better places around town.

text: We went for lunch today. The room was beautiful and everyone was really nice. The food came out quick. It tasted very good but felt like it was a tiny bit pricey. A little noisy but it was a very dreary day so there were no open windows. I would definitely go again in the spring. The outdoor area looked really nice.

text: It was delicious, fast and wonderful. I called in my order it was ready when I got there. The people were very friendly. I was able to substitute the baking for a great which is great. It was no add a charge for that. They were very accommodating and friendly.

text:
This has 'college crowd' written all over it.  Laughing Planet is quirky, funky, and delicious, and you cannot help but walk out the door with a smile on your face after hanging out here for a bit.

The food has a major emphasis on healthy eating.  It is vegetable-heavy with lots of organic products, and as much house-made ingredients as they can muster.  You can find sandwiches, wraps, bowls, platters, and other familiar serving options.  But don't let the list of weird grains or veggies make you hesitate, as most everything here is very, very tasty.  The Thai Bowl is a constant favorite of mine, with fried tofu over brown rice and delicious Thai cole slaw.  You can also check out their rotating specials, such as today with their Lebanese Burrito loaded with spiced chicken, lentils, and yogurt sauce.  As far as beverages go, they have some great house-made iced teas, and a selection of kombuchas, too.  But for my money, I go with one of the various local beers they have on tap.  And speaking of money, I do have to say the prices are pretty decent, though not exactly what you'd call a cheap lunch either, but you get really good quality for the price.

This was the second location opened in Reno, and they did an amazing job fixing up this old house right across from campus.  The seating arrangements are plentiful, and the entire building looks amazing, with cool decor, potted plants, and historic photos festooning the walls and tables.  I love the upstairs lounge, but you also can't go wrong with their lovely outdoor patio.  The entire place has a great energy to it, and you just feel at home when you plunk down at your seat.  The service has also been very courteous and prompt, with orders coming up fairly quick even during lunch rushes.  Parking is usually pretty easy, but can get a bit tricky during the semesters, so you are better just walking or biking over.

I love that there is more food joints like this popping up in Reno, showing that this sort of grub doesn't have to be bland or joyless, but can be really tempting for even us carnivores to enjoy.

text: Food's halfway decent but the service here is awful. text:
So if you're reading my reviews in order, you'll know that the staff at Starbucks which are locals to Nola recommended Mother's Restaurant.  You'll also know that we were hungry the entire time in Nola due to long lines to eat because of Memorial Day Weekend.  Here we go, we turn the corner and guess what...there's a huge line in front of Mothers!  OH NOoooo!  We were at that point though that we said let's just wait in line. When we got to the back of the line, an employee was passing around menus to speed up the process.  We were told there was a 45 minute wait, "Growl" said my stomach.  Luckily, the staff must of eaten their Wheaties that morning because the line moved fast. We waited 20 minutes outside and another 10 inside, better than expected. 

You order at the counter and then choose a table. Many tables are communal and we ended up sharing one with a nice group from NYC. The feels of Mother's is authentic southern food, like it has so much history and so many people have dined there. They have old school photos on the walls and 3 dining rooms to choose from.  

The meal came 20 minutes later and it was just what I needed to calm the stomach monster.  Fried chicken, potato salad, beans, green beans and a local beer, Dixie.   I doused the fried chicken with some local hot sauce that was on the table that gave the chicken a kick.  Washed it down with Dixie Lager that was light but not unflavored.  The green beans were to die for. Best green bean salad I've ever had. They were warm with a slight vinegar taste. 

Extremely satisfying meal at Mother's. I was a different person walking out than I was coming in!  Oh yea a little heavier too! :) I recommend Mother's to anyone that wants a decent priced southern comfort meal, around $13 pp.  It's not fancy, just a casual place to eat hearty, worth waiting in line for.
name: Monica

text: First of all this place is extremely over priced for the quality of food they serve. Okay I ordered an omelette and there were bits of shell throughout. The bacon had an old taste to it. text:
I first came here a couple of years ago and it was great.  Giving a place a five star review on one visit is something I don't often do, so I went with 4.  but this last weekend I came back and had the Opening Act Omakase.  IT was sublime!  Best uni I've had in Florida (have had to go to Seattle or Tokyo for better).  The scallop was amazing, never mind about the toro.  But I won't bore you with each dish as since it is Omakase, you'll have to just see what you get based on what is best that week.  But do give it a try. 

I have this issue, I spent a month in Japan and having sushi in Florida pales in comparison.  So I stoped eating sushi in Florida for the most part.  But the other day my wife asked me what I wanted for my birthday and I said "really good sushi"  and Noble Rice jumped to mind and the fact it has been two years since I had tried them.  It was great then, and the idea of having an omakase dinner was perfect.  So we drove up from B-town and went, and it was.  If this place was closer I would be there all the time.  

Great service, 8 perfect bites of heaven.  What more do you want?  Oh, well we decided to have Saikyo King Salmon & Kinoko Gohan.  The mushroom rice.....so amazing and perfect.  The miso cured salmon is something to dream about.  The selection of sake, lovely.  

The quest for perfection and the striving to give the best possible experience and sublime food is found in a little spot in Tampa. text:
My in-laws moved near here and when my husband and I visited them we decided to check this place out. We went on a Saturday and arrived around 1:30-2. The restaurant was pretty empty and we were able to get seated right away. It was very clean inside and there were a lot of servers and people working so the service was pretty quick as well. 

My mother in law and her sister got overly excited about it being AYCE and ordered almost the entire menu... not really kidding about that at all. At one point I remember hearing my MIL saying "all of the seafood." We all got the AYCE hot pot and KBBQ option for around $30/person. They also have a sign that says that if there is food waste there will be a 20% surcharge on your bill. I started getting worried because they were ordering so much. I think something important to remember is that you can order more at any point, you don't have to order everything at the beginning. If you order as you go you can avoid the worry about finishing everything because you don't decide the portion of each side that comes out. There were 6 of us and we all decided to get our own broths for the hot pot. I got the special rib broth. It tasted like a standard beef broth, although it was a little bland. By the time they brought out what we ordered, they couldn't fit everything on the table. They had to leave a cart for us and all 3 shelves of the cart was full. I was starting to see my life flash before my eyes wondering how we were going to be able to finish everything. I'm not the biggest hot pot fan either so I knew I wasn't going to eat that much. One thing that I really liked about the hot pot was the sauce bar. I really liked being able to customize your own sauce. For the KBBQ I remember we ordered the bulgogi, LA Kalbi, and garlic pork belly.  I would probably not get the pork belly and the kalbi again. The pork belly was the really thinly sliced kind where if it's on the grill for longer than a minute it's overcooked and dry. The kalbi had good flavor, but I couldn't eat most of the rib because it was so fatty and barely had any meat on it. 
The bulgogi I thought was good though, it was a bit fattier than I would prefer, but it was very tender and had good flavor without being overly sweet. 
If I was only getting the barbecue I would have tried more of the meats, but seeing as how we still had so much hot pot ingredients to finish I knew we weren't going to be ordering any more. 

Although I don't think it's the best quality, it's certainly the best value! If you want to eat a ton for a price that you would usually pay at a Korean restaurant for a couple dishes I would definitely recommend this place. The eating area is clean and tidy, the workers are all friendly, fast and good and there are a ton of options. 

ALSO pro tip: Go when it's your birthday and you get to eat for free, but I would make sure that you have your ID on you to prove your birthday. Such a great deal!

text: In my opinion, this place has the best cheesesteaks in the area. The portions are huge and prices are in line with other typical pizza shops. text:
I would say this is a hidden gem of the dry spell of healthy food restaurants in this area. For one it is located inside powerhouse gym athletic club, but anyone can access it that is not a member. 

Since I am a member of the gym, I have more exposure to it. It also doubles as a supplement store, so sometimes I get protein or amino acids from them as well. They carry a lot of popular brands.

I am happy they expanded this restaurant to offer more food options than it did before it moved locations. They have so many selections to fit your diet whether your just wanting a nice healthy meal to macro counting for a meal plan. They can accommodate keto, gluten free, paleo etc...

They also have their own combinations of bowls, wraps, salads etc... if you don't want to customize. 

They have all the food freshly prepared and you can look to add what ingredients you want. They have more protein, base, and topping options than other restaurants of similar style. 

After a hard workout, I usually opt for a bowl. I get a lean protein with lots of vegetable toppings and a good carb. They are close to my job too, so sometimes I will order from here when I don't pack a lunch. They also offer their own pressed juices and protein shakes. Everything is made to order which I love.

text:
Good food and friendly staff! It's a just a little eating area in a small grocery store, but the food was absolutely delicious. I had the mixed fajitas (beef, chicken and shrimp), and I thought the seasoning on the fajita meat really put them above other fajitas I've had. It had a nice spice to it that went nicely with the fajita veggies. My friend is a vegetarian, and they didn't have much on the menu that was vegetarian (pescatarian really), but after talking with her for a few minutes, they were able to put something together for her, so she could have more than just chips and salsa/guac. She ended up with grilled tilapia, and I'll just say she didn't have any leftovers at the end of the meal. 

We also ordered the queso and the guac as appetizers while we waited. It was a white queso, not dressed up with much, but if you like cheese, you're probably going to like it. It was runny enough to easily scoop it up but not so runny that it wouldn't stay in the chip. The guac was a pretty standard guacamole dip. Hard to go wrong with that. 

This isn't the type of place to hang out for a long time enjoying a drink, but they did have a bottled beer selection, including the popular Mexican beers like Corona, Dos Equis, Negra Modelo, etc.

The grocery store also had a nice little selection of ice cream and desserts which we browsed after our meal.  They had other items too, of course. In talking with the owner, it sounds like they do a pretty good take out business and they have plans to expand in the future. The owner was very excited to chat with us about his food and his business. He even offered us a sample of some of their popular foods. He said his goal was to make Mexican food the way it was back home. I hope they keep up what they're doing and stay in business. Stop in and give this place a try!

text:
I happened to be in the area after a photo shoot one night, so we stopped in for dinner. It was a Wednesday night, so there was no crowd at all, even though the bar across the street was pretty packed for 7 in the evening.

I started with the calamari, which was very tasty and a nice start to the meal. We got a few rolls: salmon and avocado roll, tuna roll, crunchy dynamite roll, Royal roll and a rainbow roll. The salmon and avocado roll and tuna roll were perfect. The fish was super fresh and they had a lot of flavor. The rainbow roll was a typical rainbow roll and very tasty and fresh.

The Royal roll came was spicy tuna, snow crab, asparagus, fresh salmon, tuna, with ponzu sauce and spicy mayo. It was good, but if I ordered it again I would tell them to not include the spicy mayo. In fact, most of their specialty rolls are made with spicy mayo and that's just not something I need in a sushi roll. I dare say that if they didn't include it, no one would even notice and the roll would be a smidge healthier. 

I like that even though the special rolls are large, they are cut in such a way that makes them easier to handle and eat. There's nothing more frustrating than gracefully trying to fit a huge roll in your mouth.

All in all I liked my dinner. I've heard the ramen is excellent, so I might try it next time I'm in the area. The rolls are a little pricier than you can find elsewhere, but that's to be expected since it's near the Quarter.

Once we left we were laughing because we saw few other restaurants with practically no costumers. I guess the vibe here at Sambo's is really great! Cheers!

text:
Nice place to hangout especially in the summer. Who can resist the freshness of mango in the summer time??

We tried their mango mille crepes and greentea mille crepes. Mango taste better greentea. I had once tried thier pancakes, it basically only fruit and whipped cream wrapped. I will be back to try thier shaved ice and durian bowl

text: Potstickers were good but the lo-mein my boyfriend got weren't even cooked. They were just hard uncooked noodles and some peppers.

text:
If you want ambience, this place has it.  i kept looking around to see if Jimmy the Greek or Don Corleone was at a nearby table.  It's a classic heavy duty steak house.  Come prepared to eat ample portions and to drink hearty wines.  

We parked on the street and were taken immediately to our table.  The server was well-informed and entertaining.   The three of us ordered deep friend calimari for a starter; very tasty, could almost melt in your mouth.  For a main course, I went with the lamb chops; my colleagues selected the boneless sirloin tip.  Each came with multiple side offers.  I picked the baked potato and a salad.  It was all fresh and the lamb chops were to kill for.  For dessert, I took the key lime pie imported from Florida (the real thing) while my colleagues took an apple cobbler (delicious) and a chocolate cake (he ate it all).  

Two of us drank wine--I let the server pick a petit syrah for me, while the other drinker picked a cabernet sauvignon.  They were just right for this meal.  

I'm not a big meat eater, but this place is first rate if that is your preference.  We found parking on the street and the noise level inside was very reasonable.
name: Bob

text: Just stopped in tonight to grab dinner and so glad we did.  We tried the chicken, brisket, pork and smoked meat loaf. Sides of potato salad, mac-n-cheese, beans and greens. Husband said the greens were "to die for" and everything was absolutely superb! Some of the best damn BBQ sauce I've had in my life.  So nice to finally have a real BBQ place locally.  We will definitely be back for more.  Excellent quality!
name: Michelle

text: THIS PLACE!!!!  We are addicted to your love!  We go to Street Tacos at least twice a week, and when we don't go, we get withdrawal.  There is nowhere else we want to eat tacos!!!  Cool vibe, quick, accurate and friendly service, a wonderfully diverse menu, and the salsa bar ROCKS, compared to the competition.  Meats are tasty and tender, veg. options fresh and delightful.  Beers are great; bar service is on point.  Nothing not to love!! Please open a second location. We will never get tacos anywhere else in Tucson.  A true gem!!!
name: M

text:
First of all, the food here is amazing. My girlfriend treated me for dinner and props to her for picking this place. I thought they were understaffed at first but it was a slow rainy day. Service was awesome and we both left full. If you like lamb, falafel or gyros this is the place for it! Didn't get to see the belly dancers cuz it was on the wrong day lol

Definitely recommend!!!! Enjoy yourself!
name: CJ

text: I love this restaurant! And they are the only one (that I know) that serves absinthe. Thumbs up!!!!!!!
name: Nhu

text: Arriving here, you would see a big parking space and a small building with the name "sweet spot" on it. The cafe is pretty spacey and there is no obvious start to the line so you would need to follow how the locals lined up. Food wise, I like how they have choices of donuts and other breakfast items such bagels. I ordered the bacon, egg and cheese bagels and ordered some donuts. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. For a busy night they handled it okay. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. I wouldn't write it off, but I also wouldn't hype it up. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent.

Every night is special at the Buck, because there are specials every night at the Buck, from the time you walk in the door and are greeted and seated, to the time that you leave with that great full feeling.                                             
You will love the Buck !

text:
Good pizza. Delicious beer. Slow service from the bar and the flight of beer (4 beers) was $14!! That's double what most places charge. 

I'll be back. I won't buy a flight.

text: What the heck happened??? Fifendekel was once the pinnacle of good pie in Edmonton now it's the pits. Gone is their thick, flakey signature crust now replaced with a thin, tasteless one. The creamy, hand stirred, yummy, egg based, custard fillings replaced with starch based,bounce back, stick to your mouth, gobs of pure yuckiness. And the mounds of fresh cream topping, and gorgeous, thick piped, rosettes replaced with a thin swipe of cream, and a small edge of piping. Even the fruit fillings that used to be big, bright, and chunky, look like they were poured out straight from a can. Asked to stay or to go? Did it matter??? Even the in-house experience was lost on thin plastic plates with plastic forks rather than a dish and cutlery. The whole experience a loss. The only "upside"??? A reduction in price which "almost" reflects the reduction in quality. Oh Fifendekel...who did this to you my old friend? So sad.
name: Judy

text:
Confession: this is my favorite local restaurant in the Temple Terrace area, and perhaps my favorite Vietnamese restaurant of all time. I visit the restaurant about once per week. At this point, I am surprised that I did not write a review sooner. 

Saigon Bay is family owned and the wait staff are very friendly. I could go on and on about this wonderful family, who I am now on a first name basis with, but instead I'll stick to the basics. 

I highly recommend the beef pho, any of the fried rice options, the pork bun, pork chop platter, and the spring rolls with shrimp. More often than not, I order the beef pho with extra beef and ask for a side of the chili oil. When you come in they will tell you to pick out a table and will follow the basic routine. Definitely ask for their recommendations. Jason (a wonderful server) has often recommended the fish (I believe it's a whole salmon). 

I plan to continue making this place an affordable and regular part of my week; attending with friends, family, and USF colleagues. 

Thank you Saigon Bay!
name: Kristopher

text:
The hubby's coworker brought donuts in from here, and he really liked them. He kept saying that I would too.

So it was nice that they have a drive thru...
Even though I had a really good steak breakfast, I thought this was going to be a nice finishing touch!

Hmmm I ordered a chocolate and maple bar.. was thinking the real test of a donut shop is how well they can do a glazed... (good thing I didn't add on a glazed)!

The best glazed donuts are in San Jose, called Ben's...
It's a simple donut shop and the lines are super long.

My ex-sister-in-law would always get me a dozen for the holidays!

Anyway, I was really disappointed! Barely enough frosting to cover the bar and really oily tasting. Only had one bite and that was enough for me.

I'll keep dreaming of the glazed at Ben's!

text:
After seeing 1.3k reviews with a 4-star average thought we should give it a try.  I'm a bit confused about the hype.  It was an average restaurant with pretty average food.  Limited menu on the first floor.  Now looking further into reviews I noticed there are typically other food options on different floors.  Either these areas were closed or the host didn't tell us.

Girlfriend got the Local Yokel which she said wasn't good and didn't finish it.  I got the burger which was your normal average medium size burger.  The reason for the 3 star review instead of lower is due to the live music.  Stellar band was playing.  Wish the food matched the bands quality.

It was 11 pm they had only half of the menu available and when I asked why the guy working the drive through had the berve to say there was only 2 people working! That is not an excuse that is laziness. The drive thru had aa sign that they close at12 am  how if theybare open 24 hours? This is the most ridiculous McDonald's i have ever been too! This is absolutely absurd. DO NOT GO TO THIS MCDONALDS! THEY ARE LAZY AND DO REFUSE TO DO THERE JOBS!

text: Want to counter Joe's S. review from last night.  We had the unfortunate experience of sitting next to him as he was calling the waitress stupid and telling the owner to shove his free antipasto platter because it should have been free wine.  You'd think he would want food and not more alcohol after waiting "so long" for a table.  I get he wasn't happy about waiting, but the owner, John, did his best to make it up to him.  Nothing was going to please "Joe".  My husband and I have been going to Avalon for years, since their original location, and are never disappointed.  The food is always delicious and the wait staff always courteous and attentive, and last night was no different.  The ricotta gnocchi melted in my mouth and the braised short ribs were amazing.  We did have a short wait for our table, but the restaurant was packed.  You don't pack that many people in if Joe's review was anywhere near accurate.  And having a drink first at the bar and listening to the live music was more than enjoyable.  Didn't mind our wait at all because the food was more than worth it.

text: Great spot with great waiters.  Their beers hit the spot and their burgers were awesome.  I loved the blond and the wheat/ginger.  My husband had the cider they had on tap.  The deck outside has misters for when the weather is hot!

I had a Belgian waffle with eggs and bacon, my boyfriend had pancakes. My waffle felt a little overdone since it was crispy and dark brown. In the summer it's fun to get your blizzard and sit outside. Turnover is kind of high with high school students, but I think that's normal. Also a great date spot...with my wife.

text:

There are also two small restaurants inside that I have yet to try - but they looked really good! I will definitely be coming back soon!

text: Hands down my favorite local burger spot! Thank you so much for coming to downtown Carmel! I love that you can get a salad instead of fries as a side (husband & I usually get opposite sides & share!). The quality of meal has always been superb. We went elsewhere one night (not a true burger place) & I was craving a burger, but then was so let down & went back to you all the next week...that's what I get for branching out

name: User

text:
My husband and I came here for my daughter's 19th birthday. She specifically requested Irwin's so although I did not choose to come here I ended up really liking the place. We made a reservation online and it was very simple. 
It is just so odd to walk into a former Bok High School because it looks like it is still a functioning school (but it is not). Since this school was designed by Irwin who also designed many other Philly schools they all have the same "feel". 
Parking is a bit difficult because the lot that Irwin's and Bok Bar use across from the building was closed. The neighborhood is very typical South Philly so parking is not a forte for this section of the city. 

Both the restaurant and the bar are on the 8th floor. We opted to dine al fresco since it was such a nice day. Our server Jeanine (sp?) was super friendly, helpful, accommodating, and funny. I felt like I knew her from way back, she is that type of a person. Irwin's is very lucky to have her work there! 

All the food we ordered came out very good! My favorites were Carrot Fritters, Lamb Kofta, and Tahini Brownie! Aside from the awesome food and service, you have to come here for the view! The restaurant deck is a nice open space and the view is okay. However, just go across and go to the Bok Bar terrace, especially the night skyline view is amazing!
name: YangHwa

text: Delicious donuts. But the best part were the two girls working there very pleasant and helpful, just all the round refreshing customer service, thank you.
name: Dawn

text:
So we are in Tucson for a few days, checking out the Gem & Fossil show, and we forgot it was Valentines week. Usually, I dont like going out on Valentines day because it seems the restaurants jack up their prices but, we were able to get in at The Keg Steakhouse in Oro Valley at a very last minute, I was soo happy there were some opening slots available. 

When we first arrived, they placed us in booth almost to the kiddie korner - which is nice, I love big booth so I have space.  But, as we sat down and waited for awhile, we notice that our server hasnt been over to our table nor water service. However, because we were waiting there for sometime, the server finally came over and there was some mix up, he apologized profusely and we were all good because he came over and recognized the situation and handle it very quickly! He also told his manager who also came over and apologize and we were really okay but, shocked and happy of their service.  dont know what it is but, Tucson community seem so nice, laid back, and relaxing! 

Food was excellent - my 2nd time dining at the Kegs Steakhouse but, first time at this location and It was the BEST VALENTINEs DINNER I had and I am not much of a steak person my husband and for me I really have to be either 1.) SUPER HUNGRY (which I was) 2.) In the mood to eat Steak (Which I was) but, I love their filet mignon and lobster tail - it just hit the spot with our Mushroom Neptune and shared Iceberg lettuce.

And having our pinot noir!  

All the staff and including our waiter was so generously nice, great customer service, ambiance is peaceful, relaxing, and beautiful and again, food is amazing!
name: Millie

text: So excited to have a new restaurant with a great patio and roof top! The food and cocktails are on point as well! You must try the butcher's choice - super tender steak covered in chimichurri sauce! Come see Laura at the bar!

text: I'm a New Yorker so I know good pizza.  The pizza here is really good with a delicious crust that is unique BUT this establishment looses 3 stars because they are not sanitary and pose a health risk to all those that eat here.  The cashier in the front (pink hair) handles your pizza with his bare hands AND in the same swoop he collects your dirty money.  You read it correct, he's both the server and the cashier.  GROSSSSS!!!  When I told him "you know you're wrong for handling the money and the food", he took a long pause and said "well what do you want, them to hire a separate person just to handle the money?".  I said Yes! or use gloves....DUH!!!!

text:
Big miss. Took my office staff after Christmas for dinner, what a mess. Waited 45 minutes for my martini, and all they could say was that they had one bartender for the entire restaraunt. I don't mind paying $68 for a steak, but the service better be on par. Unfortunately in this case, both the food and the service were off.
There are too many great steakhouses in the area to have sub par food and/or service. So, this one is off my list!

I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The food was good and the service was easygoing. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer..
name: User

text:
This isn't your usual review, but I firmly believe in complimenting when someone does a good job. 

I went to this McDonalds this morning, and I only went for a sweet tea. I was greeted by this sweet, soft spoken young man at the pay window. Not only did he do his job right, he was so polite, professional and kind, asking how my day was going. 

When I get to the second window to pick up my tea, I was greeted by yet another very polite young man, with a big, sincere smile. He promptly handed me my order and told me to have a nice day, the smile never left his face. 

I can't tell you if the food was good or not, I haven't eaten at this McDees in probably a year or more. But these young men were so professional and kind, I felt I had to say something. Especially in this day and age where millennials are disrespectful and don't want to work. These young men were an asset to the place. I hope they stay like that, they'll go far in the work world. 

Wish I'd gotten their names, I didn't think. But both of them deserve some sort of commendation.  Well done, guys!
name: Kc

text: Lovely little spot with a great patio, artistic atmosphere and a good menu. (Connected to the art museum but still worth going if you're not visiting the museum). Breakfast burrito was one of my favorites I've had. Seasoned Barista's and espresso here- I ordered a traditional macchiato and it was excellent.
name: Riley

text: This place is amazing! Half fish market, half restaurant. The lobster roll is out of this world and so is everything else on the menu. I normally get a lobster roll or the alligator bites. This is by far my favorite place to get quick seafood.
name: Jackson

text:
We came here for dinner our 2nd night in town. The food was incredible. The service was a tad slow, which we only noticed due to having 2 children at our table.

But talk about a tale of two visits. We came here for lunch a few days later, much smaller menu than dinner. We ordered our drinks, 3 people ordered the sangria, big mistake. The sangria was as bitter as bitter can be with zero flavor. After our drinks were delivered, we didn't see our waitress for roughly 15-20 minutes. My father in law had to go in twice to let them know our drinks were bad and we needed new ones. 

  The drinks were bad, the food ordering was limiting and the service was inexcusable.
name: Ryan

text: They have new owners. Soft opening was today. Excellent service. The food was impressive.  This is not your typical beach bar food restaurant.  I wish I would have taken a picture of my grouper with orange chutney and black rice. Best I've had on the island and the presentation was beautiful.  Felt like I was at a high end venue. My husband had the roasted chicken which was cooked to perfection. We also had the oyster stew that was full of flavor and fresh oysters. We were their first customers so the owners bought us a free round of drinks. (Margaritas need improvement.) The owners were friendly and welcoming. They have multiple televisions for watching your favorite sports too! Make sure you check this place out. Can't wait to go back!
name: Deborah

text: Delicious seafood right on the marina in Santa Barbara. Clem chowder was good as were the oysters. The clam strips were a little heavy on the breading with a sweet note in the breading. Overall good service and good food.
name: Melissa

text: Super tasty and fresh. Really enjoyed the spring rolls and pork belly banh mi. Savory and bright flavors. Great crunch and then softness in the bun. Juicy shrimps in the rolls.
name: Chris

text: I grew up in Southern California where Rubio's was a staple in our rotation. So, on a recent trip to Tampa I was so excited to see it had made its way to the east coast! If you're in the market for more authentic "Fresh Mex" flavors than you typically encounter in this part of the country, try Rubio's! Seriously though, I had two lunches on the same day just so I could get my Rubio's fix, much to the surprise (read: horror) of my boyfriend.
name: Moore

text: This is the very best bar in Boise! Their food is extremely delicious. Everyone that works there is awesome! Big shout outs to Jules, Rachel, and Dusty for providing such a great time every occasion that I've stopped by!
name: Chris

text: I'm in Philly 1-2 times per year and after trying out most if not all of the "top" cheese steak places in the city I have settled in Lorenzo's as my clear favorite.  The cheese steak is classic Philly with perfect bread, juicy steak, and the appropriate cheese options, which are generously applied.  Don't skip out on a slice of pizza while there as well because it's amazing.  The crust has the perfect chew and the toppings always seem to be in the perfect ratio.  The guys who run the place are a great group as well and it's always a fun and pleasant trip.  I absolutely recommend Lorenzo's as a must try.
name: Sean

text: Very good Greek food.  My wife and I usually get the Gyro platter.  Always bring food home.  Will be returning again and again.
name: Ron

text:
Five stars for this local Chinese restaurant conveniently located in downtown Waterloo located across from the Monroe County Courthouse. 101 North Market Street. There are red lanterns hanging outside and a large sign in the parking lot, but sign on store was not lit. Parking lot is safe, but store itself doesn't look open and inviting. 
We popped in on a Monday evening before Christmas. No waiting. There is a hot bar where you can load up with one- two- ($5.75) or three- entrees  ($6.25) with steamed rice or loMein and crab Rangoon or egg roll. Eight entrees to choose from for Ja's hot bar. Hot pepper chicken and beef broccoli were my favorite. We brought home $25 worth of food, fed five adults (Chinese buffet style at home) with enough leftover for three more lunches. 
Portions are generous, staff friendly, no msg in this quick service Chinese restaurant. Glad we took it to go, inside dining area is more like an outdated fast food restaurant--no ambience, but there was a Christmas tree!
name: Jill

text: Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The food was good and the service was easygoing. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon.
name: User

text: Love the food! Super fresh , waiter are kinda nice but I love the food and the boba tea !!
name: Vijen

text: Dierks, I love your music and we were so excited to come to your bar tonight. The band was a lot of fun and the only reason I'm giving the place 2 stars. At the end of the night it was a complete down pour and I was waiting for my uber which was at the light across the street. I was standing in the awning to avoid getting soaked. Your security boys repeatedly pushed the door into my back to push me onto the sidewalk and would not let me back inside to escape the rain when I asked. They threatened to call the police which I told them to do because I had  broken no laws. My friends and I celebrated a birthday and spent a significant amount of time and money at your establishment. I never expect to be treated that way simply to get into a safe ride home. Shame on your staff. I was not belligerent nor drunk. No one should he treated that way.
name: Leigh

text:
One-of-a-kind service. Must experience it to believe it!

If you do nothing else, you've got to visit this Popeyes. You'll find rude service, long wait times, mixed up orders and a staff that acts as if they're generally intolerant of your existence. The reviews can't fully describe it. You just have to go there, but only when you've got some time on your hands. It's a national treasure. They get one star because the food, when you finally get the correct order, is delicious! And because you can't give zero stars.
name: Esther

text: I have to share a story about what happened here last night. First a little back story, my fiancé and I came here on our first date almost 2 1/2 years ago. Last night after a performance at the Old National Center we decided to come for a late dinner. The food as always was outstanding and as we were chatting with our server Danny we mentioned this, and that our wedding was in a week. Later when Danny came back with the check he informed us that once a month he's able to do something special for a guest and our entire bill for the evening was going to be a penny. Our jaws hit the table, we've never had anything like that happen to us before so thank you Danny! Thank you Eagle for being a special place that empowers your people to make special memories for your guests. As someone who has been in the industry his whole life I can tell you that is so very rare. You now have lifelong fans! See you again soon!
name: PJ

text:
My second time here. I was a little let down. I was here 3 years ago and since I know that some things change I didn't know it would go down. I made reservations to eat here the night before we drive to NYC. I was pumped up about the food remembering how it was a few years back. We arrived there on time and only waited a few minutes to be seated. I gave specific instructions on the seating arrangements and they were not met. This place wasn't packed, roughly 50%occupied. Before we walked in, we reviewed previous comments about Relish and they were not good. 

They still have the live band playing across the way by the bar and they were ok. The waitress walked up to us about 3 minutes after we sat down. I got a Long Island and my lady got a Gin&Tonic. They were not good. They did get there quick. Our appetizers didn't take long to come which was a blessing cause a brutha was hungry! The entrees didn't take long either. The food was just ok. The staff was great except for the host who gave me bad seating. Again, the food was just ok. It was like bad foreplay. I am a guy of second chances but I'm not sure about this one. I'm not sure if it's new management but whatever it is, it should be better. We spent $126.00 on food and tip for a meal I could have eaten at my cousins house. Let's not mention the cost to ride Uber to and from there. Exactly 5 miles away from the hotel and a straight shot. We decided to Uber because I wanted to be responsible because I was ready to get nice and tipsy.  That alcohol was like watered down Kool-Aid...SMH
name: Reggie

text: Antipasto salad was mostly lettuce.  Dressing was mediocre at best.  Salad was missing pepper Cheaneys olives and noodles to be claimed as an antipasto salad.  Pizza wasn't cooked in the middle but tasted great no the outside.  Super busy and there wasn't enough help.  Left without the extra sauce I asked for as we were tired of waiting.  Will try again and undated review.
name: True

text:
I thought it would be hard to find parking but it is not that hard. Far away from the normal downtown scene or French Quarter, on the rooftop of The Pontchartrain Hotel. This rooftop bar is small dimmed and with very relaxing music. The wine list holds some very good French wines and the list of alcoholic drinks is quite nice. 
It is one of the most amazing views of the city. You can see the Mississippi River, the bridge towards the WestBank and the super dome. Very unique views. The music not so loud makes this bar a place to easily conversaré with other people. It's a good place to start your night as it doesn't close extremely late but also you do not want to go there and party. Perfect for dates as well, specially if you just finished eating at one of the magnificent restaurants in the hotel or the area. Their drinks are well priced and the service is nothing less that great. I would recommend this to anyone looking to get some beautiful night views of the city get a drink and not have some crazy person ruin your night.
name: Immanuel

text:
This is such a cute little dessert place in Chinatown. 
This place is known for lower sugar choices. It's a matcha heaven. 
I ordered the matcha latte and it was perfect. 
The lychee panna cotta was also delicious. The perfect balance between sweet and tart.
name: Lacey

text: The service here is horrible! Sat down and waited 15+ minutes for a waitress to arrive. We were finally able to order asked her specifically what came on my sandwich. Placed our order and another 30 minutes later our very basic order finally arrived. My sandwich was covered in pickles. I told the server that is wasn't suppose to have pickles, but after waiting so long I didn't want to wait another 30 min for a new sandwich. Waitress finally shows up and wants to argue what she told me, luckily I had a witness. When I mention the wait time for my order and the fact that many other tables that came in after me had already been served and were almost done, she says "oh Kitchen is doing shift change"....uhm then how are all these other tables getting food? From there she disappears and I don't see her again the whole meal until my bill finally arrived. She removed the sandwich from my bill from what I noticed, never bothered to apologize or mention she took it off the bill. This was my first time and will be my last time..Hope they don't really bring Zion here, if this is the best in town the Pelicans will never sign him
name: Eric

text: They're good. It's solid. They're quick for hot food. I actually look forward to flying out of A terminal knowing I can stop here for some comfort food before a long flight.

text:

The customer service was friendly, but awfully slow. I waited in line for about 5 minutes for someone to take my order. There were two people in line ahead of me, all who were grumbling about the wait. 

When the food arrived, I did not get what I ordered. Not only that, but the burger and fries I got were cold for some reason. They were fine with providing me a new one. I can only surmise that I came here on an off day, or to a badly managed location.

Either way, I have a hard time believing that the construction had something to do with this, which is why I would avoid this place.

text: Nosotros estuvimos preocupados cuando entramos en el Taco Maya nuevo, pero fuimos equivocado ser porque estuvimos atónito de el nuevo gigantesco, pintoresco edificio. Nosotros estuvimos apasionado sobre los paredes manchados dentro del restaurante viejo que le dio carácter, pero este tienda nueva superó nuestras expectativas. La comida auténtico que fue servido dentro de este restaurante jovial valió la pena el comercio de mi dinero. El restaurante fue muy accesible y los precios bajos que fue bien para nuestro presupuesto sin duda hizo esta reseña un 5/5 porque nosotros lo pasamos bien. También, nosotros subestimado la calidad de la comida y porque era tan inesperado, estábamos inquieto para volver. La única cosa enfermante sobre el restaurante es que nosotros estuvimos equivocado sobre la comida cuando pensamos que lo fue venenoso por la razón de que la lechuga con E coli en nuestra zona. Los propietarios son confiable y serio y se aseguran que la comida natal siempre es fresca. Aunque estamos agradecidos por el nuevo restaurante, echamos de menos el chapado a la antigua restaurante anterior. Este restaurante debe ser galardonado  el mejor a nivel nacional y posiblemente a nivel internacional. Preferiría morirse de hambre que ser un testigo a este restaurante en vías de desarrollo en una cadena.

text:
A good German Doner Kebab is one of my very favorite foods. I've chased that specific taste in numerous countries over the years, but for me, nowhere comes close to the German style. This place really hit the spot!

The beef/lamb Kebab was outstanding. The meat was lean and tasty. Some places use ground meat, but I much prefer this style which is actual thin slices. The bread was also perfect, pressed nice and thin with just the right amount of crispness. I'm so happy to have found a great German Doner outside of Germany! I will definitely stop back at this place on future trips through Santa Barbara. Thanks for bringing German style Doners to Southern California!!

PS: the reviewer(s) claiming this is some kind of wrongful "cultural appropriation" are ridiculous. Everyone knows kebabs originate from the Middle East. Kebabs are now available in most of the world now though, and are often influenced by the local cuisine. A German Doner is a very specific thing and should definitely be advertised as such. I certainly would have never even tried eating here if they didn't advertise that it's German. Check Wikipedia for more info. Their Doner Kebab article has a huge subsection on "Regional Variations," with several paragraphs specifically dedicated to Germany. Here are a couple interesting highlights:

Even orders placed in the Turkish language in Berlin will ask for the hot sauce using the German word "scharf", flagging the hybrid nature of the Berlin style of döner kebap. This variation served with pita bread has influenced the style of döner kebap in Germany and in other nations. A 2007 survey showed that many people consider the döner kebab to be the most characteristic food of Berlin.

Annual sales of döner kebabs in Germany amounted to €2.5 billion in 2010... Tarkan Taşyumruk, president of the Association of Turkish Döner Producers in Europe (ATDID), provided information in 2010 that, every day, more than 400 tonnes of döner kebab meat is produced in Germany by around 350 firms.
name: scott

name: Nick

text:
I rarely give 1s....and when I do it, I do it VERY judiciously since it takes a reasonable amount of not being happy with my food to do so.  In fact, I would like to give it a 1.5 because there were a couple of bright tastebud bright spots.

Admittedly, this review is LONG overdue (we went in June and yes, I still remember the food), but given the experience I recently had at Favoloso I want to get this one in....and yes, I still have the photos from my culinary outing at Franco's to show my experience.

Every year, with my teaching team, we go for a "end of the school year" dinner and this year, because others had mentioned it and more so, Franco's is considered "really good" and "you have to go" types of comments, we went.  One my colleagues told us that it is very good and that we would eat well.  Well, let's just say I have a different appreciation for melted cheese after having eaten here.

Why we didn't order the pizza is still a mystery.  This being said, I am not convinced I would have been any happier.  I will say, the staff is nice enough and attentive, and it is nice that they have outdoor seating for the summer months.

Off to our food.  I was in the mood for pasta so I ordered the Rotini with sausage.  The description of the dish said it was a sauce with sausage and I definitely got sauce and sausage.  The sauce was over the top in terms of flavours and the sausage was quite sweet for me.  It was served with toasted bread (something I don't understand with all the amazing bread now that you can get, even from Costco, to accompany any dish).  While the rotini were al dente, it was not a great dish.  Too much in terms of flavours in the sauce and it just didn't do it.  Alongside this, we also ordered the lasagne which were more baked cheese and sauce wth a few sheets of lasagne.  My colleague needed a spoon to eat it :-/ with all the WATERY sauce there with the melted cheese.  Yes, I did say watery sauce .... in fact, once tasted, my colleague didn't finish it and let's just say, it was a bit of a downhill culinary experience from there.  I will say that we ordered the Fried Calamari appetizer which were quite good and we did enjoy.  They have a reasonable selection of wines at a good price per bottle.

No, we didn't order the dessert....for me, I had wasted already too many calories to risk anymore.  

IF it should happen I EVER go back because friends insist, I will...this being said, I will SHARE a very SMALL pizza and only a small pizza so I can hopefully have a better experience than this one.
name: Antonella

text: Ordered through Eat24 run by GrubHub to pick up food on a Monday night about 6:00 pm. text: This place is seriously delicious. The people that work there are extremely awesome as well! My husband, mother-in-law and I went for brunch and we're not disappointed. We got the Firebird, Ralphie Deluxe and Bam. Everyone was very pleasantly full ;) we will be back and hope everyone eats there so they stick around!

text:
A solid personal hot pot place that won't force you to make a trip down to LA to satisfy your craving. 
A good price point for the area. 

Taste is similar to other personal hot pot joints I've tried. I'm always a beef fan, so I like to go with the beef hot pot, medium spicy.
They have 3 types of dipping sauces (chili oil, chili paste, garlic soy sauce) for you, I always like to mix all 3. Hopefully they offer more variety in the future! 

Servers are friendly and working hard. Also only lunch time is when they have a free tea with your meal! Eventually they will have their own teas, but for now they have some canned chinese classics like Jia Duo Bao, which is one of my favs~

As the only personal hot pot place here with the right taste, that alone deserves 5 stars. Blessed that they even decided to open one in this area!!
name: Vivian

text: Alright, my first visit here was good. This time it lacked everything. I ate to eat. The falafel was crispy and warm... that's about it. I had a few leaves on my plate... I think it was supposed to be a salad? The pita, *sigh* it's store bought. My husband had the chicken shawarma plate- pretty sure it was a plain chicken plate. Okay, so falafel plate, chicken plate, side of pita, side of hummus $35. What a disappointment. Won't be back.
name: M

text: I am a big fan of chocolate so if you are then this is the place to go. I got the fondue set which was amazing! I would def recommend to any chocolate lovers to try
name: Reema

text:
This place is big, a lot of tables & a big bar! Our waitress was Priscilla and she was very good & very helpful.  My husband had the wings, he said they were good.  My daughter had chicken nuggets with 2 different sauces, she liked them.  I thought they were fair.  The outside seemed a little over cooked, so I thought they had a slightly burnt taste.  I had the made to order sandwich, grilled chicken with the honey lime siracha sauce, which I liked, however they did forget the pickles.   Both times our beers came out we were given the wrong ones.  That was a problem between the bar & waitress, but luckily we know what our beers taste like & switched.  It's a typical chain restaurant food, not bad, not great.  I'll try it again. 
       Went back tonight with a friend and sat at the bar.  It took 10 mins before a bartender came over to get us a drink.  We ordered the trio dip app, which took 45 mins to come out.  We were told the wait was because they were making fresh guacamole.  What a joke, it takes 5 mins to make guacamole lol.   My second beer, I was given the wrong one, I knew immediately & it was rectified.  I'll leave my rating at 3, once again, I may return but I'm in no hurry too. 
     Second time tonight.  Ordered a beer, waitress came back, they were out.  Picked a second beer, waitress came back, they were out.  UPDATE YOUR LIST!   Ended up with a Blue Moon.  Was looking forward to the chicken avocado salad they have shown on their FB page, but they don't have the new summer items.  Got the chicken Fiesta salad, it was ok.  My son got the rice with his kids meal. It was old, dry & crusty.  Terrible they would even serve that.   The place was empty for dinner time Sunday night.  After reading all the bad reviews I'm sure people just aren't returning.  I'm in no hurry to return. 
   I was surprised when we pulled in this place was empty.  I felt bad for our server, she was so happy to have a table to wait on, so she was great.  The food was good. The weird thing was our check took off $4.17 for being a reward member & .83 for our pretzel bites.  Since our server was new she asked a manger about it.  He came back and apologized for the entire $5 not coming off since we had a free app on our card.  However the new check did not take off the $5 but now only took off $4.10 & charged us .90 for the pretzels.  .7 cents more! (Which is all they were worth, tasted liked super pretzels cooked in a microwave).   Maybe this is why the place is empty, shouldn't be so much confusion when there isn't even any customers 
    This was definitely my last time there.  We were upcharged $1 for Sweet potato fries on a kids meal.  Then charged .50 for an xtra hot sauce because the waitress miss understood the order and brought out half my husbands wings dry.  I hate places that nickel & dime you for everything.
name: Jennifer

text: I couldn't wait to write this review, so here I sit eyeballing my empty basket. Now this is big because I have about 5 - 10 reviews I haven't had time to write still. I've always wanted to have Nashville hot chicken because, well, I love fried chicken and I love hot. I found a parking spot and hurried around the corner before the line got too long. Yes, you heard me right... THERE WAS A LONG LINE! It wasn't terrible because I got there right as they opened but as we waited people kept coming and coming and by time I got to the door the line was around the block! I got inside and the aroma of fried hot chicken alone was awesome!i ordered a 3 piece tender combo with homemade pimento Mac and cheese and collard greens. I got my tea and found a place to sit out front. When I got my food I didn't even know where to start. I moved my side dishes out of the way and dug right in, starting with the Mac and cheese. It was some of the best I ever had! So cheesy and flavorful! The greens were what you would expect with little bits of bacon adding a smokiness and saltiness to counteract the bitter greens. And now the chicken. This is honestly (don't tell granny) the best fried chicken I have ever put in my mouth! It is hand breaded to perfection and the hot aspect was so good. I ordered hot( you can also get mild, medium, or damn hot) but this is nashville so I had to try hot. It was just spicy enough to make your nose run and sweat a little, but oh so flavorful! I love everything about this place from the music, to the servers and the ambiance. This place is a must if you're in Nashville, find a way to get here, and wait in line you won't regret it!
name: Jacob

text: Great well seasoned food! Very cost effective!! One of the best meals I had while visiting!
name: Rachel

text:
Decided to give this place a try with the nice weather and views of Geist!

The staff wasn't over friendly or helpful, and the service was kind of slow, so if this is important to you probably isn't the best spot for you, but I've had worse. 

You can dress up or down. There was a mix of dressy and people coming off the boat in athletic wear and swim attire, so I don't think there's necessarily a dress code.

The margarita was okay, tasted like normal mix. I also tried the smokehouse nachos which were good. There were good flavors and the bbq pork was good, needed a tiny bit more queso though, over 3/4 if the chips were completely bare. 

Overall though this is a nice place for a quick casual snack or dinner with a gorgeous view. May be back again.
name: Heather

text:
We hired Tim's BBQ for a company event and open house.  We were so happy that we did.

The service was exceptional - Tim came out for a site visit before the event so that we could plan everything in advance.

He also worked with us to make the cost of the catering fit our budget.

The food was fabulous!  We are still receiving compliments on the BBQ.  There was almost nothing left . . .

I recommend wholeheartedly.
name: Sandra

text: New favorite BBQ spot. We were surprised to see that the little Brazilian joint closed but in its place something much, much better. The place is a cute little spot with simple dining tables and a self serve beverage fridge.  I ordered T's Famous Fried Chicken (of course) with a biscuit and a side of Mac and cheese. The breading of the chicken is so simple yet so delicious. It's so obviously real, juicy chicken cooked to perfection but that breading is another level. The biscuit was coated with an almost crumble like topping loaded with spices and I could not stop eating it.  The Mac and cheese was real penne pasta and made from scratch.  My husband ordered the two meats platter, the brisket and peach wood pulled pork with the potato chip casserole and cucumber/tomato salad. Seeing that we share all good (one of the best parts of marriage) everything was absolutely delicious.  Used to drive down to Sweet Lucy's for bbq but we now have a new spot. Definitely worth it, check it out!!
name: Giovanna

text:

The yaki burger is the fire bomb booyah schnizz.  

Hopefully they'll get popular enough to upgrade the location.

text:
I had planned this evening carefully, and made the reservation weeks before the day. My sister and I celebrate our birthdays together (September) and this year it was my choice of restaurant. I really wanted
Cajun food, and there are at least 3 choices within Edmonton, however I decided to go with Cajun House. The place itself is attractive and the service was really excellent. Three of our party were pleased with their meals as they seemed substantial and tasty. My husband and I, not so much, and mine was extremely disappointing. I contacted them directly (after the night) and received no reply whatsoever. To me, this should be part of attentive customer service. Let me mention here that seldom do I complain about a meal. For a 'po'boy' sandwich that costs as much as a huge plate of Jambalaya or pasta, I would have expected to get MUCH more than a tiny bun, with 3 deep-fried oysters, tomato and some alfalfa sprouts. So much for my birthday dinner! I gave it 2 stars for the fact that the wait staff was excellent and the others within my party enjoyed their meals.
name: Shannon

text:
I have lived in Sparks for over 26 years and know WV like the back of my hand.
I have lodged at the hotel a few times before and after it was remodeled and overall, I am quite impressed. Each room is cozy and clean with fancy lamps all around and a huge HDTV. Nice Italian paintings and a decent view of the surrounding foothills. Also, the beds are super comfy with plenty of covers and soft pillows. Oh, and the marble counters, add another plus.
My only complaint is the noise. While trying to sleep, I heard doors slamming shut constantly during check-in hours (to no fault of the renters, the door bolts are just  noisy!) Plus, some guy was blasting his stereo in another room for about an hour and I was about to call the front desk, but he finally turned it down.
So, minus the occasional sounds, the hotel is quite decent and has a decent price.
I'm not a gambler, so I visit the casino for the food. Cafe Ballini (formerly "The Marina Cafe") has decent food, but not always fresh. I recently ordered a club sandwich and although it looked good, I hardly tasted it. However, their breakfasts are to die for! I ordered biscuits and gravy with fried eggs and it was perfect! The surroundings are attractive and the servers are quite friendly.
I also get to go orders from PRIMO. Their burritos are the best I've ever eaten! Loaded with veggies and taco meat in a whopper size, you can't go wrong! They also offer excellent tacos and hot dogs. The food quality at this stand has not changed since I've lived here, perfect every time. I always order to go because the tables are usually occupied and are way too small for my size.
The Steak House is very comfortable and relaxing. We used to dine their on Christmas Eve every year. Good sea-food, especially the crab legs.
Pancho and Willies has attractive Spanish decor, cozy fireplace, and complimentary chips and salsa, but the main course is hit or miss. I've ordered enchiladas that were mushy, while the steak tacos were on the mark!
Nice to have so many eating choices and the cafe is open 24 hours.
WV is an ideal place for locals or anyone visiting. It's right off the highway too, convenient.
name: Ryan

text:
There was nothing wrong with Crescent City Brewhouse, but there was nothing overly exciting about it either. I think it's fairly busy because of its location and the fact that they're one of the only local breweries in the touristy area of New Orleans. The first night we tried to go they said there was a 40 minute wait so we passed. The second night we went much later and were able to be seated right away. 

Their Weiss beer was really tasty and had solid flavors of bananas and cloves. That was really the highlight of my meal to be honest. The fresh shucked oysters were good but they're oysters, you can get them anywhere really. I would have enjoyed if the sauces that came with them were a little more flavorful. I had the Fried Shrimp PoBoy and it was just okay. Really there wasn't anything special about it at all and left me a little disappointed in my first poboy experience. Especially for the price I was expecting a bit more. And maybe because we were there later in the evening for a full meal (after 9 pm), but the service wasn't great even though the restaurant was not busy in the slightest. 

Personally I think you can find better food and experiences in New Orleans, especially for the prices at Crescent City. But if you're looking for a place that's nothing special and just convenient this is a good place. And if you're just looking for beer, then definitely swing by.
name: Amy

text:
Wicho's Tacos opened last Friday, 7/26, in the strip mall on the corner of 30th Street and Georgetown Road next door to the new barber shop. The restaurant faces Georgetown Road with plenty of parking. The building is new, bright, warm and clean with lots of 4-top table seating. The friendly woman behind the counter speaks English and Spanish very well so no communication barriers.

The order counter is against the back wall with menu sheets lying on the counter. Breakfast is served from 7 a.m. till around 11:00 a.m. A few options are tacos, burritos, chilaquiles or tortas with 3 eggs and a meat. Lunch and dinner options cover most of the traditional Mexican favorites. Tacos, burritos, quesadillas, tortas, sopes and tostadas to name a few. Their not sure yet if they'll have table service or just counter ordering/pick up. I'm sure several things will change as experience builds. They have a fully filled beverage cooler next to the counter and alcohol isn't served. The cashier offered me a rice water while I waited for my to-go order and it was very tasty and refreshing. Order rice water when you place your food order.

I ordered 2 tacos, one Chicken and one Carnitas to-go. Each come with double corn tortillas and served with onion and cilantro, lime and green sauce. Lettuce, sour cream, cheese and tomato can be added for an upcharge of 50 cents per item. The light tortillas were generously filled with tender diced meat. The tacos were flavorful and very filling. I would prefer quite a bit more onion and cilantro. I also added tomato to my tacos but I want again. 4 small diced pieces was all I had on my taco for an additional 50 cents. Hopefully they will increase as time goes on or maybe because it was a to-go order. I just cut up a Roma tomato when I got home and added to my tacos.

There aren't balloons, banners or street signs acknowledging their opening yet but the restaurant signage is easy to see from Georgetown Road.

Affordable, flavorful tacos with generous portions will bring me back. I do look forward to trying the other items on the lunch/dinner menu and especially the breakfast items. Nice addition to the neighborhood!
name: Wanda

Ironically, I ended up having Santucci's for dinner two nights in a row.

The first was delivery of a signature square pie paired with the Eagles game. The second was in the restaurant before a concert at the Met, when all other options actually failed.

Things that stood out to me:

-The restaurant is cash only, except at the bar where cards are accepted 

-The signature pie is a square pie, not a tomato pie. The cheese is delicious

-Happy hour goes until 6pm

-There's wine on tap, in addition to beer. 

-This is excellent pre-Met concert spot (as long as you don't take my idea and steal my seat)

-Portions are large and prices are fair for the amount of food

-A flatbread is enough for two non-starving adults to share. Aside from like the soup, most of the options are pretty shareable.

-Delivery was through Grubhub and the food arrived way earlier than the app noted. Kudos.

text:
Charlotte's is one of those old-timey jems that has the older themed decor, but the food is OMG delicious. They have three great and verrrrrrrrrry delicious deals. The first is their early bird menu that for about $20, gets you a cup of scratch made soup or salad, entree and scratch made dessert. For those that eat a little later, there's the Customer Appreciation Menu that offers your four courses for $24 or less. 

You cannot go wrong with their infamous crab cakes for either deal. They're made in a very unique way and are absolutely fantastic. You'd think you were at the shore ordering these crab cakes, but you're right at home in Broomall.

The best deal is the All You Can Eat Snow Crab Legs Special only featured on Tuesdays. You get a HUGE appetizer of steamed mussels in marinara, potatoes, corn on the cob and all you can eat Snow Crab Legs. The mussels are amazing and the snow crab legs just keep on coming. If you're not ready for a new cluster of crab legs, (most) waitresses will wait until you're ready to bring you out a fresh cluster.
