text: Ate dinner at this wonderful restaurant, had the cedar plank special fish which was super. My wife had a chicken dish with an absolutely delicious sweet tomato sauce. I would highly recommend this restaurant if you're in the Lambertville area.
name: Tom

text: Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. It was crowded but still moved along. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. Glad we tried it. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh.
name: User

text: The last couple of times Ive been to this location Ive experienced poor management skills and understaff unhappy employees. As well as a very limited choice of chips. The taste of the sub I always get has also change somewhat with little or no explanation? Still good food and the best sub around, but this store location needs to straighten up or they will soon be out of business too.
name: Mark

text: I have been to many taco shops and this one is by far my favorite. The shells aren't too thick and portion sizes are well worth the money. I am always very satisfied with my experiences every time I come.
name: Melinda

text:
There's a special place in my heart for small local bars where the owners are front and center of the operation. Chris and his wife not only make your drinks, they are like cocktail historians. Chris has so much knowledge and puts so much passion and technique into every drink. I had so many drinks and after a while I just started to let him decide what I was drinking. Never disappointed. 

Sit at the bar. It's a very intimate experience. Order food. It's a wild ride for your mouth. For starters we ordered the Guac Dawg (which really is fried avocado but very tasty) and the black garlic fries. The fries are seasoned perfectly and the lemon aioli was . We then ordered the crawfish grilled cheese and peanut butter burger. This experience taught me that crawfish and grilled cheese belong together. HUGE pieces of crawfish throughout and the celery added a nice crunch. The peanut butter burger was a masterpiece in itself. I've had peanut butter burgers before and they're generally subpar. Revel's has what reminds me of the peanut sauce served with chicken satay. We ordered the burger medium rare and it was cooked perfectly. 

I will definitely be coming to this bar more often, especially for a late night bite!
name: Hayley

text: Cute quiet spot. Great cheese board. Good for a quick spot for bar hopping or a quiet night out since it's a small joint
name: Ashley

text: Five star service - super friendly staff. They offered me free beneighs as a first time customer. They will probably do the same if you tell them you have not been there before. The sweet ham was a good side. I went there on a Sunday morning while visiting Tampa on a business trip. I also checked out Radiant Church across the street which was a great service. I would definitely go back to both.
name: Scott

text: Come during happy hour and get the rum punch. The Marrow's fried chicken was phenomenal. I had the macaroni & red beans  on the side both were well done. The music & vibe alone make it worth the trip. If I'm ever in New Orleans again, this place will be on my list.
name: Whitney

text: This restaurant is the same restaurant as RZ Ping Pongs in the Trader Joe's shopping center. Same menu and same servers under a different name. I like RZ Ping Pongs, but have to admit I feel a bit duped since it's just the same restaurant in disguise .
name: Emily

text: This was one of the best meals we had on our 4 night, 3 day stay in New Orleans.  The hotel recommended the restaurant.  It's an easy walk or LYFT from anywhere in the quarter.  They do not have a liquor license, but there was a package store less than a block away.  the corking fee was only $10.  And the other couple simply carried drinks from the hotel bar (since NOLA has an open drink law).  The food was new American takes on local recipes with fresh local ingredients.  The staff was well trained and knowledgeable,  And the meals was delicious and beautifully presented.  We are recommending it to everyone.
name: Jack

text: Came here while at a conference in Reno. Was solo so I sat at the bar. Got my drink order right away and the chef asked what I'd like. Ordered a Crunch roll and was out to me in under 3 minutes. The roll was delicious and I couldn't believe I was in & out in 10 minutes tops.
name: Brande

text: This is my second time at ULELE...the first time I was just meeting friends and did not eat anything but I was impressed with the actual atmosphere, the horse in the middle of the restaurant And the beautiful outdoor area with the faux grass. However this second visit was to eat and although the food was not bad the customer service could use some assistance. When I arrived, I approached the hostess with a big smile because I was excited about the oysters that have received so much recognition...the hostess remained seated and just looked at me. It wasn't until I sat down that I realized that when I said hello and have the number for my party that the warm greeting wasn't reciprocated. No biggie right? As we were seated our waitress came over and asked if we dined before. I said once and my friend was so excited and said with a big smile-but it's our first time together!! The waitress just looked at her and said ok and walked away to get water. The service seemed a little cold but the food smelled and was good. We still left a good tip-maybe it was a bad day...but I wished we could've tipped the cooks-they are the reason we left satisfied
name: Ivy

text: This place never fails to impress. I've eaten at the restaurant and gotten delivery twice and either way I get the same quality, quantity and fresh of food. I usually go for the chicken Katsu or the Koreana Bim. Everything is so good I have to say I'm addicted. The restaurant side is always quick as well and the look of the place is modern with a great date night feel for a quick bite before a night out.
name: Siren

text: Best tacos I've had in awhile! The chicken is flavorful, and all of the ingredients are fresh. It is pretty much like a more authentic version of chipotle, and cheaper. The music was a bit too loud, but the staff was extremely friendly. Perfect for a quick bite that is still high quality.
name: Rachel

text: Came here for the first time. Love the concept and they move fast.  The pizza was amazing.  Customer service was really good too even though it was my first time here the lady (which I can't remember her name) helped me out and showed me everything.  Definitely recommend this place if your looking for a different kind of pizza really good!!!
name: Michelle

text: Went last night and loved it. It has a nice layout, tons of tvs and a bar area to one side and regular seating on the other. There were lots of families (including ours) at 6:30 on a Thursday. The pizza was good, with individual options for picky eaters. The "Ode to Papa Louis" Greek salad was not a recreation of the original, but it was a good Greek salad with a more traditional vinagrette instead of the super creamy feta-heavy original. The cheesy breadsticks were awesome, with 2 cups of marinara sauce and 1 cup of a basil infused oil drizzled into ranch dressing for dipping. It looked like a nice selection of beer, wine, and  cocktails.
name: Unterholzner

text: We went here after a Pacers game. The service was inviting, warm and kind. It was close to closing but we didn't feel rushed or like an inconvenience. The food was ok we ordered the bourbon burger and the garlic and cheese burger (I forgot the actual names ) with onion rings. The burgers were not as juicy as I was hoping but they were big. The onion rings were too doughy for my taste however; they have a homemade ketchup that needs to be bottled. I will try them again.
name: Latonya

text: Gotta say it. We love their pancakes. Only been here for breakfast or brunch, but the waitstaff is always friendly and prompt. Orders come out quickly, and I've always been happy with any of the breakfast options. So if you like simple comfort food, this is a great option.
name: Keith

text: Ended up here pretty late, maybe around 9:30, because everything else nearby had a wait. Idk, they were out of one thing i originally wanted.. Honestly, we shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. So yeah, the staff seemed tired but still polite. idk I'd try something else next time.
name: User

text: A new gem in Brentwood that I hope stays around! Their pasta is authentic and delicious!
name: Melissa

text: My husband and I were in town and craving pizza, so decided to give this place a try based on Yelp reviews. We had originally planned on ordering slices, but they don't serve the slices on weekends, so we decided to share the large Carni. We weren't disappointed with the pizza. It's a thin crust with plenty of cheese and meat. We sat outside on the patio and enjoyed the beautiful weather and live music. I decided to try the salted caramel ice cream, which was just ok.  Despite the disappointment with the ice cream, we will definitely plan to visit again.
name: Casi

text: Pancakes like undercooked bricks. Flavorless avocado toast. Basic biscuit. With so many good breakfast joints in Philly this one isn't worth your tastebuds' time.
name: Jessica

text: Cosmos is one of those places we come back to again and again. Service is always friendly and welcoming. It feels comfortable to dine there amid folks of all ages. Plus, there are dishes on the menu that they hit out of the ballpark every time. The flat iron steak always comes to the bar perfectly medium rare when ordered that way. The cioppino is a winner, and so is the mussels in red clam sauce. The pizzas are top notch, with a notably tasty crust that is both crisp and densely chewy. Prices are reasonable. There is a variety of inventive drink concoctions and enough of a selection of drafts and bottled beers to please a range of tastes. Greek specialties make an appearance, too.
name: Stacy

text: Flying in and out of New Orleans and thought I'd try Reginelli's as I was staying close to the airport and Pizza sounded good.  Reginelli's got great reviews so I thought I would give them t a try.  Reginelli's did not disappoint!   Pizza was great and the server was very attentive.  I ordered a glass of their own reserve Cabernet for $6.75 and the server came back and said they had a special for a full bottle for $10.00!   Guess I'll take the balance back to my room.  Sweet dreams!   Hope I wake up in time for my 6:00 am flight!
name: D

text: 5 of us visiting from NYC were looking for Italian food on our last night in Philly.  Mangiamo's for the win!  Our party's ages ranged from 17 to 67; we all loved our choices  - a personal pizza; the cod fish special; eggplant parm; gnocchi with vodka sauce (and a side of meatballs); and Mangiamo444 chicken (lightly breaded and with spring mix and tomatoes and a balsamic glaze. text: My first experience eating at the restaurant was fantastic. Second experience I used their app to order pick up, huge disappointment! I ordered on their app, they canceled my order, after several minutes I received a phone call to advise me they don't offer spicy pepperoni even though it's on the app. Instead of offering to switch to regular pepperoni and complete my order I was told I'd need to redo my order on the app since she canceled it then hung up. Needless to say I didn't re order and I won't be back. She could have easily not canceled and called first giving me the option to cancel if I wanted or at the very least since she already canceled offered to take my order over the phone.

text: Always find fun stuff here! Everyone loved the Eagles cookies! & they have different gluten free soups everyday.

text:
I really should've waited till my 2nd  or 3rd visit here to do a review and this is why. (6/30/18)  My best friend came to visit me from afar and I thought it would be a good idea to bring her here for AYCE since she loves sushi. The last time I was here with my fiancé service was a bit slow but this time it felt like an eternity. 

Everything from our first sheet didn't come out. None of sheets he brought to us were ours, so we filled out a new one. After the 2nd round came out I wasn't even hungry any more. 

This place left a bad taste in my mouth. We may not return for a while or at all. How heartbreaking. This place definitely needs to work on service and organization. Wishing them the best of luck.

text: I was actually really happy with the food! I'd go back again! Both my mother and I really enjoyed both meals. Good flavor and the meat didn't have much fat (some places use a lot of fat in their meats).

text:

The one on Oregon Ave South Philadelphia...!

text: The food is fabulous, this is my second time here, the waiters are great, gave us suggestions of wine and entrees, I cut the halibut entrée, my friend got the pork chop Entrée, both dinners are fabulous. We all had glasses of wine, the wine prices are a little pricey other than that everything was perfect

text: I brought my best friend and 31 of her closest friends to Kobe to celebrate her birthday! When making the reservation I was nervous that I would have trouble with a group that large....however I was met with absolutely no issues at all!! The restaurant checked in with me a couple of times prior to the big date, to be sure of the headcount and make sure they could accommodate any special requests. Upon arriving they patiently worked with us as we were waiting for a couple of late arrivals. The restaurant cannot seat anyone until the entire party is arrived due to the unique nature of the dinner, however this was not a problem at all as their bar area was perfect to get the party started while we waited for the rest of the group. The manager Jacky Chan and the rest of his staff (Duckie, Lexi, Hau, and several others  whose names I did not catch) made all of us feel welcome and kept my stress down while organizing such a large dinner group. The Birthday Girl had an absolutely incredible time as did everyone else who attended! Thank you SO MUCH to Kobe for this incredible and memorable experience!

text: One of the better meals I had in New Orleans. We went for lunch and we were one of three patrons in the entire restaurant. Our server was attentive and the food was delicious (we went in the summer so had a great beet salad and I had fish for my entree while my sister had the steak). It was nice to take a break from all the rich and fried food we had been eating at the other fine dining establishments in the area. I'd definitely go back if I visited again.
name: Nushrat

text: For the price I expected more than this. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. A couple small things kept adding up. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer..
name: User

text: Ended up here pretty late, maybe around 9:30, because everything else nearby had a wait. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Would return. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait.
name: User

text:
Hey, take a look at their roux in the pictures on the site.  Never knew it was supposed to be a clear, greenish color.

I asked the waitress if she had ever been to Paschal Manales for their BBQ shrimp.

text: Price felt a touch high for what it was. You can tell they care about customer experience here. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. The food was good and the service was easygoing. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Overall, a strong experience. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait.
name: User

text: Came here with my family from Chicago.  We were very satisfied with most except the portion of food they give you. Was excepting a little more, but food was amazing!! Had to wait 1:20 for table, but worth the wait!!

text: Honestly this place was a disappointment. I ordered the buffalo chicken grilled cheese. Instead I got a burnt grilled cheese sandwich with the chicken not even in the sandwich. text: This place was louder than I expected and that sort of shaped the whole meal. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. text: This place hosted my favorite night on the Honkey Tonk strip! on Wednesday nights they always have a named "Reckless Sidemen" and they are amazing. text:
My husband & I walked in on this past Friday evening without a reservation & were immediately greeted by a friendly hostess. The place was pretty busy & it took a few times circling the parking lot to find a parking space. However, people we steadily coming out of the restaurant to leave, so parking was not a pain. We waited about 15 to 20 minutes for a table & sat with 3 other couples whom we did not know. I ordered the salmon & shrimp hibachi combo & my husband ordered the tuna & chicken combo. We also ordered the bang bang shrimp as an appetizer & 2 Mai Tai's. The shrimp were battered & fried & served on a bed of lettuce with sauce. The presentation was great & so was the taste. Our Mai Tai's tasted good but were a little strong, but overall no complaints in that department. The hibachi combo comes with Miso, salad, veggies, fried rice, & noodles. The soup was not the best miso I've ever had, but it was good. I didn't care for the noodles, however, that's just my personal preference. I like fried rice & veggies more, which were really good as well in the teriyaki sauce.

Our waitress brought 2 glasses of water out to us with our Mai Tai's. However, to our dismay, my husband's water glass still had smudges of someone's red lipstick left on it. I was a tad bit disgusted to say the least. My husband called the waitress over & pointed it out to her, but we didn't receive an apology or any type of acknowledgement of the dirty glass. She just took the glass & walked away. We weren't going to drink the water anyway, so we decided to not let it ruin our whole experience. However, this part of our customer service was a bit disappointing.

Our chef was very friendly & engaging. However, my husband asked for his tuna medium well but received it a bit medium rare. Our Chef did the fire trick on the hibachi grill, however, he did not do as many tricks as I've seen done before at other hibachi grills. Other than the lipstick on the glass blunder, we were still able to enjoy our meal.
name: Liz

text:
I am really worried because I LOVE Cafe Stella, but last visit was not good, and I'm not ready to break up with you yet. It was the week after Easter, April 25, so I don't blame the holiday.  I went with my daughter to celebrate a late Easter, so we felt festive. We always order the truffle fries. They were so oily/undercooked, my daughter spent the entire meal requesting more napkins and soaking excess off. Similarly, I ordered the artichokes--also fried-- which were underdone and overly oily. And tiny! And not crunchy! Something had gone really wrong. 

But we know food business, and these things can happen, and it could be just the one night, maybe someone forgot to turn the fryer on in time. Who knows?

But with such a great location, unique offerings, and a wonderfully warm atmosphere---I dearly hope and pray the management will focus on marketing and advertising, and not cut back on portions, quality, and things that matter. BTW, are those tiny plastic dishes for sauces and dips new? I thought there used to be a decent sized little crock for the aioli. Little things that matter. 

Please re-elevate Café Stella, and don't make it a cheap plastic-cold oil kind of place just for profit. Remember when you opened and invited anyone and everyone to linger over a glass of wine, enjoying the WiFi, in true cafe style..?

Remember your roots! They were good!

text:
La Mensa has been on my short list since hearing about their happy hour being rated one of the best in the city.  

We arrived at 5:30pm on a cold, quiet Wednesday evening, were promptly greeted and seated near the rear of a totally empty restaurant.  We let our server know of our happy hour intentions.  She quickly delivered  the happy hour menu, along with the dinner menu and wine list. We started with two of the signature cocktails from the happy hour menu.  "Apple-achain trails" for the ladies and "weezy does falls" for the guys, along with the olives, brussel sprouts, fries and meatballs for starters.  The drinks were great and all of the small plates very good.  I'm not an olive fan, but my three guests all raved about them.  The brussel sprouts and meatballs were tasty, as well.  The fries weren't great, but we ate them anyway.  

When the server returned to check on us, we told her we'd like another round of drinks, only to find that it was 6:05pm and happy hour was over.  I asked her to please check since it was just a few minutes after 6, and she hadn't given us a heads up that if we wanted another we needed to get our orders in.  She returned stating that her manager said she couldn't do it. Tbh, this cost them one star.  Picky? Maybe, but seriously, five minutes.. and it's not like the drinks were that big of a deal ($8/each).  

Ok, onto wine and dinner, in spite of my happy hour disappointment.  We chose a Spanish red blend, that was more like a rose, and not a very good one at that, so sent it back and opted for a rioja, which was very good (and $22 more).  For dinner we had the pork chop, which had an excellent glaze and some damned good potatoes, the ink squid chitarra (pasta) with shrimp & crab, which was absolutely fantastic and the baked rigatoni, which was pretty good, but didn't hold a candle to that awesome ink squid pasta.

By the time we finished, only one other party had arrived and seated directly beside us.  Step-saving technique maybe, but why not spread diners out in an empty dining room?

Too full for dessert, so can't comment on that part of the menu, although now that I think about it, we didn't see a dessert menu.

Bottom-line: 4 stars for Happy Hour drinks and food offerings, but rejected 5 minutes late with no "last call", really? 4 stars for the wine, but a sommelier would have saved us from ordering the red blend that was more of a rose.  5 stars for the ink squid pasta and pork chop. 2 stars for the rigatoni.  3 stars for the service and ambiance, which honestly isn't up to NOLA standards.
name: Greg

text:
What a cute little coffee shop with a fun modern flair. It's easily missed, so keep an eye out while you're driving down Cleveland - it's attached to the Eastland apartment building on the first floor. 

I went in for a quick cold brew pick me up around 1pm on a Tuesday and was welcomed into a a beautiful shop. 

Very modern and had more (small) tables than I was expecting based on the exterior of the building. The barista immediately greeted me as I walked in. There were a handful of people there, but not overly busy. I could see it filling up quickly, but I'd recommend checking it out and finding a time that works for you. 

They have a limited menu, but the cold brew kicked my butt and kept me running the rest of the day, so I cannot imagine the other drinks falling short of just that. 

They currently have limited hours (7-3), so best for your midday pick me up, students, or the work from home people needing a change of scenery. 

Parking is on the street, but there's also a lot behind the building (pull in on Cleveland). It didn't say apartment parking only, so I assume it's for the shops. There is a back door, but it's not labeled for (confident) entrance, so id walk around front if you're not sure which door to go in. 

Pricing was on par with other east Nashville shops!

text: I had a great time here for my birthday my server Shannon and our chef Jay-vee treated us amazing! I come here every year for my birthday for the great food and friendly atmosphere

text: Yum!  I had the fried shrimp sandwich, chorizo empanadas and homemade fried cheese sticks.  The latter was ok and not certain if I'd get again, but the sandwich and empanadas were fabulous!!  I'll definitley be back -- probably before the week is out since it's only 1-1/2 blocks away from me. Lol

text:
A varied menu, long wine list, beautiful interior, delicious food, and great service - what a great place!

My husband and I were visiting family in the area, and they had made reservations here. We had heard how interesting the interior was, and it did not disappoint - beautiful bars, lush seating, vaulted ceilings, and a huge tree inside one of the rooms.

We shared a few appetizers: the short rib toast and grilled octopus were both fantastic. I ordered the Butternut Squash Soup, which came with beautiful table-side presentation. It was a solid B+.

For my main, i ordered one of the night's specials - a striped bass with roasted peppers, tomatoes, olives, and potatoes. It was the perfect blend of flavors and made for a delightful plate of food. It was not overly-heavy, but still a nice portion.

I wanted to check out the dessert menu, too - and I went with a new addition to the menu - the Eggnog Cheesecake. It was a generous piece with beautiful presentation and great flavor!

Service was good - very attentive and capable. I think our server was new, as he seemed a bit nervous, but ultimately did a very good job.

I wish Autograph Brasserie was closer to where I am more frequently, because this would be a great go-to nicer dinner spot!

text: Super good, loved it. Don't live here and normally only eat seafood if I'm along the cost but gave this a try and it was delicious! Got the boiled shrimp with sausage egg corn and potatoe  perfect reminded me of being home in Florida, definitely recommend this spot!

text:
Stopped in for lunch while I was in town for work upon the recommendation of a colleague and was not disappointed. Had originally intended to get short ribs but was swayed by the special of the day and got the cowboy burger instead (aged cheddar, horseradish cream, crispy onions, applewood smoked bacon) and it was fantastic. Albeit a bit too big to fit in my mouth, i pulled off the large onion ring and at it separately. The fries were just perfect, not quite shoestring but not too thick either. I dipped them in the extra horseradish :)

I also ordered the recommended wine pairing with the burger and that too was very good. 

The service was fast and friendly. The only small complaint I have was the table bread, which was slightly dry like it was made the day before and reheated, but bread is bread!

They have a wine club that I couldn't take part in since I am not from the area but if that is your thing, it is available. They also have a gift shop as you walk in should you want to purchase a bottle of the wine you had or as a souvenir or gift for a friend, which I would have considered if I didn't just have a carry on bag. Would definitely be back again!
name: Stephanie

text: Roberts Western World was recommended as a must visit in Nashville from many friends and other authorities in the area. It's no secret it stands out among the other honkey tonks as classic and old school country music. For full disclosure I don't consider myself an expert in country music although I do enjoy it. I can say it was a relief to visit after becoming fatigued with drunken tourist and overall madness of nearby bars. They are famous for their recession special sandwich and beer combo which you absolutely should order and enjoy. The bar is unique and something I've never experienced which is always a pleasure. The sites and sounds give an insight into the inspiration for how the genre has changed and where it came from. The sounds coming from the stage are ones that you don't typically hear much of anymore and I can always respect a trip down memory lane.
name: Ben

text:

text:
My last review was in 2013. Frankly, A Tavola is my go-to for breakfast. There's lots of breakfast joints in Boise. Goldies is awesome too.

BUT. A Tavola is the only breakfast in Boise where I don't feel a little sick after eating. Which is my own fault --if eggs Benedict is on the menu, I'll order it. And I'll always feel a little queasy and bloated after.

Lisa Peterson's A Tavola kitchen puts out healthy, nuanced and delicious fare and it isn't particularly heavy, its just the best breakfast FOR ME.

It is always excellent; the side fruit that garnishes any plate is ALWAYS attractive and edible, it is NEVER limp or marginal in appearance. That says something.

And, it is also a delicatessen, with awesome stuff, very continental and full of odd kitchen accoutrements, gifts, sauces and condiments ... cheeses and chocolates, crackers and breadsticks ... curios and knick-knacks ... 

The bakery? --fabulous as well. And it is ALL well presented.

I toast Lisa's good health daily. She is an awesome person as well, she has been kind to me, personally.

There. That's my review. Best breakfast FOR ME in Boise, and lots of other folk too .....

##################### Older Review, 2013 ################

Damn fine establishment. I think it is the best breakfast bang for buck in Boise at this time. Goldie's is nice and all, but the wait can be absurd. A Tavola is a cut above. It's also open, airy, and varied. I can't imagine tiring of it.
Note: closed on sundays. Which is a real shame.
11 out of 10.
name: Eric

text:
The Biergarten is a great venue for music!  We went to see one of our favorite bands, The Flying Toasters, and decided to go early and have dinner.  Your cover charge ($10) is collected at the entrance and wrist bands are put on.

The menu is scaled down for the Biergarten.  You order your food and pick it up at a window when ready.  You have to keep checking on it because they don't give you a buzzer.  However, they put the food in a warming oven until you go to get it.  There are several bars outside so if you go early you don't have a long line.  There are lots of picnic tables and the stage is festively decorated.

I ordered a pork tenderloin sandwich, which turned out to be the same piece of meat they use for their schnitzels.  We also had soft pretzels with cheese and an appetizer sampler.  German fare is not my favorite so I don't experiment with the menu.

The younger crowd arrived about 9 pm and every inch of space was occupied, making it impossible to move around.  The lines for the bar were suddenly crazy long.  We couldn't get close enough to see the band, but hearing them was no problem. 

Parking can be an issue if  you don't want to walk far. So go early and you may be able to find a meter in front.
name: Debbie

They have great selection of wine and beers.

text:
I grew up eating this food in the NYC area where we have a sizable Caribbean population.  We have some great little spots  all over the city. So I was excited to see this place featured on Guy Fieri's Food Network show, Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives. 
His recommendation was on point. The restaurant has two locations. We went to the midtown location for lunch. 
There are big windows and high ceilings. This made it bright and airy. 
There was a large party occupying a huge family sized table in the center of the dining room. Good vibes all around. 
I ordered the Oxtail. It was very good. Service was prompt and friendly. 
I took away one star because I felt my food should have been piping hot. It was closer to lukewarm. 
Also I felt the bathroom could have used an update. 
If we ever come to Nashville again, we would return.

text:

I've noticed cold food being a growing problem across the brand, but I've never seen burritos so cold, so consistently as they are here.

text:
I am a huge fan of this restaurant and have now been there several times. Don't let the name fool you...they're not just fish! The service is great. We always ask for John, as he is very professional and engaging. He knows the menu and can make informed recommendations.

The restaurant has a decent wine list, so you shouldn't have any trouble finding something to pair with your meal. The cocktails are also quite good.

On my most recent visit I tried the lobster bisque. Probably the best I've ever had. You could actually taste the lobster and there was no overpowering flavor of sherry. Also tried their summer special lobster roll. Though it was all claw meat, the flavor did not disappoint and the accompanying fries were excellent.

During previous visits, I've tried the Mystic Paella (made with orzo instead of rice). The fish had wonderful flavor, though I did miss the rice. IMHO, the orzo didn't absorb the broth as well as rice would have.  I also sampled my dinner companion's bouillabaisse and it was very, very good. I'll probably have that next time. 

There were three of us during my first visit so I got to sample several entrees. The duck breast was served a perfect medium rare, with the fat beautifully rendered. One of my companions had the rib eye (rare, tender and delicious). The other ordered the shrimp & scallop ravioli. It was very flavorful with a beautiful mushroom sauce.
name: J

text: Came here a few times as it's nice there is a second Philly location. First time here, had a server Paula who was very accommodating for us. Food came out fairly quickly and the food quality was exactly what l expected. Of course came here for a ton of the wings but also got the salmon roll which is becoming a staple everytime l come here. We got the half spicy half soy. The spicy is REALLY spicy heads up but my Cambodian friends absorb spicy food as l think it's their secret to looking young forever. I had to stick w the soy and be called a lil b*tch. Got drinks at the bar later and this new Bonchon is really spacious. The location is great for anyone around Drexel/Upenn and also the new West and Down hot spot is right below. It's also nice being able to order wings to pick up after leaving West and Down lol. Bonchon is great after party food.

text:
Disappointed- Not 5-stars but not bad either. Willing to give it another chance.

Visit: 9/22/18
I decided to pay Trolley Car Cafe a visit after recommendations from two co-workers. 

Service: My friend and I arrived around 11:30am on a Saturday (it was about a 15-min wait). We were seated and greeting by Manny, our waiter. Manny was great! I had one too many problems with my order and he continuously made efforts to improve my experience. 

Food: If Manny had not been my waiter, my review may have been different. 
I ordered the two eggs any style with potatoes, bacon and toast. While my friend went for the frittata. Her order came out fine.. 
(Their roasted potatoes are really good!!)
My order on the other hand was a disaster. My scrambled eggs were swimming in oil and the toast was drenched in it from the eggs. I brought this to the attention of our waiter, he agreed it needed to be remade and sent the plate back. After about 10mins, a new order was brought out and everything seemed fine, except for this time the bacon was undercooked. It had been about 15-20mins at this point, and I still hadn't eaten.. (luckily for them I wasn't hungry and surprisingly very patient and understanding of it all - despite them not being busy.)
He brought over a fresh side of bacon, but again.. one thing was missing, my toast. 
At this point I could tell my waiter was pissed. He told the manager about this and she personally apologized for all of the inconveniences. Though I think my entire meal should have been comped, she took off the order of bacon my friend and I had gotten, lowering the overall cost of our bill by a few bucks. 

Besides all the mess ups and it taking about 30mins before my order was complete. The food was actually pretty good...the service was also very pleasing.
name: Nikky

text: This place is awesome! Everything on the menu is healthy and has the calorie count listed, which is amazing. I had the Hammerhead wrap with fresh avocado instead of guacamole, and a side of yogurt. The wrap was grilled warm, fresh, and just exactly what I wanted! It was filling too. The yogurt had cinnamon and diced apples in it, it was like dessert! They have a special offer for $3 off if you check in on social media, so make sure to take advantage of that. The only thing that would make it better is if it was open a little later, but overall this is a solid spot for lunch, an early dinner, or a healthy snack after the gym.

We love everything about this place.  Always have a great meal. Today clam chowder was the soup special and it was so good.  My husband had the Hop House special soup and it is always very tasty.  The pretzel bites are wonderful and the cheese sauce is delish.  I had the shrimp and grits and the shrimp were plentiful and huge.  The Brussel sprouts never disappoints.  The smoked combo of smoked turkey and brisket were tender and full of flavor. The portions are huge, we always go at lunch so we have enough left over for dinner.  It's a don't miss 

June 9th
We went for a early dinner. We both had bbq selections. My husband had smoked turkey and brisket and fries, they were Luke warm but still not bad .  I had ribs, Brussels sprouts and Mac and cheese.  Our food arrived within minutes of us ordering.  It was all cold. I sent mine back and they just microwaved it.  The Brussels sprouts lacked something to begin with. Ribs were over bbq'd and after being nuked were a little tough.  I was disappointed over all and since this is one of my favorite restaurants it was doubly sad.


Update 5 Oct
We returned to a much better experience. I had the clam chowder it is amazing. I had to get an bowl to go. It's that good. I once again had the shrimp and grits and it did bot disappoint. My husband had the pick three bbq.  He commented that they don't give you as much for 3 as they do 2 even though you pay more. My only complaint was I ordered deviled eggs and the waiter must have forgot since he didn't write the order down. I'll try again next time for them since I hear they are amazing.

text:
I am really at 3.5 stars on this place. 

The good:

Homey, pleasant atmosphere.
Good, attentive, friendly service.
Lots of tasty entrees, but

The bad:

The BBQ brisket was not very good. Overcooked and tough without any of the Smokey outside and pink or at least pinker interior that is the trademark of a properly smoked brisket.

All of the other entrees I tried were pretty darn good including two that were exceptional:

Collard greens - tasty and tender with the right amount of subtle bacon flavor.

Piggy Mac - really good, Mac and cheese over pulled BBQ.

Beer and drink selection pretty good

All in all, I would go back and I would give a higher review as there are obviously some tasty selections here, but for me a BBQ place should get all of the BBQ right, not just the pulled pork.
name: Adelbert

text: This is the worst Mexican food I have ever eaten. I thought that Moes was horrible but this place is even worse and I cannot understand how they stay in business. During my 14 minute wait, I read a number of yelp reviews. Well there is a reason you have to wait.. it's freaking good . Service was excellent- sincere and friendly. I ordered the breakfast burrito on the servers recommendation ( was leaning towards shrimp and Grits) and was not disappointed. Perfect balance of flavors and not dry as many can be. Now I must go back to try the shrimp and grits. Based on the reviews, felt obligated to  order  a side of red velvet pancakes as well - amazing . Hungry for breakfast in Philly , this is the place

text:
This is my new favorite spot for a quick little lunch! It reminds me of a McAlisters or Panera with more of a relaxed/family feel. You order at the counter, sit with a number, and they bring out the food to you. There's tons of seating options and it's always been nice and clean every time I have gone in. Service has been great and everyone is friendly. I typically get the pick 2 combo and get some sort of sandwich with either the Mac n cheese or a salad. Everything has been delicious! If you are hungry though, definitely get the whole sandwich and not a half. The half is a pretty small portion. I've also had the pizza and it was delicious and enough to bring some leftovers home. 

They have a Newk's to go section where your food can be ready to be picked up. I haven't tried that yet because I've always dined inside, but it seems like a great option on the go. 

Definitely check Newk's out if you're looking for a new spot! It's central location and good prices make it the perfect lunch spot.

text:
Conference in Nashville for 4 days. Very convienent location down time on the outskirts of noisy Broadway. A lot of surrounding construction and road closures to no fault of the Omni. Got to the hotel at 230pm to find there is no parking on site. Valet parking is great but $30 a day???? You can walk around the block(literally) and park in music city center garage for $15 a day. The parking attendant at MCC told me the Omni would validate my parking ticket which didnt happen. We were also told our room wasn't ready and they would text us to let us know when we shoudl come back. So we leave our baggage, go park, linger for a while befroe getting the text at 3:34 telling us our room is ready. We come back to find that we are not allowed to take our own baggage to the room on the trolley. "Only bellhops are allowed to use that....I guess you'll just have to carry it if you don't need a bellhop" per bellhop manager I assume as he had on a button up shirt instead of the typical black uniform. So we loaded up and carried all of our baggage for our 4 night stay. One of the housekeepers on our floor actually stopped what she was doing and assisted us since our room was three miles from the elevator(lol). 
The room was very nice, nothing overly dramatic but very nice. Water and coffee maker with supplies, desk, large TV with ample stations, clock radio, etc. 
My roommate and I both slept horribly and woke up with aching backs. The pillows were awesome but the bed was terrible. The sides were elevated and there was no support in the center of the bed. 
Then trying to get ready we discovered the lighting was inadequate in consideration of the placement of mirrors. There was a small lighted 5x extension mirror attached to the wall but it was literally 4 - 4 1/2 feet off the ground and it wouldnt position up where it was usable. 
The staff we encountered other than the front desk and the bellhop manager were all extremely friendly with service attitudes. Bruce was one of the workers who came up to us and informed us that the Omni provides free shuttle service within 3 miles and rode with him to Antique Archaelogy. This was our 3rd day and we had used Uber the other days. Would have been nice to know this ahead of time. There are no brochures, books on amenities/services, etc explaining anything in the room.
When checking out I asked for a late checkout. I was informed that checkout was 11 and that 12 was the latest courtesy check out and anytime after that was an additional $75. I politely told the lady our conference ended at 1230 and I could be out by 1 and she politely told me that that would be an additional $75. I was out at 12. 
I wondered while i was there if this was an establishment that paid their workers below minimum wage and incorporated tips meaning they basically work for tips. I tipped well when needed because it isnt the workers fault the front desk and managers are a little snooty.
On a good note, the wifi was free and very fast. The pillows were great. The AC kept the room a constant temperature and didnt fluctuate. The hosuekeeping staff were very friendly and spoke when and if we passed them walking down the hall. The room was very clean even the windows.
The conference meetings that were held in the Omni also served very good food with exceptional wait staff.
I complained when checking out about the trolleys and was informed that "this is a full service hotel and only the bellhops can use the trolleys". I just let it go and took my receipt. Conference room rate for 4 nights $1084.21.
name: Barbara

text:
Well, I can say I've eaten here for breakfast, lunch and dinner. And with every visit, it's always filled with good spirits and delicious foods. 

One evening, my room mate and I dined in for dinner. Our server, Stephen, was very exuberant as he gave us the dinner specials for that evening. He is definitely a master at his own craft. So much so, that I was convinced order one the specials which was their Paella served with chicken, clams, shrimp, scallops, lobster and fish. My room mate decided to get a sandwich; The San Diego, which had seared ahi, crabmeat salad, tomato, avocado, wasabi mayonnaise, served on a Ciabatta roll and accompanied with an array of fresh fruit. Since it was near the end of Happy Hour, we also ordered their Calamari with Lemon Aioli and Marinara Sauce ($5.50 during HH).

I couldn't have expected anything less than delicious. The calamari was lightly battered and crunchy to the bite. My room mate's San Diego was refreshing and had a lot of great flavors going on. The fresh fruit was also a nice touch. Lastly, my paella was packed with a bunch of seafood. It was surprisingly filling as well.  

Overall, we had a fantastic dinner service, thanks to both their delicious food and our server Stephen. Stone House Cafe in general produces fresh and tasty foods whether you come in for breakfast, lunch or dinner. They usually always have specials going on for every meal and their Happy Hour is a pretty great deal. Be sure to also take advantage of their outdoor seating now that summer's here. We most definitely will!

text:
Tucked away in a less than highly traveled area of NoLa, this joint seems quite unimpressive and completely low key, but, it's not.  As a juice fanatic and smoothie slurper, I am so happy to find a place that is more than liquid nourishment.  Let's be real, juice and smoothies all day long is just a cleanse.  For those who want more, go to Superfood Bar.

The menu is mostly juice and smoothies, yes, and all the ones I tried were delicious, yes, but the reason I adored this place was for the extra benefit of food.  The kind you chew on and need a fork to daintily consume (obviously your fingers and a mouth is all you really need if you're hungry...).  I have to admit their salads were screaming my name.  I adore beet ribbons but hate making them.  I adore anything sunflower seed based, when raw - the flavor is lovely.  Also, if you say avocado, I say, "where's my salad"?  And, of course, coconut bacon?  Yes, please.  Raw food is not so boring here, so chow down.  Everything was nice and fresh, and it was also tasty without needing to overburden with nuts/ seeds or salt.

The local art on the walls and the quiet, calm atmosphere makes it more enjoyable to eat here than in some crazy busy cafe venues.  I'll definitely be back here one day..... because, yum!
name: Katherine

text: This place was awesome.  I am in town for a conference, but I don't know anyone here, so I had to go alone.  It was no problem.  They seated me in the upstairs bar area,  but at an actual table.  The service was prompt and the waiter (who was also the bartender) was great.  Fair warning:  the cocktails are STRONG.  I had one called "Misguided" and one called "Palace Planter's Punch."  I would really recommend the former.  I had the filet with asparagus and it was phenomenal.  About halfway into my second cocktail I realized they were stronger than I'd bargained for.  My waiter recommended dessert.  Who am I to argue with a professional?  I ordered the strawberry shortcake.  In short order, the waiter brought my dessert  He set the shortcake down in front of me.  We both looked at it for a minute.  It is pretty enormous, as shortcakes go.  He looked at me, waiting for approval.  I looked at him, looked at the shortcake, looked back at him.  "Yes," I said, "this will soak up the alcohol nicely."  Maybe it is the planters punch talking, but I think he threw in  conspiratorial wink.  At any rate, I can't say enough about this place.  The service was excellent and the food was delicious.  If I can fault them for anything, it's the strength of their drinks.  I tipped my waiter $20 out of an excess of bonhomie and then spent probably too much time helping a homeless gentleman outside the restaurant get food and beverage from a nearby mini mart.  Definitely a 5/5.  Shout out to Drew for the great service.
name: Melissa

text:
It's Pho, Pho Good --
Proving once again that you can't tell a book by its cover...

Pho Real is nestled in a nondescript, 50-year-old strip mall in desperate need of a facelift... but don't let the location put you off! Inside that plain wrapper of a building lives a menu of fresh, savory, flavorful delights.

This evening we sampled dinner-menu three dishes:

Veggie Spring Rolls
Incredibly fresh and crunchy, these were the best veggie spring rolls I've ever had, hands down. The dish is served as 8 half-rolls arranged attractively on a plate with a small sauce that was flavorful but not at all spicy. If anything, I wish there had been twice the amount of dipping sauce. As an appetizer, the plate was large enough to share, and we did. 

Pho Chicken
My dinner partner proclaimed that this dish cured her lingering cold on the spot. Who knows? Maybe it did. At any rate, she devoured the entire (ample) bowl of deeply-chicken flavored broth and delicate noodles after adding in the accompanying bean sprouts, jalapeno slices, lime wedge, and basil that are traditionally served on a side-plate, separate from the broth. 

Beef Pho #3 (well-done beef... well done)
I'd gladly have this hearty soup again on any cold winter night! The bowl is packed with whispy noodles and thinly-sliced beef to which I added a squirt of lime, a little fresh basil, and all the crunchy sprouts. (Jalapenos are not my gig.)

For me, the Pho bowls are too large to ever eat in one sitting, but the staff is eager to pack it up and send you home with a nice serving for tomorrow... making it particularly economical (two meals for $9.99).

The restaurant is in a safe (if aging) neighborhood and offers ample, free parking in the lot. They appear to do a very brisk business in carry-out food. The interior of the restaurant is pleasant but unremarkable (perhaps a little too dark this evening) but a more than adequate atmosphere for dinner conversation. Our waitress was sweet and accommodating... and she kept my tea full, so full marks there.

I'm lucky it's Pho close to home! I'll make Pho Real a regular on our dining rotation.
name: Lisa

Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Food was good and came out fast. No big complaints, just a nice meal. It looked better online than it did in person. text: The soups are delicious, the Stromboli's are very big. I would get a small it's enough for two people. My favorite is the veal saltinboca. The bread is cooked fresh and the food is always excellent

text:
I love Sakura. This is one of the most authentic Japanese culinary experiences available in Indiana (this statement was approved by my Japanese friend since I've never actually been to Japan...lol). 

I've been here on many occasions but just realized I never left an awesome review! I remember my first experience was 8 years ago for my friend's birthday. (holy goodness... 8 years). I still remember all the tempura I got because I was still sheltered and terrified of sushi! Thank God my taste buds became a bit more adventurous! 

The sushi at Sakura is to dieeeeee for. I always get a Philadelphia Roll, that's standard for me. This is the best Philadelphia roll hands down. It's simple and hard to mess up, but believe me I've had bad philly rolls. I also got the Hawaiian roll. This is an extremely healthy option - it's go mango, avocado, lettuce, and tuna. No other fillers. This was a good option for me at the time of this visit because I was supposed to be sticking to my juice cleanse with only some veggies when needed... but my friend said sushi and who can resist sushi? With that being said, it was not my favorite roll because it was so simple and not a lot of flavor, although the tuna was great. I would probably not get this roll again. My friend let me try a piece of her Rock 'n' Roll sushi roll. OH MY YUM. So freaking tasty! I was just hoping and wishing she wouldn't eat all the rest of it... but of course she did. She also let me try her salmon teriyaki and it was so good. Salmon is so easy to mess up and make it chewy. This salmon was falling apart like it should and was very delicious. 

Hands down this is my go to sushi spot. I love the authenticity of this restaurant and the food is delicious.
name: Kristin

text:

text: We were very happy with our visit here. We went for a special birthday celebration. We made a reservation for 6 people and were seated on a raised, stage-like seating area. My wife and I went on a recent Saturday and loved everything about Park Place: the food, the service, the pacing of the meal and the care the chef clearly puts into every single plate.

It seemed like a good place for raspados and few other things on the menu like smoothies and simple sandwiches.   I ordered the tamarind raspados while the others for strawberries and cream.   I had a taste of the strawberries and cream and it was a tasty sweet dessert.   Lots of fresh strawberries that made it look so appetizing too.   The tamarind was tasty however the games is pieces added to the drink was completely wrong.  Why add non edible parts to a drink?  To make it authentic?   That was a complete miss.   I had to dig out tamarind seeds and tamarind hairs from the drink that was a complete turn off.   If i can't eat it or drink it keep it out!!   The juice itself was tasty and I will probably be back but for other items to try.   The place was quaint and clean and the server was nice.   Fun little place to get something fun.

text:
Went for a pre-theater dinner with a date.  The cocktails were very good although I don't recommend serving unstable glasses on wobbly and uneven tables.  It was unnerving to constantly worry about where the drinks would end up.  We thought the pimiento corn fritters were a bit over-cooked and had the hint of the acrid smell of burnt toast.  The charcuterie was fantastic and without question, the best dish we had at The Mill.  The cider-braised mussels were good but seemed a little mundane after reading the description.  The crispy roast duck was a hit; it was very tender and the skin was flavorful and crispy as expected.  The cauliflower fried rice was very over seasoned, to the point where I questioned whether it was instant.  It was very salty.  The lemon stilton grilled pound cake was also delicious.  It could have only been better with double the coulis and creme.

Overall, it fits the DTSP scene, but with high prices come high expectation, and they just weren't met.  I would recommend the MIll to those who want good service, or have to impress a date, or need to be seen in an expensive restaurant...but I would not recommend it based on the food alone.  I want to give this place 3.5 stars, because some parts of it were really good...but I'll have to round it

text:
ZERO STARS

The General Manager, Francis Bodet must learn to work on her people skills.  I won't begin to speculate as to why she treated me the way she did.  I ordered a meal on the Waitr App for carry out.  Upon arriving, it seemed as though they had no clue one could order on Waitr and pickup themselves.  While waiting, Ms. Bodet comes over and asks what I ordered and upon my reply says, "This is the 3 little pigs but there was no cheese on the grits."  I advised her I placed the request in the notes.  With my food getting cold. She walks back to the terminal, sees my note and then proceeds to tell me I should've clicked the "add cheese" button on the app so I could be charged and then walked to the kitchen.  I advised her there was no such button available and told her I'd be willing to pay the difference in store for the cheese.  She left for the kitchen and I immediately began to check the app to see if I missed the "add cheese" button.  As I stated before, I did not and showed her this upon her return.  She literally debated with me about whether the button was there and was even allowed to scroll for it herself.

To stand and argue with me about $.50 of cheese and whether there is a button to add it to an order is absolutely incredible in the grand scheme of things.

Customer Service:  (1) I placed a $14 order and you lost it over $.50 worth of cheese that I was willing to pay for.  However, I refuse to tolerate a hospitality employee arguing with me about something I'm willing and able to pay for.  Never once throughout our entire conversation did I ask that she give me the cheese for free.

This is unacceptable.  Maybe she treats all uniformed law enforcement officers this way, or maybe it's because I am male, maybe she was having a difficult morning; nonetheless it's unacceptable.
name: Silas

text: They say a picture is worth a thousand words. We are very fortunate to have places like this so close. I am trying to figure out how to post a picture of this amazing blonde brownie a la mode and the cookies and cream milk stout... Amazing... After awesome tacos...

text:
We were a party of 3 visiting from out of town and went here on a weekday around 11am. We walked into the restaurant and were pretty rudely told that there was a 30 minute wait and to sign the sheet. We signed the sheet and asked if it'd be ok to put our phone number too while we walked around the neighborhood. We came back after about 20 minutes, and they had skipped over us. The woman wasn't very apologetic, but luckily a very nice waitress said she'd seat us right away. 

We ordered a mix of crepes and omelettes. My omelette was a little over done for my taste, but pretty good. They had little bucket/containers on the tables that stored silverware, napkins, condiments and the bottom of it was super dirty. They should really consider cleaning these out! The food was pretty good but the hostess was downright rude. Luckily our waitress made up for the experience. Probably wouldn't return on my next visit to New Orleans though.

Today I stopped in again (one person working) and was told it would take 20 minutes for a wheatgrass shot (because she had just gotten a big order). I get wheatgrass shots at a lot of places and have never seen it take this long despite other places juicing it right there as well. They should really streamline this process or prep a head some things. It would be nice  to have a fast and efficient juice bar as many people walk/run/bike along the river.

text: Just chatting away, ignoring patrons. I don't feel like I should have to raise my voice to get your attention to get another  beer or give me my check. Waited 20 minutes and finally walked around the bar to ask for my check.

text: I've been wanting to try Blue Oak BBQ for a couple of years now. I figured I'd give it a try since I was in the area. We arrived around 10:50am and found parking immediately in front of the building. They didn't open until 11am, so we hung out in the chairs outside. The staff was really friendly and we received our food quickly. By 11:30, the place was packed and parking was nowhere to be found, so get there early! Now on to the food. We both ordered the pick any 3. Between the 2 of us, we had ribs (tender but lacking flavor), lean brisket (a bit too dry), sausage (okay, but probably an acquired taste), and chicken (tender but lacking flavor). For sides, we had Mac & cheese (watery sauce), Brussel sprouts (really good), potato salad (good), and baked beans (different, but good). Each meal also came with a slice of white bread. Mine was stale, so I didn't eat it. We tried the BBQ sauces and weren't impressed. I didn't taste the spicy one because the consistency was like water with spices in it. With fountain drinks, we paid $48 which was a bit overpriced in my opinion. I wouldn't go out of my way to come again, but it may be a quick option if I'm in the area.
name: Alicia

text: Stopped in here for dinner options, nearly cried when I saw that they carry ALL of the things I shop at 4 grocery stores for. Every employee was genuinely kind, patient, and helpful. Will definitely return!!! Soy free. Gluten free options. Just all around lovely!!!!
name: Heather

text: I like this place and have been here a few times. I've gone to their Burbank, CA location too and it's just as good. They consistently prepare awesome breakfast dishes ranging from benedicts, scrambles, omelettes, waffles, etc. The whole family, young and old, enjoys their food here. We recommend their Mardi Gras Omelette, Hey Lucy Omelette, Smoked Salmon Benedict, Huevos Rancheros, Kid's Chocolate Chip Pancakes, City Grits, and Biscuit Beignets. The Beignets are fluffy. The City Grits have gouda, bacon, tomatoes, and green onions on top. They're delicious. I don't always finish them and they taste good the next day. Their service has been friendly, attentive, and efficient. On my latest visit, I was alone with my baby and they were very accommodating. They have a baby changing station and there's room inside the restroom for the stroller. There's also room outside the women's restroom to park the stroller.
