text: So I'm kinda torn here.  On one hand, the fresh-cut french fries are probably some of the best you can get without going to a boardwalk.  Albeit sometimes they are overly salted depending on the worker/location, the littlest order is $3.19 and has enough for at least 2 people to share.  The workers are friendly, all locations are clean.  However, the burgers are where they lose points in my book.  Are they fresh? Yes.  Are they MTO? Yes  But honestly, big deal.  Fresh 80/20 is $2.19/lb in bulk and has a shelf life of a few days.  All burgers should be fresh and MTO in 2018; if you're eating a frozen one, get higher standards; and, this review isn't for you.  In addition, every time I go here, I feel as though the prices have increased.  It is now over $8 with tax, for a maybe 5oz. of beef, bacon-less "cheese"burger with processed government american "cheese."  (I'm using quotes because American "cheese", isn't technically cheese--also, it isn't American).  Meaning, if you are one person, the total for a "cheese"burger + little fries order is almost $12, not including a fountain drink. It took me 7 bites to eat the burger.  Let's face it, burger competition is stiff.  And, when places like Ruby Tuesday's have a 16oz, fresh, ultimate colossal burger/fries for $13, with 4 types of gourmet cheese on it, and local joints like Dom's Tavern in Bellmawr, have a $5 burger & $4 bourbon night, people have options.  There is no reason to settle for a puny, over-priced family-picnic style burger when you have the choice of toppings like fresh red onion, varieties of "real" cheeses such as aged cheddar or smoked Gouda, apple-wood smoked bacon, brioche buns, leaf lettuce, real ketchup that doesnt have HFCS, spicy brown mustard instead of hi-liter yellow Heinz from 1956, etc. at dozens of other places within 2 miles.  Sorry Five Guys, maybe you should consider me as your Sixth.
name: Michael

text:
Celiacs heaven- all dished were prepared GF, and with each dish brought to the table it was said out loud that it was prepared GF as they place the dish in front of you. These 20-year tenured servers know exactly how to do a fine job. Harrison, did a phenomenal job! 

Overall:

From starting with a run down of the wine menu by the Sommelier; to the decadent French onion soup; fresh garden house salad with Cabernet Sauvignon vinaigrette; to the main course including the steak to the thickness, temperature, and cut of your choosing with a baked potato with all the fixings, Bern's special onion rings, carrots, and seasoned green beans. Following a fine dinner, you are taken for a tour of the kitchen including the "largest privately owned wine collection in the world" and the prized $49k bottle of wine, ending in the uniquely styled desert room where it is recommended to try the Macadamia Nut Ice cream or the Creme brûlée. All finished in a whopping 3 hours, just in time to be rolled back out to your valet parked car. Highly recommended if you're looking to feel like a king or queen for the evening.

text:

When I went there last week my husband got the biscuit and said it was the best biscuit he'd had in a very long time! They had a nice selection of jams and jellies as well. I had a waffle last week and it was crunchy and tasty. I had an odd craving for Cream of Wheat this last time I went there and ordered it and it was fantastic! A big bowl full of creamy, warm, comforting cereal accompanied by several options of things to add such as raisins, brown sugar and butter.

The coffee is also good which is not to be taken for granted!

Great place. Super reliable. I'll definitely be going back....soon!

text:
I can't even believe that it took me so long to finally discover the deliciousness of Paladar 511.
Tall son, Leonard was in town and I wanted to drive up to the city to Brunch and celebrate the early days of my 54th year.

As I perused over my favorite breakfast places, I noticed my bookmark for Paladar.  I thought, perfect reason to explore a new restaurant.  I had read so many nice things about the food, I knew the timing was kismet (I wanted to use kismetical, but pretty sure I just made that word up and if I did, the definition is magical fate).

I hurriedly went online and made a reservation since it takes me at least 45 min to drive up to the city.  No problems, I snagged a res for 2.  We found parking fairly close on the street and walked about a block around and down towards Paladar 511.

And then we enter........wow! It's like my dream home. A cross between rustic industrial and luxurious furnishings.  We were seated at a tiny table that butts up against the wine cellar(of course, like our cemetery's, it's really not a cellar....but you get the drift).

We scanned the menu and decided on the eggs Benedict, the lemon pancakes and the yogurt with granola.  Yeah it was way too much food. We was a little piggy like that, but heck....I'm a food lover.  Oh and we ordered a side of bacon too.

The food was amazing as with each bite, Oooohhs and ahhhs were heard between bites.  We left super full and mad at ourselves that all we wanted to do was sleep. As I passed the open kitchen, I thanked the chefs for making such beautiful and delicious food.  

I can't wait to return.  In fact I have a visiting friend in town right now and I know where I'm taking her. I want her to realize that her trip was kismetical and a trip to Paladar 511 certainly makes sense.

text:
You know how sometimes you know something is good but it doesn't hit you how good until you see it through someone else's eyes?

I've had Goldie before. It's been solid. Their falafel is pretty good, and I like falafel from time to time.

And their tehina shake. Oh, the tehina shake. I've had it and enjoyed it and thought it was surprisingly "creamy" (can you call it creamy when there's no dairy?) and delicious.

I came here again the other day when my friend was visiting. I thought she might like the vegan aspect of the shake. Having it with her made me realize how unique this shake really was. 

How DO they get it so smooth and creamy? What is this amazing Turkish coffee flavor with the cookie that is crumbly and just the right texture to complement the shake? Why have I never appreciated what was right in front of me?

Through her eyes, I realized I was taking this amazing shake for granted. There's a reason for the long lines. You don't get something like this just anywhere with no line. Try it. Love it. Appreciate it like an out-of-towner would. Thanks Goldie :)
name: Alice

text: Parking was not an issue and I did not have to wait for a table - around 6:15pm on a Sunday evening.   Ordered the stuffed mushrooms.  I did not care for them at all.  An overwhelming taste of cheese and walnuts that did not compliment the mushrooms.   My main course was the crab cake.  They were over done to almost burnt.  They looked liked they came out of a frozen supermarket dinner package.  The hash browns were just cubes of potatoes with minute pieces of onions and a weird seasoning.   The corn was covered with cyan pepper and were too spicy to eat.  I was very disappointed with my meal.   The waitress was wonderful and was very friendly, efficient and helpful.
name: Chattycathy

text:
It's really more of a 3.5 and to be fair it's only been open about a week.
Reading the menu made my mouth water.
We started with the pimento cheese spread which was solid.  Needed more ritz crackers and fewer saltines. The pickled veggies that came with it were a nice touch.
I had the the Limp Brisket Sandwich which was brisket with purple onions that were pickled/Caramelized with a nice smoky melted cheese.  The slaw on top of the sandwich made it a bit soggy/wet and the brisket was pretty good but a bit dry.
My husband had the pork Bahn mi sandwich. Loved the concept but the pork too was dry.
Nice selection of sauces & the service was very attentive.  They all worked as a team and took good care of us. Everyone was super friendly.
We'd definitely try it again in another month or so.
name: Bridget

text: My lady and I went here Saturday night for the food and live music. The food was excellent, but be warned; If you eat in the bier garten the menu is limited and all self serve. The only table service in this section is to pick up the plates and empty glasses. We tried several items and I recommend allot the. The sausage platter was very tasty and the hot mustard will light you up, but perfect for the different meats.  The stuffed mushrooms were very good and filling too. The potato's were OK,  but more than edible,  even though they went a little crazy with the sour cream. The music was great and the garten (Beer Garden) is a fun place to see/gear live music. I'm looking forward to next time eating inside so I can choose from the main menu. I would have given this place a 5 star rating had it not been for the above mentioned item. All in all,  I highly recommend this place...
name: Joe

text:
Outstanding service! Friendly, attentive, but not intrusive. 
We had several appetizers, the mushroom dumplings and the short ribs were superb. Our main dishes were; fried rice, lamb, Branzino fish, eggplant all were excellent! For dessert we sampled a chocolate-banana torte, so yummy, creamy and crunchy and not to sweet, also the tapioca which was very liquidy, unlike what we had as kids, but very good. I also had a delicious cup of chrysanthemum tea, just one of a good selection of interestingly different teas. 
The atmosphere was nice, upscale, dimly lit, pretty and modern decor. I highly recommend!
name: Anne

text:
4.5

After seeing a review of the day being featured for Nectar Urban, I knew I had to check this place out. I got a Chicken Tinga taco and a Yazoo Dos Perros Decker taco.

The chicken tinga one had chipotle & onion braised chicken, avocado spread, a house crema, and jalapeños (which I had to take off bc they were too spicy. But, hey, I still got the cool aesthetic colors with it so that's all that matters right?). The Yazoo one had Yazoo braised brisket, pepper jack cheese, pico de gallo, horseradish crema. Both were AMAZING but I really liked the Yazoo one better. As you may know in my previous reviews, I'm a brisket kind of guy so I naturally loved it better.

We also got an order of the avocado fries, served with a morita ketchup, which was absolutely delicious. A definite must with your meal.
name: Jeremy

text: Joanie was our waitress, and her great service and recommendations set us on a delicious journey! We ordered the lamb and the filet for mains, chargrilled oysters for appetizers, and the coconut cake and poached pear for desserts. Everything was perfect in terms of taste, texture, and cook. I am a New Orleans native, and the food here is exceptional--innovative and modern, but still classic New Orleans ingredients!
name: Kristen

text: Ordered food via Uber Eat, food are packaged well, tasted good! The only downside is I had a massive diarrhea for 4 days after eating them. I think it's because the food are a bit too spicy( which is my fault. I ordered the hottest option). Will eat here again.
name: Erik

text:
Previously named El Pulgarcito, this place has been around for the last few (5+) years and has amassed quite the following because of its simplicity and great food. 

Their service surpasses anyone else selling pupusas/Salvadoran eats in the area. You are greeted quickly upon seating yourself in this former BK, and although the place lacks any kind of extravagant decor or amenities, their food is on point and the service is friendly. 

Everything from pupusas, massive traditional breakfast platters, to their more standard dishes (caldos/stews, tortas, and tacos). You'll find something to love here. 

Last time we were in, we tried riguas (a compressed corn patty) which were a little drier IMO than others I've had, but I'm undeterred and don't mind trying anything from here. For now I'll stick to my usual of pupusas and fried plantains. 

La Salvadoreña is by far a family and personal favorite and I will most definitely be back again and again.
name: Soraya

text: The food was good and the service was easygoing. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Would probably stop in again if nearby. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. The leftovers held up okay the next day..
name: User

text: Food was fresh and service was quick. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. Would return. Food was fresh and service was quick.
name: User

text: Pretty interesting layout. One section feels like a pizza parlor. The other feels like a brewery. The beer were pretty amazing and the food was good. Service was on point. Only reason for 4/5 stars is there was a female bartender who came on and clearly did not know anything about beer. Couldn't answer any of our questions. Don't have employees who can't answer basic beer questions behind the bar.

text: my friend liked it more than I did. Food was fresh and service was quick. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. Also, the fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. idk I'd try something else next time.

text: Great food, super nice people, great drinks.  A solid place to spend the afternoon.  Also perfect for those OOO work days...

text: Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Not bad for a quick meal. Food was fresh and service was quick. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean.
name: User

text:
I ordered takeout from Nocella which included a steak sandwich with fried onions and sharp provolone cheese ($9.95). Also ordered a stromboli with sausage, ricotta, broccoli rabe, and provolone ($14.95).
The cheesesteak was reasonably filled in a sesame seed long roll. It was very good but just a tad pricey. There is an upcharge for fried onions. As cheesesteaks go, this is one of the better ones around town.
The stromboli was also very good, well filled, and tasty. The side sauce was a bit bland but good that it was included. Not all places provide the side sauce. Wish they had used sausage slices instead of crumbled sausage. The broccoli rabe was chewy but that is the way it is - maybe spinach would have been better.
Management was very nice and accommodating, allowing me to use my dine-in only voucher for takeout because of limited mobility. I really do not get the dine-in only restrictions on most vouchers. 
This brings me to why not 5 stars. That is accessability. They need to install railings on the front steps for those people that need to hold onto something while climbing stairs.
I would definately order from Nocellas again.
name: MARSHALL

text: Had brunch here over the weekend and it was kind of a mixed bag. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. Also, no big complaints, just a nice meal. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Anyway, nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Food was fresh and service was quick. Nice little spot, decent portions too. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything..
name: User

text: I am never visiting this place again. The food was fine but the way we were chased by our waiter was something I'll never forget. I recently moved to US with my husband and had no idea about the tipping policy. Apart from my own country we have lived in UK and Australia for a while I have never heard of 'forced tip policies'. As soon as we left the waiter shouted from the door of the cafe....Thank you so much. Confused I said thank you back. He got angrier and came into the parking lot. It was an intimidating moment where he demanded his tip in anger as I held close to my husband. Honestly I think I've learnt the wrong way that a tip is mandatory. The experience has left me in a distaste and I'd probably never visit this place again. It makes me wonder that did he understand we were new and part of it was racist?
name: Madhavi

text: one of the best clubs in the city! the security does not tolerate any inappropriate behavior which is nice considering how many hetero men come to this club. the drinks are strong and you don't need more than two to get you drunk. vibe is amazing and hey have something for everyone!!!

text:
My boyfriend and I were so excited to go here for dinner. I live above this restaurant and we finally found the time to go. We had a 5pm reservation and we were immediately rushed into the door upon arrival. They moved some tables around and we had to sit in the very middle of the small (tiny) restaurant. It was so jam packed that people's coats brushed over our bread as they walked by. Also, it was SO LOUD in there, we had to literally scream at each other to communicate. We will not be returning, and were very disappointed with the experience.

2 stars because the food was very good and the waitress was great too.

text: I've been through the drive through here a couple times, and the service has been outstanding! Like, freakishly good. That's the only reason I can think of to write a good review of a fast food joint. Yeah, clean, consistent. Too expensive for what you get, but the service left an impression. A go-to after everything else has closed, and nothing at home looks good.

text:
Came here for trivia on a Tuesday! Fun time! The trivia questions were fun. Tons of seating inside and outside. Get here early for trivia since it gets crowded! 

I ordered beer cheese fries. They were very good and fresh. 

Nice beer selection according to my friend. I don't drink beer so I didn't order anything.

text: My husband took our family here after finding it on Yelp. BBQ nachos sounded really good so I ordered that for my dinner. I wasn't very thrilled with it. The pork was super soft and the cheese had a weird texture. Not many BBQ sauce choices. My husband, however, got the brisket burger and brisket chili and really liked those two menu items. The potato chips were pretty good too and it looks like they're homemade.

text: Food: excellent, service: subpar. We had reservations for 2pm, but was told by the waiter Russell that the kitchen will need to switch over for dinner so our order will need to be placed all at once. Our food came out within 10 minutes, rushed, and we barely could get a second round of drinks before asked if we needed anything else while handed the check. I understand the need for shift change, but there is a better way to address this issue while keeping customer service in mind. Especially when you gather for a special occasion planning months in advance.

text: Not going back, we ate there about 6 months ago it was OK, I had the overpriced Pork Chop it was just OK. Must say the ambient is very nice. Tonight we visited thinking we would enjoy a great meal. The service was GREAT but the food was just plain BAD. This  place has BAD over priced nasty stuff coming out of the kitchen. Last visit for us. There are better places to eat at Wiregrass YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED.

text: We had a table, sat down and barely 10 min later got kicked out because they have to get other customers in. I felt rushed during the entire dinner and had to finish my meal early. Very Disappointing.

text:

This place did not disappoint. Spicy, flavorful and plentiful.

snow pea leaves, and the (5/5) 
Not too oily, perfectly salted and plentiful!

authentic menu and execution

Friendly and attentive staff

CONS:
Can't think if any other than it gets pretty packed once the clock strikes noon- but obviously a sign of a good place!

The noise level was beyond miserable.  The utensils were dirty. Such a huge disappointment!!!

text: Came here today for the first time because I've heard so many great things about it. However, I was pretty disappointed. I ordered the OMG burger which to me was lacking in flavor. Only had about 3 bites and I was over it. I also ordered the paradise pizza. Again, lacked in flavor and tasted like a regular frozen pizza. Maybe their other items are better but for me it was a thumbs down. The restaurant itself was also pretty dirty especially their soda area and bathroom. Sadly will not be coming back.

name: Greg

text: I don't know what was worse here. The service, the food or the coffee. We came in on a Sunday at about 1pm. We were told it was a 15 minute wait tops.  There were several empty tables. We ended up waiting around 30 minutes. First off, our server didn't greet us promptly to take our drinks order. When we finally ordered our drinks and got the coffee, it was the most disgusting watered down coffee I have ever tasted. Didn't end up drinking it. No amount of creamer could have fixed that mess. When she came to take our order, someone in my party asked what the blueberry pancakes consisted of: fresh berries or a compote. The server couldn't really tell her. The server didn't know what a compote was. When our order arrived, we asked for butter for the pancakes. She came back with refrigerated, cold butter in single serve packs. That doesn't spread well on pancakes. We asked for warm whipped butter and server said that the packs were all they had. She came back later with whipped butter but said it's usually only for the cooks to use - not to give to guests. Syrup was also cold. We had to constantly flag her down for refills, napkins, water. She brought our glasses of water with no straws. Very inattentive server. When we asked for napkins, she reached over to the empty table behind us and handed us the two napkins so she didn't have to make another trip. The only good thing about the chicken avocado sandwich was the bacon, avocado and the onion rings on the side. The chicken was flavorless and chewy. The cheese and bread were dry. Also, who serves chocolate chip pancakes with a lettuce garnish?? LOL. When our bill came, it was $61 for three plates of food, three gross coffees and two kids juices. They even charged an extra $2.69 for blueberries for their supposed blueberry pancakes and did not disclose that at the time of ordering that there were any extra charges for fresh berries. Too expensive for extremely subpar food and service. Back in the day, this was a great place to dine. It's really changed for the worst!
name: Aly

text:
Woah! Delicious! 

Let me just say, that for a food court sushi bar, I didn't have high expectations, but after ordering three rolls, I fell in love! The sushi was fresh and made right in front of us by the kindest man. I ordered the Mardi Gras roll, the garden district and a tuna roll. 

The rolls were so large and the prices were cheap! Definitely would go back

text: We enjoyed a lovely evening celebrating an anniversary and our experience was wonderful. Stu our waiter was great, food was excellent. We had a combination of small plates and meals and it was timed perfectly. Beautiful setting for a romantic night.

text: My daughter flew into Philly  and was looking for a place to eat breakfast not far from the airport..I put in breakfast in Yelp and Rythm and Brunch came up..I'm so glad it did...everything was cooked to perfection...my daughter had French toast, eggs and Turkey bacon..I had chicken wings and waffles,  and my wifethe shrimp and grits...all I can say is bravo...i have found a great spot and will be returning

A very pleasant experience. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon.

text: An amazing burger!!!  Fries terrific too and incredible variety of toppings and styles.

text: So, I have been to many Palms-starting with the original NYC location (now sadly closed) which was around the corner from my old law firm. Philly, Chicago, Houston, Dallas (gone)...now the Nashville Palm. This place right in the heart of Music Row next to all the honky tonks was great. Sat in the bar area and service was somewhat slow at first, maybe because of trade shows in town and large very noisy group of hic salesmen with booming voices at the bar. They went to diner and the service vastly improved. Had a 16 oz NY Strip cooked perfectly medium rare. Out of baked pot so had the mashed which was delicious and hot-not cold like far too many places. Ordered a martini which came in a large and proper martini glass and was great. Not in a little champagne glass which are used at far too many restaurants now. Wine a little pricey by the glass, but this is the Palm in Music Row. Inside looked to be classic Palm-clubby, white tablecloths and comfortable. Perfect place to bring clients, watch a game at the bar with great food, bring family...Would absolutely come back here with all of the above. Why not a 5? Because there are some steakhouses in Chi-town which are simply a 5 and this is not one of them. Awfully close, though.
name: John

text:
We just returned from a"Restaurant Week" dinner at Harp & Crown.
The physical layout is very nice although there are areas where people are really on top of each other to squeeze more people in.
We were told that unlike other restaurants for restaurant week, Harp  and Crown allows anything on the menu/ i.e. appetizer,entre, but no dessert, as we sadly found out.  Something was lost in translation with  the waiter, because we ordered JUST THAT. All that we thought was allowed for $35.00-  The waiter told us that this would normally be a $45.00 dinner.
It was only after our meal, when the check came, that we saw there was no RESTAURANT WEEK accomodation at all. We were charged exactly what the bill would have been on a  regular night. That was disappointing to say the least. It was AFTER we got our check that the waiter explained that it was only the items on the sides of the menu that were on restaurant week.  Duh.
Why in the world, since there are so many items on the menu that they could  not print up a special menu  for restaurant week.  
We saw our waiter again explaining the menu to others who  also had blank looks on their faces.
The food was OK but I wouldn't even begin to rate the food because the policy was so screwed up.
People hate feel "had."
For that reason, we would not return.  We don't play games and neither should the  restaurant.
name: Helen

text: Tried this spot for lunch during a work break. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. Price felt a touch high for what it was. I'd maybe go back, but I'd order differently next time.

text: So adorable inside, super old school feel. Service was on point and food was delicious! I would highly recommend this place for small parties under about 6 people.

text: I love the food here, typically, but I brought up some customer service issues through social media and e-mail, and have basically been ignored.  It seems for what a customer pays, the service should be there.

text: Ordered an Old City Special medium pizza to go. OMG, soooo good!!! Excellent service, very fast. Cheap and delicious. It's a must!!!!

text:
Definitely a different take on how to serve wine. I wouldn't call this a wine bar, they are a wine market. The bottles are on racks in the restaurant, you pick one out and they will open it for you. Prices are marked up much less than normal at restaurants and no corkage fee. There is a full service bar that has a few wines available, as well as beer and liquor selections. 
The decor is nice, tile floors, dark wood walls, moderate noise. Service was very good - attentive and helpful.
The food was excellent especially the pork cheek - very tender and flavorful. Pasta was cooked well. Nice selection of Italian food. 
Cannoli was very good for dessert. Made fresh, crisp on the outside good filling. I would definitely eat here again - even with all of the other good restaurants in New Orleans.
name: Joe

text: Wow.  This place is amazing.  From the service to the food.  All home made.  French onion soup, no better.  The dinners are incredible and prepared to order.  More than enough food and great taste.   Oh and the device... spot on!!!

text: Had brunch here over the weekend and it was kind of a mixed bag. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. The staff seemed tired but still polite. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price..

Great people watching and lovely on a day with great weather - which is pretty much every day in Santa Barbara!

text:

text:
Love having this small independent grocer in an old bungalow close by that specializes in European foods. Only 5 parking spaces are out front next to the barbecue pit. 

Inside, meats, sausage and few cheeses adorn the cases. The shelves are stocked with pastas, grape leaves and other components of Mediterranean cuisine. The also have a few unusual items that you would not expect at a grocery such including antiques and BBQ supplies. 

They also offer fresh made sandwiches, tacos etc with daily specials. Various barbecue (pork, Carolina, brisket, ribs) are found on their menu above the counter. Hand written signs describe daily specials. Today, Carolina BBQ sandwich with one side is just $6.49 or a catfish sandwich with a side for $6.99. Sides range from fries to 2 different types of coleslaw to bacon mac and cheese. 

I opted for the Carolina BBQ sandwich with fries. There is a small dining area in the back with a tv playing the local news. Vintage knickknacks adorn an old mantle. There about a dozen people waiting for sandwiches, which come out fairly quickly in little red paper lined baskets. The sandwich is hot in a kosher roll. Fries are thin cut and crispy, just like I like them. Two types of BBQ sauce are on the table and I opt for a dark vinegar sauce. The sandwich is good with plenty of chopped meat. The flavor is subtle and the meat is tender. The fries are fantastic.

The brats are made on site. I want to try those next week. They offer a selection of bottled beer and wine and also have a selection of eclectic sodas. 

Don't forget to stop at the ice cream freezer on the way out for frozen treats at $1 each!
name: Katherine

text:
It's a small little place, but a little pricey for what you get in little new port richey. 

BEST MACARONI SALAD EVER!! 

It's not fresh food and yet they are charging fresh prices.  The crab cake is great! Not that much filler at all! The grilled shrimp are cooked perfectly and are seasoned well. 

I ordered a crab cake appetizer, then the fish and shrimp. The fried shrimp wasnt too good they were greasy and it was like a thick coating that was gummy attached tot he shrimp.
I think they're frozen so I'd stay away from fried shrimp. 

The macaroni salad is great! The fries were dry stay away but the sweet potato fries are awesome! 
I would stick with grilled not fried.

text: I really love this place! I mean, what's not to love? I'm not even an omelette person but they are divine here and always cooked to perfection. My favorite is The Omelette You Can't Refuse, which includes potatoes, cheese, bacon, sour cream (perfect with some sriracha). It comes with salad and toast, but I sub the salad for fruit with no up-charge (score!). Their fruit is fresh, not canned, which makes a huge difference. Don't forget the cinnamon toast...omg. It's one of the most delicious breakfast sides on the planet (and this is no ordinary toast!). There are lots of other delicious option, such as the homemade chicken salad on fresh baked croissant, avocado toast, salads, etc. The specials are written on the chalk wall by the bar. I've never had a dish here I didn't love. The water is served from a tall glass and you have cups at the table to pour at your leisure. If you want ice, you have to ask (I normally do because the water is typically room temperature). My only disappointment is how expensive everything is. Don't get me wrong, if you can afford it, it's well worth it, but if it were 20% less in cost, I'd come a LOT more. Service is just "okay"; everyone is always in such a rush and seem frazzled since they are nearly always busy, but it's not a big deal. Service is also very quick when eating in (once seated because there is almost always a wait for a table) but much slower when ordering to-go (and trying to track someone down to grab it). I mean, I've been served within 5 minutes of ordering when eating in but to-go has never been less than a 30 minute wait once ordered. Again, the amazing food is worth the wait. All in all, give this place a try - you'll love it like myself and so many others do.

I am a huge fan of Healthy Garden's Food and am a frequent diner there with my family. I recommend them to all my friends, vegan groups and social media sites so tonight I was disappointed not in the food but in a customer service standpoint.  

I took my visiting from college daughter to my favorite place for the first time and the food was awesome and filling by the time we had soup, sweet potato fries and juice our entrees were just too much so Lauren took 4 bites of her falafel wrap(which took 5 minutes extra to arrive after my entree was served)and as we were boxing leftovers she dropped her whole container. I have worked the food industry, Lauren works at Panera and even hubby who ran a Dairy Queen long ago was surprised they didn't comp her new wrap.  

Lauren almost refused it until I hushed her, her managers would flip if anyone did that at work so she is telling her manager and coworkers which is unfortunate.  

If Healthy Gardens customer service matched the food this would be a 5 Star review.

text:
GREAT LOCATION & GREAT REMODEL TO THE BUILDING but don't trust your lunch hour at the 'Time Pit'. 

My colleague ordered the brisket sandwich with cheese added on it; it was made in front of his face and served quick. I ordered the brisket cheese steak with a side of beans, asked them to hold the peppers add lettuce tomato and mayo. You would have thought I ordered the duck l'orange since it took over 30 minutes for one sandwich.  Luckily I was given my beans right away so I was able to eat that while my friends at their whole meals. Keep in mind we entered the building at 11:20 am so they were not busy. While waiting we were asked by the same server twice if we ordered fried pickles as they wandered around aimlessly with the food.  A few moments later we were asked by two different servers if we were waiting for two club sandwiches as they each made a lap around the restaurant desperately looking for order #11. By the 2nd lap you know that food they were holding was ice cold by now.

When I finally approached the counter and asked what the status of my sandwich I was again brought the two club sandwiches from 15 minutes ago so I chuckled a bit, it was either that or cry. Finally, a cheesesteak came out of the void (the kitchen) but to my dismay, it had the grilled peppers and no lettuce, tomatoes or mayo. At this point I accepted defeat on the peppers and told them I asked for lettuce and tomato, and mayo the sandwich disappears into the void again, a server walks right back out and asks if I ordered a cheeseburger. At this point I laugh out loud as I realize this place is an official shit show, I remind him I wanted a cheesesteak with lettuce, tomatoes, and mayo. 

Finally, the sandwich which has been avoiding me for over 30 minutes comes out, I thank my server and walk back to my table enjoy this meal which was now a journey to get. As I open the bread I give a stink eye to the peppers I didn't want and smile gleefully at the lettuce and tomatoes, my eyes dart left and then right searching for the mayo but then like a kick in the throat I realize there was not a drop of mayo to be found.

I ate my sandwich and it was tasty I must admit but no where near tasty enough to be worth the frustration it was to get. Servers were friendly but lacked leadership, there is a clear disconnect from those taking the orders to those running the food. I didn't and don't want a free meal but a simple sorry for the confusion would have been sufficient for me to go back and give this place another shot. But with all the other options in this town, I'm not sure if I ever will. Hope they can get it together and don't wind up another restaurant statistic.
name: S

text:
I've been to Aksum quite a few times & the menu has changed since my last review. We usually come for Brunch; most of the food is solid at least, plus there are some dishes that I especially like.

Food summary (I use ^ to indicate a half-star and * for a full star. So, ***^ means 3.5 stars):

****^ Crispy Brussels sprouts with bacon & cheese are delicious! They're tossed in a sweet balsamic reduction so it's sweet and savory, with crispy outer leaves & tasty inner leaves. This is my fave dish at Aksum 
**** Green eggs and ham: Interesting dish with eggs cooked in fresh, fragrant basil. 
**** Lamb burger was tasty, but the potatoes were a bit mealy and dried out.
*** Beet salad was all right, nothing special
*** Med East platter included different items that were all fine, nothing special
*** Apricot creme Stuffed French toast: Solid, though not as crispy on the edges as I'd like
**^ to ****^ Spiced shrimp & grits: Grits are good. Shrimp is sometimes cooked perfectly & succulent, and overcooked at other times. Ranges from 2.5 - 4.5 stars depending on the day.
** House Potatoes often seem dried out, shriveled, mealy in texture & like they've been sitting around, rather than freshly cooked.

Dinner entrees:
***^ Rib eye was a large, thick steak. We asked for it to be cooked Rare. Part of the steak was cooked at Med Rare, which is reasonably close, but the other part was rather overcooked (Medium/Medium Well). Fingerling potatoes were good.
***^ Roasted Lamb Chops were also overcooked. We asked for Rare. One chop was MR, the other was Medium. The garlic mashed potatoes were good.
** Aksumite vegetable tagine: This dish was not very flavourful
** Moroccan Spicy Shrimp with linguine: Shrimp was overcooked. This dish was bland & uninspired, not tasty. 

Service can be uneven, though servers themselves are generally nice & friendly. Service hiccups include not bringing appetizers out until after we were almost finished eating our mains & not bringing coffee that's ordered. A couple times, staff took away our sharing plates when we were still waiting for food.

Ambience is good. It's a nice place to sit & eat brunch. At dinnertime, the restaurant is dimly lit and has a romantic comfortable feel.

text:

Update: service has improved and food is still great. I love coming here and love the variety of food an

text:
This was the first time I had ever been here but I'd have to say I'm a big fan. 

All of the meat that I sampled was cooked very well. Anything that I didn't like, it was just based on that particular taste but it had absolutely nothing to do with their skill. Just normal taste preferences. :) (The garlic steak was probably my favorite though.) 

The salad bar has a ton of options to try as well so you really feel like you can experience more than just meat. The rolls were delicious and the fried plantains were something I'd never experienced before but I would love to try them again. 

Didn't have a chance to try the mashed potatoes since they didn't serve us very many and I got a little nervous about running out and the people I was with not getting enough but my husband assured me that they were also very good.

Our main waiter checked in with us often and really made us feel welcome and answered any questions that us first-timers had. All of the other people that came by with food were also very polite, friendly, and just overall fun to be around. 

I also really appreciated that they went the extra mile while we were there for my husband's birthday. They offered him a dessert but he said he was so full that he probably couldn't eat any of it even though it sounded delicious. So our waiter boxed up a piece of cheesecake for us to take home. 

I would love to go back and try some other things that I got a little too full for the first time.

I had been looking for some good authentic Mexican food in Indianapolis and am so glad I finally found it. 

I'll start by saying the food was absolutely delicious. The only downside was I didn't have any left to take home. When they brought the chips and salsa, they gave each of us an individual thing of salsa which was neat. For the entree, I got some enchiladas which were top notch. 

Loco also had a great atmosphere, very cool decor and music. The inside is pretty big and the tables are spaced out enough so you're not eaves-dropping on the table next to you. 

As far as price goes, most entrees are between $9-12 and beers are $3-5 for domestic and imported. Very reasonable and honestly less than I was expecting for how delicious the food tasted. 

Per the waitress, this location has been open since November 2018 and was opened a little under a year after the Loco restaurant at 22nd and Delaware.

text: This is my third time coming to Wild Wasabi - it's definitely a good choice for cheap lunch specials, especially if you like sushi. The set-up is buffet style - you have lo mein, vegetables, spring rolls, sugared donuts and two chicken options at the beginning of the buffet, and it  extends into the sushi section, which has about 7 or 8 different options laid out, and then wraps up with a miso soup section and hibachi grill. Of note, I've never done the hibachi grill, but according to the big sign by the front door, it is included in the $12 buffet price. The food is pretty good - I am a sushi fan, and the buffet options are fresh, but probably not as fancy as their regular menu options. Service is good, and quick here - they check on you regularly, which I appreciate. As always, dessert is a must for me, but I've only ever seen the sugared donuts on the buffet (which I'm not complaining about). I suppose for a lunch meal, you don't need a whole lot of dessert. Lol. Definitely check them out - if you're in the Cummins Station area and like sushi, it's worth it, in my opinion.
