text: Went in last night to check out the renovations and the new concept.  The concept is cute, and the decor goes well with the theme. It was extremely loud even though the place was not full. I think they are lacking sound absorption boards because everyone's chattering voices were just bouncing off every surface and it was hard to even hear yourself think. We sat at the bar and it took 10 minutes to even get our first drink, the bartenders seemed like they were getting a bit overwhelmed with a large party in the middle of the bar, because the two guys next to me also waited a long time and weren't quite as understanding.  The cocktails are a little pricy but they're trying to be an upscale craft cocktail bar so it's to be expected.  I'm a vegetarian so I got the stuffed portobello. It had great flavor I just wish the portion of one mushroom cap and small pile of spring mix was a little bigger or had a little bit more to it for the price. I also wish they had more vegetarian and vegan options on their menu, it's just a couple side dishes at this point. It was a decent experience but nothing to rave about and we probably won't be back.

She recommended the bass so I went with her recommendation. My friend ordered the steak and we shared the Brussel sprouts. The food came and I was thoroughly underwhelmed. text:
Playa Bowls just opened in downtown Wayne, and it is a hit with everyone I've spoken to. I just had to try it, based on recommendations. I love juice bars, smoothies, and acai bowls. 

There are many juices, smoothies, and bowls to choose from....or you can customize your own, which is what I did. I chose the acai base, strawberries, blueberries, and granola on top, with peanut butter drizzle. The ingredients tasted very good and fresh. The PB tasted natural. I was so full at the end. My bowl was about $9. This is a little expensive to get everyday, but it was a fun treat on a hot day. 

My mom got a chia seed bowl. She said that it was pretty tasty, but wasn't quite as impressed with the chia seeds as I was with my acai bowl. She did agree that the fruit and granola were really good.   

The only downside was the seating. All of the seats are high barstools without a back. The tables are high, but not high enough for your knees to fit under the table while sitting on the chairs; this makes for an awkward side sit....my mom was not a fan. I'm guessing it's because they don't want you lingering? However, some normal seats would be nice so that you can enjoy your expensive treat. 

I will definitley go back again, although I probably will just take my bowl or smoothie to go instead of sitting on those uncomfortable seats. I definitely recommend you try the place; it's a great healthy choice while out and about in Wayne.
name: Elizabeth

text: So freaking good. I ordered from here tonight and we got spiced chickpeas, falafel, lamb shawarma without the wrap with toum sauce, and a falafel shawarma wrap. So good and such good flavors!!

text:
After experiencing all of the poke restaurants in St. Louis to date, I would have to say that this one is my least favorite. The customer service was satisfactory, the station appeared clean, and the dishes ordered didn't take long to prepare. However, I wasn't too impressed with the poke. Another downside is that Hiro Poke Co. did not have free fountain water. The customer will either have to buy one of their water bottles or go to a different station to get free water.

I tried the following:
1. Tori Paitan Ramen: The broth was flavorful, and I enjoyed the saltiness level. The noodles were the same ones used at most ramen restaurants in St. Louis. The chicken was tender. The portion was fair. I would likely get this dish again. Although, if you ask me how this ramen compares with others around St. Louis, I'd give preference elsewhere.
2. Aloha STL Bowl (with white rice): Plenty of color and looked like a promising choice. There was a decent amount of ahi tuna and salmon in the bowl. The ingredients tasted relatively fresh. However, I realized instantly after taking the first bite that the rice wasn't cooked with enough water. Very disappointing, considering that the rice portion is about half of the bowl. The rice was barely edible, and much of it was discarded because I just couldn't suffer through the crunchy, hard texture anymore. Additionally, I would've liked more sauce drizzled over the poke bowl. Dry rice and not enough sauce is not a good combination.
name: Winnie

text: My friend liked it more than I did. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated bc we didn't have a reservation. text:
This is our second time back to the brand new Wylder. Awesome service and even better food. 

The Bar
There are many intriguing and delicious cocktails to choose from. All of them are very reasonably priced and unique in their own way. My personal fave is the seven devils. Disclaimer: they will go down way too easily, like adult koolaid. 

Ambiance
The restaurant has a cozy feel, all while being stylish. Every little design detail is thought out and on point. Relaxing but still upbeat Music playing In the back ground but low enough that table conversation can flow easily without the "huh?!" "Whatcha say?" In particular I love the long family size table in the middle of the restaurant for a larger group and the lounge-like couch and armchairs in the back. 

Now to the star of the show, the food:
The layout of the menu is perfect, not an overwhelming amount of decisions that's leaves you completely stuck on what you want. Pizzas are broken out by red and white sauce. We have had the honey badger (house fave), the north end, the bronco, Margherita- all of them are really good and we would easily reorder. Their salad portions are generous and designed to share alongside your pizza. It would be great if they offered half portions of their salads but that's minor. For apps, they are known for their mushroom toast and oh my lord- now I know why. It was hard to resist the urge of sliding the plate toward myself and it took serious self control to not devour the whole thing. They also serve a ricotta toast with seasonal jam (usually a savory jam) and this also gave me something to daydream about. Next go around I'll have to save room for a dessert as the rest of the menu would indicate those are bound to be equally as yummy. 

Delicious food. Great cocktails and drinks. Very reasonably priced. Great service (Ashley was awesome)....what else do you need.

text:

text:
I chose this for a final Restaurant Week dinner date with my boyfriend last Friday night. We got held up having cocktails with a friend somewhere beforehand, and when I called to tell Harp & Crown we'd be 15-20 minutes later than our reservation time, the hostess on the phone gave me a clearly pre-rehearsed speech about possibly losing our seats until an unknown time if we were more than 15 minutes late. Luckily, when we arrived, we were offered seats in the downstairs lounge (next to one of the bowling alleys). Basements aren't really my thing, but if you're looking for a sort of sexy, fashionable vibe, that's a good spot for it.

The RW menu was 7 courses for $35pp (and my understanding is that the regular 7-course option is $45pp, so this was a good RW deal but not outrageous). We opted for the salad with sunflower oil (blanking on the name), hamachi, lamb meatballs, spicy sopressata pizza, crab bucatini, scallops, and corn succotash. The scallops were a mistake, not because they were bad (to the contrary, they were quite good), but because there were only two and they were accompanied by what basically amounted to the corn succotash. Had we been aware of this big repeat, we would have opted for the fried okra instead of the corn -- and I might not be still thinking about this several days later but for the fact that I vaguely had the impression our server was laughing at us as we placed our order. As for the rest of it, the pizza and salad were the real standouts in my mind, which was mildly bizarre since this is no Italian joint.

The wine was okay but not special, and the total Friday night bill before tip came to just under $150 before tip. I liked it, but due to the numerous other options in this city for great food and beverages, this won't make any of my top lists.
name: Lynne

text:
Can't say I was impressed with this place. At least, not in a positive way. We paid to park across the street... $8. Would not have ever chosen this place to go to, but wanted to join other UTK alumni for a game. We missed kick off (my bad), and the bar was packed when we arrived. One side of the bar has no windows, so you can imagine the heat when coupled with masses of drinking and yelling football fans. The open air "windows" would come back to haunt me later, when I was getting chowed on under the table by all the mosquitoes that easily crashed the party.
     But, seeing how there was no where to sit or stand, we left. We ate somewhere else, while watching the first half of the game (walking distance from there). We strolled back to the bar afterwards, and it's still overflowing of course. But, we managed to eventually find a table that allowed us to at least partially view the game. We lacked one chair though, and a few of our group circled the bar seeking one out. Out near the windows, was a very large group of fans from the opposing team. They were very loud and had obviously purposely gone there in order to egg on the UT fans. They staked their claim to an entire area and the tables and chairs within that area, even though many chairs weren't in use. I would suggest to the tavern that they close down to the public during those times, and just treat it as a private event for UT alumni. They would have made a lot of money doing it that way. 
     As it was, they couldn't have made much money. Definitely nowhere near what they could have made with some proper planning. Number one priority, HAVE ENOUGH BARTENDERS working. FRIENDLY ones, and considering the crazy atmosphere they need to be experienced and have a lot of patience. I saw ONE person waiting tables. She was understandably stressed, being the only one, and therefore extremely brusque. We ordered just one round of drinks, and made it a pitcher, so as not to tax her too much. She came across as so unpleasant that we wanted no unnecessary interaction with her, and therefore placed no other orders.
     I really hope for their sake they have used that day as a learning experience and maybe have already sharply improved. I can't imagine us going back though...but, then again, I don't live near this establishment.

text:
POACHED PERFECTION

Breakfast that tastes this good deserves a standing ovation.

This multi-purpose restaurant is located west of the Soulard district in St Louis, though it wins no flare points when it comes to their name.  They serve morning fare by day, and in the P.M. hours they transform into 'Spare No Rib', a taco/BBQ joint with a much more amusing moniker.

Needing something in our bellies before a Budweiser tour on 3/26/19, Nichole C picked this place off of a Yelp listing; there's no big signs so you might have a tricky time finding Egg at first.  Once we got seated, she ordered herself a latte ($4).

Our food arrived pretty quickly, all things considered.  My 'El Americano' ($8) came with 2 poached eggs, potatoes, 3 strips of thick-cut bacon, and brioche toast with butter & jam.  The eggs were spot on, the bacon cooked masterfully and the jam tasted homemade.

NC got a half order of the french toast ($5), which came swimming in berry compote and a dollop of mascarpone cheese.  She also got a chorizo breakfast tostada ($5.75) topped with a fried egg and salsa verde.  Both received rave reviews from my better half.

Bread = 5
Circuses = 4

Service was speedy, but our guy disappeared at the end while we waited for the check.  The dining room has a huge vaulted ceiling, and the decor/light fixtures inside could use a thorough dusting.  Lots of cobwebs hanging around doesn't set the ideal mood for eating (unless it's a Halloween brunch).

Being the stickler that I am for typos, I noticed a few spelling errors on their menu -- "fruit campot", "mascapone" -- which isn't a huge deal.....but a minor revision wouldn't hurt.  Just a thought  :)

* TL;DR *

The eggs are picture-worthy, the lattes beautiful and the prices fair.  Aside from a quick cleaning there's not much I'd change about Egg (okay, the name needs changing.  Whatever brilliant mind thought that one up needs a creativity enema!)

Overall I'd say this place lives up to its namesake.  Totally recommended.
name: Eric

text: I really wanted to like Noodleholics with their great reviews. Unfortunately for me, it was not a very nice eating experience.  I was the second person there for the evening meal, since these folks are not open all day. At a few minutes after five, a stone-faced waitress came to unlock the door but didn't even bother to say hello. No customary pleasantries or welcome. Ok. I can handle that. Then I ordered the beef brisket noodle soup. Their broth is tasty (as good as Miss Saigon or China Szechuan). However, when my soup arrived I felt it needed a little bit more chopped scallion, so I asked for another pinch. Kitchen said no. The onion is already in the soup. That's what they said. So too bad for me. But worse than that, half of my brisket was grossly rubbery and inedible. I was one of the first customers in for the evening meal, and perhaps they had not cooked it long enough since brisket is not served undercooked and full of gristle, so I mentioned it to the waitress. As soon as I took a photo of the food and started writing this review, another waitress quickly came by to offer a serving of barbecued pork and more scallions (on the house).  So I accepted. And good thing, otherwise I would have missed out on some tasty barbecued pork. Ok. Maybe I'll come back and try again. But I do think the "trendy" label is meaningless if the brisket is tough, the wait staff is stone-faced, I can't request a spoonful of scallions and the hard cold metal chairs are made for smaller butts than mine. Thank you for trying.

text: Where to begin...I made a reservation for 18 people for 9:00pm. I was told from the beginning that we would receive two tables which was fine. We were not seated until after 9:40. The manager told us we would receive a round of drinks on them for us being so patient. After being seated the waitress made an announcement to both of our tables about how the dining experience is for everyone to tell her what you want and she will decide how many to order because everything was shareable. She also said some cocktails were coming because we waited so long to be seated. She began taking drink orders. Things were going pretty smooth aside from the very large table behind us constantly getting up and knocking a few of our purses off of our chairs (at least three times). Oh and one of the ladies had on a VERY strong perfume that was giving myself and a friend a headache (not the restaurants fault but just added fuel to the fire by the end of our dining). So after we all order (both tables) they began bringing out food not too long after. We noticed that the other table with our party was getting more food at a time. We waited a little too long for more of the food to come out. Jump ahead the other table finished 45 minutes before us. We were there for a birthday and because they finished they went ahead and left. After we received majority of our food we asked the waitress where two of our pizzas were. She came over and showed her ticket and said she forgot to put them in (literally the only things not scratched off her list) and asked if we still wanted them. It was now 11:00pm. Yes we wanted them. They rushed the order because the pizza was mostly red sauce with like three pieces of mozzarella on it. Disgusting! While waiting for the pizza some people ordered dessert and we told the waitress we were there for a birthday. They brought the cake out and started singing while i was eating the pizza. I was so annoyed. Jump ahead to 11:40, we received our check. I immediately see the first round of cocktails on the bill. I tell the waitress. She says she doesn't remember what we got so they took 15% off. That would've been fine had we not had 10 people with each drink being a minimum of $10 a piece. The totals didn't equal out. We paid and tipped about 15% which is not like me but our service was terrible. I went to the restroom and while waiting I hear our waitress complaining to the manager that it wasn't her fault and that we should've tipped more. To recap the BS...we were seated 40min late with a reservation, we were told TWICE that the first round of drinks was on them, one table was finished before the other, the waitress forgot our food, we were rushed at the end because they close at 12 (hence the nasty pizza and putting chairs up while we were still in there), and now I have to listen to someone complain because of her mess ups. Lastly, the manager and the owner never once came to our table to say anything! They were busy with the table of about 16 behind us who sat right after us, got their food before us, and were finished over an hour before us. Time frame at this restaurant 9:00-11:50. It gets one star but deserves a zero. I am so sad that our experience here was so terrible.

Another time I asked for cheese enchiladas and I got chicken instead. I think the restaurant ought to do something about their service.
name: S

text: If you're looking for excellent Thai food, this is the place. I had the small wonton soup for an appetizer. It was delicious and flavorful. I then had the garlic beef stir fry for dinner. So tasty! The portions are huge, the service is great and the price is right.
name: Chris

text:
Quite honestly, I came to this restaurant without any major expectations. I literally was just hoping for a decent pasta dish for the night. 
On a snowy night, the parking lots was covered in salt. The entrance had a white sheet on the ground to soak up water. And then we enter the room was dimly lit, with old Italian paintings, and wine bottles as decor. It looked like a typical run down Italian joint. 
Regardless, the waiter was a delight and we went with that he recommended. 
The fried artichokes were a great simple start. They very outer layer tasted a little burnt, but the inside was great. 
The papperdelle ricotta pasta and fettuccine with red sauce were amazing. Fresh pasta. Cooked to perfection. Light and fresh ingredients. Literally everything I needed in the form of carbs for a cold night. 
We ended with the tiramisu of course, which was also delicious. 

The food is great. The atmosphere is okay. But I think I'd come back for a night of delicious carbo-loading.
name: Komal

text:
We came here for Tapas because we heard it was really good.  Overall our experience was good one, but not great.  I do feel like this place is a little pricey for tapas.

We started off with Mole Margaritas. Tasty though they could have poured the drink to the top of the glass.

Cana De Cabra (Murcia):  A good way to start off your meal.  If you like goat cheese I suggest you start here.  Nice and creamy and tasty!

Gambas Al Ajillo:  Probably my least favorite dish of the night. To me the shrimp tasted a little fishy.

Pulpo A La Gallega: The octopus was probably my favorite dish of the night.  The octopus was cooked perfectly and the potatoes were a great compliment!

Seared Maine Scallops: The scallops were fresh and also cooked perfectly.  I've had better Romesco, but still a good dish overall. 

We went to the rooftop bar after dinner for a night cap.  The ambiance is  great though they are a little limited on the overall alcohol selection.  I'd still come back for drinks again.
name: Randy

text: Came here at the recommendation from a local resident and I was very impressed! The inside is very clean, outside looks a little sketchy. Food was fresh and fast and the prices were fair! We will be back!
name: Cole

text: The food is delicious here, from the apps (tomato-basil soup, lobster bisque) to the entrees (braised lamb shank, chicken marsala).  Our server (Sheyla) was very friendly and accommodating.
name: Susan

text: Felix's holds a lot of sentimental value for me. It was the very first restaurant I dined in during my first trip to NOLA. It was also the very first place I've ever had a po' boy and chargrilled oysters. As you can imagine, the bar is now set very high. We grabbed a seat at the oyster bar and were immediately greeted with two freshly shucked raw oysters. I've enjoyed plenty of oysters from both coasts at a wide variety of establishments both throughout my life as well as in New Orleans specifically and the raw oysters we ordered here were by far the largest I've ever had. More sweet than briny, they were amazing! I also loved the delicate, smoky flavor of the chargrilled oysters. My husband ordered an oyster po'boy while I grabbed half a shrimp po' boy and a cup of crawfish etouffee. Both orders were excellent, with mine being the clear winner in my opinion. Loved that they offered a few combo options for people like me with limited time in the city and limited space in the tummy. The po' boys were all I hoped for and more, but that etouffee was a revelation! Washed it all down with two expertly crafted bloody marys, decked out with raw oysters and poached shrimp. A true NOLA legend!
name: Camille

text: Terrible food, terrible service! Came here after Barkus for an early dinner, and was disappointed to say the least. We used the yelp offer for a free appetizer and ordered the caprese tower which was just giant thick slices of tomato and thick old mozzarella. My friend ordered a half a dozen of oysters and they came on a watery bed of ice. No presentation at all. For our entrées I ordered the shrimp and grits And she had theShrimp ravioli. My shrimp was tough, the grits were not seasoned in the least, and there were hard chunks in it also. This may fool a tourist but I live in the Quarter and this dish would not have and  should not have been served anywhere! My friend said her ravioli tasted like it just came out of the microwave. The pasta was tough and the meat she said was bland at best. What a shame because I am always getting asked for food recommendations in the neighborhood and I will happily tell people to steer clear of this place! To top off our awful meals, The waitress charged us incorrectly I was charged for my friends meal which was significantly more expensive than mine and vice versa. When we told the waitress she just said oh... We then waited for a few minutes for her to come back and rectify it but she never did so we just left with our incorrect charges.
name: O

text: Found this place while running errands in the area and boy was I pleased. They offer a good range of Mediterranean food options to please any pallet. I opted for the classic Kafta plate with hummus and fattoush salad and man was belly and taste buds happy. The meal was flavor packed and the perfect size portions to not leave you hungry. The fresh made pita was excellent and the perfect compliment to the tasty hummus. If your in the area and in the mood for a taste of the Mediterranean or Middle East make it a point to stop in and give them a try.
name: Steve

text: This place has a great atmosphere, friendly staff and an extensive menu. The only reason I wouldn't give it five stars is the value. Most entrees are in the $18-22 range, but the quality and portions are that of a $10-14 range. Happy hour is nice though - half off wine and beer until 5:30 and select cocktails (G&T, lemon drop, The Sedona - a pomegranate/citrus/gin specialty - and one other I can't remember) are $6 until 6:30. Small plates are discounted too. All in all, a good experience but I just don't think the value is on par with the prices.
name: Aaron

text: This is a great place. A great environment with good reasonable pricing,  always good service. You always know what expect each time you go to eat here. Best Fish and Chips and Mac&Cheese in town!
name: Mark

text: Super friendly and comfortable, great food and clean! My wife and I went for breakfast today and can't wait to go back. Creative specials and high quality food cooked to perfection.
name: Jeff

text: Best Oysters in the French Quarter area! Don't forget to ask for Lorenzos' special sauce
name: Omri

text: This might be the worst Burger King ever. My family and I went through the drive-thru for lunch. There was no one in front or behind us and the had us move forward and park to wait for our food anyway. When we got home we were missing cookies and more importantly, the food was not at all fresh and the fries were burnt. I love Burger King but I don't think this restaurant should be associated with the company.
name: Rese

text: We really enjoyed dining at the Tavern. We stopped in with out reservations on a Saturday night and we sat overlooking the kitchen. The staff was friendly and the service was outstanding. We really enjoyed the food. Thanks so much!!
name: Big Daddy

text: The vibe in this place is awesome, the drinks are great, the guava burger on a Hawaiian roll is perfect, juicy and flavorful. Next time getting the speakeasy burger, oh and don't forget the waffle fries.
name: Arnaldo

text:
Came here cause of the Groupon and have heard from multiple people it's a great spot for sushi. I've yet to find my go to sushi place in Philly so it was great to try it out!

The two of ordered the sushi & sashimi combo for two, which ended up being enough to fill me up but not my friend. He ended up ordering another roll and that was enough. The fish was of good enough quality, but wasn't super impressed. The rice kind of had a spongy texture and didn't do it for me. I liked the sashimi more than the other items on our combo plate.

Their happy hour deals are really great, with half off cocktails and beers. Even on a Friday! Our server was really nice!

Our check still ended up being quite steep even with the great Groupon deal, so I'm not sure I would've paid the full price for the food. Guess I'll keep looking for my go to sushi spot!
name: Vicki

text:
I went here with a close group of friends for brunch. We had to wait about 15 minutes even though the restaurant seemed empty. Very small place. Would not recommend if you're looking to be seated right away for a big group (i had 5 people in my group). Once we got seated, it was very crowded. 

Overall presentation of the food was great. Taste was good as well. There wasn't much to critique about the food. 

Prices are reasonable as well. The only downside about this whole experience at Greg's was the wait time. My friends and I decided to walk up and down Main Street because there was no room to wait inside.
name: Mirriam

text: If it's your first time visiting Nashville this is one hot spot not to miss. Not to mention, especially if your looking for that southern taste & hospitality. I myself who isn't much of a biscuit lover or eater to say the least loved the food here!
name: Stephanie

text:
If you are looking for a great place for a business lunch then look no further, its The Grill.  Excellent food, prices and service is outstanding.  My favorite is the Atkins burger. 

Dinners are equally as good, is hmmm, everything.
name: Richard

text: Stopped by after work because I was nearby and hungry. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. No big complaints, just a nice meal. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. You can tell they care about customer experience here. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent.
name: User

text: Literally stood in line for 40 minutes because new guy kept messing up orders just to get cold food
name: Matt

text: Best service! Excellent food! Had the Molasses Ribs and it was soooo tender! Place is a must!
name: Ro

text: It is pretty good. I've only been twice and I don't think I've found my favorite menu item yet. Kung Pau Chicken was not that great but honey chicken was very good. Very quick and good customer service. Great food if you're in a hurry. Combos are about $10...
name: Maddie

text: Great restaurant with a great staff! Super friendly and very patient. The food is fantastic and the restaurant has a great vibe. Best BBQ around town for sure.
name: Anna

text: The bad reviews for this place are nonsense, at best. Every time I've been here - (especially recently), the service has been above and beyond, including from someone who I think was the manager. The pastries (I got a muffin) were good, and the latte I got was good as well. Wait was no more than 5 minutes. If you've worked in a service type industry at all in your life, you'd understand that there is a reasonable wait for fresh wood and drinks. If you use the Square coupons they have occasionally, it's a great value as well. To the person that mentioned a "weak" latte - you do realize a latte is one/two espresso shots and full of milk, right? Again, the service here is pretty good as are the coffee and food. I'll have to try the fresh breakfast items soon. Also, not to mention the atmosphere in here is extremely clean and welcoming.
name: Nicholas

text:
Not bad as far as sauce and flavor goes. I don't think the quality of meat is as high as another local place, but the flavor is nice. There is ample seating and powdered chili on the table. This is best for adjusting spice if you don't like being at the mercy of the cook.

I would definitely go back. I had the lamb, beef, bacon wrapped enoki, pork belly, king of ham sausage, korean fish cake, egg plant, fish tofu, tofu, beans, okra, and mantou. Don't get the mantou, it's sweet, which is weird, like a dessert.  The Eggplant isn't on a skewer, it's on a plate and delicious. Probably one of the best.

Fish Tofu skewers are good. Pork belly was over cooked. Korean fish cake is okay. Tofu skewers are good. Okra is good. Beans are good. Bacon w/ Enoki is good. King of ham sausage... stranage, but not bad. Just like a weird hot dog.
name: Dennis

text: We sat right next to the giant aquarium, which was fantastic! Our service was good and the food was super tasty. Their grouper was really good plus a few of us branched out and got their pasta, which was also really good. They also had a really good burrata salad with tomatoes and balsamic! The entire atmosphere was pretty cool, a little touristy, but cool nonetheless.
name: Matt

text: Just a fabulous meal for six out-of-towners!  Great service, wonderful food, enjoyable ambiance.  The short rib pasta was a favorite among the group. The truffle risotto was decadent and there was much sharing of desserts.  I was really pleased and plan to go back!!
name: Bill

text: It's a very charming atmosphere, the staff were friendly and the food was fantastic! We had the surf and turf, which isn't regularly on the menu, and a side of mac and cheese. The steak was cooked perfectly and the swordfish was wrapped in ham. Both were delicious! Overall wonderful meal. We'll definitely be back!
name: Ryan

text: Awesome food. New Chef Patrick Kelly is creating some incredible food. Must come for dinner. You will love how quaint this place is.
name: Betty

text:
Im giving Monk's 5 stars and our waitress a 3. She looked like she hated her job and the people she was serving. Monk's was extremely busy and I get that she was probably in a rush, but I'm a server too and you have to have some kind of friendly customer service. She pretty much threw our food at us and ran off. 

That being said the food and drinks were amazing!!!! One of the best burgers I've ever had..And those fries and garlic aioli, YUM!  Very cool atmosphere as well!
name: Kelsey

text: The food is fresh and delicious. The restaurants are beautiful, and their specialty drinks in the CBD are awesome. I would recommend this to anyone who likes poke.
name: Lance

text:
Based on our wait time and the great reviews, we all had high expectations going on to fill our bellies up for a Sunday brunch before driving back to Indianapolis. 

I should note that personally, there are two types of brunch spots: ones that are very healthy (i.e. Marche) and those that are not-so-healthy (i.e. menus filled with burritos smothered in cheese or similar). Marche was the first of these two with very "light" and not-so-heavy options. While that was okay for me, it's important to note so you set your expectations to a certain standard. 

I opted for the vegetarian omelette as well as cinnamon sugar toast on brioche bread. The omelette came with a side of lightly dressed greens, and I was about done with the omelette before the server delivered my bread. The star of the show was the bread, for sure. The waiter even said it flies off the shelves when it's on the menu. 

Service was great as they were slammed, so he did the best he could. 

All in all a great spot, but the portions were a tad small for me.
name: Brady

text: I know MOD pizza from Seattle.   I was so excited to hear that one opened up here.  I've been there several times, and I have to say this location is just as amazing as the ones in Seattle.
name: Dedra

text: Amazing everything!! Had the traditional pepperoni small (plenty for 2 people). Great sauce, pepperoni slices were huge, and the crust (72 hour process to make) was perfect thickness. Service was amazing too. Very attentive staff and the pizza was made soo fast! We can't wait to go back to try another pizza.
name: Frances

text:
Why 4 stars?  It's always good.  They are consistent in their food quality and the waitstaff is always super nice.  

You can't go wrong with Uncle Hershel's favorite, the only change I make is getting grilled tenders instead of the fried tenders.  If you haven't tried their grilled tenders, you should.  They are really good.  

I want to give them an extra half star for all the candy they have but Yelp doesn't allow that so 4 stars it is!  

BTW, if you like jelly in your biscuits, do yourself a favor and ask for their Blackberry jam.  It's so good!
name: Jim

text: Came here for lunch one day with my husband and we loved it!!!!!! The atmosphere to me is so comfy, yet spacious. The booths have little back pillows, nice touch. We shared a fig burger and flatbread pizza, both were fab. Also service is outstanding, my husband is the guy who drinks 5cokes (i know, bad habit) but usually servers cant keep up with filling his drinks before he needs to ask. Our server Jen was in the top 5 severs we have ever had. And we have high standards when it comes to that. Her delivery, timing, and overall demeanor was exactly what an excellent server should be. We own a restaurant in Westlake, and would totally try and poach her for our place if it was possible. Kitchen is doing their job great as well, food was very fresh. A+
name: Ahnya

text:
A completely unassuming spot inside of Port Orleans. 

If you're a beer drinker, the menu has beer pairing with all the items .

Very delicious. Very unique. Just not what you would expect inside a brewery. Everytime I've been I've eaten new and delicious things. 

Occasionally they've had beer pairing dinners that are fantastic as well. 

I highly suggest a stop in even if you're not a beer fan.
name: Maddy

text: Sooooooo sad, first had to convince someone to try Rooster (he's not a fan of trendy spots), when we walked in, the person that sat us was friendly and said we could sit where we wanted, three employees were clowning around while cleaning the tables next to us, could of given us water...The restaurant wasn't busy at 12:00 noon on a rainy Friday.  We sat there for 10 minutes and was never acknowledged, no water, no one even approached to let us know someone would soon be with us.  We walked across the street to City Diner, the waitress greeted with a warm greeting with two glasses of water in her hand.  I was really craving the awesome food at Rooster, but City Diners good too, and I wasn't invisible there.
name: Lori

text: Favorite spot for breakfast with my nephew! Super friendly staff and very down to earth environment.  Great food. Great prices. Very clean. Highly recommended.
name: Rebecca

text: Sold me horrible old buffalo wings and didn't care about the quality.  Would not send me to a manager or send a refund.
name: Andrew

text: I grew up in Kansas City, so I'm kind of a BBQ snob. Can a girl just get a burnt end?! BUT!!! Blue Oak is delicious! I have sweet dreams about they're chicken.
name: Maggie

text: Barlines was chosen based on its proximity to where we were hanging out. It's in a great spot-- nestled underneath the Omni and across from the Music City Center. We walked in rather late-- 10:30pm on a Sunday night. There was football on. Our IDs were checked and we were asked to take a seat anywhere. The security was very friendly. We took a seat and 30 secs later we were greeted by a kind female server. It didn't take us long to decide what we wanted, we were starving and exhausted from traveling from that afternoon. I ordered the hot chicken sandwich sans the bun and my friend ordered the burger. We were very happy with the taste and quality of our food. The french fries were well-seasoned as well. The prices were a little steep but based on where this location is, I wasn't surprised. I love the atmosphere and if you're looking for a solid spot to watch a game in downtown Nashville, this is it!
name: Renn

text: The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. Food was fresh and service was quick. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. It was crowded but still moved along. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. For the price I expected more than this. The leftovers held up okay the next day..
name: User

text:
This review is completely about the service because the food is actually 5 stars. I have been here a few times, and every time we encountered rude people. Today for example the man that took our food to our table was extremely rude, when he asked us if we needed anything else and we said we need napkins and a fork he rolled his eyes and leaves gets the stuff comes back and basically slams it on the table and asks us in such a rude way "is there anything else you need??" 
Last time we just got our food to go because again we had a rude woman helping us. 
Again the food is amazing but they need to train their employees better or get new ones that actually like their jobs.
name: Susanna

text:
Great service! The food was good. They easily made accommodations for our dietary restrictions. Had the chicken and the beef plates. Both came with an absolute abundance of food! Both plates came with hummus, stewed veggies, and salad with the most amazing tangy lemon dressing. 

If I had more room in my stomach I would have tried every dessert....they all look amazing!
name: Kelly

text:
This is the best Mexican restaurant around!! Amazing margaritas, food and service! I have never had a bad experience here. My husband and I go out of our way to eat here. Jose the owner is kind and very good at making amazing margaritas! Hands down the best Chalupa around, and well the only place that makes Chalupas this good! Get the steak & chicken chalupa you wont regret it! 

Try this place out! Don't let the negative reviews turn you away. Some people you just can't make happy!!
name: Britt

text: Had the Reggie with Egg, will be back for it order a side of marionberry jelly with it. You will not regret!
name: Leroy

text:
Absolutely love this place!! They have a very vegetarian friendly menu and and a plethora of board games to pick from.
The staff is super friendly and the food is delicious!
Plus their brunch is fab as well as their prices!!
name: Erika

text: Excellent service, staff and the food is amazing!!! The manager is an absolute sweetheart, the cooks can fire up some outstanding food, and the environment is one I could be around everyday!!!! Cheers to the people that have made this place what it is cause I'm a very picky person but I love this place!!!!
name: Daryn

text:
I really like OG , especially when craving some pasta. Yesterday's experience was just ok. I was disappointed that the service was lackadaisical and I found myself pushing the call server button on the table top pad which I find an extremely rude function. Had to ask for bread 2x because soup/ salad and entree had already arrived and our little server . Had to ask for refills on everything except the entrees. No desert suggestions ;( I may could have been talked into one. ) After dinner special coffee? Hey that may have been great. 
So 2 women eating early dinner at a restaurant ( I am a restaurant manager ) that only had 2 tables occupied in the lounge area. Togo boxes were offered  and were swiftly left on the table along  with the check. Now what really unnerved  me was that the waiter came over to remove the cash tip before I hardly had time to stand up from out of the booth.  
Just thought a bit of attention instead of assembly line service would have made this rare get together a bit more memorable. 
Food was fine, Sangrias were tasty.
name: Shannon

text:
Went here to celebrate my birthday with my close friends. We loved the food. The early dinner menu was so good! Portions were great and each course was even shareable (except dessert haha) so to start off we got the beet salad, caesar salad, flatbread and ricotta, and the avocado and broccoli. They were all delicious! I found my new favorite veggie yellow beets! Who knew?! My best friend and I enjoyed them so much we asked for the antipasta plate after our meal because it included them!  

For entrees we got the pan seared scallops, hamburger with fries, ribs, and the gnocchi.the scallops I got came with some sliced asparagus, some greens and crispy bacon on top. It was seared perfectly and the bacon was crisp but only having 3 scallops was a bummer. My friend's fiance got the ribs and he liked them. My friend got her burger medium well without the bun (she is keto) and she said it was ok. I'm not sure if she didnt like it because of the no bun, but it's just a burger and nothing amazing to note about it. Her fries were crunchy and delicious though.  Seriously, the gnocchi is to die for. Everyone wished they had the gnocchi as their main dish. Perfect gnocchi and chunky tomato sauce. 

For dessert we got the chocolate mousse, tiramisu, affogato, and the butterscotch type dessert, I dont remember the name. They were all definitely good, although the butterscotch one was really too sweet for me. I loved the chocolate mousse with ganache over it. Best desert that even beat the tiramisu. 

Loved the cozy booths we sat in. Loved the black accent decor with wood and twinkly lights on the tree. It reminded me of modern rustic. We loved feeling full after dinner and my friends and husband loved the food. Overall great experience I could not ask for me. 

Cons: drinks were a bit pricey $14 for "the standard" ( cocktail with vermouth, and something else my husband got it) too alcohol tasting for me. Also the food is a bit pricey on the regular menu but the early dinner menu was phenomenal. 3 courses $30.
name: Noelle

text: Love this place. Food taste amazing! They need a bigger place because it does get full.
name: Maria

text:
Wow. Just wow!!! 

Hangry, and unable to check in to our condo until the late afternoon; I found Crabby Bill's on our route from the airport to the beach. I am so glad we did. 

We walked in and were instantly greeted by Lynette, probably the kindest and most hospitable person I have ever met in my entire life. She was grinning from ear to ear and so happy to help our hangry selves pick out our lunches. She also offered us a sample of their chowder (so delish) that they have, just to take the edge off before  the food came. If you get to read this, Lynette, please know you are amazing at your job, and your hospitality and customer service are something I've never experienced from someone at a restaurant before. You truly are an expert at your job. 

Matt and I got the same thing, the fried calamari special. It was too beautiful to pass up! They have a display of what your lunch will look like, all set by the counter, and I knew when I saw it, that special was mine. More calamari than I knew what to do with, giant shrimp that I couldn't stop eating, tater-tots that had what I could only assume was Parmesan cheese and mayo that was so good it should be illegal. Then there was a side to pick. I chose green beans because I can usually them or leave them. But here, I wanted to take them all. They were still crispy, and basted in butter. I wanted to order more, but by the time we had consumed what we could, I couldn't imagine ever eating again. Matt's mom was joining us, and she got the same thing, but her side was coleslaw. I am so picky about coleslaw, (my mom ruined it for me with sad, soggy cabbage with waaaay too much dressing as a kid) I want it crisp, sweet and clean. BOOM Bill's read my mind. It was a great addition to an already awesome lunch. 

Every person we encountered while we were there treated us like we were family in their own home. I really can't wrap my head around how amazing the service was here. They checked on us to make sure we were okay, brought us extra sauces (omg that horsey sauce) and helped us box everything up when we were done and roll us out the door, and on our way. I can't thank them enough for their service. 

Guys, go here. It's bar none. 

Happy Eating!!
name: Eryn

text: Customer service here leaves a great deal to be desired. The woman at the register seems to have had some attentional issue as she had to ask me my order 4 times while she struggled to add it to the PoS touch screen. We ordered two lunch bagels one with roast beef and one with pork loin. They both came with chips, and were a little pricey at $8.75. Unfortunately, they took over 10 minutes to come out. There were a half dozen people waiting behind us also, some of which were waiting for bagels to come out of the oven, leaving me to wonder how a bagel shop runs out of plain bagels on a Sunday morning? Our bagel sandwiches were good, not much protein on either, but very good Asiago cheese bagels, crispy on the outside and not thick or doughy in the inside.
name: Mark

text: I really liked this place!! Really fun environment. They have good bar food to pick on, haven't tried any of their seafood but I'll probably be back to do that. The crab fries are something I've never tried or heard of before so that was cool, i love going places where they have something different than everywhere else.
name: Giana

text: Great food and great service.  They have just about everything for everyone.  Fish, shrimp, lobster tacos, build a sandwich, chili, nachos, salads, soups, some pastas, and a variety of sides.  The rewards card program is excellent and fire/police/military get a generous 40% discount.  Food is fresh and tastes good.
name: Ramon

text: This was a delivery order on a night when I really did not want to cook. Food was fresh and service was quick. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. You can tell they care about customer experience here. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. Overall, a strong experience. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait.
name: User

text: After driving 20 minutes from Brentwood I discovered the food to not be worth it. I ordered  the veggie dog and Mexicano fries and was very disappointed. All the food on the menu is fairly expensive for what you're buying, but dogs n frys does have plenty of options for most everyone. I expected the veggie dog to be an actual faux hot dog but instead it was cubes of fried tofu and veggies. Though the tofu wasn't bad it was not really a veggie dog so I don't understand why it was even included on the menu. The fries were okay but nothing to rave about. I would not recommend this restaurant for anyone looking for a good vegetarian friendly restaurant.
name: Madison

text: Richie's is the best! He works hard for his money! He's an amazing guy, and will hold a conversation with you unlike some businesses. I'm giving Richie's a 5 star because in my opinion he's better than any other wing place I've ever had. LETS GO RICHIEEEEE!!!
name: C

text: I got 3 pounds of crawfish, 3 potatoes, 3 ears of corn, and three sausages.  Only thing out of all of the food I purchased that had any flavor was the potatoes. The crawfish was rubbery, the corn was flavorless, the sausage had grissel all through it. I won't visit this place again!
name: Kysses

text: The workers at the drive thru are very rude. When I had a special request due to an allergy one rolled their eyes at me and seemed very put out. Then got my order wrong!! I wish the service was better but the coffee is always on point
name: Ashley

text: I've gone here for the fried chicken day and brunch a million times. The chicken is on point and the staff always pleasant. Very simple food, but that's what you want out a diner!
name: Lynda

text: I have been here before but have never been disappointed.  Today I had the Maryland crab soup, which was a tad spicy but very flavorful.  I coupled it with a strawberry salad which I loved to spiced pecans as it brought a little body to the salad.  Note that the portions are not large so I had to go with the larger portions for dinner.  The toffee that they give with the check is absolutely amazing.
name: Stephanie

text: Delicious and authentic with very reasonable price point. Definitely family owned with a friendly staff. The menu is diverse with an incredible selection to satisfy any palette. A real jewel in a small neighborhood. Great find for an out of towner looking for a great meal.
name: Paul

text: Portion size looked small at first but it was actually enough. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. Also, food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. Idk, the whole meal felt kind of uneven. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. so yeah kind of mixed on it.
name: User

text: Ordered two medium pizzas for take out.  On-line menu showed $15.95 and $16.95 each.  When I arrived for pickup, I was charged $42.00.  When I mentioned the discrepancy, I was told that I may have been looking at the website and menu of another Capital pizza; they are all independently owned and prices may vary.  When the pizzas were brought out, they were in 9" boxes.  I again mentioned that there was a mistake, I ordered mediums, these were smalls.  (BTW their menus don't have smalls, just medium and large).  Nope, I was told that 9" was indeed a medium size.  I was hungry, so I took them and left.  So......for $42.00 at Capital Steak and Pizza, you get 2 - 9" pizzas.  It was a tasty product, but for that price, I'll have a steak and a glass of wine.  Definitely not worth my repeat business
name: Thomas

text: Awesome place with awesome prices. Happy Hour is the best time to go with nearly half price sushi and appetizers along with some great alcohol specials!
name: Phil

text: This is one of the best pizzas around and they have their recipe down.  Crust is major, sauce is proper, and toppings are not skimpy.  I planned to get bbq food today but saw the truck and made a beeline over.  Try their bbq chicken and buffalo chicken pizzas if you want something huskier.  The Margherita is also on point. Ten bucks.  Worth a shot for sure if you want to switch it up from your regular neopolitan and sweet sauce pies.
name: T

text: Loved this pizza.. delicious crust, perfect amount of sauce and not greasy. Would've given 5 stars but the order wasn't exactly right (I ordered thru BiteSquad).
name: Holley

text:
Can't say I was thrilled with their New York Pastrami sandwich. It was chewy (cut too thick and overcooked with plenty of gristle)
I'll give them a try in a few years to see if things improve.
name: Capt

text:
This was our first night in town to eat seafood. We wanted to go to the boardwalk. Our first choice of restaurants was a 30-45min wait so we chose this place second due to a 4star rating. Yelpers, you 're letting me down here!  This was horrible!  How did it get 4 stars??  We tried the bread crumb oysters. - chewy and bland tasting. We tried fish dip. Blahhhh.....  we got Mac n cheese for the kids. Can you say "Kraft" out of the box for only $8?  The small portions means we reordered 2 more orders. We had linguine and shrimp. The shrimp were shriveled up dry like they had been reheated in a microwave. In fact alot of the food tasted like it was in a microwave. We did the Florida boil for $50. Shrimp was decent, but everything else was gross. One of my children ordered a pb&j for $6 - it was a processed sandwich in a factory bag!  We spent $200 on a meal that none of us were happy about. So disappointed.  
-Hungry in Florida
name: Joe

text: Post grand reopening Success! We were huge fans in the old location and they didn't disappoint at the new location.  Quality is great and the selection beats all the competition in The Fishhawk/Brandon area. Kid friendly and good happy hour spot. They kept their prices consistent, added a full liquor bar and generous kids menu that is priced appropriately. Hanna remembered our roll "the Michele roll" and offered the same impeccable quality and service we had become accustomed to at the old location. Great job and highly recommend !
name: R

text: Happy hour on the waterfront doesn't suck. Wings are good, drinks are reasonable. Local neighborhood feeling with lots of sunshine.
name: Ann

text: Every available dish is excellent. My only complaint about the restaurant is that I wish they had a more extensive menu. The western style braised lamb with cumin and biang biang noodles are amazing.
name: D.

text: I love that their the only Cambodian restaurant in nashville. Service was nice, food was good.
name: Malia

text: I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer..
name: User

text: We've now been there three times. Hope to make it many, many more. Excellent and very friendly service by a lovely family. Absolutely the best meatballs I've experienced at any restaurant. The pasta dishes are consistently strong and my daughter loved their white pizza.
name: William

text: Nothing was terrible, it just never really came together for me. Price felt a touch high for what it was. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent.
name: User

text: Enchiladas were disgusting-filled with low quality non descript cheese. Upon complaining that they were not edible- the waitress said since I had taken a bite they couldn't replace it. I told her that we had been patrons for over 18 years and that this dish had changed. She said that they were under new management and that nothing could be done. I asked to speak to the manager. The manager never came to the table-they all just stood in the back gossiping. The waitress came back and said they wouldn't refund or return it. I insisted that they take the plate and remove it from the bill. Still-the manager never approached the table. The waitress removed it from the tab. Never eat there!! They also have small flies all around the eating area-which they didn't use to have!

text: Great spot a little off to the side. Great decor and a great place to watch a game as a Pittsburgh sports fan. The food was very good and the wings were some of the best I ever had. Also the drink prices were the most fair I've seen by the beach. Matt the bar back was very good.
name: Allen

text: I'm not sure where these great reviews are coming from.  My husband and ordered food last night to eat at home. I ordered chicken tacos which I thought would have pieces of chicken and a crispy shell...couldnt even lift it up - the entire thing fell apart shell was like warm dough and fell. When I got my fork to eat it I saw thee was ground mushy stuff in the taco! Was that supposed to be chicken? Horrible - looked like it came out of a blender! All ground up! My husband had quesadillas and the chicken was ground up but chewy and bad taste- we had to throw everything out.
name: Annonymous

text: Had brunch here over the weekend and it was kinda a mixed bag. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. Food was fresh and service was quick. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Overall, a strong experience. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. It looked better online than it did in person.
name: User

text: Beautiful January night in Santa Barbara slowly moving towards the tourist season. Husband and I go in to have a glass of wine and a cup of beer along with trying some Spanish cold cuts. Greeted by a couple who are both friendly and cheerful. We devoured our anchovy crostini and three nicely portioned tapas and went home refreshed to face the end of work week.
name: Aldoux

text: Love this place! The food is delicious, the atmosphere is fun and the service is prompt and polite. I've become a regular.
name: Chelsea

text: The whole meal felt kind of uneven. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. It just never really recovered once things started off weird. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Maybe other people have better luck here. Nice little spot, decent portions too. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait.
name: User

text: This place was awesome!!  My kids ate off the kids menu and were very happy. My husband and i got the pork belly nachos and they were great. My husband got ribs and i got the tacos. Other than there want a lot of texture  in the tacos, the food was great!!  The waitress was great!! Definitely will go back!!
name: Julie

text: Enjoyed the food here got the cheese enchiladas and bean burritos. Vegetables were good as well as the rice. I think the price for this dish should be under $10. Was also treated with chips and salsa before the dish came out. Salsa was ok I think it could have used a little more kick.
name: Michael

text: My husband and I came here for date night.  We had heard that they have delicious authentic Korean BBQ and had to give it a try.  We didn't know what to get and asked the server for suggestions. She was not super helpful but it isn't her job to make up our minds so it wasn't a problem.  We ordered a hot stone bibimbap bowl and the shortrib BBQ plate. They brought out all the usual korean pickled items like kimche and mashed potatoes.  The food came out so fast!  First we got the bibimbap bowl which was all sizzly and awesome.  The stone made the rice a little crisp which was very nice.  The next item they delivered was beef bulgogi on a hot plate.  Since we had ordered shortribs we looked a bit confused and the chef/owner (I think) saw this and came right over to ask if there was a problem.  We explained the situation and he was apologetic and said he would get us the right item.  Since we weren't really sure what we wanted anyways and didn't want it to be waisted we just kept the bulgogi. I'm sure that the short ribs would have been spectacular but the beef was SOO good! Perfect marinated sweet deliciousness.  The hot stone it was on grilled it a little extra on one side.  If the plate hadn't been hot I would have licked it.  The waitress came over to apologize like 4 times and they more than made up for our little mixup. I honestly think they handled the situation better than I have ever seen before. Will definitely return to try the shortribs.
name: Stephanie

text:
I was so excited to finally try Moo Dang!  A five star experience and can't wait to go back and try something different.  

Of course, I did the Yelp check-in so I could get the free fish balls. My husband does not eat fish or seafood, so these were all mine!  I'm not sure what kind of fish these are made from, but to me they tasted like scallops.  Skewered, battered and deep fried.  And served with spicy tamarind sauce and crushed peanuts.  An order of these is $3.75 without the Yelp check-in.  They were delicious!

We tried the Chang beer, which is a lager.  Crisp and cold.  12 oz is $5, 22 oz is $9.  

My husband enjoys curry dishes, so he tried the Panang Curry with chicken added.  This is a combo of Panang curry paste, coconut milk, and kafir lime leaf, served with cabbage, carrots, and broccoli.  He ordered this on a spicy scale of 0, which is mild, as this was our first time at Moo Dang.  I tried his dish and it was very flavorful.  The coconut flavor was subtle but combined well with everything else.  

I got the Shrimp Pad Thai, it was amazing and probably the best I've had here locally.  It normally comes with chicken and shrimp, but I requested only shrimp.  

They also serve lunch specials Tuesday through Friday, that range from $8.50 to $10.75.   They are closed on Mondays.  

We will be back again to try something new!
name: Kalliope

text:
The hotel recommended we come to the market because of the diversity of food options as we had vegetarians and people who could not eat pork.  I live in an area that is probably in the top 3 of diverse food cultures and I have to say nothing here looked appetizing.

I settled on a cheesesteak since I was in Philly.  All I could taste was salt.  More break than steak and light on the cheese.  I guess if you get "extras" your food fills the bun.  If you just want meat and cheese, you basically get an empty bun.

Not a fan.
name: Virginia

text: This little shop is super! It serves home style snacks & eats under $10.
name: Jennifer

text: The soup was better than the sandwich, which I wasn't expecting. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. It looked better online than it did in person.
name: User

text: THIS IS A FAST FOOD RESTAURANT! Do not expect to bring your family of 8 and get your food in under an hour. Now, it's Sunday, very busy, and people are waiting everywhere. But an hour for a burger and fries? When we got our food, it was warmish, not hot which is pretty disappointing. Definitely will not be coming back to location. Just a note to the owner and management. Put an "express" sign up. It is not the same SNS sit down diner. You've got a lot of work to do. Hopefully this turns around.
name: Michael

text: Excellent fresh and delicious food!  Clean and great service.  We will return every time we are back in town!  We can't wait to try everything on the menu!
name: Daphne

text: I love this taco stand. The menu it's small but everything taste good. The meat and chicken taste fresh, does not taste like it's been sitting in the freezer for long. Also, she offers hot sauces, get the avocado sauce it's best.
name: Sachy

text: Oh my goodness IM STUFFED! I chose the brunch with a side of hash brown casserole and now I have a new favorite side dish. I also had Mammas French toast, boy is that hearty. The syrup is served in a little sample size bottle, how cute. My friend had a burger for lunch. The portion sizes are very good. We had a 20 minute wait on this Sunday afternoon, but that's ok because it's always fun to brows the gift shop.
name: Tammi

text:
I made a quick visit with my sister before a concert at the Raymond James stadium and was very pleased with the food. My sister got there before me and said after she was seated, no one came to her table for 5 minutes to offer any water and that she had to hail one of the waitresses, who wasn't even working that side of the restaurant. One point is dinged there.

We ordered the cobb salad with grilled chicken, traditional wings 3 ways, and parmesan truffle fries. The salad was massive! Could easily feed 4 not-so-hungry people. My sister and I barely made a dent in it. It was delicious. We got the avocado ranch dressing on the side. We got the wings in mango habanero, buffalo, and Korean bbq. The mango was not spicy so that was disappointing. Buffalo was okay. It was sour like most buffalo sauces are so I was happy about that and Korean bbq was pretty good. It had a little kick to it. I really liked the fries because I like soggy fries haha. My sister on the other hand does not so she wasn't a big fan. I was completely floored by the food and service at the beginning was sub-par so I'll stick with my 3-star rating. I would definitely be back if I'm in the area before a game or concert again.
name: Tahirih

text:
YIKES!  We've been to D&B many times, but today was a total disappointment.  Let's start with the bartender.  The bar was empty when we arrived a little before 1:00 before an Eagles home game.  It took several minutes for the bartender to wait on us, and she seemed disinterested.  In addition to a beer each, my husband asked for a Chivas on the rocks.  She thought she had it, but then she said she didn't.  We asked if it might be at another bar, and she said she'd check. 2 minutes later she said she didn't have it; she didn't check.

Now let's talk about the food.  For the 3 of us we ordered the 5 for 5 (or something like that).  We agreed the tater tots and the wings were good, but we didn't like the quesadilla or the pizza pull; the pigs in a blanket were ok.  We would not order this again.

The place itself was not well maintained.  The bar seats were stained, torn, and taped, and there were water stains on the ceiling in the men's room.

The final blow was the lack of games we used to play.  We loved the multi-player trivia game, but it was gone.  Other games we used to enjoy  but are no longer available include golf, the claw arcade game, flight simulator, the drunken man game, and others.  When we glanced at the shop where you exchange your tickets for goods we were again disappointed; they don't carry nearly the variety that they used to carry.  

One final point.   You no longer get tickets for winning a game.  That was half of the fun: filling the cups, getting them weighed, and turning them into points.  Now the points get placed directly on your D&B card.  I understand the rationale for doing this (being environmentally correct), but the fun of collecting tickets from the machines and walking around with a cup full of tickets was one of the reasons we used to go to D&B.
name: Peg

text: 2 stars because the food was good but the service was not. We ordered take out. It was hard to call the restaurant to order. Then once we picked up the food and brought it home the order was wrong. We tried calling the restaurant to resolve the issue, sense they charged us for the full order and we only got half of it. But when they did answer they hung up, twice. I do not think we will be going back ever again.
name: Jasmine

text: This spot is amazing! The staff always greets you when you walk in the door. They do this in a very friendly manner, not because they have to. Everything on the menu tastes incredible and they give you good sized portions as well. Honestly, I don't even bother with other diners in the area because they don't compare to Kitchen87's food, atmosphere, and energy. I generally don't take the time to write reviews but after going to this place consistently for the last several months, I just had to. I would recommend Kitchen87 to anyone who likes a "home town" feel and wants some great food.
name: Shane

text:
We stopped in on a whim. I have to say this is the best suchi we've had in a very long time. We will be back for sure. We tried a variety of dishes: nigiri, hand rolls, long rolls, a deep fried fish thing. Everything was fantastic.
The bar got a little crowded but it was well worth it! Did the all you can eat. We had plenty of food served quickly. 5 stars for sure!
name: Brandy

text: Another lovely evening at the awesome Friday Saturday Sunday! Went tonight with some friends and enjoyed my favorite cocktail Control State! Had the pleasure of meeting the owner Hannah tonight too, charming lady! Will be back soon!
name: Patricia

text: I was in town for work and staying near the airport, so thanks to the help of yelpers, I arrived at this location. Since I was by myself, I chose to sit at the bar. On a midweek, cloudy afternoon, the restaurant was not very busy.  I was quickly greeted and served my drink. The bartender was friendly and chatted for a minute. He recommended their duo combo platter which consist of two meats and sides. I got baby back ribs and chicken, with a side of baked beans and slaw. The food came out quick and I was not disappointed. The ribs were well seasoned and tender. The rotisserie chicken was flavorful and moist. The meats are perfectly fine on their own but if you want more sauce, they have several bbq sauces for you. The spicy sauce was my fave.  The sides were delicious and the portions, generous. The garlic bread was very buttery and crispy. This is not the place you come with counting calories in mind. I am in no way a barbecue expert, but I left full, happy, and satisfied, which is a win in my book.
name: Mary

text: I would try a cheese steak from anywhere. I thought I found a new spot but my step dad already beat me too it. Overall it's a good sandwich. If I had to complain I would say the role was a lil big for the amount of steak.
name: Chris

text: It looked better online than it did in person. For a busy night they handled it okay. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Wouldn't really choose this place again. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. It looked better online than it did in person. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Not bad for a quick meal.
name: User

text: The pancakes and potatoes are really really good!  Great vibe and surroundings! The teas are very good as well as the coffee.  Get there early because it's very popular!!

text: First time ordering from here and I honestly wasn't sure what to expect. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. This feels like a place where your order choice matters a lot.

text: Where to start, We have been coming here ever since we moved here 3 years ago and we won't go anywhere else. Food is amazing! Especially the caramel churros! Staff is always so nice and the food is always fresh. Best Mexican restaurant in town.

text: Surprised at the 4.5 star rating. We ordered Kobe beef, pulled pork and sausage. The sausage was the only decent item. The other meat was pretty flavorless and the beef was super fatty (@ $30/lb!!). Service was slow but friendly. Really disappointing overall.

text: One of the best things about Tucson food culture is the many different origins of food here. Luke's is just one of the examples serving Chicago style sandwiches. The Italian beef with hot peppers and cheese is so good you'd want to order another one even though the portions are really big. I prefer the giardiniera peppers cut/sliced much finer but theirs still tastes good and they sell it too! The pastrami is also delish. This place is also one of the few places that serve diet RC. There's a lot of room for parking, outdoor seating, and inside is also nice and cozy. They also have a drive-thru window. Although people may complain about the inconsistencies with their hours, I think it's understandable since they're family-owned. Luke's is easily one of the best sandwich spots in Tucson.

text: Pleasantly surprised at this rooftop bar! It's on the 17th floor of the Troubadour. Went on a summer Saturday afternoon and it was perfect. Seating available in the shade and nice city views with a breeze. Nice friendly diverse crowd and atmosphere, good drinks
name: Heaven

text: Service was slow and expensive.  Greasy fried food is the word.  Expensive shakes that where no better the McDonald's    The vegetarian option is a fried mushroom with cheese inside.  It's fried and taste really unhealthy.  Fries tasted ok, but threw it all out.  Not worth the price or wait.

text: This is my favorite Thai place in the Indy area!! I've never had a dish I didn't like from them and I order from them at least once a week so that's saying a lot! Their duck curry is phenomenal and so is their basil fried rice and their pad egg noodles! I feel like they're fairly priced dishes for how much food you get too, which is always a plus!

text: The wait was longer than it should've been for a pretty normal dinner service. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. So yeah, the experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. idk I'd try something else next time. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced.

text: I come here for a quick grab n go lunch when I work on campus. The location is great because it's a little off the main road so traffic isn't horrible. There is a free parking-lot and although it's not large, I've always been able to get a spot. They do a great job of making sure my gluten free meal stays contact free. The size of the GF bread is one size, but it works out great because it's dinner for later. They are quick to serve and are nice.

text: OK, so it goes without saying that Chick-fil-A has the best chicken sandwich ever. But I never realize how good the drive-through service was and the curbside assistance is fantastic this makes getting the sandwich and fighting the crowds so convenient that I will have to return over and over again. By the time you get to the drive up window they're calling you by your first name in handy order there's almost no stopping at all once you place your order it's fantastic and fast

text: This was the worst experience I've ever had!! We were waiting at the front door for at least 10-15 minutes. After we were seated we had to have waited at least 30 minutes before the waiter came over. After placing our order we waited another 45 minutes to an hour. I inquired about our food and noticed that people were receiving their food that came in after us. I tried to have patience but when other customers were receiving food way after we came in, then there's a real problem. Needless to say that Zac's won't ever receive a penny of my money.

text: This place has been on my list to try out for some time. We went this evening. The location seems a little sketchy but don't let that fool you. There is parking around the back. As soon as you walk in, the restaurant is bright and open. They have a full bar and all day every day happy hour with $3.50 drinks. The menu has a ton of options and the seafood is excellent!! This is a hidden gem. I will be back!

text: Mothers day brunch. Group of 4. Started with the grit tots...we all loved these. Little nuggets of  goodness, crunchy on the outside while warm and creamy on.the inside.  We also had some of the best french toast we have experienced. Made with french bread,  fried crunchy topped with cane syrup... crispy..sricky and fantastic . Eggs cooked correctly and bacon crispy and Smokey.  This brunch did not disappoint

text:
Walking into the market i was extremely overwhelmed with many great options to choose from. I tossed back and forth and ended up choosing to eat from Meribo's Pizza! It was a great choice. text:
