text: This is a must try Syrian spot in KOP. Matter of fact, you must try it once, twice, and more times whenever you're in the area. My gf's rehearsal dinner was at this venue. It has AMAZING, aromatic, tasty, melt in your mouth foods, BYOB and did not charge her for a venue for her event. Im not normally a fan of buffet foods nor Mediterranean (I know right!) and were blown away with the quality of the foods at Aroma. So much so, I wanted to come back for lunch another day when we're in the area again. Boy.. the lunch did not disappoint. The portion is on the large size even on lunch menu, so we did have some leftover for next day. Service was great. The waitress kept checking on us whether we need more pita and the main waiter walked around making sure we had everything we needed. We ordered a sampler platter for appetizer, and each ordered a lunch platter for ourselves. Needless to say, we all walked out with a full belly, a full pocket (they priced their foods really reasonably), and great company. My favorite things were the tomato spread and falafel from the appetizer platter; and beet spread and Kebbeh Kebab from my lunch. Def will come back again to try other items on the menu and try more things that I have not eaten before.

text:

I have no idea what they brought me.
We ordered an appetizer of calamari and listened to the table in front of us complain about their food and the table behind us complain about the service. I stopped ordering at the calamari!
The waitress brought us the calamari some 20 minutes later and was trying to brag that she cooked it herself. Why is my waitress cooking? She said the kitchen was short a man tonight. I heard another waitress use that excuse on another table.  I would not order any dinner after that. I waited another 10 minutes for the bill then paid cash so I could get the heck out of there. I spent 1 hour in there and it took 50 minutes to get drinks and an app.
The owners should shut this business down! How dare they even open the doors if they don't have the staff to run an eatery. The owners did a disservice to me and the employees by making me wait while my waitress cooked. Waitresses aren't supposed to be cooking. I would have quit if I was an employee there. What a disgrace. The owners must have no shame to open their doors knowing this is the dining experience they plan to offer to their clientele,
Don't even consider eating at this place because your food will never come. If it does, the waitress probably cooked it and it will be wrong.

This location is in the St. Louis Lambert International Airport.  It is conveniently located in the E Terminal, and does offer seating.   I was traveling with a coworker, and we decided to grab a bite since our flight wasn't for a couple of hours.  The hostess seated us right away with a view of the runways/gates.   

Our server came to our table pretty quickly and took our drink orders.  When she brought them back, she took our food orders.   I had the bacon cheeseburger with no bun, and chose broccoli as my side.   The food came out in no time, but still tasted fresh.  The presentation wasn't the greatest, but it wasn't horrible, either (see pic).  The broccoli wasn't as steamed as I'd liked it to be, but it was still good.  The burger was very tasty.   

Overall, this is a good location.  You don't have much choice when in an airport, but this Chili's is pretty decent.   The staff are friendly, it's centrally located in the E terminal, and the food is pretty good.   I'll be back if I find myself hungry and with some time before my flight out!

text:
Properly described as an island of chill in a sea of crazy. Its amazing how things changed once we stepped in here. This was one of my bucket list places in NOLA so I had high expectations and it did not disappoint in the least!

text:
This place was okay. Definitely not worth the $50 price tag for Sunday Brunch. The buffet is pretty small for $50. Felt like there wasn't many options. The to order plates were good but the mimosas were watered down and didn't look good based on my partner's review. If you don't gorge yourself on seafood then price wise it's not really worth it.

Service was eh. A lot of miscommunication with what people were ordering from the Brunch menu. Wrong plates were coming out constantly, people were waiting forever for orders cause the waiter was forgetting to put them in. Carry a pad to write orders instead of trying to memorize cause obviously it wasn't working.

Only mimosas were getting refilled but not the water, so since I was refraining from drinking alcohol, I was forgotten and got my water refilled once while everyone else who was drinking were refilled multiple times.

Deserts were dry and just okay. The only thing that was good was the tiramisu. The bananas foster was not actually a bananas foster but cold bananas drowned in caramel sauce.

The worse part was when the waiter confronted my partner outside of coming out of the bathroom and harassed him about the tip. If you give bad service you get a bad tip. Plus my partner has spent years in Europe where tipping is nonexistent and it's hard for him to tip for a bad experience.

The waiter ruined the entire experience. If it wasn't for that rude display I would have considered coming back for a regular dinner. 

There are better places that offer better service and more quality food for much less in the Ybor area.
name: Tiffany

text: I almost skipped this place because of the ratings and that would've been unfair. Food was fresh and service was quick. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. Food was good and came out fast. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. From the moment you walk into the restaurant the staff kindly greets you and makes you feel comfortable. The staff is very attentive. The food always comes out fresh. We always have to give it a few minutes to cool off. While waiting for your entrees to cool I suggest a dinner salad. They taste so fresh. It's almost as if they have a garden in the kitchen. Everything I have gotten from Tony and Nello's keeps me coming back for more!  If you're looking for authentic Italian this is a go to stop!

text: I wish I would have caught the names of the crew that was there tonight, they were all very nice and one of the girls in particular was super kind and patient.  My son has a severe dairy allergy and because of past mistakes with food he is very suspicious and almost never tries new things (we've had to have him in feeding therapy to help).   He has never had ice cream, and we've tried to get him to do sorbets at the yogurt shops in town but he won't trust them.  He was super excited about the science of freezing the ice cream, and when he could see the same brand of almond milk being used for his ice cream that he gets at home, he knew it was safe.   Once he got it, he was doing little happy food dances and talked about how great it felt to have the "coldness of the ice cream" going down his throat.    Thanks for the experience and for talking with him!  They were very careful not to cross contaminate and we really appreciate that!   Mine tasted great too (premium vanilla with Kit Kat mix in)

text: I am a local and have started to frequent this place a bit more with the warmer weather coming our way. They are constantly cycling through these incredibly well concocted different beers. Have yet to come here for brunch since I'm a musician and have essentially an opposite sleep cycle so I tend to miss it, but one of these days... everyone who works here has a unique personality and sometimes I feel like I'm part of the crew because of how easily we banter back and forth.

text: In the heart of South Tucson lies an urban international food court, a true a diamond in the desert. I used to live in this neighborhood but never had a reason to come back until now. I have visited American Eat Co. twice. The space was packed on both occasions, but the dining area can hold a great deal of people. I was able to find seating without much hassle and even received my food in approximately ten minutes. The best advantage here are the options. The selection includes BBQ ribs, sliders, gyros, tacos, poke, pizza, ice cream, and pastries. I tried Dumb Fish, Opa! Time and AZ Rib House, and Café con Leche. My favorite by far are the gyros at Opa! Time. The tender meat has a wonderful seasoning on it, and the portions are hearty enough to share. However, the ribs at AZ Rib House are also delectable. They are prepared inside the restaurant yet possess a delicious outdoor smokiness. The ribs came with elote which I found too citrusy. I was drinking a Mexican Mocha while eating the corn, however, so the collective tanginess from both could have contributed. The only reason why I had to drop one star from my review was due to Dumb Fish. I wish I could rate the restaurants individually since Dumb Fish was the outlier! On my first visit, they were closed because they ran out of ingredients. I overlooked it due to the new opening hype. During my second visit, I tried their Tuna Tataki Poke bowl and their Korean fried rice. The tuna very dry, and over-coated with coarse black pepper. The portion of tuna was too modest, and the rest of the bowl was packed with excess rice and vegetables. The Korean fried rice had an egg on top with sliced pieces of kimchi mixed inside the rice. The entire dish was extremely bitter and direly needed some form of sweetness. Other members of my dinner party had the salmon poke bowl. Again, it looked like a big mound of rice with a small side of fish to accompany it. The photos look deceiving because they stack the fish on the very top. Be warned, they use a lot of strong spices on the salmon poke bowl, some are very spicy. But do not let Dumb Fish prevent you from visiting! I will definitely return with a large group of friends who want a wide variety of food options.
name: Roland

text: Not bad for a quick meal. Food was good and came out fast. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. text: Never search for a restaurant when you're too hungry, you'll make the mistake of going corporate and immediately regret it. It'd been years since we'd been to a Carrabba's, so we decided to give it a go.  Think over chilled, over priced, no creativity on the menu, and you'll pick up what I'm putting down. It was so cold in the dining room, even after asking them to turn down the air conditioning it remained super chill, and I don't mean in a good way. The menu was not creative, especially for us vegetarians.  And overpriced, over fried, yada yada yada. The best part of the meal was the warm bread with oil drizzle for dipping, and the minestrone soup.  If we had stopped there we would have been so much happier than trying to indulge in entrees. My husband had the shrimp Parmesan, he couldn't finish his meal because of the cloyingly heavy batter. I had the eggplant Parmesan which was so heavily fried the pieces of eggplant had black edges and the grease pooled under the slices. The side of pasta with pomodoro sauce was fine, thankfully it was served separate so escaped the grease pool on the main plate. We both left angry at such a wasted meal and have learned our lesson.

text:
I'm not vegan, but I love to try new places. I got the Buffalo burger, the buffalo sauce was too spicy in a bad way (and I love spicy food) I could not taste the bean patty at all. The buffalo cauliflower was ok, not the best I tried. For some reason the sauce was less overpowering than the burger one, so that's good. Maybe are different sauces? Tater tots are really good and the dipping sauce is very unique. The Buddha bowl that my husband got was delicious.

text:
What stood out here from the moment we came in was the friendliness of the staff. You can tell they enjoy working here and that makes customers have a much better experience. If they see you looking confused at the menu when you arrive they're happy to come over and tell you what's what. The food was also great quality and deliciously prepared. We went with the veggie burger which had a falafel texture and was made in house. It was really good, but I wouldn't order it every visit like I would some veggie burgers. They also have the Impossible burger, which we love, but restaurants usually taste the same as making it at home so we went with their more creative original and were glad we did. The fries were way too good and the hush puppies are a must try. They've got a great selection of beers and cider and they fill them to the tippy top with no head, which appears to be the signifier of worthwhile establishments around here. 

You can tell they truly care about the quality of the food they offer. One guy at the bar told us about their local suppliers and that they have a "chicken whisperer" who makes sure the chickens are as happy as can be throughout their life (this was before we ordered so he wasn't just pandering to the folks ordering vegetarian). The entire staff was incredibly friendly and our server was very attentive. We realized they had fill your own water stations after we asked him to refill our waters and the guy just refilled them without even hinting that we should do it ourselves. Coming from San Diego where such a faux pas earns you a serving of sarcasm with a side of passive aggression we couldn't believe it. They were busy on a Friday night, but there were enough seats that you didn't have to wait. We shall return and perhaps I'll update in a year when I have a list of favorite menu items.
name: Richard

text: I love their fresh take on donuts! And none are overly sweet and greasy like traditional donuts. May favorite is the hipsterberry! It's the perfect balance of a sweet, fluffy donut with a slightly tangy and tart icing.
name: Andrea

text:
My husband and I were there w a group of friends Friday 4/13/18.... which was the first 80 degree day of the year!  The place was packed!  We loved the atmosphere... on the water!  Even tho every bar seat was full, and there was another layer of people hoping to gain bar space, the bar staff were very prompt and attentive! We did have to wait almost 2 hours for our table, but it was expected because of how crowded it was and we had 6 people in our party.  The food was great!  I especially loved the Smoked Brisket Nachos !!  Delish!!  Yes, they could offer sour cream and guac, but the taste of the Smoked Brisket on the Nachos was amazing!  Liked it so much that we took our daughter back on Sunday because we were in the area for an event at Widener!!

The wait staff was FANTASTIC!!  Both Friday night and Sunday afternoon the waitresses were very friendly and knowledgeable of the menu!  We will definitely be back to visit! And hope to sit at a table on the dock!!

text:
There's a lot of good things going on at the Capital One Cafe. My favorite parts being drinks are half-off for Capital One debit card holders, there's frequent happy hours which means free drinks, free grilled cheese and tomato soup days provided by Milkhouse, there's an ample amount of space for quiet reading and studying, and there's very strong Wi-Fi. This is perhaps my most frequently visited Cafe in Center City and I often recommended it to people who don't want to pay for shared workspaces like wework.

A pro tip I'll offer is to not bother buying drinks here if you don't have a Capital One card. At that point it's overpriced. Also, they serve Peet's Coffee which is the worst coffee I've ever tasted. Consistently I cannot drink any of their coffee drinks without a good amount of sugar and milk in it. The food is overpriced so I would shy away from that. If you want good tasting black coffee head directly across the street to the new Shakespeare & Company.
name: John

text:
I used to come here religiously for their liver destroying $2 margaritas and blood pressure raising $1 tacos every Tuesday. They don't bring us water unless we ask because we're regulars and apparently that means we don't drink water. But that's besides the point. Occasionally I like to drift astray from the $1 tacos and order from the real menu. One Tuesday I ordered the "Burrito Loco". I was expecting a real loco quality burrito to show up and satisfy my drunken taste buds. Instead I was insulted with that pip squeak of a burrito shown in the photo. There's literally just dry chicken on the inside and a dab of cheese sauce spread on the tortilla. If it at least came with that cheap azz rice on the side I would've been OK. But $8.... for that??? Oh nah. So I asked the waitress "is this the burrito loco?" And she says "yEs ThAt wHat yOu oRdEr" and walks away. At this point I'm shocked and appalled. Like, she had an attitude about me asking about this rip off of a burrito she just brought me. Long story short I ate it, but I didn't like it and I will not be returning. Taco Bell has more "loco" burritos than that for half the price and QT has those packaged Chimichangas that are more filling. I should've just went to the gas station for dinner apparently. Moral of the story, don't stray from the Taco Tuesday specials unless you're prepared to be disappointed or you're okay with really small low quality portions that you would probably be served in prison. 

In fact, they should rename it "Prison Burrito" instead of Burrito Loco so everyone can lower their expectations ahead of time.
name: Aiko

text:
Friendly fast and tasty
Fried rice with duck!
Lamb gyoza (Japanese friends got cuisine shock with this one but I love love loved it!)
name: Chou

text:
Group of 13 on a Wednesday night. Y'all. This is NOT the place for groups. Or if you want even remotely quick service. They would only split our bill 3 ways AND would only take a maximum of 3 credit cards for the order. What kind of BS is that?!! 

The server brought out our bill and had us write beside what we ordered which check it should be put on. So imagine 13 people taking their turn marking down what they ate on the bill. THEN brought back the 3 bills and we had to figure out who owed what on THAT bill. Thankfully we had cash!! 

I ordered the shrimp platter. Asked the server if I could get onion rings. Would've gladly paid an up-charge. He said no. I thought he was being sarcastic, but he wasn't. He literally said he's not allowed to make that substitution. WTH seriously?? What kind of restaurant doesn't allow substitutions?? 

My shrimp platter was average. Reminded me of Popeyes fast food shrimp. The Boo fries were surprisingly good. I was drinking Hurricanes. They were $9 each. Not worth it. I'm not a heavy drinker. I had three hurricanes and barely had a buzz. 

The server was very slow and didn't seem to care if we were happy with anything. 

Best part?? An 18% tip was automatically added to the bill. Ordinarily I would have no problem with the tip being included, but our server was more along the lines of 10% gratuity. 

If I'm ever back in nola, I won't be visiting Acme again. Nothing about this dining experience is worth repeating.
name: Amanda

text: Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. text:

I would come here for a casual dinner as it's clean and a good eating experience. However, if you are on a budget or really hungry, maybe try somewhere else.

text:
REPOST CAUSE THEY HAD THE AUDACITY TO GET MY ORIGINAL REVIEW REMOVED BY YELP WOW HAHAHA don't try me. 


DON was our server and he was rude and non-attentive. Our group of 16 came and they originally split us in two tables. We asked specifically for split check and he said yes but then gave us all one check at the end and acted like he forgot. I said it twice to split check and watched him write our order on a different page. Why combine it after??? But that's not why the review is one star. 
My steak was ordered Medium rare but arrived completely well done. There was no pink in it AT ALL. When I told him it was too well done he made me cut into the middle again cause he didn't believe me. Then I had to use my phone light to shine it onto the steak because it was so dim for his eyes to see. How embarrassing and degrading that I had to draw attention to myself for their kitchen's mistake. After he took it back he came back within like 5 minutes and the steak was still moo-ing. It  was blue/rare... seemed to be only seared. Another server noticed I wasn't eating and asked if I wanted it sent back. I said I was letting it rest and showed him how rare it was (without the light this time because he had some human decency). He took it back and promised he won't forget it because I was hungry and I didn't want it done wrong a third time. After all this we didn't receive any apologies or offered any kind of compensation. Never even saw a manager table touch. Was there one there that night? 
While passing to help his other tables he hit two of our friends in the back of their heads with plates. And he even SPILLED A GLASS OF WINE while clearing the table. His response? "At least it wasn't you, birthday girl". Ok so he managed to treat the birthday girl well but no one else. He never table checked after food arrived so everyone sat with empty water glasses for the entirety of the meal. Not sure how he's still a server here. 
Pretty sure he didn't care about us since we were a large party and he was getting an automatic twenty percent gratuity. That doesn't mean you can just punch in our orders and forget about customer service.
P.S. all the food is pretty salty. Why are their water glasses so tiny?
name: Andora

text:
Wow, this place has changed a lot in the past 5 years! It has gone from a divey diner that was on the brink of closure to classy, modern and a very happening spot. I will mourn the loss of some of my late night favorites on the menu like the 2000 calorie spud mountain, but also embrace their new healthier options too. You would have never seen a vegan option before and now there are so many! For this occasion, I was getting together with family and close friends for breakfast. Upon arrival, I was delighted by the delicious assortment of pastries. They looked so beautifully decorated and too good to eat! They also have a full bar, which was not there before. It was actually very crowded, but our large group was able to be seated pretty quickly. 

I was curious to try the red velvet pancakes so I ordered them. They were just ok, not much different tasting than a regular pancake. The bacon was a tad too crispy, bordering on overdone. Everyone was satisfied with what they ordered though and our waitress was so awesome! She kept checking on us and refilling our coffee mugs. That is the nice thing about diners, everyone can order something that appeals to them. The prices are very reasonable too. I am happy that the Colonial diner has made so many changes, but still kept it's roots there with lots of old pictures of the town on the walls. It may be different looking but still feels the same to me.
name: Angela

text: One of my favorite craft cocktail stops in New Orleans. Bartenders are super fun and really know their cocktails! Literally carved ice off a block for our drink! Do yourself a favor and stop here for a couple of drinks before wandering around the french quarter!

text: Anyone who says El Guerrero Canelo doesn't make the best Sonoran Hotdogs should not be trusted. text:
I had two seperate experiences:
1. I came with some friends and the plan was just to get drinks, I did not know they didn't serve anything except a margarita that is offered with entree's. I was feeling sick that night, so I planned to get food to go at the end of the night and the waitress brought me a margarita anyway. By the end of the night, I didn't touch my margarita, and canceled the to go meal (before i ordered it) but I still had to pay $18 the margarita.
Mostly everyone else enjoyed the food, so i came back a few months later for the food and drink with my girlfriend. The giant menu was unwieldy and the dim lighting made reading it obnoxious. The food is not the mexican you are expecting, but a contemporary alteration of it. I came in wanting a nice traditional meal and a margarita, and ended up with a piece of seasoned chicken and guacamole that did not resemble anything of a latin spice pallet. Admittedly it was a good dish, but not what you would expect at a mexican restaurant. The chicken came with veggies and rice and was topped with a Poblano sauce that the waitress could not describe in any way, shape, nor form aside from "Pepper sauce".  The portion was also small for the sheer price that is demanded. Honestly I would give them another shot but try to find a more traditional latin dish. Margaritas are little bit on the weak side and very sugary.
name: Tim

text: My first stop on my first trip to NOLA, and it did not disappoint! I like the different take on their Asian dishes! I'm Asian (Viet), so I can be very picky with Asian food, especially Viet food. Their wings were to DIE FOR. Please don't hesitate to get them. My boyfriend got their bone broth pho, which was delicious even before hoisin and sriracha was added. I got the curry clam dish, which was different, but I still enjoyed it! A little heavy for me, but to be expected. The service was amazing too--great server. I definitely recommend.

text:
I didn't get to make it to Willie Mae's the first time I visited NOLA, so for the second time around, I made sure it was one of my stops. Our party of 6 arrived on a Monday at around 1:30. We signed up for the text alert, which told us it would be a 40-minute wait and it was accurate. The trick to not having to wait 40 minutes is to come with a party of two. A few couples were seated before us because I guess there are more tables for two inside, than for larger groups.

I ordered the fried chicken plate, which comes with three pieces of chicken and a side. You can choose either white meat or dark, but you can't mix it. I prefer dark anyway so that's what I went with. The meat itself was good - very juicy. However, the outside was extremely greasy. And I know, it's fried chicken - what do I expect? But I've had fried chicken at other spots before that weren't dripping in grease. My friend even said that she thought Popeye's was better. For the side, I had mac and cheese, which was a little mushy. Reminded me a little bit of school lunch mac and cheese.

I think people come to Willie Mae's because it's well known, but I'm sure there are better fried chicken spots in NOLA.
name: Mel

text:

text:
Okay. Do not come here during snow. At all. It really messes with their scoring system. 

That being said, we didn't realize how badly it messed with the scoring system and how frustrating it would be to deal with so we initially bought 2 hours of game play. About 30 minutes in, we couldn't deal with it anymore and asked if we could stop at 1 hour. They said sure no problem, well just stop you with an hour to go so you don't pay for that second hour. Which, great. 

They came over and told us with 20 minutes remaining that we only had 20 minutes remaining. Cool. Then at 5 minutes remaining they did the same. Then they completely disappeared?? And we had to actually ask for our checks and everything. 

Then our checks were a mess and our poor server had to go back and forth before a manager just talked to us and cut out the confusion. 

I don't really think any of this would have been a problem had the snow not messed with their systems. So I'll give it a try in the spring and update then. But for now, I'm not impressed.
