text:
Oh.My.Goodness.

We found this little gem of a pizza shop by word of month and decided to give it a try. It's convenient to the blvd and plenty of street parking.

The pickle white pizza was absolutely phenomenal. My family had some hesitation when I said I wanted to try it. But, they were pleasantly surprised! 

The hot wings (we asked for well done and they were!) and chicken ceased salad were equally as good! We will definitely be back!
name: Lisa

text:
tl;dr- chicken was salty, line was long, but overall great meal

Went to New Orleans to visit and try all the foods, we HAD so stop by Willie Mae's for their famous friend chicken. We waited for about 45 minutes for a table and, another 30 after ordering for our food to arrive, so if you plan to go, leave plenty of time to enjoy your food. I tried the fried chicken entree with a side of butter/Lima beans, and shared cornbread, fried Okra, and Brussels sprouts to. Chicken was a bit too salty for my tastes, but the batter used made for a great crunch, very crumbly but packed with flavor. The cornbread was amazing- a must try! Fried okra, Lima beans and Brussels sprouts were also pretty good; not too overpowering but complimented the main dish well. Great service, everyone was friendly.
name: Zoe

text: I went to the new tin roof tacos in meridian today. NEVER AGAIN. Cold food and when I returned it the owner was a real b word. No tact no apologies and how can you be in your second day and not be on the line. Get a new career. You are not equipped for the restaurant business. Also a word of advise. EVERY real restaurant owner checks for flavor and temperature BEFORE the doors EVER OPEN. I will tell everyone I know to steer clear of this joint.
name: Rick

text: Super neat place.  So cute and very chic.  The wine list is extensive.  The food is really good.  We had the smoke trout for a starter and loved it.  Then i had the salami sandwich which was really good.  The bananas foster bread pudding was amazing!!!!  Can't wait to come back when it's warm.
name: Scarlett

text: My in-laws (they're Chinese-Indonesian from Indonesia) make it a point to stop here for legit Indonesian food when they're in Philly or just passing through Philly. It's delicious, affordable, and no frills. Highly recommend if you're in town and want authentic Indonesian food!!
name: Joanna

text:
Shapiro's is an annual tradition for many of the BOA families and chaperones but this was my first visit. Upon arriving, I noticed this place was big and reminded me a bit like a school cafeteria, especially with the winding line around the dining room. I'm told the line when we arrived was "short" because it usually is outside and winding around the building. Now I'm intrigued to see if this place is worth all the hype!

The menu is nearly as big as the dining area so even though I glanced at the menu beforehand, I began to panic halfway through the line because I wanted nearly everything on the menu! I also heard quite a bit about the portion sizes so I knew my options would be limited by quantity alone. After seeing the portion size of the desserts, I quickly realized these were not (or maybe shouldn't be?) one person portions. The sandwiches were about three inches thick with meat and the kid meals weren't allowed for adults (minus the star since that's my go-to with my teeny tummy, especially when I can't take leftovers). I opted for the german potato salad (basically to compare with the ol' family recipe) and potato pancakes. Both were different than what we find in Wisconsin but still good. If I return here, sharing a sandwich, side and dessert with my daughter will more than suffice for the two of us!

This is a no-frills kind of place. Good food, fast service (ya better know what you want cuz the line and employees move fast!) but there could be some investment into the seating area and bathrooms especially (which were pretty awful). The prices were reasonable but even better if you're sharing the enormous portions!
name: Natalie

text: Blondie's. Coffee, Wine and Desert Bar. Not so much. More like a really nice cafe that serves cocktails. (Image included.) The family and I were supposed to go to another place in the local library that has been closed because they are short staffed. I'm happy they were because if not we may have never found this gem of a place. The atmosphere is great and the coffee is hot. Great for a cold day in January. However they do have outside seating for those nice warm days as well. Down to the nitty gritty... we ordered Popovers as an appetizer for brunch and they are great! Light, fluffy and served with your choice of flavored butter. We chose two, strawberry and apple butter. My doctors ears are ringing... but well worth it.. main course is here... be back soon! So I ordered the Breakfast Burrito, my wife ordered the Blonde Benedict and the kid ordered the Blondie's Slinger. I tried them all. The burrito was great! It had a very nice flavor and presented very well. Of course my wife and I split our meals so I also had the Benedict as well. It had hollandaise sauce. I've never had a good hollandaise sauce. Before I get into that a little back story. While waiting for our seat I spoke to a very nice person, Andrew. The Blonde Benedict was Andrews choice, with an added side of salmon and scrambled eggs instead of poached. We ordered exactly the way Andrew suggested. Back to the hollandaise. Excellent! Not bitter, slight hint of rosemary and great with the eggs! If this is how hollandaise sauce should taste I've never had it made correctly. The kids meal was made with chorizo. I'm not a big fan of chorizo and it hasn't changed my mind. The meal tasted fine and the chorizo was not as pronounced which was fine with me. I would give his meal a 4 outta 5. Mine and my wife's was a 6 outta 5. Excellent. I would highly suggest Blondie's and I may have to come back for the cocktails. The service was excellent and I did do something I had not in the past. I dropped the ball that I was going to review Blondie's to our server because I got caught taking pictures! But I truly believe this didn't change the outcome. I promise next time to keep it top secret! So in conclusion. Come to Blondies. Enjoy the atmosphere and have a cocktail or breakfast! Come early though because I believe they close at 4 on Saturdays! Bon appétit!
name: Matt

text: Went there tonight for the first time. Taylor was our server. My wife and I are in our fifties but have 30 years in the restaurant industry combined. We're aren't hard on servers but we also know great service. Since we moved to Tucson 6 months ago, Taylor was the best server we've had here. Burgers were great and loved the Zinburger with the Manchego cheese and GF buns. Drinks were also very good. Can't wait to come back.
name: Mike

text: good size portions, pork roast, a little dry, very little, I think because it kinda steams while keeping warm, but the flavor of pork was not a disappointment, corn pudding, I like mine a little drier but the flavor was on point, and then came the brown beans and corn bread yum, It tasted like it was cooked in a cast iron skillet just like it should be had a little crust. em em good. They have lots of recognition for good food, rewards line the wall. My first home cook restaurant in Nashville didnt disappoint.  Next I have to try their breakfast. No fuss, clean, friendly good food. great atmosphere. I recommend it
name: Deana

text:
Oh WOW! I've been wanting to check out Alon Shaya's new restaurant and over MG week, I finally did. My visitor was surprised to get a reservation on a Friday night but she didn't realize that night's parades were starting just blocks away. Zero problems being dropped off by a rideshare. 

Food was delicious. We had the beets, feta, and the roasted apple, along with brussel sprouts hummus. Everything was amazing, delicious, rich, interesting, well prepared, all the superlatives. Neither of us was starving since we had each had a large lunch but we wished we had room for more food. The apple was interesting in that it was roasted with tahini but was so gorgeous, we hesitated in demolishing it...until we tasted it then all bets were off. And of course, the pita was delish and was whole wheat the night I went so a little more substantial then the usual white wheat.

I had a yummy old fashioned while I was there. There drink menu is super inventive but I just needed an old standby. And of course the wine list is good too.

Service was attentive without being pushy. The atmosphere is lovely and airy. Definitely will be back soon.
name: Jen

text: Ordered take out,  happy with presentation and portion sizes. Chicken kabob was juicy, well seasoned and cooked perfectly. Salad was crunchy and fresh, rices was perfect, and Suzuki sauce was on spot on. Great food will order again, love the location, service and price!
name: Penny

text: We love Mod Pizza. Honestly this place has become my kids top dinner choice so we tend to come here for the occasional quick meal, birthday celebration dinners and early dismissals! I love how everyone can get what they want and they have Daiya cheese! It makes everything so much easier and adds this place to the top of our list!
name: Jamie

text: I hadn't been here in a few years but tonight I had the most amazing cheeseburger with fries than I've had in a long time.  The burger was cooked done but oh so juicy, run  through the garden, my fries were perfect in every way and popping hot. The waitress Cindy, was friendly and attentive, we didn't want for anything. Loved sitting under the stars with friends enjoying our meal.
name: Tina

text: I come in to Doc B's frequently, It's one of my go to spots for their turkey burger, sweet potato fries and salmon. It's health oriented with the ability to accommodate my dietary restrictions. One of the managers, Genevieve always recognizes me as soon as I arrive. She talks to my friends about Doc B's, is always attentive, helpful, and friendly. This is definitely the best food on Bay Street with service to match.
name: Joey

text: I would give it 4-stars if I had read the ingredients and realized I was eating dates in my chocolate ice cream--I'm super allergic to dates.
name: Iris

text: Worst customer service, please don't waste your time here , never again , i order a sandwich which takes half to get it done and its worst sandwich ever also they were slow not busy at all never again
name: Kim

text: Great breakfast and plentiful. I can never finish my meal. Hug menu to select from. Food arrives hot and with a smile. Enjoyed French toast. Turkey sausage, and scrambled eggs. Everything was delicious and with minimal wait. Parking can be scarce at times but stick it out... so worth it. I'll be back.
name: Albrika

text: We visited Desi's Prime Burgers on a recent trip to my old neighborhood, Harahan. We had the Fried pickles appetizer. They were handmade and delicious. My wife had the salad with the bison burger. i had the Desi Classic Burger. It was very good. The fries were outstanding! I will grab a burger here again!
name: David

text:
We try to come to philly once a year basically just to go to Tom's. The food is amazing. Best soup dumplings I've ever had (and I've had a lot). The service is great. We were waiting for our Bao buns but we had gotten all of our food (I was busy eating and hadn't noticed) when the manager came over and said that the reason for the delay was that they make everything fresh but it would be out soon. Definitely worth the wait. They were DELICIOUS and we got another order of soup dumplings to go! 

Must haves: Soup Dumplings & scallion pancake. 

Laid back atmosphere. Always a great experience!
name: Julia

text: Awesome place tried many barbecue restaurants all over Nashville this is definitely my number one choice prices excellent food absolutely delicious my husband and tried the ribs pulled pork chicken and sausage our sides were beans collard greens cowboy stew everything was excellent definitely will be back!!!
name: Linda

text: What a wonderful surprise to find such a lovely woman selling such scrumptious vegan treats at the Rillito Sunday Farmer's Market. I appreciate that all of Alaine's super yummy baked goods are made with the highest quality ingredients. Her tempeh chickenless salad was so tasty, I had to get an extra container to take with me for my flight home to Oregon. Take a bite of anything Alaine makes, and you can tell that it is made with love.
name: Gail

text: The chicken soft tacos and the crispy chicken taco were soooo good! I'm definitely coming back. The only problem is that they close at 3pm every day.
name: Kaiden

text: I wanted to like this more than I actually did. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. Kind of landed in the middle for me.
name: User

text:
Really great food!! All fresh and authentic. Staff was super kind too and also gave us a delish free dessert!
And he won our hearts with telling us to Boiler up!
name: Audrey

text:
I came here for a staff lunch recently. I had been wanting to check it out, but I won't lie, the prices scared me away for many months. 

The first thing you'll notice as a vegetarian: there aren't many options (at least options that seem to be enough for a meal. I opted for the roasted mushroom burger. It was delicious. The cheese that they put on it tied everything together quite nicely. The simple greens on the side were a nice, light touch to the heaviness of the burger, and the french fries were delicious. For $15 - it was a tad too pricey as I didn't get a ton of food. 

I look forward to getting back during the fall time weather and enjoying a warm cocktail on their fire-lit patio and hopefully get a nice veggie-friendly dish while I'm there too. 

Great food, you just pay more $$ for it.
name: Brady

text:
Check them out if you like bad service, bad food, and expensive prices. 

We were put at a table that was squished against the wall by a large table. The mama chair was touching the side of our table. We asked to move. 

The server was super weird and took orders one at a time (waited for drinks to come before asking about appetizers, waited for appetizer to come before asking about entree, etc). It became such a problem the table next to us asked for a manager. The manager checked on us too and we gave the same review. No one apologized. No food was comped. He also knew nothing about the menu. Super awkward because I already looked at the menu and knew more than him about their selection. 

When the food finally came, it was terrible.  The French toast was bland and the biscuits were hard. The bacon ($5 for 4 small pieces) was too salty. 

The only redeeming factor was the atmosphere. It was a pretty restaurant. But not pretty enough for all the nonsense.
name: Nicole

text: The pizza was very doughy , if it's an oven brick baked pizza , why can't they get it right ? Why can't they bake it and it serve it fully cooked ?
name: Sara G

text: Fantastic friendly service. Had the alligator as an entree. Super flavorful! A definite must try!
name: Elle

text: I have been here numerous times and each time they NEVER seem to let me down! They have the best bread pudding that I've ever had. The warm greeting you receive from the door all the way down the hot line with your tray to when you take a seat at the tables. All the staff members are friendly and it's a great atmosphere. I've had the chicken fried chicken, green beans, Mac and cheese, meatloaf, fried fish and shrimp IT WAS AMAZING!!!! I tell anyone if you haven't been to Arnold's you should definitely go. The best southern food in Nashville and the only one that I've found that is worth spending your money on.
name: Tandrea

text:
Nice apple tart. 
Nice coffee (black coffee).
Great space to study or work.
No parking space but you can street parking.
name: Laurie

text: One of my favorite king cakes! I go out of my way to get at least one every Mardi Gras season. Customer service is great!
name: Janna

text:
I don't like to leave negative reviews but I was so disappointed.  We got up early to go get donuts from here which is not close to me at all so we did go out of our way.  We had the lemon lavender maple bacon, a long john and the coffee crumble. I will give you that these donuts are huge, but not at all tasty.  I looked forward to the lemon lavender so much but I tasted no lemon or lavender only sugar. Same with the maple bacon.  My daughter took a bite of each of hers and asked to go to Tony's, our favorite donut shop and by far so much better.  My mother ate her lemon lavender but only because she didn't want it to go to waste. 

The price was very high for quality. A can of coke was two bucks and if it were a bottle I wouldn't complain but for a can???

The restaurant was clean and comfortable but small. The lady who served us was nice and explained the difference between the round and the square donuts but when we told her we wanted to eat there she seemed bothered, like she didn't want us there at all. She also made it a point of telling us because she had not sold out yet, she knew she would be there until two which is closing time.  Overall I didn't feel welcomed, it was more take your donuts and go which I did not like.

Overall this was not an enjoyable outing which made me a bit sad since I'd looked so forward to trying these donuts which sounded so good and get such great reviews. However, we left with a firm knowledge that we will not go back again.
name: Deborah

text: Benedict! That's all I can say. Fullblast is a wonderful breakfast and brunch place. I met a friend there for a bite and they have like 5 kinda of Eggs Benedict and while I went traditional for round one I can see me going back for crab cake Benedict soon.
name: Mark

text: It tasted fresh, just not especially memorable. Idk, for a busy night they handled it okay. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. For the price I expected more than this. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. So yeah, the food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. For the price I expected more than this. The leftovers held up okay the next day..
name: User

text:
I am so happy that I found this little spot hidden a couple of blocks off of Mass Ave.  I had heard of Kaffeine but I just happened to be driving down a side street right by it.  I knew I had to return! 

The inside is so cozy.  They've done a great job with the interior.  Their coffee selection is simple by design.  Personally, I love my large iced drinks and there wasn't any of that.  I went with the Spanish Latte, iced, and loved it!  It was only a 12 oz drink, but it was so tasty.  I don't know if I would go out of my way to return, as there are so many options around the city, but I am so glad I stopped here. I recommend it!
name: Kylie

text: Excellent Chinese spot with great customer service!  The food is hot, fresh and delicious and so fast!  Bustling restaurant but still attentive and kind.  Get wrekd for $20 like we did!
name: Laura

text: We went here on a whim on Mother's Day. They were understaffed and over worked. We were treated with friendly service that apologized for the messy kitchen and longer wait times. We were from out of town and just hungry, so we were patient. We were given great food and discounted for things not being up to what they considered "normal." Our family will be back when we are in town again, the food was great.
name: Caleb

text: Cute little spot next to our hotel.   It's bar food so nothing spectacular about it.  Brought my husband there and he was beyond disappointed.  He ordered the Cuban and it was too greasy.  I ordered wings and it was too dry.  Service was a bit slow.   Four staff members went by and never acknowledged us until we finally flagged them down even though they made eye contact with us 10 mins later.
name: Viriya

text:
This is without a doubt the best restaurant in Indianapolis and I am upset that I did not come here earlier. The food was beyond delicious. We tried multiple dishes off their menu and everything tasted so so good. 10/10 would recommend. It is pricey, so this is def a place for a nice birthday dinner or some sort of celebration.

My only hangup is that this place is too small, crowded, and therefore very loud. I often times could not hear my partner speak, though he was sitting across the table from me.
name: Klaudia

text: We just received our delivery order. I'm really disappointed, it took over 2 and a half hours to arrive.  The caprese salad gets smaller and smaller and sloppier every time I order it, and it's just not very appetizing any more.   Everything was cold including our pizza and grilled cheese. We would order from here more, but it seems more often than not that they under deliver in various ways. Sad :(
name: Adam

text: GREAT burger and excellent shrimp and okra gumbo. Interesting and delicious cocktails. We had the Absolution which was very light and refreshing. Then we had the Duck Fat Sazerac and the Bubbles and Butter. Both taste exactly as described on the menu and were delicious.
name: Jacqueline

text: We had a beautiful meal. The bonus was meeting the owner! Food was unbelievable and service was superb!!!!!
name: Bruce

text:
Studio Movie Grill is my go to date night location!
Not only is it a great theater but they have food and a full bar, how great is that?
The specials they have during the week are my favorite - Tuesday's and Thursday's are my go to movie nights. Tuesday is $5 movie night which makes for a cheap night out with some good entertainment! My boyfriend and I try to go on this day each week to see new releases. Thursday nights are great for movie release nights since it is $5 dessert night at SMG. 

Overall we love the quality of service here, the great food choices (coconut chicken is one of my favorite meals) and the availability of new movie releases! We have been going here since it opened and will continue to return again and again!
name: Kaela

text:
A coffee stand in a historic indoor market? Yes, please! Here's what's to love and one thing to keep in mind when going:

1) Atmosphere: It's on the second floor of the old indoor market building just north of downtown Indy, which is still a working market. The coffee shop has bar seating and a few tables nearby to people watch.

2) Coffee: It's some of the best beans I had in Indy and their latte was on point.

One thing to keep in mind:

1) Service: Maybe I went too early on a Saturday, but the barista was so unkind. I overheard him making fun of customers and was just a cold person. Visiting from the East Coast, I may expect that from other cities, but not that's viewed as the heart and soul of the Midwest.

Regardless, if you like quality coffee, Mile Square is a good option when in Indy.
name: Austin

text:
I really enjoy the consistency and excellence of the food at Arnold's. Their sides are great and, no matter what protein is available (it switches every day), you won't be disappointed. 

On top of that, Arnold's service is really friendly, what southern hospitality is all about. The only downside is that if you drag your feet on certain days (Friday, for instance), you'll end up in a long line that seemingly stretches down the street. And if you've been there before, you'll wait patiently because you know it's worth it.
name: Kenneth

text: Had brunch here over the weekend and it was kind of a mixed bag. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Also, solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Honestly, nothing was awful but i left disappointed. For the price I expected more than this. so yeah kind of mixed on it. For the price I expected more than this. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine..
name: User

text:
Not sure what all the hype is about. It was a solid meh. I had the Croque Madam and the ingredients seemed fresh and all but there was surprisingly little flavor. Hardly any sweet in the donut, no salt in the rest. I was really hoping for a sweet/salty taste experience.

I tried the cinnamon roll too. It was cloyingly sweet and the center half was completely raw and doughy. 

Iced coffee was not bad.

Staff seemed constantly confused as to what they were supposed to doing. 

Booth was terribly uncomfortable. 

I really wanted to like this place after all the local hype but it just didn't deliver.
name: Vasula

text: Ended up here pretty late, maybe around 9:30, because everything else nearby had a wait. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. It was decent, just a little uneven.
name: User

text:
This was our first visit and very disappointed. They were out of two of the three kinds of chicken so I ordered the potato soup and my husband ordered a bowl.  He ordered the medium bowl for around $7 and to add chicken (the one they had) was an extra $4.  The soup was tasty but hardly warm and a bowl was $5 which was supposed to come with bread which they were out of also. 

We each ordered a soda and asked about refills because the soda fountain was behind the counter. The gal told us there were free refills. While visiting with friends and sitting there awhile we had gotten up to get a couple refills. We decided to get some cookies after sitting there for a little while, of which the 4 kinds offered only had one flavor and also out of the chocolate you can dip in. We were then told by the staff after ordering cookies ($3 each) that we wouldn't be served any more refills. 

Over priced and average food - won't be back.
name: Donna

text: Visited the place yesterday, Saturday April. It was a Very pleasant surprise - pretty modest place with native people kindly serving you that authentic native meals which was just delicious. Real, very healthy, very tasty , very natural . Great place to visit and relax. Very nice kind service eager to explain about meals , traditions and habits, joking and very kind. Visit the place, enjoy the meal  - you wouldn't regret !
name: Lyudmila

text:
Hadn't eaten at Boutros in years. Had lunch there with my bf, and we highly regretted it.
The falafel wrap I ordered was heated up for a bit in the microwave. As I was eating it, the falafels just crumbled. It was the dryest falafel I'd ever eaten. The wrap was thin & mealy. On top of that, my bf mentioned that the woman who served us, when trying to pick up the food with wax paper, used her bare finger to push them into it. I didn't finish my lunch. The gyro he ordered was even worst. The meat was dried out (up?) possibly from the hot weather and/or from sitting around for awhile. And the tsaziki sauce had a sour taste to it. He felt sick afterwards.
The people were nice enough. The baklava I had for dessert was decent. Still, avoid this place. The fact that the Bellevue food court is lacking in places to eat (and wasn't bustling with diners) should have been a sign to avoid eating down there. 
For falafel go to Mama's or Goldie's. For a tender gyro check out Moustaki.
name: Lisa

text: We went to dinner at Red Lobster this past Friday, and had one of the worst experiences I've ever had at any restaurant. We ordered dinner which included soup as an appetizer. We received our soup and salads immediately. Then we waited for over 30 minutes and still hadn't received our meal. The waiter came by several times to apologize, but we sat there. Finally I told him to just write us a check for the soup and salad, and forget the meal. He suggested just getting up and walking out since he hadn't entered the soup into the system yet. I declined and asked for the check. It took him another 10 minutes to come back with the check for soup, which I paid for in cash, and we left. We sat without food for over 40 minutes, while people around us were served expediently. Terrible service.
name: Steve

text: Great food. Totally tasty! Good service and neat environment. Ideal place for brunch. Order The fried chicken. Worth to try.
name: Jinghan

text: I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. For the price I expected more than this. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. It looked better online than it did in person. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh.
name: User

text:
Wow, is this place beautiful. I didn't stay overnight here, but had a table at an author book signing in Feb 2018. Our signing room was very large and was beautiful. The only couple of problems were that our organizer didn't want to pay $35 PER PERSON (come on Gaylord that is unreasonable) for us to have wifi. I can't blame her, but for a Canadian with no data, that simply doesn't work. Also, the place is HUGE. We had trouble finding the signing room, and I had to wonder if maybe some attendees did too.
The hotel was like a city inside. Lots of restaurants, shops and even a river ride inside! Fountains and plants were everywhere. It was simply stunning. Some of the fountains 'spit' into one another, like a jumping line of water hopping from fountain to fountain. There was something beautiful to see everywhere one looked. I would have loved to stay here, but our 'special' rate was more than I would ever pay for a single night at a hotel with parking on top of that.
We were a bit mislead by the valet. He told us that if we ate at the hotel our parking would be comped. This isn't entirely true. We spent almost $30 on pizza, but were told we had to eat in one of the really expensive restaurants to get parking comped. That was so misleading and, I felt, deceitful. He never specified that.
If you're into the fancy stuff, this hotel is a feast for the eyes and is spectacular looking with lots to do inside. If, like me, you're not into grossly overpaying for your room, this hotel probably is not for you. Gorgeous but overpriced. The pizza place did have a gluten-free option which is a huge plus.
name: Claudette

text: Awesome food and great beer. Super friendly service.  Nice porch on the water. Small dining area--go early!
name: Beth

text: I had the Kapoon (spicy) and it was so so good. The colors of the dish were pleasing to the eye and the taste was even better than it looked!! The service was great too! Will definitely return and recommend anyone stopping in for lunch or dinner.
name: Lisa

text: I've seem better seafood in a dumpster in Florida. Well they tried. I would recommend better seasoning.
name: Blake

text:
I was on the Eastside and happened to be close enough to 5th Street Deli to stop in for a sandwich.  It looks like some changes had taken place and something was off.  The meat cases have been reduced to one and I was a little unsure they still did deli sandwiches.  The counter person reassured me they still did sandwiches but he was out of some items.
I ordered a regular corned beef sandwich with a side of macaroni salad to go.  They do have seating but the eating area, but it looked thrown around like they were trying to fill up space to replace items removed. The grocery section is now just along a corner wall and looked very limited.  
The sandwich had a generous portion of meat and the macaroni salad was a nice size served with a dill pickle.  It made for a filling lunch but both were lacking in flavor.
Overall, it was an average visit which made little to make me say wow.
name: Ken

text: For the price I expected more than this. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. Wouldn't really choose this place again. It looked better online than it did in person. Food was fresh and service was quick. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Not bad for a quick meal.
name: User

text: I just walked out of the store and I am completely disgusted. I have to explain because I did have three experiences. When we first walked in we browsed for a second and the first female worker walked directly in front of us and the item we were looking at. She never said excuse me nor a simple hello. We moved over to the olive oil section and were questioning to ourselves a bit then a another female worker came over and stood in front of us filling bottles. She never said excuse me nor did she even speak. My counterpart did ask if the size description and she gave a quick response. Never did she seem to want to engage. There was a young male worker that did speak and stated if we needed any help to let him know. By that time we were done and had already made up in our minds that we would not be purchasing. It was a huge disappointment because they seem to have some good items but customer service determines where I will spend my money. I still give kudos to the young male worker. I just hope that this was indeed just a bad day of customer service and certainly not because we were two African American males.
name: Kevin

text: Cool ambience.  Decent food but terrible service.  They lost my credit card at the bar, the tasting menu was brought out all at once to our awkward table for two on a couch.  And...everything was slow.
name: Bill

text: For the price I expected more than this. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. It just never really recovered once things started off weird. Probably not coming back. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. The food was good and the service was easygoing. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.
name: User

text: Great music, amazing food, awesome cocktails. Nothing negative to say. My wife cried because the pork belly was so good
name: Thomas

text: Really delicious kosher food. Falafel is really good and their meat hummus is very yummy! Super nice staff, fairly priced
name: Don

text: Arrived for a party in a private room at Moontown Brewing. Nice facility/ comfortable seating and tables. Had the Pretzels and smothered nachos both excellent. Several craft beers to choose from, every one seemed to find what they liked taste wise. On busy nights parking is a premium. Excellent place for a gathering.
name: Robert

text: I almost skipped this place bc of the ratings and that would've been unfair. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. Food was good and came out fast. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly.
name: User

text:
You hear the name Sheraton and have an expectation. They fall very short.  The facilities are tired and worn. 

Staff was not complementary. There was loud kids yelling in rooms at 1 am. Reminded me more of Motel 6. 

We had a block of rooms for 50th birthday celebration. We all gathered in the bar and where spending money. We brought a cake. We were told it was state law we could not have the cake in the bar and had to move to the lobby. Okay we will accommodate. Maybe it is the law. Then we asked it they had any paper plates or plastic forks we could use and where directed to the little store to purchase. 

Then on top of an overly inflated room change for a worn out room we had $9 parking.

The over all evening was disappointing. Will not be back. Makes me curious if Sheraton as a whole of struggling?
name: Ronald

text:
I had to try that mac and cheese grilled cheese but wasn't super hungry, so I ordered it to-go to pick it up and take it home to split it with a friend who was in town for the weekend. I called and placed the order, and was told it would be ready in 10-15 minutes for pick-up.

It was a Monday evening on a holiday weekend, but when we showed up, it was pretty quiet and mostly empty here. Parking is along the street with mostly metered spots, but I was able to just pull up front and run in, and fortunately my order was ready so I was in and out pretty quickly.

I ordered the Arlington without the bacon, and decided to check the order when I got to my car to make sure it was correct. When I saw it, I had to try it right there. The bread was thick enough to support the massive amount of thick elbow mac that it held within. On its own, the mac and cheese probably wouldn't have been anything special, but with extra cheese and put between two breads, it was actually pretty good! It wasn't even very messy- I was able to eat it without any mac spilling out on me.

I'll have to return sometime to dine-in and try some of the desserts, but so far, I like what I've tried.
name: Gia

text: Wish they had better service and weren't selective of who they wanted to serve. I would say that they were understaffed in my opinion. Only 2 bartenders behind bar on a Friday night.
name: Ashley

text: Came here with a large group- food and service were great. Wasn't terribly impressed with the bar service, but it's certainly not a deal breaker!
name: Susie

text: The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. The music was louder than it needed to be. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. Pretty happy with it overall. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine..
name: User

text: Their homemade dumplings are to die for. They are hands down the best I've had. Their overall food is your general Chinese take out kind of food, but their fried rice is not the usual kind (in a good way though, much better). Their dumplings are the star of the show though, they come in shrimp, chicken, veggie, and pork. Both take out and eating in at this locale is good, and the staff is incredibly friendly and cheerful when I went there during the dinner rush.
name: Emily

text:
Great Greek grub!   

The ingredients are fresh.  Prices are fair.  Service is friendly and fast.  And the spaces are clean, lively.  

Our family stopped in for lunch on a weekend.  We were pleasantly surprised by our meals and experience.  The portions were ample, and the food was tasty.  [Though the falafel was a bit bland.]. The hummus was fantastic.  We'll definitely come back.
name: Joseph

text: Wandered into the Red Bicycle because the reviews on yelp, and I must admit I'm pretty impressed. The food is delicious and the coffee taste great. There's a nice coffee shop vibe and the staff is very welcoming. Wish I would have tried the desert crepes cause they look amazing!
name: Sirena

text: I was so looking forward to dinner at Blood and Sand but was disappointed and honestly embarrassed to have picked it for a special event with friends.  Our waiter was kind and well meaning, but would have been more suited in a significantly more causal setting.  The food was "good" at best but the lobster wontons were honestly empty.  I should have sent them back, but again, this restaurant was my choice and I didn't want to cause a fuss with the special friends we invited.  Expensive isn't the right word.... overpriced is more accurate
name: Katherine

text: We've been to this sushi pier 3-4 times in the last 6 months. It seams like every time we go to sushi pier the service is slow even though they aren't busy. There's usually several servers standing around chit chatting. They have messed up my order every time I've been there. I don't add or change any ingredients that are listed on the rolls yet it seams the chefs don't even know the menu. We went today and the bathrooms are nasty, I mean worse then a gas station in the middle of the hood nasty.
name: Heather

text: Excellent service from the moment I opened the door. It is a mom and pop cash only place. They make you feel at home and I'm visiting from out of town. Definitely coming back!
name: Vianey

text: Went out to grab a bite and my friend chose Pancho and willies at the western village. The casino was packed and we were given a 55 Minute wait for a table. We went to the sports bar and enjoyed a lemon drop and dirty martini. We got our call for a table after about 35 minutes. We were surprised to enter because the restaurant was half empty so I'm assuming it was a waiter issue not a table issue. We were greeted immediately with chips and salsa and water as we had carried our drinks into the restaurant with us. Dawn our waitress appeared after a few minutes and give us plenty of time to read the menu. I ordered the chipotle salmon which was pretty spicy for me my friend had the halibut which was covered with a spicy cream sauce. There was a lot of food and it was very good and hot. At the end of dinner we decided to have a margarita and finish our meal. Everything was good and we used a two for one coupon which made it even better. Will definitely return.
name: Cora

text: Really good food, prices are reasonable. Recommend to try it out if you haven't. Friendly people serving you.
name: Wilmer

text: George, the owner, was incredible in his hospitality. Before we even entered, George had waved his hands to signal us to come inside. He made us feel welcomed. It was about 7 of us and we were treated like family. We were able to be accommodated quickly, but also the food was delicious! Super affordable and friendly environment!
name: Elisabetta

text: I have breakfasted here 3 times now, and every time I tried something different and the food was always excellent! The menu is a little pricey for breakfast but I have always enjoyed what I ordered very much. This is an upscale restaurant. The servers are friendly and courteous, the meal delivery is a little slow but worth the wait and comes out hot.
name: Joe

text:
Listen.............
On a day when I really didn't care what I stopped to eat, I was lucky enough to come across Antonella's... I only stopped in to buy a sandwich and wound up sitting down to a great meal with pasta and meatballs... Anyplace that says that they have meatballs, I always ask are they made fresh... Please don't lie to me just to earn a buck. 
Let me
Tell you that this place makes one of the best meatballs that I've eaten. I had recently spoken to a random stranger from Boston. But she had gone to school at Villanova. We were talking about food and I mentioned good places in the area to eat and that I knew a place that made great meatballs and sauce... This woman hadn't been in town in a few years. But she blurted our Antonella's before I got a chance to say it!!
Back to my meal... I finished it a happy man. Thanked the owner and told him how great the meal was. And I also bought more food to take home for dinner.... 
Yeah.... it was really that good. 
If you're ever in the area. This business will not disappoint you.
name: Tim

text: I love going to this place everytime I go to Nashville. They have the best pickle spears! Thats the reason I go there. I havent ordered a beer there in a long time because they were always warm and $6. $6 is expensive. Its outragous for a warm beer. I would have given more stars if it wasnt for the beer prices and temp.
name: Candy

text:
Yes, yes and more Yes!
If you are new in town, visiting or a local, you MUST try this restaurant.  I am hard on food because I work in the industry but this place is the real deal. I promise!
Exactly what I thought  a Philly should be coming from the south. I first ate at Geno's when I landed on the recommendation of an airport employee--It was terrible. Then, I went on Yelp and found this place and the heavens opens up! 
Big, huge, happiness of flavor!
DO IT!
name: Malia

text:
Staff was overly friendly!
Food portions were very generous.
And they gave us plenty of containers for our leftovers along with a healthy amount of BBQ sauce to take home.
name: T

text: This was a delivery order on a night when I really did not want to cook. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. The staff seemed tired but still polite. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. There were a couple things I liked and a couple things I probably wouldn't get again. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Not sure though.
name: User

text: I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. Worth checking out. Food was good and came out fast. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. The food was good and the service was easygoing.
name: User

text:
This is one of the best restaurants in the city and in Northern Nevada!  Although I come here a lot either by myself or with friends or family I've never shared the always incredible experience.  Today is the day as we close out 2018.   The service is ALWAYS outstanding - from the warm and inviting smile of manager Ebony - to the impeccable hospitality of Mike, Anthony, Chris and Andy to name our top favorite personalities!  
Now let's talk about the delicious selection and of food from always a little bit 'twisted' takes on favorites like burgers or pizza to the most flavorful vegetarian tamal or short rib arepa to name a few.  Excellent quality, EVERYTIME!  There is always a very tasty homemade soup with a variety of original flavors and specials!
Here's to the vast array of restaurant specialists whether tending the outstanding bar, serving superb quality food or just making people feel welcome EVERYTIME!  Thank you - you are the best of the best!  This is for the Twisted Fork in Reno, Nevada
name: Gary

text: Incredible food! Incredible people! Thank you for being so kind. We walked in and everyone greeted us with so much hospitality! The bbq sauce was the best I've ever had! Try their turkey ribs
name: Peter

text: Ate here last Thursday night, had customers in from Indiana and they loved it! I had the 9 oz filet and it was cooked perfect, good food and good service.
name: Bill

text:
TLDR - My butthole's on fiiiirrrreeeeeeee 

The hype around Hattie B's was at an all time high comin into Nashville, and the expectations were met. Though, we made a mistake for sure. I'm not sure what spice level the other reviewers chose, but anyone saying it's not spicy did not have the "Shut the Cluck Up" spice level. Because of those reviews, we only ordered hot, damn hot, and shut the cluck up. My gf couldn't eat cuz was in literal pain and started drinking the ranch for comfort. I was too, but I actually enjoy spice. Definitely spicy enough even for heat lovers. Don't believe the lies and slander! The good thing was, the taste of chicken was still full, and I loved the flavor in every bite. 

All in all, I loved this place, just might tone down on the spice level next time I'm in town. Full discretion, I haven't tried Prince's yet. 

Protip: I recommend this location over others if you aren't a fan of waiting in long lines. This was about a 20 minute wait and I hear that's on the shorter end compared to other locations like the one in midtown.
name: Zhen

text: I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. It was crowded but still moved along. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Food was good and came out fast. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The leftovers held up okay the next day..
name: User

text: Good place for lunch, very accesible prices, big portions. Staff very friendly, food came out quick. Very delicious!!
name: AC

text: Wonderful little brunch gem! Byob! Excellent service, DELICIOUS chilaquiles and cafe con chocolate. Cozy Philly spot. Can't wait to come again. Gracias
name: Casandra

text: Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. Price felt a touch high for what it was. For a busy night they handled it okay. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. Pretty happy with it overall. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really.
name: User

text: Fave Chinese food in town. My baby love their dumplings and portions are really good.
name: Nicole

text:
Cafe Poca Cosa is an experience that can't be missed!  The staff were very friendly and walked us through their menu (which changes throughout the day), answered any questions we had, and were very careful when we mentioned allergy concerns.

I highly recommend their Tamale Pie (when being offered) with a Con Fuego margarita for those that want to add a bite to their drink.

Do not come here expecting traditional Sonoran fare, but don't let that stop you from missing out on this wonderful place.
name: Sam

text: With the knowledge that South Jersey does not have great Indian restaurants, our expectations were somewhat subdued, even before we placed an order. Even with minimal expectations, our experience was incredibly disappointing to say the least. The Chicken Tikka which is one of the staples of Indian cuisine was over cooked while the Biryani, one of the most important entrees in Indian cuisine, was undercooked. Maybe this is a one off, but I am still somewhat scarred from this experience so I won't be going back here unless this is the only remaining restaurant in Cherry Hill.
name: Ritesh

text:
This was my first experience at hot pot where everyone gets their own pot.  Usually it's a fight for the meat bits in a communal pot with my friends.  This nice civilized dining experience was a welcome change!  My mom, her friend, and I went for their lunch special which featured the choice of a soup base and then you choose somewhere between 5-7 items for a reasonable price of $15 (approx) per person.  We went on a Wednesday at 1pm at it was not busy at all.  We were seated immediately and our soup and items came promptly.  There was a cart that had a variety of sauces to choose from which I happily did.  I ordered the Tom Yum soup base and I was happy with my selection.  My mom ordered udon noodles and she commented on how impressed she was with the quantity.  I got the sweet potato noodles and I thought they were delicious.  Would happily go back again.
The decor was a bit outdated and it didn't scream pristine in the cleanliness department - not a food safety concern by any means!  Just old and well worn floors/walls/furniture.  No real complaints though.
name: Katrina

text:
What changed at this restaurant. The service and the food are going down hill fast. We stopped in for lunch on Friday afternoon. Usually a busy day with a wait for a table. The parking lot was packed as was the market. The line for doughnuts was 10 people deep. We should have bought a dozen it would have been the better choice. 

The restaurant was 2/3's empty. We still waited for someone to show us to a table. They offered us a window table. Normally a nice table except when the ants  are cleaning the food scraps. When I found one crawling up my arm we got up and moved to a table away from the window. It took 5 mins for the waitress to notice we moved. The hostess didn't question the move even after we pointed out the ants  the hostess sat another couple at the same table. She never stopped to clean the crumbs or address the ants . Our waitress finally arrived with our iced tea key word iced. As there was no ice in the tea on a day when it's 90 Degs outside. 

After 10 mins we noticed the people at the ant  table had received their food. FYI we warned them about the ants . They brushed them off the table and said it didn't bother them. However they had no problem complaining to the waitress. 

Our waitress said they were having a problem in the kitchen. Ok I said can we at least get some ice tea with ice in it. She returned with one glass of ice for us to split. Our sandwiches finally arrived. They were as disappointing as it gets. How do you serve a burnt turkey club. We asked for take out boxes and left. We should have left after the ants . This place is usually better than this. The best part is the burnt club sandwich cost $11.00 dollars .
name: Len

text: I started coming here a few months ago, because I've been on the hunt for a good oatmeal bar in the city. This is a small and busy breakfast/lunch spot in the BNY Mellon that is connected to Suburban Station. They have ready made breakfast sandwiches, an ordering station for a variety of breakfast sandwiches, omelets, and pancakes, and a separate ordering station for juices/shakes/smoothies. They also have parfaits, fruit salads, beverages, snacks, and a coffee station for those on the go. I typically order an oatmeal a couple of times a week topped with fresh strawberries, bananas, raisins, and brown sugar. I love the consistency of the warm and creamy oatmeal and the fresh and sweet fruit toppings, it's ultimate comfort food to me on a blustery winter morning. Today, since I'm currently experimenting with the "eat like a king for breakfast and eat like a pauper for dinner" kick, I ordered a bacon, egg, and cheese multigrain sandwich, and purchased a side order of berries. The breakfast sandwich was filled generously with scrambled egg and bacon, but it was definitely on the greasier side. I'm probably going to stick with the oatmeal, but stop by if you need breakfast! The staff has been friendly thus far, and you get your food pretty quickly.
name: Heather

text: If you want to be a part of the fantastic live music scene in Tucson this is the place to go! It has a great stage, sound system, and dance floor. Also, they have a delicious food menu with something for everyone. That, and an extensive bar, make for a great evening out of music, dancing, and dining!  The courtyard is beautiful and provides year around comfort with either patio heaters or a misting system. Surrounding the courtyard are several artisan shops where you can find unique and one of a kind items. Monterey Court is a jewel so don't miss out! Reservations are highly recommended.
name: Linda

text:
I went here back in Jan 2018. Its next to a Salon. Has some couch seating, three tables seating four people and has calm lighting. There is a separate room perfect for a smaller business meeting and is well lit. At the time, there was one barista and there is hot tea as well as plenty of specialty drinks. They have some breakfast grab and go options. 
Two sizes- 16 oz and 20 oz. 
I was given a rewards card. They have some craft sodas for other options as well. 
They have Chauvin coffee beans. I wouldn't call this place kid friendly either, they share bathrooms with the salon and there is no table to change babies and there isn't a highchair. 
If you're looking for a blonde roast like I usually am, they did not have one. 
This local small coffee shop was a win in my eyes though, I would be back.
name: Eleni

text: The food here was great, the service even better. Wait staff, bartenders, and managers make sure everyone is taken care of. We came here looking specifically for banana foster, but turns out they don't have it on their menu any more. Lou was amazing and called their sister resturant and made reservations there for us so we could get it asap. The balcony was a great place to sit and watch the people perform in front of the St. Louis Cathedral. Would definitely recommend Tableau.
name: Rubi

text:
Grabbed some brunch here while on vacation.  I intended to listen to some live jazz, but I made my reservation too early.  I just assumed that the band would be playing when they opened at 10:00.  Still, we took our time and heard a little bit of music towards the end of our meal.

The brunch menu includes a bunch of Southern classics that have been modernized in a good way.  There were four of us at the table and I don't think anyone had a bad dish.  The bloody mary bar is pretty comprehensive and they have an eclectic selection of vodkas to choose from.

Would totally resist this place for brunch, but i would make my reservations an hour later.  LOL
name: Mark

text: Probably the best burger I've ever had! I was so excited to get a burger with a gluten free/egg free bun! The only thing that was disappointing was that the fries don't have a dedicated fryer, so they aren't GF. I will for sure come back!
name: Patricia

text:
Area A- 

My only issue is the parking area which should be done soon which will make the whole area pop!! The view is immaculate and you have a view of the water!! 

Customer service A 

Very nice and on time with everything even though the place is packed! 

Food A++

THEY SEASON THEIR FOOD!! Small plates which make it an good experience!! Their braised short rib tostones is to die for!!!! Their mussels is to die for as well! Their drinks is very good as well!! 

Overall A+ 

A must visit place in the Tampa Bay Area! Great food, great drinks, great view and it is also a bar at night! I definitely WILL be coming back!!!!!
name: Cordereo

text: Authentic. Fresh. Accessible. New. Friendly.  Addicting.  Fowler stepping their game up.  The spicy salmon was good.
name: Trader

text: Love this place! The staff are great (mostly) and the food is good. I had a bad experience as the Spanish Springs location was dying. But this place is so much better. I go in for lunch a couple times a month. Always meets my expectations
name: Blake

text:
Just wrapped our department Holiday Lunch at Ludlow & Prime.  From the planning process with Rachel to the event today we could not have been more pleased.

First of all, the food was awesome.  Our 54-person group can be hard to please, but everyone raved about how good the food was.

The service was truly wonderful as well.  

We had a great experience all thanks to the owners and staff at Ludlow & Prime!
name: Sherra

text: This doesn't look like anything when you pull up, which was a little worrisome, but it was definitely worth trying.  The beef and snow peas was great with nice, meaty chunks of beef instead of the usual thin shaved pieces.    Plain fried rice had a nice Smokey taste to it, and egg roll had a wonderfully unexpected flavor.  Prices were fabulous, too.  Would definitely recommend!
name: Kim

text: Cool place. We went not knowing what to expect, and without reservations. They still accommodated my husband and i at a table quickly. The food was delicious, a little pricey, but worth every penny. It was nice to be able to order anything on the menu without having to worry about what's in it. We had a really nice date night here, we'll be back.
name: Jamie

text: Visited this past Sunday after attending a cheer competition and wanted a sit down meal before heading back home, to Memphis. We arrived a little after 12pm. The competition just ended and we were trying to beat the church crowd. We did! No long wait, stood in line for about 15mins, which was cool because we were reading the menu board and trying to decide what 2 eat. It was 3 adults and 2 kids in our party. So, we get to the serving line n just looked at one another.. Definitely not what we expected. The dressing was dry and stuck to the bottom of the pan. It crumbled as she was scooping it out of the pan. The meatloaf looked dry. They didn't  have any pork chops, no turkey wings, dry tough looking turkey legs, fried chicken and smothered wings, sliced roast beef in beef juice/drippings. I opted on 3wings. 2 fried and 1 smothered in gravy, greens, mac and cheese, banana pudding , cornbread and half sweet tea/half lemonade. My total was $20. Our server was friendly and attentive. The bathroom; the floor was clean, trash wasnt full but some of the toliets either didnt work or something..But it wasnt nasty. Just needs better tending too. Let me be clear and break it down.. I'm from Memphis, TN where we learn how to cook traditional complete meals at an early age...I wasnt impressed. This was my 4th time visiting St.Louis and I've never been pressed to visit, because I felt it would be average food. N in my opinion it was just that, average. Some items were over cooked n dry, some was good n some was take it off my plate. The banana pudding was nothing to write about. Only ate a few spoons full.In my opinion: they arent famous for GOOD food, their famous for having a southern family focused TV show. I recommend changing the menu board to make it customer friendly. I recommend paying attention to the food and not over cooking simple things such as dressing and macaroni and cheese. But, the employees were very nice, smiled and chatted. They were the best part‼
name: Toya

text: This place was louder than I expected and that sort of shaped the whole meal. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, tho the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. It was decent, just a little uneven. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait.
name: User

text:
I'm kind of ashamed for not coming here before Indy burger week, but I'm glad I did. The beau and I decided to venture out on the last day of the special. We were able to bypass the line and find open seating in the bar area. Our waitress was amazing; she made sure to check on us frequently for the duration of our dining experience. :) The BBQ Bacon Burger caught my eye so I went with that sans the cheese. I eat cheese but not on burgers for some strange reason, but it included bacon, barbecue sauce, and onion ring on a  1/2 lb beef patty. I prefer my bacon soft not crunchy and I think it was a happy medium. I took a bite and was in love. I had to ask for more bbq sauce because it wasn't enough though. I also got the tater tots and they were shaped like the little Tetris game tiles. I kind felt like a kid again playing with my food. 

Another thing I spotted on the menu was the drink options. I wanted to taste the pineapple cider and noticed that you can get three 5oz samples for $6 so I chose the pineapple cider and the beau got the dreamsicle ale, and cougar ale. The last two reminded me yet again that I do not like bear AT ALL. The dreamsicle did smell like its name, just didn't taste like it to me. I loved the cider even though it was a bit sweeter than I thought. Overall experience was great. Thanks to Indy burger week, I'll be back to 317 burger sooner than later.
name: Tianna

text: We had the chicken and al pastor tacos. Pretty good. Plenty of table to sit at. Prices were reasonable. I like the chips and salsa bar. Chips was crisp and the salsas were tasty. The only thing I did not like was the guacamole. I asked for a side of guacamole and I felt like I was eating a bunch of tomatoes... not a fan of tomatoes. Other than that I would come here again!
name: Dolores

text: I brought (ok, dragged) two of my omni friends here for Philly Vegan Restaurant Week. We had the pre-fixe menu: Caesar salad, penne pasta, deliciously seasoned chimichangas, buffalo wings and chocolate fruit nachos. As a chocolate lover, the dessert was my favorite but everything was amazing IMHO. My friends did not love one course so the owner Joseph discounted the cost of their meals. He was so welcoming and friendly and we all enjoyed our experience there. You should check it out! There will be a second restaurant opening in Fairmount soon.
name: M

text: Food took forever but ended up being better than I expected. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. Kind of landed in the middle for me. For the price I expected more than this. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Nice little spot, decent portions too.
name: User

text: Been here before and was great but this time, horrible service. Walked in and no one bothered to greet us or give us a table. We had to go look for someone and then she looked irritated. She placed us in a dirty table covered in salt and cheese. Sat down for not even a minute and left. Horrible customer service.
name: Tammy

text:
Don't read fake reviews that food is good , if you go to T.G.I. Friday's it's gourmet food compare to this nasty place 
First of all it's old and stinky , $30 chicken and mashed potatoes from the can it's really expensive
Than that have $45 3 course menu that is definitely not worth it 
There are 100's places to eat here go somewhere else 
Best think in this place was glass of water
name: L

text: Food tastes good BUT there are some things that are unacceptable in food industry! Point in case: piece of blue nitrile or latex glove in my chicken katsu. Tonight we went to L&L and I had never been there before. Evidently they were short staffed (1 chef instead of 3?) so our food took nearly an hour from when we initially placed our order. I think that this must be a violation of some sort of food code! The piece of glove was in the middle of the cuts of my chicken katsu meaning that at some point the lone chef had a chunk missing from his glove, which I almost ate! This particular location NEEDS to be under review!
name: Pascal

text:
Attended the soft opening last week because I read that the owner was a previous nominee for a James Beard award and I was so impressed!  Let me just start by noting the decor: this restaurant is so adorable.  Super cute rustic-modern decor, obsessed with the floor tiles, and amazing patio!  It was perfect for the beautifully sunny 70 degree day in Boise after a long day at work.  

It was a soft opening so I will make no judgments on the service; the workers were a little confused on delivering drinks and food to the correct tables, etc. but I am sure that will be smoother now.  This is a counter-service type of restaurant and they bring it out to you at your table.  They have a nice selection of local beers and wine.  

Let's talk about the food, it was delicious!  They are primarily all about the tacos so I tried the potato and chorizo as well as the grilled fish.  The potato and chorizo one was by far my favorite, the fish one needed a little more seasoning in my opinion but also very good.  I also ordered chips and guac, I do feel like it was a little overpriced at $8 for the quantity but it was very tasty. 

Overall affordable, great place to meet a friend for a bite and drink, enjoy some patio weather and ambiance.  I will be back soon Madre!

text: $35.90 for two "endless dinners." Definitely worthy of many return trips for the sushi-- not so much the hibachi, unfortunately. Waiter Brilly G's favorite Hokkaido is now our favorite, too. The Dancing Crab roll, the Crab Rangoon, & the Miso were all worthy. And the service was top notch! Only 3 downers on this visit-- (1) the hibachi meals were oily & much less flavor-packed than at other hibachi establishments, & the accompanying veggies (sadly just broccoli on my plate) were unevenly cut, which meant they were unevenly cooked. (The oily noodles were the worst aspect of the entire meal.) (2) There is no eel on the menu. No eel?!!! None. (3) Also wasn't thrilled w/ the dimly lit dining room (so dark it was difficult to see the person across from me at the four-seater table). I really want to see who I'm eating w/, not have to put the menu up to my nose to read, & be able to check on the cleanliness of my table & surroundings. (It was ridiculously dark.) This all-you-can-eat eatery offers a lunch special; the portions brought to the table are smaller & the price is around $10 per person. Such a great concept-- a full menu w/ many categories & you get to order anything you wish-- any items in any quantities. Just don't leave a lot behind or face an upcharge. text:
We had the beef cheeks, skirt steak, shrimp with garlic sauce, and potato croquettes. 

The beef cheeks was probably the best thing we had all night. It was so tender, my girlfriend did not need a knife to cut it. The slaw added just enough acid to balance out the dish and the tortilla added a nice textural element. 

The skirt steak was a little under (request medium rare, came out rare, but I didn't mind the temp. The side we're good, but was missing a crunch or textural element to the dish. Overall, it was a good dish. 

The shrimp with garlic sauce (Gambas al ajillo) was a delicious starter. The shrimp was perfectly cooked and the crostini soaked up all the sauce and the crust was still crunchy. Definitely would recommend this dish. 

The potato croquette was a typical croquette. Nothing to rave about, but the sauce was a good accompaniment to the dish. 

Overall, great restaurant and good service. I docked one star because I wish they told us the specials like they did for the other tables around us. I know it's a tad petty, but I really wanted some of those specials. Don't let this last part hinder you from going. Still a great restaurant and had a great ambience and atmosphere that fits the Santa Barbara Style.

text:
What a cute place to enjoy a drink and some socialization! They even have a kitchen that serves appetizers and a happy hour that runs until 7 PM. I showed up an hour early for Drag Queen bingo and there was another event going on at that time which was a bit confusing at first. We confirmed with Tyler that bingo would be starting shortly and he showed us to some comfy seats on the couch. On this particular night, they had one waitress and two bartenders working along with whoever was back in the kitchen. The waitress really held it together but I could see some stress on her face as she tried to keep everyone happy that was sitting out on the floor. The place was packed with so many people that several were standing to play bingo on clipboards. It's $10 for 5 sheets of bingo cards (there are 5 rounds) and you can purchase as many as you like. The proceeds from the bingo purchases go towards various non-profits and this month's event was for the Nevada Humane Society. With bingo purchases alone, the event had raised over $700 and the queens were able to round up more donations pushing that amount to several hundred more by the end of the night.

I had read a few reviews and saw pictures of food items before coming and was excited to have some dinner before the festivities began. I was surprised to find that they only offer finger foods and realized I should have done more research before coming.  There just wasn't enough to really fill me up for an actual dinner. At the end of the night, my friend and I had a few drinks each (one on happy hour) and 3 different food items. While it was all tasty and the drinks unique, it was a pretty expensive evening for us. All in all, I will likely come back for events but won't be back for drinks or tapas unless I'm looking to spend a bit more for a special occasion.

text:
I've reviewed this place before and it was mediocre at best due to the service but the food has always been pretty good. I'm reviewing again and after last night, I definitely will not be back. The service was very poor from start to finish. If I could give less than one star, I would.

First- we waited about 25 minutes longer than we were told. We had been told it would be a half hour wait, it ended up being an hour. I inquired twice at the host desk and was told "a few more minutes". Give a realistic wait time so that diners can make a decision as to whether to stay- we would've gone somewhere else.

Second- we had to wait an inordinate amount of time for water. I was incredibly thirsty, we requested water immediately. I couldn't believe how long it took our server to bring water, a food runner brought our appetizer before we got water. We were 5-10 minutes into an appetizer before she finally brought over water. The appetizer also cost $5 more on the check than it did on the menu- a pretty large discrepancy if you ask me.

Third- we requested bread. The bread never came. When our entrees came out, she must've remembered we had asked for bread because she told us she'd bring bread out. That didn't happen. When we were just about done with our meals, she asked us if we still wanted bread. We declined.

Fourth- we asked for tarter sauce and then saw our server go talk with other servers for about ten minutes. Near the end of our meals, she finally brought the tarter sauce.

Fifth- the scallops were over cooked and the food was just ok. Our check was over a hundred dollars and paying that much for terrible service and ok food will stick with me enough that I will never return to this place. I would much rather pay more at Eddie Vs and get great service and great food. It's really shameful that an establishment charges this much and doesn't think more of its clientele.
