text: The food was really delicious...ribs, brisket, Mac and cheese, collard greens and banana pudding.  The ladies working here were super friendly and so welcoming.
name: Angela

text: This place has a very authentic atmosphere and food selection. The owner and workers are all very tentative and make coming to eat at Yummy Pho a great time.
name: Bob

text: It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. No big complaints, just a nice meal. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Worth checking out. Nice little spot, decent portions too. The food was good and the service was easygoing. For the price I expected more than this. No big complaints, just a nice meal.
name: User

text: I was randomly looking for somewhere to eat today and I was in the mood for something new. I got turned around a few times and was hungry and frustrated so I settled on this place. I had never been here before. The staff was very friendly and patient. I ordered chicken noodle soup and a fish sandwich. The soup was delicious, the crackers I got with it were a bit stale but I didn't complain. The sandwich was huge! I couldn't even eat it all lol. My waitress was super on it with bringing drinks which is important to me. I enjoyed it and I'd visit again.
name: Ashley

text: I would like to send a shout out to the cook tonight at Taco Bell.  He helped out in drive thru to get out order correct and hooked us up on all the extras.  I didn't catch his name though. This is actually my favorite Taco Bell.
name: Shannon

text: Not the best place to take someone on the first date, but the food is great. The place needs a little updating. Lamb curry was full of flavors and no gamey taste. The portion was more than enough. My go to place for Indian food.
name: Beibei

text: Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Food was fresh and service was quick. Food was good and came out fast. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait.
name: User

text: I love coming here on nights out dancing. I like the brussels sprouts and potato latke. I have had the wings and they are pretty good too. I really enjoyed the steak frites too but, I think it is over priced for how much I got. I have also ordered the brisket sandwich and it was edible but the brisket wasn't good at all. I'm from TX and we have amazing brisket so, of course I was disappointed. I should have known better though than to expect good brisket up north. In my opinion, this place is super good for late night partying or just appetizers and drinks - not for your main meal.
name: Samantha

text: I've had more than one horrible experience at this Honeygrow, I've been patronizing Honeygrow for years now and in the last few weeks I've been going to this location and twice my order has been incorrect, I have the receipt and twice I've been called a liar by the staff in so many words. Today was probably my last time in Honeygrow, the young ladies are so rude, nasty, they have absolutely no customer service skills and they are unapologetic when they're wrong! I have been humiliated in this restaurant, where I pay my hard earned money (I'm a female working construction in the area and I've wondered if my appearance is a problem but my MONEY is green just like everyone else!) I'm not making things up, I'm not making ridiculous request, I'm just expecting what I ordered and what I paid for. Today the young lady basically accused me of lying about ordering chicken on my salad, she very loudly and very rudely said I didn't order it, I did, she went back looked at the ticket and then said to her coworker "oh yeah she did order chicken" but she NEVER apologized, she made me feel like less of a person with one small gesture because this unfortunately wasn't the first incident. Service skills and being nice goes a long way! And there's nothing wrong with checking twice before making accusations and being loud, wrong, nasty and unpleasant. The experience I had today was unacceptable!
name: S.

text: A server directed us towards the most scrumptious things on the menu! Chicken fingers rolled in hot honey garlic sauce!!! And the buffalo chicken dip is to die for!!! Such a fun st Patty's day
name: Colleen

text: Great authentic Indian food. Friendly family run.  Very nice atmosphere.  BYOB.  Server very attentive and helpful.    We will definitely be back.
name: John

text: Very glad I took the time to eat here. Great ribs, wife had chicken and really happy with our sections at this cool little place. Bake beans were off the wall. Wife had cheese mac and dug into it. Fries were good, sweet tea was good. Skip taco bell and get into some good food here at this place. Hats off!
name: Bruce

text:
Mediocre food but great service from Benny BOO!
Get a cpl of Margaritas..... but Uber home.  They are FAB!!
name: Pegan

text: Staying in Santa Barbara and was excited to see a new restaurant with Vegan options. Oliver's atmosphere and beer/cocktail selection were great but the food didn't live up to expectations. The two of us ordered the Kung Pow cauliflower, Margarita flatbread and Pad Thai. The cauliflower was fantastic but the flatbread tasted like rancid oil. The Pad Thai had nice flavor but was essentially just julienne cut vegetables in a pool of broth. The service was also lackluster with us having to flag down a different server for our check (after our initial server couldn't be found). We truly wanted to like this place but can't recommend it after the meal we had. We were left with much to be desired.
name: Ryan

text:
I'm not normally the type to post reviews haha, but my friends and I were really unsatisfied with our server. I, first, want to say that this review is based solely on the service, not the amazing food! Our waitress, Hillary, was pretty jerky and didn't give the best service. First, my friend asked if there was any type of dairy in your meat sauce because she is severely allergic to dairy. Our server said, "are you gonna, like, die? I don't know. I can't promise you that they won't use the same spoon that they used to stir something with cheese in it. It's a restaurant, you know?" Then, we told her it was our friend's birthday and she said "cool do you want dessert?But I'm not paying for it." I have no idea why she said that, but we all found it really rude. We wanted someone to sing to our friend and no one did and y'all are KNOWN for that!! :(
Later, she said that she was going to give us our checks and take plates from us. We thought she was coming back for the plates after splitting up our checks, but she stood there for a second and rudely said, "uh, you know you have to actually hand me the plates." Maybe she was having a bad day or that's just her personality, but I've never had a server this jerky before. The food was amazing though!! Not my best experience at Buca.
name: Katie

text: Roast pork with 1/2 + 1/2 (that's 1/2 spicy and 1/2 sweet green peppers).  Excellent sandwich.   Next time I'll try something different.
name: Jason

text: Got takeout from here twice now so I feel like I can say a little more. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. The food was good and the service was easygoing. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. You can tell they care about customer experience here. A very pleasant experience. The leftovers held up okay the next day..
name: User

text: I think that each time I order from here, something doesn't sit well in my stomach. One time the breadsticks, another time the lava crunch cakes, but whenever I'm feeling a little off, I remember that I recently came to this location for something. The ambience inside and color on the walls is really hard to stare at, so I recommend never planning to eat in. Workers are all a little distracted and busy chatting amongst themselves, which is probably why it takes twice as long to get any deliveries done.
name: Gloria

text:
I am super excited that there is another cuisine to choose from in the area. My daughter and I enjoyed our visit. The location has plenty of lot parking, easy to find and the restaurant is colorful with a warm feeling.

We started with empanadas and chips with dip. The empanadas were flavorful and cooked perfectly. My daughter had the steak tacos and I enjoyed the chicken enchiladas in red sauce. We both thought the flavors of the dishes were on point and delicious. I loved the horchata served in a mason jar. 

The staff was friendly and welcoming and the restaurant was clean and had ample seating.  We definitely will return.
name: Shawn

text: I don't give a lot of five star reviews but, when it comes to taking care of large (really large) crowds, Dave and Busters is second to none. I came in tonight with a total of 600 high school kids, and they were all fed a very good meal within an hour. The reason for the quick turnaround was that they were also serving about 2000 more kids throughout the night and they did it all with precision and ease. It was the night before the Thanksgiving Day parade and many of the participating marching bands were being fed. A special thank you needs to go to Toni, the manager, and one of the severs, Char, who went above and beyond to cater to several students with food allergies. Y'all were wonderful! Thank you!
name: Sidney

text: Today was my first time visiting The Fish Guy because of the raving reviews and recommendations. We went around 430 on a Wednesday and there were 4 tables ... which included ours ... with one waitress who, unfortunately was not attentive at all. Overall the food was great and the service was less than acceptable.
name: Trinity

text: Peanut butter stout... to die for. Not a huge fan of their IPAs but they have so many options that there is something for everyone. Bartenders are nice. Prices are great.
name: Stephanie

text: Definitely recommend. My husband found this tavern on Yelp. We pulled up and we looked at each other and said "what do you think" I said I'm thinking not. I read the reviews on Yelp and decided to go in. I'm really happy we did!!! It appears to be basic bar food. But read the description of the sandwiches. I had the Patience Wright. It's baked tofu!!  I was so excited!!  I omitted the buttermilk ranch and switched the bread from rustic white bread to rye (they didn't offer whole wheat, no biggie). I am not a vegetarian but started a healthier eating style. Eating out is hard but I live for it!!  The Tavern offers wonderful choices!!! A house salad is the side for all burgers and sandwiches, fries are a substitute for a $2.00 up charge. This was a very nice change as we always pay for a salad. The bartenders, Jessica and Shawn were very attentive and super nice!!!  They use paper straws. Parking is street parking. I definitely recommend this restaurant!!!!
name: Georgianna

text: This place is a gem. Seriously tasty baked goods. We were offered a sample of the Lemon Cooler cake and it was over. We took one home. The employees were very friendly and helpful. My Aunt was right this place is the Best!!! No wonder she would drive from the shore for birthday cake. Try this place. You'll love it!
name: R

text: DON'T place any birthday cake orders here.... the so called BUTTER CREAM ICING is loaded with sugar... the so called BUTTER POUND CAKE is more no BUTTER all POUND. I was TOLD the extra cost for the flowers I asked for made the cake jump to $43 for a 10inch round. highest ever.. the look is plain they don't decorate for the holidays at all. I also signed a paper on how it looked when I picked it up but If I tasted it before hand I would have never ordered it from L&M Bakery.. when I called about it I was told They made all the cakes for that day which didn't make any sense.. I also was told The owners would give me  a call back sadly to say it's been 8 days no call. NO PROFESSIONALISM . WELL NOW I WILL TAKE MY BUSINESS ELSE WHERE. AND PAY IT FORWARD IN TELLING ALL MY FAMILY AND FRIENDS and so on..
name: Edward

text: Had my daughter's college graduation party there last weekend. Very nice upstairs room, quiet, big enough for dozens and room to move around. Very good value. Food was good. We had pasta, meatballs, roast pork, salad and brought in our own snacks like chips and salsa, soft pretzels, cake, etc. Have two kids graduation parties next year, HS and college. We'll be back
name: Francesco

text: This is one of the best vegan meals I've had in a long time. My friend and I split the mac and cheese and an order of the vegan ribs. The owner is very nice and it's in a cool Farmers market. The seitan is made in house and it's tastes great. Would definitely recommend and will definitely go back.
name: j

text:
Absolutely a terrific find. We were lucky enough to sit at the bar and visit with Josh and James. I admire their passion for their city.

BLT's has been open for 8 months and Is bound to be a great success. The food was amazing and the hospitality was incredible.

My friends both had tacos. I couldn't resist the NOLA Shrimp and Grits. They were decadently delicious!

If we go home via St. Louis, we will visit again!
name: Debbie

text: Even though this place has made me mad the last couple times I've gone they have the best burgers in St Pete. the reason I wasn't happy the last couple times I've gone as they did not have enough high chairs for my kids.
name: Hailey

text: Love this sweet place! Friendly atmosphere and they really strive to make your coffee just how you want it.  It's in a strip mall so the location isn't scenic but very clean and has a modern vibe
name: Marcee

text: I love the ambiance that this place gives. I stopped by this place because of the countless reviews of the famous hurricane and it was delicious + inexpensive. It may not taste as strong but it will definitely hit you later. The courtyard is very relaxing and perfect for a drink or two to enjoy the scenery.
name: Cindy

text: So I go through drive thru and the lady sounds very unhappy to be there and is barely listening to what I am ordering. I get to the window and they barely know what is going on. I wait 13 minutes for my order and they barely put any marinara on my chicken parmesan sandwich. I had to use the marinara that came with my cheese sticks so I wouldn't have to eat a dry sandwich.
name: Meggean

text: I took my brother here and it was not good food. I got super sick not long after we ate. The salsa was not mild and the waiter asked if he should bring out tomato paste? wtf I won't be coming back.
name: Sabrina

text: My nephew and I had an awesome time when we stopped in here one sunny afternoon. I really enjoyed the lavender ice cream!
name: Jessica

text: One of those meals where nothing is exactly wrong but you're not excited either. Idk, delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Anyway, nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Service was friendly, just kinda slow once the room filled up. Honestly, everything was tasty and the place felt clean. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it.
name: User

text: The staff were extremely friendly and helpful. The Mary B.E.A.R. was delicious and I would recommend it to anyone. My mother enjoyed the seasonal fritatta and they had good gluten free options for my father. The taller half got the slider and really liked it. Their cibatta buns are so tasty. While not the cheapest place it is definitely worth a visit.
name: Sarah

text: Love this place! Service and food always top notch! Shouts to Gabriella! Hope you get that vacation!
name: Kevin

text: Was visiting family and they wanted to try to place. First thing and most important thing to note is that it is Cash Only. They have an ATM on site with a "small" fee to use it.. I think the sign said it was $1.50; which could be much worse. The seating is somewhat limited inside with more tables outside in front of the storefront. The cheesesteak itself was pretty good. I got it with Wiz and Onions. The only thing was that I thought that the cheesesteak was a little small in size and that the onions were a little chunkier than I would have preferred. I wouldn't say that this would be the first place I would look to go get an authentic Philly cheesesteak; but I wouldn't try to avoid it at all costs. It's kind of a middle of the road kind of place that if you are near Penns Landing and looking for a cheesesteak, it's worth consideration; but would not be my first or second choice.
name: Rob

text: This place was outstanding. Free falafel right when you walked in - absolutely!! The place itself has a Chipotle set-up, which I wasn't expecting, but the food was incredibly fresh and the staff was very friendly. I ended up ordering a spicy gyro with fries -their fries are homemade and super fresh and hot. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for a casual, quick bite to eat minus the greasy-ness of a typical gyro joint!
name: Sabrina

text:
Not impressed! The place smells like a smoke house upon entering so I was excited to try this place. Also reading some of the reviews I thought it'd be better than what it was. Opens at 11am daily and we arrived and placed our order at 11:23am which we were the 1st customers of the day. Thinking it'd be quick service....we'll think again!!! Went here with a group -- I was the 1st in the party to order, I ordered the lunch special which was a pulled pork sandwich with 1 side and a drink which for my side I chose Mac n cheese (again based on other reviews that it was good). Sat at our table and waited for my number to be called for my food to be delivered to the table....I waited and waited and waited some more until everyone at my table was served except for me and my coworker which was on the same ticket as me since I paid for his lunch. 11:43am (20 minutes after I ordered) we asked for a status which the staff came and picked up my receipt and went to the register, came back and told me that he would handle it. 5 minutes passed so asked for a manager. Manager comes and advise that I've yet to get my lunch and so was the birthday boy we were with! He said he'd handle it and apologized. Waited another few minutes and he brought my coworkers food but mine still wasn't there!! Omg. So I asked him where mine was. He said they were probably waiting on my fries to cook. I said I didn't order fries!! And what I ordered others at my table already received. Makes no sense. He went away and came back in another few minutes with mine. Finally got to eat around 12pm!!! Absolutely ridiculous!!!!  The manager came back over, spoke to my coworker asking what type of pie he liked. And brought over 2 pecan pies for the inconvenience. I get that the gesture counts but I won't be back here. Telling others back at the office about this experience and they agreed that service has definitely gone downhill. 

Food quality -- food arrived luke warm....tried my friends collard greens which lacked salt and flavor...pork was just ok. Couldn't even eat my sandwich on the bun since my bun was hard!!! Didn't feel like complaining anymore since they just don't care. 

You failed on several attempts Jazzy's and unfortunately you chose the individual in the party that DOES post reviews!!!!!
name: Brigitte

text: Moonshine testing with Cassidy - she was great!  Joe showed us around the new place - thank you!  Live music, beer, moonshine, food, and a comfortable place to go to.  Indoors & outdoors!  Close to hotels & downtown.  Must see!
name: Debbie

text:
Okay I am pleasantly surprised to have decent Vietnamese food in the suburbs! Granted I do not expect much from Asian restaurants in the suburbs of PA since it is usually very Americanized to cater towards the suburb crowd. 

We went later in the afternoon so there wasn't too many people there.  
Everything was well cooked from our chicken wings appetizer to the lemongrass chicken vermicelli plate.  

The pho was good as well - fairly standard. Nothing remarkable and nothing bad at the same time.

The summer rolls were enjoyed which only had shrimp in then and not shrimp and pork.

Portions are great. 

Parking: free parking lot

Location: on Old York Road in a stand alone building
name: Enjella

text: We can here for brunch during our New Orleans trip.  There was a pretty long wait around 10am even after I had us on the waitlist via yelp.  Since we were able to order drinks at the bar while we wait, it wasn't too bad.  I ordered two different eggs Benedict and the stuffed French toast.  The brisket one was pretty good but the fried chicken one was kinda dry.  My friend thought the fried chicken one tasted freezer burnt but I don't know what freezer burnt taste like.  The stuffed French toast was really good.  I would say it's a pretty average brunch place and the drinks are kinda on the expensive side for brunch.
name: Sandi

text: So so so so delicious. We live out of town but make it a point to stop in anytime we are in Broad Ripple. The menu looks intimidating and it can be a little confusing to order and pay if it's super busy. But I have tried 6 sandwiches and each one has been unique and so delicious. Highly recommend the Neds Gold & Evil Doer. There is something here for everyone. Try it out!
name: Alyssa

text: Hands down some of the best Thai food I've had.  I feel sorry for other Thai restaurants because these guys have raised the bar in my opinion. Some of my favorite grab and go's: Shrimp pad Thai, curry rice with lump crab, and basil peanut rolls
name: Michael

text: Consistent quality food, friendly staff. Reasonable prices.
name: Courtney

text: Had such a great time! Itzel was an amazing server and JV was awesome! Will definitely be returning. :)
name: Whit

text:
Came here for an extravagant steak meal with my work team after hearing about this famous cheese steak. Of course we had to order the cheese steak, served with half a bottle of veuve clicquot for $120. We had this cut into fourths as an appetizer before diving into our tomahawk steak. 

The wagyu cheese steak was good, but way too rich. Foie gras, wagyu, truffled cheese whiz-- it was pretty much dripping with fat and oil. That said it was still tasty (the others at the table loved it) and I'm glad we could say we tried it. The tomahawk was juicy and cooked to perfection, and service was top notch. All in all, a lovely evening. Definitely one of the more memorable steakhouse experiences.
name: Priyanka

text: 5 stars for the service. Our waitress was fast, friendly and funny. Thee best hash browns I have EVER had! I had the eggs Benedict and unfortunately my eggs were overcooked, but it was still good. Not a big juice drinker, but on vacation so figured why not, it was amazing tasted fresh to me. Hubby didn't really care for the French toast was kind of dry and tasteless. Whatever you get make sure to order the hash browns:)
name: Kara

text: The shrimp po boy sub is unreal and really good but the portions are rather skimpy and bare. They gave me three French fries with my 4 inch sub I left hungry and a bit disappointed. People need to eat this isn't Africa
name: Anthony

text:
Awesome experience! 

Originally told 1 hr wait which was fine because we cruised around the wharf area and local shops. 35 minutes later we received a text our table was ready. We arrived and were seated promptly and Kacie arrived to take our drink order. She quickly recommended some favorite beers and starters and whisked away to fill our alcohol needs. When she returned she took our order and advised us on her thoughts in which she was spot on. The food was amazing as well as the beers and we will definitely return and refer friends as well!


Thanks again Kacie and team!!!!
name: Matt

text: Love this little gem. There are not a lot of these healthy grocery stores in Nashville. Only one Traders and Whole Foods thats where I usually go. So I was very excited to check this place out! Lots of healthy food and local love that! Only stopped here once and was able to pick up some good thing! Like local pasture eggs and grassfeed beef bones for bone broth.  Will be coming back here for sure!
name: Amanda

text:
Great cheesesteak stop! All the people working were super nice and everything seemed very fresh. The pizza didn't look great but it's not New York!

We got a few different cheesesteaks including the buffalo chicken one, and all were great. They have a window to watch the steaks cooking and everything looked fresh and the kitchen was super clean. The buffalo sauce wasn't very spicy, but we were able to add jalapeños onto it, which they had complementary on the side with pickles!!

One downside is that they won't give out water cups, which kinda stinks when eating a cheesesteak.
name: Alyssamarie

text: Great food and awesome experience! The food is very vegetarian friendly and the wait staff is great. Nice atmosphere as well:) the restina wine was amazing
name: Mandy

text:
I was actually really excited to go here, as I have literally been eyeing it as a go-to place before a show at Fox or Powell. But I was really disappointed. The burger tasted like it had been cooked an hour before. My duck was overdone, but evidently that was normal since it was smoked...um.....
They ended up replacing both of our entrees with a pasta, which was okay but overpriced.
 Server was really nice, but when two out of two entrees are not great, and the replacement entree was just "acceptable", I can't say I'll go back.
name: Christina

text: First time here at Seasons 52. They were busy and we didn't make reservations, so we ate at the bar. It was still very nice and great food. Our server was prompt, attentive and pleasant. I recommend giving them a try, we'll certainly be back!
name: Bob

text: Awesome coffee at Coffeebar!  We ordered both a dry and a wet almond milk cappuccino, the dry cap was actually dry with great foam and the wet  cap had great foam too, nicely packed, light crust on top, simply awesome!  Counter staff and Barista were both friendly, service was quick, and the place has a great vibe.  Parking is so-so, price was great!  The food was also awesome.  Our second time back we tried the avocado toast which was very good - could have used a little bit thinner slice of bread, but the taste was very good, I would recommend it.  We also tried the veggie breakfast burrito which also had great flavor.  We didn't care for the sriracha aioli that came with the burrito as the flavor kind of overpowered everything else in the burrito but fortunately, it comes on the side so we were able to discard it.  I would highly recommend this place!
name: Wayne

text: The falafels were on point! Definitely took me back to a tiny middle eastern experience. The chicken shawarma tasted exactly like one I had in Dubai!! Middle eastern food has not translated well in the US and I have tried other places but glad that this shop is close by and brings good middle eastern flavors back to life!
name: Charles

text: Best Stromboli Nd garlic knots around!!!  The sauce is so full of flavor and awesome cheese!  I won't order pizza or Stromboli from any place else!  Friendly staff too!
name: Nancy

text:
Girlfriend and I stopped in for lunch on a roadtrip. Who do I talk to about opening up in Houston? 

Lemon pepper wings were so lemoney and peppery and crispy in all the best ways.
Bread pudding is a must. We tried the white chocolate almond and I'm sure the berry one is just as delicious but girlfriend said I wouldn't finish a second one.. I still think I could have.
The crack fries were good but we we're so full from all the delicious food we couldn't finish them

Bulgogi banh mi is what's up too! I'd have one for lunch everyday. 

Staff was really friendly and work hard to make sure customers are happy. Really attentive and helpful even when super busy! 
 Hope you see this spot in Houston one day
name: Gustavo

text:
Just as good as their place on Monroe and 4th in Nashville.
Only issue we had: pizza was not sliced completely and had to use a knife to separate the pizza slices.
Other than that, we will be back!
Had the pie been sliced all the way thru, I would have given it 5 stars!
name: Fred

text: Aki Sushi is one small gem found in the middle of Oldsmar. Sushi is amazingly fresh, service is always on point. Lunch took a little longer than usual today as they have new owners but the food was delicious. Reasonable lunch specials, I got the 1 specialty roll and 1 classic with miso soup for $15.95. They have happy hour specials from 5-7pm which changed from what they had before of 4-6pm.
name: Angiesaurus

text: Deke's use to be my favorite go to for wings, but something is not right about the quality of their poultry lately.  The last two orders were wings with thick, rubbery skin.  I will stick with their brisket from now on.
name: Karen

text: Always a fan! This place may be a chain but it is a great chain! I love the fact I can add little sides for $1.50 and be super full AND have leftovers after. I have traditionally only gotten the penne rosa with feta cheese for nearly fifteen years, but I tried the pesto cavatappi and it'll be hard for me to choose next time! I don't think that I have had anything here that I do not like. It is filling and does not hurt my wallet.
name: Amanda

text: I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Food was fresh and service was quick. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish.
name: User

text:
Food: Good but overpriced.

Drinks: Intriguing, but not unprecedented or unique.

Atmosphere: Unremarkable. If you went to Bourbon Street it hasn't really changed, but the menu and pricing is a stretch for the environs.

Service: Weird. Tables are shared by all the waitstaff, so everyone is constantly checking on you and has no idea if you have more food coming out, so they always ask you.

Overall: There are better options for cocktails, Asian food, and cigar bars. If you want all three at once, go here. Otherwise, roll on.
name: Robby

text: Love it! Food is good! Service is quick :) my husband isnt much of a seafood eater but there are plenty of things on the menu to make him happy and plenty more for sushi-eating me! And both our kids are under 5 and eat for free.
name: Kat

text: Definitely a good place to hang out for drinks and to munch on some food and shared plates. A little pricey for the portions, but I feel as if they use good quality food. LOVE, LOVE the cheesesteak eggrolls!!! Some of the best I've ever had. Not huge portions for the eggrolls (I believe you get 4 halves for about $12), but worth it for sure. They brew their own beers there which is a great selling point for me because I love trying new beers, especially from a local place. My favorite spot in the restaurant to dine is upstairs on the outside deck. It overlooks the water and you can also people watch. Upstairs inside bar can get a little rowdy for happy hour, which I don't mind at all. I believe the downstairs dining is a little more chilled out. The place can get pretty crowded, which to me says something good about the restaurant. Worth a try if you've never been.
name: Stella

text: I have eaten here almost every trip to Nashville.  They have fantastic service and great staff. The food is very good at a reasonable price. The reason I am giving a 3 star rating is that the lime with a vodka tonic looks like it was cut a week ago. I brought it to the attention of the waitress and she replied you should have seen the first one I grabbed. Personally I would not have let this drop but my wife would not allow my to fully voice my opinion.
name: Louie

text:
Arrived at 10:50 on a Sunday morning. Waited for 50 minutes to get seated after being told to expect a 5-10 minute wait. When we were finally seated it was upstairs in the outside covered porch. Mind you it's a chilly 45 degrees today. We sat at a metal table and on metal chairs with NO heat. It was absolutely unbearable and none of the staff or management even cared. All four of the tables outside were upset and repeatedly asked for the heat to be turned on....only to be ignored. 

The service was spotty at best. One of our party ordered a tuna melt and the server said "this comes with chips. Do you want fries instead?" He requested chips but when the meal came out without chips, the girl said that was the only sandwich that doesn't come with anything. Again no care that they gave wrong info and no effort to make it right. Otherwise the food as always was excellent. 

This establishment just can't handle a party of more than 4. And making your patrons sit in a freezing cold room is outright unacceptable. Long wait time, freezing atmosphere and management not making things right garners them 2 stars.

Something to compensate her for the shower she received.  To our surprise the bill came and no discount, no free dessert, there was nothing.  While I know that there was no "fault" , it still was an inconvenience caused by their restaurant.  I'm disappointed in the manager for not acknowledging my sister's discomfort.  

It makes me think twice about dining here.  Because we didn't raise a stink they just let the situation drop.  It's pretty sad when people are nice about a bad situation and then completely ignored.

text:
The Refinery- Tampa, Florida- 2.75- Stars

If you live anywhere in the state of Florida or read any of the following publications:  Zagat, Southern Living, Conde Nast, Forbes, Esquire, USA Today, New York Magazine, etc. you have heard of The Refinery and the man in the kitchen, Executive Chef/Proprietor Greg Baker.  Boasting 4 straight semi-finals in the Best Chef category by the renowned James Beard Foundation as well as a semi-final showing for Best New Restaurant of 2011, it's hard to ignore his accomplishments.  I have had exquisite meals all over this country and as any loyal reader knows, several in the state of Florida, to say I was looking forward to sampling Greg's wares would be an understatement of the most egregious kind.

Not wanting to leave anything out, I wanted a good sampling from the menu and as such started with something off of their ambitious cocktail menu.  I ordered their take on one of my favorite drinks, the Old Fashiond.  Sadly, they were out of my first choice, so I went with a Camus Cognac Demonde Old Fashioned.  This was a wonderful take on an ole standard and I thoroughly enjoyed the flavor, however, It was a very light pour (straight 1 oz.) and while cost usually doesn't concern me or play a factor in my reviews, that is a profit of $323/bottle of Scotch.  I understand that most of the profit in running any eating establishment is found in the beverages, that seems a tad excessive to me.  Sipping my cocktail I asked my delightful server, Chelsea, if I might have an order of Hominy Stew, Fried Chicken Biscuit, Meat Sweets and the Buffalo Sweet Breads.

Beginning with my soup (stew) I was pleasantly taken in by this bold take on the common fare, talk about layered, complex flavors!  It really hits the mark.  The stew was extravagant in its flavoring and beautiful in its presentation, the freshly chopped chives sprinkled on top lent an air of ascetics to the looks while adding a nice finishing note to the dish.

Moving on to the Fried Chicken Biscuit sandwich.  I don't know what to say here, the biscuit was so hard as to be inedible and the pickle was depressingly flaccid.  The chicken breast itself was dipped in a what I can only surmise to be a hush puppy like batter and then fried.  Steeeeeeeeerike!  You're out!

I was hoping the next sammich to be tasted was exponentially better or I would soon find myself seeing a Dentist for a chipped or broken tooth.  The Meat Sweets was an amazing conglomeration of meats wedged into the cheapest bun known to mankind.  I don't know what was going on here, but the bun was bland (think flour and water).  The meat seasoning was uneven and lacking flavor. The Yukon Gold fries were fresh cut, fried to perfection and a delight on the palate, I love good fries and these were exceptional.

This brings us to the final item in my order, the Buffalo Sweet Breads.  I was expecting something similar to the Buffalo Sweet Breads I sampled at Crush XI and I was not disappointed.  The sauce was exceptional containing a wonderful mix of garlic, butter and spice and the sweetbreads were cooked to perfection having just the right texture and not chewy at all.  I mention this as it is hard to find properly cooked sweetbreads.  They are not supposed to be chewy, but should divinely melt in your mouth with the gentlest of bites as these most certainly did.  They certainly beat the stuffing out of Buffalo Style Chicken Wings, that's for darn sure!

All in all, it was an O.K. dining experience and not one I was expecting in the least.  I found the drinks to be excessively overpriced for the pour (make it cry, baby, make it cry) and the food, while ingenious in flavor combinations, to come off as average.  I don't know if Greg gave up, he was off that night, or it was just a bad day.  Whatever the case, I was assuredly let down.

Big Boy says, "Pass by The Refinery, there is much better food in Tampa." #iamthebigboy #bigboydiningout
name: Todd

text:
Where do you take a discerning (picky) non-gluten eating aunt who hails from Los Angeles when she comes to visit? Answer: Craft Kafe. This Kafe (Greek short for "Kafenio", a homage to the owner's heritage) is on point. 

Everything on the menu is sans Gluten and pretty delicious. There are a variety of teas, coffees, salads, sandwiches, soups, quiche, omelettes, and other assorted baked goods. As a non-coffee drinker due to reasons I cannot currently control I cannot comment on their divine smelling coffee except to say that they have some fancy coffees, a Kyoto Drip and a Cold Brew offering also. As a gluten eater and lover I don't miss any while dining here not do you even notice that the stuff is Gluten Free--its just delicious. 

On the many occasions I have been I am a fan of their Vegan Burger (be forewarned that the bread roll it is served on is a but more substantial than other GF bread you may have had before but I love it because its filling and hearty. The quiches, the soups, the pizza slices including their great tasting Vegan Pizza slice, and their other baked goods DO NOT disappoint. They have a phenomenal chocolate coconut dessert and the Galaxy Bars are delectable (and vegan) if that is your thing and even if not-try it! 

Its an order-at-the-counter-and-your-food-is-delivered-to-you type of establishment or you can order ahead and pick up. For the holidays you can place advanced pie of baked good orders. The staff is always welcoming, friendly, and always able to field any questions or provide assistance as necessary. The cafe has nice decor and a front wall of windows which lends natural light. There is also a water dispenser with glass drinking jars or clear plastic cups for you to use as well as real flatware in addition to plastic (if you need to grab to go). 

This Craft Kafe location is nestled next to a restaurant and a health food store in a store plaza in a convenient location. The parking lot has a good amount of angled parking. Craft Kafe has opened a second location in downtown St. Pete which I have yet to visit but hear is very successful. I will continue to patronize this glorious place.
name: Tina

text:
We went to Mercer's this weekend and had a great experience. 

Mercers is located in the ICE district making it convenient to stop by for a drink before a concert at Rogers or to go out for a night of dancing!

When we arrived at Mercer's, there was a bit of a line. However, the line moved quickly and the bouncers were really friendly. 

In terms of value for money, I would say it's slightly below average. A shot of Burt Reynolds on a Saturday night was $7. This is a bit pricey as most competitors down the street have the same shot on happy hour all night for $4. 

Although I didn't order food, I would still say the service was great! The bartenders were friendly and quick to take orders. They also hand you all of your change instead of holding your change over the tip jar which was a nice surprise. 

The music, the good vibes and the people were deadly! Mercers is definitely a gem in the city and I will be returning.

text:
What else can you say about a place with almost 4000 reviews and four-and-a-half stars?  The food is good, the history shows and it's cool, but the service is impeccable. Seriously. You can get good gumbo and pecan pie in other places. But it's hard to find the kind of service that makes you feel like you are the only person in the dining room. 

The food is creative (king cake beignets, shrimp and tasso Henican, a sweet onion tart, bread pudding soufflé) and it is very good. There were a couple of small mis-steps (one of my poached eggs on the couchon de lait eggs benedict was over cooked - hard yolk - and the crust on the pecan pie was really tough - I gave up trying to cut through it with my spoon and just ate the filling and pecans), but overall everything we ate was very good. 

Definitely a place to go if you like visiting icons of history, and if you like top notch service.

text:
Had a great time at this little Pizza place recently with my family. It is a very interesting setup and I am grateful to my fellow Yelpers for giving it a shout out. BYOB situation helps tremendously. The wait staff was great! We had zero issues despite of some reviews. Our waiter was super prompt and cool. Pizzas came out in minutes. Almost to the point where it was too fast. Like 2.5 minutes after order!
I thought the menu was not overbearing, with only a handful of pies in both red and white and a few salads. The pizza is very much in Neapolitan style and is different that your average pizza joint. Is it a real deal - no - let's face it, it's hard to reproduce the original. Especially after trying at THE original, first pizza shop in Naples. 
Dough - soft and has a nice texture and char form the wood fired oven, but lacks any sort of crispiness. It was so floppy, it was impossible to eat  without fork and knife. Which is totally fine but I found it almost too mushy in certain places. Also, was hard to mange for kids.
Sauce - perfection! We tried both with the sauce and bainca and both were delicious. 
Toppings were hit or miss. We had pepperoni and sausage, both were delicious. The pizza with an egg, was also very yummy. But the funghi (mushroom) one, we were surprised to find raw mushrooms that gave out a lot of water and made the pizza even soggier. Maybe they should be pre-cooked ahead? 
The price - is not cheap -but would be worth for good pizza. Would definitely come back!

text: The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Worth checking out. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly.

text: Five star reviews are special and reserved for places that epitomize good food. That a take-out establishment could exceed any expectations regarding the palette experience serving superior food that is local, vibrant, and delicious places them in this five star category. text:
My boyfriend introduced me to Planet Sub in Chandler when we were visiting his parents. I had no idea they were opening one here in Tucson until I saw a Groupon for the place. I bought three of them! My boyfriend likes the meatball grinder and the beefeater. I have always ordered the green turkey; it has turkey, bacon, tomatoes, cream cheese, sprouts, salsa, and guacamole. The subs are served on house-made wheat bread, which is soft and fresh-tasting. You can also order your sandwich on gluten-free bread or in a tortilla or lettuce wrap. This would be a great place for people with dietary restrictions, and they have a good selection of vegetarian options as well.

A half-size of any sandwich is plenty for me, or I will order a full size and save half of it for later. I'd expect to pay about $10-12 per person, depending on if you get a side or a drink. I just ordered the sandwich and got water, but they have bottled drinks as well as a Coke Freestyle machine. They offer chips, cookies, and pickles for sides. I read they also have soup on the menu, which changes daily, but I didn't take notice of it on my visit.

There were two guys working when I was in. They were both very friendly, and the place was clean.

text:
First impressions:
- Lovely interior...and I'm going to sound like a snob, but seriously, why would you wear a hoodie sweatshirt to eat here? I just don't understand how casually some of our fellow diners were dressed. I don't personally take offense, but it seems rude to the people who work here and run the place. I dunno. It's NOLA. I know, I know.
- They surprised us with a free round of champagne because I'd noted on the reservation that we were celebrating a special occasion. Still, I certainly hadn't expected anything quite so nice. It set things off on a really good note.

Food:
- Since I have a shellfish allergy, we did the ricotta dumplings for our appetizer. They were delicious but nothing to write home about in my opinion.
- I had the duck confit for my appetizer, which was fantastic. There were a few bites of crispy, oil-laden duck skin that particularly blew my mind. It paired nicely with the deliciously seasoned lentils, and I was able to avoid the fingerling potatoes strewn about the lentils that did absolutely nothing for the dish.
- My husband had the pan-fried pork chops, which he enjoyed. "It was like a cross between a more tender chicken-fried steak and a German schnitzel, and had a really good sauce," he said specifically. I concur, based on the bite or two I had.
- Because the service was quite slow, they unexpectedly (we hadn't even complained!) brought us a free side of the chilled roasted beets, which were delicious if not very inventive. I've had this same dish a million times at other restaurants.
- For dessert, we had the chocolate peanut butter bar, which was delicious. The smoked mascarpone ice cream was a particular standout. Give me some of this in a bucket and just let me bury my face in it, please.

Drinks:
- Free champagne to start, as noted above, was nice!
- I had a glass of the Paraduxx 2013 red blend, which was perhaps the best red wine I've ever had. (I'm a cheap wine drinker, so this glass was a splurge for me, and worth every penny. But then again, I'm a cheap wine drinker, so consider the source.)
- My husband had the Blood Oath and the 100 Years Cocktail. He thought they both were the best cocktails he had of our entire trip.
- The Feist 10-year port was phenomenal. My husband started hunting for this everywhere we went. Haha.

Service:
- As noted, service was quite slow. We were there late (8:30 pm) on a Sunday evening, and they seemed understaffed. It didn't bother us, especially since they were so nice about it. This is the sort of place where you go for a relaxed, lovely, leisurely dinner...so it was fine. But I appreciated their concern and approach to customer service of apologizing before anyone even complains (not that we were going to).
- The one rough spot in the evening, in my opinion, was that our server said she'd only been working there 5 days, and she wasn't able to give any opinions about items on the menu. I found it a bit frustrating when she didn't even offer to get someone who might be able to answer our questions for us -- not even consulting with the bar when I asked specific questions about their wines by the glass. Still, she was new, and I have to cut her some slack. She was very sweet and clearly was trying her best on a night when they appeared to be understaffed.
- Service was appropriately attentive when we needed them and left us alone when we didn't.

Overall:
- A lovely evening, delicious food, and drinks were a standout.
- Great for a nice-but-not-stuffy occasion.
name: Anne

text:
Found this place on yelp while looking for suggestions for gluten-free options. Was not disappointed. They have one spot out from for EV Parking with a charger. Just a few other spots to park in the front so not much. 

Nice and spacious on the inside with bright colors and a good amount of seating including a bar area. The ambiance was nice and brights as well. When you walk in your automatically standing in front of the ordering area. They have some pre-made drinks such as Lemonade and Tea you can get and fountain sodas off to the side (alcoholic beverage as well).

The servers were nice and food only took about 10min to come out. There are many food and drink options to choose from. All the ingredients are few and healthy. They offer gluten-free, vegetarian etc, The meals tasted great especially the Chili. The salsa was excellent and you can order mild medium or hot. 

They play some relaxing upbeat popular music and it's pound enough to enjoy but not too loud where you can't enjoy a conversation. This is a family friendly environment to.

I definitely recommend this place and will return.

text: Great food. Everything was delicious especially the monkey bread. The waitstaff was very prompt and attentive even though the restaurant was packed. Would definitely eat there again.
name: Myron

text:
I know that the concept of Southgate is Korean with an American style, but to be honest I'd say it's the other way around. I felt like I was eating mostly American food influenced by Korean cuisine.  For an appetizer, I ordered the octopus and dduk skewers (unfortunately gobbled it down before getting a picture) but you should know that there were only two pieces and there was only one piece of the octopus confit on each skewer (which was the best part).  The dduk was a little tough - there's a way to cook dduk crispy on the outside and soft on the inside which is what they were going for and did an ok job of.

The galbi we ordered was really good, but again I really wouldn't have called it galbi.  If you served this to me and I didn't know what the dish was called or where it came from, I would've never suspected it to be Korean.  That being said though, it was really good though just judging it based on its stand alone quality. The meat was really tender and the marinade was delicious, but again I just had to laugh a little at how it was supposed to be remotely Korean.

I also got a beef dolsot bibimbap, and it was really good but also bibimbap is low key one of those things you can't really mess up.  I wish they put a little more of a finishing sesame oil drizzle and more spicy gochujang but overall it was satisfying.

I also ordered a soju flight (they house infuse their sojus) and they were all pretty pleasant and worth a try if you've never had soju before. It's a very impressionable spirit and takes on the flavor of whatever is in it easily, so it may feel a little like drinking juice but the flavor combos were interesting and my partner and I did enjoy them.

Service was great, and because of the lovely weather we asked to be seated outside and were able to, so I didn't see much of the interior space. 

I think just all in all, it truly was a three and a half to a four star restaurant experience because it's not that the food wasn't good - I just think if you are craving Korean, skip this place. 

Another little tip: don't get the kimchi it was foul.  Also a little miffed they charged for banchan - I know the concept again is "Korean American" but I think you'd enjoy just sitting at a fully Korean restaurant and getting your free (and way better quality) banchan experience there with your meal.
name: Grace

text: The crespelles and the hickory burger are great, I'd give the food 5 stars but due to the the service quality which is heartbreakingly subpar Hickory Lane gets 3.5 stars.  We had to go up the server multiple times to get their attention and get our own utensils.  The place is in a great area, right off the corner of Fairmount near the penitentiary.  I'd still recommend giving it a try

text: This particular location isn't what its hyped up to be. The food wasn't as good as the original Graze location, and the entire soda fountain seemed to be serving the sodas flat without anyone even noticing or caring for that matter. Won't be coming back here because I have higher expectations for the price you pay for this food.

text: Came all the way from California for the Eagles and stopped here on the way! This is easiest the best food we have had on our trip! The fig & gorgonzola bruschetta melted in my mouth. name: User

text:
Been eating Portillo's for over 30 years so as a newbie to Indy (last 10 years) I was very excited that we were getting one. Since I have eaten Portillo's probably hundreds of times in the Chicago area I feel it is my duty to clue you in. This one is not quite the same. The workers are slow. They just don't get it. Portillo's have excited workers who hustle to get your order right, to make your food fresh, to call your order in a unique way. Not here. I have had my second set of cold fries from Portillo's in the last 2 months from the Fishers location. I had never in the previous 30 years gotten a cold fry. I had a mistake one one of my orders. That has NEVER happened. As I sit here typing, inside of Portillo's Fishers, I've been waiting on my order for over 15 mins. It should have been up 5 mins ago. It's not busy. Everyone is waiting. This is not good. 

My 2 stars is for the taste of the food. But if Portillo's plans on branching out, they MUST get that perfect system down. The one we so love in Chicago. Because this is looking a lot like McDonald's right now. 

Unimpressed 

EDIT: After I received my order it was incorrect. My beef and cheddar croissant didn't have the hot peppers I ordered. It also tasted horrible, almost slimy. I didn't ask for fries, they were there. I looked at my receipt, sure enough I was charged for them. I wanted a large iced tea, I was charged for a regular sized one. I didn't complain. I just ate through what I could bare and left. 

Horrible in each and every way. Had that been the first time I've visited a Portillo's, I would never return. I don't think I can handle Portillo's Fishers. I'm taking away a star.
name: Lady

text: I received TERRIBLE service today. I always tip, but for the first time ever tipping was not an option. The waiter was utterly RUDE and had the smartest mouth ever. Today was certainly my last day at this establishment and I will not be returning. I have never experienced service this bad.

text: Stopped here for dinner. The place is nicely decorated and has a good vibe. We ordered drinks and our food and we waited. We waited and waited and waited and waited. After about 20 minutes, I asked the status and the bartender (since we were sitting at the bar) said it would be right up. We wait for another 5 minutes and ask again and she said she will go check. She made about 5-6 drinks after telling us this and then I think asked a server to go check. Mind you, the place isn't that crowded. At least a third of the tables in the front were empty. She never gave us an update so I asked again. Again, her response was it takes awhile to cook the hamburger well done. I said, it doesn't take 30 minutes. After seeing someone who was seated at the bar 10 minutes after us get their food, a manager finally shows up and says their was a mix up and our food is being plated. So after about 40 minutes or more we get our food. The food wasn't half bad but the service was terrible. The manager did us a "favor" and knocked 25% off our food bill. Thanks a lot!  As we got the bill and her tip was in jeopardy, the bartender was making up every excuse why it wasn't her fault and it was the kitchen. Way to be a team player!

text:
Soooooooo, all the rave of this new Chinese little hole in the wall. Used to be China diner, oh the memories I've had there as a young adult drinking downtown and stumbling in to get some fast Chinese food. But now they've made it into a nice little Chinese restaurant, still with late hours but not as late, which is fine. 

This is my second time coming in and I just feel like it's the typical sweet same sauced Chinese food. Although, I was listening to a side convo and heard about a special authentic Chinese menu that I would have tried but I didn't know about. 

They just printed it this week from when they've been open for about 2 months now. But I will be back to try this secret, only 2 prints authentic menu. And I will update my review. 

The staff is pleasant, the cook which is the owner is very nice. Comes out occasionally to make sure everything is good. 

The duck is awesome, but for a cheaper price I can get more at other establishments. The potstickers are very plump filled with meat and the wrapper is thin and very tasty. 

The five spice calamari and pork is probably my favorite. No sauce so none of the sweet sauce that I'm not much of a fan of. Eggplant is very fresh but in the same sweet sauce that I'm just not to excited about. But hey they are accommodating to the pallet of their customers that come in. So when they have been asked to do authentic they did and that's why they are trying the special menu out for a bit. I wish they would advertise it more though, but I gotta give them some time since they just printed it this week.
name: Jeana

text: Food was good and came out fast. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.
