text: I've normally have been going to Central Po'boy but it was too packed so we tried here on this particular day we went in and I tell you I was not in any way disappointed! I got  an extra large shrimp po boy and the shrimp were huge and they were absolutely cooked just perfect! And Ms.  Brenda was just as sweet and accommodating as she could be, the lady that took my order, and she was nice enough to give me some gravy so I can make some debris fries and that gravy was just scrumptious! I will definitely be coming back here soon as possible to try more items!
name: Janet

text:
This is a bummer because I've ordered from Urban Cookhouse multiple times before and today was considerably awful. (Ordered through doordash). 

Ordered two White BBQ Chicken Sandwiches with sides of rice pilaf. Ordered an additional bottle of BBQ sauce. Got refunded for the bottle of sauce, as they didn't have any on hand, which was fine. But we did NOT receive White BBQ Chicken Sandwiches. 

We got some dry grilled chicken tenders, cut in half, and placed on soggy hoagie rolls with limp strips of bacon. No bbq sauce. None, no sauce whatsoever. The rice pilaf was ice cold. 

I called to request a refund and was told I could only be refunded for one sandwich because the wait time we had was the driver's fault. Sure I get that, but it wasn't the driver's fault that the sandwiches weren't good at all. We didn't end up eating the food at all, it got tossed and we ordered Jimmy Johns. 

Really, really disappointed. Only gave an extra star because if you do eat on site, it isn't horrible.
name: Emily

text: The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. It was crowded but still moved along. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. Price felt a touch high for what it was. No big complaints, just a nice meal. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon.
name: User

text: Great spot! I got the teriyaki tofu bahn mi and the Billie jean matcha tea and coconut milk drink. I loved that the drink wasn't overly sweetened, so you could actually taste the matcha. But I guess I should've thought ahead because the teriyaki tofu was almost too sweet for me. But regardless, tofu was cooked to perfection, bread was amazingly soft on the inside while crunchy on the outside (the perfect bahn mi roll) and service was friendly and quick! I just wish they had boba! And I'm sure as time goes on they'll get more tofu options. I'll definitely be back.
name: Chloe

text: Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. No big complaints, just a nice meal. You can tell they care about customer experience here. Would return. Food was good and came out fast. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really.
name: User

text:
This place is below average. 
I walked in and was made to look like an idiot for asking if I should sit anywhere or if I should wait to be seated. 
The service is less then enthusiastic.  There was one girl with a tattoo on her arm who was very helpful but she wasn't even my waitress but took my order becasue mine was no where.  THen I watched as as I waited  for my bill my waitress Just stand and chat with another girl and I had to walk up to pay.  
The busser was friendly.  
Food was nothing to right home about.  I probably won't bother coming back with so many other alternatives where I feel welcomed and am treated well.
name: Cindy

text: I get the appeal, I just don't totally share it. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. I'd maybe go back, but I'd order differently next time. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable.
name: User

text:
Found this gem on Happy Cow app while passing through SB on a Wednesday night. It's a couple miles off the freeway, but not hard to find. Nice, rustic atmosphere and has table service. Good-sized patio with heaters, plenty of indoor seating, and even room for a large party (which we couldn't hear in the other room).

Almost everything on the menu is vegan, and we all had a hard time choosing. In the end, I went with the chlorella risotto. As expected, it's green! And rich. I couldn't eat it all. We also had the grilled cheese, which is chock full of other things, like a poblano chili, tahini, and more. My son had the burger and said it was incredible. I tried a bite and it was seriously good. 

I couldn't resist the baklava for dessert. Vegan baklava!! It comes with three scoops of delicious vanilla "ice cream."

Service was incredibly fast and friendly. Prices are a little on the high end, but not too out there for a vegetarian restaurant.
name: GM

text: We visited this morning for breakfast.  The meal arrived slightly warmer than room temperature.  We sent it back and they brought their second attempt which was also cold.  My eggs were not cooked to order and the biscuit appeared to have been purchased at Sam's.  I was really hungry, so if anything had been slightly tolerable, I would have probably eaten it, but that disgraceful biscuit was a decisive "NO."
name: Cathy

text:
First visit. Service was attentive and quick. Very good margaritas with an extensive tequila menu. Salsa was fresh and queso blanco was as expected. 
The enchiladas had pieces of grilled moist chicken breast, a step above the shredded meat at most places. The beans were flavorful which is a measure of a good spot! Definitely will be back.
name: Paul

text: Good wine and beer selection. We thought the brussel sprout appetizer was pretty dry though it tasted pretty good. My daughter's pasta dinner was tasteless. My steak frites was medium, not as ordered medium rare. It is a kabob which was not obvious on the menu. The barbeque chicken sandwich was pretty plain and not very good. They ran out of Coke at 6:30, ran out of the Grouper special at 6:45 and out of steak at 6:50. Overall not very good. The service was good.
name: Paul

text: Finally! An excellent street taco in St. Petersburg! This is the real deal, authentic street tacos not the American version, although they do offer those as well. Steak and chicken were flavorful with chopped onions and cilantro. The Verde sauce was tasty but with a nice heat. $1.99 per taco is a bargain. I'll eat here weekly.
name: Martin

text:
The hubby and I are authentic Mexican tacos lovers and connoisseurs. So when the hubby spotted this place while driving by we knew we had to make a stop at some point in our trip. This place is not fancy by any stretch. It is located inside the convenience store of what very obviously was once a gas station. Service is on par with the establishment. Again nothing fancy but authentic. Tacos are delicious. We started out with 6 (3 each) and ended up ordering 5 more.

The ONLY criticism for us is the Al Pastor tacos do not have pineapple and are not made in a "trompo" (rotisserie). The taste is delicious none the less.
name: Valeria

text:
We went as a party of 4 after a convention concluded. It's very convenient; easy walking distance from the convention center and nearby hotels. 
3/4 of us arrived early and had drinks at the bar which they offered to move the tab to our table. That is a nice touch and seen too infrequently. The drinks were just right. 
We started with mojillas as an appetizer; man, I love a grilled pancreas. Delicious. We all ordered the special which was an off-menu steak and I can't recall the cut. LaBoca had 4 for the night...gone. We asked them to be cooked Pittsburgh/rare (x1) and Pittsburgh/medium rare (x3). They nailed it, as they always have. Asparagus and brussel sprouts were ok. Sprouts were fried which surprised me. 
For dessert, our table ordered the "digestif flight"...that's what it is. It's the best deal in town...shhh!
Looking forward to the next opportunity to enjoy LaBoca!
name: Zane

text:
This was my wife and I's first introduction to New Orleans and the food.We started we a Jambalaya and two crawfish dishes. We got the Crawfish Beginets, and Crawfish Pie.

 The Jambalaya has just enough heat that give your mouth that bit of tingle and also a building burn if you like that sort of sensation. Its pretty simple it kinda looks like a sausage and chicken fried rice but with spice, but the flavour is there. 

The Crawfish Pie didn't had more bits of crawfish than the Beginets but I appreciated the density of it compared to the Beignets. The beignets remind me of more like a hushpuppy maybe a bit denser than I had pictured in my head when I hear beignets. Overall the two crawfish dishes helped to make the meal a more filling lunch for two. 

The service is pretty quick and they have a seating area. This place also gets quiet busy during your lunch rush hours, but fear not they have a oyster bar here as well. 

This place is pretty good for a quick snack or stop to just sit and eat some oysters. This was our first of many stops in New Orleans
name: Eric

text: Unbelievable burgers! Husband said it's the best he ever had. I had the Fresco Melt, it didn't look that big but boy it was filling! The onion rings had a little sweetness to it. Don't even get me started with the giant Grape soda float! Highly recommended- unless you are on a diet.
name: Andrea

text: No big complaints, just a nice meal. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. Food was fresh and service was quick. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable.
name: User

text: This once was a decent hotel restaurant. However the menu posted here is way old and outdated. Now it's a corporate menu similar to what many hotels are doing. Few selections, high price and low quality. This place meets that to a T. I'd almost rather have spent the same money in the gas station next door and taken my chances with the rotisserie hot dog. It's a waste of your time and money eating here.
name: Brian

text: While driving the kids home from school today I looked up restaurants on Yelp and chose this one simply because I like to support locally-owned restaurants in Tampa and had never been there before.  We love Cuban restaurants and were not disappointed. The food was amazing, and the staff was incredibly friendly. It's not often that you find a gem like this in our fast-paced Tampa community.  If you like Cuban restaurants and live in Tampa look no further. This place is amazing and the staff went out of their way for us. Even my kids want to go back soon!
name: Timothy

text:
I felt a little like Michael Scott getting Sbarro pizza during his trip to NYC in "The Office," but I really was craving a Philly cheesesteak and decided that if I really wanted to indulge this urge I should at least try a cheesesteak that was on the gourmet side, and Cleaver's cheesesteaks seemed to fit that. 

I ordered the classic cheesesteak on a roll with sesame, waffle fries, and a fountain drink. It was pricier than street food (~$19 for the three items), but overall not too bad for a large-sized lunch. The cheesesteak was excellent in every regard - the meat itself tasted great, and the cheese and roll only enhanced the quality of the meat. Fries were only okay and were brought to my table lukewarm and not fully cooked. Despite this, I would recommend Cleaver's for people looking for the Philly cheesesteak experience in a non-street food setting.
name: Gaige

text:
My family was visiting Philadelphia Easter week and we decided to stop at LongHorns Steakhouse for the very first time...(and very last time) there were 3 of us , plus our 6yr old granddaughter.  We ordered drinks then our meals. Our waitress, Latetial L. was very pleasant and tenative. After our meals were served and we  started to eat, I noticed a black hair in my broccoli , which I moved that piece to a side plate..when the waitress came around I calmly showed her the hair and she asked if I wanted the manager to see it. Definitely, I said..
she took the broccoli into the manager, Michael Caparas. Latetial returned shortly and told us the manager,  Michael said he would take $2.99, the cost of a "side" off our bill!  I would hardly say that $2.99 is compensation for a hair in our food! I was calm and did not cause a fuss, but I feel this was very unsatisfactory. Our bill was $100 and anyone else finding a hair in their food would have been very disrupted, we feel this was nit the proper way to treat a customer.  We will never visit this restaurant chain again.
name: Darlene

text: Wanted to go here for a long time. Didn't live up to my expectations. No seafood other than lobster and crab. Very pricey. All food we ordered was just "ok". The only standout item was the hush puppies, and Port Royale drink. Hard to find. Small sign that is not noticeable. Service was pleasant. With the variety and level of competition in the STL city market, I don't see how this is surviving. Old building it's located in is cool.
name: Shana

text: This is my go to supermarket.  The seafood department is very good and the folks that work there are always pleasant and helpful.
name: Robert

text: The food is great and at a great price. Best coffee, my opinion. Sometimes I stop in just for it but can't help to get a chocolate chip waffle. The dinner is amazing too. Home made tortillas with the tacos. Very kind staff and takes care of out service members too. The short server is cute too.
name: Colin

text: The best restaurant!! Came here for my birthday to try some place new. The staff super-served us (they put customer experience first) and the food was AMAZING! I didn't even want to use condiments it was so good! ;) This place will be a regular.
name: Julia

text: Great food, good atmosphere!  I had the pasta dish and my wife had the BBQ shrimp.  Our server was personable as well.
name: Elijah

text: Anthony Bourdain hates brunch. I am clearly the anti-Bourdain!! I enjoyed my birthday brunch beyond my expectations...and they were high. The restaurant is like someone's Creole cottage, set up to entertain friends. The service never missed a beat. We were a party of four, and one cinnamon bun was generous...we all had a great sample. Something as simple as their coffee was above par. Don't get me started on the mimosas!!! Two of us ordered steak frites with eggs over easy...satisfying and flavorful, plus done to a perfect mid rare. One member ordered the brunch burger...another mid rare which was perfect. Number 4 ordered biscuits and debris....perfect. Chocolate mousse was last up..,and it didn't disappoint. It was our first visit, but it certainly won't be the last.
name: Susan

text:
It's one of the best places for parathas in this area. It's a must try and all the parathas here are amazing.

The owner here has a bit of a attitude but the taste is well worth it. There is a chance your order might get messed up and even then the owner would still be mad at you but trust me once you get the food you won't care about the attitude at all.

Don't get the mango lassi though - tastes like preservatives.
name: Rupa

text: If I could give this place 0 stars I would. SUCH A SCAM!!!! A girl pulled my friend into the shop and forced us to take shooters. After they made all of us do them, they demanded $24 each!!! When I said I didn't have the cash, the girl looked into my purse and saw money and told me to give her that!! I should've just walked out at that point but I didn't want to start any drama so I just gave it to her. If you ever come across this place do not give into it!!!!
name: Elana

text: Finally went to Ruby Sunshine...great location and was stoked about this trip. The food was average at best and nothing at all to be stoked about. The service was the greater concern. The young lady that delivered our food was rude and the table waitress was uninterested in how the food met our expectations. It was 45-minutes from when our drinks were delivered until our waitress stopped by to check-in. Far too much competition in this beautiful little town to survive with this combination of mediocre food and poor service. Very hopeful you get it fixed Ruby cause you could be a great spot.
name: Jeffrey

text:
Dear management: if you want to make money, you need to fill the restaurant and not half the tables.  The entire back part of the restaurant sat empty while the wait exceeded 2 hours during prime dinner time. We were extremely disappointed that we couldn't  our name in for a large party.
Bar staff were great and great service. 
Once seated the wait staff seemed disgruntled and not service oriented.  We ordered a cheese and chicken burrito and got a burrito filled with just cheese.  Menu is very small!   Kids quesadillas were more than adult items?  
Recommend trying ANY other place inside Opryland including the Delta food court!  Food is similarly priced and ten times faster.
name: Melanie

text: This place never disappoints. Fresh and tasty sushi, and friendly staff. They even made a bear out of an orange for my daughter Zoey.
name: Bill

text: Like many Chic-fil-a restaurants, this one gets insanely busy at lunch and dinner. And the location right off of busy Baltimore Pike can add to the craziness. Still, having been at these times, the staff does a good job of keeping the customers moving in and out. The employees have been pretty professional in my experience, a pleasant change from the typical I-hate-my-job demeanor that you encounter in fast food joints. Breakfast time has relatively light traffic, so that is when I usually patronage the place. The food has been on point in my many visits.
name: J

text: Worst experience ever. Food was horrible and me and my family well never return. This place won't be around long. I hope they fix it soon because the location is perfect.
name: David

text:
My husband and I had a really nice dinner at Nori this week. We arrived early on a Wednesday evening because we had tickets to a show nearby. There were very few tables occupied during our time there from around 5:30-6:45. I brought a bottle of white wine and we received an ice bucket upon arrival. 

Since I arrived first, I ordered some edamame to take the edge off. They were simply salted, nothing fancy. Once my husband arrived, we ordered the tuna tartare to start. It was again on the simple side, just diced tuna and avocado with some tobiko. Fresh and light, a good start to the meal. 

Next, we shared three special rolls: spicy girl (spicy salmon, spicy yellowtail, spicy tuna and crispy shallots), flaming hamachi (spicy crunchy yellowtail, tuna, jalapeño, scallion and sriracha), and blue ocean (spicy crunchy shrimp and cucumber, topped with smoked and fresh salmon, avocado and lime juice). 

My favorite roll was the flaming hamachi, because I loved the crunchiness of the jalapeño, followed by the spicy girl. I'm not big on smoked salmon so the blue ocean was my least favorite, but my husband enjoyed it. 

Prices were reasonable and there are some great lunch specials I'd like to try. Looking forward to next time!
name: Michelle

text: We tried both the chicken and regular cheesesteak. While the chicken was good, the combination of the smoked meat and gouda was delicious! A bit pricey but worth it.
name: Kaye

text: Best taco chain in Montgomery county. I always take out and never have to wait too long for my order!
name: Keith

text:
I came with 7 of my coworkers. Called ahead and Nicole was very accommodating with out group, even after several modifications. We were on a tight schedule so we called our orders ahead of time and got a few orders to go. 

After we arrived, the food was promptly served. Portions were large. They even offer an XL portion. I ordered the Bun Bo Hue, which was one of the best I've had. As mentioned by other reviewers, it is a more strongly flavored broth  compared to Cafe Diem. This place has joined Cafe Diem as my top Bun Bo Hue bowls in Philadelphia.

My coworkers also praised the food and Nicole and team's service. Most of them were non Vietnamese food eaters, but they all enjoyed it. They particularly enjoyed the Pho and Thit Kho. 

I very much enjoyed my experience here. We had quality food and fast  and friendly service. Would come back again.
name: Veng

text: Great brunch location. One of the best Bloody Mary's I've ever had. A nice diverse menu and the food was awesome.
name: L Adam

text: This is my favorite New Orleans coffee house. Iced coffee and a bran muffin from hete and my morning is set.
name: Ronald

text:
Bad service and forgettable food

The only reason this post is getting two stars at all is because 2 of the things ordered were good. When we first arrived, Siani took our order and wasn't friendly at all. She barely acknowledged us and I honestly wasn't sure she had heard the order at all. If I hadn't been meaning to try this restaurant I would have just left. My mom ordered a sandwich and an iced coffee and I ordered the 2 for lunch deal. When our food came there was no coffee and when my mom mentioned it the girl who brought our food to the table said she would get it for us. We ate our food and no coffee ever came. My mom gave the benefit of the doubt and thought maybe it had to be made. When she went up to check it turns out it could just be poured so my mom waited on a coffee for her meal simply because of bad service. On top of that, the whole reason I wanted to try the restaurant was the chicken pesto sandwich and my sandwich had no pesto. None. At all. Pesto is literally in the name. The salad with my sandwich was good but not enough to make me ever come to this restaurant again.
name: Haley

text: I ordered for takeout for a birthday celebration. In the past we have been fans of the freshness of the fish. This time out we were a little disappointed in the spicy salmon. It seemed a bit mushy. The flavors were a little bland as well. All of the rolls seemed to lack seasoning.
name: Karl

text: Yeah the legend is true. The burgers are huge. The interior is fun. Taste was pretty alright too. Not a diverse menu or anything, good for a quick bite.
name: Stephanie

text:
My update is Very Good!!
Food, delicious!! Beer, Cold!!! Fun customers, and the staff is amazing. Come in weekly when I can, that's if I'm not out of town for work.  Not one complaint, not that I'm a complainer in the first place, but most bar and grills don't do everything well, except for Roadside Bar & Grill, they have the right recipe for success. 

Highly recommend stopping in for a true Nashville experience of Southern Hospitality!!
name: Maint.

text: Experienced the absolute worst service ever on our last visit on 6/23. I pulled up to the drive thru window at 8:00am on a Sunday morning. There was 1 car in front of me, who pulled forward right away. I sat at the box waiting to order but no one ever came on. I could hear every word being said inside so I said "hello!", and nothing. So again I said "Hello!?", quite loudly this time, still nothing. I waited another couple of minutes while screaming into the box but no one ever answered so I pulled thru to the window, without ever placing an order and was met by a lady whom seemed to have no clue what she was doing. The manager was yelling at her to unlock the headset but she never did. She finally asked what I wanted so I ordered a breakfast sandwich, which seemed to confuse her but she finally understood and placed the order. I asked 3 times for no cheese but when I got home there were 2 pieces of cheese!  Normally the food and service are pretty good so we'll be back. I support everyone's right to work but maybe that's not the job for her.
name: Denise

text:
Their deep dish is so, so, so delicious, my stomach is growling just thinking about it! Heads up though- it can take 45 minutes- an hour once you put your order in for a deep dish since it has to cook in the oven. WORTH THE WAIT, but plan on getting an appetizer (the burrata and the spinach artichoke dip are my favorites) or just don't go when you're super hungry.
Great beer and wine selection as well. And a vegan deep dish option!!
name: Nichole

text: Come here religiously every week. Service is def getting better which is a plus. The only complaints I have is you cant make things your own. They wouldn't turn a burrito into a bowl for me? It's simple just don't serve it with a tortilla. It's always their way or no way. Other than that the only reason we come back is the food. Please step up your game!!!
name: Caitlyn

text: Breakfast burrito heaven!! Only place I'll go for a bfast burrito now. So good and so big! Their salads are also amazing. Love this place
name: Dani

text:
Love me some Maki Maki! I have been frequentin Maki Maki for years and it is definitely my go to sushi place in Old Strathcona. 

They have a wide variety of sushi rolls, with my favs being the avocado rolls, yam rolls and salmon rolls. Also, they have some delicious vegetarian tempura with a wide variety of vegetables (mushrooms, broccoli, yams, onions and more), as well as some killer green onion cakes. 

Great place to share a variety of dishes with others! Also, the service is excellent and there is always a table ready.
name: Jenny

text: Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. It was crowded but still moved along. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really.
name: User

text:
Usually I don't eat at chain restaurants so I didn't eat at an Outback for a very long time but I am so happy I went back! The service both in restaurant and curbside has been great. They messed up my order once for the curbside and they couldn't stop apologizing and made it right. 
Highly recommend the ribs and the bloom petals and new bloomin chicken!
name: Amanda

text:
I love reading then sampling "best of" food, desserts, drinks and services.  Recently I read the Lost Bread Co. pretzel shortbread cookie was named by New York Magazine as "Best Cookie." A Philadelphia based company being voted by New York as a Best of ....  how exciting, I couldn't wait to sample it. Early Sunday morning (the business is only open at this location on Saturday and Sunday) my son offered to ride across town , with me, to sample the cookie. It was most certainly worth the wait. The texture, taste and concept was totally new to me but boy was it tasty. 

Note: A bag of 8 cookies after tax is about $13, a bit pricey but from what I read it's very time consuming to make the cookies
name: Dannie

text: This place is really yummy, and really clean. Definitely a good find! Owner is friendly and great menu for a quick bite.
name: Eric

text:
Disappointed!! Me and a friend walked down there to get some food to go. My friend chose to get something on the cold bar, or whatever that was. There was nothing there to tell you what it was and the food behind the counter was not visible. Confusion!!. 
I went to a main food line that seemed to take much longer than expected. While I'm standing in line,  my friend asks me to see if they would let her sample a siracha meatball.  When I finally get up there to build my bowl, I ask for half greens and half rice. Well the drone behind the counter couldn't compute that and tried to instead settle for charging me extra. I guess she only works on whole numbers and skipped fractions in third grade. So I said never mind, just give me the rice. After getting veggies and chicken, I ask the guy if he can put one meatball on there for my friend to sample, and again, I am told I can buy three for an up-charge.  Now, I'm starting to see a pattern. Finally, I get to the station with the extras and ask for Feta  cheese. Surprise!! There are out!! So not liking any of the remaining extras that are free of up charges, I ask for guacamole and of course, she informs me that it costs extra. I retort with the fact that you did not have the thing I wanted, so can't you not up-charge me? She looked stunned, as if her programming hit a glitch. Finally, after awkward silence, I said, just gimme the guacamole.  I did not care about cost really. Never do, but the lack of customer service skills or maybe just the company structure made it feel like I was constantly being hit up with another fee by staff with no people skills. 
Ever see Fargo when Steve Buscemi tries to exit the parking garage and the attendant makes him pay even though he had just gone in and immediately left? That's what it felt like. https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=MXcxWsdjYHA
If they want to go ala carte on so many items, then fine, be ready to be flexible. This is a Fresh Kitchen wannabe. Fresh Kitchen never turns down a request and their staff understands the concept of fractions. They also allow sampling because they know they are building a relationship with a repeat  customer.
There was decent traffic in the store. Seems like one of those hipster places where people go to feel cool, so I guess that explains some of the traffic, but it may be a while before I head back there. I am cool already.
BTW, the food was just ok.
name: Rick

text:
I can't gush positive enough about my experience with Proper Bagel and co-owner Heather.
A friend's father passed away and I wanted to send food to the house.  Heather made it easier than I could have hoped for.  She made magic happen.
The end result was an incredibly grateful family that got a perfect platter or bagels and fish.  Even fussy Upper Westside Jewish New Yorkers thought the bagels PROPER!
name: Joanna

text: Every time I go here I enjoy myself . Great atmosphere and customer service . The Korean short rib tacos are to die for !
name: India

text:
After a very enlightening three-hour New Orleans Cocktail History Walking tour through the French Quarter (I highly recommend this tour), my wife and I figured that we better get some food in our system's if we planned on keeping the party going. After doing some research we settled on Mr. Ed's Oyster Bar. With a little slur in our speech and stumble in our walk (don't judge us, we were getting the full French Quarter experience), we made our way over to the restaurant.
 
Although the restaurant was scheduled to close in less than two hours, we were warmly welcomed by a bunch of staff that were congregating at the entrance of the restaurant as we walked in. Less than a minute after being seated, we were greeted by an enthusiastic waiter named Renard. Renard gave us a brief breakdown of the menu and provided us with some of his favorite items on the menu. We both settled on the Southern Fried Catfish dinner and I ordered a tea based alcoholic beverage (Renard recommended that I have the drink how he would have it...stiff).
 
Less than twenty minutes later our food and drinks arrived. We were impressed by how well our seafood was fried (it wasn't saturated in oil), and how subtly strong our beverages were (the tea was definitely a creeper). Most importantly, we were thankful (keyword) that the meal (obviously not the healthiest choice), was proportioned so that we both wouldn't look like we were three months pregnant as we walked out of the restaurant. Throughout our duration in the restaurant, Renard was very personable and professional. He even provided us with a small list of activities within the French Quarter that my wife and I should engage in.
 
If you're looking for scrumptious food and great customer service, make a quick stop at Mr. Ed's Oyster Bar!
name: Raheem

text:
Nice and clean good waitstaff quick service and very attentive.
Food was acceptable Jambalaya needed some more heat but that is my liking shrimp were slightly overdone. The blackened shrimp and chicken Cobb salad was more than filling as the regular Cesare salad was also.
I will return.
name: Woodman

text: Worst wine tasting experience ever. Herded like cats into a small tasting room for a tasting that lasted no more than 5 minutes. Little to no information provided about the wine tasted; no opportunity to select which wines to taste.
name: Mindy

text: Took my managers to Cooper's for dinner the other evening. This is a must visit for locals or those visiting Tampa or any area that Cooper's is located that looking for good food, great wine and a great dining or simple wine tasting experience
name: BballdadAtl

text:
A cool outlet mall with tons of stores, restaurants, a food court, a movie theatre, dave and buster's.  We only had 3.5 hours to spare at the mall and we only completed 50% of the mall. This place is ginormous!! I think this mall takes the entire day! Other than that, the mall is very clean and spacious with too many things to do.

The entrance to the mall is across the famous grand ole opry music venue.
name: Sandra

text:
I was invited as a guest to this Carrabba's for a Wine Dinner. Each month these Italian Grill's host a little known differently themed wine dinner, July's theme was Lunar Effects, celebrating the 50th anniversary of the Apollo 11 landing on the moon. A specially designated area of the restaurant that is decorated for the event and a special menu connecting to the theme is presented by an event dedicated staff. Each course is paired with a different wine selected to compliment the food. This evening in Bensalem, about 30 people were in attendance, and some were regulars to the monthly events. We were greeted promptly on entering by a hostess and then by a staff member from another part of the company attending this as guests. The event was to start at 6:30 and promptly the restaurant's proprietor, Mary McGrath introduced herself and welcomed everyone to the event. She introduced our lead server to us whos name escapes me, probably the wine, lol and she announced that our first beverage would be served in a souvenir​ glass that would be washed and returned to us by the end of the evening. Our servers began serving Blue Moon Draft beer in a full-sized​ pilsner glass with really cool (literally​ too, it was a frosty chilled glass), commemorative​ markings of the 50th anniversary of the moon landing and the Blue Moon logo.
The draft beer was refreshing and served in clean lines with a fresh,​ clean, crisp flavor, and the hint of valencia oranges used in the brewing process and each had a fresh, meaty orange slice garnish. Please note I put milk in the glass at home the next day to be able to clearly show the design. Within minutes our first course was served, Calabrian Roasted Wings, this was the first time I had their wings, they were delicious and roasted not fried, hard to believe they were seasoned with spicy​ Italian​ peppers and served a really good gorgonzola dipping sauce. Our server or Mary described each item in-depth​ as they were being served. As everyone was finished and perfectly timed we were served a glass of Rocca Delle Macie Moonlite, a Toscan white wine crisp and aromatic paired with Mezzaluna Carrabba, a portion of half-moon​ ravioli filled with romano cheese and spinach tossed in alfredo sauce and topped with wood-grilled​ chicken strips, sauteed mushrooms, ​and peas. The chicken was a little overcooked​ and could have used a bit more alfredo, but the flavor was nice. I appreciate that Mary was focused on the guests and noticed some of the chicken on a couple of our plates wasn't​ being eaten and inquired as to why​ she immediately apologized and offered to get fresh. She then quickly disappeared briefly to probably coach the kitchen staff on this minor misfire. You could tell she was disappointed by that showing ownership of the issue and obvious pride in her restaurant; she even mentioned it again at the end of the event. Our third beverage was a glass of Alta Luna Pinot​ Noir a lush, full-bodied​ red wine with a hint of cherry paired with Pollow Sorrento a wood-grilled​ thin chicken breast​​ topped with unique crispy eggplant, prosciutto, mozzarella​ and tomatoes and then their Lombardo Marsala sauce and a side of garlic mashed potatoes. Again the chicken was a bit dry, but the eggplant, prosciutto, ​and the sauce were very tasty. The garlic mashed​ was perfectly seasoned and delicious. Our fourth and final course was Cinnamon Apple Crostata, I have enjoyed this before when it is normally served in a cast iron mini skillet and is awesome, it is an apple tart with a great hazelnut filling, vanilla ice cream, ​and caramel sauce typically the tart is crispy and has a generous scoop of ice cream and is sinfully delicious tonights was in a ramekin did not have a crispy crust and a real tiny scoop of melted ice cream it tasted  doughy possibly undercooked. This was paired with Saint M Riesling a crisp fruity sweet and flavorful dessert wine. 
During this event,​ there were three baskets raffled each attendee was given tickets and had the opportunity to earn additional tickets with trivia. All this was right around $40 plus tax and gratuity. Although I was a guest and didn't have to pay,​ I thought it was a fair amount of food and beverages well worth that price. Remember this is a casual dining chain so the wine dinner may not be what you are​ accustomed to at other wine pairing events but the group of people there and the service made it fun, made new friends and it was a social event much better than​ a simple meal.
IMPORTANT NOTE: The restaurant or staff did not know I was a member of the Yelp team until I was leaving. I typically do my check-in​ & review after so I can enjoy myself as well as to not let the​ staff know.
These events are held monthly and can be found online, for planning purposes a reservation is required and can be found at carrabbas.com/winedinner each one can vary in price a little. The next event is titled 'If Grapes Could Talk' a photo of that menu is posted.
name: Jerry

text: I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Would return. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Not bad for a quick meal. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text: Visiting from NY found this gem on Yelp. We ate dinner there last night. Superb service and treatment. Our server, Tammy, was excellent and personable. We had Veal Parm and Capellini with oil and garlic ( off menu item) they were happy to cook it for my wife. Capellini is one of her favorites . Both meals served on large plates and large portions.  Veal was well pounded and soooo tender.  Capellini was not over seasoned. Prices were very fair and we give this Italian charm a five star. No complaints from us.
name: Kevin

text: Great fusion restaurant! I definitely recommend the paneer tacos, samosas, red curry and rice dishes. We either order in or eat at the restaurant 3-4 times a month. It's also decorated very nicely and is a quiet nice place to eat.
name: Aradhana

text:
Manee thai has been on my radar for a while. I had heard good things about it and their menu looked delicious. Like any good Christian family, we go out for some sort of Asian cuisine on Christmas eve. 

We started off with some appetizers. They were all delicious. The dumplings, shrimp in a blanket, and chicken satay all were filled with flavor. The entrees however were not as satisfying. Not to say they were bad, however, they weren't anything special compared to other thai resteraunts in the area. I personally had had the lava trio which is a dish containing seafood in a chili sauce. The flavors were delicious, however it cam served over a bed of iceberg lettuce  and had more onions than seafood. Also, the fried mussels weren't very good and ended up being very chewy.

The bright spot in the entrees was the spicy eggplant stir fry. It came with shrimp and chicken in addition to the eggplant. It seemed to have pretty good.flavord and a solid mix and portion size.
name: Brendan

text: The food here is really good! The one suggestion I would make is maybe changing the pho section of the menu to say not say "noodle soups" at the top Because apparently the soups do not include noodles. That is pretty misleading. Other than that I really recommend the food!
name: Sally

text:
I've been a handful of times for dinner and always came away feeling satisfied. The olde bar fries are a dynamite and sinful appetizer to get. Good cocktails also!

They have a good happy hour. I find myself coming here once or twice a month for the fish house punch, crab fingers, and fried shrimp. All very good and CHEAP! if you're ever in the area stop in (happy hour 7 days / week)
name: Bob

text: Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. It was crowded but still moved along. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Definitely coming back. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Food was fresh and service was quick. Food was good and came out fast. Would probably stop in again if nearby. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text:
I really really really hoped this place would be good since it's the closest vietnamese restaurant to our house, but unfortunately we were very disappointed.  I ordered bun bo hue and my fiance ordered pho. We also ordered a side of bun bao. First of all, the food is just a tad pricey (no big deal we thought) the bun bao came out and it was "okay". The side plate of veggies came out next and it was underwhelming (this gave me a slight premonition of what was to come but I tried to stay optimistic). 

Finally the soup came out, and not to my surprise turned out "underwhelming". The soup tasted watered down, as if it wasn't made from scratch using some type of base - not only that but my bun bo hue didn't use traditional meat. I was a little sad but I decided to deal with it and started eating my 12 dollar watered down bun bo hue with pho meat. I then asked for a side of bread to eat with my soup. The waiter came back and it was very awkward. Why you ask? Well, turns out that they don't do that. The owner had to come out and tell me that they don't sell that bread. I pointed at the case of unused bread and asked, "that one?" He nodded and said, "Yes, we don't sell that. You would have to buy a sandwich to buy that bread." Even the waiter (who was new) looked shocked. 

Wow. I paid my bill, tipped the poor waiter, and left. 

I'll gladly drive a bit farther to go to a cheaper more authenticate place with better food, service and atmosphere.

Never going back and I caution anyone who wants to try it. 

Food 1/10
Service 1/10
Price 4/10
name: Dara

text: The sauce carried most of the meal. The staff seemed tired but still polite. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. Honestly, the food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kinda leveled off after a few bites. Anyway, everything was tasty and the place felt clean. so yeah kind of mixed on it. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait.
name: User

text: We ordered the generals chicken, pork fried rice, and house special chow mein. Everything was great, a lot of local Chinese restaurants taste really greasy and heavy. New Garden was neither of those things, the fried rice and generals chicken especially had the perfect amount of seasoning and sauce. My 2 year old devoured the noodles and veggies in the chow mein. Will definitely be ordering again.
name: Angela

text: Excellent experience!! Will absolutely recommend to my friends who visit. The food was out quickly, and the oysters were delicious!
name: James

text:
Quiet place for dinner, hardly anyone else in the restaurant on Wednesday night. I got the sweet and sour tofu. The sauce was rather interesting but the tofu could have used a longer fry time to make it crispier. For appetizer, I had the pork fried potatoes, which is really only good with the spicy mayo or spicy mustard sauce, otherwise I would skip them. For dessert, I had the cornbread donuts, not worth the price in my opinion.

I had to wait a while for the food. Probably about 10 minutes for the appetizer and another 15 for the main course. 25 minutes is a long wait for this style of food.

I'm not against returning but I wouldn't choose to return to TKO on my own. I think the empty restaurant shows others are thinking the same thing.

text: I get the appeal, I just don't totally share it. Price felt a touch high for what it was. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. I can see why people like it, even if I wasn't fully sold. It looked better online than it did in person.
name: User

Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. It was decent, just a little uneven. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..
name: User

text: Came back here on my 4th trip to NOLA this morning, and this one woman staff working was rude and snarky with our party of 3. We asked if they had fried chicken but, was told it's only served on, Thursday. Ok, fine today, was Monday. They didn't have fried chicken this particular day, which was what my daughter wanted, and was told that they were also done serving breakfast for the day, too. So, we turned around to leave and find somewhere else to eat with food we wanted. Apparently, the woman working behind the counter began to yell at us to watch out for a man coming in while we were leaving. I had no clue what she was talking about because there was no man coming in at all. I personally, didn't hear any of this conversation but, my sister heard the woman complain to the other customers that we had ignored what she said. She was mad because we hadn't ordered anything, left, and didn't open a door for a man to walk into the restaurant first. However, where we come from, ladies go first, and men usually open doors for women, anyway. Sorry, but all that attitude she was giving us just doesn't cut it with me. The first time I visited this restaurant with my husband lat year, we had an excellent, friendly server who I didn't see. Unfortunately, not this time. And because of this rude woman and that incident, I won't ever be returning. Get over yourself, lady. There's better restaurants in the area who value their customers and who are friendly.
name: doreen

text:
Calafuria is a delicious little Midtown Reno bungalow which has been converted into a trendy eatery. You have a choice of indoor or outdoor seating. Tonight was a mild spring evening, so we chose outdoors, though I wished they had an outdoor heater, as my jacket was a little thin for the breeze. 

We started off with 2 types of delicious bread - focaccia and regular Italian bread, with some Parmesan butter.  We skipped the appetizers, though they sounded enticing, and went straight for the main course. We tried 2 of their nightly specials - octopus pappardelle, and a duck and Italian sausage combo (there was a fancy name in there somewhere, but I can't remember it!), and one regular menu item - spaghetti alla chitarra.  

The pasta is house made and is so light and fresh! The sauces were excellent, though a tad on the salty side. The duck and sausage was quite hearty but heavy - probably a better winter dish than spring. The sausage was spicier than I was expecting, but still delicious. 

For dessert, we ordered the chocolate mousse and the panna cotta. They were both very light and airy, which was nice after a hearty entree. The mousse was especially nice because it was not overly sweet, and allowed the bitterness of the dark chocolate to come through slightly to contrast the sweet crunchy toppings. 

Upon paying, we were offered complimentary limoncello, which we gladly accepted!  I wished it was a little colder, but it definitely tasted lemony, possibly with some fresh zest added to it. They even add f a nice little touch of labeling our leftovers box!

Overall a delicious experience.
name: Jeannie

text: For the price I expected more than this. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. A couple small things kept adding up. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Food was fresh and service was quick. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. Food was good and came out fast. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..

We loved being seated in the jazz room where a trio played great jazzy tunes from long ago. The waiter brought us a heart balloon, such a sweet gesture to highlight our anniversary celebration dinner. The band spotted us and came to our table and played us a wonderful romantic song, it was like we went back in time. The food was delicious! And so was our dessert. Dining at Arnauds was a wonderful experience.
name: Dina

text: Ok this place is so incompetent! how hard is it when ordering food to get what you want! my wife clearly stated we wanted a triple burger with cheese and may and bacon  meal and she wanted a double cheese burger plain.  that's what we ordered we get home  and the triple burger has only mayo no bacon and my wife didn't even get her burger and to boot the fries are cold. so needless to say we will never be going back to this establishment again . I advise that no one eat there as well
name: Rory

text: Arrived around 5:00 pm on Saturday, it was an hour wait for a table but we were able to sit at the bar with no wait. They took our orders and the food arrived about 10-15 mins later. That was the positive of the dinner, they never asked if I wanted another drink, and really didn't ask how we were doing until we were done. They must be trying to conserve water as well. When my son finally got their attention and asked for more water they filled his glass but left mine and my wife's empty. The blue cheese slaw was good but I think they could use more green vegetable choices. My wife and son had sandwiches that were good, but my brisket and pastrami were very dry, and no hot mustard for the pastrami. Atmosphere was nice but there is definitely better smoked meats out there.

text: For the price I expected a little more care. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. For a busy night they handled it okay. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would..
name: User

text: While the Crab Shack doesn't look like much, it's packed with some of the best crab in town. On Tuesdays and Thursdays they sell "All-you-can-eat crab legs" till 9:30. This Tuesday evening they served snow crab. It was very tender and well cooked, served with French fries and coleslaw that's topped with paprika. Everything that was ordered was absolutely exquisite, 11/10 would recommend.
name: April

text:
This place is just what you need after a long day! Great service, great great service! great food! Great beer list! I want to make a special thanks to Melissa the bartender, and Heather the server.

I had the wings l, dry rub, they were delicious. The nachos are huge! Definitely enough for a group. 

....Thursday night. Another great visit. Feels like a place to just have a dinner party with friends.  Thanks again Melissa!
name: Jon

text:
I was really excited for this to be added to the south side of Indy. I have been watching them build this location everyday when I drive to work. 

The drive thru service was superb. They were quick and prompt. I was able to be in and out in under 5 minutes. 

I had the hotdog and Italian beef, both were adequate. My favorite is the chocolate cake shake! Must try. Just might need to hit the treadmill afterwards..
name: Tina

text:
Mom n me out on the town - another adventure of two hep chicks! Tuesday evening edition...

My mother was born a week before Christmas more than 80++ years ago this eve. I asked her, what do you want for your birthday dinner and she was very specific- a corned beef & pastrami special from Famous on 4th. My mother has been through a lot during the last seven years so her dr would probably have had me arrested if she knew i took her to Famous for corned beef & pastrami, but birthday ladies should be able to have what ever they want and mom rarely goes off the dietary rails... Famous sandwiches are around a lb+/serving so we shared one. For around $22 we received two giant halves on extra thick slices of rye bread (no seeds).  We chose extra cole slaw and thousand island dressing as our side. Since we were already in heart attack city, we began our meal with the chopped liver app.

Service 6/5
The gentleman who waited on us has worked for Famous for over 34 years and is as thin, handsome  and sweet as the day he started there and we love him. He's so nice and though it's been a few years since our last visit, he remembered us. My mom is a the kind of lady everyone remembers, but you can tell that he's the kind of service professional who remembers everyone who has ever graced the doors of that grand ol eatery.

Food - savory 5/5
chopped liver app 5/5
This app consisted of at least 9 oz of chopped liver on a platter with two giant slices of sweet white onion and equally beautiful slices of tomato on three Romain leaves. A very nice presentation of very fresh chopped. Liver. Perhaps it's an acquired taste but we both thought it was delicious!

Corned beef & pastrami special Sammy with one side 5/5
What can i say that hasn't been said about the corn beef and pastrami at Famous? Okay so it was a little saltier than I remembered and waited for mom to offer forth her usual comments about why is food always too salty in restaurants? This time I said I agree it's salty but then she added, well it's supposed to be :)

Rice pudding with golden raisin 3/5
This giant portion could easily serve six folks would have received 5 stars but the rice was way undercooked. I mean it was not raw but still way too hard. It could have used another 10 minutes in the steamer or double boiler. It was a disappointing end but not a disappointing evening because dinner with my mother is always a special treat.
name: Elisa

text: What a delicious change of pace in New Orleans! Loved the vibe and decor of this new neighborhood gem, the food was delicious (lamb Barbacoa is a must!) and the drinks were on point. We enjoyed our large group gathering with timely service and a very accommodating owner.  Can't wait to try the in house taqueria that's open late every night! A must try for sure!
name: Mahereen

text: Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Food was good and came out fast.
name: User

text:
We normally don't eat at Pizza Hut very often, but I do have fond childhood memories of eating pie from here... always consistently tasty, and inexpensive compared to some of the boutique pizza places. Better than most chain pizza, IMO.

While moving, the last thing you want to do is try to cook, with everything you need in boxes, and the kitchen in a total transitional mess. So someplace like Pizza Hut rocks for a quick and easy meal.

The first visit was the new Double Cheesy Crust Pan Crust base with Pepperoni Lovers topping... and it was delicious! Healthy? NO! Yummy? YES! I ate most of that large pizza all by my self, I think my girlfriend had two, maybe three slices. So yea, I pigged out. 

We probably wont eat here often, but on the occasional splurge weekend... heck yea!
name: Charlie

text:
Wow. Just. Wow. 

When was the last time that you were "wowed" by a take out restaurant experience? Probably the last time you ate at Hong Minh. 

Picture it: Thursday. You're working late. You're hungry. You didn't take anything out the fridge and don't feel like cooking. You call DH who is stumbling around blindly and would probably just end up laying on the couch weak from hunger instead of boiling water for noodles. 

The answer: Chinese food. But where? You've been hurt before. You're weary. They have names like Star and Dragon and Family Happiness and they are all lies. 

You pull up your trusty Yelp app. See someplace new that closes in WHOAH 15 MINUTES!! You panic. You must male a decision NOW. You dial. You can't believe someone picked up. But now you're emboldened. 

So you ask for the duck (apparently that's their specialty). Yes. Fried rice. Yes. Mixed veggies. Yes. 

I'm going to be there just minutes before the doors should lock. 

I walk in. It smells amazing. It's a family business. Kiddos are sitting on their screens, dad's in the back. The lady says "we made a little too much rice, so we gave you more" oh yeah. This can only get better. 

It's not fancy inside. But it was bright with natural light. 

The food was delicious. Just a warning if you get the half duck, there's half a head in there. And if you have half a brain, you'll dine at Hong Minh.
name: Michele

text: Unbelievably good! It was our 1st time ordering takeout and it was the best, freshest and most delightful pizza we've had in years. Greenwood is lucky to have this establishment and I hope they do very well.
name: Chris

text:
Such a cute little brunch place across the French Market. Dainty little decorations, bit more classy than the rest of the FQ..but yet decent prices.

Food we ordered:
Mimosa- 3/5. Usually I like my 'mosas more champs than juice but this had hardly any OJ. Disappointing cause I was looking for a nice refreshing pickmeup after last night's activities. 
Chicken and Waffles- 3/5. Chicken was fine but the waffles were definitely over-cooked, a little on the burnt side. Drenched in syrup, wish they put it on the side at least. 
Stuffed French Toast- 5/5. Delicious, they didn't hold back on the cream cheese filling. But the seasoned fruit it came with... NOT FRESH FRUIT, tasted like it was straight out of a can and I couldn't eat more than 2 berries even. 
Honeysuckle sweet potato fries- 5/5. The star of the meal. BEST sweet potato fries EVER. Fries smothered in gorgonzola, pecans, and honey...went pretty quickly at our table. 
Crawfish spring rolls- 4/5. Decent but barely tasted any crawfish, more veggies.

If you ask me, this place has better appetizers than their main entrees and I could see myself coming back in for a mid-day snack. 

We were a party of 7, had no reservations and they seated us without a problem and no wait!
name: Tina

text: We have loved their food for years now, and are locals who have tried everything. Unfortunately, a day after last eating there, they were shut down for an EXTENSIVE list of sanitation and food risks. The health inspector closed it the DAY AFTER we ate there, and we had no idea. Will not be going back until I am assured they are safe and sanitary. Proceed with caution. The food is great, but apparently deceivingly so... Disgusting. Ruined Anthony's for me and my family/friends.
name: Nichole

text:
Grays on Main is a modern southern restaurant. The fried chicken (airline chicken beast) with garlic mashed and green beans was amazing. The short ribs with smoked Gouda grits were really good as well, which led me to get a side of the grits, because you can never have too much grits. 
As good as the food was the bar seemed to get backed up, since drinks took quite some time to get. 
The craft cocktail menu is very unique and the drinks are tasty. 
It is also one of the only 2 "Brandy Bars" on the East Coast. The other one is in NYC. 
Desserts such as the Banana pudding and Browny are a very nice and tasty way to end your meal. Maybe with a Port wine.
But it is over priced.
name: Ralph

text: Reading some of these complaints now feels a little overblown. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Not bad for a quick meal. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Nice little spot, decent portions too. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything..
name: User

text:
Crab legs specialty eateries seem to be all the rage in STL these days, with new spots opening up all over the area.  With so many (superior) options, thankfully, there's no reason at all to visit the Delmar Krab Kingz.

The first thing i want to preface this review with is despite identical names, the Krab Kingz location on Delmar which this review is about is a completely separate entity all together from the establishment on Watson.  While I frequent the Watson location often and have never left disappointed, I've seen enough to swear off the Delmar version forever.  

An itemized list of fails during my visit:

1. Unorganized order taking set up that had me and my date walking in circles upon entering

2. Inattentive cashiers that appear barely conscious while alternatively switching from staring off into space and fiddling with their phones...no greeting or even asking if we were ready to order

3. Obnoxious wait times.  After ordering we sat and a waited a little over 30 minutes to receive our food.

4. Once finally getting the food we had to wait another 5 minutes to be handed table ware and crab crackers (which requires a $5 deposit).  

5. After getting the utensils we finally dig in, only to find out.... surprise, the sausage and eggs were missing from our platter.  They arrived 10 after we informed the server they were omitted 

6. The owner Cortez Burnett is a total creep.  He came to our table several times to ask how was our meal.  I was just ready to leave and gave generic answers, my date said she was unimpressed.  When I visit the restroom before we leave he asks her to add their page on Facebook, only to try to hit on her via DM hours later.  To call this sleezy and unprofessional is a monumental understatement, but certainly explains the service we received.

To their credit, the food itself is decent.  Not as good as the Watson rd location by any means however.  I'd happily drive the extra 20 minutes there if faced with the choice again.  I'd encourage anyone that wants crab legs in the U City loop area that can't make it Watson to go to Mad Crab less than five minutes away.
name: Christopher

text: This place is every bit as good as Yelp reviewers suggested. Wife and I split an east nasty and a bonut order and it was the greatest breakfast ever.
name: Aaron

text: Web site was easy to use to place our order.  We are from out of town and found them on Yelp.  Our order was delivered in half the time what they indicated.  And, the pizza tasted great!
name: Stuart

text: I love this place. A cool, dark respite from the Arizona sun with a slightly goth vibe. Very friendly staff and a television over the bar that plays horror movies all day and night. Good drink prices, pool tables, and all kinds of creepy but fun decorations. Apparently they host burlesque shows and other special events. I can't wait to go back.
name: Matt

text: Oh my goodness. I don't even know where to start for Zaytoon. Zaytoon is AMAZING. The vibe I got from Zaytoon was classy and elegant. I loved the concept of it being outdoor seating. The details of the outdoor seating were perfect. I loved sitting by a fire while I ate my food. My mom and I shared a combination plate. We wanted try a little of everything. The food was delicious! On top of that the experience was so unique. Towards the end of our dinner, a belly dancer came out and started to walk around to tables and dance. I thought it was funny how some people would put money in her belt as she walked by. If you're in the area, Zaytoon is definitely worth your time and I guarantee you'll have an amazing experience.

text:
I dont know why I waited so long to come here.

We were quickly seated during weekend lunch times & the atmosphere was awesome, snake skins on the wall, Texas related pix & NASCAR hood's.
We started with warm bread that melts in your mouth. Then we had their version of a blooming onion which along with a margarita & Sam Adams. Drinks are strong & soon help you forget how many country songs you just listen to.
We all ordered from the mix & match section. We had Steak, ribs, chicken & grilled shrimp. Every bit was delicious, juicy & seasoned very well. There could have been a few more shrimp though.
The sides were ok (could use improvement) but didn't take too much away from an impressive first time.
There was no room for dessert, but they looked good.
Next time we will share a plate so there isnt so much leftover & room for a treat at the end.

text:
Awesome neighborhood restaurant! Onesto is a terrific little Italian restaurant with great food. We had the house salad-perfect for sharing (dressing was just right) 
Chicken Parmesan, Stromboli and chicken spedini. Also a side of Brussels sprouts that were on special. There was a slight mix up with our order but the owner Nick took care of it right away! Also a free tiramisu which was amazing and authentic. Portions are the perfect size and prices are fair :) The complimentary garlic knots are also a plus, yum!!!
name: Britt

text:
This is now our go to Italian restaurant. This was our first trip here. We arrived around 7:30 on a busy Friday evening. We waited about 5 minutes as the hostess had a table cleared for us. 

We were seated and out waitress was at our table within three minutes for drink orders. Drink orders came out and the waitress asked if we had any questions, which we didn't, and brought bread back and took our order. 

The salads we're out quickly. The house made ranch was delicious on the mostly romaine salad. The salads did have some cheese, a red onion slice, and some wondering garlic croutons. 

The only downside on our dinner was that the entrees did take some time to come out. Fortunately, they were well worth the wait. My wife enjoyed the Alfredo Con Scampi and I had the Chef's Sampler of Lasagna, Manicotti and Fettuccine Alfredo. 

My wife stated that the Alfredo sauce is the best that she has had from a restaurant and I'd have to agree with her. It didn't need any extra seasoning added. It was delectable on its own. The shrimp in her entree were cooked perfectly and had great flavor. The lasagna and manicotti in my dish was superb as well. The meat sauce in the lasagna again was seasoned perfectly and the ricotta mixture in both the manicotti and lasagna had a wonderful flavor and beautiful texture. 

The Italian bread was warm and tasty, served with seasoned olive oil for dipping. The bread was the perfume accoutrement for getting the last bits of sauce from the dishes. 

It is a shame that we didn't have any room left for dessert. 

I can not wait for the next evening we want to go out for Italian. That being said, I was envious of every diners plate that came out with a steak on it. They looked divine with roasted red potatoes and mixed veggies. So I guess we may be back for our next steak night.

text: My all time favorite burger is here, the NOLA Nica burger will be your new craving. If you want Latin food with a twist you must try them.  Everything is delicious!  The staff is very friendly and professional.  One of my top restaurant food choices.

text: Good breakfast. If you are staying at The Conrad you may receive a breakfast voucher. With the voucher you can get the continental breakfast for free or $10 off of anything else you order. We ordered and it was pretty good. Selected 3 options for inside the 3 egg omelette. Was nice and warm when it came to the table but the egg part was pretty tough. If you like your omelette tender I'd recommend asking them to cook to your liking. Maybe we were just hungry but we ate it anyway. Almost like the filling was just added as an afterthought. Originally ordered sourdough bread as a side but the kitchen ran out so the server offered a blueberry pancake. Excellent choice btw.

text:
The short of it: the food is good and the atmosphere is awesome. Now for the rest of it...

I really liked this place. Seriously. But, in MY opinion, it's just too expensive for what it is. My husband and I spent over $120 on two plates and four drinks (2 beers, 1 cocktail, and 1 wine) at a communal table, in the harsh sun... on Wells. I just don't find that to be worth it. The food was delicious; I had the trout and my husband had the mussels. The cocktail was lacking and not worth the price, which is why I switched to wine after my first one, and my husband couldn't find a beer he cared for. 

Overall I would have been fine to pay those prices for a special occasion dinner but $120 for a Friday night hangout at a casual beer garden on Wells just isn't for me. I just don't think I'm the customer this place is looking to attract, and that's okay. Just kinda bummed because if it weren't for the prices of food or drink I'd probably be here alllll the time.

text: Went here for my moms birthday with a party of ten on a saturday afternoon. We were trying to find a bbq restaurant and the reviews raved over this place so we decided to go for it. text: Haven't been to a Cracker Barrel since my wife got sick on fried green tomatoes about five years ago. Otherwise our experience was always pleasant; even that day if I remember correctly. That's probably my fault though, I'm a tea drinker and when I do drink coffee, I stick to the no-frills kind. Bottom-line, great experience across the board.

text: I was really excited to try this place out but unfortunately i won't return. First i had some chow mein, pizza & pasta from the asian & Mediterranean section. Everything there was really good! Next i tried mac & cheese, fried chicken & rice however it wasn't as good as i hoped. Sadly i only had a couple bites & put the rest aside. For dessert i tried sugar cookies and a mini cinnamon roll however both were really hard & i didn't finish my dessert either. I was happy with just eating what i did end up liking, however my appetite quickly went away when an employee was rude to me. I went to the pasta section & an elder male employee was standing behind the counter watching me. He didn't say one word. I noticed some penne pasta with tongs so i decided to serve myself some. Next thing i know, the man literally SNATCHES the tongs out of my hand & says its not for me to serve myself. I was so confused because The glass window was open so i figured i could serve myself. After all it is a buffet. He then tells me the pasta is cold & im supposed to ask them to cook it for me, and that he "forgot" to close the glass window so customers wouldn't serve themselves. The other end of the station had pasta sauces & the windows were open as well so im confused, did he forget to close those too? I didn't appreciate his attitude or the way he went about stopping me. It was very embarrassing & very rude. Instead of standing there staring & snatching away the tongs, i would have appreciated if he asked me nicely if i needed a pasta put together Or politely brought to my attention that i couldn't serve myself there. As a business owner myself, i know there are definitely better & nicer ways to approach a customer when they are doing something incorrectly.

text:
I placed an order online while at work, and set the time for pickup at 4:30pm. I paid online at the time I ordered, and tipped too. When I pulled up at exactly 4:30 on my way home from work on a Friday, the order was ready.

I ordered the pasta with marinara sauce, and the chicken piccata, which both came with your choice of garlic bread or garlic knots, and a salad. You can also choose the type of pasta you want with any pasta dish, with the choices being spaghetti, fettuccine, and rigatoni (which was technically ziti, but I'm not that picky).

Both dishes were made exactly as ordered. The marinara was really great! I was expecting the super metallic chunky sauce I've come to expect from take out places, but the sauce was smooth and tasty. The garlic bread was great, and the salad wasn't bad either. My boyfriend enjoyed his chicken piccata as well.

Portion sizes were great. Prices are a bit high for take out Italian food, but you get a lot of food for your money. I look forward to ordering from here again!

text:
The food was good but the service was very poor. Upon entering the restaurant, my wife and I were seated and had to wait several minutes for our server to arrive. When she did arrive, she complained openly about other tables that she had. I have worked in customer service and realize people can be difficult, and even expressed sympathy, but I found her behavior to be a bit unprofessional. 

My wife and I had questions about the menu and when we asked the server, she rudely cut us off and seemed irritated that we were asking questions. I should have just left then but since we had made a reservation and the place was recommended, we stayed. I ordered a Hurricane and it took nearly 15 minutes for the drink to arrive. The server was also very pushy when I ordered the drink; requesting that we order the entire meal immediately with our drink orders. 

The food itself was very good and filling. Once we did get the food, our server was no where to be found. She never checked on us and I had to flag her down from across the restaurant to get a simple water refill. We were not offered boxes, drink refills (water or cocktails), and I had to flag our server down again for the check. 

As far as service in a restaurant goes, I am really not that hard to please. Keep my drinks full, check on me from time to time, and answer any questions I have about the menu and I'll gladly tip well, come back, and even recommend the place to friends. Our server did none of that. With so many good places to eat in New Orleans, I'd skip this one if you're thinking about it.
name: W

text:
Walking the French quarter and decided to drop in for a late night dinner. We were greeted at the door, and seated quickly- no wait. The service was great, super friendly and quick to take our drink order. 

I ordered a Bloody Mary, the vodka is in a vessel on the counter steeping with olives and sun dried tomatoes- it was delicious! My friend ordered the hurricane, sweet but he had to try a staple of New Orleans. We started with the alligator and the charbroiled oysters. Both equally delicious, I definitely preferred the oysters to the alligator but I've had alligator before, and it's like fried chicken. For our entrees we had the sampler which came with a trio of soups and I ordered the shrimp po boi. The trio was good, a lot of rice, so very filling. And the the sandwich was delicious with perfectly fried shrimp, just lacked some sauce. I should of ask for tartar sauce. But came with fries, and on the sandwich itself lettuce, tomatoes and pickles. 

I'd stop in again, good food, friendly staff and super fast service! Win in my book!
name: Taryn

text: The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Nice little spot, decent portions too.
name: User

text: It looked better online than it did in person. Service was friendly, just kinda slow once the room filled up. A couple small things kept adding up. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Food was good and came out fast. Food was fresh and service was quick.
name: User

text: I'm addicted to this place. They sell the best Tacos!! They are delicious. Tamales and sopes too
name: Franciele

text: Wow! The bar is the PLACE to be my friends  Little Rickie (aka Rob), Rick and David are phenomenal! The service, craft cocktails and eats are top notch too! Feels like we have known these fellas forever! Thank you! Cheers to Sand Key!
name: Kristi

text: If you want your food on time don't come to this location. They never have it right, they never get it on time. Just be prepared to be disappointed. This place is ridiculous. And when they screw up they don't even offer to make it fully right. Maybe just half off.
name: Kyle

text: Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Nice little spot, decent portions too. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Food was good and came out fast. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait.
name: User

text: Today my work ordered catering service from the cafe. I was able to try the shredded pork with BBQ sauce w/ macaroni and cheese. Both food items were delicious and the catering menu is individualized with several options. I would definitely order again.
name: Tati

text:
This spot rocks! It's not located centrally in the city but it's close to Penns Lansing and what the quality of fish is awesome. 

Presentation is awesome and I love the chirashi deluxe bowl that I ordered. The oysters were a bit small but overall, their fish is really fresh with generous portion. 

I've been coming back again and again every time I visit Philly.
name: T

text:
