text:
Large well lit, colorful chairs.  Lots of TV's.  
Tableside fresh guacamole.  
Chils were warm but not thin.  Just ok.  Salsa was weak.  
Chicken Adoboro was ok.  Butterflied chicken breast was very thin and dry.  
My wife said fajitas were kind of bland.

text: This place is a must if you're only in STL for a short time. The line for lunch and dinner can be out the door and around be corner, so make sure to arrive early. The BBQ is fresh daily and absolutely delicious. I have not had a bad thing on the menu. But definitely get the grilled corn on the side - it is fantastic.
name: Emily

text:
Once in a while, I get the urge to try ordering lunch from a "new" spot - a place I haven't ordered from before. It's always a hit or a miss, but even with my handful of regular spots and countless failed lunch orders, I guess I'm a glutton for punishment since I decided to give Margaritas a shot.

For lunch, I ordered two things through GrubHub: the "Quesadilla Extravaganza" and an order of queso. The prices were pretty high ($12.99 for the quesadilla and a whopping $6.49 for queso), but I crossed my fingers for large portions and high quality, in exchange.

Instead, what I got was yet another "ah, why do I do this to myself.."

The quesadilla was definitely not an "extravaganza." It was a very meager quesadilla with what looked like half a spoonful of guacamole, lettuce and tomatoes smashed into the corner of the container. Inside the quesadilla, I struggled to find the cheese, which kind of defeats the purpose of a quesadilla. The meat (I got the braised beef) was cardboard dry. The only thing that was spot on was the sour cream.

The queso wasn't terrible (it came with a big bag of chips, at least), but for the price the amount that came (less than half the container, like someone started scooping some into it then forgot about it) left me kind of speechless.

Another lesson learned. Margaritas, never again.
name: Lexy

text: Absolutely love this place! I visited for the first time last night. The service and food is exceptional! My table enjoyed the sampler to start. If there is something on the sampler you don't want, you can substitute (we are not tofu people but gave it a try on the sampler this time). For dinner, we had the eggplant stack and pad Thai. Both delicious! Be advised-- they will ask you how spicy you want some of your dishes on a scale from 1-5. I love spicy food and asked for a 3. It was wayyyy too spicy for me. If you can't handle spice, go for a 1 or 2. For dessert, we shared the mango sorbet which was also very yummy. Overall, we had an excellent experience here. The owner is lovely and so is the other server we spoke to that night. They checked frequently to see if we were happy. We will be back for sure! Oh, and it's BYOB! There is a liquor store right next door for your convenience.
name: Meg

text:
We live several blocks away and were anxious to try Chez Ben. We went on Sunday for dinner and it did not disappoint. It's great for tourists in the historical area and has a French flair. The decor is spectacular and stunning inside the Renaissance hotel at 3rd and Chestnut. It was recently featured on ABC FYIPhilly show. It's sophisticated yet comfortable. 

Just a gorgeous and nice place to enjoy a cocktail, relax and have a great meal. Love the artwork on the walls and the Ben Franklin theme. 

The cocktails were delicious and imaginative and nice wine selection. The restaurant also has the adjoining cocktail lounge M Brown. 

We had scallops ceviche to start and my husband had wonderful French onion soup.

I also had the amazing roasted chicken. It is somehow crisp and juicy and pounded on the outside. Carrot purée and some tasty charred baby carrots. Never had anything quite like that. My husband had the roast lamb which came with some charred celery root squares that tasted somehow scrumptious. Pomme frites awesome. Many small plates and choices like burgers also. Open for breakfast lunch and dinner. Great coffee choices and desserts also available.
name: Mommy

text:
We joined the waitlist on yelp, so when we walked in we only waited 2 mins before we were sat. I love that when you order coffee you get a whole pot on the table, and it stayed hot the whole time! We started with the million dollar bacon which was a seasonal special, and it was delicious (wish it would have been a little more crispy)
My husband got the traditional breakfast with the chicken sausage, and I got the Tri-fecta with the pork sausage. The waffle with the berry compote was amazing! Incredibly airy and light. 
Our server Mwnyana was delightful and seemed to know every table she was taking care of! Will definitely return!

text: Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. A couple small things kept adding up. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait.

The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. The leftovers held up okay the next day..

Would probably stop in again if nearby. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon.

Maybe better dine-in than delivery, hard to tell. Food took a while and didnt really feel worth the wait. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Not sure though.

text: Not sure how this hotel was awarded 4-stars because it's nothing more than 2. Ok, I understand that the aesthetics are pretty nice, but honestly, most of the plants are dying. They aren't maintained very well at all. It's kind of hard to get good service around here. If you know you're a big facility and host numerous conventions, there should be enough staff to accommodate most people's needs. They have a smiley face button on the phones, and they are the "consider it done" buttons. They instruct you to hit that button if there is anything you need at all. And I mean anything. So my room was never cleaned two days in a row, and you guessed it. Both days I called "consider it done." Well, it wasn't done and to top it off, the person I spoke to on the first day gave me attitude. Don't advertise something you can't provide. It's called false advertisement. Next, my husband wanted something sweet, so we walked over to the gelato shop. There were 4 staff members there, and the one we had helping us just happened to be the rude one. All the other gals were sweet and inviting. It's unfortunate their good attitudes could not rub off in their snooty colleague. Another poor experience was when I tried to find a place to grab lunch at a normal lunch hour. Only the sushi and sports bars were open. Honestly, I wasn't in the mood for sushi or greasy bar food. Ended up not eating but I'm sure it was better that way because all the restaurants here are all under 3 stars. If you ask me if I'll come back, probably not. Not unless I have to for a convention. And even then, I might just find the nearest 5 star establishment and go there instead. Rant over.
name: Dina

text:
Very disappointing, I don't understand why everyone on Yelp (and the buzz on the streets) has a love affair with Fogo. All I ever hear is "fogo, go to fogo, every other rodizio place pales in comparison."

Tonight, it was a let down from the get-go. The valet parking? To be kind, it has "areas of opportunity." For one, chestnut st around here in midtown village can be a bit busy. Does this mean that Fogo had a crew of hustling valets working to clear the mess of double parked customer cars from the street? Of course not! We sat around for 15 minutes easily before they even acknowledged us to get the car. Then it was another 15 for them to get it from God knows where. We arrived before the rush (6:15 pm). When we left at 8pm, it was a straight up shit show at the valet stand. The guy acted entitled for a tip too. I had the nerve to hand him the ticket back before the tip, and the valet jumped the gun and made a passive aggressive remark to me before I handed him some cash. I don't appreciate that...it was frankly insulting. 

As for the food. It's very inconsistent. Well, what WAS consistent was them coming around with the cheap meats! We were offered some nasty looking pork Parmesan at least 4 times, as well as some cheap chicken and pork sausage combination. They also have a "pineapple chicken," that is extremely dry and tastes of nothing but salt. 

Some of the beef and lamb cuts were pure fat. I'm not exaggerating. It was a total waste. Inedible and disgusting. 

Others were good: the garlic steak had a good flavor and (the second time around) was cooked nice and rare. The lamb steak was also good and rare, but it was gamey. Good lamb isn't gamey...lamb chops were also gamey. My girlfriend loves lamb and she didn't eat them. I also enjoyed their top and bottom sirloins. The filet mignon didn't even taste like filet mignon, not properly cooked and not really tender. Girlfriend didn't like that either. 

The salad bar area is decent but nothing special: some good cheese and prosciutto, bacon, along with chickpeas that looked good, caprese salad, some fruit, and greens. Also smoked salmon/lox that were good. There's probably other stuff I'm forgetting. But you don't come here for the salad bar. 

Service was pretty good, although be careful that the gouchos don't squirt meat juice all over you. It seriously goes FLYING when they hack up the meat. The white table cloth had seas of juice and grease at meals end. Fortunately my clothes got spared as figured out mid-meal to lift up the plate near the goucho to accommodate their knife. 

One gentleman deserves extra credit, he didn't have any rare sirloin on his skewer, and he said he'd come back with some rare meat. I was skeptical but he was true to his word! Very impressive. 

Wine was decent but a rip off as usual. $13.50 for seven oaks Cabernet, which I recommend, very tasty. A bottle costs the same at your local package store. 

Ambiance is loud and pseudo upscale. Our serviettes did get folded for us when we got up once. That is a nice (unnecessary) touch you don't see at your local Olive Garden. We were probably served by a dozen different people easily. A bit chaotic and not relaxing at all. 

Fortunately, we each had a $25 off coupon that took away some of the sting. Pre-tip total with tax was a hair under $100 thanks to these. 

As someone mentioned, sign up for their e-club and you'll get a coupon in a few days. Do this before you go!! Also save money and have drinks before you go if you want to get buzzed and not go broke! 

So for a too long, didn't read: Come here once, get your coupons, say that you went, then head to Picanha in north philly for a far superior experience with regard to value for the money, unpretentious environs, easy stress-free parking, affordable dessert, and best of all: BYOB!
name: Will

text:
Such a waste of a good location. There is nothing good about this place. Hubby and I started with the spinach and artichoke dip, which our waiter recommended. Worst spinach dip I ever had. It literally tasted like cream... just cream with chunks of artichokes. I ordered the veggie pasta, which had so much oil from the pesto. I had to ask for extra marinara sauce just to balance it out. Lastly, babe ordered Alfredo which wasn't bad, but not "Olive Garden" great. 

Moral of the story... only come here if your craving pasta and olive garden and local Italian restaurants are packed with people.
name: Adrianna

text: After a long week, we opted to stay in and order delivery from Le Vera based solely on the GrubHub rating.  We were not disappointed.  I ordered the baked ziti, cheese bread, thin crust pizza and Old Bay fries.  The order arrived within the promised time and it was delicious.  The cheese bread was crispy with broiled cheese, so was the ziti.  The Old Bay fries were well seasoned. Next time I want to try some of the specialty pizzas or a calzone.  Great quality and price.

text:
A great place to go for a night with friends
Great food and just a totally relaxing place to hang
Servers are all friendly
A real sense of teamwork

text: They refused service 30 mins before closing time.  I was super excited to try the food and was famished from the long drive from other state

text: While the hotel is beautiful, our dining experience was shockingly horrible. The restaurant was pretty much empty but it took 15 minutes for our server to acknowledge us. Other guests in the restaurant were even commenting on how no one would help us. No one even asked if we wanted anything else besides water. I ordered the crab pasta and my dad ordered the gumbo. text: This was a delivery order on a night when I really did not want to cook. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. I wouldn't write it off, but I also wouldn't hype it up. It looked better online than it did in person.

text: Joes steaks and soda shop will always be called Chinks to me. their milkshakes are simple and delicious and you can smell the cheesesteaks while walking up to the door. this is a iconic stop for anyone who's looking for a great philly cheesesteak. seating is very limited. not sure of there hours but I do believe they close early, the neighborhood isn't what it used to be.

text: Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Overall, a strong experience. Food was fresh and service was quick. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Not bad for a quick meal.
name: User

text: Disheartened by the lack of service. The restaurant was not full at all, yet the hostess (older lady), attempted to sit us away form everyone else over by the window. I politely asked for a booth (just like everyone else). Once seated, and after 6 minutes, I had to stop a waiter and ask him who was servicing our table. Surprise, it happened to be him. Next, I asked if the pickel bar was for everyone. Surprise again, it was. (Why wouldnt he have told me that once he took our order??) After going to the pickle bar, I sat looking at my bowl for about 3 minutes.. Why? Because we we never given any place settings (mat, utensils, napkin). I had to yet AGAIN ask for it. Now the food arrives and less than 2 minutes later, the server placed our check in the middle of the table. Now, prior to our food arriving, I'd told him that I was going to also order something to-go. So, why would you give me my check?? I had to stop him a few times because he forgot to bring an item or a food item wasn't delivered, etc..... This experience was not welcoming at all, in fact, I felt as if my son and I were not wanted. Now I am not one the play the race card, but when we are the only people of color in the restaurant at that time and we receive lesser-than service, I couldn't help but think this. My 15yr old even noticed it. I didn't have to say a word. Especially when he says "Wow Mom, that table (of 5) got their food fast". I could only respond "I know". I cannot take anything away from the delicious food, however, the staff needs some work.
name: Kelly

text:
What a horrible experience. Took my parents and my niece and nephew at 2 and 7 years old for Mother's Day brunch. We were the first table seated when they opened at 8am because having two young children, we wanted to get in and out early. Once the first round of drinks came and the order was placed, we did not see the server again, at OUR table anyway. After seeing several other families get served (which were seated WELL after we were) our food finally came out a full hour after we arrived there. 4 of 5 entrees were cold and overcooked. Needless to say, everything was sent back. I finally had an opportunity to order another drink at this point and we proceeded to wait another 15 mins while our food was "re-made". The manager personally delivered the second round of food to the table only to find out that not only was the food cold and overcooked, again, but was most likely the same food we sent back initially just warmed up. At this point we were fed up. After over an hour with two children and no food, we left and went to a local restaurant where we were treated with class and professionalism and we were finally able to have a decent meal. Being a career restaurant manager, I understand the challenges of providing a quality experience, especially on a holiday, but also, I understand that with proper planning and preperation these days can be smooth and issue free. 
I would have left no star if I could. We will not be returning to this place again. Ever.
name: Blake

text: For some reason, the food was very bland. Everything I ordered taste the exact same Maybe the cook took advantage of happy hour! ‍
name: Delores

text:
Santa Barbara is super weak when it comes to their pho selection. THAT BEING SAID; Noodle City is the most fire pho place you will find in the area. I usually come around 12-3 and it's always decently busy. But when I get here, I know what I want and I order immediately. The wait is never too long and the pho is definitely pretty solid. I always get rare steak & well done brisket. 

Also, I'm usually straight FAMISHED when I get there. So I usually get the super bowl size. I believe it's less than $12 and they give you way more than their large size. Definitely worth. Enjoy the slurp.
name: Sheck

text:
It's been a couple of years since I've had lunch in the food court at the Bellevue, and if this is any indication of the quality of the restaurants I haven't really missed anything.  

I ordered a gyro lamb wrap on special, side salad, and a Coke.  The salad was the best part of the meal.   It was a decent portion, full of large chunks of peppers (maybe too large) and cucumber and feta.  A little heavy on the dressing, but good flavor and the vegetables were all crisp.

The gyro was a different story.   It was too large and overstuffed to really eat by hand, and the thin pita was falling apart from the loads of tzatziki sauce and other ingredients.  Worse, the lamb was burnt.  Defiantly a case of more not being better.

And the topper, I'm pretty sure I got Coke Zero instead of regular Coke, so I didn't even have the satisfaction of washing the taste out of my mouth.
name: Randy

text:
I've been to Tinto three times, most recently as a part of a bachelorette dinner, and two out of those three times I've been vegan. AND although there is nothing strictly vegan on the menu, I've nevertheless had excellent dining experiences on each visit. .

Tinto is probably more well known for meat and seafood, but they also make really yummy vegetables (that can be adjusted to be vegan - while still being delicious)! For my last visit I had veganized versions of a bean dish, mushrooms, and shaved brussel sprouts - they were all fantastic. The mushrooms are INCREDIBLE. They're some of the best mushrooms I've ever had, and I eat a lot of mushrooms. 

The non-vegans with me loved their meals as well - some highlights were the octopus, calamari sandwich, and duck and ham sandwich. 

Regardless of your dietary needs or preferences, tinto is a safe bet.
name: Aelita

text:
My wife and I had our anniversary dinner here  My wife had written a review where she was rather critical with the set up in the service due to the unfortunate circumstance of her veal scallopini coming out cold which was immediately rectified.

I received a call from Christian the general manager who had read the review and was quite concerned about its content And justifiably he did an outstanding recap of the evening And clarified what had happened he was most apologetic and for the general manager of an establishment to take time out of his busy day and call me personally to discuss the review says a great deal to me about how much they very much care about their reviews and the reputation of the restaurant.
Based upon this conversation I will most certainly be bringing my wife backTo show her that this is indeed a very high quality and one of the better restaurants in Nashville..

 Every restaurant may have an off night however having spent a year in Italy for business I will say that the menu and the food match up extremely well with what I had while I was in Italy and I look forward to seeing Christian again and enjoying another fine meal here as well as recommending this place to all of my business associates.

text: Really tasty home cooking. Big portion with mama in the kitchen. I will go back. Get a menu so you know what the daily specials are.  If you are looking for home cooking this is one of the best in NOLA

text: It had been a few years since we had been here, but it has only gotten better.  Started with a caprese salad. Was delicious and the size was shareable. Next a garden salad that comes with the entrees. Excellent and dressed well with balsamic.  My wife had the angle hair spaghetti with tasty meatballs.  I had a pasta dish with chicken, shrimp, buttery sauce with garlic, tomato's, broccoli and wonderful spices. Yum.  This restaurant is tucked into a quiet area of Broad Ripple.  Outside dining this summer night was perfect, but it was cooler than some summer evenings.  Inside of this house is welcoming and charming. Sign in by the fireplace and wait. They don't take reservations for small groups or couples.  Wait was about 15 mins. on a busy Friday.  So glad we returned.  Our waiter BJ was professional and knowledgeable.  Great service made the meal even more enjoyable.

text:
The venue: Loads of fun! This is like an adult version of Chuck-E-Cheese. There are all kinds of arcade games, you can win tickets to trade for prizes, and there are adult beverages to help you loosen up and help your inner child go bananas.

The food: Meh. Just... meh. I really wasn't impressed by anything I had, but I won't deny it's a good deal to grab dinner and a game card. If you go that route, be sure to ask them to "super charge" it (adds a small fee, but also more points to your play card).

Overall? Not bad. I had a good time. It's a fun distraction if you're in the area, particularly if you have a group of friends with you. 

I think the experience is worthwhile, even if the food isn't.

text: Stumbled into this by accident and was very pleased with the food and service.  Their menu was extensive and had non sushi food choices.

The sushi is always fresh and so tasty.  We've tried many different menu items and don't have one complaint. We love the special rolls, shrimp shumai, Kani salad and the poke bowls are the best ! text:
I've been coming to Honeybaked Ham for years and I don't recall this particular franchise being dirty. Then again I don't really stay to eat, I grab my food to go. But recently I did stay and eat with a friend and didn't see anything wrong.  One of the workers can seem pretty rude at times.

text:
We saw the commercial about $1.69 chicken fries and literally got up and started our way to Burger King. We got there and ordered our 5 boxes of chicken fries and the lady over the intercom rudely commented "I have to cook them so you're gonna have to park." We didn't think anything of it. Just said thanks for the heads up but we still want them.
By the time we got to the window, we had remembered that we wanted 7 boxes instead of 5. I have worked in the food industry so I can understand how frustrating it is when people do this but the BK was empty and there weren't more than 3 cars (including us) in the drive thru so we asked if we could add 2 boxes. The lady looked at us and VERY rudely remarked "You're gonna have to drive back through the line because we cook them to order." We were so taken back that this woman spoke to us like that and then it got worse.
When she had finished putting all the food and sauce in the bag, she just stuck it out the window and handed it to us. Not a single thank you, not a single have a great night. 
We are very reasonable people and understand when someone has a bad day, it alters their mood. However, there was absolutely no excuse for the way this woman treated us tonight. Will not be returning.

text:

I got the beignets and my mother took home the jambalaya. I'm used to light, puffy and fluffy beignets and these left more to be desired. The taste reminded me of a sugar-free coffee roll - mostly just cinnamon and pretty dull. My mom seemed to like them though.

text:
Visited the area, and had a taste for BM. Normally BM always delivers. The food is normally fresh and tasty with very nice portions. Today was clearly not the case. Once we entered, the manager was pushing their "new" rotisserie Marsala chicken. It looked good on the picture! So we jumped right in. Our order came out timely as normal. We sat down, and at first, it looked really good. Then I noticed the  cuts were "REALLY" small. Almost Cornish hen size. 

Maybe it was just small chickens. No worries, so I bite in and immediately noticed not only were the cuts small, but very old. It was very very chewy. I removed the sauce and found that in fact it was old, days old.

So out of respect for the establishment, I went up and requested to speak to the manager. I asked he come to my table to speak privately. After waiting 20 min at a chicken joint, I went up again, this time a bit pissed. I requested him a 2nd time. He didn't show AT ALL! He sent his assistant Manager.  She was pleasant and extremely helpful. I told her I have been eating chicken for a looooong time and I know when it's not as fresh as it should be. she apologized and took care of us immediately. The first order was so bad, I tossed it in the trash receptacle. BM, you need to remove the manager, he doesn't understand customer's come first. Rose deserves the opportunity to make it right the first time. The problem is, I normally never complain, this had to be said. BM will be liable for making someone sick selling them old chicken. I believe it's a violation of the OSHA law. If you expect better, you must do better.  Give your customer's what they pay for.
name: Johnathan

text:
