text: We've been here many times. It's very convenient and close to home. I love how open it is and we're always able to put tables together to accommodate larger groups. The food is decent, nothing special, but pretty good. The owner is very nice and he's always busy helping the staff bus tables, seat guests, and run food. That being said, the reason for only three stars is because of the service. Almost every time I've been there, we wait a very long time for a server. It seems like they are very under staffed, or they have a bad seating system, sometimes ignoring us all together!  The servers hardly ever know what is on tap, they usually let us look at their "cheat sheet" in their server book. They are always very nice, but in my opinion under trained. We will most likely be back because of the convenience and atmosphere, but hopefully we will get better service!
name: Lauren

text: Meh. We ordered the loaded potato appetizer and it was ok but very under seasoned and completely underwhelming. I had the shrimp entree and the honey siracha sauce + the shrimp was delicious, but the rice served with it was incredibly bland. I expected something more unique and enticing for hype and price.
name: Patty

text:
UPDSTES YELPERS ay bottom. 

It is so exciting to have a great dining restaurant on the north side of Tucson. What a pleasure to see this treasure. I came to share in an anniversary dinner with colleagues. And I'm so glad I did. 

When one enters the restaurant, one notices the details of tiles, a large water feature and elegant furniture. But what is more, the owners themselves come and greet you. Once we were seated, the waitstaff brings a plate of fresh herbs and flatbreads. They explain how to prepare the breads with the butter and herbs. 

We shared several of the combination appetizers. The plate consisted of some Greek salad, fresh sliced tomatoes, hummus, olives, dolmas, and a small pickled salad. Everything was fresh and quite tasty. Most of us filled the items into our flatbread or later onto rice. 

For the main dishes, there was lamb kabobs, marinated chicken, plenty of vegetarian dishes and more. I had an eggplant dish with toasted onions. Mine was delicious, but mushy like baba ganoush.  My partner ordered a vegetarian rice with mush and other vegetables. Her's was a main dish, but we both agreed although it was good, it was more like a side. 

With the atmosphere, the kindness of the owners, I am the lovely ambience, we can't wait to come back and try this place one more time. It's like a hidden treasure with more treasures to find.

UPDATE: Just went there on Saturday. I can't even begin to understand exactly what happened. My partner asked if they excepted a Groupon and the lady at the reception said not on Saturdays. Then instead of asking if we wanted to come on in and eat she just stood there. My partner was beginning to get irritated to say the least, and so I asked if we could eat anyway? It still took her a moment before she would see at us. From my experience of teaching culture and grammar at Pima College I thought maybe it was some cultural misunderstanding between us all. Then after we ordered, the waitress brought out the wrong plate. She had requested a side of rice along with some vegetables that are cooked and spices. I had ordered a sampler appetizer platter for us to share, but what came out was a huge platter of rice and meat. When my partner tried to explain, the waitress argued that she had told her it was a combo platter. But my partner told her she understood the waitress to mean her vegetables would come on a platter with the rice. Then she asked where my appetizers were. Again, the waitress said I never ordered it. But I said to the waitress Yes I did as I asked for extra basil. She told me she misunderstood. She whisked away the meat in exasperation; and left to get hot rice leaving my partner's veggies. No I was afraid my partner would have called vegetables with hot rice. All this confusion, and I paid three dollars extra for a sprig of basil. Also, to top it off, you can tell from the photos but this place looks beautiful. Also, under the name the subtitle says "Fine dining". However, I did include a few pics from the female restroom. For being a fine dining establishment these touches we're not very fine to this customer. I hope it changes on both the service, overall reception, and the final decor touches.
name: Jodi

text: I've eaten here numerous times over the course of a few years and the food has only gotten better. I used to get the Napa salad (which is no longer on the menu) and truffle fries- the literal best things I've ever tasted. Yesterday, I tried something new: the California Burger Bowl, and I substituted a veggie burger (I'm a vegetarian) with grilled jalapeños instead of mushrooms and tomatoes instead of avocado. So. Good! It was the perfect portion too. I will definitely be coming back every time I'm in town just for this. As far as I remember the milkshakes are really good too and well priced, especially for the size. Overall, it's a nice atmosphere for a casual lunch or dinner. In my opinion, Fox restaurants are some of the best in AZ.

text:
We had a great time, and excellent service. All food items were fresh, unique, and high quality. Nothing appeared to be pre-made,
Except for the ice cream which was exceptionally good. The waitress was very sweet and friendly

text: OMG we are new to the state and came across this gem of a restaurant. Upon entry we were greeted right away with only a short wait time (though it gets pretty crowded and the wait can be long) our wait staff was amazing and didn't steer us wrong with the steak omelette! I also had a waffle light and fluffy my son had the French toast which he loved. The restaurant was CLEAN by the way. We will definitely make this our breakfast spot.
name: H.

text:
One word : BRUNCH
You just gotta try the brunch. Never have I eaten so much high quality food for such a low price... I died and went to brunch heaven. 
And waiter Julian is surely the angel of this brunch heaven. The service was stellar. Our rowdy hungry party of 10 didn't faze him at all. He took all our request and even separate check in stride. Kudos Julian. Psst management, give the man a raise...

So you can choose any and all items on the brunch menu's right side and at any quantity you like. We tried about everything, except the beef or fish  tacos... and oversight on our part. All the tacos are quite small, but you can have as many as you want, so it's all good. 

Chips and fire-roasted salsa: The chips are awesome, seem to be made in house. Not a huge fan of the salsa as I like mine a bit chunkier, but it is tasty.

Breakfast Tlayuda: When they say giant crispy tostada, they mean giant. That thing had to be 15 or more inches across. It reminded me of a breakfast pizza with a nice thin crispy bottom. Lots of toppings and the flavors play well together. A must have.

Sweet corn tamales: I'm not a big tamale fan, but the rest of my crew found these to be delicious. 

Queso Fundido: Damned that stuff is delicious... yeah, I said damned... a big bowl of melted cheese that is a little crispy on the edges, a few flour tortillas and some salsa... you can add stuff like chorizo or mushrooms, but it really doesn't need anything else... I enjoyed the cheese on my chips, but it would taste great on anything. 

Adobo chicken tacos:nicely seasoned chicken and all the fixins... yummy

Cauliflower carnitas tacos: Good, but not our favorites

Al Pastor tacos: yummy, one of my personal favorites

Cholita Benedict: Deemed very good taste wise, only drawback was the Hollandaise was a bit too thin, it could have been a bit creamier

Mexican chocolate waffle: a favorite of the entire table, served nice and hot and so chocolaty

Cholita chilaquiles: i wish ii would have discovered those earlier into the meal. By the time I got around to these I was already quite full or I would have had a ton more of these. The crispy chips with all those toppings and the perfectly flavored pork carnitas was like a party in my mouth.

Mexican street corn: yes,  you must have some of this. Simply delicious. 

Bacon wrapped hot dog: I was a little surprised that this is a taco. I didn't care for the beans in there, but the rest was yummy. I mean how could you go wrong with bacon wrapped anything? 

Mexican style crispy chicken Milanese sliders: this one will surprise you as it is quite spicy. Tasty, but spicy. 

Cinnamon spiced churros: Piping hot, crunchy on the outside, soft on the inside...num num... I would like to have a bit more sauce with it to dip it in. Yes there is some decorating the plate, but I like to dip them. 

And don't forget the libations to go with your brunch. We indulged in margaritas, of course, which you can get by the pitcher, if you are serious drinkers like we are. 

I highly recommend trying the different flavors of mimosas (passion fruit for the sweet folks and pomegranate for those less sweet) and then there are the Bloody Marias... 

And as if we needed more food, we ordered a round of guacamole and chips , which ... you guessed it... was also delicious. Freshly made, nice flavor and with little chunks in it. 

Needless to say, our entire party will be back. I am  pretty sure they will raise their prices on the brunch soon, as they cannot possibly be making money this way... I am just happy that I got to experience such a fabulous meal.
name: Sigrid

text:
BEST BREAKFAST BURRITO. 
Beware this place is crazy good... and slightly addictive. It's DANGEROUS how good their food is. I get the carnitas breakfast burrito every.single.time. It is THAT good!!

A spinach tortilla filled with delicious fall apart carnitas, fresh avocado, green chilies, cheesy goodness, potatoes, and sour cream! It has a nice char on the outside and just melts in your mouth. 

I crave it everyday, and can't go a week without it. It's enormous and usually feeds two people or makes for a good breakfast and lunch! I could go on and on with other amazing dishes, but it's a MUST TRY!

text: This is the kind of fun, family friendly place we need more of in the Heights.  It can be enjoyed by those with kids, for date night, or to catch a game on the big screen.  We also really enjoyed the fresh, quality ingredients and creative takes on bar food.  I'd definitely recommend to all.

text:
I had a to a double take when I first walked toward it. Down a sort of back alley street in center city, you come upon what looks like a row home that has been made into a quaint bar.
They have a really nice, extensive cocktail menu and it generally is not too crowded during the week, so can be a really great date/catchup spot if you are looking to meet up. It is definitely better to visit in the summer when there is a little bit of outdoor seating and they can open the window in the front, because this is a SMALL venue downstairs, I mean it really cannot hold many people otherwise.
There is a nice upstairs lounge but again this is small and can fill up quickly.
Overall- I think its a nice chill off the beaten path spot, just don't expect to go with a large group.
name: Joshua

text: Went with family on a Sunday and it was louder than I expected. Food was fresh and service was quick. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Overall, a strong experience. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything..

text:

text: 2 stars for atmosphere, location, and sometimes you get an exceptional meal & service. I have had very unprofessional experiences with staff at this location. The server was not trained well, the timing was off, sides incorrect or missing, steaks cooked incorrectly and missing the requesting condiments. I was very embarrassed after raving about how this was one of the best places in town. I have not been back and do not intend to return for business purposes after that expereince. There were obvious issues with this experience and it was not acknowledged by the establishment (perhaps the server was trying to hide it?). I have had some of the best meals at this location to return and experienced a mediocre version at best. The manager at the new location on 54 was very accommodating after this experience when the Oldsmar location could not accommodate. I previously gave a lot of support to Flamestone, rooting for the underdog as a family owned restaurant. I hope that this feedback is valuable for the continued and future success of Flamestone.

text: A must when in the French Quarters! This place was amazing! This place is going to become a staple of New Orleans if they keep doing what they are doing right now. Service was amazing. From the guy taking names outside to the waiters and bartenders. Everyone is on point and ready to serve the customers. We came once and had to come again our last night and we were not disappointed. Nicolette was our server and she was awesome. So informative she steered us in the right way on what to order with her great suggestions. We were very satisfied with our orders and we all ordered different things. The oysters are a must so delicious. The New Orleans trio was so yummy. The gumbo was my favorite and of course you can't go wrong with an all American cheeseburger for the kids. We're from NY so we know good burgers and my son said theirs was a very good burger. So yes young and old will be satisfied at Mambos. You must give them a try they are soon going to become just as popular as the other surrounding restaurants. We'll soon be waiting 2 hours outside to eat here - so yeah give them a try while they're still new and not so touristy!! This place is definitely making good food and providing even better service. Which is not an easy to come by combo in New Orleans, at least from our experience, but Mambos is doing both very well!! Oh drinks are good too.
name: Jennifer

text: Great place, delicious food, great service! Will return and use as my Thai food carryout also!

text: My Chinese spouse requested the roasted pork and eggplant  without added sugar. When my pork and broccoli arrived, they told us their dishes all had added sugar as the Chinese fare had been 'Americanized', so my wife ordered a beef noodle pho dish instead. It was to her liking, and my pork was ok, though the broccoli was actually cooked perfectly. It was still crunchy, but not cold. The decor and excellent service contribute strongly to the overall 'Good' rating.

text:
Been back a couple of times lately and found a couple of new good things for our tastes. In the winter, Geri's soups are wonderful, flavorful and not over salted. Also, her hot dogs are the best in Eagle. Since I am on a low salt diet, I can share a hotdog and not OD.

They also have beer now and when the weather gets better, I plan to have an order of her French fries and a beer in the sun outside. Their fries are the best. Also try the onion rings as a side with a dog or sandwich, some of the best rings around. 

They still serve breakfasts on Saturdays only and for corned beef hash made fresh this is the place to go.

text: I came to dine in on 9/10/2018 at 8:30pm. Looks like they were closing up soon. They ran out of chili and barely anyone staffed. I waited about good 8-10 minutes before I was greeted. We had eye contacts, but no one is stepping up to take my order. I was patient. I didn't want any spit in my food.  I got nice hot fries but my burger was cold and bloody bun. I thought it was juicy burger, but the meat was still cold in the middle. I went home and sat on the toilet for good while. Unfortunately, they didn't give me my receipt.

text: Fantastic and interesting drink choices and wide variety of delicious food! Definitely something for everyone!

text: Not saying it's perfect, but some reviews make it sound way worse than it is. The food was good and the service was easygoing. The staff seemed tired but still polite. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Food was good and came out fast.

text:
Went for Tuesday lunch.  Service was good despite looking incredibly busy.
Chips and salsa quite good.  Side of guac OK.  Could use a little more onion and garlic.   
I had a fish, shrimp and crunchy pork taco.  The fish started a little fishy and the a little overwhelmed by the pickled onion and the same with the shrimp.  The crunchy pork was tasty but minimal bite.  Beans were good.
My wife had chicken and steak.  She thought the steak was good but the pollo loco was bland. Service took a 2 rating to 3.  
The room was also very dark.  Hard to read the menu.

text: This place was a gem! Came here with my boyfriend prior to the Cirque Du Soleil VOLTA show. I got the limited time shrimp bowl with rice, beans, avocado, shrimp, lettuce, and tomatoes. I don't like beans so next time I will get it without beans but that is a personal preference. Everything was delicious!! I also tried the mango lime agua fresca which was so refreshing! The prices are reasonable for the quality of food that you are getting. Very nice atmosphere. My favorite part was that they seem to be very environmentally conscious. Would definitely recommend!

text:

So she calls back when she was told to and books our office group in for a lunch at the ThreeTen restaurant, bowling and axe throwing. Well, fast forward to the day of our team building event and she gets an Email...that's right...not a phone call, but an Email stating that our booking has been cancelled due to their Toronto sales team being in town or something to that affect. Oh, so you bump a group of paying customers, who were going to be there all day eating and drinking and partaking in your activities, to accommodate employees instead? Cool cool.

The pizza came in a timely manner, but there was not ANY tomato sauce on the pizza.  I am from New York, and thus  VERY familiar with classic food adaptations.  But this was just leaving one ingredient --TOMATO SAUCE-- out!

We had a bad phone connection and so she may have missed my order of a Margherita pizza with "tomato sauce and cheese."  AND she did read the order back to me, saying "Margherita pizza" and I DID assume she had heard my original order.  BUT if you are going to change a CLASSIC pizza recipe by leaving out a critical ingredient--I think it would be best to specify this. text:
I was excited to try Cleo's Bodega & Cafe after reading Richard P.'s excellent, and detailed, review. This area has struggled so after the local grocery store closed and this Bodega brings some much needed relief. I have friends in this area and hear often of the impact not having a convenient grocery store has taken. Now folks have some relief with this wonderful option of both a Cafe and mini grocery store plus it offers employment through the Flanner House.

Cleo's is very easy to find with street parking or a small lot on the North side of the building. A huge mural is painted on the North side of the building and easily seen. As you enter through the left door you turn left for the Cafe or right to go through the door for the grocery store.

The Cafe is bright with natural lighting, a cheerful atmosphere and very clean with several dine in tables. The free customer Wifi user name and password is taped to the end of the table. A wonderful pergola covered outdoor deck provides additional seating overlooking the new Flanner House greenspace. 

Display cases are filled with pastries (Crossiant, muffins, cookies, danish), parfaits, beverages and snacks (granola bars, chips). The menu is located on the order counter and consist of Smoothies and Coffee flavors. I was told today they expanded the menu and are now serving sandwiches. The new menu wasn't printed yet but sounded as if it's a perfect addition to bring more patrons in the doors. They serve Tinker House coffee and offer 8 types of Smoothies including build your own. The counter staff was super friendly, worked well together and happy to answer questions. I ordered the Helly Smoothie with strawberry, blueberry, raspberries, blackberries, vanilla yogurt and orange juice. It only took a few minutes to prepare, ice cold and reasonably priced. Lots of berry seeds, which I'm not a fan of, and Ken mentioned in his review. I worked around them as the Smoothie was very refreshing and flavorful. Maybe next time I'll make my own with a maximum of 5 ingredients.

The other half of the building is the Bodega or Under the Sun Discount Market. It is the perfect size for this location. The isles are wide enough, the shelves were clean, well organized and grouped accordingly. You'll find daily $1 general merchandise bins. They use a simple pricing, color-coded method ranging from 50 cent (no sticker) to $1 (black), $2 (blue), $4 (green), $6 (red) marked in the bar code area. Some of the bulk items run more than $6 but most things are $6 or less. They also have a weekly staple schedule so you can be assured your staple is available. 

I found fresh veggies from the Flanner House, Urban Farmers and others, dairy products, fresh meats, bread, spaghetti sauce, canned meats, cake mixes, cereal, pastas, and many more packaged foods. A very nice variety for a small grocery. The staff was extremely friendly and helpful explaining pricing and the weekly staple schedule. 

Offering employment opportunities, a friendly cafe offering sandwiches, smoothies, coffee and snacks to a much needed Bodega in this food desert area. Definitely stop in if you're in the area.
name: Wanda

text:
Bridge Tap House was lovely! I had been a few times before, but only for drinks. Happy to finally try the food!

For my meal, I got the grilled cheese and tomato soup. The soup was up there for great tomato soups - on the chunkier/thick side and very flavorful. The grilled cheese was good, but not my favorite. It was a bit squishy, and didn't love the tomato jelly with it, but that is just a personal preference. 

Loved the ambiance and the aesthetic, and parking wasn't too bad for being downtown. 

One thing I thought was a bit wonky is that they have a Pad Thai on the menu, but the ingredients look more like a Pad Thai/ Curry mash up. Thought it was a strange food item for such an American restaurant, and didn't really appear to be true Pad Thai. 

Will be back!

text:
It was just...mediocre. I went with a group of six for dinner, and for starters, our service was incredibly slow. Like we're talking 20 minutes to get a bottled beer and never refill the water glass kind of slow. I ordered the osso bucco, which was decent, but a little too heavy on the mushrooms for my taste (just my taste. It was fine). The meat was tender and my fork sliced through it like butter. The mashed potatoes were nothing to write home about though. They're clearly in-house, but lacked any substantial flavor and the texture was all off (pro tip: put egg yolks in to finish and that'll fix your problem potatoes, make them richer, and they'll hold up under the sauce without turning to potato soup). Initially my food did not come, but the runner didn't explain why I was sitting there without a plate. Eventually they told us that osso bucco looks a lot like beef Manhattan (what? Lies) and the expo grabbed the wrong plate. It showed up a bit later, but that was awkward. My boyfriend got the pork ribeye (what part of the pig that is remains a question), and one slice was completely rare. If in six months he tells me he has a prion eating his brain, I won't be surprised (that's sarcasm. Relax. Pigs are prion resistant). The folks who ordered the fish and chips were pleased, but they ordered slaw and tartar sauce, and that took several minutes to come out even though it was requested with the order. We ordered dessert because they do offer reasonable portion sizes, and also dinner took three hours, so we were basically hungry again. Rave reviews came from those who ordered the cookie with ice cream and the pecan pie. I, however, screwed up and asked for peanut butter pie. It was a gelatinous heap of barely peanut butter flavored and excessively sugary goo with a dollop of cream on top and a rubbery, chewy, puffed up and not even slightly flaky crust. 

As for the atmosphere, the decor was cool. The exposed metal ceilings are very high and the floor is painted concrete, and the walls have barn wood. We had to yell at each other all evening because the wood was the only thing to dampen the sound. We were also unpleasantly dealing with blinding sun whenever the door opened. 

Overall, it was stressful, crowded, slow, and my chair was continuously bumped. I'm looking forward to never going back.

text:
