When they did come over, I could not understand a word they said for the life of me, so I was never really sure what I was getting. 

I left this place still feeling hungry. To be fair, that's to be expected when you spit half your food out. A few of the dumplings were ok. The others left me wondering what the heck I just ate. I'm not sure the sweet and sour chicken was actually chicken. I've carved quite a few chickens in my life, and I still cannot figure out which part of the bird that came from (rest in peace kitty?). It was mostly chewy, bony and just overall inedible. I munched on bok choy for pretty much the rest of the time we were there. It was the safest bet. I will not be back.

EDIT: I went here a few years ago and for some reason this didn't post hence the recent date.
name: Jill

text: Customer service was terrible. We asked the Host if we could sit at the bar and he put us at a hightop instead. We found out after getting to the hightop that the happy hour only applied if you're sitting at the bar. We ordered the cocktail of the day and it was hardly drinkable. We ordered the nachos as well and got hardly edible pork rinds with gross fake cheese sauce. I had very high hopes for this place and was seriously let down.
name: Charlotte

text: it was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Not bad for a quick meal. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. No big complaints, just a nice meal. For the price I expected more than this. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. The leftovers held up okay the next day..
name: User

text: Stopped here for lunch on our way out of town. Thoroughly enjoyed our meal. Had a tough time making up my mind and settled on YOLO, fried egg over fried chicken over biscuits and gravy. Very good. My wife enjoyed here Northwest salad as well. Will be back next in or through SB.
name: Timothy

text: The best Döner Kebab I've had in a long time, and I was just in Germany last year. There's a place near where I live called Döner Bistro that hype up their German imbiss style Döner and the Döner at Yiro Giro blows it out of the water. I'd like to kidnap the owners of that establishment and fly them to St. Louis where they will be trained in the school of Yiro Giro. It's a crime this place is only open for lunch on weekdays but downtown St. Louis seems pretty dead so I guess it makes sense.
name: Joseph

text: I'm more of a wine gal, but this place is all about the cocktails. Prices are reasonable for craft cocktails, with many in the $9-10 range. The menu is extensive, but luckily, my bartender knew his stuff and made me a WISCONSIN OLD FASHIONED, BRANDY SWEET. This is a big deal, people. He muddled up some fancy cherries and an orange with a sugar cube, threw in the bitters, mixed in a heaping shot of brandy brandy, and a good splash of soda on top; even topping it off with an orange and a gorgeous cherry garnish. It was definitely the closest I've had to a perfect Wisco drink since moving here last Spring, and now I know where I can go to get my fix. It was popping on a weeknight after work, and the place it small, so definitely arrive early if you have a group!
name: Kelly

text: Little Fish is an absolute gem of a restaurant.  They only serve fish and outstanding desserts.   My wife and I tried both the scallops and tuna starters. We had the tuna main which was served with a risotto and was outstanding.   LF is a BYOB and the total cost is well under $100, and a bargain at that.  The servers were amazing the the open kitchen is a highlight.
name: Brad

text: I'm an Eggs Benedict snob and, as such,  often disappointed. Eva's was as outstanding as the service. I love everything about this neighborhood treasure..
name: Melanie

text: Love this joint, great burgers better people and the milk shakes are to die for. I've been here many times and not once has it disappointed me. Love the wings.
name: Patricia

text:
A sushi lover's dream -- all-you-can-eat for a price you just can't beat! The menu offers an incredible variety of sushi rolls, with combinations that are creative and flavorful. From the very complex to the very basic, the fresh sashimi is a great way to go if you prefer more simple and delicate flavors. Having side options of soups and salads is also nice before or in between the sushi courses.

Even though it's hard not to just keep ordering delicious, endless sushi, I always save room for a little mochi ice cream for dessert. While dessert is one of the few things not included in the all-you-can-eat price, I don't mind considering how great the value is for the rest of the meal.
name: Carla

text: It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. The food was good and the service was easygoing. You can tell they care about customer experience here. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Would return. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Ordered a few things and liked most of it.
name: User

text: Not saying it's perfect, but some reviews make it sound way worse than it is. Food was fresh and service was quick. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. It was crowded but still moved along. Maybe expectations are just off for some people. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Food was fresh and service was quick. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait.
name: User

text: For the love of God, please get new tables haha!!  Having "sticky feeling" tables feels dirty.   But Great Place with Great Food!  Some of the best potatoes out there!!!
name: Anthony

text: Are they making the pizzas from a bunch of flower?? Talk about s l o w!! We ordered our pizza a half hour ago!! When is it going to get here??? Seriously!! I'm hungry!! I love pizza!!! When is it going to be cooked?? If you want your meal before you starve don't come here!! You'll die before you get it!! Slow service.
name: Alan

text: Food was cold and undercooked. Very small portion for a lot of money. Our waiter also kept leaving before we could finish talking to him.
name: Mary

text: Food was great, I will never however when I saw a mouse run a cross the floor by the bar.... Get a pest control company....
name: Ranae

text:
Whatever you're doing, put it down and go to this place immediately. Get the homemade tacos. Get all of them and pick your favorite. They're amazing! These tacos are served in a homemade tortilla, each meat is perfectly cooked and not greasy, over spiced or anything bad. Each is served with cilantro, onion and a lime wedge which only brings out the flavor even more. Also, try their red or green hot sauces for extra kick and flavor. 

Ok so the decor is very much like a typical Mexican place, but very humble and not flashy. The staff was friendly! So happy to have a great place in Smyrna like this one!!! We will be back!!!!
name: Mark

text: We made the mistake of coming in for dinner without a reservation on a night when there was multiple conventions in town and at the start of Mardi Gras week. We were able to sit at the bar to dine, but the restaurant staff were hurriedly trying to get orders out and the only bartender, who happened to be our waiter too, was struggling to keep up. I commend him for doing the absolute best he could under the circumstances, but unfortunately we were lacking a little bit of the level of service you'd be used to in this kind of restaurant.  The food was good, but nothing really special. I ordered the pork chop and it was MASSIVE. I appreciate them trying to provide a large portion size for the value, but I wish it wasn't so largely intimidating. My entree was also supposed to come with potatoes, and did not. I didn't realize it until after we had finished our meal though. Overall the flavors were good and the atmosphere would probably be nice if you were seated at a table, but this is not the best food I've had so far in New Orleans and I expected a little more out of this restaurant.
name: Kelsi

text: Went to sharkeez for the happy hour and I ended up falling in love with the bartender Elliot! He's awesome and paid us extra attention. Will definitely be back!!
name: Datoine

text:
The advertisements all over the store says "Chinese Restaurant" but inside, it is 100% Korean. 
All the servers, words, dishes, style, is all Korean. 

The food is good. 

Our server was a young Korean girl that was super rude, never checked on us, doesn't speak English, and messed up our payment. 
It was easy to tell she didn't know what she was doing. Most likely racist. 

If you are an Asian but not Korean, you better hope you don't get her as your server.
name: Zeta

text: Ordered takeout because I didn't feel like cooking and it held up okay. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed.
name: User

text: It's difficult to find good pho in the central coast, but this place is one of the best around! I drive from Santa Barbara for my bowl of pho regularly. It's good, affordable, the location is always clean, the staff is friendly, and there's never an issue with parking. They're also really good about giving you extra veggies for your broth if you ask!
name: CL

text: Customer service is over and The Nugget put the nail in the coffin. This is more about special circumstances than staying at the hotel itself which I didn't do. I had booked and paid in advance through Expedia a room for a night while traveling. I arrived late at night around 10pm and at check-in, they asked for a $100 security deposit. I didn't have it as my credit cards were compromised that day and it's why I booked the room in advance with help from a friend until I straightened out my credit card situation. They insisted on the $100 security deposit. I had Expedia call them, I spoke to several different reps of the hotel, I offered personal belongings (driver's licence, etc) but to no avail. I didn't get the room and was sent out into the night. So I just kept driving all night to my next destination. The Nugget also kept the money I paid for the room I didn't get and have refused to refund it. This speaks volumes to the lack of personal customer service I seem to find more and more this last few years. No one cares anymore and it's a shame. Corporate culture at it's best.
name: Keith

text: This is by far my favorite pizza place in the area. Food is phenomenal and employees are extremely friendly.
name: Amaya

text: So unhappy with my experience. I love the food, hands down one of my favorite places, HOWEVER, the customer service that I received (and have been receiving from Stephanie on multiple occasions) was appalling. Stephanie was rude, unapologetic and frankly a deterrent as a customer.  Again, the food is delicious and always prepared in a timely fashion. After speaking with my friends (who also swear that this is one of their favorite places eat) agreed that Stephanie's customer service was far below what should even be expected from a Mc. Donalds employee, NOR is this first time we were taken back by her comments to us. If I were the manager of this store I would highly suggest employing a new front staff to work hands on with customers who love your food so much. Stephanie, as the first impression of your store has accumulated an extremely poor representation of your company.
name: Jessica

text:
Our favorite place to drop in for a casual meal.  There are so many great items to choose from but my favorite (currently) is Pollo Loco while my husband loves the Soulard Primer.  
We like to take home a quart of Voodoo chicken salad and enjoy that until our next visit.
This is not a typical STL barbecue spot.  This is the real deal smoked meats like you have never had until you visit The Wood Shack Soulard!
name: Nancy

text: Came here due to it being the only Indian restaurant I could find that serves beef. The beef haleem was very well prepared and tasted exactly how it should have. Naan is also a definite go to. The only thing I wasn't absolutely smitten with was the chicken biriyani. It was just okay for me..
name: Jamesa

text: It was alright .   Our server wasn't very good, he told me the beet salad is an entree size.  Which it wasn't, possibly one beet cut up with a few pieces of greens.  My husband had the pork chop special, pork chop was fine but they put cold sour cream on the potato and made it cold.    Maybe they should put the sour cream in a side dish.    Can't say I won't go back.  But it's not on the top of our list.
name: Kathleen

text: Horrible Food and Service was really let down by this place as I was expecting a higher caliber. We asked our server about putting "sauce on the side" on one of the dishes and they said it was not possible so one of our dinner guests did not get to eat dinner. Working in the restaurant industry I know how easy putting "sauce on the side" is so to me its really just a lack of hospitality.
name: Jillian

text: It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Price felt a touch high for what it was. The food was good and the service was easygoing. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. Food was fresh and service was quick. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. Would absolutely visit again. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price..
name: User

text: We dined at Bob Evans on Wednesday evening, June 20, 2018, party of 4. My 12 year old daughter ordered the chicken tender meal - 3 tenders and fries. She ate one and a half of the tenders, I finished off the rest after I had already eaten my meal. As soon as we arrived home from dinner, less than one hour after eating, I was on the toilet. She was up all night vomiting and with diarrhea. I was spared of the vomiting, but have been in and out of the bathroom over night and appears to be continuing this morning. We both woke up with lingering stomach pain. She'll miss a day of pre-paid summer camp (non-refundable) and I'll have to struggle through a day at work. The worst thing a restaurant can do to a customer is mishandle food and make them sick. I have had cold food, mediocre quality dishes, and poor customer service, but making a customer ill due to food mishandling is simply unacceptable. I am extremely disappointed with Bob Evans as we were long time customers and unsure we can trust their food handling and preparation to consider ever returning. I do not think we are permitted to state the names of the persons at the restaurant, but our male waiter's name is shared by one of the 3 Musketeers.
name: Eugenio

text: You walk into a clean, well kept dining area and seat yourself. The waiter brings you menus and water. We got the vegetable pakora, potato paratha, and cauliflower paratha. To my disappointment the vegetable pakora wasn't actual fried pieces of vegetables. It was a fried dough ball with the traditional pakora spices and some cilantro in it. The potato paratha did not have much potatoes in it but it tasted like a samosa, delicious.
name: Tiffany

text: Decent crepes, nice atmosphere, ok staff. My friend and I both ordered lunch crepes. She and other customers had two times the side salad I had, no explanation as to why I had so little. They also didn't take my substitution into account. I wouldn't return.
name: Ruby

text: What a great little place. We were just looking for something small for lunch and stumbled across this place. We walked in and were instantly greeted with a smile...so friendly and nice. Lee got a burger and I got a Rueben. When we got our food, there was a lot! One thing we have never had is when you get your food and take a bit, the food is steaming! Definitely recommend this place and will go back when able!
name: Heather

text: Popped by this location while venturing around New Orleans and got some gator tail. It was great. It's easy to overcook but they did it up right!
name: Rem

text: We came here for brunch on a sunny day as we wanted to sit outside, but after hearing that there was over an hour wait, we decided to stay indoors. The indoor area is vast though not too many tables. There were a few other tables filled, but it wasn't too busy for a Saturday late morning. The brunch menu itself was a little confusing; there were not many 'typical' brunch foods like egg dishes, and the menu mostly contained meaty and lunch/dinner options. We split between the table the fruit and granola, the french toast (there's a 'flavor of the day' each day and ours was strawberry cheesecake), the honey and goat cheese pizza, the avocado and grapefruit salad, and the brussel sprouts. I was not too impressed by the fruit and granola, which were sparse. In addition, the strawberry cheesecake french toast was overly sweet and syrupy and quite thin (a disappointment since they didn't offer classic plain french toast). I did really enjoy the honey and goat cheese pizza. It had a drizzle of pesto and the goat cheese was great with a touch of sweetness from the honey. I also enjoyed the avocado and grapefruit salad; a refreshing plate for the hot day. The meal was pretty pricey and the food itself was ok. I would come back but I don't think I would do brunch again.
name: Sophia

text: OMG, what amazing food! I went for lunch with my colleague, and truly enjoyed the food. Ordered gobi manchurian for appetizer. Done to perfection, instead of testing (like most restaurant) the coating outside, you can actually test the fresh gobi inside, really well done. For main dish I had Appam with Goat Curry, yes it was a bit spicy for me (although I asked for less spicy), but the flavor and the aroma was so good that I could not stop eating it. The only down side is that I think there are too many tables and very little space to move around. We were sitting int he middle section, and literally felt like we were eating together with people from the next table, we talked to them multiple times.  I am going back for sure.
name: Marlen

text: I have to admit - I'm a little surprised by this place. In an area that seems to be devoid of great thai food, Thai Square Restaurant is a great mom-and-pop store tucked next to Naval Square. They only seat like 20 people, but has a relatively quick and inexpensive menu. I got the vegetarian drunken noodles, which was flavorful, soft, and filling. It's a great spot for your standard thai food. I've been told to avoid grubhub though, so it might be better to visit this establishment in person!
name: Neil

text: The photos made it look a little better than it actually was. The staff seemed tired but still polite. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. I'd maybe go back, but I'd order differently next time. Ordered a few things and liked most of it.
name: User

text: this is the best bakery ever.i have been using them since they were in levittown.then i didnt know what happened to them.i found them again in hatboro.everyone there is wonderful.the cakes are the greatest.if i dont make my own,i only go to lochels.
name: Mary

text: We rented out Laurel for our wedding dinner. Chef Elmi, Jane Fryer, and the staff could not have been easier to work with. They planned a nine-course menu for us that was flawless. Dinner included ice cream with caviar, oysters, juneberries, and the famous lobster press from Le Bec Fin. It was such an honor to see Chef Elmi in his element. I highly recommend this restaurant if you are planning a special event (or just want to enjoy an amazing meal!)
name: Laura

text: Loved this place. Total divebar feeling but fresh and good food. Service was fine. No hard liquor on the menu which was a slight disappointment but anyway, great experience. If you're looking for something free of crazy tourists that feels like a locals place, come here.
name: P

text: Tried this for the first time for Devour Indy and was not disappointed. Went with the tart cherry cider.l and would recommend. Refreshing and not overly tart. Shrimp and fritters for our two small plates. Both were very good. My wife was over the moon for the sauces. Fritters were light and tasty. Shared a beautiful ribeye. The sear on it was great and seasoned nicely. We typically take steak medium rare and this one was just a touch under. A minute more each side would have been perfect. Cheesecake was one of the creamiest I've had and not too sweet. Seating is very limited and not many large tables so groups of more than four might have a tough time.
name: Andrew

text: Escargot was phenomenal and my waiter was so friendly and gave me a ton of recommendations for the city. I will come back next time I'm in town.
name: Kaylee

text: Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. so yeah kind of mixed on it. It looked better online than it did in person. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price..
name: User

text: Sandwiches were great but dessert was even better. I will forever dream about the salted peanut butter chocolate chip pie wonderfulness! I would make this a must for lunch. Very close to WWII Museum.
name: Kristin

text:
This place was so aesthetically pleasing and bright and turned out to be a nice study spot for me and my friends. There are some tables but not too many so if you get lucky, grab a table and spend the afternoon there! 

I got a latte and a chocolate croissant which were both good but not spectacular. Overall I would come back and have an afternoon coffee and snack and get studying done or have a cute little coffee date here!
name: Jessica

text: This was a delivery order on a night when I really did not want to cook. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. The whole meal felt kind of uneven.
name: User

text:
At first site you go hmmm..... when you walk in makes you do a double hmmmm... the menu is posted on the wall. They have a " wall of fame " of sticky notes from Customers that have left their comments. So you start reading them and go well, everyone is leaving positive comments. We watched a Customer receive her food who graciously let us peek at it. We were sold and ordered the same thing. 

We smashed!! My daughter discovered this place. It is delicious.  We're heading out tomorrow on our cruise but will return before we leave the Tampa area for sure!!
name: Cocohantus

text: We were a last minute party of 10 and the staff and server were amazing and so accommodating. We are talkers and the even honored our request to lower the volume of the music! Great food and fabulous service - shout out to Crista our exceptional server for making us feel so welcome!! We will be back all 10 of us!!
name: Dino

text:
We came here for the Clayton restaurant week ($35 for 3 courses). The meal was definitely well worth it. It started with freshly baked bread which we really liked. I enjoyed my clam chowder which was creamy but not heavy. My filet mignon came medium rare which was cooked to perfection. The aged strip was flavorful but the part attached to the bone was kinda chewy in my opinion. Both entries came with sides (green beans and mashed potatos) The highlight of our meals were the desserts. The flavor of the espresso cake was so intense and addicting that we couldn't stop eating it! The cheese cake was alright but the berry sauce was a nice touch. 

The parts we didn't enjoy as much was our green salad which didn't taste very fresh. I also wasn't a fan of my tequila drink. But overall, we really enjoyed our experience here and certainly will return.
name: Winnie

text:
This is the pizza joint that is closet to my new home in Reno!

We ordered over the phone and picked it up. The menu had a lot of different items to choose from. They also have the take n bake option which I love.

I always ask for extra sauce when ordering pizza because i find most
to not have enough for my taste. When i did it here, the pizza was kinda
undercooked, probably because of the extra sauce. The next day when i reheated it; it was superb! 

I will definitely try this spot again and try the take and bake option. its really close to our new home which is a major plus.
name: Mary Ann

text: I wanted to like this more than I actually did. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. It was crowded but still moved along. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus..
name: User

text:
Really some of the best service i have ever received! The food was made fresh with quality ingredients all of which you could taste. Do not be fooled by the outside of the restaurant (it's location and outside appearance isn't much to look at honestly) go in and enjoy!

If you are riding your bike or running on the Loop this is also a great place to stop by for lunch or dinner! My next visit will definitely be while i bike from my house on the Loop.
name: Kovia

text: It's okay! If you want this and you don't feel like cooking at home, go for it. It's not one of those restraunts that I just think of or crave when I want to go out to eat. Returning customer-yes, once every year or two
name: T

text:
The next time ya want something good to eat, ya don't want typical drive thur crap, you're not in the mood for Pizza, you don't want to cook, and for whatever reason don't want to leave the house. (you know...Freezing 15 degree days like today!)

Steak Out to the rescue!  
Far better than pretty much any drive thru and better than many sit down restaurants.....Now is it to the level of the select St Louis Independents who I have given and absolutely deserve 5 stars? No.....but this is a different level! 
My favorite? The Ribeye Steak Sandwich! Far better than pretty much any burger joint around and I know of No Steak Sandwich better period!  Why? Lets not be comfused, this is Not a shredded mystery beef sandwich called a "steak" sandwich...No! This is a real ribeye! 
To be clear Steak Out does have a Philly Style Steak Sandwich...but when the Ribeye Steak Sandwich is available I can't bring myself to switch!  Back in the day I used to order the grilled chicken as well....and while really good, the Ribeye Steak Sandwich has my vote...add the Onion, Lettuce,Tomato...(Grilled Onions for an additional charge) Comes with chips but multi sides available for a small upcharge!
While I'm very happy Steak Out delivers to my home, why there aren't more Steak Outs around as they are really good! Give'em a try! (Online ordering available!)
name: Randy

text: I just left your drive thru. You gave me an iced coffee with curdled milk. How do you not realize this when you made the coffee. You have lost my business for good. I feel awful since I drink half the coffee before I noticed it. Thanks a lot !!!!
name: Anthony

text: The hamburger was fabulous. The service was good. The beef dip sandwich was awful. Stick to their burgers and shoestring fries.
name: P

text: For the price I expected a little more care. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. Parking was annoying, although that's prob more about the area than the restaurant. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Ordered a few things and liked most of it.
name: User

text:
My husband and I went here last night and had a lackluster experience.

We were 'greeted' by a waitress at the bar who essentially barked at us to see the hosted on the deck. We were then promptly seated at a table, that was in VERY close proximity to all other tables around us. 

Then the wait began. We waited, and waited, and waited, for someone to come and introduce themselves and take out drink orders. By the time our waitress -- the same one from the bar -- arrived at our table we ordered our drinks, appetizer and entrees all at once in fear that it would be another 15-20 minutes before she came back. Turns out, that was the right decision. 

Onto the food. A runner brought our appetizer out to the table without plates or napkins. We were half way through by the time our waitress came over to check on us and offer to bring plates. By the time she returned with our plates, the app was gone. The same runner brought our sandwiches to the table. We should have left after the app -- it was the best part of the meal -- I got the South Philly sandwich and my husband got a burger, and both left something to be desired. We didn't see our waitress again until we were done eating -- our plates were not cleared, the food was that just bad that we were just done faking that we liked it.

This was not our first time coming to High Tides, but it was definitely our last. Every time the service has gotten significantly worst, and after last night's experience I will not be returning. 

Its a shame that it didn't go better because it certainty was NOT an inexpensive meal. And going out to eat and supporting local places is something my husband and I both enjoy. But I hope someone else learns from this and doesn't make the same mistake.
name: Sarah

text:
This place was good, don't get me wrong, but I had higher expectations based on the number of people who told me I just *had* to try it. 

The cheese and meat board was heavenly. It comes with puffed bread squares (?) And some candied fruits and nuts. It's a plentiful appetizer! 

We got a pulled pork pizza and while we wanted to love it, it was just.....doing too much. The flavors were competing and it was a much better pizza after we picked a few things off. For an $18 pizza we expected a bit better.

I'm willing to give Domenica a round 2 in the future.
name: Amanda

text: Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent.
name: User

text: Absolutely amazing Chinese food! This isn't your average Chinese restaurant. Beautiful setting and the food is well presented. Servers are very friendly and attentive. It's nice to have Chinese food made with fresh ingredients and delicious vegetables, which isn't always the case. The ambience was very pleasing and relaxing. Very enjoyable place to visit when in the mood for Chinese food in an elevated (but not stuffy) atmosphere. I'll definitely be back again!
name: Danielle

text:
If you like a great Friday night wind down over good food and a drink you should try this place! The food is authentic, tastes fresh and has a little bit of flair. I loved the hibiscus margarita and the cilantro rice was a nice touch. The service was personal and prompt. The prices were comparable to similar restaurants. Although we sat at the bar we saw lots of regulars as well as new visitors coming in with kids or as couples. 

Definitely try Las Palmas if you love Mexican food on a Friday night. We will be back soon.
name: Drea

text:
I've been passing this place on my way home for the last few months. I love hole in the wall places because they typically tend to be top notch and this was nothing short of that. 

I wouldn't say I am a Philly cheese steak connoisseur, however, I would say it's one of my favorites and I have had many in my lifetime. They did a great job of preparing my meal quick. The Philly cheese steak was fresh, flavorful and they didn't skimp on the meat. And the sandwich came with a MASSIVE side of big ole fries-hell yeah! 

I will definitely be back to try some more of their dishes!
name: Chelsea

text: Dessert saved this a little. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. So yeah, pretty smooth experience from start to finish. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. So yeah, the host got us seated quickly, which i appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. Honestly, delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. so yeah kind of mixed on it. Would probably stop in again if nearby.
name: User

text: The fries were probably the best part of the meal, honestly. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. So yeah, the fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. idk I'd try something else next time.
name: User

text: This is one of those places where I can see other people loving it more than I did. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. Honestly, the portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. not sure I'd order the same thing again.
name: User

text:
I had high expectations when I went here... And it was WAY BETTER than expected.  Me and the wife went here for takeout on a Saturday night around 8pm.  We ordered a few different sandwiches to have a variety.  A  1/2lb Stuffed Mushroom & Swiss Burger, Steak and Shrimp Jumbo Sandwich, Philly cheesesteak, and a Gyro.

The wait was about 15 minutes but we'll worth it for fresh food made to order.

Max was the most pleasant friendly person you could imagine.  Veggie in the sandwiches we're well cooked, a definite plus especially for my wife.  The gyro was great but the real stars were the other 3 sandwiches.  Everything was monster portions.  The Stuffed Burgers are perfectly cooked Medium, juicy and full of flavor.  The 2 steak sandwiches were the BEST I've ever had, full of meat, veggies and cheese.  The bread had just the right amount of chew.

Definitely a great spot and it will be a place to go to every time I'm in Nashville.  Keep up the great work!!  Hopefully they'll be around for years to come, a great addition to the Nashville food scene.
name: Lonnie

text: Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. Service timing was efficient even tho it was busy. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Food was good and came out fast.
name: User

text: This is one of those places where I can see other people loving it more than I did. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Food was good and came out fast.
name: User

text: The sauce carried most of the meal. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. I left full, which at least counts for something. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. For the price I expected more than this. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean.
name: User

text: Don't come for the beer if you are vegan or vegetarian...come for the food.  Had lunch there Saturday and the food was excellent.  Not big on craft beer but will come again and again to try everything on the food menu.
name: Nick

text: This review only applies to the downstairs area.  We had a group there to watch a band that has members that are part of our extended family,  I and several others ordered burgers and they were mediocre at best.  Stale buns that were falling apart, preformed burgers that were dry and tasteless.  The draft beer was not cold and they have a very limited selection.  I can't see myself returning here.
name: David

text: Good Pizza.  Heavy Cheese, less crust, less sauce.  Seems expensive for what you get.  That being said, i'll always support local restaurants.
name: Rich

text:
I swear most of my reviews on this app are for different HoneyGrow locations. I went for a first time a little bit ago, and maybe two days later I HAD to bring my boyfriend to this Cherry Hill location so he could see what all the hype was about. 

All of the ingredients are locally sourced and made fresh daily. I love the ease of ordering with the kiosks as well as the ability to customize without too much difficulty. The wait wasn't long, and the portion size had you full, literally could not be anymore perfect. 

I now know what all the HoneyGrow hype is, and I'm very much obsessed!
name: Rachel

text: Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.
name: User

text:
Ok so I don't usually eat fast food or review it on yelp but I reallllllllllllllly had to because this place KILLED the fast food game! I mean the service was slow for how little people were in there on a Sunday afternoon, but otherwise, it was AMAZING.

The environment was typical fast food chain, but it was clean and tidy. Nothing was out of place. The staff were very friendly. I have never eaten at a popeyes before so I really didn't know what to expect. I ordered like the 8 piece family meal for me and friends with biscuits and mashed potatoes and gravy. We also got one of those oreo cream pie things. 

The chicken- holy heck for fast food fried chicken it was moist and tender and delicious. I mean I was truly surprised how much I enjoyed it.

The biscuits- moist and fluffy and buttery. I mean I could have eaten 10 of them. 

The mashed potatoes and gravy- for fast food mashed I was impressed. They were not dry or bland, they had flavor and would so good. I wasn't a huge fan of the gravy solely for the fact it wasn't my taste palate. Otherwise A+.

All in all this gets five yassssss's out of five from me and if you are looking for cheap, fast food fried chicken with friendly staff- go here!
name: Emily

text: This Is the Worst Place ever ! I ordered two simple smoothies and They completely messed them Up ! I also put in the notes that I wanted extra Sugar to my Smoothies and they came with Guess What it didn't come with any sugar at all! When I called them the manager or supervisor was extremely Rude and unprofessional! I will it order from this place again unless they make this right !
name: Damorris

text: Makeready was honestly everything that I was looking for when I went there. A smaller menu with in-season specials and good drinks. The burger was absolutely amazing and the pig ears (special) was cooked perfectly.
name: Trevor

text: I'm going to rename this place. From now on, I'm going to call it the "SWEET JESUS, MARY MOTHER OF GOD, THE WORLDS COMING TO AN END BURGER JOINT." I didn't order off the menu, instead I built my own. The "Get Saved Burger" I call it. A 7 oz patty smothered in bacon, mushrooms and Swiss cheese. It had to be carried out from the kitchen lovingly on a work bench! It came with enough fries to hide federal witnesses in. Truly a burger emporium or denomination if you will. Mention the good lord and get 5% off your next "Going Straight To Hell Burger!" I know, blasphemous right.  Be prepared though, your penance for this act will be a bill of about $21.00 - $22.00 per miracle. My little heaven came with fries and a drink at $21.49  If I continue eating here I will either have to get a second job or wind up homeless. Nonetheless, this is not your average burger place. The burgers are massive and visually stunning as well as extreme on taste. So what are you waiting for, make an appointment to see your cardiologist and then hit this place up on the way over.
name: John

text:
Pull pork platter is Insane. 
BBQ Nachos to die for. Creamy Mac. Fast service.

text: Love the ambiance. Food is good. The impossible burger is the best! The truffle mayo is a good choice. The infused fruit water is a nice touch. The potatoes are good.

text: Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. Food was fresh and service was quick. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. Worth checking out. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. Not bad for a quick meal. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything..
name: User

text:
Located near Drexel, Savas serves pizza, Stromboli, pasta, wraps, and paninis. I had a large Stromboli and wow, was it large. Like I usually eat a lot and o couldn't finish this Stromboli, it must have been at least 18 inches long and 5 inches wide- you could feed 2-4 people with it. The chicken was kind of dry and uneventful, but the meat lovers one was much better- would definitely recommend that instead. 

The best thing I had there by far though was the fries. They are the kind of soggy kind- if you are a crispy fry elitist you will probably hate these, but I'm more of a soggy type person myself so I LOVED them and would definitely recommend it. Pro tip- get the garlic white sauce to dip your Stromboli/pizza/fries in. 

Overall, seating was plentiful but the service was kind of slow- we had to keep asking for water and didn't have enough utensils. Also they ran out of garlic sauce.
name: Alfred

text: Excellent ramen! Very excited that this place lived up to expectations. The best part was the soft boiled egg. I should have ordered an extra one. Very large portions as well, we had to take home leftovers. The fried chicken small plate was a yummy indulgence also. Can't wait to return and try a poke bowl.

text: Favorite Mexican in town. Best salsa, great food and prices. Very consistent lightning fast service. Very nice staff! Been eating here for years!

text: Had brunch here over the weekend and it was kind of a mixed bag. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. No big complaints, just a nice meal. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. You can tell they care about customer experience here. Overall, a strong experience. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean.

Also, the margaritas were so good . My favorite taco was the shrimp taco . I had to order one more ! Will definitely keep coming .

text: Award winning Chicago deep dish? I didn't expect it to be just like the real thing but you could at least watch a you tube video to see what it looks like. Pizza hut has a thicker crust than this. If you are from the Chicago area or anywhere near the Midwest don't be surprised if you get this pizza and feel very very let down.

text: Wow...messed up on lobster tail...way over. Had to send it back and order something different.. scallops and shrimp...which were cooked correctly but plating it to hide the half scallop...could've done it a little better.  Disappointed again.

text: So. Much. Whiskey! A super-knowledgeable staff! But you knew that, already, didn't you? We've all read the articles. They're glowing. But not enough people know about Lunch here. At least when I stopped in it was almost empty. That's maybe good and bad. Good, because the food was amazing and who wants to have to wait for good food during a busy lunch hour? If you need noise and all of that when you head out midday, then this wouldn't be the place for you. I used to have the habit of doing Lunch Dates on work days. It's so easy to step out for 45 minutes and not have to worry about how to "keep the night going" early in a dating sitch. I think Ripplewood is the perfect escape for that kind of lunch outing. Curated menu, maybe a half cocktail or glass of wine, and some seriously flavorful food and then *boom* it's back to work and that might be the best meal your guest had all week, lunch or not. We know what this spot does right, I just wanted to share one more idea on how to enjoy Ripplewood.
name: Baker

text: They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. text: The wait was longer than it should've been for a pretty normal dinner service. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. For a busy night they handled it okay. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. Maybe better dine-in than delivery, hard to tell. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh.
name: User

text:
We've been fans of China Fun for *years*, and it is my sad duty to report that ...

.            CHINA FUN HAS CLOSED :-(       

Very depressing.

CF was a family run operation, which was given to the daughter about 6 months ago.  When the daughter took over the food became uneven (one day it was perfect, the next day it was salty dogfood), and attendance started to suffer.  The inevitable end came around the beginning of March (2018).

We will miss China Fun badly - it was (literally) the only place to eat in the area, and the family was friendly beyond all reason (really, *really*, good people).

So long China Fun: we knew thee well...
name: Nonaht

text:
Love this place! Right next door to the Roosevelt for a bite and their happy hour is insane! Half price pizza, wine, beer well drinks. Being right next door to the Roosevelt you're next door to luxury, but this restaurant brings you right to Italy and to a comfortable, non pretentious, but smart, classy and high end feel. It's lovely. The music is subtle. It's lounge/club meets Vegas love! 

The menu boasts flavors of smoked beets honey whipped ricotta, & hazelnuts for an antipasti

Small or Large Courses my pick was the Bucatini: Shrimp, Guanciale (Pig Cheek) Sumer Squash, chili $15/$25 

Pizzas were half off 2pm-6pm daily 
$13 (margherita)-$20 (clam pizza)
Can go half and half
name: Mariana

text:
I've eaten here twice, and it was awesome both times.  

The menu includes some truly creative offerings, both appetizers and entrees.  The prices seem low for the quality and uniqueness and QUALITY of the culinary creations... But I'm not complaining.  

Ample seating, including an outdoor area.  Acoustically, it can be a bit noisy when crowded, but the historical all brick-and-hardwood, high-ceilinged building perpetuates that.  And the charm of the interior should not be altered in any way.

I hope Cobblestone stays in business for a long, long time.
name: Steve

text: We had dinner last night, July 4, to remember the anniversary of our engagement, here 3 years ago. Everything was perfect. The service is very attentive when it needs to be. The courses are delivered right on time. There was no wait for anything. Of course the food was amazing. My wife had the double cut pork chop, well done, but still very tender and tasty.  She didn't care too much for the greens but I found them appropriate. I had the fish which was delicious.  Not a complaint but I was in the mood for beef but there was not an option on the menu. I would also like some less expensive wines.  Delicious California wines can be had at $10 a bottle. So a modest markup could put them a little closer in reach. Especially when dinner for two easily tops $100.  Dessert was delicious. Bread pudding and the creme brûlée .  Thanks for a wonderful time.
name: Paul

text: Chevy's in the Central West End.  More of the same tired menu and poor execution of typical Tex-Mex.  generic in every way.
name: Jose

text: The overall environment and staff friendliness is appreciated. The accuracy of fulfilling orders has been frustrating. We have eaten in once and ordered takeout 3 times. All 3 times that we ordered takeout, our order has been wrong. Specifically for our toddler. We are either missing items or our food items are prepped with ingredients we asked to be removed. In the case of our toddlers meal, we have had to find something else for him to eat because theres mo way he could eat the spicy food. Double checking the specific order would go a long way.

text: The decor and atmosphere are great. You can tell they really put the heart and details into making this space look great. The menu seems a little boring and nothing really caught my interest much. I wish they would work on more interesting appetizer and sandwich options. Fish and chips could have used more seasoning (this is coming from a person who does not like heavy salt) and buffalo fries could use some more sauce as it didn't have much topping. The crab bruschetta was a big miss - dry and flavorless almost like canned tuna on a cracker. I really wish this restaurant well and hope it only continues to improve. I do plan on giving it one more try.
name: Renata

text: Not bad for a quick meal. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Nice little spot, decent portions too. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Food was fresh and service was quick. Not bad for a quick meal. The leftovers held up okay the next day..
name: User

text: It hurts me to leave a bad review for Los Camarades, but they earned it from my last meal (8/1/18).  I live nearby, and have eaten here several times.  Its usually been pretty good, B+ to A...but they screwed up literally everything for us on yesterday's dinner.  1st off, the waitress was inaudible...you know the asian girl from Pitch Perfect who whispers everything?...that was our waitress.  You couldn't freaking hear her!  And its kinda loud in there...speak up girl!  Next, our drink order...wife orders a margarita...doesn't get asked if she wanted it blended, on the rocks, w/ sugar or salt.  I order a Corona.  I expect a bottle with a lime in it.  What I get is a can of beer!  What is this, a college frat party?  I have to go to the bar to ask for a glass.  The chips and salsa:  salsa was so-so, not as tasty as it normally is, but the chips have zero salt on them, and some on our plate are soggy!  Let me tell you, bland salsa and saltless chips are fairly gross.  We order the Nachos with brisket on top, the "Best in Philly" they claim.  Again, salt on the Nachos makes the dish tasty...we need salt to taste the vibrance of the flavors...so this dish was rather bland....and quite heavy handed on the crema if you ask me.  Just nowhere near as good as normal.  We order the brisket tacos...which come doubled up with corn tortilla shell.  The Tortillas were so dried out and stale that you literally couldn't bite through them, they were close to shoe leather.  You couldn't cut them easily with the knives provided either.  How long have they been sitting around??  This was gonna be our "cheat meal" for the week.  What a waste of calories!  Their quality control has really slipped.  There are way too many other good Mexican places around to waste my time here anymore.
name: Lucas

text: Okay so I would give this place 3.5 stars. I didn't read reviews beforehand so not sure if it mentioned that this restaurant is setup more so for takeout than dine in. That being said we dined in and both my husband and I agree that if you are set up as a dine in then there should be a restroom available for customers. Now onto food- we ordered the drunken noodles and red curry. Drunken noodle 4/5 it was flavorful, red curry 2/5 was not so flavorful but steaming hot. They served it in take out containers and plastic plates. We may order from here again if we are absolutely craving Thai but we will make sure it's take out.

text:
New to the area so decided to wander around Hyde Park Village.  Stumbled across this place so we decided to stop in and have lunch.  Pretty dead inside but found everyone was sitting outside!

Here's a case where I would love to give a 3.5.  Service is OK - definitely could be more attentive.  Great wine choices by the glass, however the white wine I ordered was ice cold.  I had to let it sit for a while and it was still really cold.  Maybe they do this because it can get so hot here, but it was only 70 degrees that day...  

The food is quite good!  I had the ahi tuna with seaweed salad.  Veggies were a simple roasted veggie medley which was quite good - the rice was uneventful.   My husband had the Salmon Dijon - again same veggies and rice.   Salmon was really good as well, not over cooked but maybe a tad oversauced.  Would I come back?  Maybe, but would probably try someplace new when in the area again.

text:
I had heard a lot of buzz about this place so decided to check it out on a Saturday night after church.  It was not very busy at the time, so I was able to order almost right away.  I got the lamb sausage and shared an order of the raclette cheese fries with a friend of mine.  The lamb sausage was pretty tasty, but nothing mind-blowing and at $9, was on the pricey side.  I get that everything is made in house and that could contribute to the higher prices, but $9 is a high price to pay for a sausage which is average size.  You would probably need to order two of them if you come in on a empty stomach.  Raclette cheese fries were good, but since the cheese hardened pretty quickly and distribution of cheese on fries was poor, ended up with a couple of small handful of fries with all of the cheese on them.

All in all, ok experience in a great location.
name: Gregory

text: Overall, my experience at Daleng was very good. What I loved most about my time here was the chicken banh mi, which is the best banh mi that I've had in recent memory. text:

Really, it's just a solid experience. So much so that when other fried chicken aficionados are in town, it will be a go to must. 

If you haven't tried Freebyrd, you are definitely missing out. If you want this type of food and are with a friend or loved one who wants something different too, no need to worry. There are plenty of other options in The Bourse too so everyone can get the fix that they are craving. For me though, that's going to be Freebyrd.

text:
So I was in a tourist-heavy part of town where it seems every singer has a restaurant and/or bar with his name attached to it... we found this one and decided to venture in just based on where we were walking at the time.

Service was great. It's a big space with plenty of seating. There was (good) live music playing, which is to be expected. 

Service was prompt and VERY friendly. 

The menu was BBQ-heavy. There were burgers and salads, some inventive appetizers ("Memphis sushi," which is a sausage/cheese/sauerkraut plate), but the focus here is clearly on the smoked meats.

Caveat: I'm a Texan, therefore I'm a BBQ snob. So I went in with low expectation but an open mind. I left feeling validated. The barbecue here was "OK" -- nothing special, but not horrific. I got brisket -- the menu said 1/2 pound, but if so, then it was the most meat I've ever gotten in a half pound. The flavor wasn't as smoky as I would have expected, especially after the menu talked about how it was smoked for 12 hours. It just lacked when it came to that part.

Worse was that, despite the presence of fat in the brisket, it tasted dry overall. I kept dousing it with sauce not only for the flavor, but just for the moisture content. (For the record, there are four sauces -- sweet/mild, "gold" [mustard-based], smoky and hot.) I went with smoky. Good, but not smoky enough.

You'll have a good experience if you just remember "I am a tourist eating in a tourist spot. I am a tourist eating in a tourist spot."

text:
To say I've been under the weather lately would be a dramatic understatement. My appetite's been way off, so currently, on the sadly rare occasion that I get a hankerin' for something, I generally give in and get it.

This afternoon the only thing that sounded good was spaghetti 'n meatballs and the closest, most-reasonably-priced place to get it was from Pizza Baron, so I jumped in my car and scooted over there.

I am totally factoring in the fact that this is, first, a pizza joint, and second a bar. So I didn't go in with the expectations of a gourmet spag as you'd find in a little mom 'n pop place with checkered tablecloths and candles in wine bottles on each table.

My first impression is the place is super bar-like, even at 3-something in the afternoon. Not full, but loud enough to be a little grating if one had chosen to dine in. But I ordered my stuff to-go so no biggie.

The employee (bartender maybe?) was super duper nice warm and friendly and happily changed a hundred-dollar bill for me, which is kinda rare anywhere these days. She took my order and promptly brought my change.

I got the spaghetti ($6.95) & meatballs ($1.25) and for good measure (and extra iron and vitamins and shit) I also got a tossed green salad ($4.95). I always feel confident ordering a salad in a pizza place since they generally have fresh veggies in abundance. 

The spaghetti & meatballs was good. It wasn't amazing but it was by no means sub-standard. The pasta was overcooked (way beyond al dente, but again - this is a bar) but the sauce was good and the meatballs were tasty. It also had some melted cheese on top which ordinarily might turn me off but today added to the comfort-foodiness of the dish. 

The salad was awesome - chock full of VERY fresh veggies and just deelish.

The only drawback which REALLY bummed me out was the side of burned garlic bread. 

All in all, though, I had a perfect meal from Pizza Baron. Next time I'm definitely going to try their pies!
name: Jenny

text:

text:
Oh man, what can I say about this place?  

Bring your money and your appetite!  My hubby tells me that he wants to eat some Vietnamese desserts and of course, there's some local areas to find his wish list but when we're in the Vietnamese town in Philly, I suggested to stop by here.

Here goes our diet.  We ordered few and variety of banh mi (buy 5 get 1 free), sweet desserts, rice cakes (che), spring rolls (buy 5 get 1 free), vegetarian rice noodle platters.  There's many rice and noodle platters made ready to eat.  They make their own fermented meat (nem) and pork roll (cha lua).  There's a large variety of smoothies and bubble teas here.  Their French baguette is the best I've had in a long while.  Crispy on the outside and not too much dough inside.  It's light and fluffy.

My hubby raided their desserts and I can't really pick out a favorite.  I would suggest trying them all and buying smaller portions.  If you like what you taste, then buy more.

Their spring rolls are delicious and is a hit for us.  We will definitely come back next time we're in town.

text:

text:
We ordered from here via caviar on a Wednesday evening at around 8pm. 

For reasons involving GI room and dessert, I only ordered 2 "entrees" and an appetizer. There were a few items my eye balls lingered on for longer than usual: mapo tofu, charred cauliflower, charred BRUSSELS SPROUTS (why didn't I order that??? Hmmph.), I'm now also noticing vegetable fried rice with LENTILS. Interesting.

Ultimately I was feeling strong in tofu's corner and ordered both the tofu tower and stuffed tofu. For an app I went with the napa cole slaw which unfortunately did not meet my expectations of traditional, mayo soup cole slaw but rather a more light and fresh, sans-fat version. 

The tofu tower was essentially a kebab with seasoned tofu and some veggies (shrooms, onions, all the things I don't like but bae is more than happy to suck up for me). The stuffed tofu was INCREDIBLE. Crispy outer edge with this DELICIOUS creamy shit on the inside. I don't even see it on the online menu rn which is a TRAVESTY. STUFF ME inside that shit, please. 

This place seems to have some unconventional but tasty items as well as an unusual and refreshing twist on classics. I would definitely order from here again as well as go in person.

text:
Ahh, McDonalds.

The location remains, the building is completely NEW !! 

I dig the interior's functional layout and double lane drive thru. This location is 24 hrs. 

The seating options here are cool. Up dated bench and stool seating and lounge couches. 

The design concept is warm, dare I say earthy *gulp. Yes, I said it. Ordering and pick up counters flow in a functional manner. Table service is available.

It has been awhile since we have been to McDonalds, certainly less since adopting a plant based diet. Muriel, the GM greeted my son immediately. Commenting on how much he'd grown. I asked about Vegetarian options, currently Mcdonalds offers few. Muriel, shared that the company is looking to release new menu options by the end of 2019. 

As my son finished his meal, which was accurate and prompt, an employee brought him a piece of celebration cake. Simultaneously, a group of team members were clapping and singing happy birthday, to a team member. 

It was kind of, a hekk-of-a-day at McDonalds. Ha!

If your team can be calm, timely and accurate during the madness of a grand opening. I expect regular service days, will be a breeze.

Who gives McDonalds, five stars - me. Muriel and her team have repeatedly earned it, I am sorry I did not review this location sooner !
name: Christina

text:
Thinking this was a typical greasy spoon diner, I wasn't expecting much from this place but I was happily surprised!  My husband and I ate here twice during our 3 night stay; both times were late breakfast/early lunch times.  We even had two really great servers!!!
I had the chicken tenders both times because they were awesome.  Freshly prepared, dipped, fried, and served with super crunchy fries.  You can't go wrong with them!  And it's big enough to share.  My husband first had the pancakes with eggs and bacon then had the french toast with bacon during our second visit.  He enjoyed both meals.  The pancakes were large and fluffy, the bacon was crisp, and the eggs were always cooked to order.  The french toast was prepared nicely and dusted with powdered sugar. 
Our only negative thing would be the length of time between being seated and being acknowledged by the server.  This place is poppin' busy and open 24 hours so the servers are hustling their best but there is a delay from the time you're seated to the time your server is there. 
I would recommend this place anytime of the day!  Just don't be an entitled d*ck and be patient once you're seated.

text: Went to this place with a group of 8 on a Sunday. We were in town for the weekend and based on the stars gave it a shot. I'll start with the positives, the food is great. If you're looking for brunch this place has the food that's worthy. That's the only positive I can say about this place. The service was TERRIBLE, we were told the wait was 45 minutes. Only to be told after an hour and a half wait that our party would be split and we wouldn't eat together. We were not told this up front and only found out after asking. Once we were finally seated they apologized for the wait and said "we will take extra care of you". We looked through the menus and upon ordering were THEN told they were out of bread therefore have the table couldn't have their orders. We were told by the owner that they intentionally run out of food so it doesn't go to waste.The mimosas were warm from hot champagne, the food didn't come out together so our food was cold once it was all served. Once we finished our food they missed up our checks after we explained it to them twice it was couples. Only for them to say "why didn't you guys sit next to each other from the start". Lastly we ordered 3 carafes but only got two and when the checks came the owner told us "I didn't charge you for the extra carafes", again we only got two after ordering 3. All in all the food was a 4 out of 5 but the service brings this place down.

text:
Decided to try something new, and i have always loved mongolian. Almost no one in there which seemed a little odd.  The greeter/waiter told us to follow him, not friendly at all, very intense and not patient.  We were brought to a table and told to sit, we were about to sit down then told to come here like we were dogs.  He walked us over to the beginning and started to question us like we were being interrogated, backed into a corner with a bright light shining is what it felt like.  No where in this country at the many Mongolian grills i have been to had the waiter not only been extremely rude, but refuse to let us start without being asked 20 questions.  You want small or large while shoving bowls in our faces, what noodle you want?  Mongolian grills are not a new concept and all are pretty much the same with slight variations.  The rules about all the different bowls are clearly marked so it would be difficult not being able to figure out you need 2 bowls and a plastic cup.
I told him what noodle out of desperation for this to end, but then when i got to the noodle section i realized a different noodle sounded better, but it was already on my card so i was afraid of more problems if i wanted to switch.
We finally finished that whole stressful ordeal and dropped off our selection.
The food was ok at best, definitely nothing to write home about and the prices are way too high for what you get.  Needless to say, i will never go back.  High prices, horrible service is probably the reason no one was in there. AVOID!!!
