text:
I'd say this location has about a 50% mistake ratio on our orders. There have been a few times when we've placed an order through the drive-through, been handed our bag(s) of food, and when we got home found out that something was missing or incorrectly made. (For example, a request for a plain cheeseburger may still end up with condiments). 

As an another example:

I know one time they forgot Chicken Nuggets and instead threw in two extra french fry orders.  Of course, we didn't discover this until we got home.  So I called and was told to come back and they'd make it right. Their idea of "make it right" was to give me a box of nuggets and they told me I could "keep the extra fries they gave us before".  Yep, okay. So in the meantime, my kiddo didn't eat the fries at home because she wanted to have hot french fries with her hot chicken nuggets. Of course, by the time, I had called them about the error, drove back, parked, waited in line for someone to correct the order, and then driven home again... the original fries were stone-cold and limp.  I had a pretty miserable kiddo for the evening, because they couldn't get their order right and their idea of "making it right" wasn't up to snuff as far as I'm concerned. 

There's a reason that if time allows, we actually go to another McDonalds that is a little bit further away from us, vs. this one.

However, whatever food is accurately made has the usual McDonald's flavor and style, so there is that.  :)

text:
We wanted P.J. Clarke's to be better than it was but nonetheless still enjoyed it. Dined inside in a back room with windows and a cool view after asking if we could not sit in the dimmer dining area. The restaurant is very large and boasts interesting Philadelphia-related photographs and archival pieces on the walls. 

Food was pretty good. The oysters were the star of the show and their specialty. I had the chicken pot pie because I don't like seafood and decided that would be a good meal to have in the middle of June¿ It had really good flavor but took a while to cool lol. Mom had a burger which had great fries but honestly wasn't worth the price. Dad's lobster roll was good but had tomatoes which he said is not traditional to a lobster roll ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ No garnish on any of the plates either. Definitely recommend the cocktails :) and there is a hefty dark liquor selection. 

Service was fair; it was definitely SLOW which stunk. They were fairly knowledgeable but not all stars. 

The bathroom situation was weird enough for me to mention: gender neutral single stalls which is cool and progressive but there were far too few stalls for the size of restaurant so we all waited in line and made small talk. Not sure I'd go back but if you're an oyster fan then this is the spot for you- especially with $1 happy hour per oyster.
name: Caroline

text:
What can I say, it's a true St. Louis institution - going on for more than 60 years! I've eaten here a couple times, once for lunch and the other for dinner. The atmosphere is great, as well as the hometown feel. The prices are, yes - pricey. But look at it this way, so are a lot of other restaurants on The Hill. I've had Rigazzis' Parmiciano, which was very different and worth trying. Get it with a side of fries and you'll be set for lunch. I'm not really sure how to describe their pizza. The crust is very hard and thin, so its crispy. According to one of the workers there, they "O.D." on the provel cheese, which is definitely not a bad thing. They really load up on the toppings if you're getting the special "Aiazzi's Da Bomb Pizza" where they put bacon, green olives and plenty of meats on top! I had their smallest size, and it still filled me up! 

I'll definitely be back because I know there's a lot of menu items I'm missing out on. Would love to try their toasted ravioli and their spaghetti & meatballs. I also still haven't had their signature "beer in a fishbowl glass"! Next time I am up for an alcoholic beverage while dining here I'll go straight to that. 

Like I said above, it's an iconic St. Louis place. Has a lot of history as well. I didn't know the Blues hockey team hung out here after games at the old Arena. Plenty of celebrities have eaten here too. You gotta check out their Blues hockey memorablia upstairs (if it's open). And get a selfie with Al Capone at that one booth. They also have their stl250 cake from five years ago still on display outside by the patio.
name: Jason

text:
Nice modern Latin-style atmosphere in what appears to be a converted gas station or garage.  Their food has a shareable plates approach, which doesn't always work out perfectly when vegetarians and non-vegetarians are dining together!

We ordered a couple of plates, the best one was the Mollettes, which was an amazing open-face toast sandwich with black beans, manchego, avocados and topped with onions and greens.  I would go back to have this again!  Also had the Local Mushrooms which was somewhat of a textural adventure, it featured a selection of mushrooms (some of which I had never eaten before) in an intense Mole sauce.  

I can imagine this place is much more attractive in nice weather with it's doors open in the evening and the patio filled with diners drinking and eating.  We'll have to come back anytime but winter and try other vegetarian options.  

Their menu changes monthly, so the one posted on the website may not be what you see when you visit.  Also there is a small parking lot next to the restaurant which is easy to miss when you drive by, but there is usually nearby street parking.

text:
We are new to the area & had just been to Wiregrass Mall for the first time. We were out longer than expected & looking for some dinner. We checked Yelp & Trip Advisor & this place was well rated & GRILL sounded like a good & meaty dinner. I was craving some grilled shrimp & figured this joint would be great. 

The restaurant had a very nice decor & was very comfortable inside. We often get cocktails but this night we did not, I will say though that their cocktail menu was intriguing & looked great & their bar was rather packed for early evening on a Thursday. We each had soup, he the Jamaican style pumpkin bisque with crab, myself the soup of the day which was a portabello mushroom with artichoke (or asparagus?), both soups were very good (although there was very little crab in the pumpkin soup). 

There were very few grilled items on the menu considering  the word grill was in the name of the restaurant (there were no grilled shrimp other than as an add-on side item). I was curious about their crab & shrimp burger as being from MD I love crab, though I rarely try crab cakes out of my home state. It was explained to me that the shrimp & crab were ground together & made to a patty/burger then breaded & deep fried & put on a bun, um no thanks, & just why? (why make a point of saying jumbo lump crab if there aren't going to be visible lumps & why add the shrimp if you won't be able to taste it once it's ground into the crab ? This entire idea baffles me as a Marylander) The only reason this would be done where I am from would be to disguise the quality or lump of crab being used & since down here in the gulf shrimp is cheaper than blue crab my guess is cutting the crab with the shrimp is a cost saving measure. 

We both ordered off the specials menu, I got the meatloaf which came with sides I disliked but the waiter was very accommodating & let me switch them out for green beans & au gratin potatoes my fella got the beef pot pie. Both meals came to us in cast iron mini cookware presented on wooden cutting boards, so a cute/unique presentation. Both meals tasted very good, they just weren't what was expected.

I'll start with my dish, the meal plate overall presented as very greasy, the green beans had a wonderful flavor but were very greasy, the au gratin potatoes came in a little crock & the grease sat about 3mm above the actual potatoes, (I immediately folded 3 cocktail napkins & stuck them in the side of the dish to soak up the grease, they soaked through & it took two more placed in the container to get the grease off & to an edible level). The meatloaf was actually a chopped steak/salisbury steak with mushrooms & sauce (I will say if this is what their burger is made of then their burgers are probably very good) & the mushroom brown sauce was that came with my meal did have a good flavor. 

As for his pot pie, it too came in a cast iron serving dish, it had a huge piece of puff pastry on top (we had asked the server ahead of time if this was an actual pot pie, you know, bottom & top crust baked alone in a dish & he had said that it was, it clearly was not) when he cut into the crust to get to the gooey goodness below that is typically a pot pie it was very dry under the puff pastry & there didn't seem to be much in the way of sauce or veg. He removed the puff pastry & what lie beneath were 3 large pieces of beef, some large pieces of carrot & some halved fingerling potatoes & almost zero gravy. This was not a pot pie, this was a pot roast with a slice of puff pastry on top if it. I gave him my sauce to help combat the overall dryness of his meal & specifically his meat. 

Overall nothing was bad (except maybe the potatoes, good lord 5 napkins full of grease?) The food tasted good, it just wasn't what we thought we had ordered, if you have pot roast, just say it's pot roast with a puff pastry on the side & for god's sake give it some gravy, if your serving a chopped or salisbury steak just call it that. If things had been clearer on the menu I probably would have gotten the pot roast & he probably would have gotten a burger & this review would have been one happy non critical paragraph.

text:
What a great place!  Excellent service (Thanks, Emma!), met the owner (nice, dedicated man; sorry; didn't get his name), wonderful, creative and innovative menu, generous portions, marvelous flavors. 

I took my 87-year-old mother to eat lunch there this week. Her palate has gotten a bit more adventurous since I moved back here almost 5 years ago) and she likes our "Pooh Adventures" to new places and sections of this region,she tells me. 

One of her favorite foods is calamari, and she's sampled it at many places over many decades. She stated that this "flash-fried" calamari was "one of the best she'd ever had"! 

I ordered the grilled pork belly banh mi sandwich and used her calamari dipping sauce (she doesn't  like sauces, much) on it: delicious!  Enough for two meals! 

I also ordered the shrimp, garlic basil fried rice. Gave a couple of shrimp to my mom, who pronounced them "delicious." I liked this dish a lot, but the half a banh mi filled me up. I ate about 1/6 of this and took the rest home: got 2 more meals out it by adding some leafy greens! 

This entire meal, which turned into 5 meals for the two of us (1 for her and 4 for me) cost under $36 dollars, WITH a generous tip for Emma! So, can't beat the prices. 

Also, bonuses: they turned the music down immediately when asked. We found parking right in front (meters; need quarters -- no card option), and have take-out menus on paper you can take with you (but it is over 30 minutes' drive each way from where we live, so unless I'm in that area, anyway, doubt if I'd do carry out). 

Very good location, right off South Grand, behind The King and I Thai restaurant. 

Good decision, not to offer pho, since about 20 other places within walking distance already do. This menu is innovative, creative, unique, tasty and inexpensive. 

Only drawback: VERY uncomfortable chairs. They do have booth seats, though, on one side, so that's something. 

They do take reservations (which we made, but did not need). They recommend making reservations for arriving any time after 4 PM, especially on weekends. Tey do have an upstairs for overflow and large parties, but no elevator. 

HIGHLY recommended. I wish it were closer: I'd go back to try about 10 more items!
name: Sally

text: The food here is really exceptional. It blows away bar food standards. I would come here for lunch or dinner. Drinks are colorful, vibrant, and flavorful. Staff is friendly and professional. Venue is clean, well lit, and tons of fun. You can't be let down, highly recommended.

text:
Located on 2nd Avenue in Downtown Nashville, less than one block from the Honky Tonk's and boot shops of Broadway sits Mike's Ice Cream. Its not a big place, so get ready to get cozy with your fellow ice cream lovers. The Building is deep and long, not wide, so when you walk in you have to walk to the back of the building to get to the ice cream line. On my visit, the line was out of the door, which apparently seems to be the usual with this place, so be prepared for a wait. However, the wait was not terrible and the line moved really quick. I will say it took us about 15 minutes to get from the sidewalk to the register. 

Ill be completely honest here...I walked into Mike's with every intention of getting a cup of ice cream, two scoops actually, but ended up walking out with a cookies and cream handmade milkshake. Do I regret my choice? Absolutely not! Did I still end up sampling an ice cream before making my choice, yup! So, technically I can speak to multiple products that Mike's has to offer!

In addition to their homemade local ice cream, Mike's also offers a variety of coffee drinks, assorted danishes, milk shakes, brownies, old fashioned sodas and frozen drinks such as lemonade. As mentioned above, I ended up with a cookies and cream milkshake and it was delish! They offer the basics of milkshake flavors from vanilla, chocolate, etc...or you can choose any flavor ice cream they serve to have a shake made out of. Speaking of their ice cream, they have a plethora of flavors for you to choose from, upwards of 20-25 when the case is fully stocked! Of course they have the staples such as chocolate chip cookie dough, mint chocolate chip, vanilla and chocolate; but additionally, they have some really creative and tasty flavors such as blueberry cornbread, chocolate banana pudding, superhero and many more! I ended up sampling the blueberry cornbread, because you don't see that flavor listed and at least sample it! I enjoyed it, but my heart had already fell for a milkshake. 

In addition to the treats themselves, everyone that worked there was genuinely nice, patient and helpful in all interactions I was involved in and that I witnessed. Overall, I can tell why this place is jam packed at all times! It is certainly on my recommendation list and "return to" list for my next trip to Nashville!

I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean.
name: User

text: I have been ordering the classic octopus which is grilled and served with capers and cucumber salad. I'm just in heaven when I get it, now my husband is addicted too so we have to order two!
name: Trixieee

text: Amazing sushi both in fish and rice quality! They also are one of the few restaurants that serve uni. Fish is the freshest in town I've had and rice the best quality
name: Christina

text:
Not a bad place, but limited menu with mediocre food that is very over priced!! 

Been here 4 or 5 times over the years.

Won't be back in less I have to?

Nice ambience however.
name: Tommy

text:
This was recommended to us by a friend so went there for our lunch. I ordered the combo with 4 pcs of bbq ribs, 2 pcs of thinly sliced brisket and pulled pork like a size of a tennis ball and 2 sides fries and potato salad for about $22. Since I'm a small eater I shared it with my friend and we're both full. There are 6 different kinds of sauces for the meats and I like the white sauce and the bbq sauce. I find brisket dry so that's my only complaint.
If you come in a group, you cannot have somebody save a table for the group coz somebody will check on this which I think fair.
name: Perla

text: Loved the bubble tea. Had a mayo slush with tapioca. The drinks are pretty large. The food is good as well. However, I enjoyed the wings the most.
name: Marsha

text:
Good priced seafood. I enjoy the variety that they have as well as the sauce choice. I usually go for the shake sauce, which is all three of the cajun, garlic butter, and lemon pepper mixed. 
I wouldn't waste my time on their wings however because they are very similar to the type of wings you can get at your local chinese corner store. 
Another complaint is that the past few times I've been there, I've always had about 2-4 bad clams/mussels.
name: Angel

text: I had 2 family members visiting from CA! One was starting her birthday celebration & we were thrilled with this wonderful Restaurant. From the moment we walked in, Southern Hospitality was all in! The Service, Food & Atmosphere was Perfect!! You will NOT be disappointed making this one of your Stops in the charming location of Franklin Tennessee!
name: Leah

text: It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon.
name: User

text:
Love this place! Breakfast, lunch, dinner, whatever you want and it's amazing!! 

Are usually stick to the mini tacos since they're always very good, But the rest of the food was great as well. Make sure you try the green chili sauce!
name: Anthony

text: I ate at Honey Pit again on Friday.  They had a fried Cod special that was amazing.  It was great that they had options for people that don't eat meat on Friday's.  The staff was so friendly!! The atmosphere is very cool!
name: Jim

text: This place is wonderful. Some of the best Thai food in New Orleans. I always visit when I'm there. I like both the FQ location and Uptown locations. My favorite is the spicy eggplant with chicken.
name: Terrell

text: The manager is so rude. if you did not buy anything from there, he will kick you out right away.
name: Blank

text:
This once was the place I would venture to drive an hour and a half to see. Finally moved to the NJ suburbs outside of Philly and I have no reason not to come more.

I noted on the OpenTable res that it's our anniversary...they decorated the table with rose pedals and gave us candle lit dessert. The waiter and the maitre'd both wished us a Happy Anniversary and made good conversation. Really lovely dinner.  

Food was delicious. Table side made Cesar salad, mussels (oh my), Fettucini Carbonara and Duck Breast. So so so good. We're the sharing type of couple and made that known and they kept up with us and multiple plates. It was great. Water service was always around and my wife's spicy Sangria Primavera had a good kick but was smooth.

Thank you for making our night a special one. We'll be back.
name: Jeff

text:
This was a first time visit to the restaurant although not the first to the GSR and its several predecessors.
We were seated promptly and probably had drinks on the table within 8 or 10 minutes although curiously not served at the same time. I appreciated being asked if I would like a glass with my Kirin but my wife was not impressed with the size of her saki relative to cost.
We both had cups of Hot and Sour soup at $5.95 each. Hot for sure, spicy but otherwise average. We both ordered sushi rolls at the high end of the menu and delivery was reasonably timed after almost being served a meal intended for other guests. The rolls were nicely presented but I have never seen sushi rolls so appropriate for Weight Watchers. I am used to sushi rolls being close to 2 inches in diameter and these were closer to 1 1/4 inch and each slice barely a bite.
We were given the bill for another guest at the end of our meal. Coincidentally, an identical total amount so we can excuse that one.
An ok dinner if staying at the hotel but certainly not a destination restaurant.
name: Bruce

text: Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Food was good and came out fast. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. Not bad for a quick meal. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. The food was good and the service was easygoing. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..
name: User

text: This our favorite place when We come to Reno. Staff is wonderful, Food is great. Highly recommend.
name: Beth

text: We ended up at Burger Up after waiting over an hour at a nearby popular burger place (and still another 20 minutes to go!) and are we glad we did! Burgers are fresh and tasty with a good variety to choose from. The house mustard and ketchup are a great add to your burger and fries.. Much better than the traditional Heinz. The potato soup was good but is more broth based than cream based we expected (although it did have cream in it) so be aware. Very delicious. And the Krispy Creme donut dessert (like a bread budding) was soooooo much better than traditional bread pudding. It was really my favorite part of the menu. It's hard to get really good desserts at places that don't specialize in desserts but Burger Up nailed this!!The location is great! You can shoot next door to The Soda Parlor if ice cream desserts are your thing. But you won't need to because the Krispy Creme Pudding will take care of your sweet tooth. Get it. You won't regret it. The service was amazing. He was busy but still attentive. We will be back and recommend to friends.
name: Ianthia

text: Best steak and chicken fajitas around. Great atmosphere and even better drinks! I highly suggest getting the tres amigos. Also if you are doing the fajitas for two make sure you are both big eaters otherwise you will have a ton of leftovers. Two people could easily share just the one serving of the combo fajitas and get more than enough food. I really liked their chips and the white quest that they have. The strawberry margarita is super good too! This please will not disappoint.
name: Sara

text: I want to start off by saying I am personally not a big fan of pho. I guess I should say I WAS not a big fan of pho. After a long weekend of punishing my liver with heavy drinking, my girlfriend and I decided to try this place located right next to our favorite grocery store (First Oriental FTW). I went for the number 13 (all the meats) and the bowl came out almost instantly. The large portion is a misnomer as the bowl is the size of a medium pizza. The broth is clear and beyond flavorful, and submerged beneath the surface of that amazing broth are piles of perfectly cooked meats and noodles. I decided to eat the noodles using my spoon as a small for so I can add more heat with their sriracha and chilli sauce options without changing the broth as I wanted to savor every sip of it untainted. And after eating until the point of being uncomfortably full, I still had enough for another meal to take home. My experience was so memorable that I returned the next day for lunch and got the same thing. Don't miss out on this place!
name: Jeff

text: Strangelove's is a great place to grab a beer after wrok. Good local draft selection, and many of the beers are $3 during happy hour. The vegan nachos are among the city's best, and can be had for a mere $5 during happy hour. Recommended.
name: Roger

text: Wasn't that great to me. Took a total of three times for bf and I to get to come play a game the first two times they were packed (after going, I'm not sure why). This time we went on a Saturday night and honestly I was not impressed by anything, not the drinks, not the food, not the bowling, definitely not the prices. Our server never even asked if I wanted another cocktail, which I did. I'll drive the extra 10 mins over the bridge to Pinsetter which has a bar, better prices, parking, and a lot more lanes next time.

text:
Sunday brunch - got there around 12pm. No one else is waiting but I have to wait to be seated for about 5 minutes. The place was not packed. Waiting for food was also brutal. It would be a challenge to come here if I want to just get in and out. 

Veggie Benedict - the white eggs were not even white and still somewhat clear. This was too raw to my liking. The overall dish tasted good though. Just enough salt and flavor from veggie and mushroom. The fries seemed like it was left on the stove for too long - hard and burned. 

Chicken and waffle Benedict - looks good but very bland. Eggs were also too raw and potatoes were left cooked for too long. 

Ordered a side of pancake - nothing special. Fluffy but not much taste. 

Our waitress was nice and attentive.

text: Terrible experience...apps. we're horrible..octopus inedible...waiter. just plain dumb..or inattentive..gave my one friend the wrong sauce..and the other the wrong spaghetti..only a butter knife to cut the veal parm..put food on the table..and we had to flag him down for every l last  thing..pass on this place...we were going to sit outside...but passed....trash..!

text: Got takeout from here twice now so I feel like I can say a little more. Food was fresh and service was quick. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text:
The guava cheesecake was a ten out of ten, absolutely excellent. The cook seems to take pride on the presentation and quality of cooking the food. Few adjustments needed. The presentation of the food is that of a chef who is becoming excellent. The presentation on the menu and presentation of the food on the plate is excellent. Awesome idea to use iPads to look at the menu, loved it!
Now the taste of some of the food was too bland needing P.R. flavor. Would be excellent if it had a little more flavor. Not horrible just lacking flavor. The bar setting, the flatscreen TVs, and the music makes the environment better.
There is a disconnect between the server and the service received by customers.
If you can make the service as good as the cheesecake you have the potential to become a top ten restaurant in the area.
Server was very inattentive. Customer service when it comes to being attentive from beginning to end of the customer experience is lacking and is below 4 on a scale of 1-10. The lack of sense of urgency contributed to unnecessary waiting time and thirsty customer waiting for a refill. Never was able to order my drinks because server never came back to get the order for any drinks. 
Server never checked in at the table other than to place the initial rushed order and to receive the bill. Servers must check in more often for drinks and desserts to make your service better and make sure customers get what they want and need. Servers were totally Frankeinstein straight faced, no smile nor pleasant interaction. 
Alcapurrias are way overpriced and seemed to get all the salt the rest of the food needed, alcapurrias were pure salt. You get more for your money buying alcapurrias at La Isla Restaurant at Pinellas Park.
The ceviche was very good and the price was ok. The bathrooms need to be cleaned. There is no excuse for a filthy bathroom in a P.R. restaurant. There are pros and cons to this restaurant. A lot of potential to become one of the best if they make the necessary adjustments to improve. I have eaten in many restaurants and tasted and even smelled what Latin flavor is and what it is not. Perhaps my military background is causing me to have too high of a standard but anyone who is going to pay 40 dollars or more deserves great quality, cleanliness, and great service not anything that is mediocre.
name: Heri

text: Today was probably our "hundredth" time going to Jack's for lunch. And unfortunately, we left before ordering. The problem was we couldn't even get anyone to come take our order. Waitstaff was attentive to other tables; even to those who were seated after us. And the staff person who took our drinks order was rude. It just wasn't our day, I guess. The service and care just doesn't seem to be a priority anymore.

text: Best ribeye I've ever had. Everything they serve is top notch and my girlfriend and I have made this our anniversary dinner location. I've tried plenty of other steakhouse around Pinellas County and none compare to Bascom's.

text:

text:
I don't know what has happened to the McDonald's across from the Silver Legacy. It is really having some issues with staffing and quality of food. My visit tonight was not a very good experience as it took almost 10 minutes for two double cheeseburgers. It wasn't too busy as it normally is during the day
 Plus the shorter hours closing before 9:00 p.m. on a Friday night? But then again maybe it isn't as busy like it was because of the quality of the food. The only thing keeping it going is the $1,$2 and $3 menu deals that help the budget minded visiting or traveling in the downtown area. The trash was overflowing in most of the containers too.
name: Doug

text:
It is sad to see a 3 star average review for this place. The food here is the best breakfast and lunch food in the area. If I want to take someone out for lunch, this is my go to place. The menu is fairly short and to the point, but at the same time, everything is customizable, so you can specify a particular type of bread or cheese. For example, they have 10 types of cheese available and no other place in the area has that many choices. They always have a varietal and flavor coffee each day. They make the fancy lattes with the swirl on top. Made to order smoothies. You can order anything on the menu and it will be made perfect every time. All the ingredients are fresh and they have 2 soups each day which change weekly. The prices are a bit higher than other places for lunch, but we find the quality of the food to be worth the extra cost. Their method of payment is kind of odd, but it is how they choose to do it to make things easier overall. You pay up front, get a number and they serve your food, they kind of expect you to clear your table and trash when you are finished, and they have a tip jar that gets shared for the staff. So you are not obligated to tip one individual server. The place is fairly small and has one restroom, which is good and bad. It is private and clean. 

After eating here many times, the same thing people are leaving negative reviews for this place also makes it one of the most positive. The chef is so passionate about the food she serves that the way she treats her employees comes across as negative when she really wants the best for them, but still the customer comes first. Owning a restaurant is a hard business and while it comes across as yelling, she is trying to teach all of her employees at the same time. She is very strict about food safety and will strait up yell at her employees in front of everyone, but I see it more as a positive learning experience for them. As a customer you will get the most respect and very good quality food that you are paying for. And they have one register and balance walk in orders with phone orders, so sometimes the line will get backed up. And not as important, but really cool, and kind of shows the personality of the owner, they play the most cool mix of music. Oldies to reggae and sometimes an odd mix of music and it makes the time spent that much better. The busy times are hard to predict, but often it gets very busy on the weekends. Usually the weekdays are less crowded. But expect to wait in a line on the weekends, sometimes they get slammed. They have a few newspapers to read and bins of toys for kids to play with. This is a really cool breakfast and lunch place, great for bringing family, friends, or having a business interview.
name: Andrew

text: I enjoyed it! Fun environment. Ordered my pizza to go and they didn't cut it. Don't know if that was an accident or something they don't do in to go orders? Also friend said the drinks from the soda fountain seemed really watered down. I agreed. May have just be an issue with the system. Anyways, pizza was good! Will be coming back.
name: Siena

text: The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. They were out of one thing I originally wanted..

text: Stopped by after work because I was nearby and hungry. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly.

text:
Went there for the first time the other day with my partner and their family. It was excellent! Between the 4 of us, we ordered 3 of the combination platters. We are all fairly big eaters and it was the perfect amount of food. Had just enough room for some delicious baklava for dessert! Good service as well. I wish I could recall all of the different dishes, but there were so many I don't even know where to start.
 Only disappointment is that they had turned off the espresso machine by the time we had dessert. 
I can definitely see this being a go-to place in West Philly

text: Very Disappointed! The host didn't bring us to the seat, she just gave us the menu and let us to find an empty table by ourselves. Also, the waiter was not friendly and made us not want to come here anymore!

text: This restaurant provides a nice dose of Chinese food - I like the noodle soups that they have. The restaurant is usually quite busy, as it is conveniently placed underneath Sheraton Hotel and right next to a university. However, there is usually enough space, so you don't have to wait too long. The portion sizes are large, and the price isn't too expensive. The service is alright, but the staff seem really rushed and try to hurry you along.
name: Bel

text:
First time here. Got, to go: won ton soup (pretty tasty. I loved the large size won ton s), one shrimp egg roll, a roast pork roll, beef with broccoli. Unlike a lot of reviewers I liked, for the most part, what I ordered.

Though the shrimp egg roll wrapper was VERY greasy I was pleasantly surprised the roll itself wasn't (oil soaked wrapper aided that, probably). Having said that, that one wasn't as tasty as the pork. I'm enjoying the beef with broccoli still. (Only complaint about latter it could be a bit tastier too.)

4-5 stars, had everything been seasoned better.
name: Joan

text:
This always looks like a very cutesy touristy place to me but also entices me every time I pass their charming space.  So I finally went, heck,  do the "staycation" thing,  one Sunday morning. 
It was busy but service was attentive  and food arrived quite quickly. Complimentary kringle which was very sweet.  Normal breakfast~brunch fare with some thoughtful specials.  It was okay, just fine. Presented nicely but nothing amazing. 
They have a special dog menu; what a kick! 
Desert and treats here are something special here,  ( mmmm...love the  scrumptious pumpkin kiringle),   and there I've always had  always stellar service. 
I think it  is a lovely place to sit outside and just have desert with good friends ( & furry ones too) , local or visiting.
name: Felice

text: For a busy night they handled it okay. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated bc we didn't have a reservation. Definitely coming back. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..
name: User

text: My friend liked it more than I did. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. Maybe better dine-in than delivery, hard to tell.
name: User

text:
Skip this place. BBQ in Santa Barbara is generally poor and this place is no exception. Buddy of mine and myself ordered the variety plate and the chicken, ribs, and pulled pork were a complete joke. Dry, badly seasoned, poorly executed food. It was so bad we didn't even eat most of the meat, as seen in the attached picture. 

The one saving grace was the brisket, so I went to order more of it with an Axxess deal. The brisket combo is $16, which is one dollar more than their BOGO Axxess deal max. No problem, right? They'd probably just take $15 off the cost. However, the cashier said this wasn't possible and when he asked someone else behind the counter, they loudly exclaimed that they would "absolutely not" do that and offered no alternative options. Seriously? I simply said "we're going somewhere else" and left. My friends couldn't believe it when I told them how it played out. 

TOTAL miss for both the food and service. Let this one die off like all of the other mediocre restaurants that the Public Market has chewed up and spat out since it opened. Go to Empty Bowl or Corazon instead.
name: Michael

text: Neat concept but the service is the worst. The manager Paul was great I highly recommend this cool spot best flat bread and fries
name: Joe

text: I found my taco spot! Ive moved nearby about 9 months ago and wished I had found this place earlier. Great al pastor tacos! Steak tacos good too. I had a burrito a la mexicana and it was really really tasty. Look at the picture and you will def want to order it. Taco Tuesdays they have $1 tacos! Horchata was refreshing. Plus free chips with refried beans on top when you eat in, not a big deal but I like the little things. Go and you won't regret it.
name: J

text:
Due to some health issues since Dec we've had to tamper down our dining out so that I could adhere to a bland, boring diet.  Well, now that I am 90% back to normal we figured we come back to Acqua e Farina for my first pizza in 3 months.  This is not just any pizza, it's more artesian and a good part "heart" by Salvatore the pizza chef extraordinaire; he has outdone himself. 

We came on Sunday with friends and we all walked out with happy bellies.  Each couple started with a menu salad, FORMAGGI E NOCI [SPRING MIX TOSSED WITH WALNUTS, BEETS & WARM GOAT CHEESE IN OUR HOUSE DRESSING] and ALLA ARUGOLETTA  [ARUGULA SALAD TOSSED WITH RADICCHIO IN OUR HOUSE DRESSING TOPPED WITH SHAVED PARMIGIANO]  both were very good and so fresh that no DNA was left on the plates. 

Next, my wife asked an order of the stuffed meatballs, used to be on the menu, you can ask for it.  Possible one ball as already made and waiting while they made the second; one was soft and tasty while the other was burnt and hard.  So so.

For our pizza selections, my wife and I ordered the SICILIANA [FRESH TOMATO SAUCE, BUFFALO MOZZARELLA & EGGPLANT]  and our friends had the CONTADINA [FRESH TOMATO SAUCE, BUFFALO MOZZARELLA, ROASTED PEPPERS, KALAMATA OLIVES, EGGPLANT, ZUCCHINI & MUSHROOMS WITH OIL & BASIL; both were terrific an no leftovers.  

The crusts were puffy with slight burn marks from the wood-burning oven, you could smell the pleasant aromas from the oven.  Like in the three little bears story, these pizzas were just right.
name: Brian

text:
First time visit at suggestion of a friend... did not disappointment! 
Beautiful sunset view at the end of the Stearns Wharf Pier... 
Sat at the bar and ordered the specialty 1lb lobster with onion rings and slaw. Cold glass of beer to wash it down. 
The shellfish was steam cooked and finished off on the grill, leaving it succulent and sweet complimented by the wedge of lemon and melted drawn butter. 
The coolness and acidity of the slaw and the crunch of the perfectly deep fried rings was artful simplicity at its best! 
At the next visit I'll try the crab on a bed of linguini pasta, that passed by...
name: G

text: Rude people. Not kid friendly. Full price on kids ayce no matter what age. I probably would have tried if was just the adults. Had 2 kids 7 and 8, would love to go up to the line a couple times with us and probably get small portions. The hostess showed us a small metal bowl and said this is kid size. If they go a 2nd time, will be charged for 2 trips. Place was fairly empty compared to the noodle place across the parking lot. Sorry had to go across the way and had better service and food.
name: Tech

text: Love the look and feel of this restaurant, and it's perfect for brunch or dinner time. Their happy hour prices from 4-8 are unbelievable, and I also love trying to guess the popcorn flavor your server brings out. Some of the menu options are a bit overpriced and the service can be slow as they start to get busy, but overall I enjoy every time I come here!

text: Amazing! I love the daiquiris here! They are so fresh and made with real fresh ingredients. It's almost like an icy smoothie with liquor. The crawfish was excellent but the wait time was a little long. There was only one person working the front area which slowed the service down a lot but the lady working the front was awesome and managed to keep everything moving.
name: Chelsey

text:
OMG!!!! How is it that I have not been here before today!!!!  
What a find! It is a little, kinda ratty looking place, may have been a fast food place that had gone out of business. Well now, it has some of the best Mexican food I had.  It is very small and very busy. It only has a counter with some stools and a few more stools along the wall. The kitchen is right there so you can see everything as it is prepared. There is outside space to sit and the hot dog station is out on the patio. I decided to try several options... I started with an asada caramelo the meat was tasty and tender... then I had one of the ribs they were cooking right in front of me as I sat at the counter. The rib was tender and meaty but a bit salty. I then got a pastor taco ( again tender and tasty) and then another asada caramelo. I added a soda with all of the other items..all that for $13. There is an ample salsa bar with all the fixings including 3 salsas, pico de gallo, cukes, onions, radishes etc....If I didn't have company coming and a quiche in the oven I might just go back for dinner.
name: Laurel-Heather

text:
Great place to get ingredients you wouldn't find elsewhere. 

My friend was making pho from scratch so he was in need of some pretty specific ingredients that you don't find at your neighborhood Publix. We started at MD Oriental, but there were two spices he couldn't find. He also was prepared to go to a butcher to get beef bones. Lucky for us, I called Melony R. while we were at MD Oriental and she said we should check this place out to find our missing ingredients. She was right! We ended up finding everything else. Funny enough, the two things we ended up getting at Publix, cheese cloth and jugs of water, we couldn't find here. 

They have a fresh meat section in the back where you can get filet and beef bones! It looked pretty legit. If I lived closer, I would get all my meat from there. 

This place is pretty big. It definitely fills a niche and has different ingredients than what you'd find at Publix or even MD Oriental. People who live in this area are super lucky!
name: Christina

text: Moved to Exton area and have tried all the local pizzerias and Mario's is by far the tastiest around. I consider myself a pizza aficionado and can tell the difference in quality of ingredients. We order the pepperoni with the spicy peppers and wowzas! Definitely give this local hole in the wall pizza place a shot!
name: Yvette

text:
This place is EXTREMELY FANCY! My SO and I popped by as it's part of the newly renovate area (right next to a badly needed new parking structure in front of the funk zone!). We only needed a cup of coffee but scoped our the place and thought it was just okay for our taste. 

They have an amazing cold brew coffee, yummy pastry and cute space but overall the food was VERY expensive, not a lot of options, slower service and seem to only apply to a niche of people.

I'll be back to try other items on the menu and update my review to make sure I'm not being harsh, but overall sadly wasn't too impressed by this new place!

- J
name: Jess

text:
This week, a group of friends and I checked out a new spot, La Mordida Grill. This is a Peruvian and Columbian restaurant that had great reviews, so we had to check it out. 

A group of us met there about 7 PM. We were greeted and seated immediately.  Our service was great throughout our visit. They have a full bar so we started out with a few cocktails and appetizers. I ordered yucca fries, cheese sticks, and an arepa with chorizo. A buddy ordered an arepa with blood sausage as well. For our main meals I went with La Mordida full HD burger. It came with a beef patty, chicken, fried egg, cheese, bacon, and chorizo. My girlfriend ordered the cazuela paisa which was a large bowl of pork and beans. My buddy ordered the choriperro which was a huge hotdog with chorizo, slaw, cheese, and crushed potato chips. All of our food came out in decent time and it looked great. They also delivered the food with a wonderful assortment of various sauces that were loaded with flavor. My burger was a beautiful monster! It had so many different meats and textures. The flavor was amazing and I really enjoyed it. My buddies hot dog looked amazing as well and he enjoyed his meal. The pork and bean stew my girlfriend had was very tasty too. Everyone enjoyed their meals and appetizers.  

Overall, we had a great meal. We tried food that we had no idea was offered in Columbia and Peru. The meal we had was very tasty and reasonably priced.The owner and chef came out and introduced himself towards the end of our meal. He told us about a few upcoming events and live music they will be hosting soon. We really enjoyed ourselves and will be back soon to sample some other menu items.
name: Joshua

text: Good cupcakes. I've never eaten here but the plates look good. Espresso beverages are good. Slightly better than average. Only drawback is that only one register makes the wait to order seem very long.
name: Danae

text:
Great little cafe with romantic atmosphere! We decided to eat here because the reviews looked great & the dress code was casual. The hubby had the special which was a jerk style pork tenderloin. The flavors were delicious according to him and accompanied with yummy green beans. He also really liked the local Nola beer.  I had the citrus chicken, which the server recommended for being marinated in fancy citrus from a local farm. The chicken was baked and was juicy and savory with a lemon/citrus flavor. They served it with asparagus and mashed potatoes, that were excellently prepared. We also shared a beet salad with goat cheese that was very generous with the roasted beets in balsamic drizzle. We did not have dessert because we had a party to attend later but the table next to us had an amazingly decorative seven layers cake I wanted to try!!  

The service was excellent and I enjoyed the old fashioned romance of the building, we ate in the carriage house. The patio is adorable but it was too hot weather when we visited in a June day.
name: Megan

text: Great place to try to eat healthier and have a quality food pizza with friends.  The modern look and feel inside is pleasing and I am glad to have this an another lunch option locally.
name: Kevin

text: Finally experienced terra sur.. It is questionable as to why I have not eaten here yet since I have heard sooooo many great things. So finally my boyfriend and I stopped in on Labor Day for a good dinner. We were seated right away and I really enjoyed the paintings and atmosphere all over the restaurant. It's a romantic/ warm welcoming atmosphere. For dinner we ordered the JALEA mix & the tallarin verde.. while waiting for our food we were brought some hot delicious bread.. which was wonderful because I was starving and who doesn't love being served bread. Our food came out shortly after. The pasta was out of this world but my boyfriend wasn't crazy about his steak.. it was a little more cooked than what he had asked for. And as for my JALEA.. the fish was a little on the colder side.. but flavor wise everything was delicious and portion size was wonderful as well! I'm sure we'll eventually be back to bring my parents!
name: Jenna

text: Parking was annoying and I was already in a bad mood by the time I got inside. Also, pretty smooth experience from start to finish. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. So yeah, the tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than i pictured from the photos. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Not bad for a quick meal. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait.
name: User

text:
After extensive research about Tennessee hot fried chicken, I choose Hattie b's and we were not disappointed by any means. The chicken was like going to super market and getting a rotisserie chicken, but the flavors in the fried skin were fantastic. 

The line moves quickly and efficiently. You basically pick your chicken...white, dark, etc and you pick your spice level. I picked damn hot and it was HOT. I couldn't eat it straight up, I had to eat the juicy chicken with pieces of the spice to limit the amount of spice on each bite. The sides were good..I would suggest putting some of the vinegar based hot sauce on the greens. 

I would return back to Hattie bs again and I truly enjoyed it more than the local bbq.
name: Arthur

text: Food is good, service suuuuucks. Definitely avoid if you're with a date, group or family, or any situation where you don't want to be frustrated or disappointed. My guy and I came on a Thursday night, 8:30 p.m. and the poor waitresses were way understaffed and disorganized, completely befuddled by two larger tables, though the rest of the place was pretty slow. When we finally got our drinks and food it was great, no complaints about what we ate (dip trio, shrimp appetizer, nachos) but we had to wait awhile for it, or for any drink refills and any follow-up requests (definitely need more chips ... with everything). Overall they just need better management and they'll be fine.
name: Emily

text: Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. No big complaints, just a nice meal. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. You can tell they care about customer experience here. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. A very pleasant experience. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly.
name: User

text:
Get ready for a journey that Zahav takes you through with food. So first thing we did not have reservations but it was a snowy night so we figured we could walk in.  There is usually a two house wait but it goes pretty quickly and not really the two hours.  We were seated in about an hour.  While you wait you can get drinks and just people watch.  Finally we sat down and since I had the reviews we stuck to the chefs tasting menu. Between two people you get to choose from one hummus.. go for the Turkish it's really soft and creamy... four from the mezze and two al ha esh.. if you want the lamb get there early or have a reservation it usually sells out pretty quickly. Along the way the service staff did an amazing job speaking to us about the food and restaurant.  This truly feels like a place of amazing things are happening just from the hummus you can tell why this is a James beard award winning chef.  Chef Michael came around and spoke to us.  You will never feel
Rushed and the attention to detail is far beyond. From clean utensils to bringing out the actual ingredients of what you are eating is phenomenal.  As for the food this is both a vegetarians delight and a meat eaters paradise.  This is place to discover  what makes Israeli cuisine and taste the influences from the region that creates this.  The desserts are also very unique and I would try them all.  From the first course that features  a vegetable medley to the final drop of good Israeli vine I give this place a perfect 5 stars..
name: Arjun

text: Good solid Mexican food that you're familiar with. All dishes I've tried are very tasty with good fresh ingredients. BYOTequila and they provide margherita mix what's not to like
name: T

text:
I got to Hattie B's at the tail end of a rain storm, thinking "perfect! If it's raining, no one will be in line!". Wrong! Apparently half of the Nashville tourists share our same love for fried chicken.

There were about 75 people in line ahead of us at 2:30pm on a Saturday. Ordered at 3:30pm, and got our food at 4:00pm. It was an hour and a half wait, but it was worth every bite!

So obviously we went all out. We ordered a large white meat meal that was the equivalent to a half a chicken. We went with the "Hot" seasoning temp. It had a great kick to it, so I recommend to all my spicy eating Yelpers out there.  We also added three tenders, because why not! Chicken was so incredibly moist and had a perfect thin layer of seasoning.  For sides, we went with the Mac and cheese (soooo creamy!!!) and crinkle cut fries (they come seasoned!!!).  Then we got an additional side of really delicious pickles for an extra $0.50.

Outside is covered so we didn't have to worry about getting rained on or fighting for one of the seven tables inside. There is some hip music playing in the background so it gives you a little something to rock out to that isn't the sound of your stomach rumbling while waiting for the food. 

Overall, if you don't mind waiting, I would definitely check out Hattie B's.  If you don't want to wait, at least order online and go pick it up!
name: Jeannine

text: The sauce carried most of the meal. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. I can see why people like it, even if I wasn't fully sold. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait.
name: User

text: Tried this several times, and each time the food is cold and even taste a little weird compared to the regular restaurant.  Also usually have missing items. We paid too much for these types of mistakes.  Fool me once shame on you, fool me twice, shame on me.  Will not make this mistake again.
name: Kim

text: Possibly one of the worst Mexican restaurants I've ever been to. The queso didn't even taste like queso, their idea of "melted cheese" was putting a slice of cheese on top of the nachos and melting it in a microwave. Terrible. Just disappointing.
name: Matt

text: I'd been wanting to try this restaurant ever since we moved near Mass Ave. we finally went on a special occasion and it was such a treat. We started with dumplings and eggs rolls which were both delicious- especially the dumplings. Then we split the chicken pad Thai which was also great. We even had a full take home box to take with us-big portions!! On top of that they had drink specials on their vodka. Staff was very nice and it was a relaxed, inviting atmosphere.
name: Karley

text:
I have been here multiple times and it's always been a great experience.
Tried many dishes, noodles based, rice based, curries and they are all awesome. Great flavors, as spicy as you wish and with really fresh ingredients.
Service is really good, very attentive and friendly.
The restaurant itself is very well decorated, plants everywhere and beautiful colors.
This place stands up to any Thai place I have been in Philly city center. 
If you are local and looking for Thai, this is the spot. If not local I would say it's worth a trip.
Oh, the fresh pot of coffee is really good!
name: Stephen

text: Cute little place.  We popped in at Christmas Eve so of course figured it would be busy.  Snagged a table in front patio to watch the parade.  Ordered a bottle of wine & 4 tapas dishes.  We were told kitchen was 45 minutes behind.  Hour later & on to our second bottle of wine & no food.  Started noticing tables arriving before us ordering, eating & leaving.  First dish came out 1 hour & 15 min after we ordered.  Next two dishes 30 minutes later then 45 minutes after that.  When a table sat and were told it was 2 hours for food then after 15 minutes asked for their food & it starts coming out we cancelled our last dish & left. Had to go buy another meal elsewhere.  3 hours, 2 bottles of wine & very little food.   Server never told us ovens went out but we heard it mentioned to other tables.  When I'm spending more at a table of two than a table of 8 I expect updates.  No discount either & table beside us got free dessert for their wait.  Will try again as I have heard it's an awesome place but leaving me sit for 3 hours with no updates or food was a bit too disappointing for me
name: Tina

text: I love this place. The spicy miso ramen is spot on.  I ordered mine to-go and they packaged everything separately so that it maintained its integrity when I came home and put all together again. Staff is friendly and the service is quick even when they are busy.
name: T.

text:
My first time here. The front entrance is so nondescript as to disappear. It wasn't really obvious that it was the main entrance, and I might not have pulled on the door if it hadn't been the only door near the corner. But inside it was quite attractive, and larger than it appeared. The staff was friendly and inviting. 

I admit to being slightly disappointed compared to the reviews that brought me here, but in the end, great service bumped it up to 4 stars. The food alone might have been slightly lower. The alligator was very tender and delicious, and the roast pork was very good but not great. The Lima beans and Mac and cheese were great, though.

Beyond the food, the service was very attentive and prompt. The vibe was very hipster, and my "older" group didn't seem typical of the customers. The beer list was minimal. The sound level was quite loud, although maybe if I drank more I wouldn't have noticed. I'd not hesitate to come here again, but admit I wouldn't travel far to come here. In my normal rating system, that would reduce the rating to 3 stars, but the service and some of the food should be higher, so I arrived at 4.
name: Chuck

text: The music was louder than it needed to be. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. Will be back. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. Food was good and came out fast. No big complaints, just a nice meal. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.
name: User

text: Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. Ordered a few things and liked most of it.
name: User

text:
The food is like drunk food. So like if you want to get a little lit after work and munch on something, you wouldn't really mind the quality. I've only gone sober for a quick lunch and it's okay (I mean you can't mess up chicken tenders) but the 2 Star is really for service. 

The service is very selective. If you aren't a regular or white, I'm just putting it out there for my black folks, then the service is poor. I watched them do it but my most recent encounter will be my last. Needless to say I didn't even get a chance to order anything because I wasn't waited on.
name: Ayanna

text: Croque Madame, Ham & Cheese quiche, Key Lime tart. Food was fresh, good, and very flavorful.
name: Channing

text: I ordered from this restaurant while staying at the Springwood Suites on Canal Street, they popped a menu under my door. I ordered the margarita pizza online. Delivery was fast and free and the pizza was hot when it arrived. Absolutely delicious! It's made with the freshest tomatoes, basil and loads of top-quality fresh mozzarella. Homemade Ranch Dressing made for a scrumptious dipping sauce. Highly recommend!
name: Kerry

text: This place is amazing.  The food is excellent and the service was great.  We have ordered from here two days in a row because they are so good!
name: Jonie

text: We have attended conventions in Louisiana and have been meaning to check it out.  I had the blackened fish of the day and my wife had grilled chicken pasta.  Service was good, food was above average, and price was above average.  If you are staying at the convention center hotels nearby and looking for a place to eat, this is a good choice.  It has a large dining hall so seating should not be a problem.
name: Ray

text:
Finding out about Jimmy John's delivery was a HUGE game changer. Since learning about it two weeks ago, I've already ordered delivery 3 times. I'm always stunned by how quickly it comes (often in less than 10 minutes)!!

The subs are delicious, but the pickles are the main reason I keep coming back. I truly have yet to find anywhere with better and bigger pickles. They also sell buckets of them, which is wonderful but dangerous. They're so good I can't trust myself not to eat them all in one sitting!

The staff is exceptionally friendly. I've never had such great conversations with servers at other fast food joints!
name: Nicole

text:
The restaurant looked promising. It's small and just 4-5 families can fit, then you're sitting at the bar, which accommodates 3 people and a cash register.

The beef was very good, but that's the best part. The chicken on several items that I've been there is boiled and hard. Traditional Vietnamese food but much lower quality ingredients give it a loss of a star.

If you expect high quality foods, there's one on the south side of waters close to Dale Mabry. Same atmosphere but completely different food quality.

If you're wanting traditional Viet, Waters and Dale Mabry or West Waters by Wheeltec is better.
name: Chris

text:
Went with my husband and my dad. They got pizza by the slice with bread sticks and loved it. They just rolled out an updated menu today and I tried the new eggplant Parmesan sandwich, it was amazing! (10/10 would recommend). The owner was very friendly and personally checked in with us several times.
The atmosphere is really nice, music was great, and there are arcade machines. Definitely a family friendly establishment!
name: Olivia

text:
Like many, i love a place that combines food, drinks, and games! Went here to celebrate my nephews bday. We decided to go on a Sunday at abt 11am. This was a great way to beat the crowds. There is convenient paid parking in the bldg but I was able to score free parking on the street...no meters on Sundays. We werent given many options for seating...they had half of the seating closed. This sucked for a group of little kids..pub height chairs arent the best for them.

I dont like their policy of kids being allowed until they close...but thats my own selfish issue..at midnight I dont wanna have to wait for a 3yr old to finish air hockey so i can play it (happened to me previously). 

Crystal was our server and she was great! Very attentive with our group and efficient. The food was pretty good for bar type food. There are specials that combine food with game play. The games are pretty pricey. Overall my nephew had a good time so thats what counts but I dont think this will be a regular place for me to hang out.
name: Uriia

text:
A real homey diner just off the NJ. Turnpike. Selina our most friendly and cheerful waitress was the charm and the highlight. It didn't matter that the coffee was weak and the home fries bland. (Throw an onion in with those spuds next time). Patrons were a lovely bunch of characters from the 7-year-old-boy with his grandpapa to the older women friends sharing life advice. Overheard: 
"Pick up that lamb chop and eat it with your fingers, that's what god gave them to you for." Directly across the street from a towering DuPont industrial site, (no odor once inside the restaurant) it was a slice of Americana worth visiting. And great prices! 

Husband disagrees about the coffee comment and was very pleased with his combo breakfast.
name: Maggie

text: I have been here multiple times and the staff is always friendly.  today Grace and Peter helped me. I was searching for a wine and though they didn't have it, she searched for it and I was able to sample a few other wines with Peter... This is a great place if you are looking for wine , beer or spirits and don't quite know what you want as they are very knowledgeable here
name: Felicia

text: This place has been on my list to try and so glad I finally did! Every flavor looks amazing, but we settled on banana stracciatella, pistachio, and salted almond for the flight. We also ordered a scoop of raspberry (non-dairy) and it was equally delicious. Every flavor was delicious and unique in its own way-definitely recommend the banana and pistachio. The staff was extremely generous the whole time and let us try samples first. Definitely coming back to cure my gelato cravings.
name: Khoi

text: At one point when I lived here before I would have given this place 5 stars.  Things have changed.  I don't think there is anything on the menu I would rave about, but the chips and salsa are always good.  The strawberry margarita used to be the main draw, but with our last trip even they seemed to have changed the recipe.  I love the guys at the bar.  Matt is the best.  If you want a drink and some chips and salsa come here.
name: Julie

text: Portion size looked small at first but it was actually enough. For a busy night they handled it okay. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. I can see why people like it, even if I wasn't fully sold. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. Nice little spot, decent portions too. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable.
name: User

text: Great food took my family here for Dillion's birthday and he loved the rice and chicken combo. My other son Kyle, who is soooo annoying got fajitas keep in mind he's 5 and split it all over him self, melting his cock off. So now i have a daughter named Kyle smh.
name: Clint

text: I adore this location! The manager is such a sweat heart and Rachel, the assistant manager I believe (or needs to be) is so kinda and funny and super quick! She's always a joy to see and knows exactly how I like my bowl! I come here with my girlfriends every Sunday after work and frequently through out the week on my lunch breaks! Awesome place to go!
name: Kiri

text: I wanted to like this more than I actually did. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. There were a couple things I liked and a couple things I probably wouldn't get again. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon.
name: User

text: We LOVE this place. Great tacos for a very affordable price. It's never a long wait and my favorites are Fajita chicken and Fried chicken. Delicious.
name: Jules

text: Stopped by after work because I was nearby and hungry. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Food was fresh and service was quick. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. A very pleasant experience. The food was good and the service was easygoing.
name: User

text: We walked up to order, and you would have thought they had never had walkup customers before. They seemed confused, which made us confused and made the ordering process more difficult. The food was solid. About what you would expect from Sonic. The only other thing was that they brought the wrong amount of change out when we paid for our meal.
name: Jacob

text: Overall, not super impressed. I gave it 3 stars because there was nothing overtly WRONG with the food. I've been here twice now. My first impression was pretty good, but I thought It was fairly pricey for what you got. Each pie is about $8 and roughly the size of my fist. I got one to start, and it wasn't much at all. The atmosphere was warm and trendy and the staff was generally helpful enough. Went back a second time and It was very disappointing. Ordered food to go that was in the case when we ordered. They said they would bring it right out, gave us a number, and we waited a good half hour. The food was ready in the case, so it would appear the ticket never got sent through or whatever. After a pretty frustrating amount of time a manager came over and asked us about our order. He went and immediately got it out of the case and we left. Got all the way to our destination and they got my order completely wrong. I'm assuming pies were put in the wrong spot, but I ordered a vegetarian pie and got steak and gravy. Pretty sad when you were aiming for a meat free option. I tried calling and nobody ever answered so I messaged on Facebook and I got an automated response saying they would get right back to me. That was a week ago now so I've long since given up hope of them caring to rectify the situation. Honestly not bad or good food. Just middle of the road, but the employees don't seem to have their ducks in a row.
name: Brianna

text: Delicious! Ordered the monkey burger and green Chile fries. Service was great and delicious food.
name: Nealy

text: Loved this place!  It's a bit misleading from the front, but this is no dive.  Very clean and nice.  Even the bathrooms were nice and clean.  Food was outstanding and the wait staff very attentive.  Their specialty is fajitas and I can't say that I've had better.  One order is likely enough for two people to share - we took home a considerable amount of leftovers.  Pretty convenient to get here if you're traveling I-75 between Tampa and Sarasota as we were.  You'll be happy you stopped by!
name: Jeff

text: We had an amazing dinner here last night!  Great food - we had Lobster, swordfish, and oysters. The service was excellent.
name: Kaya

text: Super great service from Alex S! She was wonderful. Margaritas were delicious! Spicy Mango Margarita had the right combination of sweet and spicy. Will definitely be back for Saints game day with bottomless margaritas!
name: Tracey

text:
I love me a good brunch spot, and Half & Half fits that bill just fine. Blueberry pancakes were super good. Very fluffy with crispy edges, my favorite! Biscuits and gravy were also good. Despite the biscuits with hard bottoms, the gravy was super savory with a slight kick. Very delicious.

Only negative:  our male server was wearing super tiny shorts and you could see the outline of his business which was very off putting while he's leaning across the table delivering food. I'm all for freedom of expression, but maybe not while you're crotch-level with your customers?

Overall, though, very good food. We'll come back next time we're in St Louis.
name: Dianna

text: Really delicious pizza. I have ordered from here 3 times so far because it's so close to my new house. The pizza toppings are really good and I appreciate the diverse selection in pizza options but I will say that all 3 times my pizza crust was over cooked. The pizza was still good but it would be GREAT if it wasn't overcooked !
name: Velour

text: Wonderful food and even better service!!! We will definitely go back! I love that you can do half portions so that you can try more than one thing on the menu!
name: Marlene

text:
Ugh - I hate leaving bad reviews, especially when the service was so good! We've been here a few times before and each time the service and the chefs have been stellar. Last night, my family came in for dinner, we were promptly seated at the bar. We were starving, so our Chef quickly got food out to us. All was good, until I got home. 
Folks, I am going to come right out and say it. I was sick, all night sick, food poisoning sick. It was one of the worst nights of my life and my stomach still isn't right. 
I hope the Manager reads this before anyone else gets sick.
name: Brent

text: Ok service. Easy on the eyes. Pricey for the neighborhood, but Ay-yo!!! Their sammies are stupid GOOD! I housed the tuna melt and previously a wrap special too yummy to finish in one sitting. This one's a keeper.
name: Micky

text: I was having a day of being under the weather (pneumonia), I didn't want to leave the house but knew I needed some good nutrients and was craving an açaí bowl. I had never tried Clean Juice but it's close to my house so I decided to make the drive. WELL WORTH THE OUTING! The staff were super kind, and gave me their suggestions. I ended up getting the Immune Booster Shot which was really tasty (ginger lemon & carrot) and the Berry Bowl (açaí bowl with berries, almond milk, bananas, granola, honey, goji berries- your basic açaí bowl). Hazel was the employee helping me at the counter and ended up giving me what they call a Kindness Card - meaning that as a random act of kindness they completely covered my bill, on the condition that I pay it forward with a random act of kindness sometime. I cried right there at the register, it was such a caring gesture. Moreover, the bowl and shot were delicious, filling, and gave my body exactly what it was craving. Wrap around TLC from this place - physically and mentally - and I will definitely be a return customer. Thank you!
name: Kellie

text:
So so so so happy to have a place that serves such great and trustworthy vegan food! The vegan fish and chips were the first dish to draw me in, and I was so impressed with the taste and texture; I couldn't believe they achieved such a great flavor in quite an unexpected veganized dish. The vegan tenderloin they just featured for the Indy 500 was so close to the real thing - flat, fried, and way too big for the bun; I hope they add it as a permanent staple to the menu.

Speaking of permanency, they have rotating food features along with the regular menu, making sure the regulars don't tire of options. 

I've been so focused on the food that the beers haven't stood out to me much; I like the heaviness and flavor of the porter, but couldn't tell you much else about what I've sampled. 

The atmosphere is great, akin to a traditional English or Irish pub, with dark interiors and heavy wood decor. There's also an outdoor seating area if darkness isn't so much your thing.

Service can be a little slow most of the time, so don't go here if you're in a rush. Sit back, take in the atmosphere, down a couple pints, and gorge yourself on vegan and omni foods.
name: Amanda

text: We really enjoyed our food and the service was great. The fish was fresh and the rolls were delicious. We ordered the Agadashi tofu, three rolls, and chicken yakisoba for our kids. The tofu and yakisoba took us back to Japan. We'll definitely be back.
name: Erica

text: Ok... we're totally confused by all the amazing ratings. We finally got a tough to acquire reservation for 8 pm tonight and when we arrived ten minutes early our seats were not even close to being available. In fact, the couple sitting where we were supposed to be seated did not leave for at least an hour after we arrived. So we were seated next to the grill (not even kidding) where it was about 150 degrees. Oh, and that was after being asked to wait at the rear bar where there were people standing and sitting about three layers deep and most were eating dinner... there was no way we were getting anywhere close to the bar. So, once seated and sweaty, we popped open the wine list. Hmmm... $600... $300... $150. Of course, all of that would've been fine if the bottles were actually even close to being worth that much. We ended up with a Super Tuscan for $92 that retails at $29.  Wake up call--  this is sleepy Wayne, not Manhattan! The service was slow, the food was fine. Because the reviews were back-and-forth we ordered the $35 small cheese board, and the reviews that say it's not worth it were right. It was fine. The steak frites were fine. The pasta was fine. Everything was fine. Overpriced, under-impressed would be the headline.
name: Elena

text:
Their coffee is incredible. 
Came here on a Friday morning, it was much busier than I expected it to be. I absolutely love the atmosphere of this place; vibrant colors, plants, cute decor. 
I had the House Specialties section on the coffee menu which changes around from time to time. Anything I have ever ordered from that part is always fantastic! I will always love this place for their coffee. 
The service is always top notch as well.
name: Nidhi

text: Nice venue, decent Cuban sandwich and they have excellent deep fried pickles.  The ladies behind the bar were very friendly and helpful.  Had a flight of their beers, their wet hopped IPA was excellent.  Clean restaurant but I find it interesting when sitting at the bar eating my dinner and drinking my beer that one of the guys who works there starts dropping "F" bombs 3 feet away from me with clear earshot with out a second thought.  I would not bring in my wife or friends to the venue simply because they are a bit more tasteful in regards to the colorfulness of the language they choose to use versus the breweries employee.  Would have normally rated the place a 4 star.
name: Chet

text:
Not good...GREAT!!!

The BEST Banh Mi I have ever had, & I've lived all over the country, eaten at every Banh Mi place in every city. I've never had one so fresh, so stuffed, so flavorful. I'm lucky to be 1 block away. In fact, I'm going there now to pick up 3 more, for my wife & sick friend in the hospital.
