name: Tricia

text: Food was good - the portions are large! Only real complaint is that our waitress kept forgetting to bring sugar for our coffee, but it was a very busy Saturday morning. I had the Healthyman meal with spinach added to the egg whites and it was delicious. I don't usually like turkey sausage, but this was pretty good - same goes for the whole wheat pa cakes which were amazing. My wife had the Nova Benny with the hollandaise on the side and added avocado. She really liked it and they gave her a good portion of avocado. We got there at 10:45 and parking was tight, but we sat right away. By the time we left around 11:45 there was a pretty good line of people waiting for a table. There are so many options, we'll be back to try out more of the menu!
name: Britt

text: Everything on the menu was unbelievably good! Was very impressed with the Broccoli Rabe cooked perfectly and no bitterness whatsoever! The Gnocchis, made with no potato just cheese, are as light as a fluffy pillow", As described by the waitress who is very knowledgeable of all the plates. A little corner restaurant, not pretentious... But everything is four-star quality!! 5 Starts for Yelp!
name: Maria

text: Every year I go to New Orleans and every year my first stop in the French Quarters is Felix's. My father took me here when I was 5 years old to have my first raw oyster. I always get raw oysters and charred oysters. This is also the first place I had charred oysters as a suggestion by one of the shuckers and it's on my crave list ever since. I've  had charred oysters at Acme, Dragos,  and Antoines...each great in a different way,  but Felix's are my personal flavorite. They have more of a yummy crust layer on top. I prefer to sit at the bar and chat with the shuckers, who have always been friendly and entertaining to watch. They shuck the oyster and throw it on the bar in front of you. So fresh and delish. And you can mix up your own sauce with the ketchup, horseradish, Tabasco and lemon to your liking. Felix's sometimes gets a line but not anything like the line at Acme across the street. Enjoy oysters at Felix's and wash it down with an ice cold Dixie on tap.
name: A

text: Always been a fan of Reginelli's, but I had kind of forgotten about in the wake of Theo's taking hold of the city. We dined in recently and really enjoyed our experience. Mostly because of the Detroit-style pizza special. Man, that thing is good. If this sticks around, so will I. Couple that with the beer/wine specials, and I'm definitely going to add Reginelli's back into the rotation.
name: Keith

text: This is our new favorite place for Mexican food. The prices, proportions and friendly staff are all awesome. Definitely recommend.
name: Keith

text: Tried this spot for lunch during a work break. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. So yeah, the wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. Also, the leftovers held up okay the next day.. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. Not bad for a quick meal. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly.
name: User

text:
Great service, good selection of meats and non-meats. They only had 1 steak that we wanted left, so they went and cut us 3 more. High quality meat, sous vide then sear in cast iron, perfect marbling and just tasty. Highly recommend this place for any and all of your butchering needs. 

Check out the owners cool collection of steins from Germany and enjoy the great customer service, cheers!
name: Elliot

text:
Now this is Detroit style pizza!!!  The 8 corner pizza with premium mozzarella cheese and hamburger is really on point when its on sale. They use premium mozzarella. 

The crust is how Pizza Hut's use to be back in the early 1980's.... That fried skillet cornbread crispy taste ... Awesome.....

This location is what would be consider downtown Webster Groves. The inside was clean but it was kind of dark inside not sure why all the lights were not on when i went.
name: Anthony

text:
We don't normally go to chain restaurants but we had a voucher to use so we figured why not. It was crowded on a Saturday night but we got seated right away. Our server seemed nice and came to take our order pretty fast. 

We got our drinks and our salads pretty quick. That was where the good ended. The house salad was just lettuce, 2 olives, and some banana peppers. No vegetables like tomatoes or cucumbers or anything in it.  Our waitress said she was bringing bread out. She then disappeared for 20 minutes. Someone else brought our food out and we had to ask him for bread. Another 10 minutes later our server finally brought our bread out as we were halfway done our meal. My husband wanted to order a beer but decided against it because we probably wouldn't get it till we were done dessert. 

The food was ok but nothing special. I got the fettuccine weesie. The mushrooms tasted like the marinated jar mushrooms which I don't care for. I did like that the fettuccine had a light texture, it tasted possibly homemade. But the Alfredo sauce was bland it needed to be thicker, creamier and more seasoning to it. There also wasn't that much sauce on it either. My husband got spaghetti and meatballs, the meatballs tasted kinda mushy and plain. We got the cannoli cake also, which was ok but huge. 

We were going to use our credit card to pay the difference of what we owed after the gift card, but after waiting awhile again for our waitress to come over we decided against it and just threw down some cash so we could leave. 

Glad we went to use my gift card up, but not planning on returning. Service isn't good and the food is just ok.
name: Lauren

text: The whole meal felt kind of uneven. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. A couple small things kept adding up. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Maybe other people have better luck here. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Food was fresh and service was quick. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. Would probably stop in again if nearby.
name: User

text: We had the Garbage Can ice cream and the Caramel. It was very creamy and delicious. The Garbage can ice cream is made with Vanilla ice cream and 7 different candy bars. My husband had the Banana Split which was a nice size portion. The line was out the door and almost to the street when we left. This place makes all the ice cream and everything on the premises. We were only visiting but I definitely recommend it.
name: Cynthia

text:
Best service we had in a while! No long waiting times and excellent food. Bottomless mimosas are the way to go 
Coleen was an awesome waitress. Always there if we needed something and super friendly - would definitely come again!!
name: Ines

text:
Overall I think this taco place is highly overrated. Do not use the app it doesn't work and makes you wait for over an hour anyway.
I'm not sure what the hype is about the tacos they are just okay.
name: Chandra

text: We just had lunch here and the service was awful. The kid took our order then gossiped with his two buddies for 40 minuets. Then dropped the food off and back to gossiping. Never asked how the food was. It was horrible. The fries where old and stale. The tomatoes on the wrap tasted gross like they where old and mushy. My meal was $15 and I only ate about half of the sandwich. If I get sick I will be pissed.
name: Suzi

text:
What a treat! My wife and I were trying to find somewhere we haven't been to celebrate her birthday. We couldn't have made a better choice. Everything was fantastic from the greeting at the front door, attentive service and drinks at the bar and our waiter, Marko, who made the evening extra special. The Panko Crusted Sea Bass and Grilled Pork Chop were amazing. Cant wait to visit this spot again. Thanks 
Kief and Marsha
name: Kief

text: Haven't been in quite some time, but their deli sandwiches (named after dog breeds) and soups are spot on.  Really good stuff here!
name: Gary

text: One of the best shrimp poboys I've had. Bread was perfect. Liked it so much I went back the next day for lunch again. Highly recommend! Also got the roast beef debris fries which were good.
name: Ryan

text: Loved the brunch on Saturday. I had the B&B Biscuit w a cafe latte! It was amazing! Loved the options to sit at the counter looking at the kitchen or at a table. Also an adorable outdoor court yard!
name: Wendy

text: Nice atmosphere for a quick refreshing ice tea or one of the craft beers.   Outside seating is nice.  Appetizers are great too and reasonably priced.  Allowed dogs too which is nice.  Wait wasn't too long.  Fried pickles were skinny slices and the "ranch" dressing was a homemade type and didn't taste like the Hidden Valley Ranch that most people are used too.   I'd still recommend this place
name: Jane

text:
Don't miss Seis! A popular Mexican restaurant in the Tucson area. 
Great carnitas tacos, the guacamole with perfect chips and the accompanying salsa were my favorite.
name: Nereida

text:
I found this minimalist comforting cafe just a few blocks from my hotel when I had to stop by from NYC. I called in to check if I could come by to take some photos of the interior and food to write about in my blog. Bastien O, the head chef/baker from France, picked up my phone call and gave me great advice on ideas of when's best to come and invited me over. He met me personally and told me of his whole routine from coming in as early as 4:30AM to start baking. Not sure how he makes everything seem so effortless, but his story is really impressive and work is magical.

For my brunch, I ordered the mushroom/spinach quiche that was accompanied with a side salad. As a sucker for citrus sweets, I ordered the orange tart in the display: the tantalizing orange tart was brushed with a syrup and crusted with sugar crystals. And because I was so sleep deprived, one nonfat latte. Bastien, one of the humblest chefs I've ever met, even came out to speak with me about his background and passion in baking and customer service.

Loved the interior (the back also serves as a great spot for some to work) the attentive staff, cleanliness, quirky restroom with facts about toilets along the wall. Although I've left, part of my heart is still longing for that orange tart.
name: Lillian

text: Ended up here pretty late, maybe around 9:30, because everything else nearby had a wait. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didnt have a reservation. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. It was crowded but still moved along. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. No big complaints, just a nice meal.
name: User

text: Although small, the store offers an interesting selection of bakery goods. There seems to be ample selection of gluten free and some vegan options. The highlight of summer 2018 has been their ice cream sandwiches, made with meringue "buns" (think of a giant macaron with ice cream in the middle). Gluten free food is generally subpar, but a lot of the selection here is quite tasty, even comparable to regular options. I'm not gluten free, but I enjoy stopping here while in the neighborhood. The staff is friendly and easy to interact with.
name: Christopher

text: Decided to stop in and give them a try this morning and they did not disappoint. Their espresso was outstanding and ordered a iced vanilla latte that was amazing as well. Will definitely be returning. SUPPORT LOCAL BUSINESS.
name: Amelia

text: Recommend if you are trying to separate from the group you are with. Door men run a tight ship. Can only review from 1st and 2nd floor. Never needed to climb higher. If you find the hotdog stand right outside, also highly recommend.
name: Claire

text: We stumbled upon this little shop on our way into town. It's close to 275 so it's not too far off of the main strip - speaking of "strips", it is actually located right next to an old run-down strip club of sorts... strange? Yes, very much! Haha! We were happy to see such a great variety to choose from. Being our first time here, we decided to check reviews and see what the faves were of the locals. We picked The Rolando and The Reuben. Rolando was cool, not too impressed per say, but Reuben was pretty yummy! So, I recommend the Reuben! It was a bit greasy on the outside, but I've never come across a Reuben that didn't have a bit of a shine. I especially loved the slaw and the sauces they used. If you're hungry for a Sammich and you don't want the norm, stop in and try something new! :)
name: Jessica

text: nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. Pretty happy w it overall.
name: User

text:
This was a pleasant surprise. They have a dog friendly patio with a water bowl and umbrellas on the tables which is ideal. I had an odd combination of a blueberry bagel with cream cheese and lox but somehow it worked. The bagel was fantastic. Crispy yet not too hard nor chewy. It was one of the best bagels I've had and I'm from New York/New Jersey. 

The smoked salmon/lox wasn't too salty or smoky and had a great taste. I loved everything about my sandwich. I also ordered a side of potato salad. They gave me a huge portion which I appreciated so I could take it home and enjoy later. Clearly homemade as it was delicious and not too heavy with any particular ingredient but rather just the right amount of flavor. Honestly everything about my meal was fantastic. Can't wait to go again with my dog.
name: Sweets And Popcorn

text:
I go here about 1-2 times a week and love this place. The tacos are amazing, the people are genuinely friendly and the atmosphere is very inviting for families. 

Will continue to keep this a regular spot for me.
name: Mike

text: Not my favorite food but definitely with a try for the interesting menu. It is very vegetarian friendly. Overall I was sort of underwhelmed by the taste but nothing was at all bad. The broccoli tabulleh and the deserts were excellent. Shakshuka, roasted, yogurt, cheese and cauliflower were ok. I don't think I I would return on my own but would happily go if others suggested it.
name: Michelle

text: It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..
name: User

text: Sunday lunch 12:40pm, decent crowd but not so crowded that we can't find a table. The outside tables a are also still available although no one is sitting out on the 100 degree weather even thought the mister is on. Fast service, pizza comes out in 5 minutes with the gas fired pizza oven. Thin crust you either love it or hate it, I actually like it, the kids like it too, I'm surprised the pasta meatballs are also pretty decent tasting although the meatballs are just slightly hard but not bad. The  chicken pine nuts salad with Gorgonzola is simple but good too, overall a quick and decent  place to have a quickie...
name: Leo

text: I gave the place a 1 star rating only because I had to pick something. Bloody was ok, just a mix with vodka. Ordered the black and blue burger at a cost of 9.99. It came with fries. I had to laugh when it was served. A plain hamburger from McDonalds had more meat on it. The burger, if you want to call it that was surved on a white bun, barely any blue cheese. Would not suggest this place at all!!
name: Debbi

text: Really large menu.  Great service.   Pancakes are a bit disappointing but there breakfast rocks.
name: Sonya

text: i love a lot of things about drake's! it is close to my house and if i want a late dinner with friends i can come. not a lot of places are open late in the area. i like sitting by the fire in the big comfy chairs. the relaxed environment is my favorite thing about it. four stars because service is always a little slow but, anything on their menu is yummy!! my favorite is the buffalo chicken wrap & sweet potato fries...so filling & a lot of food for what you pay!! go to drakes if you're looking for a relaxed environment, fun music, + good food :)
name: Laura Grace

text: This was an amazing surprise. Our meal was excellent. I had the wedge salad which was the perfect size and the miso salmon. My husband had the salmon bowl. It was a noodle like spicy soup. I had a taste and it was great. We like spicy food! The corn crab cake fritters were crunchy and soft. Tuesday is half priced bottles of wine up to $25 off, so we enjoyed a nice bottle of wine. Our server was very nice and attentive. It's definitely worth the drive to try Redux from Indianapolis!
name: Lauren

text: Great food. Sweet server and very accommodating for my picky son. Wife loved the pear margarita. Awesome desserts salted caramel cheesecake was to die For
name: Stephen

text: Service here is as amazing as the food! Hubs got the bacon and eggs and I got the Apple pancake. Apple pancake it's HUGE. We both ate it and we took half home! Coffee is good and the orange juice is unbeatable. Selena was attentive and so friendly! The wait time is insane, but if you call ahead it's super manageable.
name: Elizabeth

text:
We loved everything about our dining experience at Alpen Rose!  Ringing the doorbell to have a small door open with the hostess greeting you was a fun introduction.  When we walked in, it felt like we were at a speakeasy or a large dining area in someone's elegant home.  I loved the decor all the way down to the lovely plates and glasses.  Our waitress was welcoming and prompt.  And then came the best part....

I ordered the No. 76 and my husband ordered a Manhattan -- both were fantastic after a busy workday.  I enjoyed being able to see the steaks being cooked over the fire and the bartender prepare drinks with surgical precision while we waited for our food to arrive.  We ordered the smoked bacon which was perfectly cooked and flavorful, and the bone marrow toast which was heavenly.  We split the Tomahawk which has so good my husband carved as much meat off the bone as he possibly could.  For a second I thought he'd pick it up and gnaw on it!  I loved the way the potato wedges were presented.  They were crispy and complemented the steak nicely.  They also had a very good but not overwhelming selection of wine -- mine was a cozy Cabernet Franc. 

We finished off by sharing a coconut cream pie, oh my goodness it was so good.  I can't think of one negative about this place, we had such a nice time.  Well done Chef!  Next time we're bringing some friends.
name: Diana

text: When I was in town recently, I took my mom here for lunch as it's close to her place and she'd been wanting to give it a try. We both had their prime rib sandwich and they were really delish. My mom loved the sticky toffee pudding. I had a nice cider to enjoy with my meal. I would definitely come back for another meal next time I'm in town.
name: Donna

text: The best breakfast I have EVER had. The Pineapple Rum Raisin French Toast was fantastic. The customer service is amazing, they really work together to make the experience amazing. Expect a wait, the place is tiny but it's so worth it.
name: Veronica

text: Ended up here pretty late, maybe around 9:30, because everything else nearby had a wait. The staff seemed tired but still polite. It looked better online than it did in person. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. For a busy night they handled it okay. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Idk, nothing was awful but i left disappointed. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine..
name: User

text: VERY slow service. Especially late night. Expect to watch your gas tank plummet sitting in drive thru.
name: Ryan

text: The food is not that great! It was very salty. The teriyaki sauce tasted like salt. The service was VERY slow. We ordered sushi at the beginning of the meal and it took so long to get it it was no longer desired. The manager came to the table and proceeded to argue with my cousin. She was demanding that she pay for something that took over an hour to come to the table. The other manager came to side of the table and proceeded to stare at everyone at the table. Would not recommend this place to my neighbors dog!
name: Kia

text: Got a great vegetarian sandwich on the garlic bread. They actually had several veggie subs to choose from which is awesome. I will be back!
name: Christina

text: Have been coming here since they opened. Staff is friendly and the food comes out quickly. Enjoy ever meal here as well as the bubble tea. Kids enjoy the food too and are always happy to come here. Prices are reasonable. Haven't gone back to our old Pho place after these guys opened. Will definitely be coming back and recommending.
name: Leib

text:
We've passed this place going to and from the shore, and finally thought we'd try them out. No reservation required, and there's a pretty large bar area plus table seating. I'm not sure about alcohol prices or specials, but the bar sure was popular. Fortunately, there wasn't any wait for a table on this Sunday evening.

First, they bring out the (endless) bread and butter- well, once you order, that is. The bread tastes fresh and warm, the butter is cold but still spreadable. I ordered the housemade spaghetti with marinara, which did taste good and fresh. My sister ordered the chicken parmesan, and received a whopping portion (a whole plate was just the chicken, with the pasta in a side bowl). Prices are a little more than expected, which is worth it for the portions- however, I felt that my pasta portion was a little underwhelming after seeing the chicken parmesan portion. Our meals also came with house salads, which I thought tasted great as well.

Service was consistently fast and very friendly as well. We're looking forward to our next shore trip so we can stop at Francesco's again!
name: Gia

text:
Decent view-I enjoy the lit up tree and decent music too! The weather right now is great for enjoying this rooftop bar. 
I ate the meatballs. They were very good! And the frozen rose is a cute drink for a young girl to have at a rooftop bar.
However, service was poor for me. I'm not sure if it's a Nashville thing. I'm from Santa Monica and lived in Newport Beach through college and I've never been treated so poorly by staff at restaurants and bars. weird. I ordered food and they wanted to seat me in a corner of a table that hadn't been wiped down. They seemed irritated that I wanted a napkin or something to happen to at least wipe it down so I could sit.
name: Mondana

text: The staff is always extremely friendly and accommodating. The food is good and the portion sizes are large. Great local dinner for breakfast.
name: Shelly

text: We were disappointed Martin's (3/1/18.)  It was recommended from our hotel and had good scores on Yelp.  Needless to say it was below our expectations for good Nashville BBQ.  The ribs were a bit over cooked and were more like roasted port .. not like the low & slow end product one should expect.   They were scored between the bones to mimic easy to pull apart but they were not.  In a brighter note, the pulled pork seemed decent.  Needless to say we left a fair bit on the late which we never do.
name: Dan

text: Great meat selection and salsa bar.   The tortillas are good and the portion size is large IMO.
name: Michael

text: Came here on Sunday evening to celebrate my Moms birthday. We had high hopes based off the reviews, but were very let down. To start, the service was great. He was very knowledgeable, and had a great sense of humor. However, I can't say the same for the food. Where we sat was lovely, the piano playing was very classy, and the ambience was dead on. Unfortunately the food is lacking. I've been in the restaurant industry for 20 years, so I know a thing or two. For one, the pricing is extremely high for the quality of food you get. The filet was tough, over cooked, and not a good cut of meat. The salmon we ordered came out, and was very bland. After getting close to the center to see it's completely raw. Yikes. The crab cakes appetizer was ok but very fishy. When we mentioned to the server that the salmon was raw, he took it off the plate, they put it back on the grill, and brought the same piece back. That's not how it should of been handled. They should of made the entire entree over and cooked correctly. It was not taken off the bill and my sister did not eat it. Overall, for the pricing? They have a lot of kinks to work out with their food. It should be top notch for the pricing. Everything else is great from service, to atmosphere and drinks.
name: Jackie

text: Love this place we went back next day. Every floor was awesome and a great mix of music and food. With a. Large party it was perfect so that everyone got food they liked. The sushi is fabulous I had tempura shrimp roll. It was so good next day same thing- best sushi. The music is awesome -a mix of all different genres - the first floor is country the second floor was hip hop and roof top was a dance party mix of like club dancing music we loved it you kind of start on first and work way up it's perfect.
name: Megan

text: Hands down the best sushi in St. Petersburg. The omakase was spectacular. Quality fish and great flavors. The atmosphere was relaxing and the service very personable.
name: Dawn

text:
Had my birthday dinner here! Grade A service. The owner also came to me and wished me a Happy Birthday! 

The server was excellent and timed everything beautifully. The Turtle soup is beyond amazing and he told me to try it. The entire experience was wonderful and so happy with everything.
name: Anna

text: It was my first time here. The place has so much potential. It's a great atmosphere and they put so much work into the place. It looks amazing! The food wasn't bad but there was ZERO flavor. We ordered the spinach and artichoke dip and roast beef poboy. The spin dip seemed fresh and the roast beef was actually debris. I had to add lots of salt to both though. The worst part was our server. She seemed more interested in other tables than ours as well as the jukebox. We got more service from the other servers than our own. We had to constantly ask other servers for help or to get her for us. Basics like placing your food order was a giant task for her.
name: Callie

text: No big complaints, just a nice meal. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. Would absolutely visit again. Nice little spot, decent portions too. It looked better online than it did in person. Food was fresh and service was quick. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish.
name: User

text: Tried this spot for lunch during a work break. Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. Overall, a strong experience. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. No big complaints, just a nice meal.
name: User

text:
Stopped in the next morning for breakfast.   Yum.  Eggs perfect, grits and the absolute best ham ever along with a big home made biscuit!  Strong New Orleans coffee.  Wow.  

2 days later stopped in for breakfast again.  Had a great omelette, more great grits, another biscuit and some good strong coffee.  

Great food, service, prices, etc.  If I had stayed in NO longer - I would have gone back again for more of what they offer on their menu.
name: Chris

text:
Great dinning experience. Gluten free options and knowledgeable about menu and preparation. 

The pork chop was fantastic in two GF sauces. 
The scampi was good with pasta and fish shrimp and mushrooms. 

The wine list comes in a book, so go nuts. 

Will return. Reservations are a must.
name: Rob

text: The oysters was Great!!! Food was good but a little over seasoned (salty). I will still recommend the oysters.
name: Lashawn

text: No big complaints, just a nice meal. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Nice little spot, decent portions too. It looked better online than it did in person. Would probably stop in again if nearby.
name: User

text:
Just moved to the area- decided to finally try Cappy's!
We ordered a deep dish pepperoni pizza- it was delicious. I would absolutely recommend Cappy's! Just beware of the parking lot-VERY limited parking.
name: Katie

text:
4.1/5

I've been here twice and have somehow wound up ordering almost the exact same thing both times. My favorite is their Winter Melon soup. It's extremely refreshing and the perfect thing to have on a cold winter day, when you're sick, or when you just want some good hearty broth. I also like their Peking duck, though I wish they gave more scallions with it (there's enough for maybe 3-4 wraps with a healthy balance of scallions, hoisin sauce, and duck...the next 10ish wraps are just duck + hoisin :P)
name: Kimberley

text: They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. Worth checking out. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. No big complaints, just a nice meal.
name: User

text: Went with family on a Sunday and it was louder than I expected. Idk, service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. The staff seemed tired but still polite. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. idk I'd try something else next time.
name: User

text: i go here once a week i love this place with all my heart, cheap prices and amazing!  Service is super fast and it never disappoints!
name: Julia

text: Not bad for a quick meal. Also, my friend liked their dish more than i liked mine.. For a busy night they handled it okay. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. Honestly, we shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. idk I'd try something else next time. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. For the price I expected more than this. The leftovers held up okay the next day..
name: User

text: I ordered two chicken nugget kids meals, a chilli, and a diet soda. I waited awhile, it's ok, food has to cook. I can see everyone on their phones, again it's ok, everything takes time. I receive in my kid's meals a snack wrap and the other gets a bacon burger. I also received a regular coke. I go inside after driving home to exchange my order and everyone is on their phones. I couldn't even back out of my parking space because the drive thru line was so long.
name: Blair

text:
Good and Tasty food, I love their menu and selection of items
Spice level is perfect.
Their items are a bit overpriced so they need to revise.

I wish I could give it more than 3 stars but they really need to work out the "new restaurant" service issues. They were very accommodating when we needed to change our reservation from 4 to 5 people. We watched the hostess lazily call out names at the hostess stand and not even bother to check if the people waiting outside the door were those parties. 

Once seated, the server took forever to get us waters. We ordered and the food took extremely long to get to us. Luckily we were provided delicious LeBus breads and butter to snack on. My eggs with multigrain toast, home fries, and bacon were swimming in butter/oil and the home fries were not fully cooked through (crunchy potato slices in not a good way). We ran out of water and coffee multiple times and I had to flag down the server to get refills. We also weren't offered condiments and had to ask for them- things like salt and pepper, ketchup for home fries, and syrup for pancakes.

Overall, everyone enjoyed their meal of choice. The pancakes and French toast were delightful. Great fries with the sausage and egg sandwich (I recommend sharing- it's huge!). A side of sausage was $5 for a tiny homemade patty. Awesome breads and croissants, of course! 

I hope to be able to go in another month and see some of these seemingly simple kinks worked out. The space is absolutely gorgeous (albeit a little smoky from the open kitchen) and a great upgrade to East Falls.

text:
The Chef is an artist and a genius. 

Each plate and bowl was custom ordered/designed by the Chef such that every minute contour of the dish was calculated in the pouring of a sauce or plating of a meal. For instance, if the bowl had a tiny nook in it, that nook was designed to hold sauce; and if the plate was slightly, one degree, concave it was because the plate was designed so that the sauce would culminate in the center. 
What I'm saying is that every shred of your experience is calculated. It feels as if every tiny grain of salt has a purpose, and the dish wouldn't be perfect without it. And the dishes are perfect. 

It's not worth your life savings if you simply can't afford it. It IS just food, and at the end of the day you can get an excellent meal for much cheaper. But if you are looking for an experience, an artisanal experience, and you don't mind splurging a bit then definitely, Laurel is worth every penny.

text:
My husband and I were in the area (I recently discovered Suburban Square and let's just say I'm obsessed) and looking for something new-to-us for dinner. Biga popped up on a search for pizza and had great reviews, so the decision was easy! 

We were greeted warmly by the hostesses and seated. I loved the interesting non-alcoholic beverage options and ordered a grapefruit concoction called nautical nonsense, which was reminiscent of a paloma. It was refreshing and a great cocktail substitute. 

We started with the farro salad which was super tasty. I don't think my husband has ever been so into kale! Next, we shared a classic margherita and da bomb, with soppressata and chilis. The latter packed a punch in both flavor and heat. We loved both pies and they were sizable enough to enjoy several slices from each and still take a few home. 

Great experience all around and I will definitely think of Biga again next time I'm in the area!

text:
Eagle Diner on Street Road, Warminster, PA, is a traditional Greek food emporium with broad multi-page menu covering all three meals, plus a significant salad bar. It is open 24/7.  The only thing missing is a counter with stools for those who prefer that old line dining experience, like me. 

I stopped in for diner last weekend, hoping for a good meal for this solitary traveler. I had to wait about 15 minutes for a table, as the place was SRO when I arrived around 6 pm. A stool at a counter would have eliminated the wait, but I did not mind standing in the entrance area and observing all the scurry from the staff. It also gave me the chance to check out the cakes, pies and other bakery goods made on premises. Certainly did not hurt my appetite. 

I was eventually shown to a table in the back, and handed the short novelette menu. So much food; so little time. I chose their meatloaf mini dinner, with mashed and cup of soup or salad bar. I grazed over the greens for a while and returned with a full plate of various salad components. It wasn't a stunningly broad spread, and a lot of it was processed and not fresh, but it still provided many colors and flavors that worked well on top of a lettuce base. Three bean salad, beets, red onion, macaroni and potato salad, baby spinach, pickled everything, cheesebread and 1,000 Island dressing, kept me munching while waiting for the mains. 

When my entre arrived, I was confronted by two huge slices of baked/grilled beef loaf and a dish of white mashed, with brown gravy on the side. The meat was tender and tasty, but better with a jet of ketchup, than the brown sauce (a bit salty). The slices were about 1.5 inches thick. I couldn't finish the meal. Absolutely no room for the luscious looking desserts.

At a price around $10., the value was evident in every bite. 

I'm told Eagle does a good job for breakfast, too. Next time I'm in the area that time of day, I'll stop in again to check it out.
name: Gerald

text:
Pass the fried chicken please. Pass the grits please. Pass the ...Just pass everything ok? Not the typical conversation you have at a restaurant sitting beside (temporary) strangers. This is what they call "family style" here at Monell's. You see, it's a Nashville institution kinda like Elvis is to Memphis. Did you really just go there? Listen up ya'll.
If you are lucky to beat the crowds, you will be seated at a large table reminiscent of family reunions except with people you don't know. It's a good idea to introduce yourself to your new friends. This allows you quicker access to some of the best southern cooking around. 

The breakfast food is standard fare but the biscuits were amazing and the fried chicken was um um good. I really like sitting with strangers that don't look like you and possibly leaving as friends. 

Don't miss this place located in an old mansion built in 1929 right beside the airport. If you skip this place and head to say Denny's,  You ain't nothing but a hound dog...See what I did there?
name: Chris

text:
Oh Sweet Jesus help me! They've put a Maple Street Biscuit Company within a mere 30 minutes of my front door. I am going to gain 100 lbs.... I love this place. I love the hokey Southern theme and the schtick where they ask you a random question when you order like, "what is your favorite band?" or "what would you name a child?" It is all in good fun and a change from the norm. I like hearing them shout it out when people's orders are up, it serves as entertainment and an interesting study in personalities. I think I heard "Dave Matthews Band" the most in case you were wondering. 
Now let's talk about the food. That Squawking Goat is to die for. I could probably guzzle a gallon of pepper jelly but don't even get me started on the goat cheese and fried chicken. I know they are the "Biscuit" company but I don't even notice the biscuit. I like the guts of the sandwich. The biscuit is just the vehicle to get it in my mouth. The coffee is pretty good too, I just wish it was served hotter. Maybe it is my fault for squeezing in a healthy dose of homemade maple simple syrup and a liberal cream pour but still....

We were sitting on the patio and it had a very nice view of tucson and the pool area. The chrizo queso appetizer was amazing and great portion for two. We shared the chicken mole with beans and rice. The sauce was a bit heavy and could use more flavor. The beans were dry, but the rise and chicken was good. Too bad the sauce over powered the good tasting chicken. Our server was a little slow for service throughout the night. Yet she did give use a cheesecake for our anniversary. The cheesecake was very good. text: I hesitate to write a bad review but being this is the 3rd time it happened I thought it would be best. I'm a local. Come here all the time with my friends for dinners, celebrate birthdays, relax and just to catch up. Food has always been great. Portions are smaller now but the prices still go up. The past few times I just felt like we were rushed and my friends had made similar comments with their experiences as well. I was there last week with a friend for dinner, hadn't seen her for a while. We usually come here for dinner to catch up. No seats were available at the bar so we ended up being seated inside the restaurant in a booth. Waiter came by a couple of times to take our order, seemed anxious. We didn't really have time to look at the menu to order, we felt like we were being hurried. We just ordered dinner which was brought out right away. After dinner we decided to have another drink while catching up. The Waiter just kept pacing by our booth which was making us uncomfortable so we closed the tab and went over to the bar to hang out for a while. No seats were available at the bar so we decided to go across the street to another location where we did not feel rushed. I know it's the season and they're busy but rushing customers is not very polite. Couldn't even enjoy my dinner. Just disappointed.

text:
The pizza at Blaze is terrific. That's a given. So, my review will focus on concept, execution, and atmosphere.

For me, the concept is revolutionary for pizza, although other reviewers mention similar places. You have absolute control over your pizza. Want two sauces, three cheeses, nine vegetables, three meats, barbecue sauce on top? It's all included and encouraged with there "build your own" concept (12 in pie for $8.25). You can also order a one-topping, two-topping pizza for slightly less, or select a "specialty pizza," but that defeats the whole concept.

At most places, if you dine as a couple or group, you are going to have compromises. One person hates anchovy, one likes artichoke, white sauce? Meatballs or pepperoni? No more need for half-this, half-that, or "let's just order the specialty." At $8.25, each person gets their own pie, or you could easily get "1/2 my design,  1/2 yours. The crust is thin, but if you want thick, it's yours for $2.00 more.

It is possible for two people to share one pizza or three people two pizzas, and I saw a family of five with three or four pizzas. Anyway you slice it, I think you will pay less than most dine-in places and have great pizza. Call ahead and carryout are also available.

Execution: What is it actually like? The first time I ate at Blaze, I was in a group of five, and there was a long line. (You order and move through like at Subway.) But the lined moved quickly and when it is your turn, you get the complete attention, and encouragement, of "your" server. (The second time there was no wait.) You are constantly asked things like, "Is this enough sauce?" "Do you want more cheese, or a second cheese, etc." This really seems genuine, not perfunctory.

If you care about staff treatment and morale, you will be very impressed. The workers seem engaged and happy (maybe because the restaurant has only recently opened). But the store manager seemed very upbeat with employees and was right on the line, helping out and managing by example. I saw him interact with many staff and customers, always in a pleasant and positive fashion. Some reviewers mention the young workers. I didn't see any problems - the main thing is they appear to be closely supervised, efficient, and friendly.

The restaurant atmosphere is not what you would get at most pizza restaurants, or even at a dine-in Pizza Hut. There is no table service and you get your own drinks. But it is clean and reasonably quiet and orderly, thus relaxing. (The first visit, though, there were people waiting for our table, so we left a little sooner than we normally would.)

I am not the kind of person who is a loyalist to a business, chain, or brand, but I might have to make an exception. You can find some places that serve great pizza (usually expensive) and cheap places that sell adequate or good pizza. To me, Blaze offers the best value of all! 

Definitely give it a try!
name: David

text: Nice addition to the area and good use of old Hard Rock building. Still new and working out the kinks. Waitlist system is nice. text:
I had Dandelion bookmarked as the food pics looked good and the prices were right. 

ATMOSPHERE:
The charm started from the exterior with its old-style architecture that draws you in.  We, along with many others entered from the corner door that leads to the pub area that's void of a host stand, so you stand there dumbfounded once inside.  The main entrance is actually on the side of the building, right of the corner door.  Dim lighting, dark woods and tavern vibe were coupled with clubby background music and very loud conversations.  

MENU:
English-style apps, charcuteries, soups, salads, seafood, poultry, meats, pastas. 

BEVERAGE:
Basil Punnet - $13.00
Perfect mixture of sweet & bitter via vodka, strawberries, basil and honey. 

FOOD:
Carrot Soup - $11.00
Thankfully, this did not taste anything like carrots and more like a butternut squash soup.  Creamy with notes of curry. 

Dandelion Salad - $11.00
Greens I don't really care for (arugula and cucumber) were mixed with romaine, avocado and dandelion sprouts in a lemon vinaigrette.  Eh, I'll take a Caesar instead. 

Bangers & Mash - $18.00
AKA sausage over mashed potatoes, and I ate the whole thing!  My months of healthy, no sausage-eating ended here as I devoured the two tender links, smooth spuds and tasty onion gravy.  

Pan Seared Norwegian Salmon - $26.00
The spouse's dish.  The moist filet was dusted (not crusted) with dukkah (Egyptian herbs, chopped nuts & spices) over a tomatoey chick pea stew.  I thought everything married well together but the spouse felt that there was too much going on. 

SERVICE:
The only reason why this isn't a 5-star review.  As mentioned earlier, we walked in through the pub door.  We were immediately greeted, taken to the host stand a room and several flights of steps away, and brought back to where we started.  Couldn't they have just pardoned themselves and gotten us menus instead of following them like puppies?  

Christina was our server.  While she was nice, she was also very inattentive, made us feel rushed and gave off the feeling like she really didn't want to be there.  No introduction of her name, and instead of the usual "Can I start you off with anything to drink" opener or mentioning of specials, we were asked for our food order.  Asking questions resulted in answers but her attention would stray to tables behind her as she'd look away instead of engaging and staying focused.  Pausing even a few seconds to answer resulted in her saying "Let me give you some time" and quickly walked away.  After the salad and soup were brought, there was no offering of pepper (as there was none on the table).  Not once did she follow up on us throughout our experience.  Only a gal who I assume was a manager, asked us if everything was okay.  Its been a while since we've had such dismaying service.  The uncomfortable service made me want to scarf down my meal (something I do not do) and get the heck out of Dodge.  We don't need our butts kissed but would appreciate the common courtesies when dining out.  

OVERALL:
Delightful menu and appetizing cuisine.  We just got stuck with the wrong server.
name: Vince

text:
I wish I could give half stars, because I would give Bistro Romano 4.5 Stars... back in December 2018 I made dinner reservations and called to book the private wine cellar. It was a Christmas gift to my boyfriend for us to enjoy restaurant week in a place a bit more private and romantic. Upon our arrival, our table wasn't ready so we headed to the bar for some drinks. When we were sat, we were told our reservation was messed up and that the manager would come speak with us. I was very upset since I had the reservations for about a month... the manager was very kind and sincerely apologized for the mistake. To make it up to us, they brought us a bottle of champagne and mussels, both of which were a kind gesture... 

The restaurant week menu was pretty good. The only thing I didn't enjoy that much was the Parmesan Sformato. I thought it was going to be a great idea to branch out and try something new, but the taste and texture were not my forte. The complimentary mussels were delightful. My boyfriend wasn't a fan, but I gladly at them all! 

The gnocchi was great, my boyfriend also enjoyed the roast chicken. For dessert, he had the chocolate cake-- which had a fudge consistency-- and I had the tiramisu. Both were great, I wish we would've had them placed in a to go box. 

The service was also great. The server made sure we had everything we needed, I assume he was on his A-Game due to the mishap with our reservation. I also appreciate the accountability of the manager. Maybe we will be back one day to have a correct reservation at the wine cellar.
name: Jennifer

I'm sorry, I really wanted to like this place but I would not return. 
Pros:
Food is pretty good.

Cons:
It is so insanely loud in here. Like I felt like I was at THE KLERB. 
Bathroom is co-ed. Not genderless, but co-ed, which means when you leave the stall you wonder why all these people of the opposite gender are washing their hands and have a mini panic attack thinking you went to the men's (or women's) room by accident.

text:
I'm normally not a huge fan of smoothies, but I love Blenders. It's exactly what Jamba Juice is not - it is about good quality in their ingredients, great customer service, and drinks at a good bang for your buck. 

One thing I love about Blenders is that they have a huge menu with something for everyone. It was so hard for me to choose what I wanted. I ordered the strawberry piña colada smoothie and I loved it. It was creamy, yet did not taste overly sweet or artificial. I don't remember the exact supplement I added, but as many reviewers mentioned, they do offer a free supplement of your choice to add into your smoothie (and they have a lot of different ones too!). 

The employees were genuinely very friendly and personable. They were also very quick to help us and give us their suggestions. I will definitely be back when I'm in the area!

text: Came here after a long night bar hopping. The pepperoni pizza is delicious. The pepperonis taste like they are hand made by someone's grandmother. They were so good I went back the next day for more pizza. I've been in stores trying to find pepperonis that taste that good ever since, with no luck.

text:

My wife and I are admitted foodies. This is a go to place. It's not high end (which is why it's a triple D joint) but it's a gem of a place all the way around. One of my favorite places anywhere. 

If there were a sixth star I'd give it. It is  that good.

text:
This is a little spot in Fishers with fresh food and great beer selection. This place is busy during lunch but slow during dinner time. Our server was super sweet and attentive. 

I had the vegan tacos. I always get these. They are filled with fresh squash, corn, black beans and tomatoes. I like them with corn tortillas rather than flour because they tend to not fall apart in your hands. 

My boyfriend got the Philly cheesesteak sandwich and said it was tasty with gooey cheese. 

We've been here before and would recommend it to anyone near the area!
name: Hanna

text:
FOOD: We went for the Devour special, which was a barbecue feast for two with ribs, brisket, sausage, pulled pork, and BBQ chicken. It also came with two sides (we picked cornbread and mac and cheese) and apple cobbler. The meat was delicious. There was more than we could eat. The cornbread and mac and cheese were fantastic, especially the mac and cheese. The BBQ sauces were good. The apple cobbler was not good. 

AMBIANCE: We were seated against a giant window (the whole wall is window) next to the parking lot. The cars park facing that window. Someone turned on their car and sat there in the spot for 10 minutes with their headlights shining directly at us. 

SERVICE: Our waitress was very inattentive. It was not busy at all. She came right over and took our drink and food orders, and our food came quickly. Five minutes after the BBQ was dropped off, someone from the kitchen came and dropped off our dessert. Which was apple cobbler with a scoop ice cream. Why would someone bring dessert five minutes after the main course came? We had barely started eating our food. So then the ice cream sat and melted. We wanted to say something to our waitress, but she never came back to our table. We finished our BBQ. Our drink glasses were completely empty. We decided to go ahead and eat the melted cobbler so we could get out of there. The cobbler honestly wouldn't have been good even without melted ice cream. The apple slices had tough skins on them, and there were barely any oats. After we gave up on dessert, we sat there for several more minutes with empty plates and empty glasses pushed aside, waiting for someone to notice us. Our waitress eventually wandered over and asked if we were ready for our check. We said yes. She handed us the slip of paper and walked away. Did not take our dishes or notice our empty water glasses. Did not offer us more water. Did not ask how everything was.


Overall, the food made up for some of the poor service, but we would not eat here again.
name: Liz

text: Good food, good ambiance, and good service. Check in on Yelp so your wait isn't so long. The Bloody Mary is amazing!

text:
Everything about the Townsend experience was fantastic - the food, the service, and the atmosphere. 

We called ahead, and they said they were happy to accommodate vegetarians, as long as they knew they were coming in advance to give them time to prepare options. When we arrived, there was a menu tailored to vegetarians. They explained that the chefs were actually very excited to have vegetarians as it gave them a new creative challenge.

And I must say - they did a wonderful job!

The meal started with a couple types of bread (the sourdough was very tasty) and butter. They also sent out a small portion of complimentary potato and onion soup which was so good I would have ordered it if it were on the menu. Next, we had the Chanterelle Mushroom Ficasse which was sourdough bread topped with mushrooms, sun-dried tomatoes, microgreens, and saba - this was really delicious and well-balanced in terms of flavor. We then had the Fennel and Apple Soup which was not only tasty but a really unique flavor. For our entree we had French Green Lentils served with eggs - again, very good. It was a subtle but really delicious taste like comfort food. And lastly, we finished things off with their Chocolate Gateau - a dense chocolate cake with coffee chantilly that wasn't overly sweet.

The food wasn't the only great part - the service was outstanding. The staff was very professional, and our server (Megin, I believe) was a delight. She was very friendly and knowledgeable about the food and restaurant. In addition to having a great personality, she got all of the small details right - little things that make a big difference, like the fact that our water was never empty during the meal. 

The atmosphere was also very nice. It's a repurposed house turned restaurant, so while it has a polished, upscale look it doesn't feel pretentious. It's actually quite charming, as it has a lot of its original features like an ornate tin ceiling and stone fireplace. 

Townsend was without a doubt a 5-Star experience, and I can't wait to try it again.
name: Marlena

text: Got takeout from here twice now so I feel like I can say a little more. You can tell they care about customer experience here. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. text:
Yelp described this place as "Asian fusion." With this in mind, and seeing the decent star ratings Yelp users gave it (but not having actually read any of the reviews), we decided to go here. It is in the same strip mall as the Saddle Up club and some other questionable businesses near the Castleton Square Mall, so I didn't know what to expect. Upon walking in, I was relieved to see it was very clean and modern, and most (if not all) of the employees and other customers were Asian, which suggested to me that the food was probably authentic. On looking at the menu, though, it appeared that everything except the appetizers was ramen. One could argue I should have gathered that given the "Meet Noodles" name, but in my defense there are plenty of Asian non-soup entrees that are served with noodles. The person I was with doesn't react well to things with really high sodium, and usually tries to stay away from soups for that reason, so it was disappointing that there were really no options for him. He was also disappointed that there were really no substantial meat options. He ended up getting ramen, as did I. Our meals were decent, but we probably would not have gone there if we'd known it was just a ramen joint, and probably won't return for that reason. After the fact, the person I was with looked through reviews and saw pictures suggesting there were non-soup options for entrees, but we did not see any on the menu, nor did the menu contain pictures of the menu items. 

Overall, this was a decent place, so please don't take my review as a complaint; I'm more just offering it so that others considering going here know what to expect, and as feedback for the business that an all-ramen does not appeal to most men and that they may want to consider branching out and adding some dishes that are not soup-based and/or that contain more edible meat.

text:
Pho Loc Tho is a very small spot that delivers big flavor! This little place is located in a busy strip mall area off of boyette and balm riverview near Riverview HS. Parking can get a little congested at times due to the numerous other businesses in this plaza. It is also a very small space, so don't expect to bring a huge group here. There's some tables throughout and a small bar area to sit at as well. 

I got a rice dish with marinated pork chop and the flavors were on point! The pork chop was well seasoned with just the right amount of chew! They served it with the right amount of vegetables and rice. I don't think I left a single grain of rice on that plate! My wife got an egg noodle soup dish and she said it was very tasty as well! We both agreed however, that the price was just a bit higher than other places charge in the Tampa Bay area. So that's the only set back we really had and the main reason we don't go more often. 

All things said and done, this place is probably the best Vietnamese cuisine you'll find in the South Shore area. We will definitely be returning when we get that craving again!

text: We are 100% done with King Wok. I seriously cannot stand this place. The people who answer the phone are very short and rude. We ordered 2 orders of steamed dumplings with extra dumpling sauce, boneless spare ribs combo platter, general tso's combo, and chicken and broccoli. The boneless spare ribs were actually good, general tso's and chicken and broccoli were unexciting and quite bland. The fried rice was a joke, a literal joke. The rice was not fried at all and there was 0 toppings in it. No egg to be seen, no peas, no carrots, plenty of flavorless undercooked onions, and maybe 4-5 little pieces of pork meat. A serious joke, they use to have good fried rice years ago, now it's like they don't even care or didn't have the ingredients, but sent it out anyway. Dumplings were flavorless, boring, and a waste of money. I will not be giving King Wok anymore of our business, I remember when they opened years ago and were very good. Now it is completely different, maybe different management? Or maybe they just don't care anymore. Not sure which, but unless they make an active effort to improve the quality and service, I will not be back ever and neither will our friends and family.
