name: Ashley

text: Dessert saved this a little. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. I'd maybe go back, but I'd order differently next time. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text: It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Nice little spot, decent portions too. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Food was good and came out fast. No big complaints, just a nice meal. It looked better online than it did in person. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price..
name: User

text: Jessi was our amazing server! Such a fun atmosphere and phenomenal food great break from the broadway scene for a bite to eat! Awesome service!
name: Jenna

text: This place was very good! I've been here a couple times, but this is the first time I took pics of my food  and such! I was meeting friends here for Sunday brunch, so we knew it would be busy which is why we made a reservation. The reason why I put 4 stars instead of 5 was because it took 45 minutes for them to seat us. To me, that is kind of ridiculous because the point of a reservation is to avoid that! While I was waiting, I sat by the bar and got a brandy milk punch! It was very tasty, and the bar tender can right up to me with a menu right when I sat down! After I sat down, I got an order of the biscuits to start! They tasted so great, and the jam with them was also really good! It seemed house made, but I'm not sure! For an entree I got crab cakes and poached eggs. The crab cakes were perfectly crispy and the eggs nicely poached! The arugula salad was also a nice touch! Overall, I am happy with my experience here and will definitely come again!
name: Kaitlyn

text: I was really disappointed. I ordered takeout and I was so excited because I havn't had honeygrow in a while.  Everything was great at the beginning. The noodles I got tasted really good, but when I hit the bottom of the takeout box, I saw this clear plastic. Of course I found it after I ate the whole meal.. I was so disgusted. The worst part about this whole situation is that the next day I felt sick to my stomach and eventually got food poisoning. I was sick for 4 days. I couldn't eat anything. I will never go to honey grow ever again because I don't want to risk getting food poisoning. It was one of the worst experiences I've ever had. Please be careful everyone. I am so upset that this had happened because the other times I've had honey grow I enjoyed it very much.
name: Danielle

text: This place has such amazing food! And the service is good too. The food is great and nicely priced. You basically make your own taco or burrito, which is awesome. The buffet of toppings for your meal is filled with a huge variety of fillings for your burrito/taco. Now for the bad comments, the atmosphere is horrific. Fruit flies were everywhere! It makes me wonder if they are just settled in the salsa sitting in the open, no lid or anything to cover the bowls of delicious salsa. I swear there were more fruit flies than grains of rice. Which is amazingly bad, considering this is a Mexican food restaurant! Other than the fruit fly problem, the place is great. Plus, there's unlimited chips, you should really consider eating here.
name: Natalie

text: Yummy. Great bar, excellent food, amazing service. This place is a gem.  The empanadas were tasty; the roasted artichoke is a must have!
name: Shona

text:
We visited for weekend brunch during a recent trip to Charleston.  The restaurant is beautiful and spacious, with high ceilings, lots of seating.  The vibe is both industrial, and warm and rustic.  It was busy but we got seated within 15 minutes.

We got the Pistachio Rose Croissant, Avocado Toast, Brown Rice Bowl, Shakshuka, and Spicy Carrots.

- Pistachio Rose Croissant - Absolutely fantastic- super crispy and well browned!  Honestly couldn't really taste the rose but it had plenty of pistachio and was otherwise really tasty.

- Avocado Toast with zata'ar and coconut on sourdough - The avocado toast was good, excellent bread, but otherwise not super remarkable.  I'd try a different toast next time.

- Brown Rice Bowl with almond butter, vegetables, and poached egg - This was my favorite, and now I add a smear of almond butter to all my rice bowls at home.  

- Shakshuka - We had never had shakshuka before, but this was great.  Satisfying without being too rich.

- Spicy Carrots with yogurt, salsa verde and crispy grains - A great side, but not a great pick if you're weak on spice.

Top recos: Get a pastry and get the brown rice bowl.
name: Kirsten

text:
I miss indie neighborhood restaurants like this. Feel like St Louis is sort of a "Chicago Jr." (minus the ambitious murder rate).

The Mud House is a real gem. We reunited with dear friends here over a lazy breakfast and talked for hours, it was the perfect setting. 

There's nothing like breakfast to confirm you are on vacation. The "slingers" here are tops, the "English" breakfast also a winner! 

You cannot lose with anything on the menu. It is on our "must eat" list for St Louis, highly recommended.
name: Rich

text: I honestly want to be able to give this place a better review. I love the atmosphere and the selections on the menu. The captain crunch shrimp are FANTASTIC. Their appetizers are definitely where they shine. Ive also had the spicy chicken toasted raviolis, and they were pretty good as well. Where I feel like I can't give a full 5 stars is the wait. I've come here when there were only 3 other parties and I've still had to wait 30-40 minutes for appetizers and an hour or longer for the main course. The entrees are decent- nothing super wow-ing, but decent. But definitely don't come here if you're in a hurry! It stinks too, because it'd be a great place to go before hitting the movie theatre right there but you just can't count on the timing at all
name: Danielle

text:
I'll skip the part where most people talk about everywhere they've eaten tacos, and therefore you should really take their advice. I'll keep it short and sweet and say this place is legit. Some of the best street style tacos I've had. I opted for a mix of Diablo shrimp and steak. Combine that with their house made sauces I had fun experimenting different mixes.

I save 5 star reviews for top 3 ever type places. Taco Bar earned it.
name: Bob

text: Had an amazing breakfast here today. Wonderful ambiance, terrific menu, great service and the best biscuits I've had in Nashville. Will definitely be back.
name: H

text: Food is terrible!! I have tried and tried this place and no matter what time of day or what I order, it is always terrible. Moreover, the manager is rude. Avoid this place. There are so many other good places to go - why bother with this one.
name: Sue

text: We will not be back. Worst bartender/manager we've ever encountered. She was so rude to us...unbelievable. She insulted my sister-in-law on her choice in clothing. Who does this?!
name: Brian

text: The hot and fresh donuts here are one of my favorite treats in Philly. So when we walked in a little after 8 o'clock on a rainy Sunday and there was no line, I figured I'd have that sweet strawberry lavender melting in my mouth within a few minutes. But no - it was a 20-30 minute wait for a half dozen because there were some pre-orders to fill. Believing that a business model where you essentially devalue the customer right in front of you to fill online orders is a poor one, I said, "...but we're right here, and there's no line." The dude behind the counter snapped at me: "it's Sunday and I have a lot of pre-orders." Sheesh. I get it, he doesn't make the rules. But at least be apologetic about it and act like you value the customer. And maybe management can figure out a way to accommodate special orders AND in person customers at the same time. Not coming back.
name: Julie

text: Always loved Hooters.  Hadn't been in awhile.  Stopped here because we were in the neighborhood to see a movie.  My better half got wings and I got boneless wings.  Both were good.  But we've been long time customers of Hooters sporadic over the years.  Felt like we were being nickled and dimed.  $1 extra for celery.  $1 extra for blue cheese.  I can get great wings and great boneless wings for a lot let money at the local dive bar north county and have the celery and blue cheese included.  Won't be running back.
name: Anne Marie

text: I actually like/love this pizza, ditto for my family.  Today picking up my pizza made me question some things.....anyone that actually thinks about business and profits knows that pizza is almost 100% profit,  it's dough, literally. But now you go and raise your price by at least $1 for a plain pie and I have to think if it's not to cover the costs of you opening your Roxborough site because you have made no upgrades to the Broad St location.  There is no auto soap dispenser, towel dispenser in the ladies bathroom. Toilet seat covers non existent.  Hand air dryer from the 90's and these are disgusting anyway.  Any upgrade here to justify the upcharge would be greatly appreciated.  Tip jar on counter reminds me of the attitude you would get from Tacconellis servers when you picked up.  Listen, we love your pizza but we're not going to be taken advantage of by a booming neighborhood business.  #shameonyou
name: nina

text: The Bobbie is such an amazing sub sandwich. It's thanksgiving in a roll. This location is clean with friendly staff. Awesome industrial ambience and quick service. If you're a fan of Capriotti's from the west coast, this location in Nashville does not disappoint.
name: David

text: Not for tourist. Didn't feel very welcomed. Slow service. Probably a locals place. So anyone traveling, beware.
name: Joseph

text: I like Foodies because it's quick and everything I've gotten there is always good. I like that there is always a mix-up of slots.
name: Carol

text: For the price I expected more than this. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. By the time the food came out I was already annoyed. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon.
name: User

text: The food came out fast, which was good because we were starving. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Also, the leftovers held up okay the next day.. The food was good and the service was easygoing. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. No big complaints, just a nice meal.
name: User

text:
A family favorite. The food is fresh, always hot (unless it is supposed to be cold!), and very tasty. The portions are generous. The staff is friendly - the owner is terrific - and the restaurant is very clean.

My favorite is the meatloaf, which has a great flavor. My twins tend to like the drum stick and my little one loves the greens and the white beans.

Yes, you can get fast food cheaper, but this locally owned place has quality food, fair prices, and friendly service.
name: Clay

text: It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Not bad for a quick meal. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Food was fresh and service was quick. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. The whole meal felt kind of uneven.
name: User

text: The photos made it look a little better than it actually was. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. Maybe better dine-in than delivery, hard to tell. It looked better online than it did in person.
name: User

text: Good food but every time we go in. It never taste the same. So we are constantly ordering different things and it's good but we can look forward to it tasting the same anymore because.. it's never the same.
name: Francine

text:
1) No staff acknowledged us when we arrived
2) Staff were either on their personal phones or talking to each other
3) The food literally tasted like grease
4) It wasn't until we went to pay that a staff member addressed us
5) We got our own menus and had to go to the counter to ask for another refill

If I could, I wouldn't give it any stars.
name: MB

text: If you want Authentic Italian food, COME HERE!!! This place is a hidden gem! We love this place. My favorite was the lobster pasta and the shrimp scampi appetizer!
name: Ashley

text: We were pleasantly surprised and enjoyed our dinner and drinks!  The bartender takes pride in his craft of making drinks.  I had the Philly Love which was amazing.  Bartender also altered it for another patron with Tequila instead of Vodka.  We had an nice conversation with the bartender and enjoyed watching him make his specialty drinks!  The dinner was excellent and reasonably priced!  The wonton soup was enough for two.  My husband had the General Tso's and I had the Chicken Pad Thai which was awesome!  The staff was very nice and accommodating!  I definitely recommend this restaurant and will be returning when I am back in Philly!
name: Lori

text: We had a party of 9 and they wouldn't seat us until every person was inside the building. We have a toddler so that made things hard. Then the service was SO slow. I get that we had a big party of people but still. It was hard to even get a refill. I thought we were never going to leave! Good food and cheesecake but wow they need to do something about the speed
name: Caitlin

text: Be advised that if you order a Chicago Style/stuffed crust that it will take awhile (40 minutes) and can't be baked concurrently with a regular style pizza - unless you have 2 ovens! Wish this was on the menu or I had been told by the workers when ordering!
name: Bill

text: Meh. I've been several times and it's just not great. I got poutine today and it didn't even resemble poutine and didn't taste like it, that's for sure. The crack fries are good but I'd be equally as happy eating Rally's for like 2 dollars. This place is nothing special in my opinion.
name: Jake

text:
We visited Cafe Amelie for dinner when we were in New Orleans in Jan 2017.  The restaurant is beautifully decorated and has a lovely courtyard.  We sat on the second floor of the restaurant, at the window, so we could glimpse the lovely courtyard down below.  Service was excellent throughout and the food was absolutely delicious.  Perfect New Orleans style fare.  

We ordered the following:
-Shrimp and Grits (with corn andouille and maque choux) (we both ordered this and loved it)
-Gumbo
-Mint Julep (very tasty and refreshing)
-Amelie Oysters (creamed spinach and artichokes made with housemade crostinis)

The food was amazing!  I'm so glad we got to have a nice, classy, sit-down dinner while in New Orleans.  I would love to return again.
name: Pegah

text:
Josephines is AWESOME! We went once and had the bruschetta and a white pizza, and we were sold! 

Now, we can't help but go a couple times a month; the food is INCREDIBLE, the people are so incredibly wonderful and nice, great service, great price, always clean,... I can't say enough good things! 

Not to mention, once a month all-you-can-eat pizza event...it's unbelievable! (That includes dessert pizzas!)

Favorites: WHITE PIZZA (best!!!!), tomato pie, bruschetta, cheesesteak, and honey-mustard chicken pizza. 

Everything tastes fresh and like it is made with real, good, and fresh ingredients, and you can see the food being made and just how well everything is handled. 

Seriously, I cannot recommend highly enough!
name: Carolyn

text: I'm a regular here and all I can say is eat here!!! Amazing food and service for a great place. There's a lot of variety so it accommodates all. My favorite spot in Philadelphia for sure!
name: Alexa

text:
Pros:
* Great food
* Different selections
* Amazing friendly staff
* Nice atmosphere
* Fancy yet affordable dining experience
* Very open minded and accepting (they'll feed a meal to the homeless which is a plus in my eye)

Cons:
* Can easily get crowded and busy due to location & popularity
* Kinda small
* Not a franchise lol (needs to be everywhere)

Summary:

I'm kinda biased as I've gotten to know a good amount of the staff but this place is a great dining experience for locals and tourists alike. The food is really good and homemade (as far as I know). They're the sister restaurant of The Wild Cow and is adjacent to them while even having workers from there pitching in to help. Overall this is a great place!
name: Jern

text:
Coming from NYC, I have high expectations for falafel. The very first Middle Eastern restaurant in the U.S. is in the West Village and you can get great falafel from food trucks back home.

Goldie does falafel justice. It's a bright green inside, which I have been told in the past is the authentic kind. It also has a light crisp on the outside and is fluffy in the inside. It does not seem like it was sitting in oil very long.

I had the falafel salad, which had a great snap to it from the cabbage, hints of dill, and colorful beet cubes (which I usually hate).

Only downside is the line -- it was the only establishment at Franklin's Table with a wait. But it was worth it.
name: Peter

text: Nice restaurant. Parking lot is shared. Outside seating available. Staff are helpful and attentive. Tried the green chili meat burrito - thumbs up.
name: Dave

text:
How does anyone like this place? The $8 "huevos rancheros" consisted of scrambled eggs, canned black beans, a table spoon of sour cream and diced tomatoes with onions to pass as "salsa". Let me not forget the single tortilla rolled up on the side. 

Also if they mess up your order and put bacon on your sandwich when you ask for no bacon, they'll just take your sandwich back and take off the bacon and just return it to you instead of remaking it. So don't come here if you have dietary restrictions.
name: Z

text: The service was too bad, two people gave us a very tiny  table, I have no place to put my clothes, and when I borrowed a chair to put clothes, the waiter forcibly took it, and the waiter did not pour the water. No service... So bad, I will not come again.
name: Liliana

text: First experience here, and with Indian food in Reno in general, was great. The naan here is addictive- we got plain and fire naan. Even if you don't know what the curries are exactly, our waitress recommended some (vegetarian) curries that would go well together. We got a fruit/nut curry and Palek Paneer and both were delicious. Portions are pretty generous too.
name: Eily

text: Service was nice, kitchen was just moving kind of slow. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. Food was good and came out fast. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. The whole meal felt kind of uneven.
name: User

text:
I was in the mood for hearty Pho and came across this place one day so I had to check it out. 

Upon walking in, I was immediately greeted by friendly staff. They were really patient with me as I tend to be indecisive. I ended up ordering the "35" Sliced beef n' meatball and crab rangoon to-go.
Everything was separately packaged nicely, kind of like a pho kit if you will. 
The portion sizes are huge hence the name Super Bowl.
Upon constructing the pho to my liking, I noticed they completely forgot to add my meatballs in my package. A little disappointed but overall it was delicious.

I will be returning sometime soon for some yummy Pho!
name: Jazzy

text:
Came for restaurant week and always wanted to visit a capital grill.  So glad we have one in St. Louis now!

The bread service is top notch.  The dark brown was my fav.  The sour dough was also very good.

Clam chowder is super tasty.  Lots of chunks of clams and potatoes and a creamy hearty broth.

The filet mignon was cooked perfectly and so was the bone in strip.  Super flavorful along the bone sections.  

Creamed spinach was good but not our favorite. Flemmings is still the best.

French beans were a little too crunchy for my taste.

My wife really liked the mashed potatoes.  

Chocolate cake was rich almost like a truffle.  Creme brulee was good too.
name: Leo

text:
This place was wonderful! I ordered the chorizo quesadilla and it was delicious. I especially liked the atmosphere of this place. It was upbeat and it's located in a nice part of town. 

The service was excellent. Our waitress was extremely friendly, and it was a great location for a Friday night date!
name: Hannah

text: The atmosphere in Luke's 32 is pretty cool.  I am a big Luke Bryan fan and everything in his restaurant was related to his music in some way.  Even the drinks were named after songs!  I got the Drunk On You and my boyfriend got the Backstage.  The food was also really good and they have peanuts for you to snack on before your food comes out.  Everything was a little pricier, but nothing out of the ordinary for Broadway.  I also went back later in the night with some friends and they had a DJ playing with people dancing everywhere.  It was a really fun time and I will definitely be back!
name: Phoebe

text: Delicious!  I had he pork tacos, potatoes, and donut.  Hit the spot. Service was excellent as well, even after both of my kids spilled their waters!
name: M

text: I ordered the Big Ch-Easy added bacon and it was really good! And those fries with the liquid crack poured on top, OMG! So good!! Nice atmosphere and the wait wasn't too bad. We enjoyed dining upstairs and I will definitely go back!
name: SJones

text: Not good.. but they have great to go packaging for thai ice tea (they packed it on a soup package so u dont have to worry about the leak)
name: Laurie

text: Came here for lunch yesterday - it was pretty busy and from what I've read here, that is the norm.  And there is good reason.  The sandwiches here are ridiculously good!  Service is friendly but very efficient.  They are taking orders at the window, orders on the phone.  Everything is well organized and it went too bad of a wait.  Maybe 10-15 minutes?  My husband had the cuban sandwich.  It wasn't a slab of pork with ham, it was almost like a pulled pork.  Succulent and delicious!  I had the pollo asada - SCORE!  Mango mayo and avocado I could not have been happier.  The soda fresca is really refreshing.  Several flavors to choose from we had the hibiscus and the orange ginger.  Good think I don't work right in the neighborhood cause I might be there every single day for lunch!!!  Yea, its that good!
name: Clare

text: Nothing was terrible, it just never really came together for me. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didnt have a reservation. There were a couple things I liked and a couple things I probably wouldn't get again. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh.
name: User

text:
Thank you for being the only juice spot that opens before 9am- greatly appreciated! 
I am SO STUFFED as I'm writing this review 
You're Yam cupcake was soooo delicious, and let's not talk about that Keylime Donut- Deeeelicious!
This was my first visit, and based on what I've tried so for...I'll definitely be back fore more! I'm so impressed with the owner's concept for this business; It's totally geared around health, food,and business. 
The prices are the  same as pretty much anywhere else in Tampa, so I feel I got my money's worth 
I loved the variety of cold pressed juices, nut-butters, take home meals, Kale chips, baked goods, and the list goes on! Let's not forget the bonus room filled with all the athletic gear- loved it!
Over all this juice spot was great, and and enjoyed every bit of SOHO JUICE CO THANKS!!
name: Velda

text:
Rather large location, but not so efficiently laid out and/or utilized. The coffee station and the cashier is on one side of the store, while all the seating and a small stage is on the other. While this is fine for slower times, there was a bit of confusion as to where customers should be waiting for their drinks and if it would be brought over to them when ready (which the answer is yes, expect they forgot the most recent time we visited). 

Drip coffee and Cubans were good, though the lattes were just alright (could be warmer for sure). Blueberry muffin was a let down, so definitely will not be trying more pastries as we were disappointed the visit previous to this as well, unfortunately. Lighting in this store could be better as it was rather dark and lastly, please fix the wobbly tables! 

They have other locations, of which the one in Brentwood is our favorite amongst them - much brighter and has a livelier vibe to it as compared to this outpost (located right next to the university).
name: Via

text: Tried this spot for lunch during a work break. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Maybe better dine-in than delivery, hard to tell. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus..
name: User

text: Dessert saved this a little. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. It was crowded but still moved along. This feels like a place where your order choice matters a lot. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. They were out of one thing I originally wanted..
name: User

text: This is one of those places where I can see other people loving it more than I did. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Not bad for a quick meal. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine..
name: User

text: No complaints. Staff were friendly. Ordered 2 cupcakes, one mocha something or other and a triple berry one. Tasted on par or better with what I normally get at Swiss Haus, a popular local bakery in Philly.
name: Daniel

text:
The Bang Bang shrimp is always good, as are the entres. The Spinach Bacon Blue Mahi Mahi was very tasty and the twine lobster tails my wife have were good as well.  That is, for only the first half of the meal. The temperature in the restaurant is always painfully cold, each and every time we've been here.  So cold, the drawn butter was not warm for long, as the arctic cold air drew down the temp and the candle flame wafted to the side, thereby becoming ineffective.  We used the salt and pepper grinders to shield the breeze to give the flame a fighting chance.

All this probably explains why we are not here very often (once or twice a year).
name: Andrew

text: Coming from Southern California, the Mecca of Mexican food in my opinion, this was a very tasty taco spot. The priciest tacos in my opinion but they are so worth it because you can't normally get great tacos in St. Louis (No offense). Al Pastor is my favorite, and the Torta is fun and delicious. Very kind staff! Where they fall short is the small menu, but it's understandable because it's a taqueria! I only complain because I'm a Hispanic away from home and would love more of a variety!
name: Chris

text: The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. The wait felt longer than it should have. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Food was good and came out fast. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh.
name: User

text: I had the steak and arugula pizza and my wife had the chicken and spinach. We eat here quite a bit and have never had a bad meal.
name: Andy

text: Great experience trying my very first canolli ever! They have their very own parking lot for customers which was a plus!
name: J. P.

text: Easily the best Chinese I've had in Reno since moving here from San Francisco.  Ordered the beef chow fun and it was spot on with the correct ingredients and cooking style.  The pho had fresh ingredients but the soup base seemed to be missing a bit of flavor.
name: Raymond

text: Great pizza!  Excellent NY style pizza. Timely delivery. Enjoyed by all! Definitely added to favorite list. Thank you
name: Kathy

text:
Imagine Panera with less carbs. It feels big business but what you're eating is better and less processed. I feel like there could be more dressing to my salad (probably all the kale) but still one of the best salads I've had for a while. If you're getting the Roasted Tofu but you don't want the carrot chili dressing, the miso works just as well. 

I also shamelessly tried all of their lemonades which I totally recommend. You can't really go wrong with any of them
name: Sarah

text:
The Croquettes are pretty great. Overall the service is great here. The house salad is pretty popular but it's not my personal favorite. I say go with tapas and you're good.

The meats are awesome and the Croquettes. The paella is close to the best you can get in Clearwater but not that Amazing. Overall it's a great place, whoever you take here won't be disappointed.
name: Aaron

text:
Great place!! Much better tasting food and cheaper than the Southern Steak and Oyster restaurant around the corner!
We had the Fried Catfish and the Meat Pizza.  They were excellent!
name: Carol

text: First time ordering from here and I honestly wasn't sure what to expect. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. The staff seemed tired but still polite. I left full, which at least counts for something. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent.
name: User

text:
5 stars for not only tasty, fresh, customizable food, but for excellent service to boot!

Came here on their 1st anniversary celebration for a late lunch. As it was 3pm, I was the only customer and the lady behind the counter greeted me warmly and asked if it was my first visit there. It was. She proceeded to give a brief introduction about the store and how the menu worked.

After reviewing my options, I decided on the lunch bibimbap but instead of mushrooms (eew!) I was able to substitute it with any of the other toppings in the case - so I chose the edamame.

For protein, I asked her for her recommendation, and she suggested the pork - so I went with that.

And for the sauce, she checked on how spicy I would like it (Me: not much) and opted to give me a blended sauce option which I appreciated.

text:
Peg Leg Porker is a neat Barbecue experience in The Gulch, definitely worth a try if you are in Nashville. 

If you'd asked me five years ago what I knew about barbecue, I'd probably point you to a 6 pack of kosher beef hot dogs and stack of hamburgers from Costco. In the past few years, I'd like to think that my barbecue palate has stepped up a few levels. Peg Leg Porker came to me as a recommendation from a few coworkers, and even after living in the Nashville area for a few months, I found that I still hadn't been to a great barbecue place. Luckily all of that changed recently with my first visit to PLP. 

My friends and I stopped by the restaurant on a rainy Saturday night, not sure what to expect. What we found was a massive line all the way out the door, into the outdoor patio (I was hoping the outdoor part was the entire line but no dice). PLP is largely cafeteria style -- order your food, pick it up, and take it to an open table. It took us about 30 minutes to traverse the 100 person line, but we all had our food within 2 minutes of ordering. Do not let the line discourage you. Another alternative to waiting in line: eat at the bar! There is a decent sized bar near the restaurant entrance, where you can get drinks and still benefit from the near instant food delivery. 

Onto the real important part: The Food. I ordered a half rack of ribs, with a side of smoked green beans, and coleslaw, as well as an additional side of the pulled pork. The sides were alright, and the pulled pork was solid, but the ribs were excellent! I am not big on most rib sauces since they are so sweet, but PLP uses a delightful dry rub that leaves you wanting more. The cost is really manageable when you consider all you're getting for the price. (In case anyone is curious, PLP does cook their Smoked Green Beans with pork as well). 

Keto/ Low Carb Folks: PLP is a barbecue joint... aka your dreams come true. Be careful in what sides you get, but other than that, go nuts! I think the combo of 1/2 rack of ribs and pulled pork was a good amount of food for me.  

All in all, great value and good experience; go check out Peg Leg Porker!

text:
We made a decision to do brunch here on our last morning in Nashville.
I love brunch (or really, any breakfast food at any time of the day, any day of the week) and the main high point was that we could walk here from our Airbnb. Because we found free parking near where we were staying...and parking in Nashville is stupidly expensive.

We walked in around 9:30am on a Wednesday morning. You form a line around the small retail space. Menus are in a basket next to the door when you enter. You order at the counter, are given a number to set on your table, and you seat yourself. There are two water stations where you can get still or sparkling water for yourself. When your food is ready, it is delivered to your table, and later your empty dirty dishes will be bussed for you.

You'd think at a place with the word 'biscuit' in the name, that is what I'd have to get. But they tend to sit heavy in my tummy, and we still had at least another mile to walk back to our car and Airbnb. I wanted something a little lighter, and I definitely wanted eggs.
As soon as I saw the Lindstrom on the menu, I was IN. I love brussels sprouts and will order them any chance I get. The ingredients together actually sounded like a salad I make, only with eggs and without avocado and bacon. Color me intrigued! (And hungry...always color me hungry!)
The sprouts were so yummy! And the poached eggs were an awesome component added to the dish. I think I might have liked it more if the eggs were over easy (ore at least ever so slightly less runny), and you *can* get them done another way. It just kinda sogged down the mean a little bit. It was all still DELICIOUS, though.
My only complaint is that my coffee didn't taste great. I usually make my way through two cups during a brunch, but I didn't even finish my one cup. Maybe my tastebuds were just off that day. But it left me under caffeinated and a little sad about it.

I would happily return here on a future visit! And if you are staying nearby, consider them for a breakfast-y meal!

We ordered the Survivor Omelet, Veggie skillet and from some of the other reviews, my husband who LOVES burgers, ordered the Mad Rex Burger well-Done. The burger came out last and it was still Raw!!! I'm really trying to see most of the Positives here, I mean, the Burger costs $14.00.  How is a Bleeding Burger, Well-Done?? Most of All, our server Never came back to check on us, let alone, tell my husband that they ran out of Ranch dressing and unsweetened Tea. During this time, I accidentally spilled my water and our server just stood there, once he snapped out of his Daze, he used our napkins to clean up the mess and left our table soaking wet. Just disappointed in his attention to detail, he was More concerned with selling us Virtual Reality time then helping to take care of us. We were the second table of people that day, so, it wasn't like he had a Ton to do. 

 My mom's and my eggs were delicious and the Fries were very tasty, but our Server, Shawn acted Oblivious!when he brought us our coffees, but no creamer or sugar.... or Spoons!! I'm Not sure how that even Works!
The Drag Show was fantastic, but now I realize Why this really Cool place was EMPTY!

I mean,...Come on, If you have a Job as a Server, DONT  FORGET  to COME BACK to Check on your GUESTS!!  Serving People Is Your livelihood. When I asked for a manager, the young lady at the front told me that there was no one managing that day. I can see how the inmates were literally running the asylum. 

I'm Not sure if Shawn should seek a different profession or Just be Retrained!!  Most of the staff was in a bubble! The bartender girl was acting like she Never tended bar and she kept asking people how to Make drinks. 
I guess I thought the staff would be more experienced, unless they don't care about their Clientele. They may just Do More business in the evenings. I'm not sure if their staff wrote the other positive reviews on Yelp, but we left Deeply disappointed and STILL hungry. 

Not sure if we will be back, but the Fries Were pretty Amazing!

text:
It's a cat cafe in St. Louis! In other news, hell has officially frozen over. But if you haven't checked out Mauhaus yet, you should go right meow!

As a mother of two adopted cats, I am in love with the mission of this place. It provides shelter cats with a temporary home and, most importantly, a chance to find a furever home! That's right - most of the cats at Mauhaus are adoptable, with the exception of a couple permanent residents. What's more, you have a chance to interact with these furbabies firsthand in a more natural environment than a shelter kennel to see if your personalities really click! 

You can go to Mauhauscafe.com to make an hour-long reservation for $10 - this will guarantee you a spot and gets you 1 free drink at the cafe. Plus the money is basically a donation toward the care of the kitties here! I believe they also take walk-ins at $5/person but you will have to wait for a spot to open. 

The cat play area is walled off from the cafe, so there are absolutely no sanitary concerns. Everything is kept super clean, no furball tumbleweeds here. The staff is friendly and care a lot about the animals here. Most of the cats enjoy human interaction. And pro tip - if you put your coat down on a chair or window seat, a cat will almost always claim it for their bed! 

The cafe serves the usual coffees, teas, and desserts/pastries. The food rotates on a seasonal basis but looks like standard bakery fare. When I came I had the London Fog drink and was surprised at how good it was. Make sure to guard your food and drinks from curious kitties looking to steal a bite!
name: Kristin

text:
Rione is good. It brings a different take on pizza that's exciting to see in the city. Crust is light, topping options are interesting, and cheese was pretty good quality. Being a Roman style pizza place I had hoped that they would cut to different size portions upon request, but the pre-cut pieces were reasonable enough sized where 2-3 pieces were more than enough.

Enjoyed the Margarita DOC, Diavolo, and Crudo -- all of which you could tell were well prepared with consistent amount of toppings. 

I found the reheating process of the individual cuts a little underwhelming and didn't have that "piping hot and fresh" feel, but maybe they're not supposed to and that's just me not embracing the true Roman style.

Seating was pretty plentiful as well if you're coming in with a group for lunch.

If you're in the area and looking to try something new and quick, check out Rione for a different take on higher end pizza.

text: We regrettably stopped by Vietnam Restaurant for dinner before driving back home to New York. Mind you, the service was great. I had my little one with me and had a few requests, all of which were met. However, we were not too pleased with the food. My other half and I are pretty sensitive to monosodium glutamate. Not that I can attest to the use of it in the food, but something was very off about the pho. If it tasted a bit more natural, we would've found our meal to be much more enjoyable. Thumbs up for the great service, but thumbs down for how the Vietnamese staple, pho, was concocted.

text:
Great place, really good food. 

If you're hungry, like really really hungry, this is a great place. All meals are like Sunday dinner at granny's house. The food is reminiscent of love and long conversations at the dinner table. It's what's defined as Sunday's, Thanksgiving, Memorial Day, all days that you eat until you can't move...kountry Kitchen is that. 

This place is quietly located off college and 16th...slow down or you'll miss it. Matter fact, you won't. There's usually a line of cars outside which means they're open to feed your soul and stomach. 

We ordered the combo plates. I ordered the whiting and wings and she had the catfish and pork chop. The sides were sweet potatoes, Mac and cheese, cabbage, and corn. If you're not ready to eat, please stay home. This was plenty of food. This looked like a small catering job. 

The fishes were fried to perfection. The sweet potatoes were just that. If you can't take the sweet, stay outta this candy shop. The cabbage, Mac and cheese, and corn were "hallelujah" good. 

The staff was exceptionally wonderful. This seriously felt like home. I loved every bit of this experience! See you soon!!

text:
Saffron is easily the best Indian restaurant in Tucson, and probably one of the best we've ever been to. We had tastings for our wedding at many different restaurants in both Tucson and Phoenix, but Saffron was well-above the rest. My wife and I decided to hire Mintu and the Saffron team to cater our multiple day wedding for a Friday night dinner and Saturday night reception, each with over 400 guests. We had many tastings with Mintu at his request to ensure that the food was exactly as we wanted for our events. He went out of his way for us and our families to make sure everyone was happy.  He had many great ideas for both food options and presentation and worked with us to achieve the perfect result. Our most important requests were that the presentation be above and beyond, and the taste/spice level be at a specific level. Mintu had made a list of promises to us based upon those requests and executed them perfectly. Everything was so delicious! Our guests were so impressed with the food and the display, with many calling it the best Indian food they've ever had. Many of our guests from California even said that it was better than the top and well-known Indian caterers in Southern California. Our guests from India also commented that the food was amazing!

Mintu's team was punctual, friendly, professional, and efficient. Mintu, himself, was at our events overseeing everything to ensure there were no errors. He even plated us our own meals at our sweetheart table, working with my dietary restrictions. Overall, we are extremely pleased with the Saffron team and very grateful for their work. Mintu and the team are family to us now. Thanks for all you did!
name: Sahil

text:
Marrakesh is dinner and a show in and of itself, complete with amazing food, incredible service, and a very unique dining experience.

The entrance to this hole-in-the-wall restaurant is a bit hidden, off a slightly sketchy alleyway. Once you enter, there's just one medium-sized room with about six stylized little wooden tables set up against some patterned red couches. Dim lighting, gorgeous decor, and the service-oriented waitstaff create an ambiance which is intimate and exciting.

The meal comes in multiple courses. To start, the servers will bring around rose water for washing your hands and pita bread to use as your only utensil - you won't find any forks or knives here. The first course is a platter of veggies and other appetizers for you to share at your table. The second course for us was an entire roast chicken (also shared among the table). The third course was our choice of beef or lamb skewers. After those mains, we had a course of a couscous-based dish. Lastly, for dessert, they brought fruit and baklava. Everything was delicious, and the pre-determined menu plus the family-style way of eating meant we didn't have to worry about what to order, but rather got to enjoy a lot of different things.

The overall experience ultimately blew away all my expectations. You ideally need a group of at least 3 or 4 to make it work most effectively (and you can have more, but you might be split at different tables). It's also BYO, so if you want to drink, bring that yourself. Either way, come to Marrakesh for an amazing Moroccan dinner adventure you won't forget!
name: Kevin

text:
I've been wanting to try PokeOno for MONTHS, so took advantage of the fact that my husband's car needed serviced, it took forever, and PokeOno was on his way home.  

I'm so happy we finally got a chance to try this deliciousness.  Our bowls brought a touch of brightness to an otherwise cold and dreary day. 

We each had a spicy tuna bowl, mine with mixed greens, his with rice.  Both were fresh and delicious.  Now, I'm picky when it comes to mixed greens.  Very picky.  PokeOno met my standards plus some.  

The spice level was just right and the crunch from the onions made the entire bowl.  

I'm so excited that this place is fairly close and we can fill our poke needs without driving into the city!

text: Grimaldi's Pizza is THE BEST pizza around. It is literally our favorite pizza place for my husband and I.  We order a custom pizza with traditional sauce, pepperoni, ham, garlic and pesto drizzle on top. It is TO DIE FOR GOOD! We order it with a side salad and bottle of wine and it's our favorite date night ever. Also, the staff at the Westshore location are always phenomenal! 5 stars all around.

text: The old Thai Star! Inside is completely remodeled and nicely decorated. I've only dined in once, but have ordered for delivery, and both times I've ordered their Pad Thai. I have not had anything else, but man, its one of the best I've had. The first time I had it, I ordered it with no spice, but the second time I ordered spicy and it was so much better than the first. The noodles were cooked perfectly and the pad thai sauce was the perfect combination of sweet, sour, and tangy. It's on their lunch menu and a great value for the amount of food you get. My coworkers have had their fried rice and curry and highly recommend. Service was fine, attentive and fast, especially for lunch. Parking and get in and out of the lot can be a challenge, but so is most of the restaurants on Thompson Ln.

text: Great spot! We have been wanting to try it. Stopped in for lunch and we both got burgers! I got the volcano - stuffed with blue cheese, fresh jalapeños, and buffalo sauce. Everything was yum! We will be back for sure!

text:
After a nice afternoon at the Audubon Zoo with the Fam - went in search of sustenance and rolled on over to Jacques-Imo's - and, by some miracle, we were able to get a table right away. The last time I was here was at least 10 years ago but it left a lasting impression on me. The Alligator Cheesecake and the Soft Shelled Crab that night were just perfect. Maybe the best Soft Shell Crab I've ever had. 

So it was with high expectation that I walked in with two people who had never been here before. And it was just as good as I remembered. Within minutes of arrival there appeared a plate of Buttered Garlic Parsley Cornbread that I could have just eaten all night. Following that was a pan of flash-fried Brussels Sprouts and part of that process involved some sweet & sour sauce that just WORKED. These too were so amazing that a coupe orders of those would have done me fine for a meal. 

For a main I had the Blackened Redfish with Sweet Potato Mash and Mustard Greens also nicely done. The combo of all three of those was really the best part about that dish. Each item on its own was very good and just short of amazing but the three together became something special. 

One of our party was celebrating a birthday so the surprise Bread Pudding and Creme Brûlée with the obligatory candle was a nice touch at the end. 

Avery took GREAT care of us so huge shout out there.....

Another great meal and memory in the greatest culinary city in the country.....

text:
Definitely my favorite pizza spot in town. The prices are very reasonable, service is always great, and the food never disappoints. I'm a big fan of the crust, which goes well with their huge container of honey. Their pesto wings (dipped in the buffalo sauce and ranch) are also amazing. I like to try their monthly pizza special, which always impresses me. Ask to peruse their binder that has all their previous specials in it. The options are endless!  A special thanks to Kevin, who always provides us with friendly and attentive service. We'll be back again and again! 
Dec 2019 Update: Simply still the best! We sat at the bar and received exceptional service from Kelly. His service was truly five star in every way. The Naughty or Nice Pizza Special is worth a try! We couldn't decide which one we wanted to be so got them both!

text: I had passed this place many times, and finally my curiosity got the best of me on a day I was craving fish and chips. text:
We've been going to the Park St location for many years & were very disappointed when we learned it was moving, but being loyal Outback customers, we were open to trying the new location. 

The Good
 Food & service was what we have come to expect from Outback. 

The Bad
Location. What was a 20 minute drive for us is now a 40 minute drive.

Atmosphere. One big wide open room that reminded me of eating in the high school cafeteria. Yuck!

Noise. Partly because of the wide open concept the noise was deafening. We could hardly hear ourselves talk & we were no more than 3 feet apart.
There is always noise but this was just over the top.
 
No Booths. The "booths" are just tables in the middle of the room with 2 person padded benches on either side instead of chairs. Sorry, that is not a booth. I saw maybe 3 or 4 traditional booths in the entire place.

Experience. If you are looking to have a nice dinner with your significant other or just good friends and you want any semblance of privacy or intimacy look  elsewhere because you won't find it here.

Men's Room. I can't speak for the ladies room but the men's had one stall & one urinal. Really Outback? You couldn't find five more feet to add another stall & urinal. When I went in there were three other guys crammed in there waiting for the stall!

Needless to say but this location was one & done!
name: Joe

text:
Great Tex-Mex restaurant!

This was my first experience at Casa Garcia and I think it was great. The restaurant is very clean, painted with fun colors, and Mexican decor. I went at lunch time and the restaurant was not that busy, but their was quite a few of us there for a Tuesday afternoon. The staff was friendly and our waitress was very sweet and very fast.

We started off with complimentary chips with salsa and a bean dip; which was great. I ordered the #1 on the lunch menu which consisted of a beef taco, a cheese enchilada, a beef flauta (which I switched for a chicken flauta), Mexican rice, retried beans, and guacamole with sour cream. My favorite was the chicken flauta so I'd probably order the flauta combo next time. Everything I ate was still good (tacos could be better) but I would order it again. My husband enjoyed his meal was well (#4). We then ordered the fried ice cream which was amazing! It may sound like a crazy concept but it's a must try.

Overall, I say this place is great and I would give it a try if you're are in the area.
name: Jasmine

text:
This cafe was a disappointment on my first trip to NOLA. We were looking for a cute cafe to spend lunch and were not impressed with many aspects of the experience. Although the decor is adorable and the cafe open to sunlight, the food was overpriced for the portions received. In addition, the service was poor to mediocre and in our party of 8 there were 3 members that did not receive our meals for 45 minutes. Even then, we had to ask multiple times for updates on the status of our meals and were met with annoyed looks by the staff. Finally we had to specifically tell them what we had ordered and they went to make the meals. When my food was finally brought out it was given to the incorrect table and the patrons were left to figure out the mix-up on our own. 

Overall- Although the food was standard quality and tasted fine, I would not recommend this cafe to anyone on a time crunch or looking for friendly service. It was a disappointment compared to many other restaurants we visited on the trip.
name: Ellen

text:

This place is a great atmosphere that is not stuffy or uptight.   The drinks flowed with regularity and the community folks are wonderful.    What a great place to have a good time.  

They have darts, foosball and pool.   Plenty of seating and decor that is welcoming.   A must see and enjoy.  

Thanks Ken for a great evening!

text: My daughter and I were craving oysters on the half shell (NOLA is so famous for).  We waited over 10 minutes for someone to make eye contact with us, much less seat us. Staff was clearly unhappy and could care less about their customers. Oh well... As long as the oysters are good...right? WRONG!! They were out of oysters. How can a restaurant named oyster bar not have oysters??? Gumbo was served on a plate with the soup spilled all over it. We also witnessed the staff bickering and complaining about lousy tips....here's a tip...provide good service and maybe you'll get a good tip!  Too many other fantastic places to eat to bother with this one. Later on we went to Red Fish Grill for a fantastic meal!!

text: This place is located in the public market and their food  is great! We got pad Thai and curry noodles. I had a hard time choosing which one was better because they were both so good. The pad Thai is cooked with tamarind so it adds a unique sweetness to the noodles. And the curry noodles have a coconut curry broth with those pad see ew noodles (the thick noodles) at the bottom and crunchy noodles at the top. There is also a thick chicken breast in the broth  but the chicken isn't the star of the show, it's the broth because it's so delicious! All is all I would 100% recommend this place if you are a fan of Thai food.
name: Austin

text: This restaurant is adorable! It's family friendly and has a very eclectic retro vibe to it. We went while visiting from out of town. My husband had the gator dog which he loved! The fried okra was tasty as were the fries. I got the boneless wings which I didn't care for but that's my own fault for not asking about them before ordering. I like boneless wings that are chicken breast meat and these were minced chicken like McDonald's nuggets. Overall it was really good, and we would definitely stop in next time we are in town.

text: I was visiting Indy and was told I had to try a fried pork tenderloin sandwich. A few people suggested that this was the place to get it. The sandwich was massive and pretty good, but it didn't blow me away. I got onion rings on the side and they were outstanding.

text:
The two of us came here last night ready for some delicious food and drinks.

The chicken and waffle bites were sweet and savory, but everything else fell short.

We ordered crispy steak tacos but the there was nothing crispy about them and lacked flavor.

And after having to ask three separate times if our fried chicken sandwich was on it's way (later discovering that the waitress never placed the order initially) we wish we never ordered it. It was lackluster, over done, and loaded with salt. We love our salt and generally add it to all our meals but in this case, we needed less--much, much less.
It was so bad I couldn't take a second bite. When asked how our meal was, we did not hold back our disappointment. Hopefully, they will be less heavy handed with the salt in their batter next time. 

But between the service (had to continue to ask for water refills and check on our drinks and food order more times than anyone should) we won't be giving this place another visit.

There are far better places in Santa Barbara that serve Finneys entire menu way better.
name: Armita

text: We loved our experience!  Rachel was amazing!  The dumplings and homemade biscuits are amazing!  We will definitely be back!

text:
It was Mother's Day and my family made the reservation as a surprise. When we arrived there was only 1 seated table and some people at the bar. They wanted to seat us right in front of the entrance, We asked to seat further back. 
There was a special Mother's Day menu. Nothing extravagant but Well diverse. We ordered an appetizer for the table. It arrived timely. It was calamari and while they were tender they were flavorless and oily. (Fryer temp probably to low ). 
Salads and soup came with entrees. Average at best. 
We had a broiled fish that was poached and shrimp scampi and fillet mignon. Not one of the entrees wowed is. 
The only other table in the place while we were there told us not to order the chicken piccata as it was over cooked and the dessert was just ok. 
This was our first time here and we were not impressed. Ooh well.

text:
Azian is a great place to get sushi on a budget. 

The rolls are priced affordable, but remember that for most of them you will receive four pieces, or half a roll. 

I have enjoyed most of the rolls I got but would never order the green tea roll again. 

Azian also has a kitchen lunch special but I usually show up for sushi. 

The restaurant is clean and the staff is typically friendly and attentive. One time my tab got mixed up with an acquaintance and I accidentally paid for both. I didn't complain because I noticed after the fact, but I wish that hadn't happened. 

Sometimes Azian is pretty busy and you may have to wait for a table if you show up at a busy time. 

Azian is a great place for cost minded exploration.
name: Krista

text: Outstanding food.  For lunch we split the "Shut up and eat...You'll love it!". This is a chefs special, which is different every single time. We are told that 10 people can sit at a table and order this meal, and each person may come out with something completely different. Ours was a black linguini with shrimp in a rich buttery cream sauce.  I highly recommend you trust the chef and see what happens.

text:
The space where Cholita now occupies has seen it's fair share of businesses open, and then close, within a short amount of time. Within the last 2.5 years that I have lived in the Broad Ripple area, this might be the 4th restaurant/bar to open in this particular space. Due to this, when I heard that another Mexican taqueria was opening (there is also a new trendy/hip taqueria that just opened down the street very recently as well), I was nervous to see how business would end up at Cholita. However, after visiting Cholita on three separate occasions, I hope they're here to stay!

Two of the instances when visiting Cholita, we attended their brunch on a Sunday morning. And wooooow is their brunch delicious and cheap. $15 for an unlimited amount of brunch, sign me up! We ate so much food and everyone ordered something different on the menu, so we were able to try almost everything on the menu. The last instance that we visited Cholita was for dinner. The dinner was good and our cocktails were delicious and beautiful as well. On top of that, our service at Cholita has been great every time as well. It is definitely a spot that we will continue to frequent!

text:
The first time I visited Retrograde Coffee I was in a bit of a hurry.  I had my 7 year old son with me and I was on my way to an appointment. What made me want to come back was that the place is a serious knock out. The hard wood floors you'd luv to have in your living room and the marble top counters with gold finishes make for a great-looking location that begs you to come chill. 
Fast forward a couple weeks till today when I took my entire family after church. We ordered a plain coffee, three decaf Americanos, a sausage and cheese pastry that was light and buttery along side a delectable but not overly sweet cinnamon bun. Oh yeah and I got a cookie. The baked goods were from Brightside Bakery. The coffee from Onyx Coffee and the cookie from Hi-Fi Cookies. I was glad to see High Garden Tea and Spindrift Sodas in their offerings as well. You can tell the staff has an eye for notch treats with a twist.   

The prices were what you would see in coffee shops of this caliber. Note that, It may be on Dickerson Pike but places like Retrograde signal that Cleveland Park is growing in what it has to offer.  Retrograde has zero clutter but it is not cold and tweely modern. There is a coziness, mostly informed by the paintings on the wall that work in a sharp electric palette, that give it a distinct quality. Whether you are in a hurry, need a space to chill, or knock out that work project I think Retrograde will fit the bill. My only regret is I forgot to snap a pic of the rad window sign.
name: Adam

text: It was busy but the food didn't take long to come out once seated. Had the piggy omelette and it was good. Will definitely be going back.

text: Warning: you will absolutely become addicted. There's no way around it. One taste and it's all over. FK will be what you crave all day every day. text: Not impressed. Sat me and my best friend at a table with Wells for the hot broth we would cook our ingredients in. No less than four servers came over to explain how shabu shabu works, even though I indicated I already knew. I will say that's actually probably a good thing for the uninitiated, but it was a bit much for us. It works like a sushi bar, check off the ingredients you want to cook and they bring you huge plates of meat, seafood, vegetables and noodles.  I ordered ramen. I expected wiggly, soft, fresh noodles. What I got was a hard block of $.39 Maruchen-style noodles probably liberated from its foil spice pack in the back. The broth I ordered was so full of whole peppercorns it was impossible to eat anything I cooked. Meat was really fatty. I did like the shrimp came whole, heads and all. There's also a list of signature martinis for $5, which is a great price these days. I was mainly disappointed because the hibachi place that Crab General replaced was SO GOOD, I expected the same quality.   I wouldn't say no to trying it again to make sure, but our first visit was really disappointing.

text:
Came to St Pete for a business trip and wanted something warm on a cold Tampa night.  Honestly first appearance, this place is hip and I thought it was a club because of the loud music...Seriously, this place makes me want to dance.  LoL.  I thought I would try it because it's hot and new but was a little turned off when I didn't see any Asians in a Japanese resturant but then again, I'm in St Pete...just sayin.  The food quality wa very good.  

The staff was very helpful and attentive at first, but after the shift change...no one came to see if I needed more water of tea.  "Hello...I'm sitting right in front of the kitchen." Eventually a new waitress showed up and was attentive.  

For starters ordered Hamachi Kama, the yellowtail collar,  I have to say they missed the mark on this.  Fish cooks very fast.  It was definitely crispy on the outside as it should be but it was totally overcooked.  The meat was dry and hard and didn't easily fall off the bone.  It wasn't succulent and juicy as it should be.  The up side is the fish was very fresh.  

My main dish, I ordered the Chicken Paitan Ramen...it was very tasty and definitely had an abundance of flavors but is was not hot in temp.  It was served warm and the ramen noodles al dante...Ramen in Japan is never served al dante. It is served hot and firm. Aside from the noodles being under cooked, I don't understand why half of an egg cost $2.00.  All ramen (especially in LA) places come with half an egg already. I think because the ramen was not hot I really wasn't into eating it. 

At last the Halo Halo...I have to say, was delish!  I love the different layers an flavors of this desert. Rice crispy, condensed milk, vanilla ice cream, shave ice, coconut, jack fruit, agar agar, red bean, mung bean, jelly fruit, guava and whatever else I missed.  It was really really good and worth the $10.00.  

A little shocked a small pot of tea was $6.00. But then again it was probably from Teavana.  

All in all I really think with a few tweaks here and there, this place has definite potential to be a 4 to 5 star establishment.  I would come again just to see if the food stays consistent.
name: Vera

The red beans and rice are fantastic too. The tropical storm is sweet and tasty drink. This is also my first time trying a gator. I enjoyed the blacked gator than the crispy one. 

My husband ordered swamp tea and it was okay. He also enjoyed the red beans and rice, jambalaya and the blackened gator.

text: Lousy. Primo's has an excellent selection of sandwiches, but this location is straight up awful. Only reason I chose this spot was because the Ritner st location was already closed. Can't tell the difference between a tomato and a hot pepper?? Hoagies are skimpy and cost more. Ritner st location is WAY better!! Thick hoagies and cheaper

text: The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. The music was louder than it needed to be. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Definitely coming back. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..
name: User

text:
I rediscovered this jewel of N St Pete on 62nd Ave.
How great to see the owner, Peter and great server, Cindy still there. All the Olde English favourites still there too! Fish n chips,  Yorkshire puddin', and even 
lamb shanks on Thursdays. There is a nice selection of ciders and beer. He even bakes his own bread, makes his own cole slaw daily and uses fresh produce and meats. There are weekly events like trivia night. It's like a neighborhood pub.
name: Bill

text:
So I've held off doing a review to allow them to get some time to get their footing. I'm sad to say that at this moment, Salt Shack on the Bay is becoming a place to enjoy the view and drinks...but not eat. 

The view is the best in Tampa. Bridge to open bay give this place the beast backdrop for any occasion. Sunsets are amazing. 

Dining is all outdoors. The main dink g area has a bar and lots of tables and of course the roof protects from the rain. The bar pavilion (as I call it) is the
Best spot to hang. I'm hoping they invitation in some protection from windy rain because the roof will not provide 100% coverage for those afternoon storms. They also should look into a cooling/misting system. 

Service can go from lightening fast to normal. Bartenders have always been friendly, but they lack any real knowledge of the food offerings. Food usually comes out via runner and we have yet to get our food 'hot'. Today's grilled grouper was warm and tasty, but the bun was stale and the fish fillet barely covered the bun. The portion of fries were a joke - maybe 10. These were not the yucca fries...regular cheap fries. The onion straws were tasty but cold. 

The burger was more medium well then medium. If you can't cook a burger to order, don't ask how I want it. The side of jicama slaw appeared to be just regular ole cabbage slaw. When we questioned the bartender she just said "yeah, all I know is we don't have regular slaw...we have jicama slaw". Obviously this was not jicama as we often make it at home and know what it looks like. The burger was 'warm'. 

Past visits included the tuna tartare, smoked fish spread and wings. The tuna presentation was on point but overall was very very bland. The smoked fish spread deserves some credit and one of our faves. The wings were also a hit. 

The menu is also strangely narrow without options to really customized. When asked if I could get a side of vegetables with my sandwich, I was told they can't do that. Looking at other plates, the vegetables are more garnish than side dish (small potion).  Gluten free guests or keto diets will have very limited options. 

We hope they get the kitchen and service in order because they have so much potential.  The vibe, view and overall look of the place is the best around.
name: Mark

text: Had a morning work meeting here and while probably not the best place to hold a meeting (hi, fancy coffee machine that is loud), the food & coffee were both delicious! We attempted to sit in the very back for the meeting but due to the product delivery coming through the back doors, they asked us to move up front. I had the California bagel + caramel latte and could only eat half the bagel because it was loaded! They also have a variety of baked goods that I REALLY wanted to try but I opted for not one, but two lattes this morning. One with breakfast and one for the trip back to work. While this isn't located on my daily commute, I feel certain I can leave the house a few minutes early to go out of my way to stop by again!
name: Caitlin

text: honestly I think I ordered the wrong thing. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. For the price I expected more than this.

text:

Out of a table of four, half of what we ordered came to the table too salty for human consumption.   The food that was edible wasn't exactly inspired cuisine.

name: Joel

text: I have no idea how this  place got its stars. It does not deserve more than too and I feel like I am being generous. The omelette was bland, home fried potato not edible. Service took a long time. Everything too greasy. How hard is it to make eggs and coffee? This is the worst breakfast I have had in a while. Run away.

text:
Great place to call an order in for a quick meal.  Their food is very good.
Great selection of home cooking type food.

Their sandwiches are fantastic.  The Jazz will fill all categories needed for a great sandwich.  Good hamburgers. Great mac&cheese.

Need cat litter or TV dinners at 3 am?  NOT A PROBLEM!!!!

text: Holy cow it is all great here!! I am not one to eat out for breakfast but now I am! The million dollar bacon was so rich in flavor. I absolutely loved the kale tonic even though I don't like kale haha. The flavors are just super rich and super fresh. It is worth what you pay for it and the service is always friendly.
name: Tim

text:
This place has gone so far down hill and I am so seriously disappointed.

We show up at 815 pm and get in the one line open, we both opt for burritos. We got barbacoa and chicken, and made it through the line, I know they like to add little amounts of money here and there to up the price, but there was loud music, the couple in front of me was complaining loudly about politics, the girl that was helping me was shorter, and significantly quieter, so when she asked me if I really wanted extra cheese I was surprised? (Turns out she was telling me cheese WAS extra, but that's definitely not what came out). Get to the register, and to my surprise, a SPRINKLE of cotija was $1 extra?! I checked the menu, no mention of it ever. When I brought it up to the woman checking me out, she LOUDLY proclaimed, "she didn't TELL you?!" which was accusatory and not what I meant and made the woman helping me look bad which isn't what I wanted, so I clarified that it might be nice that they put that the cheese they put on first counts and if you would rather have cotija later to let them know at the beginning? (I had NO idea and I would have told them no cheese at the beginning if there had been a nice comment on the board where it includes your choice of cheese at the beginning as part of it; the menu makes it seem like the cheese on the beginning comes with it and you have the option of adding free sprinkled cheese later). The person checking me out says its not her problem and it I want I can tell it to the manager who is at the register next to her (she was slow and a line was building so he hopped in to help out). I mention it calmly to him and he says its not his problem. By that point the girl helping me shoves my two burritos, one bag of chips, and two cups at me and walks away to do something else. She had forgotten the 2nd chips and dip and when I tried to get her attention she blew me off, I tried to get the girl making burritos attention since the manager was busy checking someone out, but she either couldn't hear me or ignored me. The manager finished so I tried to get his attention and he leaned around me and asked for the next couple, meanwhile my husband and I are standing there waiting, blocking the way, just trying to get the chips and dip I paid for. Tired of the attitude from them, I finally interrupted the manager and told him I PAID for chips and dip and never got them. He then gave me this super judging look and checked over my tray and I told him I had ordered two, and he looks around like maybe I put the extra chips and dip elsewhere and was trying to cheat him?? (Seriously the look on his face was so condescending). I told him that he had seen me standing right there the whole time and all I wanted were my chips and dip that I paid for, so finally he demands my receipt, gets the chips and dip and shoves it at me.

I'm sorry, your day may have been busy, it could have been a bad shift, other bad things could have happened, but for how consistently NASTY I was treated I won't be back. Your prices have increased significantly, you charge a ton of extra money for every.little.thing, and your employees AND manager give your customers attitude? No, I'm not supporting a business like that. I seriously miss the old Felipe's from like 4 years ago :(
name: Elizabeth

text: The 404 Kitchen chef took over this menu and ruined what was Fin and Pearl prior. For the price, go to somewhere better. Just having to be honest

text: I spent the most fabulous weekend at Belmond El Encanto. Romantically secluded on a hill yet so close to Santa Barbara downtown..... such a perfect place for two people celebrating love or a group of people gathering together for such occasions as weddings, bachelorette parties, conferences, wellness retreats.... it's so quiet and peaceful. The heated swimming pool overlooking the Santa Barbara, the patio with the most beautiful sunset I ever seen.... it's classy and cozy.... well check out the images... they speak for themselves....

text: First time and not so sure if I'll return . I ordered something simple to try  out , western omelette & home fries . The omelette was sooo dry even with the cheese , the home fries were burnt and the toast was so soggy ugh . I should of asked to look at my food before I left since it was take out smh .
