I did like the topping combination of prosciutto, caramelized onions, basil, and it was supposed to have red pepper but I did not see any. Overall, the food was okay and priced fairly. The outdoor patio was cute and the service was pretty good. I'm glad I tried it! I thought the restaurant was substantially better than when I had their pizza at the Indy 500. The pepperoni pizza from the food truck didn't have the light and crispy crust.
name: Samantha

text: The outside and inside is very 70's, but the food was great! We were seated right away and got the deluxe dinner something for two and got chicken, shrimp, and steak. The steak was some of the most juicy, tender, and delicious filet I've had in Boise. Highly recommend if you're looking for a good meal with a friend or two.
name: Kendall

text: Visited yesterday from Chicago, food was decent, building needs to be updated, but did see insects in the bathroom unfinished portion of building visible. Expected more.
name: Mercedes

text: Perfect place, delicious turkish food, everything is ok. Lentil soup is wonderful. Mixed kebabs are nice
name: Osman

text:
Y'all! Mangú!! Mangú is like the most savory buttery flavorful creamy mashed green plantains you could imagine; very similar to  mashed potatoes, it's incomparable to potatoes but somewhat similar. Dominicans know how to DO IT!!

I tried the Mangú Criollo- mangú topped with shrimp and pork skin cracklings. Yea, that's right -- creamy, buttery savory mangú topped with shrimp, aguacate cilantro sauce AND crispy pork skin cracklins! I went here during a work lunch so I didn't want to over order and then want to take a nap, BUT I wanted to try everything! Although I appreciate such a great menu selection, it was really hard to rein myself in with such an amazing selection!

My only wish is that they would have given me more aguacate cilantro sauce!! And I wish the menu wasn't with such small text (kinda hard to read). But I LOVE the space it's decorated so adorably 

I can not wait to return and try the empanadas!
name: Alison

text: Great place! Never disappointed in food or service. Took my bf here for his birthday as he chose bascoms over Berns.
name: Jen

text: My wife and I had beer flights, the pretzel appetizer and we shared "The Bomb" burger. I have to say the food was fantastic. The burger in pizza dough....... can't believe I hadn't had a burger like that before. So good! We will be back for sure!
name: Madison

text: We went for our anniversary on a Saturday night. We had the mussels as an appetizer, and we often eat mussels, they were phenomenal! Most restaurants use too much garlic, but these were perfect. We then split a bone in filet. It was very good. We eat a lot of filet and this was good. We got it prepared Oscar style --this was okay--have had Oscar style preparations. For dessert we had the Alaskan something. It was an orange homemade frozen custard covered in a toasted merengue -- it was absolutely amazing!!! One of my favorite desserts ever! The dessert chef is awesome! Our service was great. Ambiance is ok. Basic nice steakhouse ambience. Overall we were very impressed! We will be back for sure.
name: Beth

text:
This is a nice place for brunch. They also have decent amount of vegetarian options for people who eat eggs. 

The complimentary cakes are nice as well and a very different concept. 

I would definitely recommend this place for brunch or desserts because that's all i have tried here so far.
name: Rupa

text: Parking was annoying and I was already in a bad mood by the time I got inside. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. The food was good and the service was easygoing. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly.
name: User

text: Closed for repairs. No timeline for reopening provided - but I'll be there when they do!
name: Kyle

text: A cool space and building, with a diverse enough menu, but food is mostly bland. We stopped here for the view and stopped to eat as well. We ordered the lemon chicken and the salmon. The salmon was absolutely nothing to brag about. Very bland flavor and over cooked. The cocktails were also super sweet but lacking in alcohol.  Not worth the price.
name: Amber

text: Had a great experience staying here for 3 nights for a work convention. Rooms were nice and the hotel is in a good location. The only downfall is that the hotel is huge so it was a long walk from my room to get to the convention center
name: Trevor

text: The Boathouse at Hendry's Beach is a great spot to go have some drinks and relax. It has great ocean views along with good sea food. It also has a nice patio area and a cool bar. Can't wait to come back here again.
name: Ramiro

text: Came here on a whim with some co workers on a busy friday afternoon and everyone in my party had a good time. We all agreed to come back again. They hook you up with the drinks. Seriously. We were told by the staff that they pour generously and don't really measure which is a win for me I think. I ordered a long island and it was pretty good. Still tasted like a long island but it got me already which was my goal.lol. We also ordered some appetizers that came quick and was delicious! Would recommend the 3 layer quesadilla! The wait staff were very friendly and fast. We had a great time and would come back again!
name: Gay

text:
We came here strictly for the beer and we weren't disappointed! Parking wasn't the easiest, but we were able to snag a spot in the back lot after a few times circling around the block. 

It was a Saturday afternoon and the inside was crowded. The hostess told us there was another bar downstairs where we might be able to find a seat instead of waiting for a table, so we ventured down and she was right. We ordered a flight of all 7 beers for $14.50 and enjoyed them all. The Mosaic Imperial IPA was our favorite. The Chinook Pale Ale was a close second which we wound up getting a crowler of to take home. I highly recommend both beers!

The bartenders were friendly and attentive. The couple next to us had a delicious looking pizza and they said it was amazing. We'll be back next time we're in the neighborhood and will try their food.
name: Tom

text:
Went with a group last Sunday to celebrate, and had booked a table for one of their tea party days a few weeks before.

It's the first time I went there, as we usually go somewhere else like Hotel Macdonald, and I can tell you right off the bat that the one offered by The Art of Cake is much MUCH better!

Their shabby chic decor is absolutely adorable and tasteful! The tables were decently spaced and lighting warm and bright. The staff were also super sweet when chatting and checking in on us during the course of our tea party.

The menu was mouthwatering. Other tea parties, while sticking to bite sized portions, also stuck with scant fillings/toppings and little variety that always left me feeling like I should go for a burger run after. The Art of Cake's was not only as generous as they can be with the fillings in the bite sized portions, they were also varied and left my palette (and stomach) leaving well satisfied.

Their plating and food presentation was fantastic and pleasing to the eye. It left me feeling reluctant to bite into some of the pieces  because they were too cute and perfect!

Would definitely recommend, and would go again!
name: Jihan

text: The chicken liver paté appetizer was amazing. The cocktail I originally ordered was not available so the waitress brought me one but did not tell me what it was but said that if I didn't like it she would bring me another. I kind of would have liked to know what was in it. I had the steak and parmesian fries which was a little too salty and my friend had a fish filet fish that was a little too buttery.
name: Austin

text:
We hosted the Boise Supper Club at the Pad Thai house for our March meet up and it was such a huge hit! 

Not only did we have AMAZING customer service, but our food was sooooooo delicious! 

They don't take reservations so if you have a large party send one person early to get your name on the list.  We had about 15 people and I called the month before to coordinate, but also knew to go early.  Once we were all seated, our waitress did a phenomenal job keeping orders straight, refilling drinks, getting food out while it was hot, etc.  Rockstar waitress for sure!!!

My table got the cream cheese wontons, they were awesome!!!!  I love the glaze you dip them in! I also love that they don't have seafood in them! 

My hubby gets the sweet and sour soup and the chicken lo mein spice level 3.  I got the sweet and sour pork (or sometimes I get the sweet and sour chicken).  Either way I get mine with 0 spice. 

For whatever you order you can choose 1-5 on the level of spice.  I love that so I can get something I like, he can get the spicy level he likes.  

I also like that my meal comes with a salad and rice.  I love the salad and the dressing.  It's the perfect portion size for me with the perfect amount of dressing.  The meal you roofer is usually large so you'll likely have leftovers. 

Overall- it's always busy, plan ahead!  It is a phenomenal restaurant and the secrect is out and that's why they are always busy!
name: Amy

text: Does not honor happy hour prices if you sit at a table... Like, if you have a stroller, and you want to sit inside with an infant.  Happy hour is only at the bar, or outside. It was 95°.
name: Colin

text: Kaleigh was an amazing server! She was on top of everything and super friendly!! Our chef Chris A was top notch and the food was amazing. Highly recommend for special occasions and birthdays!
name: Brandon

text: This was a good restaurant if you are looking for a fresh taste of seafood meal. Don't be in a rush there will be a wait.. well worth it.
name: Terrence

text: Such a fun experience. It's a go in and go to the counter type of ordering. There was a group of 5 of us and I made a reservation online prior. When we made the reservation, they put us upstairs which was super nice because not only was it cooler up there (temperature wise) but it was less crowded and could hear ourselves talk. The food was really good! I wasn't a huge fan of the run they use on their ribs but that's just my pickiness. The sides were amazing and if you like pickles. Try the kool aid pickles. Sounds bizarre but definitely worth a try and tastes just like a real pickle.
name: Kari

text: 5 stars in a gross understatement. I don't even know where to begin! Everything just stands out, the food is UNBEATABLE especially for the price. I'd probably pay double if I had to. The pasta and chicken kebab really hit the spot for me. They put this super unique sauce on it and it had a spicy tang. Nothing I've had before. Aside from the food, the customer service is good. Everyone is very nice to me. The environment is nicely designed and very European-like. Great coffee too, definitely not your average Starbucks grade coffee. Lots of beer too, can't get enough of that. Overall a great place.
name: Chris

text:
Quaint and charming little spot. Total hidden gem. 

We've had Ethiopian food before in South Tampa and at a couple of spots in Orlando. This particular place is very close to my house so I know we'll be here more than every 6 months. The owner was a sweet heart and the service was excellent. 

We had just finished up a late night cultural performance and we were starving ... go figure it's Sunday and everything in Tampa closes at 9pm... we were hungry at 9:30pm and finally had time to think about food. We didn't want to be those people that just showed up at a venue so we called ahead to find out what time they were closing. She said they close at 10 and asked how far away we were. Our answer to distance was 10 minutes and she said come on down. We were warming greeted even though it was almost closing time. 

We had a wonderful meal with a mix of beef and veggie dishes. She explained all the dishes as she presented it and that added to the restaurants charm. =)
name: Jenette

text: I almost skipped this place because of the ratings and that would've been unfair. Food was fresh and service was quick. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Not saying it's the best place ever, but it was totally fine. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Food was good and came out fast. It looked better online than it did in person.
name: User

text: The food came out fast, which was good bc we were starving. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Food was fresh and service was quick. The sauces helped more than I thought they would..
name: User

text: Biscuit Cafe is a Mexican restaurant in the Broad Ripple area. The first time I went, I was not a fan, but this second time it was not bad. They have a good selection of food and nice decor. The staff were super friendly and kind. It was good to talk to them in Spanish. My boyfriend and I split a chorizo torta. The plates are huge! The only disappointment was the lack of fresh hot salsa. The salsa they served us was super mild and not that flavorful which was disappointing for a Mexican restaurant. Yet, I understand why given the location and most of the customers are Non-Mexicans. I ordered an horchata drink, but it did not taste like most horchatas. It tasted more sugary with a mix of whipped cream, which does not go with the traditional drink but had an interesting taste to it.
name: Gloria

text:
What if I told you that Swiss Haus has a cake that is so light that even your sharpest knife will have a hard time not making a mess of it. What if I told you that... that the cake is so light that you could take five bites... and it won't even feel like you took one bite! I ate a slice and it was gone so fast I thought, "what just happened!?" I ate another slice and it was gone so fast it was like deja vu... like I've been here before. 

I needed something... anything... to understand that it was real. I took the cleaver (yeah I cut my cakes with a cleaver) and I scraped the icing off the tray and I licked it off the knife like a savage (don't tell anybody I do that) and it just dissolved on my tongue instantly. This is a sophisticated, upper echelon, grown and sexy, smooth criminal, special snowflake of a cake if I've ever had one. They call it the "Sacher" ...the Sacher Cake. I loved it. Absolutely. It's not even the best cake I've ever had, but it's an evolution. It's on a refined level-- a true indulgence-- a work of art. They have these available everyday. I can't believe it has taken me this long to try it. This is a "me" cake... for those times when you're just looking out for number one.
name: Anthony

text: You can tell they care about customer experience here. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Food was fresh and service was quick. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Overall, a strong experience. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait.
name: User

text: We were really pleased with our experience here.  The service was outstanding.  Very knowledgeable, proactive, informative, and attentive.  We ordered Pisco Sours, Cucumber Mules, and Malbecs, all of which were meticulously crafted and/or of top quality.  Two orders of the freshest ceviche(scallop and tuna), the lamb shank, and the crispy seafood assortment were all delicious. The desserts were also impeccable and unique.  Passion fruit tres leches was my personal favorite.  Definitely a welcomed addition to the finer dining scene on Magazine.  Can't wait to go back.
name: Morgan

text: OMG!! I had to stop eating to write this review. I'm from Memphis, TN and have been in Florida a year looking for the right BBQ spot that would satisfy my taste buds like the places back home. WELL I finally found it. I judge a place off the simple things. If the Pulled Pork Sandwich and Baked Beans are not good, then I can't trust it. My lunch was so delicious and flavorful that I have to come back to try other items on the menu. It helps that's it's a black owned business with good customer service. This is my new spot!!
name: Carlean

text: The menu is really impressive, unique and fun. I was excited for the lobster chowder, but it came cold and basically just corn. No lobster which made me sad. The impossible burger is always a favorite when places offer it, but it was burnt as was my husband's regular burger. Maybe it was a bad night for the cook, but I was really disappointed
name: Kaylee

text: I'm from California and found this place on yelp while visiting friends and family. The reviews looked promising and I was not disappointed. It was so good, I ended up going twice! First morning I had pork roll and eggs with hash brown and a grilled muffin. Only mild complaint is the hash browns, good, but not great and too much food. Next day we were there on a Saturday and so I had the chipped beef, eggs, and muffin, skipping the hash browns and it was amazing. Just be aware that it is cash only, but prices are very reasonable, especially compared to what breakfast costs where I live!
name: Brian

text: I've visited quite a few times. I've tried the tenders and the white meat dinner option. Both are great. If you don't do spicy, I suggest getting it without any sauce. The Mac and cheese is wonderful as are the fries. The different soft drinks are also a nice touch. Be prepared for a bit of a wait during peak times as well. Overall a must try but make sure not to order too spicy.
name: Callie

text:
The food here is very good. We normally come here for brunch. It has a varied and great selection. You will find something to your living for sure.

The wait times here are bad and disorganized. Despite tables being open, you may find yourself waiting 20-30 mins in a very small, crowded, space.
name: Boba

text: Big freaking THANK YOU to the whole staff on hand for the catering order I picked up today. Bill did a fantastic job making sure I had everything I needed. The food was a hit amongst my coworkers. We got the biscuits and gravy and I didn't hear anyone talking because they were too busy eating. Great job! And thank you again.
name: Dionna

text:
This place has some of the best coffee in Reno! The service on the weekend is a little less quality than the normal Mon - Fri morning crew I'm used to. 

My tips for this place is to ask for your coffee extra hot. Sometimes the heat dies a little to quick.. and make sure to grab a loyalty card. After 10 purchases you get one on the house!
name: Michael

text: I had a very good experience here! My girlfriend and I walked in without a reservation on a busy Sunday night. They were more than happy to accommodate us and told us there would be a little bit of a wait. We hung out by the bar until we received our text that the table was ready (awesome feature)! The food was phenomenal. We ordered two appetizers and two entrees which were perfect portions! We had just enough room for dessert which was strawberry creme brulee- yes, also vegan!!! The setting, staff, service, and food were all exceptional.
name: Joel

text:
Walked through the door and the first thing the front cashier told me was that I couldn't bring my coffee in. Wasn't the welcome I was expecting but I digressed. 
We had a big group. They got us in quick which was nice. We all got our food at different times which is fine and expected in big groups but half of us were done eating before the other side of the table got their food. So I would suggest not going with large groups. Orange juice is freshly squeezed everyday and boy you can taste it. All of the food was delicious. I got the koko chicken sandwich and my gf got the guacamole toast. Food is worth the visit!
name: Devin

text: Pretty tasty! I had my first oyster experience and they were delicious! We got the char grilled oysters and they were fantastic! They give you bread to sop up all the delicious sauce that's left over. Mmmmm so tasty! I got the crawfish po boy and it was pretty good. Our server Eve was delightful. Overall pretty good.
name: Marissa

text:
Chargrilled Oysters is a MUST when coming to this gem! First stop when we arrived in NOLA and definitely set the tone for the rest of the trip. The Etoufee was also a great addition. 

We waited in line for about 15-20 mins. The wait wasn't too bad but then again it was 3pm on a Thursday. There were 5 of us and we ordered a pretty decent amount of food, the server remembered all the orders and everything came out in a timely manner. Definitely can not wait to go back!
name: Stephanie

text:
I officially hate this Noodles and Company location. The amount of times I have tried but to be let down again has numbered around 6-8. No more!

The main thing is, quality is awful here - especially for the Mac and cheese. TOO MANY TIMES there has been not enough cheese or the cheese has been watery. On my visit this month it actually tasted so bad, I barely ate it and just tossed it out. I should have said something, but it was right before closing by then and the staff were rushing around... sigh. This place is a waste of money. 

There always seems to be something wrong on all my visits. The one day my Noodles rewards gives me a free pop, the pop machine broke. Once the AC or fan in the back was broke and staff were (understandably) cranky. Sometimes the cash register doesn't work. 

But mostly - if all those things and the food you make me is still terrible? I am done. Bye, Noodles!
name: Nicole

text: I would have given it four starts, but our waitress didn't listen well. She missed an important request and left something off our order.
name: Rachel

text: Finally came by when there wasn't a line to get in. Bartender couldn't have been sweeter. The food was absolutely incredible. My husband is still raving about the charbroiled oysters with the crab on top. If you're in the quarter check them out.
name: Adrienne

text: I rely on a lot of online reviews but I never write them. We have dined in at this restaurant last summer and my husband just picked up our take out order a few minutes ago.   Sorry to say this restaurant is mediocre at best.  When we dined in last summer, we ordered a whole fish entree and pad thai...both were decent but nothing to write home about.  We chose other restaurants when we were craving Thai.  We decided to give this restaurant another try tonight out of pure convenience (we live close).  As soon as I opened my container of take out drunken noodles, I noticed that it was filled with uncooked/undercooked veggies and hardly any noodles.  There is a decent amount of shrimp and the flavor is good.  However, it does not make up for the fact that my $12 drunken NOODLE dish has hardly any noodles and half of it is just uncooked cabbage/broccoli.  Close to home or not, we won't be going back.
name: Leena

text: Portion size looked small at first but it was actually enough. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. The staff seemed tired but still polite. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price..
name: User

text: Sahm restaurant group has better options.  Schnitzel is always good. Spaetzel is just ok.  Other foods vary from just ok to not really that great at all. They would have been much better to stick with the tried and true pub food options.   Excellent location.  Awesome beer garden going up out back for next summer.  The food is the problem. Let's see how long this "German Bier Hays" experiment lasts.
name: Jane

text:
First time to Charley's and have to say we were rather disappointed. We showed up a tad early for our reservation, and were seated promptly at our reservation time. It took awhile for the waiter to take our drink order despite having visited the table 3 times and after bringing water. We knew we were in for a slow meal so we didn't order appetizers. It didn't matter because it took forever regardless. None of us were drinking wine, but the server left the wine glasses in the table despite our asking fir them to be removed. They sat there in our way until dinner was served. After ordering our meal, we expected salads and bread, but they did not come for some time, so we sat there forever with nothing. I know some of this is nit-picky, but when spending top dollar for your meal you expect impeccable and flawless service.

I had ordered the 21 day aged 22 oz. prime bone in strip and was very excited to dive in when the meal finally arrived, but was so disappointed. What was supposed to be a fantastic cut of meat was overcooked and tough. I ordered medium rare and the steak was well done on the edge and barely mid rare right next to the bone. I didn't bother sending it back because 1) my server did not bother to ask if everything was cooked properly, 2) it took so long to get it, I was starving, and 3) the last thing I want is the fake apologies of some apathetic manager whose sole job is to go around apologizing for poorly cooked meals. When paying this kind of money, I expect perfection right out of the gate. To expect otherwise is to go to Outback, which is where I should have gone in the first place because this steak was subpar at best. I cannot say I will return any time soon.
name: Curt

text: We've been here a few times and each time has been delicious! The food is consistent and the staff are very attentive and friendly. Great cocktails! Highly recommend the veggie pizza!!
name: Sara

text:
Hands down, THE BEST food, beer and service we've had in Nashville while visiting!
Our bartender Betsy treated us like family, making sure we ordered exactly what we had in mind, and picked out the perfect beer selections for us. The Manager, Andrew, came to our table and had an actual conversation with us, not your typical "fly by" by management. Great overall experience!
Update: we loved this restaurant so much we dined there again tonight...two nights in a row! Kathleen took GREAT care of us, plus the entire staff is amazing! Food was perfect!! Thank you Andrew!!
BTW...the Apple Strudel and The Pretzel Bread Pudding is out of this world!
name: Lynn

text: Excellent food, excellent prices, and excellent service! I can't believe the size of their lunch items and they are all between $7.50 and $10.50. Will definitely be coming back!
name: Ed

text: Had brunch here over the weekend and it was kind of a mixed bag. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Would absolutely visit again. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent.
name: User

text:
We love to come here and get BBQ. Really nice people. The pulled pork and brisket is second to none. This place is a hidden secret worth exploring you will not be disappointed!

Also great for large orders. We have picked up several pounds of pulled pork, racks of ribs and brisket for quite a few parties. They always have had plenty, no need to pre order unless your feeding more than 50 or coming late in the day.
name: Cassaundra

text:
This particular branch has always been slow (food is never ready when the confirmation e-mail says it will be ready).  But last Friday 2-1-2019 I ordered online, and went to pick up my order.  E-mail confirmation said ready by 5:50.  When I checked in with the counter person at 5:55 , he said it would be about 5 more minutes.  So I waited for another 30 minutes, at least 3 times someone asked for my name again, looked at the waiting food and then wandered off.  I stood in there until 6:30, and was never apologized to or shown any concern by the entire staff.   Since I am not a middle aged woman with a "I need to speak with the manager" haircut, I didn't cause a scene I just left and got food from a competitor.   When I noticed later that they had charged my credit card , I called the corporate number from the website.  They said all branches are individually owned so I would have to call this specific store.  When I did call and ask to speak to someone about a complaint, I was hung up on.
The horrible service I received from this branch has helped me decide to not patronize any Jets pizza any more.
name: John

text: I love ole Smokey moonshine so this is the perfect spot.  I never knew there were so many different flavors.  The strawberry fields was so delicious.  The mango jalapeño moonshine was amazing.  It was sweet with a little heat.  The punch cooler was great too.  So cool and refreshing.  We sat inside at the bar and the weather was perfect.  Our bartender was sweet and very helpful with the recommendations.  I definitely want to go back the next time I'm there
name: Dore

text:
I am such a Dizengoff fan that I resisted Hey Hummus for months.

BIG mistake. Their hummus is completely on the same level as Dizengoff PLUS their hot sauce is an awesome kick. You get pickles and olives on the side of the regular hummus bowl and the pita is fluffy and warm. 

Will totally go back and try their other options (including shawarma and Shakshuka!)
name: Kelly

text: This was a good restaurant. I'm not a beer drinker, so I can't speak for the beers, but my companions seemed pleased with the selection. Everyone in my group seemed happy with their food choices. No one was oohhhhing and aaahhhhing, but when asked, everyone seemed happy. I had the turkey swiss bacon sandwich, and I thought it was yummy. But the highlights of the meal were at the beginning and end. The potato chowder was really tasty and satisfying. But the beignets with butterscotch sauce were amazing! I wish there had been 20 more (and that's saying something because they give you an excellent portion for sharing). I could have just drunk the butterscotch sauce by itself and died happy. If you go here, don't skip the beignets!
name: Jenny

text: I HAVE TO RATE IT HIGH FOR MY COMMENTS TO BE THERE FOR OTHERS TO SEE BECAUSE WHEN I WENT BACK TO LOOK AT MY COMMENT IT SAID: "REVIEWS NOT RECOMMENDED"...It seems as if every time I step foot in Five Guys Manhattan location I encounter horrible treatment from the SAME man!! His name is Michael "Mike" the store manager come off as a huge RACIST!! My first visit to the store when I walked in I was politely greeted and asked my order by the worker Damian (Hispanic) and Mike got mad with him and went off on him and sent him home because he beat him to the punch!! When I came in today I had a friend with me who was new to the store and asked about the menu and Mike raised his voice at him as if he was slow or hard of understanding and it made him so angry that he won't ever return!!! I just hope someone hurry and get rid of him!!
name: Kaylen

text:
Shrimp scampi for me,
Fried Mac & Cheese Balls for my youngest,
And Oreo cheesecake for me babe!
Soooooooooooooo goooooooood! Everybody loved what they got. This is one of my top places I love to go to in the area.
name: Taylor

text: The 'shift manager' on 10/5 at noon has the worst customer service skills I've ever experienced. I asked for two hot dogs, which is on their menu, and was told "I don't have any ready". Not "we're out of hot dogs" not "they're not ready, would you mind waiting" just no hot dogs. I know they don't keep them ready made as I've had to wait before, which wouldn't have been an issue. She just didn't want to take the five minutes to make them apparently. This girl should not even be in any kind of customer service, let alone a shift manager.
name: Megan

text: I recently tried this place after living here for awhile. Want to say we enjoyed the food. Had excellent service thanks to our server Drew. Very friendly and attentive. Will be back again!!!!
name: Cindy

text:
Is it possible for a restaurant to kick your ass? To physically assault your palate in such a way that you LIKE it? We are talking some Fifty Shades of flavor here. The kind of masochistic torture that is so good you dare not utter your safe word? (My safe word is Bun Bo Hue, by the way.)
     The secret is out. Some of the best Thai food in the area is in Chalmette. Commingling with the tire repair shops and Latin grocery stores. Secret Thai Restaurant hides in a little strip mall in a sharp bend of Judge Perez highway. Blink and you might miss it. But don't worry, the name is actually quite ironic, there is no possible way you could miss it. During the day the colorful murals shine like rainbow swirls across the building. At night the neon red signage breathes light like dragon fire into the parking lot.
     The food here is good. Like REALLY good. Let me get that out of the way. It is also cheap. Like REALLY cheap. But I'll get back to that.
     For about ten minutes we scratched our heads and searched our phones trying to decipher the menu. Then threw caution to the wind and ordered half the menu at random. Specifically the words we didn't understand.
     "You want it spicy?" YES MA'AM. We eat it spicy. 
     And so it was. The dishes started rolling out as they were completed. This is family style, so come with friends that don't mind you reaching across the table for another helping. And wear deodorant, because it's about to get sweaty.
     First came the Nom Tok. A funky beef salad pounded in a pungent fish sauce/lime juice slurrie so good you could drink it on its own. Red hot chili's cling to the beef. Smoky, toasted rice powder brings depth. Fresh cilantro and mint brighten it all up. Served with a wedge of cabbage that we rolled the beef into and moaned in satisfaction between crunchy bites.
     A plate of Pad Woon Sen tasted clean and healthy with fresh hunks of tomatoes, carrots, cabbage, and mushrooms stir fried up with chewy, clear glass noodles. 
    Pork Larb was similar to the Nom Tok, but the sweetness of the crumbled pork made this one of our favorite bites. If you are unsure what to order, the Laarb is a GREAT place to start.
     Massive bowls of Khao Soi came next. Sweet curried coconut broth packed with turmeric yellow chicken thighs and spicy chili's. This bowl of noodles could easily feed two people. Maybe three. There seriously seemed to be a pound of chewy egg noodles in this bowl, and we struggled to pass it around the table it was so heavy.
    Wide drunken noodles tossed with vegetables and chicken was refreshing after the richness of the Khao Soi. And the noodles tasted like they were possibly freshly made. They were wide, chewy, and the silky sauce clung to them perfectly.
     A green papaya Som Tam salad came last. We thought it would be a refreshing end to the meal. It was the exact opposite. It was scorching hot with Thai chili's. But in that kind of way where you keep going back for more. Sweating, I pulled out the tiny crabs that give the Som Tam it's lovely fishy flavor behind the heat and started sucking the juice out of them. The papaya was crunchy and little green beans covered in smashed garlic were packed with more flavor than a green bean should ever have.
     Most of these dishes hover at $12 bucks or less. Eight massive plates of amazing food shared between six people provided plenty of leftovers to take home. And the bill landed at $100 bucks. This is absolutely mind boggling for the amount and quality of the food.
     My only other advice? Go with the flow at Secret Thai. There are just a couple of ladies back there producing every dish from scratch. This isn't fast food and it isn't "your way." You get it how they have made it their entire lives and you should consider yourself lucky to be in the position to enjoy it. Our meal clocked in at just around two hours. And what a glorious two hours of eating it was!
name: Skillet

The owner/ Head chef happened to be in the restaurant on the day I came and she came to my table and we chatted for a few very pleasant lady and beautiful if I may add. This was the best food I had while in Naw'lin. Come early to beat the crowd. I was the first customer on 8/14/2019

text:
I haven't had a Wawa hoagie in years and for whatever reason, yesterday I needed to have one. Maybe it was a subliminal message in their Hoagiefest commercials?!?

The parking lot for this location isn't very large but I went early (11:30) so there were lots of spots available. The interior is clean and there are large TV screens above the food prep area showcasing all of their current promotions and new products to try.

I ordered a shortie hoagie with Turkey, pepper jack cheese, LT, hot peppers, and oil. It was $4 during hoagiefest. The cashier that helped me was very enthusiastic about Wawa products. She vouched that this would be the best hoagie ever. Soon after I paid, my hoagie was ready. My sandwich had everything that I asked for on it and the taste was good for a Wawa hoagie.

I would recommend this location for convenience and cleanliness. Just be sure to get there early if you're driving so you can get a spot!
name: Nicole

text: Yum!! The Gluten free pizza was awesome! I recommend the cheese curls too. They are killer and the sauce for dipping makes it even better! Figure out what you want to order before you sit down because the wait can be kind of long for the pizza.
name: Maggie

text: Just tried this place. Ordered palak paneer and paneer tikka masala with rice and naan, two of each. My partner likes things spicy and me not so much so asked to make one mild and one spicy. Azaad Foods accommodated and it was delicious. Not the best I've had but hey...I come from Jersey City where the food in little India is top notch. I would definitely order here again and will try some apps with chutney next time.

Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. text:

The restaurant seemed short staffed. We were done eating and wanted to pay and leave, but another table kept sending our waitress back with their drinks, so we had to wait.

text:
I love Chopt in Brentwood, Tennessee! I've been here a few times and I've tried a few different salad combos - my favorite is the Mexican Caesar salad. In addition to the ingredients it comes with, I add avocado and cucumbers, and for my dressing I use a mix of the Mexican Caesar dressing and the Mexican Goddess dressing (I think that's what they're called). Each salad comes with a fresh piece of bread, and while their fountain drinks are limited to teas and lemonade, I find the hibiscus tea mixed with lemonade plus a few slices of lemon to be the perfect drink combo here. 

Overall, I am so happy to see that a place like this exists in the Nashville area - it's better than a lot of other salad places I've been to in Dallas and NYC. I really hope they succeed and stay - it's so refreshing to have a place that primarily focuses on making great salads and wraps. I highly recommend you give Chopt a shot if you're looking for a healthy, fresh salad!
name: Monica

text: Ordered pickup for our office.  It was prepared quickly and right when they said it would be.  The food was delicious and all of m coworkers asked where I got lunch from.  Great food. Great price. Right on time.

text:
Its a great location, right next to the beach.  No view of the beach but you can easily go for a walk after your meal and explore the beach area.  Its not to far from the public garage either.  The place does a lot of fajitas so it may have a strong food smell inside fyi.  They have lots of outdoor seating as well.

text:
I wish I had a better first time experience here :( my husband has been wanting to try this place for the longest. His birthday was Sunday, so I gathered all our family to come here for his birthday dinner. 

When we first got there we were seated right away at our table. The server came over and greeted us and got our drink order. Right off the bat - things were bad :( there wasn't anyone behind the bar making drinks, so the servers were handling their tables and normal drinks along with making any alcoholic drinks. I did feel bad for her because it seemed like a lot for her to handle our party plus all the drinks. 

After she brought our drinks I immediately ordered an appetizer of bread baskets and my husband ordered some empanadas. Our empanadas were delicious and came out quick. However, the server never asked if anyone wanted to order any appetizers and the bread basket - never came until our dinner and it was because I asked another server why the status was. We had 3 kids, one is a 1 year old and we needed something for him to snack on, so not having the bread out when we asked caused a bit of a problem.

The delivery on the entrees was horrible. Half of the table got their food while the other side had nothing. Never ever in a restaurant with a big party do you bring only some of the people's food out. Meanwhile, we ordered a kids meal - which they only option they have is chicken fingers and fries and it was not good at all. Finally after ten minutes of the first group of entrees being brought out the rest of us got our food. Mind you 2 of us ordered a salad with our dinner and asked for it to come out first and it didn't. 

When it came time to check out - our checks were all mixed up. At this point we were all so frustrated, we just paid and left and they also automatically put a 18% tip on parties of 6 or more even if everyone is separate checks. 

I am so disappointed to leave this review, because I have heard nothing but great things about this place and we did not have a good experience and what is more upsetting is that it was for my husbands birthday :(
name: Chelsea

text: LOVED IT! Walked over after bike riding in City Park and it was certainty a treat! We sat outside overlooking the cool Katie's mural across the street. The debris fries were so BOMB! I had The Legend, which went amazingly with the fries. All of the people we came into contact with were super friendly and nice. Even the armed guard was attentive! He was like- it looks like you need a bag for your leftovers! I was impressed! We will definitely be back!! It's no wonder it was voted BEST NEIGHBORHOOD RESTAURANT!
name: Liliane

text:
Let me first say that I have eaten at the RTM location on several occasions; and I profess my love for the roast pork w/ broccoli rabe and sharp provolone. It's the best...the gold standard that I judge other roast pork sandwiches against.

That being said. I was a bit concerned when I walked into the Montgomeryville location on 1/25/2018 at approximately 3:00 pm. The place was completely empty. Not one customer. 

After waiting for a few minutes at the counter, a young gentleman who was in the back of the room had visually indicated that someone would be out soon. 

Big Hoss came out of the back and put on his apron and asked me for my order. The phone then rang and Hoss started taking and answering questions for a catering order from the caller. Not a big deal. He finally told the caller to hold on because he had to make a sandwich (for me); nice, right?

So, I'll take the roast pork w/ sharp provolone and broccoli rabe and also a side of long hots and roasted peppers. I was sharing a half sandwich with a friend from out of town.

The rule of thumb...you always eat w/ your eyes first!

I watched Big Hoss sift through the pork/au jus in the bain marie with a contraption and pull up bits from the bottom. No sliced roasted pork...Just the bits left over from the lunch crowd (hmm?).

I will say the taste of the small bits w/ the sharp provolone on my roll was decent, but I would have preferred some sliced pork to take it to the next level. Unfortunately the broccoli rabe looked pretty sad. I also observed broccoli rabe that was taken out of it's hot container and left on the counter because it was heated too long.

All in all. I will come back for a second visit. This time I will come earlier. Perhaps at lunch time to see if there is a difference.

Thank you. And YELP on!

John W.
name: John

text: Not really a bagel house but a convenience store with a small kitchen to order bagels and other sandwiches. Bagels of very poor quality, stale, dry, no flavour. Only a small strip to sit down & eat. No bathroom, dirty store, smells. Just lousy. PASS!

Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. A very pleasant experience. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. They were out of one thing I originally wanted..

text: My second trip here, updating my review. On my first trip I used the drive through and regretted it. My server, Alliyah, was awesome. Per her suggestion, I chose the half rack ribs combo (both dry rub and bbq), collard greens and corn on the cob. The corn was amazing! I loved it the first time too but it's even better when hot. Comes with corn bread-- nice surprise on the added jalapeno & corn. Collard greens were nicely done with bacon, but I'd never had them before and wasn't a fan. Alicia offered me the potato casserole instead--yummy! Ribs were very good. I preferred the bbq to the dry rub. No worries, 3 kinds of sauces on the table including the original that is on the other half of the ribs. I'll be back!

text: The food was good and the service was easygoing. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer..

They can be understaffed as well, which leads to lengthy waits in service times and different people coming to take the order. Tonight, we asked for a condiment and the server never returned. text: I would like to state that I have been going to this restaurant for about 8 years and have always loved and recommended it. We loved this place and for several visits tried to deny that there have been some issues. I have always ordered the mussels and had a great experience there before. text:
We decided to visit Taste of Dubai after my partner spotted a particularly delicious-looking platter of grilled meats on social media that included lamb.  We are obsessed with seeking out and sampling different international lamb dishes around town.  Taste of Dubai is described as an Emirati restaurant by the International Marketplace coalition, as in the United Arab Emirates (which contains many different Middle Eastern and Asian cuisines...thanks Wiki).  The restaurant was easy to find, in the middle of the small shopping strip behind Saigon off of 38th street.  We arrived a little after 5PM on a Saturday and had our choice of tables (including tables/chairs or floor seating).  We sat in one of the few more private tables with curtains which provided a more intimate experience.  Our friendly server immediately brought us complimentary servings of hot spiced coffee, which was the perfect touch with the cooler weather. She was also very willing to explain any parts of the menu we were unsure about...but we were already on a mission to obtain all the lamb and other grilled spiced meats.

For parties of 2-4, I highly recommend ordering the Mixed Platter option (#16 for $28.99).  We received an enormous platter of fragrant biryani rice, pickle, roasted shallot & tomato, and a wide selection of grilled meats and kebobs, including:  sharwarma, lamb-beef and chicken kofta meatballs, lamb and chicken shish kebab, and shish taook (chicken). The lamb meat options were my favorite; so savory and uniquely flavored, especially when dipped in the accompanying addictive yogurt sauce.  I was also impressed with the chicken offerings; the chicken shish kebab was similar to tandoori in appearance, but was not dry and had a lovely cardamom aftertaste.  I could taste cardamom and other wonderful warming spices in almost every dish.  

We rounded out our mixed platter with the fattoush salad and another appetizer consisting of...shocker...more lamb.  We selected the lamb saltah stew, which was a sizzling hot bowl of shredded lamb "sauce" and veggies; we asked for it "hot" and could see lots of green peppers added in.  The saltah also had a complex flavor. You can use the accompanying bread to maneuver the hot lamb saltah mix into your mouth...just allow it to cool a bit first, as I burned the roof of my mouth from being over-eager to try it.  The fattoush salad provided a nice veggie, cooling balance to the meat-centered meal.  The bread part of the fattoush salad was fried, crispy pita chips and a generous sprinkling of sumac powder offer its signature sour taste that complimented the salad's lemon dressing.

I was definitely interested in the kunafah dessert, as fried cheese pastry, rose water, and pistachios sounded perfect to me...but alas, we were stuffed (maybe next time).  I did enjoy the adani spiced tea with sweetened milk, which was almost dessert-like.  It was served steaming hot in a stryrofoam cup and I took most of it to go. Be careful about the bottom of your tea cup, as I may have ingested some tea leaves and spice debris when greedily trying to drink every last drop of the tea. 

I highly recommend visiting Taste of Dubai as the service and food were excellent.  The prices are also reasonable, given the large portions and high quality of food that is offered. I thought the Emirati and Middle Eastern flavors and spices were great and the dishes much more flavorful than the kebabs and similar dishes you find at  Mediterranean-style places. I can't wait to go back and try out the mint lemonade, a piece of kunafah...and more lamb!

The skimmer was found on Thursday, June 20 at the store at 1780 Sumneytown Pike. 

It was located inside the self-checkout register. The suspect took extra care to include a Royal Farms sticker on the shell of the skimmer. 

Police said it is not known when the skimmer was placed on the register. 

The good news: the WiFi signal was not working when police recovered the skimmer, and no victims have yet been identified. 

Residents who may have visited the store should check their bank statements for suspicious activity.

text:
Making the world a better place, one eggs benny at a time.

As we were making our way there, I used the Yelp live waiting list to put our names down. Just had to wait 10 minutes after getting there. It was quite the popular joint that morning. 

They have many locations, but this one was closest to where we were going. I'm assuming this is one of their newer locations given the drastically lower number of Yelp reviews.

We both got the peacemaker, an option that allows you to mix and match from two different kinds of egg bennies. My favorite was definitely the eggs cochon, which is like a buttery braised pork topping. We also tried the Chicken St. Charles (the classic fried chicken on an eggs benny), shrimp boogaloo (shrimp in a salsa like sauce), and the corned beef (corned beef is corned beef).

We also threw in a creamy vanilla spiced latte that was just a little too sweet for my liking.

I didn't think eggs benedict would be so filling, but I definitely walked out stuffed. Highly recommend this place for a nice brunch!

I almost don't know where to begin...but let's start with the extraordinarily long line-it's Essence Fest so I get it, lines are everywhere.   But we were 7th on the wait list and waited over 2 hours.  We watch while "celebrities-not" breezed in from off the streets to be seated in front of myself and other paying customers who also had been waiting for HOURS for what would be a mediocre meal.  

We were told that the "owner was hosting them at his private table."  Problem is the place has 20 tables and a bar so if the owner wanted to pay for or host "celebrities"  -he/she should've closed for the day.  It's called, "closed for a private event." And then I get inside and order and wait, and wait, and wait another hour before food finally arrives.  My sweet potato pancakes were dense-not moist or fluffy and my spinach and feta omelette was unseasoned and light on the feta. Everything was warm-not hot, not cold-just warm.  Did someone forget to grab from the window on time for a hot plate to arrive to my table?  It wasn't just me though the salmon, bananas foster, and shrimp and grits that my friends ordered all arrived warm.  The grits are dense and bland and not at all cheesy-really.

Once half of our order arrived the waitresses disappeared and we were hunting folks down to ask for silverware hot sauce and syrup.  Wait staff seemed uninterested in our polite feedback and dismissive.  

This is a new restaurant trying to make a good name but it left a bad taste.  I will not recommend and will not be back.

Since we visited during low season, there was no wait for a table. Service though was a little awkward and staff definitely need a lot more training.
