text:
When everyone knows it's good, why bother? Because it's SO DAMN GOOD. This place has been here forever, and there's a reason for that.

The BBQ oysters were insane. A neighboring diner recommended them, and I almost insisted on raw. Thank goodness we listened. Yum and yum and yum. Just a little parmesan on top of a whole lot of delicious.

Fried chicken with red beans and rice. Again, who needs to be told, but sweet Jesus they were good! Big Fredia called them creamy and she didn't lie. Nobody will best it.

BBQ shrimp! Huge! Plentiful! Fresh as you can find them! Amazing.

Mix that with some laughs, colorful patrons and lively atmosphere, then wash it all down with fair prices and a coupla cold Dixies and you KNOW you've been in New Orleans. Some things never get old.
name: G

text: I was a bit disappointed in the quality of the food when I ate at this restaurant, given the high ratings on the web. We ordered the bacon wrapped dates to start out. This dish was basically all bacon with a very tiny resemblance of a date inside. My mom didn't finish this dish. Perhaps some people like all bacon with essentially no date. But this should be noted by the server. We also ordered a Carmelized eggplant appetizer. It left more to be desired. Was just average. We finished with a field green salad given that none of the tapas were tasty, which was good. Overall, I expected much more from this restaurant. It was just average maybe a bit below for a tapas restaurant in terms of food. The nice ambiance with live music elevates it to an average tapas restaurant rating.

text:
I went here on a Saturday night, and it was lively. BUT, the whole set-up/layout of the building is awful. I​ and my friends were dancing and we kept getting shoved/bumped into by staff. We weren't even standing near their kitchen or anything. We bought shots at the bar that were totally OVERPRICED and not even that good. And the cover charge was the worst part. I had to pay $5 just to experience this awful place?! I still prefer Sharkey's over this place.

1/10, won't recommend.

name: Nick

text:
Lebanon's Cafe IS excellent, but I do have some recommendations for a smoother experience since today was a bit far from it.

Because they don't have a hostess table to get you a seat, if its a busy restaurant day (like during the lunch crowd), when you seat yourselves, oftentimes you get overlooked for quite a while. Also, for a packed lunch today inside the restaurant and out, they only had like 2 servers working it seemed, and the one handling outside AND some inside seemed incredibly frazzled and rushed every time she saw us, which caused some major confusion when she gave us the bill and it was the one for a different table and incorrect, but then when she split it it was way more than it should have been? Perhaps someone called in sick last minute and this isn't the usual case, but if it IS the usual, I think they need to invest in a little more help during the lunch crowd.

The Lebanese tea is excellent, albeit pricey at $2.75 and their gyro lunch plate is $12.99 and comes with hummos/hummus & salad (and you can add feta for $1). The location is excellent, sitting right on Carrollton Ave. and that probably raises the food prices a bit. Just after how hectic it was today, and I did tip 20%, I just can't justify spending $40 for service that is okay at best and your typical Greek/Lebanese food. I'll definitely come back to give them a second chance, but I really prefer Albashas & Pyramids to Lebanon's in terms of service, quality & food!
name: Elizabeth

text: Submitted an order online and went to pick up and the location was closed. No indication online or at the location they would be closed today. May change the review once a refund is processed.

text: We came here on a Friday night, as our first option had a long wait. When we entered, the place was practically empty, that should have been a giveaway of how our experience was going to be. Finally, when our waiter came, we order our drinks , I got The Havana, and my two friends ordered Aloha traveler, 5 minutes later we find out they are all put of it, so they got leininkugel shandy. We ordered the crispy brussel sprouts which come with pork belly meat, the picture on the menu looked appetizing, but it was the complete opposite when it came. The plate looked like we got leftovers of what someone else didn't finish, the dish altogether was very bland. For our entrees we ordered the Bacon mac Burger, which the mac and cheese had a rubber consistency, and my friends got the Farmhouse Burger and the Bison Burger, which they barely finished.  I definitely would not come back here again, and regret that we did not wait at the first option ( it would have been worth it)

I can go to other bakeries that don't have bad days at a much cheaper price point. The cupcakes are the only thing reasonably priced, so maybe they just don't put the same effort into the cupcakes.

text:
Great potential as a BBQ restaurant. First off, the food was superb. We ordered the BBQ sampler platter, full rack of ribs, chili, macaroni and cheese, etc. We liked everything we ordered. The chili was surprisingly good. Well done and I consider myself a bit of a chili connoisseur. Why the three star review then? The service.

This restaurant could have easily gotten 4 or even 5 star if the service was bare minimum decent. First of all, the hostess appeared confused and overwhelmed when dealing with multiple parties. She came off as rude as she refused very reasonable requests like our desire to sit inside versus outside even as the restaurant was half empty when we walked in. We sat outside as our fears of being swarmed with insects were realized. The waitress was pleasant but neglected to bring us bread for the table when every other table around us got a basket of bread. Weird.

I really hope management reads this review, rewards the kitchen staff that prepared the delicious BBQ that almost made up for the lackadaisical dining experience and reviews basic hospitality skills with front office staff.
name: Mr.

text:

text: My roommate told me this place opened up in Lakeview which is close to where we live.  I got off of work and was looking forward to eating a good poke bowl and thought I would give this place a shot. It turned out to be my first mistake. There was literally no one when I walked in. The place looks very presentable and is very nice looking.  It was very clean and modern inside. I had high expectations. I order a custom bowl with brown rice/spring mix, with my 3 protein choices being  spicy tuna, yellow tail and crawfish.  I had it with a Lime Sriracha  sauce with all the veggies and chili sauce with the ponzu sauce mixed in. My second mistake was not eating the bowl inside.  I took it to go.  I certainly would have mentioned to them the issue I had which brings me to my next complaint. The rice on first bite looked odd, like it either was undercooked or too cooked to the point it was dried out.  I suspect they didn't add enough water for the brown rice.  It was practically inedible.  I couldn't chew it it was so hard.  Imagine chewing rice that has the consistency of a hard seed.  That was my experience.  It was terrible.  The proteins look low grade, especially the yellow fin.  I will never go back and I don't recommend anyone else does either.  If you want good poke in the Lakeview/Metairie area just make the drive to Poke Loa or to Lemon Shark.  It is worth it, trust me.  The other reviewers who complained about the rice are telling the truth.  If I could give this place zero stars I would.
name: Jobe

text: The photos made it look a little better than it actually was. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. It was crowded but still moved along. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Maybe better dine-in than delivery, hard to tell.
name: User

text:
If you are traveling through philly and need a place that both feels like a neighborhood bar and has the
Word of mouth to ward off disappointment, this is the place for you. Open up the beer bible and you will
Know what I mean. This place has a beer for you. And even better, a beer you didn't know was for you.
name: Elianne

text: Nasty employees, ok food... If it's actually the right order. They actually accused me of lying because they got the order wrong! Totally disrespectful! STAY AWAY!
name: Bryan

text: Amazing food!! The taste of New Orleans and Oysters were delicious!! Their shrimp creole was the best and left you wanting more!! We sat outside by the fountain and it was so nice !
name: Natalia

text: Food is very inconsistent. Sometimes good, sometimes bad. Sometimes made differently than last week , sometimes entirely different chicken fingers, etc. Continually seeing different employees and it appears that management offers zero training to the new employees. Drinks are inconsistent. They also continually run out of certain beers and liquors. No one knows WiFi passwords. Heating Or AC controls, how to change the channels, etc. It's just awful right now.
name: Michael

text: Awesome and unique coffee spot, great atmosphere and one of the best almond milk lattes I've had! Paired it with the Cuban cheese toast, can't get much better than that :)
name: Alexandra

text:
Vessel

The embodiment of love, beauty, grace, and fine dining. It's located in an old 1914 Lutheran Church.  Simply gorgeous, dark wood, high ceilings, and stained windows.  

I favored this beautiful place a few times during lunch.  I thought, what would the Vessel Dining Experience be like at night?  

A girlfriend traveled with me on this trip.  She's a newbie to New Orleans.  So imagine her facial expression with a smile when we drove up to the Vessel, "it's a church, it's a restaurant?"  She was like really, is this it, no, really...

We were frozen in our tracks, admiring the outside. Remember, I have never eaten here at night.  It's dark, and these lights are cast upon a white church, which is the Vessel!

My friend was in love with the inside.  The dinner menu is the top of the cake!  It's awesome with a great selection for all kinds of palates.  Can't go wrong here!  The wine menu was impressive too.  

We had a fabulous night, the atmosphere was relaxing, the wine good and food excellent!
name: Tracey

text: Viva Cuba! - Cuba lives in between the walls of Manolito --  if you are fortunate enough to find this little gem in the French Quarter, you are muy suerte indeed. I know Manolito is in the Quarter, but I promise you, it's not a tourist trap. In fact, it's anything but. Konrad, Maggie, Josephine and company represent the absolute best of southern hospitality and are seriously some of the most talented bartenders in the city. The mojitos and hand-shaken daiquiris do not "rival" those in Cuba and Floridita, they surpass them - you will not find better in New Orleans.  And let's talk about that Cuban sandwich. Y'all... It. Is. Everything. I cannot say enough about the charm of Manolito, other than that I feel all sorts of happy that I live close enough to this darling little spot to call myself a regular.
name: Amanda

text:
Overall a great experience and evening! There were 11 adults and 8 kids in our party. The staff accommodated us well and took great care of us all.  We enjoyed various dishes from burgers to breakfast, pot roast to chicken fried steak. 
Also a big shout out to ELIZABETH for diligently treating us so well, and also Vanessa who served with a smile, too! 
Delicious food and terrific service and staff!!
Will definitely be back
name: Melani

text: Absolutely awful. Don't advertise a shamrock shake then fail to maintain your shake machine. Lazy staff, long lines.
name: Todd

text:
After a friend recommended FWJ I had to try it. I'm so glad I did. 

Another friend and I shared the Croque Monsieur, Country Crepe and Nutella Crepe. Everything was delicious. 

The pastry case was very hard to pass up on this visit. So many delicious looking creations.  Next time for sure!
name: Stephanie

text: Slow service. They do offer some vegetarian options and a full bar. All fried food. Said vegan options but nothing was vegan on the menu. Had to get menu ourselves and ask for service twice. Seat yourself and cafeteria style seating.
name: Jordan

text: Excellent breakfast. The coffee was hot and very flavorful. Helped warm us up during the cold weather. We walked right in were attended right away. The portion size is huge so I would recommend sharing if you can. My coffee never got to less than half a cup before it was refilled again. I had scrambled eggs, grits with cheese and a pancake. My boyfriend had the French toast. We have no complaints at all.
name: Krystine

text: Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. The food was good and the service was easygoing. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. For the price I expected more than this. No big complaints, just a nice meal.
name: User

text: Mr. Wish has a large menu with many variations of bubble tea and a couple small bites to choose from. They are very well equipped to find something you like, and they are knowledgeable in your craft. The bubbles are cooked better than most places that I've tried. Additionally, there are other types of tapioca pearls and jellies you can try. The price is reasonable, and I would definitely return if I was craving some Bubble Tea. The atmosphere is standard for a bubble tea location, and is fairly bare so you may like to get your drink and enjoy it in a more exciting area. Regardless, they do play the top pop songs if you're into that!
name: Daniel

text: Great outdoor patio dining!  Nice dinner with a nice view on the heated patio looking out at the ocean on a cool night. Enjoyed our rib appetizer, awesome guinzaglio pasta n focaccia with extras. No tiramisu for dessert but the chocolate plate was excellent!  Can't wait to return for happy hour and to try the great looking wood fired pizza our neighbors were having.
name: Marilyn

text: Parking was annoying and I was already in a bad mood by the time I got inside. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. It was crowded but still moved along. Not a bad stop, just not one I'm rushing to repeat. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine..
name: User

text: The food is mostly good, but tonight it took 1 hour 20 minutes for our food to arrive. Large Greek salad was very small, another salad had to be returned because it wasn't prepared to order. This is sfter the one hour 30 minute wait.
name: Sue

text: A delicious spot to visit for great bakery goods and coffee.  You can sit on enjoy your treats, inside or outside, or rush home to devour them in privacy.  There should be a warning sign  on the door as their cookies are very addicting.
name: John

text: We were visiting Cali on winter break. We were craving Nepali food so much that we were so happy we found this place. The chicken Momo was really good and I wish I could make chicken choila as great as them. So yummy, and when we go back to Santa Barbara area we will come back here. Wish we had more Nepali restaurants here in Vegas. Because this place was great!
name: Serine

text: The sauce carried most of the meal. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. It was crowded but still moved along. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. There were a couple things I liked and a couple things I probably wouldn't get again. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced.
name: User

text: Not sure why there are so many good ratings. After some locals suggested this place as "New Mexican", I thought I would give it a try. I really wanted to love this place as it is close to home.....I had the Large Combo with a couple chicken tacos, a enchilada, and a Chill relleno.  I want to say first that the service was mediocre at best. Second, the food was cold. The tacos were so bad, I ate one, and the dog wouldn't eat the other one...and he will eat anything. The relleno was undercooked. The salsa was average, not as hot as people say. I definitely did not taste the Hatch flavor in any way.  I see this place is busy, but I chalk that up to it being the only Mexican place in town, and very close to a retirement home. This place is in a decent location, and I think with a few changes, could be really good. I would improve the service, and retrain the chef.
name: Kevin

text: I am giving them a 5 star review because although they have some kinks to work out, I felt they were trying very hard to accommodate a LOT of people on a busy Friday night. We made a reservation so we had very little wait for our table. The main room was crowded with every table filled. The wait for our drinks, appetizers and main course was long. Having said that, we understood and therefore just enjoyed the company at our table. When the food took too long, the server came out and offered a second round of drinks on the house. That was a simple gesture on their part but made an impression on us. They didn't have to do that. The smoked salmon appetizer on home made chips was excellent. I order the ribeye (and I am fussy about steak) and it was very good and cooked to the temp I requested. My husband had the pork chops and enjoyed them. If I had one suggestion, it would be to do something about the noise. The room needs some sound barriers. The noise level in the room was very loud and it was hard to hear the each other talk. That would not work if you wanted to come here for a romantic evening....Other than that, it was a great night and we are happy to have this new restaurant in the neighborhood and we will be back!
name: Lisa

text: We love this place!  The Best French toast you'll ever have.  It's always a treat to go there.  Service was friendly and prompt.  It's a must if you're staying in clear water beach.
name: Ronald

text: At least qualified as Japanese restaurant. It has both Japanese dishes and American Japanese dishes and most of them tastes ok. Overall, a go to Japanese food in my area considering how terrible are the qualities of Asian restaurants in Tucson.
name: Zichan

text:
This is a very family friendly place which is awesome for me since I have kids :) They have a play area outside at the back if you decide to stay outdoors. They also have a collection of board games for the kids to play indoors.

Inside and out are both beautifully decorated with comfortable and stylish chairs. The scenery is wonderful specially with the sunset at the background. They have a second floor with a nice balcony too where you can sip your wine and just enjoy life :)

The staff are very attentive and friendly. Can't complain about the service. You will smell the good food once you walk inside and it truly is delicious. I'm not a wine pro and I am more into sweeter wines like moscato and riesling which I didn't see in the menu but they have wine slushies on a regular basis I think and they had wine sangria pitchers when I went there the last time so no worries. There are options! There's a few selection of beers too for those who prefer beer instead.

They offer summer concert sessions I think and have several fitness and art classes offered on certain days of the week as well. Check out their website!

I have visited this place when they first opened and again during their one year anniversary and it just keeps getting better. Will for sure come back!
name: Gay

text: Service was nice, kitchen was just moving kind of slow. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. The staff seemed tired but still polite. Maybe better dine-in than delivery, hard to tell. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.
name: User

text:
This is one on the best Taco Bells in the area!! I stop here from time to time when I'm in the city because every time I go, it's on point.

My only gripe is that one time I went and ordered a burrito supreme and its was literally most beans and a lot of them. There was like a small sprinkle of everything else. Otherwise, everything else I've ordered has been properly portioned, hot, and delicious.

Hands down one of the best Taco Bells.
name: Rachie

text:
Chihuahua's came high recommend to us, so we tried it out, I had a wet chimmichanga, it was a bit on the small side compared to other chimichangas, I have had.  The red enchilada sauce was amazing, it had this real Chile flavor and it was thick and covered the chimichanga.

The red sauce was so good my wife asked for some to dip her Taquitos in and yes, she really enjoyed the red enchilada sauce too.

The chips were crispy and the salsa was fresh and tasted good.  The knock is the portion of the amount of food on each plate and the service was marginal at best.  Server really did not know the menu and we had to ask for more salsa, more sauce, more water, more chips, more drinks, they never asked us if they could get us more of anything we had to do the asking and the place was not busy at all, one party outside and a table by the bar and us...........  Real lousy bus service.

The food was good enough to try again in a couple months, hopefully the service will improve there is way too many Mexican restaurants in  the Reno/Sparks area to pick from.......
name: Mark

text: Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. No big complaints, just a nice meal. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Nice little spot, decent portions too. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Not bad for a quick meal.
name: User

text: My rating is no stars because of the discrimination I've experienced. I've experienced one of worst costumer service by the manager/bar tender at this bar, Kylie. Do not go to this restaurant and bar unless you want to get discriminated and treated like less then a human being.
name: Breanna

text: Would prob stop in again if nearby. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. It looked better online than it did in person. For a busy night they handled it okay. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Nice little spot, decent portions too. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. The whole meal felt kind of uneven.
name: User

text: If you love high prices ! If you Love cigar smoke blown in your face while you are eating..  if you love average service ( can't blame the help ). You will LOVE this place !!     Cheers !
name: Mike

text: A legit place for sandwiches and more!!! Hoagies take me back to childhood, freshly sliced and prepared ingredients.
name: Steven

text:
Mr. Toro has a great selection of meats (cooked and raw, marinated or not) and sides, as well as produce, drinks and canned goods. The prices are very competitive!

Also, they are very generous with samples (they gave my wife half an order of ceviche to try after I pointed out they carried it. 

They also have seating if you want to dine in! 

Do yourself a favor and try it out!
name: Dustin

text: Carne ottima. Servizio veloce ed educato. Quando siamo stati, era sovraffollato perché era il giorno delle graduation. Caro, ma si concilia con la qualità del cibo, vino e servizio.
name: Giuseppe

text:
Amazing biscuits like no other breakfast spot could offer. Unique and 
delicious with a bit of spice.  Bourbon maple syrup is off the charts. Take some home as well. Coming back soon! Not a meal but an experience!
name: Howard

text: Very friendly, but the employees are too quick to listen to the orders.   Not a big deal, but a bit expensive.   Fresh and tasty, as well as clean.  Good sandwiches, and we go here about every other month.   Try it!
name: R

text: I love this spot. After 3 different positive experiences here, it is safe to say the tap room is great! Recently, I had the vegetarian cheese steak. The veggies were fresh and the roll was so good. Their dry cider selection is always great. My fiancé got the Monte cristo and also loved it. We will definitely be back.
name: Amanda

text: Not sure why this place has such split reviews, but my experience was mostly fine. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. For a busy night they handled it okay. I'd maybe go back, but I'd order differently next time. Not bad for a quick meal. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. Ordered a few things and liked most of it.
name: User

text:
Placed an order for our office online.  Website does not allow for special instructions i.e. lite beans, sauce on the side etc... We put names with each item ordered.  Nothing was identified in the bags and it all looked the same.  The person making quesadillas either they have never made a quesadilla before or they need more training.   The flavor is good but ordering process and presentation need work.
Much better when ordering in person.
name: Laurie

text:
This place was so good it was life changing.

We went for lunch and each got drinks, classic caiparinha for me and pineapple cilantro marg for wife. Both delicious, strong, but balanced. 

We started with yuca frita based on a recommendation and enjoyed it a lot. But the arepas stole the show. Amazing, super filling, meaty cheesy with a perfect level of acidity and deliciousness. 

The service was great: good recommendations, good descriptions, water always filled, but not too hands on. 

Very happy, wish i was local. Go here!
name: Bill

text: Great fried oyster po-boy! Imported gulf oysters and Leidenheimer French bread. Chef is from New Orleans. I seldom eat Cajun when away from home (NOLA) but this place does it right. Also love the bacon grease popcorn.
name: Jerome

text: Friendly staff, great service, delicious food, $1 taco specials on certain week days, amazing salsa bar. Highly recommend!
name: Rachel

text:
The Western Village Casino may not look attractive from the outside, the hotel looks dumpy, the casino decorated like it's sister - the Peppermill, however, the Steak House is a very pleasant surprise!

Excellent fine dining service at reasonable prices. We had Salad, a Rhubarb Sorbet with Champagne Topper, Lamb Chops (2 large encrusted chops with a mint gravy dipping sauce) Macadamia Nut Encrusted Sea Bass, and Bananas Foster - flamed at your table!  There are not many places that will flambé adjacent to the table (not even some cruise lines).  The Waiter rolls out the flambé cart (they also do Cherries Jubilee and Strawberry Romanov) and prepares the dish next to your table.  Minimum order of two for any of the flambes - well worth it for this grand dessert and accompanying flambé show!

Since it was our anniversary, we received complimentary pictures, complimentary cheesecake dessert with an anniversary candle, and dark chocolate cookies with white chocolate chips.  So nice.  Service was excellent and reservations are a must!
name: Scott

text: This is a nice little place to get lunch. The service is friendly and fast, and the ambiance is modern but cozy. I felt a little adventurous today, so I ordered the Bun Bo Hue, as recommended by a fellow reviewer. I really love spicy dishes, so this was a good pick. My only problem with the soup was the beef with tendon. I LOVE soft, silky, gelatinous tendon, but these bits were hard and chewy. I felt bad that I couldn't eat it, but the texture was really throwing me off. The congealed pork blood, for those freaked out by the idea, was similar in taste to liver, but not as gamey, and the texture is very similar to tofu. So, if you like liver,  you shouldn't have an issue with it. The noodles were larger and easier to eat than the thin vermicelli noodles. The broth was VERY flavorful. The shrimp and pepper pastes were very good, but I didn't need to add any. The broth was already fairly salty.
name: Jessica

text: Absolutely one of the dirtiest restaurants I've been to. If it hadn't been so late and we were not pressed for time, we would have gone elsewhere. Trash bins were full with boxes stacked on top. The floor was littered with trash and pizza sauce.
name: T

text:
Greasy spoon hole in the wall that is cheap and open 24/7 to help soak up all the booze one consumes on Bourbon Street.

Pretty much the only true diner in the area. Since 1939, and looks the part. Small and gritty with a nice/patient/understanding staff, this is the kind of joint you roll into during the wee hours of the morning in a drunken drooling stupor to order up some breakfast, a greasy burger, coffee, and some tater tots to recover.

I enjoy these kinds of places. A piece of Americana from simpler times.

Small spot with a few tables and some counter seating. The grill is right in front so you will be covered in the smokiness of the food being fried up. It at once smells a bit off-putting and amazing at the same time. Like you need to be here. Like you need to walk out smelling like week old fried food. Take in the aroma in all it's glory. Breathe in deeply. 

As for the food? Actually not too shabby, just don't expect a gourmet experience. It's down and dirty diner eats in it's most simplistic form. Our breakfasts and coffee were decent enough and did the trick. Sent us back on our way for more debauchery on Bourbon Street. 

Also, read the menu closely. There are some funny one-liners written throughout it in between the food listings.
name: Phil

text: Great new McDonald's . The open concept where you can see the kitchen in the front is nice to see . Clean place and friendly staff . Every time I have stopped by with my family we have been happy with everything we have purchased . Will keep going here .
name: Shaun

text: Goodness - now that was delicious.  It was our first time and we had the best waitress to help us navigate the expansive menu.  Nearly everything is made from scratch.  They smoke their meats on premise.  The restaurant is low key, the service fast and efficient.  We went with Benedict's and started with an incredible Snickerdoodle pancake as an 'appetizer.'   We will be full for days!
name: Beth

text: So this is a solid breakfast choice that didn't show up in my search right away.  I'm glad it is here.  It is right across the street from the Hilton Garden Inn.  Breakfast is all day.  It was reasonably priced and clean.  The omelet, the waffle, and the poached egg all were great.
name: Michael

text:
This was a great spot! I met up with a friend here who had already been waiting for me to arrive for a while. Drinks, chips, and guacamole arrived around the time I sat down, so from my perspective the service was fast and courteous, but apparently my friend felt that the waiter hadn't been attentive with bringing drinks and appetizers, so perhaps I just happened to arrive at the perfect time. The place was very busy though, so some amount of delay I think has to be expected!

The chips and guacamole were fine; not particularly incredible but they certainly got the job done. A second disappointment was the original menu item I ordered, a fancy quesadilla, involved ground beef, but the waiter told me that they had run out of ground beef that evening. He offered to sub in chicken instead, which probably would have been just fine, but instead I decided to change tactics entirely and go with the "BBQ Chicken Burrito."

Who knows what life would have been like if I had gotten to enjoy that quesadilla, but I can say with certainty that the life I'm currently living having had the opportunity to enjoy the BBQ Chicken Burrito is quite the nice life indeed. It was really delicious; I was a little afraid that the BBQ sauce would be overpowering, but my fears were unfounded. The sauce didn't necessarily feel like BBQ, and instead was more like a slightly sweeter/slightly smokier enchilada sauce. It was great. And the burrito itself was lovely too. I probably should have taken half of it home, but once I started eating I couldn't help myself and kept going until I cleaned my plate.

So yes! A fun little place!
name: Ben

text:
There's usually not much special about a wing spot with beer and a few TVs, but I'd say this one stands out as far as food quality and location. 

The wings were delicious and made to order. I got the salt and vinegar dry rub with Asian zing and spicy garlic sauces for dipping. I prefer to dip my wings as opposed to them covered in sauce that I may not like. It's an additional .60 cents for each small condiment cup of sauce. The wings were cooked perfectly and not dried out or too hard. They also granted my request for all drums. 

The only negative is that the menu is vague and instead of them saying that the traditional wings come in a 5, 10, 15 or 20 piece, they'd rather give these ambiguous names like "snack" and "small" to infer wing amounts. It's ridiculous. The food took a little longer than expected to come out, but it wasn't long enough to cause a fuss. Also, I'd like to see a couple more options for people who don't want fried, greasy, starchy sides. But if you don't mind that, the potato wedges are pretty good and taste homemade. 

The service was good, but then again I came on a cold, Sunday night and the place was empty.  I couldn't speak on a day where it was packed. All in all, if you're in Ybor and want something other than pizza, I'd say this is definitely worth a try.
name: Phalan

text: One star for bad service, food is good. Make sure you are dressed to impress or you will be ignored. Embarrassed to have brought a friend visiting here from DC. Bartender rude & dismissive, wait staff unprofessional "I had to come in on my day off." Price not worth the attitude
name: Melanie

text:
Let me start by saying this review has nothing to do with the food because everyone knows miyako hibachi is amazing. But, the customer service I experienced when I came here was very disheartening. I came here with a group of friends for a birthday celebration. We had reservations for 8:00pm. When we arrived the hostess took about 15 minutes to even acknowledge us but then told us it would be a 30 minute wait. We were confused because we had a reservation but the hostess was trying to avoid giving us a reason. An HOUR passes and we are still WAITING to be seated for a RESERVATION. At this point we are beyond irritated. The reservation is for 15 but they seated us at a table that only had room for 12 and then said that the chef could not make any more meals than 12. So basically the 3 people who couldn't fit would just be out of luck. The hostess then mentions that the only room that would even fit 15 guests is an additional charge and it was already occupied. We are VERY confused because there was a reservation for 15 and this was never mentioned during the booking. Fast forward, 3 guests decided to just be team players and go sit at a separate table (where they were told they couldn't order any hibachi) but they were never serviced so they ended up just leaving. The hostess was not apologetic and couldn't explain why these issues were not brought up when the reservation was originally booked. Very disappointed and won't be returning.


Also, there was no bartender working so we sat in the lobby irritated and sober until we were able to flag down a staff member who was trying to avoid eye contact to make us drinks. Deep sigh.
name: Victoria

text: Saturday morning and was told the wait was 45-an hour. After being seated, we immediately ordered and still the food took a long time. I think they were short staffed in the kitchen. The waiter was super friendly and attentive though. I got the eggs Benedict and I was highly disappointed. Lacked so much flavor and I don't believe there was any hollandaise sauce which I've never encountered that before. I ate it because I was super hungry but I wouldn't recommend. Almost like I could've made myself tbh.
name: Maggie

text:
This place was amazing! I got the shrimp and grits and it was absolutely delicious! The flavors were all there with the briny shrimp and buttery grits. I also tasted two other dishes from my friends and both were just as tasty, so it's not a fluke.

Great decor and ambiance, and service was top notch for such a busy brunch time. Can't wait to return if I ever get a chance!
name: Tori

text: It looked better online than it did in person. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. The wait felt longer than it should have. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Just not for me. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. It looked better online than it did in person.
name: User

text:
Nice environment, tasty food. Service can be better for this kind of restaurant. 
We were here for New Year celebration. 
A restaurant practically closed its doors at 11 pm, no countdown,no happy New Year. Being out of town and middle age it was kind of weird to do New Year count down on a street.
name: Emily

text:
Disappointing.  We were walking Main Street on a rainy Thursday evening and stopped in for dinner.  The area was pretty empty on account of the rain and it not being one of the Christmas celebration days so we were not surprised to find the place empty.  Our waiter was nice, but got at least one thing wrong at every step.  I'm pretty flexible so I only asked him back if it was a critical error, but even that got annoying over time.  Much of this could have been solved if the waiter paid attention to basic details.  For example, my friend ordered a salad, actually said "I'll have the XX salad" and the dish was served as a wrap.  Items generally expected for a dish were not included or offered such as ketchup for fries or malt vinegar for fish and chips.  

At the end, we asked for boxes, only got one.  Then we asked for separate checks (2) and got one.  One of us paid with cash (needing change to leave a tip) and the other paid with a card.  When the waiter collected payment, he picked it up and started walking away.  I stopped him and requested the be split by person (again) and he nodded and kept walking.  I had to follow him into the back room to clarify what was supposed to be charged on the card and what was to be covered in cash.  When he returned to our table, the charge was correct, but our waiter decided to round down the cash change to his advantage of a larger tip.  

Both myself and my friend are generous tippers, and having been a server myself, I know the ropes and usually tip 30-40% or more on slow nights.  We both tipped only 15% (minus the extra change already taken) but the server could have gotten much more had he paid attention. 

The food was ok, typical bar fare, not great enough to inspire a return visit.
name: Taunya

text: Got takeout from here twice now so I feel like I can say a little more. The staff seemed tired but still polite. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. Not a bad stop, just not one I'm rushing to repeat. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The menu wasnt huge, which I usually prefer..
name: User

text: Ordered the $10 box meal. (Pizza, breadsticks, cinnamon sticks). They called after my order was placed online to say they were out of both breadsticks and cinamin sticks. We got an $8 pizza instead. They said it would be 15 min. We ordered at 10:53. It's 11:25 and I am still standing here with no pizza. The only person working is outside on her cell phone. Said our pizza is still in the oven. This sucks.
name: Gordon

text:
Walked in hoping to have a meal of chaats, but was disappointed that they had a curry buffet like you see at most Indian restaurants and very few actual chaat options. I did indulge in some pani puri at the buffet station, but with the name Chaat house, you'd think there would be more chaat. 

Curries were mediocre and were too sweet for my liking.
name: IJen

text: No big complaints, just a nice meal. Food was good and came out fast. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. The whole meal felt kind of uneven.
name: User

text:
Friendly staff...you order inside at the food side then sit down and pick it up when ready. They also have seating outside, more like picnic tables..but hey, it's New Orleans. They have really good beers, especially the Lambics. Lots of choices.
If you go, try their poutine...it is amazing.
Only problem is there isn't a lot of parking..and if you park across the street on River road make sure you're careful. People fly past there.
Not really a kid place, unless you sit outside.
name: Laurie

text: The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. It was crowded but still moved along. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. No big complaints, just a nice meal. For the price I expected more than this. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait.
name: User

text: This place is a dive, in a good way...I love dives...the only reason they recieved a 3 star was because they took about an hour and ten minutes to bring out our food. The service was great and the food was awesome...I strongly recommend the wing and pizza combo...I'm not a big Chicago style pizza type of guy but this one is good! Their calzone is out of this world...fresh, hearty and delicious...The calzone didnt even fit on the plate...this thing is huge!!!!! Perfect for sharing!!! If you take a date there, order a calzone and a couple beers and your good...I will definitely be going back!
name: Andy

text:
If you have time and the chance, DEFINITELY take the cooking class  here!  I'm a foodie and it was heaven!  We took the demo class and not only did we learn how to make gumbo, jambalaya, bananas foster, and  pralines we got to eat it too!  :)  

We also learned a lot about the Creole and Cajun cultures and New Orleans history.

Such a fun time!!!!!

text:
Way overpriced, quality is not there. The selection
Is weird and all over the place.fast casual food with 
Fancy restaurant prices and quantities.
Not going back!

text: While taking classes at a local college last summer I found this place on Yelp. After reading the reviews and seeing that it was conveniently located next to a market I had to check it out. I was not disappointed, while the mac salad was a bit too bland and had too much mayo for my taste, the platters are a great deal with much food. If you are nearby do not miss out on this hidden gem.
name: Elizabeth

text: Food was fresh and service was quick. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Not bad for a quick meal. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. No big complaints, just a nice meal.

text:
Need to add more than 1 person on the register on whopper Wednesdays. Lines are too long. In the past, this bk handled crowds better. Totally disorganized now. 

Several weeks later...still long lines on whopper wed. 1 dude at register. Ummm...what's up with that?

Wow. Came back to give this place a try after 6 months. What a mistake. It's a whopper Wednesday and as usual, standing in line FOREVER. GOTTA get back to work soon. What a mess.
name: Donald

text:
Came here for lunch. It's not huge on the inside but there are plenty of tables. You can park in the back and there is a rear entrance so that is nice. 

No complimentary chips and salsa but you can order it for not too much money. We decided to get the guacamole instead. It wasn't a huge amount of guacamole but it was really good with just the right amount of kick. The chips were thick and very crunchy. We had plenty leftover. 

For lunch I was thrilled to see that they had mole sauce that you could pretty much get on top of anything since you could pick your sauce for most everything. I have not found very many Mexican places that offer mole but this one does! I ordered a grilled chicken burrito with mole sauce. It was really good. The mole sauce was really good. 

The kid ordered enchiladas and decided to be daring and try the mole as well. Hurray! Another convert! 

This lunch was about 25 dollars so not too bad! I would definitely eat here again next time I'm in the area.
name: Cheryl

text: We have been coming here for a long time. Every time we are in Johns Pass, it's a must, however, I gotta say, this place has gone to the birds. One person in front of us and we waited 20 minutes and ended up leaving. I watched a few other groups leave in that time too. The one guy working there has no clue how to make coffees as he tried to give me a large cup of Milk and syrup with no coffee! He forgot the coffee and then acted surprised when I asked him why . He was also extremely slow. It's sad because, no way this place stays in business like this.

text: Great meal today. My husband picked this place for his birthday lunch. I had mild shrimp curry and biryani rice with some naan. My husband had a medium creamy spinach chicken dish. Delicious too. He also had the rice and naan. Service was excellent. The owner came out and chatted and sent some delicious sweets for dessert to help celebrate his big day. It was an entirely delightful experience

text: Portions are big. Italian sandwich is seriously good!!!!! Free refills and very friendly staff. Love this place!

text: What a great experience we had here last night. We met the best people!  The place was packed!  The wait for a table was at least 30 minutes. This is where a bar would have come in handy. It's the only reason I didn't give 5 stars. Once we were seated, the service was friendly and efficient. The food was delicious!  Definitely recommend this restaurant!
name: Kathy

text: This is by far the premier Indian restaurant in Tampa! Their lunch buffet is excellent, especially on Thursday and Friday, when they have an incredible variety at a slightly higher price point than the early part of the week!
name: Joseph

text: Mixed opinions of food but service was fine. We had a large party on a busy day for a holiday luncheon. Calamari was prepared excellently and served with a tasty marinara sauce. Veal portions for the dishes were on the small side served with potatoes & veggies. Salmon was over cooked and dried out but the accompanying risotto was flavorful. Overall apps were best part of meal. I dined here before and had much the same experience. So to me its average at best and probably will not return.
name: Joe

text: This winery is nice, but the wine tasting itself left something to be desired. The wines weren't very unique and lacked flavor. My friend and I both ordered a glass of sangria after the tasting, but it was watery and disappointing. The view was nice and there was a very friendly dog on the property. I'm glad we came, but probably wouldn't come back.

text: Decent at best. I ordered the veggie egg rolls (which were good)... 3 for $6 seems very expensive. I also ordered the vegan pad Thai. I specifically asked for veggies on this- there was probably two carrot pieces and two broccoli pieces on it. Disappointed. I paid about $15 bucks for one meal and it was mediocre. Won't be back.

text:
I give 3 stars due to atmosphere, menu selection, and execution of the dishes, including the stale $9 cheesecake I had for dessert. I'd go back again, however, in my opinion, it's a little pricey for what you get and what you have to choose from. Their main protein was short ribs. Almost every dish featured beef short ribs. Nothing against short ribs, but meh. I want more variety. My husband and I split the Brussels Caesar salad, which was good, but due to how they reuse the same 1-2 ingredients throughout the whole menu, it made me feel like they just took leftover cooked Brussels sprouts from someone's uneaten dish and tossed them into my salad. I ordered the NY strip for my main. It was perfectly cooked, but featured a TOTAL LACK of seasoning. The bacon jam on top was good, but more sweet than salty, so the lack of salt was very apparent there. I didn't try my husband's dish, but you guessed it, it had short ribs in it. We had cheesecake for dessert which was clearly past its prime. Hubs ordered the apple walnut cake which was very good. I'm sure the desserts are not made in house. Decor was just as bland as the (lack of) seasoning on my steak. 

White paper over the tablecloths, and a crooked, precariously-hung heavy cotton curtain separating the back of the house from the front of the house. I thought it was going to fall every time a server had to pass through it. Little nit-picky, but overall this place is good. For price, I'd expect a little more, personally.
name: Jamie

text: The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. You can tell they care about customer experience here. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. Would return. text:
This is  in one of those plazas that you just drive by but never go into.
The interior is small with a brick wall and brown floors/silver metal chairs. It's clean but looks a little dark,flat, and unappealing.

I went for a lunch since it was barely 3 miles from the house.
There are 2 lunch specials depending on toppings/pizza slice. one for 6.25 and one for 7.50.Both include a fountain soda.
 Now there were 2 pizzas on racks , a Sicilian cheese, and a thin white/spinach pie. I ordered the Sicilian (2 slices) and asked if there was pepperoni on it since I couldn't get a close look. He said yes. However, when it came time to pay , my order was $9 bucks. Apparently he thought I asked if i wanted to ADD pepperoni to it which upped the price $1.5 

Also it was a bit annoying that the tip option is asked before you complete the transaction on the card reader. Usually most businesses complete the main transaction FIRST, then the tip or ask you to write the tip on the receipt. They give you a plastic cup for the fountain drink and the machine is a Coke centric one. Nothing else to write home.

The pizza was decent, but not  a revelation.The crust tastes different than many other places. In fact, since I had Jet's sicilian pepperoni just a few weeks ago, I think I like theirs better. Blasphemy, I know to like a chain place over indie , but oh well. Plus, Jets was $5 for exact same meal basically.

They should just make the lunch special one uniform price ($8) instead of doing upgrades imo.

Overall: Ok, but not a place I'd run back to soon
name: James

text: An action packed venue with so much to choose from. The pretzels were delicious. Lots of fresh produce, cheeses, meats, seafood to take home and cook. Also a great variety of cuisines to try and explore. Share dishes w others to get the most exposure to the different offerings.

text: This was a great location to eat at. Even though I had been to one before,very briefly, this was my first time really sitting down and eating.My kids and I had a great dinner here tonight. We came right before the dinner crowd and it was quite quiet, but I liked it like that. We also received a free toasted ravioli which very good. The food was delicious and hot. Our server was very attentive and sweet as well. I think this location will be a family favorite.

text:
In town for a wedding, and Baja Cafe was strongly recommend by the groom. Party if three adults, arrived just after 8 on a Saturday. Host took our name, but we were taken to a table almost immediately. Very small restaurant, but comfortably bright and airy, we specifically noted how much more space there is around the tables than at most diner-type restaurants.
Ordered Shaggy Snak, Classic Ranchero (huevos rancheros), and Roadrunner 4.0(benedict). 
Food was outstanding. It looked awesome, it tasted fantastic, the flavor was bold but balanced.
Server was super friendly and helpful. 
As stated first timers, we got a free snickerdoodle pancake, which was very large, but fluffy and light. 
Fair warning--the location is crap, the decor is meh, and the tables and chairs are pretty poor. Server was slow to refill my coffee, and kinda sloshed it all over when he leaned on the wobbly table. But I don't care; this restaurant is tops. Can't wait to go back.

Nice little spot, decent portions too. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.

text: Feliz restaurants have always been my favorite. We love coming here for brunch, with a group of friends, or a random date night. The food and service is great, it's so hard to choose a favorite dish. The Baja Fish Tacos are in the top 5. My husband and I had our rehearsal dinner here with a group of 60 and were so pleased with the service and hospitality. We worked with Kelly Fink to plan the event and she was always friendly and responded to questions quickly. If you're looking for an amazing meal or a place to host an event, look no further!
name: Kait

text: I stopped in to get a red curry (my comfort food) on my way home from work. They were very polite when I placed my phone order for take out & when I came in to pick it up. The food was ready on time & an easy stop off a very busy 49th St. The red curry was a perfect level of medium spicy (which I requested), the sauce was creamy with the good blend of flavor. I'm a picky red curry eater & this passed the test. Only thing I would change for my order for next time is to request much less bamboo. The amount of bamboo strips resembled a side order of shoe string French fries on top of my sauce (which would be an interesting fusion, but when it's sometimes chewy bamboo, less is more). For me, not the #1 red curry in town, but a close runner up & very convenient to get in, pick up your food & be back on your way.

text:
Came here for lunch on a busy Sunday prior to the Saints game. There was a 10 min wait time when we got there, however this restaurant is huge and had rooms that were mostly empty so not sure why the wait time. Pretty loud in there I wouldn't recommend this place for a romantic date. Ordered the crab cake app and the fried seafood dinner. The food was pretty good and the service was decent, atmosphere not much my cup of tea.

Food 4/5

text: So many bunch options in the city and this is my least favorite. Our waiter was all over the place and we barely got any service which normally I wouldn't are but I brought out of state guests. Not returning.

text:
We've been twice now and both times have been more than pleased. My wife has done totally custom and I riffed on two of the signature bowls. 

The ingredients are freshly prepared. The sauces and spices are well-crafted and thoughtful. It is obvious that Kelvin and his staff have a passion for this dish. Don't hesitate to ask for suggestions. They know what they are about. 

Please give this locally owned and operated business a try. You will be pleased you did.

text: Popular joint! If you can make reservations I would consider it. The food was really good and they have many options on the menu. If you've been to a Snooze, Ruby Slipper is very similar to that. I got the pancake with fudge and marshmallows. I don't remember the name but it resembled s'mores. It was good but a little too sweet for my tooth. Regardless everything else was good and I still finished the pancakes!

text:
Recently while on a trip to New Orleans one of the folks that I was traveling with highly recommended that we eat here at Central grocery and deli based on some prior memories and what an amazing place this is to eat at. Walking in you can immediately smell the sense of Italy and being in an old-school deli. The walls are lined with every ingredient you can imagine for cooking like seasoning, olives, sauces, olive oil etc...

We came here for the original Muffuletta sandwich. This sandwich is so simple but so so amazing! It consists of freshly made sesame seed loaf split horizontally and covered with layers of marinated olive salad, salami, ham, Swiss cheese, provolone, and mortadella. It is also comes in a few sizes be aware this full size one is huge. We split a 1/2 3 ways and still had enough to eat. This is hands down one of the best sandwiches I have eaten in my life. I have already been on-line as well and will be ordering some olive spread and a sandwich for an upcoming NFL Sunday. The guys working here are great as well and was such a pleasure coming here. I highly recommend it if you in the NOLA area.
name: Jason

text: They definitely could use some renovations however their food was delicious. text:
I really wanted to rate this higher but our check out experience was pretty distasteful. 

Pros: 1 star for the bar downstairs and drink/ food quality. The bartenders were always friendly and the quality of the food and drinks were good. 

1 star for the hotel location. - it's literally around the corner from all the downtown Nashville shenanigans but just far enough away to avoid the lights and the noise. 

1 star for the hotel decor. They really do try to tie in a country music theme. The Johnny Cash wall in the lobby is great. 

Cons: 
Never have I been questioned so much about my relationship to my mom over utilizing our Marriott explore rate. Upon check in I was asked who, what she did, what department she was in, how
Long she's worked for Marriott, which specific Marriott she works at and so on and so forth.  
Like damn, I understand making conversation or checking a thing or two but I didn't think an interrogation would be a part of the welcome.  

- Our bathroom bathtub wouldn't drain the water appropriately. And no, it's not operator error. I tried telling Brionna at check out and she couldn't care less when I asked that maintenance check it out before they rent it out again. 

Checking out: 
So we were charged for valet for our stay on accident. We didn't get a rental car so we Uber'd and used Lyft the entire time. When I checked out this morning I told Brionna we were charged incorrectly and that I'm more than happy to show her my Lyft and Uber receipts. She barely uttered a word and proceeds to call the Valet guy to check to make sure I wasn't lying. I understand verifying information but maybe try to be a little more discrete about assuming I'm lying next time. 
She didn't ask how our stay was. She didn't greet me good morning or say " thanks for staying with marriott". She actually didn't say ANYTHING at all. It was awkward as hell.  

The pool was filthy. We actually opted to not use it at all which was a shame because it's an indoor pool and with the heat and humidity it would have been nice to be able to use. 

I wouldn't recommend staying here to anyone. There are a ton of other Marriott or Marriott affiliates I would use as opposed to this one. We won't be back.
name: Jessica

text: This place was definitely good but not the best I've had. I came with three friends and we did the thing where you order a bunch of small plates and share. We got two salads - the roasted red pepper, which was very good, and the cauliflower, which was good except that the anchovy was unevenly distributed, so we ended up with some overly fishy mouthfuls. We had the octopus, which was delightful. Good flavor, good texture. We had a few pastas: The gnocchi, which wasn't all that flavorful and the texture was a bit dense. Also, the server warned us it would be super spicy, and it definitely wasn't. I don't like spice, and I didn't think it was spicy. The bucatini with peas, which was good, especially nice for spring. And...I'm forgetting the third pasta. We did both entrees - the half chicken, which was delicious!! Really well cooked (i.e. juicy and not dry), and lots of flavor. text: This is easily my go-to Pho restaurant in Tampa. I love this place so much! The pho is incredibly flavorful and seriously warms your soul. My personal favorite is the beef pho, but I'm sure any kind they make is wonderful. This restaurant is spot on with their sauces, herbs, and spices. My favorite appetizer is the eggroll. I'm glad an order only comes with 2 because I can't stop myself with these crunchy beauts. Their dumplings (both steamed and fried) are delicious too and really, I'll get the sample appetizer too because it's all good. I've honestly probably gotten almost everything off the menu at this point, but aside from the pho, my other favorite dish is the beef lemongrass stir-fry. It's served with white rice and tons of tasty veggies. I rarely ever get beef dishes but Simply Pho has excellent beef that's clearly high quality. Their prices are low for the food you're getting. My second favorite dish is their grilled chicken rice platter. I always order mine with a fried egg, but it's a tasty, healthier option that I was stuck on for over a year until I finally branched out. Seriously though, just try this place for yourself- I know you won't be disappointed!

text:

The mother came out after and greeted us warmly and came around the counter to see our baby. She was very nice. We ordered the rooster which was delicious. The chicken was moist and tender and warm. text:

There was a 5/$5 special on their smoked wings, which were DELICIOUS, my friends got an order of their house salad and pretzels which they raved about.

Despite the good atmosphere and good food, the service was a bit lackluster. I can understand that it was very busy, but our waitress hardly ever visited our table, got our order wrong, and we had to track her down to get our checks. Not to worry, we will definitely be back...maybe when it's a little less crowded!

text: We had brunch at the Blue Willow Cafe a week ago and just wanted to thank them for still being in town. Our meal (we both had omelettes) was wonderful as was our server (wish I had her name). text: If you want to tty authentic Nigerian food, this is the place to stop by. For first timers, try the jollof rice and chicken which is made with hot pepper and palm oil that gives it a spicy, nutty flavor. The fried rice is less spicy and similar to Chinese fried rice. For a real taste of Nigeria, however, you should get the pounded yam with egusi soup. Pull off a little yam and dip in the egusi sauce for a great taste combination. The spicy, peppery soup perfectly complements the starchy yam which is like a very stiff mashed potato. The boldest will also enjoy the meat and fatty skin piece that comes with this dish, but you may want to ask the servers not to give you that if you're a first timer. The puff puff is basically fried sweet bread and chin chin is a crunchier variety. The fried plantain is as good or better than what you may get in a South American restaurant. Overall, you got to try this food. It is not at all like Ethiopian or Middle Eastern food. It is all its own, so come with an open mind and the expectation of enjoying a great meal.
name: Harold

text:
This is hands down the best Indian restaurant in the Nashville area.

We eat here regularly in the evening and the cleanliness, friendly service, and food quality is awesome. If you've not tried Indian food before the amazing staff will guide you through the extensive menu and find the right spice level for your taste. Forget the thought that Indian food is just "curry" the choice and subtle flavors will blow you away. Prices are reasonable and the ambience is just right for a meal with friends or date night with that special person. Easy parking at front or rear and close to Centennial Park.

I understand they also have a great lunch buffet but we haven't tried it.
Thoroughly recommended.

text: Town Square brewing is a micro brewery . On my first visit to the brewery I had the opportunity to taste all of the 10 different feature beers because I won a beer tasting and tour in a raffle. Brandon, (an owner) was friendly  and knowledgeable about the different beer and the process used to obtain the different flavours . The master brewer showed us the equipment and explained the process involved in production. The production area was incredibly clean . We found the staff very pleasant and accommodating. The beer that I took home had so much more flavour than most commercial beer . I came back the following week with friends and enjoyed some items from their  unique menu. The dining area is small and rustic and just a very pleasant place to hang out and chat with friends. Although I've never been an avid beer drinker I will return to buy beer from this brewery in the future.

text: I love 1000 Figs! The fresh bread and hummus alone is worth the visit. The falafel and hibiscus tea are also fantastic. I like to go with a friend and split a bunch of small plates together. text:

They also had a varity of pickles to choose from with some interesting flavors like jalapeno and hot garlic that are all homemade. The sandwich shop also sells pies and other pastries. The prices range from $3-$12. Sandwich platters are also available with 24 hour notice. 

Their location makes them easily accessible. There is parking on 3 sides of the building. The farmer produce section is nice and spacious. The produce is assembled for easy access. My reason for four stars is that the sandwich shop did not appear very clean. I didn't feel comfortable ordering food from this venue. I will continue to shop here but only for produce.

text:
For 20 years this was my go-to place for greasy-spoon burgers and fried everything.  Unfortunately for St. Louis, Frank Cunetto hung up his burger spatula last year -- Frank was the driving force behind Carl's and could always be seen behind the grill with a friendly smile.  The good news is the burgers are the same wonderfully crispy-edge smash burgers of my childhood.  The bad news is that the new owner for some reason has discontinued the Pork Steak sandwich, which, aside from the burgers themselves, was the best thing on the menu.  The chicken filet is still there (too dry), as are the onion rings (awesome) and fries.  The chili is, as far as I can tell, still the Edmond's chili, which in St. Louis is immortalized as the standard at O.T. Hodges.

Net, know what to order (double cheese, onion rings, foot long chili dog with cheese and onions) and Carl's still dominates the scene.  Under new ownership, we seem to have regressed a bit.  And by the way, root beer says it's IBC but if it's the same as when Frank was there they make it themselves and it's fantastic.

text:
I want to start this review by saying I hate writing this...I love Donatos. My family has loved it and been eager to convince my Dad to pay the extra money so we can get Donatos. We ordered regularly, and living on my own, I still order a (large) pizza and breadsticks for myself more than I probably should (lol). Remember, I give the pizza a usual 5 but I am giving this experience....a -2 if I could.


My brother and his wife moved to Nashville and do not have a Donatos close by. They were in town Friday night (arrival at 11PM) and the ONE thing my brother requested was Donatos. Keep in mind, this event included me, my mom, my boyfriend, my brother, my sister-in-law, and my brother's bestfriend. We submitted an online order at about 10:30. The confirmation page said "Your pizza will be ready by 11:59". Okay, sweet. It is a Friday night, no worries, it is worth the wait. We are hanging out by the Bonfire, still no doorbell or call, it's 12:30 so my mom calls the store. We think this was a manager. He told my mom that his driver was out with the pizza and to call him back if it did not arrive soon (my parents live 10 maybe 15 minutes from the delivery store). We wait until 12:45 and still no word, so my mom calls again. The manager immediately answered the phone and said "he still isn't there?" My mom says yes. The manager then proceeds to tell my mom how he only has one delivery driver. Apparently this driver has been having car problems and lost his cell phone. Okay, we call BS...anyway, the manager then offers to fire up the ovens again, make our pizza, and personally bring it to us. My mom told him forget it and reimburse us. She then tells my very disappointed older brother who takes her phone and calls the manager back asking him to re make the pizza because he wants Donatos so bad that he will stay up and wait for it. I understand that it was really late and it is very understandable that this manager was probably having a REALLY bad night as I bet we were not alone, but the manager proceeded to try to make excuses so he would not have to do what he had already offered us. My brother was adamant, as he should be..its customer service and we buy a lot of pizza from them..and the manager agreed. But wait, he was still going to CHARGE us full price for the order we had placed 2.5 hours ago. At this point, he was on speaker phone and I yelled no way when he tried to charge us. Very disappointed. Handled very poorly. I feel bad for my mom...I remember when they said they would credit me before and they never did. I hope my mom sees her money back...Donatos ain't cheap. Oh, btw, the driver never showed. My frustrated brother got in his car and bought frozen Donatos pizzas at Kroger (not nearly as good)
name: Katie

text:
Tavolino knows how to make pizza! Located just off the ferry in Algiers Point, Tavolino is worth the visit for people near and far. (Plus, you can make an evening of it and take the ferry with friends!)

Happy hour runs from 3-6 and has deals on pizza and drinks. Pizzas are $9 during happy hour and the pizzas are FIRE! My friends and I are greedy and decided to each get drinks and a pizza. The drinks were all super sweet so I wouldn't recommend getting those. However, the beer menu was clutch and so affordable! I was drinking Carpe Rose for $3 a can. Next, for the pizza. I got the fungi and OH MY GOD I CANT STOP THINKING ABOUT IT! It was so delicious, I had to physically stop myself from eating it all. My other friend got the carne and loved it as well!

Tavolino is some great pizza! The place is small and took a little while for the pizza to come out but it was worth the wait! Highly recommend making a visit!

text:
I think I've found the answer as to why attitude and subpar food was served yesterday. I haven't confirmed it yet, but Chula's Mexican Grill quietly turned into Chula's Mexican Restaurant. This is usually the sign of demise for a once hot and lively local. It's perfectly fine to buy a thriving hot little restaurant that's usually packed all weekend long. 
     
But, don't expect your customers not to notice the changes, the attitude from staff who've probably seen their wages/tips plummet. 

The menu shrinking to half or fewer choices from the original and becoming bland and flavorless. 

The lack of any other patrons on what used to be a packed, noisy, lively Saturday afternoon.

So, to the host/waiter that gave me crap about my lack of shoes, I forgive you. I'm sure you're just towing the new corporate line of uniformity and intolerance. To the cook/microwaver, I forgive you for either being forced to deliver food below grandmas standards or for not having grandma ingrain standards into you.

To the new owners, I forgive you for thinking business would be the same after making changes to everything that people liked about Chula's. 

So, long Chula's you were good while you lasted.




It's probably not the best idea to get an attitude with your only customers on a Saturday afternoon. Especially over something trivial that isn't even a law.

Lovely place! Staff is pleasant. Space is neat and clean. Food is tasty and drinks are reasonably priced. New menu format is easier to read, but not sure what they removed. If anything. Spanish music can be a touch loud at times, but not overly so. Definitely try the Enchiladas Cuarteto! The Rellenos' are ok, but they don't have a crispy version. Maybe that's a Colorado thing lol. Beer is tasty and cheap, just wish they'd chill the mugs.
name: Aaron

text: We went to Bon Appétit for dinner with a large group of people, celebrating a friend's birthday.  Food and atmosphere were EXCELLENT, especially the piano dinner music. Presumably because of our significant bill ($750+), our waiter (Alessandro, btw wonderful!!!) offered a voucher for a complimentary bottle of champagne on our next visit. Since we are not from the area, we decided to return the next day for drinks and to redeem the voucher. The voucher clearly stated that no purchase was necessary, only requirements being minimum party of 4 and dine in only. After presenting voucher to the waiter and ordering a large round of drinks, we were told by the attending manager, and ultimately head manager, that they would not honor our voucher.   He more or less indicated it would be accepted ONLY if we would be ordering 4 food items.  After a brief conversation, it became quite apparent the head manager has a RUDE, non-customer oriented demeanor and had NO intention of honoring his restaurant's voucher as written.  Very poor business choice, as 2+ rounds of drinks would have exceeded a small food order (which wasn't a requirement per the voucher in the first place.)  We left without purchasing anything.  In summary, GREAT food, but HORRENDOUS business insight.  They should consider hiring a lawyer, or perhaps just someone with common-sense, to write their intended promotional offers.

text:
This place isn't for everyone (even among vegetarians). Diners beware of a few small issues:

-The menu is very limited. I think there were 6 smaller dishes and 5 bigger dishes. That doesn't make for a lot of options. Make sure you're ok with the menu before coming, or you could find yourself leaving hungry.

-If you can't do spicy food (I love the taste but my stomach can't take it), do not come here. When I told the waiter I wasn't great with spicy food, he went through the menu, eventually finding TWO DISHES that are not spicy (one was cauliflower, which I don't like, and the other was charred corn & avocado, which we ordered and was indeed really good). He claimed the Peruvian fries weren't spicy, but the chipotle mayo was blazing (even my spicy-tolerant girlfriend couldn't eat them). Meanwhile, the kimchi tacos are NOT spicy (the kimchi is very mild)... but they're not very good, either. 

-They do not have soft drinks. This one earns a big F-U. I hate when places try to be more-artisinal-than-thou by not offering mass-made products. I could have tolerated the mediocre menu if I could have had a diet coke and whiskey to wash it down with. 

-We were there on a hot night, and the restaurant interior was very HOT. I was literally sweating through my meal (and no, it wasn't because of spicy food, since I didn't eat it). They need another air conditioner (or two). Otherwise, the interior is really nice and decor is pleasant. Would be a cute date spot if you're ok with the spice and the heat.

text:
Chicken waffles
Sunday morning

This place is well known and recommended by many so there were high hopes for a good brunch.

Location: in a very cute town of collingswood. This specifically location was in a small downtown with mom and pop shops, too bad it was Sunday so everything was closed. There are locations in philly as well.

Venue: bright, open space floor plan, high tops and short with large and small group seating areas. Decor was cute and innovative. It was very inviting.

Service: quick friendly efficient. There were lots of staff to cover each other and each had their roles to keep things moving and clean. Very impressive.

Food: the menu was sooooo boring. It was typical American food, without any flare or anything that made it exciting. It was difficult to find anything worth trying to be honest. Your typical omelets, French toast, salads..... luckily I saw the chicken and waffles in the dinner section and asked if they offered it during brunch which they did! The dish itself was simple. The chicken was crispy to perfection but the rest of the plate was very bland. It was just waffles and syrup, no extra spice or distinguishing flavors. I've had many chicken and waffles from the south and each place always has a signature flavor added to their version of chicken and waffles, this place did not. But again the chicken was impressively crispy!

Overall: it was a good time with good company, flavors were subpar, menu left something more to be desired for. Definitely a lot of other options in the area that would have more interesting dishes and options. But if you want comfort american food, this is the place.

Happy eating!
