text:
Really enjoyed my experience here...

If I were writing solely based on the food, my rating would be 4 stars instead of 5 simply because of a few small things. The fried rice was light and included a lot of fresh vegetables. I had pork fried rice, and the pork was nice albeit simply cooked. The veggies were a bit undercooked for my taste, but my wife really appreciated that fact, so just understand what you're getting into ordering it. The flavor was pretty good, but again, it was very light. Personally, I would prefer a bit more soy sauce but I guess that's part of the appeal of a "lighter" fried rice. I also had tempura chicken on mine. It's only a dollar or so more, so the 4 pieces made sense, however the cut of meat was not great. I don't mind a bit of dark meat, but my wife is not a fan, and I have to admit the exact cuts used here were not the greatest. Everything else was fantastic, though. All of their sauces are homemade and truly delicious. I think they might have the best crab rangoons in Tucson.

The thing that really put me over the edge with the star rating however, is how incredibly friendly and nice the two people working there were. As I was sitting in the drive thru waiting for my fried rice, I was offered a crab rangoon in sweet and sour sauce to try. It was so good, that I insisted upon getting a full order of them in addition to what I had already got. When she returned with it all, she also gave me an apple pie egg roll, which I dont remember seeing on the menu, but it was tasty and unique. 

Everything was clearly made with love here, and while not everything was exactly to my taste, it certainly warrants a return visit in the near future. I hope people are not dissuaded by how the building looks on the exterior, because it is a valued addition to our Tucson food community!
name: Gabriel

text:
This place is a hidden gem!! It is a short menu but very well balanced.  It has Gf/Vegan/Vegetarian options to choose from.  I was in between ordering the Rolled Uttapam and the Citrus Mojo Pork Mofongo.  I sat at the bar so I asked Kathryn, the bartender, what she suggested from the two.  She suggested I go with the porks so I did.  When my dish came out and I took the first bite I was in love.  The pork was crispy on the outside, very tender and tasted amazing.  All of the ingredients on the plate complemented one another; the crispy pork shoulder, grilled plantain cake, sofrito, roasted pepitas citrus mojo and salsa rosada where delightful.  It has been hands down the BEST dinner on my trip.  Then Kathryn  asked if I would like dessert, being gluten AND dairy free I almost never have dessert options.  This place had two! I went with the Coconut Banana Foster... I'll be dreaming about this dessert... it was very sweet, perfectly suited to my sweet tooth after the great meal.  Everyone was very helpful, friendly and I could tell that they all worked well together.  I was able to see the cooking happen and the finished dishes come out perfectly ready for a photo shoot. Catherine kept making awesome looking drinks and the place was packed. I would highly recommend this place.  I will definitely be coming back for more before my trip ends!! 

PS. No pictures, I was too busy eating and enjoying every bite. Sorry.

text:
Following this truck to its next stop is going to be worth your time....  

We had the vegetable curry with green beans, potatoes and an iced coffee with sugar, cream, and cardamom.  The curry was earthy and slightly spicy.  It paired extremely well with the rice and the subtitle sweetness of the green beans.  As a whole, the dish was impressive in how well each part of it amplified the flavors of the other parts of the meal.

And.  Then.  There.  Was.  The. Coffee!!!

It was 7:30pm, which was far too late for an iced coffee in my opinion.  But, after taking the first sip I couldn't have cared less what time it was.  It was one of the best drinks I've had in my life!  In my life people!!!  It had all the elements of an iced coffee that you typically expect.  The coffee flavor was very good with the sweetness and creaminess you expect from sugar and cream...  duh.  But the addition of the cardamom took my drink into a different world.  It added another depth of flavor that really woke up the entire beverage.  If you are a coffee drinker...  this is for you.  If you are not a coffee drinker...  this is for you.  It's amazing.  Trust me.  The end.  

Overall, the service was great.  The prices were on point.  And the food was exciting, flavorful, and well-done.  This is not just a food truck...  it is a destination!

text:
Customer service from our server was excellent with a great ending result from management but because of the experience we had, I'm rating this as poor. 

Perhaps it was an off night but for the price you pay, you expect nothing less than perfection. I understand it is normal to sometimes encounter some type of dissatisfaction but considering my partner and I were celebrating our 13th anniversary, this was not acceptable. 

First, my rib eye was well done, I asked for medium. Server took it back and said he would get another one out asap but I realize they still have to cook it, etc. Second, 20 mins later and after my partner was finishing his dish as we did not want his steak to get cold, the manager approaches us and asks me how my 2nd steak tasted, I said "what steak, I've not gotten another one yet." He apologized, ran to the kitchen and brought my dish 20 seconds later, and also served us fresh mashed potatoes. Finally, I'm now eating, alone, but second steak is perfect. Well, as I take a bite of the mashed potatoes, I'm also now chewing on what appeared to be plastic or wax. What is going on?! 

The dinner experience we were hoping for, given that we were in celebration mode, was far from great. We are from Texas and although Nashville has been great, I definitely won't be back to this restaurant when I visit again. They did make things right and comped our entire meal and gave us 3 free desserts but nonetheless, not what we were expecting!
name: Jesse

text:

text: If I could give negative stars I would. Let's start by saying my entire family has been coming to this location since it has opened. The restaurant was not packed when we arrived. My wife noticed a large group behind me getting their order delivered so we assumed this was the delay. So we waited some more. At the 10 minute mark we noticed the waitress who's section we were sitting in approach a table of man and woman who had literally just sat down and took their drink order. Still ignoring us. I approached the hostess to see if we had been sat in the wrong section, asked who are waitress was, explained no one had come to our table and that it had been over 10mins. text:
So Culver's is one of my favorite burger places that isn't In N Out. I have a few of those places, but Culver's really kills it with an extensive variety of menu offerings, frozen treats and full meals. The cheese curds are by far my favorite. 

So why three stars? Because. Season your meat, Culver's, for the love of God, season your meat.  My Wisconsin melt is amazing after I douse that baby in salt and pepper and add some condiments. All I ever get at any Culver's is a Wisconsin melt and cheese curds instead of fries. Sometimes I get a concrete, which is like a customizable mcflurry or Blizzard from DQ. I generally stick to my old trusty, chocolate with Reese's. They also sell pints and sundaes. 

Get the cheese curds and be prepared to season your own meat!

text:
I was first won over by The Rooster once I learned that the Federal Donuts crew came up with it so they could repurpose their unused chicken parts into delicious soup. And I was even more won over when I learned that they donated 100% of their profits earned towards Broad Street Ministry and their hospitality collaborative. With a good cause like that it was inevitable for me to go and try it out, especially once they rebranded into a Jewish diner concept. And my visit led to everything I hoped it would be and then some!

The interior is a laid back casual basement diner with a modern touch. But once you add in late night karaoke on the last Saturday of the month, bottomless bloody Mary and mimosa deals during Saturday and Sunday brunch, a good weekday happy hour, and some stellar cocktails, it doesn't take much to realize that this isn't your father's diner of yesteryear.

When you go to a spot like The Rooster you instantly build up a craving matzo ball soup and pastrami. Fortunately doing the two at once is pretty affordable since you can combo a cup of soup onto a sandwich order for just $3. and the delicious Yemenite matzo, green onions, and bits of chicken combine for a refreshing mix. As far as pastrami sandwiches go the delicious meat, onion, and horseradish sauce of the Montreal Smoked Meat combine for one of the best in Philly. Tune up the Alice In Chains song, because this rooster ain't gonna die (https://youtu.be/uAE6Il6OTcs)!
name: Bill

text: My wife and I visited this location on December 4 at around 8 PM. Upon pulling into the parking lot the majority of the chairs were on the table as if the restaurant was closed. We walked into the restaurant and noticed it was open till 11 PM. The restaurant was fairly empty however it took a few minutes for the cashier to greet us because she was busy getting the dinning room cleaned for closing even though they were open until 11?  We ordered two small bowls with starch, protein and toppings upon getting our order we sat down and enjoyed them although the portions were very small the food was tasty. Upon completing our meal we went to get two more bowls to go.  One of our children is a vegetarian and wanted a bowl with no meat the restaurant will not allow us to get extra starch even know we were not getting any protein. While waiting for our to go bowls we observed several employees committing food safety violations including handling raw chicken and then handling prepared food. We called the one 800 number and spoke to customer service we were told we get a callback no one ever called us back we also put a comment on their website with request to get a call back and no one has ever called us back. Will not be visiting this restaurant anytime soon.

text:
Absolutely amazing. Started off with fresh baked rolls and whipped butter that was still warm. Then had the firecracker shrimp as an appetizer. Incredible flavor with a tad bit of kick at the end. Works perfectly with the bread. 

I had the jerk swordfish and it was amazing. The pineapple salsa offset the sweetness of the swordfish. However, my only complaint is that there were TONS of beans on my rice. I understand it's beans and rice, but it was probably over half a can. 

My parents had the Caribbean snapper and both loved it. The curry shrimp on the side had lots of flavor, but didn't overpower the delicious snapper. The rice also mixed with the curry sauce, which were a perfect combo.

The staff were very friendly and attentive. My water glass never went empty, but not to the point that it was annoying. Great service. Good came out surprisingly fast for how busy they were. 

Overall, it was excellent. The fish tank from "Tanked" was a great view. 20/10 recommended going there. It's a little pricy, but definitely worth it.

text:
What an exceptional experience! I had a terrible day, got lost, and showed up at the reservation late. The GPS sent me to Berwyn for some reason. We walked in got sat quickly and the front desk staff were so accommodating. I did almost walk into 'Harvest' they are right next door. text:
If you are from Tampa, the Thai Temple is a must visit. Before you go be sure to show up early as parking is limited. Also, the noodle line can get very long (and for good reason) before they even start serving, so trust me, go early. Also, remember to bring cash since they do not except any other payment types. Lastly, please dress appropriately, there are far too many people who do not dress up at all for this and it does come off as a little disrespectful since this is a Temple.

There is a whole lot of seating but this place is very popular and all of the picnic tables along the river will fill up fast. You may have to share a table with some other patrons but most of the visitors are very friendly.

When you are done with your meal make sure you take some time to enjoy the view of the river. They also have some tables set up in the corner selling a variety of unique fruits and plants. Some of them are pretty cool and if I had a better patio at my home I would have bought a few of them.

text:
Decided to stop by on a Friday for happy hour.

I started off with their old fashion(ed). Perfect amount of bitterness and sweetness. Just an excellent old fashioned. Plus, it's only $6.

We ordered a couple happy hour items, the arancini and the toast. Arancini was good. It came in a hot skillet and was very crispy. The sauce was on point. The toast was fantastic! Delicious whipped blue cheese spread with olive oil and tomatoes on top of a perfectly toasted sourdough bread. Absolutely amazing. I wished we had ordered a bunch more toast.

I had the fremont burger for my main and my wife had the fish sandwich. The burger was cooked a tad over (I asked for medium-rare). The saltiness and the creaminess from the blue cheese with the sweetness from the red onion marmalade truly made it a perfect combination and it was all encased in a delicately toasted brioche bun. The fish sandwich was amazing as well. The caper lemon mayo truly enhanced the flavor of the beautifully cooked mahi mahi. It was delicious.

Excellent food. Complimentary valet parking. Great service. All the makings of an excellent restaurant.
name: Paul

text:
Two nights in a row. Had the Oyster BLT poboy. Scazeracs spot on good. Oysters BLT poboy off the hook. Here are my dings. Sandwich = awesome, battered fries served two nights in a row room temperature. French onion soup nice presentation but crock half empty instead of flowing over. ( over salted as well imop) NOLA blonde beer = happiness. Second night the sandwich was 3/4 the size the night before. 

Bar staff awesome and engaging. 

Good joint just lacking a bit on the quality control. Keep up the good work
name: Kile

text: Food was just Ok. I had fajitas and the chicken was pretty dry. My wife had a chicken burrito but we couldn't find much chicken in it. Every table got chips and salsa upon sitting down except the tables our server had. I'm really hopping these are just issues that will get worked out with them being open longer, but we'll probably wait awhile before giving them a second chance.  Overall disappointing.
name: Andrew

text: This is a first for me....it's the first I've ever gone to a place with great Yelp reviews, and then was totally let down.   I actually only wanted to give Detroit Coney Island 2 stars, but the service there was truly excellent.  The food however was hugely disappointing & the prices seemed very high.  There were two of us, & we each ordered a Coney & fries with just tap water for our drinks.  The bill with tax & tip was nearly $20!  Seriously the Coney was just an average hot dog with chili & onions.  I must be missing something here.
name: Alan

text: price felt a touch high for what it was. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Food was fresh and service was quick. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. A very pleasant experience. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Food was good and came out fast.
name: User

text: This little unassuming place sports two things - a friendly owner and a really good plate of food. The general feel of this place is very low key - not somewhere you would take someone for a formal date or impress them with the decor. However, you will enjoy the food and there is plenty of it!  The combo gyro plate includes a selection of yellow rice, salad, tabouli, chicken, gyro meat and naan bread - all of it excellent in flavor. I have not tried the pizza or calzones, but the Greek items are definitely worth a try. Finally, the owner (who wears many "hats" there) is kind and attentive. Not upscale, but definitely worth your time if you are visiting Nashville Shores or venture over into the Hermitage area.
name: Frank

text: Stopped in with a friend for some post-quarter drinks and food. Sat the bar with Jonathan and had great conversation, drinks & food. The shrimp fritters were delicious and the rigatoni was perfect. This place is perfect for date night or a stop on night out with a few friends.
name: Allie

text: I love the environment, the dishes and all the free add-on's, the attentive servers, the price, and especially the taste! This has become a local favorite of mine!
name: Eric

text:
Fantastic experience at this wonderful restaurant! Everything was outstanding start to finish. Our waitress Tori was so kind and accommodating. My best friend has a milk allergy, like full blown anaphylaxis no B.S. Tori worked with the chef to custom make my friend a fantastic entree. 

For appetizers my friend and her boyfriend had the Tuna Tartare and I had the Lobster Ravioli. Both were delightful. For our entrees, I had the Scalibut, the gentleman of our party the Red Snapper and my friend enjoyed her dairy free entree with grouper at the center. For dessert, the vegan Samoa was thoroughly enjoyed by my friend and I found the Carême brûlée to be delicious and a huge portion. I also found the red wine selection to be excellent. 

If you're in town please try to make it to GWFins, you won't regret it!!
name: Lindsey

text: This place makes really good tiramisu, flan, and macaroons, and Delice. But stay clear of the napoleon. It is harder than cardboard and the custard part isn't very good either.
name: Ethan

text: good southern fried spicy chicken. Note: consider spice to be ONE STEP HIGHER when you order: I ordered Hot and it tasted XHot., wish I had ordered Medium which woulda been equivalent of Hot. Their range is: plain/mild/medium/hot/Xhot/XXhot. this place is nicer and larger than their Ewing Dr branch. not as tasty as Gus chicken (Memphis which is amazing). waited 45 mins on a weekday non-busy time lol but worth it. they have so many ppl waiting for takeouts - tells how popular they are. V friendly service, felt like a sports bar with Xle TVs playing sports channels
name: Raakesh

text:
Have been meaning to try this restaurant for over a year. It is always crowded when we pass. Finally got a chance this past weekend. 

When we first walked in, the staff was pleasant and welcoming. The decor, however, was somewhat off-putting. We were seated in a back room with old paneled walls and small tables with the kind of wooden chairs that were popular in the '70s, and dated carpeting. 

We ordered a bottle of wine (decent wine list) and were bought the heaviest wine goblets you can image. When we asked for lighter glasses, we were told they didn't have any and some patrons bring their own glasses! Okay, note to self for next time, which there will be because...

The food! This is why I'm a fan. We started with sharing an appetizer of Fiocchi. They were absolutely delicious and served in a perfect brown butter sauce. 

The veal abruzzi was excellent with all of the ingredients melding together to make an outstanding dish. Also ordered the chicken arrabiata. When I think arrabiata, I think heat. While the dish did have a little background heat, it was too lemony and reminded me more of a piccata without the capers. Both dishes were served with an al dente pasta.

We shared the lemon Napoleon, which had a beautiful lemon curd. It was a great way to end the meal (along with a cappuccino). 

We're looking forward to trying some of the other entrees next time.
name: J

text: The restaurant is really tiny, but boy is it delicious. Had the avocado toast with potato salad and dirty chai latte. Everything was perfectly seasoned. The potato salad had a kick of curry and was very creative. The toast was super pretty and flavorful. It had more than just the avocado on it. And you can tell the bread is good quality bread. Overall just great.
name: Paige

text: I made a reservation in Open Table for Friday night March 16th for 7:30.  We showed up at 7:30 only to have out name put at the bottom of a long list by the owner.  I said "we have a reservation" he said "do you expect to show up and have a table waiting for you".  We left.  I have dined here for years with my family for special occasions and just casual dinners now and then.  I will NEVER eat here again.  The owner was rude and unapologetic.  If you take reservations you should honor them.  We will take our money and spend it where it's appreciated.  So long Casa Ludovico.
name: Kellie

text: This is a newer location and I have just visited once so far but like always my usual was amazing! Carne Assad's fries and shrimp tacos. Will check in again at my second visit
name: Jennifer

text: Yummy! Overstuffed pulled pork sandwich is enough for two meals, so go hungry. Friendly service, nice atmosphere and clean restroom!  I wish them much success in a rather tricky  location that has changed themes way too often.
name: Janet

text: Love this place.  Great food and they deliver on the east side!  Awesome Pho, Spring Rolls, and Fried rice!  Friendly staff as well.
name: Chris

text: Burger Study exceeded all of my expectations and then some. We rolled into Indianapolis on Friday night and were hopeful for this burger joint. Our server named Gabby was very nice and helpful. I ordered the Double Major. It is two thin patties,American cheese, pickles, lettuce, and their signature "Study Sauce." My comrade ordered their Southwest Classic burger. He loved it! The only downside to this visit was the douchey man sitting across from us who was wearing Brutus Buckeye socks. This is not Burger Study's fault obviously. It's a shame that this wonderful city has to be contaminated with Ohio State fans for the weekend. Anyway, Burger Study is delicious and I would love to be back next time we come to Indy.
name: Emerson

text: Wow, wow, wow! Review could be done with just those three words. Amazing and authentic cuisine. Mr. & Mrs. B have created a little slice of paradise - no one could expect this st this location. Atmosphere is trendy, live music was current and relaxing. Friendly people, great food and great music...we will definitely be back. Outdoor seating is beautiful.
name: Kathleen

text:
My family and I love Los Agaves and we have never had a bad experience until yesterday 8/3... We went for lunch around 1:30ish pm .

I ordered a molcajete and my aunt ordered the carne azteca. On the menu it said both dishes come with chorizo but when we received our plates the chorizo was missing. We told the manager and he said the chorizo was being cooked. He went and brought us two pieces of chorizo. As I started eating my molcajete I noticed a small round plastic thing in my food and it was a small rubber band !! 

When I told the manager he didn't even apologized and went on saying how finding rubber bands in molcajetes was something that happens all the time. He claimed this was not the first time this has happened. In other words he told me that was normal and I shouldn't be worry about it. I told him that was not okay and how I could have eaten it and choked and he then blamed it on the cilantro? First of all my molcajete had no cilantro and if it really was part of cilantro then that means they don't wash the cilantro which is why they didn't notice the rubber band. I told him I did not want to keep eating my food and I wanted my money back. He looked kinda annoyed but gave me a refund for my plate ..

 My mom told him we knew it wasn't his fault but this was unacceptable and all he kept saying was "it was the cilantro" & "I don't know what happens in the kitchen" he then asked us if we wanted a FLAN or anything else. Uhm??? instead of asking he should of just brought us one as a way of apologizing for the bad experience especially when we payed almost $100 dollars ! Overall I was very upset with the way the "manager" handled the situation.

I'am looking forward to write a good review next time I go to Los Agaves .
name: Lilianna

text: Wonderful lunch on a rainy Thursday.  Took a suggestion from John the bartender.. Mussels Ghent style.
name: Eileen

text: Really good Thai food. Drunken noodles, chicken satay and yellow curry. Yum! And they new location is really nice.
name: Sue

text:

text: People are being a little dramatic in these comments honestly. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. I had a better visit than I expected to. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.
name: User

text: A great place to grab quick lunch when I'm in Pinellas Park. Fortunatos downtown is now closed, but you can still get their pizza in Pinellas Park. Sandwiches good too, as they've got a bunch of lunch specials (til 4pm) which adds nice variety. Tough to pass up those desserts up in the front case!
name: Tanner

text: Two stars because the chicken breast was flavorful and tender.That's the highlight.  We just moved to town recently and this was our second time trying this restaurant. The first visit was ok. Service a little slow for no apparent reason. I have read the  5 star reviews   and now I am puzzled. Maybe it depends on the time of day that you go here?  We REALLY wanted to like this place, love the decor. We tried it Tuesday afternoon; they were NOT busy. First we were seated in the bar area, and told the server will be there "in a little while". Huh??? When the meals finally came, I was served rancid corn, and when I brought it to our server's attention, she made some excuse for the kitchen, and seemed to think it was amusing. The chicken breast had a lime wedge on the side that looked like it had already been used. Condiments for the chips and salsa were tiny souffle cups that were half full.  So food was so- so. What about customer service? When the server is MIA, and you'd like a refill, while you observe employees yakking it up about personal stuff, oblivious to their customers....I guess that's MY bad? Guess  we'll look for another place before going to our movie. They must not need the business.
name: Pj

text:
Really good food and super cute atmosphere.

I was with my fiance', my mother, and my 18-month old son, and we each had something different, but they were all delicious. 

The burgers are clutch, the salmon salad was HUGE and delicious, and the turkey club probably could have fed a couple of people (I of course just ate it all myself). The fries were perfect, and even when you felt like you'd explode if you ate another bite....you'd still eat more fries. 

The shakes are money, and the music they had piped out on the outdoor patio was perfect 90s hip hop. Loved it. 

It's a bit pricey, but you get SO MUCH FOOD....so I guess it kind of justifies it. I'd come back for sure.
name: Katrina

text: Food was good and came out fast. Also, really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Food was fresh and service was quick. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. The whole meal felt kind of uneven.
name: User

text:
So, I walk in by myself, eating alone. They recommend the bar area tables. Okay. I go in, walk around, and come back out. All the tables are still dirty from the last diners. So I ask again for a table in the dining room. "Sure." They take me to a table and put my napkin-wrapped silverware and menu on a wet table with a wet seat. At least they wiped the seat off, but c'mon! This isn't rocket science! I am able to get napkins from a busser to dry the seat, table, and menu. Okay, time to check out the menu.

Why??!

Why do some restaurants tell you which sides come with which entrees?! Maybe I don't want mashed potatoes and green beans! And why does it take the server telling me I can order any sides? Maybe, me being the customer, they could just let me decide from the beginning.

How was the food?
The sides were serviceable. The steak was cooked to the correct point. It was decent, but not exceptional.

What was really good about this whole experience? The waitress, Kelly. She was helpful, personable, and professional. I'm thankful I had her to wait my table.

Overall?
A 5 or 6 out of 10. For a chain restaurant, not too bad. If the details were considered from a customer's perspective, it would cost make it a very nice place to eat.
name: Paul

text:
A good addition to the Whyte Ave scene, Dorinku is a loud and lively izakaya offering up Japanese "street food" and drinks. We tried their pressed wild salmon sushi, spicy tuna, fried rice and chicken karaage. Overall the food was good but it wasn't "amazing".  For each of the dishes we tried, I know I've had better.  I'll probably be back to try their sashimi, ramen and other dishes. 

Service was ok considering how busy they were.  

The only oddity was that my friend had an awkward/confusing exchange with our server regarding getting change after paying cash. In the end, my friend wasn't too happy as the server seemed a bit presumptuous re: gratuity.
name: Jenny

text:
I've driven past here dozens of times but today was the first time I ever turned off the main road and wound my way down to the Cold Spring Tavern. What an amazing place! It's an old stagecoach stop, and retains all of the charm (and rickety wood construction) of its historic past.

Outside, a stream cascades down the rocks at the bottom of the canyon, and the building is surrounded by lush growth.

The restaurant is divided up into intimate rooms, with great mood lighting, and views of the woods.

Lunch offerings include salads and sandwiches and burgers. Both the chiliburger and venison steak sandwich were excellent, as were the accompanying fries and salad. Apparently the quiche is amazing, with a wonderful pastry crust, but the person before me got the last order!

Service is friendly, and the staff are definitely having a good time working there.
name: Steve

text: Brunch was great.  Chicken and Waffles were amazing.  The lamb and shrimp apps were good too.  Great Bloody Mary.  Wish there were 6 Stars
name: Jay

text: Chose this restaurant based on good Yelp reviews and proximity to our location.  The service and ambiance were great. My pescado a la Veracruzana was as good as any I ever had in Mexico, or the USA for that matter. And the topping on the evening was a troupe of local Mariachis whose performance was pitch perfect. We have already nominated El Charro for our new favorite Mexican restaurant in Tucson.
name: L

text: Local lunch place for work.  Best salads around filled with a ton of chicken grilled to perfection.  Yummy buffalo sauce hot and spicy.   Ate my lunch too fast to even take a picture.   Also try the chicken salad club pictured below its so big that you have to eat it in pieces and is delightful. Get the crinkle French fries.
name: Ilene

text: Good tasting donuts.  They fresh fill their jelly donuts when you order and they do not skimp on the filing.  Great to have a good donut shop nearby.  Thanks.
name: Edchuk

text: One of those meals where nothing is exactly wrong but you're not excited either. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. No big complaints, just a nice meal. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. so yeah kind of mixed on it. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Would probably stop in again if nearby.
name: User

text:
I do thoroughly enjoy this restaurant's food. Pork belly buns are fab. Pho is solid. 

There is one staff member that has rubbed me the wrong way.  Repeatedly. He has an overly sarcastic response to every question I have ever asked about the menu. I literally turn around from the business when I see that he's working. He's not helpful and extremely rude.
name: Meagan

text: This is our "go-to" place for breakfast on the weekends even though it's 40 minutes from home!  With fantastic gluten free and vegetarian options it meets the needs of our entire family!  The food is always fantastic and consistent!  The coffee and cocktails are exceptional as well.  The only downside is the seating because it is more open and family style versus having separate booths and tables for your family or group.
name: Carrie

text:
I got my Spanish fix, I got my Spanish fix, I got my Spanish fix, hey, hey, hey, hey!!!

I love Spanish food. I love that when you go to a Spanish restaurant its filed with culture, tradition, pride, and good food. Each restaurant has its own identify based on the type of cuisine they are severing. Freddy's is all of the above! Its like someones parents opened up a restaurant and cook everything themselves because they just LOVE to cook. 

I've had take out from here twice and both times I was left beyond happy. Yes, food makes me happy, good food makes me happy. We ordered from here from work and we knew we were in for treat when we read the menu. We ordered everything from tostonas to pepper steak and bistec empansado. Everything was seriously delicious!! 

Thank you, Freddy's! Thank you for reminding me of all the times I went to my friends house and their parents made me dinner. Thanks for reminding me of all the spanish spots in Jersey City that have dear places in my heart. 

A bit of a dramatic review but this place was that good!
name: Feebee

text:
This is a solid AYCE sushi establishment, better than your average. About 8 tables filled when I walked in on a Tuesday evening.  It is the standard two sheets of paper where you choose from items from the kitchen and second page is sushi/Maki/roll options.  Friendly service, quick refills on water, fish was fresh (not smelly).  

Will definitely visit again next time I pass through the neighborhood. Easy free parking in lot.
name: P

text: The food presentation was great, the service  was outstanding. All the items on the menu were great. You are probably asking how does he know that, I spend a week in Missouri and had the pleasure of eating there for the entire stay.
name: Jahn

text:
Can't say enough great things about this place. I had the half chicken which had the perfect amount of spice and the sweetness of the puréed carrots were a great balance to the heat. My fiancé had the hangar steak. Both meats were incredibly tender. We started with the drop biscuits, but this was probably the only part of the meal that lacked for me. What truly sealed the deal was the chocolate and hazelnut mousse. Oh. My. God. I haven't stopped talking about it in 4 days. 

We happened upon this place by pure luck but I'm so glad we did. It's also a charming little neighborhood off the beaten path which was a welcomed change from the chaos of Broadway. We would definitely go again!
name: Lauren

text: The food was tasty, but our second waiter (trainee waiter?) declared that he was sick "it's not contagious. That's just why I'm not talking." which didn't excuse his bizarre, unpleasant demeanor. At no point did he smile or appear to enjoy his job at any level, and at numerous points he seemed confused as to what we told him and our primary waiter. Refills were an inconceivable task, and at certain moments I wasn't sure if the guy (I don't want to say his name- This was very weird and annoying, but I don't want to get him fired) was actively trying to insult us ("I wasn't sure if you were finished talking.") My mom had been very excited to take our large party to this historic restaurant, but after this experience I will be sure to avoid Antoine's in the future.
name: Jessica

text:
This would have definitely gotten 5 stars... If I had checked my to-go order before I left this place. I guess I should always check my order before I drive all the way back home to make sure they got it right. I ordered a Turkey Club Wrap with no tomato, and the girl seemed to have trouble figuring out how to do that in the system, and she did not ask one of the two coworkers standing a yard away. I would suggest having your employees read the order back to the customer to make sure everything was right. Everyone was very friendly, so I didn't think to check my order. I just wanted to get home so I could eat it because I was so excited! However, when I opened the container at home, there was not a wrap in there, but a panini. I am not sure what kind, but instead of a wrap with turkey, cheeses, avocado, and bacon in it, there was just turkey, lettuce, and red onions. I picked off the red onions and am now left with bread, lettuce, and turkey. I was so excited to try this place, and am now pretty disappointed. Always check your to-go orders...
EDIT: I decided to drive back because I really wanted the wrap, and it was the best decision. They were very accommodating and the wrap is so delicious!
name: Lauren

text:
We got to visit this restaurant during our trip to New Orleans. It was such a great idea. The restaurant is super packed and there's always a line so you know it's good. But that means you have to go early to get a good spot.

We waited about 30 minutes to get in. We sat at the oyster bar and was able to get a full menu. We ordered oysters of course. They shuck the oysters fresh right in front of you. It was super fresh.

We also ordered the wood grilled oysters. I don't usually like cooked oysters, but these were amazing. I just squeezed a bit of lemon and some hot sauce in it and it was great. 

We also ordered the jambalaya with sausage. New Orleans obviously makes the best jambalaya. It was super flavorful and the rice was perfectly al dente.

We also ordered a basket of fried shrimp because we saw it come out for someone else and it looked so good. We thought it was going to be super greasy and breaded but it actually wasn't. And the shrimps were even flavored. The fries that came with it were also very good.
name: Kieu

text: Yummy all-you-can-eat sushi. It's great and the service is awesome. I enjoy hot tea with sushi and theirs is delicious. The fish is fresh and the rice is perfect.
name: Sierra

text: Food was good, but service was terrible. Hostess and clerk were super rude. They got our order wrong, but told us we should've checked the receipt.
name: C

text: Great find in Sobro!! Street tacos are awesome! Pork was my favorite of all. Queso is amazing!! Amelia at the bar is a cutie!
name: B

text: After eating here I was shocked at the bad reviews. We all loved our meals. The fried curd and marinara was excellent. My oriental chicken was the best I ever had. Pulled pork sandwich was excellent. Their specialty drinks were amazing. Especially the margarita and some lemonade drink. Also loved the set up with live music or pool tables and darts if you wanted. The waitress was excellent.  We all left very happy and full. Would definitely return.
name: Jacqueline

text:
These are the best tacos in Tampa by far. Ribeye and carnitas tacos are always fantastic. According to friends who know what "authentic" tacos should be (I really don't), these are the real deal. I just know they taste fresh and amazing especially when you add some queso fresco and lots of lime.

Sure the wait is long, they don't have enough tables, and it's hot waiting outside. I'm excited to try their new location in hopes of having more room, but I hope it doesn't ruin the authentic vibe of the whole thing!
name: Ali

text:
I like Kansai, is good and cheaper than others restaurants around. 
Also they're super fast.
name: Daiane

text: Great environment. Definitely crowded but worth the wait! I had the shrimp andoullie corn pasta, which was amazing. The bartender was friendly and always available.
name: Alka

text: I'm from Canada traveling everywhere in North America for work. It's the only place I couldn't pay with my credit card. They say it's company policy and they need a zip code, I have seen that before but people would clear it with an ID. Not there, they didn't even seem mad when I said ok then I'll go somewhere else and left my stuff on the counter...

text: Stoped here for lunch.  Order was correct and the food was very good. Had soup and salad.  Soup was hot and delicious and the salad was excellent, great portions. Fast and friendly service, my order was brought out to me.  Will be back.
name: Katy

text: They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. The food was good and the service was easygoing. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really.
name: User

text: I wanted to like this more than I actually did. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. Nice little spot, decent portions too.
name: User

text: UME - we got the scallop roll and THAT was actually pretty good. We also got the sashimi platter. The sashimi was fine, not grade A fish but not terrible. Something you would find at ay revolving sushi bar. The shrimp, though, was dry. They definitely used just a regular ol shrimp and not sweet shrimp. We also got the Ume sample platter which is mostly a platter of their fried offerings like eggrolls, fried dumplings, cheese wontons, and chicken wings. Nothing special. The wings were the tastiest and least over-fried. We also got the ramen which was NOT ramen unfortunately. Basically, it's like they got a pack of quick noodles, frozen vegetable stir fry, and hard boiled eggs (not the soft boiled ones in authentic ramen places) and dumped them in a pot and called it ramen. I wouldn't recommend it. We ordered a seafood noodle soup. I commend them for putting a lot of toppings because most restaurants won't give you a lot of toppings and just make the bowl look full with noodles. This one was actually hearty from both the udon noodles and all the seafood in it. However, the entire dish just tasted salty. So that was also a miss. Finally, the drinks. We ordered cold sake (good; can't go wrong with Sake) and two Shiso Sexy cocktails. As my sister put it, "This cocktail is not what I expected. This is like if Windex we're a cocktail." It was STRONG and affordable  though, so if you are not much for the taste of $15 craft cocktails and just want to get hit HARD, you might enjoy have enjoyed it. GREAT service though.
name: Karsie

text: Really delicious food for a fair price! I had an omelette that was to die for paired with a bloody Mary. Definitely a great place to go for breakfast, brunch or day drinking.
name: Brittni

text: The soup was better than the sandwich, which I wasn't expecting. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Not a bad stop, just not one I'm rushing to repeat. They were out of one thing I originally wanted..
name: User

text: By far and away my favorate eatery at Armature Works!! They have a Burger 1910 on the menu that is fantastic and the Tuna Tartine is crave worthy!! Plus the "Gravy" Croissant Waffle Brunch Item is a huge favorite.  We go here 1-2 times a week and it is consistent and amazing!
name: Susan

text: Fantastic food! Location was near the LSU campus which was great! Very little wait time!
name: Nici

text: Great food, nice calm environment. Good place to come for a date, or just a night out to get away from the busy restaurants around. Check them out
name: Richard

text: For the price I expected more than this. For a busy night they handled it okay. By the time the food came out I was already annoyed. Maybe other people have better luck here. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Food was fresh and service was quick. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent.
name: User

text: Stopped by after work because I was nearby and hungry. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. I'd maybe go back, but I'd order differently next time. The food was good and the service was easygoing.

text:
Visited this place twice - once in 2013 and once in 2019. Both times,
it's absolutely blown me away.

The service has been impeccable both times - we were seated fast, given a quick and efficient run-down of specials, and waited on hand and foot.

I'm generally not used to dining at a sushi restaurant where the customized rolls are the main event, but these are spectacular. My friend and I ordered the Truffle Eel Daikon Roll (the Vetri, last time I saw it), the Bronzizzle, the Philly Style roll, and the Wasabi Tuna, which all together are enough to fill two people to the brim.

The Truffle Eel Daikon Roll is to die for - it's crunchy, packed with nice smoky and sweet eel flavor, and the shredded cucumbers on top add some nice texture and softening of taste. The Bronzizzle was also very good - many different flavors going on in one bite, and it certainly makes every roll seem more substantial. The Wasabi Tuna was perfectly sensible as well - fresh tuna, good balance of wasabi and strong flavor.

The star of the night for me, though, was the Philly Style Roll. It's a delightfully bizarre little number that combines high-quality beef, provolone cheese, and lettuce with a horseradish-aioli side dip and a hot chili pepper for garnish. Crazy, but darned if it doesn't remind you of a high-end haute cheesesteak.

Love this place and look forward to returning.

text: Hands down my favorite brunch place. Yes it even beats surrey's!! We've waited almost an hour at this place before and it's well worth the wait. The staff are always so friendly. Their lattes are the best! My favorite from the menu is their cat daddy and the chia pudding. The potato crisps are a must also. We sat at the bar one time that overlooks the kitchen which was a pretty cool experience. Getting to watch the chefs execute everything. This place doesn't take rsvp so be prepared to wait. text: The first time I went I was impressed by the service, food, beer and ambiance. I went back a week later and had a completely different experience. The Pretzel Nugs were very hard (to the point where I literally couldn't eat them), our service was mediocre at best and manager working behind the bar was beyond rude. text:
I was visiting my girlfriend in Philadelphia and she made a reservation at Scarpetta because it was near her apartment and had availability on a Friday night. What was expected to be a pleasant Friday evening turned into an infuriating dining experience.
 
To start, we were seated behind a pillar and no one attended to us for the first 15 minutes. I noticed four Caucasian girls were seated behind us after us and were immediately greeted with menus and glasses of water. Our designated waiter realized we were waiting without menus after flirting with the four girls for a good 5 minutes. (Fred C.) had a look of -oh shit- written across his face. He finally came by with menus and asked what type of water we wanted.
 
After taking our order, we still did not receive our water and two Caucasian girls were seated next to us. We finally received our water after they served us our drinks. Then, we noticed the girls next to us received their bread basket, and yet again, our table did not. Our appetizers came and still our bread never came. We had to bring it to the waiter's attention and THEN he immediately brought our bread basket over.
 
It was becoming difficult to feel like this was not an act of discrimination. We brought it to the attention of the manager and he responded with "Sorry, it is really busy. We will give you an extra dessert." I am not sure why he thought dessert would fix everything and he completely ignored the fact that we felt neglected throughout the entire dining experience thus far. It felt like he wanted the dessert to shut us up and it would make up for all the mistreatment at a dinner I am paying for with my time and money. It seems obvious a restaurant would be busy on a Friday night, and so why was that an excuse? Did he want a pity party? Did he want us to sympathize with him and manage the restaurant for him? I've been to busier restaurants with impeccable service despite the crowds. (Honestly, it wasn't even that busy for a Friday night.)
 
Finally, the bill came and instead of charging my girlfriend and I for the glass of wine we ordered, he charged us each for a bottle. I was livid and done with the entire experience at that point. I probably should have walked out the first 15 minutes. Safe to say I will not come back just to pay to be treated with negligence for an hour of my life I will never get back.
name: Tiffany

text: Fun, quirky environment with a delicious selection of interesting breakfast items and especially loved the fresh squeezed OJ. Will definitely be returning!

text: Thank you Yelp again for the good recommendation. Did not disappoint. Super clean and excellent food!

text: We love this place. Over time, we've even come to prefer the grilled chicken over the hamburgers. Excellent flavor and prepared perfectly. Fantastic shakes, when they have them. Recently, I've noticed a lack of truffle on the Parmesan truffle fries. Loads of Parm, but lately the truffle is gone. Not sure what's up with that. Definitely a staple in our rotation nonetheless. Bring back the truffle!

text: My first Korean meal. A little afraid coming into restaurant. Very friendly and comfortable ambiance. Quickly seated. I told fine waiter that I had no idea but that I liked spicy and great beer. He recommended Spicy Galbi (short ribs) and Korean lager Kloud. While waiting four tasty appetizers arrived, one being Kimchee, which I had heard mixed reviews about. Well, the kimchi did not have a bad smell at all, and was quite delicious, along with the other 3 free appetizers. The main dish arrived sizzling and incredibly yummy. Then the attentive waiter brought another free round of those great appetizers with a couple of new dishes.  The beers were perfect and cooked palate along with rice and three other side dishes of yummy vegetables.  Quite a successful initiation into the world of delicious Korean cuisine, at a very reasonable price.

text: Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The sauces helped more than I thought they would..

My panini was filled to overflowing and I had to take half of it home.  My son had a giant slice of Sicilian pizza and loved it.  We found a new favorite place.

text: It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all.
name: User

text:
Among walking in, it looked like nothing special, the menu was somewhat overwhelming so I order my usual caramel macchiato and Alec got a Red Eye. Both were enjoyable! 

Later, after reviewing the menu we decided to order a pizza! So many choices but we went for the cheesy garlic bread an a small chicken spinach  Alfredo pizza (olives on  my half) perfect for two!

DELICIOUS! 
 
Full of fresh ingredients and gooey cheese! 
No regrets. 
I'm hoping to try the Picasso next time!

text:
Hands down, these are the best wings I've ever had. As a fat, middle aged guy, I've had plenty (really, too many) wings over the years and all of their flavors are fantastic.

I've had their regular pizza, which is solid and their deep dish, which is borderline great (but a little small), but no place in Pinellas county can touch their wings.

This place has a great beach-bum feel even though it's a couple miles inland. The owner, Lucas, is quite possibly the most personable owner I've ever met at a restaurant. He goes out of his way to make everyone feel welcome and he tries to learn your name if he recognizes you.

If you're looking for a relaxing place to have a wide selection of draft beers (approx 20 on tap), some good food and feel like you're amongst friends, make sure to stop in Tikanis!

Also, in case I wasn't clear earlier, GET THE WINGS!!
name: Dan

text: I ordered General Tso chicken for lunch last Friday and I got extreme food poisoning within a matter of hours. I had to cancel evening plans with my family, skip dinner and I felt sick till Saturday afternoon. It was my second and the last time ordering food from this restaurant.
name: Iryna

text: I hadn't been there in years and went there for dinner and a movie date night with my wife.  Fortunately the waitress was great and the soup was very good.  After that, the meal was all downhill from there.  The chicken croquettes I ordered were bland and the coating soft, not crunchy.  The bed of mashed potatoes they were on was thin and bland.  The potatoes were almost runny.  The stewed tomatoes were a waste of table space.  My wife ordered penne pasta with alfredo sauce.  She can't eat alfredo many places because of the richness and spices.  This dish was just the opposite.  After dumping half the grated cheese onto the meal, it finally had a flavor other than plain white sauce.  The penne were cooked well and were not al dente.  I took the leftovers home and mixed it with another sauce to make it presentable.  Then came the coup de grace:  the Oreo Cake!  A fantastic looking chocolate layer cake with Oreo crumbs!  My how looks are deceiving!  A chocolate layer cake that was so bland that Julia Child is turning in her grave!  Diners are supposed to have great food.  This is definitely the exception.  At least I had a coupon to lessen the blow of a miserable meal!.  At least the movie made up for the lousy dinner.  I won't be returning for many years to come.
name: Mach1mustangman

text: I wanted to like this place but it was so ridiculously crowded, with barely any space to move, and most stores having lines that were way to long. Siting is very very limited. Unless you're going during less busy times, I'm not sure it's worth it.

text:
Taco restaurant located right in DT Boise. 

The food: Great food. We had the chips and salsa and their version of queso dip, both were really good. The tacos were bigger than I anticipated definitely should have only ordered two instead of four. Everything thing we had was packed with flavor. 

The service: We had a great server checked in us often but not too often. Very friendly. 

The decor: Very open and clean spot, they also have different music playing on different nights. 

Overall: this place gives of a very friendly vibe we had good conversation with the couple next to us, not all places give off such a vibe that people feel comfortable enough to chat with neighbors.

text: This place has come a long way since they've opened.  In the beginning I probably would have only given it three stars.  The service was very inconsistent and the food was so so.  Things have definitely improved.  The service has gotten much better, servers actually recognize that they are not just there to hang out and ignore you or feel that they are too cool or above the fact.  The menu lately has been really great the cauliflower appetizer is amazing - sriracha and buffalo flavors, had the vedge meatballs recently and really enjoyed them.  The acai bowl is good as are the smoothies and the desserts are delicious as well I really like the one avocado chocolate one (excluding the donuts, not a huge fan of them as I find them a bit dense and heavy).  Recommend for any time of the day really... brunch/lunch and dinner.

text: Easily my favorite restaurant in Tucson! I've been eating at Yoshimatsu for what seems like forever, at the relatively new and former location. text:
Giving this place a solid 4.   The bottom line is... The food is tasty and fresh and the service was good.   

I ordered the Carnita Bowl and I the meat was sprinkled on the top with a mountain of rice and beans underneath.   It felt like the ratio was a little off.  

The music was super loud and I'm no old lady... I love when the jamz are pumping but I had to lean over several times to hear what my friends were saying.  

The restroom was the most memorable part of the meal.  I entered the single bathroom and as soon as I locked the door the song, "It's raining tacos" played for the entirety of my time in there.  Not gonna lie... it made me smile and dance a little and I'm tempted to go back and see if it's programmed to do that each time someone goes in or if I just have impeccable timing.
