text:
Ok so I like this place, I can't lie. It's everything you expect. Busy, loud and slow. Awesome burgers and fries and it opens late. Beer to choose from and liquor to drown your sorrows. Details bellow:

Big place but they seem like they are always full, can they make the place any bigger, rooftop? I do like their tables. They have a few big booths that could fit 4* people on each side (*not children size smarty pants but in my opinion) and a big table in the middle that can fit all the yummy food you'll order. They have a candy cane shape bar (that's what it looks to me anyway, it has a short side then curves and it goes longer till it hit the kitchen door/wall. I think it works for the layout and is big enough for the place. They have a few high top tables at the entrance and yes it's going to look like that's it, just keep going there's more to the back. The lady's bathrooms are big and they were clean enough. They could use some Beyoncé, they are a bit dated. I like that they do have a changing table and children are allowed until 5pm. Not sure if it is just during the week days or weekends too. 

Food: Taste is good. I like their burgers and I like that they have waffle shape fries! Those are my favorite shape if I had to pick and if they are seasoned* even better! (*they don't have seasoned fries though FYI, sorry.) 2 of us had the regular bacon cheeseburger and 2 had a burger with guacamole and egg? Everything was delicious! 

Service: this is definitely a hit and miss for me. I've been here before and the service wasn't the best and when it has been good, this was one of the not so good ones. It wasn't horrible but it could of have been a bit friendlier.

Cleanliness: average I guess for the type of decoration and atmosphere. I couldn't see the kitchen but their score was good so I guess I thrust the professionals there. 

Overall I will definitely be coming back every now and then to get me some good burgers.
name: Veronica

text: Do yourself a favor and buy TV dinners from the frozen aisle in Publix if you want to eat here.
name: Caraleine

text:
Save your money and eat somewhere authentic ! The decor is amazing however the food menu is overpriced and under portioned. Feels like a hipster Mexican restaurant. I've been a couple times and won't be back.

Update.
I thought I'd come back and give this place another shot ! I went for taco Tuesday so at least the tacos were fairly priced at half off.
The pork in their "al pastor" taco tastes like it came from the slow cooker but was cold and the steak tacos were very underwhelming. I'm not sure that they could even pass for " tacos". They should really focus less on being a fusion Mexican and more on the actual art of
name: Steph

text: Great food with something for everyone. Space is a really cool example of repurposing old and ugly into new and beautiful.
name: Derek

text:
We LOVE going to Maggie's. We decided to try it because it had great ratings and we wanted to see what it was about. We got there and the customer service was delightful to match the great food and affordable prices. The person at the register is very helpful and knowledgeable of the menu. 
While you wait for your food they bring out this super cute and delicious zucchini soup. I'm not a fan of zucchini but oh my god this soup is so good. Just enough for while you wait. It's delicious. Then they bring our your drink. We've tried the orange juice and the strawberry banana shake and it's so fresh I can tell they just made it. Within 5-7 minutes of ordering your food is ready. Very fresh and delicious. 
I've tried the huevos con chorizo and it was amazing! Next I tried the chorizo breakfast burrito and I was not dissatisfied at all. It's so big and cut in half for convenience. I was surprised my breakfast burrito came with a tiny side of flan, I love flan! After we paid they gave us two pastries to go. We didn't even order it but I think it was like a thank you to the customer. 
We live in California but every time we come to Reno, Maggie's is a must. I salute the lady making the food in the back, not sure if that's Maggie but she is very good on the grill!
name: Kassandra

text:
We love the griddle, it is our go to place for brunch. They have amazing crepes and omelettes. The orange juice is as fresh as you can get! Must go to place. 
If you go on Saturday or Sunday make sure you get there early or be willing to wait 40 minutes to an hour. I would say unless you are totally starving it is worth the wait.
name: Tori

text:
It was okay. 

This restaurant made me feel like I was at a Denny's or some other diner with no love in their food. Of course we ordered the gumbo but we were unimpressed. It tasted fine but so so so plain. 

If you're here for a week, sure, try this place if you're walking by and you're hungry. If you're here for a weekend, just don't.
name: Stacey

text: What happened to Davio's, my favorite after work spot? First they got rid of the complementary happy hour food, which were slices of gourmet pizza, cheesesteak spring rolls, and olives. Then they changed the cozy sofa setting to tables and chairs. I have been a Davio's Center City Philadelphia regular for 15 years and I am very saddened to see how the happy hour vibe has changed.
name: Cindy

text: We order from them frequently because they are so close by.  But it's sometimes hit or miss.  Twice I ordered eggplant parm and they sent chicken parm instead.  Food is decent, nothing spectacular.
name: Jackie

text:
Wow. So happy to have found this place. The fried tofu appetizer was crunchy outside and soft inside with a wonderful sauce. Vegetable Pad Thai was full of flavor without being too spicy hot. Service was on par with expectations. Served so much food that have leftovers for tomorrow's lunch. I will definitely be back.
Second time here. Tried Volcano Shrimp. Fantastic! Service was actually better than first time here, and first time here the service was fine. The coconut lemon grass chicken soup was a great starter with the egg rolls. I can't wait to come back and try something else.
name: Jim

text: Great place for football game day! Over 12 large TVs and cheap drink specials. Food was fast, hot and really well priced! I got 3 specialty drafts and a sandwich with fries for $17!
name: Emily

text: It was ok, I went for breakfast and the bacon was soooo hard. I paid extra for bacon on the side and I was unsatisfied. I also got the dungeons crab Benedict, the reviews don't lie, it was OK. Wasn't that good and definitely not worth the price. Very upset about the food, they have a nice name, nice restaurant, and the employees + manager are nice but the food is whatever. Really hope The Row gets there act together.
name: Gemelie

text: I was disappointed in the service not enough staff for the amount of people. Food took forever my steak was supposed to be medium and it was Cold Completely Red inside. Just disappointed
name: Heather

text:
Went on a Monday at 5:30 with no wait for a table.  It was beautiful outside!  

Fish tacos are delicious for sure!  Rice needs some flavor.  I ordered with sweet potato fries the last visit and will go back to that or an alternative side.  My daughter had the dirty Mac n cheese for her entree and said it was good. 

Love the outside seating and ability to wander over to the Monon and walk the food off!  

Definitely a gem in Broad Ripple.
name: Kensuewoo

text:
EXTREMELY Disappointing

I ordered $90 in pastry, breakfast, and dinner rolls online to be picked up Christmas eve morning.  They were indeed ready when I got there, but I would have preferred they wouldn't have had the order ready and waited until the dough was actually cooked before packing my order.  I'm assuming it was because of the Christmas rush that they were trying to crank out so many that they were all half done balls of gooey dough.  Only the fruit pastries were cooked through, the tray of 24 breakfast balls and all 3 trays of dinner rolls were terribly (not even) half baked, with soggy, wet bottoms.  We ended up having to cook them for about 20 minutes to get the dough cooked inside...and some of us just dug the middle out of the raw breakfast dough, ate the filling, and threw the raw dough ball away.  I hope this was just a bad day, but I'm not willing to spend money to find out.
name: Eunice

text:
Years ago I checked out this locations predecessor, A taste of Key West which was a divey glorified Tiki Hut with a great view.  Apparently the township bought the property and worked with some local chefs to combine the marina with a restaurant.  The buildings outside is beautiful and the inside is very nice.  The outside seating along the water is great, the outside bar, which has retracting doors to give you an unobscured view to the water is a great touch.  If you go deeper inside you have a nice standard sports bar tucked away from the outside and the elements.  
The bar areas have a lot of seating options and TV's.  Ambiance wise this is a great place.

I decided to sit at the "outside" bar facing the water which provided a great view.  The bartender was really nice and friendly.  The food ... well it was ok.  I ordered a Cubano sandwich which took forever and when the bartender noticed that, she comped me a beer.  Good move!  My sandwich finally came out and had a soggy bottom.  Not a good move! The Cubano Sandwich - Mojo marinated pork, fire smoked ham, spicy garlic pickles, cumin spiced mustard & swiss on Cuban panini bread.  The panini bread was not flat/pressed so it was puffy and didn't have that slight crispiness.  The flavors were a bit unbalanced and the mustard was plain yellow mustard.  It was a let down.

I think on my next trip I'll get a salad and enjoy the view of the boats and the Darby Creek.  They get four stars because of the ambiance (for this area of delco it's tough to find a view like this) and the bartender, but the food was a 2.5-3.
name: John

text:
I have driven by this Cuban restaurant on Hillsborough Ave hundreds of times, so I finally stopped in on a Friday for lunch. It's a small place, with a counter when you first walk in, then about ten tables to sit at to the  right. I was sat right away as there was only one other couple in the place at the time.

The good:  Service was quick and friendly, and in no time my order for grilled grouper was in, and I had my water to drink.  Plus, complimentary bread with garlic butter spread on top was brought out, and it was delicious.

The okay:  My food came quickly, and sadly, my grouper was not cooked all the way through, so I had to send it back. Once it returned it was good, although a bit more garlicky than I had expected. The yuca and tostones served with it were excellent.

The not great:  The menu is in Spanish with brief English descriptions (mine simply said "grouper" on the menu). I wish it was a bit more explanatory.  Also, for being so small, the place was surprisingly loud.  The chef in the back was non-stop pounding on something, a baby was crying, and another customer was talking loudly on his phone the entire time, plus television and overhead music were on.  Finally, they automatically added on a "Thanks (10%)" on to the bill, and didn't say anything about it. Is that a non-Cuban person tax?  A tax for being a woman?  A solo-person tax?  I could understand it if I were getting an item to go, but not for someone dining in.  I was very tempted not to add anything additional, but felt too guilty, and did.

One and done; this just wasn't my kind of place.
name: Karen

text:
Went here for dinner with friends and they have really good food. My friends loved their Pho Noodle Soup. I couldn't try it since it was not vegetarian (made with beef broth). 

I ordered their vegetable spring rolls for starters and garlic eggplant for the main course and both were super yum! Definitely recommend this place. 

Service is a little slow though since the place is super packed. But it's totally worth the wait. Will surely make another visit to this place before I leave Franklin.
name: Lalitha

text: I don't really get some of the harsh reviews on here. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. I had a better visit than I expected to. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait.
name: User

text: It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. Pretty happy with it overall. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh.
name: User

text:
Ordered 2 items online from this store. One of the items was the wrong color. The other had a very poor fit compared to the tagged size and there was no other suitable size to exchange for (the smallest size was way too big).

Even after an interaction with customer support, I was forced to pay for return shipping. It's too bad, the quality of the garments was OK, but if anything goes wrong, in my experience you will be left footing the bill.
name: Charles

text: Terrible food, bad service, and music was just ok. Skip this one. There are plenty of other places to go in Nashville. Try Skulls Rainbow Room!
name: Sarah

text: Gets one star for good service and one for a cool concept (different floors offer cool views and a mix of vibes). But the menu was uninspired and the food overpriced. Everything was cooked fine, to be fair. But for the price, I'd expect a little more invention. Or if you're going to keep those dishes, drop the prices 20%.
name: Doug

text:
Nice!  Wish there were a better selection of tables and how they are set up. Kind of row seating. Social seating. Sort of. Once you (we) got beyond that...enjoyed it!

Had escargot. Yum. Nice. Lots of garlic butter shredded beef etc etc. delicious!  I want more!  

Had their stuffed lobster with green corn tamale.  I liked it. The tamale was good!  The lobster was cooked right!  Nice seasoning and presented well. A total mess to eat!  Got to crack the claws etc. So be prepared. However it is enjoyable.  Had tres leches for desert. Can it go wrong with that!

Clean!  Friendly service.
name: Gene

text: No big complaints, just a nice meal. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. The food was good and the service was easygoing. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Food was good and came out fast. For the price I expected more than this. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text:
Stopped by this bike shop a few days ago ..
was NOT impressed . especially the owner, who was rude, & short with me . their prices are very high... the service is lacking & a long ass wait of one week time to return my bike, which i brought in for a tune up .
thanks , but NO THANKS . there are much, much better bike shops out there who's employees are professional,  courteous, & more knowledgeable with much better pricing .,
i would NOT recommend this shop to anyone.
name: J

text: This was a delivery order on a night when I really did not want to cook. Also, it looked better online than it did in person. Honestly, it felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The food was good and the service was easygoing. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. The food was good and the service was easygoing.
name: User

text: The drunken noodles are good, but the red curry wasn't.  Ill never go back to a Thai restaurant that doesn't use Thai red peppers for heat.
name: Pink

text:
First trip to M3. And it feels like you about to walk into a day spa. The building definitely does not look like a restaurant out front. Once inside you are greeted by a warm ambiance and friendly staff.
Menu is good and you will find mostly american classics and some pizza.
Try the grilled artichoke app. Its great.
My wife had the goat cheese pizza which she loved and my burger was great. Perfectly cooked and really juicy.
Prices were on point with any other place in town serving quality food.
My only complaint would be the beer selection. The rotating tap was 805. I like 805 but shouldnt they be highlighting a local beer? The lack of local beer is a bit dissapointing.
name: Mickey

text:
As good as downtown on the Canal.
Gourmet Burgers.
Friendly!
Another winner in Carmel.
name: Phil

text: I went with a rather large group for lunch and so we ended up needing two tables. While our waiter was attentive, he ended up forgetting about two of our dishes. However, the food was very flavorful and in large portions.
name: Lauren

text: I like the food but when I got home I was sick.. It makes sense this place according to the health has roaches, that were found in July.
name: Ranae

text:
This place is amazing! The bartenders (Blake and "Yellow" Catherine) are super friendly and attentive! 

Make sure you come early if you are here for their absolute STEAL DEAL for the crawfish!!! It's only $20 for a tray that you fill up!! And it can easily weigh between 3.5-4lbs!! 

Yes there are corns and sausages as well!! The flavors are so delicious and on point! 

Best part of my New Orleans trip for Crawfish!
name: Elton

text:
Tldr; subpar food with subpar service, especially when dealing with large parties.   Drinks are strong and seems like a good happy hour, if you're into that. Would not go back, especially since there is so much amazing food in Chinatown. 
 
We made a group reservation for a large party, and even though we arrived within 5 minutes, it took another 40 minutes to get seated. From there it took another 30 min to put in our orders and another hour to get our food. It was super busy and hard to flag down anyone to help us with our order. 

I ordered the mapo tofu and it was very salty. The portions were large, but it was so salty that I couldn't even finish it and ended up throwing my leftovers away (which I never do). 

Saving grace at the end was the waitress being nice enough to split the check 9 ways and the waitress being apologetic about the long wait. They are also accommodating for food allergies and are vegetarian friendly.
name: Daisy

text: The sauce carried most of the meal. The staff seemed tired but still polite. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text: We had a great experience on our first visit. I'd recommend the wings and watermelon soju. I'd stay away from their shumai, I'm pretty sure they buy it frozen and just heat up. It may have been a slow night for them, but our service was pretty good.
name: Lauren

text: Nice workers at this store. Consistent offerings. Clean dining room. What more could you want?
name: Matt

text:
The good: The arepas my partner and I tried (#8 and #10 ) were tasty and the portions were large. They can definitely hold their own against arepas sold elsewhere, and the prices are super reasonable. 

The bad: My partner and I sat at the counter so we were able to witness an employee wear THE SAME pair of gloves the ENTIRE time we were there. She did everything while wearing that one pair: rolled silverware, scratched her hair, wiped down dirty tables with a rag that had not been sitting in a sanitizer bucket, wiped her hands on her apron, stuck her hand in a bag of fruit and veggies to make a smoothie. You name it, she did it with that one pair of gloves.

Even though my stomach turned at the sight of it, I still ate the food because I couldn't see what was happening with the actual preparation of my food as the kitchen is in a separate room and she was on the floor while the food was prepared. Plus, I often perform sanitation audits for my job so I know the frightening things that happen in kitchens, and consequently, the risks I take every time I eat out. I like the ignorance is bliss experience though. 

I do feel guilty for not warning the poor soul who received the smoothie. I hope the dirty rag she touched before making it didn't contain bad germs and the person was none the wiser, perhaps even in a state of bliss.
name: Mary

text: The food came out fast, which was good because we were starving. The wait wasnt awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. The staff seemed tired but still polite. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. Idk, my pasta was decent and not overcooked, which i appreciated because that happens a lot. so yeah kind of mixed on it. Ordered a few things and liked most of it.
name: User

text: Extremely low staffed after the Music City Bowl Game. We needed to order from the bar while sitting at the table. Checkin in cop salad was like rubber and fried pickles were extremely greasy. The drinks were good.
name: Bill

text: Great outdoor atmosphere, great service from Brianne and a very delicious and strong Hurricane. We also bought a couple Koozies for $1.50 each which I couldn't believe how cheap. Neat experience.
name: Daniel

text: In my two prior visits would give 4 or 5 stars.  This time we got water then waited 30 Minutes for bread, 45 minues or so for salad and an antipasto plate, 60 Minutes for wine (they were out of glasses), and well over an hour for entrees.  The antipasto salad for two was a pile of lettuce, 3 pieces of salami, 2 peces of cheese and a few olives; hardly worth 13 bucks.  The pasta sauce was bland on the entrees.   Part of the order was wrong.  The server was slow and mostly absent.  We took turns going to the bathroom and looking for him to find out where our orders were. He as new and apologized but there was no offer to adjust the bill.  If you're going to spend your hard earned money on dinner there are better choices.
name: Rick

text:
Fast service!
Delicious broth and pho!
name: Andy

text:
Dispite seeing bad reviews, I was impressed by this IHOP. On a Saturday morning, I was seated right away, I was served promptly, and received my food in a short amount of time. Parking was plentiful and the staff was friendly.

As for the food, its IHOP. It's as good as what you expect in any. If you like it you like it if you dont you dont.
name: Matt

text: Serial grillers was delicious their sandwiches, salad, and wings did not dissapoint. It has a cozy  inviting environment that is very spacious with a cool but classy horror theme to go along with the  a helpful fun staff. I will definitely be coming back... also their soda machine was on point.
name: Jordan

text: Went there a couple of days after they first opened. Food was terrific but the service was terrible. We chalked it up to only being open for a couple of days. Went back a month later with a friend to give a second try. My friend waited 10 minutes at the front of the restaurant no eye contact no nothing. When I arrived she went to the owner who said take a seat anywhere. We did....waited another 10 minutes. Numerous restaurant employees passed our table....no eye contact no acknowledgment.....we got up and left, no one even noticed.  We walked a block to Royal Boucherie and were treated liked Royalty.
name: Rachel

text:
Awesome quantity & quality for your $$, it's not the best Chinese food I've ever  had or the cheapest - but it is the best first GE price,always friendly staff, always accurate with my order, typically walk in , and out within 10
Minutes with my order
name: Kevin

text:
If you're looking for good chargrilled oysters, this is the place to go! They're served sizzling hot and that just adds to the deliciousness of the oysters. We sat at the bar and the bartender, Curtis, told us not to order a half dozen because if we did, we would regret it. I'm glad we listened because they were so good a half dozen wouldn't suffice. He also told us to pair it with the Tabasco Chipotle, one of the three Tabasco sauces they offered. It added the right amount of kick and flavor to the already delightful oysters. Whatever sauce is served with the oysters pairs well with the bread they serve with the oysters. 

Next up, I tried the crawfish. They weren't that great but you also don't hear people telling you to go hear for this. The crawfish were huge but the flavor wasn't that great and there wasn't much juice in the head. I wouldn't order this here unless you desperately want crawfish like I did. 

The sides... for the sides I ordered red beans and rice and jambalaya. They were good but nothing to brag about. 

The wait... the wait is something serious during dinner time. Don't let this deter you. Experience the goodness of the oysters. This restaurant is small like many others in the area. 

Overall, come here if you want some great chargrilled oysters in a fun atmosphere. There are TVs here just in case you want to watch the game with seafood and brews.
name: Shericia

text: Great food, great service, great atmosphere! What else could you want for a five-star place! Not to mention we got one of the burgers for one penny! And it's just down the road from our house. The burgers were done exactly as we asked for and delicious.
name: Connie

text:
I can't tell you how many times I've given Lucky Dill another chance and yet another chance. Each time while paying the bill I tell myself I'm never coming back. But.... there I go again, returning for more punishment!  Their food just isn't that good people!  If you think it is then you haven't eaten elsewhere. I'm so glad I finally did and couldn't be happier and happy to report I'm eating quite well and experiencing restaurants that know how to cook and want your repeat business AND not way over priced!!!
Bye bye Unlucky Dill
name: Brian

text:
Simply amazing breakfast!!! We ate here several times during our trip to NOLA. I'm pretty sure there are no wrong choices on this menu. My personal favorite savory dish was the Chicken St. Charles eggs benedict (which I had two days in a row). My personal favorite sweet dish was the Banannas Foster Pain Perdu (I'm not even a big fan of banannas and I still thought this french toast was crazy good)! The cinnamon swirl pancakes are perfect if you like a nice lite cinnamon roll flavor. The white chocolate bread pudding was good but not as amazing as the other two sweet dishes. All the drinks were fabulous, especially the bloody marys. The Brandy Milk punch had a nice kick (similar flavor to eggnog). The wait staff was very nice and efficient. 

If you go with a friend I recommend you split two dishes between two people. Their food is simply too good to only try one dish. 

They were able to accomodate our luggage when we stopped in on our way to the airport. I strongly recommend checking in on their waitlist on the Yelp app before arriving especially if you arrive after 830 or have a party of more than 4.
name: Molly

text:
Visiting from Texas and absolutely loooved our experience here!!! Roushi was an amazing server and we WILL be back again next time. 

Sonny helped us with how to use our chop sticks (lol) and various employees stopped by our table to ensure we were enjoying our time.  Yong mei was an amazing hostess, she represents the company well and despite the 1 hour wait before getting seated, her warm smile and polite service made it worth the wait.
name: Kellie

text:
For a fast food joint I was surprised how friendly and accommodating the staff was. I phoned in when my online order was not going to be ready for another 2.5 hours! They handled it over the phone and it was ready for me shortly after I arrived. 

The location is convenient for all your center city friends to rendezvous for a quick lunch meetup! It is underneath of the Starbucks on JFK, kinda hidden in plain sight. 

The noodles were a good compliment to the saucy orange chicken. I would have liked some more color (orange from carrots and brighter green maybe from peas?) but it is fast food takeout. I'll take what I can get! 

I was not stuffed after the bowl but definitely not hungry afterwards. I am just realizing now that I forgot to eat the fortune cookie!

I've definitely had better but for $6.50 I would come back for seconds.
name: Kyle

text: Pretty much busy all the time and they don't take reservations....but it is worth the wait.  Other than that it's fantastic!  Very polite staff, large menu and food is great!
name: Michael

text: Went with family on a Sunday and it was louder than I expected. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. Food was good and came out fast.
name: User

text: The best charcuterie I have ever tasted.  Place was recommended by a friend who is a chef.  Was well worth the walk out of the French quarter to come here.  Also tried the smoked sausage and the Boudin.  If I lived here I would be stocking my fridge with the food they are producing in the deli.
name: Kevin

text:
This review's for dim sum only. China Gourmet is such a godsend for the Northeast region. Authentic dim sum with some rare finds you literally can't get anywhere else in the city, including their bbq pork buns (the crust is everything), herbal chicken feet, and sweet Phoenix buns. 

My family and I drive 40mins to come here. When you don't want to deal with parking wars in Chinatown, China Gourmet is a great option since the strip it's on has its own parking lot! 

If I had one complaint, it's that the temperature of the food kind of vary from luke warm to piping hot, but honestly that's all overshadowed by the quality and sheer variety of dishes. 

Overall, ranks among my top 3 Philly dim sum finds, the other two being Ocean Harbor in ctown and Wakano on Washington.
name: Mo

text:
Plentiful servings, DELICIOUS sauce, and tender meat.  Yay for the Reggae Grill.  

Sucks they're in the corner of such a dismal strip mall.  But perfect for take-out or a quick lunch.  The jerk pork and jerk chicken were both succulent.  The SAUCE is what makes this place though.  Perhaps they serve it on the side because it has such a kick to it?  Definitely enough food for leftovers the next day!
name: T

text: Had dinner here tonight and couldn't be happier! The meal was delicious as was the presentation.  Our server Lisa was incredibly attentive and friendly.  I highly recommend it!
name: Bill

text: I've been coming to Rocky's for many years. I've never had a chicken cheesesteak anywhere before today. This was one of the most delicious sandwiches I've ever eaten. I placed a takeout order at the counter; a small order of cheese fries And a large chicken Philly all the way. It was 10 bucks and change. The service was unbelievably fast the food was friken awesome. Of course I'll be back time and time again.
name: Natalie

text:
They're service is Com is- com sa, 

But since I've been coming there over 10 years now, the food never disappoints. 

They offer a buffet and late hours. 
You may call- in an order but don't expect them to call you when it's ready, even though they ask for your number. 

If you love spicy try my favorites
- Vindaloo
- Saag
- Chicken Masala
- The Lamb
name: Taj

text: It's nice going to a place and not having to worry if it has vegan options. This whole place is vegan. The first Saturday of the month they have a buffet which has a variety of things to choose from (soup, main dishes, sides, desserts). Prices for the buffet were reasonable as well. It was my first time there so the buffet seemed like the best option and I can honestly say everything I tried (which was a bit of EVERYTHING) was good. A few things were different but I was ok with. Will definitely be going back!!
name: Jenna

text:
Great restaurant. Steak was great. I ordered the double Eagle double bone ribeye. The staff was amazing and the atmosphere was second to none. I love their music selection and the diversity of the people there. You can pretty much wear what you want to wear from extremely casual to white or black tie. 

For the high prices, this is pretty much what I expect to receive from a prestigious restaurant. I wish all restaurants could have the same presentation as Del Frisco's Double Eagle.
name: Schoolboy

text: Food is pretty good but the service sucks big time!  They do have waterfront dining with minimum seating sometimes music outside too.
name: Eva

text: Just left this establishment. Waited about 30 min to get in and was looking forward to trying the chargrilled oysters. After 30 min we got our seafood etouffee but no oysters. I was so hungry I started on the etouffee because it was now cold. Another 20 min passed then our waiter came and told us they ran out of cheese for the chargrilled oysters so we won't be getting them. The waiter tried to make up for it by saying to order the fried oysters and if we didn't like them then we wouldn't have to pay for it. We decided to try them and didn't like them. If you don't like horseradish then you won't like the cocktail sauce that comes with the oysters and it's also in the oyster shooters. By the time we found out we weren't getting our chargrilled oysters it was 11:15p and everything nearby was closed except for olde Nola cookery.
name: Nance_

text: We had food delivered and it was really good. The marinated chicken in the tacos was delish but my favorite was the guacamole and homemade tortilla chips. Oh my gosh! Amazing. I was impressed!
name: LaToya

text: I have driven past this restaurant on numerous of occasions and decided to take a good friend of mine out while she was visiting the Philadelphia. I was dying to try this ceviche because that is what is advertised on the marquee. So then I was told by the waitress who was a sweetheart that this ceviche is more so an appetizer which I found to be quite interesting and priced at $17. The taste was horrible. My appetizer was delicious but as someone mentioned below it came out at the same time as the entree.The waitress kept apologizing for the behavior of the kitchen. The best item on my plate happened to be the appetizer which was this spicy sausage served with French fries that we really enjoyed. I feel like this was a gentrified take of  Peruvian  food. I should have known better and have just gone to a restaurant that was  authentic.
name: Jay

text: This place was absolutely amazing I've never had Mediterranean before and I am a picky eater but it blew my mind
name: Sarah

text:
New Pizza Restaurant that is sure to make some loyal customers quickly with great food, staff and next to a popular movie theater. 
Our group had the pasta, pizza and even a sandwich and everyone enjoyed their selection.
My recommendation is to add a scoop of ice cream if you get the pecan bread pudding or chocolate cookie they are great deserts.
name: Bromley

text:
I am surprised with how much I enjoy this place, like really surprised. 

CSC is actually quite the solid place! To me, chicken salad was never really a go to choice when eating this as a kid. No one in my family liked chicken salad... so we never ate it. But over the past few months, this has become one of my regular spots to go to lunch, and I'll tell you exactly why it's perfect for just that:

Lunch here is a great value! Around 8 bucks gets you a perfectly sized meal that is filling, refreshing, and far from heavy, so you avoid that afternoon slump that comes everyday at work. The food is tasty! Certainly not the best meal In the whole world, but it captures good flavors and well prepared options that make this much better than the meal your mom quickly made you back when you were a kid. 

I always prefer my chicken salad (the spicier one- kicking Kaylean) on a croissant with lettuce. For a side, I get a scope of the spice pimento cheese- which was very weird that a scoop of cheese is a side, but it is a delicious add on to your sandwich or great with crackers. 

The only downside is they only have 2 "spicy" options. I would love to see more and also see some hot sauces or sirachi readily available for customers to get. 

Service is always great and food takes no longer than 10 minutes. 

Overall, if you work near cool springs, check this place out. It might become your next go-to lunch spot.
name: Ben

text: Went there for a salad on a sunny afternoon. Very friendly people, good food, great place. Would go there again.
name: Frank

text: The service and views were lovely. We ordered the Paella on the recommendation of our waiter and it was a miss. The rice was undercooked yet mushy. It was brown instead of the traditional vibrant yellow - did they run out of saffron? The calamari appetizer was excellent though. It was a beautiful enough setting that I would give it a second chance but definitely skip the Paella.
name: Rachel

text: We always enjoy Charlie's. The service is always good. The onion rings, wedge salad with blue cheese is fantastic. The steaks are good, usually cooked to temperature but they lack seasoning, I always need to add salt. I've been many times and on occasion the steak will be a little charred and stuck to the hot plate, needs more butter to avoid this. Overall I really enjoy it, especially the coolinary and feasts.
name: Charlet

text:
I'll start by saying that my colleague and I didn't get to this place for our main dinner because we found another joint around the corner but along the way noticed the $2 beer advertisement in the window. So we politely made a screeching turn into this place to give it a whirl. We both saw the wood fire pizza oven as soon as we walked in and smelled the goodness thereof. We knew we had made a mistake by eating somewhere else. 

The beer selection is wide and includes a really good local IPA -cant remember the name after I'd had a few- we did decide that out of greed and the need to try some stuff we ordered the calamari which was freaking great! The fried citrus slices added a little mm-mm good to the dish and the creamy sauces weren't too tangy nor too weak. Not to mention a great outdoor seating situation next to the river. I'll be back here to try a few more things. Several items looked very good on the menu. 

Finally my favorite moment was noticing how they deliver the bill in a book/novel instead of the little billfold thingy. Please world encourage more reading and mental independence! Our awesome server chose to bring my bill in my childhood FAVE - The Cat In The Hat!!!! I lit up like a child!!!
name: Thomas

text: My husband and I went here on a Friday.  It wasn't extremely busy for a Friday evening, especially since it was December.  I guess that should have been an indicator.  Every other restaurant in the area had a fairly long wait and we were hungry.  We were seated immediately.  We had guacamole, which was more like a mashed avocado as it had NO seasoning whatsoever.  We had a 3 taco deal that was going on.  They were horrible.  The tortillas were like cardboard.  The tacos were thrown together as if by a four year old and one was drenched in so much barbeque sauce it was inedible.   We weren't offered seconds on drinks.  Not a good place at all.
name: J

text: I've been here several times over the years. It's pretty consistent and if you know anything about Han Dynasty, you're coming for the heat. This place also has a decent cocktail list. They close at 10 on weeknights, but if you come anywhere close to that (we arrived at 930), be prepared to be rushed out and reminded a few times that the kitchen closes at 10. I get the "end of the night" feeling as an eating establishment with staff that wants to go home (I remember my days of working in a restaurant and hoping the place is empty by closing) but it is a bit unnerving when the order is put in a half hour before the kitchen closes and it feels like you just ruined the lives of everyone that has to serve you food. It might have been because we were end -of -the -evening customers, with end -of -the -evening -food, but while the flavor and heat on my dry pepper fish was good there were more than a few pieces that were inedible. I'm not sure if they were fried too hard or were the bony tail of the fish but I couldn't even chew through them. I pushed them to the side of my plate and kept it rolling. Our server himself, was gracious and quick with a smile, which was refreshing. I don't regret stopping through. I will just make sure the next time I visit I am on the early side of the evening so I don't get the side-eye.
name: Angie

text: The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. By the time the food came out I was already annoyed. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Just not for me. Not bad for a quick meal. Nice little spot, decent portions too. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. The leftovers held up okay the next day..
name: User

text: It tasted fresh, just not especially memorable. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. Not bad for a quick meal. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer..
name: User

text: Ended up here pretty late, maybe around 9:30, bc everything else nearby had a wait. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. The music was louder than it needed to be. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait.
name: User

text: Did the lunch roll special that comes with miso soup. The soup was great and the sushi was excellent. Everything seemed very fresh and the flavors were very good.
name: John

text:
Talk about a buried treasure. Yummy, clean & authentic taqueria, hidden, nay buried, inside a strip mall (behind Winghouse-Ish in The Fountains Plaza on the W side of 19/ South of Alderman).

No signage or street visibility, but worth finding.

You walk into a bright airy space and overlook all the fresh taco fillings and toppings.

We chose to share the 3 tacos for 6.99 which was a really good deal. Our favorites were the slow roasted pork with pickled red onions & the steak fillings.

Love that he wraps them in two fresh corn tortillas each, so they hold in all the juicy filling goodness.

We ordered the guacamole with homemade tomatillo salsa mixed in. It very bright and tasty served with crispy house made chips.

Use your gps to find it and give it a try as owner, who's from Mexico City, obviously puts a lot of flavor and care into his cooking. 

I think they are open til 8pm, so next time, we'll pick some up for a Friday night dinner.  They'd pair perfectly with a cold cerveza.
name: Bridget

text: I had their sushi at a catered event once and enjoyed it so I decided to go build my own. I like that you can do half and half. I got the tastes like chicken and spicy tuna (made with not spicy tuna!) and both were really good and fresh. The price was also fair. Only problem is the sushi fell apart pretty easily.
name: Britny

text: We came here for Christmas and it was an awesome experience! Great staff and server. For us that want to go out on a holiday, appreciate businesses being open and those willing to work with a smile on their faces. Thank you Brewhouse.
name: Marie

text: Checking out the very cool Riverside Village near McGavoc and Riverside. Castrillo's is part of the Village. Very cool outside courtyard shared by other restaurants is "The Dine In" option. It was awesome on this spring day. I had a couple of slices and they were hot, fresh and loaded with cheese and sauce. Not my favorite crust as it's a bit chewy. I'd say satisfying ! The guys inside were very cool. I'd stop by again if I were in the neighborhood.

text: My wife and I have been looking for a really good pizza for quite a while and we found Tony and Roni's. It is the best pizza we have had in a long time. We will go back.
name: Walter

text: Service was nice, kitchen was just moving kind of slow. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine..
name: User

My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. text: Excellent food and great service! The menu is always changing to the season with local produce on the menu. Highly recommend the Happy Hour M-F great choices on food and drinks.

text: The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. By the time the food came out I was already annoyed. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Food was good and came out fast. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. text: This place serves decent, real Mexican cuisine. No Tex-Mex here. Breakfasts are substantial, maybe a little bit too much so. The enchiladas and tacos are well done and flavorful. Have not had the Chiles rellenos, but they look good, and non-traditional. Margaritas are not my thing, but theirs are superb.

text: Really wanted to like this place. Made my husband go in despite the awful reviews... my thought is how bad can a bar be? Then one drink ordered and immediately annoyed by a $3 rocks charge. Sure maybe it's a bit more of a pour, but a $13 whiskey on Broadway is the most expensive I have seen
name: Megan

text:
Convivo is located in the Santa Barabara Inn and if you are lucky or can reserve a romantic space outside facing the beach on a warm still evening, it has an excellent ambiance.  We had dinner reservations at 8.  We weren't too hungry. Lots of people just order pizza.  We had a couple drinks which were ok.  She had some wine but I didnt want to drink too much.  We started with the corn which was good but kind of bland.  Then we had our main meal.  She had the sea bass and I had the bucatini with pancetta.  Both were excellently prepared and well worth the meal.

I tried to get out without dessert but they insisted on getting me a little something extra for my birthday.  So I had a little espresso to go with a coffee ice cream and a little chocolate hazelnut bar.
name: Erik

text: We order domino's probably once every two weeks. Sometimes more. Lately every time we have ordered, something has been wrong with the order. Either cold pizza, burnt to a crisp pizza, or missing items. Specifically marinara sauce for Parmesan bites. We request this every time and have come to expect it won't be there. After tonight's order missing sauce... yet again we will not be ordering from domino's again. Done giving many second chances!
name: Mary

text: Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. For the price I expected more than this. Food was good and came out fast. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. No big complaints, just a nice meal.
name: User

text: The customer service was great! But the entrees that we ordered were horrible. I had heard about the legendary fish-and-chips from home plate and how I needed to try them so I took a chance and did and was quite disappointed. Both the fish & fries had been cooked in the same oil so you what that tasted like.... The fish batter was bland. The fries were over cooked and hard. Our experience here is not allow me to recommend Home Plate. I'm too scared to waste money in trying something else...
name: J.

text: After walking by this place so many times, we decided to stop in for a late breakfast. This place is so charming! We sat outside and watched people shopping during spring break. I ordered a chicken burrito was rice and black beans. The burrito was on the small side for the price but it was full of flavor and quality ingredients, definitely a few notches above Taco Bell. My boyfriend had some form of Mexican eggs Benedict for brunch, everything was great. Service was superb and even though they were busy with the spring break crowd, no one was forgotten. You can definitely taste the difference in the quality of food used. Mexican food is probably my favorite cuisine and they do it great here at Casa Tina. I love all of Dunedin and the folks here are a major part of the main drag that makes people come back for more. I highly recommend coming here with children, with a group, or just your significant other. There is something for everyone and they're willing to answer all your questions (even the annoying ones) to help you make the right choice. The drink menu here is also impressive and I cannot wait to come back from a cold one and some enchiladas. Until next time!
name: Courtney

text:
Not a fan of this location. The customer service was terrible. Instead of assisting me, the employees were talking amongst themselves and playing on their phones. Customer service is important to me if I am spending my money at a restaurant, and this place was surely lacking customer service. 

So make it up to the line, with the rude worker assisting me. I say what I want and she repeats the same things over again, I'm like yes that and that. then we make it to the register and she says the price, which is wrong for the salad/sandwich lunch deal that I ordered. 

So already 2 issues with this place, then when I got my salad and ate it, it was gross, the chicken on the salad tasted rubbery and had a bad taste.  I usually love Salad Works, but this location is the worse. I more than likely wont be back, I will stick to the Street Road location up near Knights road.
name: Dana

text:
The only reason it gets 1 star is because our server was so great. Bright pink hair, can't miss her. That, and I can't give 0 stars.
So my boyfriend, who was playing at the Fillmore that night, and I and a couple of friends decided to come here because of all the hype it has obviously.
We sat at a big table with these huge chairs that were way too heavy to even pull into the table. They were extremely uncomfortable and I couldn't touch my feet to the ground. 
Then our server told our group that we couldn't split the check and that we could only pay with 4 cards. To which we know is bull. She definitely saw the looks on our faces and went on to tell us "if we were servers"... which most of us were. Personally I've been a server for 9 years. So whatever, we'll just pay with 4 cards at the end, no big deal. But I'll get back to that.
Our server was super animated and sweet so this is all nothing against her. I can't account for anyone else's experience at our table, but my boyfriend and myself did not like anything. We started with the Gryphon which is a big ass drink for two people. It's literally bigger than my skull. I took a sip and it was ALL JUICE. If you can't put enough alcohol in a drink that size, DON'T SELL IT. I didn't even have a buzz at the end of it. 
This was our anniversary dinner celebration so we decided to go all out and get the Vigilante Bone In Ribeye. Let me start by saying that I work at a steakhouse that dry ages meat and used USDA Prime beef. They brought it out and didn't bring us plates since we were sharing. This steak that we got was just not good. It was at best, OK. And the Black Lava Rock slab that they provide doesn't stay hot long enough. We also got fries and Mac and cheese as a side. The fries were the best part of our meal and that's saying something. And the Mac and cheese was bland. *UPDATE - one of my friends got the asparagus side and it was cold... so that's great*
When it came to paying the bill - the process was just HEINOUS. Took way too long and this was the breaking point for EVERYONE at the table with me. They also tried to trick us by putting the service charge for parties of over 6 people as an itemized piece in the middle of the check sandwiched between our food items. We might have given the restaurant a second chance, but the experience we had paying made that a second chance that would never occur. We travel all over the country and live in New York City and no restaurant POS system will not split a check or split seats. I claim "Shenanigans" on this restaurant for that. And if the POS system really can't, then they need to spend the money to get a new system.  
All in all, don't waste your money here.
name: Victoria

text:
Great portion sizes! One taco is actually as big as two to three small tacos from other places. I got the mean verde. Unfortunately hey don't have any vegan options unless you customize so that's what I did! I got avocado, pinto beans, salsa verde, lettuce and pico. It was really tasty! They messed up and put queso on my first order but were apologetic and made it fresh.  My friend got the Mc Yum Tum Nachos which were huge! They could definitely feed three people comfortably. She said they were good and there is a lot of meat on those suckers. 
If you do a survey online you get a free cookie on your next visit. Yum! 
The restaurant played really good music and it was a comfortable temperature inside away from the hot Florida sun. I'm glad that this is a good Mexican option in the Tyrone area.
name: Lauren

text: The hot chicken is HOT!  Get it naked and dip your sauce. The piggy chips are a hidden gem... home made chips fries in bacon grease. Yum! Hostess at the front was a little rude,  but the rest of the staff was stellar.
name: Stacy

text: BBQ and live music this place has both. Great singer and really good BBQ. Loved the dry rub on the 1/2 rack baby back ribs. The meat was tender and no fat. Macaroni and cheese with gouda.oh my. It was so flavorful and creamy with a garlicky toasted breads rum on top. Baked beans were flavorful and there was a Cajun corn cake. I love corn cakes but the Cajun seemed out of place for me. The service was great and the singer was great!!

text: Awesome service! In the drive thru Mohammed was very nice and polite.  He repeated my order and had a smile on his face. Keep up the good work.

text: Not your ordinary Indian afffair. Steven the captain was informative and friendly. The food, wine list, and atmosphere are all refreshingly outside the norm. Nice job by Raj and the staff to pull off this unique experience. Cheers

text: We stopped in here to have a quick bite and a drink before heading downtown to a concert. The place is a little pricey but the food was delicious and the service was great. Would definitely go back.

text: Fabulous brunch and service!  Jumbo shrimp and grits is a must, best we ever had. Finally a restaurant who knows how to make good grits.
name: Kristin

text: First time ordering from here and I honestly wasn't sure what to expect. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Would absolutely visit again. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus..
name: User

text: Food was fresh and service was quick. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. Worth checking out. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text:
SHAME ON THEIR RAMEN. This the disgrace of Japanese Ramen, Japanese food, and Japanese culture. I ordered hot&spicy ramen with cost of $8.75 and I tipped them at the very beginning when I payed my order(Before service). I expected an answer that why they used instant noodle to serve their customers and never feel anything wrong with it. Why would I come to a restaurant to order a bowl of instant noodle that I can make at home in three minutes? ? ?

It was the first time in my life that I complained on the food I got. I went to the front desk and told the waitress that I was confused that they made the ramen from instant noodle. She told me that is what they serve and they are not required to tell us that from their menu. When I expressed my disappointment, she just looked at me, I had to ask and she said "What am I supposed to say?" Excuse me? It is the first time I met a waitress like this. And when I talked to the manger, who also claimed that that's what they serve anyway, and he also said, "I do not know what to say" . 

It 's just extremely disappointing that they are happy with the instant noodle they serve when they claimed that they provide RAMEN. And never feel sorry when their customer wish to have an explanation. Worst experience in my life.
name: Yuqing

text: Omg this food reminds me of HOME! Being from up North, it's been forever since I tasted something worth eating with flavor like that in Indianapolis. I mean the food here is ok! But if your from Northwest Indiana, Chicago area; you know what I'm referring too, that sauce is so good, the sides were so good! My husband and I will continue to be a customer, I had the turkey ribs(since I don't eat pork or beef) those did the trick of giving me the same taste as If I was eating beef or pork. The prices are worth the expense and drive! I will definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone who wants a meal from home lol

text: My wife and I visited the Red Cedar Grill for their 2019 Christmas Buffet.  We were truly amazed at the variety and high quality of the food.  The food was absolutely fantastic and the service was amazing.  Our waiter, Dave, was extremely polite and attentive. Everything on the buffet was so tasty that it would be difficult for us to choose a favorite.  As far as drinks go, they have a fantastic menu of craft brews.  My wife had one of their signature flask drinks, the Colmar 309 which was wonderful.  We will be going here regularly.  Highly recommended!
name: Steve

text: A charming place to enjoy a quick breakfast or brunch! We ordered the Chachuka which was bursting with flavor. It was absolutely phenomenal. The meat was seasoned very well and the vegetables complimented the dish. We also ordered the french toast which was lathered in a fresh berry compote. Though the compote could've been a bit sweeter, the dish was very pleasant. Just ask for syrup if you need it to be a bit more sweet. Would totally recommend this  spot.
name: Daniah

text: The ambiance was awesome. The drinks were awesome. Service was terrible. You have to order your food and drinks at the bar FYI. And when you're ready to close out, you have to wait 30 min in line to pay for your food. They need waiters/waitresses. Then it would be awesome overall.

text: Coffee was great, we had the two specials of the day (Cinnamon toast AND Coconut Macaroon). To eat we had the Frittata and the veggie sandwich both of which were very good as well! To top it off, t was wonderful live music yesterday morning when we went by Taylor Reed. It was raining out and this coffee shop was packed. Very cool place to hang in the mornings.
name: Scott

text: The best breakfast spot in Nashville. The Princess is worth waiting in line for. Will not disappoint!
name: Brittany

text:
Stone Turtle is located on the corner of Tamm and Clayton in the space formally occupied by Felix's.  Parking is strictly street parking.  There are 2 entrances- one on Clayton will lead you right into the bar; a second entrance at the corner will lead you into the restaurant side where you will find a hostess stand.

We were here for cocktail with friends, so we only tried a few small plates.  
-The Caesar salad was over-dressed, but the dressing itself did taste lovely.  The "croutons" were even better- they were softer, fresh bread croutons with a good bite.  
-For drinks, I had the Italian Spritz- Italian liquor, prosecco, orange twist, and lemon juice.  Much sweeter than I expected, but still a nice cocktail with plenty of bubbles.  
-Husband tried the Instagram-famous "Smoked Old Fashioned."  The drink is served in a mason jar full of smoke with the cap on.  The suggestion is to swirl the jar for several minutes while the smoke infuses the drink.  Or, you can shake vigorously for a minute to speed up the process.  The downside to shaking is that the lid is not water-tight and your drink will end up on your shirt.  The ice in the rocks glass is a huge piece with a plastic turtle frozen inside.  This drink is all hype (and the plastic turtle is a lovely parting gift), but the smoke is just too subtle to be worth the hassle.
-Husband's 2nd drink was the Blood and Sand.  This is a must try drink.  Sweet and all booze.
name: Mary

text: Ok so Seafood Exchange is now Crabby Bill's Off the Hook.  The classics of Seafood exchange are gone, but you get the Crabby Bill's experience in Westchase.  I had the crab trap to drink delicious very fruity and you can taste the liquor.  I also had the bisque which is my favorite type of soup. Mussels the only size is 2lbs.  So delicious I get the wine and butter flavor.  I also enjoy the salad I gotta eat healthy sometimes.  I'm sorry to say I've ordered this same combination 3 times because it's just that good.  Another great thing you can get delivery through uber eats.  Will I go back absolutely they're a great seafood restaurant within walking distance.
name: Bryttani

text:
Lovely little seafood place downtown..
First, the drinks. We ordered old fashioned, nigronie, dry martini... every single one was good quality drink..thumb up for the bartender.. my fiancé and I were here celebrating his birthday. We ordered the peal pescatore with garlic white wine sauce, and the see food tower for sharing. That's absolutely enough food for two. Everything was just so great.. luv the place

text: This place is a gem!! My husband and I went with another couple and brought our own bottles of champagne. We ordered a carafe of their fresh squeezed orange juice and had dang good mimosas. We ordered the bananas foster french toast to start and it was incredible, so flavorful and the syrup came on it. We got two orders of shrimp and grits, eggs and salmon, and the Surrey's Egg plate. The shrimp and grits were by far the best shrimp and grits we've ever had and the best thing at or table, everything was flavorful and fresh though. We also agreed that it was all well priced. I would like to note too, that the wait time was about 20 mins, and it didn't take that long. Add this place to your MUST go to list!

text: Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Food was fresh and service was quick. Nice little spot, decent portions too. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced.

text: Every time we come here it is the same story! Long wait, something is wrong in the kitchen, we ran out of this and that, and/or we are short staffed. The desserts were adequate, but not one of us finished ours.  This was a birthday celebration dinner. text: Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kinda leveled off after a few bites. Price felt a touch high for what it was. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal.

text: Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. Definitely coming back. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. For the price I expected more than this.

text: This is one of my top 3 favorite places in Nashville. Love their burritos.  And the creamy Jalapeno dip that they bring to the table.  I wish they would bottle that stuff and sell it. It is awesome.  I have no complaints.  Its a big enough place where if you have to wait for a table you don't have to wait very long.  Would recommend downloading the No wait app and get on the waiting list for a table when you're on your way there.

text: I will make damn sure I never go to Pat's again and will tell my family and friends the same. My female friend ordered some cheesesteaks to go and was asked to hang out with the guys at the counter for a while. She declined because it was cold and the guy at the counter said he would keep her warm. Again, she declined and said she's happily married. Then the guy got short with her. Finally, when she asked for her change the guy pulled it back and said he needed a hug before she could have it. She declined again and asked for her change two more times before he finally handed it over.  Maybe explain to the workers what harassment is and that holding someone's change hostage so the creepy jerk at the counter can get a hug is at best unethical and worst sexual harassment.  She didn't want me to post this, but no one deserves to be made to feel that uncomfortable.
name: Derek

text: Always great. Love this place, as a vegetarian/ pescatarian I've found many options. Highly recommend the veggie burrito doused in cheese. My boyfriend loves the Hacienda platter. Atmosphere is fun and welcoming.
name: Kelsey

text:
This place was awesome!

We walked in with a large group (about 8) and were seated in a booth/table combo near a back corner. The overall atmosphere was nice. They added a modern rustic touch to a historic building.

The menu is extensive and has something for everyone. Not one person in my party had a bad dish. I had scallops on scallops-- they were a bit overcooked! But the overall dish tasted great. I just wish there was more of it! For dessert, my husband and I split the pound cake and ice cream. It was to die for!

The service was friendly, and we could flag down a waiter if needed.

If you're not used to modern city dining, be prepared for the unisex bathroom. You walk through an open door and there's sink trough with mirrors above. Further back is the restroom. Each stall has a floor to ceiling door for privacy. Any gender can use any stall.
name: Decz

text: We had  bulgogi at Buk Chon's Old City Fest booth. I had it as a rice bowl and my wife had it on a roll. In deference to local culture (I guess), both were topped with cheese and I added Kimchi. The meat tasted good enough to suggest a trip to the restaurant.
name: Lawrence

text: What the pho? This is not pho!!! I've eaten package pho that have more flavor than whatever they call it here. Very disappointed. I don't understand how to describe this place other than a trap for unsuspecting travelers. I would avoid this place.
name: Rick

text:
This must be on of worst spots to have lunch. 

I paid around $7, or so I thought, for my sandwich and soup combo. First, they forgot my soup. Fine, but not a good start. Then they ask me to pay for the soup with a $1.50 discount. $4.50 after the discount. It's supposed to be a combo, yet they say you just pay a la carte. Nice logic! IMO, $7 sandwich and $6 soup = way overpriced.

I'm really curous why people come here. The soups are edible but the sandwiches are really gross. The chicken in my Chicken Bacon Pesto sandwich tasted like it was frozen and looked unappetizing overall. It had that "gray" look if you know what I mean. I can also count the amount of pesto particles they put in it too and if you're like me and enjoy pesto, then you know you need a hearty serving on your "pesto" sandwich. 

They happened to come up short of my already low expectations. 1 star for okay soup, otherwise just turn around and go to Chipotle, you can get 3x higher quality food for less.
name: Peter

text:

The hummus is so fresh and delicious. Only letdown was that the pita bread did not seem fresh. Would definitely go back to try something else on their very extensive Middle Eastern menu.

text:
When I worked on the Southside El Azabache was a weekly, if not bi-weekly, lunch spot.  El Azabache and Pho 31 were my weekly staples. I haven't been here in years and wasn't even sure it was still open. Nice to see they were still there and opened when I pulled up. 

When you enter you'll see a beautiful two tier water fountain in the center of the lobby. A server will seat you in one of the four dining areas. The decor is extremely colorful with Mexican village scenery on each booth back. 

They offer several types of Margarita's and flavors. You can order a 13 1/2 ozs., 20 oz. Medium, 28 oz. Jumbo, 48 oz Monster and a 60 oz. Pitcher. We all love the margaritas regardless of the type.

The menu offers a nice selection of Nacho dishes large enough for a meal or to share. We polished off the chicken nachos fairly quickly.

Today I ordered the Caldo De Camaron Soup. The spice was apparent but not overly spicy and made with spicy shrimp, rice, pico de gallo and fresh avocado slices. Love the soup.

Vegetarians have 6 combo plates to select from and a  children's menu is available.

El Azabache has a large lunch menu with options from fajitas, burritos, enchildas, quesadillas, Huevos dishes, Chimichangas and tacos. Today I ordered one of the new lunch specials, Polo Azabache with strips of marinated chicken breast cooked in their scrumptious hot sauce. Served with rice and 3 tortillas for $7.99. The large portion of very spicy and tender chicken strips were small enough strips to fit nicely in a tortilla. The lunch portion of rice and beans are about half what you receive for dinner. The rice was fluffy and the beans were creamy topped with cheese.

The Shrimp Fajitas are tasty and consists of shrimp, crab meat, Tilipa, scallops, broccoli, cauliflower and carrots. Served with lettuce, guacomole, rice or beans, and choice of corn or flour tortillas. If your not into the red sauce then substitute cheese sauce for red sauce for $1.00 extra.

The server was friendly and very prompt to our table. We did have a couple drink and menu questions he couldn't answer. He immediately turned to ask the bartender and answered our questions. Bonus points for finding answers to our questions. 

I still enjoy dining here with the old work group. Love the great service, the large menu variety and great margaritas.
name: Wanda

text:

text:
Astonishing!  I was in St. Louis on a business trip and yielded to my colleagues' dinner suggestions.  Soooo glad I did!

My colleague researched where the best ribs were to be found in St. Louis and Pappy's ranked numero uno.  Voted "Best Ribs in the USA" by the Food Network, this place fully lived up to its expectations!

While there was a long line to order, it actually went pretty quick.  We ordered two full slabs of ribs, sweet potato fries, cole slaw, and potato salad and the food was brought to us almost before we sat down.  There's plenty of seating, so don't worry!

They did run out of several items by the time we got there (around 6:00 p.m.), so plan to get there earlier or order something else.  

The rib meat fell off the bone and there were plenty of different BBQ sauces to slather them in, depending on your particular fancy.

Give this place a try!!

text: This is not the best Chinese food around as a matter of fact the best around is only one block away but I give this awesome place 5 stars anyway. Why you ask? Well I'll tell you the best around is pick up only and is cash only. When I have that magic double formula at my disposal I go straight to number 5 (locals will know) however when that criteria is not met, when I need delivery or I need to use a credit card I need a place that is up to the task of serving awesome Chinese food. Enter Pearl of the East. Its been my standby for years but a car smashed through the window a couple years ago and I forgot all about this place. Well I ordered tonight. Its as good as I remember and as I type this I'm thinking I might even like the garlic sauce better then number 5. Add the fact that they were not cheap with a random assortment of sauce packets and gave a whopping 8 fortune cookies with my order (which included a free quart of won ton soup for meeting a certain dollar spent threshhold). I am glad they are back and I will most certainly return and recommend them although I may not be totally ready to break up with number 5

text:
After spending all day on campus, my friend and I started our journey back home; then we realized we were HANGRY. My friend mentioned eating at Dumpling King, but I was hesitant because I am from Orange County and have had my fair share of amazing Asian cuisines. Here in Santa Barbara I have been disappointed far too many times. 

I slyly suggested eating at Freebirds for some dankass nachos, but gave Dumpling King and my friend the benefit of the doubt. So we entered this franchise and ordered a Combo #3 which came with: 8 dumplings, 4 fried chicken and a soda. We got the "three delicacies"dumpling which had shrimp, pork and chives. 

The food was DELICIOUS. They had all the complimentary sauces for our food, and definitely left an authentic impression on us. 

We noticed that there was another dish that seemed to entice the majority of the crowd there (which happened to be an Asian crowd). It was a build your own hot pot for $9.99/lb. They had so many ingredients to choose from! 

We are looking forward to coming back again to try the hot pot! 

P.S. This place is definitely family owned. Being Asian myself, it was so charming to observe how family orientated the restaurant is and it felt like I was at home! Even though the interior and exterior may look skeptical, it doesn't miss the mark on food!
name: Kortney

We next orders the bread service with the royal paneer, eggplant Hyderabad and the tomato mirchi masala, we also requested garlic naan to eat with it. Out of the bread accomplishments the royal paneer was by far my favorite, then the eggplant and last the tomato mirchi masala. text:
Very eclectic mix of food and atmosphere - you have your sushi, ramen, meat skewers, Japanese comfort food, paired with a restaurant that looks half intimate, with the super dim lighting, and then paired with a bar and 2 plasma screen TVs. And paired with American pop music and a karaoke lounge upstairs. Food was decently tasty and well-priced overall; would come back! 

Atmosphere: In one word, it was eclectic. Definitely more on the casual side, but one side of the restaurant looked like it could've been more classy - super dim lighting. Servers were very nice - Jenna did a great job explaining everything on the menu, and was very attentive! I personally wouldn't go on a super nice date here, given the bar feel at the other side of the restaurant, but maybe would come back for a fun night with friends. 

Wait time: As a caveat, we did come in on the earlier side (~5:30), so there were less people in the restaurant, but some dishes came out as quickly as 5-10 minutes.

Food: I don't think the meat skewers were particularly special - we tried the lamb skewers and bacon-wrapped shishito peppers, but they were pretty cheap - bacon shishito was $2.50. I would go back for their sushi and udon, but not the skewers.

Recommendations: My favorites were the seafood pancakes - a mix of squid, cabbage, potato, shrimp, paired with Japanese barbecue sauces - and the He Sushi. And ask about their dessert - they don't have a menu for this! I've never had a creme brulee cake before, but it's essentially creme brulee pie, with chocolate glaze. 

Overall:  - some food options were tasty, some were average, but it decently overall priced - would come back with a bigger group and check out their karaoke lounge!
name: Annie

text:
