text: Goodness, this place is good. I also love that it's BYOB although I've never brought in a bottle. It's nice that it's an option, however. Also never had breakfast, so can't comment, but have had lunch multiple times. The portabella patty melt melts my soul. It's SOOO good. Expect it to be a little greasy as it is cheesy, has sauteed mushrooms, and I assume the bread is buttered a bit since it's a hot sandwich. The BLT is also well done, although that's not a difficult menu item. I alternate between those two sandwiches. I always get the roasted red beets with the citrus yogurt and walnuts as my side with my lunch and is honestly my favorite part about going to this restaurant. I'm contemplating asking if they'd let me buy a whole container of it because I could eat it every single day, it's THAT good. They also have excellent soups. Last time it was a white bean and chicken soup. There were huge chunks of garlic in it and couldn't be happier about that. The view of the Delaware River is also beautiful. It has great ambiance and the servers I've had are always really nice and helpful. Also, I'm not a huge doughnut fan, but I highly recommend getting the brioche doughnut, which is covered in cinnamon sugar and a coffee smoked caramel sauce. I could DRINK that sauce! When it came time for dessert, I wanted the polenta budino with chocolate mousse, walnuts and smoked salt. It comes with that delectable smoked caramel coffee sauce as well even though it isn't mentioned on the menu. When I asked for that, the waitress asked if I ever tried the brioche doughnut and needless to say, she convinced me, so I ordered both for our table. I really want to try more on the menu. Most people that work there seem to really enjoy working there and seem to care about the customers' experiences, which isn't exactly common. Can't wait to be back! I'm totally going to ask about the beets.
name: Elaine

name: Mike

text: Super friendly staff. The food is awesome! I specially like the new southern chicken that they are offering here. I also like that they are very friendly to RVs and trailers. If you come on Thursdays, the sweet potato casserole is to die for!
name: G.

text:
The most difficult part of my visit here was trying to find parking! Luckily, someone pulled out of spot for me to sneak on in and it wasn't a problem. I went inside to put in my name for my group of 4 and I was told that the wait would be 20 - 30 minutes. Since there wasn't much room to wait inside the building, I sat out in my car for my friends to arrive and then I got a text just 5 minutes later that our table was ready! That was super quick, so that was a nice surprise. The staff was very friendly as well.

We went for brunch on a Saturday morning. It was so hard to choose what to order since the whole menu looked delicious! I ended up ordering the Florentine Eggs Benedict, which was so good. Next time I go, I'll probably want to try something different, because now I want to try everything! My friends really enjoyed their pancakes (which was one big super pancake for each of their meals!).

The inside is really cute and just a little noisy since it's so open, but it really is a great location to get brunch with friends. I'll definitely go back.
name: Rachel

text:
Tried Pirates again, it's been a LONG TIME, and I live within walking distance! I still love the cheese sticks, today they were 3 stars, as I only got 1 marinara sauce, 100% needed 2, also the sticks either needed to be cooked a bit longer, so the cheese was better melted or they had cooled to much being cooked in advance, and got a bit cold, although I was there right when I told to pick up my food. 

I also got the Chicken Parm, it's nothing like you've had before, and I would say it's probably not something I would order anytime soon again either. It was SUPER SAUCY, and wasn't breaded chicken, and the chicken flavor was off, like it was frozen before or something, not sure if I'd order again. 

However, I'll be back for the cheese sticks and think about a pizza!
name: ThaDragonSourceRa ®

text: We had four people in our party & had mixed feelings. My chicken sandwich was great. Super tender chicken with a great flavor & topped with lettuce, tomato, avocado, Swiss cheese, and an amazing aoli. The fries were average, and the drinks were from a classic coke machine. It is a HALAL establishment, this I liked very much. The rest of the party was just okay with their meals, no one else had what I had & weren't completely happy. My son had a burger and did enjoy it but wasn't over the moon. I will say everything looked great and it was a very clean place. Overall we will give it another shot as they are new to the area and we like to support the local business owners.
name: Kia

text: This is a great spot... Just minutes from the beach. Terrific food, friendly service, very reasonable prices. Can't beat it! A great homespun spot! We had the early bird breakfast specials - served until 11. Two eggs cooked to order, sausage, great, toast - yum!

text: When we arrived they were having computer issues.  The wait was very long to take our drink order.  It was not very crowded for a Saturday afternoon, however the acoustics were terrible.  It was really loud.  Want to go back and sit outside in warmer weather.  Meh

The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. There were a couple things I liked and a couple things I probably wouldn't get again. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Food was fresh and service was quick.

text: The food is always well prepared and delicious! They will spice it to your individual taste. The staff is friendly and accommodating.  The new dessert menu is interesting and,  the two cakes we tried last visit were delightful!

text: We were sooooooo looking forward to 4.5 star Chinese food tonight and I sent my friend across town to pick it up. Ordered online, easy peasy. It was ready when he arrived. It was not visually appealing at all. The sesame chicken did not have sesame seeds on it or in the sauce at all. The crab cream puffs were a similar to crab wontons or cream cheese rangoons that you might find elsewhere. The filling was runnier than usual but tasted alright. The bbq pork fried rice was okay, but nothing to write home about. I was expecting decent Chinese, and it was FAR from it. The food is a solid 2 stars. The ease of ordering, accuracy and being ready when he arrived is what bumped it up to a 3 star review. We won't return.

text:
Got seated right away during dinner rush at the bar. 
The hostess grabbed rolls and butter on her way to seating us, so we got to enjoy that as soon as were seated!!! Our server was very nice and informative about the menu! We ordered an appetizer and two entrees. Our fried pickles came our in no time, and shortly after receiving them, our entrees came! 

I ordered the smoothered chicken with onions and mushrooms and cheese with mashed potatoes and broccoli. It was DELICIOUS! The chicken was so tender and moist, I honestly couldn't believe it! He ordered the wings, which I wasn't a fan of, but he loved! 

Our experience here was amazing! Can't wait to return for another visit!

text: This place was louder than I expected and that sort of shaped the whole meal. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. The staff seemed tired but still polite. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. It was decent, just a little uneven.

text: Our server is always friendly and personable, the food and drinks are great, and the happy hour choices and prices are good!

text: Really good bbq. Dry rub. Fresh salads amazing coleslaw sans mayo. Menu changes. Have been here 3 times always so good!! Owner/chef so sweet comes out to chat and Remembers what I like.  Definitely a go to place!!

text: What an interesting food and cocktail menu! If you are okay with exploring different types of foods then look no farther! They have lots of plates sizes so you can easily share and try several different plates. The menu changes daily so you can always be in for a surprise. The place is small and cute. I ordered everything from the small menu, some starters, a charcuterie and cheese board (Amelia's bakery, which they get items from for this, is delicious too), and a large plate. It was fun to explore new and fun food pairings. Cocktails are also great- so don't skimp out on those! You will likely spend a little bit of time here, enjoying the different dishes, and talking among your table of the great staff and food they have!

text: Horrible customer service. We were on the waitlist and when we walked up we were told that because we didn't respond to the text that we were taken off the list. Which was ok, the hostess put us back on the list to try to sit us sooner, but the manager took us back off the list and said we had to wait. Needless to say we left!!!!!!! Will never go back!  To many good restaurants with excellent service in Nola!!!!!

text:
I must say I enjoy coming here. I am glad that I gave them another chance. The last time I went in I went with my family and great dane. We were able to sit out on the patio and have a great lunch.

The server was great and the food was exactly what I ordered. I got the cilantro and jalapeno  hummas with chicken which is large enough to share. I only wish it came with more than 2 pitas. My husband got the gyro, my kids love their kids meal and my mother in law shared the hummas with me and got a small greek salad which she said was good. 

I still love their happy hour the best. You can get a lot of different things at an affordable price. I was bummed that they got rid of the free kids meal on Tuesday and Saturdays. 

We will be returning. I am glad that I had a much better experience this time around.
name: Morgen

text: The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. A couple small things kept adding up. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Probably not coming back. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. It looked better online than it did in person. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus..
name: User

text:
Went here and ordered the basil fried rice with chicken, and the roast pork. The fried rice was awesome - I made sure to order mild and thank goodness because it was still pretty spicy. 

The roast pork is where I dinged them a bit on the stars. It clearly wasn't fresh; in fact, it tasted microwaved. I know some places prepare it in the morning then slice it up fresh, but at least that way it tastes pretty fresh. This just didn't meet my standards for roast pork and I wouldn't order it again. 

I would return to order more of the fried rice and to try the other dishes, though, as the prices were reasonable.

text: I wanted to check this place out since it opened, but it's a little far from my part of town. Finally made it in, but not what I was hoping for. I'm torn about the review. On one hand the customer service was amazing, above and beyond what I normally experience. I also loved that the menu has a lot of options to allow you to create an item specific to you. Unfortunately the bubble tea I had was horrible. And that's a hard thing to do to bubble tea. I kept it simple and got a plain oolong tea, with milk. Maybe that's where I went wrong, it's possible other flavors are better. The tea had hardly any flavor - the tapioca bubbles had more flavor than the tea, that's how bland it was. Not even any creaminess from the dairy. I'm willing to give another try, but not going to come out of my way.
name: Leah

text:
Stopped in for quick bite and ordered 2 salads and the Cajun fries. For the most part the food was good but there was additional food around the rim of the plate and some at the bottom of the plate. 
My biggest concern was if I was given a dirty plate, since throughout my trip in New Orleans, I've had poor service at restaurants. 

The manager assured me rice is next to the salads, it happens and assured me the plate is clean. Unacceptable because you did not clean the plate therefore you can not assure me it is clean. 

Nonetheless, when we walked in we were not greeted by our server. A woman came twice and asked if our waiter came and since he never showed she took care of us. it took about 30-40 mins to receive the appetizers and salads. All in all, 2 stars from me.

text: Fire the entire management and employee staff covering lunch and start over! It's a mess inside and drive-thru. Constantly long waiting times at both as employees go at whatever pace they feel like. Take your business to Wendy's in KS instead. They seem to have management better organized to lead a team through high peak traffic times.

text:
Finally had Wingstop with my brother after hearing much hype. We went in person to order takeout which was a mistake - a little over 30 mins of waiting. Order online for takeouts! 
We had the Crew Pack boneless wings with fries included. Their fries caught us both off guard. It tasted like fries tossed in sugar, super sweet with a tiny hint of salt. First time having sweet tasting fries other than sweet potatoe fries. 
Their boneless wings were very crispy, which I liked. For sauces we had the Garlic Parmesan, Louisiana Rub and Cajun. I liked the Garlic Parm and Louisiana, both dry seasoning. Cajun was a wet seasoning, wasn't a fan. Dry seasonings over wet seasonings for boneless wings here.
name: Michelle

text:
I've always been a fan of Time Market. It's in a great place close to the University and Fourth Ave. It seems to ALWAYS be open and has a lot of options to choose from.

I've always stuck with the pizza which is great and changes from day to day. The slices are HUGE! Keep that in mind when you decide if you want one slice or two. Time Market is just that, a market. They have a small section for produce and lots of interesting drink options.

Time Market is clean and has a dog friendly patio. What's not to like?

text: I wanted to like this more than I actually did. For a busy night they handled it okay. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. The music was louder than it needed to be. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. I left full, which at least counts for something. Not bad for a quick meal. The food was good and the service was easygoing. text: After finding out the background of Red's I had really high expectations of this place.   I mean if you have been to San Fran and been to Mission Chinese Food then you will understand.   But,  I knew it was going to have a twist.  Bam! It does... that Nawlins technique with that MCF cooking style.   Beautifully paired in every dish.   Got the pork buns to start.   Everybody is hoping on the bao bun craze so nothing spectacular until you get to that southern sauce inside it. Yummy.   Then tried the brussel sprouts and generals chicken.  Therein only reason I picked generals chicken was because I have tried kung pao pastrami at MCF and I saw the twist early.   I saw a big bowl with a bunch of fried chicken walking by the kitchen.   Normal I would think nah, it is just fried chicken.   But, with a influential chinese twist.  Chicken was so tender you can use a fork and knife.   Perfect southern fried crunchiness with the right amount of sauce.  Now back to the brussel sprouts.  I don't normally get them because I am temperamental about the different techniques in cooking them.   A lot come of mor being cook right and bitter.  Now these are amazing, perfectly cooked.   The balsamic vinegar with the togarashi was a puckering but sweet and a hint of that togarashi was lively.  Nice stir fry crispiness on the outside without sacrificing flavor.  I ate almost the whole thing to myself.   This is a must try fusion in my book.  Thank you to the training from Mission Chinese Food.
name: Jeremy

I never had real German food before and I was in town for training and some of the guys I was training with said they knew of the place to try.

When we walked into Rathskeller I was amazed with how large and impressive the venue was. 

We walked into the bar and the bartender was very nice and professional. 

The bar area is open sitting and we were able to get a table with no rush. I can only imagine how busy they are on the weekends and or game days. 

For dinner I had the sausage appetizer with a side of German potato salad. The sausages had a great flavor and were amazing. The cabbage tasted great and the German potato salad just as good. 

I would recommend Rathskeller to anyone that is in Indy and looking for a great place to drink and have dinner.

text:
I'm on a quest to try 'em all at Daddy's Dogs as my alter ego: Nash Ketchup.

Daddy's Dogs was a place that I never expected that I would fall in love with because "It's just hot dogs" I thought. 
After trying their "Big Daddy," I realized that I was still young and naive and have much to learn.

They have about 6-7 varieties of Hot Dogs with a bunch of amazing toppings on them. Everything is made to order, so eating the whole thing becomes a messy and hot experience. The only bad thing about their dogs is that there's so much stuff on it, that it's hard to eat! (Which is such a first world thing to complain about.)

This is the perfect drunk and sober food. They open late too, so if the 1AM hot dog cravings hit, this is the place to go.

text:
I've tried a lot of breakfast places here in St. Louis and I've got to say that this one has changed my opinion on some others. I'll go into more detail below, but the highlights are: extremely delicious, great options, great portions, and great pricing.

Service: The food came out just as fast as we ordered it. It was hot and just as we ordered. The waiters were nice but not overly conversational (which I personally like) and we were checked on by several waiters passing by.

Atmosphere: The place is set up like a diner, the tables and the place were clean. The layout is nice, not crowded, good for groups. A good place if you wanna chat and hear yourself speak. But most of all, the food was delicious. 5 stars forreal.

The food was fine for upscale bar food.  Nothing spectacular.   Might be best to go early or late for a cocktail.

text:
I visited Waffles on Maple with my bestie during our trip together this year. I always pick my restaurants ahead, researching which ones have a gluten-free menu available. My favorite thing about traveling is getting to have GF waffles or pancakes (and seafood at dinner). I had two completely different experiences when I visited here. Kind of iffy on whether I would return. I would give three stars...but the first server we had was so wonderful. That and the Walking in New Orleans waffles, which were phenomenal takes it up an extra half star.
Sadly, I don't have the receipt (which is weird for me) so, I don't know our server's name. He was so friendly and accommodating. There was one female cook who didn't speak to us when we said hello, and when I came back alone right before going home, the same thing happened. She just ignores you, and that is very offputting. 
We both came down with some kind of flu, but the first visit was before it really hit us, which was good because that Walking Waffle was unbelievable! It's covered with pralines and just screamed of caramel. I had some kind of latte made with milk, and also scrambled eggs and hashbrowns. Not every restaurant has GF hashbrowns, so those are a real treat. My friend had soy sausage. I don't eat soy, since most of it in the US is GMO, and soy can work on a female's hormones, so I can't speak to how it was. But everything I had that day was really good. I left in love with the place.
Now, fast forward ahead almost a week. I went back for breakfast before I had my tattoo done. I was pretty sick at this point, coughing like crazy, so I realize my tastebuds were off. Also my fault was the fact I didn't read the menu closely enough and ordered the Cinnamon-Roll Waffle, which was loaded with raisins, which I detest!
I picked them out, so it wasn't too bad, and the cream cheese icing made it worth it anyway almost. The eggs didn't taste as good on this day, and maybe it was because I was sick? But when I look at the photos, they looked drastically different the second day I went. I only ordered a regular coffee and found out they had no coffee cream. Really? What breakfast place has no cream? They tried to give me that powdered coffee whitener. I was surprised this is what they offer when the quality of the food was up there. Whitener is full of terrible fillers and oils that I never put in my body. Just because of that, knowing I couldn't have a coffee, probably wouldn't return. 
The girl brought me so milk, but I just don't like coffee with milk and couldn't drink it.
The thing, besides the rude cook, that really stuck in my craw? They really nice guy wearing the kippah the time we were there before gave us the wifi password. I'm Canadian with limited data in the US, so I REALLY depend on the free wifi provided by restaurants and hotels. If they don't, I remember. The girl working when I went back alone told me they don't give that out. I told her my server from the other day had done so, and she simply said, "Well, he shouldn't have done that." No wifi for me. 
Yeah, definitely won't be going back.
I give Waffles on Maple 3.5 stars
name: Claudette

text: Awesome burgers, and the fries/tots are delicious! Only downside is the tables are very narrow and crowded.

text: On a positive note, the never-ending chips had good corn flavor and good chip crunch! The salsa was outstanding! The homemade Sangria was excellent!  HOWEVER, I went expecting authentic mexican food, instead was served bad american-mexican food.  Taco Bell has better american-mexican food than this.  Pork tamale was dry and flavorless....couldn't even taste the masa.  Chicken enchiladas were not any better...where's the sauce?, the cheese? And the"Refried beans"?...  more like creamed refried bean soup. Red-tinged rice was no substitute for Mexican rice.  Thankfully, I was with good friends who's company overrode the lousy food.  IF I go back, I will order differently.  Do they serve a hamburger?  LOL

text: My last review was a year ago and it wasn't good. This time was much better. Server was the bartender, Doug. I sat at booth in bar area. Very attentive. Food was great. Only issue was pretzel sticks were not seasoned (this is not the first, second or ever third time this has been an issue)  ......  I added my own pepper. Would have been better if cooks added the seasoning. I mentioned this and was told they were suppoesed to.  I am dissappointed that Applebee's has removed many fish and seafood items....just about everything is beef or chicken. Menu limited in that regard. They also are not a full bar. They make their Applebee's drinks, and beer and wine. But if its not on their "list" of mixed drinks...its not an option.  All that being said, I had a pleasant experience this time around. They do need more staff to do an outstanding job. But with what they had to work with...was good. Most of the employees were doing the work of 2. Hands Clapping for them!

text: I love this restaurant!  Have never been disappointed.  The pasta is so fresh and delicious, the service is great, and the drinks are spot on! Best Manhattan ever!  Our waitress or waiter has been knowledgeable and helpful each time we've gone and their specials are magnificent.  Just can't say enough! Can't wait to go again.

text: Price felt a touch high for what it was. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. The music was louder than it needed to be. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. name: User

text: Great experience I had with my mom! Service was outstanding. I was really impressed how the cashier immediately suggested items and even offered to carry our tray outside. Food was fresh and a great value for the price. Highly recommended!

text: This place is so worth the drive if you're visiting Santa Barbara, it's a beautiful and secluded drive. Once you get onto Stagecoach Rd and get to the tavern you feel the relaxing comfort of good vibes. We got to the tavern and it was first come first serve seating but came quick, the server was on top of things and got our drinks right away. I ordered the chili sampler which consists of a cup of Chile Verde, game chili, house chili and a tortilla, it was beyond filling and all three were phenomenal. I also ordered the famous tri tip just to see what it was about and it was pretty damn delicious and had it with some yummy potato salad. Must try place along with a lot of history.
name: Ernie

text: My first meal in St. Louis and man did it set the bar high. We tried to be adventurous with our starters by ordering the skewers with beef heart. It was a major fail for us. I can't say it tasted bad, but the texture was a little tough. The regular beef and chicken skewers were tender and delicious though. Our entrees were delicious, the meat was great quality and each bite was loaded with fresh flavors. Our waitress was very friendly and had great insight on how each dish was prepared and what ingredients were used. A must if you're in St. Louis!
name: Melani

text:
LOVE. This romantic classic American atmosphere sets the scene for a beautiful date or catch-up with friends. The staff is professional and everything in the restaurant feels very luxury and high-end. We asked the waiter about a wine recommendation for the steaks my friend and I were thinking of getting and the waiter was very knowledgable about wine pairings, making sure to help us order a wine we know we would like based on our own personal tastes, and one that would compliment the dishes we wanted to order. I felt reassured in my wine selection due to my confidence in the waiter's knowledge. The steak, mashed potatoes, and creamed spinach were all soo delicious. One of the best steaks I've ever had. Then we ordered the Baked Alaska for dessert. It was great, I wish the outsides could have been toasted more, but overall this was one of the best dining experiences I've had. Definitely 10/10 recommend. Try to make a reservation really early in advance because they book up very quickly. 

Also pro-tip, if you know when restaurant week is, try to make a reservation during that time to get even better bang for your buck.
name: Amber

text: the first few bites were promising and then it kind of leveled out. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. The wait wasnt awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. text:
I've know About Hiroba because one of my best friends took me there when they were in Skyline Blvd. 

When I saw they loved to Sparks I was so excited because honestly I don't want to go to IJJI'S 2 anymore. So I've been here twice now. 

Once with my family party of 4 and once by myself. I don't think the visits are as remarkable as when they used to be at their old location. 

The Place: 
It's a small place at the same center where "Peg's" the breakfast place is. It was lunch time on a weekday and I couldn't find a parking spot. I had to park in front of the Hawaiian restaurant around the corner. The place has table and bar seating. 

The Food: 
The Sushi was OK, I had seaweed salad and it wasn't that good. I got some mussels and they don't do mussels in shells. Instead they put them in a container. I wasn't a big fan of them.
I got some "upside down shrimps," they were good. 
I had "Donald Ducks" nigiri and this is when I felt something tasted off. I'm not picky at all with food. But the avocado tasted bad and had some brown spots. The flavor was spoiled by the avocado in my opinion. 
I also had some "Sierra" which is like the mountain roll, it was delicious! I really like it. 

I understand sushi is so different, and hard to evaluate, one ingredient not being fresh enough and it can make the whole lunch taste bad. 

I would come back and give them another chance, because they are close to my house and it's nice to have different sushi options. 

For desert I had Vanilla Ice Cream and it was good! 


The Service:
Service was great, my waitress check on me constantly and brought the check fast.
name: Salma

text: Got the Harvest Bowl Salad with added avocado. Yum Yum! The server guided me with wit and intelligence in making my choice. I enjoyed watching him choreograph the outcome and having it be the perfect choice on this cold winter's eve.

text:
I almost don't want to review Bok Bar because that means more people will want to go and I want to keep it to myself. But I will!!

First of all, Bok Bar is in an old high school which sounds weird, and kind of is, but in a very cool, unique way. You get carded downstairs and then head up to the bar in a huge elevator. All part of the experience. 

Then the bar itself is a perfect rooftop view of the city. Like, almost cried because of how beautiful it was at sunset, perfect rooftop view. 

And they have decent happy hour deals/fairly inexpensive drinks to begin with. Lots of beer, lots of wine...what more could you ask for?!

If you are for some reason not satisfied or are perfectly satisfied and just want more food than Bok Bar can offer, literally right across the hallway is Irwin's, which is delicious.

text:
Texas BBQ comes to Corona!   We finally got the chance to sample Tay's this weekend. We don't have a lot of options out here so when a promising place comes along it gets noticed.  

We wanted the ribs but they were sold out just an hour into the evening.  They also do not do phone orders for take out (which is strange to me) but made an "exception".  But they were very friendly and helpful. 

We ordered two beef brisket plates with different sides.  The brisket was INCREDIBLE.  Tender. Smoked so well with that pink ring around the beef.  The sauce was a little spicy and a little sweet.  I cannot rave more about the brisket.  It was perfect.  

The sides were good.  The beans were excellent. I am not a fan of chili spice but when in Texas....Cole slaw was fresh and creamy.   The Mac and cheese was average.  The waffle fries were good but a bit soggy.  

We cannot wait to go again, but they are only open on weekends.

text:
Merchants is my go-to restaurant on the strip. I've been coming here for years and have had lunch, early dinner, and late supper here. Each time the service has been impeccable, the food delicious, and the experience fantastic.

Merchants starts your meal off with a complementary tumbler of seasoned popcorn. It had a ranch-like season blend which was amazing. Since it was over 100 degrees outside with the heat index, we decided to eat light. Mom ordered the Cobb salad and I went with the arugula salad with blackened salmon. She had their home brewed tea and I chose a glass of cava to go with the fish. Best salmon salad I've ever had! Fish was moist and flaky with tons of flavor. Mo raved over the chunks of roasted chicken and thick bacon on her salad.

I'd told the restaurant that this was a special birthday (Mom only turns 75 once) and they offered her a choice of desserts. She went with the peach cobbler which arrived with a grapefruit-sized scoop of butter pecan ice cream on top. Our server also brought a card signed by all the staff. Mom was so overwhelmed by the thoughtfulness. Merchants is a class act all around. Whether you go for a casual lunch or special occasion, you're always in for a treat!

text:
The atmosphere of this place is excellent.  Country cool, and welcoming.  I'm glad we went on a Tuesday night (for our 14th anniversary) as this place has been packed since it opened and we got seated right away!  The waitstaff was very knowledgeable and kind for answering all my questions.  The menu is very varied which is great for any bbq place as meats do and will sell out on any given day.
We kept the starter simple getting the cornbread madeleines which were fantastic.  Savory with a fun butter adornment.  We did know that this isn't typical traditional bbq, so we did keep an open mind and I made sure I asked questions to avoid certain ingredients.  I had the two-step so I could try more items.  I selected pork belly and pastrami with the fries and coleslaw while my husband had ribs with the beans and fries.  My highlight was the blue cheese slaw.  Very tasty and a great twist on a bbq staple.  The fries were ok, nothing real exceptional or exciting.  The meats were...ok.  For the price, not much meat and both were coated in black pepper.  The pastrami also has a very chemical taste to it.  The sauces were ok, but contained copious amounts of black pepper.  My husband's ribs were ok and coated in, you guessed it, black pepper.  Like there are no other seasonings on the meats, just black pepper and tons of it.  My husband's beans had the perfect consistency, but tasted only like peppers both the veggie kind and that dang black pepper again.  I really would have loved to have any other flavor on those.
We will probably go back, and I'll be watching to see what changes are made, but as far as the meats go so many better local options are out there.
name: Jessica

text:
Totally my first experience in this establishment. There was an expected wait prior to being seated. It wasn't as long as expected...maybe 15 minute wait. The hostess was very friendly and had a smile on her face the whole time.  Well worth it whatever the wait would have been. After we had been seated the lines were much longer. 

For appetizers we had the crab cake and BBQ shrimp.  It was not what I know as Texas BBQ at all.  Not even remotely the same flavor.  I was impressed with the tastiness of this appetizer.  The crab cake was so full of flavor that just burst in your mouth. Way yum!! We had the yummy bread and butter. For our main course we had the chicken andouille gumbo which was authentic (of course) and was very tasty.  It was like having a party in your mouth! What an experience. For dessert we had the fudge brownie with a scoop of ice cream. That was exactly the topper for the evening. 

This was a great dining experience. Our waiter was friendly and attentive.  This place seemed to be one of the places to visit. Even though the lines can get long, as I stated, it is well worth the wait. As soon as a table empties they clean the table and it is ready for the next group of people.  It moves rather fluidly and effortlessly.
name: Vera

text: Pogues Run Grocer is my happy place and it is important to me to support Indy's only food cooperative. I love having access to healthy, locally-sourced, organic, and vegan food on the near east side. Come visit the store, order a sandwich (great selection of vegan sandwiches too, Rambo is my favorite), peruse the aisles, and inquire about becoming a member.
name: Holly

text: This was a delivery order on a night when I really did not want to cook. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine..
name: User

text: Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. The staff seemed tired but still polite. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Maybe other people have better luck here. Would probably stop in again if nearby. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer..
name: User

text: This place is amazing! The fact that its brand new and the kitchen is putting food out promptly and to perfection is incredible. The staff are all friendly and very knowledgeable. If you're looking for a quick bite or a full meal this is the place. Prices are very reasonable and the atmosphere is welcoming. I highly recommend.
name: Jon

text:
Some of the most delicious noodles, dumplings, and scallion pancakes I've had in my life! I really wish I could give 5 stars and I'm usually tolerant of service but the service was really subpar that I have to take one star off.

My boyfriend and I came here on Thanksgiving for dinner. We decided to visit Philadelphia for the long weekend and a friend recommended this place knowing I love noodles. She was spot on with the dishes being delicious!

The dumplings had thick skin and good texture, along with generous portion of meat inside as well. 

The scallion pancake tasted so fresh and fluffy rather than dry and oily like I've had at many other places; definitely the best scallion pancake I've ever had.

My boyfriend got the house special noodle soup with hand drawn noodles while I got the egg and vegetable noodle soup with hand cut noodles, so we got to try two kinds of noodles as well as two kinds of soup. Hand drawn noodles are thin, cylindrical, and long while hand cut noodles are thick, flat, and shorter. My boyfriend and I both liked the hand cut noodles more because we prefer thicker noodles in generalC but the hand drawn noodles were really delicious too. However, the broth was so-so. The egg and vegetable noodle soup was a bit bland. The house special noodle soup was a bit better flavored but still quite simple in taste.

Service isn't the worst I've experienced, but given that the restaurant wasn't terribly busy I really expected better. First they gave us someone else's order. We noticed that one bowl wasn't what I ordered (the other was what my boyfriend ordered) and let the waitress know. She said "oh but you nodded when I put these on your table" before taking the bowls and passing them along to the table next to us who actually ordered them. Then, I believe our noodle dishes were forgotten because they checked in with us and said "oh looks like you didn't get your noodles yet" and it was another 10 minutes before our noodle dishes finally arrived. We had already completely finished eating our scallion pancake and dumplings by this time, so we waited quite awhile for the noodles.

Definitely would come again if I visit Philadelphia again because the food is just so delicious! I'd be prepared for not the best service but it would still be worth it.
name: Diane

text: I wanted to like this more than I actually did. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. This feels like a place where your order choice matters a lot. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really.
name: User

text:
Update review 2/26/18. Came for brunch.  I think they have s service problem waited over 10 minutes AT BAR. For a drink. Problem appears to be caused by inexperience and inefficiency behind bar.  Had to bus our own table. Last few times we've been here we've had same experiences. 

Pat review- Food is amazing. Not a fan of ordering at a counter. Patio space is the best in Boise aside from Arid club. The Fork has better bloody Mary's.  Definitely will be back. 

Came back a week later. Tried bacon sampler.  So good. Hubby had Mac.
name: Jennifer

text: I ordered the crawfish etoufee and it was horrible. The rice was not cooked properly and pieces of it were hard as a rock. The flavor was average, the crawfish was alright. Everything that my family ordered needed salt. Very disappointed and definitely not worth the money you will spend.
name: Nicole

text: Unassuming at first (and last) glance, this restaurant nonetheless serves up some really good Korean food. We dined on the bulgogi and bibimbap, both of which were fresh, super flavorful, and cooked to perfection. All in all, a good dining experience - we look forward to returning again in the future to sample more of their menu items.
name: Michael

text: Meh. Food,meh. Drinks, meh. Mediocre..... fish place next door was cleaning fish and feeding the pelicans which was sweet, but I don't think the hut can take credit for that.
name: Jessica

text: The food is amazing and the service is top notch. All the food Sierra recommended was delicious and she is a great server. Would definitely recommend and will be coming back
name: Ileana

text: Awesome place with really good home cooked food we will be back for sure. Be prepared to wait.
name: Nikki

text: We have been looking forward to eating at this place for years now. We were so excited to get in line today. We ordered and finally found a seat. The food came fast so it was a great start, right? The food itself was WAY over rated. I must admit that we all ordered just plain chicken and no spice. Still, it was just bland ol fried chicken. I would be willing to try the mild and maybe it has more flavor. The sides I ordered was potato salad and baked beans. Both were just ok and a can bean would probably have been better. On the plus side the banana pudding was on spot! Wow, it was really homemade! So over all it was ok, but I don't understand the hype over it. Maybe next time...
name: Jeremy

text: Had a really great meal at Rodizio tonight. Everything was really well seasoned and perfectly cooked. Huge improvement from the last time we dined here. Nothing was bad last time, just a little bland. No issues with that this time. Our server Tori was really nice and kept up with my insane water drinking. My cup was always full which I really appreciate. She even gave me some extra water! The manager Alex stopped by to say hello and tell us about the venison special they were offering. That was really delicious, thanks Alex. Right before dessert they had an impromptu dance party blasting awesome Brazilian music over the speaker system. Was really cool, and loud! We will definitely be back, had a great time.
name: Jason

text:
This is the second time we came here. First was to buy a cake and the second was tonight when we came for blizzards. 

We ordered at their drive thru window. Service was super fast and they were very friendly. My husband even commented on how happy the guy at the window seemed. I was surprised at how fast they took our order and we didn't have hardly any wait for our ice cream. 

Both the Heath and Oreo blizzards had the right amount of candy in each. I almost ordered extra Heath based on the reviews I read prior to coming here. I'm glad I didn't. They handed both of our blizzards upside down. 

Overall, great experience. We will be back.
name: Erica

text: So, I have a rule. (I may have just made it up, but nevertheless, it is now a rule.) What's the rule, you ask? Well, I'm glad you asked! The rule is, I force myself to wait three months after eating at a place before coming back to Yelp to review it. "Wow Alec," you might say, "that's a pretty great rule." To you, I reply with "I know, right?" But for the other readers who don't immediately understand my genius, allow me to explain. Basically, if I don't remember eating at the place after three months then it must have been "fine". It didn't blow my mind or else I'd remember it, and it wasn't so awful that I immediately ran to Yelp to write a poor review. So...three stars!
name: Alec

text:
Ordered at pizza and salad, shared the salad but they literally would not serve us unless we paid for another salad because I took three bites of the one. Unbelievable the boss here. Will never come back here. I will go to the others around town. The most ignorant motherfucker ive ever met in the food business.  do not here. Period
And i was in their with my mom and he embarrassed us all. Their pizza also sucked as much at the manager.
name: Jack

text: If I could give it zero stars I would.  Going in on a Wednesday and the service was horrible. The one lady was super rude and snippy. The other woman making the sandwiches was also rude and said they couldn't put extra meat on my sub even if I paid for it. They only had 2 breads available and didn't look phased when telling us they were out of things. Their customer service was not up to par by any means.
name: Krista

text: Ill be short .......................BOMB!!! Adam our waiter really knew his stuff about the food and drink menu. Also about how they cook the food. Overall good experience. Adam was an amazing waiter (how they all should be) and the food was amazing! Definitely recommend and will be coming back!
name: Josue

text: Good service place for the usual wings. Nothing super special but nothing wrong either. Great to have some consistency. Many many flavors of wings and small appetizers. Downside is there billion calorie each, but you aren't going there for a healthy meal
name: Dennis

text:
Yummy! This review is as a first time customer and to go. 

We ordered the rainbow roll modified (no issues with the modification skipped the white tail and added spicy tuna soooo good!) and a Sakura roll. On the menu the Sakura roll doesn't say anything about coconut but the top of the roll but it was covered in shredded sweetened coconut so it made it sweet not exactly what we like for a meal. 

We were able to scrape it off but you could still taste it just not as strong. It could of been a mistake either on menu or by adding but next time I would ask for no coconut. 

Over all I would gladly order from here every pay day :)
name: Delilah

text:
Not a good experience.  I called as asked if we should make a reservation for 5.  I was told no, at this time of year no problem getting a table.  4 of us arrived and the hostess took us to a small sized table for 4.  I said what are we going to do when/if the 5th person shows up.  She told me would could sit outside and that I should have made a reservation.  I told her I was told none was needed.  She looked at me and said, Oh well and walked away.

It was fully packed and the noise level was awful, we had to yell to hear each other.  To walk down the row between tables to go to the restrooms you felt like you were walking down a narrow aisle on an airplane.

The food was mediocre and overpriced for the quantity and quality.  I will never go back and do not recommend.
name: Cliff

text: Besides sitting in line in the drive through for 20 minutes after ordering, had to pull up to wait on for for another 15 minutes for the food to get ready and wasn't acknowledged by any of the employees for having to wait for so long.  Will not be going back.
name: Brett

text:
It's crazy to me that people wait months to go to this restaurant.  Yes, the food was good but I don't think its worthy of that long of a wait.  Not to mention, the food is SO expensive.

It's funny people I just happened to stumble upon this restaurant and actually walked in and was seated at the kitchen high top.  I didn't realize people made reservations for this place so far in advance.

We did the taste of Zahav, which is a good choice if you want to try a few things.  We started out with the humus, which was really good.  The fried cauliflower was also good.  For the main dish, we had the brazino which wasn't my favorite, but I'm not a big fish person so that is probably why.
name: Kristina

text: I wanted to like this more than I actually did. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. I left full, which at least counts for something.
name: User

text: This place is great for all types of events even if you just want to hang out and get appetizers. The service is always friendly and prompt. I have been here multiple times with my husband and friends either eating a meal or enjoying oysters and drinks outside. I would definitely recommend stopping by here and then strolling around the Riverwalk. As for favorites -- any of their fish dishes (grouper, pompano) and the charbroiled oysters. Also my go to drink is the Ring of Fire. If you want a kick in your drink, this is the one to get.
name: Kim

text: Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Idk, the menu wasn't huge, which i usually prefer.. Also, the leftovers held up okay the next day.. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. Honestly, no big complaints, just a nice meal. not sure I'd order the same thing again.
name: User

text: Soooo delicious! Would come back to New Orleans just for this place. The pork belly was my favorite dish. Gumbo was the best I've had. The live music was beautiful and very romantic. Cute place, clean bathrooms, fast service.
name: Camila

text: The atmosphere in this restaurant is so cool. The food was really great-from the salad to the shrimp and grits stuffed pepper to the chocolate torte-everything was perfection. Jim, the owner took the time to visit with us and he's a really nice guy who's passionate about his craft. Check this place out!  You won't be disappointed. A foodies dream!!!
name: Dana

text:
Another Update 2/12/18: If you go for brunch, you must try the breakfast bomb! We're talking eggs, sausage, bacon, and cheese wrapped in dough.... oh my goodness! It was incredible!! If you want superior service then ask to be in Brandon's section. He's amazing and has served us several times. I bumped it up a star because of the food and the service has improved. Way to go guys xoxo


This updated review is for the Sunday brunch. The chicken and waffles deserves 5 stars all by itself. The belgian waffle was fluffy and insanely flavorful. I was actually surprised how delicious it was! It's topped with a fried chicken thigh (boneless) instead of a breast which I didn't mine because it was moist and seasoned nicely. The peppercorn gravy on top is a nice touch. Sadly, this was my husbands food I was eating (and eventually had to give back) as I waited for my replacement meal.

Trying to live life on the wild side I ordered the country fried steak, big mistake. Literally the steak was a ball, like a fist. I knew something was off when I looked at it. Trying to give them the benefit of doubt I tried to cut into it. I needed the jaws of life to cut the thing. It was sooo tough. Not wanting to strain my wrist any further I sent it back and asked for the french toast instead. 

Now, the french toast is yummy. It's almost like bananas foster. Although my plate didn't have the candied walnuts the menu said it would. Granted our server apologized and quickly brought them to me. 

The gouda grits were another let down. Kudos to them for not using instant grits and actually seasoning the grits but all of that is a moot point when the grits are underdone and your left feeling like you're chewing sand. *sigh* So disappointed. 

If I return for brunch, it would be for the chicken and waffles and nothing more.
name: Auyanna

text:
This was one of my top meals in NOLA. 

There is a daily happy hour from 3-6 with 75 cent oysters (warning they are large oysters if you prefer small ones)! They have a great French 75 as well! A group of us of 8 went for dinner so we tried a large variety of items. 

The seafood tower was spendy but was so much food. Honestly, we could have been happy with that and not order anything else.

Highlights of the meal were the duck duck rice with crispy rice - the crunch and flavors were spot on and jumbo Louisiana Shrimp en cocotte which was rich in flavor so best to get this and a something on the lighter side. The service was great - they were patient with us as we continued to order many drinks! This is the place to go for a nicer meal in NOLA!
name: Cindy

text: Had high expectations. At first when I arrived I was second guessing it. My expectations were met. The food was great. Flatbreads, pulled pork sandwich, parm fries, salad, all of it! The ciders were great. They had live music and friendly staff. Try it out. Super cool building also.
name: Blake

text:
Vivid memories of this place being THE end all place back in the day. Sadly, how times change

My wife and I arrived at around 3 pm for a late lunch early dinner. There was no host/hostess to seat us nor were there any people on the main side. We waited at the door for a couple minutes then my wife suggested we go into the bar area. We walked into the bar area and there was a table of 5 guests and 1 booth had 2 guests. That was it. We looked at the bartender (Leslie) and she said "you can sit anywhere" (in the bar area we assumed). We sat down, got comfortable and then the bartender looks at us and says "do you mind moving to the other side" (of the bar). Sigh, so we got up and moved to the other side

My wife got the chicken salad and I ordered the "HEFTY MEATY RIBS". I asked the server if I could get something besides cole slaw because I know that Friday's cole slaw sucks. The bartender rambled off the other sides and I decided on mac & cheese. She said there might be an upcharge but wasn't sure (and I was never told other wise) At one point, she began telling us how she just got out of the hospital and how tired she was. Sorry, I don't care. I have my own problems. My wife and I had just been to the hospital so my wife could get an M.R.I. done. I didn't start regaling her with our troubles

Food finally arrived. "HEAFY MEATY RIBS" was actually a joke. Looked more like a simi rack of ribs. I asked the bartender if this is what there full rack looks like. She said yes. I know I had a puzzled look on my face and then, instead of showing any empathy, getting the manager or something....she says and I quote: "Maybe it was a small pig". REALLY??

We ate, paid the check and left. The "upcharge" for the mac & cheese was $1.49. Not a lot of money but would have still been nice to know ahead of time. Thankfully, the mac & cheese was good

Like I said in the beginning, this was THE place many years ago. Now, it's pretty much non existent. With the type of service along with the lack of service (no host, really?) I don't see this place staying open much longer. Across the street is a Chili's and a Longhorn. I know when I pay for a full rack of ribs there, that's what I get there. We shall be taking our business there moving forward. Shame on you TGI Friday's, Shame!!!
name: Edward

text: Visited Nashville.  Tried this place. Had pulles pork.  It was dry and tasteless.  I don't normally complain about a meal but this is an exception because it was that bad!  Tsharrish@aim.com
name: Tim

text: So sad this location is now closed. The Manayunk one is still open and still super delicious.
name: Lia

text: LaTao hotpot is conveniently located near campus and offers many options for hotpot at great value. It's especially cheap during lunch hour and the atmosphere is great!
name: Jennifer

text:
We were stoked to find a spot with outdoor seating on one of the first nice Friday evenings of the year.  Table for 3 seated right away at about 6pm.  There were about 6 out of 8 empty tables outside...at 6pm...on a Friday...on the nicest day of the year.  My radar should have been on high alert.

It was a really nice and trendy ambiance and I was excited to try some stuff off of their detailed and extensive menu.  We ordered the calamari for an appetizer.  Its our go-to app because its the one everyone in the family can agree on.  What we did agree on this time is that it was one of the worst calmari dishes (or bowls, yes, it was served in a narrow tall basket/bowl) we've ever had.  The breading tasted like fish and chips breading and every piece was over fried/cooked which made it very rubbery.  The lemon aioli was delicious though, but not enough for the amount of calamari they give you.  

My husband ordered a burger with sweet potato fries, which he was sick from the remainder of the night.  Enough said.

My daughter ordered the kids hot dog and fries.  I'm surprised she ate it because it was very pale.  Definitely boiled or microwaved.  For $4 though, I didn't complain.  Most kids meals now-a-days are double that and don't come with a drink.  This one did.

I was in the mood for fish tacos but didn't want tilapia, which is what they come with.  After speaking with the server, I asked if I could sub in (and understood there might be an upcharge) grilled shrimp for the tilapia.  She asked and they accommodated which I appreciated.  The plate came with 3 tacos.  Each taco had one shrimp broken up in to 3 pieces.  So when I ate the first taco I didn't really notice the lack of shrimp because the piece was scattered throughout the taco and there was a ton of mango (delicious) salsa on top.  As I take a bite of the second taco, I'm realizing that it seems thin so I take out the shrimp and could put it together like a puzzle and its ONE piece of shrimp.  Same for the third taco.  The only flavor was that from the mango salsa.  But I was starving so I just ate them and figured they wouldn't upcharge me since they barely gave me any food.

Nope.  They added $5.00 for the shrimp.  So the tacos are $12.95 with the tilapia and now become $17.95.  Almost $18 for 3 flavorless shrimp!  I wasn't going to say anything but after a while I just couldn't hold it in and wanted to just let our server know that next time, if someone orders this to have the kitchen put more than one shrimp on each taco.  So I let her know and she was very apologetic, however, nothing was done about it for my bill.  I get if I added on shrimp on top of the tilapia, however, I substituted shrimp which I knew would have been a small upcharge, but $5.00 for 3 shrimp is ridiculous.  

We left the Red Hen feeling unsatisfied and ripped off.
name: Amy

text:
Okay Phoenixville! My gf and I came in on quiet Sunday night after seeing a fun Cirque show and were seated at the window table. People/Dog watching at its best! I saw zero golden retrievers, so that was unfortunate. Whatever.

Our server shared a few personal suggestions and crowd favorites.  We over ordered, (standard) and were glad we did so. Everything ordered was proudly devoured. 

All dishes were beautifully plated and although the bbq lettuce cups stood out as my favorite the chicken BBW, holy crap. The coating tasted just like KFC (that's a legit compliment for me.) 

Let's talk about the Carnitas Plato.  I haven't eaten pork in 5+ years and I remain mind blown how well jackfruit can mimic actual meat. These were flavorful and had me questioning why I agreed to share. 

I am already looking forward to a return visit as there was much more on the menu for me to get into.  Next visit might i suggest that Taste arrange a golden retriever meet and greet? Thanks in advance.

Until next time Bravo Taste, Bravo!
name: Brigit

text: This sushi place is by far one of my favorites in Reno. The rolls are a good size and they aren't filled with too much rice so you are able to try different rolls without being too "stuffed." The appetizer menu is very tasty, I would recommend trying to Yakiton and of course the mussels !
name: Destiny

text: I have eaten here about three times and I love. The only problem I have had is my son wanted a bloody Mary and they couldn't make one???!!! It was late afternoon but it also was a Saturday. It is all one level so with children and the disabled it is great!
name: Cynthia

text: Very bad. Not pleased. Felt very uncomfortable and unwelcome..... :( :( :( :( :( :( :( will definitely not come get ever again. Food is basic and not filling. Waste of money.
name: Laura

text: Wanting to be upfront, I am from KC and I do love KC BBQ.  That being said, I enjoy any of the regional BBQ styles.  Had to give Martin's a try based on the many positive reviews.  I ordered the brisket sandwich with a side of beans and my wife ordered the pulled pork sandwich.  The pulled pork was not warm and was more like a chopped pork sandwich.  Also, she did not care for the house table sauce (vinegar-based).  I enjoyed my brisket sandwich and really liked the sauce.  The BBQ beans were equally as good.  I would have given a 4 star rating, but the quantity of brisket (two slices each about 2 square inches) seemed skimpy for the price, thus the 3 star rating.
name: Bill

text:
We like going to local places and supporting our community. However, this place was just not impressive. 
My husband and I went to get breakfast this morning at 10 am, which admittedly on a Sunday morning is a very busy time for a breakfast joint. We expected a wait, but had no idea we would be waiting over an hour to eat. 
First of all they told us the wait would be 15-20 minutes to be seated, even though there were clean empty tables visible. We ended up waiting 30 minutes to be seated, and then waited another 30 minutes for our food to be served. 
The waitress was only semi friendly and the service was mediocre at best. My husband ordered toast on the side, and paid $2 for ONE piece of toast. I ordered the hangover hash browns for $3 and got a child's sized potion! 
The food was good but overpriced. The wait was excessive and with poor service it made for a very lackluster experience.
name: Crystle

text: just ok. nothing was OMG that I would want to go back for a second time. The best part of the meal was the bread and butter...I'm so stealing that seaweed butter recipe. Although the food was a 3 star, the service and ambience were 5 star so aversging a 4 although should probably be a 3.5. The waiter was very attentive, patient, and made recommendations based on personal preferences and dietary restrictions. We went for the experience, that's enough
name: Sienna

text: Pauline and Mary catered our wedding and what a great job they did. The food was excellent: chicken and beef fajitas, moist, tender and tasty along with their chicken enchilada casserole....mmmmm yum!  They were timely and actually adjusted their schedule last minute due to our request. Thy did a great job keeping the food fresh and hot and served about fifty people efficiently and fit right in with our families. Perfection, couldn't have asked for better food or service, thank you ladies!
name: George

text: Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. Pretty happy with it overall. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean.
name: User

text: I don't really get some of the harsh reviews on here. The food was good and the service was easygoing. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. I had a better visit than I expected to. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Would probably stop in again if nearby. For the price I expected more than this. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent.
name: User

text: Very enjoyable first Korean BBQ experience. We had the burrito and a couple tacos. We enjoyed very much. If they were in a better location, they would be doing so much business I feel because the product is fantastic.
name: Andrew

text: We stopped in here twice on our short visit to New Orleans, it was that good!  The pho broth was so delicious, and the perfect antidote to too much of a good time on NYE.  We got the tofu and chicken and both were excellent.  The banh mi bread was perfection - just the right amount of toasted - and the meats were delicious as well.  We tried both the pork and chicken on the banh mi.  We'll be back to visit New Orleans again, and this will be on my must visit list.  We look forward to trying more of the menu!
name: Lori

text: The ribs were amazing. They were incredibly tender. The collard greens are new and are also amazing. Highly recommended. Convenient location nearby I44 made this an easy choice for us!
name: Taylor

text:
Where do I begin? This was horrible! We're staying here for weekend and wanted to eat at steakhouse, owner of rental house suggested this place.

1 star for artichokes. Filet mignon was tasteless. Mashed potatoes tasted like spuds from a box just add water. Mac and cheese was grainy like it was rushed and cheese wasn't blended well. Lobster ravioli had 3 raviolis which barely had lobster. Scallop was so tiny and covered up in bread. Linguine alfredo was just butter and cheese.

Overpaid and really bad food.

Don't ever consider going to this place. Better off going to McDs!
name: Leleh

text:
I love visiting Santa Barbara.  Whenever my wife and I go up there we make Red Pepper one of our dinner stops. Living in the "626" (aka San Gabriel Valley) we live in what is supposedly Chinese food paradise in the U.S. And there are lots of good Chinese restaurants where we live but also lots of really bad ones and they are strewn all over the place. Red Pepper wouldn't be in the upper echelon of the 626 but they would still be a worthwhile place to go and for the Santa Barbara area I think they are the best place if you're looking for Chinese food. 

The restaurant is located in an odd area off the main street but that makes for easy parking.  It's a comfortable place, nothing fancy but with nice artwork on the walls, tables/booths not too close together, and the people who work there are very nice and friendly. The menu selections are varied and reasonably priced, and tasty as well. 

We've been here several times and have never been disappointed. You'll find all the usual, traditional Chinese dishes on the menu and they are pretty authentic, not "Americanized." It's well worth a visit.
name: Rico

text: Just went to the drive thru... took them 3 minutes to acknowledge us, then waited another 5 minutes for them to come to the window. There was nobody in sight, so we drove off. text:
I decided that a Sunday morning while the rest of the house was sleeping, I would sneak out - get some coffee and then bring some donuts home for the family. I searched through my Yelp list of places I had yet to try and living in WG this was just a quick drive as the rest of the items on my list were in the city. By proximity - Donut Drive In won!

I was able to find a parking spot out in the lot, shocking, as the moment I got in line (there was no room to stand inside with the four people at the counter, yes, you read that correct - no room to stand INDOORS with FOUR people inside) and I was the first one outside of the door. 

I entered and a young woman greeted me amidst the chaos, but despite there being people shoving and jammed in there - I had this girl's undivided attention. I told her it was my first time there and she made a point to say she wanted to make my first experience positive! Told me all about the different donuts and which ones were cake, etc. I chose a turtle cake, four glazed, a cinnamon twist, a blueberry cake, a chocolate sprinkle glaze for my toddler, a buttermilk bar, and a cruller. 

The minimum for credit cards is $10 - so either bring cash or secret better option two - get $10 worth of donuts!

The donuts were really tasty - the glazed were light and fluffy and golden and not overly glazed.

Be prepared to wait, dress warm if its winter, but you will enjoy the old school donuts they have here - especially the cinnamon twist and the buttermilk bar (warm it up and its heavenly!).
name: Alyssa

text: It's been about 10 years since I was last here. I had a bad experience with the wait staff back then, but the manager did tons to make it right. Fast forward to tonight. When my husband and arrived at 8pm on the dot for our 8pm reservation we were greeted with a hostess who didn't even acknowledge us (it was a slow night) for about 5 seconds as we stood at the hostess stand. She was was looking down at something. I decided to see what she was looking at and to my surprise, it was a book and not her phone. She then looked up and without an apology or much of a greeting. She said our table would be ready in a few minutes and we could wait at the bar. We waited about 5 minutes and she very casually looked over at us at the bar, waved us over and said, "Come with me."  We followed her onto the elevator. She didn't attempt to make any small talk or say anything, which made the ride a bit awkward. She led us to our table without menus. A few minutes later a woman greeted us and she basically said she was not our server, but she would be helping us. We assumed the server would be coming over, but he never did until after the app. She came to take our order and didn't ask if we had any questions. I did and she didn't have the best understanding of the menu. We ordered the special honey Sriracha wings, the whole Red fish and Drum fish. The wings were AMAZING! Big portion and delish! Loved the peanuts on top which made for a delightful crunch. The fish dishes were also very good, however the color of the sauce under the Drum fish was different, but tasted good (I wish I had more of it). For dessert I ordered the Buttermilk pie and the "server" didn't thoroughly explain it to me (again due to her lack of knowledge of the menu) since she was not actually the server. I ordered it with a side of vanilla ice cream. The dessert came out really cold (would've been better served warm or room temp). The ice cream was practically melted (which I can't stand). I asked if I could have a scoop not melted and was assured I would. Unfortunately, that was the last scoop of vanilla they had. They brought me some "Monkey" ice cream that had a banana flavor in it (which I don't like). I ended up not eating the ice cream and only had 3 small bites of the pie. They did end up taking both off the bill, which I appreciated. We ended our meal around 9ish and I suppose it was closing down time since the staff was braking down tables around us and our actual server was moving a bunch of chairs over his head across the restaurant.  I felt like it was closing time at a chain restaurant.  Overall, it was not a bad experience, but I was a bit disappointed by the lack consideration for the guests to have an overall welcoming and enjoyable dining experience. The "server" and the actual server were very kind, but would've appreciated a bit more attentiveness and menu knowledge from the "server".  The restaurant is also REALLY loud, but that's probably due to the set up. I know i may sound a bit picky, but i was expecting a bit more of a "fine dining" experience. Not sure I will return on my next visit.
name: Katie

text:
My wife and I came here after stopping in the middle of The Great British Baking Show because we felt we needed that 4D experience to finish the season. MBC did not disappoint!

We each got two items and had a lot of trouble sharing. Everything that was supposed to be flakey was flakey. Everything that was supposed to be light and subtle was exactly that. We truly did feel like we were sampling the things on the screen. This store has been around for around 90 years and it's clear that they are on the path to perfection when it comes to baked treats.

The staff was extremely friendly and knowledgeable. They gave us details about the store, the treats themselves, and helped us to make the best choices.

The store, located on The Hill, is small and unassuming. If your not looking for it, you may miss it, but honestly, there's no better way to experience any cooking show than accompanied by a cannoli or any other item from The Missouri Baking Company.
name: Zac

text: We were a party of 3 for brunch on a saturday morning. We ordered a bahn mi sandwich, wild mushroom scramble skillet and the french toast.  If there were any wild mushrooms in my scramble, I must have missed them, and my two eggs over easy came hard cooked, plus the portion was a little dinky for $11. My husband's french toast was really a slice of warmed-over bread pudding, just OK tasting and smallish in portion.  Our friend's bahn mi was quite generously sized and apparently tasty, but it was served with a side of onion rings that resembled intestinal tape worms.  Service was friendly, chatty and cute, but slow and forgetful.  Overall this restaurant felt a bit amateurish to me, like a business run by high school students as a class project.

text:
When we had some friends fly in for Charlotte for the New Year we decided to check out some of the "best of" items around the city...of course we start with brunch and this massive bloody mary!

The "accoutrements" of the cocktail were the best part - the perfect appetizer to keep me from getting too hangry. The bloody mary itself though was a little disappointing to me. It was pretty watery and didn't have any of the savory flavors I love about this drink.

The food was pretty tasty, as a bar this place does fried food amazingly. I want to go back already and try their beer battered chicken tenders. If you like onion rings, get those too! They were massive and delicious!!

Lastly, the service was quite slow so don't come here hoping to get in and out quickly. It seemed they had only one waitress for the entire dining area (which was packed for Sunday brunch.) The lone gal was a fantastic server though, just severly over burdened!

text:

And, just for checking in on Yelp, I received a free mini-pastry. 

There was plenty of outdoor and indoor seating, and it seemed as though service was pretty quick. It was both a very trendy and intimate setting; I would totally come here with a few friends or on a date! 

BEST OF ALL, their plastic products are all compostable. I am sometimes apprehensive to eat out because of the heavy plastic use in carry-out restaurants, but I was so pleased to see they use compostable cups and paper straws. 

The cashier was very friendly and eager to answer questions I had about the baked goods.  The snacks and watermelon cooler were DELICIOUS. I am really excited to visit again with friends.

text:
The guy running the burlesque show was SO AWFUL tonight!!! Seriously we were embarrassed we waited 45 minutes in a huge line to get in here because we thought it was the hot spot in Nashville and paid $20 a person, and then the guy in charge of the show was just so awkward. It was by far the weirdest burlesque show I'd ever seen and just not sexy at all. He was trying to do old school cabaret but instead of making it about the girls he made it all about him. It was a basically a very poor version of Hugh Jackman in The Greatest Showman led by the nerdiest guy in choir. We left when the guy tried to get people to pay him to take his clothes off... I'm telling you, no one wanted him to take his clothes off. It was just SO damn terrible that I'm cringing thinking about it.

The front door team folks were nice but management directed them to not let people in due to capacity. When we finally got in there we were shocked because there were so many open seats and a giant booth in the back with a staff member rolling silverware that could have easily been used for paying customers. TONS of standing room!!! And you have people waiting for nearly an hour or more - Wtf?! My husband ran a bar/nightclub for 20 years and I bartended for 10 years, so we are very familiar with capacity rules and there is NO WAY in hell that the place was to capacity.

We had high hopes for this place but we will tell everyone we know visiting to avoid it. I tend to think the people flocking out of the bar at intermission would agree. It is a complete tourist trap! Btw, the picture I took is 10 minutes BEFORE intermission when we were let in.

text: I kept driving past this place and have been wanting to try it. I don't know what took me so long. I stopped in tonight and I am writing this as I am eating. I ordered a kraut dog and the Kevin Bacon Burger. The hot dog came out first and it was delicious. You can tell it was grilled on the flat grill because it had the perfect snap and taste. The kraut was grilled with it so that also added to the flavor. I am ordering another one it was so good. The Kevin Bacon burger came out next. I added a little ketchup and took a bite. The meat tastes fresh and is full of flavor. You can tell it isn't a frozen patty. It was grilled to perfection and served with enough toppings to add even more flavor but not over power. This is my new go to for classic American fare. They have some great specials, a drive through, and some unique things on their menu. The decor is vintage posters and there are some games on the counter like connect 4 and Simon. This place is really effin good and if you're in the neighborhood I suggest stopping here for some amazing classic comfort food!!!!

text: So yummy! Everything about our dinner was great. The food the service was excellent. I ordered the duck and wished it was cooked more as it was almost raw but it was still good.

text: This place has gone down hill. The service is super slow, I came dining alone. I dont need 20 minutes to decide what I want. Honestly, I can just tell you right then and there. No need to hand over paper to have me fill out and keep waiting for someone to come pick up. My miso soup was cold when they brought to me. The sushi didn't seem as fresh as it use to. The service is just lacking here, I need to find a new sushi place.

text:
We discovered this hidden gem a few months ago and we've been regulars ever since. The food is absolutely amazing, and a friend of mine from India says it's authentic as well. The family who owns/runs the place are super sweethearts, they treat us like royalty every time. Also, they deliver for a small fee - which is a life saver when our household is sick or busy. 
I hope more people find out about it and go there. I get the feeling it's a newer establishment, and they deserve to be really successful, which is why I'm writing this review.
If you haven't already, check it out!

text: I live roughly 20 minutes from here and somehow I stumbled across this place through Facebook. My husband and I decided to give it a try and it was AMAZING! We chose to eat in and the staff was very friendly and the service was great. I'm a bit of a Chinese food connoisseur and hands down they have the best wonton soup I have ever had. We will without a doubt be going back.
