text: Besito has an amazing happy hour from 4-630pm! For $50, two of us enjoyed 2 margaritas each (if you're not drinking Patron, get the casa, it's stronger than the classic), 4 substantial tacos (fish, shrimp, carnitas, and chicken - $2.50 each), guacamole (only item not on the happy hr menu), and a GIGANTIC - seriously, this thing was huge - plate of steak nachos (listed as tostaditas - $5)... plus the complimentary chips and salsa, which we barely touched. We will definitely be back for another happy hour at Besito!

text:
Baja Cafe is a must-try breakfast/lunch stop in Tucson. Their menu, specializing in variations of eggs Benedict and pancakes, have a wide variety of items on their menu. As you can read from the many reviews here, Baja Cafe does them all right.

I had the "Anomaly" eggs Benedict. Here's the description:

Mac and cheese waffles placed over a tomatillo green chili sauce. Topped with a combination of julienne bell peppers,  fire roasted green chilies, caramelized onions and our house smoked habanero chicken sausage. Finished with poached eggs, smoked gouda cheese sauce and pico de gallo.

Yes, did you read that? "MAC AND CHEESE waffles." Did you oooh and aaah at that description? I did, too. That's why I ordered it. Bonus--since it was my first time there, I got one of their famous Snickerdoodle pancakes gratis. The Anomaly was tasty. The mac and cheese waffles were interesting and gave a good flavor balance. Because of the chilis, this meal definitely has a kick to it. Baja Cafe really does a poached egg right. The yokes were perfectly creamy. The whole eggs were nicely oval all the way around, not flattish as you would have a poached egg done in your pan at home.

It also comes with a side of hash browns. I'm pretty picky with my hash browns and these were excellent. The Snickerdoodle pancake was amazing. Not too sweet.

The service was great. Our waiter was friendly, informative, and attentive. The lighting was surprisingly dark. It was dark. You get used to it.

I would go back just for the poached egg. But I look forward to trying many of their other menu items.

5* = A top favorite. Mind-blowing good. I will definitely return and I will go out of my way to go here. Worth every dime of my money.
4* = Outstanding. Tucson-top-tier. Some elements not quite as good as it gets, but it still is worthy of my regular business.
3* = Good experience. I might do repeat business if it is convenient, the only option, the only one in its category, or on a whim, but would not be among the first thing to come to mind. Would definitely recommend you trying it to get your own take on it.
2* = Not so good. Would not recommend at all. Waste of money.
1* = How are they still in business? Stay away at all costs!
name: Brad

text: Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. No big complaints, just a nice meal. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. It looked better online than it did in person. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed.

text:
This is a friendly local convenience store but I have to say, five stars is a little over the top for what it actually is. Driving all the way here as if this is a top destination is just not reasonable or rational. The Cuban is fine but sorry, there are definitely better ones in Tampa Bay. 

They do sell Powerball tickets which I appreciate when I'm feeling lucky. If I win, I'll crank this review up to five stars for sure.

text:
Somewhat disappointed tonight.  Honestly, nothing stood out in our dinners.  Average salad and minestrone; we went with eggplant and chicken parm and they were both average.  As the young folks say: Meh!!

Service staff did not deliver the requested glass of wine with my entree. Resolved with free dessert.

Not what I hoped for.

text: Just like any other In-N-Out. The dining experience and food is exactly what you'd expect lol. But the staff is really great at this location. There's a bit of a wait on Friday nights or after local events, such as football games, etc. Otherwise, not a bad In-N-Out.

text:
Yes, yes, yes! I have been wanting to try Midtown Tacos for MONTHS and finally stumbled across it and I am so pleased I did. 
First, can we talk about the adorable setup? Tucked around the back of Death and Taxes, Midtown Tacos is really just an enclosed walk-up counter-style restaurant but they have done it so well.  The glass doors make it feel larger than it is.  The outside seating area is cozy but plentiful.  The family-vibe behind the counter makes me want to give them all my money.  I just fell in love with this place and all of that was before I even tried the food!
Ok, the food. I had veggie tacos (they are street style) and they were so freaking tasty. Cauliflower, jalapeno,  and green apple? What? YES! Oh, it works in the best way.  My friend had a burrito sans tortilla and pretty much licked their plate clean.  
Stop reading and go give these people your money!

text: The atmosphere is nice and the food is savory. However on a non busy Tuesday night the bartender forgot my drink and still charge me for it without apology. After a new check was presented I was told they would not accept my cash. I can respect a restaurant policy if it's clearly communicated; however, the only indication that this was a cashless establishment was a 4-inch sign at the base of the host stand. Two stars.

text: I love the original Steve's Prince of Steaks and I thought I was going to that location, but I ended up here.  I was happy with my cheesesteak because it tasted just as good as the original place, which is one of my favorites. The cheesesteak does have thicker meat, but don't worry it is not dry. Shared on our end...had the cod, chicken,  shrimp, fries, coleslaw, beans n tator salad.

text:
First time visit and I'll definitely be back! This place is truly five-star in every way: service, food, atmosphere. We sat outside on a steamy night and enjoyed the sidewalk vibe. We had the $5 happy hour snacks - anchovies, asparagus/leek something or other and the mushroom croquettes. All great. And this place knows how to do mushrooms! The Duxelle burger was not the usual portabello, but a thick patty packed with umami goodness. 

Adding to the great service was the horror our awesome server Arianna showed when my friend suggested the blanc de blanc might be flat. She whisked it away with apologies. They needed to chill a new bottle and while we were waiting for that, they gave us a comp glass of a Spanish white. Classy! The definition of customer care. 

Love this place!

text: You know it's good local food when you are the only one in the restaurant that doesn't speak Korean.   If you are looking for great Korean food, this restaurant has it.   There is no smoke from table grilling, but the bbq is done in the kitchen.  The Kimchi soup and the Beef bulgogi are delicious and plentiful.  The side dishes of pickles are fresh and tasty.   The staff are very friendly and attentive.  A great to get a group and get the traditional fare or explore the specials.

text:
Please note-we went to this restaurant in May

Friends had invited me out for my birthday so I went online and bought a restaurant.com coupon.  We all arrived and the place was maybe 1/4 full.  We opted to eat outside since the noise level inside was already high.
It was nice on the patio.

We ordered the bread plate and the potato fritatas.

These came out in a timely manner along with 2 drinks other than water.
And then the wait began.    Our waitress was never in our vicinity, but the person serving water kept our glasses full.  When ask where the waitress or manager was he was sweet and mentioned that it was only his 2nd day so he'd go find them.

The waitress finally showed up with our food - 2 out of 4 entrees were unacceptable at this point.  The manager showed up 30 - 45 minutes after we asked to speak to him.

There were problems in the kitchen we were told.  At this point my normally calm, jovial husband lost it.  In a restrained voice he told the manager what he thought of the service-where upon the manager said our meal was fully comped.

You know what?  A fully comped meal does not make the situation better.  We gave the waitress a really good tip and left-never to return.

text:
This review is looong overdue...
I've been to Center Square Tavern (CST as I like to call it) several times now since they opened, and each time has been absolutely phenomenal! Food, cocktails, and especially the service are impeccable!
I've been here with my wife, friends (adults only), wife and daughter, and families...and CST is perfect for each one of these groups. While family friendly, it's also a great spot to just grab a drink (or several)! This place has private dining, a nice sized bar, plenty of seating, live music on certain nights, and an outdoor patio area.
The wait staff is here is very nice and super attentive. Every dining experience has been great, but two that stick out are Kelly (my daughter absolutely LOVES her), and Madison (this gal ran across the entire parking lot after us because we left something behind).
The bartenders here are awesome. Elizabeth always has some new spicy drink for my wife to try, Joey G is a man that can pour, and Kelly ensures your glass is never empty.
The food here is incredible! CST has officially been crowned the Best Wings in South Jersey (by me)! Seriously. Too Hot is my absolute favorite--while it's definitely quite spicy, it is not overbearing and has an excellent flavor. The Executive Chef Dan Luber came out to meet us and see the "daring couple" that ordered them. All the dishes I've had here have been awesome--kudos to Dan for a job well done! Also, you'll see Dan roaming around the dining room speaking to the diners about the food and their experience--he's a great chef, but also a really nice guy!
All in all, hit up CST if you're looking for great food and drinks with good vibes!

Recommended Dishes:
Ahi Tuna Tartar
Blackened Shrimp
Buffalo Shrimp
CST Wings (try the Too Hot on the side first)
Fries
Southwest Chicken Salad
Blackened Mahi Mahi
Grilled Chicken Bruschetta
Twin Lobster Tails

*For kids: my daughter loves the Kids Chicken Bites and the Kids Pasta

text: I've been going here since the early 80's. The quality has never wavered, the dough is made daily, the sauce is wonderful and they have a good selection of toppings. They have expanded their menu over the years and now they have wings. Large meaty wings which are great!! I've tried most of their sandwiches, Calzones and salads. My favorites are the Italian Sausage Sandwich, the Anti Pasta Salad, and the wings. The salads are fresh, the lettuce crunchy, tomatoes are ripe and then whatever toppings you get are plentiful. I always get the small sandwich and it is the perfect size for me. The bread is fresh, they give you a good amount of fillings (the steak is really good too). I've never had a bad meal here. I have a friend who comes to Tampa a couple of times a year and this is the first place she wants to go to get a slice. This is a great little pizza place, I love the fact that you can order a slice or the whole pie. They also do a white pizza and a deep dish. They are now serving cannoli and they are very good. The staff is always pleasant, they talk to you, to each other and you can tell they enjoy being there. The original owner has retired somewhat and his son is running the place. They remodeled a few years ago and things seem to be working out well. You can purchase bottled beer and specialty sodas, they also have a regular drink machine. It is a fun place where good food is served in a very pleasant atmosphere. If you are looking for a slice or the whole pie or even a good sandwich and salad try them out.

text:
The first time we went to Rue Bourbon was not long after it officially opened. We enjoyed the lively ambience and our server did her best to attend to us despite being extremely busy. We received our drinks fairly quickly but after waiting nearly an hour for our Shrimp Po' Boy, the owner came over and apologized. There was a major problem in the kitchen (fryer wasn't working) and he offered us a Muffalata instead. Since I don't eat red meat we declined but expressed appreciation that he spent some time talking with us. We understand there can be some kinks to work out when opening a new restaurant so we vowed to come back at a later time.

Last night was our later time! It wasn't nearly as crazy crowd-wise and we were invited by an older gentleman to sit with him at a large table to get a better view of the band. Our server took our order right away - we were excited to finally try their Shrimp Po' Boy sliders with fries. I was happy to know they still offered Breaking Bud IPA on draft and had that while my husband had a different double IPA. 

A few minutes later, the gentleman at our table asked the server if they had any chicken on the menu. She responded that yes, he can have the sliders made with chicken so he ordered them. A few minutes after that, she arrived and delivered his meal while we still waited for ours. The gentleman expressed disbelief that his meal was ready so quickly. Of course, you all know what's coming, our server came out a few minutes later saying she made a big mistake and the gentleman was eating the Shrimp Po' Boy that we ordered. My first thought was that thank goodness he didn't have a shellfish allergy! My second was that mistakes happen and we knew we would get our order eventually. I did feel bad for the gentleman because he barely touched his food. 

When we finally received our order, we did very much enjoy it. We both enjoy Cajun food and both the Po' Boy and the fries were spiced just right. We also enjoy the ambience here and knowing there is a reliable place to catch a jazz band in town.
name: Kimberly

Best super cheap chinese buffet in St Louis County. Seriously its like less than $10 for a full buffet and dead uncooked fish bait (i am told this is called sushi and is a good thing). 

The restaurant is very much your standard chinese decor of strange lights and little fat happy guys. Pretty comfy and quiet place. 

What you want to know: food ratings.

4/5 - pepper chicken

text:
Really nice vibe, trendy diner place. The menu is not as overwhelming as a regular diner would have but what they do have gives you a refined version. 

The Chef's Special of the day which is the Scallop Watermelon Salad with Corn, Jalapeños, Pickled Onions drizzled with Balsamic Elderberry Sauce was good! Sauce really paired well with the watermelon and balanced the taste of the ocean. The portion is a bit on the small side but quality over quantity! I give this a 4-star instead of 5 because of the cook on the scallops--They were a tad overcooked but wasn't too dry to send them back.

Another entree we tried is the Short Rib Chilaquiles! Sooooooo good! I love how the corn chips came with the apple poblano salsa already on them! The salsa was hot enough but wasn't too strong that you're mouth is left burnt. Not sure if you were supposed to crack the poached eggs over it but they were cooked perfectly! The only thing was that I wasn't a fan of the horseradish crema but that's more a personal choice than anything. Overall, a good dish!

Both dishes were great and the staff are friendly and attentive to boot! The ambiance and the decor is relaxing, it kinda seems like you walked into a trendy 50's diner. Next time we'll try their drinks!

text: WOW! "Lulu's Casita" is AWESOME! I had heard about it from a few friends and finally got a chance to take the kids over to Ardmore to check it out for myself. It was a chilly day, so indoor play was in order! Grandma is tired of cleaning up the disaster my kids keep leaving in her family room. So, off we went to Lulu's Casita! Lulu's Casita is a huge play space with several different themed play areas, COMFY couches FOR PARENTS to chill on while the kiddos play, and a large cafe. You enter Lulu's from street level, but you can't see the actual play space until you walk down the stairs, so you have no idea what awaits you when you first open the door: A MAGICAL SPACE to light up the imaginations of children and adults alike! The staff was super friendly, informative, and cleaning constantly. The space is welcoming and well-maintained. I was super impressed by the decor, much of which included sensory opportunities for the little ones. It is abundantly evident that Lulu's Casita was created out of a love for people and play. It is a work of art, and ode to whimsy! My favorite part of my life is being a mama and my favorite part of being a mama is discovering cool new places with my little ones. They both had so much fun exploring today and I loved seeing their expressions as they discovered each different play area. Grandma had fun too!

text: First visit rocked. Vanessa took such great care of us, but Stacy the manager stole the show. She made superb recommendations delivered personally to us with a smile. Try the Cherry Bomb on a fried rice ball or ichi sea bass on spicy crab nigiri style. Even the matcha ice cream was special. You must eat here!
name: Jeff

text: We love the atmosphere of this place, particularly outdoors in the summer. All the food we've tried has been excellent, and the lemonade is to die for.
name: Jennie

text: The music was louder than it needed to be. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. Price felt a touch high for what it was. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. Definitely coming back. Not bad for a quick meal. Would probably stop in again if nearby.
name: User

text: Hello all, first of all Indianapolis is one of saddest sports town I have ever been in. On numerous occasions I have to ask for them to put a local games on.  I was in Detroit over New Year's and the Lions were playing Green Bay Packers, with No Aaron Rogers, and neither team had Any Playoffs implications.  But they had a full house at Ford Field and it was so cold out.  Today I went to the Stacked Pickle in Plainfield and you have the No.5 in the country playing "Purdue" local, and they are showing the Michigan vs Michigan State game with sound.  So sad.  I asked why, they said it was their feature game.

text: I'll keep it real- I always go to Goodfellas for a slice of pizza and a breadstick after a night out on Mass Ave. They are open late and for a few bucks, you get tasty pizza and a HUGE breadstick! It's a cute spot on the Ave to sit and snack with friends, have a drink at the attached whiskey bar, and enjoy top 40 hits! The staff is friendly and always quick service.

text: Went with family on a Sunday and it was louder than I expected. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. For the price I expected more than this. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Food was fresh and service was quick.
name: User

text: Excellent Mexican food made by family who love what they do. Service can be spotty but not enough to deter me from visiting.  Tim's of good food made by good people.
name: William

text: Dropped it last night for an after dinner drink and was very impressed in the overall charm of this restaurant. Had a drink and sat out on magazine street people watching. The restaurant does offer some really unique appetizers and a variety of beignets to choose from. Next visit I plan to have room for dessert.  Very beautiful and a somewhat French charm. Actually felt like I was in Paris. A+

text: My uber driver recommended this place and man thank goodness for him!! Super delicious food, I had the breakfast burrito and it hit the spot. My mom had the American, a perfect simple sandwich. It can with a side of the kefir herb dressing and that was soooo good and super refreshing!! Delicious cold brew as well. Reasonably priced. If you ever need a quick breakfast or lunch spot in the garden district this is it!!

text: It is so nice and fancy here. There is a large variety of sushi rolls and the price range will suit most.
name: Judene

text: Ordered takeout bc I didnt feel like cooking and it held up okay. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. It was decent, just a little uneven. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.
name: User

text: Food is actually "ok" not great but, don't show up on Taco Night Monday because you are treated like crap! Even if you are a regular who comes during the week they don't care !   Just rude, charge you for eating too much salsa, sour cream, no hot sauce at tables, Margaritas are watered down!, and most of all on Monday's they just want you to maleate and move on!!!! Hey, be nicer to your customers!

text: Beyond amazing! Short walk from our hotel....and worth every step! Food 5 Stars, service 10 Stars!!! Try the Hail Mary if you prefer beer with all the Bloody Mary fixings!
name: Rachel

text: decided to give this place a shot.   already a bunch of taco places on 4th so wasn't sure we needed another one.   but holy amazing tacos Batman!!!   this place blows all the others away.   first off they have the softest tortillas I have ever experienced.   absolutely delicious.   I tried several different tacos.  huge menu so easy to do.   fried pork.   grilled shrimp.  steak.  thry all have names but I just remember that each one was better than the last.   it was crowded but line moved pretty fast.  girl at register very helpful and made good suggestions.   had my first Florida snowball.  won't spoil the surprise but definitely have to get it.   won't disappoint.   overall this place is now not only my favorite taco place on 4th but my new goto spot in st pete!
name: regular

text: Went upstairs on a weeknight and it was empty with music blaring so loud we had to yell to hold a conversation. Burger was what was to be expected. The mushroom cuban sandwich was really small and lackluster for the price. The chef used not pepper but half cracked peppercorns (ton of it). It was overpowering, made my stomach and sinuses hurt. I am sad because I have been going here on off for years... probably won't be back.
name: Lucky

text: This is a hidden restaurant right off Williams Blvd, where the old Trauth's was. You get plenty for the reasonable price.  I last tried their shrimp fried rice!  It was fantastic!  As the lovely waitress said they do not use a lot of oil which makes it extremely moist!  I had enough leftovers for two more servings!!  Their seafood is wonderful and soups are great!  It's a must go to place!!!  SEE YOU THERE!
name: Pam

text: In a great area, nice and very comfortable.  The King room is a little small but it will do.  Great view of the city of New Orleans. If I have to I will stay again.
name: Mae

text:
I thoroughly enjoyed my gumbo combo dinner! Though i arrived at dinner time the wait for food wasn't long. Both employees that I encountered; one who took my order and another who served my food were polite, professional and helpful.
The gumbo was delicious and so was the thin fried catfish and garlic potatoes. Everything was very filling so I didn't eat my bread. Though I did have a little of their free soft serve ice cream 
Price was very reasonable, especially considering everything that it included
name: Tina

text: Came here to celebrate our 3 year anniversary and the experience was amazing! Megan is such a great server and appreciated and enjoyed her suggestions.
name: Melissa

text: Delicious burgers from well cared for cows is a good thing. No extra charge for 6 toppings is a great thing. Yummy food in a well lit modern atmosphere, plus amazing shakes. Eat here
name: Megan

text: Solid hoagies and very good wings. I like the fact that you can order a mini sandwich or a whole sandwich depending on who it is for. Prices are on point
name: john

text:
Dear Yellow Submarine, My kids had your pizza at Skyzone in Maple Shade New Jersey.  We've been on a pizza tour for three months plus, and this is stop number 20. I have to say at this point I'm not sure that I really like pizza. I have been opting out for salads.   

However, your pizza was actually very, very good.  My daughter gave me a bite of her pizza. When the kids disappeared to go jump around on the trampolines, I went back and ordered myself a slice. I have to say that I enjoyed it. I have NOT enjoyed pizza very much since stop number 15. So, congratulations for putting my faith back in pizza.
name: Linda

text: The best eggplant parm in the area. Tastes like grandma's recipe. Overall nice atmosphere too.
name: Brittany

text: Went here last night to celebrate my birthday and will be coming back again. We have a favorite restaurant in New Hope but we wanted to try something new and I'm glad we did. The ambiance can't be beat. It's illuminated mostly by candles so it's dark, cozy, and romantic. It is small because it's a historic colonial house, but that adds to its charm. We were seated at a table downstairs so I can't comment on the upstairs room that everyone raves about, but it was still a great atmosphere downstairs. The music was a lot of 80's new wave hits and some 90's alt rock, so if you grew up in these decades you can especially appreciate the playlist. As for the food, everything we had was great. The goat cheese crostinis with honey were amazing as well as the Brussel sprouts with siracha. Burgers were juicy and salted nicely, balanced with the sweetness of caramelized onions. They have a nice selection of wine and beer, although I plan to come back for a girl's night and try some of those cocktails and check out the upstairs. All in all, a very tasty meal in what I would deem the most enjoyable atmosphere in New Hope.
name: L

text: Staff is very attentive and the vibe is very cool. Noisy in the bar area but the menu is diverse and offers something for everyone. The food is excellent except the prime rib. I ordered it but not what I expected, thin and prepared on the grill? The manager made things right and all is good.
name: Marcia

text: My friend liked it more than I did. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. For a busy night they handled it okay. I'd maybe go back, but I'd order differently next time. Nice little spot, decent portions too. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. They were out of one thing I originally wanted..
name: User

text: Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. The staff seemed tired but still polite. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Just not for me. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Not bad for a quick meal. Food took a while and didn't rlly feel worth the wait.
name: User

text:
Phenomenal! 

Love the purpose, love the place, love the food.
Genuine and unique foods made with passion. The most delicious vegan dishes I have ever tried. I was a little hesitant as I do tend to enjoy my red meats and hearty dishes, but boy was I wrong. What I discovered was something completely different and beyond my expectations. The mushroom pasta and veggie bowl were packed with flavor. After one bite of each, I was in awe. 

I can't seem to get Mesa Verde off the back of my mind. Perhaps another visit is in order.
name: Rick

text: If you have been to St. Pete Beach but have not yet been to Larry's, then run (don't walk) to try their gelato. They have an excellent selection and very reasonable prices for the fantastic gelato that they have. Serving was much bigger than back home. You can tell that they are meticulous about making delicious gelato. I'll go back again next time I'm in the neighborhood. (Vision Scientists, GO! You won't regret it!)
name: Drew

text: It's so true this is the best Danish I ever had. I ended up eating two Danish for breakfast. Almond croissant is very tasty too. One of the best bakeries I've ever been to.
name: Yi

text: This place is small but amazing food very good buzz about the restaurant I would highly recommend anybody to try this the food is amazing.
name: Kirk

text: Love this place! Food is delicious! Service is outstanding! We drove almost 3 hours to eat here. Worth the drive!!
name: Lily

text: Leverock's is our favorite seafood restaurant in the area.  I used to go to the original  twenty years ago and that was fabulous.  When they brought in the new chef a couple of years ago to the new leverocks it became a fabulous again.  My wife and I have tried many seafood restaurants in the area and leverocks still has the best pricing, the freshest fish, and if you're in a group they do not rush you.  It is the spot where we eat once or every two weeks and always bring guests with large groups to experience fresh fish.
name: Bill

text:
We went to Blackbear today in a group of 10 for a work lunch/co worker's bday. I ordered one of my favorite things- chicken and waffles. The portions are WAY big but still a disappointment. My waffle was pancake batter with waffle edges. I don't LIKE pancakes. The chicken was crispy and seasoned well so they get two stars but nah.. a coworker had the cheeseburger salad and I swear to you it was a 3 person dinner portion. They brought her salad dressing in a coffee cup. If you like biscuits and gravy (I don't) this might be a good spot for you, they were huge and a coworker said they were good. I won't be returning. 
Ps. The bday girl's food came out 15 mins after the rest of us had been served and she only ordered a sandwich.
name: Kalyn

text: I had heard of this place before and didnt really understand the hype. From the road it just looks like a place you can go in and buy seafood, but being in a landlocked state you kinda become iffy on the seafood choices we have around here. We happened to have a coupon for a buy one entree get the second one for free for dinner and my husband has been wanting to try for months so we decided to give it a go. I got the fried shrimp with beans and rice and macaroni and he got the fried alligator.  Both were out of this world, I swear my shrimp were jumbos and you got alot of them. I couldn't finish off all my food because there was just so much of it. The sides were small but enough that you were leaving the restaurant full. Even my husband couldn't finish off all of his food and he normally will finish his and whatever is left of mine. Needless to say this is a place we will be venturing up to the north side too again.
name: Danielle

text: I absolutely love this place. Sushi is fresh and you cannot beat their happy hour prices. We come here 2-3x a month and can order 5 rolls for $25-30 dollars. Ramen is also delicious and waiters are friendly and great with kids. Best sushi place in STL!
name: Rachel

text:
We've been in Tucson for 3 years and have been looking for some good, spicy chicken sausage and have been unsuccessful until we arrived at the Sausage Shop. It has been an ongoing search. We are spoiled from being from the Northwest and the great sausage made by Isernios.  This sausage far exceeds any sausage that Isernios makes!!  I am originally from New Orleans and looking forward to their Boudin.....unfortunately, they were out when we were there but we will be back and am sure that it will not disappoint us.....while there, my wife and I had a deli sandwich and they were both excellent!!  My wife and I will be back many times to come in the future (even if it takes us 35 minutes to get there)....when you find an establishment like this, it doesn't matter.....and, the people are very nice and friendly!!

James Bailey Flemming
Marana(Dove Mtn. area)

text:
The BBQ shrimp and milk money latte were AHMAZING. And beautiful!

My husband and I split the BBQ shrimp and it was more than enough. The biscuit was good, but certainly nothing life changing.

The ambiance was cool and the service quick. Try the espresso chocolate cookies too!

text:

text:
Went in on a Wednesday evening around 7pm and was seated right away. The first thing that caught me was the ambiance: definitely more of a darker, cozy vibe, with plush purple velvet seating, mood lighting and dark wood, well, everything. It's in the old Midtown Eats space, so it's definitely on the smaller side, but it was a comfortable fit for two adults and two younger children. 

The menu is ample with a handful of offerings under each course--some more conventional, like garlic and herb fries, while others were a bit more unique, like shrimp and grits. I opted for the Roasted Beet salad with grilled chicken; the lemon champagne vinaigrette was DELECTABLE! The S/O and little man went with a traditional burger and fries, while our princess chose the tacos. No complaints from anyone (rather, both boys raved about the pickled onions that accompanied their burgers!), but I did notice the taco shells looked like the precooked ones you buy in a pack at the grocery store...I could be wrong, but they certainly didn't look like they just popped out a fryer or anything like that. Considering almost all their fare is sourced from local growers, I found this to be a slight deterrent from the overall expectation. 

With four meals and two drinks (non-alcoholic, for the babes), the price was right under $70, so I'd say it's one of the more affordable "non-franchise" dinner options in the area. And from what I hear, they'll also be serving lunch and breakfast soon too, so we're looking forward to going back for more--with hopes the box taco shells are just a memory of Gastropub past!

text: They are out of business :( place says for rent. miss this place it was delicious for brunch

It was extremely insulting that they would assume a customer would be happy with that! The service there is awful and the food is crazy over priced! Definitely do not order food from Boca using Uber eats! They have a shitty staff and the portion size is like I said insulting! Never again!

text: Food was fresh and service was quick. You can tell they care about customer experience here. Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Would return. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. The whole meal felt kind of uneven.

By far the BEST roast beef sandwich in town. There is always the perfect amount of meat and cheese and the rolls always taste fresh. The gravy fries are a must try. Even though the fries were completely smothered in roast beef and gravy, they kept their unbelievable crispness.

text: I appreciate what they do here and making everything from scratch. We tried a muffuletta and a pork belly sandwich. The muffuletta was nothing to rave about, the the pork belly was very delicious. It can get very crowded with the convention center being very close to this location.
name: Sam

text: I have been here innumerable times to enjoy a meal, but this review is specifically for a large party event. The portion sizes were big, the selections vast, and the prices very reasonable. I was glad to be able to bring friends here to enjoy a great night out together!
name: Angela

text: Had brunch here over the weekend and it was kind of a mixed bag. Idk, everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Food was fresh and service was quick. Also, no big complaints, just a nice meal. For a busy night they handled it okay. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Would probably stop in again if nearby. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything..
name: User

text:
I decided after having a not so great day, that I would have a nicer lunch than I usually do, so I thought I would come here. I was sat quickly at a table that literally could not be in a worse spot.  I was bumped into by servers every few minutes,  who clearly could not have cared less that they just ran into someone with a food covered plate. Then my server Kelly, pops up out of no where before hand and bluntly asks if I know what I want to eat. I just sat down? Later she comes back,  takes my order,  and I literally never hear from her again. 

At first I thought it was because she had a lot of tables,  but soon, all of those tables left and still,  literally not one peep from her. Like,  other people delivered my food, and she didn't check once that it was ok,  nor did she refill my drink. I looked her right in her face twice to see if I was just being weird,  but she just looked right at me and kept walking.  It was seriously weird.

 Then I finally stopped someone who got her to bring me my check,  which was 22 bucks and some change. She was then all over me to get my card which was also annoying,  there was literally not even 1 minute between getting the check and giving her my card, whereas before she couldn't even be bothered to check in on the food. She ran my card and comes back with a slip for 25 bucks. I asked her how that happened,  and she said she didn't know.  What??? You literally just gave me the check and in 2 minutes it goes up and you don't know why? I figured out that the original check didn't have the tea on it,  which was fine. That answer would've been the correct and honest answer to give,  not,  "Oh, I don't know". Meanwhile I'm sitting there with trash and plates all over my table,  which I put in an easy pile for her or someone to pre-bus, no one could've cared less. I still gave this server over 20% tip, because it was the right thing to do,  but honestly she didn't deserve a dime of it. Honestly she should be ashamed of that level of service,  as someone who was a server for several years. I was legitimately creeped out by the blatantly bad service,  having no idea what I could've possibly done to deserve it. 

3 stars because the Marathon Burger was honestly really great,  and so were the fries. Minus two stars not only for Kellys bad service,  but frankly everyone who worked there besides the friendly girl I flagged down was completely oblivious,  like it was all of their first days. Your restaurant is way too tasty and pretty to be acting like that.
name: Michaela

text:
Excellent bartenders. They ran out of an ingredient for my drink, but exchanged it with a hand crafty beauty. 

We had a dozen gulf oysters, which were fairly large in size. 

For a side, the poutine was the dish of choice. And let me tell you their fries are excellent. 

Will definitely be coming back for their amazing happy hour

text: It looked better online than it did in person. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. A couple small things kept adding up. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon.
name: User

text: We stopped in on a whim after going to the Farmer's market. Having never been before we asked the lady who served us for some recommendations. She recommended either the Garlic Soy or Korean BBQ chicken. My partner and I elected to share their deal which comes with 5 prices of chicken, a half salad, a can of pop, and either fries or a corn fritter. With a bill that amounted to only $15.00 for two of us, we wondered if it would be enough food and we were not disappointed. The portion was more than enough, the chicken perfectly cooked and crunchy, and the sauce was delicious. The fries were excellent and we ordered a corn fritter as well to try it. While I never would have thought to drizzle milk over a fritter, it was superb. This place offers not just delicious food, but is an excellent value.

text: The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would..

text: No tomatoes, a half a piece of bacon and a half of a lettuce leaf, WOW! Service suck on top of that. If I had dined in,  I would of threw it back at them in their face and walked out. Don't GO HERE!

text: It is such a shame that this restaurant is empty every time I go. The food is absolutely incredible and the service could not be more 1st class. El Libre provides an interesting creole twist on Cuban food and consistently delivers incredible meals into the mouths of hungry people. The brunch is absolutely unreal. Advice to management: relocate or market the shit out of this place to the nearby college campuses. Would hate to see this place go because business is too slow.

text:
Cute coffee house vibe with plenty of healthy/organic breakfast & lunch options. We went after the lunch craziness, & were able to get seats. 

I ordered the grilled salmon BLT. It was delicious & generous portion! I ate half there, and got home just to eat the other half. It was too good. I was able to add a fruit cup as my side which was much appreciated. They have smoothies & coffee, along with huge selection of healthy drinks including coconut waters, organic iced teas, & La Croix seltzer's. 

Pricing is fair. 
Parking is ok - go into the neighborhood around the corner, & there's street parking. Just read signs for any restrictions.
name: Erika

text: First time eating here and I was not disappointed. I'm eating keto and they had lots of options. I ordered off their secret menu. Bacon wrapped yellow peppers stuffed with cheese and shrimp. It comes with a yummy dipping sauce made with soy sauce and herbs. I was also in love with their cucumber pico de gallo. The service was awesome and the restaurant was very clean.
name: Melissa

text: Comparing this to Texas de Brazil or Fogo de Chao, it suffices. Their sides leave more to be desired but their cuts of meat are quite good. Large variety for lunch more than the other two places. The meats are not over seasoned with salt, in some cases they could have used a bit more but that helped me drink less water and got more meat down. Sides that worked well for me were the plantains and beans. Salmon rice was ok (with beans);Yucca was ok; salads ok. Great place to get your meat fix
name: D

text: We had a fantastic dinner here last night with great service. We had the imperial rolls, vegan nachos, Japanese sweet potato fries, pineapple fried rice, portobello avocado rolls, and cauliflower pizza. I loved everything except the portobello avocado rolls and that was mostly because there was seaweed and it didn't state that on the menu. The hot sauce they make in house is out of this world good. This place is 100 percent gluten free and vegan. Definitely a place to visit if you are in the Rittenhouse square area. This establishment is also BYOB.
name: Nisa

text:
I am a Chinese-American from California, so you can imagine that I am pretty picky about Asian food in general. Tucson's options for good and authentic Chinese cuisine are rather limited. Therefore, my expectations for Asian restaurants here are lower than back home in California. With this mindset, I expected the noodles to be something like mediocre ramen, but I was SO wrong. 

The first time I came here, I ordered the House Wonton Noodle Soup. Now I can't stop ordering it. The handmade noodles, the pork wonton, bbq pork, chicken, shrimp, and bok choy are all cooked to perfection. The flavors blend harmoniously together in chicken broth. I really need to try other dishes on the menu but this one is so good that it is hard not to order it. This is my go-to spot for authentic Chinese noodle soup. I always leave with a warm and happy stomach. Honestly, I'm kind of embarrassed by how often I go haha.

I know that the two are quite different, but if I want good noodle soup, I will choose Noodleholics 100 times over any ramen joint in Tucson.
name: Andi

text: Dessert saved this a little. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. The music was louder than it needed to be. I left full, which at least counts for something. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..
name: User

text: One of the best food around here. Had ribeye and the banana foster. Both were really good and the show was good! Really nice decor and popular place.

text: Just ate here with my family. Great options including a good kid's menu. First up - shrimp fresh rolls. Very fresh and the peanut sauce was thick and tasty. The kids meals were big and both were devoured quickly. I had the pork bun and my wife had the chicken bun. Both were excellent!  We will definitely be back!

text:
Today is the fifth time we have visited we got there and there is a bit of a wait, however we had the mind set to get reservation for five people at 8:30am on a Sunday Father's Day, so we expect it to be busy.  The wait is huge like seven to eight parties waiting for tables, so we were lucky they got our reservation correct and were seated at 8:30, no wait.   

We sat inside where there were, I  counted Seven tables open and five open spots at the bar.   We ordered at 8:50am mark, it took the food server twenty minutes to take our order

The server came back to the table to make sure her had our order correct and came back again to make sure our order was correct and he can back a third time  to tell us there was no shrimp and grits, and then came back a fourth time to make sure he got the veggie omelet right.   

Our breakfast arrived 9:40am an hour and ten minutes after being seated.  I believe the kitchen was running slow, however our food server was awful, he was a crappy food server, he spoke really fast and was hard to understand, he kept getting our orders wrong.

Sad part is after the long wait our orders were still wrong.   What a joke!  

We like the food, service is crap!
name: Mark

text:
I very, very rarely give one star but wow.  This place, or maybe it was the night we were there, was an absolute fail.

Let's start with the greek flaming cheese appetizer....that we never got.  The waitress forgot it and then brought it over at the end of our meal.  It was lit for a moment and barely singed.  Not melted or crusted at all.  Cold in the middle.

The dinner salad basically was covered in olive oil and garlic.  It was so strong the garlic made the salad spicy/hot.

The octopus appetizer/meal is what I personally ordered. The octopus meat itself was perfectly cooked.  Hence the 1 star.  However, it was then drenched in butter and most likely the same garlic that was used on the salad.  I love Octopus and couldn't finish it.

The rest of my four top table all got giro platter.  The meat had been shaved probably that morning and dried under a heat lamp.  The taziki sauce never came.  When it did two ramekins were brought for three diners, but that's okay 'cause the third dinner was forgotten too.  It just never came at all.  

Which kinda worked out since the cheese came at the end and my friend got to eat that instead of the giro meal he ordered.

Whew!  Don't go here.  Keep walking down the street and get some real food.
name: Jeannie

text: I'd be able to comment on the food if they had served us anything but room-temp coffee in the HOUR we spent waiting. We finally left because we were starving and there was no sign of our food coming out.
name: Hanna

text:
I could eat and drink here everyday!

For such a busy place, the service here is amazing! Not sure how they could keep a smile on for a whole shift dealing with hangry people all day. 

For drinks - if you enjoy margaritas as much as I do, try either the coconut kiwi margarita or the flip flop margarita. I made the mistake of ordering a key lime colada and it was pretty tasteless. I'm assuming most of the frozen drinks are...

For appetizers - order the garlic crab fries and the tuna stuffed avocados. Then try both the fried AND the Cajun grouper, UPGRADE to the super size version to have a nice bun to fish ratio, and thank me later! The fries are also pretty good if you wanna upgrade from the chips too.

As much as it's tempting to come here for dinner followed by a lovely sunset, I would suggest going here for lunch. You are more likely to get a table on the patio facing the ocean. Otherwise, expect to wait well over an hour for dinner! It's worth the wait either way. There are 2 other locations about a 5 minute walk away if you decide to skip the view and just EAT.
name: Thu

text: NY style pies. Super thin crusts and a phenomenal taste of a sliced meatball pie is what I chose for my first experience with this place.  The staff was super friendly. You can buy it by the slice or the whole pie. I found a new goto pizza place.

text: It's sad to even write this, but since the days of my childhood this place has gone downhill. The food quality, the culture, and the customer service has gone from satisfactory to horrible within the past five to ten years, and this seems to be a popular consensus among locals....So because I'm from the neighborhood and this place is special to me, it actually took me a while to write a review about my last few visits here which have not been pleasant. So I'll share a bit about my last visit here was on Friday May 3rd at 11:15pm. I walked in hoping to grab a cheesesteak from here before they closed at 11:30, only to be welcomed by the snark remarks of disgruntled employees. One male worker grunted, "I thought I locked that door". Which I let that fly by. There were a few other customers in the store still who were being serviced. So one of the young ladies says, "I hope y'all are giving us a tip for coming in so late." I let that slide by as well, saying to myself "okay, whatever", I just want my cheesesteak. So as I'm waiting to make my order another female employee comes out of the back chattering with the other employees, then she says in a jokingly yet sly tone, "The guy with the burgundy shirt needs to turn around and leave out." Okay now you all wanna get personal. Now I go into a whole discussion with these employees about how the store says that it closes at 11:30 and I made it here 15 minutes prior, which is more than enough time to make a cheesesteak. Why am I now going back and forth with employees about a service that they filled out an application for doing, and it's still before 11:30 as we're talking lol? I then try to end the discussion by saying to them well the sign says that the store closes at 11:30, so whatever. One of the younger female employees then says, "We close at what time "we" say we're closed". This back and forth exchange goes on with different employees all the way until I get my steak made, which consisted of reheated dry steak meat that they got from the back which was apparently cooked and left over from earlier. Smh, not the first time this has happened, and now the meat is filled with gristle every few bites. Needless to say, after that experience I didn't even eat the sandwich. That horrible experience was the last straw towards keeping me from going to a place that meant so much to the neighborhood and the tradition of Philly. R.I.P to the spirit of the old Pagano's.
name: Jeffrey

text: The broth is everything to me and this broth is so good! I am definitely looking forward to coming back again. We needed a place like this in SB! I definitely recommend the black garlic ramen and the spicy ramen

text: The fries were probably the best part of the meal, honestly. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. The staff seemed tired but still polite. I wouldn't write it off, but I also wouldn't hype it up. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price..
name: User

text:
Soooo.... 

I am sitting here remembering the second time I came to this restaurant...... That time when I had the perfect steak,  the perfectly browned rolls,  the hot baked potato.  Ahhh...... It was amazing.  FAST FORWARD
Ive been sitting here since about 8:30 waiting on food.  Well actually,  it already came and left.  Why?  Because I asked for a rib-eye a little extra done on the edges and they bought me a staek my steak knife wouldn't even cut into.  What was supposed to be creamy mac and cheese was a dry,  burnt greasy concoction of bad decision making by the kitchen.  The potatoes looked ok,  bit what was the point without the rest.  So they took it away.  What came back was much better looking food,  BUT ......the mac and cheese was ice cold,  the steak tasted as though there was no seasoning,  and two potato lumps.  Oh,  did I mention the almost RAW rolls they bought out the first time?  

Maybe I could have gotten past all this if I didn't have a hostess get mad at me when I came in the door because I didn't want to sit at the bar!  Hmmmmm.... You decide if this place is for you,  because it CERTAINLY isn't for me.  I'll stick to other steak houses.

text:

I think it would be much more of a pleasant experience if they would hire more people especially on the weekends knowing that people are coming in there to get hoagies I waited almost 40 minutes for a hoagie. :(

text:
3/5 stars for products, not customer service.

This is a cute little eclectic place with a variety of goodies and local knick-knacks to peruse.  I went here to meet up with some friends for breakfast and the drive-thru was keeping the workers pretty busy.  We weren't helped for about 10 minutes, but that wasn't what bothered me.  My husband and I ordered a variety of baked goods and I had a matcha latte while he had a house coffee.

The matcha was bitter, and the coffee was burnt.  The quiche we got tasted like it was made a few days prior, and it was microwaved so much that it was hard to chew. My husband's croissant breakfast sandwich was decent, and the vegan muffin was moist and probably the only saving grace for the entire meal.  While the staff was friendly, I don't think I'll go out of my way to grab anything from this cafe again.
name: Sherissa

text:
It was OK. We live in OV and decided to try a new spot since we've heard good things about BBC. The place is cute, clean and old school diner style decor. They have a great patio area that would be awesome when it's nice out. 

The coffee was pretty good. I asked for a carafe of actual half and half (not the little plastic fake creams) and the server was able to accommodate. Not stoked about the food - it was just alright. My mom had a scrambled omelet and she said it was ok. I ordered the corned beef hash, and it was eh. The seasoning was too much (I think I tasted rosemary?) - so I didn't actually eat much of it. The potato cakes were pretty much just seasoned hash browns shaped into a patty but they were good. 

The service was great. Our server was very sweet and very attentive. Kept our coffee filled the whole visit. The rest of the staff was very nice as well. 

I just don't think the food was so great that we would drive all the way from OV for it. Glad we gave it a shot though.
name: Vanessa

text: Went here for happy hour and dinner and I was impressed! Great deals on food and drinks. The place had a cool vibe - especially the outdoor space. I didn't expect the sushi to be as good as it was (some sushi spots in philly just try to be "hip" but serve up super basic subpar rolls) but this place exceeded my expectations and had some unique options.

text:
I know! Four Stars! It's this location! They have fast service, friendly staff,  consistently good and hot pizza. $5 for a Hot n' Ready Pizza is perfect for the kids, me on a movie day or just need a pizza that isn't breaking the budget. I often place my order for sausage pizza, if not immediately available, and still only 8-10 minute wait or less.

The lunch special is my favorite for $5.99 for 4 slices of Detroit style deep dish plus a beverage. The Italian Cheese Bread, $4.99, is perfect for a side or lunch. So give this location a try if your location isn't hitting the mark. Stuffed crust, deep, deep dish, or classic crust covers most peoples pizza favs. Need a few sides to go with your pizza, then try the oven roasted wings with BBQ, Buffalo or Garlic Parmesan Caesar sauce. 

Sure it's not Union Jacks Pizza but it isn't $25 dollars either. There's a time for Union Jacks Pizza and more often time for Little Caesars.

text: Best deli ever!  My memories of this place started in the early 1980's when I was a kid, as the "go to" place for baseball cards and Big League Chew chewing gum. text: I absolutely loved this place. It's awesome feel good food. The staff was very friendly. The wait for the food was a bit longer than expected but food was very good and so were the drinks. They gave it to me with mustard and jalapeños ranch anyways. I absolutely hate Dijon mustard. They were very apologetic and offered to remake it. I instead asked them to take it off the ticket and they did. I definitely recommend this place and will go back next time I'm in st Pete.

text: My husband and I get massages at Atlantis every 2-3 months. Our massages (or facials for me) are always amazing. The rooms are relaxing and enjoyable. The problem.... the women's changing room (I'm sure its got an official name, but I don't know it). It's awful, so much so that it can ruin the whole experience. It is so hot, that women who are getting ready to leave are standing naked trying to blow dry their hair with the dryer on cool. They always give up. It's so hot that you simply can't dry your hair, you are sweating too much. Your make-up runs, clothes are sticking to you. It is a miserable way to end what WAS an amazing day. Last time I was there, (2-18-19) a group of 4 ladies said that they would rather go to the Peppermill's spa. It doesn't have the rooms to relax in, but you can get ready to go out in nice, cool temperatures. Oh, and don't think about telling the bosses and getting it fixed. The Spa manager can't do anything, it her bosses that don't care. So if you want a great massage, relaxing rooms to hang out in, and a HORRIBLE ending to you day while you try to get ready to leave, this is the place for you. Oh, and don't forget that you also need to have a desire to be ignored when you bring up any concern....

text:
I've previously been to El Gallo Giro on a couple of occasions as it's less than a mile from my home. Each visit has brought great food & memorable service. One visit led the manager to offer me 1 million tacos if I signed with his city league basketball team. 

Tonight's visit was no exception. It was my first trip here for their famed Taco Tuesday(that I've been hearing about for the last 18 months. 5 different meats, multiple shells & all the fixings in a self serve format let me do some serious work on my waistline. After tonight, they may just have to change the reader board to say "Rob Loves Tacos"

Our waiter knocked it out of the park, with his humor, magic tricks and attention to our needs. I'm probably going to take off work next Tuesday so I can spend more time eating their tacos. 


UPDATE 5/15/18
I keep going back for Taco Tuesday, and bringing friends with me. Javier has been our server every single time, and he continues to be incredible. I only understand half of his jokes, but he is always entertaining. I keep eating until I'm miserably full(every single time) and it's so worth it. Customer for life.
name: Rob

text:
First of all, I DO want to point out how awesome the service was here. Our server was on point and it was very busy that night.

However, the food quality just wasn't as good as other teppan grill restaurants I've been to and on top of that, the prices were higher than others. 

The steak was fatty and had a lot of gristle. I got scallops (which costs extra there) and I kept biting into extremely gritty, sandy textures and I seriously thought I chipped a tooth at some point. The scallops were small and rubbery and not cleaned properly. 

And I know the chefs often make jokes and poke fun at guests (it's part of the experience) but this dude would seriously NOT stop harassing me and it really started making me uncomfortable. Even other people at our table were like, ugh....wtf?? Not a fun experience. 

The layout is cool and the people who were working inside were nice but in order for me to want to return, the food quality would have to be much better.
name: J

text: Not a very large selection on the menu. Just sandwiches and burgers really. It took forever to get our food. When it came out half of it was cold. The burgers were over cooked and dry and the waitress never asked how we wanted them cooked.  Fries were old.  Not very apologetic about the wait.  I'm surprised this place is as busy as it is when there are issues like this.  Numerous tables had the same issues.
name: Natalie

text: Dont let the location discourage you from dropping into this hidden gem for delicious cervapi and ajvar. Located close to the Italian Centre, this family run resturant has a front bar end and resturant seating in the back that serves delicious little Serbian sausages called cervapi, and when wrapped in the traditional soft buttery sweet lepinja flatbread, bits of raw onion (it works!), creamy cream cheese like kajmak spread and a healthy dallop of ajvar  a roasted sweet red pepper condiment... oh man. Just close your eyes and your tastebuds will dance. The staff are super friendly and happy to explain what items are. They excell at their cervapi but they have skewers and traditional burgers too. They have a behemoth sized Šarska Pljeskavica which is like a folded meat pancake stuffed with kajmak and ?mozzarella served with rice and lots of well seasoned melt in your mouth tender grilled zucchini and red peppers - hubby's a fan of the Šarska Pljeskavica. We recently had a birthday party so we had multiple gypsy platters.. each one feeds way more than 2 hungry people with 2 skewers of chicken/pork, 2 grilled chicken thighs, 10 cervapi, salad, rice, grilled veges and bread. Dont forget to ask for the kajmak and ajvar! If you're going as a big group call ahead to make reservations and a rough idea of what you will be ordering - it's a small family run place so the more notice they have, the faster you get to eat when you arrive!! You can always order takeout too if you need your cervapi fix.
name: Jan

text:
Tonight was our first experience at this eatery.  The inside is tastefully decorated with seating both inside and out.  There was a line when we arrived, however it moved swiftly, maybe a little too fast.   Let me explain, as I ordering they were three steps ahead and put bacon bits in my salad.  I didn't want bacin bits, can't stand them.  She did offer to redo the salad, but I was not going to hold the line up.  Very similar to Chipotles in how they serve you.  The salad was fresh, but needed more flavoring.  I could tell it was meat but it was a flavorless meat.  

My friend had the ginger steak bowl.  There was a good amount of "heat" which they liked.  Again, their complaint was not enough seasoning on the meat, flavorless.  The one turn off with this bowl was they take your food, flip it out into another container then steam your food.  GROSS! I have no idea what was in that steamer bowl before my food went in.  Good thing I am not allergic to anything.  Cross contamination is a no no!!

The lemonades they created were all delicious!! 5 stars for the drinks.  Not sure about the price as it was all free for grand opening.

My friend recommended Wang Gang highly, but after visiting, it's just OK. The restaurant is nicely decorated, with lots of hanging lights; very clean and modern. Service was pretty good, too.

If my friend insisted on coming again, I'd go along. But personally, I wouldn't recommend Wang Gang.

text:
We were there last night and the service staff were quite rude--not directly to us but toward two other parties within our viewing/hearing--which is actually worse.

First of all there was a couple seated behind us who appeared to be wrapping up their meal but in a leisurely fashion. It was 15 min before closing time (8:45pm which seemed like an early close, but maybe it's because of the holiday--we didn't know what time they closed when we arrived, only that they were still open). 

A waitress started stacking chairs and making such a racket I couldn't hear my son who had briefly called me on the phone to check in. 

Having shooed away the other couple (we were still getting our food), the noisy waitress then started mopping shortly there after which made the whole outside area of the restaurant smell like a third-rate jail.

Meanwhile I had to use the men's room and noted that it looked like it hadn't had a thorough cleaning in days. Maybe it had and it was just the end of the day, but it was pretty dirty so it probably needs a more frequent cleaning.

While in the restaurant, I could also hear our waitress saying something derogatory about someone to the cooking staff since the service window is right there by the restrooms.  She seemed to be in a foul mood.

Right around then,  a patron arrived just minutes before closing. Instead of informing him that only take-out would be available at that time, the two waitresses began criticizing him to each other right near where we were sitting (we were in outside area, he was seated inside apparently). We could easily hear their conversation.

This was putting us off (since we could easily imagine they would do the same thing to us--we had just come in ourselves only moments before). My wife was shaking her head about it and we just thought it was such bad manners. Have people become so disassociated with their surroundings that they don't realize they need paying patrons to get paid?

In any case, our waitress came over and said "I hope you don't think we were talking about you guys...we're not. Some guy came in just before closing. I'm sure you hear us talking about him and it's not about you."

We were dumbfounded! How does that make it any better? So she _knew_ they were complaining within our hearing them and did it anyway.  Then she came and told us they were doing that but "hey, it's ok, we're just complaining about that other stupid customer, not you stupid customers..."

Of course, she didn't _say_ "stupid" but that's how it all came across and she must have thought we (and the other patron) were or none of it would have happened.

I've been coming to this restaurant for almost two decades now. 

Over the years the quality of the physical restaurant (repairs, cleanliness, etc.) have been dropping as has the service.  But we have overlooked it since we have been generally ok with the food quality during that period. (Back in the early 90s, it was much better too.)

But now that I look at it, there's really nothing special about this place anymore, other than that it is located by one of our favorite beach spots. Since we come from the mainland, we'll just have to bring something with us on the way out from now on.

It just feel's like Thai Pan Alley isn't being created anymore--like it's in neutral and just gradually rolling down a long slow hill (note: eventually that hill ends a ravine). 

Nothing ever stays the same in this world. Someone is either actively making things (like restaurants) better or worse. There's no "same". 

Unfortunately, Thai Pan Alley doesn't seem to be doing the former.
name: Hans

text: Sean set us up on a wine tour for us and our family visiting from out of town. text:
Please don't pass this place up if you're looking for lunch in the central city area! Quaint and simple, Cafe Reconcile is not only a great place to satisfy your need for a nice home cooked meal, but is a great giveback to the local community! This place offers hospitality training programs for youth in the community and has been around for over 20 years!

Let me start by saying i have never had a turkey neck in my life. But now after eating the fried turkey necks here i have found a new favorite! Omg they are like sweet and spicy FALL OFF THE BONE. We had them as an appetizer and i had to order them for my actual entree! Lordy so good. We also had the biscuit beignets (so sweet and yum with the strawberry sauce). My coworker had the seafood stuffed pepper (Tuesday special) and my other colleague had the jerk chicken (she def enjoyed it because it was all gone before i could get a bite). 

They also have a different special each day, but they are only open for lunch and have pretty tight hours. 

I also had the cornbread muffins, collard greens for my sides. So good!

Check this place out! They're doing cool things for the kids in the community while serving awesome Home cooked meals.
name: Rachel

text:
My boss told me about SFC and said it was the best chicken she's had. 

I came in with a friend. We were in the area, and looking to give this place a try. We'd driven by a few days before and noticed it was packed with people and there was hardly any parking. That was on a Saturday night, so I can figure that. 

Even a few days later, on a Monday at 4pm, this place was full of people. And I can see why. The restaurant itself is quite small, there are only a handful of places to sit and eat. I got an order of the 5 piece cilantro lime chicken. The chicken is breaded and fried, but unlike other fried chicken places (ahem Colonel) this chicken is not greasy, but it's still moist and delicious. 

The cilantro lime has cilantro (full leaves and lots of them) and has a lime/cilantro Chimichurri sauce for dipping. It was a amazing. There are a few other types of chicken and sauces you can get, as well as sides and drinks. The 5 pieces was way more than enough food for me, but I've heard the the corn fritters are also amazing and huge. 

This place is busy, and you might need to take your order to go. If you're craving delicious fried chicken that isn't greasy, but still flavourful SFC is the place to check out.
name: Alouise

text:
Here's the bottom line.  The Stone House Cafe is on the expensive side.  When a place charges those prices, you expect them to provide a great experience.  A great experience means quality food, service, and ambiance.  The Stone House Cafe does a pretty good job at two of the three, food and ambiance, but fails all to often at customer service.  

Here are some examples of service failure:

1. Whenever we try to make a reservation it takes a long time, being put on hold several times and often being disconnected before getting it done.  The last time, we got a stern lecture from them when we called on a Sunday to make a reservation for later that week. Apparently they are too busy to take reservations on Sunday, so we were told not to call again on Sunday to make a reservation.  

2.  We arrive for breakfast on a Monday at 8:15am and wished to eat out on their nice patio.  We were told the patio isn't open until 8:30am, so we decide to wait the 15 minutes.  At 8:25am we walk up to the hosted area to get ready to be seated and are told the patio won't be open for at least another 1/2 hour.   

3. The owner/hostess is a nightmare at times.  Just one example is when we were trying to exit their very small parking lot, which has one lane and goes one way.  A car was just sitting there in the driving lane blocking the exit.  I waited for a couple of minutes, thinking it must be a customer who ran back inside to get something they left behind.  Finally I had enough, left my car and went inside to complain to the staff that a car was blocking the exit.  One of the staff members looked at the vehicle and told me it was the owner's.  I asked if she could move it, but neither of us could get her attention.  They had a small band set up that night and she was singing with it and apparently did not want to be bothered.  I went back out to my car thinking I was as going to have to back out, but my wife was able to help me maneuver around her car with a good deal of difficulty.   

This restaurant is so close to our house, that I imagine we will eventually be back, but not until the bad memories fade.   If you want confirmation of this review, just check out some of the other reviews.  There is one reason this place only has 3.5 stars as I'm writing this and that is because of the poor customer service.   Fix that and this place probably is a 4.5 star restaurant.  Go ahead and give it a shot if you want, you just might have a 5 Star experience if it all goes well, but definitely be prepared for it not to.
name: Z

text:
Syberg's: The gift that keeps on giving. Original location, where the magic happened first. Multiple expansions over the years evident, giving each room a different feel. Seating inside mostly jam-packed with royal regulars, and no room spared for table coverage; you'll end up doing the tummy-tuck maneuver, at least once, squeezing through the crowd. Spacious, outdoor patio provides an intimate, roadside view.

Employees' hustle in the fast-paced environment that is Syberg's. There is no time for games and asking about menu suggestions. Can't go wrong with the Chick Strips, served w/ Syberg's unique sauce, a staple of the franchise. These aren't bland, log-shaped Strips flash-fried from the County Fair. No, lightly-breaded, tender crisps, and perfect for dipping purposes. Try the Chicken Wrap for full effect. SIDEBAR: Sub a small salad for the CROUTONS! They melt in mouth on contact!

***This is that place where coach takes the team after a big win, long days at the pool, or a babysitter watchin' the kiddos for the night! RANCH DRESSING: 8/10***
name: Andy

text:
If you like crappy 'American' Mexicanish food, this is THE place. The 'salsa' was obviously out of a jar from the cheapest local American grocery store around the corner. Or maybe they just smash Tomatoes in the back room. Want guac? This was light green so it remotely resembled guacamole but other than that, tasted more like nothing. How can something taste like nothing? How did they accomplish this?

I ordered a 'plate' with chili relleno, cheese enchilada with rice and beans. 

The last time I had this version of this horrible rice I thought I was going to explode within the hour. It's what I ended up eating the most, bc the rest was going to take some nerve to eat so I had to build up nerve, and thought surely the rice was safe but I ate maybe half a cup. Holy mackerel this stuff expands in your stomach so badly that within the hour it was like eating a thanksgiving meal, and not the good kind. 

The sauce on the 'enchilada' was sweetened!!!  When do they put sugar in sauce??. I ate maybe 3 bites each of the cheese enchilada and chili thing but it was a struggle. How do they get away with feeding this slop to people??  And no one protests??!! 

This experience affected me so badly I had to go home and get in a fetal position because that's what the bomb in my stomach that was growing into the rock in my intestines. 

By morning, I was in deep regret. 


So, my summary: don't bother, in fact, just hit the Chick-Fil-A. 
Get over to Nolensville, (and not Hacienda) for real Mexican food. If you want good Korean or Vietnamese, in Nashville, Charlotte road is the place, which is where this crappy place is but at all costs, avoid this intestinal atrocity.
name: Uma

text: My wife and I have been going here for almost 30 years, since the sign in the back room read "unattended children will be sold as slaves." Really. We are going less frequently than before, because while the ambience has improved, food quality has been declining. It used to be a great value, but no longer. It's still a good value, just not as good. Avoid the clam strips, they may as well be rubber. Craft beer on tap includes a 3 Daughters ale that is not to be missed (if you're into that). Parking is generally ample, with an adjacent lot that is accessible only from the street just north of the restaurant. Service is consistently good.

text:
This one lives up to the reviews. We came in on a Sunday morning and had to wait for about 30 minutes but the hostess was nice enough to grab us and let us know a couple bar seats were open (they are open seating but were full when we got in). While we waited we got a latte, flat white and a delicious chocolate croissant. The croissant was delicious and actually had a substantial amount of chocolate in it!  

The coffee they brew there is custom made for them from a company in the Midwest and it's all delicious, the baked goods all looked delicious. When we finally sat down we ordered a frozen apple cider (I had been eyeballing it on another table) and a milk money latte (made with vanilla bean milk). Both were excellent. For our food we chose to share two dishes. The fried chicken biscuit with Tabasco honey and the hangover bowl (a short rib and grits bowl). They were both so yummy! 

The restaurant itself is adorable down to the uniforms they wear. It's absolutely worth the wait (but they do take reservations).
