text:
It is so unfortunate that such tasty food can be so unenjoyable due to such terrible service.

We happily waited for a table, and when our party of four was seated, we waited at least 20 minutes to be greeted by a server. A bar tender eventually came to take our drink orders. They took a little while even though we only ordered soft drinks/water. We also had to remind someone that one of the orders was missing.

We ordered an appetizer from the bartender at the same time - just chips and dip. We waited about ten minutes. The queso and chips were nice and warm, the guac tasted fresh, and the mango salsa was good, too.

It would have been nice to have received silverware, napkins, and plates at this point, but we made do without. Eventually, someone brought us one silverware roll... Then another. At this point, we're laughing because... What the heck? Finally, we receive the last two rolls of silverware. We never received separate plates for the appetizer. Not a big deal to us, but usually standard in case anyone has a problem with double dipping.

Now for our entree order. We had a Mexican pizza, a plate of three tacos, a quesadilla, and chicken and Portobello mushroom fajitas. Another wait. We're super chill about it all.

Food comes out. We've got the Mexican pizza, the quesadilla, tacos, and all the fixins for fajitas, but no fajitas. We wait a couple minutes. The three lucky eaters began, not realizing that the stuff in front of our friend wasn't her main dish, but once we do, we share a few bites. Finally, our friend points out to our server that she doesn't have her meal. He clearly did NOT realize, which means he really didn't check his table to see if everything was correct. When it finally came out, the plate had steak instead of chicken. Our friend politely pointed that out and asked if she could just get some fajita chicken brought out. She didn't want the plate to be taken bc she was quite hungry at this point. Another wait. 10 minutes go by. The rest of our table has finished our meals. I start looking around for a manager. I get up and stand at the bar. It still took a couple minutes to make eye contact with staff. There were 5-6 employees very nearby - all with their backs turned towards me, looking through the kitchen window. One employee saw me waiting at the bar but did not venture to ask if he could help. Once I got someone's attention, I was able to ask for the chicken. It came out a few minutes later.

A few other things. A couple of people tried the steak fajitas since it was there. The steak was burnt. My partner even likes a little char, but even he thought it was pretty terrible. The Mexican pizza was good, but stuck to the pan. We managed with a knife and some determination. Think about trying to eat a Mexican pizza without the bottom hard shell layer. It doesn't work. This is pretty basic food service logic. The customer should not have to work that hard to eat the food. Other than that, the black beans were salted to hell and back. The rest of the food was tasty.

In between finishing ¾ of the food and still waiting on the chicken, the hostess came back to offer us the utensils she must have forgotten at the start. We laughed aloud. Did she expect us not to have gotten food after all that time?

Our waiter apologized multiple times. He said it was busy, he was taking care of another, large table. It's Mardi Gras season. He was very sincere in his apology and very nice. I've been in his shoes before. He may need a little extra training in things like checking the table/order and consolidating steps. I gave him some feedback concerning the problem with the chicken as nicely as I could, but I truly felt he needed to hear it since that was a really bad experience.

The manager heard the conversation and came up to ask about it. I told him about the same thing with a couple of extras, like about the black beans and pizza stuck to the pan. He was also apologetic and used the same reasoning (busy, Mardi Gras, etc). Now, it's not like they weren't busy, but there were a few empty tables by that time. This part of the city didn't have a lot going on in the area at that time. Honestly, at some point, a manager has to just say, "We need to do better." He did offer a gift card since we'd already paid. I told him that it should go to my friend since she's the one who waited for her food for so long. Plus, I live in Houston now and will not be back to this establishment.
name: Kaci

text: I went here with my family and ordered the shrimp and grits, when it came it was not as described in the menu at all. In the menu it was shrimp and grits with collard greens and a drizzle of BBQ sauce. What came was a bowl with a bright redish orange greasy sauce with sautéed mushrooms and peppers. text:
A relaxing evening with good service and fine food.  It's interesting how the interior is fairly conservative, but then there's an entire wall filled with tile patterns and mirror utensils like a giant mosaic.  Plus there is artwork throughout that is for sale.  Our waiter was very good.  He was low key, helpful with ordering, and checked on us frequently.

Food was top notch.  The menu is not extensive, but more than sufficient.  Half of it is continuing items, and the other half is specials (both one time and rotating).  Rather than standard starter bread, you get crispy flatbread pieces with a tasty carrot hummus spread.  The wife's Ellie's salad was delicious.  It had a great mix of well chopped ingredients that were fresh and crisp (romaine lettuce, grape tomatoes, red onions, artichoke hearts, provelone cheese, and a light sweet & sour dressing.  My bourbon-roasted peaches were similarly delicious.  Peaches were warm and flavorful, with a sweet/mellow ricotta buttercream and served on toasted panko.  The entrees also exuded good flavor and tenderness - both the rosemary and red wine braised pot roast, and the pan-roasted rainbow trout.  Cheddar cheese macaroni was ordered by me as a side dish.  It was a standard, yet good dish.  All the dishes were attractively presented, as well.  Finally, we topped it all of with a nice piece of strawberry, peach and blueberry pie - basically a slice of peach pie with strawberry and blueberry accents.  Good stuff, though.
name: Doug

text:
I happen to like Mediterranean food a lot.  And this place was extremely good.  It's located on the same strip as the Mandarin Chinese Restaurant.

It's run by a husband and wife team and they are extremely friendly.  Went there with friends who are very picky about what they eat and we all gave it a thumbs up.
  Plus it's a BYOB.................

The Falafel and gyro were great.  Surprisingly my husband raved about the baba ganoush in the sampler.  The lamb and chicken platter were delicious.

And the baklava was devine.  No drippy, soppy honey running all over the plate.  It was crisp and flavorful without being goopy.  And surprise the shortbread lemon bars were perfect.  Not really Mediterranean food, but who cares.

I dropped a star because I was disappointed in the Kibbe and Chicken Shwarma wrap.  Hmmm, considering everything else really shines these two dishes are something I will avoid when I go back.

And per the owner if you like chocolate bread pudding, call ahead to see if they've made it to schedule your next meal.

text:
We decided to enjoy Zasu, a trendy new restaurant along the N. Carrollton corridor (just off Canal) in Mid City.  Chef Sue Zemanick artfully combines both local and non-native ingredients to create thoughtful and tasty dishes. 

Libations: 1) Cosmo - martini was well crafted and a refreshing start to a rich dinner. 2) 2014 Pinot Noir was smooth and velvety; perfect compliment to the beef entree. 

1st Course: Lobster Bisque - rich and creamy, with small bits of sweet lobster. Perfect for a cool night. 

2nd Course: Beef Bourguignon ($32). Served with fingerling potatoes, crispy bacon, sweet pearl onions, seasonal baby carrots, and crispy haricot vert. The serving of beef was quite substantial - at least 10oz. It was so tender and flavorful and sat atop all of the accompanying vegetables, which were well prepared and seasoned. 

3rd Course: Chocolate Pot du Crème ($11). This is a classic New Orleans dessert but it is THE BEST I've had in town. It's a twist on the traditional dessert because of the contrasting salted caramel in the midst of the pot. It was topped with whipped crème fraiche, cocoa nibs, and fresh raspberries. A must, so save room!

Pricing: Overall, this trendy spot seeks to add to the upscale restaurants in the Mid City corridor. However, it's a bit more expensive than similarly situated restaurants. 

Dećor: The interior is new and fresh, with green walls and retro globe lighting. Of note, Amanda Stone Talley, local New Orleans artist, created the beautiful, green wallpaper, which is reminiscent of views through a kaleidoscope - whimsical circular, whirring shapes. While beautiful, the decor lacks the ability to absorb sound. This makes for a VERY LOUD dining experience. In fact, I sat with two others and we struggled to hear one another across the table. Drapery would help to absorb the chatter throughout the long, hard space. 

Signage: For those aware of its predecessor restaurant, this new spot is not hard to find. However, for newcomers, be aware that the signage is a bit too modest/small. Plus, because the restaurant is set back from the street, it may be a benefit to increase signage to make it easier to locate. 

Overall, I enjoyed this experience and will visit again. Hopefully, they'll find creative ways to bring down the noise level. Though it is definitely a splurge to eat here, it's worth it on special occasions. Kudos, Chef!
name: Tamia

text: My personal experience dining at Costa's Restaurant by the Sponge Docks at Tarpon Springs would not rate 1 star. My girlfriend and I stopped in for a drink to check the place out and the young female bar tender seemed aloof; did not say hello as we sat at the bar and chose to BS with a fellow employee.  Was about to get up and walk out and then she graced us with asking us what we wanted to drink.  Clearly she has no clue that liquor sales are just as important as food.  The smells from the kitchen during the lunch period were alluring but we had breakfast earlier and decided to come back at 6pm for dinner.  While the your female server was friendly, she was not at all attentive spending more time at the bar probably texting friends.  Never came and asked if the food was good and if we wanted another drink.  We started with the Saganaki (flaming casseri cheese) which is typically a must appetizer in every Greek Restaurant.  Our server could not light it and clearly did not know what she was doing and stunk up the place.  I made the mistake of ordering the Greek Roasted Lamb with oven potatoes.  The food came out in less than 10 minutes even though it is supposed to be slowly cooked; obviously the lamb was at least a week old and reheated, tuff as leather and no taste whatsoever. Generous amount of potatoes though. I should have had a clue when the restaurant was practically empty. Highly recommend going to Mama's across the street, Hella's or Dimitri's on the water where they are 5 star Greek Restaurants. Have tried each one and now know not to return to Costa's.

text:
I'm from Miami and moving up here left a hole in my stomach for good Cuban food. This place, however, has filled it. Great place to get some good Cuban food and a cafecito for that pick me up. 

Recommend the Cuban Sandwhich or the ropa vieja if you are hungrier.

text:
Lovely little restaurant. Definitely Italian !
Each entre comes with a delightful salad. Not over-dressed, perfect dressing flavors. Light and not over powering.

Slightly creamy red sauce with just the right amount of spices and capers. Cooked to perfection. More than enough to take some home for a second meal.

All & all, a very top notch meal! Highly, highly recommend.

text:

Got a pepperoni pizza and chicken, bacon, ranch pizza and both were really good.  Sizable enough to share it seemed like they were coal fire baked with Neapolitan style crust. Very tasty with quality ingredients.  

Selected a couple of flights comprised of the mainly of the IPAs where were top notch.  The New England style IPA and grapefruit were two of the best!
name: Matt

text:
Sansom St. is like a back alley hidden between two much larger streets. It's one lane and one way, but don't let that deter you from checking out Giwa. The problem with any restaurant in this part of the city is finding parking. So factor that in when you decide whether to go or not (or just walk if that's a possibility). 

Anyway, the food. We ordered two stone pots (dol sot), a plate of beef bbq (bulgogi), and a plate of japchae noodles. We are Korean, so authenticity does matter. A big measuring stick is how my two picky sons do with the food, and they ate very well! 

The stone pots were a little under-sauced. I had to ask my wife for some of her gochujang, as I prefer a lot in mine, but I didn't want to pay the upcharge. I would suggest you order it on the side and it seems like they give you more. 

Overall, the basic bowl is $11.50 without any add-ons including the protein. The meat or tofu was extra, as was the egg on top (a standard at Korean restaurants). So my entire entree cost $15.50, which is a little high for a stone pot (I'll usually pay around $12 to $14). Overall, very good and we'd love to come back if we're in the neighborhood.
name: David

text:
I recommend you go to Long John Silver's over this place. Absolutely consistantly overcooked to the point the flavor is lost completely.

Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. For the price I expected more than this.

text: The soup was better than the sandwich, which I wasn't expecting. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable.

text: Manager left one Whopper out of our drive-up order but evidently didn't feel it was worth an apology.  How hard is it to just say, "I'm sorry."

text: Hooray for another central location for dim sum. Love that you can get the traditional tea cart service. The dim sum, although more pricey than other restaurants in town, is good quality and fresh. Friendly staff and quick seating made the experience pleasant. Getting on the right side of Broadway and into the side/back lot parking can be a bit inconvenient but this place hits the spot when craving the typical dim sum classics.

text:
A friend has been recommending this place for months, constantly touting the cheap prices. Unfortunately the 50% off everything, all the time is just a gimmick. Our bill was not much less than our regular sushi spot. I wish we had gone there instead.

When we arrived we were immediately seated downstairs instead of up, which was more lively and had nicer decor. Downstairs booths have very dim lighting and menus were tough to read without our phone's flashlight. Service was friendly but slow even though we were the only people there.

Now for the sushi; I think their 50% off refers to the quality of the food. The fish was limp and warm. Sauces all tasted the same and the sushi that was not supposed to be spicy... was hot and spicy. We even double checked with our server and he confirmed that it was not spicy. Oh well, he was wrong and so were we for listening to our friend. 

We didn't complain about our orders. It took so long to get our food we didn't feel like waiting for more terrible sushi. We couldn't wait to leave. Definitely a one and done. We won't be back.
name: Aimee

text: breakfast burritos both delicious and so many good salsas!
name: Taylor

text: Always delicious! I got the Cheese Burger and my husband got the Farm Burger. Both served with a large portion of sides (tater tots and fries). Will eat here every time I am in Nashville.

text:
This is our go to sushi restaurant in Wesley Chapel. It's always clean, and the staff is amazing and attentive. Both the sashimi, nigiri and the rolls are on point. I always like to start with the edamame and they stick to the sushi menu. Check it out, you'll love it. 

Best bet is to go early so you won't need to wait. We went for my daughter's birthday tonight and it was delicious.
name: Michelle

text:
Found this under utilized lounge when my flight to St Louis was delayed due to a bird strike.  Since I had 5 hours until my connecting flight left, I decided to give this a try.  For $38 you get 4 hours of lounge time.  Unlike the American and United lounges, this one was super clean. The staff was on top of their cleaning.  They were also very friendly and attentive.  For your day pass fee, you get the usual selection of drinks (including some beers and wine) and snacks for free.  You could also order a wide selection upgraded alcoholic drinks as well.  For those that happen to stop in during lunch or dinner times or anytime they are open really, you can order from a nice selection of sandwiches, flatbreads, salads, and wraps.  This was a really nice perk.  I didn't have to leave the lounge at all to get lunch.  

Of course you also get secured fast Wifi as part of the fee.  If you come to STL or NYC, consider getting a membership.   

I really enjoyed my time in there.  The quiet,  cleanliness, and hot or cold made to order meals really set it apart from the other lounges.
name: Dong

text:

My tacos were amazingly good!!!!

text:
Cook: how's the Jam (Jambalaya)?
Me: it's really fucking good
Cook: yea I put a lotta love into that one

This kitchen makes some of the best food I've ever had, I'd eat here at least once a week if i lived in New Orleans. The jambalaya is the best I've ever had... piping hot, spicy and made with heart. 

The most rare experience you can have as a foodie is having something that tastes home cooked, as if your aunt is cooking specifically for you, putting her love and affection into the meal;  that's how I feel whenever I eat the food from Marie's, like I'm home away from home. Whoever was smart enough to start a kitchen there and hire the cooks they did has succeeded far beyond what they hoped for, I assume. To pay $8 for a  bowl of 
Jam that good is a treat.

The servers bent down to pet and rub the dog, then carried our plates of food to the table.  Yuck.  I asked the server about it, and she said if we didn't like it, she'd put the dog upstairs.  Frankly, it's not the customer's job to enforce hygiene and sanitation.  We went once more after the official opening and the dog was still there.  Management has to decide whether to keep the customer or the dog.  Unfortunately, we're not likely to return.

name: Makenzie

text:
My best friend from High School and I stopped in a Fitzgerald's Irish Pub to spend some time before our 40th High School Reunion Dinner.  I had a Half and Half.  A half and half is made with Guinness and Harps Lager.  They didn't have Bass Ale on tap for a Black and Tan, which is what I ordered.  Trish made sure to inform me of what I could get, as you know these Irish pubs (at least the authentic ones) are very particular on their beers and nomenclature.  The Half and Half was excellent and presented expertly.

I also had the Sam Adams Summer Ale, which is one of my favorites; it is flavored with lemon zest and "Grains of Paradise," which a rare pepper from Africa... It is absolutely delicious; and, so refreshing.

My friend had 3 bottles of Michelob Ultra.  Trish was very efficient, not overly friendly; the bar was doing a good business; but, it wasn't very busy.  We thought about sitting outside; but, honestly, it was just too hot.

Compared to Orlando, prices were great, so I left a tip of about 30%, as we sat at the bar for about 2 hours.
name: John

text: Came in because we wanted gator and needed a kid friendly place. Ended up being the best meal of my entire trip. We had shrimp platter, eggplant fries, gator half and half, catfish po boy, red beans and rice and chicken and sausage gumbo. Everything was amazing. Great service too. Bloody Mary was on par with everything I've had since I got in town too. So glad we stopped here!!!!

text: Stumbled onto the place during a business trip. Food and service was both great. Had the cioppino & the bacon-wrapped dates and both were wonderful.
name: Allen

text:
I love walking through West End, as there are shops, restaurants, and hotels galore. Steakhouses are often only known for their steaks, but their signs out front mentioned their brunch and happy hour specials. As I was strolling by I couldn't help but swing in to check out these happy hour specials.

I was warmly greeted by a kind and welcoming staff, and was led to an open bar seating. I got there fairly early in the evening so there was plenty of seating available. Still dressed in my office work clothes, I felt fine--but I would definitely come dressed up, not casual or else you may stick out.

I got an order of the lemon drop mojito, which was genuinely one of the best cocktails that I have ever had. The bartender was absolutely lovely and very attentive to anything I may need. I ordered a happy hour app that was something along the lines of philly cheese steak egg rolls. It was delicious, and I was also brought out a basket of bread. I cannot rave enough about the delightful service that I received, despite being by myself and not ordering too much, I was always paid attention to.

Hot damn. 

The Mrs. and I were craving pho this morning but, upon discovering our favorite restaurant was closed, decided to try K Japanese as it was within walking distance of my house. We walked in at 11 (which is when they open) and found the place empty. The entire staff greeted us and were super friendly and the menu was detailed and easy to read. 

The food was fantastic. We ordered a Monkey Ball without knowing exactly what to expect and had our minds blown by what we received. This sushi thing was huge! Perfect amount of tuna and the fried outer layer wasn't too thick. We then split a red dragon roll, tootsie roll, and an unagi roll and were not disappointed. The rice/good stuff ratio was perfect and this was the freshest eel I've had (in Tucson, that is) in ages, the tuna was flawless, and you can always count on a tootsie roll. 

Total bill came out to be $36 which is a little pricey... but considering what we ordered, it was definitely worth it and I'd pay this over the $25 all you can eat at Sushi Garden any day. 

Overall, I'd give it a 4.5/5. This could possibly become my go to spot for sushi (especially since they're next door) and I hope their business is steady enough to keep the doors open. It'd be a shame to lose this place.

text:
Welp, here we are. For all its hits and misses, Five Points Cocina was a Main Street staple and a familiar part of Edgefield. To replace it with... another Mexican restaurant??... is an interesting gambit and time will only tell how well this works for them -- especially given that the local/neighborhood food landscape has drastically changed from when FPC opened.

If you've been to Cilantro's Melrose locale, you know what to expect: crowd-pleasing Tex-Mex that doesn't always please the crowd. I'm not such a purist that I can't get down with some good Tex-Mex (especially given that a lot of folks who scream for 'authenticity' can't name the various states of Mexico, much less the regional differences in cuisine; 'Mexican' food really isn't a thing) but I do need it to be good. I don't know whether this location is too new, I came on a bad night or too close to close but I don't think that best efforts were in play.

One thing that stood out: all the waiters were very nice... and there were a lot of them. I sat outside (I think everyone was outside) and there were a swarm of waiters. What there wasn't, was light. And, when sitting outside, you need some. I used my cell phone to read the menu. I started with a watermelon margarita, frozen. It came back to the table relatively quickly. It was fine. It didn't make me dance like the pineapple margarita I had on my most recent Tex-Mex adventure. The watermelon flavor was faint (to be expected) and it melted quickly (we were outside). It was fine and when I finished it, I didn't bother to order another. I thought about it, though, considering I was never brought water. Again, new/bad night/close to close? I dunno. But, I needed free hydration. I didn't get it.

I considered the tacos but I couldn't get myself to pay $10 for 3 tacos -- even if they came with a side of beans. So, I went with the Monterrey Chicken. It's exactly what you would expect: flat, pounded grilled chicken breast in some sort of semi-cheesy sauce and the rest of the white space of the plate filled with shredded lettuce, diced tomatoes, guacamole, and rice. I'm not saying this to shade them. I'm saying that it's exactly the Tex-Mex plate you expect. Nothing more. Nothing less. It, too, was fine. 

I don't know that 'fine' pays the rent in Edgefield these days. We'll see. Cilantro has the advantage of muscle memory wrt location and food type. What people experience once they get there, though, is a different matter. Let's hope things improve with time.
name: John

text:
I really wanted to give five stars after hearing so much about this place, but I really couldn't. Let me start by saying this is based on my take-out, and my husband's dine-in experience.

My husband dined with a friend, and ordered a pastrami sandwich. As I'd heard the servings were massive. He brought have of his home, along with latkes, (potato pancakes), and my order, a Manhattan dip.
His sandwich was very tasty, on soft rye bread, with Swiss cheese, almost too big to get your mouth around. The pastrami was really good, well flavored, well-spiced, and clearly fresh; my only problem with the sandwich was the cheese, not enough to compliment the overly large serving of meat. Manhattan is known for their big, big servings, and if you're going to make a huge sandwich, compliment it with enough cheese to give it some cheesy flavor, too.

On too my sandwich. It came with roast beef and melted white cheddar cheese. Again, there was plenty of good tasting roast beef, but not enough cheddar, I couldn't even taste it to enhance the flavor of the beef. They sent along au jus for dipping, but in a big disappointment, forgot my cole slaw, which I was REALLY looking forward to tasting. My husband didn't realize it until he got all the way home (we live in the North Valleys), so there was no way he was going all the way back for it. That's one of the reasons I'm nocking the review down to four stars. I really wanted that cole slaw, and was sorely disappointed I didn't get it.

The latkes were delicious, crispy on the outside and creamy on the inside, just like they are supposed to be, (even reheated), and my hubby had blintzes with his lunch, which he said were also delicious, better than he remembered from his childhood. So, the lunch was mostly a success, along with good service, except for my missing cole slaw!

I'd like to try it in person next time; I'd go for the Manhattan dip again, ask for extra cheese, and get that missing cole slaw, for the perfect meal.

text:
There is a LOT to review here, so I'm going to split into their brewery side and the restaurant side. 

Brewery: Sockeye is a central hub for Boise. They've been around for a long time and they make some damn good beers. I love their Lonesome Larry Lager (mostly because I can give my table mates a fun Idaho history lesson that none of them asked for, lol) and the Woolybugger Wheat. 

Sockeye beverages are everywhere. You can find them in all the major grocery stores and on tap at a lot of restaurants. Their brews are tried and true and they really reflect Idaho. You can do a brewery tour here too, which is super fun. You'll just need to set it up in advance. I absolutely love the smell of beer brewing. It smells homey to me. Yup, I know that's weird. 

Restaurant: I was very bummed when their Cole location closed. It was a favorite haunt for my old co-workers and one of our favorite places to have "choir practice". But the Fairview location is HUGE and beautiful. They can accommodate very large groups. My father in law loves to take us all out to dinner when he comes to town (and this ends up being 15-ish people) so we frequently come to Sockeye. They can always get us in and don't seem to mind our large horde of loud Italians and squalling babies. They have a large, nice patio with plenty of shade for the summer months. 

The food is pretty good. Probably my least favorite thing about the whole experience. Nothing has ever been bad or even mediocre, but I never leave feeling wowed. I would recommend the trout though. Trout screams Idaho to me and Sockeye does it well.
name: Michelle

text: I moved to the states from PR about 7 yrs ago. Lived in the southwest, south and now FL. We've tried several places throughout the years to get a nice meal from back home. text:
Me and the missus visited Amuse for brunch on a Sunday. I purchased a voucher for $49 dollars from Travelzoo. The voucher allowed us to order the following: two entree's up to $20 each, two drinks from the bar up to $14 each and two soft drinks up to $6 each.

We arrived early and began looking for on street parking but didn't have any luck. We had to pay $30 to park in a nearby lot. So plan for that if you're driving down.

The restaurant was very nice located inside a swanky hotel in center city.

We were seated immediately and we looked over the menu. I ordered orange juice and the missus had coffee to start. We started with the Potted Trout $12 Smoked Trout / Lemon / Olive Oil / House Made Cracker. The smoked trout was delicious and paired well with the cracker.

For our entree's I picked the Croque Madame $17
Thick Cut Brioche / Gruyère / Smoked Ham / Mornay / Sunny Side Up Egg / Herb Roasted Potatoes and the missus ordered the Bourguignon Hash $ 17 Shredded Braised Short Ribs / Kale / Jus / Pommes Anna / Sunny Side Up Egg.  Both dishes were underwhelming. The croque madame was a big sandwich with an egg on top. The best part was the gruyere cheese and smoked ham. I felt the thick cut brioche was to large for the amount of meat and cheese that was inside. The potatoes were over cooked.  The braised short rib in the Bourguignon Hash was salty and not as tender as expected. The potatoes and egg were fine.

We finished the meal with two Stormy Maria's their take on a spicy Bloody Mary. The drink was not good. It tasted like cocktail sauce mixed with vodka. I'm pretty sure it had horseradish sauce sitting at the bottom.

The brunch got even worse when we got the check and it had a $14 dollar service charge on it! We're in the process of working with Travelzoo too find out why the establishment charged this fee.
name: Tariq

text:
So we just happened to find this place on a limb and my partner and I absolutely loved everything about it! 
Not only was the service amazing, which I can't even remember my servers name! Ugh! But he was so kind, gave us some local spots to check out, and even hooked us up with some extra rolls to take home( They bake all of their pastry's fresh and right in their restaurant). Very personable, attentive and he made the entire stay so much better! 
Now let's talk about the food......
AMAZING!!! 
We've eaten at many restaurants, in many different states  and this has to be by far our favorite dining spot ever!! 
She ordered the seafood Marigny and I had the special which was a surf and turf for our entrees, for our appetizer we had fried green tomatoes and a cup of their jambalaya. 
Let's just say that everything piece of protein was cooked perfect, my fish was delicious and so so moist, it had crab meat on the top which was delicious, my steak was absolutely perfectly seasoned and cooked! Her salmon was so moist and everything on our plates was outstanding! 
The cornbread is to die for and trust me when I say I'm very picky about cornbread because a lot of places cook it too dry, K-Paul's definitely has the best!! 
If you are looking for some good food, a nice dinner, and good service, you have got to try this place out!!!

text:
Holy hot fried chicken! This was our second stop for fried chicken while we were in Nashville. We got here early afternoon - found parking easily and made our way in. We waited about 5 mins to order, found a seat and waited about 15 mins for our food. We really didn't have the long wait like others have stated, prob bc we went during a non peak time during the week instead of weekend. Wow, the staff worked like a well oiled machine - as soon as someone finishes their meal, the table is already cleaned and ready for another starving patron. All staff were very friendly.

We ordered half chicken medium and chicken sandwich medium. I was afraid to go any hotter. For sides, we got Mac and cheese, potato salad and fries. Mac and cheese was ok - bit too saucy for my liking and the pimento had a very strong flavor. Potato salad was ok as well. My fave were the fries - hot, crispy and plentiful. Half chicken was nice and juicy and heat level was just hot enough for me. But the sandwich - wow, the sandwich has got to be one of the best sandwiches I've had - was almost tempted to come back one more time while we were here, but held back my salivation. I ordered a blue cheese on the side - really didn't need it.

Last but not least, the banana pudding - what monkeys dream of. I saw reviews praising the peach cobbler but the cashier told me to definitely get the banana pudding and I am SO glad she did bc this banana pudding was the perfect way to end our meal. Yes, it is hype but worth it - make your way here for some delicious food.
name: Mary

text:
Lives up to the great reviews! I finally went to St. Elmo after hearing over and over how great the food is. It's such a good place for special occasions. I went for my boyfriend's birthday and they gave him a free dessert and bday card signed by the staff. It was really nice! They also don't sing happy birthday, which is great.

You must have a reservation coming here. I would recommend getting a reservation a few days in advance, maybe even farther in advance for a weekend night. I went on a Tuesday night and it was super crowded! 

The food was really good too! Obviously it was expensive, but it was a lot of food for the money. We started off with their famous shrimp cocktail. It was really good but the cocktail sauce is really spicy! Our waiter recommended putting some of the cocktail sauce in our bean soup (which comes with the meals) and it added a good flavor! I had the filet mignon with mashed potatoes, but I'm sure all of their steaks are good. The mashed potatoes were to die for. I'm not sure what they put in them but I've never had anything like it.
name: Catie

text: As far as I know, this was my first aquarium themed restaurant experience and I absolutely LOVED it. Seafood while I watch sea creatures swimming along? The best! The food was good (not fantastic for the price) but good enough. I had their shrimp scampi and was definitely filled upon the completion of clearing my plate. I was also happy to see that had a draft beer list. (Kudos to the Nashville brewery scene!) I must say - I was honestly thrilled with the photo/video ops in this restaurant and it's a great place for people of all ages. Although I'm no longer a huge fan of large shopping malls, which is where this restaurant is tucked inside, they've placed it in a way that you can check out the restaurant without diving into Opry Mills if you so choose. Many laughs were had during this dinner so I would recommend it at least for the atmosphere.

text:
If you are looking for a great gastropub with decent prices and really delicious bar food, then this is your place! The scene is your typical bar scene with a little grunge (but the good kind in all the best ways!) This is the type of place where you want to go with a group of friends any day of the week to hang out/grab a drink/or even just have a really good burger!

With that, the draft selection is phenomenal, not an overwhelming amount but decent top notch choices over a great variety. I love it when I can find a Troegs Dreamweaver on tap! 

The food scene is great, I built my own burger and I have to say one of the best burgers in philly for a great price! We also ordered nachos and you have the option of chorizo or braised beef on top! So of course we asked for both! They were incredible, each layer of nachos had a different type of meat on them. It was not the typical all your chips on the bottom and then meat on top. Every chip you grabbed automatically had meat on them! My only wish is that it came with some red salsa and a container of it. They were a little dry with the overwhelming amount of meat! (But not disapproving of that!) 

Definitely will be back to venture out more of their appetizers. Unfortunately I got their at 6 PM which is when their happy hour ends. Did not realize that they had an early one, wish they could extend it to at least 6:30!
name: Stephanie

But pulling up even just to the strip mall my hope spiked. It smelled good. There were words in NOT ENGLISH(!!!) and it almost reminded me of San Jose or a Westminister plaza.

I got the bun bo hue which wasn't as spicy as I'm used to and didn't have the porks blood but the flavor was there and I couldn't stop drinking it UNF

text:
This is a decent Mexican restaurant located in the entrance to the Sierra Summit mall in Reno. They have a wide variety of options, so there is something for everyone and their particular craving. 

The chips for the table were very fresh, and tasted particularly fresh, so that's a score! We had the guacamole, and it was aesthetically served in a fried shell, so it was like an additional big chip we weren't expecting - another score! 

I had the ground beef with my meal and wasn't particularly impressed as I felt a bit sick after, but my friends had the chicken and did not have any complaints. The rest of the meal was very tasteful and served in generous portion sizes - so we definitely came out of there feeling filled and satisfied.

The food here satisfied our cravings for good Mexican food in the area, and the prices did not make us feel guilty. Overall, it's a decent establishment that I see a pretty strong potential for!

text:
I equivocated for a week about what restaurant to choose for my husband's birthday, but settled on Harp and Crown because of the ambiance and menu.

When we arrived for our 8:30 reservation, we were offered a seat in the front garden area by the window, but I preferred the larger back room. Wasn't a problem; the host came over to the couch where we were waiting and gave us an estimated wait-time--which was well-worth it!

When we were escorted to out table 20 minutes later, we found a spacious booth with two flutes of champagne! Such a thoughtful touch. 

Regarding food: my husband wanted to try a little bit of everything, so we ordered the tasting menu. I'm not a big eater, so the seven dishes overwhelmed me a little. I do, however, highly recommend the tuna appetizer and the brussel sprouts. The new salmon entree is also delicious; the dijon glaze was amazing.

As for drinks? The Ruby Slippers is light and refreshing without being a sugar-rush. 

Can't wait to take guests here!

text: My husband and I did not have a good experience at this restaurant this afternoon. We decided to eat outside as it was a nice day. It took over 1 hour for our food to arrive. We ordered soup, chicken fingers and a cheesesteak, which I think was pretty simple. There were two waitresses waiting on us. Neither one was very attentive and took very long to come back to us. Finally after 1 hour we asked them when our food would be arriving as we were so hungry and were getting really to leave to go somewhere else. Finally our food arrived. There was no soup, only the chicken fingers and a sandwich. There was also no silverware to eat with. Upon telling the waitress about the missing soup she replied " sorry we are both new here so things are just all messed up."  This I feel was a completely rude statement. Once I realized we had no silverware I went back into the restaurant to get some. Halfway through our meal my husband needed his water glass refilled. When one of the waitresses finally returned he requested his glass to be refilled. Finally she came out with water and only filled my husband's glass and not mine. We could not wait to receive the check and just leave. Horrible, rude and untrained service. This restaurant is located on the pier where you can park free for 90 minutes. I highly recommend and will return.

text:

Scoopers is a great place to grab a fast and delicious lunch or dinner and just chill for a minute. The thing though is... milkshakes. Dang! My daughter got a Salted Caramel shake and I got a Heath Bar shake. They were totally off the hook!  

My friend Brenden recommended the place and I'm glad I listened. Next time in Reno, I'm going back. I'm craving that shake again!
name: Will

text: Love this place! Best happy hour in the city along with great service. Their menu cocktails are delicious as well and they'll go above and beyond to make you off menu drinks.
name: Mallory

text: The wait is long enough. Finally a great family own soup dumpling spot in the Northeast. I entered this spot greeted with smiles of the owner and workers. The food was great, tea was flavorful (not watered down like other Asian restaurants), the food came out quick, left with a smile and a full stomach. Now that I don't have to travel to Chinatown and stress about finding parking, this is gonna be my main spot whenever I crave their soup dumplings.
name: David

text:
We stopped in for dinner on Halloween night.  
The restaurant is adorable outside. Loved all the plants. Comfy booths inside. We ordered the stuffed dates.  They were pretty good, have experienced better tho, and they could have been hotter.  Also tried the beef fillet with the blue cheese fondue. This was delicious and we'd definitely order it again. The meat was really tender and flavorful. The blue cheese fondue was a bit liquidy for fondue and a little sparse on the blue cheese but we loved this dish. We tried the coconut crusted fish bites and they were really good.  Another thing we would order again. Their lobster bisque was one of the best tasting ever but it was like they dropped in a bit of lobster right before serving it and the lobster was not completely warm all through but the bisque was hot. My husband had the French onion and that too was very good..not too salty which seems to be the case with some. 
It seemed like the bartender was having trouble keeping up with orders. Maybe because he seemed really focused, maybe too focused on some regulars sitting at the bar.  The menu boasts about having the best margarita on the beach.  That's not true, imo. But it was good enough to order a second one. Unfortunately, that drink came out really short, like some was spilled? I didn't bring it to the attention of our server but I probably should have.
We will  definitely be back for the food!
name: Sheila

text: I don't really get some of the harsh reviews on here. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. My experience was honestly fine. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. It looked better online than it did in person. Not bad for a quick meal.
name: User

text: Been wanting to try this place but usually super busy during breakfast. Finally got lucky during much time and it was worth the wait. Everything was excellent
name: Laura

text:
This was my first visit to Seasons 52 and I must say that I am impressed. It was our anniversary dinner and they made sure to wish us a happy anniversary and provided amazing service the whole night. 

We ordered the Lump Crab, Roasted Shrimp & Spinach Stuffed Mushrooms for an appetizer and for entrees we had the Southern-Style Shrimp & Grits and the Wood-Grilled BBQ Meatloaf. Everything was delicious and the portions were perfect. To drink, I had the Cucumber Basil Smash and it was so crisp and tasty! We also got free dessert since we were celebrating and it was our first time. 

I have no complaints, as this experience was great and made our anniversary night unforgettable! Thank you to the staff and chefs, our meal was perfect.
name: Paige

text: Best Lox I've had since leaving New York. I was worried when I got there because the line was out the door, but it moved so fast, and I got my food way quicker than I anticipated. I carried out, so I didn't have to worry about finding a seat, but the staff was on top of clearing space once people left, so I'm sure it wouldn't have been an ordeal. Fantastic savory and sweet bagels. Definitely coming back.
name: Kelsey

text: We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. The staff seemed tired but still polite. Pretty happy with it overall. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. It looked better online than it did in person. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. The food was good and the service was easygoing.
name: User

text: Haven't been to this location in such a long time, I'm talking yearssss. But we met friends here before the Saints game because it's close to the Superdome and not much has changed at all. It's still a much smaller location with a tiny parking lot. However, our bartender SKYLER was nothing short of amazing. Skyler made the best skinny margarita, which tasted like a regular margarita, and was extremely knowledgeable about the ingredients of each margarita. Skyler was also patient enough to explain the differences, pros and cons between the two drinks. Just exceptional service!

text: For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. The food was good and the service was easygoing. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. A very pleasant experience. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon.

text:

text:
My wife and I stopped in at Felix's on Monday for a couple of drinks because we were early for our dinner reservation. We had decided to delay our Valentine's Day celebration to avoid the frenzy of the actual day.
We were pleasantly surprised to learn that it was happy hour. Marquita was our server and she was very pleasant and attentive. She familiarized us with the happy hour specials and we really enjoyed chatting with her while we were there.
Although it's a bit out of the way for us, we'll definitely be going back again.

text:
White Dog is a coveted main line restaurant with my college aged crowd even though it is a bit expensive. My friends and I had never been, but had always heard the rage. We decided to compromise and go for happy hour to try it out but on a budget. 

We were seated outside and the waiter helped us with the umbrellas that were only half useful at blocking out the bright sun. We ordered the $5 specialty cocktail "WM2" which was a watermelon mint vodka concoction. Upon first sip I realized this was a STRONG drink. Strong to the point that I felt like I was sipping a watermelon vodka shot from a fancy glass. For me, if I order a fruity cocktail, I want there to be alcohol but I don't want to taste it. And I definitely tasted this. It became hard to drink at the end (but ya girl powered through). 

We were given complementary bread and butter to start before we ordered food. There were $5 snacks and $10 plates for the deals. My friend and I split the truffle fries and cheese plate (you choose the 3 cheeses which are accompanied with grapes, nuts, crackers, apples, etc.). I thought the food was excellent. The fries were crispy and all three cheeses we ordered were delicious (cheddar was our favorite).  Sort of small portions but it is a pretty nice restaurant and we weren't paying much. 

Overall, the whole experience was fine, but I would probably elect to go somewhere else on the main line for happy hour. I might come back for a special occasion dinner (and be wary of ordering a cocktail--does that make me a wimp?!), but I think the (white) dog days are over for happy hour.
name: Gwen

text: Appears to be poorly managed. 10 minute wait in drive thru. Saw Car in front of me where Staff had to go back in for forgotten drink. text:
Let me begin by saying that, if I could give this experience negative rating, I totally would.   It was an absolute dumpster fire.  We were a party of four, and since two of us arrived early, we asked to be seated so that we could order some wine and enjoy an appetizer.    Boy, were those lofty goals...  

We were told that Courtney would be our server, but whether or not we got her will never be known because the young lady who came to our table (after we sat there for 10-15 minutes) never bothered to introduce herself by name.  We attempted to order a bottle of Chateau Ste. Michelle Riesling, but after repeating the name several times, the server told us that we'd have to show her on the menu.  Consider that red flag #1. 

After waiting another 10-15 minutes, the server came back to the table, asked if wanted some waters, and told us that she was still waiting on someone at the bar to get our wine.   She brought four waters to the table, and a few minutes later, she seriously dropped straws on the table as she walked by without saying a single word.  Consider that red flag #2. 

Our daughter and son-in-law then arrived, and as they were being brought to the table, our server stepped on our daughter's foot and never said a word - not an "oops" or an "I'm sorry" or anything.  A few minutes later, she finally brought the wine to the table, along with four glasses, and this is when the whole experience imploded.   

First, she literally plopped the bottle down on the table and was going to walk off without ever removing the cork from the bottle.   She seemed oblivious to that fact until my husband pointed to it and asked if she'd mind actually opening it.  That question was met with a blank facial expression as she walked away.   Not only did she not open the bottle of wine, she brought four glasses to the table and sat them down without ever asking to see IDs from anyone (2 of the 4 at the table are 25 and under).  I am confident that the ABC would have had a field day with that lack of due diligence.  However, since she apparently had no intention of opening the bottle, I guess she was preventing the possibility of any underage drinking.  

Second, the glasses all had water puddled inside, as if they had just been rinsed out.  Even worse, when we held them up to the light, at least one of those glasses had a lipstick smudge on it, which reinforced our horror that the glasses were dirty ones that had just been dipped in water and rinsed out.  

At that point, we got up and walked out.   We notified the managers on duty of the nightmare experience before we left the property and during a follow-up call, and for that, I would give the management team five stars.   While they all graciously attempted to make it right by treating us to dinner and even graciously offered to give us a gift card, we simply wanted to just distance ourselves from what was one of the worst restaurant experiences we've had.
name: Shannon

text:
If you want your event ruined go here. 

I'll start by saying that i was a fan of this place for a bit until today. I ordered a custom cake in advance with specific instructions on what i wanted i.e. garden roses on top of a navy square drip cake with gold covering the top and dripping off the sides. (See pictures for what i ordered and what i got) i specified that i absolutely did not want fondant as i hated it and went in and spoke with the owner of the shop, where i advised her that i wanted hearty flowers that did not wilt easily, because that was a huge concern for me. She agreed she could meet all of my criteria and provide me with the desired cake for my event. 

My surprise birthday was ruined by this cake because i had to show it to the person whose party it was because i didn't want to be embarrassed by it. The cake looked like a messy envelope / purse intended for a mailman's retirement party (this was not that kind of party) the assortment of flowers she put on the cake was not what i requested and was wilted the day i picked it up. I later found that the cake was indeed made entirely of fondant. 

I was advised by the owner that they decided to change the cake because what i was asking for would be "too chunky" but never was i included in the decision of how to change the cake and what would be done. So if you like someone making the cake decisions for your wedding, birthday or special event and leaving your opinion completely out of it, this is your place. 

Throughout this entire ordeal i made the owner aware of my displeasure to which i was advised that there was no opportunity for a refund and wished me the best. 

No one ate the 140.00, 10"cake at my event.
name: John

text: Server was great. Was upset that a soccer team of young boys came in and sat in the bar area. Should of been told not to.? Became loud and parents didn't care.

text:
Great pizza, super cheesy garlic cheese bread, huge salads and all at an affordable price! 
They have great happy hour and daily specials. 
We will definitely be back when downtown Boise.

text:
Was pleasantly surprised with this cute little place in the middle of the busy St Pete beach. If you are after classy service, proper crowd and clean table cloths this is a place to come to.

Ever so slightly on a higher price range meals were well prepared and executed promptly. My kid had a burger which was executed in a classic style, nothing fancy, I had a Caesar. All was well, clean, fresh and prompt.

Keep up the good work!

text: $9.00 for 2 nice size Crawfish Beignet. I recommend ordering this as a meal if you are not sharing with 1 or 2 people. Great taste,a ton of crawfish,tomatoes, my only problem I would recommend a thicker sauce or cheese; because the sauce was very loose and messy or a dipping sauce would go great together. I, normally would complaint about getting just 2 piece for the price of $9.00. But this item really is worth $9.00.

text: Yeah this place is legit. Heads up prepared to wait in long lines. It's well worth it tho. My recommendation get the surf n turf with fried pickles. Definitely the best comfort food after a night of drinking. Seems like root beer is the thing here but that sweet tea is legit. I got one tip I've noticed people look down on others for saving tables well before ordering don't be that guy, order first.
name: Casey

text:
This is a fairly new coffee shop that is connected to a cowork space and law firm. The shop has coffee, food, and mocktails and the idea is to provide a space that allows people to network and also get work done.

Some coffee shops have this attitude that they don't want to have people work out of them and Networking Leads Coffee House is the opposite of that, they actually want you to work there and its obvious by the amount of plugs, Wi-Fi, and comfortable seating spread throughout.

They invite speakers from around the business community regularly to talk about their businesses and network with others which is pretty neat considering Tampa really needs more of that.

The coffee tastes great and the barista has plenty of experience in hospitality and food and it's really obvious. During my visit I had the chicken salad sandwich which was delicious as well as some street tacos that were also quite good. It's great to have a coffee shop that offers more than just baked goods or sandwiches. 

This coffee shop is a really great choice for people who have business in West Tampa, South Tampa, or even North Hyde Park and is in a central part of town being close to Raymond James Stadium, International Plaza, and other local attractions and business districts in Westshore. 

I'll be back for more.
name: Carlos

text: I do live this place and have to admit I dont go often enough.  Portions are not huge, but quality and taste are.

text: The photos made it look a little better than it actually was. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. The music was louder than it needed to be. I can see why people like it, even if I wasn't fully sold. It looked better online than it did in person. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish.

Price felt a touch high for what it was. Food was fresh and service was quick. Would return. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..

My boyfriend loved his dish and I was pretty fond of mine . My only complaint would be that their spice level is off. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. I wouldn't write it off, but I also wouldn't hype it up. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..

text:

text: Stopped in tonight to have a small amount of food, was extremely pleased when my waitress was Tabby. I wouldn't write it off, but I also wouldn't hype it up.

text:
I've been to the mass ave location and loved it, so I was really happy that this place is so popular that they opened up in the fashion mall.
If you haven't been to the fashion mall you can find mini blues in their food court it's in between garden table and Tobu the sushi place.
Love the set up inside, it's bright and modern/ but classic in its own way.
Outdoor seating is an option but I decided to stay inside at one of the smaller tables 
The menu is simple, you can choose from 3 or 4 meatballs, sandwiches and sliders are also options as well.
Choose from a variety of different meatballs with sauces, my personal fave is the garlic butter. The salads to start and tasty and fresh! You can also get sides to split! The macaroni is creamy with just the right amount of cheese and they also have a great veggie risotto!
Full bar with plenty of options, take a friend that way you can split things and try more dishes!

text: I ended up going over there because people would rave about it from work I was excited to try it but everything tasted as if it were dried out or product that had no quality. Maybe I got the wrong menu item so I might try it again but it reminded me of a cheap work holiday employee provided lunch of wonder bread and ballpark hotdogs.

text: Our dinner was delicious!  Our waiter was very enthusiastic and actually eats the food that they serve.  A big pet peeve for me is when a waiter/waitress tells you that they haven't tasted the food for whatever reason...how the heck can you recommend dishes without tasting it!  Our waiter did a terrific job answering our questions and explaining the food. We ordered several small plates and the pork ramen.   Everything was fresh and delicious.  I would definitely go back when I'm in Nashville!

text:
The Continental is a cool place - perfect for sharing food with friends and having a few drinks. The space itself is unique, with two floors of varied seating elements, including large group tables, swinging chairs, and a shag carpet ceiling on the second floor. 

The menu has varied american and ethnic-inspired eats meant to share, ranging from salads to egg rolls to pastas to quesadillas. The menu is all over the place, making sure anyone can find something to eat there. 

For our group of 10 last night, we ordered a great deal of dishes. Some of the stand outs were the tender GRILLED CARROTS topped with crunchy pumpkin seeds, the crispy BRUSSEL SPROUTS, the flavorful TUNA TARTARE (although I did not care for the presentation), and the CALAMARI SALAD with a soy dressing. Others enjoyed the korean wings, french onion soup dumplings, meatballs, and more. 

A cool spot for a group, or when you're looking for something easy, or just want to snack and drink with friends.
name: Rory

text:
My girlfriend and I regularly visit the location in Brunswick, NJ. It's about a 2 hour round trip just to get our KBBQ Fix. We were absolutely thrilled to discover one was opening here in Philadelphia! 
K-POT delivers traditional flavors in a modern styling that rivals most if not all other KBBQ restaurants in the greater Philadelphia area. 

We ordered the japchae, short rib, bulgogi, smoke pork belly & garlic shrimp. I spent the first 10-15min enjoying my pork belly. Seasoned and marinated to perfection it's definitely a must have! The short rib is a close second. Tender, juicy, sweet! The garlic shrimp was big and well seasoned. The bulgogi was very tender and marinated very well. The bon-chon is pretty good as well and pairs well to any of the entrees you order. The server Phoebe was extremely helpful and nice. A couple servers periodically checked on us and cooked our food as we were stuffing our faces. There is NO other restaurant that pairs "All You Can Eat" with quality like K-Pot! 

The fact that this is in the upper northeast also makes this spot amazing. Parking is plentiful, near malls, stores etc. The restaurant itself is pristine. The decor has a nice modern theme. The TVs play sports and random Korean dramas. The music is usually upbeat kpop. They play some American pop hits too. We will be back very soon! Thank you KPOT for getting a location out here!

text:
Istanbul Restaurant has been a long time favorite for my wife and I when craving Turkish/Middle Eastern food. This is not a chain restaurant, so don't expect a polished glitzy atmosphere. For me, this small neighborhood cafe feel is part of the charm of Istanbul. The restaurant decor does include some pictures of Turkey which help match up the atmosphere with the cuisine.

The staff has always been very friendly and inviting, and we felt like we made friends with these folks from the first time we visited. They're always willing to describe menu items you may be unfamiliar with and make good recommendations. The service and food preparation time is right on the mark, and portions are generous enough for some take home if you want it.

You will find that the menu selection and affordable prices are a huge plus, and the consistency of the food quality is exceptional. Everything I've tried on the menu is excellent, but my favorite is the gyro platter. This platter includes a choice of cucumber salad or tabboulle, and you can't go wrong with either. They serve a generous portion of gyro meat on a bed of delicious rice with cucumber sauce for dipping. 

Pita is served with the meal and you can add a delicious serving of hummus as an appetizer. Don't be surprised if they offer you free samples of soup before your entree arrives. They also have a good beverage selection with free refills on fountain drinks.

I usually end the meal with their delicious baklava and my usual cup of Turkish coffee. Turkish coffee is not the same as American coffee, so don't do the bottoms-up approach when finishing or you will have a mouthful of coffee sludge! 

Folks, it's all good here, and you won't break the bank enjoying this fine Turkish and middle eastern cuisine! I give the Istanbul Restaurant a well-deserved five stars because the high quality and affordable prices that have remained remarkably consistent through the many years we've been eating there!
name: John
