text: The owner had made our visit right by refunding our money on full for the burnt calzone and pizza we received. Thank you
name: Mary Beth

text: Ordered takeout because I didn't feel like cooking and it held up okay. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. It was crowded but still moved along. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Food was good and came out fast. No big complaints, just a nice meal.
name: User

text:
Great food. North County mentality though. I can ask for extra salsa, which they charge $2 for (I can understand if not the only thing you're ordering or if you are asking for a large) and they'll just put the cap on loose so I loose it.

Let's be honest. North County is not where you eat to be stress free. Unless it's Culver's or chik Fil a. It's sad that fast food has better customer service skills than a full priced restaurant.

Great food though.
name: Robert

text: New Orleans is known for its fun and of course food and there is no shortage of choices.  If you are tired of seafood or are craving Italian I recommend Irene's.  Was in New Orleans for. Business function and was in charges of setting up then dinners and chose Irene's for our last night and the entire dinner was a success. All that attended the dinner that night loved the place.  It is a couple of blocks from the French Quarter and if you were not looking for it there is a good chance you would never notice it.
name: John

text:
I was so excited to come to Atchafayala due to the raving reviews and it was on my self guided American Horror Story Coven tour. This place DOES not disappoint. I had planned on getting the eggs Atchafayala, but ended up with the most delicious duck hash! I don't even like potatoes but they were so good I ate almost all of them! Their use of the bacon vinegrette under the perfectly, and might I add most creamy, poached eggs there ever were with the flavor and tenderness of the duck, just Divine. It was a Saturday morning and there was already a line before it opened so make reservations or be in line early. It's definitely super yummy. 

And I love the wall made out of frames.
name: jessica

text:
The worst and rudest employees I've ever experienced!!!! 
Ebony needs some customer service training!!!
I will never go back to this place ever again in my life. This is not the first time they have been rude!!
I'm done with this place!!!!

text: Super great place. Ate dinner last night at the bar, our bartender Jacob (I think) he was on the third floor. Super great guy! Helped us around the menu with apps and entree. The crab spinach dip was great, not too fishy. I had the shrimp Alfredo which was really good, I'm typically picky with my Alfredo but was great! My boyfriend got a strip which was good too, there was some seasoning on it but needed just a little more too it. Overall great staff, they help each other out and friendly. I enjoyed that he gave us some tips about the area and where to go and what's fun around here! Thanks so much!
name: Summer

text: While it is not to everyone's taste, it is easily my favorite pizza. Especially since moving away from St. Louis, this is a must stop anytime I get back. This location specifically seems to have maintained it's quality a little better than some of the others. Service was fine, and there is plenty of seating. Parking can be a bit of a challenge due to the odd shape of the parking lot and the small size.
name: Marc

text: This place was a breath of fresh air, compared to other diners. The service was impeccable. Our waitress, Sandy, was the sweetest and most warm person and really made our experience what it was. I would go again simply for the fact that the staff are all so sweet. The food is also great - the pork chops tasted amazing. The place is also very clean, has loads of parking, and is spacious inside. This is definitely a new diner spot for me. (I just wish they carried waffle toppings!)
name: Daphne

text: It was a must to come here and I was so glad I did. It was my first time trying the beignets and it was the best experience of my life ! Oh and yes the powder sugar gets everywhere but it's okay.
name: Nallely

text: A solid choice for breakfast, especially if you fancy bacon. Plenty of options, always something interesting on the blackboards, and packed. Service is still prompt and friendly in the busiest of times. Been here several times now and will keep coming back.
name: Kovia

text: This is a good restaurant for people who is is the first time be this city like me. Rachel, our server, warmly recommended some delicious local foods and the tropical alcohol drink.
name: Zhiguang

text:
I LOVE Peruvian food and was always bummed Philly doesn't have many Peruvian restaurants.  I saw this restaurant opened in NoLibs on Postmates and ordered last week, however we never got our food.  

We swung by the restaurant yesterday afternoon, however the restaurant wasn't open despite their posted hours reflecting they were supposed to be open.  We ended up going to Vista Peru and loved it.

The only problem was, we were now craving Peruvian food.  

Tonight we decided to give Postmates another shot, and actually received our order!  However, the food was a huge miss.  We both got the Lomo Saltado and ceviche classic.  Both were subpar.  The lomo was overcooked and tough despite requesting medium rare, it was in a thick brown gravy that tasted like powdered gravy, there were no tomatoes and only a handful of onions slivers.  The sauce is my favorite part of the dish so it was really disappointing.  The ceviche was mediocre.  The fish warm, tough and a bit too salty.  The sweet potato was a brick.  

We were really looking forward to having a spot to grab lomo in the neighborhood as we really loved Bar Ferdinand, but unfortunately we won't be returning.
name: Ebony

text:
Our most recent visit, a few months ago, was much better than the last.
We sat in the bar area and order a bunch of appetizers.  
Our server was awesome!  She was in a great mood, super friendly and actually had conversations with us, which I love. I don't know why more people aren't like her.

We will be going to this Chili's again and hopefully our new friend will be working.
name: Deanna

text: Stopped in quickly today for some macarons and they were delicious! Found this place from looking on yelp, because I wanted macarons and I came to the right place. I got 2 rose, 2 raspberry, and 2 strawberry. So good and fresh.This was my first time here, and I'll definitely be back!
name: Dresden

text: Had an amazing dinner here with the wife the ravioli  was on point.  My wife had the lamb ragu it was great and the portions was huge. Finished with some gelato that was phenomenal.
name: David

text:
If I could give zero stars I would.  Ordered a pizza and paid for it online to get to my children while my wife and I had a meeting at church.  This was at 7, and we go back to pick them up at 8:45 and the kids said "we thought you were the pizza"

Tried to track delivery and it said my order had been cancelled, for no reason. And without saying anything
name: Ryan

text:
I had an absolutely wonderful experience here during East Nashville Restaurant Week! They had a full Asian inspired menu, with a special touch added to several authentic dishes that were all beyond delicious. 
We tried the Spicy Cucumber Salad, Dry Fried Eggplant, Pork Soup Dumplings, Seafood Pancake and Duck Buns to split between two people. (FYI - this was too much food.. I think four would've been plenty, but we wanted to taste everything, and leftovers are always good anyway!) I traveled to Shanghai recently and fell head over heels in love with Soup Dumplings... how exciting to have a place in Nashville that offers them!!! 
Every bite was delicious. There wasn't a single dish that I wasn't above and beyond impressed with. Their chef is truly something special. 
Our waiter was also amazing. He was great with drink recommendations, allowing me to try different wines and I learned quite a bit from him! As a big wine drinker, it was really cool to have someone knowledgeable and excited about sharing his knowledge. I didn't catch his name, but I feel like they have a high standard for their staff, and that really adds to the experience.
name: Traci

text:
I was excited to try this place since it has such great reviews on yelp! 
It was a little hard to find since it's tucked away in some weird building around the corner from crying wolf. 
I ordered a savory muffin and coffee- it was okay but nothing special. 
I don't see how this place has such great reviews. 
Atmosphere is 4/10
Food is average. 5/10 - I've had better breakfast at Starbucks 
Their coffee is okay as well. 5/10

I live in Nashville and I would not give this place a second chance. Skip it and go to a better place.

text: This place is fantastic ! Have gone 3 times in a month ! I cannot get enough ! Every time a friend suggests dinner I meet them at high note cafe . And i ordered a to go meal for my husband and he was mindblown how tasty it all was. Especially the vegan cheese  cool atmosphere super friendly staff . The only thing i would say was one night when a musician played it was a bit loud . my friend and I couldnt hear each other talk . maybe have the musicians play outside on the patio? Other than that i LOVE this placr and im so glad you switched to an all vegan menu
name: Marci

text: We sat on a charming patio out back and enjoyed a delicious peach and burrata salad with a few jalapeños to give it a tiny kick. The salmon sandwich was grilled rare and tasted so good I had to share half of it with my wife. Fresh and tasty.
name: Chris

text:
We visit Bianchi's Italian every Wednesday evening for dinner and Karaoke.Debbie is by far our favorite server. She is attentive to our needs throughout the evening and prompt with her service. 

Sadly, she was off this last Wednesday and the service was far below what we have come to expect. We had to find menus on an empty table, walk up to the bar to order our drinks and let someone know we wanted to order dinner. One young woman took our order, someone else delivered, and then.... nothing. When we found the young woman and asked if she could take another drink order, we were informed that she wasn't waiting our table, a young man was. Think we'll stick with Debbie from now on.

For Karaoke, Tiffany is tops!
name: Grace

text: This is a great atmosphere and friendly staff. A few mishaps with a broken glass and super busy staff that may have gone a little long between drink and food orders, but overall the food was excellent. Highly recommend trying when they aren't slammed and you have time to enjoy your dinner.
name: Jenn

text: Stopped here on the way home from Clearwater beach . Ordered tacos , a burrito , and chips and salsa . Absolutely delicious ! Huge portions and quick service .
name: Diana

text: Great stop. Visiting this area and saw the rooftop seating. Margaritas are great while waiting for the table. Had the Johnny cash burger....amazing!
name: Joe

text:
Saigon Slim's food truck brethren should take note of what SS is doing. 

Low carb and salad offerings are not common amongst the area food truck scene and SS hits it out of the park. 

I had the Boo Coo salad (no vermicelli noodles) with lemongrass chicken. Huge, fresh, and filling. 

I look forward to trying the Saigon Caesar with house made dressing and wonton croutons.
name: Lauren

text:
I stopped by Corner Bakery Café when I was trying to find a semi-healthy lunch option close to St. Joseph's hospital. They definitely have healthy meals but I couldn't resist the good stuff that included bacon and lots of sugar. 

I had the club sandwich and a blueberry hand-pie. Sure the sandwich was good but that hand-pie was on point. Delicious filling, and crispy, flaky crust. It's obvious that they only serve fresh pastries at the Corner Bakery Café daily.

I ordered to go and the service at the counter was friendly and fast. They have a very large menu with many options so I plan on returning for sure, even if it's just for another tasty pastry.
name: Stephannie

text: This place is garbage. I don't write many reviews, because generally I'm cool with mediocre... It's whatever I can eat after work. These jabrones call what is clearly chuck steak (pot roast) their "short ribs". If my mom hadn't introduced me to shitty food I probably wouldn't have known better... But she did and now cooks better than these fucksters. text:
Most delicious authentic ramen!
Sauces are made from scratch and broth are thick (the way it's suppose to be)!
I had taukemono, noodle without the broth, and donkotchu ramen!
It was worth stopping by before heading home!!!!
name: Hana

text: Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Food was good and came out fast. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. It looked better online than it did in person. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. Would probably stop in again if nearby.
name: User

text:
Rewards: Don't forget to sign up for their rewards program! Ask your server how to sign up. There have been a couple times that I've eaten in and they forgot to ask me, no worries, just write your phone number and the word "REWARDS" at the top of your receipt when you pay. 

Vegan Desserts: There are very few place where I can find vegan desserts, and it's a huge comfort to know that Great Full Gardens will always have my back. They have a constantly rotating selection of tasty vegan treats in their cold case. 

Alternative hot beverages: Their turmeric latte is to die for. It's like drinking a warm cup of sunshine in the morning. Their magical mushroom drink is surprisingly very good. I was a little cautious at the thought of a mushroom drink but was pleasantly mistaken. Top of my list is their Aztec D'Oro. An incredible mocca drink with cayenne. Don't knock it until you try it, it's next level amazing. 

Sauces: All dips and sauces are 100% vegan. 

Food: I've never had a meal I didn't like here. Before going vegan their Terrific Turkey Pesto was my go-to favorite meal. Now that I am vegan, I'm absolutely addicted to their vegan grilled cheese sandwich. I order it at least once a week when I'm at work. It's the perfect cure for a bad day. 

One of my top 5 restaurants in all of Reno. (All of their locations).
name: Savannah

text: The ribs were not the best that I have had. The hostess did not want to sit us in the dining room and instead us sitting us at the bar. The rib quality needs to be more consistent for a BBQ joint.
name: Eloy

text: No big complaints, just a nice meal. Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Price felt a touch high for what it was. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. It looked better online than it did in person. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really.
name: User

text:
Don't let the corner bar appearance fool you.  You've come to the right place.   

The best time to visit The Original Clam Tavern is on a weekday.  The weekend is always packed tightly and rightfully so as you can't beat the fresh seafood offered here.  Reservations accepted and recommended.   

On 8/4/2019 I was there with family and ordered soft shell crabs sauteed at the recommendation of the waitress.   It came in a bright lemon butter sauce.  And, the vegetables were divine.  OMG!

You probably know soft shells are small but this order was so big I had to take one home in a dogie bag.  Fat chance any dog would be given this delicacy as I warmed it up the next day and it was still yummy. 

Recommended?   In a heart beat!
name: Sharon

text: Went on a short trip to Reno and saw this place on yelp. BEST POTSTICKERS EVER and the waitress told us that they are made fresh every morning and you can definitely tell they are. We also got the sweet and sour chicken, along with the general chicken. The sweet and sour chicken was alright but the general chicken was the best I've ever had. I'll definitely be coming next time I'm in Reno.
name: Gabriella

text:
I can't believe what I've hear from them.
They DO NOT want to deliver because they are too busy and we are out of Area EVEN 2 house down next door is the IN AREA. Less than 50 feet away, inside of same gate. are you kidding me?
This is totally BS and the guy on the phone was ridiculously rude.
Do not use this location. NOT worth to spend your money.
name: Sayaka

text: Food was good and came out fast. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. For the price I expected more than this. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which prob says everything.. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent.
name: User

text: My family and I are Longhorn.regulars and we visit this location often. Like most places in the north Philly area this location can be a bit busy but the staff and food are usually pretty good. Any issues are typically handled by the server or management promptly.
name: Lavares

Anyway, we walked in and were welcomed by a empty hostess stand in a 7ft by 7ft drapped "waiting area" with no seating. text: The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. By the time the food came out I was already annoyed. Probably not coming back. No big complaints, just a nice meal. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. The whole meal felt kinda uneven. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus..
name: User

text: Had a tea latte.  Not bad. Nice relaxing environment. Some people were playing chess.  I hate coffee but it looks like everyone was quite pleased and relaxed.
name: David

text: I've ordered on the app three times now, and I still have to wait in line and go to the counter. Second time I went, my order wasn't even set out, I had to show the girl at the counter what I ordered on the app. So then she just started grabbing whatever pizza and got it wrong the first time. I pay for ranch. They only have buffalo ranch. So in a three month period you can't stock up on plain ranch in a pizza place? The pizza wasn't bad for the price.. but the whole process of this place falls short.
name: Leilauni

text: We ordered 2 family meals for our youth group at NCYC. The food arrived on time, was exactly as advertised. I can't say much about the pizza - I'm spoiled by NJ and NY pizza - but  everyone was happy. The wings were great. The family salad served all 9 of us - with enough left for  another meal. Very satisfied!
name: Bob

text:
Well upon booking this hotel, there was no mention of the restaurant and club lounge being closed. The bar and restaurant has been temporarily relocated. 

I had some free beverage vouchers and decided to visit the make-shift bar. Free wine was excellent, service was a little pushy and the food was just okay.
name: Scott

text:
Excellent Breakfast at this vintage style diner. The service was excellent and food followed. Eggs, scrapple, potatoes and toast for the win!
It's conveniently located on Rowan University campus. Looking for a breakfast spot check this spot out. 
CASH ONLY fyi

Cheers
name: Daniel

text: The food is ok, but the service is really slow. We sat down at 5:50pm. Noticed that wine was on happy hour - great!  Waited...and waited...our server first came to our table at 6:01. I ordered wine. He told us that happy hour was over. (Um...ok...). We ordered our food at 6:01. My hamburger arrived at 6:27. We didn't see our server from the time he brought my wine (full price) until our food arrived. Didn't see him again until our finished plates had been in the table for awhile... (we will just go to Down Under next time)
name: Euge

text: We just moved to Nashville and this was our first BBQ stop and we were not disappointed! It'll probably be hard going somewhere else after this place has set the bar so high. The atmosphere is so fun and lively. You order at the counter and seat yourself. This did not take away from the customer service as we were still waited on for extra condiments or any other needs we had. There's also a full bar that serves drinks/beer/wine in mason jars! I don't know why but that just seals the deal for me. Last, but not least THE FOOD! Absolutely delicious and can tell it was slow cooked for hours, yet still made to order. The white BBQ sauce is to die for and the collard greens so perfectly seasoned! This is a must go to place when in Nashville!

Tell me how when we started eating the rice it didn't taste like fried rice and it wasn't hot at all it was medium warm kinda like they cook fried rice and leave it in the fridge till someone orders rice man that rice tasted like it was made yesterday and was just put in the microwave.  That was not fried rice. It was warmed up rice with veggies       Also. It was my first and only time here I saw the front and back doors open that's just gross. Out back is a dumpster nearby the wide open door. ... I think they keep the doors open to circulate air so they don't have to pay as much for electric bill.   Never go here I can't wait to see this place close

text: Top notch pizza n salads. Little pricey but still delicious.  They have a well organized, quick and East take out as well.

text: UPDATE:  We have been back 4 visits since the review below. Primarily because the Manager ( Tammy) responded to the original post. Tammy is super!! We eat out frequently at Bonefish, Long Horn, etc. and you never see the manager, much less have one so caring to ensure your visit is outstanding.  ORIGINAL REVIEW FOLLOWS: My wife and I have eaten here a few times.  But, it's been over a year since our last visit.  We decided last night to try it again. We arrived at 6:02 PM and were put on the wait list, and told it would be about 10 minutes.  Well, almost an hour later at 6:53 we were called.  I only know the times because they took my cell number and texted me when I went on the wait list at 6:02, and when they were ready to seat us at 6:53. I realize you can't ask customers to free up their table, and I realize restaurants get busy.  But......to tell us it would be about 10 minutes, and then it turns out to be almost an hour wait is unacceptable. We would have gone to one of 3 other restaurants in the shopping center and had dinner much sooner if we'd know it would be an hour wait.  Once we were seated, things improved however.  "Hanna H" our waitress was super. She apologized, and was able to quickly get an appetizer order in as happy hour prices ended minutes after we finally were seated.  For dinner I had the steak frites, my wife the grilled red snapper, and we shared chocolate cake for dessert. Food was excellent.  Service was excellent.  But the hostess clearly needs some training in estimating wait times when you're off that far in your wait estimate.  We'll go back and try it again, but make a reservation thru Yelp, and see how close actual seating comes to the reservation time.

text:
Gioia's on the Hill has been around for 100 years, as of 2018, but I've never been there. That's how much of a West Countyite I am.

In fact, I grew up around the corner from this Creve Coeur location. But as long as I've lived in the area, I've never once been to this shopping center. I'm not even sure if I've ever seen it. Because I'm kinda blind, I probably just drove right by it.

According to the Google, this used to be a Mr. Goodcents. It's too bad, for the sake of sandwich marketplace diversity (if that's a business term), that they had to get rid of its predecessor. I spent like a million dollars in Goodcents, when it was at the top of the street, behind the bank.

The inside still kinda looks like a Goodcents. It's all clean, new-ish and well organized, but there's nothing about it to warrant the premium price point, nor is there anything about it that suggests the shop's supposedly historic pedigree.

Maybe I just couldn't see (literally, I only have about half of one eye left), but I don't think they list the prices of the sandwiches, sides and what have you. I wasn't sweating it, because I was willing to spend as much as $15, i.e. entirely too much for a sandwich, for the sake of citizen food journalism.

The hot salami is their bread and butter, so to speak, but I was actually more interested in a sandwich called the Porknado. It comes with three different kinds of pork, and I'm constitutionally incapable of not buying a sandwich that comes with three or more types of pork.

Specifically, it comes with salami, ham and bacon on garlic cheese bread. I think there's cheese on the bread, and then they let you add more cheese. I chose provel, because this is St. Louis, albeit a somewhat distant, culturally deficient outlying area.

The sandwich is put through a little toaster, like at Quiznos, or a gas station that has a toaster for the Landshire sandwiches (e.g. the "Super Nike"), and then you get to customize it. It looks like the Italian sandwich comes with toppings pre-selected, which I would have preferred, because having choices makes me anxious, and because I lack respect for people with weird dietary needs and food preferences.

I went with the standard LTOP plus pepperoncini and hot mustard. If I had it to do over again, I would have added mayonaisse. I don't know how authentically Italian that is, but if you just get mustard they only give you but so much of it, like maybe they expect you to get two different sandwich spreads. The pepperoncini comes with the stems still on it, which makes it quite literally inedible, but also provides a sort of rustic charm.

I'll eat a toasted deli sandwich, but they aren't really my thing. (The Pepe at Jimmy John's is the best deli sandwich there ever was.) Still, there's no denying that the sandwiches at Gioia's are amazing. The meats are piled high, but not so high that it throws off the proportions. The bread is good enough that you could eat it by itself, if you ever fell on hard times. The bacon, which is pre-cooked, mediocre-quality restaurant bacon, kinda overpowers the ham and salami, but that, my friends, is what I call a high class problem.

With a bag of Billy Goat chips and a soda, my order really did come out to $15. At that price, for a sandwich that isn't even my favorite kind of sandwich, I probably won't be back ever again, but if I did come back I definitely would enjoy it.
name: Byron

Charred cauliflower - amazing. Has medjool dates and tahini and charred to perfection

Dinner:
Teriyaki quinoa with tofu - beautifully well balanced bowl, with the right blend of spice and toast, as well as snap peas and other vegetables that give it wonderful texture. 
Artichoke pesto pizza - great. Has almond ricotta, which is such an interesting cheese replacement and never makes me feel like I'm missing out on anything. Mm mm good.

text:
Dined here on a recommendation with a caveat that their service has gone down the tubes lately, and boy, were my friends not kidding! Overall some of the worst service I have ever had (complete with servers lying about prices to get us to order more and managers saying it was our fault because we should have known better when I brought up this situation). This, coupled with average food with poor presentation, led me to the 2 star rating. Trust me on this, skip it, and go to another one of the dozens of Cuban places in Philly, if thats what you are looking for. 

The full story in case you were wondering: We sat for approx. 15 mins with no service when I finally had to go to the hostess to ask to send someone over. Finally a gentleman comes over, we both order a margarita ($11 each), he asks if we want salt, I said of course, and then he suggests us getting a pitcher because for only $7 more, we can each get 2 drinks instead of 1. Wasn't planning on that, but hey, it was $7 only. We also put in our app with this dude. 30 minutes later (cmon people), our app finally comes out and it looks like a 5 year old plated it. It was the bruschetta and the taste was good. 10 mins after that, for a total of 40 mins after we ordered, the margaritas finally came out. The waitress that we were switched to did visit and say they were backed up, that they only had 1 bartender for a very busy fri eve. I appreciate her keeping us updated. Back to the service. During this wait time, we ordered dinner, which arrived over an hour after we ordered it, yes at this point I started timing things. Thank goodness we at least had our app otherwise I would have had to go to the store on the corner to get a snack while we waited for our food to come out! The food was average at best. I had the shrimp over rice and friend had steak. Then thats when things got even more interesting. We get the bill and see that the pitcher was $38, not the 11+11+7= $29 we had been told by the first dude. We ask, the manager comes over, makes then dude come over, and he proceeds to try to tell us that we ordered Mojitos and that that was $7 more for a pitcher. Umm clearly you asked us about salt so you knew better. This went back and forth. Plus the MANAGER said that we should have known better, than we had more than 1 extra drink each with the pitcher so we should have expected it to be more money than just $7 more. Um I am sorry lady, but 1. thats not my job, and 2. how am I supposed to know because we were pouring into tiny glasses. So besides the server lying to my face, even giving him an out and said, I get it, its busy, you must have made a mistake, he kept on with his mojito story trying to blame us. After 2 hours there, I wish I had my time back. At least we finally got our money back. 

Overall, if you are a business, please dont lie, dont blame me, dont serve food that looks a hot mess, and make good food, and I'll definitely come back. Unfortunately Mixto didn't follow this recipe. Rarely do I write a review like this, with such fire, so you know if I am writing like this, I really mean it. This is even after I let a few days go by, I was that upset. Get it together people! 

To add some positivity to this review, the real MVP of our experience, the water lady! She was on point! My glass was never empty and she was just a sweetheart.
name: Thea

Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. You can tell they care about customer experience here. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait.

text: The soup was better than the sandwich, which I wasn't expecting. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. I left full, which at least counts for something. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced.

text:
When everyone in line ordered pizzas, I braved the curious stares and deviated mightily.  I couldn't resist the fresh homemade meatballs and the potions were huge.

The spaghetti pasta was nothing to write about.  They were cooked ahead of time and I knew it.  Instead, I focused on the meatballs.  The dish came with three gigantic meatballs.  To give you an idea, I was only able to consume one.  It was juicy, flavorful and tender.  The meatballs alone was worth the $11.  

I highly recommend the spaghetti meatballs.  Perhaps there's an option for just meatballs.
name: Michael

text: Stopped into this great local find during what happened to be TR19's 6th anniversary celebration...and it's no wonder... this place is a stand out among others in South Philly. Warm and friendly ambiance is delivered through the classic pub environment and attentive staff. Buffalo wings were perfectly cooked with just the right amount of heat, a hearty Cheese Steak was superior to others in the city, Nashville Hot Chicken as authentic as any I've had in Music City itself, and an innovative selection of daily specials ensure there's something for everyone to enjoy. Fresh ingredients, expertly prepared dishes, and an extensive selection of beers on tap makes this spot your best option when in South Philly, or worth making TR19 a destination on it's own!
name: Amy

text: Friendly, professional and went above and beyond for my order today!! When I ordered online and accidentally placed my order at the wrong store the staff helped me navigate a solution in a timely manner.
name: Kait

text:
We came to Tucson for the 4th Avenue Street Fair and wanted lodging that wasn't your typical chain.  I prepaid for a room through one of the booking sites and check-in was fairly smooth.   Ivonne noted she was going to give us a complimentary upgrade to their newly remodeled buildings, nice of her.   

We got settled in and while we weren't wowed with the room, it initially seemed good enough for a night's sleep before the next day's fair. The visit goes down-hill from there.   The upgraded room was small, had cracked tile on the outdated bathroom counter, had mold stains the shower and the bathroom floor grout was filthy.   This is the first hotel where I took the bedding apart to look for bed bugs.  None found, thankfully, but that's the quality level of this place.

The neighboring room blared their TV starting at 9:30pm.   I called the front office to ask them to ask the other guests to lower their volume level.  Nothing happened.   No follow up, no phone ringing in the other room.  The walls are thin enough to hear a phone ringing.

We decided to tough it out and I hoped that getting to sleep quickly would solve much of the frustration.  No such luck.  Apparently, the folks next door need that level of TV sound to sleep through the night because the TV stayed on all night.

I checked out in the morning and the young woman working the desk was exceedingly unhelpful.   She explained the room we were in was the upgraded room, most recently decorated building on the property.   I told her that if the room we stayed in was the most updated room they had, I'd like to see the crap room that I was supposed to stay in because I had paid a pretty penny for a room that shouldn't have been sold for more than $50.00.   She said those rooms were the most recently updated...about 10 years ago.   Wow, thanks.    I noted they need to work on how they present these 'upgrades', because nothing about that room felt current.

This place is pretty on the outside, seemingly well maintained.  But it's false advertising.   The staff is awful and the rooms are worse.  There are so many other non-chain properties in Tucson that deserve business.   Travelers beware.
name: Barbe

text: So I decided that I wanted to buy some Chinese for lunch, but enough that I would have leftovers for dinner too. I have never been here in the years its been around so I decided to give it a shot. I ordered chicken lo mein and Mongolian beef, which came to about $24. I thought that it would be a decent amount of food, but when it came it was 2 small to medium size chinese take out boxes (should have taken a picture). It took about 15-20 min to make the food. As I was walking out the door the hostess came up and said they made a mistake, they made Mongolian chicken instead of beef and that they could switch it out but i would have to wait. I decided to just leave. I got it home and the lo mein did not have much flavor to it honestly, but the Mongolian chicken was pretty damn tasty. Me mixing the two, plus some rice and soy sauce made a decent meal. Based on the other reviews and my experience I have to think its an "ok" place for Chinese. All in all give it a shot if your in the area, if not don't bother.

text: the first few bites were promising and then it kind of leveled out. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. text:
Absolutely the worst fast-food restaurant I've ever been to. I've given this location 3 or 4 tries in the last two years, and every single time it's a complete disaster. I will never go back...and based on the lack of customers (zero) at 6:30 on a Friday evening, I'm guessing I'm not alone in my decision. 

The gentleman working the drive-thru has messed up my order each time I've been in. He first charged me $28 for two Fill-Ups and one popcorn chicken combo. I said there must be a mistake. He tried again and came up with $23. Eventually had someone else do it and got it right ($18.00 something). Then I figured they had messed up the food order, and I was right. Had to go into the restaurant to get the correct meals. As I entered with my bag, I got no smiles, no "how can I help you?"; instead was greeted with the "manager" saying to the drive-thru man, "your order's wrong". Wow, wow, wow. I would also think the food would have been fresh between 6:30-7:00...also wrong. Biscuits were hard as a rock and the chicken definitely had not just been fried. To top it all off, not a "thank you" or a word said when they hand you your food. 

Not sure how this location stays in business.

text:

They do some different takes on the Chinese-American classics and they have a lot of unique dishes I've never seen before, all of which are amazing. Some very authentic recipes along with interesting fusion-ish offerings as well. I've eaten here at least a dozen times over the last few years and I've never been disappointed. You MUST have the beef wrapped pancakes. Ask for the house spicy peanut sauce to dip it in as well. One of the best things you will ever eat, I promise you!

This time I also ordered the roti, mango chicken, chow kueh teow, and a side of hainanese rice. All of it was delicious, the noodles had a good ratio of noodle to veg/protein. text: Hidden gem. I was in the area and decided to try this place after hearing about their food. I'm so glad I did. It's a nice simple restaurant with wooden tables and a small bar with a small TV. It offers a comfortable and inviting atmosphere with 70s&80s music playing in the background. (Loved it). I ordered the buffalo cauliflower and the fried tomato BLT. The buffalo cauliflower was delicious. It wasn't overcooked and you could actually taste the buffalo sauce.  It had a nice crunch from the cauliflower and flavor without being greasy.  They nailed it! The sandwich was also delicious. It was served on buttered and browned bread. It truly reminded me of home cooking.  It was simple but delicious.  I also ordered a simple salad that only had tomatoes and sunflower seeds, but the dressing complimented the salad and my meal. The service was good. They were super friendly and allowed me to order smaller portions for lunch, which I appreciated.  Good hearty comfort food and friendly service in small, but quaint location.

text: Coffee is delicious! I particularly love their cold brew. I've also tried the blackened shrimp wrap with remoulade, and thought it was delicious. Flavor was great, and they were generous with the shrimp. There's a drive through, and I actually recommend that because parking can quickly become a nightmare.

text: Stopped in here for lunch on a Saturday afternoon before catching a show at the Walnut Street Theater. I was surprised to find out that this place is table-service and I was surprised by how big it was inside. Behind the bar area, they had a pool table and some arcade games. TV's can be found throughout the place and they had various college football games on while we were there. We had good, attentive service throughout our meal. We started with the crab and artichoke dip, which was really good. The cheese on top was pretty thick and we had to kind of cut through it to get into the crab and artichoke part of it. Chucks of artichoke could be found within the dip. We ran out of chips, but they happily offered us more to finish off the dip. We all went with the Cyclone dog but modified it to our liking. Happily, my wife was able to get a gluten-free bun for a $2 upcharge. Overall, the dogs were good. We ate it more as a fork and knife dish, so I kept cutting into the paper that was on top of the tray that the meal is served in. I would have preferred it had been on a plate. We also ordered the regular fries and truffle fries. The truffle fries reminded me more of crab fries and had a little bite to them. Not a real big deal, but would have been nice to know that the lemonade did not include free refills, but soft drinks are.

Very friendly and made some really great recommendations. If you are even in New Orleans you have to check this out. An!!

text: Not a bad place to grab a quick bite for lunch.  Being located right across the street from the convention center, though, it might not be that quick if a large convention is in town.  But I got my order takeout, which lessened the enjoyment some for me.  Not that the food was that bad, but I called about 1/2 hour before I was going to be there, and told them when I'd be there.  They apparently prepared the food right away, because it was fairly cooled off when I got back to my office (only 5 minutes away) and ate it.  The food itself was pretty good, for the most part.  Very mild as far as heat goes - perhaps that was just the dishes I ordered.  Hoy jaw deep fried pork dumplings had a lot of meat in them, and were tasty.  Khao soi with chicken was savory and pretty good, but the chicken was kind of chewy.  Had the chicken been tender, and had the food been hot, four stars.  But as it is....

text:
Umm...get the King Crab toast. Period. 

We decided to split the Charred Shrimp and King Crab Toast as an appetizer. Both appetizers were large enough to stand on their own as an appetizer for two (but I love to overdo it.) The shrimp was amazing, but the toast was the most amazing, buttery, satisfying flavor. I could have had this an an entree on its own. 

We split the Scallop entree and it was delicious as well and a perfect serving size for one person...assuming they don't eat two large appetizers. The drinks and Apple Streusel cake were delightful as well.

text: The staff we very friendly and helpful. The food was delicious. If we were local, it would definitely be a regular place to visit.

text: I went for breakfast during the week without a reservation, though if it was lunch or a weekend, may have waited a long time. The breakfast was amazing. The atmosphere was along with my coffee was what made it great. It is the kind of place to take your mother on mothers day or girls brunch.

text:
Honey's has some of the best breakfast in Philly. The coffee is great, the service is good, and the food is fantastic! My boyfriend and I visited on a Saturday morning and the wait was about 15 minutes. Once seated, we were helped immediately with some really good coffee. The food was good, and brought out quick. My only reason for knocking off a star is that our server forgot my bacon.

The mood inside is pretty loud and kind of fast paced. It feels kind of like a diner. Everyone is friendly, and it's a very welcoming environment. The decor is really vintage. Overall it's a really fun place!

text:
I dined here for the first time last night. Food was delicious (except for the cauliflower which was oddly and extremely sweet) but all the food presented very well. 

The Asian guy filling water glasses kept unnecessarily touching the mouth part of the water glasses, the girl filling water glasses maneuvered herself in a way to put the water that she did not have to touch the glasses at all, so it appears some staff are trained and some are not... 


My only real caveat was that half way through the meal some lady came over, interrupted us, and started moving things around on our table while we were in the middle of eating. We looked at each other like 'who is this??'

text:
We came here because we had a coupon and gift card and there was a location nearby. I usually don't have super high expectations for large chain restaurants located in shopping malls but this was even worse than my expectations.

Started out with the Bang Bang Shrimp appetizer, which was quite good. They cover it in spicy mayo and place it on a bed of lettuce leaves. Great app to start but then it all went downhill.

We ordered two specials, the Seafood Risotto and the Angler's Catch. Neither of us finished our entrees. The Seafood Risotto was incredibly oily and I could hardly find the risotto. When I did, it just tasted like oil and bland cheesy mush. The Angler's Catch was described as a "tempura dish" but was actually just ultra fried seafood with French fries. We peeled off all the batter and just ate what was inside. Would not recommend either.

The only reason I'm giving this place two stars (as opposed to one) is the service and spaciousness of the restaurant. Our server was extremely nice and the ambiance was relaxed and not too loud. The Bang Bang Shrimp was decent but not enough to bring me back.

text:
The burgers really do live up to the hype here! 

Expect a wait. I put our name in on the yelp app and it quoted 20-30 minutes of a wait on a Sunday night around 6. We got there in 20 minutes and waited another 20 to be seated. There's a few parking spots  in a lot right before the restaurant so try to snag one if you can. 

Once seated, service was quick and we ordered our food right away. I ordered the farm burger but made some changes because:
1. I personally don't need ham, bacon, and burger meat all on one sandwich. 
2. If it's going to be a burger, it better have cheese on it and this one doesn't. 
3. Not a huge fan of maple flavor, so wanted to change the mustard. 

I changed the maple mustard to horseradish mustard and 86'ed the ham in favor of some cheese. These changes were awesome and the burger was by far one of the best I've had. I just find it irritating that they still charge you additional to make changes- 50 cents just to replace the mustard type, and 1 dollar to add cheese even though ham was 2 bucks and I didn't get any. It's not a big deal in terms of the actual cost, but it just seemed unnecessary. 

Either way, the burger was great and the tots were also crispy and delicious. Get a side of beer cheese to dip them in and you won't regret it. The hubs also enjoyed his rather boring but classic pharmacy burger with fries and happily dipped into the beer cheese as well. 

Definitely would come back next time we're in the area!

text:
I was really looking forward to having dinner at Will BYOB with my partner and his family, but I was sorely disappointed by the food. I admit that I am a picky eater, but my partner, a self-described "trash-person" will eat and enjoy almost anything, and even he agreed that the meal was a complete disappointment. 

The plating was simple and attractive, and elements of the dinner were great (OMG that sourdough pretzel bread tho, easily the best part of dinner). The service was impeccable; between our waitress Amelia, and two other staff members who occasionally checked in we felt incredibly welcome, even when one member of our party expressed that the fish was too salty (I also had the fish and found it inedible but I don't complain much so I gave it to my partner who ate it despite agreeing that it was awful) and requested a different entre. The staff clearly cared about our dining experience, were knowledgable about the food being served, and were very friendly and accommodating of the food restrictions that we had.

Unfortunately the food nowhere near lived up to the greatness of the service. Maybe the chef was just having a bad night (the celery soup was far too sweet) or was trying some new things that didn't land well (oh mylanta that fish was just NASTY), but the dinner was absolutely NOT worth $72 (including tax and tip) per person.

Anyway. Maybe we'll try again on a different night in hopes of the presence of a better chef as the ambiance and wait-staff were amazing. Thanks great waitstaff!

text:
Amazing little gem in the area. If you have been to university city or West Philly, you will realize how rare it is to find Southeast Asian cuisines. Most of the market are Chinese. This place deserve a star just for existing. At Daleng's, you can get Thai, Vietnamese and Cambodian food, and all for a bargain.

This restaurant itself is small but comfortable. The staff were very friendly and helpful with the menu. We opted for chow fun with beef in gravy, chicken and veggie curry, pork egg rolls, a small and a large Thai tea with one can of chrysanthemum tea. So first of all, let's talk about how much that cost us. We had an order of 5 egg rolls plus the chow fun and curry with rice with one thai tea at the restaurant and two drinks to go. All that for 2 people was $32!! How do you beat this price? An amazing deal!

The chow fun was pretty good, the gravy was sweet and savory without overpowering. The beef was tender and they gave just the right amount of food. The curry was very pleasant, it was light and I don't mean in flavor, it felt light and good unlike some curry where it's heavy and thick. The flavor was more akin to massaman curry but more soupy. The egg rolls were super crunchy and spanking hot. It was such a deal to get 5 egg rolls for 4.75. Most Vietnamese places charge $5 for 2!

The chef came out to check on us multiple times and made sure we felt at home. A rarity for the location, great authentic food, awesome services and cheap eats. While there may be a lot of good restaurants around town, on this block, Daleng is the best and is highly recommended.
name: Luan

text:
Mixed review. Really wanted to leave a 2.5 star, but I'll be nice and give em a 3. Last night was my first time there. We took a big group, but not a "huge" group. We went after church let out. It was only a group of 10 young adults (we are all over 18 years of age). We were quiet, we were not disruptive in any way. The food was good, especially considering it was my first time there. 

The downside is how ride the guy was to us. At 9:92pm he came and said word for word in a very heavily sarcastic, full of attitude tone: "we close at 9, so you might want to hurry up and get you and your friends out of here." 

Okay...I get it. We are sorry, we didn't realize you closed at 9. We didn't realize we had stayed over by two measly minutes. But one of our group members was not finished eating his nachos. They could've at least let us stay until he finished those. Or, if we absolutely had to leave that very instant - dude could've been nicer about it. 

We aren't gonna let this keep us from going back, but just a heads up to Blue Coast, you may wanna teach your employees some manners. 

Great food, much better than Chipotle. I tried there one time and was not a fan of the food at all so I was hesitant to try blue coast. Had the staff been nicer, this would've been an all around great experience. Again, the food was fantastic. That guy with the bad attitude is my only issue out of this whole thing. The girl that was on staff last night, she was super nice. The guy was the rude one. 

Great food, bad attitude.

text:
I think it sums up my feelings that my stomach started to rumble as I began this review... A perfect evening in Fishtown at a relatively new restaurant - 5 stars for Sutton's!

We were visiting friends who lived in the area and accidentally missed our other reservations because we had spent too much time at the pre-dinner watering hole.  Having been to Sutton's on a few occasions, our friend raved about it and dangled the phrase "best mac and cheese in the world" before our hungry hearts, and we were in!  I was apprehensive about 5 of us wandering in around 7:30pm on a Saturday evening without reservations, but thankfully we were promptly seated in their adorable dining area.

Our server was super friendly and fun, he was being trained that evening -but his service was prompt, his jokes were funny, and he was attentive enough that we weren't searching for simple things like more water or napkins as is sometimes the case.  

We were ravenous when we sat down, and at the recommendation of our friend, ordered the Mac and Cheese starter and the Brussel Sprouts for the table to share.  I am not usually a mac&cheese order-er; but I have to say, this was damn good.  The bowl was piled high with delicious noodles covered in cheddar, curd, gouda, and parmesan panko crust - and for $10, it was plenty to share 5 ways - I even got a small helping of seconds!  Seemed like there was bits of carrots or vegetables in the mix, it wasn't too glutinous (not to be confused with glutenous - it was definitely had gluten), and was perfect for a cold winter evening.  The Crispy Brussel Sprouts were the other show stopper at the table - absolutely phenomenal.  They're fried Brussels Sprouts tossed with sea salt and lemon - plenty for $6!  I know that frying vegetables, somewhat negates the whole point of having vegetables, but just try these, and tell me you're not in love.

For dinner, the hubs and I shared the Warm Winter Salad and the Sutton Burger.  Both were delicious - see below for deets!
//Warm Winter Salad: We chose to add the Moroccan chicken - which was amazing - for some extra protein. This salad was delicious, the vegetables were all super bright and flavorful, and tahini dressing was the perfect amount of creaminess - I'd order this again in a heartbeat!  According to the menu, it's made with arugula, but that night it seemed they subbed spinach for the arugula - i REALLY liked the spinach though!  Bonus - it's served with more of those crispy brussel sprouts! (toasted bulgur, arugula, cabbage, fried Brussels sprouts, toasted almonds, with tahini dressing).  
//Sutton's Burger: This was a really delicious burger! We ordered it medium, and it was cooked perfectly.  The whole thing would have been too much to handle on my own, it was very heavy with all the flavors.  I asked for a couple extra pickles on the side and they brought out a whole bunch (of the most delicious pickles!!) - so I loaded it high with those crunchy vinegary pickles - it really brightened my half of the burger up a lot! #pickleobsessed.  The fries were really good too - the hubs ate most of them, though (blue cheese, sweet balsamic onions, fresh greens, garlic aioli, on a brioche bun with fries or a salad).

They had a full bar, and the drinks were pretty creative looking! I can't wait to come back!

This place does not take reservations.  It's only about 5 months old, and I can guarantee this place is already growing a cult following.  Check it out soon, before it gets too popular - you won't be sorry!
name: Robin

text: I've had the fries, chips, burger , & pizza.  All very good & fast.  Friendly staff & patrons.  Relaxed & not snobby.
name: Brian

text: I really enjoyed their salsa and their enchiladas. The food has a little kick but it's a good. The atmosphere And setting was great. The service was OK nothing over-the-top but I would definitely recommend the restaurant.
name: Micheal

text:
Not sure why 3 stars- our service was great! Drinks delicious & tacos packed with flavor!

We had a six top out on the patio, and all of us really enjoyed our meals and our cocktails. We are looking forward to heading back!!

text:
1 Star is for the pretty building and setup. 

Aesthetically pleasing food hall but food is less than desired.  There are various food options but they're not tasty. 

Sanitation is an issue since only one person is handling food, prep, service, and cash! 

This place is off the beaten path so it takes awhile to find it. 

Ordered 
Char oysters decent 
Lump crab salad isn't lump crabmeat but shredded 
Vietnamese pork noodles are okay but sauce is salty 
Rotisserie chicken sandwich was greasy 
Quesadilla at Mexican place is extremely greasy and oily. Elotes were good though
Daily fish plate was decent 

Also we came around 8 and there was one place that hasn't finish prepping for dinner yet. It closes at 11! 

Don't waste your time and $ here. I wouldn't recommend it.

text: Went for brunch with my Mother and 1 1/2 year old little girl.  The hostess said it would be a 20 minute wait, after 40 minutes, (I was giving them the benefit of the doubt) I went and checked in and the hostess said we were next, after 10 minutes more we left without brunch...  Nope, will not return, menu is strange anyways.

text:
This was a great find!
We came Sunday night as a party of 5 and everyone loved what they ate. You get a significant amount of food for a reasonable price. The nachos, horchata and desserts (3 Leche cake and Churros) were group favorites. I will definitely be coming back!

text: Had breakfast this morning. This is such a cool setting. Love the industrial/rustic vibe. Coffee is very good. Eggs benny was mediocre. They use a weird mustard sauce instead of hollandaise. The bacon is good. Server was super friendly but painfully slow.
name: Erin

text: First time at The Eastern Peak. We've passed this many times and after a fun night out decided to stop. The food was good and came out quickly (although it was a Monday night so not a busy night), and Iris, our server, was very pleasant.
name: Naomi

text:
There's a general lack of hospitality, a dose of "I'm too busy" and the general malaise of a high end franchise. 

It compares nothing to Las Vegas Stripsteak whom the curators aided in this spot. 

So foie gras is on the appetizer menu, but not available as an add on for a steak? Excuse me? After the bar waitress verified with the chef she realized she was in error. My rib cap came out with the foie it needed. 

I think this is a case of people being undervalued and managers choosing the wrong people. Maybe the wages aren't good enough to keep the service as par as Vegas or other locations.

text: This is quite easily my favorite spot to get a burrito in Brentwood. I visit regularly. This spot offers a wide selection of ingredients and an authentic taste. However, yesterday my food was NOT good. The chicken in my burrito was so over cooked that it tasted as if I were eating rubber. $6.54 for ONLY a 5-6 bite burrito, no chips or beverage, that was the texture of rubber was not satisfying by any means. I never mind paying the higher than average prices at Chile Burrito because the food is usually more than worth it. This time it was not.
name: Tay

text:
I'm not from Philly, so I can't say what is real amazing cheese steak, but Cleavers is good! The portions are huge and they have plain cheese steaks and unique cheese steaks. If you work downtown, I'd say this is a great option is you're craving a cheese steak. There is also plenty of seating on their 2nd floor and a good variety of beer options. 

Great place to hang out after work!.
name: Ina

text: After a long day of furniture shopping with my family we stopped here for dinner. The best choice we have ever made! Super friendly and welcoming staff. Our waitress was amazing and super helpful when it came to suggestions. If there are any Corona Light beer fans out there, try the Almaza beer. You'll be very happy. The hummus was great and was a perfect size for a snack. As my entrée I had the Lamb Kifta plate. Very delicious! Always great to go out of your comfort zone. I'll try the Lamb Kifta sandwich next. I'll definitely be coming back!
name: Kandice

text: This has become my fav eatery in Tucson.  Cool atmosphere, great food and the drinks!  You must try their gin ramos on a warm evening!
name: Lee

text: Has cult following for good reason. Have been coming for many years. Always great and consistent. Frankie is wonderful. Italian cash only. Reservation on weekends.
name: Frank

text:
So this place makes me wonder if restaurants just want to churn and burn rather than pay attention to the details.

I arrived before my friend and I wanted to order a cocktail while I waited. When I asked the server if she had tasted one of the specialty cocktails, she said she hadn't. I told her to bring it for me anyway. I had asked for a blood orange limoncello drink, but she brought me just a limoncello martini. I like both so I didn't send it back. Besides, my friend arrived and I was anxious to catch up on all of our holiday stories. My friend ordered a glass of wine only to be told that the particular wine was out of stock and would she like to try another? My friend asked the cost of the alternate and was told "$9? $9.50?". The server never made an attempt to confirm the cost - just stood there with a quizzical look on her face. (I was then beginning to think that this wasn't going to end well...keep reading).

We ordered the antipasto plate to share and it was delicious. However, our entrees were delivered way too early and we then had to get creative with the table real estate to accommodate all of the plates. Poorly timed food is a peeve of mine. Just pay attention...it's not that difficult. We kept the antipasto on the table to nibble on after our entrees. Thankfully we did, because my veal parmigiana was pounded so thin, that all I got in each bite was a mouthful of overdone breading and a shoe leather shaving of veal. I had time to balance my checkbook in the time it took to finish chewing the first bite. 

My friend and I finished the antipasto plate (me without a knife since the busser took mine in his haste to clear our table. We opted to order dessert (both of us being creme brûlée fans). Our server delivered the plates with crocks of brûlée and a squeeze of "whipped cream" on the plate underneath. The sad slice of strawberry that was added as a garnish to my friend's plate should have never been allowed out of the kitchen. She and I both recognized the familiar oily taste of Cool Whip, after tasting the "whipped cream".  Hmmmm. Then I  looked at the crock of brûlée and realized that I had seen it before - in the freezer section of my local Target store! (See photos below) After cracking the crystallized sugar top, the center of the creme brûlée was fridge-cold. No bueno. The server came to check on us and when we asked if they made the desserts in house, she assured us they were.  I didn't have the heart to challenge her, because I'm sure she was just trained to say yes. When she asked if the desserts were ok, I gave her a clear "no" and she removed them from our check. 

The restaurant was open until 10pm and the crew was very clear at 9:20pm that we were in the way and stopping them from "leaving early". We left soon after (and well before 10). I will not be returning anytime soon. The company was wonderful, but the food was mediocre. Our server Katy was sweet - but the rest of the experience was "meh" at best.
name: Beth

text: The sandwiches are always good and the service is friendly...BUT....clean the freaking tables...PAAA...LEASE...every time I come in the staff is standing around...if ya got time to lean...ya got time to clean!!!
name: Flip

text: Had the pleasure of brunching here a couple weeks ago while in Nashville. The restaurant is in what looks to have been a house, very cute decor and setting. The service was great and so was the food. Nice strong bourbon cocktails as well. I had the vegetable plate which included a tasty af portion of grits along with other delicious and inventive veggies. Friends loved their shrimp and grits and the breakfast plate was a nice big portion of yummy bacon and other fixings. A little more quiet of a spot that my usual haunts but defs worth checking out for the food and drinks.
name: Noemi

text:
I expected this to have great reviews and the reviews didn't let me down!

Came here for a Saturday brunch with a friend and we're met with smiling friendly faces by the staff and escorted to the outside deck area which had an amazing ambience and background noise of a trickling fountain. The lighting is really cool and the table decor is fresh and clean.

Our server, Nick, was very sweet and attentive. The brunch menu was delightful because it encompassed a lot of different flavor profiles and the drink specials were great but we didn't order any.

I ordered the quiche which surprisingly didn't have mushrooms in it! That would've made it one notch better! Since Kennett Square is the mushroom capital of the world! But it still had an amazing bond of ingredients and a lot of them inside of it! My friend ordered the salmon and she said that it was great! It was exactly what she wanted.

The salad that came on the side of my quiche was phenomenal! Arugula, candied walnuts, and golden raisins! It was really really amazing! And the quiche was served at a perfect temperature so the cheese was delectable. 

We also had the pleasure of Savona pizza at the party we attended the night before, five different ones! And the fig arugula and balsamic glaze pizza it was out of this world!

I can't stop talking about how yummy this food was!
name: Lea

text: Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Not bad for a quick meal. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. The service was off and the meal kinda followed that energy. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon.
name: User

text: Great local brew pub with excellent beer, good food and great service. Nice outdoor seating. Appreciate their commitment to quality, local ingredients.
name: Patty

text: Yummy! Great service and delicious food. Loved the shrimp pasta. I only wished I had saved some bread to wipe my bowl clean! That sweet potato ice cream sandwich tho! Loved the atmosphere of this restaurant as well. Very chill and inviting. If you make a trip to Nashville it's a great spot for a date or with a group of girlfriends...

text: I noticed the coffee shop was opened this morning for breakfast. I stopped in for coffee and was off put by the coffee shops attendant. Kim was hr name, I think. She seemed to think raising her voice and arguing with the kitchen was more important than helping me. I was off put by her disposition and frankly, she was rude and unprofessional. I went and was seated in the restaurant by the host who was gracious and kind. The food was perfect the service was fantastic. Forget coffee!
