text: That 'Return of the Mac' sandwich is the TRUTH. I was a skeptic, but again...I see my coworkers go to certain places and it sparks my interest. That is some amazing Mac n Cheese. It just melts in your mouth...it's so creamy and flavorful..and then to pair it with Texas Toast...OMG. To be quite honest, I know good and well I'm lactose intolerant, but my stomach apparently loved this stuff (as cheesy as it was) cuz I haven't had ONE single issue since eating it earlier today. Lol. If that doesn't convince you to go, I don't know what will.
name: Susan

text: Very disappointed with quality, flavor and doneness of steaks. Very sub-par cuts - steaks very tough.  Over cooked and tasted like it was broiled not cooked over open fire.   Was here 10 years ago and it was fantastic but no longer - other steak houses around are far superior and less expensive.
name: Gail

text: Should have known that The wobbling table was a bad sign . The fried chicken was greasy, salty and over cooked . The meatloaf tasted as if it had been recycled from a previous day and then nuked , like rubber . Truly dreadful experience.
name: Tom

text:
Good Mexican food with solid protein and tortilla chip execution. Salsas were hit or miss. Vegetables were undercooked. 

I ordered the Chicken Fajita Burrito. This came with a free starter of chips and salsa. The chips were thin, crisp, and fresh with pleasant notes of frying oil and corn. The salsa is very fresh. It's just the right balance of savory and bright. Note that it is a pureed blend. But I found the salsa still very much dippable. 

The burrito wrap was soft and chewy. It came with three salsas atop: green, queso, and red. I found the green salsa to be very grassy/herbal in an offputting way. 

The chicken in the burrito was well executed: tender and well seasoned. They chop it into very small strips. Unfortunately, the vegetables, particularly the green bell peppers, were undercooked. With the soft tortilla and tender chicken, the green bell peppers very much dominated the flavor and mouthfeel of the dish. 

There were some clear execution errors and inattention to flavor profile. However, overall the food was enjoyable and adequate, though not overly generous, in portion size.
name: Jack

text: Outstanding steak house. Amazing location great food. Superior wine list. Outstanding staff. A win win all around.
name: Raymond

text: Good bbq. Interesting sides. Authentic inside, full of the locals, and staff is almost entirely 20 year old girls. Sauces are very simple, no mopping or mustard based sauces, very little heat. Real FL BBQ. The Sweet potato side really sticks out, very tasty. Be sure to try it.
name: Frank

text: I love their menu; there are various coffee/smoothie options as well as homemade treats. Workers were friendly and fast. A great study spot--they got the wifi, ample seating and bathroom.
name: Katie

text: It looked better online than it did in person. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. A couple small things kept adding up. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Maybe other people have better luck here. Nice little spot, decent portions too. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean.
name: User

text: First time here and I only got some coffee drinks but I know I want to go back and try the food. I ordered several different lattes and coffees. The lattes were delicious. And the barista decorated the cups (which my husband noticed and loved) service was friendly and fast and the place is very cute inside. the food menu looks great so I cant wait to try a few different items and see how it is.
name: Theresa

text:
Rosie's!!!!! 
We usually go to Rosie's in Zionsville on my day off. 
It's so busy in the weekends, but we'll worth the wait. 
Today, Amouris was our server. We enjoyed conversing with her. 
The food: As usual - DELISH. 
I had Rosie's Special with bacon, potatoes and  a pancake for sharing of course. My egg whites were scrambed perfectly. The biscuits are  always fluffy as was the pancake. 
Hubs had the Fall Scramble -OMG! 
Quinoa, sweet potatoes, mushrooms and onions were tge base the base for the eggs. So good! 
I have to tell you, Rosie's has hands down THE best coffee! 
Let's not forget the sweets! Coconut Macaroons? Yes, please! Gooey Butter cookies? Don't mind if I do!
name: Erika

text: Went today and it was phenomenal !  3 staff people waited on our table. The outdoor covered patio is cute with a Victorian domed ceiling and windows rounded along the entire exterior !  The French toast is to die for and the tots brunch ( tater tots more like Japanese  potato croquette ) casserole is yum!l with peppers pesto and spicy sausage .
name: Ang

text: First time having frog legs. Amazing. Service was great and all the food was perfect.
name: Dave

text: I was on vacation in philadelphia so this is ZHE PLACE for a real Philly cheese steak . The stars was not for the food. I gave them  to the cashier, good customer service. Food was nasty nothing to compare with the real Philly cheese steak. Cheese look like cream cheese it was horrible
name: Ausanka

text: Burgers are always awesome! Had the buffalo chicken sandwich  so good! My favorite thing to come here for is the fried pickles  they are so good you must try! Fries are always fantastic as well.
name: Lauren

text: I came here with 4 friends and we all ordered different things. All of our coffee was marginal at best. The cold brew was see through and weak. I ordered the drip coffee and it was full of coffee grounds. The chicken on the chicken sandwich was 1/3 the size of the bun. On the positive side both the ham sandwich and the veggie burger were pretty good. This place is over priced and under delivers on quality.
name: Gary

text: First time here was on 5/10/2019 around 8:30pm and probably won't come back. We sat at the bar and it took forever for us to get acknowledged. Once we got a drink it took forever for one of the bartenders to take our order. I should mention the bar wasn't even full. There were several open chairs. We ordered tacos that were mediocre at best. We ordered the octopus, spicy tuna, pork belly, and pulled pork. The pulled pork was the best out of all 4. If service was better I might have considered going back but, the bartenders were too busy worrying about their friends.
name: Kasey

text:
Don't get me wrong, the burger was great. The service here just sucks. I walked in at about 4pm, with nobody in line. Ordered a bacon cheeseburger, fries, and a coke. With the restaurant almost vacant, and more employees sitting at tables than guests, it took almost 20 minutes for my order.

An order which cost $15.34, by the way. 

I almost walked out when I saw the prices, I regret not doing so. 

If the market supports those prices for a bacon cheeseburger and a 20 minute wait, so be it. But I'm not in that market anymore. 

I don't like writing bad reviews, but this is the 3rd time I've been to this location and have had to wait around forever for a grossly overpriced burger. I paid the same amount for a double double and fries at In-N-Out visiting California as I did for fries and a drink here.
name: Rob

text: was surprised that it was not a long wait. Good amount of food for the price. Had eggs, grits, ham and roast beef. Good portion of food. Food was good. Good customer service
name: Karen

text: Wow. Coffee is amazing. Atmosphere chill and relaxing. They have wifi. Ordered a caramel frappe that is crazy good. Also got greedy and had an almond donut which was amazing! They have outside seating on the side. Staff friendly and offer suggestions too. Will def come back...
name: Sha

text: I was really impressed with the food but it would have tasted so much better if the service itself were better. The cashier was short and seemed annoyed that I'd ask what they were most known for or what suggestions she could offer. A little bit of hospitality  along with my delicious $15 breakfast sandwich would be great.
name: Dan

text:
Morgan's has moved into a much better, much cleaner location!

This was my first time visiting their new location.  We were told by the lady at the cash register to seat ourselves wherever we wanted.  We chose a booth by the wall.  It had an outlet near it, and I was thinking that they would have something cool if they turned those outlets into USB hubs/outlet upgrades.  Then people would chill and charge at the same time while taking advantage of their free wifi.

Our server was nice and sassy.  You could tell she was comfortable working here.  Hubby and I both ordered unsweet iced tea (brewed, yes!!!!)  and the special of the day:  Chicken pot pie in a bread bowl.

Despite the entree containing TONS of peas, it was actually really good.  It was creamy and chickeny, so I didn't notice the peas as much (peas aren't my favorite, in case you couldn't tell).  It was a large portion of food, and I finished it in its entirety.

There is a new restaurant coming in next door any day now, so I would strongly suggest that they upgrade those outlets!
name: Erin

text: This is a great Chick-til-a normally. Great service and workers usually. But tonight there was this girl worker and she just completely messed my order up. She didn't put in three of the frys I ordered and gave me to wrong sized salad and no straws. Then when I went to go get the forgotten things she took long to get them and I could hear her and her coworkers slacking off and saying bad things about me and how she "knew I was lying". This made me very mad. Also sometimes this Chick-fil-a's food isn't even that good. Not impressed.
name: Saroya

text: Not a really big selection but if you want deep fried chicken this is the place to go
name: Niki

text:
Best food I've had in a long time.  My wife and I tried the pork satay, homemade sausage, one of the salads and the seafood hotpot.  Everything came out somewhat fast and was super delicious.  I could really tell the ladies cooking really enjoy what they do.

We then tried the poached banana and the coconut pudding for dessert. Both were a pleasant treat and a good way to end the meal.  Otherwise, service was great and the place was clean.  We'll be going back because there's a lot more we really wanna try.
name: Sean

text: Great restaurant!!!  Good selection of gluten free options.  I really like the atmosphere.  You can eat inside or outside. Nice view too as your on the second floor.    I had a burger and my husband had a steak. Both very good.  We will definitely be going back.   Next time I'll be saving room for the gluten free chocolate cake
name: Mary

text:
We are back for the first time this year.
Lorenza ordered the Sashimi/Tempura lunch and I order the Sashimi lunch with grilled squid appetizer. 
We love the atmosphere. The Japanese waitresses have been here for decades and the booths have the feeling of old Japan. 

Oi Shi Ney.
name: WILLIAM

text:
If you're looking for excellent service, incredibly tasty mexican food, and a fun atmosphere, you've found the right place. At El Taco, you'll be welcomed by a well-kept, clean restaurant with both indoor and outdoor seating and kind employees who want to serve you. The menu itself is expansive with a wide variety of options. As a vegetarian, I am usually hesitant to eat at restaurants that serve lots of meat dishes, but at El Taco, their sweet potato protein is more than enough to keep you satisfied. Like any great Mexican restaurant, they also have a long list of salsas, organized by heat, which I hope to explore further when I visit next. Their burrito bowls are also next level, having the bowl be made out of a tortilla shell. This made my experience all the more delicious as the crispy bowl served as an extra crunch when I so desired. After the meal, I was full, satisfied, yet I didn't feel gross after eating it like I do at many other Mexican restaurants.

Would recommend El Taco to anyone looking for a great meal and a better experience. Will absolutely be placing El Taco on my list of restaurants I eat at regularly.
name: Albert

text:
Nippon Tei used to be my go-to sushi restaurant.  EMPHASIS on SUSHI! With the new year however, they have completely changed their menu.  Basically, there are VERY FEW sushi choices.  The menu has been replaced with entree type dinners. In fact, menu is so different I wonder if it's under new ownership?  Though still Asian, it now longer has sushi at the heart of the menu (a very big disappointment).

3 stars for the 2 spicy tuna rolls that were available..plus, fairly slow service for a weeknight with restaurant half empty.  They were a-OK.
name: Tina

text: The store was nice and there was a line. I got my kids donuts for the first day of school, four donuts for them. The next day two donuts were still in the bag. The kids said they didn't like them so I haven't been back
name: Victoria

text: I've been to Pub N' Sub probably close to 10 times and it's never disappointed. I always go on Monday for their happy hour where pizza is half off if you eat it there. Depending on how many toppings you select, you can get a large pizza for barely above $10. The pizza is also delicious! It's sometimes pretty greasy but I've always enjoyed it. I've ordered a pizza with garlic on and it came with whole cloves are garlic, which I had never seen before. Whether it's a simple pepperoni or a combination pizza, it's bound to be delicious.
name: Eric

text:
A few friends and I stopped in for drinks on a Friday in December.  The interior is very well decorated and when its warm their outside patio is awesome.  I had always wanted to try their sushi and I did get a chance to have indulge on this trip.  I was pleasantly surprised at how GOOD it was!  I'm a bit of a sushi snob but the two rolls we ordered were top notch.  I will have to come back and try the Sashimi because that's the only real way to judge how good the fish is.  

The bartenders were all very good EXCEPT for one.  Our group was sitting at a table in the bar area and knocked (2) glasses off of the table.  It was a mistake and no one was intoxicated.  She handled this accident about as bad as humanly possible.  Hopefully she can improve on her people skills because they are non existent.
name: Zach

text: Had brunch here over the weekend and it was kind of a mixed bag. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. Not a bad stop, just not one I'm rushing to repeat. Food was fresh and service was quick. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.
name: User

text: One of those meals where nothing is exactly wrong but you're not excited either. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. It was decent, just a little uneven. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable.
name: User

text: NOT authentic Chinese cooking as they stated! All the dishes I ordered were very typical Sichuan food, and without exception they all failed!
name: Rachel

text: Super cool place super nice staff sub par coffee .   I kinda expected a place with such a cool set up to have more superb coffee.  I had an americano that was on par with gas station coffee.  It seemed like a busy place but for the coffee connoisseur this is not the place.
name: Lance

text:
Having popped in here for a Yelp event and enjoyed what was offered, I'm looking forward to having a full-on meal here this year, maybe even with my family in tow. Jury is still out though because we have teenagers. Might just be me and my husband.
On the evening of the event the restaurant was packed, and I mean packed! And to be clear, this was regular traffic, not Yelp event traffic. We were all the way sequestered in the back. And because it was so full, it was really loud. I feel that it would be rather difficult to hold conversations at your table when it's packed like that. 
As Yelpers we were offered margaritas and a little pork belly street taco. Margarita was absolutely delicious, but I'm vegetarian, so didn't partake of the pork belly. Other folks were reaching for more, so they were obviously pretty tasty. 
While in there, I scanned a menu and noticed they offer a menu of items that sound scrumptious. I also noticed the prices, which is why I'll probably return without the kids. Or we might head down and try out their brunch instead to keep the family budget tight.
If you go, be sure to check out the graffiti-inspired decor in the restroom area. It was super cool.
name: Kristie

text: Excellent food. Juicy and flavorful chicken parm! Fried ravioli was good. Kids tenders and fries were fried perfectly. Will be back for sure!
name: Brian

text:
I stayed here on 7/16/2018. After a 3 day Vacation in Las Vegas. We decided to be adventurous and drive back home (Sacramento) 95 North. By the time we made it to Reno it was getting dark so we decided to stay in for the night. We went on Hotwire and liked the prices here. After a long ride we were ready to go freshen up and do a little gambling. We checked in with no problem. When we got to our room we went in and there was a cot in the room that looked like someone just did slept in it, with a used towel with suspect stains on it . We didn't ask for a cot. Certainly one that's been slept on. 

  So we took a picture and went back down to check-in.  When we finally got to the counter. We told the Customer Service Rep. About the disheveled cot in the room with the suspect stains on it. His reply was ," What? You dont want the cot?." 


So we get another room. As soon as we get off the elevator we smell smoke, smoke, smoke ( we originally had a non- smoking room). I will admit the room was clean. The linen was clean ( I  know because I always do a bedbug check). The bed was very comfortable. The view from the new room was awesome. I did enjoy that. For the view, comfortable bed, and the fact I won $170 ( I only put $20 in the machine ) they get 3 stars.
name: Tomeka

text: Best service and the best Mexican food in Tampa. Everyone there is always so friendly and Maria is the best! You can't go wrong with anything on the menu.
name: Fadi

text: You can tell they care about customer experience here. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. A very pleasant experience. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon.
name: User

text: Love their Bloody Marys and sitting at the bar! It's always pretty packed weekend mornings but there's a lull around 1pm when the brunch crowd rotates out.
name: Jen

text: I have been having pizza hut pizza for over 25 years. This has been the absolute worst experience I have ever had. I don't know who I was speaking on the phone with tonight but he was so disrespectful All I did was ask him a simple question and he was so disrespectful to me that I was just furious at the way he responded to a customer just axing a question. Who has been eating Pizza Hut before he was born. I will absolutelyOrder from this establishment ever in life. I will definitely go to google I will definitely go to your guys personal website. I will post negative responses every week to every major website. Hopefully no one will ever eat or order from this establishment with races disrespectful people that work there. I was on Pizza Hut website and they said that they were open for delivery when I placed my order. But it said something went wrong. So I called the store to ask them what happen with my order.
name: Mike

text:
First time trying this place. Initial thoughts were that we liked it was a locally owned place and it was pretty easy to get to from our house. We were able to park in front but I saw a sign for additional parking. 
The inside decor was outdated but that's okay. We ordered an appetizer which was essentially cheese balls with a little kick. I'm glad we ordered an appetizer because it took quite a bit to get the food. We saw a note on the menu that talked about the wait for food due to freshness so that's why we ordered an appetizer. I ordered the burger with fried pickles while my husband ordered a veggie burger with bleu cheese crumbles. While the fries fell short of expectations, the burgers were delicious. My husband commented that he could tell the bleu cheese crumbles were fresh because of the sharpness. Overall, we would visit again.
name: Jessica

text: Me and my good friend are regulars here and let me tell you they hook it up!! Only pho thats worth the money, you'll pay more for less elsewhere, and it doesnt compare in the least. Ive now been coming here for a whole year and I refuse to go anywhere else! Definitely reccomemd having an empty stomach before coming in, and get the fried spring rolls!!
name: Allison

text: I've been eating at New Delhi for 24 years. It's always been my goto in Philly for decent Indian food. They have a great variety and the restaurant is clean and fairly modern. Unfortunately dessert like ice vream is no longer included with the buffet.
name: Emily

text:
This particular restaurant has a nice atmosphere and is quite comfortable. 

The food was well prepared and delicious. Nice ingredients and flavor. Servings are moderate, however the Pad Thai is the smallest serving size I have ever received in a Thai restaurant, in this country or in Thailand. 

The sequencing and timing of the food coming out of the kitchen was poor, totally confused and entirely syncopated. We mentioned it to our servers which didn't seem to make any difference. The fault most likely lies with the management and kitchen staff. There doesn't seem to be a prescribed plan of how to sequence the food service. We had ordered food for six. Several salades, pad thai, several curies and the spicy eggplant.  The first items to arrive at the table were the pad thai. Perhaps 5 minutes later followed by the curry, then in another 5 minutes the salad and in another 5 minutes the eggplant. 

The food as I mentioned was great. The service was average to poor. The atmosphere was nice. A tricky one to rate.
name: Coleman

text: Being from Chicago, I was highly disappointed in the pizza. First of all, I can tell that the crust was frozen, and the pizza arrived about 10 minutes after ordering. I gave this place a second chance, and the same outcome the second time. Actually, I had stomach problems both times after eating the pizza. You have to realize that this is not an Italian restaurant; it's Greek. Stick with the Gyros sandwich or not in-house made desserts. You will still wind up with a mediocre dining experience. Realize that you are in Clearwater Beach; a tourist area not frequented by locals. Need I say more?
name: Wayne

text:
Great service and diverse food choices. We did the happy hour and sat by the sushi bar; best location to watch the sushi preparation. 

We ordered all but one happy hour dishes; why not, it's only $6 per plate and you get a normal size order. Will definitely be back!
name: Jo

text:
Open seating, so meet new peeps. Smells drive me to eat.... 
when I look in most of the kitchen areas you'll see Hispanics working. Now that's different. 
Try new things ppl. The world is bigger than your backyard
name: Dinah

text: The menu is dreamy..!!!try the stuffed long hots with a glass of pinot gri....perfection....the menu is fantastic..my date got the carribean salad...it's just a great place...great friendly  bar staff...the are attentive...and nice....it's just great....
name: John

text: I keep trying to like this place. I like the food a lot. And the free frozen yogurt is a nice touch. Unfortunately the service ruins it for me. Came in 45 min before closing (8:15pm) and the girl behind the counter asked if it was ok if we took our food to go since they were closing soon. I told her I'd prefer to dine in since I had plans to go elsewhere after dinner. She obliged my request...as long as I didn't "hang out for a while." While waiting for my food, she convinced the family who came in 10ish min after me that they would have to eat outside since they were closing in 30 min. The girl behind the counter drank her soda while staring at the three parties finishing up at 8:45. I would give the service zero stars if I could. I couldn't get out of there fast enough.
name: Jen

text: My fiancé and our families came to dinner and ordered and the waitress took our order but completely messed it up!! My dads plate didn't come and when my food came I found a long piece of hair in my steak. I told my waitress and she stated the manager Chris would be over. It took Chris 25 minutes to come but once he did he stated he would re make my meal. He offered in the meantime to bring me some appetizers to munch on. He was very nice. I'm just irritated because I'm hungry and pregnant!! The piece of hair was SO LONG...I almost threw up. The lights in here are so dim....can barely see anything! Glad I caught it..
name: Rene

text: I actually really really love this casino- It's beautiful and mostly clean and most of the people are super friendly. And a special shout out to Tony the valet. However, I use a walker and the doors to enter and exit the casino are very heavy. I have spoken to the administration at Parks casino several times and they have told me that the security guards that stand in front of the door are supposed to open the door for handicap people. However, when I am leaving, they never do. Sometimes they are busy carding people and I understand that. But the last three times I have exited no one helped me at all with the door. Here's a picture of them as I'm trying to exit the door. Notice- they are not busy at all. What do I have to do to make this place more handicapped friendly? Why isn't there a handicap door that we can push a button and the door will open for us, Because obviously the current handicap door plan is not working.
name: Karen

text: Eating tacos in a fancy place is kind of an oxymoron. It just doesn't work. That's precisely why this place works. It's eclectic, very homey like in abuelas kitchen, super friendly service and the tacos were too legit to quit. The price is just right. I love the bullfight posters and super cold Jarritos in the fridge and they offer $1 fresh made beverages as well. Can't go wrong. Good for a weekday lunch since they're not open late or on the weekend.
name: Mark

text: Went with family on a Sunday and it was louder than I expected. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. Food was fresh and service was quick. You can tell they care about customer experience here. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Would absolutely visit again. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean.
name: User

text: Very disappointed..had the Italian beef sandwich. Beef tasted old..not spoiled but old. Anyone knows their beef..knows what i mean. Guess I'll have to keep driving to Gallatin, Tn to Campiones of Chicago. They never disappoint on their beef sandwiches..bit of a drive, but worth it!!
name: Patty

text: Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Would probably stop in again if nearby. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Nice little spot, decent portions too. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Food was fresh and service was quick. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Nice little spot, decent portions too. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Food was fresh and service was quick.
name: User

text: Not sure why the low average score. First time I've ever been to Wong's and I was very surprised at the service. The staff is excellent. The sushi was on point, especially the fried varieties. Very underrated Mongolian grill style food makes up for the otherwise medium to low tier variety of food. Wong's buffet specializes in quality over quantity. Definitely coming back.
name: Drew

text: I ordered a large pizza for delivery and the food came at a timely fashion and is always good but i can't help but complain about the girl who took our order. She was very rude and sounded like she hated her job. For a great pizza place i would hate to have someone so mean answering the phone. Just because you hate your job, you don't have to have such an attitude and take it out on the customer.
name: Jamie

text:
I will start this review by naming the positive aspects of our experience here: the ice cream at the end was amazing. That's literally all there is to say that is positive.

Where to even start. Upon arrival, we were given a menu and attempted to ask a few question and get some suggestions from our server. He was completely disinterested and did not want to even give us the time of day. Pretty much just told us to read the descriptions. If an employee isn't excited about the restaurant, I am certainly not going to be. After ordering, we had to ask him to bring us the salad and bread that came with our meal. It was clear he would not have brought them if we wouldn't have said something. I think he was hoping we missed that part of the menu?? Once the food arrived (which was mediocre at best), our server never came back. Once he finally came back, we were excited to order another cocktail but were instead greeted with a check. Did not ask about our meal or even say thank you. Just set them down then left. (Side note: the house wine is boxed Franzia. I know house wine is not supposed to be top of the line but I also thought I was going to a well respected restaurant, not a frat house. How tacky)

We paid and decided to move to the bar. Should have known that this experience wouldn't be any better. We walked to the bar and were met with a confused look by the bartender. We asked if we could sit down and order some after-dinner drinks. He said "sure" and walked away. We sat there for another 15 minutes and he never came back so we finally just left. 

To the Old Spaghetti Factory, I am so sorry that we had the nerve to inconvenience you with our service!!! Never. Again.
name: Kelsie

text: Visitor from out of town. Exceeded all expectations that I had read. Service was great and chefs were engaging. Crab & lobster bisque was unreal, seasonal fish was delicious, and scallops melted. Enjoy!
name: Mike

text: Wonderful breakfast spot! Long long, but worth the wait!!! The restaurant is beautiful, milk & honey latte is heavenly & the food was perfect. I had the chicken & waffles. Definitely recommend getting the biscuit as an appetizer!
name: Melissa

text: So so so good!! I am so glad there is finally a place that has biscuits with turkey sausage gravy since I can't eat pork.  Everything we ate was delicious and fast.  Our picky 4 year old even drank the healthy juices!  I would eat here again and again!!
name: Mieke

text: We came last night. It took awhile to be seated at the door, so we went and sat at the bar. The bartender did say she would be with us. But we were sitting for awhile with no menu and no drink. We left and went to millers ale house and we had a way better experience
name: Kelsie

text: You really can't go wrong at Glory Days. Although not a culinary masterpiece, it definitely fills the void of local joint. You can watch sports here, lots of TVs and a speaker at each table to hear. Our faves are the blueberry lemonade, mac and cheese burger, strawberry salmon salad (I substitute chicken) and the flatbreads. I want to like their chicken and waffles more but it was just ok, with not a ton of flavor. Good place for a quick meal. Servers are friendly and attentive.
name: Meredith

text: Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. Anyway, it looked better online than it did in person. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. The food was good and the service was easygoing. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait.
name: User

text: Great coffee, food and ambiance. Some may be turned off by the prices, but quality isn't cheap.
name: Joseph

text: Not sure why this place has such split reviews, but my experience was mostly fine. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. This feels like a place where your order choice matters a lot. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed.
name: User

text:
Parking is tough and there are very few tables. It was crowded with a wait when I was there. However the wait staff were nice and (for most of the time) attentive. 

A basic diner breakfast. Would return.
name: Bobby

text: The only thing better than the food was the service.   Andy was awesome!. We had the tableside guacamole ,it was the best.
name: Sondra

text: My boyfriend and I found ourselves here through recommendation from a local friend. It's a cute, small, romantic restaurant that wasn't too far from where we were staying. After a long day of work and traveling, this was the perfect place to unwind and catch up. Our server was very accommodating and helped us find seating where our luggages weren't in the way. We started with some garlic bread and a glass of wine each. One order of garlic bread was definitely enough for the both of us. I ordered the pan-seared gnocchi and he ordered the spaghetti and meatballs. My dish was small enough for one person and I loved the sauce that topped the gnocchi. His dish was so large, we ended up having to take the leftovers home with us. The meatballs were a generous size and there was the right amount of seasoning. This spot is perfect for dates nights and small groups.
name: Krystle

text: I simply love this spot! You can't go wrong with the gumbo, red beans, butter beans, ribeye, fried jumbo shrimp, fried catfish, smothered pork chops, shucks... I haven't tasted anything that I didn't love yet. The only issue that I have is although the gumbo price is quite reasonable, the way they "pick through" the ingredients in the gumbo and keep dropping the meat and putting more juice in your container drives me batty! If you pick it up, put it in my bowl! Other than that I recommend Broad & Banks highly!
name: Juleta

text:
I've come here for years and absolutely love it everytime. It is a very family friendly chain, so if you are looking for a more sophisticated outing - this isn't your place. There will absolutely be kids here. 

I've always loved it, and it was nice to bring my new daughter here because I felt perfectly comfortable bringing a baby as the place was filled with kids. The food is great. The burgers are all great. If you get fries, make them garlic Parmesan fries. Freckled lemonade is always a favorite as is their shakes and jalapeño coins. 

If you are looking for a spectacular outing, it's a family friendly chain. You get what you should expect. If you're bringing kids, you will have a wonderful time! Service is fantastic. I don't think she's there anymore, but my favorite server was Fancy. The fact I remember her years and years later is a testament to what awesome service she provided.
name: Jessica

text: Ended up here pretty late, maybe around 9:30, because everything else nearby had a wait. Food was fresh and service was quick. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Would absolutely visit again. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Would probably stop in again if nearby.
name: User

text:
Came here while in New Orleans to celebrate my birthday with my parents and had a really lovely time. We came here because of the incredible reputation and we were not disappointed. 

We got here a little early but we're seated right away. This is definitely a place to dress up for! Business casual, with nice dresses and men in jackets. It was nice to see everyone in the restaurant showing respect for the establishment. For my birthday, they had balloons on the table which was a really sweet touch. 

I started with a bourbon and lemon drink which was yummy, and then switched to wine which was also tasty. 

For starters, we had the crawfish gnocchi, the sweet tea pork belly, and the commanders salad. There is also plenty of fresh soft bread on the table! The pork belly was the highlight for me- it was so complex and tender. 

For dinner I had the filet and my dad had the tuna so I got to try both. They were both good. My steak was maybe a tiny bit underdone for my taste, but still super tender and flavorful.  The tuna was also yummy, wish there had been even more sauce! 

For dessert, we had the bread pudding soufflé. It was awesome how they took a heavy dessert and elevated it to something light and decadent. And I couldn't get enough of the whiskey cream  they brought out candles and a chef's hat as well. 

Our server Lorenzo was a character- he had been there for a long time and was delightful. 

Would definitely come back!
name: Lyssa

text:
Went to Demitris on the water several times previously. Always had great food and great service.
However last night it took nearly 2 hours for our meal. 
We had 4 people in our party, but only 2 at a time was served. So while 2 were waiting for food, the other two were eating.
By the time the other two got their food, the first two were finished.
One steak was way under cooked and the other tough as leather..
By the time one of party got their steak, everyone else was finished.
We spoke to the manager who was rude and unsympathetic....
I guess the days of "satisfaction guaranteed " are long over....
I guess in short... you got a 50/50 chance at Demitris..
name: Kenny

text:
Nashville is a foodie lovers dream!! If you are visiting I highly suggest you stop at Bartaco. It's super trendy and nautical themed. They do not take reservations, but you can call ahead 30 minutes and put yourself on a waitlist. They also have free parking around back! 

We arrived on Monday around 5:30 and were seated and greeted by our server right away. She was very helpful with explaining the menu items and making recommendations. One thing I didn't like about the menus was the fact that they didn't tell you what all game with that item. For example the chicken pastor came with small chunks of pineapple, but it doesn't say that on the menu. It just says chicken pastor. I'm very detail oriented and I like knowing what all comes on my entree. When you know you want to order you mark it on a sheet and place it on the clip for the server to see and they will come right over to pick it up. Chips and salsa are not freebies here, but they do have a nice variety of salsa for you at the tables. 

They do not serve Pepsi products here. Which is something my mom always gets when we go out to dinner. She ended up getting sweet tea and I ordered a ginger mint tea. I knew they were going to be freshly made, since all of the alcoholic beverages were hand crafted using real fruit. I didn't expect the tea to come up in a giant carafe. The tea's were $3.50 each and for as many glasses as I poured it was well worth it. They even give you to go cups to take some home. I never had ginger mint tea before and it was extremely refreshing! I highly recommend that one. 

For our meals - mom ordered the cauliflower bowl and I ordered the duck taco and chicken pastor (dark meat). The cauliflower bowl comes with bell peppers, two scoops of brown rice, roasted cauliflower, onion and a special sauce (a little spicy). She loved it and it was a recommendation from our waitress. I added a side of diced pineapple with lime juice (highly recommend adding the lime juice). The duck taco came topped with white onion and was a little on the tough side. None the less it was still very flavorful. The chicken pastor was a little on the spicy side, but cooked to perfection. These tacos are tiny, so order accordingly. Overall, I was very happy with my first Bartaco experience and wish we could get one of these restaurants up in Pittsburgh!
name: Lacey

text: This was a delivery order on a night when I really did not want to cook. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. For a busy night they handled it okay. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. Ordered a few things and liked most of it.
name: User

text:
Good food and great selection.  Those who read my reviews know that I focus a lot on vegetarian options and the willingness of a place to adjust menu items, within reason.  Cafe Natasha has a vegetarian section on the menu and they are always happy to answer questions.  The staff is friendly but with a bit of the typical Persian edge.  It sometimes come across as passive-aggressive, but is just he nature of the culture and is often misunderstood by some guests.  

There were 5 of us for this visit and we mentioned that we needed three separate checks.  I think the server forgot this and brought one check, which we asked her to split.  She did so without hesitation, but when she returned, she mentioned that she removed the 18% gratuity since we split the check.  The original one she brought had the gratuity added in.  This confused us since there were only 5 of us. But a good example of the personality trait referred to earlier.

I had the kookoo sabzi which was light and fluffy and came with eggplant casserole which was delicious.  My favourite items here are the pomegranate yogurt and the spinach yogurt dips.  The vegetarian cabbage rolls are also very good.  And ending with persian icecream is always a nice treat.

There is also a great selection of spirits, some that you don't typically find in St Louis, as well as a good selection of things from local distilleries.  Overall a great place for a nice dinner.  We eat here every two weeks or so.  The dining room can be a bit noisy, so be prepared for that.  The reason for the four stars, rather than the five, is they consistently try to sit groups of 5 at a table for 4 with a chair at the end which is a personal pet peeve of mine.  It is not comfortable for 5 people to eat this way and they always seem disagreeable to doing this, even though I always make reservations for 5 people.

Nevertheless a good place with good food, highly recommended.
name: Shaun

text: I'm not sure why this restaurant gets good reviews. I've been coming to NOLA for years and the food was mediocre at best. Don't order the seafood special - the fish was rubbery which didn't seem to bother the waiter. And they ran out of Bloody Mary mix so we couldn't even get a drink. Look elsewhere for good creole food.
name: Lynda

text: Amazing hookah spot. I visit this place twice a week for a good hang out and happy hour spot. The owner is very nice and the waitress are amazing also. The cook make some good wings, please try them. Overall great place.
name: Daqueisha

text: I went there today with my friend, the foods are taste so good, I really like the steak and the fries alot, the steak is soft enough for my bad terth to bit LoL, and the sauce that their use on the fries is super tasty , also,  the staffs here are very sweet, friendly , the service is excellent! We will definitely come back !
name: QIwen

text: I've been to throw location a few times. This is a family friendly restaurant. The service was just okay today. The food was good as usual. I had a milkshake with whip cream and a cherry. He only thing different was when the cashier handed me my milkshake and just looked at me. I had to blink a few times because I normally get a thank you, then I say thank you and they end it with my pleasure! I love that kind touch when I go to Chick Fil a. This day I received a you are welcome after I said thank you. Other than that it was your typical Chick Fil a experience.
name: Terra

text:
I have been dying to try this restaurant ever since my husband and I were strolling around Safety Harbor one afternoon and saw it.  We finally made it there Thursday night. We arrived a bit before 6PM, and it was already hopping. There were a few tables open and we got a seat right away.  We placed our order for our meal around 6:10.   My husband got a soup to start and it arrived within minutes of ordering it.  But then things went down hill. 

We kept waiting and waiting for our dinner to arrive.  Worse, we noticed that people who arrived 30 minutes after us were getting their meals and yet we sat with nothing. The waiter came and told us our meals would be up next, and yet we watched as three more tables of people who came well after us got their meals.  

Eventually at 7Pm we received our meals.  The waiter apologized for how long it took, joking we must be starving.  I honestly think that he forgot to put our order in and that when he came to tell us we were up next, is when he actually put it in, because that is the only thing that makes sense.

I had ordered the fried chicken with mashed potatoes and collard greens. My husband got meatloaf with mashed potatoes and asparagus.  Everything tasted good.  We were offered dessert and with the promise it would be right out, we ordered the tuxedo mousse cake.  I thought it looked pretty but it wasn't something I would order again.  

The waiter brought our check and then said "I bought your ice tea for you since you had to wait so long for your meal."  We almost burst out laughing, but waited until he left to do so.  Honestly, that was ridiculous.  He clearly forgot to put our order in.  He should have just been honest, and he should have comped the dessert, or the two glasses of wine, but iced tea! C'mon!

So overall the food was good, but I am not certain of the service. The waiter was super nice, and attentive, but the whole issue with our food, and a comped iced tea, left me unsure about going back.
name: M

text: I love the open air concept of this restaurant, it fits in with trendy St Pere. The prices are pretty economical for what you're getting. Don't expect authenticity though as the food is more commercialized Mexican similar to a Moes or Chipotle. We ordered the chicken street tacos, chicken quesadilla and pork carnitas street tacos. Our food was edible but lacked flavor, we needed an abundance of salt and sauces. I mean the food isn't awful but it's not great either. If you are looking for authentic Mexican you'll be disappointed, if you go in thinking this place is like Moe's flavor then you'll enjoy it.
name: Vanessa

text: Great atmosphere, great food!! A really fun place to watch sports events or to have an event.
name: Karla

text: Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. So yeah, dessert was weirdly the highlight, which i wasn't expecting at all. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. maybe I just came on an off day.
name: User

text: Another amazing dinner here.. second time in one week. I got souvlaki with tzatziki sauce and grilled chicken. For a second I thought I was in greece... maybe at mykonos island. It was awesome. Can't wait to try their whole menu, it seems one thing is better than the other!!
name: Eleni

text:
I visited on Sunday evening. A small but very quaint restaurant. Their service was very fast, unlike some of the reviews on here previously. 

From their expansive menu, we ordered the Oilers Roll, Dragon Eye Salmon Roll, Spicy Tuna Roll, Chicken Karaage, Edmonton Roll, and Blazing Unagi Roll. Everything was decent taste-wise and portions were satisfactory. 

Prices were a bit higher than some of the other sushi shops, but not outrageous. I will most likely be back to sample some of the other menu items (from their list of hundreds).
name: Peter

text: Walking in the door the whole place smelled like smoke so this was a good sign.  I had the brisket with slaw and baked beans.  I ordered MOIST brisket (the person at the register seemed to understand what I was talking about, so this was another good sign).  I also got slaw and baked beans.  The brisket was OK.  Definitely smokey with a decent amount of fat.  The sides weren't too memorable.  I give this place 4 stars because relative to other places in the area, it is one of the few that seems to actually smoke their meat.  It would probably get 2 stars if I was in texas.  Still, not a bad option given the choices you have in the area.  I'll also have to try the pork.
name: E

text:
Excellent crispy fried chicken and baked beans. I really enjoyed it. Came out fast, hot and cooked to perfection! Baked beans are sweet and have a nice flavor. The mash was not the best and the gravy ok, hence the 4 star rating. 
I'll be back, as they have other options such as a steak sandwich or catfish.

text:
Blaze is the love child of decision-making and deliciousness. I'm such a fan of Blaze. It's fresh dough, with any choice of sauces--from pesto to alfredo to your classic pizza sauce. 

You go through and have the ability to choose your sauce, cheese(s), meat(s), and veggie(s).  That's right, you can choose multiple cheeses, meats or veggies. With the build your own option, it costs the same amount whether you choose one of each or go all out and pile everything on. 

If decisions are too much, or you're having a friend pick up your order, you can also choose a pizza that they've already masterfully put together.  They still make it fresh, but the toppings and everything are already picked out for you. The pizza is also baked in a fiery oven, right before your eyes. The place always smells heavenly. Oh, and did I mention you can get a sauce drizzled over your whole pizza after it's been cooked to perfection? Wow. Amazing. 

They also offer salads and a few desserts, if you're into that sort of thing. Which I definitely am. The brownies are soft and chewy, just as a brownie should be. 

The location is also pretty stellar. Between being close to campus for students and close to downtown, it's hard to beat. I went last night, and with the summer weather making me feel summertime fine, we took our pizza party down to the canal and had a small picnic. 10/10 Blaze for giving the people the best pizza we could ask for in the fastest amount of time.
name: Arianna

I have been in New Orleans for about 3 years and went to Dickie Brennan's with some friends from out of town who wanted a great local place to try.  I have to say I was pretty disappointed.  

The wait staff was great - very attentive, friendly, and professional.  My only complaint is that I don't think I ever say the same person twice come to my table so I was never quite sure who to look for when I needed something.

Our creamed spinach arrived 15 minutes before our food so it got cold, they did replace that with a fresh one.  The asparagus arrived with the meal but was obviously over cooked.  I had the twin filet while the other three at the table got got the traditional filet.  I ordered mine medium rare (more rare), I received it almost full well. My meal also can with shrimp and it was over cooked as well and the shrimp were not fresh, the final bite of shrimp gave me such issue due to taste that I had to spit it out in my napkin. We ordered a filet to split and macaroni and cheese, mashed potatoes, asparagus, and a boomerang of margaritas, and it was all excellent. I like my steak on the rarer side while my partner doesn't, and they took her half and put it back on the grill for her and brought it back with another helping of mashed potatoes on the house.

text:
I run hot and cold on this place - so I averaged that to a solid "meh."

Tonight, we were very nearly greeted by a angry looking hostess. When we walked in, the party in front of us was a little confused about whether or not friends they were meeting were already there - they were young, and posing for an inordinate number of Instagram photos while walking into the place - so I can see where the hostess would be annoyed. However, when I stepped forward to indicate that we were a separate party of two, the hostess turned around and walked away.
She came back about a minute or two later and said something like, "how many again?" as though we were picking up a conversation that had actually started. Eh, everyone is allowed a bad night tho, amiright?

So, we were seated at a corner table, next to another table that had two folks sitting mid - meal. No problem - except the rest of the dining room area was vacant. Why smoosh us so close to an already occupied table?

Sitting at these tables means that one of the patrons has their back to a very cold exterior window. It's cute looking, and probably saves them some space, but it's not comfortable.

Anyway, our waiter took our orders and delivered the food promptly. The pizza was great - the badabing salad was wonderful. The meatball appetizer was no longer warm. There was cheese or something on the top of it, but by the time it got to our table it was a hardened weird substance. 

After a while, our waiter came by to ask about our meal - I looked up and smiled, because I had food in my mouth, but by the time I could open it to comment about the meatballs - he had already said,  "great!" and turned away. Our glasses were never refilled. 

No great sins were committed during the course of our meal - there were no heroes of the evening either. Tomorrow, I will try to jazz up the remaining meatballs and see if I can't improve on what we were originally served.
name: MB

text:
I don't really understand the five star reviews.  First, I came knowing that it was expensive, and this review has nothing to do with that.  I was prepared to pay top dollar, and in that, my expectations were met.  

Maybe we should have sat below deck.  The downstairs was beautiful.  But we wanted the open air.  It was a beautiful evening, about 70F and no humidity, so why not?  We got our table for five after a minimal wait, which was OK.  It didn't seem to be terribly busy, and there were plenty of waitstaff around.

We sat down and there were only four place mats for the five of us.  Oops.  So we swiped one from an empty table nearby.  

No place settings.  The waitress (who was pretty casual about keeping an eye on our table in case we needed something and pretty skilled at avoiding eye contact as she cruised past our table) took our drink orders and returned shortly with picnic style place settings - a knife and fork for each of us, all unceremoniously dropped at the end of the table, each wrapped in a paper napkin.  Should they be placed by each person at the table?  This didn't impress me, given my expectation that I'd be paying about $45 average for entrees and $15 for appetizers.  

Our table was no more than ten feet from the bar, so why did it take fifteen minutes for our drinks to arrive?  And no draft beers, another minor thing piled on top of several other minor things.

The appetizers were tasty but the portions were sub-par.  Three shrimps?  About a half teaspoon of lobster in the lobster bisque?  You can do better.

The entrees were delicious, no complaints there.  It took a while for it to arrive, but we were in no hurry.  

Dessert was not up to par.  A couple of us ordered them, and it was obvious when they arrived, after a considerable time, that they weren't made to order, as I would expect considering the price, but merely taken from the freezer.  So why would it take so long for them to arrive?

No coffee!  I asked for a cup of coffee (I didn't order dessert) and was told that they didn't serve coffee on the deck because it was so far from the kitchen.  What?  What kind of BS is this?

Finally, the music was SO loud.  I guess I should have asked if they could turn it down.  It wasn't like anyone was dancing, but it was loud enough to drown out normal conversation.  

So except for the dessert, I give the food four or five stars.  Sitting on the deck enjoying the open air was very nice.  But the indifferent, inattentive service rates only one star.  I feel like for the prices you can expect to pay, you should expect attentive service and at least a little pampering.
name: Steve

text: We got the large meal while celebrating my son's birthday.  5 adults and we had just a bit leftover.  Some of the best ribs and brisket I've had in a long time. text:
If you're looking for authentic, plentiful food, this is your place! 

I ordered roast pork, which essentially comes out of the kitchen as a mountain of meat, with a side of tostones (crispy, savory fried plantain cakes). I also got to try their yucca fries (similar to french fries). 

I can't say enough about THE GREEN SAUCE that comes drizzled atop the dish. It was like a chimichurri and added the necessary freshness/acidity to the delightfully fatty pork. 

Our mofongo came out with a little flag on top, swimming in a flavorful broth. From what I understand, it's fried, mashed plantains and lots of garlic shaped into a mold. It was delicious! 

The portions are HUGE and you can tell they put a lot of work into each and every plate. We'll definitely be back when I feel like my arteries can handle it! 

My only feedback to the business would be to find a way to make the menu a little easier to understand. It's in both Spanish and English, but maybe do one Spanish side and one English side rather than trying to combine? 

PRO TIP: Order the mofongo as a side rather than a standalone because it comes out cheaper!

text:
The first thing that caught my eye when I entered Uncle Bobbies was a tiny shelf with a small selection of books. Mind you, I went to Uncle Bobbies with the sole purpose of 1, seeing what all the hype was about, 2, enjoying a latte and 3, to purchase a book or two. Surely you can understand my disappointment when I saw what I thought was Uncle Bobbie's book selection. The cashier took my order and I was ushered to the side to wait for it. Instead of waiting, I walked to the back of the shop and it was as if the heavens opened before me!  There were books on top of books on top of great books! My inner bookworm started to do back flips! I was so excited. After retrieving my latte from the counter, I perused the book shelf, picked up "Assata" and found a spot on a comfy couch. For the next hour, I sipped and read while occasionally people watched. Uncle Bobbie's customers are just as diverse as its books selection. 

Now onto my review...

Uncle Bobbie's offers a diverse selection of books by African American authors, including children books, which is a major plus! Uncle Bobbie's is not the only bookstore in Philadelphia specializing in books by African American authors, but it offers something that the others don't...ambiance- a cozy, relaxing atmosphere! The front of the shop, decorated with a comfy couch and high back arm chairs looks more like a living room than a coffee shop. It makes sense that this black-owned business is perfectly nestled in the heart of Germantown. Great location and plenty of free street parking! I had been putting off visiting Uncle Bobbie's because I heard of how crowded it gets. I wanted to wait until the hype wore down. Not sure if the hype is over, but I went on a Saturday afternoon and although it was crowded, seats were available. My only dislike was the music playing in the background; it was a little too loud when you are trying to read, write or hold a conversation. 

The menu selection and the prices are the typical coffee shop selections/prices.  I live in South Jersey so I can't visit Uncle Bobbie's as much as I would like to, but when I am in the area again, I will be sure to check in on Uncle Bobbie's !
name: April

text:
This Chicago girl loves her Chicago-style pizza, and in her search for some of this pizza in the Tampa Bay area she finally found what she desired at Cappy's.  I have eaten both the Chicago-style thick crust pizza as well as the New York-style thin crust pizza here at Cappy's and I love both of them (though perhaps slightly biased towards the thick crust pizza for obvious reasons).  

The thin crust isn't too thin and thick crust isn't too thick - they are making some perfect pies here at Cappy's, especially with their sauce that is a perfect balance of tanginess and sweetness.  The dough is delicious as are all the toppings; I love that there isn't a whole pre-made list of pizzas to choose from, rather you choose the style of pizza you want and pile on the toppings from there!

Cappy's is a small spot, but it's poppin'; they are really cranking out the pizzas!  With it being a small space, the pizza aroma fills every particle of air and I am obsessed with it.  Can we bottle the fragrance of Cappy's and make into a Yankee Candle, please?  While I wait for that to happen, let me just say that I also love the old-school decorations that are pinned up all over the restaurant along with the 1950's fridge they use to chill their beer glasses.  Great food-check.  Good food-check.  Friendly staff-also check.  

So far, this has come to be my favorite pizza spot.  It's tough competition for any other pizza shop that wants to try and steal my heart.
name: Harlow

text:
I'm not Indian and not really a huge Indian food fan although my wife is a big fan.  I went here because I was intrigued by the setup and really thought it sounded interesting.  The reviews were stellar here on yelp and now I know why.

Frankly, this is some of the best food I've had anywhere let alone Indian food.  I could eat here every day.  This may look like "fast food" but it is far from it in my opinion. I'm not expert but i'm told this is more northern tradition in India not south.

First, the menu is clear and concise. Too many places lately just get way too many confusing options and ordering is a chore.  The staff help a lot in making it easy and you can get samples of anything to try before you order which is HUGE!  How many places do you go into and have never tried before and waste money on something you don't like? I've sampled all the sauces and all of them are fantastic.  You really can't go wrong, although my last choice would be the vegetable marsala.  

Second, the kitchen is fun to watch and so very clean. Staff seems to be excellent and they seem to have the process down well.  It is really great the way the place is setup to let you see how they make the food. There are four large clay ovens (with names!) that they cook the food and naan bread in.  I love watching them cook!  

Finally, the food! Oh the food! It is fantastic!  As I mentioned, I tried all the sauces but after eating there twice, I'm a big fan of the chick pea marsala.  I do like the Yellow Lentil Marsala too.  My wife is a big fan of the Tikka Marsala.  Nothing in the sauce is too spicy.  I did however find the Lamb Meatballs too spicy for me but that is just me.  I'm a wimp.  My wife and I both have had the chicken and it is fantastic and tender and perfectly seasoned and flavored.  You can't go wrong.  The rice is delicious too.  Such a simple thing but it is perfect.  The Mango Lassi is a delicious dessert treat.  Everyone there was getting them so we tried them and loved it.

What is there NOT to recommend?  Nothing really. However, in the interest of having them constantly perfect their service I'd like to mention a few things.

1 - Why oh why in the last 5 years has Cilantro become the season of choice for everything.  I swear even ordering Ice Cream I'm one day going to have to ask to hold the cilantro.  20% of the world population thinks Cilantro tastes like soap and I'm one of them.  Why would you risk ruining everyones food every time for this.  Please ask if you want Cilantro.  It disgusts me and my second time there I forgot to say to leave it out and it was on literally everything. The sauce, the meat, the rice, the bread - everything!  My fault but one simple questions would prevent this.  My wife was a peach and took it off. The food is so good it overcame this problem but it could have been better without it in the first place.  I have my issue with this at Chipotle too...

2 - Speed up the checkout process...this seemed to be slower than necessary for some reason?  Not sure what it is but there was a small hold up here both times I was there. Could be the sampling issue but they need to segregate and move along the people who don't need samples.  The cash register for me the second time took a dump too.

3 - Consistency - the first time there the bread was outrageously good - second time there it was just good.  I think there was butter or something they put on it the first time. No idea what it was. The second time it was dry and greatly disappointing but not enough to ding them for it.  It was good but not out-of-this-world good.

4 - Wish the sauces, extras, utensils were separated more from the trash.  There is a bottleneck here and I really don't like my garbage next to the good stuff.  Nitpicking here but it could be better.

My greatest disappointment --- THERE IS NOT ONE NEAR ME. :)
name: Anthony

text:
My review reflects the caliber of the Windsor Court not as a hotel per se, but as a wedding venue. After months of extensive planning and coordination with the amazing event planning staff, we held our wedding reception at the Windsor in May. With our guest list shaking out at around 300 heads, the Chinoiserie ballroom, with a lovely outdoor terrace overlooking the Mississippi river and NOLA skyline, was more than equipped to handle such a large party.

The level of precision exhibited by the team was honestly astounding. No NOLA wedding is complete without a raucous Second Line, and at risk of sounding self-indulgent, ours was absolutely legendary thanks to the Windsor court staff. We essentially shut down Canal st and paraded 300 strong through the city's main thoroughfare with stiff Hurricanes in hand and a brigade of police escorts. The guests were then moved inside to begin a buffet-style dinner while my wife and I were ushered to the second floor restaurant for a "private dining moment" with a veritable feast of options from the reception menu laid out before us, along with our pre-requested drinks of choice (Macallan 12 for me and a dry martini for her). The guests thought the dining options were incredible, particularly the seafood display, and we 100% agree. After this brief respite from the craziness, we were escorted to the ballroom where much dancing and revelry occurred until midnight, after which many of the guests shifted to the bar for a post-game hangout. It felt like a seamless production from start to finish and both we and our guests were thrilled with the end result. 

Special shout out especially to Haley Kennel (catering sales manager), who was an absolute angel and did everything from manually exchanging my wife's shoes when we first arrived for walking-friendly sneakers to bringing us scheduled water q30 minutes during reception to ensure hydration. It is not the cheapest of venues, but you definitely get what you pay for and I cannot recommend the Windsor Court and their in-house events team enough for hosting your own wedding!
name: Ritodhi

text:

The lamb biryani is soft and mushy. Again- too much oil. All the rice is clumping together like mush. Flavors just aren't there.

text:
Located in Fountain Square, Gavel neighbors Three Carrots and The Inferno Room. Indoor seating is limited, but there is a spacious outdoor patio (weather permitting). There is additional seating in an area called "The Tube" after 5 p.m. (even though the cafe is only open until 6 p.m.). Free parking is available outside on Virginia Ave for up to 2 hours, and there is WiFi access but limited outlets.

In addition to serving house-made pastries, Gavel offers a variety of snacks and grilled cheese sandwiches with bread from Amelia's, a local bakery. The beverage menu includes brewed coffee, lattes, teas, sodas, beer on tap, wine, and cocktails. Coffee grounds sourced from the Indianapolis Tinker Coffee Company are also available for purchase.

After requesting a Cafe Miel and being told they didn't have all the ingredients to make it, I ordered a Salted Mocha with oat milk (the barista's recommendation) and classic grilled cheese. I was impressed with both items, especially the grilled cheese. I would've liked the sandwich to be a bit spicier, but according to the menu, a different specialty grilled cheese is offered each week. I'm interested to see if they'll offer one with pepper jack cheese in the future. I also want to try their lemon shake up; it seemed like many people were ordering it during the hour I studied at the bar.

text: So I think we all can agree that Olive Garden isn't the place to go for authentic Italian cuisine. It's usually just a matter of convenience if we go here and it's usually mediocre, at best. Yesterday I was craving pasta, and to be honest I do like the salad. We were seated and glanced over the apps and opted for Fried Pasta Chips with marinara. The pic looked amazing, like Italian nachos. The server brought them out quickly and they were hot with sauce and a few peppers on the top. I was excited and put a pasta chip in my mouth,, WHOA!!! SALT!!!! OK so maybe that particular area got hit heavy. Tried another chip. Same. And I don't mind food with a some salt, but this was completely inedible. The hipster server asked how the app was and I explained why we didn't care for it. He understood and agreed. He also said they're made in the morning. MORNING??? It's 6pm!!!! We ate our salad and breadsticks, which oddly seemed very salty as well. Since we bailed on the apps I decided to order a couple of meatballs, on the side. Now, in my experience, a side of meatballs are usually a good size, more than a few bites each, and brought to the table covered in sauce. Well, when the entrees arrived, which were just fine, the two meatballs were placed on the table in dish, bare. Naked. Sans sauce. And small... So small my wife looked at me like this was joke!! I asked the server if we could some sauce on them and he then brought them back with sauce. You could barely tell it was sauce. Mearballs should come swimming in sauce, enough for them to be at least a third covered. Come on!! That told me that they really don't care what they serve. Like they were saying 'f you, here's your sauce.' I will gladly give up going here and will gladly go out of my way to one of the many great local Italian restaurants that do know how to serve great food with heart, and passion. F you OG. We're done.
name: Roger

text:
This hot spot in south Tampa is all about the ambiance. It's theme is prohibition era drinks, which are amazing and full of flavor. I had el presidente, it had a bit of a kick to it in flavor but was well worth the $12 I paid for it. 
Food portions are small so if you intend to come here and be full, you might want to think again. Remember this place is more about the drinks and ambiance not for its large food portions. I had the duck breast on a bed of quinoa and a poached egg for $21. The duck was a bit chewy and served rare, but the quinoa and egg where amazing. I would not recommend the duck just because of how chewy it was but the flavor was amazing. 
The servers are all amazing, fast, have great attitudes-and are dressed to impress. 
There is a large bar that seats around 15 people and several cocktail tables for two to eat dinner. There is also the private booth seating that are curtained off, it really creates a romantics and individual experience. I would highly recommend asking for the private booths over the cocktail tables although for me if was fun being able to experience both. 
The inside is dark as all the lights are dimmed down, remember the theme prohibition era.
If you are in the area and have some money do spend on amazing drinks and food this is a spot that everyone needs to experience at least once.
name: Hernan

text:
Came here with some co-workers after work. This place is suitable to get a round of drinks after work or to have dinner, I wouldn't come here for lunch in the middle of a work day though because of how long it takes the food to come out.

We got a ribs platter, a pulled pork sandwich, and a half charred chicken. My work companion indicated the half charred chicken was "charred to perfection." We were presented with three different BBQ sauce options. I tried all three on my ribs. Each one was unique and all were delicious.

Pulled pork sandwich was made by the sauce. Came with a side of mac and cheese which was also good. Ribs platter came with sides, baked beans, candied yams and cornbread. Baked beans were plentiful and tasty. Yams were sliced and cooked with cinnamon, probably brown sugar and butter. Cornbread was like a cornbread cupcake, sweet and moist.

Ribs were not falling off the bone but were tasty with the sauce. 

Atmosphere was nice. It's not a big space but there weren't too many other people there, a couple of guys at the bar and another group of two or three in the dining area. They just changed their draft beer selection and haven't updated their lists yet, but the still had some craft selections. Mixed drinks seemed a bit pricey, $7 for a whiskey and pineapple juice. Overall it was a good time.

The service seems great, but it's very very small and I think large orders can easily overwhelm them. For instance, one time we went in a decently large group (probably around 9 people or so), and it took a really long time for the orders to come out, and we definitely couldn't all sit together. 

The interior is very simple yet colorful and vibrant. Overall, it's a wonderful no-frills type of restaurant that knows its Mexican food.

text:
My friends and I thoroughly enjoyed our dinner here this past Friday night (March 2, 2018). Great atmosphere, friendly service, and they held our reserved table for us even though we were 10 minutes late.

We reserved a table weeks in advance, primarily due to the fact that one person in our party is in a wheelchair and could not therefore dine upstairs. They saved us a seat close to the door that made getting in and out of a breeze - and because the sidewalk traffic was far more hectic than we had expected, we arrived late. It was no problem for them, though.

We started off with the deconstructed rangoon appetizer, and it was delicious. The homemade ranch sauce is a meal in itself, and we wanted to drink it up! Then came the main courses - beautifully presented, huge portions, and I had the opportunity to have both the traditional hot chicken and their version of Nashville hot, which our waitress had undersold as merely having a "lingering, smoky flavor". The reality was that their version of Nashville hot was much, much spicier than the traditional - seasoned to perfection and just delicious!

One dining tip: the portions are enormous, and it's likely you won't finish. Rather than leaving them, ask for to-go containers. There are a number of transient and homeless folks out on the streets of Nashville; kind, not-at-all aggressive, and they tend to keep to themselves. We combined the leftover mac and cheese (decadent and the perfect complement to the hot chicken) with hot chicken and a few pickles, and two additional folks feasted on our leftovers.

Thanks for the great dining experience, Stillery downtown Nashville team!
name: Sean

text:
