name: Pasquale

text: You are going to like the food. You are going to like the indoor/outdoor seating.  You are going  to like the fast styled ordering.  The price is a bit too much; but, otherwise, it's a GREAT place.
name: Joshua

text: People are being a little dramatic in these comments honestly. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. My experience was honestly fine. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. No big complaints, just a nice meal. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. They were out of one thing I originally wanted..
name: User

text: Loved this place. I got a chai latte iced and it was delicious. We were able to relax and we read for a bit while we enjoyed our drinks. There were quite a few USF students studying. We really enjoyed our time here.
name: Jessica

text: Been here a couple of times for afternoon tea on Saturday lunch time with 3 friends. You need to make a reservation for the afternoon tea. They brought out a cake stand with enough for 4 people. It was really good - sandwiches, scones with cream and jam, sausage rolls, little cakes.  They have a large tea menu and you can choose 2 different types of tea to drink with your food. The inside of the restaurant is pretty plain but the food is good.
name: Scouser

text:
Awesome latin fusion tapas spot. Great food, drinks and atmosphere. Had almost everything on the menu and everything was delicious and well seasoned. Keep in mind, this is tapas style so portions are small and shareable, this allows you to order tons of different things on the menu and try everything. 
My favorites include ALL the empanadas, the elote, ceviche, churros and trio of desserts. SO GOOD.
name: Rebeca

text: The fries were probably the best part of the meal, honestly. Price felt a touch high for what it was. For a busy night they handled it okay. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. It was decent, just a little uneven. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything..
name: User

text: Great meal. We had the salad with lemon. I love lemon and nuts so this was a fantastic salad. The Verde pizza was very good. Amazing crust and the pistachios were a nice touch. This place is hard to find but when you do you will be happy!
name: Duane

text: Love this hot chicken shack! Tender Juicy spicy!!! Sometime the food wait is long - so try to go off peak.
name: Jackie

text: So good! The mole is the best we have ever had!!! Highly recommend. Maybe just order the Mole Enchiladas.
name: Matt

text:
The food (that we received) was really good; however, the service-not so much :(

One of our orders came out wrong. Everyone else is finished eating and that entree has not been brought back out. Our waiter hasn't checked on us since we were served.  Our drinks have been empty for about 15 minutes-not tea or water but revenue generating alcohol.


Our last night on the island, not impressed.

Ps Still sitting here with no drinks and empty food plates filling our table.
name: Jennifer

text: A much needed REAL bakery in the area...focused on using REAL ingredients.  This place has not disappointed.  Try the carrot muffins...you will be glad you did!
name: Lisa

text: Just walking into the explosion of colorful decorations already made it one of my favorite places in Nashville. And then the food was so good I think I'll come back tomorrow for seconds.
name: Cody

text: On our go-to circle of restaurants The GKT nails it with fresh blackboard specials and consistently excellent food. We are loving the fall menu but just got to say that the burgers and Beaujolais last night were awesome!
name: Donna

text: Stopped by for a late breakfast.  Two of us ordered lunch:  cheeseburger (wife says the cheeseburger was one of the best she ever had) and philly chicken.  Breakfast was chicken fried steak, which my daughter said was very good.   I tasted the steak, which was very tasty.  Food came out piping hot.  The fries were a little soggy, but ok.  A plus was the fries were all you can eat.  On a side note, the server was very nice looking.
name: Eric

text: This place is TERRIBLE I ordered a Supreme Burrito the sauce was way too concentrated On the 2 burritos not that big for $14 took them 48 minutes to bring the food the chips had no flavor salsa was like water.When my drink ran out I had to wait a while for the waiter to come close to ask them I came with some friend (10 people) we ended up paying $134 1 meal per person TERRIBLE do not go there ended up throwing up when I got home.
name: Jesus

text:
I hate to do it, but I've got to take it down a notch on my initial love for Village Whiskey. We've had a number of service issues in the last year and another disappointing experience this past Thursday night around 9:00pm.

We showed up and asked if we could sit outside for dinner. "Dinner or just drinks?" the hostess demanded. I just said "two for dinner" but sure, no problem, happy to repeat myself.

We get seated outside and then nothing.... for 15 minutes. It was odd at first but became increasingly evident that it had been longer than that since the other tables had seen a server. One table was waiting to send something back that came out incorrectly, another was seated just after us and also looking to put in food/drinks. One table tried to snag a food runner and put in another drink order as he dropped off their plate but he just sort of shrugged them off and walked away. 

All in all, the worst thing ever? Of course not. But when you have a city full of fantastic burgers with better service (and even better yet, reservations) I just dont think Village Whiskey is worth it. 

We didn't stay so I can't say how much longer it was. We did however find out that Tria Taproom has a delicious burger that night.
name: Kelly

text: The soup is delicious, I love that they give you so much, and it's all fresh ingredients.  The staff there has always been friendly and polite as well.
name: Tammy

text: Super busy, good service, great prices, good food. I would return but not go out of my way to do so.
name: Teressa

text: Love the service, atmosphere and the toasts! And of course it's in the best neighborhood in St. Louis...Shaw!
name: Rebecca

text: Walking in you see great decor and great use of space.  The staff were very friendly and patient for new guests.  It was relaxed, cozy, and welcoming.  You receive GREAT value for your the more-than-fair price; the food is AMAZING.  We tried the chicken, snapper, oxtail, and appetizers, and all were more than outstanding.  We found this location by chance; definitely will be back!!!
name: Tony

text: I recently went on a BumbleBFF date here and it was so much fun! This place was busy (probably because the amazing food) but they managed to get us in super quickly! It was the perfect place for drinks and conversation, while enjoying some yummy food in a fun atmosphere! Love midtown and would recommend for anyone unsure of a good place to go for the first time!
name: Kayla

text: Best damn donuts and coffee around, hands down.   You won't regret it!  Try the maple bacon!
name: Rusty

text:
If you are on a diet then please don't come.  This place is delicious.  How can a store be delicious??  Well just walk in and I bet you can't resist buying something that you can eat while walking around the store.  I mean even the smell is intoxicating. 

We went in for some zucchini bread and walked out with a basket load of items.  From quiche, cookies, donuts, honey, cupcakes and chocolate pretzels, if it's delicious they have it.

Make sure you stop through.
name: Cee

text: This place sucked all around. The service was terrible and super slow. The food was not good at all. My boyfriend got one taco just to try it and wouldn't get anything else. I had a burrito that also was pretty gross. It was also disappointing that their margaritas are made of wine. This is definitely not a place I would come back or recommend.
name: Allison

text: I'm such a big Sharky's fan. I had one close to me in Pasadena before I moved back to SB years after college. Was really glad they opened one here. Such consistently tasty food with so many healthy options. Service has always been great. My only complaint is that they don't let you use sharkys bucks with coupons haha. But it won't stop me from coming.
name: Sarah

text: These guys have it all figured out!  And the sauce right at the table to make it even sloppier is a nice touch.  Friendly family run beehive of activity kinda place that allways remember you and appreciate your business. Get there early on weekends though, they aren't open very late.
name: Rocknroller1999

text: We went tonight because all the great remarks. Service was great and she anticipated our needs. However the food was really not that good. The chicken and waffles were so bad that I will probably not return. The chicken is only legs and thighs and they chop them into pieces so it's like eating wings but paying 13.99. Waffles were burnt so our serve brought over jalapeños corn bread which was very good. The grits were runny. The catfish was soggy. I was so looking forward to a new place but it just did not live up to all hype.
name: Robin

text: The food was good and the service was easygoing. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Not bad for a quick meal. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. For the price I expected more than this.
name: User

text: Every year we come to the Indy 500 for 13 years, camping all weekend....we've tried so many places..all have been good......but, Mug 'N Bun is always our first place to dine out without question.
name: Donna

text: The owners themselves take care of you offering the highest quality Puerto Rican recipes. I should give a 5* but the wait time doesn't allow me but except for that, highly recommended.
name: Indhira

text: Got the taste of New Orleans and there was nothing on there worth ordering again. Friend got a seafood platter and he didn't care for it. Pretty pricey, surprised there are so many good reviews but have good for them.
name: Brad

text: The best oysters in town! Walk right in and sit at the oyster bar!! Excellent service at the oyster bar!! Great food and hospitality!! Definitely coming back!
name: Julie

text: I love this place. So much so that I'll cough up the $100 for the chicken sandwich that doesn't come with the drink or side ;) But I can't complain too much you get what you pay for and by God their chicken sandwich is delicious. Only thing I wish they would incorporate a kids menu already because my kids love it just as much. Oh and I love the decor of this place.
name: Stacey

text: This place is TERRIBLE!!! 20 Min wait for a glass of wine....20 Min wait for a Frozen hamburger patty. Ran out of wine glasses and our cheese "board" had to be served on a paper plate because they were out of dishes. What. A. Shit Show.
name: Zach

text: A little gem off the beaten path!  Fresh juices, packed flavorful omelettes, my Papa's French toast was AMAZING!  The decor was pleasing, the staff was so helpful and on point.  Definitely coming back!
name: Deneen

text: Parking was annoying and I was already in a bad mood by the time I got inside. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The staff seemed tired but still polite. It was crowded but still moved along. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. I wouldn't write it off, but I also wouldn't hype it up. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text: Great East Nashville spot for brunch! My husband and I met some friends at Fort Louise for brunch yesterday, and it was a great meal! The restaurant is charming (in a small old house), the service was great, and the food was delicious! We all had coffee (none of us elected to have brunch cocktails this time) and started with the smoked salmon bagel sliders (mini bagel halves with cream cheese, smoked salmon, pickled onions, capers, and dill - a great start. I had the breakfast burrito, which was actually really great. Definitely had to eat it with a fork, but everything was delicious (the eggs weren't overcooked or dry or chalky - I usually shy away from scrambled eggs at restaurants for this reason): eggs, sausage, tater tots, sour cream and salsa on top! My husband and one of our friends got the challah French toast (which they both liked, but is a little sweet for my taste), and our other friend tried the Eggs Benedict which was served with a slice of hashbrown waffle! Everyone liked what they ordered, and the food was good overall! I also thought it was very affordable and reasonably priced. The brunch entrees were in the low 10s, but the portions were really big! We went home with half a burrito in a box! Parking isn't great, but other than that, it was a great meal. We got a reservation for brunch, but I'm not sure if that's necessary. There was at least walk-in group of four that were seated, but outside. Definitely give it a shot!
name: Alexis

text: Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Parking was annoying, although that's prob more about the area than the restaurant. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. Definitely coming back. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Would probably stop in again if nearby. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price..
name: User

text:
Unbelievably disappointing!   Nothing is fresh, every food item we order was either old, stale, frozen or from a can.  
Examples:  The fried mushrooms cost $8.99 and are frozen balls of nastiness.  An entire bag can be purchased at Walmart for much cheaper.  
The turkey sandwich consisted of store bought generic luncheon meat, a stale sub roll and lettuce, tomato and onion that were visibly wilted and bruised.
The Chicken Parmesan was served in a piping hot metal bowl that came straight out of the broiler with a side bowl of luke warm, watery spaghetti.   Each one had a different sauce, of which, both were tasteless and bland.  I actually had to ask the server for a dinner plate to assemble my dinner so it could be properly eaten, although after 2 bites I pushed it to the side.
The basket of bread were rolls straight out of the plastic bag - not seasoned and/or toasted.
Other reviews state that the steaks are good but the table sitting directly behind us sent their steaks back for improper cooking and being a bad cut of meat since it had an extreme amount of grizzle in them.
Needless to say, we will NOT be back to try the steaks, pizza, subs or any other processed menu item.
Wish there was a big, fat 0 rating because this place above all others deserves it!
AVOID THIS OVERPRICED, UNAPPETIZING PLACE AT ALL COSTS!  WORST RESTAURANT IN SPRINGFIELD!
name: Teddilynn

text: This place is awesome. He menu is HUGE. There are options for anyone. Portions are huge. Prices are great for the portions you get. Bakery items are delicious, and they have a lot of options as well. It is a huge location, with many tables. Decor is super cool. From the times I've been, it seems they are becoming increasingly popular. The last time I went was on a rainy Thursday for lunchtime - around 1pm- and they were packed. 20 minute wait time. Definitely call ahead if you can. Service has always been great. Wait staff is friendly and attentive. A family favorite restaurant for us.
name: Caroline

text: Superb. I'm a fourth generation fan of Commander's Palace. It honestly doesn't get much better.
name: Liz

text: Nice atmosphere, craft beer and super happy hour.   Super friendly staff.   And their happy hour starts at 3pm!!!
name: Karen

text:
I have been to a few other all you can eat sushi bars, and this one was relatively decent though a bit too pricy. The their crab meat sashimi was not very fresh, but the salmon sashimi was nice and tender. 
The wait time was quite long, and they really don't bring things in order. I got out appetizer after an order of ice-cream! lol
They do have a pretty decent selection of rolls as well as specials.
name: Peter

text:
Let's just say...it sufficed.

Booked a Sunday brunch for a party of 13 ladies in town for a bachelorette weekend. 

Pros: Easy to book online, and they had availability. Bread was warm and plentiful. Service was good, they kept the coffee and cocktails flowing. They were prepared to explain which dishes were gluten free for our celiac friends. Standout entrees were the gumbo, crab omelette, and crepes. Can't beat the location either.

Cons: While I understand that it is historic and has a certain look and feel, the semi-private room they assigned us to was dark and smelled a bit like a dive bar. Actually, the awful "morning after" bar smell was quite overpowering when we entered the establishment, immediately at the front door. Crawfish hash was depressing - a handful of potatoes, no more than 5 crawfish tails, and every poached egg at the table was horribly overcooked.
name: Jessica

text: Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. For the price I expected more than this. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh.
name: User

text: Just had the best chicken tikka masala of my life here -- the sauce was incredible. They used to offer the aloo puri on their brunch menu and we asked if we could still order some and our waitress and the chef were both so kind--it was so delicious and made our day! Very happy to have such a great restaurant run by friendly people in the neighborhood.
name: Erica

text: Got here first thing and wasn't disappointed. I got the burrito, chips and a drink. Plenty of seating, friendly staff, and good selection on what to build. I would compare this to a chipotle or freebirds. They also have a small bar in the front.
name: Haden

text: Food took forever but ended up being better than I expected. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. It was decent, just a little uneven. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.
name: User

text: This is my favorite Italian chain restaurant.  Never had a bad meal or service here. This is just slightly more expensive than other chains but you get what you pay for. The best is family style dining, this way you can have a bit of everything. They also do banquets and I have been to 2 weddings here and loved them both.
name: Lucy

text: Had a fun experience on the General Jackson. Went on a Saturday night and had a thoroughly entertaining evening. Dinner was delicious, especially for a buffet. Roast beef was cooked properly, and a good selection of sides.  Our server, George, was very attentive and added to our enjoyment of the evening. Other members of the crew took the time to talk to us about the mechanics of the paddle boat and it's navigation on the river. The trip on the water was beautiful with the bridge lights and view of downtown Nashville at night. The show was fun and total energy! So glad we chose to do this.
name: Sue

text: Had an amazing Saturday morning breakfast! First time visiting Philly and was so happy I found this place after searching through several yelp suggestions! First I love that it is black owned!!! Second the serve and the food was amazing. The place is located in a beautiful area so although we had to wait 20 minutes the time flew by, and they gave us a call once table was ready. Started with OJ, very fresh! Ordered the home fries with peppers and onions, fried chicken and waffles, and the sampler plate which included red velvet pancake, stuffed French toast, and a cinnamon swirl pancake!! Definitely worth a try, all was amazing! The serve was great, had three lovely women all checking on us throughout our dining. Would definitely recommend and go back again!
name: Brandi

text: Incredibly friendly and great food. Dined here with a teenager who discovered that he couldn't eat oysters with bleucheese and our server, Susanna, couldn't have been nicer about switching it out. All of our food was fantastic!
name: Tammy

text: The first few bites were promising and then it kind of leveled out. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. This feels like a place where your order choice matters a lot.
name: User

text:
A new restaurant with an excellent and price-competitive lunch menu!! 

I usually don't write reviews but felt like this one needed a hand in getting its name out there. The first time I dined here for lunch, I got the roast pork sandwich and wasn't impressed. I was quite turned off by the sauce, felt like it was too sharp for the sandwich. My friend ordered the pappardelle and it looked so good that I ended up eating some off of his plate. I did not regret my primitive behavior as it was delicious. This was what categorized The Common in my mind as a place to give a second chance to. 

Today, I was in the mood for a quality yet inexpensive lunch again. There are at least 5 entrees available for under $10! So, off I went to the Common. This time, I made the right choice and ordered the chicken milanesa with salad. Each bite was absolutely decadent. My only complaint was that the sauce was not spread evenly in the sandwich which caused it to ooze out one side while I was eating. The salad was fresh and paired well with the vinaigrette. 

Overall, great place to have a peaceful lunch with enough left over for dinner!
name: Sophia

text: A little hidden treasure! Breakfast, lunch and drinks... can't go wrong. Great community spot whether you live in Bexley or the surrounding areas. Eggs and bacon, BLT, ice cream, brownies, beer and wine
name: Tabatha

text: Excellent service Excellent food!!! A must try! This place was warm and comfortable. The employees are super nice! Our server IKE was amazingly great. It's hard to find good with amazing service. Again, a must try
name: Jeanette

text: Big shout out to Austin the bar tender.  Great guy, made my visit very enjoyable.  Bar has a great selection of very interesting whiskey, rye and bourbon at very reasonable prices.  Good farm to table food.  One of my go-to places.
name: Ken

text:
This was our first time here and we had a blast! The conveyor belt system is fun, the food is high quality and tasty, and the service is prompt without being overbearing. 

Our favorites were: the tomato oxtail broth (so rich and beefy!), the wagyu brisket, and the lamb shank rolls. 

It's not all you can eat some other hotpot places so it'll be a little more pricey - but definitely worth a try.
name: Ioana

text:
A very cute place to eat or grab a drink in midtown. The place is very small, probably only seats about 20-25 people MAX! If you have a group of 4 or more you probably want to call ahead and make sure a table is available. There is only one server/bartender during the day so be prepared to wait a little while, if you're trying to grab a quick bite probably try somewhere else. 

The food- 
The food is the only reason I'm giving this place 4 stars. I have the vegan breakfast tacos, they came with eggs, peppers, jalapeños, onion, cilantro, and a couple other veggies I can't recall off the top of my head. They came with like a chipotle crema on top and breakfast potatoes that were absolutely delicious. They were spicy with the jalapeño so if you do want to try them and don't like hot food, be sure to let your waitress know. Another guest ordered the sausage breakfast tacos and he said they were excellent, so if you prefer protein you can get sausage or bacon. My son got the brick oven Mac n cheese and the gastro pub French fries, he preferred the French fries which were seasoned really well. The Mac n cheese was a little disappointing mostly because it came out cold?

The bad-
The place filled up as we were in there and the service suffered. I never got a wine list so I just asked for a house chard, which wasn't great. We didn't get a single refill on waters or an offer to refill my wine. We waited 45+ minutes for our food, and like I said the Mac n cheese came out cold. We said we would like to start with the Mac n cheese and fries under the "starter" section in the menu hoping I could feed my son before myself but everything came out at once. When we were done with our meal we did not receive the check so after about 10 minutes waiting with empty glasses and plates we walked to the bar and paid. 

Overall, I will return to try more of the menu. The food is all very fresh and like the name states "homegrown" locally. Probably without my son next time since he doesn't quite have the patience for how slow this place was. They have someone bussing tables, maybe they should consider also having him run food so it doesn't come out cold.
name: Raylene

text: I like to stop in here for a few drinks and apps to hangout with friends, young adult crowd
name: Elise

text: This is my first trip to Luke's new place the food is amazing, we had the Nashville hot chicken and the loaded kettle chips and a cheeseburger,, we also had a Country Girl drink LOVED IT!!! Frank was our server,,great server he was helpful with menu and was very quick with the drinks!!!  Thank you Frank!!!
name: Louise

text: Great food both authentic in flavor and appeal. Very relaxed atmosphere. But be prepared it's not the best faster option for lunch.
name: Christopher

text: This is a very good, slightly more upscale restaurant in Irvington.   The food is excellent and the prices more than fair.   Service is friendly and helpful.
name: Peter

text: This place is busy!!!! I guess that was a good indication when I decided to try their food. Menu is the same as all other Chinese takeout businesses in the area. Prices are in line with the other Chinese businesses in the area. When I say this place is busy, it does not mean they are slow. My order took approx 20 minutes and I watched no less than 10 others picking up theirs orders in that time. Staff was friendly. I will definitely be ordering again. My only recommendation is to go to Publix and buy a jar of good duck sauce as those little packets are just blecch!
name: Beansaguaard

text: Such good food! Coffee is good, they have mimosas! Service is a little slow, but by far, best diner food there is. Lemon poppyseed pancakes are the best, you can't find them anywhere else but there and they're to die for! I highly recommend eating here!
name: Bentley

text:
Recently came with my daughters to check out this brand new location. I will say that being brand new, they were efficient in how they handled a large lunch crowd and our food came out without much wait.

If you are a fan of thin crust pizza, you will love this place. The crust is extremely thin and has a nice crispiness to it. They have a variety of options and toppings sure to please whatever craving you are having; and if you are like my family and all want different things on your pizza, they have the perfect size option to have your own pizza!

On the trip, the girls and I shared a pepperoni pizza, with sausage (added just on my side). It was wonderful. Not too much sauce, perfect crispy crust. Both my daughter and I loved it and we will be back! Well done MOD and welcome to the area
name: Peter

text: Good find based on Yelp review. I was in the area and it pulled it up. I got the shrimp taco which was great. Coming back on Sunday with kids because my daughter loves quesadillas and this variety will blow her away.
name: Sally

text: The TX Brisket here is very good and far from its namesake. The presentation of the platter is unique with a 50/50 combination of tender, sliced brisket coupled with burnt ends.  Almost like two different meats in one. Good job in a comfortable atmosphere where whiskey and beer options abound.
name: Jim

text: Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. It looked better online than it did in person. Nice little spot, decent portions too.
name: User

text: Terrible service. My family went there and was told that we could sit anywhere. We sat at a booth and waited over 15 minutes for someone to greet us, but no one came. The hostess came and got our drink order and we wanted to order an appetizer - she responded, "oh, I'm not your server," and proceeded to walk away. We waited another 10 minutes and no one to approach us. We left. We were given ugly stares for walking out on an establishment that paid no mind to customers. If I could give zero stars, I would.
name: Tina

text: I get the appeal, I just don't totally share it. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. I can see why people like it, even if I wasn't fully sold. Nice little spot, decent portions too. The leftovers held up okay the next day..
name: User

text: Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. For a busy night they handled it okay. Worth checking out. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really.
name: User

text:
I went to the Rams Pizza on New Years Day for dinner . Very dark atmosphere and they have No Waitress staff. A customer from the bar can over and took are order. I found this after 30 minutes after we ate. Waiting on a 
check that we never got  we go to the bar and he told us they do not hire help. And from New Year Day night I have l had a cough from all the cigarette smoke in that place . I more than likely will not be returning to this place at all.
name: Patricia

text:
Black Bean noodle, it's the best here in Tampa!
Kalbi Tang (savory beef soup) is really good. Will drive here for 45mins just for this. Great service. Came at a great time when the place was slowing down for lunch hour. Recently renovated so everything is brand new and sparkly!
name: Xeriel

text: tough night for OPA.  Food was good, but we were told they ran out of Lamb, so I got the pork chop.  I have had it before and usually a good thick chop.  Then, the table next to us asked about the lamb and someone checked with the kitchen (since it was Friday night) and they did get more that afternoon (ran out at lunch).  To add insult to injury the food took forever and when it arrived, the chop seemed small compared to what I had before.  They offered us an extra dessert (did not ask what we wanted) which we wouldn't have ordered, so all around a bad experience.  There were better options they could have offered based on several mishaps in one night.  I think we will wait and see if this is a trend before we go back.
name: Dave

text: My favorite food is Indian cuisine and I am exceedingly impressed with Flames. The food is exceptionally delicious. The service is exceptional as well. I have visited the restaurant ~5 times and have had consistently good service each time. I also feel that although the food was good when they first opened it has gotten even more delicious. Also, I have small children so am very cognizant of the cleanliness of restaurants because my kiddos inevitably end up picking crayons, etc. off the floor. Flames is very clean and well maintained. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.
name: Jamie

text: Company was great!  The old fashion was the BEST I've ever had.  At a Vino bar,who would have guessed.  Cynthia did enjoy the wine and the small plates were delicious BUT stay away from the desserts. Definitely the downfall if you are a coffee dessert person.  Nice place and great service . Again DO NOT order dessert
name: Patty

text: I can't believe the worst restaurant in Sparks had the balls to open a second location.  The menu is out dated and the quality of preparation is poor.  It would have been nice if a quality restaurant went into this great location by the movie theater but apparently the land lord is not interested in delivering quality.   If you enjoy freshly prepared food don't go here.  Most everything is covered in a crappy cheese blend.   Flavor is also something the restaurant needs to learn how to incorporate into their food.   Hopefully this place will go out of business soon and the Legends mall will put a decent restaurant in its place.
name: Matt

text: Excellent service.  Yummy sand witches. Wonderful Italian groceries. Clean.  Large portions and great price.  Bread just got soggy too fast.
name: Colette

text: Service was friendly. It's a popping place! Food was mediocre. Chicken fried sandwich was dry and over fried. It was lacking a savory flavor.
name: Alia

text: Went with family on a Sunday and it was louder than I expected. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. For a busy night they handled it okay. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait.
name: User

text: Everything about this ice cream shoppe is wonderful!  The ice cream is delicious and make locally with the finest ingredients from sustainable farmers. I had the mint chocolate chip in a sugar cone dipped in chocolate - amazing!  The staff is very kind and polite!  Be sure to check out their FREE compliments too!  Please support this great local shoppe when choosing ice cream in St. Pete's Beach!
name: Denise

text:
I was super stoked when I found out they were building one in Sparks near my home. I didn't mind driving to their original location in Northwest Reno but now I could def take advantage of my points with them & the fact that whenever I am craving Poke , its now just down the street. 

Went in , the store was pretty empty but it was about 7PM and I assumed with them just opened they are still building their customers on the Sparks end.

Same deal , choose your size of bowls, base, protein, sauce, toppings, etc. I got two bowls, paid about $27 and def was filled up after. 

I don't remember the other Poke King having 3 protein options, but I was able to get 3 proteins this time but being pregnant , I was limited with only getting tofu or shrimp as my proteins. 

Either way , excited to start going here more and probably might end up being a regular!
name: Clarissa

text:
This has become one my main go to breakfast spots in Downtown Boise. Always amazing and made with love. The owners are great and take pride in their restaurant. The staff is always personable and willing to go the extra mile to make my experience great. One of my favorite things about Wild Root is the vibe and atmosphere. Great local spot that really highlights what Idaho is all about. 

My personal favorite is the steak and eggs. Flawless!
name: Daniel

text: So you know how I love hole in the wall diners? This one was probably the smallest diner I've been to. There are only six tables and the counter. The French toast hit the spot. Plus they were playing 80s pop so I felt right at home.
name: Charity

text: Everything here is fresh and healthy my mom and dad take me here all the time. The atmosphere is very clean and the price is good
name: Anthony

text: This place is a long in the tooth joke.   The host was a condescending douche canoe and very judgy.  Money is money and these people have no clue how to treat guests.   Poor chef.  Food is probably good but his front line is awful.  Don't go if you dislike stuffiness! Go to the fun happy welcoming places when you're here in NOLA!  The atmosphere is a bust - it's like a cafeteria!
name: Shelly

text: Delightful. Very broad selection of cheeses, excellent recommendations for pairings. The beer selection was most impressive! This restaurant is a very unique find, and will not disappoint!
name: Patricia

text: Great addition to the City of Carmel. Great looking place. Nice that they allow children. Great beer and food options. One large draw back, noise. It was so loud, conversation was barely possible. They have outdoor seating which is nice. Today was raining so outdoor was not ideal. The way the facility is set up it looks great. However there needs to be changes to accommodate the large number of people and the noise that comes with it. Concrete and steel do nothing to make the levels enjoyable. We all want to be there with friends to enjoy. But if we can't even have a conversation whats the point?  I really hope Sunking is listening!  This is a fantastic place. I dont want to have any negatives keeping me from being there to enjoy.
name: Jessie

text: I have been eating here for 27 years, it will always be one of my favorites places to go. Weekday for lunch is when I will go.  Rice, pepper steak, chicken and an egg roll is usually what I always order.  Owner is a hard worker and has been doing this ever since I came there the first time at 15 years old.  He used to be open on Sunday's, glad he isn't anymore as he needed a day off.  Can't go wrong with some good old Hot Wok!
name: John

text: I've been going to this restaurant since I was 8 years old, currently I am 25 years old. You can imagine we've had our ups and downs at this restaurant over those many years, but the downs are so few and far between and the ups are so many. One thing to be said about this restaurant is the food is consistent, if you order the chicken enchiladas 1 year come back and order it again it'll be the same thing. I've been getting ground beef tacos from them ever since we started going there. Occasionally I'll drift to a different item but that is my go-to since I was eight up until now same taste same flavor I can rely on what I'm getting. Overall this is a great restaurant that is ran by great people.
name: Zachary

text:
Our favorite NEW healthy music city food place to eat.  If you're looking for delicious & nutritious breakfast, lunch, brunch (our preference) and dinner, this spot is for you!

My wife just became vegan for health reasons, and it's hard to find places that have "normal" food, prepared vegan, gluten-free, sugar-free and delicious.  True Food is our go-to restaurant that checks all the boxes for us.

Try the healthy banana pancakes, if you'd like a sweet "treat" (brunch only).  And our favorite bowl of food is the Ancient Grains bowl.  We seem to order it every time.  Probably because it's SO tasty and nutritious.

You can make reservations on their website or through Resy, and we suggest that for sure - it's busy for a reason!!
name: Mike

text: Recommended by a friend. Atmosphere feels like a ship. Live entertainment. Waitress was knowledgeable and very patient with our table of seafood allergies. Food Was excellent! Didn't give five stars because the non-seafood options were limited. Husband loved the stuffed flounder. A definite stop if you are a seafood lover!

I think when you're walking up to a place and their main exterior decoration is just the words: "STEAK PANCAKES STEAK PANCAKES, etc." You know what you can expect. & You would be right, simple, straight forward tasty - FOOD. Served up by staff who know what tf they are doing because they have been doing it the right way forever.
When I went I had a skillet, and it was a complete delight. Everything was prepared - just right, I don't know how else to describe it. Not too much of anything, not too little. Great portions for a big eater like myself. 
Just an all around great place and great bang for your buck, go eat at Albert's or don't call yourself an Edmontonian lol

text: We were there on Saturday, Sept. 1, 2018 - got seated right away, sat there while waitstaff kept passing us by and taking orders at other tables.  I got the attention of one of the busboys after 15 mins of waiting, finally a waitstaff came over to take our order.  I ordered the flavor tea when he brought it out and I took a sip, it was just tea - another waitstaff came by and I grabbed her to take my tea back and get me the flavor tea - our waiter came out to explain that someone made the flavor tea wrong, so I was given tea with lemon -we put in our order - just appetizers - 20 mins go by - we grab our waiter - what's going on with our order - other people who came in after us and received their food - he went to kitchen came back out and said there was a mixup that our food would be out in 5 mins.  We waited 30 mins go by - the manager came over and said he would comp our bill - all we had to pay for was the two ice teas - he would go get our order - another 15 mins go by and someone brings out our appetizers - the bill came and the manager only took off $6.00.  This was the worst service - lots of excuses - and the manager lied about taking of the appetizers that we waited almost 1 hour to get.  Never go to this restaurant.  The worst ever!!!!

text: I was highly disappointed in my experience here. First off they don't take reservations, we had to "call ahead." We arrived and were seated right away. We ordered our beverages which came at a timely manner. But some of the mugs were dirty. We received new ones. Then we ordered avocado toast as our appetizers (one plain, one with eggs). They were both very delicious and came out after our drinks were served. We asked for side plates so we could share. Every plate was dirty. We asked for new ones because they were all dirty (food residue) and the waitress looked at us like we were insane. We ordered our breakfast and it took almost 45 minutes. Our waiter who was very nice brought out chips and salsa for us. We did not want chips and salsa we wanted our food. We kept wondering why he brought us this. We figured it was because the food was taking so long. Then finally our food arrived. Well here comes another problem. I ordered the lemon blueberry pancakes. They were just blueberry pancakes (which I don't like). It had no lemon and nothing else that the menu described (I would have ordered something else). Then the other orders were completely wrong. One person ordered no mushrooms in their eggs and as it was being placed on the table you could see it was chock full of mushrooms (had to be taken back) and the other asked for no potatoes. There were potatoes on the plate. And she asked for other things to be included and they weren't. Both had to be remade. The manager came over and apologized and took both meals off the check. We were a little worried because one person at the table special ordered her meal and the waiter wasn't writing anything down, so we though he might get it wrong. My biggest problem with this is that people have food allergies and if they eat something they asked to be replaced they could get sick. I wish they would be more careful. They gave us a gift card to come back (I don't live near there so I gave it to a friend). I was very disappointed. I will not be returning or recommending to anyone. I gave 2 stars because the food was good. Everything else gets 1 star.

Our waitress was horrible and kept forgetting things that we asked for, we constantly had to ask her for our drinks and run her down for things we needed as a first time customer going into this establishment on a "what they call a karaoke night," (which we were unaware of it being Karaoke night) we were unaware that they automatically charge you 18% gratuity fee due to sitting on that side of the room until our waitress brought us the check. When speaking with the manager he constantly said that they couldn't remove the gratuity off our ticket...which we all know that's a LIE!!!! We weren't disputing our food however didn't want to pay that amount in gratuity due to how our service was rendered. But the excuse we got was it's plastered on the walls and they can't remove it off our check, and we still have yet to see these signs!! With that being said....how many of you go into an establishment for the VERY FIRST TIME and read the rules on the wall? Not to many of us do...because you would expect for your waitress to provide that information. Our service was so horrible to the point both the manager and owner had to bring us our drinks and food....but all of a sudden you don't remember doing this because you were too busy!! I'm sure the manager don't remember asking us how was things going and hearing us say it wasn't good either....because you were too busy walking away from us once we started complaining. I DON'T CARE how busy a place is during any hour, if you have complaints about your establishment the one thing you don't do is tell your customer you can't do anything about it. text:
I am so happy I stumbled upon this place.  It's in South Tampa, but just a tad off the beaten path.  I've been twice and both times have been excellent.  The food and service are five stars.  The ambiance is nice too--casual yet relaxing.  

For starters, the complementary bread and dip is so good.  It's so much more interesting than the standard bread and butter.  The dip appears to be a mix of olive oil, spices and tomato.  

Both times, I have ordered the chicken saute with red sauce.  It's packed with super fresh veggies (onion, garlic, peppers, mushrooms) and tons of chicken.  It's zesty and full of flavor without being heavy or greasy.  It's so good!  It comes with deliciously rustic bread over top.  

The prices are very reasonable for the freshness and quality.  I've had leftovers both times and my dish is $16.  

I tried a cup of hot tea, Turkish tea, this time as well.  It was amazing!  

Honestly, this place is so good.  If you want flavorful, fresh and somewhat healthy food, come here!

And it was walking distance from our hotel. When we found out it was a hotel restaurant, i was worried. But we were seated promptly and our waiter was so nice, we started to feel at ease .

We started with the crab bisque and the soup du jour, both were really nice. Nice pieces of blue crab on the bisque.

Then we order a wedge salad that was very large and delicious.
We tried the Trenasse trio with Louisiana crawfish pie, delicious fish menieure and lamb chop, everything on our plate was absolutely delicious!!
Good selection of wine by the glass since we didn't order a bottle.

The dessert was lavender infused creme brûlée, my favorite.

Would recommend and come back without hesitation.
name: Carolina

text: Love this place. The sushi is so fresh. The owner and staff are lovely. I can't say enough good.  They are always welcoming. I get a lot of takeout but eat in as well. text:
When you procrastinate at work, you catch up on reviews that may or may not be 6 months in the making (Sorry, Party Fowl!).

Anywho, I consider myself a Bloody Mary connoisseur, and one night last June my husband showed me this Facebook video that did little exerpts on cool drinks, and there was the GORGEOUS Bloody Mary with what looked like fried chicken on top and without thinking I told him we HAD to go. So out of curiosities sake, I googled the place, and to my surprise... It was in Nashville! My husband and his family are from the area, so we quickly starred planning our trip there, and decided the eclipse in August would be the best because it was also my birthday. Then I found out they only make SEVEN a day and ONLY on Saturday and Sunday, so I quickly got on my handy dandy Yelp app and made reservations for that Sunday the moment they opened at 10 and made sure to request the special Bloody Mary because it was my birthday and we drove all the way up from New Orleans just to try it. I literally had nightmares starting a week before we got there that they would have forgotten and I'd show up and not get my bloody mary, that's how serious my desire to try this place was. Saturday night I even messaged them on Facebook to make sure they had my RSVP, and they quickly confirmed that as well as putting a special note that it was my birthday and to make sure I had a nice visit!

We showed up 30 minutes before they openes, and were the first in line of a very long line that quickly formed (either the brunch scene is a big deal in Nashville, or Party Fowl is that amazing, or both!) but we were quickly seated and though it took a few minutes, our waiter came over and greeted us and we promptly ordered the "brunch for two" (that's what they call it) and thankfully my nightmare didn't come true and they were able to make one for me! It took a few minutes to make, but it was totally worth it.

The "Brunch for Two" is a 55 oz bloody Mary topped with two Nashville hot Cornish hens, a whole avocado, two scotch eggs (pickled eggs covered in sausage and fried) olives, celery, and fried okra. The bloody Mary itself is eh, kind of standard and nothing crazy seasoned, but the hot chicken drippings gave it some kick! However, the toppings definitely made up for it. The hot chicken was so yummy and moist on the inside, crispy on the outside, and just the perfect kick. The avocado was a mice touch to cool my mouth down. I didn't think I'd like the scotch eggs, they seemed like an acquired taste, but I actually found them quite nice and enjoyed them after all! For $50, it's definitely worth it, but you'll be feeling the buzz for a while.

 It was definitely a struggle to finish it, I won't lie. Our favorite part was when this waiter Joe came up to us to check on us and told us he had never seen two people finish it before, hahaha, but he said it made sense after we confessed we were from New Orleans (lol). This was definitely a bucket list item and I'm super glad I was able to cross it off my list, and we will definitely be back next time we're in Nashville so I am try other stuff on their menu because the yelp pictures and the descriptions look and sound absolutely incredible. Thanks for making my birthday So special and helping me on my quest to find the greatest Bloody Mary (this is 100% still the winner).
name: Elizabeth

text:
Mmm pastrami heaven! On the west coast we have delis that charge $17-$20 for pastrami sandwiches that don't taste as good so getting one at Hershel's for $10-11 was a treat. Came here using a Groupon. Can not recommend this place. Food was edible but certainly could not be called good. I had quesadilla carnitas. text:
I'm a vegan of 12+ years with tons of allergies (dairy, tree nuts, etc.), and an out-of-towner so that's the perspective you're getting here.
Which means, I know my shit as far as vegan restaurants.

First, the reviews saying this place is too pricy- you have to understand the factors that go into that. First, the food you source will be more expensive because there's not the demand, or the abundance as factory farm meat, and often the owner sources from reputable places and chooses organic options. That drives the food cost up considerably. Secondly, the demand for vegan food isn't anywhere near the demand for omnivorous food, so having a smaller customer base but keeping your doors open makes it so you have to either compromise on cost or quality. Not sure about y'all, but I'll always choose a place that opts for quality. Lastly, since it is a niche market and customers are clearly willing to pay their prices, why would they lower them? This isn't fast food, and I hope the prices mean the staff gets a living wage.

Ok, enough ranting. On to my review!
Be still my vegan heart guys- this place is awesome. I'm in town for a conference and just assumed I'd be microwaving Amy's meals in my hotel (you know, like a cool kid), considering NOLA food tends to be heavy on either meat or dairy. Discovering this place 15 mins walking (or cheap uber ride) distance from my hotel was fate. The menu is extensive, the servers are polite and helpful (I asked one about how safe it would be to walk alone to a brewery nearby and got an honest answer), and my meal was bomb. I got the fried tofu nugget things and waffle. The nuggets were tofu done WELL (fellow veggie people know tofu it hit or miss depending on the chef), didn't have too much batter-to-tofu ratio, and was seasoned in a way where it had a pleasant kick that contrasted nicely with the sweetness of the syrup. The waffles were light and tasty! My mimosa was 99% bubbly, which is freakin' awesome. When I wimped out halfway through they offered to add more fresh squeezed OJ and put it in a to-go cup.
Which leads me to my embarrassing moment of having raised my voice a little too much in surprise when I said, "holy crap you can drink in the streets here!!!" (Duh Tairi, what did I think Mardi Gras was.)
After sounding like an idiot, I paid and walked to the cute vegan boutique next door sipping my mimosa and wondering when I'll ever not embarrass myself in new situations.
 
10/10 would joyfully yell obvious facts at a server here again.
name: Tairi

text: Great ambiance and great happy hour apps. Came here and loved it. Would have liked a few more options for apps, and longer HH hours. Other than that, Great service, unique dishes. We will be back!

Normally, this is something that would turn me around at the door but my husband saw that the reviews were great and wanted to try it. text:
The 3/5 rating is based upon the service and food combined. I've been to the eagle numerous times. 9/10 good service. My friends and I went on a Saturday night and were told it would be an hour wait so we went to a bar down the street. Upon receiving the text that our table was ready, we were seated in the very back room.

I've been seated back there before, however this time was different. We walked passed atleast 5 empty tables, to the very back where all of the African American people were seated. I hate to make things about race, but this was very strange. The other people mentioned it to us as well. We asked the man who walked pass if he was the manager for that shift, and he said yes but I am getting off of work abruptly, dismissing us. We saw him go pass again and stopped him again! The moment we said this doesn't look right all of the black people in the back room, he immediately moved us, still in the very back but into the main dining area. Service: 6/10 Food: 10/10

text:
Let me start with that I can be hard on people with customer service. I've worked my share of customer service jobs, including retail management and bartending. So I kinda know what is expected as far as providing quality customer service. 
I flew into Tampa today, from Key West. Still in vacay mode and wanting a bloody Mary on my layover. 
I sat at the bar and wasn't greeted by anyone. Several waitresses passed by and saw me looking behind the bar for a bartender. It was 12pm. Maybe 10 customers in the joint. Not one waitress said she'd get a bartender for me, much less even acknowledged me. 
10 mins pass and I move to a table thinking I'd be noticed by a waitress. Sure enough, I was greeted. 
I ordered chips and salsa and a Bloody Mary. 
The salsa was brown.  
Needless to say, I only ate the chips. 
The Bloody Mary was good for desperation. 
My waitress only returned to give me my bill and portable credit card reader while I was only half way thru my drink. Not that I was going to order another of those,  but she didn't know that. So I signed it, cashed out, and left no tip. 
I should have walked further down to Pei Wei instead. Next time I know.

text:
I'm lucky! I have a beautiful woman in my life and we are both foodies. We find the best places to eat! 
I get to eat great treats in the presence of magnificence! 

We stopped in to Kally K's for lunch, not sure what to expect. But, we left highly satisfied and will definitely be going back. 

Antonio, or Tony, took excellent care of us from the moment we entered. He was very polite and made us feel welcome. He immediately took our drink orders, and briefed us on the menu and the Salad Bar. 
He REALLY got my attention when he said there were 2 soups on the bar and one was Clam Chowder! I couldn't wait to pick something off the menu and then get a cup of Chowdah! 

The Clam Chowder was really, really good. Nice chunks of clam and potatoes in a creamy smooth base with lots of taste. Just like it should be!
Funny thing! Up until recently, and I'm talking within the last year or so, I didn't even eat Clam Chowder. My beautiful Fab One convinced me to try some one night, and ever since then I've been on a Chowder Bender! 
I love that Mollusky Medley!

Along with the soup from the Salad Bar, I made myself a nice salad, and other goodies typical for a well stocked bar. Everything was fresh, flavorful and delicious. 

To go with my soup & salad, I ordered the Gyro Sandwich, with fries. What I got was a huge handful of pita packed Wow! The meat was juicy and succulent with that peppery good lamb flavor note. 
And I raved about the Tzatziki sauce that was drizzled over my Gyro!!!! This white bite of dill-liciousness swept me off of my Happy Feet.....I asked, or insisted that Tony congratulate the person responsible for this Heavenly Greek gravy! He did, he did..

Fab one simply ordered the Salad Bar, and started out with a cup of Chowder as well. She smiled the entire time, and I KNOW the look of contentment on that loving face....

Give Kally K's a try, and tell them John & Beth sent ya!

text:
I will review this again when I eat here for dinner, but I felt the need to give an early review.  I had made a reservation for early November because I've been really looking forward to this place opening.  I will likely be cancelling the reservation as I am not as excited to come back after my experience at the bar.  1. The location is an odd choice and quite surprising after seeing the really nice photos of the restaurant.  The outside is steps away from a parking garage.  The bar is steps away from the hotel check in.  Which is also steps away from a large window also facing a parking garage.  While sitting at the bar I was literally being occasionally blinded by the headlights from that garage shining through the window.   2. Way overpriced in my opinion.  I am a big mezcal drinker and I understand how pricey good mezcal is.  That being said I thought the choices were limited and all of the affordable ones I had (12-13 dollars for a 1 oz pour which is less than a full shot) were not great mezcals.  I will continue to go to Tequila's instead for mezcal, who has a far superior selection.   3. We got the guacamole for 2 of us.  Not a good sign when the bartender asked if I wanted 1 or 2 orders.  Since when is a guacamole order only meant for 1?  For 15 dollars you get an mediocre amount of decent guacamole with 3 large tortilla chips.  Yes, 3.  Within 5 minutes we had to ask for another order of these tortilla crisps.  I am convinced it was a mistake that we weren't charged for this additional order.

With all of that said, I am open to seeing how good their menu is beyond the guacamole.  From what I hear the tacos are quite good and hopefully I can update this with a more positive experience.

text:
Vernick is the one restaurant (besides Zahav) they people won't shut up about. Given it's reputation, I expected everything to be exceptional. While I'm more of a 3.5, I'll give Vernick a 3 based on all the hype. 

But I will say that their toast is the best toast in the city. And while the service was slow - it took over 30 mins to get our order in - our server was also sweet - my husband and I were celebrating our anniversary and they gave us a couple of glasses of champagne on the house

The good:
- toast!!! If you get anything at Vernick get the toast. The bread is phenomenal and grilled to perfection. The beef tartare is excellent but there are so many good choices.

- the tuna. Nice light dish, unique preparation with wonderful flavors. A nice modern revamp of tuna tartare. Fusion of European and Asian flavors

- baby artichokes. These were lovely and surprisingly filling. Unique preparation. The name is a bit misleading as the artichokes are lovely and large. Nice blend of textures - roasted artichoke, cream, cheese, and the confit

Didn't deliver: 
We opted to get the larger dishes and wished we stuck with the smaller plates. 

- the sea bass with lobster sauce. I was looking forward to this dish and was disappointed. I thought the flavors would be more dynamic and complex. I like sea bass because it's more meaty and less fishy. Unfortunately my dish was a bit too fishy for me. I did love the gratin but it wasn't amazing enough to make up for the rest of the dish

- desserts. We got the brown butter fianancier and the petit brownie. Neither were exceptional. I was so looking forward to the financier but it was dry and dense. Brownie was ok - nothing special

text:
Short:

For a fine dining restaurant, not incredibly expensive. The bill still will be high but they have sides included that are not a la carte.  You can get away with just ordering a steak and be completely full.  Steak is delicious, menu is large, service was good but was incredibly crowded and loud where we sat.  There is no self parking, only valet.

Long:

Come here for the first time the other night, celebrating my mother's birthday.  When we first arrived, we had to go through Valet, there is no self parking.  At the time, valet is $5 which does not include gratuity.   Walking through the entrance, we are welcomed with a large mirror and lots of red decor everywhere. Give you the impression of royalty.  We waited in the lobby for about 10 minutes to be sat, even though we had reservations.

Once we were called up to be seated. We are walked into a room that looks like a large corridor.  The have several pictures on the walls of some landscape to give the illusion of windows or making the room larger.  It honestly felt a little tight, due to the amount of tables there.  The room was incredibly loud with the amount of guests there and we had to shout in order to hear each other.  If there were less tables, maybe that would help with the noise, but its also good for them they have so many guests. 

Looking through the menu, it was like a book.  I love all the extra information but I felt they could've shorten it a little.  The wine list is enormous, our server was friendly and helpful with any questions we asked.

To start, we ordered the Bern's house steak tartare. First time having this, it is server with several slices of break.  It is rare beef, but you honestly wouldn't even know by the taste.  It was light and delicious.  I recommend you get this if you haven't had it before.

The steak, each entree comes with several sides, french onion soup, salad, baked potato, onion rings, vegetables.  All delicious.  The french onion soup is amazing.  Cheesy and lots of flavor.  One of the best I've tasted so far.

My fiance and myself split a 20z Delmonico steak.  When this came out it was a large hunk of meat.  We ordered it medium rare and our server sliced it in half for us.  I'd say I wasn't incredibly impressed with it.  It was delicious but a bit chewy, not exactly tender.  I had flavor but wasn't out of this world that I was expecting.  I still enjoyed it.

After dinner, we moved to the dessert room.  Which should be a review on its own.  With reservations, you are automatically reserved a table in the dessert room, you just need to inform your server you will be going after dinner.

The dessert room is upstairs and each table feel like its own intimate room.  Our server was great, he went over recommended items and what his favorites were.  Any questions we threw at him, he had no problems answering.  We ordered an array of dessets, too much to list, but they are all delicious.  The prices here aren't actually that bad.  Ranging from 6 to 30 dollars.  

Overall, I'll definitely be here again.  I'll have to try another steak to get a more accurate representation if another steak with live up to their expectations.  Definitely come here for nice evening out with someone special.

text:
I came to Texas Roadhouse for the first time tonight; somehow, this is one of the few chain restaurants I had never been to. I've had some of the best BBQ food in Texas and Tennessee, so I have fairly high standards for BBQ, but found that this was pretty decent food in comparison. I LOVE their rolls - they were super soft and fresh, and the cinnamon butter is awesome. 

The portions here are huge and more than enough food for dinner and lunch the next day (and possibly the day after). The restaurant gets packed on weekend nights and the actual food service slows proportionally, but our server was still attentive to our table with refilling bread and drinks. If you're looking for good BBQ without traveling south, Texas Roadhouse is worth the trip.
name: Ashley

text:

We had a nice waitress but wasn't very attentive; the kitchen took over an hour to deliver our food which consisted of their signature gumbo, a burger, and a breakfast dish. Even the waitress knew it was bad and gave us free dessert.

text: The sushi from here is pretty great. I typically order through Ubereats. Today, a Sunday, I decided to stop by and try their lunch special while I had the time. I asked the server for their lunch menu and he tells me it's no longer happening. I made sure to check the website before driving out there - lunch special Monday through Sunday. He then grabs his manager when I question it, and he comes to my table and asks how he can help me. I let him know I am looking to order from their lunch menu as it was 1:45 and from what I saw on their website, lunch ends at 2:30. He tells me the lunch menu is no longer valid on Sundays, only Monday through Friday. I kindly let him know he should update the website, so this doesn't happen again. Instead of doing anything to accommodate and keep my business, he proceeds to sarcastically say 'maybe I should' with an annoyed look on his face. There are plenty of great places to have sushi and Thai in Nashville without dealing with the nasty customer service. Nashville is HUGE. There are tons of people that are going to go to your website and see that you have a lunch special. If you've stopped it on the weekends, no problem! But update your website and don't be nasty to a customer when they question it.
name: Sara

text:
For starters the food is very good. 
BUT, I've been twice in the last 2 weeks on relatively slow nights - Friday & Thursday and the service is terrible !
Walk in to no hostess both nights. 
When someone does recognize you are waiting to be seated "Oh, I'll be right there". Not, may I help you, how many in your party, where can we seat you ? NOTHING. 
So we seat ourselves. 
No waitress for 10-15 minutes. 
Give the whole order - drinks, food, etc. 
Drinks come out in an ok time frame. 
Food 25-30 minutes later. Remember, maybe 20 patrons in a restaurant that probably seats 150. Very slow evening for them. 
When the food does arrive, my wife's is right, my sons is right. BUT oh no, mine was made wrong. They have to do it over. Waitress tells me it will be out as soon as they can make it. AS SOON AS THEY CAN MAKE IT ??  WTF !!
I've already waited now over a 1/2 hr. Maybe 45 minutes in total. 
Then she stops back to our table with no food and says "it will be out shortly". 
I told her don't even bring it. 
The service at this location just doesn't deserve anything other than a complete thumbs down. 
I won't go back. Too many other good places to choose from in this area. 
If you have all night, great. Otherwise pass on this establishment. It's just not worth it.

text: Truly a New Jersey treasure! Grounds For Sculpture is a great place for families, for date-day, for friends, and to go stroll alone. Sculptures are fantastic works of art intermingled with plants and flowers. It's an art and botanic experience. If you purchase tickets online in advance you can save a couple dollars on entry! I went with a friend and spent about two hours on the grounds. There is a restaurant within the property but it closes quite early, we couldn't sit down for dinner at about 6pm on Sunday. I would highly recommend attending. We were talking with a groundskeeper and he told us about some hidden sculptures. So here is the secrete: next to the large lake there is a small pond with sculptures surrounding it and a small door that reads "keep out" if you push the door open there is a "party" going on behind it. That's all I will say! Check it out for yourself.

text: Great news! Life jackets not necessary on this water adventure. Gimmick-y... eh, not really. Tourist trap... maybe. Loved by kiddos... definitely! I have to admit that most of the dining we do as a family are mostly restaurants that don't have entertainment like this. Yes, think under the sea and yup, feel like a mermaid for the time being. It wasn't fine dining by any means, but it kept my daughter engaged and amazed and I always love seeing her happy. The fams and I went there for an early dinner, which worked out perfectly because we were able to be seated immediately. Our server was very courteous and attentive. Southern hospitality at its finest. We totally did not expect the best service, but we got it! We ordered a seafood combo platter that we were all able to share. It was complete with shrimp, lobster and crab cakes. My daughter loved getting up to walk around the aquarium. There were so many awesome sea creatures, so it was a treat to see. The ambience was dim, but not too dark where we could not see our food. It was a few days before Christmas, so we were expecting it to be packed. Thankfully because we arrived earlier, we beat the crowds. After eating, we still stayed around to look at the aquarium and visit the gift shop (connected to the restaurant. It's located inside the Opry Mills Mall, so after eating, you can walk around for some retail therapy, too! I highly recommend this for parents with little ones, but the adults will enjoy it just as much.
name: Rebecca

text:
What else can a Yelper say about Talula's Garden that has not been written about in the 1500 plus reviews already.  Talula's had been on my radar for years and I finally made it happen.  On a nice breezy no-humidity weekday evening, I made an early reservation and was able to choose a table in the cozy outdoor dining space.

For our first visit we decided to share our way through the menu, we started with the Mini Mushroom, "Pizza", Handmade Flatbread, Buffalo Milk Taleggio, Thyme and Sweet Onion. It was a great start to the evening.

For the pasta dish we chose the Ricotta-Goat Cheese Ravioli, Preserved Lemon Sauce, Fresh Green Asparagus, Chives and Chili Spiced Breadcrumb. More Please :))

For the Main dish (so many great choices) we decided on the Pan Roasted Scottish Salmon, Crispy Curried Potato Croquettes, Green Garlic Sauce, Asparagus and Roasted Radishes. It was a great choice.

For dessert we went ventured solo and selected the PB&J Crunch Sundae - Strawberry sorbet, peanut butter ice cream and rice crispy crunchies.  I went with the Strawberry Mascarpone Cheesecake with roasted strawberries, black pepper shortbread and balsamic syrup. Both enjoyed with an espresso.

The service from the team at Talula's Garden was fantastic, attentive, on point, not rushed and pleasant. All in all a great experience.
name: Fred

text:
My wife and I have dined at Krazy Kat's several times with mixed experiences relative to food, service and the venue itself.  Last night's meal at Krazy Kat's was fair to poor.  

We both started with the heirloom tomato caprese salad.  The main ingredient-heirloom tomatoes were not appealing in looks or taste.  They were generally huge slices of a thick, overly meaty fruit.  The chef should reconsider the cultivar of heirlooms he is using and select a juicier one.  The rest of the salad-arugula , cheese, dressing-were OK but couldn't rescue the salad.

I had the wild boar spare ribs for my entree, my wife had the lobster.  The ribs were prepared with a pedestrian bbq sauce.  They were cooked well-fall off the bone done-ness but there was nothing that would cause me to recommend them.  The lobster tails were simply over cooked.

The server was nice and attentive but resisted helping in our selections.  The bus boy was more engaged.

This time around we were seated in the back sun room which is significantly nicer than the main area which is excessively dark.

My wife had a very good Chardonnay, I had Sprite.

The bill was $150 including the tip.

A solid 2 Star event.
name: Joe

text:
So. Passing thru DE heading south decided to pop in this place. "Outside sign" suggested it was like a "food court"
   Inside there was a huge  buffet offered for $18 bucks but you could also order from the menu.   Buffet had lots of varying meats to choose from and many salads (seafood tuna pasta lettuce etc) but I decided I'd try the flounder off the menu

I could tell it's a pre-breaded frozen piece of fish they simply thawed and set atop shredded iceberg. No season no flavor and the breading falls away from the fish each time you use your fork
    
As my meal mate stated (she ordered shrimp fajita) it's basically an over priced diner.  

Menu with too many options.  Duplicated options with minor variations. 

Sorry I can't recommend the place for food. I asked were the mashed potatoes from scratch.  Was told no.  Restaurants shouldn't be allowed to serve potatoes from a box 

Lots of tvs for many sports options, so that was good. And I liked their reisling  wine

Waitstaff was ok. Ambiance: a mix of sports bar and older folk at a buffet.   No line no waiting. Didn't take long for food to come out

My $10flounder dinner ended up being $27 after tip.  Paid $4 for a side and $9 for the wine    Hence my thighs on overpriced

For the sides not to be homemade they shouldn't cost $4.  Coleslaw was ?4oz perhaps. Which I guess is a serving size: but since they aren't made by the chef, should have two come w a meal and if you have to pay, pay no more than $2

For that: shoulda ordered the $18 buffet and got dessert. Not sure I recall seeing any vegetables on the buffet, but may have overlooked

text:
Okay so I'm going with 4 but my husband and I debated for quite some time over whether to give 3 or 4 stars. 
Beautiful restaurant. Check out my pics. Very nice place for special occasions and it happens to be our wedding anniversary. 
We made a reservation which was easy to do an hour beforehand. Glad we did because they really started to get busy after 6:30. We had to wait for a few minutes but the person showing us to our table apologized profusely. 
The dining area was large but we had a quaint table for two in the corner. Next time I may request a table by the window overlooking the river and apparently Philadelphia skyline I'm told. (We're from out of town )
Dress is casual, people wore everything from dresses to shorts. 
Food was delicious for the most part. Calamari was ok, nothing spectacular. Crab stuffed mushrooms-delicious! House salad was the best I've had-really. Caesar salad was good too. Crabby delight was light and delicious, salmon was ok. I would prefer my husband 's salmon. I've had juicier salmon. But the desserts tho!  The cheesecake was as light as a feather and the lemon cello was phenomenal. 
The downside and why I feel wushu washy on the four stars is that we weren't impressed with our server. She did not give us her name, no intro at all. She did not check on us often, my water glass was almost empty before it was refilled, she cleared our table of used dishes but left my empty plate of marinara sauce from the calamari after coming back to the table 3 times, but the kicker was bringing out dessert forks and my husband took a bite of his cheesecake realizing too late that spinach was on it. When we let her know she chirped 'ok' and announced she'd bring another. There was no apology, acknowledgement that that was gross, unacceptable, nothing. 
Everything else with the restaurant just didn't match up with the level of service we received from her. It was mediocre. I would still encourage anyone to try this restaurant and hopefully you won't get the server we had...whatever her name is.
name: Stacey
