text:
I specifically asked if anyone had a recommendation for banh mi in Nashville that serves pate in the sandwich, and I was recommended to try Hoang Tofu. There have been too many times that I've ordered banh mi in Nashville and have been severely disappointed that some or several of the main components of a banh mi are missing.  I'm Lao, and in Lao we call banh mi "kow-jee pate" which literally translates to "pate bread," so the fact that I get served banh mi without pate makes me very sad. It's a critical element of the sandwich and adds a unique richness. 

All that is to say, Hoang Tofu DOES put pate in all of their sandwiches (except probably the tofu one - I didn't clarify). I only ordered two sandwiches to try, #1 cha dac biet (special) and #4 BBQ pork. The French bread is buttery and flaky, and just crusty enough to not tear up the roof of my mouth when biting into it. Y'all know what I mean. Both sandwiches had pate, cilantro, cucumber, mayo, Maggi seasoning, and pickled carrots and daikon. The only topping missing was jalapeno, but they absolutely nailed the rest (especially daikon and Maggi). The #1 had almost all the meats expected, but no headcheese, but maybe Nashville's not the market for that. The #4 BBQ pork wasn't really barbecued or grilled, so it lacked that charred flavor, but still good overall. 

They also serve a few other noodle soup dishes like pho and bun rieu, but I did not try them. My boyfriend tried the pho, and as a pho addict, he said it was good. 

As others mentioned, Hoang Tofu also sells other items that you can grab and go. I also saw them bringing in fresh tofu, so I assume that you can buy tofu here too. I went home with some steamed sticky rice with mung bean and pork wrapped in banana leaf, one of my favorites. Will definitely be back for this as well as the buy 5 get 1 free banh mi deal! I bet you can also order the veggies "outside" the sandwich if you order a large quantity.
name: Caterina

text:
I came to New Orleans for a conference and it was at Hilton New Orleans Riverside. Since I have been to NO several times, I was excited to stay at a different property overlooking the River. So I arrived with excitement that soon changed to a bit of frustration.

As a frequent traveler for business and a Hilton Diamond member, the check-in process at this particular hotel is one of the worst I have experienced in recent years. Completely understanding there were many conferences going on during my stay, the front desk on the Hilton Members side was totally understaffed when a colleague and I arrived at 2 pm. After waiting in line for an exceptionally long time, I was waited on by Derrick (I believe was his name). First, he seemed completely out of it so not sure if he worked the night shift through the day but he should have been napping instead of working. Once he checked me in, without acknowledging my Diamond status, he promptly told me that my room was not ready and that he would text me when it was. Now, I never throw my status around, however, I arrived with a co-worker who has no Hilton status at all and he was able to get a room. My co-worker was generous enough to allow me to park my luggage in his room while I waited for the text. His room was extremely nice with a river view--I bring this up for a reason you will soon hear about.

It did not take that long for the text to come through thankfully, so I went to the front desk to Derrick where I waited until he finished with his current guest. Now, I did bypass the long line as I thought I would be able to just get my key, but as soon as Derrick finished with his current guest, he called the next guest ignoring me standing there. I interrupted by saying that I just need to get my key. All he said was, "You have to wait in line." I reminded him that I checked in earlier by him and just needed to get my key and he again said that I had to wait in line. So, after waiting in line again for a rather long time I met Sunshine. She did everything right. She thanked me for being a Diamond member, offered me bottled water and gave me a coupon for breakfast for 10% off food. Now, wonderful Sunshine stated that due to my inconvenience she was upgrading me to a Premier Suite. Well, that was wonderful and made my day until I got to my room and realized that it looked exactly like my co-workers room, except I did not have a river view--not so premier. During my stay, we had meetings in my other co-workers room (in tower 1 and 2) and all had a river view and tower II a bigger room than I did. This certainly does not sound like I received a premier suite, or maybe everyone gets a premier suite. 

There is a nice-looking restaurant in the hotel, but it was so busy I never ate there. 

All that being said, the rest of my stay was great and the staff friendly.
name: Eddie

This place was always on my list of places I wanted to try but never found the right time and mood for it. Finally today I gave it a shot at lunch. Being an architectural designer, I loved the interior design and industrial look of the restaurant. The appealing river front outdoor seating and bar area would also make it a great spot to hang out and have a drink or so. We were a party of two and seated immediately even though it was during rush hour at lunch time. 
My friend and I both ordered a drink (a bit pricey- $7 for a draft beer) which arrived fairly quick. I ordered three sisters stuffed portobello and my friend ordered a burger. The food was brought to us after 15 to 20 minutes wait which was understanding at that time od day. But at least expected to receive the right food I have order after the long wait... my order came as a portobello burger which I could count that as an honest human error. My portobello  burger came with a side of mashed potatoes which was in my opinion a bit dry and it was served with some popcorns. In conclusion I might go back to this place to grab a few drinks with my friends after work but would not order any food.

Ordering at the counter/register and yes you do ge a Red Blinky Light Coaster RBLC when your tray is ready for pickup.

Parking can be a tricky at times during the Summer months. This place gets real busy, the kids really like to party here. Nice picnic like benches and tables for that in the park feeling on the grass.

Get ready for the Pacific Surfliner Choo Choo as it barrels thru like a freight train on the tracks. The kids love it... enjoy.
name: Scott

text: Oh Wawa, you must be the go-to store either in this state or around all of the east coast, because there is one everywhere! Everywhere! No joke. It's a convenient store that also makes and sells sandwiches and hoagies. I got a small Italian style hoagie, about a 7 minute wait, and I thought it was really good. Better than Subway or Jersey Mike's. 10/10. Would return. They also sell individual pieces of candy, so I bought a laffy taffy for .25, thought it was cute.
name: Shanae

text: Not sure why this place has such split reviews, but my experience was mostly fine. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. No big complaints, just a nice meal.
name: User

text: Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. Food was fresh and service was quick. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. It was crowded but still moved along. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Ordered a few things and liked most of it.
name: User

text: The food is just average.  Table service inside is okay.  Whenever I've called for pick up the food is never ready at the time they say it will be so I wind up waiting 15-20 mins.  The worst is delivery.  I have had 3 bad experiences with their delivery from getting the wrong order to not getting the extra toppings I paid extra for and even had to call a couple of times to find out why I was told 45 mins for delivery but it didn't arrive until 75 mins after I called and it was barely warm.
name: Jessica

text: I've written a review about them before and I just have to stress it again. This is the best Indian food in town!!!! If you're looking for a real authentic Indian food this is the real deal. It's so delicious and it never fails to satisfy. My favorite is their chicken makhani and chicken curry. Their naan is so amazing and isn't dry like other places in town.
name: Erin

text: Oh my - I found this bakery on Yelp and because of the reviews here, decided to try it out.  My intention was to buy some cupcakes for my mother-in-laws birthday dinner.  Once I got there, I saw the cakes.  I was in such a dilemma as to what to buy because EVERYTHING looked awesome, I ended up buying 2 cakes because I would have just gotten older before finally making up my mind.  Then I topped it off with some baguettes for good measure.  Well the bread and cakes were a hit!  I try hard not to partake but these cakes were just so beautiful and the reviews were so good that I hade to try it all.  And I was not disappointed!  One of the cakes was a buttery cake with strawberry buttercream inside and the other my favorite of chocolate with buttercream.  Both were the moistest cakes I've ever eaten and the buttercream was light and buttery that just paired so well!  I ate a piece of both unable to resist.  The bread was crunchy and just perfect!  I will be visiting again and again - next trip will be for cupcakes but I'll need to decide which of the 15 varieties to buy before I go or else I'll be bringing them all home!
name: Kristy

text: Tuesday night on the walk home from dinner, we noticed that La Bamba had finally opened in downtown St. Louis.  A little bit of research showed that La Bamba is an offshoot of El Burro Loco in the CWE.  We grabbed dinner there tonight and it was everything we expected.  The margaritas were cold and flavorful, the staff was attentive and courteous, and they kept the chips and salsa well stocked.  We ordered a Fajita Burrito and a Carnitas Chimichanga.  The food was hot, fresh, and hit the spot.  We did not get the chance to try dessert, but noticed they had Tres Leches cake on the menu.  La Bamba is destined to become the Mexican hot spot in downtown.
name: Chuck

text: This place is perfect for first timers. The oysters are top notch. Service is warm and friendly. A little pricey but you get what you pay for. We will be back and highly recommend you try this place.
name: William

text: Lots of stuff to like about this place ..the food, the service , the rooftop seating. Just do yourself a favor and stop by while you are in town. I went with a group and we had a number of items on the menu from the lobster tater tots to the drunken noodles and all were good.
name: Boen

text: Beyond exquisite. They obviously take pride in their cuisine. I can't wait to try other dishes. Truly delicious.
name: Rojas

text:
Bento House is a new Broad Ripple addition where Boogie Burger once was. It is a good place for a quick bite, we had great service, and the meals are super customizable.

Because I went on a Sunday, they were serving the dinner bento all day. I was amazed at everything that came with it. You have a choice of soup; choice of entree; choice of fried rice, steamed rice, or noodles; choice of rangoons or spring rolls; choice of fried or steamed gyoza (dumplings,) shrimp tempura, or edamame; AND a teriyaki chicken on a stick. If bento boxes aren't your thing, you can get a full entree with soups and salads, assorted noodles, or order a la carte.

They have a good selection of bubble tea! I loved the Thai iced tea with tapioca bubbles.

I wouldn't consider this a very "adventurous" Asian restaurant. You have your standard fare--assortments of fried rice, orange chicken, etc. so picky eaters will be satisfied. The flavors are what you would expect, pretty rich and salty! They also offer take-out.
name: Olivia

text: I get the appeal, I just don't totally share it. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. I wouldn't write it off, but I also wouldn't hype it up. It looked better online than it did in person. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..
name: User

text:
What I got:
-American IPA
-Southern-Style IPA
-Red Ale
-Kolsch w/ Hemp
-Imperial Stout
-Beet Hummus
-Pretzel Bites

What I would get again:
-Imperial Stout
-Beet Hummus

I'm kind of on the fence with Dunedin Brewery.  At least I know if I were ever to return, there would be something on the menu worth my "beer buds."
name: Allison

text: Went with family on a Sunday and it was louder than I expected. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. It was crowded but still moved along. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. Kind of landed in the middle for me. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. For the price I expected more than this.
name: User

text: I finally decided to stop in after having a massage and acupuncture upstairs at the Center for Holistic Health. They close early afternoon so I've never been able to catch them open. It's a quaint little café with several tables inside and out. They have a fairly extensive breakfast and lunch menu as well as specialty coffees, baked goods and plain old joe. I had a decaf and a corn muffin. The muffin was delicious and moist. Coffee was decent; unremarkable. I would definitely stop in again and try something more substantial from the menu and one of their artisan coffees.
name: Aimee

text: Kat (the GM) provides horrible customer service.  My online order was placed over 1.5 hours ago and I have still not received my sandwich.   Naturally, I call to check the status of the order because I did receive a text notification that the amount has been taken out of my account from Jimmy Johns of $11.50.  Apparently they never received my order because there was an issue with the online website.  They suggest I contact their corporate office to resolve at $11.50 issue.  What a joke.  No compensation, no apology, horrible customer service.  I'm very disappointment with my experience here and guarantee my business will be taken elsewhere.
name: Laura

text: Best hoagie shop around! They make the best Italian hoagies around. Only complaint I have is that they close early and aren't open everyday. Give them a try!!
name: Stacey

text: Great food quality and service. Loved the atmosphere and presentation on the restaurant. Good variety but maybe not for the pickiest eater. Great drinks. Good location. Small but utilize the space well. Outside dining is not ideal when busy outside just regular table and chairs off sidewalk. I would come back.
name: Katie

text: Mediocre, overpriced, overrated. The peanut butter burger was disgusting. Even without the peanut butter, the burger itself was overcooked. This place seems to focus on a hipster ambiance more than the quality of its food. May be acceptable to some, but personally I would prefer to take my money to five guys.... or McDonalds
name: Emma

text:
We brought our Korean foreign exchange student/son here  so that he could have a taste from home. Our service was prompt, and our student couldn't stop smiling from ear to ear. He had the spicy ramen and was more than happy with the food. My family had not eaten Korean food; I can't tell you if this is how it's supposed to taste, but we all thought it was very tasty. We had Bulgogi, Korean BBQ pork & chicken, and Udon noodle soup. If my Korean son gives it a thumbs up, I can only agree. Oh, our boys enjoyed the mochi (ice cream dessert), and I had the coconut sherbet also. It was all yummy! I do recommend this place!
I read some of the reviews stating there was slow service. We did not have that experience. We received everything promptly. Truth be told, I think I would have put up with a bit of a wait because of how happy this food made our son.
name: A

text:
I came all the way from NYC-2 hours and 20 minutes away-for their seafood cheesesteak (chopped salmon, broccoli, onions, ketchup, mayo, cheese, topped with shrimp on a hoagie) and it was worth the drive! That thing is absolutely delicious and seasoned to perfection! The staff is very accommodating and friendly, so feel free to tell them to hold the onions, mayo, etc. if you so desire.

You can dine in if you like, but this is more of an "order to go" spot. I will definitely be taking the 86 mile trek across the bridge again very soon. It's worth it, and this time I'll make sure to order two!
name: Lisa

text: Food in this place is decent and there is plenty of parking. There are several tvs to watch games. They also serve breakfast but the only problem is that the service is very slow. Even when the place is not crowded you could wait  a long time for your meal. The need more help.
name: Tamara

text: This is the BEST PIZZA in Nashville. After spending time in Sicily and missing the Italy Pizzeria. This is the definitely a go to place.
name: Robert

text: Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Price felt a touch high for what it was. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Worth checking out. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait.
name: User

text: I was excited to come check out the place where Fitz's root beer happens. Well I guess the drinks are what makes this place popular, not the food. These ice cream floats are so damn big & everyone gets them which is like a meal in itself. I ended up getting a vanilla mint soda (interesting flavor) as well as the veggie burger w/ onion rings. I had never seen a veggie burger like this before. I was eating it & then had to take it apart to see what it looked like. I asked the server to double check it wasn't meat & she assured me it wasn't. She was very nice. I was skeptical but kept eating. I ended up sick to my stomach through the night & was so annoyed since couldn't sleep thinking about possibly eating meat. I called & spoke to the manager to share what happened & she again assured me that it was the veggie burger. I felt better knowing I hadn't eaten any animals. I later discovered I am allergic to soy & probably what the base of that veggie burger is (not a brand am familiar with since not from the area). So yeah, do like everyone else & get an ice cream float & drink your calories.
name: Kristine

text:
I'm giving it 4 stars because I've been 3 times and I've yet to have a steak that knocked my socks off or "wow'd" me. The entire experience at Berns is like no other. The wine selection is hands down the best in Florida and I'd argue the best in any restaurant.  The service is phenomenal and the level of knowledge the servers MUST have to be on the floor is impressive and admirable. Again I've had bone in NY strip. I've had the bone in ribeye and I've had a porterhouse there. None of them made me say Wow! Like I would have hoped, but I'd be lying if I said I didn't enjoy them. Where Berns really stands out is the entire experience, from the service to the wine room tour to the dessert experience upstairs in the dessert room, the whole ambiance of the evening is incredible and really goes above and beyond what you'd expect from a night out to dinner. I tip my hats to you all for the overall but I'm still waiting for that steak that makes me say... whoaaaaaa!

Special shout out to Bruce our waiter. He was Johnny on the spot with everything and you can tell he takes pride in his work!
name: Jeff

text: My husband I went here for a date night. We went to the roof at first to see the big fuss, it has a nice view and a bar up there and I got a pickers vodka drink, which is amazing . We decided to head downstairs, second floors didn't have much seating area, so we went to the bottom floor. We found two seats at the bar. We order fried pickles and their wings, both were super delicious. The cover band (I can't remember their name) were awesome and that man could sing!!!! It was a great night. Hope to go back again soon
name: Tiffany

text: Ate at this place a few times and the food was good. My most recent time eating here (4/20/2018) I found a long black hair in my food. I do not have hair. Needless to say, I will no longer be eating at this establishment.
name: Benjamin

text: We tried a plain and the special pizza take out and both were great! Nice thin crispy crust. Nice char on the edges without burnt flavor. Only downside is they are cash only. Would definitely recommend trying and will definitely be back!
name: Stella

text:
From the moment we sat down our dinner experience was one of the best we've had in cc Phila. in a very long time. This unassuming place in the Fairmont section of the city delivered one of the best meals we've had in a long time and we eat in cc Phila often. When they bring you their  basket of a hearty bread (cut into small pieces) it's accompanied by a garlic-oil with a dollop of lemon ricotta that is incredible!! With one of their craft beers it was so perfect. The 3 of us each ordered off of the special menu as well as standard menu and we were not disappointed. The apps were out of this world!! Beets, ahi tuna poke w/ taro chips and shaved Brussels sprouts appetizers I would have all over again. Between the 3 of us we had a pasta dish, chicken and hamburger and if we could have licked our plates we would have. We shared the budino dessert out of gluttony but it was worth every calorie!!
Can't wait to go back!
name: Lise

text: Mediocre at best and would have been happier with Taco Bell. Had to ask for a server. Lackadaisical staff. Water glasses were dirty. Fork was dirty. Nacho chips were chewy. Nacho cheese was cold. Hardly any chicken in the buffalo chicken wrap. I could keep going but it's not worth it.
name: Maddie

text: This place is like going to a relative's house for breakfast. The staff is friendly. There's plenty of parking. All of the food is made fresh to order. And the serving sizes are huge. I left stuffed.
name: Jerry

text:
We tried this place a few weeks ago. It was disappointing. To begin, the portions you get are too small for the price. Then on top of that, there's nothing redeeming about the quality of the food. The broth is bland and there is very little meat. It's not the quality you would expect for a restaurant; it's what you might expect from instant noodles (and much more expensive). Also, it took quite long for our food. 
So, I would recommend staying away from this place. There are plenty of better restaurants (even in IV). If you're really looking for ramen, you could make your own instant ramen which would be of comparable quality.
name: Ben

text: Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. The food was good and the service was easygoing. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Nice little spot, decent portions too. The food was good and the service was easygoing. The sauces helped more than I thought they would..
name: User

text: Smoke has gotta be my favorite BBQ in New Jersey.  The food is so good and it has amazing baked beans. The service is very good and nice.
name: Lyle

text: This is our go-to place for a quick cheesesteak!! We have tried multiple cheesesteak spots over the four years we have lived in philly, and we like how Joe's is fast, the meat is minced, and they put a good amount of cheese on there. My favorite is the cheesesteak with whiz and onions and mushrooms with an egg added to it. The 10 inch cheesesteak is huge and although I planned to save half for later, that never happened! It's a BYOB (my favorite) and there is an affordable ACME nearby that sells a variety of beer, or the Bottle Bar East which is more expensive but has more craft beer options. I always bring family here and they also loved it!
name: Jasmine

text: I ate in with my boyfriend. They provided chips and salsa - standard but tasty. We ordered a mango shake, which was good but could have been more flavorful. I had a torta. It was a pretty generous portion - after half the chips and half the shake, I could only eat half the sandwich. Also pretty standard - good but not amazing. Overall, I was satisfied.
name: Faer

text: Uhh not good. I was craving a nice crispy Vietnamese roll with juicy pork.. you know A bahn mi bout came a cold roll buttered with MARGARINE! Cold pork cold everything and the veggies were it even pickled at all. One sliver of cilantro and spruce of jalapeño. I knew when I walked in n saw the decor n it's kinda dirty I should have turned back around... big bummer
name: Murphys

text: OMG, where to begin?  There's a reason for the 1 star, people....  ordered the box deal - two pan pizzas, breadsticks and 6 wings for what ended up being $28, give or take.  Carried out, got home and opened the box to find a hot mess excuse for dinner.  These were supposed to be "pan pizzas", but were flatter than a pancake.  Some of the pieces were practically nothing but crust!  Everything was cold, flavorless and pretty much disgusting.  When I called the store to complain, the manager wanted to challenge me, as though she didn't believe me.  I said I took pictures just to prove a point and she asked me to text them to some random number.  No ma'am.  Do not order here.  The food is horrible, the service is horrible.  Spend your money on better good elsewhere. Never again.
name: Marshall

text:
I love Mexican food and the quality of the food here was not bad. However there are things that other customers should know before coming to this place. Here is what went wrong:
My friend ordered a shrimp plate with guac (guac is $1.35 extra) and the people working there did not know how to properly portion their sizes. They scooped some rice that was such an amount that would be finished in one bite. And she argued with them about giving more rice and the employee gave another worm-sized scoop. Then the other employee came and said he apologized, dumped all of the rice, and gave her one small scoop which was less than before. She ended up paying $13 for the food, and I paid less for more food because I got the taco bowl. I felt bad for her for getting less bang for her buck, and it was the fault of the employees not knowing how to give a healthy amount of food. Long story short, be wary of what you order, and if your portions seem small then consider ordering something else or asking the staff.
name: Irfan

text: Excellent mall. Plenty of food options including destination restaurants like Rainforest Cafe and Aquarium. The stores are standard mall fare but well appointed. The mall is easy to walk and has ramps as well as stairs on level changes. Very good mall near the Grand Old Opry.
name: Steven

text:
I've had two experiences with this particular BWW and I will share both. One was a dine-in, the other was a pick-up.

DINE-IN: Came here around 4PM on a Tuesday. The server was both attractive and attentive, but had just come on her shift and was a bit scattered at the start. As my glass of soda was never empty, I let that slide.

I ordered a large traditional wing (desert heat). I was seated with 5 others at the table and let me tell you, we waited. We waited so long for our food to come out that we were all almost late for our shift at work which started at 6PM. We sat down at 4PM. We didn't leave until 5:40PM. Our server was great, this isn't on her. The kitchen must've only had half a fryer working that afternoon.

PICK-UP: I ordered traditional wings and had 3 orders of boneless. The server/host who took the order down read it back to me exactly correct. When the food was picked up, the receipt had it exactly correct. The food in the bag was the wrong order. Not /only/ was everything boneless, it wasn't even the right flavors AND we were missing a small order of garlic parmesan boneless chicken. 

When I lived in CA, the boys and I regularly ate at BWW for days off work, before work, game days, etc. We've always had good service, food that tasted great, and that came out in a timely manner. The two times I've ordered from this establishment...

-Service: Fine. Had no trouble with the servers. 
-Food: Dry. Very lightly seasoned/sauced. Very little flavor due to that, worst I've had from any BWW.
-Decor: Acceptable. Although smaller than other BWWs, it was clean and had plenty of TVs to keep everyone entertained from all around the table.
-Pick-Up: Got the order wrong. Very wrong. Completely unacceptable.

I will recommend to everyone who will listen NOT to waste their money or time here. The kitchen is slow and the food isn't worth the wait, at least when they get the order right. I'll always be a fan of BWW, especially on game day, but not THIS one.
name: Mr

text: Greeted by a very nice hostess and was seated right away. Prompt service, knowledgeable staff, good atmosphere, prices are as expected, and the sushi was wonderful. What's else can I say other than I would highly recommend this place and I'll definitely be back. Cheers!
name: Stacey

text: Great food and great service!!!! Just a GREAT place to eat. I just love little "finds" like this on a road trip!!
name: Becky

text: Nice size sandwiches, can feed two. Gumbo was good and good customer service. The bar is very pricey, need more selections for happy hours.
name: BD

text: I've had 4 or 5 different burgers here now and they're all so good. This is for sure my favorite burger spot in East Nashville.
name: Allen

text:
We were celebrating a friends birthday on a Monday night. We were promptly seated as there were only three tables with customers. We did not order drinks and ordered our meals quickly. Our appetizer and salads took 90 minutes to bring out. I might be able to understand that it they were busy, but with only three tables not likely. Unfortunately for them, their kitchen is open and we could see the cooks doing nothing. Our waitress would disappear and even the manager tried to serve us someone else's meals. Another 30 minutes later and our entrees came out. The salmon was very dry and over cooked as well as their prime bone in ribeye. Ironically the asparagus and Brussels sprout side dishes came out nearly raw. We were so hungry by this time we ate it anyway. We complained to the waitress and the manager never came by (only one other table by then).  Three hours of "fine dining" later we paid the bill.
Normally I would never had done a poor review, but we complained to their corporate office and never heard a word back. We too will never be back.
name: J

text:
IF I COULD GIVE THIS PLACE SIX STARS I WOULD!! Just an incredible experience. My friend and I ended up spending nearly 4 hours dining here, and neither of us wanted to leave. 

Appetizers:
We started with the foi gras which was incredible. The bread, the strawberry rheubarb, the candied ginger: all made with such attention to detail. The taste was somehow better than the presentation, which was beautiful. 
We also had french onion soup. They weren't shy with the cheese and it was the best french onion soup I've ever had.

THE STEAK:
We shared a 16oz chatteubriand. My friend wanted it medium rare and I wanted it medium. NO PROBLEM. They cooked it medium rare cut it in half and then sizzled mine again to make it medium. The meat was cooked to perfection for both of us. Steak came with a sweet carrots (amazing), a baked potato with chives and onions (nothing special), and garlic strings (meh).

We then toured the kitchen and the wine cellar. (Yes, ANYONE can choose to do this). If that doesn't show how confident a kitchen is, then I don't know what does. The wine collection was incredible. I don't drink and don't know anything about wine, but I was captivated by the presentation, and mesmerized by the cellar itself.

DESSERT:
Lastly, we went to the dessert area. You get your own private dessert room with multiple radio stations. The dessert menu is quite extensive. My friend ordered the macademia nut ice cream. He said it was the best ice cream he's ever had. I'm lactose intolerant and I agreed. We both paid the price for it later, but it was well worth it. I got a trio of things called Brown Sugar, the highlight was definitely the chocolate chip cookie dough cheesecake. The brown sugar blondie was also incredible. The ice cream sandwich was standard.

A great experience. If you are in Tampa, you have to make time for Bern's, i'm so glad I did!
name: Tareq

text:
Great food and bourbon selection

Very clean and warm spots wife loved the cold beer

Don't miss this place on your next visit to NO

text: The food was outstanding and it's a great atmosphere. I ordered the Veal and it was cooked perfectly.

We come here all the time and if I could just have a trough of the little tasting soup they give u at the beginning of the meal, I'd die happy. Tamals are my favorite! I would tell you about the food, but It is 45 minutes in and we still dont have the sandwiches we ordered. Place is half full, ordered 2 hot sandwiches.  Not sure what is taking so long. 
And that was after we were told they dont make one of the sandwiches on the menu. Not a good forst experience

text: First time here. Good food and great service. Love the big patio. We will definitely be back.

text: It was crowded but still moved along. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. Will be back. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable.
name: User

text: The music was louder than it needed to be. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Glad we tried it. It looked better online than it did in person. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Nice little spot, decent portions too. They were out of one thing I originally wanted..
name: User

text:
I ate there the other day and I'm not very satisfied. Its good bar food I suppose, but the more I think about it the more upset I am. As I was eating in the restaurant (which was very small and has almost no parking) I looked outside the window and saw a delivery man with a dolly loaded full of boxes. Very large boxes that were red with some white in places and had bold black lettering. Very large boxed that appear to very reminiscent of bulk containers of dry ramen noodles. In shock, I watched the man push the dolly all around the building and delivery it to the front of the store. I laughed it off in the moment, but now I am a little upset. I could've made instant ramen at home with the same broth, which was what appeared to be a large container of College Inn chicken broth, and put some leaner meat in and more toppings. Speaking of the pork, it tasted fine but was ridiculously fatty. Like there were only a few chuncks of meat encased in fat. In addition, the karaage (which tasted fine) seemed to have been purchased as well. The texture of the chicken, in addition to how the batter and meat was pressed, reminded me of some I had gotten frozen before. Looking at this reviews, it's almost sad to see people cheer the restaurant on. The comments of "the noodles were bland" or hard make sense. They were instant. The shoyu ramen tasted fine but it was something i could make at home. Save your money and buy some cup noodles.

Edit: 
The karaage starters is like 5 or 6 (being generous) small chicken nuggets, but i would suggest skipping it. The ramen portion is so big that you probably won't  have room for both. In addition, I dont recommend the ito green tea they have. I love tea and it did not taste good to me. On a positive note, the service was fine.
name: Had To Make Account To Review

text:

Definitely was full at the end, portion sizes are big, but the chef cooked the fish with too much lemon flavor and pork chops were dry. My honest opinion, wonder if this restaurant would still be in business if it weren't for the fixed three course menu price. The restaurant was empty, weird ambiance, looks like it was previously a diner with the grille in the back.

Our server was super nice, and there was a pain in the ass kid at the next table over, but I can't kncock them for that.

Cool place.

text:
Before you even walk into Pine State Biscuits, you know it's going to be good. I mean, it's biscuits. How can it not be good? Breakfast is my favorite meal. Not just of the day, but of all-time. And biscuits are one of my favorite breakfast items on any menu. All that being said, Pine State didn't disappoint. 

For my first time, I kept my order simple and got the Reggie. But let me tell you, no biscuit at Pine State is merely simple. The fried chicken is succulent, salty and sweet in all the right ways. The cheese is melty perfection, and the bacon is crisp. But the gravy and the biscuit are quintessential southern goodness. Put all those factors together and you get one delectable breakfast. Seriously, I was in breakfast heaven.

I'm also a huge Bloody Mary fan, and Pine State didn't disappoint here either. I'm a fan of depth over pure heat. Don't get me wrong, I can handle the heat, but I prefer to experience layers of flavor in a Bloody Mary. Pine State's version is deeply layered, equally dominated by the flavors of garlic, spice, brine, tomato, you name it. Unfortunately, I don't have a picture, but the manager actually came over and told us a bit about their prized recipe. If I remember correctly, the pickled green bean (?) garnish is local to Portland, which added a level of detail that goes back to the restaurant's Portland roots. 

My boyfriend, Aaron, had the McIsley. I'm not a huge fan of mustard, so it wouldn't be my first choice, but the added pickles and honey perfectly offset the typical overwhelming mustard flavor. Being the mustard fiend that he is, he enjoyed it immensely, so I'd say if you're into that kind of thing, go for it. 

Finally, we both treated ourselves to Pine State's seasonal Pop Tart, which was S'mores at the time. Let me tell you, it's a winner. Completely authentic and wholesome, and so decadent. Fair warning though, these babies sell out quick, no matter the seasonal flavor. If you want to order one more towards brunch or lunch, they may be out.

The service is great considering how busy they always are. Be prepared for a line and difficulty finding seating, but it's worth it if you're patient and looking forward to a delicious meal. Besides, it's not so busy that it's unmanageable. In fact, I tend to think it's a good sign when a restaurant is busy. 

We look forward to going back soon. It's been awhile since our last visit, but we just might have to make the trip downtown to indulge some time soon. 

Happy eating, Yelpers!

text: This place is amazing dumplings are delish and their Boba teas are on point.  Love the small business owner feel very friendly staff

text: I was curious to know what exactly Osteria meant since my italian is limited to naming at least three different types of pasta and a car.  Osteria means a simple and inexpensive Italian reataurant, at least they got the Italian part right. Novio and I were walk ins at about 600pm and they wete fully booked by then and we choose a perfect corner spot in the outdoor bar. MAKE A RESERVATION please, this place is hot, new, and an instagrammers dream so if you arrive anytime after 6, expect to be turned away. The bar was full 15 min after we arrived. We ordered drinks though I cannot remember the names I know I ordered the Moscow Mule and fer ordered what seemed like an old fashioned. Order the Coccoli $19!!!! You will not be dissapointed, balls of dried dough over chese and smoked prosciutto all drizzled with truffle honey ( my mouth is literally salivating right now). Novio and I ordered the Margherits pizza and asked them to out pepperoni on it!!!! The pizza is $18 and we thought it would be a bit larger but alas t'was a personal pizza. We had to order another one because it was so absolutely delicious, easily one of the best pizza I've had in Tampa Bay (don't worry Domenica, I haven't forgotten you). They have $5 valet parking which makes everything so convenient. I wish the portions were bigger so you could get more bang for your buck. An $18 personal pizza is a bit much for me but there are people that don't mind the prices. Entrees are northing cheaper than $18 (caccio e peppe). Honestly this place is absolutely beautiful and I think it is something Tampa was lacking. The only reason I gave it four stars is because I was dissapointed in yhe price to portiom ratio. Osteria is really an amazing restaurant and I would recommend it to anyone, just make sure you make a reservation and go on pay day. Fabio, you did good.

text:
A lovely addition to Rittenhouse! Don't let the name confuse you, this Mediterranean gem of a restaurant opened up just a few weeks ago and has been praised for its delicacies. So I had to check it out. Made reservations on Wednesday for Friday at 6 pm, only three spots where open! 
We reached around 5:50pm on Friday and were almost seated immediately. You will be surprised at the size of this place, it has a full bar upfront and plenty of high tables, inner section has sofa benches or family tables. It is adjoining the Warwick and share their restrooms. 
Our server was with us shortly and asked us if it was our first time. She was happy to have explained the menus and gave us great suggestions on the drinks. We ordered the organized chaos and rest in Pete's. 
For shareable apps we ordered the yoghurt crisps, chili chicken kebabs and the shabazi fries! 
Oh my god each dish was better than the other, the fries were seasoned so well and the harissa aioli was devour worthy. 
We didn't get any entrees, but I am so looking forward to my next visit! 
Ambience 5/5
Service 5/5 
Food 6/5 
Cost 4.5/5 ( slightly expensive, but hey it's Rittenhouse)
