text:
We were really excited to give this place a try. In all fairness, totally didn't think about getting a reservation, but they were able to seat us at the bar really quickly. Beyond their ability to seat us quickly and the hostess being friendly the only other positive thing would be the atmosphere of Husk. They seem to take great pride in presentation of the food.

Our servers were two of the bartenders in the very lower portion of the building. It took close to 5 minutes, in a not very bust atmosphere, for us to get acknowledged. The bartender was exceptionally short with us all night. We had never been to Husk, and this really seemed to set the tone for the night. We were unfamiliar with items on the menu and had questions, she was not knowledgeable about the items and seemed annoyed that she had to look at a food prep list to tell us what things were. To be honest, the couple sitting next to us were more knowledgeable and willing to talk to us than she was.

Like I said previously, the food presentation is top notch, however the portions are small, unless you get the veggie sample plate. The other disappointing thing is that there was literally not one menu item that we looked at and thought, everything looks good. At prices like this they should allow you to make one substitution. I would have gladly paid more money to have been able to get something I wanted to eat. The chicken dish I had was mediocre at best. At $30 for an extremely small piece of chicken breast meat and what would equate to maybe (at best) one baby red potatoes cut up and covered in sauce....far from the quality I was expecting when we selected this place for a nice dining experience while we visited Nashville. See the pictures posted. The potatoes were the best part of my meal. My gf had the veggie plate. It came with a dish of cucumbers, a dish of parsnips and carrots in pesto, a dish of okra, and a dish of one other item. I would probably remember better if the server didn't get annoyed when we asked what the items were because they read through them so fast the first time. 

Looking through the drink menu, I decided to have a cider....typically related to a beer....this was more like an un-sweet wine with a dab of apple flavor. I think the caption would have read better as 'You'll wish you had a real cider'. 

Overall very unimpressed. If I were to rank this experience with the 4 other places we ate food it would be fourth, just below the shell station that we got some skittles, peanuts and water to fill us up after this experience. Perhaps the experience would have been better if the server/bartender had a personality and was willing to offer service and check on us and answer questions that we had about the menu. That's never a good start to a dining experience, when you feel like they could really care less if you are there or not. Add in the price of the meal and it's totally unacceptable for the type of service we had.

I've been back a few times and not been quite as ecstatic as I was the first time. The yuca with black beans is still the best thing I've had from them; their other options have been interesting but haven't quite excited my tastebuds as much. I've also been miffed about being surprised with extra charges, notably for salsas that were delicious but were offered without saying they cost extra, and one time where I was billed for the wrong dish. These things seemed more careless than malicious to me, but I still expect better.

They are a gluten-free establishment and they offer plenty of vegetarian options-now listed with the main menu instead of separately-but I do find them oddly selected. The starchy vegetables and squash they build meals around lack the heartiness and the protein that one gets from beans, mushrooms, and dairy. I appreciate the effort, but I do hope the menu continues to evolve.

Having said all that, it's still a nice setting, and the food is still delicious, especially the house tortillas. I still plan on dropping in on occasion, and I may just go back for the yuca and beans I had the first time.

Fool me once....

text:
WAIT. JUST WAIT. Don't go yet if ever. They don't have their shit together yet. I guess if you are staying at the hotel, go ahead and eat but if you are a neighbor, skip it for now. We have now ordered to-go twice and both times they screwed it up. The first time, we could live with it. The second time, we couldn't so I returned it. I ordered at 5:54pm and it is now 6:47pm. I literally live across the street so that's how long it first, took to get the order, they said 15, it was over 30 and then when I went to return it, she took my credit card and was gone for 15+ minutes. I thought I would get my money and go. Nope. No one knew where she was. I asked for them manager, he walked into the restaurant and then walked away. What a horrible experience. Nothing offered for the problem AND she kept the tip. On the way out she was then like do you want to stick around and I will comp you? WHAT?! did I miss something? You've taken almost an hour of my time and my family is waiting to eat. We are done. There are WAY too many awesome places to eat in St. Louis. 


Started out the first review as a 3. Not anymore.
This place is brand new, as in open to the public on its second day when we went for dinner new, so I hope to upgrade this review as they evolve.

This place is literally across the street from our house so we have high hopes of a good new restaurant coming to downtown St. Louis. 

Let talk about the best thing first. The Friday special, the 30+ hours smoked beef short rib, was INCREDIBLE! Chef Birk is a genius with that smoker. The meat was falling off the bone and the meat was the size of something from the Flintstones! 19 bucks got you that 40 pounds of meat (ok maybe slightly exaggerated), absolutely delicious homemade mashed potatoes and my husband switched out the shaved Brussels sprouts with lardons, aka bacon for the spinach side. I recommend doing the same. They were delicious. I thought this was a great value and we look forward to trying the pork steaks on Tuesday. There is a smoked special every week night for $19.

So I ordered a BOWL, now remember that, a bowl of chicken and dumplings. I asked her how big it was and she said it's like a soufflé ramekin. I thought she was misunderstanding me and telling me the size of the cup of chicken and dumplings. Ummmm no, that was it. A 4" diameter 1 3/4" high 6.5 ounce capacity standard ramekin on a plate way too big for it. They charge 8 bucks for that! Seriously!? It really was more of a very thick chicken thigh stew with 2 pinky finger dumplings in it. I LOVE dumplings! And I wanted dumplings in my soup, lots of them. Didn't happen. I ate the 2 pinky finger dumplings, and let it sit. The cup btw is a coffee cup she said. Just FYI, most coffee cups are 8 ounces and it costs $5.

And for the record, I wasn't going to pay 8 frickin dollars for soup and not take it home if I didn't eat it but they didn't have a take home container yet. Thankfully, she took it off our bill.

Our server is going to be the bartender at the roof top bar and she will be PERFECT for that! She was chatty and used words like "sweetheart & darling" and told stories. She tried to answer all of our questions, and I had a lot, because I didn't have my phone to google the terms. Finally, she got the Chef and I am glad she did. My husband has a severe allergy and she guessed wrong about it. No biggie. That's why we ask and ask and ask and offer every scenario of its presence.

I also had their house salad. A VERY good value at $5. I expected dumplings the size of the salad plate and salad the size of the dumpling plate. This sucker was really big! Like dinner plate that is a shallow bowl big. I added the butter croutons because I like a crunchy touch in my salad. I liked the shallot vinaigrette dressing, it was pretty mild. I also asked to taste the Gus' pretzel crostini.

Gus' is a landmark pretzel business in St. Louis and a beloved institution. These crostini were slightly rubbery tough to chew pretzels cut on the bias. When you microwave the pretzels to eat them on the second day, they are a bit like this. I expected them to be buttered and toasted crispy, they were not. If your teeth need a work out, try them, if not skip it and have a Gus' pretzel while you are in the city.

My husband asked on the way home if I was glad I went. I told him yes, because I am a nosy neighbor and have been watching this rehab for a long time. The hotel is very beautiful and they are preserving a landmark in our city. As to the question of did I enjoy my meal, No, not really. No, I was disappointed. I enjoyed HIS meal. The rest of the menu seemed pricy to me, I told him I thought everything but his meal seemed $5 over other area restaurants. 

Do I recommend it? YES! Eat whatever is smoked that day. Try the French Onion Soup, it's a local specialty and a nod to the shuttered department store next door. I am curious to try the chicken fried chicken. I'm sure we will go back at least once a week.
name: Colleen

text: WORST MCDONALDS EVER. Service is horrible. You have to yell at someone all the way in the back to come place your order. Then they get it wrong. However, I get it .. it's Mcdonalds & you get what you pay for but if you don't like your job THAT much to where you make this little mcdonalds as miserable as possible to where ALL the reviews are horrible - get a new job. text:
Beijing House is the best-known Chinese restaurant I've heard since I moved to Tampa. But I've never have a taste until now. 

My friend and I arrived early for dinner at around 5pm, so there was plenty of available space both for parking and for seating. 

The menu is designed to be bilingual. It attempts to cover most traditional dishes all over China in one page. My friend and I ordered the grilled fish this time, which is famous for spicy flavor, similar to Sichuan food. We asked for mild spicy based on our taste and it's cooked right to the degree we could bear. 

The service is pleasant and swift. And our waitress could speak mandarin as well, making the experience quite warm.

text:
Elegant dining experience with a minimalist interior, friendly service, and decorations/menu covers seemingly inspired by Asian folklore. Unfortunately, the food fell short of expectations. 

My friend and I came for a casual dinner, and ordered the following dishes served in tapas-style: Black Pepper Tofu & Broccolini, Pan-Seared Octopus, & Mie Goreng. The Pan-Seared Octopus was beautifully presented with an octopus atop some nicely-browned potatoes, and a delicious sauce that gradates from orange to light green. The octopus was smooth and tender, and the sauce accompanies it and the potatoes both so well that we couldn't stop every bite. However, I couldn't say the same for the other two dishes -- the broccolini was slightly too hard and bitter, while the mie goreng left a bland impression when I would expect more flavor coming from an Indonesian dish. 

While I enjoyed the dining ambiance, I wouldn't come back for the food given each tapas dish ranged from $12-25 despite the small servings. Perhaps, Sama Sama Kitchen would be better enjoyed as a happy hour spot or introduction (rather than accurate representation) into Asian fusion/food.
name: Shela

text: Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. It was crowded but still moved along. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Food was good and came out fast. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..

text: I'm not sure if its because I'm Mexican that I am overly critical but here it goes... This is not and I mean not authentic Mexican food. It's more like Tex-Mex and if you like that type of food then go for it.  The rice and beans you can tell are not made fresh.  They probably come in a can or a box pre-seasoned.  I'm giving it two stars only because it is located in a cute location and the day we went, parking was not an issue.  I ordered the Caldo de Siete Mares. It was mostly small shrimp with little pieces of potato and carrots. I was missing my pulpo and just a bigger plate. It was way too salty and had no flavor and overly priced for what I was given. I came with my family as a special lunch for Easter Celebration, so we ordered more plates. The other plate was the Stake Fajitas, it was purely bell pepper and a few onion slices and I could count the stake pieces, maybe like 6 pieces you could tell from a flank stake. So it wasn't even from a tri-tip . Anyways, it was also expensive and it was just bell peppers.  The Next dish was fish tacos and it was just tomatoes hardly any fish in them, and last the biggest dish was there sampler plate, which was the only one with some flavor because the enchiladas and chile relleno, and tamal had cheese and like the pato sauce.  Lastly, the tortillas that came with the Caldo and the Fajitas came late and we forgot about them because we were so hungry.  It took them forever to heat up the food and bring it to us.  What's ridiculous is that I  know the food was not fresh and then the waiter and waitress because it was never the same person.  Such fake "friendly" attitude from the waiter.  The other reason it has a two is because of the micheladas those were good.  But I don't think will be going back there again, unless its the only place open in all of Santa Barbara. Please improve the freshness of your food, your authenticity of what is Mexican food and your service.  For the prices you charge, it should be a 5 star restaurant.
name: Isabel

text:
A few months back it was made abundantly clear that I wasn't welcome anymore at Parasol's.  Good riddance, I thought.  Total dump.

But today I found myself longing for their roast beef Po-boy.  I took a chance that the restaurant side of the establishment might not even know that I was asked to never come back... and I was right.  I slipped in through the side door, placed my order, and no one batted an eye.  But I wish someone would have shown me the door before I took a bit of that sandwich.

What happened in here!?  This used to be the best roast beef in New Orleans.  Now it is literally diarrhea on a bun.  Words can't describe this sandwich.  It's hazmat.

Do yourself a favor.  Stay away.
name: Brandon

text:
Great Burger!! Home cut fries are a must try!! The Daly sauce gives a special kick that you have to try!
Big taste from a small town grill !

text: Damn this was fresh. I love our immigrant brothers and sisters runnin' gryo shops all over the city, but this was fresh, next level. $13 for lamb gyro and fries (no drink) so just fyi. But it's worth it. Parmesan on the fries was tasty too; exceeded my expectations.

text: Great juices.  They have a few vegan options as well.  I really enjoy the potatoes that they have and the avocado toast.  The place has limited parking so make sure to be prepared to wait for a spot and peak times.  The layout of the restaurant is a nice place to gather for sure.
name: Daniel

text: The food came out fast, which was good because we were starving. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. They were out of one thing I originally wanted..

Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean.

text: Tried this spot for lunch during a work break. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. You can tell they care about customer experience here. No big complaints, just a nice meal. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh.
name: User

text:
I did some searching prior to coming here and I had already had my hot dog picked out as well as my friend. 

To be honest, you walk in and it seems pretty dirty and not taken care of and the music is very loud. We went with a truffle mac and cheese dog and fried chicken dog. The service was actually pretty fast to get the dogs up. I'm all about a good amount of food for a good price but this was excessive. The amount of mac and cheese on this dog made it impossible to eat. It was falling all over the table. The hot dog was falling out of the bun. I personally just didn't find it enjoyable at all. My friend who ordered the crispy chicken dog ordered it all due to hearing the chicken is super good at it dog. The menu doesn't state that you will get a hot dog covered in chicken it just states "fried chicken, spicy sauce, cucumbers" I guess that's our fault for not asking if it includes a hot dog as well. In which she felt was very bland and filled to the max. 

We reached into the cooler to grab our drinks and the table that the coolers are on is filled with dust that seems like it is glued on it's been there for such a long time. 

Personally, I wouldn't give this place another try. The staff was friendly and the hot dog itself was good but the toppings and quantity was just overwhelming and disappointing.
name: Britt

text: awful!!! very bad quality for a chipotle. void of all seasoning, always out of guac, dont give you that much food. go to the elmwood one, always!!!

text: Over time this location has been worse and worse. I honestly don't understand how it can over a hour to get a pizza when you are less than 2 miles away. The app has done nothing but show the complete inefficacy of this location. My food will say finished for nearly 15-20 mins before the delivery has started. Constantly forgetting dips or sodas. Living so close to this location you almost have to try to mess up to be this bad. Last time trying to order from here.
name: Brian

text:
My party went to this restaurant late at night following several recommendations. Although the area is rather sketchy, the restaurant itself is very clean and spacious, just don't mind the security guard standing at the door.

Since this place is known for their salchipapas, we each got an order of different versions of the entree. Although each version had different toppings, they were all the same size. For the cost or french fries and sliced hot dogs, the price is relatively high for what you get. The regular salchipapa is $6, while the orders with cheese, chicken, chicharrones, etc., goes past $10. 

My biggest issue with this restaurant is the service. Once we were seated, it took a very long time for the waiter to take our order. Moreover, they do not have free water, and they will charge you for plastic-bottled water. According to other reviews, tip is already included, but the iPad/payment device doesn't show the itemized list, often making customers giving an additional tip. When we were making our payments, the waiter looked directly over us signing the receipt and selecting the tip, making it uncomfortable to put no tip. 

The only reason I would come back again is for the restaurant's late night hours. Otherwise, it'll probably be better to try another restaurant or fast food place.
name: Megan

text: Service was top notch. Our server helped and offered suggestions, which we were glad she did. The food was delicious.
name: Tracy

text:
OH NO, NEW OWNERS!!! That was the thought when we went in after a trip out of town about a month or so ago. The change was noticed because the corner table had paperwork and a laptop along with 2 new faces but there were still a few familiar faces behind the counter so we weren't too shaken. About a week later we saw in the TBT that the restaurant indeed changed hands but because we had just been and everything remained the same fresh and tasty food we didn't fret. Until last Friday. 
We made plans to meet some family, who are (were) also regulars for dinner. The door stated that there would now be new hours and they would no longer be open until 9 instead closing at 8. It was 7:35 and there were chairs stacked on tables but a few people still eating, we thought at worst we would be taking our food to go.  Each one of us entered the restaurant in a state of shock. What was always the exceptionally clean restaurant we had come to know and love had floors that were black, food on the walls, the place smelled like heavy duty cleaner and dirty fryer grease, with the menu chalkboard having items crossed off. We were greeted by a new face at the register (assuming new owner) she assured us we were ok to dine in and was friendly taking our order. My sisters ordered their usual (Vegetable Hu Tieu), my other half his usual (Chicken Pho), finally my turn I ordered (my usual Shrimp Summer Rolls no noodles sub extra lettuce and a Green Mint Salad.) The woman at the register seemed caught off guard that I would order the summer rolls without noodles so I had to explain I'm sensitive to rice and always get them this way I'm aware of how they come (Phuong's peanut sauce was some of the best I've ever had so I think that was the primary focus of eating these.) 
We sat at the cleanest table we found and I went to wash my hands. The bathroom was disgusting, urine on the toilet seat, smelled terrible, and had a dirty sink/faucet.
What used to be a quick wait for food took about 20 minutes coming out in pieces. First the summer rolls, then the vegetable soup, then the pho, finally the salad. Having frequented this restaurant for the last 5 years or so my salad looked totally different. It had what looked like fried onions sprinkled over top, chicken that was grilled to death on the outside and looked like pork (which I am extremely allergic to) and the dressing already pored over it (it used to be served on the side.) My sister made me get up and ask what was in this new version of my old favorite because nobody wanted to risk me having a seizure. I asked the girl serving our drinks and she replied that she wasn't sure they recently got new owners so she would have to ask, enter new owner. That same woman at the register came to her rescue and said "Oh you've never had this before, you don't know what's in it." I became a little irritated replying that it is what I get regularly but have never seen it come out that way. She informed me that it was indeed fried onion  (no breading) and she promised it was chicken not pork. I asked her to remake it without the weird fried onion on top and she instead told me "No, because I am trying to get rid of that item from the menu, but I can make you something else instead. Maybe lettuce wraps?" This no doubt made me more annoyed but I was hungry so I told her that was fine but with tofu instead, to which she obliged taking the salad out of my hands. I went and told the rest of my party they were making me something new to go ahead and eat. Both of my sisters tasted their soup and stated it tasted like water, while my boyfriend tried his Pho and asked me to taste it because he thought it had soap in it, he wasn't wrong it did taste oddly floral. Then I reached for the sriracha to add to the peanut sauce to at least enjoy the summer rolls and the dirty dispenser was complete with a hair atop it. So I took a bite sans sriracha, the lettuce inside was brown and tasted like Subway restaurants smell and the peanut sauce was no doubt from a vat not the homemade of prior. What shouldn't have surprised me at that point, definitively broke me. My sister, who had paid for the meal suggested we just leave. Normally I would take it up with a manager or an owner but this was absolutely the most atrocious experience and I just assumed she would argue with me so we got up and left $50 worth of food on the table and drove down the road to our favorite Thai restaurant and had a meal that was accurate and delicious. I feel as if I have lost a relative in this experience. What should have been a 30 minute dinner rolled into an hour and a half and cost us double and we are out our favorite Vietnamese/Pho restaurant in the long run. 

Congratulations Henry and Phuong on your retirement though you and your family will be missed greatly we are happy for you.

R.I.P  Green Mint Asian Grill you were one of our favorites and we will never step foot in you again.
name: Athena

text: Food here is pretty great, although the chef is finicky about modifying. All of the soups are great, the Kpop tacos are great, the tostones are great. But If you're a frequent falafel eater, i wouldnt recommend their falafels but there are plenty of other great dishes to choose from. Pan Bagna is usually my go to! Their portion sizes are also HUGE, for a decent price. Overall would highly recommend.
name: Reshma

text: The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. It was crowded but still moved along. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean.
name: User

text: Wait a little longer than what we expected but it was a great place to eat I'll come back to this place and wait as long as I have to again
name: Chris

text: For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. Food was fresh and service was quick. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..
name: User

text:
Small counter service breakfast & brunch place with an open kitchen in a casual & colorful space. Open every day for breakfast, but also have brunch on the weekends. Specialize in breakfast classics with a fun twist. Also have drive-thru.

I came on a Sunday morning with my sister and it was very crowded, however the line at the counter was moving very quickly. I ordered the breakfast sandwich with spicy turkey sausage and an egg over hard, and my sister ordered the baked oatmeal (which was a very cool concept). They had a lot of creative options. 

We were luckily able to grab a table, but the place was packed and most people were sharing communal tables. The food came out in a reasonable amount of time and was delicious. They also have good "serve yourself" style coffee. The only reason Yolklore is getting 4 stars is because the space is pretty cramped.
name: Zack

text:
The good:
Server Jess was wonderful. Friendly, attentive and helpful.
Margaritas nice and tart with fresh lime.
Comfortable high top seating along the 
wall.
Chips and salsas - 2 kinds roasted red and verde both delish. Chips were good but needed more salt
Sides of corn salad and blsck beans were pretty good.
Corn Truffle taco good.

The meh:

31/2 stars

text: Have you tried their brunch? It's to die for. The service wasn't entirely the best, as we say for about 10 minutes before a server came over, but the food made up for it. Try the blue crab cakes. You will not regret it.
name: Alexandra

text:
Great food, quick service, friendly staff, the restaurant istself is clean and well cared for. love the Loco Moco special. Salad is always 
fresh. Menu has plenty of delicious choices to choose from. Even if your just passing through town, its definitely worth stoping by. I Would recommend this restaurant!!
name: Andrew

text: Some friends and I were in New Orleans last week for a conference. We were looking for a good place to eat and listen to music on Frenchmen Street. So glad we picked Three Muses. The atmosphere was friendly and inviting. The cocktails were great. And the food was delicious and different from other places we'd been eating. We shared a bowl of olives, the kale salad, some mac and cheese, and some ice cream. Everything was delicious, and we were able to sit there for hours and enjoy the food, the music, and the company.
name: Nicole

text:
Wow you can't go wrong going here. Service was fantastic as far as our server, however the hostess wasn't the friendliest. Ambience was great. 
Ordered the gumbo and the beet and goat cheese salad. The. Gumbo. Was. So. Good! Amazing flavor. 
My friend got the shrimp and grits I believe? Also amazing. Definitely suggest dining here for lunch or dinner!
name: Colette

text: My family ate dinner here on a recent trip to St. Louis. We were a party of 6 and made a reservation since we read it can get crowded. We were seated right away and received prompt and friendly service from start to finish. Everything we ordered was very tasty. I don't eat pasta so I ordered sides of sausage, meatballs, and broccoli. The broccoli was cooked in brown butter and was delicious! I loved the antique feel and stained glass. My family left very pleased with our visit!
name: Kelky

text:
Firebirds is wonderful to have in Brentwood. The food is delicious and the service is friendly and professional. Been there many times and leave happy every time. Today was extra remarkable because of the spring menu items offered. The "Impossible" Burger is delicious!! I don't eat red meat and miss a good grilled burger...well, this is it! Wouldn't know it was vegetarian if I hadn't read the menu. Don't know how it's done; but, I'm going back for another very soon. Might have to go again tomorrow! Please add it to your permanent menu

My husband had the steak sandwich and it's now the best sandwich he's had in Nashville...been living here 50+ years, so that says a lot. The seasoning was a symphony of flavor. The management of this restaurant is reflected in the atmosphere and staff. Kudos to the general manager and the chef in charge. There's lots of restaurants to choose from in Nashville; but, not many you consider a perfect one to have on your rotation list...Firebirds makes the list.
name: Valerie

text: So I used to rather like Thai Express. And the staff member I interacted with was pretty pleasant/helpful. But gosh the food has gone downhill. My red curry fish was pretty flavourless (except one bite which tasted spoiled :( ) and I wasn't terribly fond of the tray in which the food was served. In the end I ended up only eating about half my meal as it really wasn't great. I was surprised as red curry is supposed to be the most spicy (and I've had quite spicy versions of it from Thai Express before) but I've never had a more bland red curry experience than this one. The texture of the fish was also mediocre as well. This was not good and I'm unlikely to return anytime soon.
name: Ali

text:
I saw this spot as one of "hot/new businesses" awhile back,  then our friend couple wanted to do double date here, so we came here on a Friday night. We walked in at 7 and luckily there was a spot at 8 pm. The host told us about olio across the street so we got drinks there. Thank goodness for his recommendation, that place was super cute/hipster. 
Everything we ordered here was soooo good! I think it's my favorite place I have eaten at so far in STL. I read that the owner/chef owns Nippon Tei (this is my favorite Japanese place). 
1)Japanese eggplant with some yogurt like sauce was good but I wish the sauce on eggplant was a little sweeter
2)chili prawns were DELICIOUS  and a bit spicy  
3)shrimp toast also very  tasty!
4)crab rice also very good but more rice vs  and I liked the salmon eggs that accompanied it
5)short rib curry accompanied by paratha... this was the most filling dish but they only gave 4 little pieces of paratha compared to the short rib curry... they really need to give more to finish the dish. Taste wise, it was perfect!

text: Great place. Food choices were very interesting and I had a difficult time choosing. All four of us loved our food which was excellent. We especially loved the homemade pasta. The service was very good and the only downside was the noise level was a little excessive. We will return often.

The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. text: Good Pizza went in not knowing what to expect. But the Sicilian pizza was great! The sauce was really good. The wings were surprisingly good. This was our first time in we were pleasantly surprised. They even have a pull up service that they bring your pizza to your car. They also have beer and wine inside which was also a surprise. We will be heading back their and won't be going to any other chain pizza places after our experience!

text:
Good food, comfortable ambiance, HORRIBLE  service. I've been there several times. They don't have adequate ventilation in their food prep area so the smell of greasy smoke will permeate your skin, hair and clothes. Most recently I took my wife and young daughter for lunch. We were the only patrons there when we placed our order. Nearly 20 minutes went by when we realized that the 12 people who came in after us were served and eating. My wife went to the counter to inquire about our order and the young man scolded her saying loudly that they were busy. Really? If he had been gracious, offered an estimate of time or a simple apology we would have felt very differently. But to scold a woman who asked about her meal because her child was hungry? How does being busy excuse serving 12 grossly out of order become become the patron's fault? 

Some advice for the owner: 
1. Train your staff to be courteous. 
2. Change your menu so that your understaffed help can provide a decent level of service.
3. Hire more staff.
4. Install a more powerful ventilation system.

From now on I'll stick to Starbucks across the street. I thought I was doing the right thing by giving a small business my business. No appreciation.
name: Jason

text: This was my first time having hot chicken and it was pretty good! My friend and I split a half chicken and we got the hot flavor. At first, I thought I was fine. I was starving so I ate very fast, and then it started to hit me. I teared up a bit, I snotted a bit, but it was worth it. I'm not sure how anyone handles any flavor hotter than hot... but it goes all the way up to XXX hot. We also ordered online in advance so the food was ready when we got there. Luckily there wasn't a line so we got our food right away. However, I saw other people pick up their online orders and they had to wait in a tremendously long line. So even if you order online in advance, you'll have to wait in line to pick up your order.

Everything was tasty especially tuna wraps, pasta, cornbread, flatbread, short ribs.   Get the beet juice cocktail so you can pretend to eat healthy.   Somehow our waiter remembered us from our last visit and remembered I ordered the pasta with clams-how is that possible? We ate almost every meal here

Ribs are overly drenched in sauce and the tri tip is not great. It's not tender, cut in huge thick slices, doesn't come with sauce, and has grill marks on it! Meaning they just reheated the meat on grill before serving.  We liked the street corn best ha.

text: Met a couple friends today for brunch. The three of us ordered the farm fresh egg  breakfast, nothing complicated - eggs over easy, toast, potatoes and sausage ( a 15 minute order). We were enjoying our time visiting so we didn't leave like all the tables around us - eventually I left - I was getting the shakes from all the coffee and I was STARVING. My friends stayed and were served shortly thereafter which was over 2 1/2 hours later....to get eggs .....and the restaurant was not busy....2 1/2 hours for fried eggs. I was so hungry I had to drive through and grab a burger before I passed out.
name: T.

text:
Several reasons I give Another Broken Egg Cafe a 5-star rating:
- Hours: I am originally from Colorado, where people wake up and eat breakfast before 10am... It kills me that very few breakfast/brunch spots open before 11am in Tampa Bay, so the fact that this place opens at 7am is wonderful. **Tip for those that don't like to wait long: show up before 9am and you'll be seated within 10 minutes**
- Food portions and prices: The highest priced meal is $15, which is salmon or shrimp so I get it, I can't stand it when I see a $17 pricetag for chicken n' waffles on the menu, this place is pretty well priced and especially when you get alot on your plate(s). It's also nice that when you order pancakes/waffles/french toast, you also get 2 eggs and sausage or bacon. Each time we visit, we are unable to finish everything on our plates and my husband very rarely leaves food on our plates.
- Menu and Food: The menu is quite expansive with many delicious options to satisfy anyone, we always have a hard time deciding what to order because there are so many items that look so good. We have always really enjoyed whatever it is that we end up ordering as it is delicous and fresh tasting every time, but what stands out the most is the City Grits (seriously delicious and could make a meal on it's own) and Lemon Blueberry Goat Cheese Pancakes (I didn't know it was possible to make a pancake so good, no syrup or other toppings needed). The hot sauce is also great that we bought a bottle to take home last time we were there.
- Coffee: There are many coffee options, but I usually go for a regular cup of coffee but have hazelnut syrup added. My husband really likes their cold brew.
- Service: we have always had good service, I'm sure there are some days that the service lacks a bit for customers, but so far we are pleased with the service considering this is a very busy place with little room to work around and lots of various options going on.

So overall, this is our favorite breakfast/brunch place in Tampa Bay and we will be back many more times.
name: Ashley

text: Definitely one of the better BBQ places in this area. Their baby back ribs and pulled pork sandwiches are great. Love their selection of six sauces (although Smoky Mountain is the best). Friendly staff.
name: Nomal

text: Very friendly staff EVERY time I've been in there. Usually there's one bad apple on the schedule at every place but not here in my experience. Quick, efficient, and healthy. A nice grab and go type of operation, and free parking at the end if the block!
name: Ben

text: Horrible service from this restaurant. And worse yet an incompetent Manager who failed his local neighborhood Patrons. He failed his front host staff also! The epitome of If You Don't Take Care Of Your Customers, Somebody Else Will ! I'm never ever going back to this Restaurant!
name: Rick

text: There's no good Japanese food out here but this place is worth trying. I had Katsudon a plate I grew up eating in the Bay Area & it wasn't bad. My son had a bento box & every Asian food place should know how to make teriyaki chicken right? I thought that until I ate at this place in Nampa. My son loved it & I had his tempura not bad but ask for extra sauce. My wife had the Bulgogi which is Korean BBQ & also this place is actually a Korean restaurant but half the menu is Japanese food. She also liked her plate. Really good service & low priced. If you had other Japanese or Korean out here you should definitely give this place a try.

text: Been to Buffa a couple of times since my last review. Aside from the occasional great music in the back Buffa's menu is actually pretty good. My recommendations are the boudin balls, the burger which competes with some of the best in town including its more famous neighbor down the street and surprisingly a great reuben sandwich. Their prices on red beans is a bit expensive but they are also very good.
name: Christopher

text:
Have been here multiple times and recently came across a better Mexican restaurant on the Main Line (El Tio in Berwyn) so I'm sorry, NO, this is not the best Mexican on the Main Line. It's very ok. The enchiladas are satisfying, the tacos are alright, and the burrito is very medium. You'll be satisfied here. But you probably won't be blown away. It's a popular spot so it can be busy (lots of Villanova students) on Friday and Saturday nights. But this doesn't really reflect quality, instead, convenience. I've also experienced longer-than-I'd-like wait times. 

After visiting Xolo Tacos and then El Tio (quite good), I will not be returning to El Limon.
name: Elizabeth

text: The food was not good. This was my second time here, and will not return. It took three tries to cook my steak to medium, and was extremely tough to cut. My Italian salad dressing was straight vinegar.
name: Mary

text:
How have I not reviewed Ulysses yet? This is one of our go-to restaurants in North Wilmington that never lets us down.

We tend to go on Wednesdays because it's Burger Night. They expand their menu beyond their usual burger offerings to include 5 burgers designed for the occasion that vary week to week, though some favorites make return appearances and the "Classic Burger" is regularly featured and is often my choice --- featuring American cheese, lettuce, pickles, onion, and "special sauce" as a standard All-American cheeseburger should. The burgers typically come with housemade chips, which are delightful, but I always opt to upgrade to the Truffle Parmesan Tots ($3 upgrade) because who can resist that anything that involves truffle oil, parmesan cheese, OR tater tots? 

They've got a decent variety of appetizers; one that sticks out in my mind are their Russian Roulette Wings --- most are coated with mild wing sauce, but one is coated in an extra-spicy sauce, and you don't know which one. Definitely a fun little gimmick to play with a group of friends.

For dessert, we almost always get the ice cream cake which is from an amazing local creamery, Woodside Farms. They typically have the mint chocolate (oreo crust, red peppermint ice cream, and a thick layer of chocolate ganache which I tend to eat around because I hate trying to jab my spoon through it but can't wait til it warms up enough), though once they had a strawberry flavor that was a nice change. 

Beverage wise, they have an extensive beer menu with reasonable prices, along with a "what's next" list so you can anticipate when your favorite beer will next be on tap if it's not currently offered. As more of a cider person than a beer person, I appreciate that there's always a cider on their list. 

We've almost always been able to walk in without a reservation on the weeknights, though I could imagine they get busy at times. Service balances being attentive with giving some space. Overall, a reliable choice for a good dinner.
name: Kate

text: My friend liked it more than I did. Anyway, the wait wasn't awful, just longer than i expected for the time of day.. text: I love this place!! And so close to home! I stopped in yesterday (have been through the Drive-Thru many times) this is my 2nd time coming inside the store. The atmosphere is pleasant and relaxing, and is a good family oriented place. The service is always good, the food was hot and fresh, and the price was good for 1 person; less than $10. They have an enclosed play area for small children where parents, guardians can sit and eat while watching their kids,etc. The dining area is very clean and well kept. The only negative part of my visit was hearing a few customers who were sitting near to me shooting off F bombs, in their conversation, near children who could hear what they were saying, etc. Being that people know who Chick-fil-a represents, it would be nice if people would be more consciencious and careful of the words they allow to come out of their mouths when eating there, especially because little ears are hearing what you say. All in all, Chick-fil-a is a great place to enjoy good food with family and friends! As long as their business goes on, me and my family/friends will eat here! text:
I was starving, and I didn't think a pizza place would be the best since I'm celiac, but I stopped in anyways. I'm glad I did.
After I was seated, my server, Ryan, came over and took my drink order. After going back and forth on the menu, I decided on a gluten free pizza crust, with olive oil and garlic sauce, cheese, and chicken. Ryan politely took my order and left the table. A few minutes later he came over and let me know the chicken and steak aren't completely gluten free because of the way they're stored. Since I mentioned I was celiac instead of just gluten free, he made sure to let me know. I thanked him and ordered the pizza with Italian sausage instead of chicken. It took a bit, and Ryan was really attentive during the time, letting me know their separate "gluten free" oven wasn't on the right temp. I was cool with it! When the pizza came however, it had red sauce. Which I'm not crazy about since I have mild heartburn too, lol. He took it back and the right pizza was brought out more promptly.

IT. WAS. AMAZING. Easily the best gluten free pizza I've ever had. They loaded up on the cheese, the Italian sausage was spicy, and the crust was crispy. Ryan was back to check on me and boxed the incorrect pizza as well. This is my first visit to this place, and I appreciate the attention to detail from Ryan. He's the absolute best! I will definitely be coming back here.

Thank you Ryan!!!
name: Bella

Food...

Overall this was just a great experience. If you're looking for great food and a small hometown feel then this is the place.

text:
So this place...I really wanted to like it. I mean, really wanted to like it, but alas, it was not meant to be. 

The decor is phenomenal! I mean you are transformed literally to Mexico. The restaurant was designed on point. But that is where it ends. 

First our waitor informs us that we cannot get the Margarita specials at the table and would only have to get it at the bar. Ok - I guess we can live with that. 
Secondly, he informs us that he cannot provide a kids special, posted at the table due to a holiday. What was the holiday you might ask? It was national Margarita Day. Are you kidding me? I mean, I am sure there there is some unknown holiday every day of the year. 

I would be willing to overlook all of this, if in fact the food was good. But unfortunately, it was not. It took a while to come out, probably because they were busy (due to Margarita Day) and when it did finally come out, we were not so pleased. Both my husband and I ordered a form of Carne Asada, he in the entree version and I, in the tacos version. It was inedible to say the least. The steak, tough and chewy. Everything else was mushy and did not have the amazing freshness of the Mexican food I had on many occasions in Mexico. 

On another note - I just added a star back to my review. The guacamole was pretty good and it was the most reasonable price I have ever seen for an enormous (2.5 avocados) portion of guac. So the guac and decor take my review to 3 stars, with that said, we will not be coming back.

text:
First of all let me start off by saying that I have been to an unhealthy amount of diners and this one has taken the cake.. or should I say pie. Yes, their pies are as delicious as they look and I usually don't go for cream pies but their coconut cream pie was like heaven in each bite. But I'll get to that later
This little gem is amazing and the minute you walk in it's like home - it's like walking into your favorite aunts house who always spoils you. Everyone working their, especially the cooks wife, is so extremely kind. 
All of the ladies we had waiting our table were so sweet and personal which made coming here a really special experience. My boyfriend and I got the same omelet with ground beef, sausage and bacon and wow I never thought an omelet could taste that good. The meets were different from other diners and it wasn't overly greasy which made this especially tasty. Their hash was also to die for - crispy and soft and their sourdough toast.. oh my goodness.. have you ever had a thick, fresh slice of sourdough? Again, I couldn't tell you why it was so good, it was just toast but it was addictive. We weren't super full (full but not sick or gut-busting) so we decided to try their coconut cream pie - which according to our waitress was her favorite one. Like I said before , I'm not a huge fan of cream/meringue pies but this changed my mind. Light, sweet, smooth and perfect! 
The restaurant itself was pretty small but there wasn't a lot of people there so space didn't seem to be an issue. 
And like I said before the waitresses just were so sweet and friendly and I would come back just to mingle with them. 
I had a go to diner before but this is my new  favorite spot - delicious classic diner food and the greatest people you'll ever meet working there! Loved it!

More fries would have been nice but they were completely slammed and people were waiting for a table. Staff was friendly though and I'm sure we will be back!
name: Jacqueline

text: Just okay nothing special. The staff still learning very noisy environment over priced .
name: Felix

text:
I have been hearing about 400 Degrees for awhile and decided to head there for lunch.

400 Degrees is located on the northern part of Nashville, so it was a bit of a drive and as I pulled in I guess the kindest description would be that its ambiance is nondescript and unassuming. OK, it is nothing fancy, but there is nothing wrong with that. My introduction to hot chicken was at the old Prince's location and that location brought nondescript and unassuming to a new level.

The people working here are friendly and warmly welcomed me and took my order. Hot chicken is made to order, so it will take a bit to get to you, but hot chicken is more than worth the wait. I am more than slightly obsessed with this culinary godsend.

I must say that I was intrigued by their hot porkchop and hot shrimp, but I wanted to start this on a level playing field and try a hot chicken breast, prepared their hottest.

As much as I would love to say that it was life altering (much like when I first stumbled upon Prince's about seventeen years ago), I found this to be rather run of the mill. I have had worse, but I certainly had better. The potato salad i had was pretty good, but again, i ha e had better.

I will give here another try, this time with the hotter off the menu heat level and I will try the pork chop. I hope that perhaps I caught them at an off time, like I said, they were such nice people.
name: John

text:
You would think that with their grand opening, they would have prepared better for loads of customers! I entered Bambu and was told that if I wanted bubbles, I would have to wait 30 minutes. I said no thanks and ordered my drink with one specific instruction (no milk). Shockingly, I spent more than 30 minutes waiting for my drink and they messed it up anyway. What if I were lactose intolerant? I realized maybe I should have waited the "30 minutes" because I spent much more time there! I also kind of felt as though they were serving people that they knew first.

I decided to give them another try because I went during their grand opening. Drinks are great but I do think it gets a bit unprofessional. There are customers that walk behind the counter and hang out to talk. One time, one of the customers walked behind the counter to chat and I had to wait because the worker was chatting to the customer. I don't know...it just makes me feel as though there should be some boundaries regardless if you know the owners.

They do take debit which is awesome and they don't require a minimum which I do appreciate! I just wish there was more of a professional atmosphere and listening skills.
name: Mary

text:
We were visiting Philly and decided to try this place we had heard so many reviews about. The place was good, however we felt that it needed
maybe more salt. On the bright side that's why we added cheese wiz on the side and that helped a lot. My girlfriend and I each got our own sandwiches but we realized we should have gotten one . Big portions and decent price!
name: Candace

text:
Delicious!!!!! 
The pistachio ice cream , coccorum, and tira misu were amazing . 
I also tried the Spivey egg plant pizza and that was delicious also ! 
Great place deff coming back for more !
name: Melissa

text:
Somewhere in Reno, there's a bar with a lousy happy hour, surly service and awful food. Our Bar is definitely not that bar -- not by a long shot.

Wow, wow, WOW! Just seconds after I stepped through the really fun automatic front door, Bartender Emily welcomed this newbie like he was a regular.

Overwhelmed as I was by the amazing selection of beers on tap, I was even more blown away by the Taco Tuesday curry chicken tacos. I ordered 3 and would have ordererd 3 more if my old tummy could have fit them in.

Bottom line? Great service, friendly atmosphere, tasty beer and amazing food. I plan to make Our Bar my bar, and you should, too!
name: Briggs

text:
Such a cute, cozy bakery with delicious scones, cookies, muffins, and coffee! Love the scones here particularly, but try coming on the earlier side to pick from all their options! 

Atmosphere: Really small, so it's more of a place to grab a scone to go and maybe eat on Rittenhouse square. Not much seating inside - I wish there were more (maybe can fit 5 people seated max). Baristas are very friendly too.

Food: I love their scones the most - not too sweet, and pair very well with tea. The chocolate rice crispy, peanut butter bar was a bit too rich for my preferences - worth splitting with another person or two.

Overall: 5 / 5 - Would love to come back to try more scones, which usually change day by day!
name: Annie

text: This is simply my favorite and the best Mexican restaurant in St. Louis! The shrimp quesadilla is outstanding! The tortillas are superb. The service is fast, and they are very helpful with descriptions of menu items. The drinks area in fact MASSIVE if that's what you're into.
name: Arkay

text:
First time in nashville and this is our second day, first meal we have without issue of some sort. Sat down, relaxing atmosphere, attentive waitress, walking distance from our apartment. We made reservations through open table after having nightmare experiences with waitlists and food availability the day before. Just being seated quickly made the perfect start to the amazing meal to follow.
Waitress was very nice and service was great. Food was delivered with little wait, nice amount of time in between drinks, appetizers, and food. Divided the meals that we were sharing in the kitchen and split the checks incorrectly, and then fixed it without us even having a chance to say anything. Kept the drinks flowing. No complaints, at all.
Food is great. Every plate I tried was a good one. I had the steak benedict and it was perfect portion for sharing. Tried soup of the day which was chicken and mushroom and the french onion. Perfect for the weather and very delicious. The dough balls they brought out were mind blowing with orange marmalade butter. Drinks were great and interesting flavor combinations. Favorite was the delta, like a lemondade with a kick. 
Everything about this spot made it a great choice for a brunch place to start off some sightseeing in Nashville
name: Vanessa

text:
I attended this establishment on day 5. They opened up too quickly. Most of the staff was frustrated and venting within ear shots about others not doing their duties. I ordered wings (not bad) and oysters. The oysters had so much fecal matter that I could  not scrape it out and had to send it back. I then ordered a house salad with caesar dressing. I asked for them to be specific on the salad because I typically get a Caesar salad and ... I got a caesar salad. The salties Calamari I've ever had. Also heavily breaded although specified as being lightly breaded.
Went back the next day to give them a second chance. Was told their was a one hour wait to be seated. 3 couples were before me. After walking to see if their was any seating I saw 4 tables with out anyone at them. I found a spot on the upper deck with table notifier in hand. I looked over and within 5 mins all couples were seated with groups of two. My notifier went off 37 mins later. I would suggest going back to this place in a couple of months when they straighten everything out.
Best thing about this place are the views!!
name: Amber

text: Unfortunately I am disappointed! I was referred to this place & I will be getting my money back from that person! The wait was RIDICULOUS for not even subpar food. The lady taking orders was okay... no real issue with her, but the portion & wait time is not worth it. JUST COOK! Cabbage was TERRIBLE & the mac & cheese somewhat edible ( its cut in a little square ) I didnt know they give u a pancake ( I guess johnny cake ) instead of the regular cornbread. The fish was probably the  highlight of the platter. The hr & 15min wait + subpar soulfood = I wont be back! I'm all for supporting black businesses, but they gotta do better.
name: Bri

text: Don't be fooled by the construction and dimmed lights, they are open! We were advised to park in the lot on the corner of Delaware and North st. The atmosphere inside was charming and cultural, not a large dining room so it is probably not a bad idea to make reservations or call ahead. We ordered the muscles as an appetizer and they were better than average, they came with bread which was great. I ordered the Lamb Tagine and I wasn't that impressed, the lamb was tough and the broth was watered down and lacked flavor. Our server was nice and polite, but slow and forgetful. Overall we enjoyed the experience and we are going to give it another shot!
name: Josh

text: First time ordering from here and I honestly wasn't sure what to expect. Honestly, i liked the soup more than the entree honestly. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. The staff seemed tired but still polite. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. idk I'd try something else next time. The sauces helped more than I thought they would..
name: User

text: Worst Outback Steakhouse ever!!!!! I guess I should not have expected it to be as good as it was when it first opened and when Outback was all the rage. Well, now there is plenty of competition near this Outback such as Grand Luxe, Yard House and Longhorn, etc. I am not even a fan of Longhorn but even that is better than this Outback. I have been to other Outback's and they are much better. The Proprietor Sue Midiri needs to make some serious changes if she wants this restaurant to survive. I have given this restaurant one too many chances, so shame on me for coming again. The food was cold and the service was lack luster. There is no excuse for poor service since the restaurant was empty. The bartender was horrible and he could not make a good Wallaby Darned. Needless to say I will never, ever, ever come here again! Bye Outback!!

text: This is a return trip pizza was delicious as usual this time I just had 10 in personal Pizza hit the spot. Would highly recommend this pizza joint do anyone in the area. I will be back again.
name: Jim

text: For the price I expected a little more care. Also, the food was good and the service was easygoing. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. Honestly, no big complaints, just a nice meal. Anyway, nothing was awful but i left disappointed. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. idk I'd try something else next time. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine..
name: User

text: Awesome place! So wonderful to take some time and hang out with the prescious kitties. Our family is visiting from out of town and we had to leave our sweet kitties behind. Visiting Cat Therapy took the edge off missing ours. Great place!
name: Jeannie

text: I have been torn about writing this review. I want the restaurant to get the accolades they deserve but I don't want anyone else to know about this hidden gem. The food is nothing short of amazing. Fresh ingredients, perfectly seasoned, I have yet to try anything I don't like. If you only knew how picky I was, you would be impressed. Give this place a shot, it is off to the corner but definitely worth the trip. First trip I had the ham and gruyere omelet and the second time I had biscuits and gravy. Both were delicious and thoughtfully prepared. I probably should try this place for lunch but the breakfast is just so amazing!
name: Jenell

text: This location on 40th st has to better in regards to how their staff act when there are customers present,  they are extremely loud and do not take into account that not everyone need to hear their conversations...they be too busy interacting with one another than taking care of what needs to be done.  Their tone of voice is not welcoming.
name: Maria

text: This is based solely on their new dish zoodles Primavera. It is amazing! The sauce is light and very tasty, not heavy at all. The veggies are spot on being tender and crisp. I added shrimp which were tasty but would have been totally on point with a nice sear on them. That being said, I couldn't wait to have my left overs the next day for lunch!
name: Lisa

text:
Strange Donuts you've made me break my vow of not bad mouthing my neighborhood establishments. Ok, in a nutshell: Your donuts are really really (no really) bad. 
  
Its not the "strange" part so much as it is the basic donut, that Strange Donuts really fails at. Uniformly, and regardless of the style, the donuts are heavy and have a strong taste of the fryer. By comparison, donuts from Quik Trip or even Schnucks would be lighter, better tasting and without an oily film thats left on the roof of your mouth. 
  
The straw that broke the camels back, was the last "Fat Steve" I tasted. It wasnt cooked thoroughly and was oddly gummy and stretchy, it made me quite sure nobody cared how this thing came out of the fryer. 
   
Doing better than grocery stores and gas stations is a pretty low bar I think for a donut, and in light of how there are some genuinely delicious donuts in this town (Vincent Van Donuts/Donut Drive In, for example) the emphasis on novelty, while foregoing quality kinda' sucks. The kicker is the fact that my kids dont even like to eat these donuts anymore, even THEY are coming to understand how crappy these donuts are.
name: John

text: Always great! I order often via Uber Eats and never have complaints. My sandwiches are always exactly how I order them and my notes are paid attention to. Quality far surpasses most fast food expectations. Veggies and bread are always fresh and the meats are very good! Turkey and provolone, meatball, and philly are my favorites. Prices are reasonable too.
name: Bridget

text: would probably stop in again if nearby. For a busy night they handled it okay. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. For the price I expected more than this. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Idk, they were out of one thing i originally wanted.. maybe I just came on an off day. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price..

text: Despite several NEGATIVE reviews for dining in, I picked up pizza on a Saturday night.  It was ready when said & one of the BEST I've ever had. Great sauce, a bit spicy but perfect. Lots of toppings, cheese & a lovely crust.  Worth every penny. So glad I live close.  I would definitely recommend their pizza!!

text: Finally went back after their update and both the decore and the menu are modernized. I love both and recommend it very highly. I got the pork belly and it was fantastic while my wife got the special lasagne. The bill was more than reasonable.
name: Jim

text: First time back in over a year. This place has steadily improved and reinvented itself from strictly modern mex to a cozy byob with a broader range of offerings (eg center cut pork chop, vegan quinoa bowl, etc). Ordered tacos for take out on Caviar and was quite pleased.  The short rib tacos are stellar in particular. Look forward to coming back

text: Oh my god !!!!!!!! One of the best pizza places I've had since I've moved to the main line. 5 star review isn't enough !!!!!!
name: Gia

text: Had lunch here with my hubby. Simple menu. Great choices. I really enjoyed my Salmon Salad. Had the bread pudding for dessert; it was delicious.
name: Teka-Ann

text:
Who knew a dope chicken and rice cart has been in a gas station parking lot all this time? My cravings for halal street food have required a trip to the city to satisfy until now. The platters at Zara compare favorably to the halal carts in Philly. The chicken, in particular, is marinated in a really flavorful blend of spices and arrives piping hot, juicy, and piquant. The lamb didn't impress me as much as the chicken, but the springy cubes of salty meat are on par with the lamb from other carts.

Sauces, both creamy white and spicy red, make or break this type of food. Fortunately, both hit the mark at Zara with the white sauce tasting tangy and the red appropriately fiery. I wish the white was less gloppy and red packed a little more punch, but I'm nitpicking. Prices run $6-7 a platter and the portions are generous. I'll definitely be back to satisfy the meat over rice craving.
name: Neil

text:
We were enjoy to be seat at the bar, Steward and Kayla are the best bartenders. Thumb up!!!
I ordered seafood combo and crawfish entofee' and my husband got soft shell crabs and shrimp with onion ring for his side and gumbo. I like gumbo better than my entire. Seafood was fresh!!
name: Miimo

text: Loved my meal here. The shared large paella was a huge hit with our group. I can't wait to return again.
name: Truth B Told

text: Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. Glad we tried it. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything..

text:

I would suggest go and check it out - perfect time for this summer weather in Indy!.  =)

text: Really good burgers! I went during Happy Hour and had a burger and 2 domestic beers for a total bill of $13. Beautiful place with great service and food, It's also really lovely inside!. Love that downtown Clearwater is being revitalized from after suffering from a downturn in business because of the local "church" that was so intimidating to so many.  It's much better now. Come back to downtown Clearwater!
name: Gena

text: Stopped by after work because I was nearby and hungry. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The staff seemed tired but still polite. There were a couple things I liked and a couple things I probably wouldn't get again. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus..
name: User

text: This place is amazing! Their staff is incredible, the food is great and what they offer makes them a very special shop. The expansion of their restaurant will be great and you can always count on the best natural products with incredible health and wellness insight! Worth going to on a regular basis! A+++
name: David

text:
Amazing is really the only word for Zahav. 

Order light and al a carte, the tasting menu is huge.
name: Jared

text: Rayaki is a casual quick eats Japanese restaurant. Loved the ordering system, where you check boxes off a menu and the items are then brought to you. I ordered the taro bubble tea, chicken robatayaki, and chicken ramen. The taro bubble tea is pretty big and definitely well priced. Very tasty too! The robatayaki was a little disappointing as one order consists of one skewer. However the price and quality makes up for it! The main attraction was the ramen, which along with its elegant presentation, smelled delicious. Personally the soup was a little thick, but was still very well balanced with the noodles. The chicken was similar to the robatayaki chicken and was definitely the standout for the ramen, as it should be. Good balance of vegetables and a nice yolk-y egg finished off the garnish and had me finish off the bowl very quickly. All in all a great experience, and will definitely return with friends!
name: Nithish

text: I came to Jim's during a bachelor party, they place is pretty open but the seating is basically a bunch of seat yourself 4 person table and bar seats. We got about 13 people in here and got food pretty quickly. The place also has pickles and pepper that you can grab as much as you like from jars. The cheese steaks are not my favorite but they are good and they were the groom to be's favorite. All in all I wouldn't go out of my way for Jim's but If I was hungry and they were close they would do the job.
name: Mike

text: I love this place. The food is great. Coffee is wonderful. I really enjoy their seasonal drink menus. The staff is pleasant. It's the whole package.
name: Jordan

text: The donuts are always so fresh. It's tradition that my family go almost every weekend to grab some bagels, donut holes and coffee! It's a must in the area.
name: LeighAnn

text: Reserved a room a month ago for a concert and when we showed up to check in the pool and spa are out of service. Tried to book at another hotel but no luck. Asked for upgrade with no luck. Got our room and could not believe they are charging 175.00 a night for these rooms. No fridge,no microwave and wallpaper peeling off the walls. Would have been beter to go to motel 6. At least they paint every now and then. I dont mind paying the price if i get what im paying for. Come on guys really.

text: Found on YELP and took a chance.   It was great!   Pressed Italian sandwich was great.   Owner/Chef was very nice and everything came out hot and fresh.
name: Bryan

text:
This isn't your run of the mill Mexican place. The menu is a little smaller then the bigger places but don't be fooled , the flavors will knock your socks off. The place is super cute with a side of trendy. The wait staff... amazing!!!! The salsa is dark, rich and oh so good. There is a hidden burrito that's not on the menu. With steak chicken and topped with Parmesan cheese. GET IT!!!  You won't regret it. 

Go now. Go to Mekenita. It's awesome!!!
name: John

text: If we hadn't done the food and wine pairing, I would have been highly disappointed. We arrived an hour early to tour the grounds and it took us about 15 minutes. We probably spent more time in the gift shop to be honest- there was more to look at. However, 4 stars because the wine and food pairing experience was amazing!! As someone who's visited nearly 20 wineries, I learned so much from our instructor. The wines weren't my favorite but I was able to appreciate how we were taught to drink them and what to eat with them. We took my mom for her 60th Birthday and she loved it!
name: Liz

text: Popped in here on a whim and were glad we did! Such a great little place. We will be back again soon.
name: LaTasha

text: The setting is pretty much unbeatable, especially on the patio. The menu is straight forward. We got a variety of appetizers; I personally tried the tartare and the calamari. The calamari was excellent and the tartare was pretty good as well. The pasta I got was the Mezze Maniche, which was perfect. Since I don't want my pasta to be too heavy on sauce, it ended up being light and delicious. Only criticism is that, for Italian food, it definitely is expensive on the basis that it's pasta and pizza.
name: Petar

text: My family came here Mother's Day and it was an over the top experience. Everything was on point, From the moment you step foot inside of this restaurant you get the whole home vibe feel and then as soon as you put the food up to your mouth you feel like you've been reborn. This is a must try restaurant for any occasion. So stop wasting time figuring out what to eat and go to Backfin now and I promise you'll be super satisfied. Keep up the good work guys much love.
name: Brandon

text: Really good food at a great price. Wont give 4 stars until I try the dinner buffet. The other customer there that day was loud and biligerant and I wish the staff would have moved them to an isolated corner. But my waitress was nice and prompt. Cant wait to go back.
name: Sara

text: I had not been to a Cantina Los Tres Hombres in some time and I've never been to the location at The Legends Mall in Sparks. We were there for last minute Christmas shopping and found ourselves hungry. We were seated quickly.  Our server was  very attentive. The only complaint is that there was no prices on the drink menu. I wanted a margarita or teo6a d often at a Mexican restaurant if you are going to have more than one margarita sometimes the pitcher is a better deal. No option to choose without asking. Not a big deal but it would have been nice. I ordered the shrimp appetizer. Really good. My dining partner got the taco salad.  He  liked it but didnt love it. Over all, good, not great.
name: Kristyna

text: Lovely little Thai restaurant in Brandon Fl. The food was amazing, and they are also veggie/vegan friendly. Nothing seemed overpriced. Good service and will definitely eat there again soon.
name: Marissa

text:
I'm a big fan of savory crepes since living in the Bay Area and long for a crepe place in Reno so I was thrilled to see this open in the Costco plaza by the airport.  It isn't really like the crepes I was longing for, but good in it's own regard.  

The crepes are enormous, soft, and generously filled.  The sweet ones in particular look really amazing, we didn't get to try one this time despite our best intention because the savory crepes were so huge and filling.  We will make a visit just for the sweet next time.  The staff is very friendly, but typically it appears there are only 1 or 2 people working so it may be a long wait.  When we went we were in no rush, but it might not be the best choice for someone on a limited meal break.  We had the ham and cheese with egg and the special Santa Fe with green chiles, chicken, and salsa.  My kids enjoyed watching the crepes being made.  

Thank you for the friendly service and delicious crepes.
name: Sj

text: Small family owned restaurant that just opened up recently with a good size menu, good portion sizes and very reasonable prices.  It's what I would call a "hole-in-the-wall" kind of place so it's not fancy or trendy but the food is solid and the owners were friendly.  The food was seasoned nicely and had good flavor.  If you're seeking a good meal for a reasonable price this will make you happy.  If you're looking for a place to impress someone this would not be the venue.
name: T

text:
Finally tried out this place on Monday afternoon. It was really just *okay*. It wasn't very busy, but service was still kind of slow. Our server wasn't very friendly. I wouldn't say he was un-friendly or rude, but he basically was doing the least. 

The menu doesn't have that great of a selection in my opinon. You basically have a couple of flatbreads and a couple of sandwich options and that's it. I ended up going for the Proscuitto and Pear Flatbread which was, again, just *okay.* 

I probably won't be back again, but it wasn't that bad of a place. *shrug*
name: Mo

text: Worse experience I've had in a while at a restaurant. We had a large group but it was booked well in advance. There were 2 servers for our group of 50. 3 hrs after I arrived they were still trying to get entrees out. No refills. To know that far in advance and not staffed accordingly both front and back of the house was very sad. 45 minutes after finishing my meal, where my daughter's hamburger was undercooked, and the steak had no flavor, I was still waiting for the check. My first and last visit  to Legend's Steakhouse. Service is definitely lacking!
name: Elliott

text: First and last time at this Johnny Rockets. This was the smallest, tasteless burger I have ever had. Ordered a spicy burger with chipotle sauce that I never got and pepper jack cheese that had no pepper in it.  The salad was not fresh that I ordered on the side.  Next time I will visit Red Robin in the same mall for less money and get a great burger and unlimited fries.
