text: Ended up here pretty late, maybe around 9:30, because everything else nearby had a wait. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way.
name: User

text:
The tourist trap ribs were ok.  The wait in line thing is a trend I don't like.  (40 min)Any how the potato salad 
Was good, and thank you for serving green beans NOT out the can.  I got a frito pie to go. Got home, opened the container only to find a "do it yourself " kit , bag of Fritos, two containers of baked beans, and a container of cheese and onions.  Ridiculous!!!
name: Ann

text: Our reservation was for 9 PM New Year's Eve, and when checking in were informed that they were twenty minutes behind on seating- and were seated at 9:10.  The only miscue of the evening was the temperature at the table, being seated directly under an air conditioning vent. No matter where we sat at the table we experienced a chill wind in our faces.  Service was very attentive and the food was expertly timed- we had no sooner finished our plump crab cakes and tender calamari when our Fideua and paella was delivered.  My Fideua had bountiful seafood, and where some restaurants would have a higher proportion of mussels and clams, the shrimp and sea scallops were the ones crowding the plate. I thought the red sauce not very spicy as advertised, but tasty nonetheless.  My husband was very happy with his paella, noting though that it was a bit saltier than he prefers.  Both of us elected to take some of our entrees home to enjoy the next day to facilitate getting dessert that night.  We probably could have shared the White Chocolate Bread Pudding.  It is served as two large warm slices with a sweet Bacardi rum sauce. I say we could have shared but was glad my husband ordered the Brazo Gitano which left more of the pudding for me.  The server was alert, bringing our check shortly after we finished, and stopped by to retrieve it moments later.  We expected to be there two hours but it was more like 100 minutes, not rushed and not waiting for anything.  We left full, happy, and committed to return for another special event.
name: Tom

text: Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. Food was fresh and service was quick. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Food was good and came out fast. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything..
name: User

text: My buddy and I ate here a couple times for the oysters and enjoyed them every single time. Service was great and was only a minute away from our hotel. He also ordered the po boy and loved it and i tried the grouper sandwich which was very tasty. We never had any issues with waiting time and basically got a seat right away every time we went in. Overall, great food, great atmosphere and great service. Would definitely recommend.
name: Edward

text:
Made for a nice Valentine dinner for the wife and me.  Menu was the regular menu, so I was able to judge the regular food vs. a special prix fixe offering of the evening.  The starters/appetizers list is quite extensive, about 13-14 different options.  They vary frequently, and come written on a small slate.  (The menu also is updated frequently, with a new menu prepared for each month.)  Interesting an unusual choices were included, such as lobster turnovers, octopus confit, sweetbreads, etc.  We went with a sampler of lobster turnovers, veal dumplings, and spring rolls.  The turnover and dumpling were both savory choices.  Spring rolls weren't bad, but pretty much like you'd get a PF Chang's, e.g.

The waitress told us at the start that she would describe everything, but we could tell her if we only wanted specific items described, the entire list, or nothing at all.  It was good to have that option presented up front, since the descriptions were extensive and there were a lot of options - both on the starter list and the main menu.  We actually opted for the entire spiel, and she did a pretty good job holding our interest with inflection and such.

For the main items, my wasabi filet was extremely tender, cooked exactly to the medium I ordered, and had a great sear and crust to it.  The wasabi was really just flavor with wasabi butter, which was explained to me beforehand.  It did add a nice interesting flavor to enhance the dish.  The wife's filet Bearnaise was similarly excellent, with a generous lobster stuffing and sauce on top.  Half of that went home for her next day lunch.  The pomme puree that came under her steak gave a nice offset to the steak and side veggies.

Dessert turned out to be a bit of a disappointment.  We got the deconstructed carrot cake.  While interesting, the deconstruction resulted in lost flavor, as the mixing of carrot cake ingredients results in a whole greater than the parts.

But generally a great place for some very well thought out entrees.  Probably too rich to eat at weekly, but certainly for when you want something a bit special.

This place specializes in craft cocktails so it should be understand that you might have to wait a bit to get your dinks.  I expect that.  Our friends did warn us that you can spend a lot of time waiting here and we certainly did.  

The food is served tapas style and it comes out as it is ready.  That works well actually given the limited surface area.  Keep that in mind as you'll probably want to order a number of things for your party.

I'd rate this place a bit higher but at the end things just really started to drag.  We ordered dessert and drinks at the same time, but the dessert came 15 minutes before the drinks. Give this place a try but don't be in a hurry.

text:
We were burglarized in our room while we were sleeping, and Marriott does not care.

I had trouble sleeping the night of Sept 21st and awoke up twice that night, so we pretty much have the exact time the burglary happened.  At 1228am I looked at my cell phone that was charging on the night stand.  At 342am I went to check the time and the phone was not there.  I woke up my wife and asked her to check her nightstand for her pone; it was gone as well.  We then realized we had a problem and checked our wallets.  Our cash was missing, but our credit cards and wallet were there.
I guess we should be glad we did not wake up while the burglars were in our room. Who knows what they would have done to us.
(When we got home we noticed that our Movie Pass MasterCard were stolen as well. Perhaps this why they did not take our other credit cards.)
As we looked around the hotel room, we noticed the front door was slightly ajar.  We then noticed our watches were missing. I immediately called the front desk who connected me to Loss Prevention (LP), and they came up to the room and took a report.   LP called the Philadelphia Police (PPD) for us.  Then LP came back to our and did some kind of mystery test on the door - we were told the test can tell if the door was closed properly and/or when it was opened, or something like that.
Later that morning, the hotel manager accompanied the PPD to our room and asked if we had called for the police and then the manager promptly disappeared.  The Officer took our report and was pretty startled when we explained that it happened when we were sleeping.  The approx. total of what was taken is $2,000.  After the PDD Officer took our information, he said he would talk to the LP and/or management to gather more information.
At different times, both the LP and PPD officers mentioned the door did not close properly.  Later in the morning I went to discuss what happened to us with the manager.  He basically looked at me like I was from Mars - he had no sympathy and wanted to end the conversation as quickly as he could. He not even over to comp us for the night.
LP forwarded info about our incident to the Marriott Claim dept.  The Claims Dept is telling me since we did not put our phones in the safe WHEN WE SLEEP, it's our fault and tough luck.  
The Downtown Marriot has been uncooperative with the claims dept; it's as if they know they were wrong and don't want to give any information. We have heard nothing from the hotel, it's like we don't exist to them.
Doing some research on Trip Advisor I noticed that another guest at the hotel was burglarized while they were sleeping in Sept 2017.  This hotel has an ongoing problem with burglaries while guest are sleeping.  
IF you VALUE YOUR well-being and property don't stay at this hotel.  When you are burglarized while sleeping in your own hotel room, Marriott will say it's your fault.

text:
As a regular at Passé for 8 years, I'm sad to say they may be losing my business. The cafe has always embodied a dilapidated charm that inspires artists to thrive and foothills folk to ooo and aw. But now their standard seems to be more dilapidation, less inspiration. Table legs have screws poking out that stab you, at least twice a month, I watch someone fall through the back of their unmaintained chairs (seriously guys, an Allen wrench, a posi-drive screwdriver, and some wood glue is all you need) miraculously avoiding injury, and now that their hours have changed, I buy coffee from the bartender, who overcharges me for coffee because he doesn't know the price. Truth is, all of that is easily fixed. But I doubt it will be.

All of that aside, what is going to chase me away (and others I've spoken to who have observed and expressed the same) is the misogynistic behavior of their new bar manager Don. I've observed him, first hand, making inappropriate, belittling, and offensive comments to/about women (customers and his fellow employees). Either this mentality was overlooked or is considered excusable by the owners, as he somehow managed to receive his promotion while demonstrating these behaviors regularly. I find them to be entirely inexcusable, even if he can also be a friendly guy, which he often is. That does not excuse him.

If such mentalities are rewarded here, this is not where I want to spend my time or money any longer. 

Bringing this to yelp because I've brought these topics up with numerous employees, but now I recognize that this will likely yield a more appropriate response from the owners. At least I hope so. It used to be that there was no place better in all of Tucson.

Chargrilled oysters were delicious. Everything that everyone ordered people were happy with. I tried the gumbo and the brownie. I also tried the banana mojito and I was pleasantly surprised with the flavor. It was not too much banana flavor.

text:
3rd visit, with 8 guests, very slow service and marginal dinners. Took 3 1/2 hours to complete dinner, at least 40 minutes between soup/salad and dinner arrival. Soup not hot, most everyone commented on food being to salty, one person had to send dish back, another's portion very small, sea scollop special salty with 3 scallops for $36!!, my clams & mussels in lemon sauce was watery and very salty, did not eat most of it. If a restaurant can't be consistent it's not a good restaurant.  Will think twice before going back. It was not a good or enjoyable evening, poor experience and over priced.  

Regretfully went to this restaurant for the 4th time because it was a group outing that others wanted to go to.  Nothing has changed, some dinners were good others not.  Waiter was less than professional. Time between salad and main course was excessive. One person did not get their dinner until at least 5 minutes after everyone else was served. Another had bones in her fish and could not eat it. No offer to remove it from their bill!!!  I don't see how anyone could give this place a good rating.
name: S

text: So spent a weekend in Indy - dined at several spots and have to say Milktooth was far and away the best, most creative and overall delicious place we tried - not a scientific study on a small sample size but if you are looking for something special this is your spot.  First accept the super hipster vibe in a renovated garage just know they did it first and were way out in front of the crowd - good news is the hosts/servers were more than friendly and proficient at their tasks - not easy given the constant crowd.  We snuck in around 9:00 am and got what appeared to be the last open table but if you have to wait coffee (really excellent coffee) is available while you wait.  So do you get a breakfast appetizer - sure - and make certain it is the toaster strudel - a rectangular piece of light layers (so many layers) of soft dough surrounding a warm interior of gushy blackberry and nectarine - should have had two - or three - split one is not enough.  Also - the coffee - mentioned above - went with their Peruvian Indy Tinker coffee and can't think of a reason to try another kind.  My dining friend did something involving maple and gave me a taste - too sweet for me but it was a beautiful cup.  So main course for me was the Smashed Chickpea Tartine - a combination of hard boil egg, chickpea, semolina, cashews brought together with a harissa yogurt and pepitas - not sure who came up with that combo but glad they did - a bright breakfast dish that I couldn't replicate at home - so good.  My  dining friend went with the Bruchetta Dutch Pancake - a savory vs sweet take with sauteed (roasted?) veggies in a garlic aioli on a firmer "pancake" that was crusty than pancakey - kind of breakfast pizza - it was very nice but maybe better for lunch than breakfast.  What was awesome for breakfast was the Anson Mill Grits - add the egg, bacon and scallions and it is a whole meal unto itself - it appears Milktooth is equally adept at keeping it simple as well as going off the wall.  Service as mentioned above was uniformly excellent and prices extremely reasonable given what is going on in the kitchen.  Need to come back and start working through their lengthy list of cocktails - next visit for sure.
name: Kevin

text: We were looking for good coffee in Fenton. The Google search led us to Russell's. We immediately loved this place because it reminds us of some of the cafes we ate at when my friend lived in Europe. The coffee was so good and the food was delicious.
name: Renae

text: I love love love this sushi place. First let me say that these 1$ sushi rolls ARE VERY SMALL! However I love that because I can try a little bit of everything! Not only that but they have really good Korean BBQ and they have those little grills at your table. Also, I love their fried rice I'm not just saying that. I truly have never had fried rice that good in my entire life! The portion is HUGE so definitely a shareable dish. (They don't do side dishes) as far as drinks they are mediocre. My mojito was pretty much water. Just get a beer or sake if you're wanting a drink. I rated this 5 starts because their menu is really unique compared to sushi garden or even Ra. I really like the atmosphere when it isn't busy lol. But again dollar sushi here my tab is about 25$ for like 6-7 different rolls you can't beat that!
name: Laura

text: I am originally from California, I grew up eating street tacos there. Ever since my relocation to Nashville I've been looking for the same experience. I have finally found it. I have had every meat option they offer. None of which will disappoint. I would say these are the best tacos in Nashville. If you are searching for a great place this is it. Also the prices are great!

text: The duo combo is absolutely amazing with the beef and lamb burgers. Then i got a bacon cheese fry that was to die for. Their burgers are definitely gourmet an they off so many toppings it was hard to choose what I wanted.

text: Stopped by for a quick trip this summer after visiting Urban Vines. Same great service and taste as the original Bru on Mass Ave. I just love the Snack Pack. Perfect portion at such a surprisingly price for such a quality restaurant. My burger was a tad bit too salty which isn't usually the case. The outdoor seating is nice and quaint. Perfect spot to just chill. Oh, don't forget to get your points for the Cunningham VIP rewards program!

text: My family and I have come here many times, and while they've all enjoyed their meals, I never have! Last time I went, I got huevos rancheros & was super excited. But the eggs were watery & soggy, there was almost no flavor/seasoning, and the potatoes were bland and very cold. I also went today with some friends to give it a second chance, and was let down again. I ordered the Smoked Salmon Eggs Benedict, and didn't take more than a small bite. The poached eggs were fantastic and so were the potatoes, but that was the only thing I took from it. The salmon was mealy & you could tell it had been sitting out for a while, or maybe purchased a long time ago. The bagel was burnt, all black (and it was soggy). The cream cheese was 100% spoiled, as everyone in my party tried it and agreed. I just could not even take more than a bite. I do love the atmosphere but it just isn't living up to any other breakfast places. The two stars are mainly for the beignets & honey marmalade, I've ordered them each time and they've never disappointed. Their iced coffees are also very delicious.
name: Anna

text: Food took forever but ended up being better than I expected. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. Food was fresh and service was quick. maybe I just came on an off day. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. They were out of one thing I originally wanted..
name: User

text: Lona's Lil Eats is a hidden gem located in the Fox Park neighborhood. Lona is known for her giant rice paper wraps and her amazing dumpling appetizer. I got the steak option for the dumplings but they have mushroom as well. They were so delicious with a spicy chili dipping sauce that was the perfect compliment. I also did a create your own wrap. For mine I chose chicken, stir fried rice, and spicy sesame sauce. For the $9.25 price it also included a side which I got the lime peanut salad. The wrap was full of flavor and giant as advertised very filling. The lime peanut salad was a wonderful accompaniment. I'm not a fan of eggplant but for those who are I've heard the spicy eggplant side is a great option as well. The only thing I don't love about this restaurant is the wait. I got there at 11:45 and the line was to the door. After waiting ten minutes and the line not moving anywhere I ended up ordering their takeout from my phone. I was able to get that in about fifteen minutes and took it home with me instead of eating in. FYI I'm sure the wait isn't going to get much better now that Chef Lona was nominated for a James Beard! What an amazing accomplishment!
name: Haley

text: Ordered the garlic parm wings. They were good and stayed hot all the way home, I love 30 mins away.
name: Ashley

text:
I was hoping for breakfast, but I got there too late. Breakfast ends at 10:30 am but lunch is also really good at this cafeteria-style meat and three restaurant. The day we went there were plenty of tables and the cafeteria line went quick. We also were able to find a parking place even though parking is limited.

I ordered dressing, pineapple casserole, roasted potatoes and vegetables, and a biscuit. The dressing was really good. It wasn't too dry like some dressings can be. The roasted potatoes were delicious, especially with carrots and onions. But my favorite dish of all was the pineapple casserole! The name may sound funky, but it was incredible. It was a cross between a side dish and a dessert and reminded me of a pineapple upside cake. I should have asked if they sell it by the quart. 

The only thing I wish they would change is to not use items that will compromise the environment. All the plates were styrofoam, the utensils were plastic and so were the cups.
name: Linda

text: This is my go to pizza place. Menu has everything you could want. The pizza is delicious and a little greasy which is nice. The honey chicken wrap and buffalo chicken pizza are some of my favorites and I would highly recommend them.

text: This place is a diamond in the dirt. Hands down the best Vietnamese I have had in the south eastern region from Texas all the way to South Carolina. The Vietnamese traditional sandwich Bahn Mi is freaking Amazing!! Next to them they make their own bread So the sandwiches are freshly made daily.
name: Zachary

text:
I recommend their quiche and hash browns. The German chocolate cake was one of the best I've had.

This place gets 3 stars because of the service. The team approach doesn't work well. We had 5 different servers taking orders, delivering food, giving refills and settling the bill with us. It gets a little tiresome when someone asks you if we've been helped a couple of times and tells us the dessert menu a few times. Seems inefficient. We paid for our meal, and our original server stopped by to ask us (in a condescending tone) if we had a chance to think about dessert-- clearly seeing we had to-go containers with dessert. We told her we ordered dessert. She essentially blamed US for not telling her to add It to our ticket. We couldn't tell what we were paying for on the ticket because there were no descriptions and it is not our fault it wasn't communicated by the 5th employee who helped us and delivered the dessert. No reason to be rude to us. The restaurant would probably have better service if one server took care of each section.

text: Stopped by after work because I was nearby and hungry. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. text: Unlike my friends, particularly Nathan C, I did not enjoy the overly-hyped food at Bonchon. When we arrived, we were seated promptly and were able to order our choice of wings in a friendly manner. However, the speed of service proved very slow, and the food quality did not live up to the long wait. Despite us being in a group of 11, the wait was unreasonable considering it was a wait for overly-fried chicken wings. While they are not bad, the wings are very dry and overly crispy (there is not enough meat on the wing in proportion to the crispy breading). While I did not want "soggy wings," I did want some meat to complement a crispiness with the breading. Also, the two sauces available on the wings reach extremes that make the wings "boring" to eat after 1 or 2. The spicy sauce is too spicy that makes them harder to eat, while the Garlic Soy sauce has a dominating garlic flavor that makes the wings overwhelming. The two sauces together did not complement well, and the flavor was ultimately disastrous. Overall, the wings were not saucy enough, the sauce available did not satisfy good flavor, and the wings did not have enough meat to the bone. While I do enjoy fried chicken coming from the Southeast, I would probably refrain from returning, to the dismay of Nathan C.
name: Reviewer

text:
4.5/5.0 STARS
The sausage patties were amazing! Throw that on some sourdough and I would have it every morning. Mmmm.
The eggs were prepared nicely. Ordered 2 scrambled and got more than I thought it would be.
I made a slight misstep with the blueberry pancakes. The pancake itself was really nice, crispy yet soft. But the blueberries were a miss for me. I think if I got the plain buttermilk I would have taken them all down!
Price is the only reason I feel like I can't give 5.0 stars. $22 for all of the food plus coffee. Merp. A bit much.

text:
I stumbled upon Portico after I came downtown early one morning to meet a friend. It's was one of three coffee shops open within a half a mile radius.  The space is very artsy, open, and has table and comfy seating. Local art is hung all over the interior.  Mostly small paintings.

I got an almond milk latte because milk isn't for me anymore and it was ok! The milk to coffee ratio was a bit off. I love strong espresso and my latte was so diluted that all I could taste was the milk.  

Staff was extremely friendly and the space was comfortable. I'll def be back to see if I'll have a 5 star experience.

text:
2nd time to Ford's Garage, 2st time at this location. I absolutely love the restaurant decorated with old Ford vehicles, car parts and memorabilia. The burger buns are branded with the restaurant logo and are tasty. The servers are all dressed as mechanics. Our server today was Kate and she did a great job of taking care of us. Our glasses were never empty. The restrooms follow the theme of the restaurant and are very very clean. The menu is pretty large with many great choices. Next time, I think I will order dessert 1st as we never make it to dessert as we are too full. This is definitely one of my favorite restaurants and it's because of the combination of everything I shared. This is an experience for sure, especially for car lovers.

4th visit today and we love this place. Today we ordered the Chop Shop Dalad with smoky ranch dressing which is a proper Cobb Salad where all ingredients are truly chopped. We also ordered a Classic Cheeseburger with green beans as a side instead of fries and the Brisket Cheeseburger which has bacon, cheese, onion straws, red onions, and topped with a smoky Brisket with BBQ sauce and a side of Mac n cheese instead of fries. All items were super tasty and well worth ordering again. We definitely love Fords Garage and have visited 2 in the state and looking forward to the Lakeland restaurant opening in 2018.

I opted for spinach and received a great Cobb Salad that hardly needed salad dressing due to the creamy avocado included. It was delicious and filling. My husband had the BLT and the decadent Oreo milkshake. A previous reviewer put us on to the shake and he wasn't wrong. You order it, you won't be unhappy. The place is very clean and bright, with a cheerful, hard working staff. I give it an unqualified two thumbs up.

text: Second visit on Derby Day and enjoyed both visits. Staff is friendly and they have valet parking during dinner, which is helpful in that neighborhood. Two reasons that I didn't give them 5 stars:  the Mint Julep was disappointing and the risotto was bland. A restaurant that specializes in whiskey should nail a Julep every time. Ours were properly served in a Julep cup with lots of crushed ice, but the mint was nowhere to be found. I even emptied my cup to make sure-none. The risotto served with the halibut special was very bland-the two ingredients that should always be in risotto (other than rice) are white wine and parmigiana.  Couldn't taste either. Otherwise we enjoyed the wings, ravioli, halibut and steak. Great people watching at the Derby Party!
name: Sara

text:
This is the only Chili's I will ever go to. Such a great staff and the bartenders are all super friendly. I always do the two for one margaritas or the presidente margaritas with strawberry and mango. Super delicious combo. I've never had any issues here and I've been going here for about 8 years now consistently. 
It's not the closet Chili's to my house, but I always choose this one over others. The bathrooms are always clean and I can't say that about other locations that I've been to.

text: The restaurant itself is brand new and has the feel of something promising. It is modern in design and is connected to the playhouse. Let's get to the food. We ordered the mushroom taco ( the vegetarian option of the Korean bbq version) and it was fantastic. The seasoning and flavor really popped. I couldn't get enough of it. My wife ordered the Buddha bowl. It was exactly what a vegetarian would like in a dish.  Impossible meatballs make it look like meat but with the recent reports about them, maybe a small change is in order. The only criticism is that it was one of the most expensive items on the menu. She said I hope they keep it but readjust the price. I had the black garlic chicken. It was fantastic. The chicken cut like butter and the raviolis were so fresh and tasty. I could have drank the sauce it was that good. To cap the night off, we ordered the chocolate cake with chamomile ice cream. It was the perfect ending. It was a light cake and the ice cream was tasty. For a restaurant that hasn't had its grand opening, it was great. One factory that you can't order was the service. Our waiter knew everything about the menu and was great. The other staff wouldn't let my water glass be empty. I hope this is a new go to restaurant in New Hope. We will be back.

Their salsa bar has a wide variety of delicious salsas. Everyone was very polite and the food was made quickly.
name: Anisa

text: The food was terrible!  I ordered from UberEats and got the worst food I've ever had.  I had to throw the entire order away.  The fish and chips were soaked in grease.  The fries were soft and greasy.  I ordered nachos with no beef (because I don't eat meat) and received nachos covered in beef.  I ordered sauce with the chicken wings for my fiance and got no sauce.  I will never order from or eat here again.  If I could give zero stars, I would.
name: Katie

text: I'm very much impressed with Craft Street Kitchen. Very trendy. Great draught beer selection (they have Reef Donkey; my favorite). I only tried an appetizer and dessert: the avocado hummus and peanut butter pie. Impressed with both. I'll be back to try entrees and enjoy more of their beer selection. Kids Mac n Cheese is great by the way. Can't wait to go back!
name: Bridget

text: I diner here for the first time for happy hour on a Sunday. I was able to make reservations on open table (a plus for me) and they have a happy hour food menu. The food was delicious (except the soup, which lacked flavor). The selection wasn't huge, but I certainly didn't leave hungry. The fried chickpeas are where it's at. The happy hour prices for drinks aren't bad either - wines are $5 and the cocktails I looked at were $6. The service was decent and the place was nice and bright (we sat up front by the window). They also have outdoor seating which is a nice option. Next time I come I'm going to try the fried chicken sandwich or burger. Both looked delicious.
name: Jennie

text:
I've been coming to this Bertucci's since they first opened in Huntingdon Valley many years ago.  During that time they've made it a point to spotlight their line of excellent brick oven pizzas.  However, many of their other authentic Italian dishes are worth checking out as well, and they usually have a rotating menu of seasonal specials to complement their core offerings.
As others have noted, perhaps the best part of a visit here is the fresh hot sourdough rolls that are brought to the table as soon as you are seated.  They are truly delicious, especially when dipped in olive oil with some parmesan cheese and spices.  There is a very respectable selection of bottled and draft beers, wines, and cocktails from which to choose.  The decor of the restaurant is pretty straightforward, nothing too flashy and yet nothing too boring either.  It's a nice comfortable spot to grab dinner for two or for the whole family.
name: Joseph

text: Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced.
name: User

text: The food is good, but the service is horrible.  You will have long waits as your table.  If got takeout and they make a mistake.  I thought I could get it replaced the next day on my way home from work, but they insisted I had to bring in their mistaken story.
name: Charles

text: Not bad for a quick meal. Honestly, i got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. So yeah, delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. Anyway, nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. The wait wasnt awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. maybe I just came on an off day.
name: User

text: So good! The Pecan Parmesan crusted Trout is always good. This location is my favorite. (Belleair Bluffs) The crowd is usually the classy type. They are not low rent, that's for sure. But it's not too expensive or anything. If you join their member rewards club you'll get $20 off ever few visits or so.
name: Stephanie

text: Enjoyed this place.  Grouper very good.  Crab legs ok, but not great.  Philly cheesesteak good.  Waiter very attentive with drink refills and making sure everything was good.  Large containers of all necessary condiments on table.  Paper towels hang above table.  Walls plastered with decorations and dollar bills.
name: Thomas

text: We've eaten there a few times.  It has a nice atmosphere, and the food is good.  We had good service.  It does have a dedicated parking lot, which is very nice to have on Magazine street.
name: James

text:
Oh-wow Oh-wow! How did this happen?! This egg McMuffin I just picked up in the drive-through. . . This thing is legitimately amazingly good! I don't know if they are holding Gordon Ramsey in there or if I've just never had a fresh egg McMuffin before! 

I can see inside and apparently the whole place was just redone and it looks nice. 

I don't know how it happened but this was delicious!!
name: Amber

text: I decided to give this place a try because of all the positive reviews. They were right! The food was fantastic. I had the bibimbap with tuna and it was excellent. Not only did it look good but the taste was exceptional. I will certainly be back.
name: Cory

text: Just tried The Blue Elephant tonight for the first time - very impressed. The updated interior is exceptionally well appointed in blue and greys with very comfortable seating and atmosphere. Lauren M was our professional server. She was very attentive and polite. I had the short ribs with truffle potatoes and my partner had the lobster curry linguine. Both were excellent, and of course we couldn't pass on Creme brûlée for dessert. I would highly recommend this restaurant and Lauren for an excellent dining experience!! We will be back again soon
name: Dennis

text: This place was amazing. The staff taking orders and cooking the food were both so nice and super attentive to getting me what I needed. The food was fried with fresh oil, the food was so good! The price was also great for the amount of food you got!. Overall I would recommend this place completely!
name: Jordan

text:
FYI: Put your name down on the iPad by the front door to be added to their waiting list! Also, the iPad above the table is just another menu, in case y'all are wondering.

PROS: You come for essentially 2 things: the novelty of the whole idea of "conveyor belt hot pot" and the wagyu beef. Literally that's it. Granted the beef is probably one of the better hot pot meat I've had in all my years of eating hot pot. It's pretty soft and melts in your mouth. Tastes better if you dip it into their house made yuzu sauce thing (which by the way was the star of the meal). The convenience of the whole thing is pretty great: you see an item you want on the belt and you take it. Our waiter was also an absolute gem. So nice and really attentive. The whole thing is definitely a fun thing to do maybe like...once.

CONS: Where do I even begin. For starters, they don't got a sauce bar. The waiter will come around with this big tray of sauces and you take from that. Then they take it away. So basically, you either leave that thing on your table and have it take up literally 75% of the space on your table or you let the waiter take it back and are sauceless halfway through your meal if you don't make enough. We also ordered some pork belly with our wagyu and that thing came in the most pathetic little slices. Like so small and so thin that you can't taste nothing after you put it in your pot. To be honest, I lost half of them in there. They also don't tell you what items are gonna be on the conveyor belt. When we went, we basically saw the same couple of items being offered on it (mainly fish balls and veggies with a few spams, tofus, and eggs). You can still order items from the menu but it'd be helpful to have some kind of like "conveyor belt" list of items or something to let you know what'll be on it so you can plan out what you order a la carte. Let me also just say that even when you order a la carte, the portion sizes vary from too much (they gave us a whole butt load of quail eggs) to LITERALLY NOTHING. Don't judge me but I actually counted how many strands of potato noodles we got cause it looked really empty in the bowl. THERE WAS ONLY LIKE 12 STRANDS! 12 STRANDS! EXCUSE ME???And lord have mercy...THE PRICE. IT AINT WORTH IT PEOPLE. It's really not. My husband and I ate less than what we usually eat at Little Sheep and had to pay MORE. Besides the wagyu beef, everything else didn't taste any different from another hot pot place in Chinatown so essentially, you're paying more to eat the same food but a lesser portion. Their stock was also...mildly flavored at best. Like dawg...if all you really have to offer me is one choice of good meat and a conveyor belt with like the same 8 items circulating around it, you better not be charging me those ridiculous prices.
name: Sherry

text: Please turn up the air! Love the food, despise the heat. Wilting.........isn't favorable, when your choosing to dine here.
name: Stacey

text: Great family friendly, killer food, amazing music kinda joint. Love the people who work here and the food they serve. Big fan!
name: Tryg

text: We were hesitant to try as it only had a rating of 3.5.  That rating is sooo off!  Cute place.  GOOD prices.  Excellent margaritas.  Food was outstanding.  Service great.  What is missing?  NOTHING!  Kellen, our bartender, was attentive and personable.  Then he got slammed and he was efficient.  We can't wait to eat there again.
name: Trusting

text:
My family and I went there on Saturday night. Not many people there but we were very happy to not have to wait in a line. We ordered the family dinner #5( I think). The girl at the counter was really helpful in helping us pick. We also ordered some smoked chicken wings and smoked bacon. Dinner came with a pick of 4 sides. We got the Mac and Cheese, smoked beans, cole slaw and collard greens. 
The pulled chicken and ribs were excellent. The brisket was really good, a little dry though. The smoked chicken wings were awesome!!  I enjoyed all the sides as did my wife. The kids really don't eat slaw so. 

I would definitely return for lunch and or dinners. We all left happy and full. Service was quick.
name: Chris

text: Great for breakfast. They cook the food right in front of you. Pancakes were amazing! Love this diner!
name: Amanda

text: Dessert saved this a little. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. I'd maybe go back, but I'd order differently next time. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced.
name: User

text: First visit to Hooks on 4th, been meaning to try it for a while. Pleasantly surprised, staff were great and a decent menu, food was great, I'll be back!
name: Pete

text: I just dropped in to get on the wifi and enjoy some iced tea(which was excellent)so I can't say anything about the food but the space had a great vibe and the service was professional, friendly and fast.
name: Isaac

text: Wonderful atmosphere, beautifully decorated! Anything I've ever ordered is delicious, really nice place to enjoy everything Italian
name: Kathleen

text: A friend recommended this place set it was very good. My S.O and i went and ordered the General tso chicken and the chicken fried rice. We get and start eating and we look down and there is a dead fly and a dead roach in our food. We left and will never go back. Why they are still open i have no clue they need to be shut down.
name: Cody

text: This place was a delight. The food was delicious...  I had a beef enchilada omlette that was out of this world.and three cups of coffee, the third one was forced upon me my our waiter, God, aka Thomas. He was funny, not funny "haha" but looks aren't everything....I loved the food so much, I'm going to try to figure out how to cook it at home since we're just passing though. Thanks for a delicious relaxing hilarious breakfast
name: Christine

text:
OMG! This place is amazing.  I am not even sure where to begin.  I guess I will stat with we didn't have a reservation.  So we showed up on a Friday night and were seated right away.  This is not something I would expect in this establishment by any means but it was a holiday weekend which I think helped our cause. 

I should preface this review by saying that we went to the Italian part of St. Louis because not only is my husband part Italian but pasta is his absolute favorite food.  And these guys did not disappoint.  

On the menu, they have a "Challenge." You have to finish the challenge in an hour and there are certain times you can get it or you have to order it in advance.  If you do finish in the specified time, they will pay for your food.  (We did not order it in advance and were dining at a time where it should have been ordered previously.) We asked if we could get it anyway.  Our server said he wasn't sure, he would ask, we had probably a 60/40 chance since it wasn't that busy.  Yay! They said yes.

My husband got the challenge and I got the Pollo Saltimboca with a mama's house salad and the side of pasta with White sauce.  For my food, it was some of the best Italian I have ever had.  The thing I loved the most about it was how reminiscent it was of Italy for me.  The pasta wasn't the "main" part of the dish, but the side dish.  But it was amazing.  I immediately wanted to spend a year in the kitchen learning the secrets.  For my husbands "dish."  Holy Moly! It was gigantic.  (I eventually learned just how much food it was but don't want to spoil it.) When they delivered the food, it was a huge bowl of spaghetti and the biggest meat ball I have ever seen.  After my husband decided he was finished,and we did pay for the challenge, I tried the meatball and can't wait to learn how to make them.  It was tender, juicy, and melted in my mouth.  

Not only was the food fantastic, the service was great as was the atmosphere.  It was a cute, quaint italian place that had 5 star service and phenomenal food.  I would highly recommend visiting this plae but remember to make a reservation.
name: Danielle

text: Pleasant atmosphere, good service, but food wasn't anything to rave about. Steak lacked seasoning/bland and fried shrimp were soggy. The best thing was the veggies. Pretty bummed for such a high priced meal.
name: Cynthia

text: Not sure why this place has such split reviews, but my experience was mostly fine. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish.
name: User

text: Some of the best tacos in town, hands down. The menu is expansive, as are the flavors. I have yet to be disappointed with the food or service! The friendly demeanor, laid back atmosphere, incredible food, and well mixed drinks will keep me going back for more!
name: Amanda

text: Get their signature spaghetti with shrimp dish and ask for a straw so you don't leave any of the sauce--it is addicting!!
name: Susan

text:
This is the best queso I've ever had.

I am so happy I visited Bakersfield! I made a reservation (which I completely recommend, especially on the weekend!) and got in as soon as we arrived. We were brought down to the lower level bar area for 21+, which was a great place to have our meal.

Our waitress walked us through the menu and told us what she recommended, which was really informative and swayed me into ordering the Pollo Mojo taco.

We ordered the queso (regular, no additions) and it was legitimately the best queso I've ever had. My boyfriend who "hates queso" even loved it!

Our tacos were great -- I would recommend the shrimp taco and fish taco! We're already planning our next visit to try the other tacos and queso.
name: Gabby

text: Stopped at this place while I was on vacation in Tampa and I'm very glad that I did. The food was really good and came out fast. Our server Andrew was very friendly and helped my boyfriend and I decide on what to order. Next time I stop by Tampa I will visit this place again and hope Andrew is our server again! Thank you Andrew!
name: Victoria

text: The wait was longer than it should've been for a pretty normal dinner service. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. Price felt a touch high for what it was. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. I left full, which at least counts for something. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough..
name: User

text: Service in the Roadhouse bar is nonexistent waiters walking all around absolutely no service. Sat in the bar for 20 minutes no one paid attention. Red sign up entire time
name: Richard

text: Yeah, you get a lot of food here, no matter what you order. The coffee cake was fine, not great. The self-serve coffee is on the weak/watery side. Good service.
name: John

text: Just the basic flavors here like double apple, watermelon, mint etc - nothing special about the menu (like Paan). The place looked kind of small and shabbily decorated but there aren't any upscale hookah places in philly anyway. Immediately after we ordered, the server came up to us and asked for the check which is super weird - don't you wait for the customers to finish a round or two of hookah and maybe order more?! The hookah itself was too strong - I'd have liked it a little more balanced. The only good thing about this place probably is the bouncer at the door who seemed pretty friendly and their music selection was good. Also, hookah is expensive here ($20 for a basic flavor) and no free water. Overall, nothing to write home about.
name: Komal

text: Ended up here pretty late, maybe around 9:30, bc everything else nearby had a wait. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast.
name: User

text:
All I can say is WOW!!! This place was excellent, was surprised we were seated so quickly. They definitely have slow times and busy times here, since the first time I came here it was a 45 minute wait (we left) but finally got the chance to try it!! 

We ordered the cinnamon roll, luckily we only ordered one cause it was BIG. We shared it between three people and it was almost tooooo much. It has a nice orange zest glaze and it was so yummy. I had the potato waffle for my entree and it was excellent. My friends had the farmhouse eggs and chicken hash, which they left me try and it was all so yummy! Wish I had taken a picture of my dish, but I ordered my egg fried medium since I'm not a fan of sunny eggs and they were very accommodating. The service was quick and the food was great. Will definitely be back to try more entrees and to have another cinnamon roll!
name: Brooke

text: Can I give Bakery Bar SIX stars?! My friend and I walked a few miles in the 90-degree heat to get here and, as a result, made some room for a slice of their heavenly s'more doberge. The hostess was large and in charge with her hibiscus-printed shirt and our waiter was sassy and fun. They both had us feeling the Bakery Bar fantasy!
name: D.S.

text: My wife and I just made our first (and last!) visit to Ludlow & Prime last weekend. To say this place was chaotic would be an understatement. Servers were rushing around and the host was dragging tables and chairs together and apart for large and small groups during our entire meal. Not exactly a cozy environment. This place can't decide whether it wants to be TGI Fridays, an upscale steakhouse or Shoney's. The host was also wearing a dirty baseball cap. Seriously??? There were To Go orders spilling out all over a table in the entry area. To be fair, our server was excellent and the food was good, but if I want to spent $45-50 on a steak, Morton's or Ruth's Chris is a MUCH better choice.
name: Neal

text: Great breakfast. Friendly people. Very consistent food.
name: Jay

text: Had an awesome patio lunch today. Started with the okra fries and corn muffins, and then selected the blackened grouper sandwich. All was delicious. Our server, Marie, was fantastic. She told us about the mission of the restaurant, and their particular focus on local ingredients and providers. Will absolutely be back!
name: Tammy

text:
We really enjoyed our time here! I mean for one it's the Rocky steps! And the art was very nice. The surrounding area was really beautiful too!
You could just not go inside and have a wonderful time because of how beautiful the grounds are!
name: Jodi

text:
The food is not very well prepared and the service is very long.  I strongly recommend that you find another location or you will be disappointed and out of your hard earned money.

The food is not properly seasoned and the wait staff are not good at getting the orders out correctly.

Do not waste your time at this place!
name: Darryl

text:
OPA!

This is a great place to visit with friends!

I am not the most adventurous guy when it comes to food, I am ALWAYS happy with a burger! However I am really glad we visited this restaurant.

We visited with friends and all ordered the flaming cheese to start... It is worth ordering just to watch the cheese literally be set on fire. It also tasted delicious.

If you do come here I would recommend ordering the Greek Islands Combination, as you really do get to try all different tastes throughout their menu.

The owners are all Greek and are very helpful when you are deciding what you want to order, while constantly topping up your drinks.

I think this is a must visit! Loved it!
name: Thom

text: One of my favorite breakfast spots. It's fun to be creative and write on the walls, the food is always good, and the drinks are always great. Expect to wait about 30-45 minutes though!
name: Anna

text: Peggy O'niels in Town n Country area. The best Irish pub obviously run by a full Latino staff. Good empanadas, beans n rice, drinks, and spacious dance floor playing good salsa and bachata.
name: Jeannie

text: Very much meh... I found this place by reading Yelp reviews and what an unusual disappointment. The fish was NOT fresh. It simply was not. Fatty white tuna should be plump and white, it was saggy and grey/yellowish. Salmon was the only thing that was sort of ok, and just ok, not good, let alone great. I guess I should have listened when my husband was telling me that we shouldn't try to eat sushi in Reno where there is no ocean near by...
name: Stephanie

text: Breakfast sandwich was delicious, but that is about the only thing positive about the experience.  Service was very slow, our ordered items came out one at a time, and our drinks were gone before any food hit our table.  The fruit plate was a half of a banana and apple- very expensive fruit bowl for such little variety.  The service staff were kind but there was no hurry in anything they did.  As expensive as the meal for 3 was, it should have been warm and served in a reasonable time frame.
name: Amy

text: We heard hat the place was great and it really was.  The food was very good and very fresh.  Our server was so friendly, professional and helpful with ordering. We ate outside and they had a big cooling unit out there s it was not so hot even on an August evening.  We will definitely be back!!
name: Joyce

text: You can tell they care about customer experience here. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. Service timing was efficient even tho it was busy. Overall, a strong experience. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which prob says everything.. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. They were out of one thing I originally wanted..
name: User

text: EXCELLENT EVERYTHING! The salad bar, the MEAT, the sides, the rolls, the drinks, the desserts, the SERVICE, and the decor. It's really quite amazing! Fantastic dining experience!
name: Laurie

text:
Loved the concept. The heat was too much for Tucson for the AC not to be working. 

The only vegan item in the only place serving anything vegan was Dumb Fish. The tofu bowl was "okay" but they didn't have vegan ponzu sauce for it. It wouldn't be worth returning for. I'd go to Obon before coming for this again. 

Everyone around seemed to like the food from the various restaurants. And I would say it is pretty clean inside.
name: Ia

text: Amazing food... great and friendly staff... the view was spectacular... and don't forget the desserts... yum!!! Would recommend to anyone looking for a great meal!
name: Brian

text:
Literally the best fried chicken I've ever had! We waited till we got home to eat it and it was still crispy after an almost 30 min drive home. I got mild cuz I can't handle a lot of heat and it was perfect for me. Just enough heat to give that kick! So flavorful, I have to go back before we head home. This is the only fried chicken I've ever picked clean. Highly recommend this restaurant!! 

Also bought a piece of strawberry cake and it was also very good. Oh and cherry on the sundae...we met Tom McGowan on our visit, he was also eating there for the first time. Super nice guy.
name: Erica

text: I hadn't been here in years and decided to drop in for drinks (it was the first cloudy & chilly day marking the end of any idea of a long summer). So we sat at the bar & our barmaid Sarah was awesome! I had the New Old Fashioned which was GREAT! The bourbon and the cherry herring were a perfect pair & it was just my kind of strong. My friend had the cosmo or the martini, I forget but it tasted good as well. Since neither of us were hungry HUNGRY we just had the soup & flatbread. He had the mushroom bisque with the mushroom flatbread. I had the butternut squash with the all natural pepperoni (replaced the pepperoni with mushroom, so it really was just an all natural). Everything was tasty. I was initially going to order the shrimp salad but when I found out that the shrimp were the small salad shrimp & not the large ones, I immediately knew that wasn't the salad for me. We had a good visit and it took my mind off of the weather and the dreary day. I would def recommend it and plan to return for dinner some time soon (a few menu items were quite tempting)
name: Des

text:
As soon as I sat down, I knew the first time I came a few months back was a fluke, the second though showed it's true colors... 

Besides the beers; perfect, great tasting, fresh... This may be the only reason to come to the brewery...

Other than that, this place is dirty, bad & pushy servers who make you wait... Managers are either drinking and ignoring you, or just plain rude to you... 

From working in a restaurant point of view, they'd rather give away the house before helping you out with the problem at hand... 

So many better choices in the area, don't waste your time!!
name: Michael

text:
Edit: They are open!! Took my sister and parents there. Everyone loved their dish! 

Just called and said they were open. Not sure what's going on but they have great Thai food!
name: Onyx

text: Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Price felt a touch high for what it was. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kinda leveled off after a few bites. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. Worth checking out. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Not sure though.
name: User

text: I love sushi koi so much! But, I am kind of bummed by what I got considering what I paid and gave for tip! I want sushi koi to survive! However, sometimes my BF and I are worried d/t price going up and (sometimes) quality going down. Despite the fact, for now, we continue to support sushi koi bc we love the staff and the quality sushi they typically bring to the CWE!
name: Hallie

text: I have been here twice and it gets better each time. For appetizers, the brie dip is amazing and peaches and brie flatbread is perfect to split. You can never have enough brie! I had the vegetarian spaghetti and "meat"balls and my husband had the chicken davinci. Both were delicious! The most recent time we went we both had the specials and those were also amazing. We will be back!
name: Sam

text:
This cafe is right around the corner from my apartment downtown, and I walk past it every day and finally I decided to walk in on a Sunday morning.

The crowd was good, and the atmosphere for a coffee shop was very quaint. This place repairs bicycle and the Tour de France is on so that's a reason why this place is packed.

I decided to order a Chai Latte with a shot of expresso and the drink is very good. WAY less sweet than a Starbucks. The staff was very friendly and prideful. The food selection is of your typical coffee shop, and the pricing is fair for the location. 

I will visit this place more often, and will update once I tried some food.
name: Tony

text: Really good, fancier, healthy bar/restaurant. It has a nice industrial feel, with a really cute large outdoor patio outside. We sat upstairs which is big and open. There were quite a few older business type people from navy yard and the sports complex, as well as young professionals. All the food was seriously delicious, there is a large salad section, sandwiches and entrees. The salads are all unique and seasonal. I really loved the peach and tomato salad, as well as the fig appetizer toast. Oo the froze is also a must if you like wine and frozen margaritas! Finally for dessert we tried 3 of the 4 options. My favorite was definitely the rice pudding which definitely tasted like it had condensed milk (aka the best milk). Others liked the little fried dough with Nutella dip. The s'mores sundae was ok. Overall it was a really nice experience, especially for large groups so definitely recommend!
name: Luba

text:
I debated on this a while, but I think that Bemison was just A-OK in my book. The cocktail I had - the rose Paloma, was fantastic, but it was one of four I could pick from on the menu. I am not a big cocktail drinker, so one of my favorite parts of going to get a cocktail is that I have a wealth of options I have never even heard of on the menu and can get adventurous. However loved my drink and the bartenders said they would make me anything -- I just didn't know what to ask for!

The ambiance is quite nice, and if you're there on a quieter night or you get lucky you can snag an awesome round booth! The prices are average (~$10 a cocktail) and they have a limited food menu I didn't try (I'll just have to come back!). The bartenders were very friendly, but you do order at the bar, no table service.
name: Anna

text: I woke up this morning hoping the overpriced, disgusting excuse for a California burrito was just a bad dream, but it wasn't. In fact, it was a nightmare.  After paying $16 for something that should be illegal to call a California burrito, we waited an hour and only got our food after we asked them if it was finished. The first order wasn't even correct either. This is the worst Mexican food in Santa Barbara, possibly America. Steer clear.

This review is 100% for Patrick. Food was great too, but Patrick's service went above and beyond.

Not quite sure where to start.  My husband and I have been eating here for well over 4 years.  First 10-12 visits were no less than perfect!
Next few things started going downhill.  The greet staff is very unfriendly and often times down right rude.  The visit before last our food was way less than stellar.  Tasted like poorly homemade food from a bad cook.  When we called to complain we were given a $30 gift card which was very nice.   We stopped in about a month later to use our g/c and give the place another shot - we know all too well even the best restaurants can have an off night.  We walked in on a Saturday afternoon (3:30ish), there were about 4 tables occupied.  Our favorite rude hostess was at the podium.  Before saying hello or welcome, the first words out of her mouth was, "we have a 30-45 minute wait".  HELLO!!   The place was empty.
Needless to say, we walked out.   We tried one more time about a month later.  It was about 5:00 on a Sunday.  We were about 45 minutes away from the restaurant so I tried the call ahead.  We were given a 30-45 minute window.  Perfect right?  Wrong.  We walked in and gave our name, she (same princess) says, "oh here you are (looking down at her list), we will have a table for you in about 45 minutes".  When I said that we were told that 45 minutes ago she said, "okay".   What does that even mean?   We walked out again.   So, here we sit with an used $30 gift card to what used to literally be our favorite restaurant in the www.   Our opinion is that they have gotten too big for their own britches.   Your wait staff is the only good thing you have going for you any more.   They are all incredible!
They need to stop cutting the corners they were famous for not cutting in the first place.   We are so sad to have to drop this gem from our restaurant rotation.

text:
Tucson is so lucky to have someone like Janos Wilder committed to expanding its culinary breadth.

We came here on a Saturday with 6:15p reservations, prior to a 7:30pm show.  We arrived on time and our table was ready.  The place is always buzzing with wait staff and that meant water never ran dry; dishes never sat long; and (extra) fresh, warm bread was always available, along with a nice, light olive oil on the side.

As I always do, I asked our waiter for his recommendations and ran with them: the flat-iron steak for me and the roasted eggplant for her.  The steak was outstanding - cooked medium and nicely spiced and accompanied with a small vegetable ensemble.  The curry eggplant was a delicious combination of ingredients as well, although our only complaint for the entire night was that the eggplants themselves were a little underdone (a bit too firm).

A great surprise was our new favorite cocktail.  We ordered the Vietnam (again on strong recommendation) which was based upon our request for something with a little "kick" and also not super sweet.  The waiter requested that the bartender only do half of the simple syrup and it was perfect.  We ordered another immediately. Truly unique, delicious and now, not adolescent sweet.

The ambiance was cozy/romantic; the bathrooms are elegant and clean; and we finished, as planned, with enough time to casually stroll to our show.  Thank you chef Wilder!
name: Mike

text:
Another solid take-out experience with Sichuan! The girlfriend is incredibly picky about Chinese food and she officially approves of this place.

We wanted to try to order a good amount from their "Authentic" menu, and you'll see several items that aren't typically on your standard American-Chinese restaurant's menu. Even though the menu is extensive, it doesn't exactly tell you anything about the dishes besides the name. A quick Google search can typically yield more information, and our research meant we knew what we were getting into.

I ordered as my appetizer the Longevity Buns. Sometimes these are called Longevity Peaches. This is a type of pastry in China that is usually filled with bean paste. I do have a picture that I'll upload momentarily. You get six of these delicious buns so that's probably too much for one person so have someone to split it with. The buns are very soft and a bit chewy. 

Mao's Braised Pork Belly was my main dish. This is sometimes called Red Braised Pork Belly, but also used with "Mao" because this was supposedly Chairman Mao's favorite dish. I'm not quite sure if this is traditionally a spicy dish, or if this is spicy because this is a Sichuan Chinese restaurant, but be warned this dish has a kick to it. The meat is very soft. The vegetables (mainly onions) could benefit from being into smaller chunks but otherwise this dish was perfect.

The girlfriend also found her Yuxiang Pork as her entree with a backup of Lo Mein in case she didn't like her selection from the authentic menu but she ended up enjoying both.

If you're on the north side of Indy or in Carmel, you really should try this restaurant out. It may be the closest thing we have to an authentic Chinese restaurant in the Indy metro area.
name: Matthew
