text: It was my second times to visited this place, yummy Philip steaks subs with cheese. Made you full! Yum yum!!
name: Natalie

text:
My only complaints about The Food Company are that it's not right by my house and I waited to long to find it! On my ongoing winter quest to find the best soups around, I heard about The Food Co and finally tried it this week! The restaurant is adorable and located right behind Green Hills. In case you can't find parking up front, they have a parking lot in the back! I do wish it was paved since it was quite messy when I went, but that didn't stop me. 

The inside is homey and inviting. The vibe was sort of Real Housewives of Nashville meets Frothy Monkey (but even better). I was tempted to order the daily special, taco salad, but I thought I'd go with a Classic sandwich and soup combo for my first visit. They have a variety of delicious sandwich combinations all on fresh baked breads and wraps. I went with the Turkey #1, which included turkey breast, mayo, Dijon, lettuce, tomato, onion and provolone on farm bread. This is not your normal sliced deli turkey. The sandwich had large chunks of fresh turkey breast, just like Thanksgiving. The bread was soft and fresh. Luckily, I also got to try their very popular chunky tomato basil soup. First of all, I don't even LIKE chunky tomato pieces, but I couldn't stop eating this! 5 stars for the soup for sure. They also offered chili and potato chorizo chowder that day. 

My food came out very fast, so you can definitely eat here in a hurry! One thing I LOVE is their ready to go items in the refrigerator. They had a variety of soups, all of their sides (pasta salads, egg salad, etc), chicken salad, ham and brie biscuits, chicken bakes, chicken enchiladas, quesadillas, and more all ready to take home. I was tempted to take a few things home, but I decided I needed to bring my boyfriend back asap, so I'll pick some up then. The staff was very friendly and helpful. This is definitely my new favorite lunch spot. Check it out asap, you won't regret it!
name: Macy

text:
My Wife has done me an absolute disservice by telling me MCL is only for Senior Citizens who need a more bland diet to keep as healthy as possible. MCL is the GOAT!!! We actually decided to eat here on a whim after picking up a couple of checks from Midwest Bartending School because we usually go on a lunch date due to all the great spots in Castleton. 

It is a cafeteria styled restaurant where you can choose from the daily special, an entree with 2 sides, or a la carte. It can be a bit tricky though with pricing due to the days and times when some items aren't the actual price shown. Our bill was close to $30, which was surprising, seeing as I got the daily special and she chose another entree, we both ordered drinks and I had a side of pasta. 

Everything was delicious! I had the crusted tilapia with broccoli and mac n cheese with sweet tea. I could've stayed there ALL DAY and tried all of the other food but my Wife strongly suggested I not do that. (She is my biggest Hater.) She had the chicken parmesan with pasta and the rosemary bread. We didn't eat any of the desserts, not because they weren't delicious looking but because we needed to exercise SOME sort of restraint hahaha. 

They have also just rolled out an All You Can Eat Catfish Fish Fry Friday for Lent I believe, which is just $5.39! So I promised my Wife I'd take her back this upcoming Friday so we will definitely be back, as I am a Woman of my Word!

text: Honestly I think I ordered the wrong thing. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. text:
Famous restaurant of Paul Prudhomme. A trend setting restaurant in the 80's that still serves recipes it made famous. 
I started with a hearty crawfish bisque. I strongly recommend this for an opener. We also a green salad with blue cheese dressing. The dressing tasted fine, but a little oily. 
The pepper infused dinner rolls were good, but I was disappointed that the butter wasn't better than Quincy's. 
My entree was the salmon topped with fried oysters. I really enjoyed this dish. Mashed potatoes that accompanied the entrees was nothing but filler.
The House creme brûlée is called custard Marie. The custard was good, but overall I was disappointed. Maybe because of the pecans in the bottom. Maybe because expectations were so high.

text:
I have noticed Revel Kitchen for a while now, and was curious to try it out. Finally stopped in for lunch today with my aunt. On the whole, we decided we liked the food and appreciated the healthy flavors, but there were a few draw backs. One - atmosphere ... the location is so odd. We sat outside because it was a beautiful day, but they are in sort of an industrial / big box store setting so you don't really get much other than fresh air and views of parking garages. Two - service. The man that helped us was sort of sleazy, and I felt like he just kept trying to upsell us on everything. He didn't simply explain the menu for us, he tried to order for us! I know what I like to eat sir, thank you; I don't need you to tell me. Per his recommendation, my aunt tried the BBQ style bowl with cauli rice ... we feel like they forgot the BBQ sauce, and when we asked for more on the side, he said that would be a charge!

On the up-side: I really enjoyed my asian bowl with salmon, but the real show-stopper was the hummus with pita bread (they call it naan but that is a stretch, its a tortilla grilled). Regardless of semantics, the hummus was out of this world and the warm flatbread with it was fab. I pretty much ate that as my meal and took the very generously portioned bowl home with me. The food is definitely a good deal. And if you have any dietary restrictions or allergies, this is the place for you! Definitely a great fast-casual concept, although I'll probably grab it to go next time.
name: Anna

text: This is one of those places that everyone tells you that you need to visit the second they hear you're going to New Orleans. I'll tell you that it's good, not great, not worth the line of annoying tourists that you'll have to endure to get in and seated. It's New Orleans... get off the beaten path, out of the tourist traps and go find yourself some awesome food.
name: J

text:
I took my friend who was visiting from out of town to Tavern expecting it to be a totally overrated but must-do Nashville brunch experience. It was actually worth the hype & more!

We arrived just 20 min after opening & the wait was already estimated at an hour. We decided to bite the bullet & we ended up getting sat after just 25 minutes! 

Our waitress was phenomenal. She told us that brunch cocktails were 2 for 1 and immediately got our drink & food orders down since the kitchen was obviously slammed. When my Bellini arrived, it was much sweeter than expected (that's what happens after living in LA for 4 years, where bellinis/mimosas are a flute of champagne with an eye drop worth of juice). Our waitress could tell I didn't like the drink, and suggested a "reverse sangria" which is mostly champagne with a little bit of sangria, as she said that would be much more dry. The drink was perfect for me, and she didn't even charge for the Bellini. 

I had the short rib Benedict to eat, but I can't remember which number Benedict it is. The short rib and hollandaise were both great! FYI it doesn't come with any side, which was totally fine with me because it was a solid portion of food, but if you're looking for a hefty brunch you'll want to get a different entree.
name: Mellissa

text: Can't rate it higher as the service for food bites at the bar. We sat in the larger bar area and there seemed to be a lot of tension between the servers and something happening with the register system. We got served drinks right away but they forgot about us until he got a bartender's attention after 30 minutes of waiting and me getting hangry. Sam was training but she was wonderful and tried to soothe our feelings by being gracious and checking in on us afterwards on a regular basis. Much better than the regular bartenders. She was swamped too with drink orders. The food was mediocre at best. For me anyways - I had the shrimp scampi and he had osso buco. He liked his dish. I feel that this is the place to go for drinks and to watch a game but not for a good meal.
name: Bee

text: Great food. Great drinks. Great service. Great specials.  Well worth the experience I have been several times and not one complaint. Go on Monday for the 10 dollar salmon or steak dinner special. Go on Thursday for the lobster tail special.  Get the crab cake or salmon sliders. Everything is amazing.

text:
Really good place to get a Po Boy sandwhich, however only rating 3 stars due to the wait. Ordered at 2:15pm, walked out with togo sandwhich at 2:50pm. The sanwhich was basic, but good. Was disappointed by the gumbo...much better places to find good gumbo in new Orleans. 

Also, cash only but they do have an ATM available if you forget to bring some.

text: Love this place. Great atmosphere and great food. Love the pizza & beer selection. P.s. have to try the turkey leg, it's massive, and the meat just falls off the bone!

text: No big complaints, just a nice meal. The food was good and the service was easygoing. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Price felt a touch high for what it was. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. A very pleasant experience. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. Not bad for a quick meal. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really.
name: User

text:
Clean place with beautiful interior and authentic Korean food! Loved it! And great prices.

The place reminds me of home in Hawaii, where I had lots of good Asian food. Unlike other Korean spots in St Louis, Joo Joo has fantastic service (kind, attentive, and efficient) and is generous with food portions and side dishes (which are unlimited!).

Yukgaejang - big bowl full of savory flavor and ingredients. A very satisfying meal, and the Korean rice it came with was so fluffy.

Kimchi fried rice - friend loved it! And the fried egg on top was perfect.

Side dishes - Rolled egg, kimchi, fishcake were my favorite. But they were all so legitimate and varied. 

Real Koreans making real Korean food here! I'm so happy I discovered it. It blows all other Korean, and even Asian, spots in town out of the water. I must come back to try more.
name: Kelly

text: After a round of golf at TPC we headed for BrewTown. Been before and thought it was decent. Great array of craft beers on tap and in bottles. Including some of the old standards. Ordered grilled cheese burger, breakfast burger and brats. Large burgers. Almost too big to fit in your mouth. Well received. Brats were a surprise. 2 brats were served smothered in sauerkraut on a roll. Add mustard and enjoy. Service was good and food served fast and warm. Definite try when you're in Lutz looking for a good beer and bar food. Plenty of tv's with all of the sports shown.
name: Ed

text:
I hate to write this because I go to the Block often. I hope that this will be constructive feedback. First, I went to Yelp to put our name on the waitlist for the evening and it showed no wait on the website. I literally live 5 minutes from the restaurant and by the time we walked in, the wait had moved to 30 minutes. It really makes customers mad when restaurants are signed up for No Wait and the do not use it! We grabbed a drink and waited and waited. We were seated we ordered another drink which took 10 minutes to get to the table. After that 10 mins we got our order taken. 45 minutes later our steaks arrived. We both ordered medium steaks which arrived charred and rare. We ate them because we were starving by this time and I have never been comfortable sending back food but we should have. From the time we walked through the door, it was almost an hour and 15 minutes until we got something to eat that was burned with a $140 plus bill (dinner and drinks).

I am not sure what is going on in the kitchen or with the management of the restaurant but I feel the quality has not been there the last few visits. I love having this restaurant in the community and have been a frequent customer but unfortunately it will be a while before I return.
name: Janelle

text:

text: Great place to hang out with friends! The atmosphere is hip & chill, typical Santa Barbara. I especially like the outdoor area. It can get really crowded during popular times like weekend afternoons. I got the vodka pink lemonade which was the perfect mix of alcohol + fruity tastes. The food seems expensive though.

text: Short and sweet, this place is great! Some of their entrées are only okay, but their curries, pork spare ribs, crispy beef, Singapore noodles, and general tso chicken are all great. Plus, they're on DoorDash, which is actually how I prefer to get food from this place. The restaurant is fine, don't get me wrong, but takeout is so much easier. Give it a shot!
name: Chris

text: If you haven't tried the Maratana Grille at the Don under the direction of Chef Emily Ferrari, you don't know what you are missing. The menu has something for everybody from seafood delicacies to steaks, The presentations of each plated meal is spectacular and served most pleasantly by a staff of professionals who wait upon you as if you were the only person in the room. Yes, it is expensive, but you know what? My wife is worth it and so are our guests. I highly recommend this for special events such as birthdays and anniversaries.
name: Allen
